meta.research_mode: Codex CLI chats with current web research and JSON-schema validation

digital_nomad_pr_review.scope: PR transitions for all 49 current digital-nomad and equivalent remote-worker countries recorded in this dataset; other fields retain their own research dates.

status_definitions.confirmed: Documented PR sequence supporting the remote-work profile, subject to stated admission and ongoing conditions.
status_definitions.conditional: A documented PR sequence requires additional eligibility not established for the ordinary remote-work profile.
status_definitions.unconfirmed: The reviewed sources do not establish the complete applicable PR sequence.
status_definitions.not_available: The reviewed framework provides no ordinary PR pathway for this profile.

digital_nomad_pr_review.years_to_pr_definition: Required qualifying residence duration, not processing time. Notes identify the relevant status, start of the clock and treatment of nomad time.

data.selection_summary: Afghanistan has no confirmed digital-nomad, ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker, or independent skilled-migration route. Its tourist visa is visitor status; the business route requires a valid business licence; and the residence visa only continues specified underlying visa categories. Although general naturalization and licensed-business residence rules exist, they do not make Afghanistan suitable for an ordinary foreign-client software engineer seeking a dependable citizenship path.

visa_application.title: Visa Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs — visa application
visa_application.notes: This is the MFA electronic consular visa form, not an application for a digital-nomad or independent remote-worker residence permit. Applicants must still follow the requirements of the selected visa category and relevant Afghan mission.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists because this is visitor status.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Not applicable
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No residence-income requirement is published for this visitor route.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; this is a tourist/visitor route.
income_requirement_display.notes: The MFA tourist visa allows a one-month stay within three-month validity. The separately operated eVisa channel currently advertises only a single-entry tourist eVisa, not residence or work authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: No monthly-income proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: MFA tourist-visa information requires a valid passport, travel-purpose documents, and hotel-booking confirmation.
The eVisa channel requires an eligible nationality and residence, an electronic passport, photograph and identification document; itinerary and accommodation evidence may also be submitted.

initial_validity.value: Three-month visa validity with a one-month stay; the eVisa is single-entry and permits up to 30 days after entry.
initial_validity.notes: Short visitor stay only.

extension_rules.value: No conversion or extension into remote-worker residence was confirmed.
extension_rules.notes: Other visa types must be handled through an Afghan mission; the residence category is tied to specified underlying visas.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Tourist status is not listed among the underlying categories continued by the MFA residence visa page.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No permanent-residence transition was found.

path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization provisions do not turn tourist stays into a qualifying or dependable residence route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status is not a qualifying remote-work residence or settlement route. The eVisa provider describes itself as a technology intermediary authorized for the Afghan Consulate in Dubai; the central MFA pages remain the primary category authority.

rejected_routes.route_name: Licensed business visa followed by residence visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum monthly income is published; bank statements and a valid business licence are required instead.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published monthly threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official page gives no AFN income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly threshold published; valid business licence and supporting bank statements required.
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a licensed-business route, not ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The MFA requires supporting bank statements but does not state a required number of months.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid business licence, passport copy and supporting bank statements.
A residence visa can continue a stay based on a business visa or certain other underlying visas.

initial_validity.value: Business visa: one month to three years; continuation residence visa: one month to one year.
initial_validity.notes: The official pages do not establish that every applicant receives the maximum validity.

extension_rules.value: The residence category continues business, service, entry, student or crew status for one month to one year and charges USD 50 for each month.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal criteria beyond maintaining the underlying status were not published on the page.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Potentially yes, after obtaining a qualifying business visa and maintaining the licensed-business basis.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This requires local licensed-business substance and is not a direct foreign-client freelancer route.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No separate permanent-residence status or transition rule was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: The citizenship law permits an adult foreigner to apply after somewhat more than five years in Afghanistan without committing crimes, but current counting and administration for business-residence holders require filing-level verification.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This general rule does not make the licensed-business route an ordinary remote-work match.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because it requires a valid business licence and therefore a licensed local business basis. The official materials do not confirm that merely having a foreign software contract is sufficient, nor do they describe a sole-proprietor route designed for ordinary foreign-client remote work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility depends on an invitation and official institutional documentation.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; invitation by an officially licensed Afghan company or institution required.
income_requirement_display.notes: Not independently available to an ordinary foreign-contract worker.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is published because eligibility is invitation-based.

key_requirements.requirement: Invitation from an officially licensed company or institution operating in Afghanistan, its official letter, and MFA approval.

initial_validity.value: Three-month validity with a one-month stay

extension_rules.value: The entry visa is one of the underlying categories that may be continued through a residence visa for one month to one year.
extension_rules.notes: Continued sponsorship or institutional basis would need verification.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Possible through the continuation residence category while the invited institutional basis remains valid.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This remains sponsor-dependent.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence route was published.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only the separate, general naturalization framework may be relevant after qualifying residence; no sponsor-route-specific citizenship transition was confirmed.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an Afghan company or institution must invite and support the applicant. This conflicts with the independent foreign-contract profile.

summary.value: No independent points-tested, degree-based or skilled-migration residence route was found. The student visa requires an arrangement with a recognized Afghan university and valid educational documents; it is not a qualification-based residence route for an already qualified software engineer.
summary.notes: No route comparable to independent skilled migration was listed by the MFA.

tax_residency_rule.value: Under the government-hosted 2009 Income Tax Law translation, a person is resident if their principal home is in Afghanistan at any time during the tax year, they are present for an aggregate 183 days, or they are an Afghan government employee assigned abroad.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The principal-home test can create residence before day 183. The text is an older English translation; later amendments and current de facto enforcement must be checked before filing.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. The translated law applies progressive monthly brackets.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No percentage is entered because no applicable contributory social-insurance rate was established for an ordinary foreign remote contractor. The historic 8% employee contribution applied to covered civil servants, not private workers; current institutional sources report that public payroll deductions ceased in 2024 and that private-sector workers receive no state old-age social-insurance coverage.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The MFA quotes USD 50 for each month of a continuation residence visa. This is a visa fee, not tax or social security, and no qualifying remote-worker route exists.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, inbound-expatriate, territorial or remittance-basis regime was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The ordinary statutory framework is the only relevant regime found.

taxes.caveats: The accessible English Income Tax Law is dated 2009. Current amendments, income sourcing for work physically performed in Afghanistan, business-receipts or fixed-small-business taxes, treaty credits, registration and enforcement require advice from the Afghanistan Revenue Department or a qualified local adviser.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with a 20% top marginal rate under the government-hosted 2009 English translation.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Principal home in Afghanistan at any time during the tax year, aggregate presence of 183 days, or Afghan-government foreign assignment.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on Afghan- and foreign-source taxable income, with a statutory credit mechanism for qualifying foreign income tax. Nonresidents are taxable on specified Afghan-source income and Afghan business activity.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: For this applicant scenario, the current sources do not identify a mandatory old-age social-insurance payroll contribution. The Labor Law describes employer-funded end-of-service and other employment benefits; the historical civil-service scheme deducted 8% from employees and received 8% from the public employer, but public deductions ceased in 2024, and current institutional reporting says private-sector workers have no state old-age coverage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 20% is the top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. The brackets are monthly and contain fixed components in the upper bands.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Monthly taxable income of a natural person
tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses about AFN 65.96 per USD from Da Afghanistan Bank on 1 August 2026.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Monthly taxable income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: AFN 12,501–100,000 per month, plus AFN 150 fixed amount
tax_brackets.applies_to: Monthly taxable income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD upper threshold; statutory fixed component also applies.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Above AFN 100,000 per month, plus AFN 8,900 fixed amount
tax_brackets.applies_to: Monthly taxable income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band and approximate starting threshold.

taxation_system.notes: Statutory tax screening only because the accessible English tax law is old and no qualifying remote-worker immigration route exists. Social-security evidence is clearer: historical civil-service pension rates are inapplicable to this applicant, public deductions stopped, and no private-sector state old-age contribution was identified.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Afghanistan has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary remote-worker residence route. Ordinary tax rules could nevertheless apply if a person becomes resident or performs taxable activity in Afghanistan.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: no_current_digital_nomad_or_remote_worker_route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Ordinary progressive PIT; 20% top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Principal-home or aggregate 183-day test under the government-hosted 2009 law.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The translated law includes foreign-source income in a resident natural person's tax base and provides a limited foreign-tax credit.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No digital-nomad payroll regime exists because there is no digital-nomad route. For an ordinary private or self-employed foreign contractor, the current sources do not identify a state old-age social-insurance contribution; the historical 8% civil-service employee contribution is inapplicable, and public-sector deductions ceased in 2024. Ordinary income-tax registration or wage withholding is separate from social insurance.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed_for_non-nomad_visas
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No nomad-specific recurring social-security or payroll amount applies because no such route exists. No private-sector old-age social-insurance contribution amount was identified for this applicant; the historical 8% civil-service deduction is not the applicant’s rate and public deductions ceased in 2024.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Tourist visa: USD 80; business visa: USD 40–300 depending on validity; continuation residence visa: USD 50 for each month.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The older Income Tax Law contains fixed-small-business and other business taxes, but their current thresholds and application to a foreign software contractor require verification.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa fees and legacy tax charges are not a digital-nomad payment package. The social-security conclusion is based on the Labor Law, the historical civil-service pension regulation, and current institutional reporting on the abolition or restructuring of public pension deductions and the absence of private-sector old-age coverage.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short visitor does not automatically escape Afghan tax: Afghan-source activity and the principal-home test need analysis. Tourist status also does not authorize a remote-work residence arrangement.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No qualifying immigration route exists; if nevertheless tax-resident, worldwide taxable income may fall under progressive PIT up to 20%, subject to current-law and foreign-tax-credit verification.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A licensed business may encounter ordinary PIT, business/fixed taxes, licensing costs and the USD 50-per-month residence-visa fee. No visitor-to-freelancer legalization route was confirmed.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Low route-specific confidence because no nomad route exists and the accessible English tax law is dated 2009.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No temporary-residence route fitting ordinary independent foreign-contract work was found. Licensed-business or institution-invited applicants may obtain continuation residence, but those are rejected for this profile.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No distinct permanent-residence status or qualifying transition timeline was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The law measures general naturalization by residence rather than by a confirmed permanent-residence stage.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization requires somewhat more than five years in the law, and the current Ministry of Justice service page requests proof of more than five consecutive years. This is not a usable timeline from any route fitting the applicant.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official processing-time standard or reliable current average was published.

key_conditions.value: General acquisition requires adulthood, a written application, somewhat more than five years of residence and no crimes during the stay. The file is reviewed by a citizenship commission and requires high-level approval; the 2000 law also prohibits dual citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Current administration is discretionary and should be verified directly with the Ministry of Justice and MFA.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Article 18 permits a foreign spouse married to an Afghan citizen under Islamic Sharia to apply without the ordinary five-year residence period. It does not publish a minimum marriage duration, so zero means no statutory waiting period was stated—not automatic citizenship.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legally qualifying marriage may support an immediate citizenship application without the general five-year residence period, but citizenship remains application-based and subject to approval.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The Ministry of Justice requests the marriage certificate and the Afghan spouse's identity document.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must comply with Islamic Sharia; the applicant must file in writing and pass documentary, criminal and security review. The law's dual-citizenship prohibition and discretionary final approval require careful advice. A sham or invalid marriage should not be assumed to produce status.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No official citizenship processing time was found.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Afghanistan combines descent with restricted territorial rules. A child born in Afghanistan to two foreign parents is not automatically a citizen at birth; Article 13 provides citizenship at age 18 if the person intends to live permanently in Afghanistan and does not opt for the foreign citizenship within six months. Foundlings are treated as citizens.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship at birth merely because the child is born in Afghanistan. The child may fall under the Article 13 age-18 territorial rule, and separate foundling or statelessness-related provisions may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Diplomatic, consular and international-organization families are excluded from Article 13.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Afghan citizenship can pass from one Afghan parent, but the precise rule depends on birthplace, the other parent's status or residence, and in some overseas cases parental choice. A child born in Afghanistan with one Afghan parent is covered.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Articles 10 and 11 should be applied to the exact family facts.

parent_benefit_summary.value: The citizenship law does not grant a foreign father automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship merely because his child is Afghan.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Marriage to the Afghan parent may provide a separate accelerated citizenship application, but the child's citizenship alone is not an automatic parent route.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status was confirmed. Any benefit would need to arise through a genuine qualifying marriage or another independently valid visa and citizenship application.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Current filing practice requires direct verification.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15; the same page separately lists Afghanistan's Individual Power Rank as 199.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations in Passport Index's current breakdown.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 29 visa-on-arrival plus 3 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports mobility score 35. Its methodology differs from Henley and from datasets that include eVisas or rank every individual passport separately.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is not an official language. It may be usable in limited international, aid, diplomatic or some business settings, but countrywide English-only living is not established and internet access is constrained.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The World Bank reports only 16% of the population using the internet in 2024; that is connectivity context, not a direct English-proficiency measure.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no evidence of broad practical use for daily administration or remote-work life was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Dari or Pashto support would ordinarily be more useful.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The checked current institutional sources do not publish a nationally representative mean monthly individual wage. The World Bank Development Update reports selected earnings means by age, job type and gender, while UNDP reports household income; neither is a national average worker salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The checked current NSIA, ILOSTAT, World Bank and UNDP materials do not publish a national median monthly individual wage. The UNDP page documents commissioning a 2023/24 household-income, expenditure and labor-force survey but does not publish a national median-wage table.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the AFN 5,500 monthly non-permanent private-sector minimum at about AFN 65.96 per USD. This rate dates from 2007 and remains listed as valid in June 2026.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national mean monthly individual salary is published in the checked sources. Household income and World Bank age/job/gender subgroup earnings are not substituted.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median monthly individual salary, in USD or with a reliable AFN value suitable for conversion, is published in the checked sources. The World Bank reports selected subgroup averages, ILOSTAT identifies the latest survey but exposes no national median on the country profile, and the UNDP page is a survey procurement notice rather than released wage results.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national maximum monthly salary or bounded upper endpoint of a national wage distribution is published in the checked sources. A population salary maximum is also not a stable statutory measure.

min_salary_local_currency.value: AFN 5,500/month for non-permanent private-sector workers; AFN 6,000/month for permanent government workers
min_salary_local_currency.notes: These are category-specific statutory minimum wages, not an observed national minimum or immigration threshold.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national mean monthly individual salary in AFN is published in the checked sources. UNDP’s AFN 8,980 figure is average household income, and the World Bank’s earnings figures are limited to selected age, job-type and gender groups.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national median monthly individual salary in AFN is published in the checked sources. A commissioned 2023/24 household and labor-force survey is documented, but a national median-wage result was not available on the cited current pages.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum monthly individual salary in AFN or bounded national wage range is published in the checked sources; subgroup means and statutory minimums cannot supply that upper endpoint.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly statutory minimums for specified worker categories; no current national mean, median, or maximum individual-salary series is published in the checked NSIA, ILOSTAT, World Bank, or UNDP materials.
average_citizen_salary.period: monthly
average_citizen_salary.notes: The only populated salary amount is a statutory category-specific minimum, not average citizen pay. National mean, median and maximum individual salaries remain null because current institutional sources do not publish those measures; household income and selected youth/job/gender subgroup earnings were deliberately not relabelled as national salary statistics.

cost_of_living_note.value: UNDP reported average household monthly income of AFN 8,980 and expenditure of AFN 11,117 in 2024, illustrating severe household-budget pressure; these figures are household measures rather than an individual cost-of-living index.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Use as socioeconomic context only, not as a visa income threshold or a universal household budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The independently accessible tourist route is visitor status. Business residence requires a licensed business, and institution-invited entry requires a local organization; neither is an ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route.
settlement_track.summary: Afghanistan is not a citizenship-path fit for this profile. General naturalization after more than five years exists, but no qualifying ordinary remote-worker residence route provides a credible starting status.
settlement_track.notes: A licensed entrepreneur might require separate filing-level analysis, but that materially differs from ordinary work for a foreign client.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No current visa or residence category was found that accepts an ordinary foreign employment or client contract as the independent qualifying basis.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous Afghanistan record. More than 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including nine new canonical URLs on labor law, civil-service pensions, current pension policy, taxation and wage data. The social-security fields now distinguish the inapplicable historical public-service contribution from the absence of private-sector old-age coverage; salary nulls now explain exactly which national statistics are unpublished and why household or subgroup earnings were not substituted. The route conclusion remains unchanged: no ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route exists.

data.selection_summary: Albania currently offers an official Unique Permit for Digital Mobile Workers that expressly accepts a foreign employment or foreign-client service contract, requires no Albanian employer or employment approval, and grants renewable legal residence. Because digital-mobile-worker residence is not excluded from the ordinary permanent-residence rules, it can count toward permanent residence after five consecutive years; ordinary naturalization becomes available after seven years of continuous lawful residence while holding permanent residence.

visa_application.title: Application for Unique Permit
visa_application.notes: The Ministry of Interior directs digital mobile workers to service code 15146 on e-Albania. The service is electronic and permits applications from the applicant's country of residence or from Albania while the applicant is lawfully present. Applicants who require a long-stay visa are processed for the D/LD visa through the same unique-permit procedure.

best_routes.route_name: Unique Permit for Digital Mobile Workers

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the official ALL 32,000 monthly requirement using the Bank of Albania reference of ALL 81.65 per USD published on the inspected exchange-rate page. Exchange rates fluctuate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: ALL 32,000 per person per month, or an Albanian-bank deposit of at least ALL 300,000 per person for one calendar year
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official Ministry checklist presents these as alternatives. Dependants increase the requirement per person.

income_requirement_display.value: ALL 32,000/month per person (about USD 392), or ALL 300,000/person in an Albanian bank for one calendar year
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: ALL 32,000 monthly per person OR ALL 300,000 bank deposit per person for one calendar year
income_requirement_display.notes: The bank-deposit alternative must be held in a second-level bank in Albania. The USD amount is illustrative only.

income_proof_months.notes: The official material requires proof of monthly income or the annual deposit alternative but does not specify a historical bank-statement or payslip lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: A valid employment contract with an employer abroad or a service contract with a contractor/client abroad, showing location-independent work performed through information-technology tools.
Lawful presence in Albania when the permit is issued; the application itself may be made from the applicant's country of residence or while lawfully staying in Albania.
Valid travel document, recent photograph, suitable accommodation and a home address in Albania.
Criminal-record certificate from the country of origin and health insurance valid for at least one year.
Foreign documents must generally be issued within the preceding six months, translated into Albanian, authenticated and legalized as applicable.
Employment approval is expressly not required for this category. Official processing is stated as four to twelve weeks.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year for the first permit
initial_validity.notes: The Ministry separately states that US, EU and Kosovo citizens receive a five-year permit on first application; that nationality-specific exception should not be assumed for other applicants.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while the qualifying basis and general residence conditions continue; official fee ALL 2,250 on renewal
extension_rules.notes: The official route page confirms renewal and its fee but does not state a digital-worker-specific maximum number of renewals. Continuous renewal is necessary to reach permanent residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved unique permit is itself a temporary residence and work authorization for foreign remote work; no Albanian employer is needed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not merely visitor or tourist status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply for permanent type-C residence after five years of legal and consecutive residence. Permitted absences are generally up to six months at a time and no more than ten months total during the five-year period; the applicant must also show lawful resources, health insurance, adequate housing and regular payment of Albanian taxes and dues.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Article 88 excludes several temporary categories, including seasonal and cross-border-service permits, but does not exclude digital mobile workers. The conclusion that digital-worker time counts is therefore based on the combined effect of Articles 68, 87 and 88.

path_to_citizenship.value: After at least seven years of continuous lawful residence and acquisition of permanent residence, the applicant may apply for ordinary naturalization, subject to housing, lawful income, criminal-record, Albanian-language, history and security requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The citizenship law requires permanent residence to be valid when applying. In the normal sequence, permanent residence can be acquired after year five and citizenship eligibility arises at year seven.

best_routes.notes: This route is a strong match for an ordinary software engineer working under an active foreign employment or foreign-client contract. The unusually low statutory income threshold should still be checked inside the live e-Albania form before filing, and the applicant must maintain residence continuity, renew on time and comply with Albanian tax obligations.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly income threshold is published for this route; eligibility instead turns on business capital and economic-impact criteria.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The inspected official sources do not publish a minimum capital amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published; adequate capital and positive Albanian economic impact are required
income_requirement_display.notes: A commission evaluates the business proposal, economic interest, expected positive impact and capital.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is stated because this is a business-substance assessment rather than an ordinary remote-income route.

key_requirements.requirement: Demonstrate an economic interest, an expected positive impact on Albania's economy and sufficient capital to implement the business idea.
Register the activity with the National Business Centre and obtain a favorable assessment from the designated evaluation commission.

initial_validity.value: For the planned business duration, up to 3 years

extension_rules.value: A successful planned activity may support permanent residence after three years; otherwise continued status depends on meeting the business conditions.
extension_rules.notes: Initial service fees are ALL 8,000 for up to one year, ALL 9,000 for up to two years and ALL 10,000 for up to three years; renewal is ALL 4,000.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct unique-permit residence after business registration and commission approval.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential permanent residence after three years if the planned activity was successfully completed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This favorable timeline does not remove the substantive capital and Albanian economic-impact tests.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary citizenship rules would apply after the required continuous residence and permanent-residence conditions are met.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this selection because it requires business capital, a positive impact on Albania's economy and commission approval. Ordinary foreign-client software contracting does not automatically meet those requirements, while the separate digital-mobile-worker permit fits without them.

rejected_routes.route_name: Albanian Blue Card / Highly Qualified Employee Unique Permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current salary threshold was not needed to determine rejection and was not established from the inspected route material.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No current Blue Card threshold was established in this audit.

income_requirement_display.value: Local highly qualified employment contract and applicable salary test required
income_requirement_display.notes: This route is rejected independently of the threshold because it requires local employment.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable as a historical foreign-income test.

key_requirements.requirement: A highly qualified employment contract governed by Albanian employment requirements and proof of professional qualifications.

initial_validity.value: Tied to the qualifying employment terms
initial_validity.notes: A precise duration was not established because the mandatory local-employment condition already disqualifies the route.

extension_rules.value: Depends on continuation of qualifying local employment

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Unique-permit residence based on highly qualified local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential under the Aliens Law, but only after residence based on the non-fitting local employment route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential only through the ordinary residence and naturalization sequence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a qualifying Albanian employment relationship and therefore does not fit independent foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: A foreign student admitted to a recognized Albanian educational institution can independently obtain a residence permit for up to one year at first issuance and renew it through completion of studies. Study time counts only at half value for permanent-residence purposes, and the student permit cannot be converted to a work permit during studies; after graduation the person may apply for a single permit if the separate employment conditions are met. A pre-existing foreign software-engineering degree alone does not create an independent residence route.
summary.notes: This is an education route, not a qualification-only or ordinary remote-work route, so it is not selected over the digital-mobile-worker permit.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Albanian tax resident if they have a residence/domicile in Albania under the Civil Code or are present, continuously or intermittently, for more than 183 days in a 365-day period. Resident individuals are taxable on Albanian and foreign income; non-residents are taxable on Albanian-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence, source rules and the domicile test can alter the practical result; the 183-day threshold is not the only residence test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening PIT rate, not an expected effective rate. Employment and business income use different brackets, deductions and temporary relief.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For a locally registered self-employed person, this is the sum of a 23% social-insurance rate and 3.4% health rate, but they apply to different minimum bases: at least ALL 50,000 and ALL 100,000 respectively. It must not be read as 26.4% of actual remote income. A locally employed worker instead pays 11.2% employee contributions, with 16.7% paid by the employer.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate minimum for a locally registered non-agricultural self-employed person: ALL 11,500 social insurance plus ALL 3,400 health insurance, totaling ALL 14,900 monthly. This is not automatically imposed merely by holding the digital-mobile-worker permit; classification and registration require professional advice.

special_tax_regimes.value: Commercial individuals and self-employed persons with annual gross income up to ALL 14 million currently have a 0% business-income tax rate through 31 December 2029. This is a general small-business rule, not a digital-nomad exemption, and eligibility requires the income to be properly classified and the person appropriately registered.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign employment income should not be assumed to qualify as self-employed business income.

taxes.caveats: The immigration permit does not itself determine tax classification. A remote employee, independent contractor and Albanian-registered sole trader can have materially different PIT, social-security, payroll, VAT and permanent-establishment outcomes. Double-tax treaties and foreign tax credits must be checked for the applicant's country and contract structure.

taxation_system.value: Mixed progressive worldwide-income system for residents, with employment, business and investment income taxed under different schedules.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence/domicile in Albania or more than 183 days in a 365-day period; treaty tie-breakers may apply.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: worldwide income. Non-residents: Albanian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Temporary 0% business-income rate through 2029 for qualifying commercial individuals and self-employed persons with annual gross income up to ALL 14 million; optional standardized-expense regime may be available below ALL 10 million turnover.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees contribute 11.2% and employers 16.7%. Registered self-employed persons pay at least 23% on ALL 50,000 plus 3.4% health insurance on ALL 100,000 monthly under the 2026 bases.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 23% number is the top marginal screening rate. Employment income has personal-allowance mechanics; self-employed business income has a separate schedule and temporary relief.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual employment tax base from ALL 0 to ALL 2,040,000, subject to personal deductions/allowances
tax_brackets.notes: PwC states this annual schedule applies from 1 January 2025. The taxable base may be lower than gross pay because of the monthly personal allowance.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual employment tax base over ALL 2,040,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate only.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual gross business income up to ALL 14,000,000 through 31 December 2029, if the relief applies
tax_brackets.applies_to: Qualifying commercial individuals and self-employed persons
tax_brackets.notes: The underlying statutory bracket is described as 15%, but qualifying taxpayers in this gross-income range receive the temporary 0% treatment.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net taxable business income over ALL 14,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: Classification and calculation use business-tax rules rather than the employment schedule.

taxation_system.notes: Official tax-authority pages confirm residence and worldwide-income principles, but some official rate pages retain older tables. The July 2026 PwC summary was therefore used for current brackets and contribution amounts.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special tax exemption for holders of the digital-mobile-worker permit was found. Ordinary residence, source and income-classification rules apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: foreign remote employee or contractor; classification-dependent
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Top ordinary PIT screening rate 23%; qualifying registered self-employed business income up to ALL 14 million gross may be 0% through 2029.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence/domicile or more than 183 days in 365 days; residents are generally subject to worldwide-income taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign income is within the tax base for Albanian residents. The tax authority states that a foreigner staying under 183 days whose employer is non-resident and whose remuneration is not borne by an Albanian permanent establishment/fixed base may remain taxable only in the residence country if all conditions are met.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed. The small-business 0% rule is general and should not be described as a nomad tax holiday.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No official source inspected establishes an automatic digital-permit contribution exemption. Local employment or self-employment registration can trigger contributions; continued foreign social-security coverage and treaty arrangements require case-specific review.

fixed_payments.status: route fee confirmed; tax and social payments depend on classification
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: If registered locally as self-employed, the 2026 minimum is approximately ALL 14,900 monthly; no automatic minimum was established for a permit holder remaining solely on foreign payroll.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Unique permit: ALL 4,500 initially and ALL 2,250 on renewal, approximately USD 55 and USD 28 at the cited exchange rate. A separate D-visa payment may apply where the applicant's nationality requires it.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Standard VAT is 20%. No digital-nomad-specific municipal tax, transaction tax or fixed freelancer levy was confirmed.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health insurance valid for at least one year is an immigration requirement and is an additional market-priced cost, not a fixed state payment.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person under 183 days may still be resident through domicile or may have Albanian-source income. Where genuinely non-resident, foreign-employer remuneration not borne by an Albanian permanent establishment may fall outside Albanian tax under the tax authority's stated conditions and applicable treaty.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Plan for Albanian filing and worldwide-income analysis. Employment income can reach the 23% marginal rate; foreign taxes and treaty relief must be documented.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Potential 0% business-income treatment through 2029 below ALL 14 million gross, but mandatory minimum social and health contributions, bookkeeping, registration and possible VAT obligations remain.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax result depends more on the contract and local registration than on the immigration label. Obtain Albanian advice before relying on the small-business exemption or foreign-payroll treatment.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Approval directly grants a temporary unique residence permit; processing is officially four to twelve weeks.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five years are counted from the first residence-permit application, assuming legal and consecutive residence and compliance with absence, means, insurance, housing and tax requirements.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires seven years of continuous lawful residence and a valid permanent residence permit. Since ordinary PR is available after five years, the earliest normal gap is approximately two years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Eligibility estimate from commencement of continuous lawful residence, not a guarantee of approval or completion.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: This is a statutory complete-file timeline rather than an observed median: up to one month for local police forwarding, six months for Ministry review and 60 days for the presidential decree. Incomplete documents and the subsequent oath can extend completion; the oath is normally required within six months after notification.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous lawful residence; keep absences within PR limits; hold a valid permanent residence permit when applying; maintain adequate housing and lawful income; pay Albanian taxes and dues; pass Albanian spoken/written language and basic history requirements; have no disqualifying serious conviction or security issue; and take the citizenship oath. The citizenship law does not state that ordinary applicants must renounce their existing citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization remains an application process and is not automatic at year seven.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must have been married to an Albanian citizen for at least three years and must also have resided lawfully and continuously in Albania for at least one year.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to an Albanian citizen counts toward the three-year marriage period; once both the three-year marriage and one-year Albanian residence requirements are met, the spouse may use the simplified naturalization rule. Marriage to another foreigner does not accelerate the principal applicant's citizenship, though dependant residence may be available.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The law waives the ordinary seven-year/permanent-residence condition and the language condition for the qualifying Albanian-citizen spouse route, but other naturalization requirements remain.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be genuine and documented. The Aliens Law permits cancellation of family-reunification residence where a marriage was contracted solely to obtain residence or where fraud/false information was used. Applicants still need legal capacity, adequate housing and income, acceptable criminal/security records and the prescribed procedure.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sham marriage can lead to refusal or cancellation and should never be treated as an immigration strategy.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is automatic when at least one parent is Albanian. Birth or discovery in Albania grants citizenship only where the child may otherwise remain stateless; ordinary birth to foreign parents is not sufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Albania to two foreign parents does not ordinarily acquire Albanian citizenship. Citizenship is granted if the child would otherwise remain stateless. Separately, a child born in Albania to parents who hold permanent residence can receive permanent residence, not citizenship, under the Aliens Law.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The special permanent-residence provision refers to parents holding permanent residence and should not be generalized to one temporary-resident parent.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child automatically acquires Albanian citizenship at birth if either parent is an Albanian citizen, regardless of whether the other parent—the father in the stated scenario—is a migrant.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father does not automatically acquire citizenship through the child.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent whose minor child is Albanian may seek simplified naturalization after at least three years of lawful and continuous Albanian residence. The provision waives the ordinary seven-year/permanent-residence condition but leaves the other applicable naturalization requirements in place.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: This is an application advantage, not automatic citizenship or immediate permanent residence.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child is Albanian, the migrant father can potentially use family-based residence and, after three years of continuous lawful Albanian residence, the citizen-child naturalization provision. If the child is not Albanian, birth alone gives the father no citizenship shortcut.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, parental responsibility, genuine family life, residence continuity and all remaining statutory conditions must be documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank on the directly inspected Albania dashboard. Henley's January 2026 release used a different methodology/update and placed Albania 43rd, so figures from the two indexes should not be mixed.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index; its overall mobility score is 123 after adding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category. Electronic visas may be classified separately in destination-level data, so this is index-specific.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 42 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 6 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: The current Passport Index breakdown is internally consistent: 75 visa-free, 42 visa on arrival and 6 eTA produce a mobility score of 123. Henley's January 2026 report placed Albania 43rd with access to 121 destinations without a prior visa; rankings change during the year and definitions differ.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is reasonably practical in Tirana and international/technology settings but cannot replace Albanian for official processes and long-term integration. EF EPI 2025 scored Albania 532 and ranked it 42nd globally, in the moderate-proficiency band; Tirana scored 557.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected test-based index rather than a census, so it supports only a broad practicality assessment.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and should not be assumed usable for immigration, tax, banking or citizenship procedures. No reliable current national proficiency dataset establishing broad practical use was found in the additional language searches.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Applicants should plan to use Albanian or, where accepted, English and professional translation.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official ALL 90,119 average gross monthly wage using ALL 81.65 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current quarterly wage release publishes a mean, not a median. The inspected Structure of Earnings Survey also reported means by category; no defensible current national monthly median was established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the statutory national gross minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the official national average gross monthly wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national monthly median was found; it is not inferred from the mean.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum wage is published. ALL 186,416 is only the 2026 maximum contribution base and is not a maximum salary, so it is not used here.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum effective 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National average for employees in Q1 2026. Information and communication averaged ALL 131,747, relevant as sector context for a software engineer.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national median was published in the inspected official releases.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No actual national maximum salary was established; the social-contribution ceiling is not a wage maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly wage per employee from administrative wage statistics; minimum is the statutory gross monthly minimum
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 average; minimum effective from 1 January 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: USD values are rounded using the latest Bank of Albania rate visible in the inspected source, dated 30 July 2026. The Q2 2026 wage release was scheduled for 10 September 2026 and was not yet available on the research date.

cost_of_living_note.value: INSTAT's 2024 Household Budget Survey reported average consumption expenditure of ALL 93,042 per month for a household averaging 3.1 people, about USD 1,140 at the cited exchange rate. This national household figure excludes durable goods, investment and imputed rent and is not a single-expat or Tirana budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Use it only as official national context; actual rent and remote-worker costs in Tirana can differ substantially.
