settlement_track.summary: The digital-mobile-worker unique permit is renewable legal residence, not visitor status, and the Aliens Law does not exclude it from permanent residence after five consecutive years. The holder must switch to permanent residence and can then seek ordinary naturalization once total continuous lawful residence reaches seven years.
settlement_track.notes: The settlement conclusion is derived directly from the digital-worker permit provision, the general PR rule and its explicit exclusion list. Successful settlement still depends on uninterrupted renewals, absence limits, tax compliance, permanent residence and naturalization requirements.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route expressly accepts either employment with an employer abroad or a service contract with a contractor/client abroad, requires IT-enabled location-independent work and does not require Albanian employment approval.

data.notes: The previous record correctly identified the route but contained contradictory selection and settlement flags, an obsolete claim that the income threshold and validity were unconfirmed, and an incorrect five-year citizenship estimate. Current official sources now confirm the direct application channel, ALL 32,000 monthly or ALL 300,000 deposit test, one-year initial validity, fees, renewal, foreign-contract eligibility, five-year PR rule and seven-year naturalization rule. Tax classification remains the main case-specific issue.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Renewed unique permits for digital mobile workers, followed by type-C permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A foreign-employed or foreign-client digital mobile worker can maintain qualifying residence and apply for type-C permanent residence after five consecutive legal years.
requirements: Maintain the remote employment/service contract and renew residence in time.
Meet the five-year continuity and absence limits, sufficient lawful resources, accommodation, health-insurance and tax-compliance conditions.
reviewed_route_names: Unique Permit for Digital Mobile Workers
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Articles 68, 87 and 88 of the official Aliens Law were re-read. Counting digital-worker time is a combined statutory inference: the category is not named among Article 88 exclusions. PR requires an application; it is not automatic.

data.selection_summary: Algeria has no dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker visa. Its law and current Interior Ministry guidance recognize residence and a renewable professional card for foreigners carrying on commercial, industrial, artisanal, or liberal activity without a local employer. However, the filing sequence remains inconsistent: the 2006 decree contemplates professional registration followed by a resident-card request, while current CNRC and auto-entrepreneur channels require residence or prior legal-resident status, and the resident-card checklist requires evidence of an already authorized activity. No official source confirms that an incoming software engineer working only for foreign clients can complete this sequence. Filing-level confirmation is required before Algeria can be selected.

visa_application.title: Entry visa to Algeria
visa_application.notes: This is the official visa-information page, not a central online application portal. Applications start through the Algerian embassy or consulate responsible for the applicant's habitual residence. The published categories include tourist, business, study, work, temporary-work, and family visas, but no digital-nomad or independent-professional entry visa.

best_routes.route_name: Foreign resident card and professional card based on an independent activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official resident-card checklist publishes no numerical minimum income for a person exercising an activity. It instead requires competent-authority evidence of the authorized activity.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed DZD income threshold is published for this activity-based resident card.

income_requirement_display.value: No numerical minimum published; evidence of a lawfully authorized independent activity is required
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign contract is neither expressly required nor expressly recognized. Whether foreign-client software development is registrable as a commercial service or qualifying liberal profession requires filing-level confirmation.

income_proof_months.notes: The current Interior Ministry checklist prescribes no bank-statement or income-history period for applicants exercising an activity.

key_requirements.requirement: Remain lawfully present and submit the resident-card application to the competent security service before visa expiry; the current Interior Ministry page states 15 days before expiry.
Provide a birth certificate, five photographs, fiscal stamp, medical certificates, valid passport and entry visa where applicable, and proof of accommodation.
Provide competent-authority evidence of lawful commercial, industrial, artisanal, or liberal professional activity.

For a professional card, establish registration in the commercial register, crafts register, or governing professional organization as applicable. The 2006 decree requires the professional-card holder to request a resident card within 90 days.

Resolve contradictory filing guidance: the current professional-card page accepts a resident card or its filing receipt, but the CNRC individual-registration checklist requires a resident card and the resident-card checklist requires evidence of activity.
Auto-entrepreneur registration cannot solve initial immigration status because a foreign applicant must already be resident under Algerian law.
After establishing non-salaried activity, complete tax registration and CASNOS affiliation.

initial_validity.value: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The general resident card and professional card are each normally valid for two years. A resident card linked to another authorizing document may instead match that document's validity.

extension_rules.value: The professional card is renewable, with the decree requiring renewal filing no later than 60 days before expiry. Resident status remains dependent on continuing to satisfy its legal basis.
extension_rules.notes: No consolidated current renewal checklist for a foreign-client software professional was published in the reviewed sources.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: If the independent activity documentation is accepted, the applicant receives a two-year foreign resident card. The 2006 professional-card decree also contemplates a professional-card holder applying for the resident card within 90 days.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The statutes recognize the status, but current agency checklists do not establish a reliable first-time sequence for this applicant profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least seven years of continuous lawful residence, a ten-year resident card may be issued. Algeria describes this as a ten-year card rather than permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Issuance is discretionary and requires current residence, tax, social-security, and justification documents.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after at least seven years of habitual lawful residence, with approval remaining discretionary by decree.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Seven years is an eligibility threshold, not a guaranteed acquisition date.

best_routes.notes: This is a genuine residence category and does not expressly require a local employer. Focused review of the professional-card decree improved the legal sequence: it expressly requires a professional-card holder to request residence within 90 days. Nevertheless, current CNRC, ANAE, professional-card, and resident-card instructions remain inconsistent, and no official page confirms foreign-client software work as sufficient initial activity evidence. Treat the route as manual-review only.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold applies because this is a business status rather than a residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The eligibility page does not prescribe a minimum income.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration threshold; a foreign applicant must already be legally resident
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligible fields include digital services, but the registration does not independently legalize residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Be of legal working age and carry on an activity included in the eligible activity list.
Be an Algerian citizen resident in Algeria or a foreigner already resident under applicable Algerian law.

initial_validity.notes: The status's card validity is not material to immigration eligibility and was not established from the reviewed public page.

extension_rules.notes: Immigration renewal rules are inapplicable because the registration is not a residence permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None directly; prior lawful residence is an eligibility condition.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It can support an already resident person's business activity but is not an entry-to-residence route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Settlement would depend on a separately obtained resident card.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path is inherent in auto-entrepreneur registration.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship depends on qualifying lawful residence under another status.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as a standalone immigration route because foreign applicants must already be resident.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-work threshold; visitor and business visas are not independent-work residence permits
income_requirement_display.notes: A business visa normally requires an Algerian operator's invitation or employer mission documentation.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard income-history period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Consular application, passport, photographs, travel and repatriation insurance, and category-specific supporting documents.
Business-visa applicants provide an Algerian operator invitation or employer mission documentation.

initial_validity.notes: Duration is determined by the issued visa; no universal duration is published.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary remote-worker extension or settlement rule is published.
extension_rules.notes: A separate resident-card filing is required to establish residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence; a separate resident-card application is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The visitor or business visa itself is not qualifying residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from the visa itself.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Only subsequent lawful resident-card time could qualify.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor or business status itself.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires habitual lawful residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor or business permission is not authorization for indefinite foreign-contract remote work and does not itself create a settlement track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Locally sponsored work visa and employee resident card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general immigration salary threshold was established.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general monetary threshold is published in the reviewed guidance.

income_requirement_display.value: No general threshold published; Algerian employment authorization is mandatory
income_requirement_display.notes: The route is tied to Algerian employment and fails the applicant profile.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Work permit or temporary-work authorization.
Employment contract and employer undertaking concerning repatriation.

initial_validity.value: The resident card cannot exceed the employment authorization's validity; the general card is two years.
initial_validity.notes: Actual validity depends on the work authorization.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continuing authorized Algerian employment.
extension_rules.notes: The status cannot be maintained solely through a foreign client.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An employee resident card is available through authorized local employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Local sponsorship is mandatory.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A ten-year card may be considered after seven years of continuous lawful residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not make the initial route independently applicable.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization eligibility may arise after seven years of lawful residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route is rejected because of local-employer sponsorship, not because it lacks residence.

rejected_routes.notes: A residence and citizenship track exists, but the required Algerian employer, contract, and work authorization make it ineligible.

rejected_routes.route_name: Study visa and student resident card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No universal amount is published; a scholarship or evidence covering study and residence is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed DZD amount is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed amount published; proof of study and living support is required
income_requirement_display.notes: The route is tied to genuine enrollment rather than the applicant's foreign contract.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard proof period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Enrollment at an approved Algerian educational institution.
Scholarship documentation or sufficient study and living support.

initial_validity.value: Up to the documented study or training period
initial_validity.notes: The student resident card cannot exceed the underlying study or training period.

extension_rules.value: Continued enrollment and supporting documentation are required.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic post-study independent-work conversion was confirmed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A student resident card follows satisfaction of the study-visa and enrollment conditions.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Residence remains education-dependent.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A ten-year card may be considered after seven years of continuous lawful residence, but no source specifically confirms treatment of student years or a post-study conversion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: An automatic student-to-settlement transition should not be assumed.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization law requires seven years of habitual lawful residence, but the reviewed official sources do not specifically address how student years are assessed.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Legal confirmation would be required.

rejected_routes.notes: Available without an employer and grants temporary residence, but rejected because it requires genuine local study and is not a route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: Admission to an approved Algerian educational institution supports a study visa and student resident card without an employer. No independent degree-only skilled migration or confirmed post-study remote-worker conversion was found.
summary.notes: A foreign university degree by itself does not establish residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: Algerian domestic law does not provide a simple 183-day safe harbor. Fiscal domicile can arise from an Algerian dwelling held under a continuous lease of at least one year, principal stay or main interests in Algeria, or the exercise of salaried or non-salaried professional activity there.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residents are taxable on aggregate income and non-residents on Algerian-source income, subject to applicable tax treaties.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate. An eligible small BNC activity under IFU may instead face 12% of receipts.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The non-salaried CASNOS contribution is 15% of its contribution base. The employee system's aggregate rate is not the appropriate independent-professional comparison.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate inferred minimum: applying 15% to the statutory minimum annual base derived from the DZD 24,000 monthly SNMG gives DZD 43,200 annually or DZD 3,600 monthly, approximately USD 27 at about DZD 133.2/USD. Confirm the current assessment directly with CASNOS.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-expatriate regime was found. Qualifying professional activities below the applicable DZD 8,000,000 annual receipts ceiling may use IFU, generally 12% of professional receipts for BNC. Auto-entrepreneur activities have a 0.5% rate, but foreign eligibility requires prior lawful residence.
special_tax_regimes.notes: IFU and auto-entrepreneur taxation are domestic small-business rules rather than visa benefits.

taxes.caveats: Classification and sourcing of foreign-client software income, expense deductions, IFU eligibility, VAT, CASNOS base, foreign-exchange collection, and treaty relief require Algerian professional advice. Immigration approval and tax registration are separate questions.

taxation_system.value: Residents generally pay IRG on aggregate income, with non-commercial professional profit taxed under the progressive scale unless an eligible IFU treatment applies.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Fiscal domicile may arise through a qualifying dwelling, principal stay or main interests, or professional activity; it is not governed solely by 183 days.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: aggregate Algerian and foreign income. Non-residents: Algerian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: IFU may apply at 12% of professional receipts for qualifying BNC activity; auto-entrepreneur activities have a 0.5% rate but require the separate status and prior residence.
taxation_system.social_security: A registered non-salaried professional is generally affiliated with CASNOS at 15% of the statutory contribution base.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 35% number is the highest marginal IRG rate and only a screening value. Effective tax depends on taxable profit, deductions, household position, and eligibility for IFU.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income not exceeding DZD 240,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate conversion at DZD 133.2/USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: IRG marginal band up to DZD 480,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: IRG marginal band up to DZD 960,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: IRG marginal band up to DZD 1,920,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: IRG marginal band up to DZD 3,840,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.
The threshold is approximate; 35% is not the effective tax rate.

taxation_system.notes: Rates and regimes are reasonably supported, but application to a foreign-client software contract depends on the accepted registration structure. Domestic residence criteria may attach earlier than 183 days.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax category exists. If the independent-professional residence is accepted, software-service income would likely be treated as non-commercial professional income or under IFU, subject to confirmation.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Prospective resident independent professional or BNC taxpayer; no digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive IRG up to 35% on net taxable professional profit, or potentially 12% IFU on professional receipts where eligible
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Fiscal domicile may arise through a qualifying dwelling, principal stay or main interests, or exercising the activity in Algeria; no automatic 183-day exemption was established.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A fiscally domiciled person is taxable on aggregate income, including foreign income, subject to treaty and foreign-tax-relief analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found in the current tax-authority materials.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A locally registered non-salaried professional is generally subject to CASNOS at 15% of the contribution base; no foreign-employer exemption was confirmed.

fixed_payments.status: Partly confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: CASNOS is 15% of its assessment base. Applying the statutory minimum-base rule to the 2026 SNMG implies an estimated DZD 43,200 annual minimum, but CASNOS should confirm the current assessment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The Interior Ministry's Arabic resident-card guidance lists a DZD 6,000 fiscal stamp for the ordinary card and DZD 30,000 for the ten-year card. Visa fees vary by nationality and reciprocity.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: CNRC lists a DZD 4,000 registration stamp plus registration charges. VAT may apply under the real or simplified regime; the standard rate is 19% and the reduced rate 9%.
fixed_payments.notes: No official calculator covers the full foreign software-professional scenario. Registration charges, CASNOS, IFU or IRG, VAT, and foreign-exchange compliance require local confirmation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no dependable day-count-only safe harbor: taking a qualifying lease or exercising the profession in Algeria can establish fiscal domicile. Short stays require domestic-law and treaty analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If fiscally domiciled and properly registered, professional income should be declared under the applicable BNC, IRG, or IFU treatment, with treaty or foreign-tax-credit analysis as appropriate.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect tax-file registration, possible IFU or simplified-BNC reporting, CASNOS affiliation, and potentially VAT. Immigration authorities require competent-authority evidence of the activity.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This remains a prospective analysis because the immigration registration sequence is unresolved.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The activity-based filing directly seeks temporary residence, and the professional-card decree contemplates requesting residence within 90 days after the professional card. No preliminary multi-year residence period is prescribed.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: After seven continuous lawful years, the available long status is a discretionary ten-year resident card, not expressly permanent residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization and the ten-year resident card both use a seven-year residence threshold, so naturalization eligibility does not necessarily require additional years after the long card. Neither approval is automatic.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Seven years is the ordinary eligibility threshold from lawful residence, not a guaranteed citizenship date.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality provisions and current Ministry of Justice document checklists publish neither a binding processing deadline nor a reliable typical processing duration.

key_conditions.value: Continuous habitual lawful residence; a valid resident card; tax clearance; sufficient means; physical and mental fitness; good character and criminal-record review; and integration into Algerian society. Approval is by decree. No standardized language-test or mandatory renunciation rule was established in the reviewed current materials.
key_conditions.notes: An uninterrupted absence of one year can cause loss of resident status and disrupt continuity.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship by marriage requires at least three years of a legally valid and effective marriage to an Algerian and at least two years of habitual lawful residence in Algeria.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A pre-existing genuine marriage can count toward the three-year period, including a foreign marriage if properly documented or transcribed. At least two years of lawful habitual residence in Algeria must still be completed.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not confer immediate citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid and genuinely continuing. The applicant must document lawful residence, good conduct, sufficient means, a valid resident card, tax clearance, health status, and civil status. Acquisition remains discretionary by decree; false or sham evidence creates refusal and legal risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The Ministry checklist operationalizes the statutory marriage and residence conditions.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Nationality is principally by descent from an Algerian mother or father. Birth in Algeria alone qualifies only in narrow cases such as unknown parents and the specified case involving an unknown father and a mother whose nationality cannot be established from the birth record.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Algeria to two known foreign parents does not ordinarily become Algerian merely by birth. Narrow unknown-parent, foundling, or nationality-undetermined exceptions may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Algeria does not have broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If either parent is Algerian, the child is Algerian by descent, subject to documenting filiation and civil-status registration.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2005 amendment recognizes descent through either an Algerian mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's nationality does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. Family or marriage-based residence may be investigated, but no reviewed official source establishes automatic permanent residence or citizenship merely from being the parent of an Algerian child.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The ten-year-card guidance recognizes mixed marriage as a possible justification but does not state that parenthood alone grants status.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Algerian, the child can be Algerian, but the migrant father remains subject to separate immigration and nationality requirements. Marriage to the mother may create the three-year-marriage and two-year-residence naturalization route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: There is no automatic derivative citizenship for the father.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category; its broader mobility score includes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 38 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations reported separately by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 66. Index methodologies differ, so these category counts should not be mixed with Henley figures.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only professional remote work can be feasible in selected international or IT settings but is not broadly sufficient for government, immigration, tax, housing, and routine administration. EF EPI 2025 places Algeria in the low-proficiency band.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Arabic is essential for many official interactions; French also remains practically important despite not being an official language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian alone is not a practical basis for immigration administration or daily life. Applicants should plan for Arabic and often French, with English useful mainly in selected professional environments.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official-language framework and English-proficiency evidence; no national Russian- or Ukrainian-usage dataset was located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest official ONS enterprise-survey mean located, DZD 43,500 net monthly in May 2022, at approximately DZD 133.2/USD. The observation is historical and excludes agriculture and public administration.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2022, 2019, and 2017 ONS enterprise surveys publish arithmetic means by sector and qualification but no national median. The older 2013 ONS distribution report publishes decile-group information rather than a current exact median, and the ILOSTAT wages catalogue did not expose a usable Algeria median value on the reviewed country-facing pages.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the statutory DZD 24,000 monthly SNMG effective January 2026. This is the legal minimum wage, not an observed distribution minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official DZD 43,500 monthly net enterprise-survey mean.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current exact national median could be established. Current and recent ONS wage releases report means; the older distribution publication is not an exact current median, and no Algeria median figure was displayed in the reviewed ILOSTAT country material.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national maximum wage is published in the official surveys. Their largest figures are group averages by sector or qualification, not individual maximum salaries, and therefore cannot support a USD maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national guaranteed minimum wage effective January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official ONS May 2022 enterprise-survey mean, excluding agriculture and public administration.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The latest official ONS survey located, for May 2022, reports means by sector and qualification but does not publish a national median. The 2019 and 2017 ONS releases follow the same mean-based structure. An older 2013 ONS publication reports decile distributions but does not provide a current exact median, and the reviewed ILOSTAT catalogue and Algeria profile did not display an Algeria median observation. A current national median therefore remains unpublished in the named sources and is kept null rather than inferred.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed ONS surveys publish overall, sector, and qualification averages but no observed national upper endpoint or maximum salary. Figures such as the DZD 114,100 hydrocarbon-sector average in the 2022 survey are group means, not individual maxima. Because earnings have no meaningful statutory national ceiling and no survey maximum is published, this value is inapplicable as a reliable national statistic and remains null.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum for the minimum field; May 2022 monthly net enterprise-survey mean for the average field, excluding agriculture and public administration
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage: 2026; average wage observation: May 2022
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum and average are well-supported but represent different concepts and periods. Focused searches of current and historical ONS wage material and ILOSTAT did not establish a current exact national median or a meaningful national maximum. Those fields remain null with the specific publication limitations documented above.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed ONS portal did not provide a sufficiently current national cost-of-living basket directly comparable to the wage figures. No cost estimate was inferred from wages, consumer anecdotes, or unofficial exchange rates.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Not applicable as a temporary-nomad warning because Algeria has no digital-nomad status and the route under review is a genuine activity-based resident card. The caution is instead that no current official source confirms a workable first-time registration and residence sequence for an ordinary foreign-client software engineer.
settlement_track.summary: An approved independent-activity resident card creates lawful residence and can support ordinary naturalization eligibility after seven years without a mandatory status switch. The track remains weak because current official filing instructions conflict over whether activity registration or residence must come first, and foreign-client software work is not expressly addressed.
settlement_track.notes: The 2006 decree provides a legal sequence under which a professional-card holder requests residence within 90 days, but current agency checklists do not confirm that this sequence is operational for the applicant profile. The ten-year card and citizenship are discretionary.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Independent activity is legally recognized without a local employer, but no official source confirms that software services performed solely for foreign clients qualify or establishes a consistent first-time registration sequence. Confirm with the competent wilaya, police service, CNRC or applicable professional organization, tax office, and CASNOS before applying.

data.notes: This unresolved-field pass reviewed more than 15 directly relevant URLs and added multiple official sources absent from the previous set, including the professional-card decree and current Interior, Commerce, Labour, CASNOS, ONS, and ILOSTAT materials. The salary median and maximum remain null for precise publication-based reasons. Algeria remains manual-review only because the independent-activity residence route exists in law but is not operationally confirmed for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

data.selection_summary: Andorra has an active, dedicated digital-nomad residence authorization that an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer can request without an Andorran employer or local company. It is genuine renewable residence, not visitor status, and can support the ordinary naturalization track if the applicant actually maintains principal and permanent residence; however, citizenship normally requires 20 years, integration, five recent years of effective residence, and loss of other nationality. The route is also quota-limited and requires prior approval from the Ministry of Economy, private insurance, housing, and annual means exceeding 300% of the annual minimum wage.

visa_application.title: D.3. Residència per a nòmada digital
visa_application.notes: This is the official residence-procedure page. The residence application is currently appointment-based rather than fully online, costs EUR 224.61, and has a published maximum decision period of two months. Before filing it, the applicant must obtain the Ministry of Economy's digital-nomad qualification; that preliminary online procedure is available year-round, costs EUR 0, and has a 15-business-day maximum decision period.

best_routes.route_name: Digital-nomad residence authorization (D.3)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of EUR 4,706.01 per month using 1 EUR = USD 1.1392. The controlling requirement is annual resources exceeding 300% of the annual Andorran minimum wage, not a USD amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: More than EUR 56,472.12 annually for the principal applicant, equivalent to more than EUR 4,706.01 monthly; add EUR 18,824.04 annually for each dependent
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Calculated from the official 300% formula and the minimum wage of EUR 1,568.67 per month effective 1 July 2026. Because the rule says resources must exceed 300%, equality may not be sufficient.

income_requirement_display.value: > EUR 56,472.12/year (> EUR 4,706.01/month), plus EUR 18,824.04/year per dependent
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR annual formula based on the current minimum wage
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Principal applicant: more than 300% of the annual minimum wage; each dependent: add 100% of the annual minimum wage
income_requirement_display.notes: USD figure is approximate. The official checklist assesses annual means and may request additional evidence.

income_proof_months.notes: The test is annual and the checklist identifies the previous year's income-tax return and bank certificates as examples. It does not publish a fixed bank-statement lookback period, so 12 reflects the annual assessment rather than a confirmed requirement for 12 monthly statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain a favorable Ministry of Economy resolution by explaining how the work is location-independent and which telecommunications and technology are used.
Fit within the regulatory immigration quota; the official procedure remains active year-round, but the page does not display the number of places currently unallocated.
Maintain principal and effective residence in Andorra for at least 90 days per calendar year.
Show housing in Andorra, passport, civil-status evidence, criminal-record certificates from relevant countries, apostilles/legalization where applicable, and complete the immigration medical review.
Maintain private coverage valid in Andorra for illness and incapacity for the applicant and covered dependants throughout the authorization.
Show annual economic means exceeding 300% of the annual minimum wage for the principal applicant, plus 100% per dependant.
Register with the relevant parish commune after approval.
For renewals, the government's 2026 newcomer guide states that Catalan A1 is required at the first renewal and A2 at the second renewal.

initial_validity.value: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: This is a residence authorization, not a tourist or visitor permission.

extension_rules.value: First renewal: 2 years; second renewal: 3 years; subsequent renewals: 10 years, subject to continuing eligibility and any treaty-specific exception
extension_rules.notes: The current newcomer guide also identifies Catalan A1 at the first renewal and A2 at the second.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval directly grants an Andorran residence authorization and residence card. No local employer or prior tourist-to-resident conversion is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The procedure is two-stage: Ministry of Economy qualification followed by the immigration residence application.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No separately named permanent-residence grant was identified for this route. The authorization instead becomes renewable for 10-year periods after the initial 2+2+3-year sequence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Andorran nationality rules focus on principal and permanent residence as a factual residence history rather than requiring a separately documented PR stage.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization is available after 20 years of principal and permanent residence, which may now be accumulated through interrupted or uninterrupted periods, provided the applicant proves integration and has had principal and effective residence during at least the five years immediately before applying.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route's 90-day annual minimum is enough to maintain the permit but should not be treated as enough for nationality. A citizenship plan requires genuine principal/permanent residence and compliance with the nationality-loss rules.

best_routes.notes: This route is a direct fit for a location-independent software engineer working for a foreign employer or client. Official wording does not require an Andorran customer, Andorran employer, startup, local company, investment, or exceptional achievement. Approval is nevertheless discretionary at the Ministry of Economy qualification stage and subject to quota availability. The applicant should obtain written confirmation of current quota availability before incurring housing and document costs.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence and work as self-employed person (J.1)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general monthly-income threshold is published on the route page; the route is rejected because it requires substantive Andorran activity or professional authorization rather than ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: For the foreign-investment company version, the official page instead requires an Andorran company, more than 34% ownership, management duties, registered active commerce, and normally a EUR 50,000 AFA deposit.

income_requirement_display.value: No general monthly threshold published; company pathway normally requires a EUR 50,000 AFA deposit
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 50,000 deposit for the foreign-investment company case
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an income threshold and exemptions may exist for separately qualified digital-economy businesses.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed income-evidence period was established.

key_requirements.requirement: Exercise a self-employed activity permanently in Andorra and fit within the quota.
Company pathway requires an Andorran company, more than 34% ownership, an administrative/management role, active registered commerce, and normally a EUR 50,000 AFA deposit.
Liberal-profession pathway requires government professional authorization and professional-body registration where applicable.

initial_validity.value: 1 year

extension_rules.value: Renewable three times for 2 years; after 7 years, successive renewals are generally 10 years
extension_rules.notes: Treaty exceptions may apply.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct residence-and-work authorization if the substantive Andorran self-employment conditions are met.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No separate direct PR grant; long-duration renewals begin after seven years.

path_to_citizenship.value: Qualifying principal and permanent residence may contribute to the ordinary 20-year naturalization history.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the route's mismatch with ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for the specified profile because it requires an Andorran business, active commerce, regulated liberal-profession authorization, or equivalent local substance. The dedicated digital-nomad residence is the cleaner route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence for professionals with international projection

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official page requires economic viability and sufficient resources but does not state a simple monthly threshold for this subcategory.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No simple monthly threshold; EUR 47,500 non-interest-bearing AFA deposit for the principal applicant plus EUR 9,500 per dependant
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The deposit is not income.

income_requirement_display.value: Economic viability and sufficient resources, plus EUR 47,500 AFA deposit and EUR 9,500 per dependant
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 47,500 principal deposit + EUR 9,500 per dependant
income_requirement_display.notes: No monthly-income conversion is appropriate.

income_proof_months.notes: Existing activities require prior financial evidence; new activities require three-year projections, but no fixed bank-statement period was found.

key_requirements.requirement: The professional base must be in Andorra, at least 85% of services must be used outside Andorra, and no more than one employee may be hired.
Prove business viability, qualifications or experience, and make the prescribed AFA deposits.
Maintain at least 90 days of principal and effective residence each year.

initial_validity.value: 2 years

extension_rules.value: 2-year first renewal, 3-year second renewal, then generally 10-year renewals

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct residence if all professional-projection and deposit requirements are approved.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No separate direct PR grant was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Could contribute to the 20-year residence history if residence is genuinely principal and permanent.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it imposes Andorran business-base, viability, international-service-percentage, and substantial deposit requirements. It is not the ordinary low-friction foreign-contract route requested by the prompt.

summary.value: Andorra offers a residence authorization for studies, scientific research, training placements, or high-level sports training without a local employer. For study/research, the applicant needs enrollment or research documentation, accommodation, criminal records, insurance covering 100% of medical expenses, and means at least equal to the minimum wage for the relevant period. It is purpose-limited temporary residence, not a degree-based migration or direct PR route and is unnecessary for the applicant because a dedicated digital-nomad residence exists.
summary.notes: No official source inspected confirmed that this education status itself provides a direct PR grant or a superior settlement track.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Andorran tax resident if present for more than 183 days in the calendar year, counting sporadic absences unless foreign tax residence is proved, or if the principal center/base of activities or economic interests is in Andorra. There is also a rebuttable family presumption where the non-separated spouse and minor children are Andorran tax residents.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The immigration permit's 90-day minimum is not the same as the 183-day tax-residence test. Economic-center and treaty rules can create residence even without exceeding 183 physical days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the statutory/top screening rate, not the expected effective rate. A personal allowance and maximum EUR 800 credit produce lower effective tax in the lower bands.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The nomad checklist mandates private illness/incapacity insurance but does not state that every D.3 holder must pay CASS contributions. If the person separately registers an Andorran self-employed activity, CASS generally shows 22% of the applicable contribution base (10% general branch plus 12% retirement), not necessarily 22% of gross income.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly state payment for every digital-nomad resident was established. Private insurance cost depends on the policy. The residence application has a one-time EUR 224.61 fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad-specific exemption, tax holiday, remittance basis, or special inbound rate was found. Tax-resident nomads fall under ordinary IRPF rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign tax credits and treaty relief may still apply case by case.

taxes.caveats: Immigration residence, tax residence, payroll status, and CASS status are separate questions. A foreign employee should review employer permanent-establishment/payroll exposure and the applicable treaty or social-security agreement. A contractor who registers local economic activity may incur CASS, business-registration, IGI/VAT-like, and other obligations that do not automatically apply merely from holding D.3 residence.

taxation_system.value: Resident individuals are subject to Andorran IRPF, including employment and professional/economic-activity income. The statutory rate is 10%, with a EUR 24,000 personal allowance and an effective 5% treatment for the EUR 24,000-EUR 40,000 range through a maximum EUR 800 credit.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in a calendar year or principal center/base of activities or economic interests in Andorra, with a rebuttable family presumption.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide-income taxation for Andorran tax residents, subject to exemptions, deductions, foreign-tax-credit and treaty rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: D.3 requires private health/incapacity coverage. Mandatory CASS treatment depends on whether the remote worker is locally registered or otherwise brought into Andorran social security; registered self-employed persons generally face 22% of a prescribed contribution base, with bases ranging from 25% to 137.5% of the prior-year average salary according to the rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 10% is a top/statutory screening rate. The EUR 24,000 personal allowance and EUR 800 credit mean the simplified bands should not be read as a pure marginal-bracket system in every case.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Personal allowance generally up to EUR 24,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: General taxable base, subject to personal circumstances and statutory computation
tax_brackets.notes: Shown as a screening simplification of the official personal allowance, not a universal gross-income exemption for every income category.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Equivalent/effective rate through a maximum EUR 800 tax credit for qualifying income
tax_brackets.notes: Not necessarily a standalone marginal bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Above EUR 40,000 after applicable reductions and credits
tax_brackets.notes: Actual effective tax depends on deductions, income classification and credits.

taxation_system.notes: Official sources establish the residence tests and IRPF rate. CASS liability for a foreign employee or contractor holding D.3 requires individualized classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special nomad tax regime was identified. A D.3 holder who becomes tax resident should plan on ordinary Andorran IRPF with a 10% statutory/top rate, personal allowance and credit; private health/incapacity insurance is mandatory, while CASS depends on employment and local-registration structure.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: digital-nomad resident under ordinary IRPF rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% statutory/top screening PIT rate; lower effective tax may result from the EUR 24,000 allowance and EUR 800 credit
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days, principal economic-activity/interest center, or applicable family/treaty analysis; the D.3 permit's 90-day minimum is not itself the tax threshold.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Andorran tax residents generally report worldwide income, with foreign-tax-credit and treaty analysis required. A person who is not Andorran tax resident may still face tax or business exposure for Andorran-source activity.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Private illness/incapacity insurance is expressly mandatory for D.3. CASS and payroll obligations depend on whether the person remains a foreign employee, is covered by an agreement, or registers an Andorran self-employed activity.

fixed_payments.status: Partially confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed CASS payment was confirmed for every D.3 holder. Locally registered self-employed persons generally contribute 22% of the applicable statutory base.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: EUR 0 for the preliminary Ministry of Economy qualification and EUR 224.61 for the D.3 residence application; renewal fees were not established from the pages inspected.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Mandatory private insurance has no government-published fixed premium. No nomad-specific flat monthly tax was found.
fixed_payments.notes: Do not interpret unconfirmed amounts as zero.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying 90-183 days may meet immigration residence but does not automatically avoid Andorran tax residence if the principal center of economic interests is in Andorra. Treaty and foreign-residence evidence remain important.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary IRPF applies, with 10% as the top/statutory screening rate. Foreign employment, employer payroll/permanent-establishment exposure and tax-credit relief require contract-specific advice.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local registration may trigger CASS at 22% of a prescribed base, business registration and possible indirect-tax obligations in addition to IRPF.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Immigration requirements are clear; the exact CASS treatment of a particular foreign employment or independent-contractor arrangement needs filing-level advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Residence is granted directly on approval; the official maximum decision period is two months after a complete residence filing, following the preliminary Ministry qualification.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No separate permanent-residence milestone was identified. The D.3 authorization renews for increasingly long periods, and nationality law instead measures principal and permanent residence history.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: There is no confirmed separate PR-to-citizenship stage. Ordinary naturalization is based on 20 years of qualifying residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: A 10-year route exists for people with the specified Andorran schooling history, which does not fit the adult applicant described.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official nationality page does not publish a typical or maximum processing time. No reliable current official service standard was found after focused searching.

key_conditions.value: Twenty years of principal and permanent residence, which may be accumulated through interrupted or uninterrupted periods; at least the five years immediately before applying must be principal and effective residence. The applicant must prove integration, satisfy criminal/public-order conditions, and comply with Andorra's nationality-loss rules, including proving loss of other nationality within the prescribed five-year period where applicable.
key_conditions.notes: Maintaining D.3 with only 90 days a year should not be assumed to satisfy principal/permanent-residence requirements.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The current official page requires five uninterrupted years of principal and permanent residence, which may occur before or after celebrating the marriage. It is not simply five years of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to an Andorran citizen can support the marriage-naturalization route, but the decisive residence period may be accumulated before or after marriage. An existing marriage to another migrant does not shorten naturalization, although the spouse may be included or seek family-related residence where eligible.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The current official rule differs from older material that reported three years.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must remain cohabiting with the Andorran spouse until the acquisition right is decided, prove integration, meet criminal-record and public-order requirements, and satisfy nationality-loss rules. Breakdown of cohabitation before the decision supports refusal and closure of the file; false documents or a sham relationship would create serious immigration and criminal risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Citizenship remains discretionary on public-order or national-interest grounds.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Andorra is not unconditional jus soli. Citizenship applies through an Andorran parent, qualifying Andorra-born/resident-parent rules, statelessness/foundling safeguards, or the ten-year parental residence rule, sometimes provisionally pending confirmation.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically merely because the child is born in Andorra. Citizenship applies if at least one parent has had principal and permanent Andorran residence for the preceding ten years; if that period is incomplete, provisional nationality can be attributed and later confirmed under the statutory residence conditions. Stateless children and foundlings have separate safeguards.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for two newly arrived migrant parents; conditional cases are described here.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Andorra is Andorran if at least one parent is Andorran. For a child born abroad, descent is more restricted: the Andorran parent must meet one of the official birth/descent or ten-year-residence links stated by the government.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The local-citizen-parent boolean refers to a child born in Andorra.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having an Andorran citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. It may be relevant to family unity or residence administration, but no automatic shortened citizenship period for a migrant father was established from the nationality sources inspected.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Individual family-residence rights should be verified with Immigration.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is Andorran, the child born in Andorra is Andorran, but the migrant father still needs his own lawful residence and must qualify independently for nationality, including through marriage if applicable. If both parents are recent migrants, the child's birth normally creates no immediate citizenship or automatic status for the father.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No automatic father-to-citizen-child derivation was found.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 50 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. The index separately displays a mobility score of 159.

passport.notes: These figures use Passport Index rather than Henley because it supplies the requested visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA and visa-required breakdown on one current country page.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable inside an international remote-work team, but it is not an official language and should not be relied upon for government procedures or long-term integration. Spanish is widely used alongside Catalan in daily life, while Catalan is legally and practically important; current renewal guidance requires Catalan A1 and then A2.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No reliable official source quantified English proficiency specifically, so practicality is stated cautiously.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or generally documented service languages. They may be useful within particular communities or online work but are not a realistic substitute for Catalan or widely used Spanish in administration and everyday integration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No current official study located provides separate Russian- or Ukrainian-proficiency rates; this conclusion is based on their absence from the principal official-language/use data.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the EUR 2,724.35 average salary reported for February 2026.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the EUR 2,165.76 February 2026 median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the statutory minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of February 2026 mean salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of February 2026 median salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable national maximum salary or upper distribution endpoint was published in the inspected sources; a maximum would not be economically meaningful without a defined percentile.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum for the ordinary legal working schedule, effective 1 July 2026; EUR 9.05 per hour.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean salary declared to CASS for February 2026. Separately, the official contribution benchmark for 2026 is EUR 2,672.52 based on the prior year's average.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median for February 2026; the January-February average median was EUR 2,180.21.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum or reliable upper salary boundary found.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly gross salary declared to CASS; minimum field is the statutory minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: February 2026 for mean/median; minimum wage effective 1 July 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The current mean and median are reported by a reputable Andorran newspaper explicitly citing the Department of Statistics; the minimum wage and annual CASS benchmark are official. USD conversions use 1 EUR = USD 1.1392 and are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: Housing is the main affordability constraint. The IMF's 2026 assessment says high housing prices discourage foreign workers and identifies housing-market bottlenecks as a key priority; applicants should secure qualifying accommodation before relying on the residence route.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No single general cost-of-living index was used because housing availability and household composition dominate the practical result.
