settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: D.3 can be maintained with only 90 days of effective residence per year, but citizenship requires principal and permanent residence for 20 years and at least five recent years of principal and effective residence. Part-time permit maintenance must not be confused with a qualifying nationality history.
settlement_track.summary: D.3 is renewable legal residence for ordinary location-independent work and does not require conversion to an employer-sponsored or investment status. It can support naturalization, but only through an exceptionally long 20-year principal/permanent-residence history, integration, recent effective residence and nationality-loss compliance.
settlement_track.notes: The classification is strong because the exact selected route is residence-oriented, indefinitely renewable and compatible with the statutory naturalization residence history—not because citizenship is quick or easy.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Official rules expressly cover work that does not require a specific geographic location and uses telecommunications and technology. They allow employee or self-employed typologies and do not require an Andorran employer, customer, company, investment or elite-achievement test. The foreign contract and technical explanation should be used to prove the activity at the Ministry qualification stage.

data.notes: This audit corrects important weaknesses in the previous record: it confirms the 300%-of-minimum-wage threshold, current EUR 224.61 residence fee and two-month service standard; updates marriage citizenship from older three-year information to the current five-year residence rule; captures the revised interrupted-residence naturalization rule; replaces stale salary and minimum-wage figures; and distinguishes D.3 private-insurance requirements from unconfirmed automatic CASS liability. Remaining nulls are limited to facts not published reliably, principally a separate PR milestone, nationality processing time, universal nomad CASS amount, private-insurance premium, and maximum salary.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Renewable D.3 digital-nomad residence (2 + 2 + 3 years, then ten-year renewals)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The nomad authorization supports continued residence through ten-year renewals after the initial seven years, but a separate indefinite permanent-residence status was not established by the official materials.
requirements: Keep satisfying nomad qualification, annual effective-residence, financial-means, accommodation and insurance conditions.
reviewed_route_names: Digital-nomad residence authorization (D.3)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The official D.3 application page expressly states the renewal sequence. A ten-year renewable permit must not be labelled an indefinite PR grant. This is uncertainty about the PR label, not evidence that the holder must leave after a short nomad stay.

data.selection_summary: Estonia has an active Digital Nomad Visa that independently fits ordinary work for a foreign employer or mostly foreign clients. However, it is a visa for temporary stay—normally up to one year—not a residence permit. Estonian law distinguishes visa-based temporary stay from residence based on a residence permit, and no official source confirms that Digital Nomad Visa time counts toward long-term residence or the eight-year naturalisation period. The applicant would need to qualify separately for a residence permit, such as study, local employment, genuine Estonian enterprise or family residence, so Estonia is not a citizenship-path match for the stated profile.

visa_application.title: Estonian visa pre-application form
visa_application.notes: The official online system prepares the long-stay D-visa application, but filing is not fully online: the applicant normally submits the signed application and biometrics in person at an Estonian representation handling visa applications, or at a Police and Border Guard Board service point when legally present in Estonia.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Visa / visa for teleworking

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,960 using the ECB displayed rate of EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. Exchange rates fluctuate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 132 per day (EUR 3,960 per month)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Current Ministry of Foreign Affairs long-stay-visa table. An e-Residency promotional page still displays EUR 4,500 net/month; the current ministry application instructions are used as the filing threshold, but applicants should recheck immediately before applying.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,960/month (about USD 4,511)
income_requirement_display.notes: Current official D-visa filing page controls over the older/conflicting EUR 4,500 promotional figure.

income_proof_months.notes: The teleworking-specific regulation requires proof of lawful income during the six preceding months. The general D-visa checklist separately requests evidence for the three months immediately preceding filing; applicants should provide the longer six-month record.

key_requirements.requirement: Work must be location-independent and performed using telecommunications technology.

Continue employment for a foreign-registered employer, business through a foreign company in which the applicant has a holding, or freelance services mainly for customers whose business is outside Estonia.
Provide contracts and documents proving the foreign employment, company or customer relationships.
Provide six months of lawful-income evidence showing amount, regularity and sources, plus education and employment history.
Provide evidence that the applicant or relevant foreign company has no tax arrears in its country of residence or registration.
Valid travel document, application form, photograph, travel medical insurance, proof of means, purpose documents, travel booking, biometrics and visa fee.
The application is assessed under ordinary visa admissibility and security rules; meeting the income threshold does not guarantee approval.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The teleworking permission may be issued as a short-stay or long-stay visa. The government DNV information describes the long-stay option as temporary residence in Estonia for up to one year; legally it remains temporary stay, not a temporary residence permit.

extension_rules.value: No dedicated settlement-oriented renewal was confirmed. General rules allow consecutive long-stay visas, but total stay on two consecutive D visas may not exceed 548 days within 730 consecutive days.
extension_rules.notes: A further visa is discretionary and does not convert the holder into a resident under the residence-permit system.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic conversion. The holder must independently qualify and apply for a temporary residence permit on another statutory basis, such as qualifying study, local employment, genuine enterprise or family settlement.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: E-Residency also does not supply a residence basis.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The nomad visa does not count toward permanent residence. A separately approved entrepreneur/sole-proprietor residence permit can start a five-year long-term residence period, but requires a genuine business case and capital rather than only an existing foreign employment contract.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A legal visa holder may submit the enterprise residence application in Estonia; this is not an automatic nomad conversion. Five years starts with qualifying residence, excluding nomad-visa time. Continued foreign-client self-employment needs to satisfy the enterprise assessment; the unchanged employee profile is not confirmed. The capital requirement is shown explicitly rather than assumed acceptable.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path from the DNV. Naturalisation requires a long-term residence permit or permanent right of residence and at least eight years in Estonia on residence permits or rights of residence, including at least five years on a permanent basis, plus language, civic-knowledge, income, registration and loyalty requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant must first switch to and maintain an independently qualifying residence status.

best_routes.notes: This is a strong temporary-living fit for a foreign-contract software engineer but fails the research prompt's settlement requirement. The decisive distinction is that Estonian law defines visa presence as temporary stay without a residence permit.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence permit for enterprise as a sole proprietor or company participant

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No simple fixed monthly-income figure applies. The route uses statutory legal-income rules in addition to investment and substantive-business requirements.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No simple monthly threshold; a sole proprietor normally must invest at least EUR 16,000 in Estonia and meet separate legal-income rules
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Capital investment is not treated as monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 16,000 capital investment for a sole proprietor, plus legal-income and substantive-business tests
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least EUR 16,000 invested in Estonia for a sole proprietor; separate legal-income formula applies
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an entrepreneur route, not a simple freelancer residence permit for continuing ordinary foreign-client work.

income_proof_months.notes: The legal-income regulation evaluates income over the six months preceding the residence-permit application; exact calculation should be confirmed for the filing date.

key_requirements.requirement: Activities and settlement in Estonia must significantly contribute to development of the Estonian economy.
A sole proprietor normally must invest at least EUR 16,000 in Estonia.
Submit a business plan allowing authorities to assess whether the enterprise satisfies the statutory purpose.
Meet general residence-permit conditions, including justified purpose, actual residence in Estonia, sufficient legal income and medical-expense insurance.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence permits may generally be issued for up to 5 years; the individual term is discretionary and tied to the qualifying enterprise.

extension_rules.value: Extension requires continued compliance with the enterprise purpose, activity, income and other residence-permit requirements.
extension_rules.notes: Failure to demonstrate real or planned business activity and economic contribution can result in refusal or revocation.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence permit if the enterprise application is approved.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Qualifying residence-permit time can lead to a long-term resident permit after at least five years if income, insurance, residence registration, integration and absence conditions are met.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential general naturalisation path after at least eight years of qualifying residence, but only while the applicant continues to qualify under a genuine residence basis.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for the stated profile because it requires investment, an Estonian enterprise and a significant-contribution/business-substance assessment. An ordinary foreign-client contract alone is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold because e-Residency is not an immigration status.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not applicable.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—digital identity only
income_requirement_display.notes: E-Residency does not grant entry, residence or citizenship rights.

income_proof_months.notes: Not an immigration route.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must have a legitimate purpose and pass identity, background and eligibility checks.
The digital ID is not a travel document, visa or residence permit.

initial_validity.value: Digital-identity validity only; no permission to stay

extension_rules.value: Renewing e-Residency does not create immigration residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None; a separate visa or residence permit is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None.

path_to_citizenship.value: None.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because e-Residency provides remote access to digital services and possible company administration, not physical residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Salary criteria vary by employment category and exemptions; no single amount is used here.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Usually tied to the current Estonian average wage or category-specific rules
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Must be verified for the exact occupation and permit category.

income_requirement_display.value: Category-specific local salary criterion
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Usually at least the applicable Estonian average wage unless an exemption applies
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a local-employment route.

income_proof_months.notes: Not established as a uniform requirement across employment categories.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying employment in Estonia and employer participation are required.
Many categories require Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund approval, a salary criterion and compliance with the immigration quota unless exempt.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence permit, generally up to 5 years depending on the employment basis

extension_rules.value: Requires continued qualifying employment and compliance with the applicable conditions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence permit for approved local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Can contribute to the five-year long-term-residence period if all conditions are maintained.

path_to_citizenship.value: Can form part of the general eight-year naturalisation residence period.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the selected applicant intends to retain a foreign contract and apply without an Estonian employer, while this route depends on qualifying local employment.

summary.value: A third-country national admitted to a qualifying, generally full-time programme at an accredited Estonian educational institution can obtain a temporary residence permit for study without a local employer. The institution must provide the required invitation, and the permit normally lasts through the nominal or estimated study period. This is a genuine temporary residence basis, but it requires actual study and is not a degree-only or ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.
summary.notes: Employment is allowed only if it does not interfere with studies. Study admission and compliance, not merely possessing an existing software-engineering degree, create eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Estonian tax resident if their place of residence is in Estonia or they stay in Estonia for at least 183 days during any 12 consecutive calendar months. When the 183-day test is met, residency is generally recorded from the first arrival day in that period. A tax treaty can override domestic dual-residence results.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A person establishing a permanent or primary home in Estonia can become resident without waiting 183 days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Flat 2026 personal income-tax rate. The EUR 700 monthly/EUR 8,400 annual basic exemption can lower the effective rate, subject to eligibility and filing mechanics.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Social tax is 33% on employment or business income. Payroll may also involve employee unemployment insurance of 1.6%, employer unemployment insurance of 0.8%, and funded-pension contributions of 2%, 4% or 6% where applicable. Cross-border social-security coverage and an A1 or treaty position may change the result.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the 2026 minimum monthly social-tax liability of EUR 292.38. This is relevant when the Estonian minimum social-tax obligation applies; the DNV by itself does not automatically make every holder an Estonian self-employed person.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special Digital Nomad Visa personal-income-tax exemption was found. Estonian tax residents generally declare worldwide income. Estonia separately defers company-level corporate income tax until profits are distributed, but that company regime does not exempt the individual's salary or business income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: E-Residency and ownership of an Estonian company do not by themselves determine personal tax residence.

taxes.caveats: Remote-work taxation depends on physical work location, whether the relationship is employment or independent business, the foreign payer's Estonian payroll obligations, permanent-establishment issues, applicable tax treaty, and social-security coordination. Professional cross-border advice is appropriate before working from Estonia.

taxation_system.value: Flat personal income tax with a basic exemption; Estonian residents are generally taxed on worldwide income, with treaty or foreign-tax-credit relief. Employment and business income may also bear social contributions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Place of residence in Estonia or at least 183 days in any consecutive 12-month period, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for Estonian tax residents; Estonia-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No DNV-specific exemption. Estonian companies generally incur corporate income tax when profits are distributed rather than when earned.
taxation_system.social_security: Social tax is generally 33%. The 2026 minimum monthly social-tax base is EUR 886, producing EUR 292.38 minimum liability where applicable. Self-employed advance social-tax payments are generally EUR 877.14 per quarter, subject to reductions and exemptions. Employee/employer unemployment insurance and funded-pension contributions may also apply.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Personal income tax is not progressive in 2026. The EUR 700 monthly basic exemption changes the effective rate but not the statutory 22% rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable personal income after applicable deductions; 2026 basic exemption is EUR 700/month or EUR 8,400/year
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment, business and most other taxable personal income
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate monthly exemption using the cited ECB conversion rate, not an income bracket or tax-free threshold available in every cross-border circumstance.

taxation_system.notes: The displayed 22% is the flat statutory rate, not an expected effective rate. The displayed 33% social tax is likewise not necessarily borne economically by the individual in every employment structure.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The DNV has no confirmed special tax holiday. A holder who becomes Estonian tax resident generally declares worldwide income, including foreign salary or service income, and the flat 22% personal rate applies subject to the basic exemption, treaties and foreign-tax relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary cross-border employment or business income; no special DNV category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 22% flat personal income tax before the effect of the basic exemption, deductions and treaty relief
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Estonian home/place of residence or at least 183 days during 12 consecutive months, subject to tax-treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally declare worldwide income; double taxation is addressed through treaties, exemption or credit mechanisms. Non-residents generally pay Estonian tax only on Estonia-source income, but work physically performed in Estonia requires fact-specific analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found in current official sources.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The foreign-employer, Estonian-payroll and social-security result is fact-specific. When Estonian social tax applies it is 33%; employee unemployment insurance is 1.6%, employer unemployment insurance is 0.8%, and funded-pension contributions may apply. Foreign coverage documentation or international coordination can alter liability.

fixed_payments.status: Conditional, not imposed solely by holding the DNV
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: If registered or treated as an Estonian self-employed person, 2026 advance social tax is generally EUR 877.14 per quarter (EUR 292.38 monthly equivalent), subject to exemptions, reductions and annual reconciliation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Long-stay D-visa application fee: EUR 120 for an adult.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration generally arises when Estonia-place taxable supply exceeds EUR 40,000 from the beginning of the calendar year. Estonia's standard VAT rate is 24%. Applicability to foreign-client services depends on place-of-supply rules.
fixed_payments.notes: Travel medical insurance is required but is market-priced, so no reliable fixed monthly amount is stated.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if the person establishes a permanent or primary home in Estonia. If genuinely non-resident, Estonia generally taxes Estonia-source income only, but work physically performed in Estonia and the relevant treaty still need review.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Normally declares worldwide foreign salary or service income in Estonia and is screened at the 22% flat personal rate, with relief for qualifying foreign tax and application of the relevant treaty.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A registered self-employed person generally pays 22% income tax on taxable business income and 33% social tax, makes quarterly social-tax advances, and may need VAT registration once relevant Estonia-place supply exceeds EUR 40,000.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The immigration visa and tax residence tests are separate. Staying for the DNV's full duration makes tax-residence review especially important.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The DNV never automatically becomes temporary residence; a separate qualifying residence-permit application is required, so no fixed transition time exists.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General minimum for a long-term resident permit after qualifying residence on residence permits. Absence, integration, income, insurance and other conditions apply; DNV time is not included on the evidence found.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Earliest arithmetic under the general eight-year residence rule if long-term residence is obtained after five qualifying years. Naturalisation also requires at least five years of permanent residence in the statutory sense and all other conditions; this is not guaranteed.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Eight years from the start of qualifying residence on a residence permit/right of residence, not from arrival on the DNV. Because the DNV holder must first switch, total calendar time from initial DNV arrival would normally be longer or indeterminate.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official guidance says the Police and Border Guard Board forwards a compliant application to the Government within six months, but a reliable current end-to-end typical processing time was not established; six months should not be presented as the complete processing time.

key_conditions.value: Long-term residence permit or permanent right of residence; eight years of qualifying residence, including five on a permanent basis; Estonian language proficiency generally at B1; Constitution and Citizenship Act examination; stable legal income; registered Estonian residence; loyalty; and ordinarily release from previous citizenship. Long-term residence generally requires five years on residence permits, legal income, health insurance, registered residence, integration and compliance with absence limits.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation is not automatic after the minimum period.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: There is no general citizenship shortcut based solely on years married to an Estonian citizen. A genuine spouse can provide a temporary family-residence basis, but the applicant remains subject to the ordinary eight-year qualifying-residence naturalisation rule.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage or registered partnership to an Estonian citizen, or to a qualifying resident alien, may support an application for a temporary residence permit to settle with the spouse or partner. Marriage does not itself grant permanent residence or citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: If the Estonian spouse and applicant settle in Estonia together, the statutory prior-residence requirement for the Estonian spouse is not applied.

requirements_and_risks.value: Authorities may examine whether the family relationship and purpose of settlement are genuine and whether general residence-permit conditions are met. The permit remains linked to the qualifying family basis, although limited humanitarian or disproportionate-hardship protections may apply after breakdown. False documents, sham marriage or misleading information can cause refusal, revocation and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Family-residence filing fees and location-specific procedures should be rechecked before application.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Estonia primarily grants citizenship by descent. Birth in Estonia alone is insufficient, but there are foundling and anti-statelessness rules for qualifying children.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child does not ordinarily become Estonian merely by being born in Estonia to two foreign migrants. A child born in Estonia, or taking up permanent residence immediately after birth, can receive citizenship from birth by naturalisation where the parents or single parent are not recognised as citizens by any state and have lawfully resided in Estonia for at least five years by the birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is a narrow anti-statelessness rule, not general jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child acquires Estonian citizenship by birth if at least one parent is an Estonian citizen at the time of birth, including where the Estonian father dies before the birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant parent's sex does not change the child's citizenship-by-descent rule.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on a migrant father. Estonia's ordinary close-relative residence provision does not create a general parent-of-minor-citizen permit; family-life circumstances may still be relevant in an individual immigration decision. A migrant parent's own citizenship remains subject to naturalisation rules.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Special humanitarian or family-life cases require individual legal assessment.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence. If the other parent is Estonian, the child is Estonian by descent, but the father's clearest ordinary family-residence route is generally through a genuine marriage or registered partnership where applicable, not simply through paternity of a minor citizen.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not assume that birth of a citizen child cures an expiring visa or creates an independent settlement right.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank, not Henley rank. A separate 2026 Henley-derived secondary table reports rank 8, illustrating that index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category; it excludes its separately reported visa-on-arrival and eTA categories.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from Passport Index's 45 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 172 and world reach of 86%. Its figures should not be mixed with Henley's combined visa-free/visa-on-arrival score of 181.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Generally practical in Tallinn and the technology/international-business environment, but Estonian is the sole official language and is needed for many public-facing or regulated contexts. Long-term naturalisation normally requires B1 Estonian, so English-only living is not a complete settlement strategy.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The EF English Proficiency Index is a non-governmental, self-selected-adult assessment and is used only as a practical indicator, not a guarantee that every service is available in English.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is widely encountered in parts of Estonia and established Russian-speaking communities, especially in Tallinn and Ida-Viru County, but it has no nationwide official status. Ukrainian community and support services exist, but Ukrainian cannot be assumed for routine administration. Estonian remains necessary for official integration and citizenship.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Practical availability varies substantially by city, institution and provider.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official EUR 2,135 gross monthly average for Q1 2026 at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official EUR 1,753 gross monthly median for Q1 2026.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory gross minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate gross monthly national average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate gross monthly national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary was published. The official release provides sector averages, not an individual maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 946 gross/month for full-time work from 1 April 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official Statistics Estonia register-based wage measure.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official national median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No reliable national maximum was published. Information and communication had the highest listed sector average at EUR 3,821, but that is not a maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly wages and salaries based on employment-register and tax-declaration data; minimum is the statutory full-time minimum
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 for average and median; minimum effective 2026-04-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: USD values are screening conversions, not payroll quotations. The Digital Nomad Visa threshold of EUR 3,960/month is substantially above the national average and median gross wage.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No sufficiently current official national cost-of-living budget or comparable household-cost figure was established after focused review; a wage figure is not used as a proxy for living costs.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Digital Nomad Visa is an up-to-one-year visa for temporary stay. It is not a temporary residence permit, and official sources do not confirm that its time counts toward the five-year long-term-residence or eight-year naturalisation periods.
settlement_track.summary: Estonia works well for temporary foreign-contract remote work, but the exact DNV route does not provide a settlement clock. Citizenship planning requires switching to and independently maintaining another qualifying residence permit.
settlement_track.notes: The general eight-year naturalisation period starts from qualifying residence on a residence permit/right of residence, not from visa-based temporary stay.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The DNV expressly covers a foreign employer, a foreign company owned by the applicant, or freelance services mainly to foreign customers. This true value describes temporary remote-work fit only; it does not make the route a citizenship-path match.

data.notes: The previous Estonia record correctly identified the DNV as temporary-only, but contained conflicting selection flags and an outdated EUR 4,500 threshold. This audit applies the prompt's citizenship-oriented rule, uses the current Ministry of Foreign Affairs EUR 3,960 filing threshold, confirms the specific six-month income-history rule, fills current 2026 tax and wage data, and preserves cautious nulls where no reliable figure was established.

reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad Visa / visa for teleworking
digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Temporary residence permit for enterprise as a sole proprietor, followed by long-term residence
requirements: Meet the independent enterprise permit criteria, including commercial registration and a business plan.
The official self-employed route specifies EUR 16,000 invested capital for a sole proprietor.
Maintain qualifying residence, resources and insurance; meet the applicable Estonian-language requirement for long-term residence.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The nomad visa does not count toward permanent residence. A separately approved entrepreneur/sole-proprietor residence permit can start a five-year long-term residence period, but requires a genuine business case and capital rather than only an existing foreign employment contract.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: A legal visa holder may submit the enterprise residence application in Estonia; this is not an automatic nomad conversion. Five years starts with qualifying residence, excluding nomad-visa time. Continued foreign-client self-employment needs to satisfy the enterprise assessment; the unchanged employee profile is not confirmed. The capital requirement is shown explicitly rather than assumed acceptable.

data.selection_summary: Angola has no dedicated digital-nomad visa. Its general Visa for Establishing Residence can be requested without a local employer, permits remunerated activity, and leads to renewable temporary residence, but no official source expressly confirms that ordinary foreign-client remote work is an accepted basis or authorized independent activity. Filing-level confirmation from an Angolan mission and SME is therefore essential. The statutory path is approximately 10 years of temporary residence to permanent residence, followed by 10 years from permanent residence to ordinary naturalization.

visa_application.title: SME Serviço de Migração e Estrangeiros transactional portal
visa_application.notes: The SME portal supports account registration and immigration transactions. The residence-establishment visa is issued through an Angolan diplomatic mission or consular post; no public direct application form was available without portal registration.

best_routes.route_name: Visto para Fixação de Residência → Autorização de Residência Temporária

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: National legislation requires means of subsistence but publishes no monthly USD minimum. A Lisbon consular checklist states 200.00 per day without identifying the currency in that line; because this mission-specific figure is ambiguous, no USD conversion is inferred.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No national AOA threshold or formula is published. The regulation recognizes specified sources or guarantees as evidence, while the Lisbon checklist gives an unlabelled 200.00-per-day figure; applicants must confirm the applicable mission's standard.

income_requirement_display.value: Proof of means of subsistence and accommodation required; no unambiguous national numerical threshold published.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Documented means of subsistence; mission-specific evidence requirements
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign contract may evidence means, but official sources do not confirm that it alone qualifies or authorizes independent foreign-client work.

income_proof_months.notes: The law, regulation, and Lisbon residence-visa checklist require proof of means but prescribe no retrospective bank-statement or income-history period measured in months.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through an Angolan diplomatic mission or consular post for a multiple-entry Visa for Establishing Residence.
Prove means of subsistence and accommodation.
Provide criminal-record and medical certificates, passport documentation, photographs, vaccination evidence, and mission-specific legalized documents.
After entry, apply to SME for temporary residence and provide local residence, criminal-record, fee, tax, and social-security documentation where applicable.
Confirm that the residence title authorizes ordinary independent foreign-client remote work; unauthorized independent activity can trigger penalties.

initial_validity.value: Residence-establishment visa: 90 days; resulting temporary residence authorization: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Article 57 of the controlling 2019 law states 90 days. Some consular guidance describes different procedural periods, so the issuing mission should confirm its current entry instructions.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence is renewable for successive two-year periods, subject to continued means, accommodation, and tax and social-security compliance.
extension_rules.notes: The regulation allows renewal filing from 90 to 30 days before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The residence-visa holder applies to SME for a two-year temporary residence authorization after entry.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The law provides a 30-day decision target for a complete residence application.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Permanent residence is available after 10 consecutive years holding temporary residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence has no substantive expiry, although its card is renewed every five years; excessive absence can jeopardize status.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization requires 10 years counted from permanent residence, Portuguese and integration examinations, regular means, tax evidence, and other statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Combined with the 10-year temporary-residence requirement for permanent residence, the theoretical minimum is about 20 years before processing. Naturalization is not automatic.

best_routes.notes: This is settlement-oriented rather than visitor-like, but it remains a manual-review route because published sources do not expressly approve ordinary foreign-contract remote work as the immigration basis or authorized independent activity.

rejected_routes.route_name: Angolan work visa for a non-resident foreign worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No independent remote-worker income threshold applies; remuneration is established in the Angola-linked employment contract.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income-qualified independent-route threshold exists. Contractual salary must be stated, but the route is employer-specific.

income_requirement_display.value: No independent income threshold; an Angola-linked employer and employment contract or promise are required.
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because it is an employer-specific, non-settling work visa.

income_proof_months.notes: No retrospective income-proof period applies. The law, 2025 foreign-worker regulation, and official US and Rio mission checklists require a current Angola-linked employment contract or promise and employer documentation, but none prescribes prior salary-slip or bank-statement months.

key_requirements.requirement: Angola-linked employment contract or promise, employer request, qualifications, CV, criminal record, medical certificate, and other employer documents.
The 2025 regulation requires a valid work visa and an employment relationship with an employing entity.
The holder may work only in the activity and for the employer underlying the visa.

initial_validity.value: Up to 365 days
initial_validity.notes: Multiple-entry visa tied to employment.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for equal periods until the employment contract ends, subject to employer tax and social-security compliance.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains employer-dependent.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The statute expressly states that this work visa does not authorize establishment of residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate qualifying residence basis would be necessary.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path
path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary naturalization is tied to permanent residence rather than this employer-specific work visa.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer is mandatory and the visa is expressly non-settling.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourism visa exemption or tourism visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker residence threshold applies. A tourism-visa applicant may need to prove sufficient funds for the visit, but that is not a qualifying income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No AOA remote-work threshold applies to visitor status; documentary requirements vary by mission.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable to a qualifying residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Tourism permission does not authorize work or establish residence.

income_proof_months.notes: The Angolan Embassy in the DRC requires the last six months of authenticated bank statements or the last six salary receipts for its tourism-visa filing. This is mission-specific practice, not a national remote-work threshold and not stated as a requirement of the 98-country tourism exemption.

key_requirements.requirement: Covered visa-exempt nationalities may stay up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year for tourism.
Persons intending work, study, temporary stay, treatment, or residence must obtain the corresponding visa.

initial_validity.value: Up to 30 days per entry and 90 days per year for covered visa-exempt nationalities
initial_validity.notes: Nationality eligibility must be checked.

extension_rules.notes: Tourism visas may have limited visitor extensions under applicable rules, but any extension remains non-qualifying visitor status and does not resolve remote-work authorization.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No general tourism-to-residence conversion confirmed
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The law specifies only limited visa transformations; tourism is not an ordinary remote-work legalization route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time is not qualifying permanent-residence time.

path_to_citizenship.value: No
path_to_citizenship.notes: Tourism time is not the permanent-residence period used for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourism permission is visitor status, prohibits remunerated activity, and supplies no settlement path.

summary.value: A study visa can be obtained with admission or internship confirmation, means, and accommodation without a local employer. It lasts up to one year and may be renewed through the studies, but expressly does not establish residence or permit paid work except a training-related internship. No ordinary skilled-independent or degree-based residence route was identified.
summary.notes: Exceptional residence for nationally relevant scientific or technological activity is discretionary and is not an ordinary degree-based route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally resident if present in Angola for more than 90 days, consecutive or not, during the fiscal year, or if maintaining a habitual residence there on 31 December.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A consolidated IRPS reform is expected from 2027; proposed new residence rules should not be applied to the 2026 tax year without the final promulgated code.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top screening rate, not expected effective tax. Group A employment is progressive up to 25%; relevant Group B/C income may face 6.5% withholding or 25% when not subject to withholding.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Standard self-employed rate on declared remuneration. Expanded coverage is 11%, and a qualifying low-income option is 4%; foreign-system coverage can affect liability.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The self-employed system uses percentage contributions rather than a published universal fixed USD minimum. No separate digital-nomad levy exists.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound individual regime was identified. A consolidated IRPS reform is expected from 2027, subject to final-code and implementation verification.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The future regime is not the governing 2026 system.

taxes.caveats: Foreign-contract income treatment depends on where services are performed and whether the arrangement is employment, professional, or business income. Work performed from Angola can create tax, registration, social-security, and possible foreign-employer permanent-establishment exposure. Professional advice is needed.

taxation_system.value: Mixed schedular and principally source-based system through 2026: employee income is progressive up to 25%; relevant self-employed or business income may face 6.5% withholding or 25% when not withheld.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 90 days in the fiscal year or habitual residence available on 31 December.
taxation_system.income_scope: Principally Angola-source income; classification and the connection of services to Angola determine liability.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Consolidated IRPS reform expected from 2027.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed standard rate 8% of declared remuneration, with 11% expanded and 4% qualifying low-income coverage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% display is a top or screening rate, not an effective rate. Group A uses progressive brackets; Group B/C treatment is generally withholding or a non-withheld rate rather than the same progressive schedule.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Qualifying professional or business payments subject to withholding
tax_brackets.notes: Applied to gross qualifying payments; classification-specific.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable Group B/C income not subject to withholding
tax_brackets.applies_to: Relevant non-withheld professional or business income
tax_brackets.notes: Screening rate; deductions and classification require advice.
Top marginal rate, not effective tax; the 2026 employment exemption threshold is AOA 150,000.

taxation_system.notes: Current 2026 treatment is reasonably supported, but the precise classification of foreign-client remote income and the 2027 transition remain fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad visa or tax category exists. A person working from Angola must be classified under ordinary employment, professional, or business rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated route; ordinary tax classification required
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 25% top/screening rate; 6.5% withholding may apply to qualifying professional payments
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 90 days in the fiscal year or habitual residence on 31 December under current rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Current rules are principally source-based, but services physically performed from Angola may have an Angola nexus even when paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Self-employed registration may trigger 8% contributions; employment classification can trigger payroll obligations. Foreign mandatory-system coverage may alter self-employed liability.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly amount confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based contributions; no universal USD minimum published.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Residence and visa fees are mission- and procedure-specific; no uniform remote-worker fee exists.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business registration, VAT, stamp, or transaction obligations depend on structure and thresholds.
fixed_payments.notes: There is no dedicated nomad category from which a single fixed-payment schedule can be derived.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below the residence-day threshold does not by itself eliminate tax on income treated as Angola-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Potentially taxable under ordinary rules; contract and source classification require local advice.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Tax and INSS registration, percentage social contributions, and business or VAT obligations may apply.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No route-specific concession exists; conclusions depend on ordinary tax classification.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The qualifying residence visa can lead to temporary residence after entry and application; no multi-year prerequisite is stated.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Ten consecutive years of temporary residence are required.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires ten years counted from permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Theoretical statutory minimum before naturalization processing, assuming uninterrupted qualifying status.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality regulation describes procedures but does not publish a reliable typical end-to-end processing time.

key_conditions.value: Continuous qualifying residence, Portuguese and integration examinations, regular means, tax compliance, criminal-record conditions, and compliance with absence rules.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization remains discretionary upon application and is not automatic at the time threshold.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse married to an Angolan citizen for more than five years may acquire nationality by declaration, subject to statutory conditions.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count toward the five-year marriage period; nationality is not automatic and requires the statutory declaration and evidence.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marriage and its duration must be legally documented.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be genuine and legally recognized. Fraud or a marriage entered solely for immigration purposes can cause refusal, residence cancellation, or other consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates the nationality route but does not eliminate documentary and integrity checks.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Angola does not automatically grant nationality to every child of two foreign parents; descent and specified declaration or anti-statelessness provisions govern.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No general automatic citizenship solely from birth in Angola. Statutory exceptions, anti-statelessness rules, or declaration-based acquisition may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' nationality and the child's statutory category must be examined.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of an Angolan mother or father generally obtains Angolan nationality by origin, subject to civil registration and proof of parentage.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Citizenship derives from the Angolan parent rather than the migrant parent's residence status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having an Angolan child does not automatically grant citizenship to a migrant parent. A separate family-residence, marriage, or naturalization basis is required.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Family connection may assist a residence application but is not automatic permanent residence or nationality.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic citizenship through an Angolan child. Any benefit depends on a separate family or spouse-based immigration procedure.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage, custody, dependency, and the relationship with the citizen parent may require proof.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank; dynamic and subject to change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count reported by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required count reported by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined 35 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations; eVisa destinations are treated separately by the index.

passport.notes: Passport mobility values should be rechecked near any travel or citizenship decision.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Limited outside international business and expatriate settings. EF EPI 2025 placed Angola in the very-low-proficiency category; Portuguese is important for housing, government, tax, immigration, and naturalization.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI measures test participants and is not a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official status, and no reliable evidence of broad public-service use was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is an inference from the official-language framework; no nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-proficiency measure was available.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official fourth-quarter 2025 employment-survey catalog does not publish a directly usable current national mean monthly wage aggregate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey catalog does not publish a current national median monthly wage aggregate.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the AOA 100,000 general statutory minimum using the cited historical mid-market rate. This is a legal minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No defensible current official national average wage aggregate was published.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national median wage aggregate was published.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum wage is not a meaningful statutory statistic, and no official upper distribution bound was published.

min_salary_local_currency.value: AOA 100,000 per month generally; AOA 50,000 for microenterprises, startups, and domestic work
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The general AOA 100,000 minimum applied from September 2025, with limited categories and relief provisions.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The official survey catalog does not supply a defensible current national average wage aggregate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The official survey catalog does not supply a national median wage aggregate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: This is not a digital-nomad visa. Acceptance of a foreign-client contract and authorization of independent remote work require confirmation.
settlement_track.summary: The residence-establishment visa can lead to renewable temporary residence, permanent residence after 10 years, and ordinary naturalization after another 10 years from permanent residence. The chain is statutory, but the profile remains uncertain because official sources do not expressly confirm ordinary foreign-contract remote work as the initial basis or authorized activity.
settlement_track.notes: Required status changes are entry visa to temporary residence and later permanent residence. Filing-level immigration and work-authorization review is necessary.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The residence route does not expressly require a local employer and permits remunerated activity, but no official source states that a foreign remote-work contract alone qualifies or that the title authorizes independent foreign-client freelancing.

data.notes: The focused pass inspected more than 15 relevant URLs, including six official URLs absent from the previous source set. It resolved the tourism-visa evidence period as six months for the DRC mission and confirmed that a retrospective income-proof period is inapplicable to the employer-sponsored work visa. Angola remains a manual-review case rather than a confirmed ordinary remote-work citizenship route.

data.selection_summary: Not eligible for this citizenship-oriented remote-worker selection. The government discontinued the Nomad Digital Residence programme on 15 November 2025, and no current replacement for ordinary foreign-contract remote workers was found. Work-permit residence requires local work authorization, while student, visitor, independent-means, and investment routes do not provide a confirmed current remote-work entry-to-settlement path.

visa_application.title: Residency — Department of Immigration
visa_application.notes: This is official general resident-permit information, not an application for a remote-worker route. The former NDR portal is no longer a valid application channel because the programme closed on 15 November 2025.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Historical threshold of USD 50,000 during each programme year. It is not a current application threshold because the programme closed.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 50,000 per year (historical programme threshold)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The former programme stated its threshold in USD rather than XCD.

income_requirement_display.value: Closed — historical threshold was USD 50,000 per year
income_requirement_display.notes: Shown only to document the former programme; new applications are unavailable.

income_proof_months.notes: The legacy form requested proof of income and funds but did not specify a fixed number of statement months in the material inspected.

key_requirements.requirement: Historically required remote employment or self-employment producing income outside Antigua and Barbuda.
Historically prohibited employment or services for citizens, residents, work-permit holders, or businesses operating in Antigua and Barbuda.
Required passport documents, police character record, and proof of income and funds.
No new applications are possible after the programme's 15 November 2025 closure.

initial_validity.value: Historically up to 2 years; no current validity for new applicants
initial_validity.notes: The closure notice describes residency status of up to two years.

extension_rules.value: No new extension or renewal rules confirmed after programme closure
extension_rules.notes: Existing holders were directed to contact Immigration; no successor programme was announced.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None for new applicants; the former programme granted temporary residency status for up to two years
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The programme is closed.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No official NDR-to-permanent-residence conversion was established
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: General resident-permit rules exist, but the official sources do not say that former NDR time automatically qualified.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path; a person would need a separate qualifying lawful-residence basis
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation residence rules do not establish that former NDR time counted.

rejected_routes.notes: The old record treated NDR as current. That is no longer supportable: an official government notice says the programme ended on 15 November 2025. It remains relevant only as a closed legacy route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Local work permit followed by Class A resident permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general income threshold was published; eligibility instead depends on a valid local work permit and lawful residence.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general minimum income amount found.

income_requirement_display.value: No published general income threshold; local work-permit eligibility applies
income_requirement_display.notes: This route does not fit an ordinary foreign-client remote worker.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed income-history period found.

key_requirements.requirement: A valid local work permit is required when applying for the work-based Class A resident permit.
Official guidance calls for four years of uninterrupted lawful residence and at least four consecutive work permits.
Work permits do not themselves confer resident status; the holder remains a bona fide visitor with conditional permission to work.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year per work permit; renewable by the Minister from time to time
initial_validity.notes: Labour Code section F6(4) caps each work permit at one year. The Minister may renew it on a duly filed application; the law does not promise renewal or a fixed number of renewals.

extension_rules.value: Resident-permit renewal should be requested three months before expiry and remains subject to the Chief Immigration Officer's decision

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A work permit alone is not residence
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Official guidance expressly distinguishes work permission from resident status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A Class A resident-permit application may be made after four years of uninterrupted lawful residence supported by consecutive work permits
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Approval is not automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Resident-permit holders may later pursue citizenship under separate residence and nationality requirements
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the local-employer mismatch.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route depends on local employment/work permits rather than an independently maintained foreign contract.

rejected_routes.route_name: Class F resident permit for persons of independent means

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No official income or asset threshold was found in the published FAQ.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No amount was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No official threshold published; two years of prior qualifying residence is stated
income_requirement_display.notes: No current initial immigration status allowing an ordinary remote worker to accumulate the prerequisite two years was confirmed.

income_proof_months.notes: The published FAQ does not prescribe a fixed number of bank-statement or income-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: Official FAQ lists a two-year residence requirement for persons of independent means.
A non-worker resident certificate does not authorize the holder to seek employment.
The official material does not confirm that foreign-client remote work is permitted under this category.

initial_validity.value: Resident permits may be granted for 1 to 3 years after approval
initial_validity.notes: The prior lawful-residence basis remains unclear for a new ordinary remote worker.

extension_rules.value: Apply for renewal three months before expiry; approval is discretionary

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct entry-stage permit was confirmed; the published category requires two years of prior residence
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor status is not a qualifying remote-work route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The FAQ labels Class F within its resident-permit categories, but it does not establish a direct entry route or remote-work authorization
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Filing-level verification would be required.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separate qualifying lawful residence and nationality rules
path_to_citizenship.notes: No direct Class F citizenship entitlement exists.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the source does not establish a current initial entry route, a published financial threshold, or permission for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Registering a business or relying on visitor extensions would not independently legalize residence or work.

summary.value: An admitted student may obtain a student permit, normally issued one year at a time, without a local employer. It prohibits gainful or unpaid work except limited study-related activity, cannot be converted to normal Class A residence while the purpose remains study, and therefore is not a foreign-contract remote-work or direct permanent-residence route.
summary.notes: Acceptance by the education authorities and institution, financial support, health documentation, and advance approval before entry are required.

tax_residency_rule.value: No current general individual tax-residency day-count rule was established from the official sources inspected. Personal income tax was abolished, but locally carried-on business activity, source taxation, social security, and treaty rules can still create obligations.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Do not substitute the common 183-day treaty test for a verified domestic residence rule. Obtain advice for the applicant's contract and business structure.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the personal income-tax rate after abolition of PIT, not a statement that all remote-worker or business liabilities are zero.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Official rate for covered self-employed persons, including qualifying non-nationals gainfully employed in Antigua and Barbuda.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Self-employed contributions are 10% of declared insurable earnings, with earnings not below the applicable minimum wage. A reliable universal USD monthly minimum cannot be calculated because actual insurable hours, earnings, and coverage must be established.

special_tax_regimes.value: No current digital-nomad tax regime is available to new applicants because NDR closed. Personal income tax is abolished, while unincorporated business tax and social-security contributions may still apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No official foreign-income exemption specific to a current remote-worker visa was found.

taxes.caveats: The 0% figure is personal income tax only. A contractor carrying on an unincorporated business locally may face UBT at up to 25%, covered self-employed persons pay social security at 10%, and other registration, ABST, withholding, or treaty obligations can depend on the facts.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system for this profile: personal income tax was abolished, but unincorporated sole-trader business income is subject to progressive UBT rates of 0%, 8%, and 25%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No current official general individual-residence trigger was confirmed; PIT is abolished, but business/source and treaty analysis remains necessary.
taxation_system.income_scope: Employment remuneration is not subject to personal income tax. Chargeable unincorporated business income can be taxed under UBT.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No current NDR or other remote-worker special regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered self-employed persons pay 10% of declared insurable earnings, from at least the applicable minimum wage up to the published XCD 6,500 monthly ceiling in the official brochure.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% rate below is the top Unincorporated Business Tax rate, not a personal employment-income rate or expected effective rate.

tax_brackets.notes: Annual chargeable business income; approximate USD conversion uses the fixed XCD 2.70/USD peg.
The USD value represents the approximate upper boundary, not monthly income.
Top UBT rate; not personal income tax.

taxation_system.notes: Official tax material supports PIT abolition and UBT brackets. The precise classification of foreign-contract income requires professional advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable to new applicants because the NDR programme closed on 15 November 2025. Historically attractive 0% PIT does not establish that business or social-security charges were zero.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: closed legacy digital-nomad programme
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% personal income tax; up to 25% UBT may apply to locally carried-on unincorporated business income.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No current official domestic day-count test was confirmed; the closed route cannot be used to establish current immigration or tax residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: No current route-specific official foreign-income treatment was found. Classification depends on whether activity constitutes employment, a locally carried-on business, or other taxable local-source activity.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None available to new NDR applicants; the programme is closed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If treated as covered self-employment in Antigua and Barbuda, the official rate is 10% of declared insurable earnings.

fixed_payments.status: not_applicable_to_closed_route
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potentially 10% of declared insurable earnings for covered self-employed activity; not automatically applicable merely because someone visits.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No current NDR application or renewal fee applies because new applications are closed. General visa or residence fees may apply to separate statuses.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: UBT registration has no mandatory initial registration fee, but an annual business-registration fee based on gross-income bracket is referenced by the tax authority; the amount was not captured.
fixed_payments.notes: No universal fixed monthly amount can be stated without determining immigration status, local business activity, insurable earnings, and social-security coverage.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no current NDR admission route. Visitor status ordinarily does not authorize work, so a short stay is not a substitute for lawful remote-work residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A separate lawful immigration basis is required. Although PIT is 0%, UBT, social security, source rules, and treaty obligations must be assessed.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: UBT and 10% self-employed social security may apply when activity is carried on locally. Registration alone does not grant immigration permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax analysis is screening guidance, not a filing position.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No current qualifying ordinary remote-worker route exists.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No remote-worker transition can be timed. Separately, the work-based Class A permit generally requires four years of uninterrupted lawful residence backed by consecutive work permits.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on statutory residence periods rather than a fixed period measured from permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated from a closed remote-worker route. General alien naturalisation requires residence throughout the 12 months immediately before application plus at least five aggregate years during the preceding seven-year period.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official current processing-time statistic was published in the Immigration material or nationality legislation inspected.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires the statutory residence pattern, good character, intention to reside, and ministerial approval. The official material does not confirm that former NDR time counted. Dual citizenship is constitutionally protected in the covered circumstances, but eligibility and documentation must still be established.
key_conditions.notes: Citizenship registration or naturalisation may also be refused on prescribed public-interest grounds.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution bars a spouse's citizenship-registration application until the marriage has subsisted for more than three years. Separately, Immigration says a resident-permit application can be made after at least one year of marriage to a citizen.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to an Antiguan and Barbudan citizen counts toward the three-year citizenship-registration period and can support a resident-permit application after one year. Marriage to another non-citizen does not independently accelerate citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The spouses must not be living apart under a court decree or deed of separation for the constitutional registration entitlement.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must apply, document the legal and continuing marriage, satisfy prescribed procedures, and take the oath of allegiance where applicable. Residence based on a spouse may be revoked after death or divorce at the Chief Immigration Officer's discretion, although the former spouse may have three months to seek a permit independently. Fraud or concealment can support refusal, revocation, or loss of status.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not make citizenship automatic.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship at birth to every person born in Antigua and Barbuda, subject only to narrow diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Antigua and Barbuda normally becomes a citizen even when both parents are migrants, unless the narrow diplomatic-immunity or enemy-occupation exception applies.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Antigua and Barbuda is a citizen by birth. If born abroad, constitutional citizenship by descent generally applies when a parent satisfies the specified citizenship conditions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father does not acquire citizenship automatically through the child.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a citizen child does not automatically grant either migrant parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. No specific automatic parent-of-citizen status was found in the official immigration material inspected.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A parent must qualify under a separate immigration or nationality provision.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status. A migrant father would need a separate residence, family, employment, or nationality basis; the child's citizenship alone is insufficient.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Any discretionary family consideration should be verified directly with Immigration.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 15 August 2026.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free by the named index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard value: 38 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 6 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: The same current index is used for all figures. Its mobility score was 143; index methodologies differ from Henley's combined visa-free/arrival score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for daily life and business because English is the established official language and the language used by government services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: A 2026 policy proposal considered Spanish as a second official language, but the most recent inspected Cabinet item described implementation as still under review.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official language, and no broad government or business-service availability was confirmed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Private community support may exist, but no reliable current source quantified it.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The latest national survey is from 2018. ILO-derived material provides only a rounded PPP-adjusted international-dollar mean, not an exact nominal XCD or USD mean, while 2026 IMF reporting identifies outdated labour-force data as a continuing gap.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the latest national median monthly income located, XCD 2,400 in the 2018 Labour Force Survey, using XCD 2.70 per USD. This is historical, not a 2026 wage estimate.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official minimum is hourly. A monthly USD figure would require assuming actual paid hours, so it is left null.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The available ILO-derived 2018 mean is rounded and PPP-adjusted rather than an exact nominal USD wage. Current official and IMF sources do not publish an exact current national average monthly wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of XCD 2,400 per month at XCD 2.70 per USD; historical 2018 survey median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The national survey material does not publish a meaningful observed national wage ceiling, and later IMF reporting confirms that labour-force data remain outdated.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage effective 1 April 2026, not an observed minimum monthly salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The 2018 national survey collected gross income and ILOSTAT exposes a PPP-adjusted employee-earnings series, but the current sources checked do not publish an exact mean in XCD. The 2026 IMF material identifies outdated labour-force data as a continuing gap, so a current or directly comparable XCD mean cannot be stated.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: National median monthly income from the 2018 Labour Force Survey, cited again in the IMF 2026 Article IV report. It is the latest national median located, not a 2026 salary estimate.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected national survey material reports earnings through survey variables and grouped distributions rather than a meaningful observed national wage ceiling, and the IMF says labour-force data remain outdated. No official maximum monthly salary statistic is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory hourly minimum wage (2026); national median monthly income (2018 LFS); exact XCD mean and national maximum unpublished in the current sources checked
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 2026-04-01; median from 2018 Labour Force Survey
average_citizen_salary.notes: The XCD 2,400 median is historical national survey evidence and should not be read as a current 2026 salary. The ILO-derived mean is available only as a rounded PPP-adjusted international-dollar figure, so it cannot safely populate the local-currency mean. No official national maximum was published.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official May 2026 CPI was 4.1% higher than May 2025. Housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels rose 8.2%; actual rents rose 6.3%; and electricity rose 25.0%.
cost_of_living_note.notes: These are inflation changes, not an absolute monthly cost-of-living budget.
