settlement_track.summary: No active independent ordinary remote-worker route was confirmed. The former NDR is closed, and the remaining residence paths require prior lawful status, local work permits, marriage, study, independent means, or investment without a confirmed foreign-contract remote-work entry path.
settlement_track.notes: A future replacement programme would require a new audit; none was found in current government or Immigration sources.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The historical NDR fit ordinary foreign-contract remote work, but it is closed. No current replacement or independently accessible self-employed residence route was confirmed.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 15 August 2026. The employer-sponsored work-permit duration is now resolved from the Labour Code: each permit may last no more than one year and may be renewed discretionarily. The latest national median located is XCD 2,400 per month from the 2018 LFS; an exact XCD mean and meaningful national maximum remain null because current official and international sources do not publish them. Thirty-three distinct canonical source URLs are listed, including eight newly inspected URLs outside the prior source set.

data.selection_summary: Argentina has an active, independently filed digital-nomad route for visa-exempt nationals working for foreign clients or employers. However, it grants only residencia transitoria for up to 180 days, extendable once/equally; it is not residencia temporaria, does not provide a DNI, does not qualify for the ordinary permanent-residence clock, and the current naturalization process requires two years of continuous legal residence as a temporary or permanent resident with no trips abroad. No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route that supplies that qualifying status was confirmed, so Argentina is suitable for temporary remote living but not for this citizenship-oriented selection.

visa_application.title: Tramitación de Ingreso Electrónico — TIE 24H
visa_application.notes: This is the official online start for applicants outside Argentina. The system requires the applicant to be outside Argentina and involves two filing/payment stages. Applicants already in Argentina follow the separate in-country digital-nomad instructions, which are presencial and not filed through RaDEX.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current official checklists require evidence of the activity, contract, employer endorsement, certifications, or income/fee receipts but publish no fixed minimum monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed ARS threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum published; documentary proof of foreign remote activity/income is required
income_requirement_display.notes: DNM may request additional evidence. A contract or income receipts satisfy the document category but do not guarantee approval.

income_proof_months.notes: The official pages do not state a required number of historical income months.

key_requirements.requirement: Be a national of a country whose citizens do not require a tourist visa to enter Argentina.
Provide remote services using IT, telecommunications, or analogous means for individuals or legal entities domiciled abroad.
Provide a signed application, CV showing experience and education/training, valid passport, and current photograph.
Provide evidence such as a foreign contract, employer endorsement, demand-for-work request, certifications, or income/fee receipts, plus at least one occupational reference.
For an in-country filing, prove regular entry, Argentine address, identity, and an Argentine criminal-record certificate when applicable.

initial_validity.value: Up to 180 days as residencia transitoria
initial_validity.notes: This is a transitory immigration permission, not Argentina's qualifying residencia temporaria.

extension_rules.value: Prorrogable for an equal period; the program was introduced as 180 days plus one equal extension
extension_rules.notes: Extension is discretionary and does not convert the status into temporary residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No official rule was found converting digital-nomad transitory residence into an ordinary temporary-residence category. A separate Article 23 ground would be required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Possible after a separate qualifying temporary-residence application, then the applicable two- or three-year PR period; nomad transitory time does not meet that requirement.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: In-country RaDEX applications are documented. Three years is the non-MERCOSUR temporary-residence period after the switch, excluding nomad transitory time; MERCOSUR nationals generally have a two-year rule. This is conditional on a different qualifying basis, not a confirmed remote-only successor.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The current naturalization process is available to temporary or permanent residents after two continuous, legal years without any exit. The nomad status is transitory, supplies no DNI, and is not listed as qualifying.

best_routes.notes: This route strongly fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work as a temporary-living permission. It fails the selection because the exact status is transitory and no current official conversion into qualifying temporary residence was confirmed.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The legal threshold is formula-based in ARS. A reliable spot USD conversion was not used because the peso exchange rate is volatile.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: ARS 1,883,000 per month (5 × the ARS 376,600 SMVM effective 1 August 2026)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The qualifying income must arise from assets incorporated into the applicant's patrimony, not remuneration for personal work.

income_requirement_display.value: 5 × Salario Mínimo Vital y Móvil; currently ARS 1,883,000/month
income_requirement_display.notes: The threshold changes whenever the minimum wage changes.

income_proof_months.notes: The in-country route does not specify a fixed history in months; the entry-permit version describes stable monthly rent for at least two years.

key_requirements.requirement: Income must be generated by foreign assets such as financial instruments, real estate, or company participations.
Remuneration from the applicant's personal work is expressly excluded.
Funds must enter through BCRA-authorized banking or financial institutions.
Passport, regular entry, Argentine address, and Argentine/foreign criminal-record documentation are required.

initial_validity.value: 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Qualifying temporary residence with temporary DNI eligibility.

extension_rules.value: Renewable
extension_rules.notes: Renewal must normally be sought in the 60 days before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct qualifying temporary residence

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential PR after the applicable two- or three-year temporary-residence period and required physical presence
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Nationality-dependent and subject to continuing eligibility.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential naturalization after two continuous legal years as a temporary or permanent resident, with no exit during the statutory period
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not applicable to the supplied profile unless the applicant separately has qualifying passive asset income.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because foreign-client software-engineering remuneration is personal-work income and is expressly excluded from the rentista category.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general fixed income threshold; remuneration must comply with the applicable collective agreement.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Contract-specific remuneration.

income_requirement_display.value: Contract remuneration must comply with the applicable collective agreement

income_proof_months.notes: Prospective local employment documentation is required instead of historical foreign income.

key_requirements.requirement: Pre-employment contract for dependent work in Argentina.
Argentine employer CUIT, tax registration, RENURE registration, and early employee registration.

initial_validity.value: 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Qualifying temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while qualifying local employment continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence through local dependent employment

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential after the applicable qualifying temporary-residence period

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential after two continuous legal years, but only if the applicant first obtains this locally sponsored status

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a local employer, pre-contract, and sponsorship-related employer registrations.

summary.value: Enrollment as a regular student in a recognized Argentine secondary, tertiary, university, postgraduate, or specialized program can support independently initiated one-year renewable temporary residence. An existing foreign software-engineering degree alone creates no residence entitlement; actual enrollment in Argentina is required. Student residence may be qualifying temporary residence, but it is a separate study strategy rather than an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.
summary.notes: The citizenship portal requires temporary or permanent residence and two years of continuous legal presence without any foreign trip. Whether remote contracting alongside studies complies with all immigration and tax conditions should be verified before relying on this alternative.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreign individual becomes an Argentine income-tax resident upon obtaining permanent residence or, without permanent residence, after remaining under temporary authorizations for 12 months. The rule has technical timing and interruption provisions; separate personal-deduction rules use more than six months in the fiscal year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 180-day nomad status normally ends before the stated 12-month temporary-authorization test, but local-source/service-export obligations may arise earlier.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for 2026, not the expected effective rate. The progressive annual scale starts at 5%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage applies. Monotributo combines tax, pension, and health components into category-dependent fixed monthly amounts; general autónomo or employment regimes differ.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Category A monotributo totals ARS 49,527.18 monthly from 1 August 2026, but no USD value is supplied because exchange-rate choice and volatility would make a single conversion misleading.

special_tax_regimes.value: Eligible small service providers may use Monotributo, a simplified monthly regime combining VAT, income tax, pension, and health coverage. Category and eligibility depend on annual gross revenue and other parameters. Service exporters issue type-E invoices; no special digital-nomad tax exemption was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign remote work performed from Argentina and economically used abroad can be treated as an export of services. Professional advice is important for foreign-currency, provincial turnover-tax, treaty, and invoicing rules.

taxes.caveats: Immigration status and tax status are separate. Physical performance of services in Argentina may create Argentine-source or service-export compliance before full tax residence. Residence, income source, treaty, monotributo eligibility, provincial taxes, foreign-exchange rules, and whether the relationship is employment or independent contracting can materially change the result.

taxation_system.value: Argentina uses progressive personal income tax. For 2026, the official annual Article 94 scale runs from 5% to 35% on net taxable income. Tax residents are generally taxed under resident rules including foreign-source gains; a remote contractor may instead qualify for category-based Monotributo if within its limits.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence or 12 months under temporary authorizations for a foreign individual, subject to statutory timing rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are subject to Argentine income-tax rules that include foreign-source gains; non-residents remain subject to Argentine-source rules. Services physically performed in Argentina for foreign economic use are officially described as exports of services.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Monotributo may replace VAT and income tax plus pension and health contributions with a fixed category payment for eligible small taxpayers.
taxation_system.social_security: Variable by structure. Monotributo uses fixed SIPA and obra-social components; employment and general self-employment use different rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 35% is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate. The thresholds below are annual 2026 net taxable-income thresholds in ARS.

tax_brackets.notes: Plus the fixed amount specified by the official scale.
Marginal rate on the excess.
Marginal rate on the excess.
Marginal rate on the excess.
Marginal rate on the excess.
Marginal rate on the excess.
Marginal rate on the excess.
Top marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: Official ARCA sources support the residence test, bracket scale, simplified-regime payments, and service-export invoicing. Individual classification still requires professional review.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The immigration permission provides no special tax holiday. A stay confined to one 180-day authorization generally falls short of ARCA's 12-month temporary-authorization tax-residence rule, but work physically performed from Argentina for foreign economic use can constitute an export of services and may require local registration and type-E invoicing. If eligible and registered under Monotributo, fixed monthly tax, pension, and health payments apply; otherwise the general progressive system can apply according to residence and source.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary digital nomad; no dedicated tax regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 5%–35% progressive general PIT; 35% is the top marginal screening rate. Eligible small taxpayers may instead use category-based Monotributo.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence or 12 months under temporary authorizations for a foreign individual, subject to statutory details.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident taxation can include foreign-source gains. Services performed in Argentina and used economically abroad are treated as service exports for invoicing purposes.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No official digital-nomad income-tax exemption or inbound tax holiday was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No automatic visa-linked contribution was found. Local Monotributo registration includes fixed pension and health components; employment or general autónomo treatment differs.

fixed_payments.status: Conditional on local tax/self-employment registration, not automatic merely from holding the nomad permission
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: From 1 August 2026, Monotributo category A includes ARS 18,246.86 SIPA and ARS 25,694.55 obra social within an ARS 49,527.18 total monthly payment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The TIE portal generates two payment stages, but the public route page does not display a stable amount; therefore no fee is stated.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Provincial turnover tax, banking/foreign-exchange effects, and higher Monotributo categories may apply depending on activity and revenue.
fixed_payments.notes: Category A is only an example/minimum category, not necessarily the applicant's correct category.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A single stay of up to 180 days generally does not meet the 12-month authorization test, but the contractor should not assume tax-free work: Argentine-source/service-export registration, invoicing, provincial tax, treaty, or permanent-establishment issues may arise.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect resident filing and possible taxation of foreign-source income under the progressive system unless eligible for Monotributo or treaty relief. The 35% figure is only the top marginal rate.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Eligible small service providers may use Monotributo and issue type-E export invoices. The monthly amount depends on annual revenue; category A totals ARS 49,527.18 from August 2026.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the published rules and amounts, but only medium-high confidence in their application to an individual foreign contract without reviewing nationality, treaty, work location, payment flow, and contract form.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The nomad route grants transitory residence immediately, not qualifying temporary residence. No automatic conversion time was confirmed.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Not reachable from the nomad status alone. After separately obtaining qualifying temporary residence, the ordinary PR period is two years for MERCOSUR nationals or three years for non-MERCOSUR nationals, with more than 50% presence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Permanent residence is not a prerequisite. Naturalization instead requires two continuous legal years as a temporary or permanent resident immediately before filing.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be assigned to the digital-nomad route because it is transitory and has no confirmed conversion. Once qualifying temporary/permanent residence is separately obtained, the statutory naturalization period is two continuous years without any exit.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official digital application material does not publish a typical processing time. The process moved from federal courts to DNM in October 2025, making older court-time estimates unreliable.

key_conditions.value: For ordinary naturalization: age 18+, temporary or permanent residence, two years of continuous and legal residence immediately before filing with no departure from Argentina, DNI, current Argentine criminal-record certificate, proof of occupation/means of life, CUIT/CUIL, physical presence in Argentina when filing, and any additional evidence requested by DNM.
key_conditions.notes: The current statute does not state a language test or general renunciation requirement. Absence tolerance is exceptionally strict: the law defines continuity as no exit during the two-year period.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The current citizenship law states a two-year continuous legal-residence requirement and the 2025 reform repealed the former statutory exceptions. No current marriage-duration shortcut was found.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine marriage to an Argentine citizen or temporary/permanent resident can support a separate temporary family-reunification residence. If the sponsor is Argentine or a permanent resident, the authorization can be granted for up to three years. Marriage does not itself grant citizenship or waive the current two-year naturalization rule.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An already existing marriage matters only if it is legally documented and the qualifying family member has the required Argentine citizenship or residence.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must present a legalized/apostilled marriage record, the sponsor's identity document, regular-entry and address evidence, and criminal records where required. DNM may assess the scope and genuineness of family reunification; false documents, false domicile, or a sham relationship can cause refusal, cancellation, and immigration enforcement.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage should never be modeled as a fictitious immigration strategy.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Everyone born in Argentine territory is Argentine regardless of the parents' nationality, except the narrow statutory exception for children of foreign ministers and legation members resident in Argentina. Argentina also permits nationality by option for a foreign-born child of an Argentine native parent.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Argentina is an Argentine citizen even when both parents are foreign migrants, subject only to the narrow diplomatic/legation exception.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' immigration category or lack of permanent residence does not change the child's territorial citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Argentina is Argentine by birth. A child born abroad to an Argentine native parent can opt for Argentine nationality through the prescribed registration process.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father's status does not prevent the child's citizenship where the other parent is Argentine.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of an Argentine child can apply for temporary family-reunification residence for up to three years. Current official rules no longer show automatic permanent residence or a citizenship residence-period waiver solely because the applicant has an Argentine child.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: This differs materially from older summaries that treated an Argentine child as an immediate PR or naturalization shortcut.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father may use genuine, legally documented parentage of an Argentine child to seek temporary family-reunification residence. Fatherhood does not automatically grant permanent residence or citizenship; ordinary naturalization still requires two continuous legal years with no exit.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Identity, birth record, parental relationship, regular entry, address, and criminal-record requirements apply.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations in Passport Index's current breakdown.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as visa required.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 46 visa-on-arrival and 9 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately reports a mobility score of 160.

passport.notes: Index methodologies differ. These fields consistently use Passport Index 2026 rather than mixing its category breakdown with Henley's broader visa-free/visa-on-arrival score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in Buenos Aires and technology/international-business settings, but Spanish remains important for immigration, RaDEX, tax registration, banking, leases, healthcare, and daily administration. EF EPI 2025 rated Argentina 'high' proficiency, 26th of 123 and first in Latin America; the volunteer-test methodology should not be read as universal fluency.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Remote work for a foreign client can be conducted in English, but settlement administration is predominantly Spanish.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited outside immigrant communities and private interpretation services. No official nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-language administrative service was confirmed; applicants should expect Spanish documents and may need certified translations.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical assessment based on Spanish being the official language; no reliable national proficiency dataset for Russian or Ukrainian was found after focused searching.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: INDEC publishes current ARS occupational income, but no USD conversion is supplied because Argentina's exchange-rate choice and volatility would materially affect the result.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Official median occupational income is available in ARS; a defensible single USD conversion was not established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The statutory minimum is stated in ARS; USD conversion intentionally omitted.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: USD conversion intentionally omitted due exchange-rate volatility.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: USD conversion intentionally omitted due exchange-rate volatility.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary exists.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory Salario Mínimo Vital y Móvil effective 1 August 2026, not an observed minimum in the wage distribution.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average income of employed persons across 31 urban agglomerations in Q1 2026; broader than formal salary alone.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median income of employed persons across 31 urban agglomerations in Q1 2026.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: INDEC publishes decile distributions and averages, not a meaningful national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly income of employed persons from INDEC's Permanent Household Survey; minimum field is the separate statutory monthly minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 income survey; minimum wage effective 2026-08-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: INDEC also reported average salaried-worker income of ARS 1,136,558, with ARS 1,375,143 for workers with retirement deductions and ARS 731,150 without. The normalized average/median fields use all employed persons for internal consistency.

cost_of_living_note.value: Price comparisons require frequent updating: INDEC reported national CPI rising 1.9% in June 2026, 16.8% during the first half of 2026, and 33.5% year over year. Housing/utilities rose 47.8% year over year. Nominal ARS salary or budget figures should therefore be treated as date-specific.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The official CPI measures price change, not a comparative expatriate cost-of-living level.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The digital-nomad permission is residencia transitoria for up to 180 days, extendable, not residencia temporaria. It supplies no confirmed PR clock or qualifying naturalization status.
settlement_track.summary: The route is an excellent temporary fit for foreign remote work but is not a settlement route. Citizenship requires switching to an independently qualifying temporary or permanent residence category and then satisfying the current two-year continuous-residence rule with no exit.
settlement_track.notes: The prior country record incorrectly treated availability of the temporary nomad permission as selection eligibility despite simultaneously classifying it as temporary-only. This audit applies the prompt's citizenship-path rule and sets selection to false.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only as a temporary-living/work-permission fit. The route expressly covers remote services for persons or companies domiciled abroad but does not supply the qualifying settlement status required by this selection.

data.notes: Twenty-five distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected. Primary official sources resolve the core result: the nomad route is active and profile-compatible but legally transitory; current naturalization requires temporary or permanent residence. Remaining nulls are limited to facts not published or not defensibly convertible, including a nomad income threshold, processing time, route-to-PR duration, and USD wage conversions.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Qualifying residencia temporaria under Article 23 (for example rentista or locally employed migrant worker)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The nomad permit does not itself qualify for PR. A holder may separately obtain qualifying temporary residence and later apply for PR; ordinary foreign remote-work salary alone does not establish the reviewed successor grounds.
requirements: Qualify independently for an Article 23 category: rentista requires asset-derived income and excludes personal-work earnings; migrant worker requires an Argentine employer.
For non-MERCOSUR nationals, maintain qualifying temporary residence for three years and spend more than half the granted period in Argentina.
reviewed_route_names: Residencia transitoria como Nómada Digital
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: In-country RaDEX applications are documented. Three years is the non-MERCOSUR temporary-residence period after the switch, excluding nomad transitory time; MERCOSUR nationals generally have a two-year rule. This is conditional on a different qualifying basis, not a confirmed remote-only successor.

data.selection_summary: Armenia has no dedicated digital-nomad visa, but it has a stronger residence route: a foreigner may register as an individual entrepreneur, conduct genuine business activity such as software services for a foreign client, and independently apply for temporary or permanent residence. Official sources list business activity as a direct basis for both statuses, while citizenship is generally available after three years of permanent residence, subject to Armenian-language and Constitution requirements. The filing must demonstrate real ongoing Armenian-registered business activity; visitor status or a dormant registration is insufficient.

visa_application.title: Applying for a residence status
visa_application.notes: Official Migration and Citizenship Service route-information page. It lists residence documents and business-activity evidence but redirects applicants through Armenia's identity and appointment system. A replacement electronic residence system is scheduled to begin on 1 November 2026.

best_routes.route_name: Residence status based on entrepreneurial activity (individual entrepreneur)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No statutory monthly-income threshold is published. The applicant must instead document genuine entrepreneurial activity.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published fixed income threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Business evidence, rather than a stated minimum income, is required.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published; prove genuine business activity
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Business-activity evidence, not a salary multiple
income_requirement_display.notes: Invoices, the foreign service contract, payments, tax registration and filings may help establish substance, but the official page does not publish a closed evidentiary checklist or minimum turnover.

income_proof_months.notes: The official service page does not specify a minimum number of months of revenue history.

key_requirements.requirement: Register and genuinely operate an Armenian individual entrepreneur or other Armenian business; foreign citizens may be individual entrepreneurs.
Submit an application and questionnaire, passport plus notarized Armenian translation, three 35x45 mm photographs and a health certificate.
Show lawful presence in Armenia and documents confirming entrepreneurial activity.
Pay AMD 105,000 for temporary residence or AMD 140,000 for permanent residence, subject to nationality-specific reciprocity exceptions.
Maintain real contracts, invoicing, business records and tax compliance; registration alone may not establish substantive entrepreneurial activity.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence: up to 1 year; permanent residence: 5 years
initial_validity.notes: Official rules separately list business activity as a basis for either temporary or permanent status.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence may be renewed for successive one-year periods; permanent residence may be renewed for successive five-year periods. Apply at least 30 days before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: Continued qualifying activity and current supporting documents should be expected.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Register a genuine business or individual entrepreneur, remain lawfully in Armenia, and apply for temporary residence with documents confirming the activity. There is no published minimum period of prior business operation.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence status, not an eVisa or visitor extension.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Business activity is independently listed as a direct basis for a five-year permanent resident card; the three-year prior-residence condition shown for qualifying family applicants is not stated for entrepreneurs.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Direct permanent residence is legally possible, but approval remains evidence-based. Applicants should verify what volume and duration of activity the Migration and Citizenship Service expects.

path_to_citizenship.value: After three years of permanent residence in Armenia, an adult may generally apply for citizenship if able to communicate in Armenian and familiar with the Constitution. Dual citizenship is recognized by Armenia.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Maintain actual residence, business substance and tax compliance. The statutory language uses permanent residence, so visitor days should not be assumed to count.

best_routes.notes: This route fits ordinary foreign-client software work when conducted as genuine Armenian-registered entrepreneurial activity. It does not require a local employer or Armenian client, and the individual-entrepreneur law permits foreign citizens. Official guidance does not define a minimum turnover, business age or exhaustive evidence test; a dormant registration should not be treated as sufficient.

rejected_routes.route_name: Armenia eVisa or visa-free visitor stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No remote-worker threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is an entry or visitor facility.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—visitor/eVisa status is not a residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status does not itself legalize long-term entrepreneurial residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No digital-nomad income-history rule is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Use the official eVisa portal if the applicant's nationality requires and permits an electronic visitor visa.
Visa-exempt visitors are generally limited to 180 days in one year unless a treaty provides otherwise.

initial_validity.value: Depends on nationality and visa type; visa-exempt stay is generally up to 180 days per year
initial_validity.notes: Not a residence card.

extension_rules.value: Does not become qualifying residence merely through repeated visitor stays
extension_rules.notes: A separate residence application and qualifying basis are necessary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic transition; the person must separately establish a qualifying basis such as genuine entrepreneurial activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path from visitor or eVisa status

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time alone is not a confirmed citizenship path

rejected_routes.notes: Useful only for entry and preliminary setup. It is not a digital-nomad visa and is rejected as the selected residence route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Local-employer work permit and work-based residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No independently applicable remote-worker threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Not applicable to this profile
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Terms depend on local employment.

income_requirement_display.value: Local employer and work-permit process required
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because the applicant works for a foreign client and seeks independent filing.

income_proof_months.notes: Not relevant to the selected profile.

key_requirements.requirement: An Armenian employer initiates the work-permit and work-based residence process.

initial_validity.value: Tied to the authorized employment period

extension_rules.value: Requires continued qualifying local employment and employer-side processing

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Work-based temporary residence follows the employer and work-permit process

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct independent permanent-residence grant under this employer-sponsored route was established

path_to_citizenship.value: Long-term lawful residence may be relevant, but this route fails the independent-application criterion

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer initiates the process.

summary.value: Enrollment in an Armenian educational program is an independent basis for temporary residence, but a foreign university degree by itself does not create a skilled or degree-based residence route. Study is available without a local employer but is not the appropriate route for this already-qualified remote software engineer.
summary.notes: No independent points-tested or degree-recognition residence program comparable to a skilled-independent visa was confirmed.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally Armenian tax resident if present for 183 or more days in the tax year or if the person's centre of vital interests is in Armenia; registered Armenian individual entrepreneurs also create Armenian business tax obligations independently of the personal-day test.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breaker rules can alter dual-residence outcomes.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for an individual entrepreneur in the general taxation system: 23% profit tax on the taxable business base. A natural person receiving salary or civil-contract service income outside the IE framework is generally screened at a flat 20% income-tax rate instead.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single defensible percentage applies to every foreign individual entrepreneur. Pension and social-payment liability depends on age, residence and tax regime, while universal health insurance is being phased in by population category.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly amount applies to every foreign entrepreneur. Under turnover taxation, the Tax Code states an AMD 5,000 monthly final profit-tax payment in addition to turnover tax. Universal health insurance has a statutory AMD 10,800 monthly rate, but applicability depends on the person's phased coverage category.

special_tax_regimes.value: Eligible small businesses may use the turnover-tax system, subject to turnover, activity and timely-election rules. The Tax Code also contains a micro-enterprise system, but exclusions mean software and professional services should not assume eligibility. Individual entrepreneurs outside a special regime use the general 23% profit-tax system. No digital-nomad or inbound-expatriate tax holiday was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Tax classification should be confirmed before registration because personal civil-contract income, IE general taxation and turnover taxation differ materially.

taxes.caveats: Armenian tax residents are taxable on Armenian- and foreign-source income, while non-residents are generally taxed only on Armenian-source income. Services physically performed from Armenia and income invoiced through an Armenian IE require transaction-level analysis even before 183 days. Foreign tax credits, treaty residence, deductible expenses, VAT place-of-supply and payer classification should be reviewed professionally.

taxation_system.value: Mixed flat and special-regime system. Ordinary salary or civil-contract service income is generally taxed at 20%; an individual entrepreneur in the general system pays 23% profit tax on taxable entrepreneurial profit; qualifying small businesses may elect turnover taxation.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183 or more days in the tax year, centre of vital interests in Armenia, or other statutory residence conditions; registered Armenian IE activity carries separate Armenian business obligations.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident natural persons are taxed on Armenian- and foreign-source taxable income. Non-residents are generally taxed on Armenian-source income; Armenian-registered entrepreneurial activity is taxed under the applicable business regime.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Turnover-tax and micro-enterprise systems exist, but eligibility, activity exclusions and filing deadlines must be checked. No digital-nomad-specific exemption was found.
taxation_system.social_security: No single rate is suitable for dashboard screening. Employee contributions commonly vary with income, while IE pension obligations and phased universal-health-insurance charges depend on category and regime.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 23% is neither a progressive top bracket nor an expected effective rate. It is the statutory general-system profit-tax rate for individual entrepreneurs; qualifying turnover-tax treatment can produce a different result.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No income bracket; generally applies to salary and civil-contract service/work income of natural persons
tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary personal salary or civil-contract service income
tax_brackets.notes: Flat category rate, not necessarily the correct treatment once the applicant invoices as an Armenian IE.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No income bracket; applies to the taxable base of an IE in the general system
tax_brackets.applies_to: Individual-entrepreneur taxable profit under the general taxation system
tax_brackets.notes: Business expenses and statutory deductibility rules affect the tax base.

taxation_system.notes: Official sources establish the main rates and residence rules. The exact effective burden depends on activity classification, turnover-tax eligibility, pension status and the 2026–2029 health-insurance rollout.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Armenia has no digital-nomad tax category. A remote software engineer using the qualifying residence route is taxed as an Armenian individual entrepreneur or, if not properly registered as such, potentially as a natural person receiving foreign service income.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Armenian individual entrepreneur conducting software or service business
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 23% general-system IE profit tax; potentially different under a valid turnover-tax election; 20% is the ordinary personal service-income rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Usually 183 days or centre of vital interests, but Armenian IE registration creates domestic business tax and filing obligations regardless of whether the individual has crossed 183 days.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident natural person's taxable base includes Armenian- and foreign-source income. Foreign-client receipts invoiced through the Armenian IE are entrepreneurial receipts subject to the elected Armenian business regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found. Turnover tax is a general small-business regime, not a nomad concession.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No local-employer payroll is required for the selected route. Pension and social-payment treatment depends on the entrepreneur's age, status and tax regime.

fixed_payments.status: Partially confirmed; applicability is category-dependent
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal IE percentage applies. The statutory universal-health-insurance premium is AMD 10,800 per month, but foreign-resident coverage and payment responsibility depend on phased population categories.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Temporary residence AMD 105,000 per issue or renewal; permanent residence AMD 140,000 for a five-year card. Citizenship application fee is AMD 50,000.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Under turnover taxation, an IE has an AMD 5,000 monthly final profit-tax payment in addition to turnover tax. VAT registration and general VAT rules apply when statutory conditions, including the AMD 115 million threshold, are met.
fixed_payments.notes: Confirm the latest exchange rate and the entrepreneur's exact tax and insurance category before payment.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Spending under 183 days does not automatically eliminate Armenian liability: centre of vital interests can create residence, and an Armenian-registered IE remains subject to Armenian business registration, tax and filing rules.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax-resident individual must consider worldwide income. If operating through the IE, apply the elected business regime; if receiving foreign service income personally, the 20% personal service-income category may apply, subject to treaty and classification analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect IE bookkeeping, invoicing and tax filings. General-system IE profit is screened at 23%; qualifying turnover taxation can differ. Check VAT, pension and universal-health-insurance obligations separately.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No nomad-specific tax ruling exists. Professional Armenian advice is warranted before choosing the IE tax regime or treating foreign-employer remuneration as entrepreneurial income.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence can be requested once genuine qualifying business activity and the required documents exist; no statutory waiting period was found.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Entrepreneurial activity is separately listed as a direct permanent-residence basis, so entrepreneurs are not expressly required to complete a temporary-residence period first. Approval depends on substantive evidence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalization requires permanent residence in Armenia for the preceding three years, Armenian communication ability and familiarity with the Constitution.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Best-case statutory eligibility from the start of qualifying permanent residence. Time needed to establish the business, obtain the card and process citizenship is additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Official service guidance states 90 working days, approximately four to five calendar months; actual elapsed time can vary.

key_conditions.value: Maintain registered permanent residence and actual residence for three years; conduct genuine business, comply with tax and residence-card rules, communicate in Armenian, know the Constitution, pass security and public-order review and take the citizenship oath. Armenia recognizes dual citizenship and imposes no general renunciation requirement.
key_conditions.notes: The official sources reviewed do not publish a simple absence-days formula. Conservative planning should preserve evidence of continuous residence and avoid lengthy absences.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must have been legally married to an Armenian citizen for the preceding two years and have legally resided in Armenia for at least 365 days during that period.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to an Armenian citizen can count toward the two-year marriage period and supports family residence. Marriage to another migrant does not create the Armenian-citizen shortcut, although family-based temporary residence may be available through the spouse's status.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Citizenship is not automatic upon marriage.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally registered and genuine, the 365-day lawful-residence condition must be documented, and a non-Armenian-origin applicant must take the Constitution test. False documents or a sham marriage can cause refusal, status loss and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The marriage route waives the general three-year residence and Armenian-language conditions when its statutory requirements are met, but not constitutional or security review.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Armenia alone does not normally confer citizenship. Citizenship follows an Armenian parent or applies through limited birth-in-Armenia and anti-statelessness rules.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Armenia to two foreign parents does not receive Armenian citizenship merely by birth. Exceptions cover stateless parents, unknown citizenship or parents unable to transmit citizenship.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for ordinary foreign migrant parents who can transmit another citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Where one parent is Armenian and the other is foreign, the child has a right to Armenian citizenship through the parents' written consent. If they do not agree, a child born in Armenia acquires Armenian citizenship under the statutory fallback rule.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Citizenship is based primarily on the Armenian parent, not broad jus soli.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having an Armenian-citizen child can create a facilitated citizenship basis for the foreign parent and can support family residence, but it does not automatically make the parent a citizen or permanent resident.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A separate application, eligibility review and documentation remain necessary.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father whose child is an Armenian citizen may use the citizen-child naturalization exception, which removes the ordinary three-year residence and Armenian-language conditions; familiarity with the Constitution and the application and security process still apply. Fatherhood and the child's citizenship must be legally established.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No automatic paternal citizenship arises at the child's birth.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on the live Passport Index page when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings are volatile.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 43 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations. Separately listed eVisa destinations are excluded.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 80. Its methodology differs from Henley, which combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in Yerevan and the technology and expatriate environment, but not a substitute for Armenian in government filings or citizenship. EF EPI 2025 scores Armenia at 515, rank 56, in the moderate-proficiency band; Yerevan scores 530.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF uses voluntary test-taker data and is not population-weighted, so it is a practical indicator rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is substantially more practical than Ukrainian for daily communication. Ukrainian has no official status or similarly broad documented coverage. Armenian remains necessary for formal integration and naturalization.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The Russian-language conclusion relies on a secondary census summary because a directly extractable official Armstat language table was not located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2025 gross average monthly nominal wage of AMD 303,140 using roughly AMD 366.9 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Armstat's current national wage series publishes an arithmetic mean, minimum wage and wage indexes but no national median. The ILO's 2023 Armenian Labour Force Survey catalog confirms that employee monthly-earnings microdata exist, but the reviewed catalog and data dictionary do not publish a weighted national median. A current national USD median therefore cannot be reported without independently processing the survey microdata and choosing an exchange-rate date.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the statutory AMD 75,000 monthly minimum wage, not an observed minimum in the wage distribution.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2025 gross monthly average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current published national median suitable for direct USD conversion was established. Armstat's series is explicitly an arithmetic mean calculated from employee tax and social-payment records. The ILO catalog identifies monthly-earnings variables in Armenia's 2023 Labour Force Survey, but neither the catalog nor its data dictionary reports the survey-weighted national median; independently calculating one would require the microdata, survey weights, population filters and a stated currency-conversion date.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Armenian law establishes a minimum, not a maximum, wage. Current official wage tables publish means and the Ministry of Economy reports sector averages, not the highest individual national salary or a top distribution bound. Consequently no defensible national maximum can be converted to USD.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Current statutory minimum monthly wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2025 average monthly nominal gross wage.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The current Armstat wage indicator and wage table do not publish a median in AMD. The ILO's Armenian 2023 Labour Force Survey catalog documents employee monthly-earnings variables and underlying microdata, but the reviewed public catalog and dictionary do not state a survey-weighted national median. Secondary web estimates were not substituted because their methodology and national representativeness could not be verified.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: There is no statutory maximum wage. Armstat's current national table provides minimum-wage, average-wage and index measures, while the official economic-outlook reports provide average wages by sector; none publishes an individual national maximum, top percentile, or reliable upper wage-distribution endpoint.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum plus official gross average monthly nominal wage from employee tax and social-payment records
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 average for the mean; current law for the minimum; 2023 is the newest reviewed employee-earnings microdata catalog
average_citizen_salary.notes: The mean and statutory minimum are well supported. Median and maximum remain null for specific reasons: current official tables do not publish them, and the ILO survey catalog exposes earnings-variable metadata rather than a computed national median or maximum. These wage figures are not immigration income thresholds and do not represent self-employed remote software engineers.

cost_of_living_note.notes: Official CPI data were checked, but a CPI series does not establish a defensible monthly living-cost budget. No current official household-cost figure suitable for this field was established, so no crowd-sourced estimate is substituted.
