settlement_track.summary: Genuine Armenian entrepreneurial activity can support direct permanent residence rather than merely a temporary nomad stay. Permanent residence can lead to general naturalization after three years if business substance, physical residence, Armenian language, Constitution knowledge and tax compliance are maintained.
settlement_track.notes: The main uncertainty is evidentiary rather than statutory: official guidance does not quantify the minimum turnover or operating history needed to prove entrepreneurial activity. Filing-level confirmation is advisable for newly created or low-revenue activity.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign citizen may register as an individual entrepreneur, provide services independently and use genuine entrepreneurial activity as the residence basis. No local employer or Armenian client is expressly required. The foreign software contract should be invoiced and administered as real Armenian business activity rather than used only as passive foreign-employment evidence.

data.notes: The focused audit preserves the independently applicable entrepreneur route and resolves the flagged salary markers cautiously. Current official wage sources publish the national arithmetic mean but not a median or maximum; ILO survey metadata confirm underlying earnings variables without publishing a current weighted national median. Confidence remains medium because immigration authorities do not publish a minimum-turnover or exhaustive business-substance test, tax treatment varies by structure, and the residence application system changes on 1 November 2026.

data.selection_summary: Australia is a partial match. The Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189) requires no employer sponsor and grants permanent residence directly, but it is an invitation-only, points-tested skilled-migration route—not a visa for ordinary work under a foreign remote contract. No current dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence route was found, and visitor status does not permit work.

visa_application.title: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189) – Points-tested stream
visa_application.notes: This is the official route page. The applicant first submits an Expression of Interest through SkillSelect. Only an invited candidate can lodge the visa application through ImmiAccount, normally within 60 days of invitation.

best_routes.route_name: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189) – Points-tested stream

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is published because eligibility is based on occupation, skills assessment, age, English, points and invitation rather than foreign income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No minimum monthly income; at least 65 points are required to be eligible for invitation consideration.
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Meeting 65 points does not guarantee an invitation; actual invitation scores and occupations vary by round.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold — points/invitation route
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a digital-nomad income test.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed number of income-proof months is prescribed. Evidence must instead substantiate claimed skilled employment and points.

key_requirements.requirement: Be under 45 when invited.
Nominate an occupation eligible for subclass 189 and obtain a suitable assessment from its assessing authority.
Submit an Expression of Interest, score at least 65 points and receive an invitation; 65 points does not guarantee invitation.
Document English ability, education, skilled employment and every other points claim; meet health and character requirements.
Software Engineer can be an eligible skilled occupation, but the applicant must verify the current subclass-specific legislative list and assessment requirements before filing.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence upon grant/entry, with a five-year travel facility
initial_validity.notes: The right to remain in Australia as a permanent resident is not limited to five years; the five-year period concerns travel and re-entry.

extension_rules.value: No residence extension is required. After the initial travel facility expires, a Resident Return visa or citizenship is generally needed to return from overseas as a permanent resident.
extension_rules.notes: Continued physical presence and travel history affect later citizenship and Resident Return eligibility.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None required; subclass 189 is a direct permanent visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Submitting an EOI does not itself give immigration status or a bridging visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence if the invited subclass 189 application is granted.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The invitation is competitive and a grant is not guaranteed.

path_to_citizenship.value: A subclass 189 permanent resident can apply for citizenship after satisfying the general residence rule: normally four years living in Australia on valid visas, including the final 12 months as a permanent resident, subject to absence, character, test and other requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant must actually reside in Australia; merely holding the visa offshore does not complete the physical-presence requirement.

best_routes.notes: Strong independent settlement option for a qualifying software engineer, but only a partial selection match because neither the foreign contract nor ordinary remote work creates eligibility. The invitation process, occupation list and competitive score must be checked immediately before filing.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor visa, ETA or business-visitor stay for remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No qualifying income threshold exists because visitor status is not a remote-work residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No local-currency threshold is applicable: Home Affairs states that a Visitor visa or ETA does not permit work, irrespective of the visitor's foreign income.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable — visitor status does not permit work
income_requirement_display.notes: Foreign income does not convert visitor status into work-authorized residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No route-specific income-proof period applies because this is not a qualifying work or residence route.

key_requirements.requirement: A visitor must remain a genuine visitor and comply with all visa conditions.
Visitor visas and ETAs do not permit work in Australia; business-visitor activities are limited to matters such as enquiries, contract negotiations and conferences.

initial_validity.value: Business Visitor stream: generally up to three months
initial_validity.notes: Other visitor subclasses and individual grants vary.

extension_rules.value: No conversion based merely on opening a bank account, obtaining an ABN or registering a business was found.
extension_rules.notes: A separate substantive visa with suitable work rights would be required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying residence path from remote work as a visitor was confirmed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor presence is not a digital-nomad residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence entitlement arises from visitor remote work.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor status alone is not the selected qualifying settlement route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because Australian Home Affairs expressly states that a Visitor visa or ETA does not allow work. Limited business-visitor activities are not ordinary ongoing remote work.

rejected_routes.route_name: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) and other employer-sponsored skilled visas

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The published figures are Australian-employer nomination salary thresholds, not a personal foreign-income test. Because the applicable Core or Specialist stream and annual market salary rate depend on the nominated Australian position, no single USD monthly threshold represents this rejected route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: For nominations lodged 2026-07-01 through 2027-06-30: at least AUD 79,423/year for the Core Skills stream or AUD 146,576/year for the Specialist Skills stream, plus the applicable annual market salary rate.
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: These equal approximately AUD 6,618.58/month and AUD 12,214.67/month respectively. They are employer-paid annual earnings floors for a nominated Australian position, not qualifying foreign income, and do not remove the approved-sponsor requirement.

income_requirement_display.value: Australian-sponsored salary threshold — not foreign income
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: AUD 79,423/year Core Skills or AUD 146,576/year Specialist Skills for 2026–27; market salary rules also apply
income_requirement_display.notes: The foreign contract does not replace the sponsoring Australian employer.

income_proof_months.notes: Home Affairs publishes nomination salary floors rather than a fixed number of applicant income-history months. Employment and salary evidence is assessed under the applicable sponsorship, nomination and visa requirements.

key_requirements.requirement: Be nominated for a skilled position by an approved Australian sponsor, possess the required skills and satisfy the applicable English requirements.
The nominated salary must meet the applicable income threshold and annual market salary rate.

initial_validity.value: Up to four years in the Core and Specialist Skills streams; some passport holders can receive up to five years
initial_validity.notes: This is temporary employer-sponsored status and is not independently accessible through a foreign contract.

extension_rules.value: Any further temporary visa or permanent pathway has separate sponsorship, nomination, occupation and visa conditions.
extension_rules.notes: The temporary visa does not become permanent automatically.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary subclass 482 status if an approved Australian sponsor nominates the applicant for an eligible position and all visa requirements are met.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The route cannot be initiated independently for ordinary foreign-client work: the temporary status rests on an approved Australian sponsor and nominated position.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate Employer Nomination Scheme subclass 186 Temporary Residence Transition application may provide permanent residence after eligible sponsored employment, but requires an approved Australian-employer nomination and normally at least two years of eligible full-time sponsored employment within the preceding three years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a conditional employer-sponsored transition, not a direct or independently controlled permanent-residence entitlement under subclass 482.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only after obtaining permanent residence through subclass 186 or another qualifying permanent visa and then satisfying the general citizenship residence and eligibility rules.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Time on subclass 482 may form part of the four-year lawful-presence period, but the final 12 months normally must be as a permanent resident; employer nomination and the permanent-visa grant remain separate prerequisites.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer sponsor and nominated Australian role are required. The current 2026–27 salary thresholds clarify the route's employer-paid salary rules but do not make it an independent remote-worker option.

rejected_routes.route_name: Enter as a tourist and register as a sole trader/self-employed worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold applies because ABN or sole-trader registration is a business/tax registration matter, not a visa or residence category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No local-currency immigration threshold is published for this scenario. ABN entitlement depends on carrying on or starting an enterprise, while lawful work depends separately on visa conditions.

income_requirement_display.value: No tourist-to-self-employed residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Tax or business registration does not itself create work rights or residence.

income_proof_months.notes: The ABR may request evidence that an enterprise commenced or that commencement steps were taken, but it does not publish an immigration income-history period because an ABN is not a visa.

key_requirements.requirement: A person must hold a visa whose conditions permit the intended work; visitor status and an ETA do not.
ABN entitlement requires carrying on or starting an enterprise; employees are not entitled to an ABN for their employee activity.

initial_validity.notes: No immigration status is created by registering an ABN or operating as a sole trader.

extension_rules.notes: There is no renewal or conversion mechanism attached to ABN or sole-trader registration; the person must independently qualify for a substantive visa with appropriate work rights.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The current sources establish that an ABN records entitlement to carry on an enterprise and that a sole trader is a business structure, while Home Affairs separately requires visa work permission. None creates a temporary-residence visa or converts visitor status, so no temporary-residence path exists through registration alone.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: ABN or sole-trader registration carries no published immigration credit or conversion entitlement. Permanent residence would require a separate qualifying visa, such as an invited subclass 189 application or an employer-nominated subclass 186 application, each with its own unrelated requirements.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Business registration is not lawful immigration residence and does not start a citizenship pathway. Citizenship by conferral ordinarily requires permanent residence plus the statutory lawful-residence, absence, character, test and pledge conditions; no current source gives ABN or sole-trader time separate credit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected. An ABN or sole-trader registration may be available to a person genuinely carrying on an enterprise, but it is not immigration status and cannot override the express prohibition on working while holding visitor status.

summary.value: Subclass 189 is available without employer sponsorship and grants permanent residence directly if granted. A relevant degree can contribute points and support a skills assessment, but a degree alone is insufficient: the applicant needs an eligible occupation, suitable assessment, English, at least 65 points and a competitive invitation.
summary.notes: This is qualification/points-based migration, not permission to migrate because the applicant already has a foreign remote contract.

tax_residency_rule.value: Australian tax residency is separate from citizenship and visa status. Four alternative tests apply, including ordinary residence, domicile, the 183-day test and the Commonwealth-superannuation test. Presence for more than half the income year can satisfy the 183-day test unless the person's usual abode is outside Australia and they do not intend to reside; all facts and applicable treaty rules must be considered.
tax_residency_rule.notes: There is no universally safe 'tax starts on day 183' rule.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top 2026–27 resident marginal rate, excluding the generally applicable 2% Medicare levy. This is a screening ceiling, not the applicant's expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This represents the ordinary Medicare levy for Australian tax residents, subject to reductions and exemptions; it is not a comprehensive social-insurance contribution rate. Employer superannuation obligations are separate and depend on worker classification.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax or social-security payment was established. Medicare is percentage-based, and a self-employed sole trader generally does not pay compulsory superannuation guarantee for themselves.

special_tax_regimes.value: Australian temporary-resident tax concessions can exempt some foreign income, but subclass 189 is permanent residence and is not a temporary visa. No digital-nomad tax holiday or special nomad rate was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Temporary-resident tax status has specific statutory conditions and should not be inferred from remote work or a short stay.

taxes.caveats: Tax liability depends on tax residency, source of services, whether the relationship is employment or independent contracting, permanent-establishment/business facts, deductions and treaty relief. Visa work rights and tax obligations are separate. Australian residents generally report worldwide income and may claim a foreign-income tax offset where eligible.

taxation_system.value: Progressive resident personal income tax. For 2026–27 the resident rates are 0%, 15%, 30%, 37% and 45%; Medicare levy is additional where applicable.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Four alternative statutory tests apply; the 183-day test includes usual-abode and intention exceptions and is not the only test.
taxation_system.income_scope: Australian residents generally report worldwide income. Foreign residents generally face Australian tax on Australian-source income, while qualifying temporary residents receive special treatment for much foreign income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Temporary-resident foreign-income concessions exist but do not apply to subclass 189 permanent residents merely because their client or employer is foreign.
taxation_system.social_security: The ordinary Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income unless reduced or exempt. Employer superannuation may apply depending on employment/contractor classification; self-employed sole traders generally need not pay super guarantee for themselves.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 45% dashboard value is the top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. Threshold USD figures use the RBA AUD/USD rate of 0.7068 on 2026-08-14 and are approximate.

tax_brackets.notes: Tax-free threshold; offsets and Medicare levy are separate.
15 cents per dollar above AUD 18,200 from 1 July 2026.
Marginal rate, not whole-income rate.
Marginal rate, excluding Medicare levy.
Top marginal rate, excluding Medicare levy.

taxation_system.notes: The 15% first taxable bracket applies from 1 July 2026. The 45% value is only the top marginal screening rate.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Australia has no confirmed dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker visa. If the person qualifies through subclass 189 and lives in Australia, ordinary resident rules normally apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: not_applicable_no_regular_remote_work_route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 45% top resident marginal rate, not expected effective tax; the generally applicable Medicare levy can add 2%.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Immigration status does not determine tax residence by itself; four alternative tests and any treaty must be considered.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: An ordinary Australian resident generally reports worldwide income, including foreign employment or contracting income, with potential foreign-income tax-offset relief. Special temporary-resident treatment is status-specific and does not fit subclass 189 permanent residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad tax holiday or nomad-specific rate was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Medicare levy is generally 2% for residents unless reduced or exempt. Superannuation depends on whether the arrangement creates an employer or deemed-employee obligation; sole traders generally do not owe super guarantee for themselves.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment identified
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed monthly amount. Medicare is percentage-based; self-employed personal super is generally voluntary.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Subclass 189 has visa application charges and possible assessment, English-test, health and police-certificate costs, but the official route page directs applicants to the current pricing estimator rather than establishing a permanent fixed amount for this record.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: GST registration generally becomes mandatory when connected business turnover reaches AUD 75,000; exports or sales not connected with Australia can affect the calculation.
fixed_payments.notes: These obligations depend on the actual business and contract structure and do not create immigration eligibility.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay shorter than 183 days does not guarantee non-residence, and visitor status still prohibits work regardless of tax outcome.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Assume worldwide foreign-contract income is reportable under ordinary resident rules unless a specific temporary-resident exception or treaty changes the result.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A local sole trader may need an ABN, income-tax filings and GST registration once applicable turnover reaches AUD 75,000. Self-employed sole traders generally need not pay super guarantee for themselves, but contractor classification can change obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax discussion is contextual only because the selected immigration route is skilled permanent residence, not a digital-nomad visa.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Subclass 189 does not require a temporary-residence stage; it grants permanent residence directly.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Direct permanent residence upon visa grant or entry; invitation waiting time and visa processing are additional.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The applicant must normally have been a permanent resident for the final 12 months, but must also satisfy four total years of qualifying valid-visa residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest general residence timeline after actually living in Australia on valid visas. Invitation and visa processing before residence starts are additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Home Affairs reported 90% of citizenship-by-conferral applications processed within seven months. Up to a further six months may be needed for 90% of approved applicants to receive a ceremony opportunity.

key_conditions.value: Normally live in Australia on valid visas for four years immediately before applying; hold permanent status for the final 12 months; have no more than 12 months total absence during the four years and no more than 90 days in the final 12 months; satisfy identity, character, citizenship-test/English and pledge requirements.
key_conditions.notes: Australia permits dual citizenship, but the applicant must separately verify whether their existing nationality permits retention.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage can accelerate access to permanent residence through partner migration, not citizenship itself. Permanent-stage partner assessment is usually available two years after the combined temporary/permanent application, with possible long-term-relationship exceptions.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage or qualifying de facto relationship to an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen can support a sponsored partner-visa pathway. Marriage to another non-citizen migrant does not independently accelerate Australian citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: For a de facto relationship, 12 months is usually required unless an exception applies; a legally valid marriage is assessed under spouse rules.

requirements_and_risks.value: Partner migration requires an approved sponsor and evidence that the relationship is genuine and continuing, including shared finances, household, social life and commitment. Permanent assessment usually follows the temporary stage. Citizenship is not automatic through marriage and still requires permanent residence and the general residence, character and test requirements. False or sham evidence can cause refusal or cancellation and may expose the parties to penalties.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Relationship cessation, family violence, death and shared-child circumstances have special rules requiring case-specific advice.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Australia is a citizen at birth if either parent is an Australian citizen or permanent resident. Otherwise, citizenship is acquired if the child is ordinarily resident in Australia throughout the first ten years, subject to statutory exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: If both parents are temporary or non-permanent migrants, the child generally is not Australian at birth merely because the birth occurs in Australia. The child can acquire citizenship after ordinary residence in Australia throughout the first ten years. If either migrant parent already holds Australian permanent residence, the child is a citizen at birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the two-temporary-migrant scenario; parental permanent residence changes the result.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Australia is an Australian citizen at birth if the other parent is an Australian citizen. If born abroad, citizenship by descent generally requires an application and the citizen parent's eligibility must be checked.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father does not automatically acquire Australian residence or citizenship through the child's citizenship.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically regularize either parent's status. Separate partner, parent or other visa requirements still apply. Parent visas generally require a settled Australian-citizen or permanent-resident child and are capped and queued, with very long current waits.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A newborn citizen child is not an immediate independent route for the father.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship. The father must qualify under a separate visa, such as a genuine partner route. A later parent route may become possible only when its sponsorship, settled-child, balance-of-family and other requirements are met, and processing can take many years.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Official estimates as of July 2026 were approximately 15 years for contributory parent visas and 33 years for parent or aged-parent visas.

rank.notes: Live Henley ranking inspected on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's score counts destinations accessible without obtaining a prior visa and can include visa-on-arrival or eTA access under its methodology.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The inspected live Henley ranking did not publish a separate visa-required total for Australia, so no residual count was guessed.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Henley combines qualifying access categories in its headline score and did not expose a separate Australia visa-on-arrival/eTA count in the inspected public ranking.

passport.notes: Rank and access are dynamic and should be rechecked before travel; each destination's entry rules remain controlling.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. Australian government materials describe English as the national and main language, and it is the normal language of government, business and professional life.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Australia has no constitutionally declared federal official language; English is listed because government sources identify it as the national and main language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian can be used within community networks and through interpreting services, but neither has nationwide official status or substitutes for English in ordinary government, professional and commercial dealings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: An English-speaking software engineer should find remote-work logistics straightforward; relying only on Russian or Ukrainian would be impractical.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median weekly total cash earnings for all employees, May 2025.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum is published.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Subclass 189 is not a nomad route. Eligibility depends on occupation, skills assessment, points and invitation—not a foreign remote contract.
settlement_track.summary: Subclass 189 grants permanent residence directly and can lead to citizenship after the general four-year residence period. This is a strong settlement track for an invited skilled applicant, but only a partial profile match because Australia offers no qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.
settlement_track.notes: The route itself is a strong settlement route, but the country remains only a partial match because subclass 189 is invitation-based skilled migration rather than an ordinary remote-worker route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No current dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence visa was found. Visitor visas and ETAs do not permit work, and ABN registration does not create immigration status. Subclass 189 can independently fit the applicant's profession, but eligibility is unrelated to the foreign contract.

data.notes: Australia should be evaluated as an independent skilled-permanent-residence option, not a remote-work migration destination. The applicant must verify the live occupation instrument, assessing authority, English result, points score and invitation competitiveness before spending on an application.

data.selection_summary: Austria does not currently offer a dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. The closest independent route, the Red-White-Red Card for Self-employed Key Workers, requires macroeconomic benefit to Austria—such as at least EUR 100,000 in sustained investment, job creation, technology transfer, or regional significance—and therefore does not fit routine software work for a foreign client. The independent Job Seeker Visa is only a six-month search visa for very highly qualified applicants and requires conversion through Austrian employment.

visa_application.title: Self-employed Key Workers – Red-White-Red Card
visa_application.notes: This is the closest official independent-business route page, not a digital-nomad application portal. The applicant normally files personally through the competent Austrian embassy or consulate; filing in Austria is possible after lawful entry and during lawful stay, but does not remove the demanding macroeconomic-benefit test. The page links the official application forms and reports a EUR 218 application fee.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No route-specific monthly income threshold is published. The decisive test is macroeconomic benefit, not ordinary foreign-client income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed monthly-income minimum is published for this category. The official examples instead include at least EUR 100,000 of sustained investment or other qualifying macroeconomic benefit.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed monthly threshold; route normally requires major Austrian economic benefit (EUR 100,000 investment is one official indicator)
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No monthly threshold; EUR 100,000 sustained investment is one non-exclusive indicator
income_requirement_display.notes: Job creation, transfer of know-how or technology, or considerable regional significance may alternatively demonstrate macroeconomic benefit. This is not a simple savings or foreign-salary test.

income_proof_months.notes: The official route page does not state a fixed number of prior income-proof months. It requires business, investment, qualification, insurance, and potentially criminal-record evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: The intended Austrian self-employed activity must create macroeconomic benefit beyond the applicant's own business benefit.
Official indicators include at least EUR 100,000 in sustained investment, creation or preservation of Austrian jobs, transfer of know-how or new technology, or considerable regional significance.
Submit a business plan, market/competition/location analysis, investment or job evidence, qualifications, and any required company or trade-authorization documents.
Health insurance covering all risks is required; authorities commonly request a recent criminal-record extract.

initial_validity.notes: The card grants fixed-term settlement and only the self-employed activity described in the application.

extension_rules.value: After two years, a qualifying holder may receive a Settlement Permit; after a completed total settlement period of two years, that permit may be issued for three years.
extension_rules.notes: Continued compliance is required. Switching to specified employed Red-White-Red categories requires a binding Austrian employment offer.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct fixed-term settlement is granted if the demanding Self-employed Key Worker requirements are approved.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Although this is a real settlement title, routine foreign-client software contracting does not by itself satisfy the macroeconomic-benefit test.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying settlement holder may seek Long-term Resident–EU after five years of continuous actual settlement in Austria and completion of Integration Agreement Module 2.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Absence and other general conditions apply. This path is relevant only if the applicant first qualifies for the substantive business route.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization is possible after ten years of lawful continuous residence, including five years settled, subject to all naturalization conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant generally must demonstrate income, German and civic knowledge, good conduct, limited absences, and relinquishment of prior nationality unless an exception applies.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile. Independent filing and a settlement path exist, but the route requires Austrian investment, job creation, technology transfer, or comparable macroeconomic substance. Ordinary remote software work for a foreign client is insufficient.

summary.value: A very highly qualified applicant can independently apply for a six-month Job Seeker Visa after reaching 70 points, but the visa is only for finding Austrian employment. A relevant foreign degree alone does not grant residence, and settlement requires a qualifying local job and Red-White-Red Card. Austrian university graduates have a separate 12-month search/start-a-business period, but that requires prior Austrian study.
summary.notes: This is not marked partial because the independent qualification-based step grants only a search visa rather than qualifying settlement or permanent residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: Unlimited Austrian tax liability begins when a person has a residence or habitual abode in Austria. In any event it arises after six months of presence, retroactively, and generally covers domestic and foreign income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and allocation rules can modify which state ultimately taxes particular foreign employment or business income.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the exceptional top marginal 2026 rate on annual income above EUR 1 million, scheduled through 2029—not an expected effective rate for a typical software engineer. Ordinary brackets rise from 0% to 50% below that level.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Indicative 2026 GSVG total for a registered trader or ordinary covered freelancer: 18.5% pension, 6.8% health, and 1.53% self-employed provision, plus fixed accident insurance. Coverage, assessment base, new-business rules, and professional category can change the result.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate minimum combined monthly 2026 GSVG amount on the EUR 551.10 minimum base: EUR 101.95 pension + EUR 37.48 health + about EUR 8.43 self-employed provision + about EUR 12.95 accident insurance = about EUR 160.81, converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1567. This applies only where Austrian self-employed social insurance is triggered; it is not a digital-nomad fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax regime or remote-worker tax holiday was found. Austria has specialized inbound relief provisions, but no official source reviewed established eligibility for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Specialist advice is needed before relying on any expatriate or inbound relief.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the relationship is employment or self-employment, where the work is physically performed, Austrian residence and habitual abode, applicable double-tax treaty, foreign-employer payroll obligations, and social-security coordination. No immigration route exists merely because the applicant registers for Austrian tax or social insurance.

taxation_system.value: Austria uses a progressive worldwide-income system for persons with unlimited tax liability. The 2026 marginal rates are 0%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 48%, 50%, and a temporary 55% rate above EUR 1 million.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence or habitual abode can create unlimited liability immediately; after six months' presence it applies retroactively.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide domestic and foreign earnings for persons with unlimited Austrian tax liability, subject to treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No ordinary digital-nomad regime. Any specialized inbound relief requires separate eligibility analysis.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered self-employed persons in 2026, typical GSVG rates include 18.5% pension, 6.8% health, 1.53% self-employed provision, and fixed monthly accident insurance.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 55% figure is a top marginal screening rate applying only above EUR 1 million, not the average or effective tax burden.

taxation_system.notes: Rates are statutory marginal rates. Deductions, credits, business expenses, treaty relief, and social insurance determine the actual effective burden.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Austria has no confirmed digital-nomad visa. A person who nevertheless becomes lawfully resident under another status can face Austrian tax on worldwide income and, if locally registered as self-employed, Austrian social-insurance contributions.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; ordinary resident employment or self-employment rules would apply
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 0%–55%; 55% is only the top marginal screening rate above EUR 1 million
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence or habitual abode can trigger unlimited liability; it applies retroactively after six months of presence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is generally within Austrian unlimited tax liability, subject to double-tax treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad exemption or tax holiday confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Foreign-employer payroll and social-security obligations require case-specific analysis. Locally covered self-employed persons generally face GSVG pension, health, provision, and accident contributions.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed tax. Conditional self-employed social-insurance minimums may apply under another lawful route.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Indicative 2026 minimum for a covered ordinary GSVG self-employed person is about EUR 160.81 monthly, including the fixed accident contribution; later reconciliation to actual income can occur.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The Self-employed Key Worker and Start-up Founder route pages state a EUR 218 application fee. This is not a digital-nomad fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No route-specific flat freelancer tax or digital-nomad levy was found. Trade registration, VAT, accounting, or municipal costs depend on the actual business structure.
fixed_payments.notes: These amounts do not make an applicant immigration-eligible.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay under six months does not guarantee non-residence: maintaining an Austrian dwelling or having an Austrian habitual abode can trigger unlimited liability earlier, and Austrian-source income may remain taxable.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A lawful resident working physically from Austria for a foreign employer or client generally needs advice on worldwide-income taxation, treaty allocation, payroll, permanent-establishment exposure, and social security.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered and insured self-employed person may face progressive income tax plus GSVG contributions; registration cannot replace a valid immigration title.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section describes tax consequences hypothetically because no matching nomad residence route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists, so there is no applicable time-to-residence figure for the selected profile. The rejected Self-employed Key Worker route grants settlement when approved.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Long-term Resident–EU generally requires five years of continuous actual settlement plus Integration Agreement Module 2. This applies only after obtaining a qualifying settlement title.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Approximate general-track interval inferred from Long-term Resident–EU eligibility at five years and general naturalization at ten years. Citizenship does not mechanically follow five years after PR and all conditions must still be satisfied.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General rule: ten years of lawful continuous residence, including five years settled. Certain qualifying applicants can use the six-year early-naturalization rule.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable nationwide typical processing time was published on the official federal pages reviewed. Procedures are administered by the federal states, so timing varies by authority and case.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires lawful continuous residence with no more than roughly 20% of the relevant period spent abroad, five years of settled status on the ten-year route, stable resources for 36 months within the preceding six years, German and civic knowledge, good conduct and security compliance, and in principle relinquishment of the former nationality.
key_conditions.notes: The exact German level depends on the naturalization basis; B2 is itself one ground for early naturalization after six years.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Early naturalization can be available after six years of lawful continuous Austrian residence if the applicant has also maintained a common household and an ongoing marriage or registered partnership with an Austrian citizen for five years. The value represents the residence threshold, not marriage alone.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can count toward the five-year marriage and common-household condition, but it does not eliminate the requirement for six years of lawful continuous residence in Austria or the general naturalization conditions. Marriage to a non-Austrian does not create this accelerated citizenship ground.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A spouse of an Austrian may separately qualify for a temporary Family Member residence title with unrestricted labor-market access, subject to its requirements.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage or registered partnership and common household must both have existed for five years when relying on the six-year naturalization rule. General income, German/civic knowledge, conduct, security, and usually renunciation requirements remain. Authorities can require civil-status, household, residence, and relationship evidence; sham or convenience marriage can lead to refusal and immigration or criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage is not automatic citizenship and does not cure an unlawful or insufficient residence history.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Austria alone does not confer Austrian citizenship. The official rule is based primarily on descent from an Austrian parent.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Austria to two non-Austrian migrant parents does not automatically become Austrian solely because of the birthplace. Separate descent, naturalization, or special anti-statelessness provisions would need individual examination.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The official descent page expressly states that citizenship does not depend on Austrian birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If at least one married parent is Austrian at birth, a child born on or after 1 September 1983 generally acquires Austrian citizenship by descent. If the parents are unmarried and only the father is Austrian, he generally must acknowledge paternity before birth or within eight weeks, or paternity must be judicially established within that period; later cases may use simplified conferral.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The exact rule depends on birth date, marital status, and timely establishment of paternity.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A child's Austrian citizenship does not automatically naturalize or grant permanent residence to a foreign parent. Austria's ordinary Family Member category lists spouses, registered partners, and unmarried minor children as the core family; a parent may need a different dependent-relative or EU-law basis and individualized review.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any derived right based on dependency, caregiving, or EU/fundamental-rights principles is fact-specific.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic citizenship merely because his child is Austrian. If the mother is Austrian, the child can be Austrian by descent, but the father's residence must be established under a separate family, dependency, or other lawful ground; the standard core-family definition does not list parents of Austrian children.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Special custody, dependency, EU-law, or human-rights cases require legal review.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 44 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations reported separately by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 173 and world reach of 87%. Index methodologies differ, so these figures should not be mixed with Henley totals.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be workable in international software teams, and the migration portal accepts supporting-document translations in German or English, but German is the nationwide official language used by authorities and courts and is central to long-term integration and citizenship. No official nationwide measure of English-only remote-living practicality was found.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Croatian, Slovenian, and Hungarian have additional official status in some regions, but German is the national official language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and should not be relied on for immigration, tax, court, or citizenship procedures. Community-level availability may exist, but no reliable official nationwide practicality measure was established.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: German-language capability or professional translation is normally required for official processes.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official headline source reports medians rather than an arithmetic mean, so no average is substituted.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximation from the 2024 all-employee gross annual median of EUR 38,043 divided by 12 and converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1567. Part-year and part-time employment are included.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Austria had no national statutory minimum wage on 1 July 2026; sector-specific collective agreements set many wage floors, so a single USD minimum would be misleading.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official nationwide arithmetic-mean salary was established from the inspected source.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: All-employee gross median. For full-time full-year employees, EUR 55,678 annually is approximately USD 5,367 monthly at the same exchange rate.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary is published; income is unbounded and an observed maximum would not represent an ordinary worker.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Collective agreements establish minimum rates for particular sectors and occupations.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official headline statistics publish medians, not a nationwide arithmetic mean.

median_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 38,043 gross annually for all employees in 2024; EUR 55,678 gross annually for full-time full-year employees
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Equivalent to EUR 3,170 and EUR 4,640 per month when simply divided by 12. Austrian remuneration can include special payments, so this monthly division is a comparison convention rather than a payroll schedule.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful official national maximum was established.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official Statistics Austria wage-tax and social-insurance data; gross annual median, excluding apprentices
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 annual income, released/compiled in December 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The all-employee median includes different work durations and working-time arrangements; the full-time full-year figure is more representative of a continuing professional software role. USD conversions use the ECB 14 August 2026 reference rate.

cost_of_living_note.value: Statistics Austria reports average 2024/25 household consumption expenditure of EUR 4,170 per month and needs-weighted equivalent expenditure of EUR 2,760. Average rent including running costs was EUR 695.10 per dwelling, or EUR 10.50 per square metre, in Q1 2026. These are national survey averages, not a personal budget or Vienna-specific estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing, household size, city, and lifestyle can produce large differences.
