settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Austria has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence status. Visitor or visa-free presence cannot substitute for a residence and work authorization.
settlement_track.summary: No qualifying route exists for routine foreign-contract remote work. Citizenship is possible only after independently qualifying for a different Austrian settlement route—such as a substantive Self-employed Key Worker, founder, family, or local-employment route—and normally completing ten years of lawful continuous residence.
settlement_track.notes: The rejected Self-employed Key Worker and founder routes can lead to settlement, long-term residence, and eventually citizenship, but they impose Austrian economic-substance requirements outside the stated profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official route catalogue contains employment, highly qualified job-search, substantive self-employed, and start-up categories, but no residence category for ordinary remote work performed for a foreign employer or client.

data.notes: Audit completed against the previous Austria record. The prior invalid-selection conclusion is retained and strengthened with current official 2026 immigration, tax, settlement, citizenship, family, wage, language, social-insurance, exchange-rate, and cost sources. Unavailable arithmetic-mean salary, national citizenship processing time, and route-specific prior-income months remain null with explanations rather than estimates.

data.selection_summary: Azerbaijan has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Its eVisa is visitor-only and prohibits paid labor. Local entrepreneurship can support temporary residence, but it requires genuine Azerbaijani business activity, at least 5 full-time or 10 part-time workers with at least 80% qualifying local workers, and—after the first residence year—at least AZN 50,000 annual turnover. Ordinary employment requires an employer-obtained work permit. Azerbaijan therefore does not fit the requested independent remote-work-to-citizenship profile.

visa_application.title: Republic of Azerbaijan Official Electronic Visa Portal — ASAN Visa
visa_application.notes: This is Azerbaijan's official online eVisa application portal, but the eVisa is only an entry/visitor channel. It permits a 30-day single-entry stay within 90-day validity and does not authorize paid labor. A separate State Migration Service ground is required for residence and work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is published because this is a visitor eVisa, not a remote-worker residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income requirement applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold published; visitor eVisa only
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of an income threshold does not make this a work or residence status.

income_proof_months.notes: No recurring-income proof period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligible nationality, qualifying travel document, online application, and payment through the official ASAN Visa system.
The eVisa is single-entry, valid for 90 days, and permits no more than 30 days in Azerbaijan.
The eVisa does not grant a right to perform paid labor in Azerbaijan.

initial_validity.value: Single entry; 30 days of permitted stay within 90-day visa validity.
initial_validity.notes: Visitor status only.

extension_rules.value: The holder must leave unless temporary stay is lawfully extended or a separate temporary-residence application is accepted under a qualifying legal ground.
extension_rules.notes: This is not a routine digital-nomad extension mechanism.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic conversion. The person must independently qualify under a listed State Migration Service residence ground.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A foreign employment or client contract is not a listed standalone ground.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from the eVisa itself.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Qualifying temporary residence under a separate ground is normally required first.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from the eVisa itself; visitor time is not the five-year permanent-residence period used for ordinary naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Useful only for short visitor entry. It is not a digital-nomad, work, qualifying-residence, or citizenship-path status.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence based on entrepreneurship in Azerbaijan

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no monthly foreign-income threshold. Eligibility is based on substantive entrepreneurship in Azerbaijan; after at least one year on this ground, renewal requires AZN 50,000 turnover in the preceding year.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official rule is annual business turnover rather than personal monthly income: AZN 50,000 for renewal after the first temporary-residence year and AZN 100,000 for permanent residence on the entrepreneurship ground.

income_requirement_display.value: AZN 50,000 annual turnover for temporary-residence renewal; AZN 100,000 for permanent residence
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: AZN annual business turnover and local economic-substance rules
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: After at least 1 year: AZN 50,000 turnover in the preceding year for temporary-residence renewal; AZN 100,000 preceding-year turnover for permanent residence; generally at least 5 full-time or 10 part-time workers with at least 80% qualifying local workers
income_requirement_display.notes: These are business-substance conditions, not a foreign remote-salary threshold. Limited statutory exceptions exist for specified startup/investment-promotion and designated economic-zone entities.

income_proof_months.notes: The tax authority must confirm turnover for the preceding year. This is 12 months of business-turnover evidence, not 12 months of foreign salary.

key_requirements.requirement: Register and genuinely conduct entrepreneurial activity in Azerbaijan; taxpayer registration by itself does not establish immigration eligibility.
Actual operation generally requires at least 5 full-time workers or 10 part-time workers, with at least 80% being Azerbaijani citizens or other qualifying local workers.
After at least one year on the entrepreneurship ground, renewal requires AZN 50,000 turnover in the last year; permanent residence on that ground requires AZN 100,000 turnover in the last year.
Passport, proof of the qualifying ground, health documentation, accommodation/registration documents, photographs, and the applicable state fee are required.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to 1 year.
initial_validity.notes: Certain high-investment or highly skilled grounds can receive longer periods, but those exceptions do not convert ordinary foreign-client work into this route.

extension_rules.value: Generally extendable for up to 2 years at a time while the qualifying ground continues. After at least one year on the entrepreneurship ground, the preceding year's turnover must be at least AZN 50,000, in addition to applicable staffing and continued-operation conditions.
extension_rules.notes: The applicant must obtain tax-authority evidence of annual turnover.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence is possible after approval of the Azerbaijan-based entrepreneurship ground.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Opening a sole-proprietor registration or tax number alone is insufficient.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially after at least 2 years of continuous qualifying temporary residence, with at least AZN 100,000 preceding-year entrepreneurial turnover, continued business substance, sufficient means, language/legal-knowledge assessment, and compliance with absence limits.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a substantive local-business route, not an ordinary remote-worker route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after 5 years of uninterrupted permanent residence, with legal income and Azerbaijani-language proof, but approval remains discretionary and is not automatic.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because the official route requires genuine Azerbaijan-based entrepreneurship, generally at least 5 full-time or 10 part-time workers with at least 80% qualifying local workers, AZN 50,000 preceding-year turnover for renewal after the first residence year, and AZN 100,000 preceding-year turnover for permanent residence. Entering as a visitor, registering as a sole proprietor, and continuing an ordinary foreign software contract does not by itself meet those immigration conditions.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employer-sponsored work permit and temporary residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Compensation is employment-specific rather than a published immigration income floor.

income_requirement_display.value: No published immigration income threshold; employer sponsorship required
income_requirement_display.notes: This route is excluded because the employing entity applies for the work permit.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard prior-income proof period is specified for this employer-sponsored route.

key_requirements.requirement: An employing legal entity, entrepreneur, branch, or representative office must obtain the work permit for the foreign worker.
Paid labor normally requires both the work permit and temporary-residence authorization.
The employer must comply with Azerbaijan's labor-market and employment rules.

initial_validity.value: Work permits are generally issued for up to 1 year.

extension_rules.value: Generally extendable for no more than 1 year at a time; the employer must apply before expiry and pay the applicable fee.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary residence can accompany the approved work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Not a direct grant of permanent residence; separate qualifying residence rules apply.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through later qualifying permanent residence and ordinary naturalization; not through the work permit itself.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employing entity must obtain the work permit. A foreign-client contract does not replace Azerbaijani employer sponsorship.

summary.value: Full-time study at an Azerbaijani higher-education, vocational, or qualifying secondary institution is a temporary-residence ground and does not require a local employer. An existing foreign university degree alone creates no independent skilled or degree-based residence right, and study residence is not a direct permanent-residence route.
summary.notes: This requires new full-time enrollment and is not a qualification-based route for continuing ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual present in Azerbaijan for more than 182 days in a calendar year is generally tax resident. If presence is below that threshold, permanent home, center of vital interests, habitual residence, and citizenship tie-break criteria can still matter.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence rules may override domestic tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for an individual entrepreneur paying ordinary income tax: 20% of taxable business income after deductible expenses. A qualifying simplified taxpayer may instead pay 2% of turnover, while 2026 private non-oil employment uses 3%, 10%, and 14% marginal brackets. Classification of foreign software income must be verified.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For 2026 entrepreneurial activity, compulsory state social insurance is 2% of gross income before expenses, subject to a monthly floor of 15% and ceiling of 100% of the minimum wage—currently AZN 60 and AZN 400. This is not a universal rate for employees or civil-law contractors.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate minimum for an active registered individual entrepreneur: AZN 60 minimum monthly social insurance plus AZN 16 monthly compulsory medical insurance, or AZN 76 total, converted at AZN 1.70 per USD. Applicability to a foreigner's particular foreign-source contract requires classification and source analysis.

special_tax_regimes.value: Qualifying small entrepreneurs may use simplified tax, generally 2% of turnover for services, subject to eligibility and exclusions. Ordinary individual entrepreneurs otherwise pay 20% on taxable business income. No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax holiday was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: VAT registration generally becomes mandatory when taxable transactions exceed AZN 200,000 in a consecutive 12-month period.

taxes.caveats: There is no digital-nomad immigration or tax category. A foreign-employer relationship, individual-entrepreneur registration, source of services, residence status, applicable treaty, permanent-establishment questions, and simplified-tax eligibility can materially change the result. The health-insurance authority states that foreign nationals' contribution liability depends on whether income is Azerbaijan-source. Obtain Azerbaijani tax advice before working from the country.

taxation_system.value: Mixed worldwide-income system for residents. Depending on classification, 2026 private non-oil employment is progressive up to 14%, standard employment/non-entrepreneurial treatment can reach 25%, individual entrepreneurial profit is generally taxed at 20%, and eligible simplified taxpayers may pay turnover tax.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 182 days in a calendar year, with domestic tie-break criteria also relevant.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents generally on Azerbaijan-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Simplified tax may apply to eligible entrepreneurs; special oil-and-gas agreements have separate rules irrelevant to an ordinary software remote worker.
taxation_system.social_security: For 2026 entrepreneurial activity, compulsory state social insurance is 2% of monthly gross entrepreneurial income, with an AZN 60 minimum and AZN 400 maximum at the current AZN 400 minimum wage. Active registered individual entrepreneurs also pay AZN 16 monthly compulsory medical insurance. Employment, civil-contract, unemployment-insurance, and employer contribution rules differ.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% figure is a conservative headline/top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate for ordinary private non-oil employment or registered entrepreneurial profit. For 2026 private non-oil employment, the top marginal rate is 14%; registered individual-entrepreneur profit is generally taxed at 20%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable monthly private non-oil/non-state employment income up to AZN 2,500
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold at AZN 1.70 per USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: AZN 2,501–8,000 per month; AZN 75 plus 10% of the amount above AZN 2,500
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the upper threshold, approximately.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Above AZN 8,000 per month; AZN 625 plus 14% of the amount above AZN 8,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate for this 2026 employment category.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No threshold; taxable entrepreneurial income after allowable expenses
tax_brackets.applies_to: Individual entrepreneurs using ordinary income-tax treatment
tax_brackets.notes: Flat business-income rate, not an employment bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Standard employment income above AZN 2,500: AZN 350 plus 25% of the excess
tax_brackets.applies_to: Government/oil-and-gas employment and other standard-rate cases
tax_brackets.notes: Headline top PIT screening rate; not automatically applicable to a foreign software contract.

taxation_system.notes: Tax rates are current for 2026, but the absence of a matched remote-worker status makes contract and income-source classification especially important.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Azerbaijan has no dedicated digital-nomad tax regime. If a person becomes resident and lawfully registers as an entrepreneur, ordinary worldwide-income, business-tax, social-insurance, medical-insurance, VAT, and reporting rules may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary employment or individual-entrepreneurship classification required
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Typically 20% of taxable individual-entrepreneur profit, or potentially 2% of turnover for an eligible simplified taxpayer; employment classifications use different rates.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 182 days in a calendar year, subject to domestic tie-break criteria and treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Tax residents are generally taxable on worldwide income, with foreign tax credit relief potentially available; source and treaty analysis is required.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax regime is published.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad exemption exists. For an active individual entrepreneur, 2026 state social insurance is 2% of gross entrepreneurial income, subject to AZN 60 monthly minimum and AZN 400 maximum. Registered individual entrepreneurs also pay AZN 16 monthly compulsory medical insurance, although the health-insurance authority states that a foreign national's liability depends on whether income is Azerbaijan-source.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad-specific fixed payment applies because Azerbaijan has no such route. For an active registered individual entrepreneur, the current quantified minimum is AZN 76/month: AZN 60 minimum state social insurance plus AZN 16 compulsory medical insurance; state social insurance can rise to AZN 400/month with income.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Compulsory state social insurance is 2% of gross entrepreneurial income, with a monthly floor equal to 15% and ceiling equal to 100% of the minimum wage—currently AZN 60 and AZN 400. Compulsory medical insurance for an active registered individual entrepreneur is 4% of the minimum wage, currently AZN 16/month. Suspended entrepreneurial activity is exempt from the medical premium under the cited FAQ.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee exists. Separate adult temporary-residence-card fees depend on validity and processing speed; for up to one year the published fee is AZN 120 for 20-working-day processing or AZN 160 for 15-working-day processing.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration generally applies above AZN 200,000 taxable turnover in a consecutive 12-month period; a 1% simplified tax can apply to certain cash withdrawals from business accounts.
fixed_payments.notes: The AZN 76 minimum belongs to ordinary active individual-entrepreneur registration, not a remote-worker program. Immigration eligibility remains separate, and the health-insurance authority says foreign-national liability turns on whether income is Azerbaijan-source.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person below 183 days may still be resident under domestic personal-connection tests. If non-resident, Azerbaijan-source income can remain taxable; immigration permission to work is a separate issue.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide income is generally in scope. The foreign salary or service income must be classified as employment, entrepreneurial, or other income before the correct rate and contribution rules can be determined.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: An individual entrepreneur generally pays 20% on net taxable business income, or may qualify for simplified turnover tax. For 2026, state social insurance is 2% of gross entrepreneurial income with AZN 60–400 monthly bounds, and active registered entrepreneurs generally pay AZN 16 monthly medical insurance. VAT and reporting obligations must also be checked.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a tax scenario only. Tax registration does not create a valid immigration ground, and foreign-source treatment requires filing-level advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No matched remote-worker route exists. Temporary residence can be obtained directly only after proving another listed ground.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: At least two years of continuous qualifying temporary residence is generally required before applying under eligible permanent-residence grounds. Absence exceeding 90 days in a 180-day period breaks continuity.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The ordinary naturalization period is five years of uninterrupted permanent legal residence, calculated from issuance of the permanent-residence permit.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Approximate general minimum of two qualifying temporary-residence years plus five permanent-residence years. It is not a timeline available through an ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route and does not guarantee approval.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The cited current State Migration Service citizenship and FAQ pages describe eligibility and documents but do not publish a representative end-to-end processing duration for the final presidential naturalization decision.

key_conditions.value: Qualifying temporary and permanent residence, continuity and physical presence, sufficient funds/legal income, tax compliance, Azerbaijani language and legal-knowledge requirements, lawful conduct, and presidential approval. Permanent residence may be jeopardized by more than 180 days outside Azerbaijan in a year. Azerbaijan generally does not recognize another nationality of its citizens, so prior-nationality consequences require case-specific legal review.
key_conditions.notes: Ordinary naturalization is discretionary rather than automatic at the end of the residence period.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No separate minimum marriage duration was identified. A genuine registered marriage to an Azerbaijani citizen can support temporary residence as a close-family relationship, and permanent residence may be sought after at least two years of continuous qualifying temporary residence.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legally registered marriage to an Azerbaijani citizen can establish the close-relationship ground for temporary residence, subject to proof such as the marriage certificate and the citizen spouse's consent. Marriage does not itself change either spouse's citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to a non-citizen does not create the citizen-family ground.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally recognized and documented. The relationship ground must remain valid, residence continuity and permanent-residence requirements still apply, and ordinary citizenship still requires five years of permanent residence, legal income, Azerbaijani-language proof, and approval. False documents or sham arrangements can cause refusal, cancellation, and other liability.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates access to a residence ground, not citizenship automatically.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Azerbaijan to two foreign parents is not Azerbaijani merely by birth. Territorial citizenship is restricted mainly to children of two stateless parents and foundlings or children with unknown parents; descent from an Azerbaijani citizen is the principal rule.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Azerbaijan to two foreign parents does not acquire Azerbaijani citizenship merely by birth. A child born there to two stateless parents is Azerbaijani, and a foundling with unknown parents is also Azerbaijani.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The result differs if a parent is already an Azerbaijani citizen.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born to an Azerbaijani citizen acquires Azerbaijani citizenship by descent, including where the other parent is a foreign migrant. Registration and proof of parentage may still be required in practice.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The citizen child's status does not automatically naturalize the migrant parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A migrant parent of an Azerbaijani citizen child may have a close-family ground for temporary residence and, after qualifying residence, potentially permanent residence. Parent citizenship is not automatic and ordinary naturalization rules remain applicable.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child is Azerbaijani, a migrant father can potentially use the citizen-child close-relationship ground for residence after proving legal paternity and the family relationship. The child's citizenship does not automatically give the father permanent residence or citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Case-specific documentation and custody or consent issues should be checked with the State Migration Service.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index when checked on 2026-08-15. Rankings can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free-only category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations categorized by Passport Index as requiring a visa.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 43 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations shown separately by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 82. A separate Azerbaijani government report citing the January 2026 Henley index gave rank 67 and access to 70 destinations without a prior conventional visa; methodologies differ, so the detailed fields use one internally consistent Passport Index source.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in parts of Baku's international and technology sectors, but nationwide reliance on English is limited. EF's 2025 index scored Azerbaijan 454 and ranked it 94th, below the global average; Azerbaijani remains necessary for official procedures and long-term integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a non-official, self-selecting proficiency dataset, so it is a practical indicator rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian may be practically useful in parts of Baku and among some older or urban residents, but it is not an official language. The current official demographic material inspected did not provide a clear nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-proficiency percentage; Ukrainian should not be assumed usable for official or everyday administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The statistics site identifies census tables for native and other languages, but those tables are not equivalent to a current nationwide proficiency survey.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official AZN 1,172.1 January–April 2026 average monthly nominal salary at AZN 1.70 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official Labour Market tables, the listed 2025 Labour Market yearbook, the 2026 Azerbaijan in Figures publication, and the January–April 2026 macroeconomic release publish average wages, sector breakdowns, and related labor indicators but do not publish an all-employee national median monthly wage. A USD median therefore cannot be calculated without inventing a local-currency median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory AZN 400 monthly minimum wage at AZN 1.70 per USD; this is a legal minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official January–April 2026 average monthly nominal salary, converted approximately at AZN 1.70 per USD.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No all-worker national median is published in the current official labor landing page or the inspected current official statistical publications, so there is no supported local figure to convert to USD.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official labor publications provide averages and category or sector figures, not a national maximum salary or upper-percentile endpoint. A maximum is not a statutory labor-market measure and cannot be inferred from the highest sector average.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum monthly wage effective from 1 January 2025; no later official replacement was identified in the focused 2026 search.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly nominal salary for January–April 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The State Statistical Committee's current labor tables, 2025 Labour Market publication listing, 2026 Azerbaijan in Figures yearbook, and January–April 2026 wage release report national averages and sector figures but no all-employee national median monthly wage. The value remains null because an average or sector wage cannot substitute for a median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official national labor publications do not define or publish a maximum employee salary, observed upper endpoint, or national upper wage percentile. Sector averages are not individual salary maxima, so no local-currency maximum is entered.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official average monthly nominal employee salary and statutory minimum monthly wage; these are labor-market figures, not immigration income thresholds.
average_citizen_salary.period: January–April 2026 average; statutory minimum effective from 1 January 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and statutory minimum are official. USD figures use approximately AZN 1.70 per USD. Median and maximum remain null after focused review because the current official sources publish neither an all-worker median nor a meaningful national maximum or upper distribution endpoint.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official household-budget and price publications exist, but no single current, nationally representative monthly cost-of-living amount directly comparable to the salary figures was established. Costs vary substantially between Baku and other regions.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Kept qualitative rather than substituting a crowdsourced expatriate estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The eVisa is visitor-only and prohibits paid labor. It neither counts as qualifying permanent residence nor supplies a remote-worker settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route is available. Settlement requires a separate qualifying basis such as substantive local entrepreneurship, family, investment, or employer-sponsored work; the entrepreneurship ground's staffing and turnover requirements make it unsuitable for the requested ordinary foreign-contract profile.
settlement_track.notes: The general two-year temporary-residence plus five-year permanent-residence framework must not be presented as available to a visitor or ordinary remote worker.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign-client or foreign-employer contract is not a standalone residence ground. The visitor eVisa prohibits paid labor, employer work requires sponsorship, and entrepreneurship residence requires substantive local operations, staffing, and turnover rather than simple sole-proprietor registration.

data.notes: Focused audit preserved the negative selection but resolved the flagged entrepreneurship, fixed-payment, median-wage, and maximum-wage fields. Current official sources establish AZN 50,000 annual turnover for entrepreneurship-based temporary-residence renewal, AZN 100,000 for permanent residence, 2026 entrepreneur social insurance of 2% with AZN 60–400 monthly bounds, and AZN 16 monthly medical insurance. Official current labor publications still do not publish an all-worker national median or maximum salary, so those values remain null with precise source-based explanations.

data.selection_summary: The Bahamas is not a current match for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker seeking a citizenship-oriented residence route. The official 2022 Immigration annual report says the BEATS remote-work program was suspended until further notice; although its old tourism website remains online, its application link is obsolete and BEATS is absent from the Immigration Department’s current permit categories. A normal permit to reside prohibits work, the work permit requires an employer/sponsor and labour-market documents, sole-trader registration does not confer immigration status, and direct economic permanent residence requires a USD/BSD 1 million investment.

visa_application.title: Bahamas Immigration Online Portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official general immigration portal, not an application channel for a qualifying remote-worker route. No functioning BEATS application was found: the legacy BEATS page links to an obsolete portal, while the current Immigration Department service list omits BEATS.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The last-published official promotional terms required proof of employment but did not publish a minimum income. No current threshold exists because applications are suspended.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum-income figure was published in the captured official terms; the route is suspended.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; program suspended
income_requirement_display.notes: The historical page required proof of remote employment, medical insurance, and fees, but the Immigration Department reported the program suspended until further notice.

income_proof_months.notes: The old official page required proof of employment but did not state a bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Historical terms required a passport, medical-insurance card, and proof of employment for remote-work applicants.
The historical fee was BSD 25 to apply, BSD 1,000 for the principal remote worker, and BSD 500 per dependent.
The Department of Immigration’s 2022 annual report states that BEATS was suspended until further notice and that existing holders could apply for a permit to reside.
The current official Immigration Department service list includes work, residence, spouse, homeowner and permanent-residence permits but not BEATS.

initial_validity.value: Historically 1 year; not currently issuable on the evidence found
initial_validity.notes: The legacy marketing site remains online, but its presence is not evidence that Immigration currently accepts applications.

extension_rules.notes: No current extension or renewal rules could be established for the suspended program.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No current BEATS status can be obtained. The 2022 annual report indicated that existing holders could separately apply for a permit to reside.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A normal permit to reside is for purposes other than work and is not a remote-work legalization route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No BEATS-to-permanent-residence conversion is established. Permanent residence requires a separate qualifying category, such as long work-permit history, marriage, or economic investment.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path. General naturalisation requires separate permanent-resident status for 10 years and substantial physical residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the official Immigration Department reported BEATS suspended until further notice. The still-live promotional website is stale and its application link is not a functioning current route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is a sponsored local-employment route, not an income-threshold remote-work route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general minimum salary is published on the official application page.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; local employer sponsorship required
income_requirement_display.notes: Approval is based on the sponsored position and labour-market process rather than foreign remote income.

income_proof_months.notes: No general income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Employer/sponsor passport and business-licence or incorporation documents are required.
A Department of Labour certificate, vacancy notification, and normally three consecutive days of newspaper advertising are required.
Medical and police certificates, passport photographs, references and a BSD 200 processing fee are required.

initial_validity.value: Annual permit; official page gives an 8–12 week update window after complete filing
initial_validity.notes: The exact duration is stated on the issued permit.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is available, subject to continued sponsorship and immigration requirements.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The permit authorizes the sponsored work and residence for its stated period.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The official PR page lists persons with more than 20 consecutive years of legal work-permit status and certain scale 5–8 workers with 10–20 years of residence, but this is not direct PR and remains category-dependent.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This exceptionally long sponsored path does not fit the requested profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: A person who later obtains PR may seek citizenship after 10 years as a legal permanent resident, subject to residence and naturalisation conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer/sponsor and labour-market documentation are mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: A financial reference stating a figure range is requested, but no minimum amount is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No official minimum financial-resources figure was found.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient financial evidence required; no published minimum
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Financial-institution reference stating a figure range and/or CPA statement
income_requirement_display.notes: The permit is expressly for living for a purpose other than working.

income_proof_months.notes: No statement-history period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Official eligibility is stated for students and dependants of persons legally authorized to reside in The Bahamas or Bahamian citizens.
The permit is for residence for purposes other than working; gainful occupation requires a work permit.
Police and medical certificates, financial reference, passport, photographs and a BSD 200 processing fee are required.

initial_validity.value: Annual permit
initial_validity.notes: The fee schedule charges for each year or part of a year.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is available subject to continued eligibility and approval.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct annual permission to reside for an eligible non-working purpose.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No general conversion from this non-working annual permit to PR is published.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A person would need to qualify separately under a listed PR category.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path is established. Naturalisation requires separate PR status and the statutory residence conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because remote work is gainful occupation and is not authorized by this residence-only permit.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Business registration is turnover-based and is not an immigration income route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum personal income is prescribed for immigration because the licence grants no immigration status.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration income threshold; business-licence tax depends on turnover
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: BSD 100 at turnover up to BSD 50,000 under the current DIR FAQ; percentage rates apply above that
income_requirement_display.notes: Tax/business registration does not authorize a foreigner to reside or work.

income_proof_months.notes: Not an immigration route.

key_requirements.requirement: A person operating a business in The Bahamas must obtain a business licence; sole traders can apply for a trade name and online licence.
National Insurance registration and relevant agency approvals may be required during business licensing.
A residence permit does not permit gainful occupation without a work permit.

initial_validity.value: Business licence only; no residence status

extension_rules.value: Business licences have renewal and annual tax obligations, but renewal does not legalize immigration status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None. Visitor entry or a residence-only permit cannot be converted merely by registering a business.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None through business registration alone.

path_to_citizenship.value: None through business registration alone.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because commercial registration and immigration permission are separate. Entering as a visitor, opening a business, or registering as a sole trader does not create lawful remote-work residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is an investment route, not an income route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: BSD/USD 1,000,000 qualifying investment
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Official page permits qualifying real estate or Central Bank zero-coupon bonds held for at least 10 years.

income_requirement_display.value: USD/BSD 1,000,000 investment
income_requirement_display.notes: Outside the applicant profile because substantial capital investment is mandatory.

income_proof_months.notes: Investment documentation replaces a monthly-income test.

key_requirements.requirement: Minimum USD/BSD 1 million investment in real estate or Central Bank zero-coupon bonds.
The qualifying asset must be held for at least 10 years.
Police, medical, character, civil-status, immigration-status and investment/property documentation are required.

initial_validity.value: Lifetime permanent-residence status unless revoked

extension_rules.value: No routine renewal of lifetime status; it remains subject to revocation and any employment restriction endorsed on the certificate.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; this is direct PR.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence if the discretionary application and investment requirements are approved.

path_to_citizenship.value: General citizenship eligibility follows after 10 years holding legal permanent-resident status, including the immediately preceding 12 months, plus the stated residence history.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation remains discretionary and normally requires renunciation of other citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: A strong settlement alternative for a qualifying investor, but expressly excluded from this ordinary remote-worker selection.

summary.value: A person attending a Bahamian school, college or university can apply for an annual permit to reside without a local employer. It is a non-working temporary status, provides no direct PR, and is not an independent skilled or degree-based migration program for a graduate software engineer.
summary.notes: Possessing a university degree by itself creates no residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: There are no individual residency or domicile requirements for Bahamian tax purposes because The Bahamas currently has no personal income tax.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence, NIB coverage, business licensing, VAT, and tax-residence certificates are separate questions.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Current screening rate: no personal income tax. This does not mean zero total tax or contributions.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Current published self-employed NIB contribution rate effective from 1 July 2024. Applicability requires lawful gainful employment in The Bahamas; the suspended BEATS route does not currently provide that status.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment applies to a foreign remote worker because no current route exists. Self-employed NIB is percentage-based rather than fixed. At the published BSD 3,510 monthly ceiling, 10.3% would be BSD/USD 361.53, but that is a maximum contribution calculation, not a fixed minimum.

special_tax_regimes.value: No active digital-nomad tax regime was found. The general system has no PIT, while a locally operated business may face business-licence tax, VAT registration and NIB obligations.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The old BEATS status should not be used as the basis for current tax planning.

taxes.caveats: Zero PIT does not legalize remote work and does not eliminate NIB, VAT, business-licence tax, property taxes, customs duties, home-country tax, payroll obligations or employer permanent-establishment risk. Contract structure and any foreign-country tax residence must be reviewed separately.

taxation_system.value: No personal income tax; indirect, turnover-based business, property and social-insurance charges may apply.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No individual tax-residence or domicile requirements for PIT purposes.
taxation_system.income_scope: Personal employment, self-employment and investment income are not subject to a broad Bahamian PIT under the current system.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No current remote-worker or BEATS-specific tax regime confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: NIB states that persons gainfully employed in The Bahamas must register. The current published self-employed rate is 10.3%, subject to the insurable-income ceiling.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable: there is no progressive personal income tax.
taxation_system.notes: The displayed 0% is the current PIT rate, not a statement that all taxes and mandatory charges are zero.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No current digital-nomad taxation scenario can be confirmed because BEATS is suspended. If a person separately becomes lawfully self-employed or operates a Bahamian business, PIT remains 0%, but NIB, business-licence and potentially VAT obligations can arise.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: suspended_remote_worker_program; general no-PIT system only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% personal income tax; other charges may apply
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No individual residency or domicile test for PIT under the current no-PIT system.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: No broad Bahamian PIT is currently imposed on personal foreign income, but home-country taxation and business presence risks remain.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None currently active or confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A lawful self-employed person working in The Bahamas is generally within NIB registration and contribution rules; the published self-employed rate is 10.3% subject to the ceiling.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly remote-worker payment established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based NIB; 10.3% for self-employed persons, not a fixed amount.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Historical BEATS fees were BSD 25 application plus BSD 1,000 principal permit and BSD 500 per dependent, but applications are suspended.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: DIR states business-licence tax is BSD 100 at turnover up to BSD 50,000, with percentage rates above; VAT registration is generally mandatory when taxable activity exceeds BSD 100,000 over a past or expected 12-month period.
fixed_payments.notes: These business charges do not create immigration permission.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No PIT day-count threshold applies, but visitor status does not authorize gainful occupation and may leave home-country tax obligations intact.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no current lawful BEATS route to model. A person with another lawful status still faces 0% Bahamian PIT but must assess work authorization, NIB and business obligations.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A licensed local sole trader may face NIB, annual business-licence tax and VAT rules, but business registration alone supplies no residence or work authorization.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the general no-PIT and published NIB/business rules; no current digital-nomad-specific treatment exists to confirm.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying remote-worker route is currently open. Annual non-working residence is a separate, ineligible category.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No BEATS or ordinary foreign-contract remote-work conversion timeline is published.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General eligibility requires 10 years holding legal permanent-resident status; approval is not automatic.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated for the requested profile because there is no current qualifying entry route or defined time to PR.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official citizenship page publishes document requirements and fees but no typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires 10 years of legal PR status, including the 12 months immediately before filing, and at least six years' residence during the preceding nine years. Statutory conditions include good character, sufficient English and knowledge of citizen responsibilities, intent to make The Bahamas the permanent home, oath of allegiance, and normally prior renunciation of other citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary. The captured sources do not publish a simple absence-limit formula beyond the statutory residence periods.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Five years of a subsisting, cohabiting marriage is the published PR threshold for a spouse of a Bahamian. Citizenship rules are gendered: the official page separately lists a female spouse as eligible to apply and lists male spouses under another form, without publishing a universal marriage-duration threshold.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Bahamian can support a resident-spouse permit and counts toward the five-year marriage threshold for spouse PR if the marriage remains subsisting and the couple cohabit. Marriage to another foreign national does not independently accelerate citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The resident-spouse permit allows residence and work and historically could be issued for up to five years, but it is a family route, not relevant to the assumed applicant unless the spouse is Bahamian.

requirements_and_risks.value: The spouse route requires proof of marriage, the Bahamian spouse's nationality, civil-status documents, police and medical certificates, and scrutiny of whether the marriage subsists. PR remains discretionary. False statements or a sham marriage can cause refusal, cancellation and immigration or criminal consequences; naturalisation may also require renouncing another citizenship.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Do not treat marriage as automatic citizenship. Current law and official forms retain important gender distinctions, so filing-specific legal review is advisable.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in The Bahamas is automatically a citizen at birth when either parent is Bahamian. A child born there to two non-citizen parents is not automatically a citizen but has a constitutional right to apply at age 18 and within the following 12 months, subject to renunciation and public-policy qualifications.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship at birth. A Bahamas-born person whose parents were both non-citizens may apply for registration on attaining age 18 or within 12 months afterward; if already a citizen of another country, renunciation and a residence-intention declaration are required.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is deferred, conditional registration rather than jus soli at birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: For a child born in The Bahamas after 9 July 1973, citizenship is automatic at birth if either parent is a Bahamian citizen. Rules for children born abroad are more gender- and marital-status-dependent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth or later registration of a citizen child does not automatically grant either foreign parent residence, PR or citizenship. No general citizen-child sponsorship shortcut for the parent was found in the current official categories.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any parent must qualify under a separate immigration category.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic status merely because the child is or later becomes Bahamian. If the mother is Bahamian and the child is born in The Bahamas, the child is a citizen, but the father still needs a spouse, work, residence or other qualifying permit.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 15 August 2026. Passport rankings can change frequently.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index; this is not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Calculated from 45 visa-on-arrival plus 9 eTA destinations. Passport Index displayed an overall mobility score of 152.

passport.notes: For comparison, the official Henley 2026 table ranked The Bahamas 21st with access to 158 destinations, but Henley combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access and does not provide the requested separate breakdown on its ranking page.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very practical linguistically: English is the official language and is used in government, business and education.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Practicality of internet service, housing and immigration permission must be assessed separately.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and no government-wide service availability in either language was found. English should be expected for applications and daily business.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Certified English translations are required for foreign-language immigration documents.
