settlement_track.summary: No current independent foreign-remote-worker route is confirmed. BEATS is suspended; ordinary residence does not permit work, and the remaining settlement routes require a local employer, family eligibility or a USD/BSD 1 million investment.
settlement_track.notes: The general ten-year post-PR naturalisation rule does not cure the absence of a qualifying route for this applicant.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: BEATS is suspended, a residence permit prohibits gainful occupation, and the current work permit requires a sponsor. Business registration alone does not change immigration status.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Bahamas record using current web research. The main conclusion remains ineligible, but the evidence is stronger: the official 2022 Immigration report expressly records BEATS as suspended until further notice. Tax, family, child-citizenship, passport, NIB, minimum-wage and historical official wage fields were also normalized. Remaining nulls are explained where no current official value or applicable route exists.

data.selection_summary: Bahrain does not currently offer a dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Independent residence options require substantial investment, property ownership, retirement income, prior Bahrain employment, or exceptional-talent approval; ordinary employment requires a Bahrain work permit and local employer. None matches the requested profile, although qualifying Golden Residency categories grant permanent residence and general naturalization may be requested separately after 20 years of consecutive legal residence for a non-Arab applicant.

visa_application.title: Bahrain Electronic Visa Service
visa_application.notes: This is Bahrain's official general visa portal, not a remote-worker application page. Golden Residency has a separate official portal, but its categories require property, qualifying prior Bahrain employment or retirement, pension income, or approved exceptional talent.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This category uses a property-value threshold rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: BHD 130,000 minimum total personal share value in qualifying Bahrain property
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current official Golden Residency materials show BHD 130,000, reduced from BHD 200,000 in November 2025.

income_requirement_display.value: BHD 130,000 property investment (approximately USD 345,000); no monthly-income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: This is capital tied to Bahrain property ownership, not recurring foreign-contract income.

income_proof_months.notes: The official document list requires the latest six-month bank statement.

key_requirements.requirement: Own one or more Bahrain properties whose combined personal share value was at least BHD 130,000 at purchase.
Provide a passport valid for more than six months, a six-month bank statement, Bahrain-valid health insurance, address evidence, and the property deed or deeds.
Pay a BHD 5 application fee and BHD 300 residence-issuance fee if approved.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residency, with residence documentation handled in 10-year periods
initial_validity.notes: The official program describes the status as permanent residency.

extension_rules.value: No minimum stay is required; continued validity remains subject to program and legal conditions, with residence documentation handled in 10-year periods.
extension_rules.notes: Applicants should confirm cancellation and continued-eligibility rules for their specific category.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval grants Golden Residency directly rather than an ordinary temporary remote-work permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is an investment-based route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent Golden Residency is available after approval.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: It is excluded from selection because substantial property investment is mandatory.

path_to_citizenship.value: There is no automatic citizenship conversion. A separate nationality application generally requires 20 years of consecutive legal residence for a non-Arab applicant, Arabic ability, registered property, good conduct, and mental competence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality service does not guarantee naturalization or expressly confirm route-specific counting for Golden Residency.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires approximately USD 345,000 of Bahrain property. It is settlement-oriented permanent residence but not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of BHD 500 using Bahrain's official fixed rate of BHD 1 = USD 2.65.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least BHD 500 stable monthly income, plus an ownership share of at least BHD 100,000 in an eligible Bahrain enterprise
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The business-ownership condition makes this an investor route rather than a foreign-contract freelancer route.

income_requirement_display.value: BHD 500 monthly stable income plus BHD 100,000 minimum enterprise share
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: BHD monthly income plus capital ownership
income_requirement_display.notes: The USD value represents only the monthly-income component, not the required enterprise investment.

income_proof_months.notes: Recent three-month personal and company bank statements are required.

key_requirements.requirement: Hold at least a BHD 100,000 share in an eligible Bahrain enterprise.
Show lawful stable income of at least BHD 500, bank statements, commercial registration, accommodation, good-conduct documentation, and Bahrain-issued health insurance.
The guarantor or an authorized person submits through the national eGovernment channel.

initial_validity.value: 2, 5, or 10 years
initial_validity.notes: Published residence fees are BHD 200, BHD 400, or BHD 600 respectively, plus application and applicable transfer fees.

extension_rules.value: Renewable in 2-, 5-, or 10-year periods while investor, income, insurance, and documentation requirements remain satisfied.
extension_rules.notes: The official service establishes renewal but not automatic permanent-residence conversion.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct self-sponsored residence is available after establishing the required Bahrain enterprise ownership and meeting the other conditions.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A foreign software-engineering contract alone is insufficient.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official self-sponsorship pages inspected do not establish an automatic transition from this time-limited investor permit to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: A separate general nationality application may potentially be made after the applicable consecutive legal-residence period; the published period for a non-Arab applicant is 20 years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Approval is not automatic, and the nationality page does not explain route-specific treatment of self-sponsored investor residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because substantial ownership in a Bahrain enterprise is mandatory. A normal foreign-client contract and software-engineering degree alone do not qualify.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary employment or Registered Worker Permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general salary threshold relevant to an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Requirements depend on the locally permitted occupation and employer or restricted registered-worker category; there is no general remote-worker threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No general remote-worker income threshold; a Bahrain work permit and qualifying local legal basis are required
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status cannot be used for employment. The Registered Worker Permit is not an entry route: the person must already be in Bahrain with a terminated prior work permit, and visit-visa holders are ineligible.

income_proof_months.notes: The official Registered Worker service does not publish a general income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Ordinary expatriate employment requires an official work permit obtained through a Bahrain employer before arrival.
The Registered Worker Permit requires presence in Bahrain with a terminated prior work permit; visit-visa holders are ineligible.
Working on a visit visa is prohibited and can result in fines and deportation.

initial_validity.notes: The inspected initial Registered Worker Permit page does not state one universal initial duration.

extension_rules.value: Registered Worker permits may be renewed for six months or one year, subject to continued eligibility and applicable fees.
extension_rules.notes: This does not make the program an application-from-abroad route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Possible only after obtaining the appropriate local work or registered-worker permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not legalize ordinary foreign-client work from visitor status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official Registered Worker pages do not establish a direct permanent-residence transition.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only the separate general naturalization framework could potentially apply after long consecutive legal residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No LMRA permit-specific citizenship pathway is published.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because ordinary employment requires a local employer, while the limited Registered Worker program requires a terminated prior Bahrain work permit and is unavailable to visitors or first-time applicants from abroad.

summary.value: No ordinary degree-based independent skilled-migration route was found. Golden Residency for talented individuals may cover entrepreneurs, researchers, scientists, innovators, athletes, creators, and other exceptional talent, but it requires exceptional evidence and specialized committee approval rather than merely a software-engineering degree.
summary.notes: A relevant university degree alone does not establish eligibility for independent residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: Bahrain has no personal income tax regime, so residence is not defined for personal-income-tax purposes.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax-residence certificates and treaty questions can still require separate analysis, but there is no domestic PIT day-count threshold comparable to a 183-day rule.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the general no-PIT screening rate, not a special digital-nomad rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The displayed 1% is the employee share for an expatriate employed by a Bahrain person, entity, or enterprise. The current expatriate-employment total is 4% of wages—3% employer and 1% employee. This is not a contribution rule for the requested foreign-contract scenario, which has no corresponding Bahrain immigration status.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal fixed monthly payment for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker because Bahrain has no corresponding immigration status. Local employment uses percentage-based contributions; permit, insurance, and end-of-service charges depend on a different legal status and cannot be reduced to one universal USD amount.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. Bahrain generally imposes no personal income tax.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business registration, VAT, social insurance, municipal charges, and taxation in other jurisdictions remain separate issues.

taxes.caveats: Zero Bahrain personal income tax does not authorize remote work or eliminate tax exposure in the payer's country, a former tax residence, or another treaty jurisdiction. A locally registered business may face VAT, accounting, commercial-registration, or sector-specific obligations.

taxation_system.value: Bahrain imposes no personal income tax on individuals; locally employed persons can be subject to Social Insurance Organisation contributions, and independent economic activity can trigger VAT obligations.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence is not defined for PIT purposes because Bahrain has no personal income tax regime.
taxation_system.income_scope: Individual employment income, capital gains, and foreign income are not taxed under a Bahrain personal income tax regime.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker PIT regime is published.
taxation_system.social_security: For expatriates employed by a Bahrain person, entity, or enterprise, current guidance reports 1% employee and 3% employer contributions, remitted by the employer. Different rules apply to Bahrainis and GCC nationals.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable because Bahrain has no progressive personal-income-tax brackets.
taxation_system.notes: PwC's Bahrain individual summaries were last reviewed on 26 July 2026. The screening conclusion is strong, but individual contract, payment, business, and treaty facts still require professional advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or route-specific tax treatment exists. A person lawfully residing under another category is subject to Bahrain's general zero-PIT system, with local-employment social insurance and business/VAT rules applying where relevant.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; general Bahrain individual tax rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% personal income tax; this does not confer immigration or work authorization
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No PIT residence definition because Bahrain has no PIT regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign income is not subject to Bahrain personal income tax under the current system. Social-insurance treatment depends on whether the income is paid through Bahrain employment.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None published.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A locally employed expatriate generally contributes 1%, with a 3% Bahrain-employer contribution. This rule does not create or validate a foreign-contract remote-work route.

fixed_payments.status: No universal remote-worker fixed payment exists because Bahrain has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker status.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Not applicable as a fixed payment for the requested scenario. Qualifying local employment uses percentage-based contributions rather than a universal monthly amount.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Golden Residency: BHD 5 application and BHD 300 issuance fee. Investor self-sponsorship: BHD 5 application plus BHD 200, BHD 400, or BHD 600 for 2, 5, or 10 years and applicable transfer fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT is 10%. Economic activity exceeding BHD 37,500 of annual taxable supplies generally requires VAT registration; voluntary registration is available from BHD 18,750.
fixed_payments.notes: Bahrain-valid health insurance is required for relevant residence categories, but the inspected sources do not publish a universal premium. Charges for work permits, commercial registration, insurance, or end-of-service benefits depend on a different status.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no Bahrain PIT residence-day threshold. A short visitor stay remains subject to immigration and work restrictions despite the absence of PIT.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no recognized digital-nomad tax category. Zero Bahrain PIT does not make visitor-based remote work lawful or resolve foreign tax residence.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Bahrain-registered economic activity may face commercial-registration, licensing, VAT, accounting, and sector-specific obligations; VAT registration generally becomes mandatory above BHD 37,500 of annual taxable supplies.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax conclusions are suitable for screening only; contract structure, payment location, business registration, treaty position, and prior-country residence require individualized advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary remote-worker route exists, so there is no matched temporary-residence timeline.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Property-owner Golden Residency grants permanent residence directly but is an excluded investment route. No conversion timeline was confirmed for an ordinary foreign-contract worker or the time-limited investor self-sponsorship permit.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Bahrain states its general naturalization condition in terms of consecutive legal residence, not a published number of years after obtaining permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The published general threshold is 20 years of consecutive legal residence for a non-Arab applicant and 10 years for an Arab applicant. This is not a guaranteed outcome or a timeline from a matched remote-worker route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official nationality service does not publish a standard processing period, so an exact month figure cannot be established.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires the applicant to be in Bahrain when applying, have the required consecutive legal residence, a good command of Arabic, registered Bahrain property, good conduct, and mental competence.
key_conditions.notes: The official page does not state that satisfying these conditions guarantees approval or publish detailed absence limits beyond consecutive residence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign wife of a Bahraini man may acquire nationality after declaring her wish and continuing to reside with him in Bahrain for five years; the Interior Minister may waive some or all of the period. The provision is gender-specific.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Bahraini man allows a foreign wife to use the citizenship service, but the statutory period depends on the declaration and continued residence with the husband. Marriage between two migrants provides no acceleration.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The applicant profile does not state marriage to a Bahraini citizen.

requirements_and_risks.value: The foreign wife must provide valid residence and authenticated marriage, identity, and family documents. The marriage and co-residence normally must continue during the qualifying period, and acquisition remains subject to ministerial decision. False documentation or a sham marriage can lead to refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The facilitated citizenship provision is discretionary and sex-specific; it should not be assumed to apply equally to a foreign husband of a Bahraini woman.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Bahrain primarily transmits nationality through a Bahraini father. Birth in Bahrain alone is insufficient; narrow provisions cover children of unknown parents and certain children of Bahraini mothers where the father is unknown or paternity is not legally established.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Bahrain to two known foreign parents does not automatically acquire Bahraini citizenship. The narrow foundling or unknown-parent provision does not cover an ordinary migrant family.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The child may inherit foreign nationality under a parent's national law.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in or outside Bahrain is Bahraini if the father was Bahraini at birth. A Bahraini mother and known foreign father do not produce automatic citizenship under the captured rule unless the father is unknown or paternity is not legally established.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The one-citizen-parent outcome is sex-dependent, so the country-level boolean is true only in qualifying cases.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth in Bahrain does not independently legalize or naturalize migrant parents. Family residence may be available only where the child or other parent is Bahraini and the applicable family-service requirements are met.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic permanent residence or citizenship for a migrant parent was found.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically obtain citizenship because his child is Bahraini or has a Bahraini mother. Any family residence requires a separate qualifying basis.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The marriage-based nationality facilitation is directed to foreign wives of Bahraini men, not foreign husbands of Bahraini women.

rank.notes: Passport Index Passport Power Rank checked on 2026-08-15; this is not the Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's category requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 41 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations. Together with 51 visa-free destinations, this produces the reported mobility score of 99.

passport.notes: Passport-index methodologies differ. Passport Index was retained because it publishes a separated visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, and visa-required breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is commonly used in Bahrain's business sector, so everyday professional life is generally practical in English. Arabic remains the official language and is required for general naturalization.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English-language practicality does not create immigration or work authorization.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and the authoritative sources inspected do not establish broad use in government or business. Applicants should expect English or Arabic to be needed for most procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national data on Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q1 2026 average BHD 931 monthly salary for Bahraini SIO contributors across public and private sectors. It is a citizen-contributor statistic, not an all-resident or software-engineer salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q1 2026 median BHD 618 monthly salary for Bahraini SIO contributors.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official Q1 2026 distribution reports 2,221 Bahraini contributors in an open-ended band below BHD 200 per month. It does not publish the lowest observed wage or establish a universal statutory minimum, so an exact USD minimum cannot be derived.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: BHD 931 multiplied by the official fixed rate of USD 2.65 per BHD and rounded to the nearest dollar.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: BHD 618 multiplied by the official fixed rate of USD 2.65 per BHD and rounded to the nearest dollar.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official distribution's highest Bahraini salary band is open-ended at BHD 1,000 per month or more. It does not publish the largest observed wage, so an exact USD maximum cannot be derived.

min_salary_local_currency.value: Exact minimum unpublished; the official Q1 2026 distribution's lowest Bahraini-contributor band is below BHD 200 per month
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is an open-ended insured-salary band, not a statutory minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average for 158,322 Bahraini public- and private-sector SIO contributors in Q1 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median for Bahraini public- and private-sector SIO contributors in Q1 2026.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Exact maximum unpublished; the official Q1 2026 distribution's highest Bahraini-contributor band is BHD 1,000 per month or more
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The top band contains 42,105 Bahraini contributors and has no upper boundary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly insured salary of Bahraini Social Insurance Organisation contributors across public and private sectors
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 monthly salary snapshot
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are official average-citizen contributor wages, not immigration income thresholds and not salaries for all expatriate residents. Exact numeric minimum and maximum remain null because the published distribution uses open-ended bands.

cost_of_living_note.value: For practical orientation, Numbeo, updated 5 June 2026, reported average Bahrain prices of BHD 343.83 per month for a one-bedroom apartment in a city centre, BHD 235.25 outside a centre, BHD 48.66 per month for basic utilities for an 85 m² apartment, BHD 15.51 per month for broadband, and BHD 13.20 for a monthly public-transport pass. Bahrain's official statistics portal publishes CPI series and identifies the 2024 Household Income and Expenditure Survey as its principal standard-of-living survey, but the official pages inspected do not publish a single current one-person monthly living-cost benchmark.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The item prices are a non-official crowdsourced snapshot based on 732 entries from 64 contributors in the preceding 12 months, so they are indicative rather than a guaranteed budget. Rent, household size, neighborhood, schooling, car use, and expatriate utility tariffs can materially change actual costs. The official CPI sources track price changes but do not convert the basket into a universal monthly budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor or eVisa status is not a remote-work residence route, and Bahrain's labor authority expressly warns that work on a visit visa is prohibited.
settlement_track.summary: Bahrain has permanent Golden Residency and renewable self-sponsorship categories, but independently accessible categories require property, investment, retirement income, prior Bahrain employment, or exceptional talent. No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route exists, so this profile has no qualifying settlement track.
settlement_track.notes: The general 20-year naturalization rule for non-Arabs does not cure the absence of an eligible initial residence and work route and does not guarantee citizenship.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official residence catalogue contains no digital-nomad or foreign-client remote-worker category. Golden Residency requires investment, retirement, prior Bahrain work, or exceptional talent; ordinary work requires a local permit, and the Registered Worker program is unavailable to visitors or first-time applicants from abroad.

data.notes: Focused unexplained-null audit completed against the previous Bahrain record. The flagged cost-of-living gap is now filled with a dated, clearly caveated practical price snapshot and cross-checked against Bahrain's official CPI and household-survey resources. The underlying route conclusion remains unchanged: no ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was found. Numeric salary minima and maxima remain null only because the official Q1 2026 wage distribution uses open-ended bands rather than publishing observed endpoints.

data.selection_summary: No current official digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary self-employed residence route was found. Bangladesh offers ordinary visas, employer-linked E2/E3 work channels, and investor routes, including an officially advertised investment-based permanent-residence option, but these do not fit an ordinary software engineer working for a foreign client without local sponsorship or substantial investment.

visa_application.title: Bangladesh Online MRV Portal
visa_application.notes: This official portal starts applications for new visas, extensions, No Visa Required endorsements, and on-arrival visas. The completed form must normally be printed and submitted with documents and fees to a Bangladesh mission or visa office. It is a general visa channel, not a remote-worker residence application.

rejected_routes.route_name: E2/E3 employment visa and work-permit channel

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum remote-work income exists; eligibility instead depends on qualifying employment, contracting, installation, supervision, or project activity in Bangladesh.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official route information does not set a monthly-income threshold; eligibility is based on the Bangladesh employer or project relationship.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; qualifying Bangladesh employment or project activity is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer/project channel rather than an income-based independent visa.

income_proof_months.notes: The current official BIDA materials require a service contract or appointment/transfer document and employer manpower information showing salary details, but they do not prescribe any retrospective number of bank-statement, payslip, or income-history months. The value remains null because this employer-sponsored route uses employer and contract evidence rather than a standardized months-of-income test.

key_requirements.requirement: E2 covers expatriates working for government, autonomous, private, industrial, commercial, branch, liaison, representative, contractor, or project organizations in Bangladesh.
E3 is for machinery or software installation, maintenance supervision, or project inspection, not continuing foreign-client remote work.

The employer files the work-permit application through BIDA OSS; required evidence includes the appropriate visa, service contract or appointment document, employer/company records, qualifications, and salary/manpower information.
Security clearance must be requested through BIDA OSS within the period specified in the work permit; failure to do so can invalidate the permit.

initial_validity.value: Up to 6 months with multiple entries; the BIDA handbook describes a 90-day-per-stay condition for the installation, maintenance, or project-inspection category.
initial_validity.notes: The visa is tied to the approved Bangladesh employment or project purpose and is not an independent residence permit.

extension_rules.value: The BIDA handbook states that E2/E3 employment visas may be extended for the work-permit period plus 15 days, for 30 days while work permit or police clearance is pending, and further in line with a renewed work permit plus 15 days.
extension_rules.notes: A first extension requires a TIN certificate and later extensions require income-tax clearance; continuing employer/project eligibility remains necessary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The visa and work permit can support a temporary Bangladesh employment assignment, but the reviewed sources do not identify it as an independently obtainable residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Local employment or qualifying project activity remains essential.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current BIDA and Home Affairs materials do not publish an ordinary employment-to-permanent-residence transition. Home Affairs identifies separate permanent-residence services, but not a routine conversion from E2/E3 employment.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalization law exists, but no official source confirms that this employment channel creates a routine settlement sequence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: It is not a usable independent remote-worker citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because E2/E3 eligibility is tied to work for a Bangladesh organization, contractor, project, or local installation/inspection activity. A normal foreign-client software contract is insufficient.

rejected_routes.route_name: PI investor visa and investment-based permanent residence or citizenship

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is capital-based, not monthly-income-based.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The published thresholds are denominated in US dollars and require non-repatriable investment or transfer.

income_requirement_display.value: Capital route: Bangladesh Bank advertises permanent residence from a minimum US$75,000 non-repatriable investment; verify the current filing threshold before relying on it
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: USD investment capital, not monthly income
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: US$75,000 non-repatriable investment advertised for permanent residence
income_requirement_display.notes: A Bangladesh embassy FAQ contains inconsistent wording about a US$100,000 minimum while also repeating US$75,000. This route requires filing-level confirmation and is excluded from the profile because substantial investment is required.

income_proof_months.notes: No monthly income-history test applies. The route instead requires investment capital, a business plan, authority recommendation, and evidence of the Bangladesh investment.

key_requirements.requirement: PI visa eligibility requires investment in a private industrial or commercial establishment in Bangladesh.
Bangladesh Bank advertises permanent residence for at least US$75,000 of non-repatriable investment.
Bangladesh Bank advertises citizenship for at least US$500,000 of investment or a US$1,000,000 transfer to a recognized financial institution, with the funds non-repatriable.

The BIDA handbook requires a bona fide investment, detailed business plan, proposed investment amount, local establishment and employment information, and recommendation from the competent investment authority.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year with multiple entries
initial_validity.notes: The handbook states passport validity must be at least 180 days; the visa remains dependent on a bona fide approved investment.

extension_rules.value: The PI visa may be extended up to 5 years, subject to current official recommendation and evidence that the Bangladesh investment and receiving company continue.
extension_rules.notes: Extension evidence includes the relevant authority recommendation, company registration and tax-payment documents, and a work permit if the investor works in the company.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A PI visa can support an approved foreign investor's stay and related work-permit process.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not an ordinary freelance or remote-worker route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: An official Bangladesh Bank investment-facilities page advertises permanent residence from a non-repatriable investment, but the exact current threshold and application mechanics require confirmation.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Official pages conflict between US$75,000 and wording referring to US$100,000. Home Affairs confirms that a permanent-residence certificate service exists but does not resolve the threshold conflict on its contact page.

path_to_citizenship.value: Direct investor citizenship is advertised for substantial non-repatriable capital and supported by a government-gazette certificate framework.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is outside the applicant profile and is not evidence of an ordinary residence-to-naturalization route.

rejected_routes.notes: Although independent and potentially settlement-oriented, this route is rejected because it requires substantial non-repatriable investment. A foreign software contract does not qualify on its own.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker income requirement; this is only the general visa channel
income_requirement_display.notes: The application form lists tourism, employment, business, study, investment and other purposes, but not digital-nomad or foreign-remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The general portal and application form do not create a remote-worker category or prescribe a standardized remote-work income-history period. Category-specific missions may request financial evidence for a visit, but that would not establish remote-work eligibility.

key_requirements.requirement: Complete the online form, print it, and submit it with category-specific documents and fees to the nearest Bangladesh mission or visa office.
A visitor or ordinary visa does not itself authorize self-employment or create qualifying residence.

initial_validity.notes: Validity depends on the selected visa purpose, requested duration, nationality, and issuing decision; there is no single visitor duration applicable to every ordinary application.

extension_rules.value: The general portal supports extension applications, but extension does not convert a visitor into a remote-worker resident.
extension_rules.notes: Category-specific approval is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The current official visa-processing materials do not identify a visitor-to-independent-residence conversion.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Home Affairs identifies a separate permanent-residence certificate service but does not publish any path to it from an ordinary visitor application.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The citizenship rules provide only discretionary citizenship consideration after ordinary residence—normally five years for applicants outside the foreign-wife category—while the current immigration and Home Affairs pages identify visa processing and citizenship/permanent-residence services but no conversion from an ordinary visitor visa. Visitor status therefore supplies neither a confirmed qualifying residence basis nor a routine citizenship path.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an ordinary visa, visa extension, or visitor stay is not a remote-work residence program and has no confirmed settlement conversion.

summary.value: The official visa form includes study as a purpose, so a student can apply without an employer after securing the relevant educational basis. No degree-only skilled migration route, post-study permanent-residence route, or qualification-based independent residence program was found for the applicant's existing software-engineering degree.
summary.notes: A study visa is education-specific and is not a route for continuing ordinary foreign-client remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident for an income year after at least 183 days in Bangladesh, or after at least 90 days in that year plus at least 365 days in the preceding four years.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence is tested separately for each income year.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the current top marginal or screening rate for the 2026-27 assessment structure, not an expected effective rate. A non-resident foreign individual is also generally screened at the maximum 30% rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No universal self-employed or digital-nomad contribution percentage was established. Workers, including foreign nationals, in covered private establishments may contribute 7% to 8% of salary to a provident fund with a matching employer contribution, but that employment rule does not map to foreign-client remote work.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory monthly remote-worker payment exists because there is no remote-worker status. General annual minimum income tax and employer-route work-permit fees are not monthly digital-nomad charges and therefore are not converted into a monthly USD value.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, freelancer, remittance-basis, or inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. General resident/non-resident rules apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Investment and approved-industry incentives are separate and do not benefit an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker automatically.

taxes.caveats: Remote work physically performed in Bangladesh may be treated as Bangladesh-earned income even when paid abroad. Residents are within worldwide-income scope, while non-residents are taxed on Bangladesh-source or Bangladesh-received income. Contract characterization, permanent-establishment risk, foreign tax credits, treaty relief, and immigration legality require professional review.

taxation_system.value: Progressive resident-individual income tax; non-resident foreign individuals are generally taxable at the maximum 30% rate. Residents fall within worldwide-income scope and may claim treaty or statutory foreign-tax relief where available.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 days in the income year, or at least 90 days in that year plus at least 365 days during the preceding four years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: worldwide income accrued, arisen, or received during the year. Non-residents: Bangladesh-source or Bangladesh-received income. Employment income earned through activity in Bangladesh can be Bangladesh-source wherever paid.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: No universal contribution was confirmed for an independent foreign remote worker. Covered-establishment employees may contribute 7% to 8% of salary to a provident fund, matched by the employer.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value is the 30% top marginal rate, not the effective rate. The FY2026-27 budget originally showed a BDT375,000 exemption; government reporting on the final Finance Bill says it was raised to BDT400,000. The remaining bands reflect the enacted-budget structure reported at the research date and should be checked against the final gazette before filing.

tax_brackets.notes: Final threshold reported after Finance Bill passage; approximately converted at BDT123.82 per US$1.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next BDT 300,000; cumulative income up to approximately BDT 700,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate cumulative USD boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next BDT 400,000; cumulative income up to approximately BDT 1,100,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate cumulative USD boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next BDT 500,000; cumulative income up to approximately BDT 1,600,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate cumulative USD boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next BDT 2,000,000; cumulative income up to approximately BDT 3,600,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate cumulative USD boundary.

tax_brackets.applies_to: General resident individual; also maximum-rate screening for a non-resident foreign individual
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not the effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The residence and worldwide-income rules are taken from the authentic English Income Tax Act text. Final 2026 Finance Bill reporting changed the basic exemption after the budget proposal, so the final gazette should be checked before filing.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a visa-specific regime because Bangladesh has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. A person nevertheless working from Bangladesh could encounter ordinary source and residence taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; hypothetical foreign remote worker under ordinary individual tax rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% screening rate; residents use progressive brackets, while a non-resident foreign individual may be taxed at the maximum rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183 days, or 90 days plus 365 days in the preceding four years
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is included for residents. For non-residents, Bangladesh-source or Bangladesh-received income is included; work physically performed in Bangladesh may be Bangladesh-earned even if a foreign employer pays it.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No independent-remote-worker rule was found. If treated as an employee of a covered Bangladesh establishment, provident-fund contributions of 7% to 8% may apply with an employer match.

fixed_payments.status: Route-specific fixed payments are inapplicable because Bangladesh has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status. General annual minimum income tax may apply above the exemption threshold, and BIDA publishes annual work-permit fees for employer/company routes, but neither is a monthly remote-worker package.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed self-employed or digital-nomad contribution was established. Any provident-fund rule is tied to covered employment, not an independent foreign-client remote worker.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee exists. General visa fees vary by nationality and category. For comparison only, BIDA currently lists BDT 5,000 per individual per year for a commercial-office work permit, which requires the employer/company route and does not legalize independent remote work.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Ordinary annual minimum income tax may apply once taxable income exceeds the applicable exemption; this is not a visa fee or fixed monthly freelancer tax. No remote-worker-specific municipal fee, registration charge, or flat transaction tax was published in the official sources reviewed.
fixed_payments.notes: The inapplicability is route-specific, not a statement that living or working in Bangladesh is free of taxes or fees. Exact general tax, visa, and employer-route charges depend on tax year, nationality, filing status, visa category, and legal work structure.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below the residence day-count does not guarantee no Bangladesh tax: services physically performed in Bangladesh may still produce Bangladesh-source employment or business income, and non-resident foreign individuals may face maximum-rate taxation.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide income enters the Bangladesh tax base under ordinary rules, subject to classification, allowable relief, foreign-tax credits, and treaties.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: No immigration-compliant visitor-to-sole-proprietor route was confirmed. Business registration may create separate income-tax, VAT, licensing, and permanent-establishment obligations but does not itself legalize residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Use a Bangladesh tax adviser before performing work from the country; tax liability and immigration authorization are separate questions.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker temporary-residence route exists.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No ordinary remote-worker or employment-to-PR timeline is published. Investment-based PR is a separate capital route.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The law provides discretionary naturalization criteria, not a fixed number of years after obtaining a standardized permanent-resident status.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: There is no matched starting route. General naturalization should not be presented as a guaranteed remote-worker timeline.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed legislation and current Home Affairs service/contact information do not publish a standard processing period for an ordinary naturalization application.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization is discretionary. The Naturalization Act requires the 12 months immediately before application plus at least four aggregate years during the preceding seven years, good character, adequate Bengali, and intent to reside in Bangladesh. Citizenship rules additionally request nationality status, Bengali knowledge, qualifications, income source, and ordinarily require abandonment or renunciation of the former status for the relevant application.
key_conditions.notes: These rules do not supply the missing lawful independent residence route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The official citizenship rules state that a foreign woman married to a Bangladeshi may be considered after two years of ordinary residence. Other applicants fall under a five-year ordinary-residence rule. The text is gender-specific and does not establish the same accelerated citizenship rule for a foreign husband.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A foreign spouse of a Bangladeshi citizen can qualify for a No Visa Required endorsement, allowing multiple entries and an unlimited stay during the passport's validity. For citizenship, an existing marriage alone is insufficient: residence and application requirements still apply, and the expedited two-year rule is expressly framed for a foreign wife.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: NVR is a travel and stay facilitation, not automatic permanent residence or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: Expect proof of the Bangladeshi spouse's nationality, an authenticated marriage certificate, evidence that the marriage remains unbroken, residence evidence for citizenship, Bengali-language review, income/source information, and government discretion. False or sham-marriage evidence can cause refusal, cancellation, or fraud consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The gender asymmetry and interaction between citizenship statutes, orders, and administrative practice require specialist confirmation.

birthright_citizenship.notes: On its face, section 4 grants citizenship to every person born in Bangladesh, subject only to narrow diplomat and enemy-occupation exceptions, which fits the schema's unconditional-jus-soli definition. However, an expert country report says administrative practice has de facto required a citizen parent, and the 2026 Pew/GLOBALCIT table does not classify Bangladesh among generally applicable birthright systems. Do not rely on birth alone without a Bangladeshi nationality-law opinion and confirmation from the Ministry of Home Affairs.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: The statutory text says a Bangladesh-born child of two migrant parents is a citizen unless the narrow diplomatic or enemy-occupation exception applies. Administrative recognition is disputed and may be denied in practice where neither parent is Bangladeshi.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean reflects the statute's wording, not a guarantee of registration or passport issuance.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child with a Bangladeshi father or mother qualifies by descent under section 5, subject to consular registration when born abroad to a parent who is only a citizen by descent. A child born in Bangladesh also falls within section 4's facial birth rule.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2009 amendment made transmission through either parent possible.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship, permanent residence, or a remote-worker status on foreign parents. The reviewed NVR rules facilitate foreign spouses and children of Bangladeshi citizens, not parents merely because their child acquired citizenship by birth.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any dependent or family application for a parent requires separate confirmation.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent-residence benefit was found for a migrant father solely because his Bangladesh-born child is a citizen. If the mother is a Bangladeshi citizen and the parents are married, the father may investigate spouse-based NVR, but the two-year accelerated citizenship wording reviewed applies specifically to a foreign wife, not a foreign husband.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Birth registration and the father's own immigration status remain separate matters.

rank.notes: Live Passport Power Rank observed on 2026-08-15. Passport rankings can change frequently.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category; it excludes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 28 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations. The index separately reports eVisas and other entry categories.

passport.notes: A separate July 2026 report citing Henley placed Bangladesh 97th with access to 35 destinations without a prior visa. Henley's score combines visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA access, so it is not directly comparable to Passport Index's separated figures.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate in Dhaka, international business, universities, and the technology sector, but Bangla is the sole state language and is important for government, contracts, housing, and everyday administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current official nationwide English-proficiency measure was identified; the practical assessment is cautious and should not be read as proof that all services are available in English.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. The reviewed government and business-service sources do not provide Russian- or Ukrainian-language service channels; English or Bangla would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practical assessment based on the languages available through the reviewed official channels, not a national language-proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the BBS Labour Force Survey 2024 salaried-employee average of BDT15,554 per month at about BDT123.82 per US dollar.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed BBS Labour Force Survey tables publish arithmetic averages, and the BBS labor and wage-statistics pages publish survey materials and wage-rate indices, but none supplies a national median monthly wage that can be converted to USD.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the BDT12,500 garment-sector minimum wage. This is sectoral and must not be treated as a national minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly average for salaried employees in the 2024 Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official aggregate tables do not publish a national median monthly salary, so there is no defensible BDT amount to convert into USD.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official sources publish averages and indices rather than a highest individual salary or upper distribution endpoint, so no national maximum can be converted to USD.

min_salary_local_currency.value: BDT 12,500 per month for garment-sector workers
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Sectoral statutory floor, not a national minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly income of salaried employees in the BBS Labour Force Survey 2024.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The BBS Labour Force Survey 2024 publishes arithmetic average monthly employment income and subgroup averages, while the reviewed BBS labor catalogue and wage-statistics page provide survey publications and wage-rate indices. None publishes a national median monthly salary in BDT, and a median cannot be recovered reliably from the aggregate tables; the value is therefore null.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official sources publish averages and wage-rate indices, not the highest individual salary or an upper endpoint of a national wage distribution. Subgroup averages are not individual maxima, so no defensible national maximum BDT salary can be reported and the value is null.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average gross monthly income from employment of salaried employees; minimum field is a separate garment-sector statutory wage floor
average_citizen_salary.period: Labour Force Survey 2024; garment minimum effective from the December 2023 wage order
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is citizen/resident labor-market data, not an immigration income threshold. BBS reported an overall salaried-employee average of BDT15,554, with substantial differences by occupation, industry, sex, and location. Bangladesh has sector-specific minimum wages rather than one universal national floor.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official wage-statistics source publishes price and wage indices but not a current household budget suitable for estimating a remote worker's monthly living costs. A private crowdsourced estimate was not substituted for official evidence.
