settlement_track.summary: Bangladesh has no confirmed current status for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Settlement is available only through materially different grounds such as substantial investment, marriage/family status, or discretionary naturalization after another lawful residence basis, so the requested profile has no usable citizenship track.
settlement_track.notes: Opening a company, registering a business, obtaining a tax number, or extending a visitor visa was not shown to legalize independent foreign-client remote work.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The current official channels cover ordinary visits, Bangladesh-linked employment/projects, and investment. The BIDA FAQ expressly places the work-permit filing with the expatriate's employer. None authorizes an ordinary software engineer to reside independently while working only under a foreign contract.

data.notes: The invalid selection conclusion is supported by the official visa portal, current BIDA FAQ, work-permit materials, investment rules, tax materials, and citizenship sources. Confidence remains medium because Bangladesh does not publish one consolidated immigration route catalogue, some legacy BIDA pages are intermittently unavailable, investor thresholds conflict across official pages, and birthright-citizenship practice conflicts with the facial statutory text.

data.selection_summary: Barbados accepts independent applications for the 12-month Welcome Stamp, which fits remote work for a foreign employer and requires at least USD 50,000 of expected annual income. However, it is a temporary visa, is deemed non-resident for Barbados income-tax purposes, and does not confer immigrant or permanent-resident status. Current citizenship law generally excludes periods of temporary immigration permission unless the Minister consents. Settlement therefore requires qualifying independently for another status; no ordinary foreign-contract route into that status was confirmed. The programme is currently authorized through 31 December 2026.

visa_application.title: Application for 12-Month Barbados Welcome Stamp Visa
visa_application.notes: Active official application form for new applications and renewals. It applies to a temporary remote-work visa, not immigrant status, permanent residence, or citizenship.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: USD 50,000 expected over the next 12 months, divided by 12 and rounded. The governing Act states BBD 100,000 annual income generated outside Barbados; current official application and route pages express it as USD 50,000.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: BBD 100,000 per year
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Statutory annual amount in Barbados dollars.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 50,000/year (about USD 4,167/month)
income_requirement_display.notes: Forward-looking annual-income declaration. The application also permits a declaration of otherwise sufficient means to support accompanying family members.

income_proof_months.notes: The applicant declares expected income over the coming 12 months. The inspected official sources do not prescribe a fixed number of historical bank-statement or payslip months.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment in a country other than Barbados, with income generated outside Barbados; the route covers location-independent work for companies or individuals outside Barbados.
Valid passport and health insurance for the entire Stamp period.
Passport photograph, passport biodata page, employer and work details, and relationship evidence for accompanying family members.
Fee after approval: USD 2,000 individual or USD 3,000 family; the official route page states that approval normally takes seven business days and payment is due within 28 days.
The holder may not take employment in Barbados other than the foreign employment for which the Stamp was granted.

initial_validity.value: 12 months
initial_validity.notes: The Act describes the Stamp as a visa granted for 12 months only.

extension_rules.value: Renewal or reapplication is available, subject to a new application and approval; the programme is currently authorized through 31 December 2026.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal does not convert the visa into permanent or qualifying residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The Stamp authorizes a 12-month temporary stay and remote work but does not grant immigrant or permanent-resident status. Current citizenship law generally excludes temporary immigration permission from residence calculations unless the Minister consents.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Conditional PR path through independently granted immigrant status and five years of residence in that status; no automatic Welcome Stamp conversion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Immigrant-status page returned 503 when opened but its official indexed content was readable. The Act and PR checklist opened successfully. No official confirmation that an unchanged foreign-employer-only arrangement satisfies section 6, or of a Welcome Stamp-specific exit requirement, was located.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No direct Welcome Stamp citizenship path exists. A holder would need a separate qualifying status and qualifying residence; temporary immigration time is normally excluded unless the Minister consents.

rejected_routes.notes: Excellent temporary fit for ordinary foreign-contract remote work, but it fails the citizenship-oriented selection rule because it has no confirmed conversion to qualifying immigrant status, permanent residence, or citizenship.

rejected_routes.route_name: Immigrant Status for a person establishing a business

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No standardized minimum income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Proof of finances, sufficient means, and funds brought into Barbados is required, but no fixed amount is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold published; proof of finances, sufficient means, and funds brought to Barbados is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a local business or professional-establishment category rather than an ordinary foreign-client remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed statement-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: The Immigration Act requires the permitted entrant to have established successfully, or be likely to establish successfully, a profession, trade, business, or agricultural enterprise in Barbados and to have sufficient means until established.

The Immigration Department requires a detailed description and location of the business, registration certificate or articles of incorporation, proof of finances, and proof of funds brought to Barbados.
Birth and civil-status documents, medical report, police certificates, photographs, qualifications, and normally an employment letter.

initial_validity.notes: Immigrant status is permission to remain for the purpose of permanent residence, but the current official page and Act do not publish a fixed card or certificate validity period.

extension_rules.notes: No periodic renewal rule was identified. Immigrant status can be lost, including after voluntarily residing outside Barbados continuously for one year without a ministerial exemption or through specified statutory disqualifications.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A permitted entrant may apply for discretionary immigrant status after establishing, or showing likelihood of establishing, a qualifying profession, trade, business, or agricultural enterprise in Barbados.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a separate immigration application and not a continuation of the Welcome Stamp.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After immigrant status is granted, Immigration Act section 5(2)(a)(i) permits permanent-resident registration after at least five years residing in Barbados as an immigrant, subject to statutory refusal grounds.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The five-year period runs from grant of immigrant status, not from a Welcome Stamp or visitor stay.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially possible through a separate settlement track: a qualifying local-business or professional applicant may obtain discretionary immigrant status and, after at least five years residing as an immigrant, qualify to register as a permanent resident. Under the Citizenship Act currently in force, an alien may separately apply for discretionary naturalisation after 12 continuous months immediately before application plus at least five aggregate years of qualifying residence during the preceding seven years. These residence periods may overlap with the immigrant-status period, but no official source guarantees immigrant approval, permanent-resident registration, or naturalisation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route can legally reach permanent residence and potentially citizenship when a genuine Barbados profession, trade, business, or agricultural enterprise is established. It remains rejected for this profile because ordinary work solely for a foreign client does not establish the required Barbados enterprise. The 2026 Citizenship Bill remained a bill in the current official sources checked.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires establishing a genuine profession, trade, business, or agricultural enterprise in Barbados, together with local registration and financial evidence. That is materially different from continuing ordinary software work solely for a foreign client.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary short-term or long-term work permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No standardized minimum salary is published on the official work-permit page.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: This category is based on prospective employment in Barbados.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable as a foreign-income route.

key_requirements.requirement: The employer or sponsor applies on behalf of the employee.
For a long-term permit, the prospective employer must show that no resident or Barbadian national is capable and willing to fill the position.
Long-term applications require employer letters, medical documents, character references, qualifications, and work-permit forms.

initial_validity.value: Short-term: up to 11 months; long-term: up to 3 years

extension_rules.value: Extension forms exist, but approval remains within the sponsored work-permit system.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary permission to work for the sponsoring Barbados employer.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not independently available to the applicant profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic work-permit-to-permanent-residence rule or timeline is published on the official work-permit page.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separate qualifying immigration residence and citizenship processes, if all requirements are eventually met.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Barbados employer or sponsor and, for long-term permission, a labour-market test are required.

summary.value: An accepted adult student may independently seek a non-immigrant student visa without a local employer. It requires an acceptance letter, certified student forms, adequate funds, police certificate, accommodation, course information, and a BBD 300 application fee. It provides temporary non-immigrant student permission for the approved course, not permanent residence, and no official study-to-PR or study-to-citizenship conversion was found.
summary.notes: A university degree already held by the applicant does not itself create residence eligibility. This is an enrollment-based student visa, not a degree-recognition or independent skilled-migration route.

tax_residency_rule.value: Under ordinary rules, an individual is resident after spending more than 182 aggregate days in Barbados in an income year or when ordinarily resident. A Welcome Stamp holder is expressly deemed non-resident for the relevant income-tax provision while using the Stamp.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The statutory Welcome Stamp treatment overrides the ordinary day-count result for this route. A later status switch, local business activity, or income outside the protected foreign-employment arrangement requires a new analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Route-specific rate: qualifying Welcome Stamp income is excluded from Barbados-derived income, and the holder is deemed non-resident for the relevant income-tax provision. This is not the ordinary personal income-tax rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No official Welcome Stamp-specific NIS contribution or exemption was identified. The Stamp does not authorize ordinary Barbados employment. If a person separately becomes locally self-employed, the general schedule totals 17.25% of insurable earnings, subject to ceilings, classification, and registration rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly state payment was identified. Health insurance is mandatory but market-priced; the visa charge is a one-time approval fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: The Remote Employment Act deems Welcome Stamp holders non-resident for the specified income-tax rule and excludes their qualifying Stamp income from income derived from Barbados, producing a route-specific 0% Barbados income-tax treatment.
special_tax_regimes.notes: VAT still applies to purchases. The exemption should not be extrapolated to a Barbados business, Barbados employment, or another immigration status.

taxes.caveats: Tax liability may remain in the applicant's home country or another country of tax residence. Foreign-employer payroll, permanent-establishment, treaty, remittance, and social-security outcomes depend on the contract and employer structure. Obtain Barbados and home-country advice before relying on the exemption.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: statutory non-resident/exempt treatment applies to qualifying Welcome Stamp foreign employment, while ordinary individual taxation is progressive.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Ordinarily more than 182 aggregate days in the calendar income year or ordinary residence; Welcome Stamp holders are statutorily deemed non-resident for the specified income-tax provision.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident and domiciled individuals are taxed on worldwide income. Resident but non-domiciled individuals are taxed on Barbados income and foreign income from which a benefit is received in Barbados. Welcome Stamp foreign-employment income receives separate statutory protection.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Welcome Stamp statutory non-resident treatment and exclusion of qualifying Stamp income from Barbados-derived income.
taxation_system.social_security: No Welcome Stamp-specific NIS rule was confirmed. Ordinary locally self-employed persons are generally scheduled at 17.25% of insurable earnings, subject to the applicable earnings ceiling and category rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 27.5% figure is the ordinary top marginal screening rate for income year 2026, not an expected effective rate or the Welcome Stamp rate. The route-specific screening rate is 0%.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary personal income-tax allowance/below the first taxable threshold
tax_brackets.notes: The BRA rate schedule begins above BBD 25,000.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary taxable income within this band from income year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount approximates the top of the band at BBD 1.98 per USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary taxable income above the threshold from income year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The route-specific 0% treatment is established by the Remote Employment Act. Ordinary rates show what may apply after switching status or conducting activity outside the Stamp.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Qualifying Welcome Stamp foreign-employment income receives a statutory Barbados income-tax exclusion, producing a 0% Barbados route rate; ordinary local or post-Stamp activity falls outside that conclusion.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Statutory non-resident treatment for qualifying foreign remote employment
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% Barbados income tax on qualifying Welcome Stamp foreign-employment income; ordinary PIT tops out at 27.5% in 2026
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Welcome Stamp holders are deemed non-resident for the relevant Barbados income-tax rule even though ordinary residence generally begins after more than 182 days.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Income generated outside Barbados from the employment for which the Stamp was granted is protected by the Remote Employment Act. Other foreign income, local-source income, or a Barbados business requires separate analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Remote Employment Act, 2020 Welcome Stamp treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No specific NIS exemption or fixed Welcome Stamp contribution was confirmed. The holder may not take unrelated employment in Barbados. Foreign-employer payroll obligations remain contract- and jurisdiction-dependent.

fixed_payments.status: One-time visa fee and mandatory private health insurance; no fixed monthly state payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No Welcome Stamp-specific fixed contribution confirmed. Ordinary local self-employment can attract percentage-based NIS contributions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: USD 2,000 individual or USD 3,000 family after approval; renewal requires a further approved application and fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Barbados VAT of 17.5% applies to goods and services purchased on the island.
fixed_payments.notes: Health insurance is mandatory for the entire Stamp but no standardized premium is published. Visa fees should not be converted into a monthly tax figure.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: The Welcome Stamp statutory treatment applies independently of the ordinary 182-day rule. Home-country tax may still apply.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: While the Stamp remains valid and work stays within the qualifying foreign-employment arrangement, the Act deems the holder non-resident for the specified Barbados income-tax provision. After switching status, ordinary residence and income-scope rules must be reassessed.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The Welcome Stamp does not authorize unrelated Barbados employment or establish a local-business residence route. Registering and operating a Barbados business may trigger ordinary income tax, NIS, VAT, licensing, and immigration requirements.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the statutory income-tax treatment; medium confidence in social-security consequences because no official Stamp-specific NIS guidance was located.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No numeric years value applies to the Welcome Stamp: once approved it is a 12-month temporary visa, not immigrant or permanent-resident status. A separate immigrant-status application is available to a permitted entrant who has established, or is likely to establish, a qualifying Barbados profession, trade, business, or agricultural enterprise, but the Immigration Act and current Immigration Department page publish no standard adjudication time; therefore an elapsed-years figure cannot be stated.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: There is no Welcome Stamp-to-PR conversion period. On the separate business or professional immigrant track, the statutory threshold is at least five years residing after immigrant status is granted; that cannot be treated as five years after a Welcome Stamp.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: No fixed PR-to-citizenship waiting period applies under current naturalisation law. Eligibility turns on qualifying residence: 12 continuous months immediately before application plus at least five aggregate years during the preceding seven years. Those periods may have accrued before PR, and naturalisation remains discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No Welcome Stamp-to-citizenship timeline exists. Current ordinary naturalisation law requires at least six actual years of qualifying residence within an eight-year window, including the final continuous year, but temporary immigration periods are generally excluded unless the Minister consents. Because the Welcome Stamp does not supply the necessary qualifying status, no total timeline can be assigned to this route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current Immigration Department requirements, forms index, Citizenship Act, and Citizenship Regulations do not publish an official typical processing time, service standard, or median processing statistic.

key_conditions.value: Naturalisation is discretionary and generally requires qualifying residence, good character, intention to reside in Barbados, an oath of allegiance, and supporting civil, police, medical, employment, bank, and property documents. Time allowed only as temporary immigration permission is generally excluded unless the Minister consents. A 2026 Citizenship Bill was published but was not established as enacted in the official Gazette sources inspected.
key_conditions.notes: The general naturalisation rules are a separate path and should not be attributed to the Welcome Stamp.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution gives a person who has been married to a Barbadian citizen a right to apply for registration, subject to national-security and public-policy qualifications. The operative constitutional text inspected does not prescribe a numeric marriage or residence period, so no number is assigned.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Barbadian citizen can support citizenship registration. An existing marriage to another non-citizen does not accelerate citizenship, although the spouse may accompany the principal Welcome Stamp applicant in a family application.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Citizenship is not automatic on marriage.

requirements_and_risks.value: The official process requires the applicant's and citizen spouse's civil-status and citizenship documents, photographs, application fees, and an oath where applicable. Constitutional national-security and public-policy qualifications apply. The relationship must be genuine; false material statements can lead to refusal and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No official language-test requirement was identified for the marriage-registration route.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship at birth to every person born in Barbados after 29 November 1966, subject only to narrow diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Barbados to two migrant parents is normally a Barbadian citizen at birth, even if neither parent is a permanent resident, subject to narrow constitutional diplomatic and enemy-occupation exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This concerns birth in Barbados; overseas births follow separate descent and registration rules.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Barbados is a citizen by birth regardless; a child born abroad to a Barbadian citizen may qualify by descent or registration under the applicable constitutional and statutory rules.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage and the date and place of birth should be checked against current law for an overseas birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Barbadian citizen child does not automatically give either migrant parent citizenship or permanent residence. A parent may qualify separately under the Immigration Act if the citizen child resides in Barbados and is willing and able to provide for the parent's care and maintenance, but approval of immigrant status remains a separate ministerial process.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: This statutory parent category is not automatic status arising at the child's birth.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically receive residence, permanent residence, or citizenship because his child is Barbadian. He must apply and qualify through an applicable immigration or citizenship category; if the other parent is a Barbadian spouse, the marriage route may apply independently.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined total of 43 visa-on-arrival and 9 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 154. Its methodology differs from Henley, so the figures should not be mixed with Henley rankings or scores.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. English is the official language and is used for government communications, administration, and public services; official Welcome Stamp material also describes modern telecommunications and island-wide connectivity.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Bajan, an English-based local variety, is widely used informally.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low outside private expatriate or community networks. No Russian- or Ukrainian-language official-service provision was identified; English should be expected for immigration, tax, banking, leases, and daily administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Cautious practical assessment based on English being the official administrative language, not a claim that no individual Russian or Ukrainian speakers are present.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official 2025 Labour Force Survey publishes counts in grouped weekly-earnings bands, not a national arithmetic mean. The government launched a new employer-sourced Survey of Employment, Earnings and Hours in June 2026 to restore detailed wage-data capacity, but the inspected announcement contained no results; no USD mean was inferred.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The grouped 2025 distribution places the median worker in the BBD 500-999 weekly band but does not publish an exact median suitable for numeric conversion.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statutory national minimum of BBD 428.40 per 40-hour week, multiplied by 52/12 and converted at BBD 1.98 per USD. Rounded approximate gross monthly equivalent.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official arithmetic mean is published. A midpoint estimate was not used because the lowest and highest earnings categories are open-ended and within-band earnings are unknown.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The exact median is unpublished; it falls within the BBD 500-999 weekly earnings band.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official distribution's highest category is open-ended at over BBD 1,300 per week, so a national maximum cannot be established or converted to USD.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum for a 40-hour work week, effective 21 January 2026. It is a legal wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.value: The official 2025 Labour Force Survey does not publish an arithmetic mean; it reports only grouped weekly earnings.
average_salary_local_currency.notes: A numerical average cannot be calculated reliably because the lowest and highest categories are open-ended and within-band earnings are unknown. The June 2026 employer earnings survey announcement did not contain results.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The median falls inside this grouped 2025 weekly-earnings band after excluding the not-stated category; the exact median is not published.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Open-ended official top band: over BBD 1,300/week; no maximum amount is published.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The Labour Force Survey reports approximately 8,800 workers in the open-ended over-BBD-1,300 weekly band, establishing only the lower boundary of the highest group.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory gross minimum wage for the minimum field; 2025 Labour Force Survey grouped weekly earnings for distribution context
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 21 January 2026; earnings distribution for annual 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are wages of workers in Barbados, not the immigration income threshold. The statutory minimum is exact. The official 2025 survey supplies an exact grouped distribution but no arithmetic mean, exact median, or upper bound; a new employer earnings survey began in June 2026, but its inspected announcement published no results.

cost_of_living_note.value: The official Retail Price Index rose 0.5% from February to March 2026, with housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels up 1.4% and food and non-alcoholic beverages up 1.0% over the month. This measures price movement, not a monthly household budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No reliable official single-person monthly cost amount was published, so none was estimated.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Welcome Stamp is only a 12-month temporary remote-employment visa. It does not confer immigrant or permanent-resident status and has no statutory conversion to either. Under the Citizenship Act currently in force, time allowed only under temporary immigration permission is excluded from citizenship residence calculations unless the Minister specifically consents, so Welcome Stamp time must not be presented as settlement-counting time.
settlement_track.summary: The Welcome Stamp fits foreign-contract remote work but is temporary only. Permanent residence or citizenship requires switching to a separately qualifying immigration status; no standard conversion route for an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer was confirmed.
settlement_track.notes: A holder must qualify independently for another status. The business or professional immigrant route can lead to permanent residence after at least five years as an immigrant, but it requires establishing a qualifying Barbados enterprise and is not an ordinary foreign-contract route. The 2026 Citizenship Bill was published as a bill; the official Gazette index inspected through 7 August 2026 did not establish its enactment, so current Cap. 186 rules are used.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only as a temporary-living and foreign-remote-work fit. It is not a qualifying settlement or citizenship-path fit.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit using 29 distinct directly relevant URLs, including six URLs outside the previous source set. The Immigration Act clarifies that the separate business or professional immigrant track can reach permanent residence after at least five years as an immigrant, but this does not make the Welcome Stamp a citizenship route. Official wage sources confirm that no arithmetic mean or maximum is currently published: the 2025 Labour Force Survey uses grouped weekly bands with an open-ended top band, and the June 2026 employer earnings survey announcement contains no results. Current-law conclusions use Cap. 186 because enactment of the 2026 Citizenship Bill was not established in the official Gazette sources inspected.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Immigrant status under section 6 of the Immigration Act, followed by section 5 permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A Welcome Stamp holder can pursue a separate immigrant-status basis such as establishing a qualifying profession or business, then PR after five years as an immigrant. Welcome Stamp residence alone is insufficient.
requirements: Obtain discretionary immigrant status on a separately accepted economic or other statutory basis.
For a business application, provide registration, business description/location, finances and funds brought to Barbados.
Reside at least five years after immigrant status is granted and meet PR documentation.
reviewed_route_names: 12-Month Barbados Welcome Stamp
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Immigrant-status page returned 503 when opened but its official indexed content was readable. The Act and PR checklist opened successfully. No official confirmation that an unchanged foreign-employer-only arrangement satisfies section 6, or of a Welcome Stamp-specific exit requirement, was located. The unchanged remote-work profile is not confirmed; the conditional alternative requires an additional independently accepted eligibility basis.

data.selection_summary: Belarus has no current digital-nomad or dedicated foreign-remote-worker residence route. A software engineer may potentially use the professional-income-tax regime for internet-delivered services to a foreign client, but that tax registration does not confer immigration status; temporarily staying or temporarily resident foreigners generally cannot register as individual entrepreneurs. Visitor/e-visa, study, employment, and locally grounded business channels therefore do not satisfy the requested independent remote-worker citizenship track.

visa_application.title: Entry visas: visa application process
visa_application.notes: This is the official MFA visa-procedure page, not a remote-worker application. Belarusian missions issue ordinary visas; the separate e-visa portal covers only short business, event, private, and tourism visits. No official digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker application channel was found.

rejected_routes.route_name: Professional income tax (NPD) for independent internet services

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum income is prescribed; this is a tax regime, not an immigration route. A minimum tax payment applies even with no income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No minimum income; minimum NPD payment BYN 45 per registered month from July 2026
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The BYN 45 amount is a minimum tax payment, not an immigration income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration income threshold; BYN 45 minimum monthly tax while registered
income_requirement_display.notes: Approximately USD 15.5 using the late-July 2026 official-rate proxy of BYN 2.9063 per USD. This payment does not qualify anyone for residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No immigration income-proof period exists because NPD is only a tax registration.

key_requirements.requirement: Use the official Profdoход application and perform an activity on the permitted list.
The permitted list includes work or services delivered remotely through the internet to individuals or organizations outside the customer's controlled premises.
Foreign citizens may be NPD taxpayers, and foreign-organization receipts are taxed at 10%.
A separate lawful basis to enter, reside, and perform the activity remains necessary; NPD registration itself grants no visa, temporary residence, or permanent residence.

initial_validity.value: Tax registration continues until deregistration, subject to monthly reporting and payment rules
initial_validity.notes: This is not a period of authorized immigration stay.

extension_rules.value: No immigration extension; the taxpayer remains registered until deregistration and owes at least BYN 45 for each registered month from July 2026
extension_rules.notes: Deleting the application alone does not deregister the taxpayer.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None established by NPD registration
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The current immigration framework does not list NPD enrollment as a residence ground.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None established by NPD registration
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence requires a separate statutory ground.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from NPD itself; citizenship would require obtaining permanent residence separately and satisfying naturalization rules
path_to_citizenship.notes: The general naturalization period is five continuous years after permanent residence, not five years of NPD registration.

rejected_routes.notes: This is economically compatible with foreign-client software work and may be useful after a person already has lawful residence. It fails selection because it is not an immigration status and cannot independently start a settlement track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Belarus e-visa, ordinary visa, or visa-free stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: These are visitor-entry channels, not residence routes.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker income-proof period exists.

key_requirements.requirement: The e-visa is single-entry and valid for no more than 30 days.
Permitted e-visa purposes are business trips, specified events or internships, private affairs, and tourism; remote employment is not listed.
Ordinary visa categories include business, study, employment, tourism, private purposes, and permanent residence, but no digital-nomad category.
Temporary visitors generally must register within ten days; longer stays require a temporary- or permanent-residence permit based on the purpose of entry.

initial_validity.value: E-visa: up to 30 days; ordinary short-term C visa: up to 90 days
initial_validity.notes: A long-term D visa may be valid longer but generally permits only up to 90 days of stay unless another rule applies.

extension_rules.value: No remote-work extension; a foreigner seeking longer residence must contact the Citizenship and Migration Department and qualify separately
extension_rules.notes: Visitor registration or visa extension does not create a settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate statutory ground such as study, family, employment, property, or authorized local activity is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No path from visitor or e-visa status alone
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A permanent-residence entry visa requires a prior decision from the Citizenship and Migration Department.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status
path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time is not the five-year permanent-residence period required for ordinary naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor and e-visa status is temporary, does not expressly authorize ordinary foreign-employer remote work, and does not constitute a qualifying residence track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Individual entrepreneur or locally established business channel

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No ordinary remote-worker threshold was published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No ordinary remote-worker threshold was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No ordinary remote-worker income threshold; business eligibility depends on separate legal status and activity rules
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an open sole-proprietor immigration route.

income_proof_months.notes: No applicable remote-worker income-proof rule was established.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreigners permanently residing in Belarus may conduct individual business on broadly the same basis as citizens.
Temporarily staying or temporarily resident foreigners generally have no right to conduct individual business unless a separate law or treaty provides otherwise.

Creating or operating a local legal entity involves separate corporate, director, work-authorization, and local-business requirements and is not equivalent to sole-proprietor legalization for a foreign remote worker.

initial_validity.notes: No independently obtainable immigration status matching the profile was established.

extension_rules.notes: No matching status exists to extend.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not established for ordinary foreign-client sole-proprietor work
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Although authorized entrepreneurial activity can appear in general residence legislation, the individual-business restriction for temporary foreigners prevents treating visitor-to-sole-proprietor legalization as a confirmed route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Individual-business rights generally follow permanent residence rather than independently producing it
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This creates a circular problem for the proposed visitor-to-self-employed strategy.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through a separately obtained permanent-residence status and later naturalization
path_to_citizenship.notes: No direct business-to-citizenship path fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a temporary foreigner cannot normally register as an individual entrepreneur, while a corporate-founder route requires a genuine locally established business structure and separate authorization.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employment visa and employment-based temporary residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: Local employment and permit required; no remote-worker threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: The decisive requirement is employer-backed work authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: The inspected sources do not publish a general income-proof period for employment visas.

key_requirements.requirement: An employment visa normally requires a special employment permit or qualifying representative-office documents.
Temporary residence based on employment depends on lawful local employment and its supporting documents.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence generally up to one year
initial_validity.notes: Duration remains tied to the qualifying ground.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires the employment ground and supporting authorization to continue
extension_rules.notes: Exact filing requirements should be confirmed with the local Citizenship and Migration Department.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available through authorized local employment
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This directly conflicts with the no-local-employer selection criterion.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially only under separate statutory grounds or after sufficient qualifying legal residence
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is not a confirmed ordinary remote-work path.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential only after separately obtaining permanent residence and completing the naturalization period
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not usable through the applicant's existing foreign contract.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires local-employer-backed employment authorization.

summary.value: Admission to a Belarusian educational institution can support a study visa and temporary residence for the study period, generally issued for no more than one year at a time. A pre-existing foreign degree alone does not create residence, and study is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route or direct permanent residence.
summary.notes: This is enrollment-based residence, not a degree-recognition or independent skilled-migration program.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally a Belarus tax resident when physically present in Belarus for more than 183 days in a calendar year. Residents must declare relevant foreign or foreign-received income; nonresidents generally fall outside Belarus tax on foreign-source income, subject to source rules and treaties.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Certain treatment, business-presence, temporary-absence, and treaty rules can modify the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: The ordinary screening PIT rate is 13%. For specified annual income categories in 2026, marginal rates of 25% and 30% apply above BYN 350,000 and BYN 600,000 respectively. Eligible NPD foreign-client professional income instead uses the special 10% regime.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For a non-pensioner using NPD, six percentage points of the 10% payment fund mandatory social-insurance contributions; pensioners are exempt from that contribution component. Ordinary employee and employer payroll contributions follow different rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the BYN 45 minimum monthly NPD payment effective July 2026, using BYN 2.9063/USD. This applies only while registered for NPD and is not a visa fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: The NPD professional-income regime taxes receipts from foreign organizations and foreign individual entrepreneurs at 10%. It is available to foreign citizens and covers permitted independent activities, including internet-delivered remote services. It does not grant immigration status.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility must be checked against the current activity list and the foreigner's separate right to live and perform the work in Belarus.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on calendar-year residence, income sourcing, whether the arrangement is employment or independent services, NPD activity eligibility, treaty relief, and immigration/work authorization. A tax regime must not be interpreted as permission to reside or work.

taxation_system.value: Belarus uses a mixed system: ordinary PIT is generally 13%, with marginal 25% and 30% rates for specified high-income categories, while eligible independent professional income can use the 10% NPD special regime.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days of physical presence in the calendar year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxable on Belarus-source and relevant foreign income; nonresidents generally on Belarus-source income. The source classification of services physically performed from Belarus needs filing-specific review.
taxation_system.special_regimes: NPD: generally 10% on professional income from individuals, foreign organizations, and foreign individual entrepreneurs; 20% applies only to the portion above the annual threshold for Belarus-registered business customers.
taxation_system.social_security: For non-pensioner NPD taxpayers, the 10% payment includes a six-percentage-point social-insurance component. Ordinary payroll contribution rules are separate.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 30% is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective tax rate. In 2026, specified income up to BYN 350,000 generally remains at 13%; the portion above BYN 350,000 through BYN 600,000 is taxed at 25%, and the portion above BYN 600,000 at 30%. The higher bands do not necessarily apply to every type of foreign remote income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Up to BYN 350,000 per calendar year for specified income categories
tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary PIT base and the lower band of specified high-income categories
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold using BYN 2.9063/USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion above BYN 350,000 and up to BYN 600,000 per calendar year
tax_brackets.applies_to: Specified employment, civil-contract, dividend, and other listed high-income categories
tax_brackets.notes: The USD value represents the upper boundary; this is a marginal band.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion above BYN 600,000 per calendar year
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Foreign-organization or foreign-individual-entrepreneur NPD receipts, regardless of amount
tax_brackets.notes: Special gross-receipts regime; activity and legal-work eligibility must be satisfied.

taxation_system.notes: Current 2026 Ministry of Taxes material supports the residence rule, ordinary rates, high-income bands, NPD rates, and July 2026 minimum payment. Contract classification and treaty advice remain necessary.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Belarus has no digital-nomad tax category. If a foreigner already has a lawful immigration basis and qualifies for NPD, foreign-client internet services may be taxed at 10%, with a BYN 45 monthly minimum while registered.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad regime; possible NPD independent-professional taxation only after separate immigration authorization
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% NPD on eligible foreign-client professional receipts; otherwise ordinary PIT generally 13%, with specified high-income marginal rates up to 30%
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in Belarus during the calendar year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A Belarus tax resident must declare applicable foreign income. Eligible NPD receipts from foreign organizations or foreign individual entrepreneurs are taxed at 10%; otherwise ordinary PIT and treaty/source rules require review.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None. NPD is a domestic professional-income tax regime and supplies no visa or residence rights.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For a non-pensioner, six percentage points of the 10% NPD payment represent mandatory social-insurance funding. Employment relationships may instead trigger ordinary payroll rules.

fixed_payments.status: confirmed_for_npd_not_for_a_nomad_visa
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The NPD percentage includes its social-insurance component; no separate minimum social contribution was established beyond the overall BYN 45 minimum NPD payment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee exists. For comparison only, the visitor e-visa costs EUR 35 for listed European nationalities or EUR 60 for most others, plus a EUR 6 service fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: BYN 45 minimum NPD payment per registered month from July 2026, including zero-income months.
fixed_payments.notes: These amounts do not create immigration eligibility.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person at or below the residence threshold is generally a nonresident, but Belarus-source characterization of work physically performed in Belarus and the legality of working on visitor status require professional review.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident generally reports applicable foreign income. If NPD and the activity list apply, foreign-client professional receipts can be taxed at 10%; otherwise ordinary PIT rules may apply.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: NPD can cover permitted remote internet services and foreign clients, but it is only tax registration. Temporarily staying or temporarily resident foreigners generally cannot register as individual entrepreneurs, and neither NPD nor tax registration supplies residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax mechanics are well supported, but no corresponding remote-worker immigration status exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No matching independent remote-worker route exists, so there is no route-specific time to temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General legislation includes eligibility after at least seven years of lawful residence, alongside other family, refugee, talent, investment, and state-need grounds. This is not confirmation that visitor or NPD time qualifies in the proposed scenario.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Current Article 14 requires five continuous years after obtaining permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Illustrative general total of seven years to possible permanent residence plus five years of permanent residence. It is not a matched remote-worker timeline and may vary with the PR ground.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The statutory maximum for an ordinary naturalization application is one year; registration cases have a shorter maximum. Actual timing was not independently established.

key_conditions.value: For ordinary naturalization: permanent residence, five continuous years with no more than 90 days outside Belarus in each calendar year, knowledge of Belarusian or Russian sufficient for communication, lawful income supporting the applicant and dependants, compliance with Belarusian law, and resolution or renunciation of other citizenship as required. Admission remains subject to Belarusian state interests.
key_conditions.notes: These are general citizenship conditions, not evidence of a remote-worker path to permanent residence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The five-year ordinary citizenship residence condition may be waived for a permanent resident married to a Belarusian citizen for at least three years who also has a common minor child who is a Belarusian citizen. Marriage alone does not satisfy this exception.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine pre-existing marriage can support family-based residence and its duration can count toward the three-year marriage condition. For the citizenship residence-period exception, current law additionally requires permanent residence and a common minor Belarusian-citizen child.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A marriage certificate supports private or family visa procedures, but the relevant residence or citizenship application remains separate.

requirements_and_risks.value: Expect proof of the genuine marriage, shared family relationship, residence registration, lawful income, housing, and identity or civil-status documents. False documents, sham marriage, or misleading information can cause refusal and immigration consequences; no parent or spouse receives citizenship automatically.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Exact filing documents and current state fees should be confirmed with the local Citizenship and Migration Department.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Belarus is principally jus sanguinis with anti-statelessness and foundling rules. Birth in Belarus alone does not normally confer citizenship on a child of two foreign temporary residents.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Belarus to two foreign parents does not generally become Belarusian merely by birth. Citizenship applies where the foreign parents permanently reside in Belarus and their states will not grant the child citizenship; a child born in Belarus to resident stateless parents is also protected.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary two-temporary-migrant scenario; anti-statelessness exceptions remain.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child is a Belarusian citizen by birth if at least one parent is a Belarusian citizen, regardless of the child's place of birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Current legal and UN summaries describe acquisition at birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Belarusian-citizen child may help establish a family relationship for residence, but the child's citizenship does not automatically grant either foreign parent permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any family-based application requires its own statutory ground and evidence.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father receives no automatic citizenship from the child's birth. If the child and other parent create a qualifying family-residence ground, he may apply separately; the citizenship residence-period waiver requires permanent residence, at least three years of marriage to a Belarusian citizen, and a common minor Belarusian-citizen child.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, marriage, residence, and genuine-family evidence may be examined.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank reported by Passport Index on the current Belarus passport dashboard.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's advance-visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 41 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately counts eVisas and may update continuously.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports mobility score 92 and rank 53 using its own category method. As a methodological cross-check, the current Henley ranking page reports Belarus at rank 61 with access to 78 destinations; Henley combines visa-free and qualifying visa-on-arrival access and therefore should not be mixed with Passport Index's category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in the international technology sector and Minsk, but English should not be assumed sufficient for immigration, tax, banking, healthcare, or routine administration. EF EPI 2025 places Belarus in the moderate-proficiency band.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a self-selected adult test dataset and is an indicator rather than a guarantee of service availability.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is highly practical and is an official state language widely used in administration and daily life. Ukrainian speakers may understand some Belarusian or Russian through linguistic proximity, but Ukrainian has no official status and should not be relied on for formal procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian or Belarusian is advisable for filings; the inspected current sources do not provide a nationwide measure of Ukrainian-language service availability.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: BYN 3,104.1 nominal gross average earnings for June 2026, converted using BYN 2.9063/USD, the latest extractable late-July 2026 official-rate proxy.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: BYN 2,314.9 gross median wage for May 2026, converted using the same rate proxy.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statutory monthly minimum wage of BYN 858 from 1 January 2026, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Nationwide nominal gross average earnings for June 2026.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Gross median wage for May 2026; Belstat calculates this indicator twice yearly.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No exact nationwide maximum individual monthly salary is published in the inspected official statistics or current wage-distribution reports. The distributions use an open-ended highest bracket, so its threshold cannot be treated as a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage effective 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Nationwide nominal gross average earnings, June 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Gross median wage, May 2026.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Belstat's wage releases publish national, regional, and sector averages plus median and grouped wage distributions, but not the largest salary received by an individual worker. The May 2026 distribution and the inspected November 2025 distribution place the highest-paid workers in an open-ended band; reports that some workers earned more than BYN 10,000 establish only a lower boundary for that group, not a national maximum. Sector leaders such as information and communications are averages and are therefore not substituted for an individual maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Nationwide nominal gross employee earnings; statutory gross minimum wage; grouped wage distributions
average_citizen_salary.period: June 2026 average, May 2026 median and wage distribution, 2026 statutory minimum
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe citizen or resident employee wages, not immigration income thresholds. USD conversions are approximate and use BYN 2.9063/USD from 30 July 2026. A national maximum remains null because none of the focused current sources publishes the top individual salary, and an open-ended upper wage bracket has no finite maximum.

cost_of_living_note.notes: Belstat publishes CPI, but CPI change is not a comprehensive household cost-of-living budget and was not substituted for one.
