settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor/e-visa status and NPD tax registration do not constitute qualifying residence. A wholly separate family, study, local-employment, property, or locally authorized business ground would be required.
settlement_track.summary: Belarus permits visitor entry and has a workable professional-income tax mechanism for some foreign-client internet services, but neither supplies an independent remote-worker residence permit. The exact proposed route therefore cannot reach permanent residence or citizenship.
settlement_track.notes: The general immigration and citizenship system has residence and naturalization routes, but none was confirmed for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker without a local employer or separate qualifying ground.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign-client remote services can fit the NPD tax activity list, but no corresponding visa or residence status exists. Tax eligibility alone is insufficient.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed. The exact nationwide maximum employee salary remains null because current official and reputable sources publish averages, medians, and grouped distributions whose highest bracket is open-ended; BYN 10,000 is only a lower boundary reported for the highest group, not a maximum. Six additional distinct wage-related URLs beyond the previous source set were inspected and added. The negative immigration-selection conclusion remains unchanged.

data.selection_summary: Belgium has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. A non-EU national may independently seek a regional professional card and, after approval, a D visa and temporary residence, but this is a genuine Belgian self-employed-business route: Flanders requires a business plan plus economic, innovative, sporting, artistic or cultural added value, and economic-category applicants must show capital and benefit to the regional economy. An existing foreign software contract alone does not establish eligibility. The route is therefore not a reliable match for ordinary foreign-contract remote work, although a software entrepreneur with a qualifying Belgian business project could seek filing-specific advice.

visa_application.title: Applying for your first professional card
visa_application.notes: Professional-card competence is regional. The linked Flanders page includes eligibility, documents, fees and submission instructions. Applicants establishing activity in Brussels, Wallonia or the German-speaking Community must use that region’s process. Applicants abroad normally submit through the Belgian diplomatic or consular post where they legally reside; professional-card approval precedes the D-visa application.

rejected_routes.route_name: Regional professional card plus D visa for self-employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of Flanders' EUR 2,408.79 monthly means-of-subsistence reference using EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. This is a Flanders requirement, not a uniform national digital-nomad income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Flanders: EUR 2,408.79/month from April 2026; economic-added-value cases also require at least EUR 22,838 in an account
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Regional rules differ. Flanders also states an annual means reference of EUR 26,086.66 as of 1 March 2026; applicants should use the amount displayed by the region at filing.

income_requirement_display.value: Flanders: EUR 2,408.79/month means of subsistence, plus EUR 22,838 capital for the economic-added-value category
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 2,408.79/month; additional EUR 22,838 account balance where applicable
income_requirement_display.notes: Not a salary threshold for remote workers. It forms part of a regional business-route assessment.

income_proof_months.notes: The official pages require proof of stable means, financial capacity and a business plan but do not publish a uniform number of prior income months.

key_requirements.requirement: Establish and carry out a genuine self-employed activity in the competent Belgian region; work cannot begin before professional-card approval.
Flanders requires passport/identity evidence, a criminal-record extract under six months old, at least level-4/secondary qualification, sufficient means and a full business plan.

Flemish economic-added-value cases require EUR 22,838 in the applicant's account and proof of job creation/investment or benefit to the existing economic structure; innovative cases require qualifying innovation or incubator/research collaboration.
For the D visa, provide the regional grant decision, medical certificate, recent criminal-record document and applicable fee evidence.
After arrival, register with the municipality and collect the professional card through the designated business counter.

initial_validity.value: Flanders: 1–3 years; Wallonia: generally 1–3 years, with a first card usually issued for about 2 years and a statutory maximum of 5 years
initial_validity.notes: Validity is tied to the approved activity and right of residence and varies by region and file.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires continued legal residence, performance of the approved activity, continued regional added value and compliance with tax, regulatory and social-security obligations. Flanders requires post-2022 cardholders to apply at least 60 days before expiry; Wallonia states at least three months.
extension_rules.notes: A material change in activity may require a new application.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: After regional professional-card approval, an applicant abroad applies for a national D visa. Following arrival and a positive address check, the municipality issues a temporary residence card while the professional card authorizes the approved self-employed activity.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The professional card and immigration authorization are distinct but linked.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Belgium has a general five-year long-term-resident procedure requiring qualifying legal and uninterrupted residence, sufficient means, health insurance and limited absences. The reviewed official pages do not clearly confirm how every year on a limited professional-card-linked A card is counted or the exact conversion step to unlimited residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Obtain case-specific confirmation before treating professional-card residence as a guaranteed PR clock.

path_to_citizenship.value: A general nationality declaration may be possible after five years of legal residence, but the applicant must hold an unlimited right of residence when filing and satisfy language, social-integration and economic-participation conditions. A principal self-employed applicant normally proves at least six quarters of Belgian social contributions over the preceding five years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The general five-year rule does not resolve whether this particular professional-card history will produce unlimited residence in time.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest independent route, but it is not an ordinary remote-worker visa. The regional business-substance and economic/innovative-value assessment makes a passive relocation supported only by a foreign software contract an unreliable fit.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Salary thresholds depend on the regional worker category; no single national threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No single generally applicable amount.

income_requirement_display.value: Category- and region-specific salary rules; no single national amount
income_requirement_display.notes: Not relevant to the selected foreign-contract profile because a Belgian employer must apply.

income_proof_months.notes: Not a prior-income route.

key_requirements.requirement: A Belgium-based employer must submit the combined work-and-residence application to the competent region.
The file includes passport, subsistence/employment evidence, criminal-record certificate, medical certificate and health insurance.

initial_validity.value: Limited and linked to the granted work and residence authorization
initial_validity.notes: Duration is decision- and employment-specific.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is normally filed through the employer before the A card expires.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved single permit authorizes work and residence for more than 90 days and normally results in an A card after registration.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially through later qualifying long-term residence, subject to applicable residence-counting and continuity rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not independently available for this profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through the general nationality rules after qualifying residence, but this route requires local employment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the application must be made by a Belgium-based employer.

rejected_routes.route_name: Belgian higher-education residence and post-study search year

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Student subsistence requirements are separate from remote-work income and may change by academic year.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No amount is used here because this is not a route based on the applicant's existing foreign degree or contract.

income_requirement_display.value: Student subsistence requirement applies; no remote-worker income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Requires admission to Belgian higher education.

income_proof_months.notes: Proof method varies, including blocked-account or guarantor arrangements.

key_requirements.requirement: Full-time enrolment or admission at a recognized Belgian higher-education institution, plus passport, applicable fee, sufficient means and insurance.
The 12-month search year is available after completing qualifying studies in Belgium, or qualifying EU mobility studies partly followed in Belgium.

initial_validity.value: Student A card normally one year; post-study search year maximum 12 months

extension_rules.value: Student residence can be renewed while qualifying studies continue; the search year is intended for finding employment or establishing a company leading to a work-purpose status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A successful Belgian study D-visa application leads to a temporary student A card; qualifying graduates may request a 12-month search year.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Not direct. The search year is designed for conversion to an employment or business status, and only half of qualifying study periods may count in the general long-term-resident calculation.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through later qualifying residence and the general nationality rules.

rejected_routes.notes: The applicant's existing foreign degree alone does not confer residence. This would require new Belgian study and is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

summary.value: Admission to recognized Belgian higher education can support an independent student D-visa application and temporary A card. A qualifying graduate may receive a maximum 12-month search year to find employment or establish a company. An already-held foreign software-engineering degree does not by itself create Belgian residence rights, and the post-study status must be converted to a work or business status.
summary.notes: This is a new-study pathway, not a degree-recognition or independent skilled-migration route for the current profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: Belgian tax residence is fact-based, not simply a 183-day test. A person is resident if their effective and permanent domicile, or otherwise the primary location of their assets/economic interests, is in Belgium. National-register entry creates a rebuttable presumption; for spouses or legal cohabitants, the household location is important.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A residence permit and municipal registration can therefore make residence likely from arrival, subject to facts and any tax treaty.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate for 2026 income, not an expected effective rate. The system is progressive, includes a personal allowance, and municipal surcharges or deductions can alter the result.

social_contributions_percent.notes: 2026 main-occupation self-employed rate on professional income up to EUR 75,024.54; 14.16% applies to the portion above that amount up to EUR 110,562.42. Fund management charges may be additional.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the 2026 minimum self-employed contribution of EUR 890.42 per quarter, converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. Actual payments are quarterly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime applies because Belgium has no such immigration category. Any separate inbound-taxpayer regime has its own employer/remuneration and filing conditions and should not be assumed to cover an ordinary foreign-client freelancer.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No route-specific exemption was found.

taxes.caveats: Belgian residents declare worldwide income, although a tax treaty may exempt particular income or grant foreign-tax relief. Contract classification, place where work is physically performed, permanent-establishment/VAT questions, deductions, municipal surtax and social-security coordination can materially change the result. Professional tax advice is appropriate before operating through a foreign employer or a foreign company from Belgium.

taxation_system.value: Progressive worldwide-income personal taxation for residents, with 2026 national brackets from 25% to 50%, an EUR 11,180 basic personal allowance, possible treaty relief and separate self-employed social contributions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Effective permanent domicile or primary location of assets/economic interests; national-register entry creates a rebuttable presumption.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents must declare worldwide income and foreign property; treaty provisions determine whether foreign income is taxed or exempted with progression/other effects.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Do not assume eligibility for Belgium's separate inbound taxpayer rules.
taxation_system.social_security: For a main-occupation self-employed person in 2026: 20.50% up to EUR 75,024.54, then 14.16% on the portion up to EUR 110,562.42, subject to a EUR 890.42 minimum quarterly contribution and possible fund charges.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 50% dashboard number is the top national marginal rate, not the effective burden. The basic allowance, deductions and local surcharge must be included in an individual calculation.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.
Marginal bracket.
Marginal bracket.
Top marginal bracket; not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official 2026 brackets and self-employed contribution figures were available.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific category. A person who actually settles and works from Belgium can become Belgian tax resident under the domicile/centre-of-interests test and must generally declare worldwide income; a locally registered self-employed person also enters the Belgian social-contribution system.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; ordinary resident/self-employed rules would apply
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 25%–50% progressive PIT; 50% is the top marginal screening rate, plus potential municipal effects
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Fact-based domicile or primary location of assets/economic interests, not an automatic 183-day safe harbor.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents declare worldwide income; applicable treaties determine exemption or credit treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None for digital nomads or ordinary foreign-client freelancers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A Belgian main-occupation self-employed person generally pays 20.5% on professional income through EUR 75,024.54, then 14.16% up to the 2026 ceiling, with a minimum quarterly contribution.

fixed_payments.status: Professional-card applicants and approved self-employed residents face both immigration/card fees and recurring social contributions.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Minimum EUR 890.42 per quarter in 2026 for a main-occupation self-employed person, excluding possible social-insurance-fund management charges.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Professional card: EUR 140 application plus EUR 90 per year of card validity; professional-card D-visa residence contribution: EUR 242 in 2026; general D-visa handling fee: EUR 250 from 1 July 2026. Translation, legalization, service-provider and municipal/card costs may be additional.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax was found. VAT and business-registration obligations depend on activity and turnover; Belgian residents may also encounter transaction-specific taxes unrelated to the visa.
fixed_payments.notes: Fees can change and consular service-provider charges vary by filing location.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay does not itself create a special nomad exemption. Tax residence remains fact-based, and Belgian-source or Belgium-performed work can still require analysis even if the person remains treaty-resident elsewhere.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Generally declares worldwide employment or freelance income and is taxed under the progressive system, subject to treaty relief and correct worker-versus-self-employed classification.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Register with the appropriate business and social-insurance systems; expect progressive PIT plus self-employed contributions and possible VAT/business obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax treatment is well documented, but there is no digital-nomad status to which a special result could attach.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The professional-card/D-visa process can lead directly to temporary residence after pre-approval, visa issuance, entry and municipal registration; no prior Belgian residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Belgium publishes a general five-year long-term-resident rule, but the reviewed official material does not clearly establish the exact professional-card A-card conversion/counting treatment. A route-specific number is therefore not stated.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Belgian nationality can generally be declared after five years of qualifying legal residence if the applicant holds unlimited residence at filing; it does not necessarily require an additional fixed period after obtaining that unlimited status.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General earliest statutory residence period, not a guarantee that the rejected professional-card scenario will produce the required unlimited status or satisfy all conditions by year five.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The prosecutor has four months from the complete-file receipt; the City of Brussels states municipal finalization may take another one to two months. Pre-filing document collection is additional.

key_conditions.value: At nationality filing: qualifying uninterrupted legal residence, an unlimited right of residence, knowledge of Dutch, French or German, social integration and economic participation. The ordinary five-year self-employed category uses at least six quarters of Belgian self-employed social contributions in the preceding five years. Long-term-resident status separately requires qualifying residence, stable means, health insurance, public-order compliance and absence limits.
key_conditions.notes: Belgium permits dual nationality under its rules, but retention of the applicant's present nationality also depends on the other country's law.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage does not reduce the general five-year legal-residence period. For the marriage-based declaration category, the couple must also have lived together in Belgium for at least three years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage to a Belgian can support family residence and later use of the five-year nationality-declaration category, but the spouses must genuinely live together in Belgium for at least three years and the applicant must still meet residence, language and integration requirements. Marriage to another non-Belgian does not independently create citizenship eligibility.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The nationality route is not citizenship by marriage automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: Authorities require civil-status and relationship evidence and may investigate or interview where proof is inadequate. Family residence also involves category-specific cohabitation, housing, insurance and means conditions. False documents or a sham relationship can cause refusal and broader immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Exact family-reunification conditions depend on whether the Belgian sponsor previously exercised EU free-movement rights.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Belgium is not unconditional jus soli. A child born in Belgium to foreign parents may obtain nationality through a declaration before age 12 when the child has resided there since birth, the parents have had Belgian main residence for at least ten years, and at least one parent has unlimited residence at declaration. Separate anti-statelessness and other statutory rules may also apply.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Birth in Belgium alone normally does not make the child Belgian. The official declaration route for a child under 12 requires birth and continuous main residence in Belgium, ten years of parental main residence and unlimited residence for at least one parent at declaration.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is application-based and conditional, not automatic citizenship at birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Belgium with a Belgian parent is automatically Belgian at birth. Rules for a child born abroad depend, among other things, on where the Belgian parent was born and may require a declaration before age five.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Belgian minor can support family reunification for a foreign mother or father who proves first-degree parentage, parental authority, effective day-to-day care and accompaniment or joining. The child does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Being the parent of a Belgian minor also provides a five-year nationality-declaration category with reduced integration/economic-participation evidence, but five years of legal residence and language/integration conditions remain.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Belgian minor may obtain family residence if he proves parentage, custody/parental authority and effective care. After five years of legal residence, parenthood of a Belgian minor can place him in the corresponding nationality-declaration category, but citizenship remains non-automatic.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Marginal contact or support is insufficient for the family-reunification right described by the Immigration Office.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026; Passport Index 2026 for category breakdown

rank.notes: Henley global rank on the page inspected on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score combines destinations accessible without obtaining a traditional visa in advance, including visa-on-arrival access; it is not the strict visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index breakdown, which uses a different universe and methodology from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reports 41 visa-on-arrival and 11 eTA destinations. Its strict visa-free count is 121, and its separate eVisa classifications mean the categories should not be summed against the Henley score.

passport.notes: Rank/access and category-breakdown figures come from two named indexes with different methodologies and should not be treated as one internally additive dataset.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Generally practical for day-to-day remote work and international technology settings: EF EPI 2025 ranks Belgium 9th of 123 with 'very high' English proficiency. Immigration, municipal, tax and integration procedures nevertheless operate in Dutch, French or German according to region, and Belgian nationality requires knowledge of a national language.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected-test index rather than an official population census; regional ability varies.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian may be useful within migrant communities but are not official administrative languages and should not be relied upon for professional-card, tax, municipal or citizenship procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national source quantifying Russian/Ukrainian service availability was found after focused research.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official EUR 4,076 gross monthly average for full-time employees in 2022.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official EUR 3,728 gross monthly median for full-time employees in 2022.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of Eurostat's EUR 2,112 national monthly minimum-wage measure for 1 January 2026. This is a policy minimum measure, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official wage value converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official wage value converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum is published. Statbel reports that the top decile earned at least EUR 6,305, but that is a percentile threshold, not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 2,112/month gross national minimum-wage measure at 1 January 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Eurostat harmonized monthly measure; Belgian sectoral minima may be higher.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Full-time employees, 2022 earnings survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Full-time employees, 2022 earnings survey.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No true maximum. For context only, 10% earned at least EUR 6,305/month in the survey.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly full-time employee earnings from Statbel; harmonized national minimum-wage measure from Eurostat
average_citizen_salary.period: Statbel wage reference: 2022, published 2024; minimum wage: January 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The official average and median are the latest detailed national wage-distribution figures located but are dated. USD values are screening conversions, not contemporaneous Belgian payroll statistics.

cost_of_living_note.value: Belgian living costs vary substantially by city and household. Eurostat reports Belgian household electricity at EUR 34.99 per 100 kWh in 2025, among the EU's highest, illustrating that utilities can be material; no single official national monthly cost-of-living budget was established.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A narrow official utility indicator is provided rather than an unsupported all-in budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Belgium has no dedicated digital-nomad residence status. Visitor or visa-free presence is not a citizenship-path substitute, and the professional card is a regional business route rather than permission to relocate solely on a foreign remote contract.
settlement_track.summary: Belgium is not valid for the ordinary foreign-contract profile. A qualifying regional entrepreneur may obtain professional-card-linked temporary residence and later pursue general settlement rules, but official sources do not establish that an ordinary foreign-client software contract satisfies the regional added-value test or guarantees conversion to unlimited residence.
settlement_track.notes: The prior record was too optimistic where it treated absence of a local employer as sufficient. The professional card also requires an approved Belgian self-employed project with regional business value.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker route was found. The professional card requires approved self-employed activity and regional business/economic or innovative value; a foreign software contract alone is not stated as sufficient.

data.notes: The no-match conclusion is based primarily on current federal and regional government sources. Belgium remains potentially relevant only if the applicant is prepared to build a substantive Belgian self-employed business project and obtain filing-specific regional confirmation.

data.selection_summary: Belize’s ordinary Permanent Residence rules are potentially attractive: after one year of lawful residence with no more than 14 total days abroad, an applicant may apply independently for permanent residence, and official financial-stability guidance expressly accepts foreign employment or foreign income. The unresolved blocker is the qualifying year: visitor extensions prohibit employment or engaging in a profession without the Immigration Director’s consent, while the dedicated remote-work Long Stay Permit lasts only six months, cannot be extended, and is restricted to citizens or permanent residents of the EU, UK, USA or Canada. Filing-level confirmation is therefore needed that ordinary foreign remote work can lawfully continue throughout the one-year qualifying period.

visa_application.title: Belize Residence Process
visa_application.notes: Permanent-residence applications are submitted in person at an authorized Immigration Office; no direct online residence application was found. The separate Long Stay Permit has an online portal, but that temporary visitor permit is not the selected settlement route.

best_routes.route_name: Permanent Residence after one year of lawful residence, supported by foreign income

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numerical minimum is published; the applicant must demonstrate continuing financial stability.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No numerical BZD threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; demonstrate continuing financial stability
income_requirement_display.notes: Foreign employment or income is expressly accepted as a possible basis for financial stability, but approval remains evidentiary and discretionary.

income_proof_months.notes: The official guide requests local or foreign bank statements for the preceding six months from applicants employed or receiving income outside Belize.

key_requirements.requirement: At least one year of lawful residence before filing, with no more than 14 total days outside Belize during that year.
Remain lawful under the current immigration status while the residence application is processed.
Demonstrate past and continuing financial stability; foreign employment/income and foreign bank statements may be used.
Foreign employment letter or contract stating hiring date, monthly salary and occupation, plus six months of bank statements.
Passport showing the qualifying arrival, Belize police record, Belize medical examination and HIV/VDRL/TB tests, photographs and supporting family documents where applicable.
Immigration and police interviews, two referees, security bond and nationality-based residence fee.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence
initial_validity.notes: The official material treats this as Permanent Residence rather than a renewable temporary permit; no periodic renewal rule was published on the inspected pages.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary renewal requirement identified for Permanent Residence; replacement or transfer procedures apply to cards or passport stamps.
extension_rules.notes: Confirm card validity and replacement obligations when issued.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying temporary-residence stage. Belize’s ordinary Temporary Residence category instead requires at least BZD 500,000 of investment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant would normally maintain a visitor or other lawful immigration status during the one-year qualifying period.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply directly for Permanent Residence after at least one year of lawful residence and financial stability, provided total absences during that year do not exceed 14 days.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official rules do not confirm that foreign remote work is permitted throughout a visitor-extension qualifying year without the Director’s consent.

path_to_citizenship.value: After holding Permanent Residence for at least five years, apply for citizenship by registration, subject to strict continuous-residence limits and other requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: After PR, absences generally must not exceed 30 consecutive days or three months cumulatively in any twelve-month period; limited employment-in-Belize and medical exceptions may be considered.

best_routes.notes: This is potentially a strong direct-PR route, and the official residence evidence specifically accommodates foreign employment. It is not marked fully valid because the official visitor rules prohibit employment or professional activity without the Director’s consent, and no inspected official source confirms a general remote-work permission capable of covering the entire one-year PR-qualifying period.

rejected_routes.route_name: Long Stay Visitor Permit for remote workers

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: USD 75,000 annual income for one applicant; USD 100,000 annually when applying with dependants.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Requirement is stated in USD: USD 75,000/year alone or USD 100,000/year with dependants
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: At Belize’s conventional BZD 2 per USD peg, the solo threshold corresponds to approximately BZD 12,500 monthly, but the official requirement is denominated in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 6,250/month alone; USD 8,333.33/month with dependants
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 75,000/year alone or USD 100,000/year with dependants
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an income threshold, not an expected salary in Belize.

income_proof_months.notes: A notarized bank reference and statement of account are required, but the page does not state a transaction-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be a citizen or permanent resident of the EU, UK, USA or Canada.
Employment must be outside Belize; self-employed applicants provide business registration and an annual tax return.
Police record issued within six months, certified passport copies and proof of qualifying residence where nationality itself is not on the approved list.
Travel insurance with at least USD 50,000 health coverage.
USD 500 adult fee and USD 200 child fee.

initial_validity.value: Six months, with presence limited to no more than six months in a calendar year
initial_validity.notes: The official page calls it a Long Stay Visitor Permit.

extension_rules.value: Cannot be extended

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a visitor permit, not Temporary Residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General PR is available after one lawful year, but the required successor stay/work permission after the long-stay permit is unconfirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official long-stay page was inaccessible; the 2021 amendment was available as indexed official text but its PDF opened to an account-suspended page. Current intake and seamless successor eligibility remain unconfirmed. The one-year figure is the general PR requirement, not a verified nomad-to-PR timeline. The 2020 Act section 19 requires written ministerial permission for employment within Belize.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path; citizenship normally requires five years as a permanent resident.

rejected_routes.notes: Good temporary remote-work fit only for the listed citizenship or residence groups, but it is temporary, nonextendable and not a confirmed settlement route. The prohibition on employment in Belize appears compatible with foreign remote work in context because outside employment is an eligibility condition, but this does not make it qualifying residence.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor’s Permit Extension followed by residence application

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is published for the extension.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income minimum
income_requirement_display.notes: This visitor extension is not an income-qualified remote-worker route.

income_proof_months.notes: The official extension page does not prescribe a monthly-income proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Extension is for another 30 days and costs BZD 200.
The holder may not enter paid or unpaid employment or engage in a business or profession without the Immigration Director’s consent.
Visitors investigating settlement may qualify, subject to an Immigration Office determination.

initial_validity.value: Additional 30 days per extension

extension_rules.value: Further eligibility must be determined by an Immigration Office; no guaranteed twelve-month extension sequence is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None direct

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A visitor may investigate settlement, but ordinary PR separately requires one year of lawful residence and financial stability.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Remote professional work during that qualifying period requires the Director’s consent under the visitor rule; no general approval mechanism or eligibility standard was found.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separately obtaining PR and then satisfying the five-year PR citizenship requirement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as an ordinary remote-work route because visitor status does not itself authorize professional activity. The possibility of case-specific consent is why the separate direct-PR route remains marked uncertain rather than definitively impossible.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum income test is published for this permit category. The current official fee schedule instead charges BZD 3,000 for a one-year self-employed permit; application guidance asks for a recent bank statement and an explanation of how the applicant will support themself.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum earnings amount is published in the current official route page, Immigration Act, government work-permit service listing or Labour Department guide. BZD 3,000 is the one-year permit fee, not an income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income minimum
income_requirement_display.notes: Applicants must document financial capacity with a recent bank statement and explain how they will sustain themselves, but the current sources set no numerical minimum.

income_proof_months.notes: A recent bank statement is required, but none of the current official materials inspected specifies how many months of statement history the work-permit application must cover. The separate PR application later requires six months of bank statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must already reside in Belize and hold a valid passport and Belize visa.
A self-employed applicant submits their own application; an employee’s employer applies on their behalf.
Approval is followed by an Income Tax Letter and permit processing at Immigration.
For residence evidence, a self-employed proprietor must show the employment permit, business registration, trade licence, Business Tax assessment and bank statements.

Current government application guidance requires a business plan for a self-employed applicant, a bank statement or support explanation, a Belize trade licence, business registration, qualifications and category-specific support documents.
The Immigration Act makes issuance discretionary, requires a Labour-authorized voucher and limits the holder to the employment specified in the permit unless the Director authorizes another employer.
Social Security registration for a self-employed person requires a card valid for employment, proof of a Belize address and, where applicable, local business, tax and trade-licence documents.

initial_validity.value: One year for self-employed workers classified as owners or managers; BZD 3,000 permit fee
initial_validity.notes: The Immigration Act limits authorization to the employment and period stated in the permit; the current Immigration fee table specifies one year for the self-employed category.

extension_rules.value: No automatic renewal or route-specific extension rule is published in the current official work-permit page, Immigration Act, government service listing or Labour Department guide; continued activity after the one-year permit therefore requires a fresh or renewed authorization confirmed with Labour and Immigration.
extension_rules.notes: The absence of a published renewal procedure is not evidence that renewal is legally unavailable; it means timing, evidence and repeat fees must be verified directly with the issuing offices.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Does not itself grant Temporary Residence
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a temporary employment authorization tied to specified activity, not Belize’s separate Temporary Residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: It may help maintain lawful status for the ordinary one-year PR rule, but requires a properly registered and licensed Belize business rather than merely retaining a foreign client.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A qualifying local self-employed business permit could support lawful presence and later PR evidence, but approval is discretionary and tied to the specified Belize activity. The sources require a Belize business plan, registration and trade licence and do not establish that software work performed solely under a foreign client contract qualifies without genuine local business establishment.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separately obtaining PR and then holding it for five years.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this ordinary foreign-contract profile after focused review. Independent filing exists, and the current Immigration schedule identifies a one-year, BZD 3,000 self-employed category for owners or managers. However, this is discretionary Belize work authorization, not a general freelancer or remote-worker residence permit: the Immigration Act confines it to the employment specified in the permit; official application guidance requires a self-employed business plan, Belize business registration and trade licence, bank or support evidence, and relevant qualifications; Social Security materials require a Belize address and an employment-valid card. None of the current official sources says that merely retaining an overseas software client, without operating a genuinely registered and licensed Belize business, is eligible specified activity. Conversely, none expressly excludes an export-services Belize business, so such a structure could be tested only through a business-specific filing with Labour and Immigration; it should not be treated as an ordinary foreign-contract route in this selection.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The qualifying requirement is capital investment, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least BZD 500,000 investment

income_requirement_display.value: BZD 500,000 minimum Belize investment
income_requirement_display.notes: This substantial-investment route is excluded by the applicant-selection rules.

income_proof_months.notes: A monthly-income proof period is inapplicable because qualification depends on investment evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Evidence of Belize investments worth at least BZD 500,000, plus local residence evidence, police record and a letter to the Director.

initial_validity.value: One year

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct one-year Temporary Residence

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current official route information does not publish a route-specific conversion from investment Temporary Residence to Permanent Residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The citizenship page requires five years as a Permanent Resident; it does not state that investment Temporary Residence time counts.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial capital investment and is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

summary.value: No general independent degree- or qualification-based residence route for an ordinary non-CARICOM software engineer was confirmed. Belize publishes CSME skilled-person forms for qualifying CARICOM nationals, but that nationality-specific free-movement framework is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route and cannot be assumed applicable to this applicant.
summary.notes: A relevant degree alone does not establish eligibility for Belize residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if domiciled in Belize or present for more than 182 days during the basis year; another provision uses more than 183 days for Part X. Filing advice is needed around the wording difference.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The practical screening threshold is approximately 183 days, but domicile can establish residence earlier.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Flat statutory rate on chargeable employment income or other individual chargeable income, not an expected effective rate. Resident-employed personal deductions can substantially reduce the effective burden.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 7% figure applies to an ordinarily resident person who opts into the self-employed Social Security program and is calculated on declared weekly income, not necessarily actual remote-work income. Ordinary employee contribution rates are banded and reach 4.5% of capped weekly insurable earnings, with the employer funding the balance of the 10% total.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal mandatory monthly fixed payment was established for a foreign-employed remote worker. Optional self-employed contributions vary with declared income; at the lowest BZD 55 weekly declaration, the contribution is BZD 3.85 per contribution week.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime was found. The Act exempts foreign-arising income of a person present only temporarily, without intent to establish residence, who has spent less than six months in Belize; however, employment physically exercised in Belize is statutorily deemed Belize-source, so this exemption should not be assumed to cover remote salary.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The Long Stay Permit page itself publishes no tax holiday or exemption.

taxes.caveats: Belize generally taxes income accruing in or derived from Belize. Employment exercised physically in Belize is deemed Belize-source even when paid abroad. Classification as employee versus independent professional materially changes the calculation: employment income is taxed at 25% of chargeable income after applicable relief, while a locally carried-on profession may instead face business tax—generally 6% of gross professional receipts, subject to exemptions and filing rules. Obtain Belize Tax Service advice before treating foreign salary as exempt or choosing a structure.

taxation_system.value: Territorial/source-based system with a flat 25% individual income-tax rate on chargeable income; Belize-source employment includes work physically exercised in Belize. Self-employed professional activity can instead attract business tax at 6% of gross receipts.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or roughly 183 days; statutory provisions use more than 182 days in one section and more than 183 days in Part X.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income accruing in or derived from Belize. Employment exercised in Belize is Belize-source regardless of where payment is received.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime confirmed. A narrow temporary-purpose exemption exists for foreign-arising income where the person lacks settlement intent and remains under six months, but remote salary earned through work in Belize may be Belize-source and outside that exemption.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed participation is optional for an ordinarily resident qualifying person at 7% of selected declared weekly income. Employee contributions are wage-banded; the 2024 schedule shows up to 4.5% employee plus 5.5% employer on capped insurable earnings.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% personal rate is flat, not progressive. Resident employees receive tiered basic deductions: BZD 25,600 when total income is at most BZD 26,000; BZD 24,600 up to BZD 27,000; BZD 22,600 up to BZD 29,000; and BZD 19,600 otherwise. Total income below BZD 20,000 is expressly exempt.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Resident employed individual with total income below BZD 20,000 is expressly exempt
tax_brackets.notes: Basic deductions may also produce no chargeable income at higher total-income levels.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Chargeable income after applicable resident deductions
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment income and other individual chargeable income
tax_brackets.notes: Flat statutory rate; this is a screening rate rather than expected effective tax.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Professional or vocational gross receipts; exemption where receipts are below BZD 20,000 and are the taxpayer’s only livelihood
tax_brackets.applies_to: Business tax on self-employed profession, vocation or occupation
tax_brackets.notes: Gross-receipts business tax, not personal income tax; classification should be confirmed with Belize Tax Service.

taxation_system.notes: The core rates and source rule come from primary legislation. Filing treatment for a foreign employer, permanent-establishment risk and interaction between income tax and business tax require individual advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax exemption is published. Remote employment physically exercised in Belize is deemed Belize-source and can be taxed at 25% of chargeable income; an independent professional may instead fall within 6% gross-receipts business tax. A temporary-purpose foreign-income exemption exists, but its application to remote salary is doubtful because of the physical-work source rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary foreign remote worker or possible Belize-source employee; alternatively self-employed professional
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 25% flat on chargeable employment income; potential 6% gross-receipts business tax for independent professional activity
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or approximately 183 days, subject to statutory wording differences.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-arising income may be outside the tax base or qualify for the under-six-month temporary-purpose exemption, but salary for employment exercised while physically in Belize is expressly deemed derived from Belize even if paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No mandatory Long Stay Permit payroll regime was found. Optional self-employed Social Security is 7% of declared weekly income for qualifying ordinarily resident persons; local employees have banded employee and employer contributions.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly tax or contribution established for the Long Stay remote worker
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Optional self-employed contribution begins at BZD 3.85 per contribution week on BZD 55 declared weekly income and rises to BZD 22.40 on BZD 320.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Long Stay Permit: USD 500 per adult and USD 200 per child. Visitor extension: BZD 200 for 30 days. Permanent Residence: BZD 1,000–6,000 depending on nationality; European-country nationals, including Ukraine, are listed at BZD 6,000.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business or trade licensing and tax registration may apply to locally registered self-employed activity; no single national fixed monthly amount was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Residence medical examinations, police records, translations, insurance and security-bond costs may add variable expenses.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Do not assume zero tax. The Act’s temporary-purpose exemption is limited to foreign-arising income, no settlement intent and less than six months, while remote employment physically exercised in Belize is deemed Belize-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Screen at 25% of chargeable employment income after applicable resident relief; confirm foreign tax credits, treaty position and employer obligations.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A profession or vocation carried on in Belize can face business tax at 6% of gross receipts, subject to the BZD 20,000 only-source-of-livelihood exemption and other rules; optional self-employed Social Security is 7% of declared weekly income.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The immigration permit does not itself determine tax residence or income source.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The potentially useful route proceeds from lawful immigration status to Permanent Residence; ordinary Temporary Residence is an unrelated investment category.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Shown as one year to PR from lawful residence, not one year after obtaining Belize Temporary Residence. Total absence during that year may not exceed 14 days.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Applicant must hold PR for at least five years and meet strict continuous-residence rules.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Best-case statutory sequence: one qualifying year before PR plus five years holding PR. Residence and citizenship processing time makes the real elapsed period longer.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official process describes submission, interview, vetting, approval, payment and swearing-in but publishes no total processing-time estimate.

key_conditions.value: Maintain lawful status during the pre-PR year; no more than 14 total days abroad in that year; prove financial stability and good character. After PR, generally avoid absences exceeding 30 consecutive days or three months total in any twelve-month period, retain passports, obtain Belize police and medical evidence and provide two born-Belizean referees acquainted with the applicant for five years. Guatemalan nationals are stated not to qualify for citizenship through registration.
key_conditions.notes: No general language test was identified on the official citizenship pages inspected. Only Indian nationals are expressly required by the published requirements to submit a declaration of renunciation.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage to a Belizean national for at least one year creates a direct citizenship-by-registration eligibility category.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count once the spouse is a Belizean citizen and the one-year marriage period is met. The official eligibility wording covers a spouse born Belizean or one who acquired citizenship before the marriage. Marriage to another migrant has no independent acceleration beyond possible dependent inclusion.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Foreign marriage certificates must be authenticated or apostilled.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must submit the marriage application form, proof of marriage, the spouse’s Belize citizenship evidence, passport, police record, Belize medical examination and HIV/VDRL tests, two born-Belizean referees acquainted with the spouse for at least one year and other civil documents. Approval follows interview and nationality vetting; marriage does not make citizenship automatic, and false documents or a non-genuine relationship risk refusal or later legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official pages do not publish a separate minimum physical-presence period or total processing time for marriage registration; confirm these points before relying on the shortcut.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship at birth to every person born in Belize after independence, subject only to narrow diplomat-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Belize to two migrant parents is automatically a citizen unless the narrow diplomatic-immunity or wartime enemy-occupation exception applies. Birth outside Belize would not qualify merely because the parents are migrants.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Belize is a citizen by birth regardless; a child born outside Belize on or after independence is a citizen by descent when either parent is a Belize citizen.

parent_benefit_summary.value: No generally applicable automatic residence, PR or citizenship grant to the migrant parent was found merely because the child is a Belize citizen. The parent must qualify under an existing immigration or nationality category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A 2022 nationality amendment referenced Belize-born children in a specific amnesty context, but that does not establish a continuing general parent route.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father does not automatically acquire status or citizenship through the child. Any family sponsorship or discretionary benefit should be confirmed directly with Immigration for the family’s facts.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No current official general parent-of-citizen route was confirmed after focused searching.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on the live Passport Index page on 2026-08-15. Henley’s 17 June 2026 ranking instead placed Belize 51st with a score of 100 because index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s strictly visa-free category; it excludes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Live Passport Index count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 37 visa-on-arrival plus 6 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately treats eVisas, so totals should not be compared directly with Henley’s combined access score.

passport.notes: Passport figures are volatile. Henley’s 17 June 2026 PDF lists Belize at rank 51 with a combined visa-free or visa-on-arrival score of 100; Passport Index is used for the requested categorical breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English is the official language and the working language of official immigration materials; Spanish, Belizean Creole and indigenous languages are also widely spoken.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Internet quality and reliability vary by location and were not quantified in this audit.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low for official processes: no official source inspected identified Russian or Ukrainian as widely used, while immigration and government services operate in English. English ability is therefore important.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from official language information, not a measured count of Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking communities.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official release and labour-force landing page inspected did not publish a national median. Older abstracts contain historical medians, but these were not substituted for a current value.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official national materials inspected do not publish a median salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum was published. The same release reported occupation averages of BZD 2,257 for professionals and BZD 2,238 for managers, but these are group averages rather than a maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum effective 1 January 2023 and still the latest official minimum identified.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly income of employed persons, September 2025.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The current official release and statistical landing page do not publish a national median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official release does not publish a national maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.period: September 2025 average; statutory minimum current as last officially confirmed
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is across employed persons, not specifically software engineers. Professionals averaged BZD 2,257 monthly in the September 2025 release. USD conversions use the conventional BZD 2 = USD 1 peg.

cost_of_living_note.value: The official CPI measures price changes rather than a complete monthly living budget. The current basket is based on the 2018 Household Expenditure Survey; current SIB releases should be used to update local price assumptions, while housing and island or tourist-area costs require location-specific checking.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The official source does not publish a reliable single-person monthly cost-of-living total, so no total is inferred.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The dedicated Long Stay remote-work permit is temporary, nonextendable and does not itself establish a settlement path. The potentially qualifying route is the separate ordinary Permanent Residence process after one year of lawful presence.
settlement_track.summary: Ordinary Permanent Residence can lead to citizenship after five PR years and expressly accepts foreign income as financial support. The track remains uncertain because official sources do not confirm how an ordinary remote worker may lawfully perform foreign professional work throughout the strict one-year pre-PR residence period; visitor status requires the Director’s consent for such activity.
settlement_track.notes: A filing-level ruling from Belize Immigration should confirm that the applicant’s exact foreign contract is permitted under the immigration status used during the qualifying year and that the entire period counts as lawful residence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign employment is accepted as PR financial evidence, but the six-month Long Stay Permit cannot complete the one-year PR period and visitor status restricts professional activity without official consent. The self-employed permit instead requires a specified, registered and licensed Belize business activity; the current sources do not confirm that an ordinary overseas software contract alone qualifies.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous Belize record. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including six official or primary URLs not in the prior source set. The self-employed Temporary Employment Permit is now documented as a discretionary one-year local-business authorization requiring business-plan, registration, trade-licence and financial-support evidence; current sources do not establish ordinary foreign-client software work without a genuine Belize business as eligible specified activity. The overall uncertain selection result therefore remains unchanged.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: A successor lawful-stay permission covering the full qualifying year, with any required work authorization
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Ordinary PR requires one year of lawful residence, financial stability and no more than 14 days abroad. A continuous remote-work successor after the short long-stay permit could not be confirmed.
requirements: Maintain lawful status for at least one year with total absences of no more than 14 days.
Establish permission for continued remote professional activity under any successor permit.
Provide financial-stability and criminal-record evidence.
reviewed_route_names: Long Stay Visitor Permit for remote workers
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The official long-stay page was inaccessible; the 2021 amendment was available as indexed official text but its PDF opened to an account-suspended page. Current intake and seamless successor eligibility remain unconfirmed. The one-year figure is the general PR requirement, not a verified nomad-to-PR timeline. The 2020 Act section 19 requires written ministerial permission for employment within Belize.

data.selection_summary: Benin has a potentially relevant independent route: a foreigner may apply for a three-year ordinary resident card by showing means of subsistence, third-party support, income-generating activity, or another legitimate interest. A local employer is not expressly required, but current official guidance does not confirm that foreign-client remote work is authorized or clarify whether local business/work registration is required. Filing-level confirmation from DEI is therefore necessary.

visa_application.title: Carte de résident — online application start
visa_application.notes: Official online start for resident-card applications. Payment starts online, followed by in-person filing and enrolment at DEI. The portal does not specifically identify foreign remote workers as eligible.

best_routes.route_name: Ordinary resident card based on means of subsistence or lawful income-generating activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numerical minimum is published; sufficient means, qualifying activity, support, or another legitimate interest must be shown.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No XOF threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; sufficient means or a qualifying activity/support basis is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sufficient means, third-party support, income-generating activity, or another legitimate interest
income_requirement_display.notes: DEI must confirm whether a foreign software contract is accepted and whether separate business or work registration is required.

income_proof_months.notes: The dossier requests evidence of employment, activity, means, or support but specifies no income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Show sufficient means, third-party support, income-generating activity, or another legitimate interest in residing in Benin.
Provide the application, photographs, a passport valid for more than one year, foreign-person identification certificate, and criminal-record certificate.
Pay online and attend DEI for filing and enrolment; a neighborhood inquiry may occur.
Obtain written confirmation that foreign-client remote work is lawful and whether IFU, sole-proprietor, professional, or work authorization is required.

initial_validity.value: 3 years
initial_validity.notes: Current DEI guidance describes the ordinary resident card as valid for three years.

extension_rules.value: Renewable. Privileged-resident status may be requested after two renewals if the applicant also proves permanent activity, property, effective marital residence, or a functioning local enterprise.
extension_rules.notes: DEI does not state whether privileged status may be filed immediately when the second renewal is issued or only after the resulting renewed card expires.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval of the ordinary resident card directly establishes renewable three-year residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence rather than an eVisa or visitor status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No formally permanent status was identified. A 10-year privileged resident card may follow two ordinary-card renewals plus a durable qualifying connection.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Current DEI guidance calls this a 10-year privileged resident card, not permanent residence. Since ordinary cards last three years, renewals ordinarily occur around years 3 and 6, but DEI does not say whether privileged status is available immediately after issuance of the second renewal or only after that renewed card runs its course. Law No. 2025-15 leaves detailed conditions to an implementing decree, and no current published decree reviewed here establishes an indefinite residence right. Older Law No. 86-012 described the privileged card as renewable by right, but it predates and was replaced by the 2025 framework, so it cannot establish current permanent-residence status.

path_to_citizenship.value: Discretionary naturalization is available after five years of qualifying residence, subject to the nationality code's other conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The code requires five years plus professional occupation, assimilation, good character, health, and tax compliance. The Ministry checklist advertises six-month processing and requests residence, work/business, and tax evidence, but its reference to more than three years of residence conflicts with the newer five-year rule and appears stale. Absence-counting rules for ordinary-card holders were not published.

best_routes.notes: This is settlement-oriented general residence, not a digital-nomad program. It may accept foreign income as proof of means, but official sources do not expressly authorize ordinary foreign-client remote work. Manual DEI confirmation remains decisive.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies to this entry visa.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable — tourist/visit entry visa
income_requirement_display.notes: The eVisa does not establish residence or a remote-worker category.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-work income-history requirement is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply online using passport and travel information and pay the applicable visa fee.
Available visitor products cover 30-day single/multiple entry or 90-day multiple entry.

initial_validity.value: 30 days single or multiple entry, or 90 days multiple entry
initial_validity.notes: Visitor validity only.

extension_rules.value: A tourist/visit visa may be renewed for the same stay duration, but no direct conversion right was identified.
extension_rules.notes: Residence requires a separate resident-card application.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct path; the person must separately qualify for a resident card.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The eVisa itself is not residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The eVisa creates no permanent- or privileged-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The eVisa is expressly a tourist/visit visa for stays of no more than 90 days, renewable once for the same stay. Naturalization instead requires five years of qualifying residence, and the Ministry dossier requires residence, work/business, and tax evidence. No current source treats tourist/visit-visa time as that residence; the eVisa therefore has no citizenship path of its own. A resident card must be obtained separately.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this is short-stay visitor permission, not a remote-worker or settlement status.
