minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is published; qualifying zone activity is required instead.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly threshold; qualifying ZES investor/operator activity required
income_requirement_display.notes: Ordinary foreign-client software work does not satisfy the published zone profile.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Be a foreign investor or operator working in the Glo-Djigbé Special Economic Zone.
Pay XOF 350,000 and complete the online appointment/payment process.

initial_validity.value: 5 years
initial_validity.notes: Published ZES-card validity.

extension_rules.notes: Current DEI guidance does not publish renewal conditions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct five-year ZES resident card for qualifying investors/operators.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Restricted to the published zone profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence grant is published.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization rules may apply to qualifying residence, but no ZES-specific transition is published.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This route is inapplicable to the ordinary remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires investor/operator activity in a designated Beninese economic zone.

summary.value: A study visa is available for study or training for up to 12 months and is renewable for the same duration. It is not direct resident status or an independent degree-based migration route.
summary.notes: No points-based, graduate, or degree-only residence route was identified.

tax_residency_rule.value: Fiscal domicile arises through a permanent home, center of vital interests, or—if those tests are inconclusive—at least 183 days of habitual presence in a 12-month period.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A permanent home or center of vital interests can establish residence before day 183.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal employment-income screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Independent activity may instead face 30% business-profit tax or, if eligible, 5% of receipts under the synthetic regime.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 3.6% figure is only the employee share of the 10% pension contribution under salaried payroll; it is not a freelancer rate. Employers additionally bear 6.4% pension, 9% family benefits, and 1%-4% occupational-risk contributions. For self-employed workers, CLEISS says occupational-risk contributions apply only to specified non-salaried categories and that, after dissolution of the former CMPS under Decree No. 2023-600, the collecting body for independent-worker sickness and old-age contributions remained unspecified. No universal mandatory percentage or fixed monthly amount can therefore be stated for an ordinary foreign-client freelancer; foreign-payroll coverage also requires CNSS confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly freelancer payment is published. The synthetic tax has an annual XOF 10,000 minimum plus a XOF 4,000 annual broadcasting levy when applicable.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound exemption was identified. Eligible small businesses may pay 5% of annual receipts under the synthetic professional tax, subject to a XOF 10,000 minimum and XOF 4,000 levy; newly registered enterprises receive a first-12-month exemption. Individual business profits otherwise generally face 30%.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The applicable turnover threshold is prescribed separately and was not established in the reviewed material.

taxes.caveats: Treatment depends on whether foreign income is salary or business receipts. Treaty residence, foreign-employer permanent-establishment exposure, VAT, IFU/business registration, CNSS coverage, and deductions require individualized advice.

taxation_system.value: Mixed: progressive employment-income tax up to 30%, generally 30% on individual business profits, and potentially 5% of receipts under the synthetic regime.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, center of vital interests, or fallback presence of at least 183 days in 12 months.
taxation_system.income_scope: Foreign-paid salary is taxable when the beneficiary is fiscally domiciled in Benin. Business-profit rules are framed around profits realized in or allocated to Benin.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No nomad regime; qualifying small businesses may use the 5%-of-receipts synthetic tax.
taxation_system.social_security: For Beninese salaried payroll, the employee pension share is 3.6% and employer charges are 15.4%-18.4%. This is not a freelancer rate. Independent-worker sickness/old-age collection remained institutionally unspecified after dissolution of the former CMPS, while occupational-risk coverage applies only to listed categories.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Monthly employment brackets apply. The displayed 30% is the top marginal rate above XOF 500,000 per month, not the effective rate.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate conversion at XOF 578.25/USD.
USD figure is the approximate upper boundary.
Approximate upper boundary.
Approximate upper boundary.
Top marginal bracket begins above approximately USD 865.

taxation_system.notes: Tax rates and residence tests are well supported. Social-security rates are high-confidence only for Beninese salaried payroll; no universal freelancer percentage is published.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated nomad category exists. A resident foreign-employee scenario is screened at progressive tax up to 30%; independent activity may face 30% business-profit tax or eligible 5%-of-receipts synthetic tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: General resident receiving foreign salary or conducting independent business
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 30% top marginal employment rate; alternative self-employed regimes may apply
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home or vital interests can create residence before the fallback 183-day test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-paid salary is taxable for a Benin-domiciled person; business-profit rules are territorially framed.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Beninese payroll uses a 3.6% employee pension share and 15.4%-18.4% employer charges. No reviewed source establishes that a foreign employer without Beninese payroll must register or that an ordinary freelancer owes the employee rate.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment; general taxes and card fees may apply
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed monthly self-employed contribution is published; the post-CMPS sickness/old-age collection mechanism remained unspecified.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Ordinary resident card: XOF 250,000 for non-ECOWAS nationals or XOF 50,000 for ECOWAS nationals.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Where applicable, synthetic-tax minimum XOF 10,000 annually plus XOF 4,000 broadcasting levy; salary tax also carries March/June broadcasting levies.
fixed_payments.notes: A repatriation deposit and associated DEI payment may apply, but no stable general amount is published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Under 183 days does not guarantee non-residence where a permanent home or center of vital interests exists.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A Benin-domiciled foreign-paid employee is subject to monthly employment-income declarations and progressive tax.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A registered independent may fall under 30% business-profit tax or eligible 5%-of-receipts synthetic tax; residence approval does not settle business, VAT, or CNSS duties.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax code addresses foreign-paid salary, but no administrative guidance specifically covers digital nomads or foreign-client software freelancers.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The card grants residence upon approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No permanent status is published. The 10-year privileged card follows two renewals, but its earliest filing point and indefinite character are not established.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on qualifying residence rather than prior permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the statutory threshold; approval remains discretionary and absence counting requires confirmation.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Ministry advertises six months and a XOF 45,000 fee. This is an administrative target, not a guaranteed maximum. Its outdated reference to more than three years of residence conflicts with the newer five-year statutory rule.

key_conditions.value: Maintain qualifying residence; show good character, health, assimilation, professional occupation, and tax compliance.
key_conditions.notes: The five-year statutory rule controls over the Ministry page's stale three-year documentary reference.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Five years from marriage under the promulgated code.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage to a Beninese citizen may qualify after five years; a foreign marriage must be transcribed in Beninese civil-status records.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to a non-Beninese spouse gives no acceleration.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must remain valid and genuine. False civil-status evidence or a sham marriage risks refusal, loss of status, and penalties.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Current filing requirements should be confirmed with the Ministry of Justice.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The 2022 code grants nationality to a child born in Benin, with a right of repudiation at majority; narrow diplomatic or proof issues may apply.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Benin is Beninese even when both parents are foreign migrants.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth registration and proof remain essential.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of either a Beninese father or mother is Beninese by descent, subject to filiation proof.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Maternal and paternal transmission are equalized.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. Family ties may support a residence application, but no automatic parent PR or shortened naturalization right was identified.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Confirm any parent-of-citizen residence basis with DEI.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father receives no automatic citizenship or residence solely because the child is Beninese.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parenthood may support a discretionary family-residence case.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 30 visa-on-arrival plus 2 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 67; methodologies differ from Henley.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only remote work is possible in an international circle, but administration, immigration, tax, banking, and ordinary services primarily use French. EF's 2025 score of 406 ranks Benin in the very-low-proficiency category.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI reflects test participants rather than a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or broadly documented working languages; French interpretation would generally be necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No national Russian/Ukrainian proficiency dataset was identified.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey does not publish a clean national median amount.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No clean national median amount is published.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum or salary ceiling is published.

average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum is statutory; the average is dated survey income for employed persons, not an immigration threshold.

cost_of_living_note.value: Nominal local incomes are low, but the World Bank indicators do not supply a dependable Cotonou remote-worker budget; imported goods, secure housing, private healthcare, and international-standard connectivity may cost substantially more than local-income comparisons imply.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No authoritative current remote-worker cost basket was identified.

settlement_track.summary: The ordinary resident card is genuine renewable residence, and general naturalization is available after five years. The track remains uncertain because official sources do not expressly authorize ordinary foreign-client remote work or state how all ordinary-card time and absences are counted.
settlement_track.notes: Written confirmation from DEI and the Ministry of Justice is needed before treating the route as fully matched.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A local employer is not expressly mandatory and sufficient means can support the application. Official guidance nevertheless does not state that a foreign-client software contract is an authorized activity or whether local sole-proprietor/work registration is compulsory.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed. The flagged notes now distinguish the 10-year privileged card from permanent residence, explain why eVisa time is inapplicable to naturalization, and separate the 3.6% employee pension share from the unresolved freelancer/foreign-payroll position. The Ministry's six-month naturalization target was added with a warning that its three-year documentary reference conflicts with the newer five-year law. data.selection_summary: Bhutan does not currently offer a digital-nomad, ordinary foreign-remote-worker, freelance, or self-sponsored professional residence route. Tourist, employment, student, business, professional, skilled-worker, overseas-employee, and investor permissions are non-immigrant categories; the current Immigration Rules expressly bar non-immigrants from applying for permanent residence or citizenship. Local employment needs Labour approval and employer undertakings, while business and investment categories require approved activity in Bhutan.

visa_application.title: Bhutan Immigration Services Portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct tourist visa/permit portal. It directs non-tourists to the Department of Immigration website; no application channel for a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker status was found.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists. Applicants must instead show adequate means for the visit.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current immigration rules require adequate means for the visit but publish no fixed BTN amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker income threshold; this is a tourist visit, not residence.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Adequate means to support the visit, without a published amount
income_requirement_display.notes: The adequate-means requirement is discretionary and is not a digital-nomad income test.

income_proof_months.notes: The current tourist portal and general immigration information do not prescribe a fixed income-history or bank-statement lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport valid for at least six months after the intended departure date and a recent passport photograph.
Adequate means to support the visit without recourse to public funds.
The e-Visa does not itself guarantee admission; immigration endorses the authorized stay at entry.

initial_validity.value: Tourist permission is limited to the actual visit or 90 days, whichever is less; the rules also provide for entry endorsement for the actual duration or 30 days, whichever is less.
initial_validity.notes: The interaction between the 30-day entry endorsement and 90-day tourist ceiling should be confirmed for the applicant's itinerary.

extension_rules.value: Any extension must be processed before expiry; it remains tourist/non-immigrant permission.
extension_rules.notes: An extension does not convert the visit into qualifying residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No tourist-to-residence conversion for ordinary foreign-client remote work was found.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A purpose change generally requires departure, and every identified alternative category has separate eligibility.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None: non-immigrants are expressly ineligible to apply for permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: None: non-immigrants are expressly ineligible to apply for citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this is visitor permission, not authorization to establish residence or work remotely. Even if short incidental activity were tolerated in practice, no official source creates a foreign-remote-work right or settlement path.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No self-sponsored income threshold applies; eligibility depends on an approved Bhutan employment arrangement.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker threshold applies; Labour approval and employer sponsorship determine eligibility.

income_requirement_display.value: No independent income threshold; approved employment and employer sponsorship are required.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Approved local employment; no self-sponsored income formula
income_requirement_display.notes: Salary is not a substitute for Labour approval and employer undertakings.

income_proof_months.notes: The official work-permit requirements do not prescribe an independent income-history period because this is an employer-sponsored category.

key_requirements.requirement: Approval from the Department of Labour.
Employer and employee undertakings and an employment visa or entry permit.
Medical fitness screening, including general health and drug testing.
From 7 May 2026, a Bhutanese bank account is mandatory for foreign workers working longer than 30 days.

initial_validity.value: Permit validity depends on the approved employment category and tenure.
initial_validity.notes: No uniform validity suitable for an independently contracted remote worker was found.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continuing employer, Labour, and immigration approval.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary stay is possible only for approved Bhutan employment, not independently for a foreign client.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None through this status: skilled workers and professionals are non-immigrants barred from applying for permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: None through this status: non-immigrants are barred from applying for citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires an approved local employer or project and employer undertakings. A foreign-client contract does not meet that requirement, and non-immigrant time does not provide a PR or citizenship application right.

rejected_routes.route_name: Business person / FDI promoter or investor permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income test exists; approved local business or FDI activity is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Investment and approval requirements depend on the underlying Bhutan business or FDI authorization; no ordinary contractor-income floor applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No ordinary remote-worker threshold; approved Bhutan business/FDI activity is required.
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a sole-proprietor legalization route for a foreign-client contractor.

income_proof_months.notes: The current non-tourist guidelines do not publish a standardized personal-income lookback period for this approval-based business/FDI category.

key_requirements.requirement: Government or Department of Industry approval for the underlying business or FDI activity.
Genuine promoter, investor, managerial, or technical involvement in an approved Bhutan operation.
A relevant government agency must recommend and vet the non-tourist application.

initial_validity.value: Tied to the approved business or investor permit.
initial_validity.notes: A standardized remote-worker validity period is not applicable.

extension_rules.value: Dependent on continued underlying business/FDI and government approval.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An investor permit may authorize temporary stay for an approved FDI operation.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This remains a non-immigrant category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None through this status: business persons and investors are non-immigrants barred from applying for permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: None through this status: non-immigrants are barred from applying for citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires approved Bhutan business or FDI activity, not ordinary work for a foreign client. It is also expressly non-settlement status.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The 2026 guideline asks applicants to disclose annual income in broad USD bands and attach proof, but it does not state a minimum qualifying monthly or annual income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current 2026 student guideline contains no minimum income denominated in BTN. Its means-of-subsistence form records annual income in USD bands and asks for proof of income without publishing a pass/fail floor.

income_requirement_display.value: Annual USD income must be disclosed and supported, but no minimum qualifying amount is published.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Annual income bands: less than USD 10,000; USD 10,000–50,000; USD 50,000–100,000; or more than USD 100,000. These are disclosure bands, not minimum-income thresholds.
income_requirement_display.notes: The applicant's existing degree does not qualify independently; actual admission and institutional processing are required. The form also collects a parent's income details where relevant.

income_proof_months.notes: The 2026 means-of-subsistence form requires proof of income but specifies neither a bank-statement lookback period nor a number of months of income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Admission to an eligible Bhutan educational institution and a recommendation from the relevant agency.
Completed visa application, means-of-subsistence form, statement of purpose, passport, and proof of income.
For the student permit, institute and student undertakings and a Bhutan-issued medical fitness certificate are required.

initial_validity.value: Up to five years or the actual course duration, whichever is less.

extension_rules.value: Limited by continuing study and the five-year or course-duration ceiling.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary non-immigrant stay for study only.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None through student status; non-immigrants cannot apply for permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: None through student status; non-immigrants cannot apply for citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires actual enrollment, is not based merely on possessing a degree, and is expressly excluded from PR and citizenship applications.

summary.value: No independent degree- or qualification-based residence route was found. A student can receive temporary non-immigrant permission after admission, and academic qualifications may support an employer-sponsored work-permit application, but neither an existing software-engineering degree nor student status creates independent residence or PR eligibility.
summary.notes: Student, professional, and skilled-worker categories are non-immigrant statuses expressly barred from PR and citizenship applications.

tax_residency_rule.value: Under section 226 of the Income Tax Act 2025, an individual is resident for an income year if domiciled in Bhutan subject to the permanent-home exception, present for an aggregate of at least 183 days in a qualifying 12-month period, or a Bhutan government employee posted abroad.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration permission and tax residence are separate questions.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate from income year 2026, not the expected effective rate. Annual taxable income below BTN 300,000 is nil-rated, with progressive rates through 30% above BTN 3.5 million.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening figure for the employee share under participating private-sector provident-fund arrangements; current NPPF materials describe at least 5% employee plus 5% employer contributions. It is not a confirmed liability for a foreign remote worker or every employment category.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly payment applies to a digital nomad because Bhutan has no such route. NPPF's private-scheme agreement permits a self-employed member to choose a fixed contribution from BTN 1,000 to BTN 25,000 per month, but the checked material does not establish that this voluntary pension arrangement is compulsory for all self-employed persons or available to an unauthorized foreign remote worker.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, non-dom, remittance-basis, or inbound-worker tax regime was found. The 2025 Act provides ordinary individual taxation and separate presumptive taxation only where its statutory conditions are met.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Presumptive business taxation and taxpayer registration do not establish that a foreign visitor may legally register and work.

taxes.caveats: Tax liability does not legalize an activity. The Act states that taxing income from an illegal activity confers no right or protection. Employment exercised physically in Bhutan is Bhutan-source income even where the payer is foreign; contract classification, residence, permanent-establishment exposure, withholding, treaty relief, and work authorization require professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive individual income tax. From income year 2026 the rates are 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, and 30%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile/permanent-home test, 183 aggregate days in a qualifying 12-month period, or Bhutan government service abroad.
taxation_system.income_scope: The Act separately calculates Bhutan-source and foreign-source income. Employment exercised in Bhutan is Bhutan-source even if paid from abroad; the exact treatment of a foreign client's business or service income depends on source, residence, and characterization.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-remote-worker regime found. Presumptive taxation may apply to a resident individual's qualifying Bhutan-source small business, subject to statutory conditions.
taxation_system.social_security: Participating private-sector arrangements generally use at least 5% employee and 5% employer provident-fund contributions. NPPF also offers a fixed BTN 1,000–25,000 monthly contribution option for self-employed members, but no route-specific remote-worker contribution exists.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate. The published formulas include cumulative tax from lower brackets.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Individual taxable income from income year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at about BTN 95.3 per USD.
Upper threshold converted approximately.
Upper threshold converted approximately.
Upper threshold converted approximately.
Upper threshold converted approximately.
Upper threshold converted approximately.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: More than BTN 3,500,000 annually; BTN 637,500 plus 30% formula
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate starting threshold.

taxation_system.notes: The 2025 Act and rules took effect on 1 January 2026. Tax calculations must use the new brackets rather than the superseded pre-2026 DRC webpage table. TPN registration is an administrative tax procedure, not immigration or work authorization.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No route-specific digital-nomad tax regime applies because Bhutan has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker immigration status. If a person nevertheless performs work physically in Bhutan, ordinary source and residence rules may apply without curing the immigration violation.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary individual or business taxation only if legally applicable
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–30% progressive; 30% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Resident at 183 aggregate days in a qualifying 12-month period, or under the domicile/permanent-home or government-service tests.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Employment exercised in Bhutan is treated as Bhutan-source even when paid by a foreign party. Other foreign-source business income is calculated separately; filing treatment depends on source and residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific contribution. Authorized local private employment may involve at least 5% employee and 5% employer provident-fund contributions.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory digital-nomad-specific fixed payment is applicable because no such immigration route exists. The current tax materials publish ordinary tax and withholding rules, while the NPPF agreement offers self-employed members a BTN 1,000–25,000 monthly contribution range without establishing it as a compulsory charge for foreign remote workers.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No route-specific fixed payment. Participating private employment may use percentage-based PF contributions; NPPF's self-employed fixed contribution option is BTN 1,000–25,000 monthly, but the checked agreement does not make it a universal foreign-worker liability.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Tourist visa and Sustainable Development Fee may apply to visitors, but these are not remote-worker residence fees; exact itinerary-specific totals were not treated as nomad costs.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer or nomad tax applies. GST, registration, withholding, or business taxes depend on a separately lawful Bhutan activity and the applicable statutory conditions.
fixed_payments.notes: Neither tax registration nor an NPPF contribution creates immigration eligibility or permission to work for a foreign client from Bhutan.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying fewer than 183 days does not automatically eliminate Bhutan tax: work physically exercised in Bhutan can be Bhutan-source, and immigration rules still do not authorize visitor remote work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days or under another residence test, ordinary progressive tax can apply, but no immigration status permits the applicant to remain as an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The tax law recognizes sole proprietors and qualifying presumptive taxation, and DRC permits TPN applications, but tax registration cannot convert a visitor into a lawful resident or overcome business and immigration approvals.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section prevents ordinary taxation, TPN registration, and optional pension participation from being mistaken for a viable immigration route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route for the applicant exists. Identified permissions are non-immigrant statuses.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Non-immigrants are expressly barred from applying for permanent residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: No ordinary route-to-PR transition exists from the statuses reviewed, so a route-specific post-PR timeline cannot be calculated.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The Constitution establishes at least 15 years of lawful residence for naturalization, while the older Citizenship Act states 20 years for ordinary applicants and 15 for specified categories. No qualifying remote-worker residence status exists, and non-immigrant time does not create an application right.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the Constitution nor the Citizenship Act publishes a typical processing duration. Naturalization requires government assessment and takes effect only through a Royal Kasho.

key_conditions.value: Naturalization requires at least 15 years' lawful residence under the Constitution, Dzongkha literacy, knowledge of Bhutanese culture, customs, traditions and history, a clean criminal and anti-state record, renunciation of foreign citizenship upon grant, an oath, and a Royal Kasho. The Citizenship Act retains a 20-year residence rule for ordinary applicants and makes approval highly discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: The constitutional 15-year floor and the Act's 20-year ordinary-applicant rule require case-specific legal interpretation; neither rescues a non-immigrant route expressly barred from citizenship.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The current rules and Immigration Card page do not publish a minimum marriage-duration rule for the spouse Immigration Card. However, a person currently in Bhutan as a visitor, dependent, worker, or student must leave for at least one year before becoming eligible to apply for that card.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine marriage to a Bhutanese citizen can support an Immigration Card and immigrant status after submission of a Royal Court marriage certificate and other documents. Marriage does not automatically confer citizenship or waive constitutional naturalization conditions.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing foreign marriage may need recognition or a qualifying marriage certificate from the Royal Court for immigrant status.

requirements_and_risks.value: The Bhutanese spouse applies or supports the application; required evidence includes the Bhutanese spouse's citizenship card and family tree, a Royal Court marriage certificate, the foreign spouse's passport, endorsed forms, and declarations. Both spouses may have to appear at renewal. Work in Bhutan still needs prior approval. A spouse without a child may lose immigrant status and residence after divorce or the Bhutanese spouse's death.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage must be genuine. False documents or misrepresentation can lead to refusal, cancellation, deportation, or prosecution.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Natural-born citizenship requires both parents to be Bhutanese citizens. Birth in Bhutan alone does not confer citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Bhutan to two foreign parents does not obtain Bhutanese citizenship merely by birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No general or residence-based jus soli rule exists in the cited constitutional and citizenship provisions.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with one Bhutanese and one foreign parent is not a natural-born citizen under the constitutional both-parents rule. The child may instead be registered with immigration and receive an immigration permit or immigrant status, subject to Department procedures.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Immigration registration is not the same as citizenship.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a child does not automatically grant a foreign parent citizenship or PR. A foreign spouse's immigrant residence is based on marriage and an Immigration Card; having a child may protect that status from the specific divorce-or-death termination rule that applies where the couple has no child.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any continuation remains approval-based and should be confirmed with the Department.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father gains no automatic status merely because a child is born in Bhutan. If married to a Bhutanese citizen, he may seek a spouse Immigration Card; the benefit flows from the recognized marriage and immigration approval, not the child's birthplace or automatic citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child of one Bhutanese parent is not automatically a natural-born citizen under the both-parents rule.

rank.notes: Non-government passport index, continuously updated; ranking methodology differs from Henley.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as visa-free by the cited 2026 index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a standard visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 33 visa-on-arrival plus 2 electronic travel authorization destinations. The index separately lists 45 e-Visa destinations, which are not included here.

passport.notes: These metrics come from a current secondary passport index rather than an official Bhutan source. They may change frequently and should be checked before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is widely used in formal education and government publications, making many professional and administrative interactions feasible in English, especially in urban settings. Dzongkha remains the national language and is necessary for citizenship naturalization.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English practicality does not imply the availability of a remote-work visa.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and no evidence was found of broad public-service availability. Daily life and administration should be expected to rely on Dzongkha or English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official language and education sources; no dedicated Russian/Ukrainian usage survey was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of BTN 24,789.3 at about BTN 95.3 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of BTN 20,000.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory national minimum wage of BTN 3,750 per month at about BTN 95.3 per USD. This is a legal wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the FY 2024–2025 mean monthly income of BTN 24,789.3.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the BTN 20,000 median reported for the first three quarters; fourth-quarter median data were unavailable.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The national labor reports publish means and medians but no nationwide maximum observed salary. Public-service pay-scale maxima are occupation-specific and are not a national maximum wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the statutory national minimum wage effective from 1 February 2014. The Ministry's current labour laws and regulations page still lists this official national minimum-wage instrument; no newer nationwide replacement was identified in the current official materials checked.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official FY 2024–2025 mean monthly income.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official median for the first three quarters of FY 2024–2025; fourth-quarter median unavailable.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current national labor reports do not publish a nationwide maximum observed salary. The Pay Revision Act contains maxima for specific public-service grades, but none represents a national upper wage limit, so no single BTN maximum is applicable.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory national minimum wage plus official monthly income of employed persons. Mean and median are labor-market income statistics, not immigration thresholds; gross/net treatment is not expressly identified in the cited employment table.
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage effective from February 2014; mean and median for FY 2024–2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The official National Employment Report gives mean monthly income of BTN 24,789.3 and median income of BTN 20,000. The separate 2024 Labour Force Survey reports a similar national mean of BTN 25,046 and median of BTN 20,000. The minimum field uses the separately published statutory national floor, not a survey observation. USD values use approximately BTN 95.3 per USD in August 2026.

cost_of_living_note.value: The official 2025 Household Consumption and Expenditure Survey, using 2024 as reference year, reported mean monthly household consumption of BTN 54,387 and per-capita consumption of BTN 17,434. Urban household consumption averaged BTN 67,616 versus BTN 46,331 in rural areas.
cost_of_living_note.notes: These are household consumption statistics, not a single-person expatriate budget; housing and location can materially change actual costs.

settlement_track.summary: Bhutan has no ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route. All potentially relevant tourist, skilled-worker, professional, student, business, overseas-employee, and investor permissions are non-immigrant categories, and the current rules expressly prohibit non-immigrants from applying for permanent residence or citizenship.
settlement_track.notes: Marriage to a Bhutanese citizen can create a separate immigrant-status route, but it is a family route and does not make Bhutan suitable for the applicant profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor status is not residence, employment requires local approvals and employer undertakings, and business/investor categories require approved Bhutan activity.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous Bhutan record. More than 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including over five official URLs absent from the previous source set. The student route now reflects the 2026 means-of-subsistence form; fixed-payment language distinguishes optional pension participation from compulsory route costs; and the salary record now uses the official statutory minimum while retaining a precisely explained null for the inapplicable national maximum.

data.selection_summary: Bolivia has no dedicated digital-nomad visa, but its temporary work residence covers remunerated or profitable activity with or without an employment relationship. The documented own-account route can fit a foreign-client software contractor who establishes and registers the activity in Bolivia. It grants qualifying temporary residence, permits permanent residence after three years, and can support naturalization after more than three years of continuous legal residence. Confirm with DIGEMIG that the proposed foreign contract, Bolivian work address, activity declaration, and registration documents satisfy its current filing practice.

visa_application.title: VISAS — Bolivia
visa_application.notes: This official portal accepts the preliminary application for an entry visa; for the selected route, the relevant entry category is normally Visa de Objeto Determinado—Trabajo. It is not an online temporary-residence application: after legal entry, the temporary-permanence filing is made with DIGEMIG. The reviewed current Cancillería page links to the visa portal, while the migration regulation directs residence applicants to DIGEMIG offices or its website but does not expose a functioning transactional residence URL. The portal timed out during this audit, so availability should be checked again before filing.

best_routes.route_name: Permanencia Temporal por Trabajo — trabajo lucrativo sin relación de dependencia

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly income threshold is established. Applicants instead document economic solvency; the procedural checklist accepts recent bank statements, a civil or employment contract, rent or sale income, or related evidence.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed law and procedure require documentary solvency but publish no fixed minimum in BOB.

income_requirement_display.value: No published fixed minimum; document economic solvency, normally with the last 3 months of bank statements or contract/income evidence
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Evidence-based rather than a statutory threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: DIGEMIG retains filing-level discretion over whether the submitted evidence sufficiently supports the intended activity and stay.

income_proof_months.notes: The available procedural checklist specifies bank statements from the preceding three months when that proof option is used.

key_requirements.requirement: Enter Bolivia legally and apply to DIGEMIG for one-, two-, or three-year temporary permanence before the current status expires.

Provide the application/declaration form, passport or qualifying identity document, proof of legal admission, photograph, applicable medical documents, criminal-record certificates, documentary solvency, and the filing fee.
Document the activity performed in Bolivia. For profitable work without dependency, the checklist calls for a sworn declaration describing the activity, establishment or place, and intended duration.
An own-account foreign worker must register in the Ministry of Labour's Registro Obligatorio de Empleadores (ROE), whether or not the person has employees.

Register for the applicable Bolivian tax obligations. SIN permits natural persons, including foreigners holding a foreigner identity card, to obtain a NIT; professional or consulting registration may require a nationally recognized professional qualification.
Tourist or visitor status does not authorize remunerated or profitable work; use the work-appropriate visa and permanence process.

initial_validity.value: 1, 2, or 3 years, depending on the duration of the activity authorized in Bolivia
initial_validity.notes: The granted duration depends on the documented activity rather than applicant preference alone.

extension_rules.value: A one-year permit may be renewed for two equal periods; a two-year permit may be renewed for one additional year. After a three-year permit, the applicant may seek permanent residence or, if the activity continues and permanent residence is not sought, apply again under an applicable temporary category, subject to DIGEMIG approval.
extension_rules.notes: Temporary residents generally may not be absent more than 90 continuous or discontinuous days per year without express authorization.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The work category directly grants temporary permanence after legal entry and DIGEMIG approval; a local employer is not required for the non-dependent or own-account variant.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A foreign-client contract is useful evidence, but current filing treatment should be confirmed because the procedure focuses on activity performed and established in Bolivian territory.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least three years of qualifying permanence, the foreigner may apply for permanent residence with continuing-activity evidence, solvency, identity documents, and criminal or police clearances.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Continuity and absence rules must be maintained.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization is available after more than three years of uninterrupted legal permanence. Permanent residence is not expressly a prerequisite, so qualifying temporary work residence can accrue the required period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Applicants must pass the elementary Bolivian culture and history examination and meet current lawful-activity, domicile, background, fiscal-solvency, documentation, and continuity requirements.

best_routes.notes: This is a general work-residence route, not a digital-nomad program. It can fit a software engineer operating genuinely as an independent contractor for a foreign client and willing to establish and register the activity in Bolivia. A person remaining solely in a foreign employment relationship should obtain filing-level confirmation because the clearest employer-independent documentation is the non-dependent or own-account variant.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No dedicated program or threshold appears in the current official visa and migration categories reviewed.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No BOB threshold is applicable because no dedicated program was identified.

income_requirement_display.value: No dedicated digital-nomad program exists in the reviewed official categories
income_requirement_display.notes: The separate general temporary work-permanence route is the relevant option if the activity qualifies.

income_proof_months.notes: No proof period is applicable because the reviewed official catalog contains no dedicated digital-nomad category.

key_requirements.requirement: No active dedicated program or application category appears in the official visa catalog or migration legislation.

initial_validity.notes: There is no dedicated status to which an initial validity period could apply.

extension_rules.notes: There is no dedicated status to extend.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Applicants must use a separate qualifying work-residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: There is no dedicated nomad status from which to claim a transition.

path_to_citizenship.notes: There is no dedicated nomad status whose time could count toward naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: The absence of a digital-nomad label does not make Bolivia unusable; the employer-independent work-permanence category is the relevant route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-work income threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—visitor status does not authorize remunerated or profitable work
income_requirement_display.notes: Solvency evidence required for entry does not convert visitor status into work authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: The official tourism requirements request solvency evidence but publish no fixed remote-work proof period because tourism is not a work route.

key_requirements.requirement: Tourists and visitors may not perform remunerated or profitable work for their own account or another person, except narrow humanitarian authorization.

initial_validity.value: Normally 30 days for the entry authorization, with an additional tourism or visit permanence of up to 60 days where applicable
initial_validity.notes: Treaty-based stays may differ.

extension_rules.value: Visitor extensions remain visitor status and do not create a qualifying remote-work route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A visitor must separately qualify for and obtain work-appropriate status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor status itself is not the selected route.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time is not the documented three-year work-residence track.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires uninterrupted legal residence rather than a short visitor stay.

rejected_routes.notes: Foreign remote work should not be conducted on tourist or visitor status because Bolivian law expressly prohibits profitable work in that category.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The regulation requires documentary economic solvency but establishes no fixed USD threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The regulation requires documentary economic solvency but establishes no fixed BOB threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; documentary solvency is required
income_requirement_display.notes: The regulation specifies the obligation but leaves the acceptable amount to documentary and filing-level assessment.

income_proof_months.notes: Article 13 of the official regulation requires documentary solvency but does not prescribe a bank-statement period. A current third-party reproduction of the DIGEMIG student procedure specifies bank statements for the last three months, remittance receipts, a notarized dependency letter, or related proof. Because an accessible current official checklist stating the three-month period is absent from the current sources checked, verify this procedural detail directly with DIGEMIG before filing.

key_requirements.requirement: Actual enrollment in qualifying primary, secondary, or higher professional education, plus the general temporary-permanence documents and documentary solvency.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years
initial_validity.notes: Renewable in periods of up to three years until studies finish.

extension_rules.value: Renewable until completion of studies

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary student permanence is available.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The regulation expressly says permanent residence cannot be obtained under the study modality.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separately approved switch to a qualifying category would be required.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct settlement path is confirmed from student permanence; conversion to a qualifying status requires separate approval.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route is rejected for this selection independently of its solvency-document period.

rejected_routes.notes: A university degree by itself does not create an independent skilled-residence route, and the student category is expressly excluded from permanent residence.

summary.value: Student temporary permanence is available without a local employer, but it requires actual study and the regulation expressly excludes permanent residence through that modality. No separate degree-only or points-tested independent skilled-residence route was identified.
summary.notes: The applicant's software-engineering degree may support professional-activity evidence but is not itself a residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: Bolivia applies a territorial or source approach to ordinary personal income tax rather than a day count that expands PIT to worldwide income. Work physically performed in Bolivia is treated as Bolivian-source even when the contract and payer are abroad. SIN provides an RC-IVA process for non-domiciled individuals in this situation.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The reviewed sources establish no generally applicable PIT-residence day threshold. Domicile affects filing mechanics, but Bolivian-source work can be taxable before a long-stay threshold.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: RC-IVA has a flat 13% headline rate. Available deductions or credits can reduce effective liability in some registered-resident scenarios.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Independent workers may contribute voluntarily at 14.42% of freely declared contribution income between one and 60 minimum wages. This is not treated as a universally mandatory payment for the selected independent-worker scenario.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax, pension, or health payment in USD is established. Taxes are percentage-based; voluntary independent pension contributions use at least one minimum wage as their chosen contribution base.

special_tax_regimes.value: Bolivia generally taxes individual income territorially. SIN guidance indicates that registered exporters of qualifying computer services abroad may obtain IVA and IT treatment applicable to service exports, subject to registration and transaction-specific requirements. No special digital-nomad tax holiday was identified.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Payment from abroad does not by itself make physically performed work foreign-source; SIN expressly addresses non-domiciled workers performing work in Bolivia for foreign entities.

taxes.caveats: Treatment depends on whether the person is non-domiciled, a locally registered professional or natural person, a qualifying service exporter, or an employee. RC-IVA, IVA, IT, registration, invoicing, pension elections, and treaty rules can interact; obtain current contract-specific advice before work begins.

taxation_system.value: Territorial personal-income system. Bolivian-source employment or service income is generally subject to flat 13% RC-IVA; physical performance in Bolivia can create Bolivian-source income even when the payer is foreign.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Ordinary PIT liability is source-based; no general 183-day worldwide-income rule was established. SIN expressly addresses non-domiciled people performing work in Bolivia under foreign contracts.
taxation_system.income_scope: Bolivian-source income for ordinary PIT; work physically performed in Bolivia is Bolivian-source. Genuinely foreign-source individual income is generally outside ordinary Bolivian PIT.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No nomad exemption. Qualifying registered exports of computer services may receive export treatment for IVA and IT, subject to SIN rules.
taxation_system.social_security: Independent SIP contributions are voluntary at 14.42% of declared contribution income, generally from one to 60 minimum wages; additional solidarity rates can apply at higher income levels. Employees contribute 12.71%.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: RC-IVA itself is flat, not progressive. Separate solidarity contributions can rise with income, and wealth tax has separate progressive rates outside this remote-work screening.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable Bolivian-source income, subject to applicable statutory deductions and credits
tax_brackets.notes: Flat headline rate, not an expected effective rate after deductions.

taxation_system.notes: The 13% RC-IVA treatment for foreign-paid work physically performed in Bolivia is directly supported by SIN. The combined obligations after local professional or exporter registration remain fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: There is no digital-nomad tax category. A non-domiciled person physically working in Bolivia under a contract with a foreign entity falls within SIN's 13% RC-IVA mechanism. A longer-term locally registered independent professional may also face IVA, IT, and RC-IVA registration and filing, subject to deductions and any qualifying service-export treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: General work residence; non-dependent professional or own-account worker
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 13% flat RC-IVA headline rate on Bolivian-source work; a screening rate rather than the expected effective burden after permitted deductions or export treatment
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Physical location of the work matters immediately; ordinary PIT is territorial and does not wait for a general 183-day threshold.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Genuinely foreign-source individual income is generally outside ordinary Bolivian PIT, but services performed while physically in Bolivia are treated as Bolivian-source even if contracted and paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified. Qualifying registered exports of computer services may have IVA or IT export treatment, but this is not a nomad tax holiday.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: An independent worker may voluntarily contribute 14.42% to the SIP using a declared base of at least one and no more than 60 minimum wages. An employment relationship can instead trigger employee and payroll rules.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly payment established; application fees are transaction-based
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Independent pension contribution is percentage-based and voluntary; if elected, the minimum contribution base is one current minimum wage.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: An official 2026 Bolivian consular schedule lists Visa de Objeto Determinado—Trabajo at USD 100. This is the entry-visa fee, not the later DIGEMIG temporary-permanence charge, and nationality, reciprocity, or the processing consulate can affect the amount. Article 13 requires payment of the residence filing cost, but the reviewed current official DIGEMIG sources do not publish a reliable 2026 amount for the exact temporary work-permanence filing; obtain the generated charge from DIGEMIG before payment.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: IT is generally 3% of gross transaction income where applicable; SIN professional guidance states 13% IVA and 13% RC-IVA, with credits, deductions, and export rules potentially changing the result.
fixed_payments.notes: The confirmed USD 100 amount covers only the work-purpose entry visa. Police certificates, translations, legalization, identity-card issuance, professional-title recognition, and residence processing can add variable costs not quantified in the reviewed current official schedules.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no confirmed PIT day-count safe harbor for work physically performed in Bolivia. SIN's non-domiciled mechanism taxes foreign-contract work at 13% and requires filing shortly after each monthly period or before departure.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary PIT remains territorial, but foreign-employer compensation for work performed in Bolivia is Bolivian-source and generally subject to 13% RC-IVA.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect NIT and registration analysis and potentially RC-IVA, IVA, and IT compliance. Registered export of qualifying computer services can alter IVA or IT treatment. Voluntary SIP contributions are 14.42% of the declared base.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax result is clearer for a temporarily non-domiciled foreign-contract worker than for a fully registered long-term independent professional, whose combined obligations require contract-specific advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is the initial approved status; processing time is not expressed as a waiting period in years.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: At least three years of qualifying permanence is required before applying.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization eligibility arises after more than three years of uninterrupted legal permanence and does not expressly require first obtaining permanent residence; eligibility can overlap with the PR point.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The legal text says more than three years, so filing occurs after the third anniversary rather than exactly at three years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: An older DIGEMIG checklist states up to seven days for the DIGEMIG stage, but ordinary naturalization also requires evaluation and a Presidential Supreme Resolution. The reviewed official sources do not publish a reliable end-to-end processing time.

key_conditions.value: Maintain uninterrupted legal permanence and comply with absence limits; demonstrate lawful activity, identity, nationality, domicile, clean Bolivian and international records, fiscal solvency, and migration history; pass the elementary Bolivia culture and history examination; and submit the prescribed declarations, photographs, and fee. Temporary residents generally need authorization to exceed 90 days of absence in a year.
key_conditions.notes: No general Spanish-language certificate or renunciation requirement was identified. The Constitution states that naturalized foreigners need not renounce their original nationality.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The rule requires two years of uninterrupted legal permanence for a person married to a Bolivian, not merely two years elapsed since the wedding.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Bolivian can support family-based naturalization after two years of uninterrupted legal permanence when the marriage is properly evidenced or registered. Marriage does not provide immediate citizenship or erase the residence requirement.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A foreign marriage must be documented in the form accepted by SERECI and DIGEMIG.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must provide civil-status documents, current identity documents, domicile verification, migration-flow evidence, criminal, police, and INTERPOL clearances, fiscal-solvency evidence, and pass the culture and history examination. DIGEMIG interviews both spouses, so a sham or non-genuine marriage risks refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Widowhood or divorce after nationality is acquired does not remove the acquired nationality under the Constitution.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants nationality by birth to persons born in Bolivia, with the narrow exception of children of foreign diplomatic personnel. It also grants nationality by descent to children born abroad to a Bolivian mother or father.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Bolivia normally acquires Bolivian nationality automatically even when both parents are foreign migrants, unless the diplomatic-personnel exception applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' temporary or permanent residence status is not a condition for territorial birthright citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Bolivian by birth if born in Bolivia. If born abroad, a Bolivian mother or father also transmits Bolivian nationality by birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Bolivian child reduces the ordinary naturalization residence period to two years of uninterrupted legal permanence and creates a basis for family-related immigration processing. It does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must complete the full child-link naturalization procedure.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Bolivian child may apply for naturalization after two years of uninterrupted legal permanence, subject to background, fiscal-solvency, domicile, migration-history, and culture or history requirements. Fatherhood alone does not confer citizenship automatically.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank, not the Henley rank. Values can change with visa policies.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count in Passport Index's separated breakdown.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category; its methodology classifies eVisas separately.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 49 visa-on-arrival and five eTA destinations. The same index reports a mobility score of 89.

passport.notes: Passport Index is used so the visa-free, VOA/eTA, and visa-required fields follow one internally consistent breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Spanish remains necessary for immigration, tax, housing, and ordinary administration. English is moderately practical in some international and technology circles: EF EPI 2025 ranked Bolivia 49th with a score of 521, while its IT-function score was 590. Consistent English service should not be expected from government offices.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF data comes from self-selected test takers and is an indicator rather than a census. Verify internet connectivity at the exact accommodation.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no reliable evidence of broad day-to-day availability was identified. They should be treated as impractical for administration and ordinary services; Spanish or an interpreter will normally be required.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The reviewed sources contain no current national proficiency dataset for Russian or Ukrainian.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q2 2025 survey mean liquid wage of BOB 2,515.873 using the historical official rate near BOB 6.96/USD. Bolivia's exchange-rate framework changed in 2026, so this is not a current purchasing-power conversion.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current INE household series publishes average monthly primary-occupation income, while accessible ECE variable metadata reports a mean and sample minimum and maximum but no median. No official national median worker-income statistic was published in the reviewed tables.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of BOB 3,300 using the BCB's July 2026 average reference near BOB 9.75/USD. This is the statutory minimum wage, not an observed distribution minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate historical-period conversion of the official Q2 2025 mean liquid wage. The local-currency figure is more reliable for comparison because the exchange-rate framework changed in 2026.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official INE outputs publish means rather than a national median, so no USD conversion was made.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful representative national maximum wage is published. Microdata maxima are sample observations rather than a national salary ceiling and are not used.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage for the public and private sectors, effective retroactively from January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean reported liquid salary in the INE Continuous Employment Survey, Q2 2025. Accessible metadata displays two means without clearly identifying the weighting distinction; the first displayed mean is retained cautiously.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: INE's current household-income tables are explicitly average-income series, and accessible ECE metadata publishes the mean plus sample minimum and maximum but does not publish a weighted national median. Deriving a median from microdata would require selecting the worker population, income concept, survey quarter, and expansion weights, so no unverified calculated value is substituted.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No representative national maximum is published; the observed microdata maximum is not treated as a salary ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum wage for the minimum field; mean liquid salary reported by workers in the Q2 2025 Continuous Employment Survey for the average field
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum: 2026; average: Q2 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The 2026 legal minimum exceeds the older Q2 2025 survey mean because the values refer to different periods and concepts. The survey covers reported liquid earnings, while the minimum is a formal legal floor. USD conversions are especially sensitive to Bolivia's 2026 exchange-rate changes.

cost_of_living_note.value: INE reported 2.15% monthly consumer-price inflation in June 2026, 4.82% cumulative inflation in the first half of 2026, and 9.23% year-on-year inflation. Relocation budgets should therefore be refreshed close to travel.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is an inflation warning, not a household budget estimate.
