settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor admission or an eVisa is not remote-worker residence. Business registration also does not replace Botswana residence and work permits.
settlement_track.summary: Botswana has general residence, business, work-permit, permanent-residence and naturalization procedures, but no current route makes ordinary foreign-client remote work a qualifying independent residence basis. Settlement rules cannot be used until the applicant first obtains a lawful, fitting residence and work category.
settlement_track.notes: The Immigration Act confirms broad permit-board discretion and investor or employee permit structures, but it does not establish an ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker category. The generic immigrant residence page alone is insufficient to authorize remunerated remote work.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated foreign-remote-worker category appears in the current visa and residency inventory. Visitor status restricts providing services in Botswana, while working for reward or investing for profit uses permit procedures oriented to employment or substantive local investment.

data.notes: Focused audit resolved the previously unexplained cost-of-living null with current official CPI evidence. July 2026 inflation was 9.4%, but Statistics Botswana does not publish a current single-person or remote-worker monthly budget, so no speculative monthly amount is presented. Botswana remains ineligible for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

data.selection_summary: Brazil has an active VITEM XIV/RN 45 digital-nomad route that independently grants temporary residence for ordinary work performed remotely for a foreign employer or client. It is limited to an initial period of up to one year and one equal renewal; current official sources do not establish further renewal or conversion based merely on continued foreign remote work. It is therefore a good temporary-living route but not a confirmed citizenship-path route.

visa_application.title: Visto Temporário XIV – Nômade Digital
visa_application.notes: This is an official consular route page, not a universal application form. Applicants abroad must follow the Brazilian consulate responsible for their residence; a person already in Brazil may apply for the corresponding residence authorization through the official migration process.

best_routes.route_name: VITEM XIV / RN 45 Digital Nomad Visa or Temporary Residence Authorization

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Alternatively, the applicant may demonstrate at least US$18,000 in available bank funds.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: RN 45 denominates both financial alternatives in US dollars and publishes no fixed BRL equivalent.

income_requirement_display.value: US$1,500/month from a foreign source, or US$18,000 in bank funds
income_requirement_display.notes: No BRL conversion is required by the governing resolution.

income_proof_months.notes: The official Brazilian Embassy in Stockholm requests bank transactions for the last three months. RN 45 itself does not prescribe a universal statement period, so applicants must verify the competent consulate's checklist.

key_requirements.requirement: Remote professional activity performed using information and communication technology for a foreign employer; work for a Brazilian employer is excluded.
Employment contract, service contract or other evidence of the relationship with a foreign employer or payer.
Applicant declaration confirming the ability to perform the professional activity remotely.
Valid travel document, criminal-record evidence, health insurance valid in Brazil and applicable fees or consular charges.
A visitor already in Brazil may request residence if the applicant satisfies RN 45 and the general requirements for the requested residence category.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Articles 3 and 4 of RN 45 set the initial residence period at up to one year for both the temporary-visa and in-country residence procedures.

extension_rules.value: Renewable once for an equal period after submitting the required renewal documents, CRNM and criminal-record evidence
extension_rules.notes: Article 6 authorizes renewal for an equal period. Neither RN 45 nor the current official route page provides a second renewal or automatic conversion to indefinite residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct: apply for VITEM XIV through the competent Brazilian consulate abroad, or request RN 45 residence authorization while in Brazil and complete registration/CRNM formalities.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is an actual temporary-residence authorization, although RN 45 also permits qualifying activity during a visitor stay subject to the applicable visitor limit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Conditional path after switching to a separately qualifying status, such as Brazilian employment residence; no confirmed PR path based solely on continuing foreign remote work.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Ministry explicitly permits in-country residence applications by the immigrant or employer. RN 45 provides temporary residence and renewal; its text does not establish indefinite residence. No nomad-time credit or single minimum period before the different employment route reaches indefinite residence was verified; years_to_pr is therefore null.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary naturalization generally requires four years of qualifying residence plus Portuguese ability and a satisfactory criminal record. RN 45 is capped at two years and no matching remote-worker conversion covering the remaining period was confirmed.

best_routes.notes: The route strongly fits temporary foreign-contract remote work but fails the citizenship-oriented selection because the exact status does not provide or confirm a complete settlement track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor entry followed by sole-proprietor/freelancer registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold exists because MEI, CPF, bank-account or other commercial registration is not itself a residence category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official sources checked publish no BRL threshold for this proposed strategy because it does not independently create immigration residence.

income_requirement_display.value: No qualifying immigration route confirmed
income_requirement_display.notes: A visitor may seek residence only by meeting an established residence category. The MEI documentation page treats Federal Police immigration identification as an input to registration; it does not state that MEI registration supplies immigration status.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable: the Federal Police sources require qualification under a recognized residence category, while the MEI page only lists business-registration data and publishes no immigration income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: The visitor must independently satisfy the requirements of an established residence category; commercial, CPF or MEI registration is not a substitute for residence authorization.

initial_validity.notes: No initial immigration validity exists. The checked residence pages do not list sole-proprietor registration as an independent residence basis, and the MEI page describes registration prerequisites rather than an immigration status.

extension_rules.notes: No immigration extension rule applies because the proposed registration strategy is not a residence authorization. Any visitor extension or conversion must instead follow the applicable visitor rules or a separately established residence category.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Only by separately qualifying for a recognized category, such as RN 45 digital-nomad residence or genuine family reunification.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The residence would arise from that separate legal category, not from freelancer or MEI registration.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct or conversion path based solely on opening an account, obtaining a CPF or registering an ordinary foreign-client freelance business was found in the official residence catalog and Federal Police guidance.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Administrative or business registration without qualifying residence does not establish the residence period required for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected after focused review: official Federal Police guidance permits visitor-to-residence conversion only when the visitor satisfies an existing category, while the official MEI instructions do not confer immigration status.

rejected_routes.route_name: RN 50 residence for graduates of Brazilian institutions

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: RN 50 establishes no minimum monthly income; Brazilian qualification and connected work or service documentation control eligibility.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: RN 50 publishes no BRL income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; Brazilian qualification and connected Brazilian work or service evidence are decisive
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign software-engineering degree and ordinary foreign contract do not replace RN 50's Brazilian-education requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: RN 50 is qualification- and work-document based and does not prescribe a number of income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Graduation or stricto sensu postgraduate qualification completed mostly at an accredited Brazilian institution, including in-person assessment.
The applicant must be in Brazil and provide an employment contract or proof of service provision connected with the completed course, plus contracting-company documents where applicable.
The immigrant or contracting company may submit the in-country request through MigranteWeb.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: RN 50 article 6 and the Ministry of Justice guided route page state that the initial period is up to two years; the authority may grant less than the maximum.

extension_rules.value: The holder may request alteration to an indefinite residence period, subject to current qualifying work or service evidence, criminal-record documentation, company documents where applicable and the processing fee
extension_rules.notes: This is an application, not an automatic conversion, and the connected Brazilian work or service basis must continue.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available only after completing the specified qualification in Brazil and satisfying RN 50's connected work or service requirements.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not fit the supplied foreign-degree and foreign-contract profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The initial residence period may be altered to an indefinite term under RN 50 article 7 upon application and proof of continued qualifying work or services.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This settlement feature does not make RN 50 usable by an applicant whose degree was obtained abroad and whose ordinary contract is foreign.

path_to_citizenship.value: Indefinite RN 50 residence could support ordinary naturalization if all statutory residence, Portuguese-language and criminal-record conditions are met.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This belongs to a materially different Brazilian-education and connected-work profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this applicant. Although the immigrant can self-file and later seek an indefinite term, RN 50 requires qualifying Brazilian education and connected work or service evidence that the supplied profile does not have.

summary.value: RN 50 lets an immigrant in Brazil who completed qualifying graduation or stricto sensu postgraduate study mostly at an accredited Brazilian institution self-file for residence of up to two years and later request an indefinite term. It nevertheless requires connected work or service evidence and does not accept the supplied foreign degree and ordinary foreign contract as substitutes.
summary.notes: Self-filing does not remove the substantive Brazilian-education and connected-work requirements.

tax_residency_rule.value: A temporary-visa holder without Brazilian employment generally becomes tax resident upon completing 184 days, consecutive or not, in Brazil within a 12-month period. Earlier residence may arise through another applicable residence-triggering event.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The result must be checked against the individual's entry history, immigration status and any Brazilian employment.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. The 2026 monthly system uses 0%, 7.5%, 15%, 22.5% and 27.5% brackets, with a separate reduction for qualifying income through R$7,350.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No official source reviewed established a universal mandatory INSS percentage merely from holding RN 45 while remaining employed and paid abroad. If treated as an individual contributor, the standard plan can be 20%; simplified 11% and special 5% plans have restricted eligibility.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly fixed payment for every RN 45 remote worker was established. Residence/card fees are one-off and any INSS amount depends on the person's social-security classification.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad income-tax exemption or special inbound regime was found. Once tax resident, taxable foreign earnings generally enter monthly Carnê-Leão and the annual adjustment, subject to treaty or reciprocity relief where available.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This conclusion is based on current official tax guidance rather than an express digital-nomad exemption statute.

taxes.caveats: Treatment depends on presence days, employment versus independent-service characterization, payer country, deductions, treaty or reciprocity relief and possible Brazilian social-security or business registration. Cross-border professional advice is appropriate.

taxation_system.value: Progressive residence-based taxation. Brazilian tax residents generally account for taxable foreign-source income through monthly Carnê-Leão; a nonresident's foreign-source income is generally outside Brazilian income tax.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally on the 184th day of presence within 12 months for a temporary-status holder without an earlier residence-triggering event.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally report taxable Brazilian- and foreign-source income; nonresidents are generally taxed only under the rules applicable to Brazilian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad tax holiday was confirmed. Treaty or recognized reciprocity relief may allow foreign-tax credits.
taxation_system.social_security: No automatic RN 45 contribution rule was found. The 2026 INSS table shows a 20% ordinary individual/facultative plan and restricted 11% and 5% alternatives.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The ordinary 2026 monthly base brackets are: up to R$2,428.80 at 0%; R$2,428.81–2,826.65 at 7.5%; R$2,826.66–3,751.05 at 15%; R$3,751.06–4,664.68 at 22.5%; and above R$4,664.68 at 27.5%. A separate reduction can eliminate calculated tax on qualifying monthly income through R$5,000 and tapers through R$7,350.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly tax base up to R$2,428.80
tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 monthly IRPF base before the separate income-based reduction
tax_brackets.notes: The additional reduction can eliminate calculated tax for qualifying monthly income through R$5,000.
Marginal bracket; statutory deduction R$182.16.
Marginal bracket; statutory deduction R$394.16.
Marginal bracket; statutory deduction R$675.49.
Top marginal bracket; statutory deduction R$908.73. This is not an effective tax rate.

taxation_system.notes: Statutory thresholds remain in BRL because a converted USD table would quickly become stale.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: RN 45 creates an immigration status, not a tax exemption. Before Brazilian tax residence, foreign-source income is generally outside Brazilian income tax; after residence begins, taxable foreign earnings generally enter monthly Carnê-Leão and the annual return.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary individual taxation; no special digital-nomad category confirmed
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–27.5% progressive IRPF; 27.5% is the top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally the 184th day of presence within 12 months unless another event establishes residence earlier.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Taxable foreign employment or service income received by a Brazilian tax resident generally enters Carnê-Leão; treaty or reciprocity rules may permit foreign-tax credit relief. Foreign income received while nonresident is generally outside Brazilian income tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No automatic payroll or INSS charge was confirmed solely from RN 45 status and foreign payroll. Local self-employment or individual-contributor treatment can change the outcome.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potential INSS depends on classification. The ordinary 20% individual/facultative contribution ranges from R$324.20 to R$1,695.11 monthly under the published 2026 table; reduced plans have restricted conditions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The official residence information lists R$168.13 for processing/evaluation and R$204.77 for the immigrant identity card when applicable; consular visa fees vary by post and nationality.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No digital-nomad-specific municipal tax, fixed freelancer tax or VAT charge was confirmed for a person remaining on foreign payroll without local business registration.
fixed_payments.notes: Health insurance is an immigration-document requirement, but the government sets no uniform monthly premium.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A holder remaining no more than 183 days within the relevant count and having no earlier residence trigger generally remains nonresident; foreign-source earnings are ordinarily outside Brazilian income tax.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: After tax residence begins, taxable foreign earnings generally require monthly Carnê-Leão and annual adjustment at progressive rates, subject to deductions and available relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local autonomous activity or business registration can create additional INSS, municipal, corporate and indirect-tax obligations and must be analyzed separately from the foreign-payroll RN 45 case.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The precise filing treatment should be verified for the contract form and payer country.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The route directly grants temporary residence; no preliminary years are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No RN 45 conversion to indefinite or permanent residence was confirmed; the governing rule provides only one equal renewal.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization is framed around qualifying residence and other statutory conditions, not a separately published fixed period after permanent residence. The service is directed to an immigrant resident for an indefinite period.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary naturalization may be available after four years of qualifying residence, but RN 45 ends after at most two years and no matching foreign-remote-work conversion was confirmed.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official service estimate is up to 180 calendar days; requests for additional evidence can lengthen the process.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalization generally requires civil capacity, at least four years of qualifying residence, ability to communicate in Portuguese and no disqualifying criminal conviction. The applicant must retain a qualifying immigration basis and document residence.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is an application and is not automatic merely from elapsed time.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The residence period for ordinary naturalization may be reduced to at least one year where the applicant has a Brazilian spouse or partner and is not legally or factually separated when naturalization is granted.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage or qualifying partnership to a Brazilian can support family-reunification residence and the reduced one-year naturalization residence condition. Marriage to another foreign national does not create that shortcut.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The relationship and continuing family basis must be documented.

requirements_and_risks.value: Family residence requires civil-status, identity, sponsor-residence and criminal-record documents plus applicable fees. Naturalization still requires Portuguese ability and a satisfactory criminal record. Fraud or a sham relationship can cause refusal, cancellation and civil or criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates eligibility but does not guarantee residence or citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Brazil is Brazilian from birth even when both parents are foreign, except for the narrow case where the foreign parents are serving their country. Brazil also transmits nationality by descent under constitutional rules.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Brazil is normally Brazilian regardless of the parents' immigration status, subject to the narrow foreign-government-service exception.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This conclusion concerns birth in Brazilian territory.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Brazil is Brazilian by jus soli. A child born abroad to a Brazilian mother or father may also acquire Brazilian nationality through the applicable consular-registration or constitutional residence-and-option mechanism.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father's nationality does not prevent acquisition through the Brazilian parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Brazilian child can support family-reunification residence and reduce the ordinary-naturalization residence threshold to at least one year, but does not automatically confer citizenship on a foreign parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Residence and naturalization remain separate evidence-based applications.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Brazilian child may seek family-reunification residence and may later use the reduced naturalization residence period if all other requirements are met.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and a genuine family relationship must be documented; the father's citizenship is not automatic.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank displayed for Brazil on the research date; its methodology differs from Henley.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations specifically classified as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combination of 44 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations reported separately by the source.

passport.notes: The source reports a mobility score of 163 and 82% world reach. Figures from indexes using different classification systems should not be combined.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be practical inside an international remote team and in some technology, business and tourism settings, but Portuguese is important for housing, banking, healthcare, government procedures and long-term integration. EF EPI 2025 ranked Brazil 75th of 123 with low English proficiency.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private self-selected-test index, not an official population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and cannot be relied upon for nationwide administration or daily life. Local community support may exist, but no reliable nationwide prevalence measure was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Portuguese is the federal official language; no unsupported speaker estimate is supplied.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of R$3,722 using the BCB reference selling rate of R$5.1217 per US$1; exchange rates fluctuate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official material checked reports arithmetic mean earnings, not a directly comparable national median monthly labor income; therefore no median BRL figure exists to convert.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 statutory minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of average real habitual monthly earnings from all work.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The focused official review found mean-income measures rather than the requested national median; substituting them would mislabel a mean as a median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Brazil has no meaningful general maximum wage, and the reviewed release publishes no national upper wage bound.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: National statutory minimum effective 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average real habitual monthly earnings from all work in the first quarter of 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current directly comparable national median monthly labor-income value was published in the official releases and tables checked.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No reliable national maximum was published, and such a figure would not be a meaningful labor-market ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average: real habitual monthly earnings from all work among occupied people aged 14+ with work income; minimum: statutory national minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: 2026 Q1 average earnings; statutory minimum effective 2026-01-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: The mean is not a software-engineer salary and is not necessarily equivalent to gross contractual pay. USD values are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: Brazil has substantial household and regional variation. The latest completed official Household Budget Survey (POF 2017–2018) reported average monthly family consumption expenditure of R$3,764.51 nationally, R$4,020.98 in urban areas and R$2,158.83 in rural areas; food, housing and transport represented 72.2% of consumption spending. These are historical household averages, not a current single-person or digital-nomad budget. The 2024–2025 POF is intended to update family-consumption structures, while IPCA measures price change rather than publishing one national cost-of-living level.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This fills the prior gap with official IBGE context but deliberately avoids presenting the 2017–2018 household expenditure amounts as current prices. Actual costs vary materially by city, household size, housing choice and lifestyle.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: RN 45 is capped at an initial period of up to one year plus one equal renewal. No ordinary foreign-contract conversion to indefinite residence was confirmed, so it cannot by itself cover the general four-year naturalization period.
settlement_track.summary: Brazil's RN 45 route is a strong temporary remote-work fit but not a confirmed settlement route. Citizenship would require changing to another independently qualifying residence basis; continuing the foreign remote contract alone does not supply one.
settlement_track.notes: The existence of general naturalization rules is not evidence that the two-year digital-nomad status itself supplies a complete citizenship path.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True as a temporary residence and work-authorization fit: RN 45 expressly covers remote activity for a foreign employer and excludes Brazilian employment. It is not a complete settlement fit.

data.notes: The focused unexplained-null audit used current official material and more than five URLs outside the previous source set. It confirmed that the three null fields for the rejected visitor-to-freelancer strategy are genuinely inapplicable because that strategy is not an immigration status, and it filled the cost-of-living note with cautious official IBGE household-budget context. Remaining nulls are supported and explained rather than guessed.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: RN 02/2017 locally employed residence, followed by indefinite residence under RN 30/2018
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A nomad resident can apply in Brazil for a separately qualifying employment residence. That status has an indefinite-residence procedure; continued foreign-only remote work under RN 45 has no confirmed equivalent conversion.
requirements: Obtain a qualifying employment relationship governed by Brazilian labour law and approval under RN 02/2017.
For indefinite residence, supply an indefinite employment contract, employment records and previous contract under RN 30 Annex III.
reviewed_route_names: VITEM XIV / RN 45 Digital Nomad Visa or Temporary Residence Authorization
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The Ministry explicitly permits in-country residence applications by the immigrant or employer. RN 45 provides temporary residence and renewal; its text does not establish indefinite residence. No nomad-time credit or single minimum period before the different employment route reaches indefinite residence was verified; years_to_pr is therefore null.

data.selection_summary: Brunei has no current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or self-sponsored residence route for a software engineer working under a foreign contract. Visitor status prohibits employment without written consent, ordinary work-pass processing is employer driven, business registration does not itself confer immigration status, and the residence-oriented professional category is discretionary and reserved for expertise specifically needed by Brunei.

visa_application.title: Visa Lawatan & Diplomatik
visa_application.notes: This is the official visa and pass information page, not a dedicated remote-worker application portal. It provides forms for visit, professional, business, student, dependent, and temporary-stay applications; no digital-nomad application channel is listed.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.notes: Business visits cover meetings, exhibitions, investor activity, and exploration of opportunities, not ongoing work.

A Business Visit Visa is not intended for working for the company concerned or waiting for a Labour Department quota.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A visitor pass is not qualifying temporary residence.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No universal work-pass salary threshold was published on the immigration page.

income_requirement_display.notes: The separate BND 500 minimum wage applies only to covered employments and is not an immigration income threshold.

Written employment contract between the local employer and foreign worker.
Medical examination, valid passport, insurance, and employer responsibility for the foreign worker.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The pass authorizes temporary stay for the work and employer specified on it.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not fit independent foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic work-pass-to-permanent-residence transition was confirmed; Entry Permit eligibility is separately assessed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Long employment alone should not be treated as a guaranteed PR path.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path. Citizenship ordinarily requires first holding a Residence Permit/Entry Permit and meeting long residence and Malay-language conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The work pass itself is not the citizenship-qualifying status identified by the official citizenship page.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the application and continuing status depend on a Brunei employer, approved local job, Foreign Worker Licence, and employment contract.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No public income threshold was found.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No public income threshold was found.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be a foreign expert or professional whose expertise is beneficial and needed for Brunei's development.
Application details and forms must be obtained from the Long Term Pass Secretariat or Immigration Department.

initial_validity.notes: The official page does not publish the initial validity.

extension_rules.notes: Renewal rules are not published on the official page.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Provides a long-term professional visit pass if approved.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a needs-based expert category, not an ordinary remote-worker program.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic transition was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence requires a separate Entry Permit category and assessment.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct citizenship path was confirmed from this pass.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship eligibility refers to Residence Permit/Entry Permit residence, not this visit-pass category.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a discretionary, national-needs expert route rather than an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route. Public materials do not establish that an applicant can self-sponsor solely on a foreign software contract.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No salary threshold is published for the professional category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No salary threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least 10 years of recognized specialist expertise
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility is assessed by a special committee or board and is not based on an ordinary foreign remote-work contract.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Internationally and locally recognized professional or specialist qualification.
At least 10 years of specialist expertise.
Expertise must be needed and scarce in Brunei, with eligibility assessed by a special committee or board.

initial_validity.value: Permanent resident status if the Entry Permit is approved.
initial_validity.notes: Approval is discretionary and the public guide does not establish a routine application path for an ordinary software engineer.

extension_rules.value: Entry/re-entry documentation validity depends on passport and nationality; permanent-resident status administration is separate from a temporary visa renewal.
extension_rules.notes: The official page lists nationality-dependent re-entry fees and validity.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; this category concerns permanent-resident status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent-resident application is possible only under the restrictive professional category if the special body accepts that the expertise is recognized, scarce, and needed in Brunei.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is not an ordinary degree-based or foreign-contract route.

path_to_citizenship.value: A foreign-born permanent resident may later seek naturalization after holding a Residence Permit/Entry Permit and residing in Brunei for at least 20 of the preceding 25 years, including the two years immediately before applying, subject to Malay-language and character requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Eligibility does not guarantee approval.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected under the applicant-selection rules because it is an elite/needs-based professional category. A relevant degree and ordinary software-engineering experience are not enough unless the special committee finds the expertise scarce and needed nationally.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Business registration has no immigration income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is stated; the published registration fee is BND 30.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; BND 30 business-name registration fee
income_requirement_display.notes: Registration of a business name is not a residence permit.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable.

key_requirements.requirement: Online registration through the One Common Portal and upload of the required business documents.
Foreign-owner eligibility and required local immigration status are not explained on the general registration page and require filing-level verification.

initial_validity.value: Business registration certificate; no immigration stay is granted.
initial_validity.notes: The portal states that approved certificates are generally emailed within one working day.

extension_rules.notes: No immigration extension exists through registration alone.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Opening a business does not legalize a visitor's stay or authorize remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed from sole-proprietor registration.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Investment and professional PR categories have separate restrictive criteria.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from business registration itself.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship requires qualifying residence and other statutory conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a business certificate is not immigration permission. The official materials do not support entering as a visitor, registering as a freelancer, and converting that registration into residence.

summary.value: A student visa/pass exists and does not require a local employer, but it requires an education-related application and guarantor documentation. It authorizes temporary study-related stay, not permanent residence, and no direct student-to-PR transition was confirmed. Separately, the Entry Permit professional category can grant PR but requires at least 10 years of recognized, scarce expertise needed by Brunei and is not an ordinary degree-based route.
summary.notes: Education is not a qualifying route for the current foreign-contract remote-worker profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: No personal-income-tax residence threshold was identified because Brunei currently does not levy tax on individual employment, self-employment, dividend, or interest income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Corporate residence and company-source rules are separate. Immigration permission remains required even when personal income tax is zero.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is a no-personal-income-tax screening rate, not an effective-rate estimate or special digital-nomad concession.

social_contributions_percent.notes: SPK requires an 8.5% employee contribution for eligible citizens and permanent residents, but an ordinary temporary foreign national is outside the stated citizen/PR eligibility. No qualifying remote-worker status exists, so a mandatory percentage for the proposed scenario cannot be stated.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory monthly payment for a nonexistent digital-nomad route was found. Employer-sponsored foreign workers instead require employer-arranged insurance and security arrangements whose premiums vary.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-personal-tax regime was found. The ordinary rule is already no tax on personal income; unincorporated sole proprietorship and partnership income is also stated not to be taxed.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A locally incorporated limited company is different and is generally subject to 18.5% corporate income tax.

taxes.caveats: Zero personal income tax does not make remote work lawful under visitor status. Company incorporation, local business activity, source rules, insurance, and immigration compliance require separate advice.

taxation_system.value: Brunei currently levies no personal income tax on individual employment or self-employment income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No individual tax-residence day threshold is material to ordinary personal income tax under the current no-PIT rule.
taxation_system.income_scope: The Ministry of Finance states that no tax is levied on personal employment, self-employment, dividend, or interest income, or on unincorporated sole proprietorships and partnerships.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound regime was found; the zero personal-income-tax rule is general.
taxation_system.social_security: SPK coverage is mandatory for eligible employees who are Brunei citizens or permanent residents under 60. Eligible employees contribute 8.5%; self-employed SPK registration is also restricted to citizens and permanent residents. Ordinary temporary foreign workers are not included in the stated eligibility.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable because the personal income tax rate is zero rather than progressive.
taxation_system.notes: The displayed 0% is a general personal-income-tax screening rate. It does not cover corporate tax or establish immigration authorization.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad status exists. If an individual were otherwise lawfully present and working, Brunei's general rule is no personal income tax, but immigration and business authorization must be resolved first.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; hypothetical individual foreign remote worker
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% personal income tax under the general individual rule; not a digital-nomad concession
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No PIT residence-day threshold was found or needed for the general no-personal-income-tax rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The official FAQ states that personal employment and self-employment income is not taxed, without limiting the statement to domestic income. Filing-specific confirmation is prudent for unusual structures.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: SPK applies to citizens and permanent residents, not ordinary temporary foreign nationals under the stated eligibility. Employer-sponsored foreign workers require employment, medical-insurance, and security arrangements instead.

fixed_payments.status: not_applicable_no_route
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No SPK contribution established for an ordinary non-PR foreign remote worker; eligible citizen/PR employees contribute 8.5%.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad visa fee exists. Visit, work, business, and resident-permit fees depend on the separate status and nationality.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A business name registration is BND 30 and company incorporation is BND 300, but neither fee grants immigration status.
fixed_payments.notes: No universal monthly health-insurance premium, freelancer levy, or remote-worker state fee could be established because there is no qualifying route.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Personal income tax remains 0%, but a visitor cannot assume that remote work is permitted; visitor-pass employment restrictions apply independently of tax.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no dedicated lawful remote-worker residence category. The 0% PIT rule should not be treated as immigration permission.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Unincorporated sole-proprietor or partnership income is stated not to be taxed, but business registration does not confer residence, and foreign eligibility must be verified before filing.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax conclusions are well supported, but there is no digital-nomad route to which they can be directly applied.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent temporary-residence route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work was found.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Brunei uses category-specific and discretionary Entry Permit rules; no automatic conversion timetable from visitor, work, professional-visit, student, or business-registration status was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: For an applicant born abroad, the official citizenship page requires holding a Residence Permit/Entry Permit and residing in Brunei for at least 20 of the 25 years preceding application, including continuous residence during the immediately preceding two years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated because the applicant has no qualifying entry route and no predictable time to obtain permanent residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official standard processing time was published. The 2025 certificate ceremony confirms approvals occur but does not establish a typical duration.

key_conditions.value: Qualifying Residence Permit/Entry Permit history, 20 years' residence in the preceding 25 for a foreign-born applicant, continuous residence for the two years immediately before application, good character, Malay-language examination, and cultural understanding requirements. Approval is not presented as automatic.
key_conditions.notes: Dual-citizenship consequences should be checked directly under the Nationality Act before applying.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The published citizenship-by-marriage route is specifically for a foreign wife of a Bruneian citizen husband. For a first marriage it requires at least 5 years of marriage and at least 3 years from issuance of the Residence Permit/Entry Permit. Foreign husbands face different, generally longer PR rules.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count from its legal marriage date if recognized in Brunei. Muslim marriages concluded abroad require Syariah Court confirmation, and non-Muslim marriages abroad require confirmation from the Attorney General's Chambers.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage alone does not immediately grant PR or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The spouses must live together in Brunei, the foreign wife must already hold permanent-resident/Entry Permit status for the required period, and good character plus supporting acknowledgements and local confirmation are required. Permission/registration procedures require extensive civil-status documents. False or sham arrangements risk refusal and possible immigration or criminal consequences; approval is not automatic.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The accelerated citizenship provision is gender-specific in the published materials and should not be generalized to a migrant husband married to a Bruneian woman.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Brunei does not generally give a child citizenship merely because of the place of birth. Nationality principally depends on descent, statutory indigenous-status rules, or registration; the official services distinguish birth registration from citizenship documentation.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Brunei to two foreign migrant parents does not obtain automatic citizenship solely by birth. The child is registered for a birth certificate using the parents' foreign or permanent-resident documents.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Any exceptional anti-statelessness or indigenous-status provision requires case-specific legal review.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child can have a citizenship or registration route through a Bruneian parent. The official service provides separate applications through a Bruneian father and a Bruneian mother, with age, legitimacy, residence, registration, and documentary conditions that vary by case.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This is not always unconditional citizenship at the instant of birth, especially through the mother or for a child born abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen or permanent-resident child can support evidence of family ties, but no automatic parent citizenship or permanent residence arises from the child's birth. A family-ties Long-Term Social Visit Pass may be relevant, while PR remains category-specific.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must obtain and maintain their own immigration status.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically receive citizenship or PR because his child is Bruneian. If the mother is a Bruneian citizen or PR, family-ties status may support a Long-Term Social Visit Pass; published PR rules for a foreign husband of a Bruneian wife are substantially longer and category-specific.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The citizenship-by-marriage route published under section 5(6) concerns a foreign wife of a Bruneian husband, not the reverse.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 42 visa-on-arrival and 9 eTA destinations shown separately by the index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 154. Its methodology differs from Henley, so the rank should not be mixed with a Henley rank.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is widely spoken and used alongside Malay in education and business, making day-to-day English communication reasonably practical in urban and professional settings.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Malay remains the sole official language and is important for government dealings and citizenship examinations.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not commonly documented local working languages. A Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking migrant should expect to rely on English or Malay and arrange interpretation where needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable official evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 overall average monthly employment income of BND 1,686 using about USD 0.774 per BND. This covers local and non-local employed persons.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 overall median of BND 1,000.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the BND 500 statutory minimum wage. Coverage is limited to employments and companies specified under the 2025 rules; it is not a universal observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 average for local workers, BND 1,879 per month.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 median for local workers, BND 1,200 per month.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official labor-force and census statistics publish averages, medians, occupation averages, and an open-ended income class above BND 5,000, but no observed national maximum for local workers. Private-sector recommendations and public-service salary scales are category-specific and cannot establish a national maximum, so no USD maximum is calculated.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory monthly minimum for covered employments/companies, not a universal wage floor for every worker.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 average monthly income from all jobs for local workers.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 median monthly employment income for local workers.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No observed national maximum monthly salary for Bruneian/local workers is published in the current official sources reviewed. The 2024 Labour Force Survey reports local-worker average and median income but no maximum; the 2021 census uses an open-ended highest income class of more than BND 5,000, which supplies no upper bound. DEPS wage tables provide averages, the MPEC private-sector guideline provides recommended minimum starting scales, and Public Service Department materials provide selected government salary scales (including high superscale or specialist bands); none is a maximum across all citizens or workers. The value therefore remains null rather than treating a category-specific salary ceiling as a national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official Labour Force Survey monthly income from all jobs for local workers; minimum is a separate statutory rate with limited coverage
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 income data; minimum-wage rules effective from 2025; maximum-field audit also reviewed 2021 census tables and current official wage guidance available on 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are citizen/local-worker labor-market figures, not an immigration income threshold. USD amounts use the BND-SGD 1:1 parity and an approximate mid-2026 SGD/USD rate of 0.774; exchange-rate movements will change the USD equivalents. A focused review found no defensible national maximum salary: published upper figures belong to particular occupations, public-service scales, or specialist schemes, while the national income distribution has an open-ended top class.

cost_of_living_note.value: The official CPI does not provide a household budget, but it indicates broadly stable recent prices: overall CPI was 0.3% higher year-on-year in June 2026, with food and non-alcoholic beverages up 1.5% and services down 0.5%.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This describes price movement, not the absolute cost of rent or a recommended monthly living budget.
