settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor status cannot be used as a substitute for a remote-work residence permit; employment on a tourist or social-visit pass is prohibited without written consent.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists. Employer-sponsored work, discretionary nationally needed professional categories, investor/business categories, study, or family status would require a materially different profile, and business registration alone does not create residence rights.
settlement_track.notes: Even the restrictive professional Entry Permit category is not a match: it requires at least 10 years of recognized expertise that is scarce and needed in Brunei, with discretionary committee assessment.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No current status authorizes an ordinary foreign software engineer to reside in Brunei and work remotely under a foreign contract without a local employer, nationally needed expert finding, investment, study, or family basis.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 2026-08-15. More than 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including seven official salary, wage, labor-force, census, and public-service sources outside the previous canonical source set. The flagged national maximum-salary field remains null because current official statistics provide averages, medians, occupational averages, or an open-ended top income class—not an observed maximum across local workers. Category-specific government and specialist salary scales were not misrepresented as a national maximum.

data.selection_summary: Bulgaria has an active statutory digital-nomad route for non-EU/EEA/Swiss foreign employment or foreign-client remote services. It grants one-year residence renewable once. General law appears to count lawful continuous residence toward permanent residence after five years, but the nomad permit ends after two years and no official guidance confirms a seamless conversion enabling an ordinary foreign-contract worker to complete the remaining period. Confirm conversion and residence counting with Migration Directorate before relying on this as a citizenship path.

visa_application.title: Visa for Bulgaria
visa_application.notes: This is the official general visa page, not a digital-nomad-specific portal. The process begins with an in-person Type D visa application and interview at the competent Bulgarian mission; after entry, the residence application is filed on paper with Migration Directorate.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Type D Visa and Extended Residence Permit (Foreigners Act Article 24(1)(23)/24c)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the annual threshold: 50 × EUR 620.20 = EUR 31,010 annually, or EUR 2,584.17 monthly; converted at about USD 1.1392 per EUR. The legal test concerns gross income for the preceding calendar year, not monthly salary.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 31,010 gross annual income for 2026 applications (50 × EUR 620.20 minimum monthly wages)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold is formula-based and changes if the statutory minimum wage changes.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 31,010 gross in the preceding calendar year (about EUR 2,584/month or USD 2,944/month equivalent)
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 50 Bulgarian gross minimum monthly wages; 2026 minimum wage EUR 620.20
income_requirement_display.notes: Recalculate immediately before applying because the minimum-wage component can change.

income_proof_months.notes: The law examines gross income for the preceding calendar year, effectively a 12-month look-back.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualify as an employee of an employer outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland, a qualifying owner/manager of a company outside that area, or an individual with at least one year of remote IT-enabled service activity.
The foreign-employee category requires the foreign employment contract; a fixed-term contract must have at least as much time remaining as the requested permit.
Foreign-client contractors must document entirely remote service activity and may not work for, provide services to, or practise freelance activity for persons in Bulgaria.
Provide income evidence, accommodation, health insurance valid for the residence period and an initial criminal-record certificate.
Foreign employer/client registration and contract documents generally require legalization or apostille where applicable and certified Bulgarian translations.
Apply for a Type D visa at the competent Bulgarian mission, then file personally with Migration Directorate after entry.

initial_validity.value: One-year extended residence permit, following a Type D visa
initial_validity.notes: The Type D visa is the entry stage before residence.

extension_rules.value: May be extended once for one additional year
extension_rules.notes: Maximum confirmed digital-nomad residence is two years.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Obtain the Type D visa abroad, enter Bulgaria, then receive an extended residence permit from Migration Directorate.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No direct online digital-nomad application was identified.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After the maximum two-year nomad permit, a separately approved self-employment route can lead to long-term residence; retaining a foreign contract alone is insufficient.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The nomad cap is in Article 24c. The European Commission publishes the self-employment successor and five-year settlement rule, but does not guarantee an in-country nomad conversion or preservation of nomad years. years_to_pr refers to the general qualifying-residence requirement, not a guaranteed five years from DNV arrival.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential sequence: five years of qualifying continuous residence, permanent or EU long-term residence, then five further years holding that status before general naturalisation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation also requires a clean record, sufficient income or occupation, Bulgarian-language knowledge and usually release from prior nationality. The nomad permit alone cannot cover the timeline.

best_routes.notes: Strong temporary fit for the foreign-contract software-engineer profile, but not a confirmed settlement match. Obtain written confirmation that Article 24c time counts and identify a status that can be assumed after the permitted renewal without breaking continuous residence.

best_routes.route_name: Self-employed professional permit and residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official route summary requires sufficient resources for the proposed activity but publishes no fixed monthly amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed monthly threshold is published; sufficient resources for the planned activity must be demonstrated
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is separate from the digital-nomad income formula.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published; activity plan and sufficient financial resources required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sufficient resources, assessed without a published fixed amount
income_requirement_display.notes: The digital-nomad threshold should not be substituted for this permit.

income_proof_months.notes: The official route summary does not prescribe a fixed income look-back period.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain a self-employment permit; provide an activity plan, relevant qualifications, at least two years of experience, B1 Bulgarian and sufficient resources.
Obtain the appropriate visa and then a residence permit after entry.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year
initial_validity.notes: Residence validity is aligned with the self-employment permit.

extension_rules.value: Renewable up to a maximum of three years; the official portal says the applicant must then return home for one month before applying again
extension_rules.notes: The required interruption makes continuity and conversion filing-level questions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available after approval of the self-employment permit and completion of the visa and residence stages.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is regulated self-employment, not tourist-to-freelancer legalization.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially relevant after the nomad permit, but official sources do not confirm an in-country switch from Article 24c or whether the required one-month return interrupts qualifying residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Manual confirmation is essential before treating this as a conversion bridge.

path_to_citizenship.value: May contribute only if residence remains lawful and continuous long enough to reach permanent or EU long-term residence, followed by the naturalisation waiting period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not a direct citizenship status.

best_routes.notes: More demanding than ordinary foreign-contract remote work because it requires B1 Bulgarian, an activity plan and a separate self-employment permit. Conversion from digital-nomad residence remains unconfirmed.

rejected_routes.route_name: EU Blue Card / locally employed highly qualified worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed USD threshold applies independently of the contract date. Article 17(2) requires gross contractual pay of at least 1.5 times the latest NSI average wage for the 12 months preceding signature. Using the 2025 annual average only as an illustration gives about BGN 3,904.88 (EUR 1,996.55) monthly, approximately USD 2,274 at the exchange rate used here; the actual filing threshold must be recalculated for the contract date.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Rolling formula: at least 1.5 × the latest NSI average wage for the 12 months before the employment contract is signed
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: For illustration, 1.5 × the official 2025 average of BGN 31,239 annually equals BGN 46,858.50 annually or BGN 3,904.88 monthly (about EUR 1,996.55). This is not a fixed 2026 threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: At least 1.5 × Bulgaria's latest average gross wage for the 12 months before contract signature
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: BGN/EUR rolling statutory formula based on NSI wages
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 1.5 × last-published NSI average wage for the preceding 12 months
income_requirement_display.notes: The European Commission portal still displays a 2023 amount, so that amount should not be treated as current. The route remains rejected because a qualifying Bulgarian job offer or employment contract is mandatory.

income_proof_months.notes: The 12 months are the statutory NSI reference period for calculating the salary floor, not an applicant income-history requirement; eligibility is evidenced by a Bulgarian work contract or binding job offer.

key_requirements.requirement: Requires highly qualified employment under a Bulgarian work contract or binding job offer, qualifying education or professional skills, the rolling salary floor, insurance, housing and other admissibility documents.

initial_validity.value: Normally up to five years, or contract duration plus three months when the contract is shorter than 24 months
initial_validity.notes: Validity remains tied to qualifying employment.

extension_rules.value: Renewable where the employment and eligibility grounds continue
extension_rules.notes: It is not independently maintainable through an ordinary foreign-client contract.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, through qualifying highly skilled local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially after qualifying residence, but only while meeting employment-route rules.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through the general residence and naturalisation sequence, not directly.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a qualifying Bulgarian work contract or binding job offer is mandatory. A foreign remote-work contract does not satisfy this condition, although Bulgaria does not apply a labour-market test to Blue Card applications.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor/Schengen short stay with remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: A visitor stay has no remote-worker income threshold because it is not a residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No digital-nomad residence threshold applies to visitor status

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable: short stay is not a residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor funds requirements do not create settlement eligibility.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker income-history test applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Schengen short-stay limit is generally 90 days in any 180-day period.

initial_validity.value: Up to 90 days in any 180-day Schengen period

extension_rules.value: No ordinary remote-worker residence extension

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence entitlement.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from visitor status.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor presence is not qualifying residence and is not a substitute for the statutory digital-nomad process.

summary.value: No degree-only or independent points-based residence route was identified. Qualifications help with regulated self-employment, but that route also requires B1 Bulgarian, experience, an activity plan, sufficient resources and a separate permit.
summary.notes: A software-engineering degree alone does not confer Bulgarian residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally resident if they have a Bulgarian permanent address together with a Bulgarian centre of vital interests, spend more than 183 days in any 12-month period, or otherwise have their centre of vital interests in Bulgaria. Treaty tie-breakers prevail.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 183-day test is not the only test; personal and economic ties can establish residence earlier.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Flat screening rate on taxable personal income, not an expected effective rate. Deductions and mandatory contributions may reduce the taxable base.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single digital-nomad rate applies. Standard covered employment has total social and health contributions of approximately 32.7%–33.4%, including a 13.78% employee share, but foreign employment and self-employment structures can be treated differently.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal digital-nomad fixed monthly payment was established. Locally insured self-employed persons use statutory insurance bases, but the payment depends on applicable insurance categories.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad exemption or special inbound flat-tax regime was identified; general Bulgarian residence, source, deduction and treaty rules apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign-paid income should not be assumed exempt.

taxes.caveats: Immigration permission and tax treatment are separate. Work physically performed from Bulgaria may be Bulgarian-source even when paid abroad. Confirm employee-versus-contractor classification, treaty residence, foreign tax credits, social-security coverage, VAT and permanent-establishment risk.

taxation_system.value: Flat 10% personal income tax. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Bulgarian-source income, broadly including employment or services performed in Bulgaria regardless of payer location.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any 12-month period, Bulgarian centre of vital interests, or qualifying permanent-address facts; treaties may override domestic tests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Bulgarian-source income for non-residents. Services physically rendered in Bulgaria are generally Bulgarian-source regardless of the payer.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad exemption found. Qualifying freelancers and civil contractors may generally deduct 25% statutory expenses, subject to classification and VAT rules.
taxation_system.social_security: Standard covered employment has total social and health contributions of approximately 32.7%–33.4%, with 13.78% borne by the employee. Coverage for a non-EU digital nomad depends on contract and insurance status.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Bulgaria uses a flat rate; 10% is the statutory PIT rate rather than a top marginal rate. Effective tax may be lower after allowable deductions.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No general threshold; flat rate on the applicable taxable base
tax_brackets.notes: Specific income categories and exemptions can differ.

taxation_system.notes: The general rules are well supported, but individual results remain structure- and treaty-dependent.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special nomad exemption was identified. A tax-resident nomad should screen foreign employment or client income under the ordinary 10% PIT and worldwide-income rules; a non-resident may still have Bulgarian-source income where services are performed in Bulgaria.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital-nomad residence under general personal tax rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% flat PIT screening rate; the taxable base depends on classification, deductible contributions and any applicable statutory-expense deduction
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any 12-month period or Bulgarian centre of vital interests/permanent-address facts, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxed on Bulgarian-source income, and services performed in Bulgaria may be Bulgarian-source even when paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No special digital-nomad exemption, tax holiday or inbound-worker rate was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Coverage is fact-specific. Standard covered employment has total social and health contributions of approximately 32.7%–33.4%; foreign employment and non-EU status require individual analysis.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Locally insured self-employed persons use statutory minimum and maximum insurance bases; the exact payment depends on applicable contribution categories. No universal payment for every digital nomad was confirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The Type D visa fee under Article 15(1) is EUR 100. A separate residence permit/card fee is payable, but a digital-nomad-specific current amount was not established from the official pages reviewed.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Standard VAT is 20%. Registration can arise under turnover or other statutory conditions; no special nomad transaction tax was identified.
fixed_payments.notes: Insurance premiums, translations, apostilles, notarization, accommodation declarations and residence-card charges are additional practical costs, not taxes.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying below 184 days does not guarantee non-residence because centre-of-vital-interests tests still apply; services performed in Bulgaria may also be Bulgarian-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect Bulgarian filing and a 10% PIT screening rate on worldwide income, with treaty foreign-tax-credit analysis and possible social-security obligations.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A qualifying locally registered freelancer may use a statutory expense deduction but can trigger minimum social-insurance and VAT obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No official tax ruling specific to Article 24c digital nomads was identified.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The route directly grants extended residence after the Type D entry stage.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General rule: five years of lawful continuous residence, subject to absence limits. Nomad residence lasts only two years, so conversion is required and route-specific counting should be confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalisation requires at least five years holding permanent or long-term residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Indicative ordinary sequence: about five years to permanent/long-term residence plus five years holding that status, assuming successful conversion and continuous qualifying residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Minister of Justice generally has up to 12 months to make a proposal on ordinary naturalisation, subject to suspensions. No reliable official typical end-to-end period through the presidential decree was published, so a total figure remains null.

key_conditions.value: Continuous lawful residence and controlled absences; permanent or EU long-term status for the statutory period; adulthood; clean record; sufficient income or occupation; Bulgarian-language knowledge; and usually release from prior nationality unless exempt. Filing is personal and includes an interview.
key_conditions.notes: Citizenship is not acquired until conferred by presidential decree.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Reduced naturalisation generally requires at least three years of marriage to a Bulgarian citizen and at least three years holding permanent or long-term residence; both conditions and remaining naturalisation requirements apply.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Bulgarian citizen can count toward the three-year marriage period, but does not confer citizenship automatically or remove the residence-status requirement. Marriage to another migrant creates no Bulgarian-citizen shortcut.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Family residence and citizenship are separate procedures.

requirements_and_risks.value: Clean-record, income or occupation and Bulgarian-language requirements still apply. Civil-status documents must be recognized, and false documents, concealed facts or a sham relationship can cause refusal or revocation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Naturalisation is completed only by presidential decree.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Bulgaria is Bulgarian only when not entitled to another citizenship by descent. This is primarily an anti-statelessness rule, not broad territorial birthright citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Normally no. A Bulgaria-born child of two foreign migrants becomes Bulgarian only if not entitled to either parent's citizenship by descent or another special rule applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Both parents' nationality-transmission laws must be checked before relying on the anti-statelessness provision.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child with at least one Bulgarian-citizen parent is Bulgarian by descent, subject to registration and documentary procedures when born abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The Bulgarian parent's sex is irrelevant.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Bulgarian child may qualify for family residence and, after three years of lawful continuous residence while providing legally required support, may qualify for permanent residence. Citizenship is not automatically transmitted to the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Parentage, custody, support and genuine family-life evidence may be required.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Bulgarian, the child is Bulgarian and the foreign father may pursue family residence; a supporting parent can potentially reach permanent residence after three years of lawful continuous residence. If both parents are foreign and the child inherits another nationality, birth in Bulgaria creates no citizenship shortcut for the father.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The father's citizenship is never automatic merely because the child is Bulgarian.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026; VisaIndex used for category breakdown

rank.notes: July 2026 Henley ranking; Bulgaria shares 11th place.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score includes destinations accessible without a prior visa, including qualifying visa-on-arrival access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: VisaIndex combines physical visas and eVisas requiring advance authorization in this figure; its methodology differs from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: VisaIndex lists 29 visa-on-arrival and seven eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Henley supplies the headline rank and access score. VisaIndex separately reports 142 strictly visa-free, 29 visa-on-arrival, seven eTA and 51 visa/eVisa-in-advance destinations; the methodologies should not be mixed.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Reasonably practical in Sofia and international technology settings, but Bulgarian remains important for administration and integration. EF's 2025 index ranked Bulgaria 18th globally with a score of 594; Sofia scored 616.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF measures participating adults and does not guarantee English service at government offices.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian may help informally because of related vocabulary and Cyrillic script, but neither is official and no reliable nationwide evidence shows dependable public-service availability in either language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Use Bulgarian or professional translation for immigration, tax, banking and legal matters.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official Q1 2026 gross average wage of EUR 1,407 using about USD 1.1392 per EUR.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest official national employee median found: BGN 1,144 gross in October 2022, about EUR 584.92 at the irrevocable conversion rate and approximately USD 666 using the ECB rate applied elsewhere. It is older than the Q1 2026 mean because NSI publishes the Structure of Earnings Survey every four years.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the EUR 620.20 statutory gross minimum wage; this is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate equivalent of EUR 1,407 gross monthly.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the BGN 1,144 gross median for October 2022. This is the latest official national employee median located, not a 2026 estimate.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum wage is not a defined or published endpoint in the current quarterly tables or latest Structure of Earnings Survey. Those sources report means, medians and category averages, so converting the highest sector average into an individual maximum would be misleading.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 620.20 gross statutory minimum wage per month from 1 January 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory floor, not a wage-distribution minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official preliminary average for employees under labour contracts.

median_salary_local_currency.value: BGN 1,144 gross per month in October 2022 (latest official four-yearly Structure of Earnings Survey; all employees under labour contracts, full-time and part-time)
median_salary_local_currency.notes: NSI defines this as the 50th percentile. The 2026 quarterly release publishes arithmetic means rather than a national median; the 2022 survey is the latest official median located and should not be presented as a current 2026 level.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current quarterly release and latest Structure of Earnings Survey do not publish a national upper salary endpoint. The Q4 2025 release identifies the highest sector average—BGN 5,739 for information and communication—but a sector mean is not an individual maximum, so this field remains null.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly wages of employees under labour contracts; statutory gross minimum for the minimum field; historical BGN for the latest official median
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 average; minimum effective 1 January 2026; latest official median October 2022
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and minimum are current 2026 figures. settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The digital-nomad permit is capped at two years. It cannot by itself reach the five-year permanent-residence threshold, so a timely switch is essential.
settlement_track.summary: Nomad residence appears capable of contributing to the general five-year residence calculation, but it expires after one renewal. Bulgaria is therefore a possible conversion track, not a confirmed end-to-end nomad-to-citizenship route.
settlement_track.notes: The unresolved filing-level issue is whether Migration Directorate permits a seamless switch from Article 24c to a suitable status and counts all nomad time as continuous qualifying residence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route expressly fits remote employment for an employer outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland and qualifying remote services for foreign clients. It is a strong two-year living fit, but settlement requires conversion.

data.notes: The statutory digital-nomad criteria, income formula, one-year validity and single renewal are established. The country remains not fully matched because no official route-specific guidance confirms how the two-year nomad status converts into the remaining qualifying residence needed for permanent residence and citizenship.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Freelance/self-employed work authorization and residence permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: After the maximum two-year nomad permit, a separately approved self-employment route can lead to long-term residence; retaining a foreign contract alone is insufficient.
requirements: Obtain Employment Agency approval of an activity plan, prove relevant qualifications, at least two years of experience and Bulgarian B1.
Apply for the successor type-D visa through a Bulgarian mission abroad and obtain the residence permit.
Meet the five-year residence/absence conditions; coordinate the self-employment scheme’s published three-year limit and one-month return requirement.
reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad Type D Visa and Extended Residence Permit (Foreigners Act Article 24(1)(23)/24c)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The nomad cap is in Article 24c. The European Commission publishes the self-employment successor and five-year settlement rule, but does not guarantee an in-country nomad conversion or preservation of nomad years. years_to_pr refers to the general qualifying-residence requirement, not a guaranteed five years from DNV arrival.

data.selection_summary: Burkina Faso does not currently publish a dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. A foreigner can independently request a long-stay business visa and can establish a local sole proprietorship after obtaining authorization to trade, but official sources do not confirm that foreign-client software work qualifies, that business registration itself legalizes residence, or that this route counts toward permanent residence. It is therefore not valid for this citizenship-oriented selection.

visa_application.title: e-Visa Applicant Web Portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official online visa application portal. It handles ordinary visa categories, including long-stay applications; no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category was found.

rejected_routes.route_name: Long-stay business visa plus local individual-business registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No published minimum-income threshold was found.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published minimum-income threshold was found.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; proof of the business/long-stay purpose is required
income_requirement_display.notes: The official page requires proof of the long-stay purpose but publishes no income formula.

income_proof_months.notes: No specified income-history period was published.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport, signed application form, recent identity photograph, proof of the long-stay purpose, and medical certificate stating that the applicant does not have a contagious disease.
Foreign natural or legal persons wishing to conduct commercial activity must first obtain authorization to trade in Burkina Faso.
Individual-business registration combines RCCM registration, tax existence declaration and IFU, professional trader card, and CNSS employer notification; the official listed cost is XOF 40,000.

initial_validity.value: Business long-stay visa category; longer than 90 days, with an exceptional long-stay category advertised for 1–5 years
initial_validity.notes: The page does not clearly state the exact validity issued to an ordinary foreign sole proprietor.

extension_rules.notes: No category-specific renewal rule for a foreign remote software professional was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not established. A stay exceeding 90 days requires a long-stay visa, residence permit, or residence title, but business registration is not stated to confer a residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visa and business-registration procedures must not be treated as the same legal status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A permanent-resident card framework was adopted in October 2025, but the reviewed official announcement does not publish eligibility conditions or confirm access from this business-visa scenario.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Filing-level verification with the security/identification authorities is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after 10 years of habitual residence, but no source confirms that this business-visa configuration supplies the qualifying lawful residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and granted by decree.

rejected_routes.notes: This is an entrepreneur/local-business route, not a confirmed ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route. The business visa is expressly associated with commerce, investment, industry and other lucrative activity, while local commercial registration and foreign-trader authorization add host-country business substance. It is rejected because official sources do not confirm that a software engineer serving only a foreign client can use it or obtain qualifying residence through it.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No digital-nomad income requirement; this is an ordinary entry visa
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor/eVisa status is not a qualifying residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: Not published as a remote-work requirement.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through the official eVisa portal and meet the requirements for the selected ordinary visa purpose.

initial_validity.value: Less than 90 days for the ordinary eVisa stay described by the official portal

extension_rules.notes: No remote-work extension or conversion rule was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None established from visitor/eVisa status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate long-stay visa, residence permit, or residence title is required for a stay over 90 days.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality code requires habitual residence for general naturalization; a short visit is not a credible qualifying track.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a visitor/eVisa stay is not a remote-worker residence status and does not establish a settlement track.

summary.value: A study/training long-stay visa can be requested without a local employer using enrollment or training documentation, but it is a visa category rather than a degree-based independent residence or skilled-migration program. No direct permanent residence benefit from holding a university degree was found.
summary.notes: The applicant's software-engineering degree does not independently create residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: Fiscal domicile can arise through a permanent home in Burkina Faso, the center of vital interests, or—if those tests do not decide the issue—habitual presence for at least 183 days, continuous or not, in a 12-month period.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty rules may override domestic residence and source rules.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening figure for a self-employed professional: the top IBNC marginal rate is 27.5%. Employment income instead uses IUTS with a 25% top monthly marginal rate. Neither is an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For an ordinary covered employee, the employee-side amounts captured are 5.5% CNSS old-age contribution plus 2.5% universal health contribution. Employer-side CNSS is 16% and employer-side health is 2.5%. Applicability to a foreign-employer arrangement requires professional advice.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: A reliable same-date USD conversion was not captured. The official local-currency health contribution for a formal-sector independent worker is XOF 15,000 per month.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, non-dom, remittance-basis, or tax-holiday regime was found. Resident employees and independent professionals fall under ordinary IUTS or IBNC rules, subject to treaty and classification analysis.

taxes.caveats: Whether foreign-client receipts are employment income, non-commercial professional profit, or business income depends on the actual contract and local registration. Residence, source, permanent-establishment, withholding, VAT, patent/business taxes, social-security coverage, and any treaty position require local advice.

taxation_system.value: Mixed schedular system: employment income is taxed monthly under progressive IUTS rates up to 25%; independent professional profits are taxed annually under progressive IBNC rates up to 27.5%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, center of vital interests, or fallback presence of at least 183 days in a 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: A resident employee is taxable under IUTS even where the remunerated activity or employer is abroad; independent professional profits attributable under the territoriality rules are subject to IBNC. Treaties can modify the outcome.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad/inbound regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee-side CNSS is 5.5%, employer-side CNSS 16%, on covered remuneration up to the published XOF 800,000 ceiling. Universal-health contribution is 2.5% employee and 2.5% private employer; a formal independent worker owes XOF 15,000 monthly and an informal independent worker XOF 4,000 monthly.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 27.5% figure is the top marginal IBNC screening rate, not an effective rate. IUTS and IBNC use different periods and bases.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly taxable employment income above XOF 250,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top employment-income marginal rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable professional profit above XOF 1,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top self-employed/professional marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: The tax rates and residence tests are well supported, but application to a person working under a foreign contract remains classification-dependent.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a dedicated category because Burkina Faso has no confirmed digital-nomad status. A resident foreign employee would generally be screened under IUTS, while a locally registered independent professional would generally be screened under IBNC.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary employee or independent-professional taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 27.5% IBNC for independent professional profit; up to 25% IUTS for employment income
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, center of vital interests, or fallback presence of at least 183 days in a 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The CGI expressly includes employees domiciled in Burkina Faso even if the activity or employer is abroad. Independent foreign-client receipts require analysis under IBNC territoriality and any applicable treaty.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee-side CNSS is 5.5% plus 2.5% universal-health contribution where covered. Formal independent workers have a fixed XOF 15,000 monthly universal-health contribution; informal independent workers XOF 4,000.

fixed_payments.status: Confirmed local-currency health contribution for independent workers; other route-specific fixed charges are not fully established.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Formal independent worker: XOF 15,000/month universal health; informal independent worker: XOF 4,000/month.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Official long-stay page lists XOF 231,000 for a business visa, XOF 126,500 for study/training, and XOF 110,000 for an exceptional 1–5 year long-stay visa. Individual-business creation is listed at XOF 40,000; foreign-trader authorization is listed as free.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Non-salaried professional activity can also trigger patent/business tax, tax-registration, withholding and possible VAT obligations; no single universal monthly amount was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa and registration charges are not evidence that the route is available for foreign-client remote work.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Presence below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if a permanent home or center of vital interests is already in Burkina Faso. Burkina-source income and business activity may still be taxable.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A domiciled foreign employee is generally within IUTS even with a foreign employer; top monthly marginal rate is 25%, subject to treaty relief and payroll mechanics.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: An independent professional is generally screened under IBNC at annual progressive rates of 10%, 20%, and 27.5%, plus registration, health, patent/business, VAT and withholding analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a tax scenario analysis, not confirmation of immigration eligibility.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-work route or published conversion timetable was established.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: A permanent-resident card framework exists, but the reviewed announcement does not publish the qualifying residence period.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality code measures 10 years of habitual residence before application, not a specified number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory residence period before applying for discretionary naturalization; it is not a timeline from any confirmed remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official typical processing time was found. The process includes a prosecutor-led investigation, ministerial report, Council of Ministers consideration, and decree.

key_conditions.value: Habitual residence in Burkina Faso during the 10 years preceding the application and residence at the time of the naturalization decree; lawful stay compliance; age 18; good character; no unrehabilitated ordinary-crime sentence exceeding one year; mental fitness; and, for an industrialist or trader, proof of significant investment or equity under applicable rules. Naturalization is discretionary by decree.
key_conditions.notes: No general language test, formal integration examination, absence limit, or mandatory renunciation rule was identified in the reviewed nationality provisions.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The code states that a foreign or stateless person marrying a Burkinabè acquires nationality at the celebration of marriage, subject to statutory exceptions and government opposition.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A qualifying existing marriage to a Burkinabè can matter. If celebrated abroad, the six-month government-opposition period runs from transcription of the marriage in Burkinabè diplomatic or consular civil-status registers.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A marriage to another migrant has no acceleration.

requirements_and_risks.value: The foreign spouse may decline Burkinabè nationality before marriage where their national law allows retention of their original nationality. The government may oppose acquisition by decree during the following six months. Annulment prevents acquisition even if the marriage was entered in good faith. Civil-status transcription and proof of a legally valid, genuine marriage are essential; sham marriage or false documents can create criminal and status risks.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Current filing practice should be verified with a Burkinabè civil-status authority or consulate.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Burkina Faso is not unconditional jus soli. It provides nationality at birth for a child of a Burkinabè parent, a child born in Burkina Faso to a parent also born there, certain foundlings/unknown-parent cases, and children otherwise stateless. A child born to two foreign-born foreign parents can acquire nationality at majority after at least five years' habitual residence, subject to opposition and diplomatic exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically at birth merely because both foreign parents reside in Burkina Faso. A locally born child may acquire nationality at majority if habitually resident there for at least five years at that time, or may claim it as a minor after five years' habitual residence. Separate foundling, unknown-parent and statelessness safeguards apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: If either foreign parent was also born in Burkina Faso, the double-jus-soli rule can confer nationality at birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Burkinabè by descent when either legally established parent is Burkinabè. If born abroad with only one Burkinabè parent, the child has a limited right to repudiate the nationality shortly before majority.

parent_benefit_summary.value: No automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship grant to a foreign parent was found solely because their child is Burkinabè. Any family-based stay or discretionary naturalization benefit must be established separately.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The nationality code governs the child’s nationality but does not create automatic derivative nationality for the parent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic citizenship from the child's status. If the mother is Burkinabè, the child is Burkinabè by descent, but the father must rely on his own immigration status or a qualifying marriage to the Burkinabè mother.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage must be legally established by civil-status act or judgment for descent rules.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's separately labeled visa-free count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count; its methodology treats some eVisa destinations separately in the country table.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 31 visa-on-arrival plus 2 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 64. A separate 2026 Henley secondary summary reports rank 76 and access to 56 destinations visa-free or on arrival; the structured breakdown uses Passport Index consistently.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is constitutionally a working language, but French and major national languages remain more useful for administration and daily life. English-only remote living is likely difficult outside limited professional and international settings.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The constitutional text says national languages officialized by law are official and makes English and French working languages. The reviewed government sources visibly publish Mooré, Dioula, Fulfuldé and Gulimancema versions, but a definitive current legal roster of every officialized national language was not located; the array lists the four directly evidenced in official government publication practice.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or working languages and are unlikely to be practical for administration or ordinary daily life without French or a local language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No official evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable same-date USD conversion or economy-wide official average wage was captured. The available current average is limited to state public employees.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No official national median wage was found after focused searches.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Current official SMIG is XOF 45,000 per month, but no reliable same-date USD conversion was captured.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official local-currency figure is retained because no reliable same-date exchange-rate source was captured.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Not published in the reviewed current official labor-market bulletin.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary or upper wage-distribution bound was published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory/interprofessional guaranteed minimum wage, not an observed minimum. The employment bulletin reports that 35.3% of workers earned below this amount in their principal activity.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average per-head salary of state public employees at the end of September 2025, excluding armed forces and diplomatic/consular missions; it is not economy-wide.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No official median captured.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum captured.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Minimum is the current SMIG; average is a public-sector employee mean and is not representative of all workers.
average_citizen_salary.period: SMIG and public-sector average current to 2025; sources published in 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The previous record's XOF 34,664 minimum was replaced with the current official XOF 45,000 SMIG. No economy-wide average or median was established, so the narrower public-sector mean is explicitly labeled rather than presented as the national average.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable current monthly household budget for a remote worker was established. The World Bank classifies Burkina Faso as low income and estimated extreme poverty at 34.6% in 2025; this macro context should not be treated as an expatriate cost-of-living estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing, security arrangements, imported goods and reliable connectivity can make expatriate costs diverge sharply from local wage levels.
