settlement_track.summary: No dedicated ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route is available. Business visas and local enterprise registration exist, and a permanent-resident card framework has been announced, but official sources do not connect these into a qualifying residence-to-citizenship route for a foreign-client software engineer.
settlement_track.notes: General naturalization after 10 years of habitual lawful residence exists, but the missing qualifying immigration route prevents selection.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category was found. The closest independent option is a business/local-enterprise structure requiring a commercial purpose and foreign-trader authorization, with no official confirmation that foreign-only software contracts qualify or produce residence.

data.notes: Audit replaces the previous weak and partly outdated record with current official visa, business, tax, social-security, nationality, language and labor-market sources. More than 15 distinct relevant URLs were inspected. The principal remaining uncertainty is the unpublished detailed eligibility for the permanent-resident card and whether immigration authorities would accept a foreign-client professional under a business long-stay application; those gaps are not resolved by the public materials and are therefore not treated as eligibility.

data.selection_summary: Burundi does not publish a dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. Its two-year ordinary establishment visa can cover locally registered profit-making activity, but requires six months already spent in Burundi, a NIF, commercial registration, a USD 500 fee, and a blocked deposit or institutional guarantee. Permanent residence additionally depends on investment, property, marriage, or other discretionary conditions. This is therefore a local-business route, not a confirmed route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

visa_application.title: Formulaire de demande de visa en ligne
visa_application.notes: Official CGM online visa application. The portal covers establishment and other visas, but it does not list a dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category.

best_routes.route_name: Ordinary establishment visa for profit-making activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly income threshold is published. The route instead requires local activity documentation, a visa fee, and a blocked deposit or qualifying guarantee.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No monthly income threshold published; individual commercial-registration fee is BIF 100,000
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: BIF 100,000 is a one-time commercial-register fee, not an income requirement. The immigration deposit is denominated in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed monthly income threshold; USD 1,500 individual blocked deposit or accepted guarantee
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: USD deposit plus BIF registration fee
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: BIF 100,000 individual commercial-register fee; USD 500 visa fee
income_requirement_display.notes: The USD 1,500 deposit is refundable when the foreigner permanently leaves Burundi. A family deposit is USD 5,000. These are not monthly-income tests.

income_proof_months.notes: No number of income-proof months is published. The separate six-month rule concerns prior physical stay in Burundi, not income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Spend at least six months in Burundi before applying for the two-year establishment visa.
Submit an approved request to the Commissioner General for Migration, passport copy, current visa copy, photograph, and any additional status-specific documents requested.
For profit-making activity, obtain a tax identification number and commercial registration.
Pay the USD 500 visa fee and lodge USD 1,500 for an individual or USD 5,000 for a family in a blocked account, unless an accepted national or international institution supplies a guarantee.
Individual business registration requires an email address, passport/identity or residence card, and BIF 100,000 commercial-register fee.

initial_validity.value: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Official validity of the ordinary establishment visa.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is legally contemplated: the 2021 law gives the Consultative Commission for Foreigners and Refugees competence over non-renewal decisions and permits appeal to the Appeals Committee. The reviewed law and current CGM service page do not publish the filing deadline, renewal documents, fee, decision standard, or maximum number of two-year renewals.
extension_rules.notes: The status is therefore renewable in principle, but renewal is discretionary rather than an automatic entitlement. Confirm the current filing procedure directly with CGM before the existing two-year visa expires.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: After at least six months in Burundi, an applicant with approved locally registered profit-making activity may seek the two-year establishment visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence linked to approved local establishment/activity, not permission expressly designed for foreign-client remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Not automatic. The ordinary permanent-resident visa requires Interior Ministry authorization, property evidence and prior establishment visas. Published eligibility includes ten years of uninterrupted residence plus investments, or economically important investment and durable local job creation; marriage rules provide separate alternatives.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: An ordinary remote worker with only foreign income does not satisfy the published investment/job-creation conditions merely by holding establishment visas.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization is legally possible after at least ten years of permanent residence, good character, and demonstrated attachment and assimilation, but is granted discretionarily by presidential decree.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Nationality Code does not establish a special citizenship entitlement for establishment-visa holders or remote workers.

best_routes.notes: This route permits independent filing for a locally registered profit-making activity without an employer in that branch. It does not expressly authorize ordinary work solely for a foreign employer/client, and the permanent-residence conditions require local investment, property, marriage, or comparable establishment. It is therefore not valid for the requested foreign-contract remote-work selection.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income requirement is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No income threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: These are short-stay categories.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Visa fees vary by duration, but are not income requirements.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page does not prescribe an income-history period for these short-stay categories.

key_requirements.requirement: The multiple-entry visa is valid for one to three months; the stay visa is valid for five days to three months.
Passport, current visa and photograph are among the published requirements.

initial_validity.value: 5 days to 3 months, depending on category

extension_rules.value: No remote-worker extension or conversion entitlement is published.
extension_rules.notes: A later establishment application is a separate status requiring independent eligibility.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence right; an independently qualifying applicant must make a separate establishment-visa application.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path from short-stay status.

path_to_citizenship.value: No confirmed counting or direct citizenship path from these short-stay visas.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor and short-stay visas are not qualifying remote-work residence statuses.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permanent-resident visa based on investment or marriage

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly income threshold is published; investment, residence, property or marriage conditions apply.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published minimum investment amount
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official page describes an important economic contribution and durable job creation without quantifying either.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; substantial local-investment/property conditions apply
income_requirement_display.notes: The visa fee is not an income or investment threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The official permanent-resident rules do not prescribe an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Interior Ministry authorization, application letter, passport copy, property title and prior establishment visas.
Ordinary route includes ten years' uninterrupted residence with investments, or important investment and durable employment creation for Burundian nationals.

Published marriage alternatives are gender-specific: a foreign woman married to a Burundian man, or a foreign man married to a Burundian woman for at least five years who owns his residential property in Burundi.

initial_validity.value: 99 years
initial_validity.notes: Official stated validity; the status can be withdrawn if qualifying conditions cease, following serious criminal conviction, or for conduct affecting public order.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary renewal is indicated within the stated 99-year validity.
extension_rules.notes: Transfer/certified-copy procedures exist.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; this is a permanent-resident category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence if the discretionary statutory conditions and Interior Ministry authorization are satisfied.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization remains a separate discretionary procedure under the Nationality Code.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for the user profile because this is an investment/property or marriage route, not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

summary.value: The CGM page publishes one-year study visas only for EAC and Democratic Republic of the Congo nationals. No general degree-based, independent skilled-worker, or education-to-settlement route for this applicant was confirmed.
summary.notes: The applicant's software-engineering degree does not itself create an independent immigration category in the official material reviewed.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they have a permanent residence in Burundi or spend more than 183 days, continuously or intermittently, during a twelve-month period ending in the relevant fiscal year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can therefore arise before or independently of immigration permanent-resident status.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: For a locally registered individual business, 30% is the flat tax on net business income and is the relevant screening rate. Employment and rental income instead use 0%, 20% and 30% progressive brackets.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 4% value is the ordinary employee share of the INSS pension contribution, not a self-employed remote-worker rate; the employer pays 6% pension and 3% occupational risk. INSS says an independent worker may continue pension coverage voluntarily only after at least six consecutive months of prior general-scheme coverage, and its form applies a 10% contribution to declared monthly income. The broader 2020 Social Protection Code and its 2026 amendment make coverage scope implementation-sensitive, but no current official schedule was found that sets a mandatory rate or fixed amount for a newly registered foreign-client independent worker.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No defensible mandatory monthly fixed payment is published for the requested foreign-client self-employed scenario. Confirmed one-time amounts are the USD 500 establishment visa, USD 1,500 individual blocked deposit or guarantee, and BIF 100,000 individual commercial registration. A July 2026 secured-residence-card ordinance was inspected, but the applicable card charge could not be extracted from the accessible official page; social-security scope likewise requires INSS confirmation under the amended protection framework.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remittance-basis, foreign-income holiday or special inbound remote-worker regime was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Investment incentives may exist for certified investments, but they do not constitute an ordinary remote-worker regime.

taxes.caveats: Classification of foreign salary versus business income depends on the contract and local registration. Residents are taxable on Burundian and foreign-source taxable income; non-residents generally only on Burundian-source income. A registered business can also face a minimum tax equal to 1% of turnover when the statutory condition applies. Treaty relief, foreign tax credits, VAT, withholding and social-security coverage require professional review.

taxation_system.value: Worldwide taxation for residents and source-based taxation for non-residents. Locally registered individual business income is taxed at a flat 30%, while employment and rental income use progressive annual brackets of 0%, 20% and 30%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence in Burundi or more than 183 days during a relevant rolling twelve-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: taxable Burundian and foreign-source income. Non-residents: taxable Burundian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary inbound remote-worker regime confirmed. Certified investment incentives are separate.
taxation_system.social_security: For ordinary covered employment, INSS pension contributions are 4% employee and 6% employer, with a further 3% occupational-risk contribution paid by the employer. INSS materials allow qualifying former insured independent workers to continue pension insurance voluntarily at 10% of declared monthly income after at least six consecutive months of prior coverage. No current official implementing schedule establishes a mandatory contribution rate or minimum fixed contribution for a newly self-employed foreign-client worker; the 2020 Social Protection Code and 2026 amendment require filing-level confirmation of scope.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard number is the top employment/rental marginal rate and also the flat rate on individual business profits. It is not an estimated effective tax rate. Individual business taxpayers may additionally face minimum tax of 1% of turnover under the statutory loss/low-profit rule.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual employment or rental income: BIF 0–1,800,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD conversion omitted because Burundi has material official/parallel exchange-rate divergence.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual employment or rental income: BIF 1,800,001–3,600,000
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual employment or rental income above BIF 3,600,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket. Individual business profits are separately subject to a flat 30% rate.

taxation_system.notes: Primary tax legislation supports a 30% screening rate rather than the previous unsupported 35%. Filing treatment should still be confirmed with OBR because a foreign employment contract and a registered individual business can fall into different tax categories.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Burundi has no confirmed digital-nomad route. A person using the establishment/business route would generally enter the ordinary resident and business-tax system.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary employment or individual-business taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 30% screening rate; flat on individual business profits or top marginal rate on employment income
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence in Burundi or more than 183 days in the relevant twelve-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Taxable for residents under the worldwide-income rule, subject to classification, available credits and treaty relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: There is no nomad payroll category. If treated as an employee in covered Burundian employment, the published INSS pension shares are 4% employee and 6% employer, plus 3% employer occupational risk. INSS does not publish a mandatory rate for a newly self-employed foreign-client worker; voluntary continuation is available at 10% of declared monthly income only to a person with at least six consecutive months of prior general-scheme coverage. The broader Social Protection Code, as amended in 2026, makes an INSS ruling advisable before work begins.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly social-security payment can be stated for this scenario. Current INSS materials publish percentage-based employee contributions and a conditional 10% voluntary-continuation contribution, while no current official schedule sets a mandatory minimum or flat amount for a newly self-employed foreign-client worker. One-time immigration and business-registration costs remain applicable.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed monthly amount is published for a newly self-employed foreign-client worker. Conditional voluntary pension continuation is 10% of declared monthly income, available only after at least six consecutive months of prior general-scheme coverage; ordinary covered employment instead uses percentage contributions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: USD 500 establishment visa; USD 1,500 blocked deposit for an individual or USD 5,000 for a family unless an accepted guarantee is supplied; BIF 100,000 individual commercial-register fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Minimum individual-business tax can be 1% of turnover when net taxable income falls below the statutory test. Capital income and capital gains are generally taxed at 15%.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of a published fixed amount is not a zero-liability ruling. The 2020 Social Protection Code and 2026 amendment broaden the statutory framework beyond the older INSS operational pages, so INSS should confirm whether and how a locally registered independent activity is assessed.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident is generally taxed only on Burundian-source taxable income, but working physically in Burundi or operating a local registered business can create Burundian-source income even before day 184.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident is taxable on taxable Burundian and foreign-source income; employment income reaches a 30% top marginal rate.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered individual business is generally taxed at 30% on net business income and may owe minimum tax of 1% of turnover under the statutory condition.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: There is no special nomad tax regime. Exact classification of a foreign employment contract, permanent-establishment exposure and social-security enrollment should be obtained from OBR/INSS before commencing work.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The establishment visa requires at least six months already spent in Burundi before application; approval timing is additional and not published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Approximate difference between the six-month establishment threshold and the published ten-year uninterrupted-residence investment condition. Permanent residence is discretionary and also requires investment and property evidence; elapsed time alone is insufficient.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Nationality Code requires at least ten years of permanent residence for ordinary naturalization, but it is not clear that this means ten additional years after obtaining the immigration permanent-resident visa. No reliable additive interval was established.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum residence screen for ordinary naturalization, not a guaranteed route-specific outcome. The applicant must first qualify for lawful residence and satisfy attachment, assimilation and character requirements.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Code incorporates an investigation procedure with a maximum ten-month investigation stage, but the reviewed sources do not publish a reliable typical total time through ministerial review, presidential decree and publication.

key_conditions.value: At least ten years of permanent residence for ordinary naturalization; age 21; good conduct and no crime/delict conviction; attachment and assimilation; filing through the competent prosecutor and Justice Ministry; presidential decree and official publication. No automatic entitlement arises from elapsed residence.
key_conditions.notes: No express renunciation requirement was found in the reviewed Code, but its dual-nationality provisions are clearest for persons Burundian by origin. Naturalized applicants should verify whether retaining another nationality is accepted in practice.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Gender-specific result: a foreign woman married validly to a Burundian man may acquire nationality by declaration without a published minimum marriage duration. A foreign man married to a Burundian woman instead faces a five-year reduced naturalization-residence rule; the permanent-resident page also requires at least five years of marriage and residential property for that male spouse route.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A valid existing marriage can qualify. A foreign wife of a Burundian man may file a nationality declaration at any time during or after the marriage ceremony. A foreign husband of a Burundian woman does not receive the same declaration route but benefits from reduced naturalization and marriage-based permanent-residence conditions.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The law is expressly gender-asymmetric.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid. Foreign husbands should expect residence, five-year marriage, property and naturalization requirements rather than automatic nationality. Fraud, sham marriage or false evidence can cause refusal, status withdrawal and nationality deprivation where acquisition involved fraud or corruption.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No source established a waiver of normal security, character or document-verification checks.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Burundi alone does not confer citizenship. The territorial presumptions principally protect children born to legally unknown parents and foundlings.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Burundi to two known foreign parents does not automatically become Burundian. Exceptions concern legally unknown parents, foundlings and certain later parental acquisitions.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Citizenship by descent or option is available when a parent is Burundian, but the Code's automatic-at-birth provisions are gender- and filiation-specific. A child outside the automatic categories may use the option mechanism where at least one parent is Burundian under the cited provisions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because the 2000 Code distinguishes legitimate, recognized and maternal/paternal filiation, case-specific civil-status review is necessary.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Burundian child does not automatically grant a foreign parent permanent residence or citizenship in the reviewed law. Any benefit must come through a separate marriage, establishment, family or discretionary immigration process.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent-residence right for a foreign father was found merely because his child is Burundian. If he is married to a Burundian woman, the separate five-year marriage/naturalization and property-based permanent-residence rules may apply.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child's citizenship and the father's immigration status must be assessed separately.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15; rankings can change as visa policies change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard field: 34 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately counts other eVisa/pre-enrollment categories outside this total.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports mobility score 56. Its methodology differs from Henley because it separates visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA and electronic-visa categories.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is officially recognized, but Kirundi is the dominant everyday language and French is important in administration and formal documentation. English-only remote work may be possible within an international workplace, but local legal, banking and immigration processes are likely to require French or Kirundi assistance.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from the official-language and administrative context, not a measured national English-proficiency score.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and no reliable evidence of broad public or administrative use was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Interpreter or French/Kirundi support should be expected for official processes.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: A reliable current USD conversion was not used because the available Burundi wage observation is old and current official/parallel exchange rates materially diverge.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Historical 2014 estimate only: the World Bank reports median salary-plus-benefits of non-farm wage employees at BIF 480,000 per year, equivalent to USD 314 per year at the average 2014 official exchange rate; USD 26.17 is USD 314 divided by 12. It is not a current-dollar wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The available ILO snapshot reports an old 2018 minimum-wage observation; no defensible current USD equivalent is supplied.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The latest clearly identified national observation found is too old for a meaningful current-dollar salary estimate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Historical 2014 non-farm wage-employee median, not a current national median: the source reports USD 314 annually at the 2014 official exchange rate; USD 26.17 is the monthly arithmetic equivalent. The estimate is based on a small sample and excludes agricultural wage employees.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected ILOSTAT material does not publish a meaningful Burundi-wide maximum or reliable upper wage endpoint.

min_salary_local_currency.value: BIF 3,464 per month (2018 legacy minimum-wage observation for Gitega and Bujumbura)
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is not presented as a current nationwide minimum. The Labour Ministry held an April 2025 workshop to update the SMIG but did not publish a replacement amount on the inspected page.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Old household-survey/ILOSTAT observation for average monthly earnings of employees; it is retained only as cautious historical screening data.

median_salary_local_currency.value: BIF 40,000 per month (BIF 480,000 annual median divided by 12; 2014)
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Historical ECVMB 2014 median salary plus benefits for non-farm wage employees. The World Bank reports BIF 480,000 per year and cautions that the median estimates use small samples; this is not a current all-worker median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A national maximum salary is not a stable population statistic, and none of the inspected current INSBU or ILOSTAT wage catalogues publishes a Burundi-wide upper endpoint. The World Bank assessment reports sector medians, not a maximum; therefore no defensible BIF maximum is supplied.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Historical average monthly earnings of employees from ECVMB/ILOSTAT; historical median salary plus benefits of non-farm wage employees from ECVMB; legacy statutory minimum-wage observation
average_citizen_salary.period: Average and median: 2014; minimum: 2018; reviewed 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and median use different 2014 employee populations and should not be compared as one distribution: ILOSTAT reports an employee average, while the World Bank median covers non-farm wage employees and is based on a small sample. All wage figures are stale and unsuitable for current salary negotiation or budgeting.

cost_of_living_note.value: No robust current household cost basket was established. World Bank reporting instead indicates very low GDP per capita, high poverty and 34.1% consumer-price inflation in 2025, so old nominal wage figures are especially unsuitable for estimating present living costs.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is macroeconomic context, not an expatriate cost-of-living estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No dedicated nomad route exists. The available establishment status requires approved locally registered profit-making activity, and permanent residence additionally requires investment, property, marriage or other discretionary eligibility.
settlement_track.summary: The establishment visa is potentially residence-oriented for a genuine local business, but it is not a confirmed foreign-contract remote-work route. An ordinary remote worker would need to change the substance of the case to local business/investment and later satisfy discretionary permanent-residence and naturalization rules.
settlement_track.notes: The general ten-year naturalization rule does not cure the initial route mismatch. No official source confirms that foreign-client remote work alone qualifies as approved profit-making activity or satisfies the investment-based permanent-residence conditions.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The complete official visa list contains no digital-nomad/foreign-remote-worker category. The establishment route requires local registration and approved profit-making activity; a foreign contract is neither a stated qualification nor a substitute for the NIF, commercial register and later investment conditions.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 2026-08-15. Renewal is now confirmed as legally contemplated, though its filing mechanics and renewal ceiling remain unpublished. Social-security text separates ordinary employee rates from the conditional 10% voluntary-continuation rule and explains why a newly self-employed foreign-client worker still needs an INSS scope ruling. A historical 2014 non-farm wage median was added; no national maximum salary endpoint is published. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including more than five canonical URLs absent from the previous source set.

data.selection_summary: Cabo Verde has a residence-oriented route fitting ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Law No. 27/X/2023 created a residence visa for employees and independent professionals working remotely for persons or entities outside Cabo Verde, and Decree-Law No. 13/2025 supplied filing requirements. It feeds the ordinary two-year temporary-residence system; permanent residence and naturalization are each available after five years of qualifying legal residence. The general consular portal is active, although the dedicated DEF Digital Nomads application remains marked “coming soon,” so applicants should confirm the filing category before paying.

visa_application.title: Portal Consular — online visa request
visa_application.notes: The official portal redirects unauthenticated users to login. The dedicated Digital Nomads page lists the route and documents, but its application button says “Brevemente/coming soon.” Confirm that the remote-activity residence-visa category is selectable; otherwise arrange filing through the responsible consulate or DEF.

best_routes.route_name: Residence visa for professional activity performed remotely outside Cabo Verde

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Current legislation requires evidence of average monthly remote-work income received during the preceding three months but publishes no fixed minimum amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The inspected legislation and official route page publish no minimum CVE amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum published; prove average monthly remote-work income for the preceding 3 months
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Average monthly professional income received during the previous three months
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an evidence-period requirement, not a stated threshold. Former temporary tourism-program figures should not be substituted without filing-level confirmation.

income_proof_months.notes: Decree-Law No. 13/2025 requires proof of average monthly income earned during the preceding three months.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport biographical page and criminal-record certificate from the country of origin.
For foreign employment: employment contract or employer declaration confirming the relationship.
For independent work: company or service contract, or evidence of services supplied to one or more entities outside Cabo Verde.
Proof of average monthly professional income during the preceding three months and evidence of current tax residence.
General residence requirements include sufficient means, accommodation, medical and vaccination documents and lawful entry; foreign documents may require Portuguese translation and legalization.
After entry, apply for temporary residence before the residence visa expires. A NIF and social-security registration may be required depending on classification.

initial_validity.value: Residence visa permits a 6-month stay while the residence application is decided; the resulting temporary residence permit is valid for 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The six-month visa is the entry/finalization stage. The qualifying residence status is the two-year temporary permit.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence permits are renewable for successive 2-year periods; renewal should be requested at least 45 days before expiry
extension_rules.notes: Continued activity, lawful income, accommodation and compliance should be documented. DEF should confirm the precise renewal evidence for the remote-work subclass.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Obtain the remote-work residence visa, enter Cabo Verde and complete the temporary-residence application. The ordinary temporary permit lasts two years.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is materially different from the older six-month Remote Working tourism/work program.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A temporary-residence holder may apply for permanent residence after at least 5 years, subject to subsistence, accommodation, character, public-health/security and language conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Applicants should preserve evidence that every year was held under a valid qualifying residence title.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization may be granted after at least 5 years of legal residence, subject to adulthood or emancipation, a valid residence title, proof of the residence period, acceptable criminal records and subsistence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary rather than automatic. The regulation gives the responsible minister up to 90 days to decide after filing, though inquiries or proceedings can extend practical completion.

best_routes.notes: This route fits a software engineer employed by or serving a foreign entity. It states no Cabo Verde employer, local client, investment, startup or elite-talent requirement. Its principal operational caveat is that the dedicated DEF application button remains unavailable; verify the filing category through the consular portal or responsible authority.

rejected_routes.route_name: Legacy Remote Working Cabo Verde temporary work/tourism program

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current official tourism page requires proof of income but does not publish a numeric threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The inspected official page publishes no numeric CVE threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Proof of income required; the current official page does not publish a numeric minimum
income_requirement_display.notes: Older secondary figures were not substituted because the current official page does not confirm them.

income_proof_months.notes: The official tourism-program page does not state an income-evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Remote or self-employed work, passport, proof of income and insurance, program registration and entry formalities.

initial_validity.value: 6 months
initial_validity.notes: The official page describes a temporary work/tourism visa.

extension_rules.value: One further 6-month renewal opportunity
extension_rules.notes: The page does not provide continuity beyond that renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The tourism-program page does not establish conversion into a residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No permanent-residence path from this temporary program is established.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official source confirms that time on this work/tourism status counts as legal residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a six-month work/tourism program rather than qualifying residence. Settlement applicants should use the newer statutory remote-work residence visa.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official permit material publishes no fixed minimum.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Adequate subsistence is required, but the inspected sources state no numeric CVE threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum published; adequate subsistence and qualifying independent activity must be documented
income_requirement_display.notes: This route ordinarily requires local formalization or a qualifying liberal-profession service contract.

income_proof_months.notes: The official permit material states no fixed evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Residence visa, accommodation, medical and vaccination documents, municipal residence certificate, social-security registration and Cabo Verde criminal-record checks.
Company contract, liberal-profession service contract or proof of commencement of activity with the tax office; professional authorization where regulated.

initial_validity.value: 2-year temporary residence permit under the ordinary residence system

extension_rules.value: Successive 2-year renewals, with continued-activity and tax-compliance evidence

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Obtain the corresponding residence visa and complete the local residence application.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Ordinary permanent residence is available after at least 5 years of temporary residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be available after at least 5 years of legal residence, subject to statutory conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: A genuine settlement route but only a partial alternative because it may require Cabo Verde tax/social-security formalization and qualifying liberal-profession activity. The dedicated foreign-remote-work residence visa is clearer for this profile.

summary.value: A residence visa exists for higher-education study lasting more than one year and requires admission. It can lead to temporary residence without a local employer, but an existing software-engineering degree alone creates no residence entitlement, and the inspected sources do not establish how student time is counted for permanent residence or naturalization.
summary.notes: This is an admission-based student route, not degree-only skilled migration.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally tax resident after more than 183 aggregate days in Cabo Verde during a calendar year. Residence can also arise with fewer days if a home indicating habitual residence is maintained in Cabo Verde on 31 December.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A residence permit and tax residence are separate tests, but establishing a habitual home can make the alternative test relevant before day 184.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate under the declarative method, not the expected effective rate. A first-year exemption may apply to a qualifying non-resident foreign remote worker.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Official immigration guidance states a 19.5% monthly contribution for workers on their own account. Foreign employees should obtain an INPS classification because liability varies by contract, registration and international arrangements.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment is established. Social security is percentage-based, while visa and residence charges are one-time or per-application state fees.

special_tax_regimes.value: Qualifying non-resident employees and self-employed persons remotely serving foreign entities receive a one-year income-tax exemption. If they remain longer, the non-habitual-resident regime may apply; PwC reports a 10% rate for qualifying Category A/B income from listed high-value-added activities. Software-engineering eligibility and interaction with immigration residence require confirmation.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The exemption should not be assumed for the entire residence period: published material limits it to one year and frames it for non-residents.

taxes.caveats: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on Cabo Verde-source income. Work physically performed in Cabo Verde, foreign-employer/client structure, permanent-establishment risk, the one-year exemption, non-habitual-resident eligibility, VAT, social security and treaty relief require individual analysis. Immigration residence does not by itself settle tax residence or source.

taxation_system.value: Progressive worldwide taxation for residents, with rates of 16.5%, 23.1% and 27.5%; qualifying non-resident foreign remote workers may use a one-year exemption and potentially later the non-habitual-resident regime.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 aggregate days in a calendar year, or fewer days with a home indicating habitual residence in Cabo Verde on 31 December.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents generally on Cabo Verde-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: One-year exemption for qualifying non-resident foreign remote employees or self-employed workers; possible 10% non-habitual-resident rate on listed high-value-added Category A/B activities.
taxation_system.social_security: Workers on their own account are generally subject to 19.5%. Employee social security totals 24.5%, normally 16% employer and 8.5% employee. A foreign-employer remote worker should confirm classification with INPS.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 27.5% dashboard value is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate. PwC reports an annual exemption for net income up to 220,000 CVE followed by 16.5%, 23.1% and 27.5% declarative brackets. Special relief can change the result.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income over 0 and up to 960,000 CVE; PwC separately reports exemption for net income up to 220,000 CVE
tax_brackets.notes: Approximation uses about 96.85 CVE per USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income over 960,000 and up to 1,800,000 CVE
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper boundary.
Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: Core rates and residence rules are supported. The interaction between the one-year non-resident exemption and a residence-visa holder's habitual-home test, and software engineering's treatment under the high-value list, still require filing-level advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: A qualifying non-resident foreign remote worker can receive a one-year income-tax exemption. If tax resident, ordinary worldwide progressive taxation can reach 27.5% unless the person validly enters the non-habitual-resident regime or another relief. Local self-employed registration generally brings 19.5% social security and possible tax/VAT compliance.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Residence visa for remote activity outside Cabo Verde, with a one-year non-resident remote-worker incentive
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: One-year exemption may apply while qualifying as a non-resident remote worker; otherwise progressive worldwide PIT up to 27.5%. Possible qualifying non-habitual-resident rate: 10%.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in the calendar year, or a habitual residence available in Cabo Verde on 31 December even below that count.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is taxable for tax residents. Non-residents are generally taxed only on Cabo Verde-source income; work physically performed in Cabo Verde requires source analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: One-year income-tax exemption for non-resident employees or self-employed persons remotely serving foreign entities. Official 2026 material says non-habitual-resident treatment applies if a digital nomad remains longer; PwC reports 10% on qualifying listed high-value Category A/B income.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Locally registered self-employed persons generally contribute 19.5%. Employee social security totals 24.5% (16% employer and 8.5% employee), but treatment of a foreign employer without Cabo Verde payroll needs INPS advice.

fixed_payments.status: confirmed_component_schedule_with_application_caveats
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed monthly amount is published; applicable contributions are percentage-based and depend on the contribution base and worker classification.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Current official fees are component-based. Portaria No. 40/2025 charges 1,500 CVE to receive/analyse a residence-visa application and 5,000 CVE to issue the residence visa; an extension is 5,000 CVE. At the residence-permit stage, normal receipt/analysis is 1,500 CVE. The e-Residence permit page displays a combined temporary-residence amount of 6,400 CVE for non-CPLP applicants, 1,400 CVE for CPLP applicants and 1,700 CVE for Senegalese applicants. The international-arrival Airport Security Fee is 3,400 CVE unless exempt. GOV.CV separately displays a general visa price of 4,898 CVE, so the route-specific 2025 schedule and actual portal checkout should control.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No universal fixed freelancer tax was established. DNRE material describes a 4% turnover regime for qualifying micro and small businesses, but eligibility and VAT or invoice obligations depend on local registration.
fixed_payments.notes: These are one-time or per-application charges, not monthly taxes. The schedule also lists 3,000 CVE for urgent residence-permit analysis, 3,500 CVE for late renewal and 5,500 CVE for renewal after expiry. Translation, legalization, medical, insurance and provider costs are additional and were not assigned unsupported amounts.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: The one-year exemption may protect qualifying non-resident remote-work income, but staying below 184 days is insufficient if a habitual home exists on 31 December. Source, VAT and social-security issues can remain.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect worldwide-income reporting and progressive PIT up to 27.5% unless non-habitual-resident or other relief is formally accepted. Obtain written classification because the residence route and non-resident exemption overlap.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local registration can trigger Category B reporting, fiscal invoices, possible VAT or small-business rules and normally 19.5% INPS contributions.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The special relief and fee components are published. Filing-level advice remains essential because the tax relief is framed for non-residents while the immigration route is residence-oriented, and the general visa page displays a slightly different price from the route-specific schedule.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A six-month residence visa is used to enter and finalize the two-year temporary residence permit; no prior years on another status are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Permanent residence requires at least five years holding temporary residence plus subsistence, accommodation, character, health/security and language conditions.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization and permanent-residence eligibility both arise after five years of qualifying legal residence; no additional post-PR period is stated.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the statutory minimum. Approval is not automatic, and interruptions or non-qualifying status can affect the calculation.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The regulation gives the responsible minister a maximum of 90 days from presentation of the nationality declaration, though inquiries, opposition or litigation can extend practical completion.

key_conditions.value: Maintain valid legal residence; be an adult or emancipated; avoid disqualifying criminality; prove subsistence; and provide residence-title, residence-period and criminal-record evidence. Permanent residence separately requires knowledge of Cabo Verde's national and official language, adequate means and accommodation, and acceptable health/security history.
key_conditions.notes: The inspected naturalization regulation does not list renunciation. The Constitution permits a Cabo Verdean to acquire another nationality without losing Cabo Verdean nationality.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse may declare for nationality while the marriage continues after at least four years; a legally recognized de facto union has the same threshold.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Time already married to a Cabo Verdean citizen should count toward the four-year duration if the marriage remains valid and is properly registered. Marriage to another migrant supports family residence but does not shorten naturalization.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The declaration must be made while the marriage or recognized union remains in force.

requirements_and_risks.value: The spouse files a nationality declaration with birth and marriage records. Authorities may oppose acquisition for lack of effective connection, serious criminality, security concerns or a marriage/union formed solely to obtain residence or nationality. Lack-of-connection opposition is restricted after six years or where the couple has common Cabo Verdean children.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sham marriage is an express opposition ground; nationality is not automatic upon marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A Cabo Verde-born child of foreign parents qualifies by option where the parents have legally resided for at least three years and neither is serving a foreign state. Nationality also passes from a Cabo Verdean parent, with anti-statelessness protection.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not unconditionally. A Cabo Verde-born child of two foreign parents qualifies for nationality of origin by option if the parents have legally resided for at least three years, neither is serving its state, and the child does not declare against nationality. Statelessness protections also apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The current regulation uses three years, replacing the five-year figure in older summaries.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Cabo Verde to a Cabo Verdean father or mother has nationality by origin. A child born abroad to a Cabo Verdean parent of origin is also covered, subject to civil-registration formalities.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule is not gender-specific.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent who genuinely exercises parental responsibility for, supports and educates a minor resident or Cabo Verdean child may seek residence without the usual residence-visa condition. This is not automatic permanent residence or nationality.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must document the relationship, actual parental responsibility and support and satisfy applicable residence conditions.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Cabo Verdean or qualifying resident minor can have a residence basis if he genuinely exercises parental responsibility and provides support and education. The child's nationality does not automatically confer nationality on the father.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, parental responsibility and genuine support must be documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the live dashboard on 2026-08-15. Index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count; the broader mobility score is 73.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 32 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 2 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Arton is used because it publishes the requested category breakdown. Henley March 2026 separately ranked Cabo Verde 70th with a score of 63; the methodologies should not be mixed.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in some tourism and remote-worker interactions because official route information is available in English, but it is not official. Portuguese is needed for government, legal and tax processes; Cabo Verdean Creole is widely used in daily life.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current nationwide English-proficiency statistic was located, so this is a source-bounded practical assessment.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and no general government-service support was identified. Applicants should expect to use Portuguese, locally Cabo Verdean Creole, or translation.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide data on Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking communities was located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2023 mean monthly insured-worker salary of 46,256 CVE using about 96.85 CVE/USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Public official outputs publish insured-worker means and labor-force counts but no national median wage. Restricted microdata were not used to manufacture an estimate.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 17,000 CVE private-sector statutory minimum introduced for 2025. The public-sector minimum was 19,000 CVE.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2023 INPS insured-worker mean of 46,256 CVE per month.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD conversion is possible because the inspected official sources publish no national median monthly salary in CVE.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD conversion is possible because the inspected official sources publish neither a national maximum monthly salary nor an upper wage-distribution endpoint.

min_salary_local_currency.value: 17,000 CVE/month private-sector statutory minimum; 19,000 CVE/month public-sector minimum, effective 2025
min_salary_local_currency.notes: These are statutory floors, not observed minimum salaries.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2023 mean monthly salary for workers insured in the social-protection dataset.

median_salary_local_currency.value: No national median monthly salary is published in the current official outputs inspected. The INE/INPS social-protection bulletin and 2027 budget guidelines publish arithmetic mean insured salaries, not a median; the IMC 2023 microdata catalogue requires prior INE authorization, so no defensible CVE median can be stated from the public tables.
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Substituting the published mean or deriving a median without the restricted microdata would be misleading.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No national maximum monthly salary or upper endpoint of a national wage distribution is published in the current official outputs inspected. Those sources report statutory floors, arithmetic means and employment counts; an observed sample maximum would not be a statutory or stable national ceiling.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: No CVE amount is supplied because Cabo Verde has no published maximum wage and the checked statistical releases provide no top observation or upper percentile.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2023 gross/contribution-salary mean for insured workers, combined with 2025 statutory minimum wages
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly; mean refers to 2023 and minimum floors to 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The mean covers insured workers, not every citizen or informal worker. The minimum is statutory. About 47.9% of workers in the second-quarter 2024 survey were informal. Focused 2026 checks did not reveal a public national median or maximum: the 2027 budget guidelines update mean public insured salaries, the labor releases report employment indicators, and the IMC catalogue places microdata behind prior authorization.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official sources do not publish a sufficiently specific current household basket suitable for estimating a remote worker's cost of living; no crowdsourced figure was substituted.
