settlement_track.summary: The 2023/2025 remote-work route is a residence visa for work performed for foreign persons or entities, not visitor-like workcation permission. It feeds ordinary temporary residence, from which permanent residence and naturalization are available after five years of qualifying legal residence.
settlement_track.notes: Using the correct residence-visa category is essential. Time under the separate legacy six-month tourism/work program should not be counted without written DEF confirmation.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The statute covers employees and independent professionals remotely serving persons or entities outside Cabo Verde. It accepts a foreign employment relationship, service contract or evidence of services and requires no local employer, local client, investment or exceptional achievement.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 2026-08-15. The route conclusion remains unchanged. The audit resolves the state-fee gap through the current DEF fee schedule and replaces vague salary markers with precise explanations of what current mean-salary, labor-market and restricted-microdata sources publish. Confidence remains medium because the dedicated application button is unavailable and filing-level tax treatment still needs confirmation.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Temporary residence following the remote-professional residence visa
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The remote-professional residence visa can lead to temporary residence, followed by permanent residence after at least five years holding temporary residence.
requirements: Obtain and maintain the residence title; the entry visa alone is insufficient.
Show subsistence and accommodation, satisfy character and public-health/security conditions, and demonstrate knowledge of the national and official language.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: This conclusion applies to the legislated residence route, not the legacy six-month remote-working tourism programme. The DEF online application buttons still say coming soon; the law and residence conditions are published. Five years means time holding temporary residence.
reviewed_route_names: Residence visa for professional activity performed remotely outside Cabo Verde

data.selection_summary: Official government material documents a potentially independent route: E-class entry followed by an EB extension is available to freelancers and people starting businesses, and the EB extension is renewable subject to work-permit requirements. However, official sources do not clearly confirm that foreign-client-only software work qualifies, that a self-employed EB holder can obtain the statutory temporary resident card without a local employment contract, or that EB time starts the naturalization clock. Filing-level legal verification is required, so Cambodia is not fully matched.

visa_application.title: Cambodia e-Visa Service
visa_application.notes: Official direct portal for initial electronic Visa E or Visa T applications. The potentially relevant route requires Visa E, not tourist Visa T. The portal does not document the later EB extension, self-employed work permit, or settlement transition.

best_routes.route_name: E-class ordinary visa followed by EB business extension as freelancer/self-employed business operator

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed official visa, EB-extension, and business-registration material publishes no minimum monthly income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official EB material publishes no minimum income amount in KHR or another currency.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Business registration, tax, visa-extension, and work-permit evidence may still be required; absence of an income threshold does not eliminate business-substance review.

income_proof_months.notes: The official EB description does not prescribe a number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Enter on an E-class ordinary visa; the official eVisa portal lists Visa E at USD 35, single entry, three-month validity for use, and one-month stay.

The government investment handbook lists EB extensions for foreigners working in Cambodia, starting a business, freelancers, and accompanying spouse or children; EB may be renewed indefinitely in 1-, 3-, 6-, or 12-month increments.
A foreigner who works must obtain a work permit and foreign employment card; the official FWCMS includes a SELF-EMPLOYED work-permit category.
For longer business-visa renewal, the official handbook says a work permit is required.

A freelancer relying on local self-employment should expect business, tax, enterprise-opening, and potentially NSSF registrations; the government single portal supports integrated registration and says correctly completed cases are decided in eight working days.

The public portal does not clearly confirm whether a newly arrived foreign individual can register a sole proprietorship for foreign-client software services without a Cambodian partner or local client; verify this before relying on the route.

initial_validity.value: Initial Visa E: usable for entry within 3 months of issue; single entry; 1-month stay. EB extension options: 1, 3, 6, or 12 months.
initial_validity.notes: An E-class visa is an entry visa; EB is an extension of temporary stay, not proven here to be a residence permit or residence card.

extension_rules.value: The official investment handbook says EB extensions can be renewed indefinitely in 1-, 3-, 6-, or 12-month periods; renewals longer than 30 days become multiple-entry, and long business renewals are subject to holding a work permit.
extension_rules.notes: Exact current supporting-document and EB-extension fee rules are not published on an accessible General Department of Immigration route page; filing-level confirmation is essential.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: EB is renewable temporary stay, but it is not itself proven to be the statutory temporary resident card. The 1995 resident-card proclamation allows specified staff, technical or specialized workers, and sellers of services or labour to apply to the Ministry of Interior; its file list includes a proper visa, medical certificate, written labour contract, social-security insurance, and proof of resident-card tax payment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No current source confirms that a foreign-client-only freelancer with EB status satisfies the written-labour-contract requirement or states a decision time. EB stay and a temporary resident card must therefore remain separate.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The immigration law and resident-card proclamation reserve permanent cards for recognized immigrant aliens and qualifying recognized investors. They do not publish an ordinary EB-freelancer conversion procedure or waiting period.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization legislation uses a seven-year continuous-residence period counted from issuance of an immigration-law residence card, plus good conduct, Khmer language, script and history, integration, residence at filing, and health or non-burden conditions. It was not established that EB time produces or counts from that residence card.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The 2018 law replaced the 1996 law; the accessible English text is the earlier law, while the 2018 record and December 2025 implementing sub-decree confirm the current framework. Obtain Khmer-law advice on current article numbering and EB counting.

best_routes.notes: This is a plausible independent freelancer or self-employed living route, not a dedicated digital-nomad visa. It is uncertain because foreign-client-only software activity, sole-proprietor eligibility, current EB evidence, and settlement counting are not all confirmed in accessible official instructions.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visa T tourist eVisa / tourist stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official page publishes no income threshold; this is immaterial because Visa T is a tourist entry route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The tourist-visa page publishes no local-currency income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Tourist status is not a work or settlement route.

income_proof_months.notes: The tourist-visa page does not require a specified number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport valid more than six months, digital passport photograph, and payment card for online filing.
All travelers must submit Cambodia e-Arrival within seven days before or on arrival.

initial_validity.value: Single entry; visa valid for use for 3 months; permitted stay 1 month.
initial_validity.notes: Tourist-only entry.

extension_rules.value: Tourist extensions do not create a qualifying remote-work residence route.
extension_rules.notes: Rejected regardless of any short extension.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The tourist entry permission does not directly grant a statutory temporary resident card.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The immigration law does not establish a tourist-to-permanent-resident conversion for this profile.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Tourist time is not shown to satisfy the residence-card rule used for general naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Visitor or tourist status is excluded even if remote work is informally tolerated.

rejected_routes.route_name: Embassy-issued Type-E business visa based on Cambodian employment offer or company invitation

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The embassy page publishes no income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The embassy page publishes no local-currency income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility turns on employment or invitation evidence, not income.

income_proof_months.notes: The embassy page does not prescribe a number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Accepted Cambodian employment offer, invitation from a registered Cambodian organization, or assignment by a registered sending organization.
Invitation or sending-company letter, passport, application, photograph, and USD 35 fee.

initial_validity.value: Single entry; enter within 3 months; 30-day stay.
initial_validity.notes: Embassy processing is stated as 7-10 working days.

extension_rules.value: The embassy page states a further 30-day extension at Immigration; broader EB rules must be checked in Cambodia.
extension_rules.notes: This rejected variant depends on employer or company evidence.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The Type-E entry visa does not itself grant a residence card; the separate resident-card proclamation requires a Ministry of Interior application and additional evidence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No employer-route permanent-residence transition or waiting period was established for this profile.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No route-specific citizenship transition was established; general naturalization uses a separate qualifying residence-card period.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this embassy variant requires Cambodian employment or registered-company invitation and does not fit ordinary independent foreign-contract work.

summary.value: The ES student extension is an education-stay category, not a degree-based independent skilled-migration route. No independent points-, degree-, or qualification-based residence route was found.
summary.notes: The applicant’s software-engineering degree does not independently create Cambodian residence eligibility in the sources reviewed.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if domiciled in Cambodia, has a principal place of abode there, or is present more than 182 days in any 12-month period ending in the current tax year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can arise before a full calendar year if the domicile or principal-abode tests apply.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal or screening rate, not expected effective rate. Resident employment salary uses 0%-20% monthly brackets; nonresident Cambodian-source salary is flat 20%. Consulting or self-employed income may instead fall under Tax on Income.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For covered employees, the pension scheme’s total Phase 1 contribution is 4% of contributory wage, commonly 2% employer and 2% employee. Employer-funded occupational-risk and healthcare contributions are additional. This should not be assumed for a foreign sole proprietor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: KHR 1,000/month, approximately USD 0.25 at KHR 4,013/USD, is shown on the government business portal for voluntary self-employed healthcare contributions. The page does not confirm foreigner eligibility, and a 2025 regional NSSF profile reports KHR 15,600 for a broader self-employed or dependent category; verify the applicable scheme.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad or inbound-expatriate exemption was found. Cambodia taxes resident employment salary on worldwide salary; general consulting income is excluded from salary tax but may be taxable under Tax on Income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Classification as employee versus independent consultant materially changes compliance.

taxes.caveats: A foreign employer may need a Cambodian fiscal representative for salary withholding; GDT materials state the foreign employer or representative and employee can be jointly responsible. A registered sole proprietor may face Tax on Income, patent tax, VAT or turnover thresholds, accounting, and other business obligations. Treaty position and income-source rules require professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: progressive monthly Tax on Salary for resident employees, flat 20% for nonresident Cambodian-source salary, and Tax on Income or business rules for consultants and sole proprietors.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile, principal place of abode, or more than 182 days in any 12-month period ending in the tax year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident employees: Cambodian- and foreign-source salary; nonresidents: Cambodian-source salary. Independent consulting and business income is governed separately by Tax on Income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or ordinary remote-worker exemption found.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees: occupational risk 0.8% employer, healthcare 2.6% employer, and Phase 1 pension 4% total. Self-employed healthcare is voluntary on the government page reviewed, but the exact foreigner category and contribution require confirmation.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 20% is the top marginal rate. Monthly resident salary brackets are 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20%; nonresident Cambodian-source salary is a flat final 20%.

tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses KHR 4,013/USD and is illustrative.
Upper threshold approximate.
Upper threshold approximate.
Upper threshold approximate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident monthly taxable salary above threshold; also the flat rate for nonresident Cambodian-source salary
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal resident rate; nonresident salary treatment is flat and final.

taxation_system.notes: High confidence on salary residency and brackets; medium confidence on application to a foreign-client freelancer because employment-versus-consulting classification and business registration determine the tax base.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Cambodia has no dedicated nomad tax category. A resident foreign-employee scenario can expose worldwide salary to progressive 0%-20% Tax on Salary; independent consulting is generally outside salary tax but subject to business Tax on Income rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No special digital-nomad regime; employee salary or self-employed/business taxation depending on facts
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%-20% progressive resident salary tax, with 20% as the top marginal rate; independent consulting requires separate Tax on Income analysis
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or principal abode, or more than 182 days in any 12-month period ending in the tax year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide salary of a resident employee is within Tax on Salary; nonresident salary is taxed only if Cambodian-source. Foreign-client consulting income requires source and business-classification advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee schemes and employer withholding can apply. The government lists voluntary self-employed healthcare, but foreign eligibility and the correct contribution category are unclear.

fixed_payments.status: Partially established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The government business portal states KHR 1,000/month for voluntary self-employed healthcare, payable in advance every 3, 6, or 12 months; applicability to a foreign freelancer is unconfirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Initial electronic Visa E: USD 35. Cambodia v-Pass is free. The government National Trade Repository guideline, still displayed without an expiry date, lists KHR 400,000 for a Visa-E foreign work permit and employment card plus KHR 100,000 for the required physical examination; an older government public-service schedule also lists KHR 400,000 for a one-year foreign work permit. Neither source publishes the current EB-extension fee, the self-employed-category fee, or temporary-resident-card tax, so a current all-in route total cannot be stated.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business-registration, tax-registration, patent-tax, licensing, banking, and payment-card fees may apply. A current all-in monthly equivalent cannot be established because fees vary by entity, activity, and taxpayer class.
fixed_payments.notes: The Visa E entry fee and free v-Pass are current official figures. Work-permit amounts come from older official schedules that remain online; confirm the 2026 self-employed fee in FWCMS before paying. EB-extension and resident-card charges are unpublished in the current official pages reviewed.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Nonresident status does not automatically mean zero tax: Cambodian-source salary is flat 20%, while foreign-source characterization depends on where employment or services are exercised and treaty facts.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide employment salary can be subject to monthly progressive Tax on Salary up to 20%; a foreign employer may need a Cambodian fiscal representative.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Consulting or business income may fall under Tax on Income rather than Tax on Salary, with registration and filing obligations; obtain a Cambodian tax classification before invoicing through the route.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No route-specific nomad guidance exists, so these scenarios are derived from general rules and must be confirmed for the applicant’s contract structure.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The numeric value remains null because setting it to zero would incorrectly equate an EB extension of stay with a statutory temporary resident card. The 1995 proclamation permits specified technical, specialized, managerial, and service or labour workers to apply for that card at the Ministry of Interior, but publishes no qualifying prior-residence period or processing time and requires a written labour contract, insurance, medical evidence, proper visa, and proof of card-tax payment. No reviewed source confirms when or whether a foreign-client-only EB freelancer receives the card.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The laws identify permanent resident cards for recognized immigrant aliens and qualifying investors but publish no ordinary freelancer EB-to-permanent-residence timetable.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Accessible law materials state seven continuous years from an immigration-law residence card, not seven years after permanent residence. The schema interval therefore cannot be calculated reliably.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: A route-specific total cannot be calculated because no source confirms when or whether an EB freelancer obtains the qualifying residence card.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The December 2025 implementing sub-decree is published, but the accessible official page does not publish an average or statutory end-to-end processing duration.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization is discretionary, not an entitlement. Accessible law materials require residence certification and seven continuous years from a residence card, present residence, good conduct and no criminal conviction, Khmer speaking and script, Khmer history and social integration, and no danger or burden to the nation. Current filing procedures are governed by the 2018 law and 2025 implementing sub-decree.
key_conditions.notes: No reliable renunciation requirement was confirmed. Citizenship-revocation law changed in 2025, so specialist advice is warranted.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The accessible English law says a foreign spouse may claim after three years living together following registration of the marriage certificate. The 2025 implementing sub-decree expressly covers nationality by marriage under the current law.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count only if it is validly registered or recognized and the statutory three-year cohabitation period and current procedures are met; marriage does not automatically confer citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Verify whether a foreign marriage certificate must be transcribed or registered in Cambodia.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship by marriage is an application decided by the competent authorities, not automatic. Expect identity, registered-marriage, cohabitation or genuine-relationship, character, and document checks. Sham marriage or false evidence creates refusal and legal risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The accessible official page for the 2025 sub-decree is Khmer-only; current detailed forms and evidentiary rules require local verification.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 9 of the 2018 law, as reproduced in Cambodia’s UN reporting, grants citizenship to a Cambodia-born child of foreign parents only where those parents were themselves born in Cambodia and live there legally. This is double jus soli or restricted birthright citizenship. Foundlings and children of unknown parents are also covered.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not merely because of birth in Cambodia. The child qualifies under the double-jus-soli rule only if the foreign parents were themselves born in Cambodia and live there legally; ordinary first-generation migrant parents do not satisfy that rule.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Foundling and unknown-parent rules are separate.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born to a Cambodian father or mother is Cambodian by descent regardless of place of birth, subject to proof and registration.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule is parent-neutral in the 2018-law text reproduced by OHCHR.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Cambodian child does not automatically naturalize or permanently admit a foreign parent. Family immigration and nationality applications remain separate; a parent who is also the spouse of a Cambodian may use the marriage route if its requirements are met.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed official framework publishes no automatic parent-residence benefit based solely on birth of a citizen child.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father gains no automatic citizenship from the child. If the mother is Cambodian, the child can be Cambodian by descent; the father must separately qualify through marriage, residence, or another lawful status.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage, marriage, birth, and civil-status registration must be documented.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026, January global ranking

rank.notes: Shared rank in the 9 January 2026 Henley table.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley’s score combines destinations accessible without a prior visa, including visa-free, visa on arrival, and eTA; it is not a strictly visa-free count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s current category count, using a different methodology from Henley and potentially grouping eVisa destinations among advance-visa cases.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index separates 41 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations; combined here. It also lists 20 strictly visa-free destinations and a mobility score of 66.

passport.notes: Use one index consistently for comparisons. Henley is used for rank and overall no-prior-visa score; Passport Index is used only for the requested category breakdown because Henley’s public PDF does not separate it.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only remote work is feasible in international workplaces and central Phnom Penh, but not reliably for government, immigration, tax, banking, leases, or nationwide daily life. EF EPI 2025 gives Cambodia a score of 390 and global rank 123, while Phnom Penh scores 472, indicating a significant national language barrier and better but still limited capital-city conditions.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is based on self-selected online test takers, so it is an indicator rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, and no reliable evidence supports using either for government procedures or routine daily life. Plan on Khmer and, in international settings, English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No current nationwide Russian or Ukrainian usage dataset was published in the reviewed sources; this cautious conclusion follows from the official-language rule and very low measured English proficiency.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest clean official national figure located: KHR 1,078,595/month from the 2019 Labour Force Survey, divided by KHR 4,013/USD. This is stale and not a 2026 wage estimate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official survey catalogue and 2019 national labour-force report do not publish a national median monthly wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statutory 2026 minimum only for regular workers in textile, garment, footwear, travel-goods, and bag manufacturing; not a nationwide minimum or observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2019 average; not inflation-adjusted and not a current 2026 average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official national report provides mean wages but does not publish a national median in the reviewed wage table.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official national wage table does not publish a meaningful maximum or upper percentile.

min_salary_local_currency.value: USD 210/month, approximately KHR 842,730 at KHR 4,013/USD, sector-specific
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The legal wage is denominated and published in USD for the covered manufacturing sectors.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National average monthly wage, both sexes, Cambodia Labour Force Survey 2019.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed national labour-force wage table does not publish a median amount.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed national labour-force wage table does not publish a maximum or upper-percentile amount.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average: mean monthly wage of wage earners in the 2019 official labour-force survey; minimum: sector-specific statutory monthly minimum effective 1 January 2026
average_citizen_salary.period: Average 2019; minimum 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The covered-sector 2026 minimum is USD 210. The official average remains old and should not be presented as current purchasing power.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed current official survey catalogue does not publish a household-level cost-of-living amount directly comparable to the wage data; crowdsourced estimates were not substituted.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: EB is renewable temporary stay for business or freelance activity, not a dedicated nomad residence permit. Do not assume EB years count toward naturalization.
settlement_track.summary: The EB freelancer or self-employed route plausibly permits renewable temporary stay and work, but the statutory temporary resident card has separate Ministry of Interior criteria including a written labour contract, and no official source connects foreign-client-only EB freelancing to that card or to permanent residence. General naturalization uses seven years counted from a qualifying residence card, so this route needs immigration counsel before it can be treated as a citizenship track.
settlement_track.notes: Official government material expressly lists freelancers under EB, but settlement uncertainty remains decisive.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Official material includes freelancers and a self-employed work-permit category, but it does not expressly say that a foreigner serving only overseas clients may qualify without local clients, a Cambodian company invitation, or local business substance. Confirm sole-proprietor or company eligibility, EB-extension evidence, foreign-worker quota treatment, and work-permit issuance before applying.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against more than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs, including more than five URLs absent from the previous source set. The pass established the USD 35 Visa E fee, free v-Pass, older official work-permit and medical-exam schedules, and the separate statutory temporary-resident-card application criteria. Current EB-extension, self-employed work-permit, and resident-card charges and a route-specific residence timeline remain unpublished or unconfirmed in the reviewed official pages, so those limits are stated precisely rather than guessed.

data.selection_summary: Cameroon has no dedicated digital-nomad visa. Its current immigration rules allow a foreigner with authorization to practise a liberal profession or promote a commercial or other activity to seek a long-stay visa and then a renewable residence permit without a local employer. However, official sources do not confirm whether ordinary software work performed exclusively for a foreign client qualifies for the required activity authorization, so filing-level verification is essential and the country is not fully matched.

visa_application.title: evisa Cameroun — official visa application portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official online entry-visa portal. Applicants create an account and submit a visa application online. It is not a dedicated remote-worker portal; a prospective independent professional would need the appropriate activity authorization before relying on the long-stay category.

best_routes.route_name: Long-stay visa for an authorized liberal profession or commercial/other activity, followed by residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numerical monthly threshold is published. The applicant must demonstrate sufficient means, a repatriation guarantee, the purpose of stay, and any required authorization for the activity.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed XAF income threshold was found in the current immigration instruments.

income_requirement_display.value: No published fixed income threshold; sufficient means, repatriation guarantee, and activity authorization required
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of a numerical threshold does not eliminate financial scrutiny. The immigration authority retains discretion over sufficient means and the proposed purpose of stay.

income_proof_months.notes: The sources require sufficient means but do not prescribe a specific bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain a long-stay visa through the official eVisa process.

Hold authorization from the competent authority to practise a liberal profession or promote an agricultural, pastoral, industrial, commercial, artistic, or other activity, where such authorization is required.
Provide a passport valid for more than six months, travel document or ticket to Cameroon, required vaccination certificates, and a repatriation guarantee.
For the residence permit, provide the passport with long-stay visa, proof of domicile, a special criminal-record extract, valid tax-compliance certificate, and justification of the purpose of stay.
If operating through a Cameroonian enterprise, complete commercial, statistical, tax, labour, and social-insurance registrations as applicable.

initial_validity.value: Long-stay entry visa: up to 12 months; residence permit: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The entry visa and residence permit are separate documents. The current MINREX page describes long-stay visas of up to 12 months, while the 2025 identity-document decree gives the residence permit two-year validity.

extension_rules.value: The two-year residence permit is renewable twice; a residence card may then be requested using the permit renewed for the second time. The residence card is valid for 10 years.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal requires continued justification of the stay, the previous permit, domicile, criminal-record and tax-compliance documents. The 2025 decree is used because it is newer than the 2023 implementing decree.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply for the qualifying long-stay visa, enter regularly, and apply for the residence permit with proof of the authorized activity and other required documents.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The 1997 law requires an adult foreigner authorized to stay beyond visitor status to seek a residence document within three months. Approval is not automatic merely because a business was registered.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After holding the initial two-year residence permit and renewing it twice, the applicant may seek the 10-year residence card, subject to approval and current documentary requirements.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a residence-card transition, not an automatically acquired permanent status. The decree requires the permit renewed for the second time, which implies approximately six years from initial permit issuance.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after five consecutive years of habitual residence, with the applicant's main interests based in Cameroon and subject to character, health, assimilation, and discretionary decree requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality code does not expressly identify foreign-client remote work. Whether time under this exact self-employed arrangement will be accepted as qualifying habitual residence depends first on obtaining and maintaining lawful status.

best_routes.notes: This is the only potentially independent residence-oriented route found, but it is not a dedicated freelancer or nomad program. The decisive unresolved issue is whether a software engineer working solely for a foreign client can obtain the competent authority's activity authorization without demonstrating local clients, investment, or additional local economic substance.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Only unspecified sufficient means for the visit are required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No numerical visitor threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient means for the visit; no published fixed amount
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a visitor requirement, not a remote-worker income test.

income_proof_months.notes: No prescribed history period was found.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport valid for at least six months, return or circular ticket, required vaccinations, proof of purpose and sufficient means, and accommodation or hotel evidence.

initial_validity.value: Up to 6 months
initial_validity.notes: MINREX states that the short-stay visa may run for up to six months.

extension_rules.notes: No remote-work extension or conversion entitlement is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None on visitor status itself
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The immigration law expressly distinguishes temporary visitors from foreigners required to obtain residence documentation.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor status is not a permanent-residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status
path_to_citizenship.notes: A visitor stay does not establish the confirmed habitual-residence track required for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an ordinary eVisa is visitor permission, not authorization to reside and perform ongoing foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.route_name: Long-stay visa and residence permit based on salaried employment in Cameroon

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold was found.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Employment compensation is contractual rather than a published immigration threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published immigration income threshold; approved Cameroonian employment contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not usable for the supplied foreign-contract profile.

income_proof_months.notes: Not published.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment contract endorsed by the minister responsible for employment for a foreigner wishing to undertake salaried activity in Cameroon.
Long-stay visa and subsequent residence-permit documentation.

initial_validity.value: Long-stay visa up to 12 months; residence permit 2 years

extension_rules.value: Residence permit renewable twice if the employment purpose continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available through approved local employment
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Requires the local employment basis excluded by the selection criteria.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A residence card may be requested after the permit has been renewed twice
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not relevant to an applicant unwilling to obtain local sponsored employment.

path_to_citizenship.value: General five-year habitual-residence naturalization rules may eventually apply
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a locally endorsed employment contract is required.

summary.value: A student may independently obtain a long-stay visa using an enrolment or re-enrolment certificate and then seek a residence permit. This is education-based temporary residence, not a degree-based skilled migration program, and no direct permanent residence is granted.
summary.notes: Continued residence depends on maintaining an accepted purpose of stay. The sources do not confirm that a completed foreign university degree by itself creates residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax domicile arises if the individual has a home or principal residence in Cameroon, carries on a salaried or non-salaried professional activity there other than accessorily, or has the centre of economic interests there. Current tax guidance also uses more than 183 days in a calendar year for a foreign national. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents on Cameroon-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Unlike a simple day-count-only rule, professional activity or the centre-of-interests test can establish residence sooner. Treaty provisions may override domestic treatment.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for salary income after the 10% additional council levy. MINFI publishes base brackets of 10%, 15%, 25%, and 35%; current PwC tables show the corresponding all-in rates of 11%, 16.5%, 27.5%, and 38.5%. This is not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Indicative employee payroll burden: 4.2% old-age, disability and death contribution plus the reported 1% employee housing-fund contribution. A foreign remote worker or registered independent professional may not fall into the same compulsory payroll treatment; CNPS states that persons outside compulsory old-age coverage may subscribe voluntarily.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly contribution for the uncertain foreign-client self-employed scenario could be established. Voluntary CNPS contributions are based on agreed annual income, while business tax instalments depend on turnover and regime.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax holiday was found. Registered independent activity may instead fall under ordinary business/non-commercial-profit rules, including 33% tax on net income from other activities and turnover-based minimum or instalment rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The 2026 3% digital-sector measure concerns non-resident digital-sector companies with significant economic presence, not an individual digital-nomad concession.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the foreign contract is characterized as salary, non-commercial professional profit, or business income; whether the foreign payer creates local payroll or permanent-establishment issues; treaty availability; deductions; turnover; and social-insurance status. Obtain Cameroonian tax advice before relocating or registering an activity.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally subject to worldwide-income taxation. Salary income uses progressive rates of 11%, 16.5%, 27.5%, and 38.5% including additional council tax. Net income from other activities is generally reported at 33%, with regime-dependent minimum or advance payments based on turnover.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Home or principal residence, non-accessory professional activity, centre of economic interests, or—under current guidance for foreign nationals—more than 183 days in the calendar year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for tax residents; Cameroon-source income for non-residents, subject to treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No confirmed special digital-nomad or general inbound-expatriate regime.
taxation_system.social_security: Formal employees generally contribute 4.2% to the CNPS pension branch; a further 1% employee housing-fund deduction is reported. Self-employed persons outside compulsory coverage may use voluntary insurance based on agreed income.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 38.5% value is the top marginal salary rate including the 10% council surcharge on the base tax, not an effective rate. Professional or business income can follow different 33% and turnover-minimum rules.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Salary, wage, pension and annuity income
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold uses 566.4255 XAF/USD on 2026-08-14.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Salary, wage, pension and annuity income
tax_brackets.notes: Rate includes additional council tax; USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Salary, wage, pension and annuity income
tax_brackets.notes: Rate includes additional council tax; USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Salary, wage, pension and annuity income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate including additional council tax.

taxation_system.notes: The core residence and progressive salary rules are well supported. Exact classification of foreign-client software income remains fact-specific because Cameroon has no dedicated nomad category.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Cameroon has no confirmed digital-nomad immigration or tax category. If the person nevertheless obtains lawful residence as an independent professional, ordinary resident worldwide-income and professional/business tax rules would apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated category; possible salary or non-commercial/business income depending on contract and registration
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 38.5% for salary income including council surcharge; other net professional/business income may be taxed at 33%, with turnover-based minimum or instalment rules
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Potentially triggered by a home or principal residence, non-accessory professional activity, centre of economic interests, or more than 183 days for a foreign national.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Generally taxable on a worldwide basis once tax resident, subject to treaties and characterization.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Formal employee deductions are approximately 5.2% when the 4.2% CNPS pension share and 1% housing-fund deduction apply. Independent persons outside compulsory coverage may have voluntary CNPS treatment rather than the same payroll rate.

fixed_payments.status: No DNV-specific fixed payment; ordinary visa, residence-document, registration, and regime-dependent tax costs apply
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal self-employed monthly minimum confirmed; voluntary CNPS contributions depend on agreed annual income.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: MINREX lists XAF 100,000 ordinary or XAF 150,000 express for a short-stay visa, and XAF 150,000 ordinary or XAF 200,000 express for a long-stay visa. The 2023 tax code lists residence-permit stamp duties of XAF 150,000 for African nationals and XAF 300,000 for non-African nationals, and residence-card duties of XAF 300,000 and XAF 750,000 respectively; current payable amounts should be reconfirmed before filing.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business registration, trade-register, statistical, tax, labour and NSIF formalities may apply. Ordinary business tax can include turnover-based advance or minimum payments rather than a fixed freelancer charge.
fixed_payments.notes: Residence-document duties were found in the official 2023 tax code but may have been changed by later finance legislation; verify them with DGSN or the tax authority.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short visit does not automatically avoid Cameroon taxation if the person establishes a home, carries on non-accessory professional activity in Cameroon, or moves the centre of economic interests there. Visitor status also does not authorize the proposed residence/work arrangement.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax-resident employee with foreign salary may be taxed on worldwide salary at progressive all-in rates up to 38.5%, subject to treaty relief and contract characterization.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A registered independent professional or sole proprietor may face 33% tax on net non-salary income and regime-dependent turnover instalments or minimum tax, plus registration and possibly voluntary social-insurance obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is reduced because no official tax classification exists for a foreign-contract digital nomad and the immigration eligibility of that arrangement is itself unresolved.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is available after the qualifying long-stay entry and residence-permit approval; zero denotes no statutory multi-year waiting period, not immediate or guaranteed issuance.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The 2025 decree permits the residence card application using a two-year residence permit renewed for the second time, implying approximately six years. Approval remains required.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization eligibility is based on five consecutive years of habitual residence rather than prior residence-card status, so eligibility may arise before the approximate six-year residence-card transition. Citizenship is not automatic.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest statutory naturalization eligibility after five consecutive years of habitual residence. The applicant must still maintain lawful qualifying status, base main interests in Cameroon, and obtain a discretionary naturalization decree.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the nationality code nor current Ministry of Justice material establishes a reliable typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: Five consecutive years of habitual residence; main interests based in Cameroon at decree signature; adulthood; good character and morals; no unrehabilitated ordinary-law conviction; sound body and mind; assimilation review; and discretionary approval by decree. Cameroonian law is restrictive toward retention of another nationality.
key_conditions.notes: No numerical language-test or absence-limit rule was found in the reviewed code, but assimilation is assessed. Naturalization is discretionary rather than an entitlement after five years.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The code provides no five-year probationary period for a foreign man married to a Cameroonian wife, while a foreign woman marrying a Cameroonian may request nationality at the celebration of marriage. A spouse of a Cameroonian may also apply directly for the residence card under the current document rules. These provisions are gender-asymmetric and approval requirements remain.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Cameroonian supports a direct residence-card application using a recent certified marriage record, long-stay visa, domicile evidence, criminal record, stamp-duty proof and tax-compliance certificate. For citizenship, a foreign husband uses discretionary naturalization with the five-year probation waived; the code's immediate declaration mechanism is written specifically for a foreign woman at marriage celebration.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A marriage already celebrated outside the prescribed nationality-declaration moment may require separate procedural advice, especially for a foreign wife.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally documented and genuine. Residence approval, security screening, criminal-record and tax-compliance requirements still apply. Citizenship remains subject to government opposition or discretionary decree depending on the provision used; sham marriage or false documentation can cause refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The nationality code is old and gender-discriminatory in wording. Obtain current Ministry of Justice advice before relying on its marriage mechanism.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Cameroon combines descent with double jus soli and anti-statelessness/foundling rules. A child of foreign parents generally obtains nationality at birth only if the child and the relevant parent were born in Cameroon, subject to statutory details and a right of renunciation.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Birth in Cameroon to two foreign migrant parents does not by itself confer nationality. Citizenship may attach if the double-jus-soli condition is met, the parents are unknown, or the child cannot claim another nationality of origin.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A parent merely holding temporary or permanent residence is insufficient under the reviewed code.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Cameroonian father or mother generally acquires Cameroonian nationality by descent, subject to affiliation rules and, in some mixed-nationality cases, a right to renounce before majority.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The code distinguishes legitimate and non-marital affiliation, but recognizes transmission through either Cameroonian parent in the relevant provisions.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's nationality does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. A foreign parent may have a family-based basis to remain with the child, but no automatic parent residence card or shortened naturalization period based solely on parenthood was confirmed in the reviewed instruments.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed residence-card decree expressly addresses spouses, not a standalone parent-of-citizen category.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically receive citizenship or permanent residence because his child is Cameroonian. If he is married to the Cameroonian mother, the spousal residence-card and no-probation naturalization provisions may help; those benefits arise from marriage, not fatherhood alone.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A non-married father's residence position requires case-specific confirmation.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed by Passport Index when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count. The index separately displays eVisa destinations in its country table, so category totals should be interpreted under that index's methodology.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 32 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 3 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 56. This record uses one named index consistently rather than mixing its breakdown with Henley figures.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate and location-dependent. English is an official language of equal legal status and public services should be available in it, but the Presidency's country profile estimates French is spoken by about 70% and English by about 30%. English is considerably more practical in the Anglophone regions and major professional settings than nationwide.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Official bilingualism does not mean every private service or neighborhood functions equally well in English; French remains the more broadly useful language nationally.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official or broadly documented working language; daily administration, business registration and immigration should be expected in French or English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current source established a substantial Russian- or Ukrainian-language service ecosystem, so this assessment is cautious rather than a population estimate.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Derived approximation: the official statistics factbook reports an overall average employee wage of XAF 589.60 per hour from the 2021 employment survey. Multiplying by approximately 173.33 hours per month gives XAF 102,197, or about USD 180 at 566.4255 XAF/USD on 2026-08-14. It is not a newly measured 2026 monthly salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable national median monthly wage was found in the inspected official statistics and social-security publications.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the XAF 60,000 general-sector statutory minimum wage at the 2026-08-14 mid-market rate. This is a legal minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent derived from the 2021 survey's XAF 589.60 overall average hourly employee wage using 173.33 monthly hours. The age of the underlying survey limits current comparability.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national median wage was published in the directly relevant official sources inspected.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary or reliable upper wage-distribution bound was found.

min_salary_local_currency.value: XAF 60,000/month general sector; XAF 45,000/month agriculture; XAF 41,875/month certain state employees covered by the Labour Code
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The general-sector XAF 60,000 amount is used for the USD minimum display.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Derived using 40 hours weekly and 52/12 weeks monthly; the official source itself reports an hourly, not monthly, average.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not established after focused review of official wage and social-security publications.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum or upper distribution measure was established.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average employee hourly wage from Cameroon's 2021 employment and informal-sector survey, mechanically converted to a full-time monthly equivalent; minimum fields are statutory monthly wages
average_citizen_salary.period: 2021 survey wage data; minimum-wage reference effective by 2024 and still reported in 2026 sources; FX dated 2026-08-14
average_citizen_salary.notes: The official average is relatively old and hourly, so the monthly and USD values are approximations. Median and maximum remain null because the additional focused sources did not publish defensible national figures.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official statistics reported 4.5% consumer-price inflation in 2024, driven particularly by food prices rising 5.6% and transport costs 12.3%. This indicates notable recent cost pressure but is not a complete monthly household budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No single reliable official current cost-of-living total for a remote worker was found, so no rent or household-budget estimate is supplied.
