settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Cameroon has no dedicated nomad status. An ordinary visitor or short-stay eVisa is not a qualifying settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: An authorized independent professional activity can in principle support a long-stay visa, renewable residence permit, later residence card, and general five-year naturalization eligibility. The track remains weak for this profile because no official source confirms that foreign-client-only software work qualifies for the required activity authorization or that it can be maintained without additional local business substance.
settlement_track.notes: Manual confirmation should be obtained from the competent activity-licensing authority, DGSN immigration services, and the Cameroonian mission handling the visa before incurring relocation or registration costs.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The law recognizes liberal-profession and commercial/other activity as long-stay purposes and does not state that a local employer is required. It does not establish that an ordinary software engineer serving only a foreign client will receive the necessary authorization, nor does it rule out local registration or substance requirements.

data.notes: This audit materially improves the previous record by identifying the official independent-activity language, current 2025 residence-document transition, tax brackets, social contributions, citizenship and family rules, passport breakdown, wage evidence, and official application route. Selection remains uncertain rather than positive because the key foreign-client eligibility question is unresolved.

data.selection_summary: Canada does not have a dedicated digital-nomad residence permit: foreign-employer remote work is officially allowed only under visitor status for up to six months and is not a settlement route. Canada is nevertheless a partial match because the independently accessible, points-tested Federal Skilled Worker Program can use foreign software-engineering experience, does not require a Canadian job offer, and grants permanent residence if the applicant is invited and approved.

visa_application.title: Express Entry: Create your profile and enter the pool
visa_application.notes: The applicant starts by creating an Express Entry profile through an IRCC secure account. Entering the pool is not a permanent-residence application and does not guarantee an invitation; the direct PR application becomes available only after IRCC issues an invitation to apply.

best_routes.route_name: Express Entry — Federal Skilled Worker Program

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no monthly-income threshold. Applicants normally need settlement funds instead.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: CAD 15,263 in available settlement funds for a family of one; higher amounts apply with accompanying or non-accompanying spouse/dependants
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official table was still labelled as updated July 7, 2025 when checked. IRCC updates it periodically, so the amount must be rechecked before submission.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income minimum; CAD 15,263 settlement funds for one person under the current published table
income_requirement_display.notes: This is liquid settlement capital, not monthly salary. Funds must remain legally accessible when applying and when permanent residence is issued.

income_proof_months.notes: The bank letter must report each account's current balance and average balance for the preceding six months.

key_requirements.requirement: At least one year of continuous paid skilled work, or 1,560 hours, in TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 within the previous 10 years; qualifying experience may be foreign and may include self-employment.
Approved English or French test with at least CLB 7 in speaking, listening, reading and writing.
A completed foreign educational credential plus an Educational Credential Assessment for immigration purposes, unless relying on Canadian education.
At least 67 of 100 Federal Skilled Worker selection-factor points, followed by a competitive Comprehensive Ranking System score and an invitation from the Express Entry pool.
Settlement funds unless exempt, admissibility including security, criminal and medical assessment, and an intention to settle outside Quebec.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence upon approval and landing
initial_validity.notes: An Express Entry profile is not status and does not permit residence or work while waiting.

extension_rules.value: Not a temporary permit. Permanent residents must continue meeting the statutory PR residency obligation; citizenship is optional after eligibility is reached.
extension_rules.notes: No visa-extension stage applies to the FSW grant itself.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None through this route; it is a direct permanent-residence program after invitation and approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate visitor, study or work status is not required to create an Express Entry profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Create an Express Entry profile, enter the competitive pool, receive an invitation, submit the electronic application within 60 days, and obtain permanent residence if approved.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Eligibility does not guarantee an invitation; CRS cut-offs and invitation categories change.

path_to_citizenship.value: After becoming a permanent resident, accumulate at least 1,095 days of physical presence during the five-year eligibility period, including at least 730 days as a permanent resident, and satisfy tax, language, test and prohibition requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Pre-PR temporary-resident days may count at one-half day each, capped at 365 credited days.

best_routes.notes: This is a strong independent settlement alternative for a software engineer with foreign skilled experience and a relevant degree, but it is points-tested and invitation-dependent. It is not permission to settle in Canada while simply continuing a foreign remote contract, so it is only a partial match for the requested profile.

rejected_routes.route_name: Digital-nomad remote work under visitor status

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Canada treats this as visitor status rather than an income-qualified residence program.

income_requirement_display.value: No published digital-nomad monthly threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Normal visitor admissibility and funds requirements still apply.

income_proof_months.notes: The official digital-nomad information does not prescribe a standard number of income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Work remotely for an employer outside Canada and remain outside the Canadian labour market.
Obtain visitor status through a visitor visa or eTA as applicable to nationality and travel method.
Leave or obtain another lawful status when authorized visitor status ends.

initial_validity.value: Up to 6 months at a time as a visitor, subject to the border officer's admission decision
initial_validity.notes: This is visitor status, not a digital-nomad residence permit.

extension_rules.value: A visitor may separately request an extension, but no dedicated digital-nomad renewal or settlement entitlement exists.
extension_rules.notes: Approval of any visitor extension is discretionary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Visitor status only
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not provide a work permit or a qualifying residence program.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct conversion. A digital nomad must separately qualify for Express Entry, family sponsorship, a Canadian-employer work route or another immigration program.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Finding a Canadian employer changes the factual and immigration situation and falls outside the ordinary foreign-contract profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor status does not itself provide citizenship. Some lawful temporary-resident days can later receive half-day credit only if the person independently becomes a permanent resident.
path_to_citizenship.notes: At least 730 days in the citizenship presence calculation must still be spent as a permanent resident.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a temporary visitor concession, not a residence-to-citizenship route. It fits foreign-employer remote work for short stays but fails the project's settlement requirement.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No single national income threshold; the offer and program determine wage requirements.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Route-specific wage rules apply.

income_requirement_display.value: No universal monthly threshold; Canadian job offer required for the common employer-specific permit
income_requirement_display.notes: Excluded because a local employer is required.

income_proof_months.notes: No universal rule established.

key_requirements.requirement: A Canadian job offer is required for the common employer-specific permit; LMIA or an applicable exemption may also be required.
Open work permits exist only for specified eligible circumstances and cannot simply be chosen by an ordinary foreign remote worker.

initial_validity.value: Depends on the approved work permit

extension_rules.value: Program- and permit-specific

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary worker status if approved

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Possible only through a separate qualifying immigration program; not automatic from the work permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Requires obtaining permanent residence first and later meeting citizenship requirements.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because the ordinary route requires a Canadian employer/job offer.

summary.value: The Federal Skilled Worker Program is an education-, language-, experience- and points-based Express Entry route. A Canadian employer is not mandatory, and approved applicants become permanent residents, but only candidates invited from the competitive pool can submit a PR application.
summary.notes: The applicant's software-engineering degree and foreign skilled experience are relevant, but an ECA, language results, 67-point FSW eligibility and a sufficiently competitive CRS score are still required.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence is primarily fact-based and depends on significant residential ties such as a Canadian home, spouse or dependants. A person without significant ties may be deemed resident after staying in Canada for 183 days or more in a calendar year, subject to treaty tie-breaker rules.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration visitor status and tax residence are separate questions; a stay shorter than 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if significant ties are established.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening maximum formed from the 33% top federal rate plus Newfoundland and Labrador's 21.8% top provincial rate. This is a top marginal illustration, not the applicant's effective rate; province, credits, deductions and income level materially change the result.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For self-employed persons subject to CPP outside Quebec, 11.9% applies to net business income between the CAD 3,500 exemption and CAD 74,600 ceiling. An additional 8% self-employed CPP2 rate applies to income between CAD 74,600 and CAD 85,000. Quebec has a separate plan.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: CPP is earnings-based rather than a fixed monthly payment. The 2026 maximum self-employed CPP plus CPP2 contribution is CAD 9,292.90 annually, but that maximum is not a monthly minimum and may not apply to a foreign-employee visitor.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax holiday or special inbound remote-worker regime was found. Ordinary residence, source and treaty rules apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: GST/HST registration may become relevant to a person carrying on taxable business activities in Canada; most businesses lose small-supplier status after exceeding CAD 30,000 under the published tests.

taxes.caveats: Canadian taxation depends on residential ties, days present, income source, whether the worker is an employee or independent contractor, the province or territory, treaty residence and any social-security agreement. The temporary visitor concession is not a tax exemption.

taxation_system.value: Progressive federal income tax plus progressive provincial or territorial income tax
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Fact-based significant-ties test; possible deemed residence at 183 days or more without significant ties, subject to tax-treaty rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are generally taxed on Canadian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker income-tax regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: CPP is generally 5.95% each for employee and employer, or 11.9% for self-employed income, up to the first 2026 ceiling; CPP2 adds 4% each or 8% self-employed on the second band. Quebec rules differ.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 54.8% is a maximum screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Federal brackets apply nationwide and a separate province/territory schedule is added according to residence.

tax_brackets.notes: Provincial or territorial tax applies in addition.
The relevant provincial or territorial top rate is added.

tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 Newfoundland and Labrador provincial taxable income
tax_brackets.notes: Included to show the highest simple federal-plus-provincial screening combination published on the CRA page.

taxation_system.notes: Rates exclude effective-rate calculations, deductions, credits and province-specific surtaxes or reductions. Filing-level advice is appropriate before working from Canada.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Canada's visitor-based digital-nomad concession has no special tax treatment. A short-term worker without significant Canadian ties may remain non-resident, while significant ties or the 183-day deemed-residence rule can produce Canadian residence; treaties may override domestic deemed residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary Canadian resident/non-resident rules; no digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 54.8% top federal-plus-provincial screening rate if Canadian resident; this is not an effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Significant residential ties are primary; 183 or more days can cause deemed residence where the person lacks significant ties and is not treaty-resident elsewhere.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A Canadian tax resident is generally taxable on worldwide income. A non-resident is generally taxable only on Canadian-source income, but employment location, business activity and treaty rules require individual analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No visitor-specific exemption was identified. CPP/payroll consequences depend on employee versus contractor status, pensionable employment, province and any international social-security agreement.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly tax or social-security payment for a foreign-employee visitor.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: If treated as self-employed and subject to CPP, contributions are percentage-based; 2026 maximum CPP plus CPP2 is CAD 9,292.90 annually.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Published fees include CAD 7 for an eTA, CAD 100 for an individual visitor visa and CAD 100 for a visitor-status extension; biometrics or other fees may apply.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: GST/HST registration can become mandatory for most businesses after the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded under the applicable quarterly test.
fixed_payments.notes: These amounts are not a special digital-nomad tax package.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 183 days without significant Canadian residential ties may remain non-resident, but days alone are not conclusive and source/treaty analysis is still needed.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A Canadian resident normally reports worldwide foreign-employer or foreign-client income and pays federal plus provincial/territorial tax.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A contractor carrying on business in Canada may face income tax, CPP and GST/HST registration issues; merely registering a business does not create immigration status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The immigration permission to work remotely for a foreign employer as a visitor must not be read as a tax exemption.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The selected FSW route targets permanent residence directly; it does not first issue temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Direct PR after invitation and approval. Time waiting for an invitation is unpredictable; IRCC's service standard for a complete Express Entry FSW application is six months.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: At least 1,095 credited presence days in the preceding five years are required, including at least 730 actual days as a permanent resident.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Approximate best-case period from becoming a permanent resident to completed citizenship: three years to meet presence plus the 12-month citizenship service standard. It excludes unpredictable Express Entry pool time and can be longer.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: This is IRCC's citizenship-grant service standard; individual cases can exceed it.

key_conditions.value: Obtain PR after a competitive Express Entry invitation; maintain physical presence; file Canadian taxes when required for at least three relevant years; applicants aged 18–54 must demonstrate English or French and pass the citizenship test; criminal, security and immigration prohibitions can prevent approval. Canada does not generally require renunciation of prior citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Temporary-resident presence may supply at most 365 credited days at half-day value.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A legally valid marriage has no published minimum duration before spousal PR sponsorship, but marriage does not shorten the citizenship residence requirement. Common-law sponsorship normally requires 12 consecutive months of cohabitation; conjugal-partner rules require a genuine relationship of at least 12 months.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legally valid civil marriage can support spousal permanent-residence sponsorship by an eligible Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Marriage itself does not grant status or citizenship, and spouses follow the ordinary citizenship requirements.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A marriage performed abroad must be legally recognized both where it occurred and in Canada; certain proxy or remote marriages are not recognized.

requirements_and_risks.value: The sponsor and applicant must qualify, the relationship must be genuine, and the applicant must pass applicable background, security and medical checks. IRCC uses document checks and interviews to detect relationships of convenience; false cases can be refused, lead to a five-year inadmissibility ban or criminal consequences, and the sponsor generally undertakes three years of financial support.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage can provide a PR route but no special or accelerated citizenship grant.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A person born in Canada is generally a citizen at birth. The principal narrow exception concerns children where neither parent is a citizen or permanent resident and a parent has qualifying diplomatic, foreign-government or equivalent international-organization status.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Canada ordinarily becomes a Canadian citizen even when both parents are temporary residents, visitors or otherwise foreign nationals, subject to the narrow diplomatic/official exception.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth citizenship does not confer immigration status on either parent.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Canada is ordinarily Canadian by birth. A child born abroad may also acquire citizenship through a Canadian parent under the descent rules, including the post-December 15, 2025 substantial-connection rules where applicable.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: For a Canadian parent also born abroad, a child born abroad on or after December 15, 2025 generally requires that parent to have accumulated at least 1,095 days in Canada before the child's birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Canadian-born child's citizenship gives the migrant parents no automatic visa, permanent residence or citizenship. Once an adult, the child may potentially sponsor parents if the family program is open and the child satisfies age, residence, income and undertaking rules.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Parent sponsorship is a separate, capacity-limited process and should not be treated as an immediate residence strategy.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic benefit: the migrant father does not receive Canadian immigration status or citizenship merely because his child is Canadian. A possible future sponsorship opportunity can arise only after the child is at least 18 and meets the program's other conditions.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The father's own current status and admissibility remain independently governed.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank observed on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 47 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations shown separately by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 169, comprising 112 visa-free, 47 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. These categories and rank differ from Henley methodology, which groups several no-prior-visa categories together.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High in most of Canada. English is one of the two official federal languages and is the dominant practical language in most provinces, although French is particularly important in Quebec and some Francophone communities and workplaces.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Provincial language rules and employer expectations vary.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited as a primary language for government, immigration and general professional life. Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking communities and services exist, but an applicant should expect to use English or French for mainstream work and administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical inference from Canada's official-language framework; no authoritative nationwide measure of Russian/Ukrainian service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of CAD 5,998, calculated from CAD 37.20 per hour at 40 hours/week and 52/12 weeks/month, using roughly USD 0.72 per CAD for screening. It is a standardized full-time gross estimate, not the observed average monthly take-home pay.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of CAD 5,334 monthly, derived from the 2025 median hourly wage of CAD 30.77 on the same standardized full-time basis.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate full-time USD equivalent of Alberta's CAD 15 hourly general minimum wage, the lowest listed current adult rate; this is a statutory wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the standardized CAD monthly calculation.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion based on the latest official annual median found, for 2025.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Canada has no meaningful national maximum salary, and no reliable official maximum wage was identified.

min_salary_local_currency.value: CAD 2,600/month at CAD 15/hour on a 40-hour week
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Alberta's current general rate is the lowest in the official jurisdiction table. Minimum wages vary by province/territory; the 2026 federal rate is CAD 18.15 but applies only to federally regulated employment and yields to a higher provincial rate.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Statistics Canada reported CAD 37.20 as the average hourly wage among employees in June 2026. Monthly value is standardized at 40 hours/week and is gross, not net.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Latest official annual median located was CAD 30.77 in 2025 constant dollars. Monthly value uses 40 hours/week and 52/12 weeks.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No official national maximum salary is meaningful or published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross hourly employee wage converted to a standardized full-time monthly amount; minimum field is a statutory jurisdictional floor
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: June 2026; median: 2025; minimum rates current/forthcoming table checked 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and median use different official reference periods and are not directly interchangeable. USD values are rounded screening conversions; actual exchange rates and hours worked vary.

cost_of_living_note.value: Housing costs vary sharply by city and province. Statistics Canada's June 2026 CPI showed national shelter prices up 1.5% year over year and rent up 3.5%, indicating continuing rental-cost pressure despite modest aggregate shelter inflation.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A single national cost-of-living amount would obscure large regional differences, so none is asserted.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Canada's visitor-based digital-nomad option is temporary-only. The strong classification applies solely to the separate Federal Skilled Worker permanent-residence route.
settlement_track.summary: Federal Skilled Worker is a direct permanent-residence route and therefore provides a credible citizenship track after the physical-presence and other citizenship requirements are met. It is classified only as a partial selection match because access is points-tested and invitation-dependent, not based on the applicant's continuing foreign remote contract.
settlement_track.notes: No status switch is required after FSW approval because the grant is PR. The visitor/digital-nomad concession must not be conflated with this settlement route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign-contract remote work fits only the temporary visitor concession. The settlement route can evaluate foreign software-engineering experience and requires no Canadian employer, but it is an independent skilled-migration route rather than ordinary remote-worker residence.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Canada record and current sources. The principal improvement is reclassifying Canada from false/temporary-only to partial because the Federal Skilled Worker Program is an independent, employer-free, direct-PR route expressly allowed by the prompt's partial-match rule. Canada still lacks a dedicated digital-nomad residence-to-citizenship program.

data.selection_summary: Not eligible for this foreign-contract software-engineer profile. Current official embassy materials expose only short-stay and 45–90-day long-stay visas; the long-stay form requires departure when the visa expires and does not establish a digital-nomad, remote-worker, freelance, self-employed residence, permanent-residence, or settlement route. Focused review of current visa, business-registration, labor, social-security, tax, and nationality sources found no independent qualifying residence route for ordinary foreign-client remote work.

Applicants outside the embassy's jurisdiction must verify the competent CAR mission.

summary.value: No independent degree-, qualification-, points-, or skilled-migration residence category was found in the official embassy catalogue or additional country-law searches.
summary.notes: A degree may support employment or business documentation, but no standalone residence entitlement for a software engineer was established. Null flags remain because an exhaustive current official immigration-permit catalogue was unavailable.

tax_residency_rule.value: The official tax code treats a person as fiscally resident when the person has a dwelling available in CAR, has the principal place of stay there, or has the center of vital interests there, meaning the closest economic and professional relations. CAR-source income and treaty allocations may also be taxable without residence. The code does not establish a general 183-day threshold.
tax_residency_rule.notes: This is from the DGID official edition updated in 2023 and hosted by Refworld. Filing-year changes after that edition must still be checked.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top screening rate, not a universal or expected effective rate. Article 86 applies progressive 0%–40% rates to employees, while Article 81 applies 30% to non-agricultural non-salaried business and professional profits. An ordinary foreign-contract worker's classification therefore materially changes the rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This numeric field represents the employee share of the general payroll scheme: 3% for pensions. The official CNSS page states 19% employer and 3% worker contributions, and ISSA shows the same 22% combined structure. The Social Security Code includes liberal professionals within its personal scope, while the U.S. SSA country profile describes self-employed coverage as voluntary and says a contribution is payable without publishing its rate. No current primary source inspected states the contribution percentage for an independently invoicing foreign-client professional, so 3% must not be applied to that scenario without CNSS confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universally applicable monthly fixed payment exists in the inspected code. For non-agricultural non-salaried activities, Articles 81–82 instead impose an annual minimum income tax equal to 1.85% of turnover with a minimum liability of XAF 1,850,000. Because that is annual, activity-specific, and not a monthly social payment, no USD monthly value is entered.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate, remittance-basis, or foreign-remote-income exemption was identified. Small activities may instead fall under the Impôt Global Unique based on turnover and eligibility, while ordinary non-salaried professional activity is generally subject to the specific business/professional-profit rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The 2023 official tax-code edition contains category-specific regimes but no nomad or inbound-remote-worker regime.

taxes.caveats: The tax analysis is hypothetical because CAR has no qualifying remote-worker immigration route. Under the 2023 official tax-code edition, residence can arise immediately from an available dwelling, principal stay, or center of vital interests; there is no general 183-day safe harbor. Employee-like foreign salary may fall under the 0%–40% salary schedule, whereas independently invoiced software services may be non-commercial/professional profits taxed at 30%, potentially subject to the 1.85%-of-turnover annual minimum with a XAF 1,850,000 floor. Smaller registered activities may instead fall within the turnover-based Impôt Global Unique, and patent, VAT, withholding, transfer-fee, permanent-establishment, treaty, and foreign-tax-credit consequences depend on facts and filing-year law. CNSS materials establish 3% employee and 19% employer payroll rates, but do not publish a current self-employed professional rate. Classification and immigration permission must therefore be confirmed separately with DGID, CNSS, GUFE, and immigration authorities before working or registering.

taxation_system.value: Mixed personal-income-tax treatment: employees face annual progressive rates of 0%, 8%, 15%, 28%, and 40%; non-agricultural non-salaried industrial, commercial, craft, and professional profits are generally taxed at 30%, subject to an annual minimum based on turnover. Residents are taxed through the ordinary IRPP framework, including reporting obligations for foreign assets and foreign-paid remuneration.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Available dwelling in CAR, principal place of stay, or center of vital interests/economic and professional relations; CAR-source income and treaty provisions can create liability without residence. No general 183-day test appears in the inspected official code.
taxation_system.income_scope: The IRPP applies to net global income of CAR fiscal residents; the code also taxes specified CAR-source income of nonresidents and requires residents to report relevant foreign assets and foreign-paid remuneration.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime was found. Turnover-based Impôt Global Unique rules may apply to eligible micro and small activities.
taxation_system.social_security: For payroll employment, the official CNSS page reports 3% charged to the worker for pensions and 19% charged to the employer: 4% pensions, 3% occupational risks, and 12% family/maternity benefits. The Social Security Code covers workers employed in CAR without nationality distinction and lists liberal professionals, but leaves detailed coverage and rates to implementing rules. A comparative SSA profile describes self-employed, informal-sector, and agricultural coverage as voluntary and says a self-employed contribution is payable without specifying the rate. Consequently, no percentage or fixed amount can be stated for a foreign-client self-employed software professional from the inspected current primary materials.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 40% is the top marginal employee rate. It is not the expected effective rate and is not the statutory rate for ordinary non-agricultural self-employed professional profits, which the 2023 code states as 30%.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD scale uses about XAF 560 per USD; this bracket does not describe self-employed professional profits.

taxation_system.notes: The official 2023 tax-code edition resolves the previous record's reliance on secondary PIT material and shows that the progressive schedule is specifically for employees. Filing-year amendments and taxpayer classification still require verification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated CAR digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category exists in the inspected sources. If a person nevertheless works from CAR, ordinary tax rules may apply: employee-classified remuneration can reach a 40% marginal rate, while independently invoiced non-agricultural professional profits are generally taxed at 30% and may face the turnover-based annual minimum.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated nomad category; potentially an ordinary employee taxpayer or a non-salaried professional/business taxpayer depending on the contract and factual relationship.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Employee-like income: 0%–40% progressive; independent professional profits: generally 30%, potentially subject to the annual minimum tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: An available CAR dwelling, principal stay, or center of vital interests may establish residence without waiting 183 days; CAR-source income may also be taxable independently.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The code taxes net global income of fiscal residents and requires disclosures concerning foreign assets and remuneration received from foreign debtors. No foreign-remote-worker exemption was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the 2023 official tax-code edition or current visa materials.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For a genuine employee covered by CAR payroll, CNSS publishes a 3% worker share and 19% employer share. The Social Security Code lists liberal professionals within scope, while the SSA comparative profile describes self-employed coverage as voluntary; neither the code nor current CNSS page publishes the self-employed rate. An independently invoicing foreign-client worker must therefore obtain a written classification and contribution assessment from CNSS rather than applying the employee 3% automatically.

fixed_payments.status: Potential annual non-salaried minimum income tax; no universal monthly nomad payment.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No current primary source inspected publishes a fixed or percentage CNSS contribution for an independently invoicing foreign-client professional.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Official embassy fees: EUR 300 for the 45–90-day visa, EUR 80 for 1–30 days, EUR 160 for 30–45 days, and EUR 20 extra for express handling.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: For ordinary non-agricultural non-salaried activity, the official tax code sets a minimum IRPP of 1.85% of turnover and at least XAF 1,850,000 annually. Eligible micro/small activities may instead fall under the Impôt Global Unique. Patent, VAT, registration, and transfer-related charges require activity-specific assessment.
fixed_payments.notes: The XAF 1,850,000 amount is an annual minimum tax, not a monthly fee or social contribution.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no general day-count threshold to remain below. Keeping a dwelling available, making CAR the principal stay, locating the closest economic/professional relations there, or earning CAR-source income can create liability during a shorter stay.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Employee-like remuneration may be taxed under the 0%–40% progressive schedule; independently invoiced professional profit may instead be taxed at 30% with the annual minimum. Worldwide-income reporting, deductions, withholding, and treaty relief require classification-specific advice.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: GUFE centralizes Greffe, tax, labor, and CNSS formalities, so lawful local activity may require business/RCCM and tax registration plus a CNSS assessment. The official tax code generally taxes non-agricultural non-salaried profit at 30% and imposes a minimum of 1.85% of turnover with a XAF 1,850,000 annual floor, unless the activity qualifies for another regime. CNSS's self-employed contribution rate is unpublished in the inspected current primary materials, and—critically—neither GUFE registration nor tax payment creates immigration residence or remote-work permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a hypothetical ordinary-tax analysis, not confirmation that a visitor may work. Immigration authorization, taxpayer category, treaty position, and CNSS coverage require separate written confirmation.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No independent temporary-residence route or conversion timetable was established.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The inspected official sources do not establish a general permanent-residence status or qualifying period for this route.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality framework measures habitual residence before naturalization rather than years held in an identified permanent-residence status; no PR prerequisite or PR-to-citizenship interval was established.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship Rights in Africa reports that Ordinance 84-022 repealed the 1966 amendment imposing 35 years and restored the prior five-year habitual-residence requirement. This is an eligibility period under the general discretionary naturalization law, not a confirmed timeline from the rejected 45–90-day visa or any remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No current government service standard or observed median/typical naturalization duration was published in the inspected nationality-law and Ministry of Justice materials. The previous record's one-year statement came from Article 26 as amended by Ordinance 66-64; Ordinance 84-022 repealed that amendment, so the former one-year waiting rule cannot be presented as either a current minimum or a typical processing time. The Justice Ministry page concerns issuance of a nationality certificate to someone already entitled to nationality, not naturalization processing.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization remains discretionary by decree after investigation and requires compliance with foreigner-stay law. The 1984 repeal reportedly restored five years of habitual residence rather than 35 years. The inspected current sources do not establish that visitor time qualifies, do not identify a permanent-residence prerequisite, and publish no routine language-test or processing-standard details.
key_conditions.notes: The accessible consolidated PDF incorporates now-repealed 1966 amendments, so it must be read with Ordinance 84-022. The 2023 Constitution makes nationality one and exclusive subject to statutory exceptions; current advice is needed on dual nationality and documentary practice.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The accessible code provides acquisition at civil marriage for a foreign woman marrying a Central African man, subject to possible government opposition within six months. It is gender-specific and does not establish the same automatic benefit for a migrant husband.

existing_marriage_effect.value: For a marriage celebrated abroad, the six-month government-opposition period runs from transcription into Central African civil-status registers. The code does not say that an existing untranscribed marriage automatically grants nationality.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: This automatic provision concerns a foreign wife of a Central African man. Separate secondary legal analysis indicates a foreign husband may use a shortened naturalization period, but current filing rules were not established sufficiently to assign a numeric value here.

requirements_and_risks.value: Civil marriage and, for an overseas marriage, transcription are required under the cited provisions. Government may oppose acquisition within six months, and annulment prevents acquisition. Genuine-marriage and document checks should be expected; fraud can cause refusal, withdrawal, or other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No current marriage-based permanent-residence procedure was located. The acceleration flag reflects the code's gender-specific benefit, not equal automatic availability to every spouse.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in CAR to two foreign parents is not automatically Central African at birth. The child may claim nationality by declaration while a minor after five years' CAR residence; when under 16, an acting foreign representative must also have five years' residence. Government may oppose within six months.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship at birth. A CAR-born minor of two foreign parents may later claim nationality by declaration after at least five years' CAR residence, subject to age/representation rules and possible government opposition.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parental permanent residence is not stated as sufficient by itself.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Central African parent can generally acquire Central African nationality by descent, subject to civil-registration and proof-of-filiation requirements.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Current constitutional and registration practice should be confirmed before filing.

parent_benefit_summary.value: The inspected nationality law does not automatically grant a migrant parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship merely because the child is a citizen. Any family-based residence benefit requires separate immigration confirmation.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No current foreign-parent residence procedure was located.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic benefit was established. If the mother is a Central African citizen, the child can generally be Central African by descent, but the migrant father does not thereby become a citizen or confirmed resident.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The automatic marriage provision found applies to a foreign woman marrying a Central African man, not the reverse.

average_citizen_salary.notes: The XAF 35,000 figure is supported by WageIndicator and the SSA country profile. World Bank B-READY confirms that a private-sector minimum wage exists but does not supply a usable national average or median. WageIndicator's XAF 275,177 living-wage benchmark for April 2024 is not an average salary and is therefore excluded from salary fields.

cost_of_living_note.value: No comprehensive current national cost-of-living basket was found. WageIndicator's April 2024 living-wage benchmark is XAF 275,177 monthly, substantially above the XAF 35,000 statutory minimum, but it is not an average household budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Coverage and household assumptions should be reviewed before using the benchmark for personal budgeting.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: CAR has no identified digital-nomad status. The only independently filed long-stay option found is a general 45–90-day visa whose form requires departure at expiry; no inspected immigration or nationality source says it grants residence, can be converted to qualifying residence, or counts toward the five-year habitual-residence period restored by the 1984 nationality amendment.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route was found. General visas do not establish residence or settlement rights; although the nationality framework appears to allow discretionary naturalization after five years of qualifying habitual residence, there is no confirmed immigration status through which this applicant can independently begin that residence period.
settlement_track.notes: The prior selection conclusion remains correct. The focused audit corrected the nationality timeline: the 1966 35-year amendment was repealed in 1984, reportedly restoring five years. That correction does not make the 45–90-day visa a settlement route, and no permanent-residence or visitor-to-self-employment conversion was verified.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, foreign-client freelancer, self-employed residence, or visitor-to-self-employment legalization route was found. The visa form's references to business or work and GUFE's business-registration services do not themselves authorize remote work, legalize immigration status, or establish qualifying residence.

data.notes: Thirty distinct canonical sources are retained, including ten URLs not present in the previous source set. More than fifteen directly relevant URLs were inspected during this pass. Current official embassy, tax, CNSS, justice, GUFE, labor, social-security, and nationality materials resolved the flagged explanations and corrected the previous 35-year naturalization claim. Confidence remains medium because CAR still lacks an accessible consolidated official immigration/residence permit catalogue, a published self-employed CNSS rate, a citizenship processing-time statistic, and reliable national average or median wage data.

data.selection_summary: Chad does not currently offer a digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, independent-professional, or independently accessible freelance residence route. Its eVisa is an entry document, while the documented work-residence process requires local-employer involvement, ONAPE employment authorization, a locally compliant contract, and a residence card. Registering an individual enterprise does not independently grant immigration permission.

visa_application.title: e-Visa Tchad
visa_application.notes: Official direct application portal for Chad entry visas. Since 11 May 2026, new visa applications must be submitted through it. It does not offer a dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence category.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary Chad eVisa, including short-stay categories

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The portal may request proof of funds or income but publishes no fixed remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed minimum in XAF is published for an ordinary visitor eVisa.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed digital-nomad or remote-work income threshold is published
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Proof of funds or income may be requested without a stated minimum
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an ordinary entry-visa process, not a remote-worker program.

income_proof_months.notes: The portal mentions bank statements or other proof of income but states no required number of months.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through the official eVisa portal at least seven days and no more than 90 days before intended entry.

The personalized document list may include a valid passport, travel ticket, accommodation or invitation evidence, proof of funds or income, profession evidence, and purpose-specific host or company documents.
Carry proof of yellow-fever vaccination for inspection on arrival.
An ordinary visitor or short-stay eVisa does not confer residence or documented permission for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

initial_validity.value: Current law provides transit visas, short-stay visas not exceeding one or three months, and a separate long-stay category not exceeding one year.
initial_validity.notes: The ordinary short-stay categories are visitor visas, not qualifying temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: If an eVisa expires during the stay, the portal directs the holder to the Direction de l’Emigration et de l’Immigration to request an extension.
extension_rules.notes: An extension is not evidence of a remote-worker settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No conversion from an ordinary visitor eVisa to independent remote-worker residence is published.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No permanent-residence transition from an ordinary eVisa is published.

path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization law exists, but the reviewed sources do not establish an ordinary eVisa as qualifying residence.

rejected_routes.notes: The eVisa can be filed independently but is only an entry visa. It neither legalizes ordinary foreign-contract remote work nor supplies a confirmed settlement status.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employer-sponsored long-stay visa, employment authorization, work permit and residence card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration salary threshold is published; eligibility instead depends on an authorized local employment relationship.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed immigration income threshold in XAF is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; authorized local employment is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No separate immigration salary formula is published. ONAPE validates the local employment contract, which must state remuneration; the general wage floor reported elsewhere is not identified by current immigration or ONAPE material as an eligibility threshold.
income_requirement_display.notes: The qualifying fact is an authorized local employment relationship, not proof that salary exceeds a published visa threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: The employer must file the ONAPE employment-authorization request before concluding the foreign worker's labor contract.
The foreign worker needs employment authorization, a work permit, residence card, long-stay visa, return visa, and an ONAPE-stamped fixed-term employment contract.

The long-stay process requires online pre-enrolment, advance payment of visa and residence-card fees, physical immigration enrolment after arrival, sufficient passport validity, and employment authorization.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year
initial_validity.notes: The linked work and immigration documents generally cannot exceed one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is possible, normally in further periods not exceeding one year while employment requirements remain satisfied.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains tied to the authorized local employment structure.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A compliant locally employed expatriate obtains a residence card through the linked employer-sponsored work and long-stay process.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is temporary employer-sponsored residence, not independent remote-worker residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No published transition from this annual employer-sponsored package to a separately defined permanent-residence status was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: A holder who maintains lawful residence may in principle seek general naturalization after at least 15 years of residence in Chad; the law does not make a separately defined permanent-residence grant a prerequisite. Naturalization is discretionary, requires a complete residence and integration file, and no source confirms that every annual work-residence period will be accepted without interruption.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This general-law possibility does not make the route suitable for the selected profile because obtaining and maintaining the underlying residence requires a local employer.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the documented residence-oriented work route, but it fails the selection criteria because a local employer, local labor contract, ONAPE authorization, and employer filing are required.

summary.value: The current framework contains a duration-based long-stay visa, but the reviewed decree and portal do not identify a distinct independent degree-based, skilled-migration, or qualification-only residence route.
summary.notes: Focused searches did not locate official application rules for an independent qualification-based route. The generic long-stay category is insufficient to infer one.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is treated as tax-resident when they have a dwelling available in Chad as owner, usufructuary, or tenant for at least one year; live in Chad for more than 183 days; or have their centre of economic interests in Chad.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The published tests are alternatives; presence below 184 days does not by itself prevent residence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal rate for annual work income, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: PwC states that a registered self-employed person bears both the 16.5% employer and 3.5% employee portions, each calculated on gross monthly income capped at XAF 500,000. An ordinary employee bears 3.5%, with the employer paying 16.5%.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal fixed monthly freelancer payment. Contributions are percentage-based and capped; enterprise formation is a one-time cost, and current visa/card amounts must be verified in the personalized application.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, expatriate tax holiday, remittance-basis, or non-dom regime was located. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The absence of a dedicated immigration route also means there is no route-specific nomad tax treatment.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on residence, where services are physically performed, employee versus self-employed classification, business registration, VAT status, and any applicable CEMAC treaty. PwC's detailed individual guidance was last reviewed in August 2024; filing treatment should be confirmed against the 2026 Finance Law and current DGI practice. No general unilateral foreign-tax-credit provision was identified.

taxation_system.value: Progressive taxation of work income, with residents generally taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on income from activities in Chad.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Dwelling available for at least one year, presence over 183 days, or centre of economic interests in Chad.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; income from activities in Chad for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime was located.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee share 3.5% and employer share 16.5%, each on monthly gross pay capped at XAF 500,000. A self-employed person reportedly bears both portions, for a combined maximum of XAF 100,000 monthly.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal screening rate. The brackets are annual and are not effective tax rates. The source appears to contain typographical commas in two ranges; the contiguous ranges below follow the surrounding bracket structure.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD value uses about XAF 575 per USD for screening only.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual work income; USD amount represents the upper threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual work income above the stated threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band; USD figure is the approximate lower boundary.

taxation_system.notes: The residence tests and bracket structure are described by a reputable country-tax source. The 2026 Finance Law changed several direct and indirect tax rules, so filing-level confirmation remains advisable.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No route-specific regime applies because Chad has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence status. Someone nevertheless living and working from Chad may fall within the ordinary resident or non-resident tax system.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; ordinary employment or self-employment taxation would require assessment.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 0%–30%; 30% is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Dwelling available for at least one year, presence exceeding 183 days, or centre of economic interests in Chad.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident is generally taxable on worldwide income. A non-resident is taxable on income from activities in Chad; services physically performed there require source and treaty analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None located.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employees generally contribute 3.5% and employers 16.5% on monthly gross salary capped at XAF 500,000. PwC states that a self-employed person bears both portions.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly remote-worker tax was established.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based rather than fixed: up to XAF 17,500 employee plus XAF 82,500 employer monthly; a registered self-employed person may bear the combined XAF 100,000 maximum.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The May 2026 official notice confirms new visa and residence-card tariffs, but dependable amounts were not exposed in the accessible public text; verify them in the personalized eVisa application before payment.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific fixed levy exists in the sources checked. ANIE’s service catalogue lists a one-time XAF 36,000 tariff for forming an individual enterprise: XAF 15,000 Treasury, XAF 18,000 service, and XAF 3,000 stamp. The catalogue is not identified as a 2026 tariff and should be reconfirmed. Ordinary business-licence tax is annual at 0.35% of turnover from year N-2, with a first-year exemption for a new business; registration duties on covered deeds range from 0.25% to 15%; standard VAT is 18%. The 2026 Finance Law expanded VAT to digital services and introduced reverse-charge treatment for supplies from non-VAT-registered suppliers.
fixed_payments.notes: These are ordinary business or transaction rules, not digital-nomad charges. Applicability depends on lawful immigration status, business form, turnover, contract location, and registration.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying fewer than 184 days does not automatically prevent residence because the dwelling and centre-of-economic-interests tests are alternatives. Non-residents may still owe Chad tax on income from activities performed there.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident is generally exposed to progressive tax on worldwide work income up to 30%, subject to deductions and treaty analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: ANIE provides an online one-stop company-formation process, and its catalogue identifies the individual-enterprise form and associated RCCM/tax formalities. Registration does not grant a foreign national permission to reside or work. If immigration permission were independently secured and an individual enterprise validly registered, category-specific income tax, annual business-licence tax after the first-year exemption, potentially combined self-employed social-security contributions, and VAT or reverse-charge rules could apply; exact 2026 treatment requires DGI/CNPS confirmation.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: These are ordinary tax and registration rules, not proof that immigration law permits foreign-contract remote work.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent route exists. Employer-sponsored applicants can obtain an annual residence card, but that route is excluded.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No current official rule establishing a standard permanent-residence transition was located.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality framework uses a general residence period, not a verified number of years following a separately defined permanent-residence grant.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization screening period only. It is not a timeline from the rejected eVisa, and treatment of particular residence statuses must be confirmed.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No observed current processing-time benchmark is published. The implementing decree requires a decree within one year after a complete application is filed; otherwise the application is implicitly rejected. That legal decision period is not evidence of a typical approval time.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization is discretionary and requires age 18, residence in Chad for at least 15 years and residence at filing, good conduct and morals, and freedom from a disqualifying unrehabilitated ordinary-crime sentence. The investigation examines loyalty, assimilation to Chadian customs, knowledge of French or a language used in Chad, and health. The file includes identity and civil-status records, criminal record, residence evidence and residence card, an employer certificate stating monthly salary where applicable, a Treasury tax certificate, and relevant family, education, or service documents. No modern standardized language-test level, absence-day limit, or automatic entitlement is published.
key_conditions.notes: The 15-year period is a general naturalization condition, not confirmation that visitor or eVisa time counts. Treatment of interruptions and each residence-card category requires filing-level confirmation.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The code mechanism permits a foreign spouse to request Chadian nationality at the celebration of a marriage in Chad; no prior marriage-duration requirement is stated. The government retains a one-year opposition period under the implementing decree.

existing_marriage_effect.value: The ordinary marriage route requires the foreign spouse to make the nationality request expressly at the celebration of a marriage in Chad; it is not an automatic consequence of marriage. A marriage already celebrated after the code took effect therefore has no published retroactive declaration mechanism. Article 41 created a one-year transitional option only for people already married to Chadian citizens before publication of the 1962 code, and the implementing decree states that this period ran from its 1963 publication, so the transitional window has long expired.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An already-married spouse may explore ordinary naturalization or ask whether authorities recognize another current procedure, but the reviewed legislation does not establish a later marriage-based declaration.

requirements_and_risks.value: The declaration is personal, normally filed in triplicate, and requires identity and civil-status documents, criminal record, photographs, and a certificate from the spouse's country confirming that its law permits acquisition of another nationality through marriage. Authorities investigate morality, loyalty, assimilation, language, and health, and may oppose acquisition during the statutory period. Genuine documents and a legally valid marriage are essential; no current public guidance describes interviews, cohabitation evidence, sham-marriage enforcement, or typical processing time.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The governing provisions are old, and historical translations were not consistently gender-neutral. Current administrative practice should be verified directly.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 12 of the 1962 code treats children born in Chad to foreign parents as Chadian. The code also provides an option mechanism at majority, and birth registration remains important.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Chad to two foreign parents is Chadian under the territorial-birth provision. At majority, the code permits the child to decline Chadian nationality in favor of a parent's nationality where legally available.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Timely civil registration and documentary proof are essential.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Chad with a Chadian parent qualifies through descent as well as territorial birth. Several descent situations are also recognized for children born abroad, subject to filiation and registration evidence.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: For a birth abroad, the precise rule depends on filiation, marital status, and the applicable version of the code.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A child's Chadian citizenship does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence, or citizenship on either foreign parent. No current automatic family-residence route based solely on having a Chadian child was located.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any family-unity or dependency application requires direct confirmation from immigration authorities.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically become Chadian or obtain permanent residence because his child is Chadian. The relationship may be relevant in a discretionary family or nationality matter, but no automatic benefit or accelerated timetable was established.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not treat birth of a citizen child as an immigration strategy without case-specific legal confirmation.

rank.notes: Live Passport Power Rank checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Visa-required count; eVisa destinations are separate.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 28 visa-on-arrival and 3 eTA destinations. The index reports a mobility score of 57.

passport.notes: Passport Index separates visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, eVisa, and visa-required access. Recheck before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low outside international organizations, larger businesses, and some professional circles. French and Arabic are the official administrative languages, so English alone is unlikely to suffice for immigration, taxation, local services, or most daily administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Practical inference from the official-language and administrative framework; no reliable nationwide English-proficiency score was located.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Very low. Russian and Ukrainian have no official or documented broad administrative role, so French or Arabic assistance would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Inference from the official-language framework; no countrywide usage statistics were located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ILOSTAT-derived average monthly employee earnings for 2022. This is employee pay, not income per capita or an immigration threshold.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ILOSTAT's current catalogue contains median-monthly-earnings indicators, but the reviewed Chad profile and data pages did not expose a national Chad observation convertible to USD. A median cannot be inferred from the available average.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the reported XAF 60,000 monthly minimum at about XAF 575 per USD. This is a secondary-source minimum-wage figure, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: ILOSTAT-derived 2022 average monthly earnings of employees.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national Chad median could be extracted from the current ILO country profile, data catalogue, or wage catalogue. ILO's Chad establishment-survey metadata describes a formal-sector survey limited geographically to N’Djamena, Sarh, and Moundou and publishes no current national median amount; the average cannot be used to manufacture a median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The checked ILO sources publish earnings indicators, not an economy-wide upper salary bound. A national maximum is open-ended and was not published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Reported by a current secondary wage dataset as the minimum wage. Exact legal coverage should be checked by sector.

average_salary_local_currency.value: Approximately XAF 118,450 per month at the research-date screening exchange rate
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Converted from USD 206 using approximately XAF 575 per USD. The underlying wage observation is from 2022.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The ILO catalogue offers a median-monthly-earnings table in principle, but no national Chad observation in XAF was available from the reviewed country/profile pages or Chad survey metadata. The field remains null instead of repeating an unsupported secondary estimate.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national upper wage bound in XAF is published in the checked ILO material. The highest individual salary is neither a representative wage statistic nor a fixed legal ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average: gross monthly earnings of employees, all sectors, ILOSTAT-derived, 2022. Minimum: reported monthly minimum wage from a secondary wage dataset.
average_citizen_salary.period: Average observation year 2022; minimum source updated in 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are employee-wage indicators, not software-engineer salaries or immigration thresholds. The average is ILOSTAT-derived; the XAF 60,000 minimum has weaker source quality. Current ILO catalogues did not supply usable national median or maximum observations, and the legacy establishment-survey metadata is limited to formal establishments in three cities.

cost_of_living_note.value: The Anker Research Institute's 2025 rural-Chad update estimated a gross living wage of XAF 85,680, about USD 150 at its June 2025 rate, comprising XAF 80,999 net plus modeled social contributions and income tax. This is a rural living-wage benchmark, not a nationwide cost-of-living average.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Urban N’Djamena and expatriate costs can differ materially.
