settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: An ordinary eVisa, its extension, or business registration is not independent remote-worker residence and has no confirmed settlement effect.
settlement_track.summary: Chad's documented residence-oriented work process requires a local employer, ONAPE employment authorization, a locally compliant contract, a long-stay visa, and a residence card. Individual-enterprise registration supplies commercial and tax formalities only, not a qualifying immigration route.
settlement_track.notes: General naturalization may be possible after long lawful residence, but no independent remote-worker status was found from which this applicant could build that residence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No current status expressly authorizes an ordinary foreign-client or foreign-employer remote worker to reside and work independently. Business registration does not substitute for immigration permission.

data.notes: The focused unresolved-field audit inspected current immigration, tax, business-registration, nationality, and labour-statistics material, including eight directly relevant URLs outside the previous source set. It confirmed a general-law naturalization possibility after long lawful residence and clarified individual-enterprise registration and tax costs, but neither changes the negative route outcome. Null median/max wage values and route-specific thresholds are retained with precise explanations because the checked sources do not publish them.

data.selection_summary: Chile is not a match for an ordinary foreign-contract remote software engineer. SERMIG’s current residence list contains no digital-nomad or foreign-client remote-work category. The closest self-employed permit requires a pre-arranged contract for more than 90 days with a Chilean citizen or permanent resident; passive-income and investor permits require materially different profiles. A visitor generally cannot enter and then convert to ordinary residence from inside Chile.

visa_application.title: Portal de Trámites Digitales del Servicio Nacional de Migraciones
visa_application.notes: Official filing portal for Chilean residence applications. It is usable only after selecting and meeting a listed residence subcategory; no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-employer remote-work subcategory was found.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for lawful remunerated activities — own-account professional services

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: SERMIG publishes no fixed monthly-income threshold for this category; eligibility instead depends on a qualifying Chile-linked contract and the counterparty’s solvency.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed CLP threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold; a pre-entry Chile-linked professional-services contract lasting more than 90 days is required.
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Contract and solvency evidence, not a published income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign-client or foreign-employer contract alone does not satisfy the published own-account rule.

income_proof_months.notes: SERMIG requests the contract, counterparty tax file or evidence of sufficient solvency, rather than a stated number of bank-statement months.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply from outside Chile through the SERMIG digital portal.
Before entry, conclude a civil or commercial contract with a Chilean citizen or a foreigner holding permanent residence.
The contract must cover intangible or specialized professional services for more than 90 consecutive days.
Provide passport, recent photograph, criminal-record certificate where applicable, the services contract and counterparty solvency/tax documentation.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The official remunerated-activities page states up to two years for the category.

extension_rules.value: Successive extensions of up to 2 years are possible while lawful remunerated activity continues.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal requires proof that the qualifying activity is continuing.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary-residence application from abroad, but only after securing the required Chile-linked contract.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The category can generally support an application for permanent residence after qualifying temporary residence, normally after at least 24 months and subject to absences, income stability, compliance and the subcategory remaining eligible.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This path applies only if the applicant first qualifies for the Chile-linked services permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: A qualifying resident may generally seek naturalization after five years of Chilean residence counted from the temporary-residence electronic stamp that led to permanent residence, while holding valid permanent residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the route’s incompatibility with a solely foreign-client contract.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the own-account option has a mandatory Chilean/permanent-resident counterparty. Independent filing and absence of a formal employer do not make it a foreign-remote-work route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for retirees and rentistas

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed USD amount is published; resources must cover basic needs under Ministry of Social Development indicators.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed CLP threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Regular passive income from real estate or financial assets sufficient for basic needs; active salary or freelance income is not the published basis.
income_requirement_display.notes: The applicant’s foreign software-engineering compensation is active income, not rentista income.

income_proof_months.notes: SERMIG specifies proof of asset ownership and resulting regular income but not a fixed number of months.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply from outside Chile.
Show ownership of real estate or financial assets and regular income directly derived from those assets.
Income must be sufficient for basic needs during the stay.
Provide passport, photograph, criminal-record certificate and properly apostilled or legalized foreign documents.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to 2 years under temporary-residence rules

extension_rules.value: Renewable while rentista status and sufficient resources continue.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary-residence application from abroad for qualifying passive-income applicants.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential application after qualifying temporary residence, normally after at least 24 months, subject to the definitive-residence assessment.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current applicant does not establish the required passive-income basis.

path_to_citizenship.value: General five-year residence rule applies only after obtaining qualifying residence and permanent residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this is a passive-asset-income route, not a route based on active foreign employment or freelance work.

rejected_routes.route_name: Investor and related personnel temporary residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is an investment route, not a monthly-income route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The principal threshold is denominated in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: At least USD 500,000 of qualifying productive investment for the covered foreign-company representative or senior manager category.
income_requirement_display.notes: Related managers and specialists must instead have the specified connection to an established Chilean company controlled by a qualifying foreign investor.

income_proof_months.notes: Investment and corporate evidence replaces monthly income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying foreign investment of at least USD 500,000 intended for production of goods or services, or covered senior/specialist personnel relationship.
InvestChile sponsorship letter and detailed investment documentation.
Passport, photograph and criminal-record certificate.
Apply from abroad.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to 2 years under temporary-residence rules

extension_rules.value: Extension requires evidence of progress implementing the investment, corporate tax records, municipal-license payment where applicable and continuing contractual/income evidence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence for a qualifying investor or covered related personnel.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially available after qualifying temporary residence under the definitive-residence rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not assessed as a suitable route because the applicant is not an investor.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization framework may apply after five years of qualifying residence and acquisition of permanent residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial productive investment or a covered role in an investor-controlled Chilean business.

summary.value: Chile has temporary residence for students admitted to state-recognized educational institutions. It does not grant permanent residence directly and is not a degree-recognition or independent skilled-migration route for someone continuing ordinary foreign remote work.
summary.notes: Enrollment, rather than the applicant’s existing software-engineering degree, is the qualifying basis.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence generally arises after more than 183 days in Chile within any rolling 12-month period; Chilean tax domicile may arise earlier from facts showing an intention to remain.
tax_residency_rule.notes: SII Circular 63 illustrates residence being acquired on day 184. Domicile is a separate facts-and-intent test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate of the progressive Global Complementary Tax for tax year 2026, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single defensible aggregate rate applies. Chilean honorarium workers can owe AFP pension, 7% health, work-accident, SANNA and SIS contributions; SIS is 1.62% from April 2026, while the AFP component and applicable base depend on affiliation and circumstances.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer payment was established. Contributions are income-based, and immigration fees are transaction fees rather than monthly charges.

special_tax_regimes.value: A foreign individual who acquires Chilean residence or domicile is generally taxed only on Chile-source income for the first three years counted from entry; afterward, worldwide income is generally included. The three-year period may be extended in qualified cases.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is a general inbound-foreigner rule, not a digital-nomad regime. Services physically performed in Chile require source analysis even when the payer is foreign.

taxes.caveats: Chile has no dedicated digital-nomad tax treatment. Liability depends on tax residence and domicile, where services are physically performed, whether income is employment or independent professional income, treaty relief, deductions and social-security affiliation. Obtain Chilean tax advice before treating foreign-paid remote income as foreign-source.

taxation_system.value: Progressive Global Complementary Tax, with a temporary source-limited rule for newly resident or domiciled foreign individuals.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any rolling 12-month period; domicile can arise separately based on intention and circumstances.
taxation_system.income_scope: Generally Chile-source income during the first three years from entry for a foreign individual acquiring residence or domicile, then worldwide income; source characterization of remote services must be reviewed.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Three-year Chile-source-only inbound-foreigner rule, potentially extendable in qualified cases; no digital-nomad-specific regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Honorarium workers within the Chilean system may be required to contribute for AFP pension, health, work accidents, SANNA and SIS. Official guidance states 7% health and 1.62% SIS from April 2026, but does not support one universal total percentage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 40% is the top marginal rate. Tax-year 2026 brackets concern income earned in 2025; current-period liabilities use the applicable UTM/UTA values and deductions.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to CLP 11,265,804
tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses CLP 913.20 per USD, the Central Bank observed rate for 2026-08-14.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal bracket; USD value is approximate upper threshold
Marginal bracket; USD value is approximate upper threshold
Marginal bracket; USD value is approximate upper threshold
Marginal bracket; USD value is approximate upper threshold
Marginal bracket; USD value is approximate upper threshold
Marginal bracket; USD value is approximate upper threshold
Top marginal bracket; USD value approximates lower threshold

taxation_system.notes: Rates are well supported by SII. Exact taxation and total contributions for a foreign-paid remote worker remain fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not directly applicable because Chile has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. A person who independently acquires another Chilean status may face Global Complementary Tax up to 40%, subject to source, residence, domicile and the three-year inbound rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–40% progressive; 40% is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally day 184 within a rolling 12-month period; domicile can arise earlier on the facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign individuals acquiring residence or domicile generally pay Chilean tax only on Chile-source income for their first three years from entry, then on worldwide income. Whether remote services performed from Chile are Chile-source requires professional analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No nomad regime. The general three-year source-limited inbound-foreigner rule may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If registered as a Chilean honorarium worker, pension, 7% health and additional insurance contributions can apply. Exact treatment of a foreign employment relationship and treaty/social-security coordination requires review.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Income-based rather than a single fixed monthly charge; total varies by AFP and circumstances.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Temporary-residence fees vary by nationality. As of 2026-07-30, permanent residence costs CLP 142,726 generally and naturalization CLP 39,742 generally; reduced or exempt family rates apply.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No digital-nomad levy found. Business, municipal, VAT or withholding obligations depend on actual Chilean registration and activity.
fixed_payments.notes: Immigration fees are transaction charges and should not be presented as recurring monthly taxes.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 184 days does not itself authorize work or guarantee zero Chilean tax; Chile-source and domicile rules must still be assessed.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Potentially subject to progressive Chilean personal tax. The first-three-year foreigner rule may limit scope to Chile-source income, but remote services performed in Chile need source analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Chilean honorarium workers may owe Global Complementary Tax plus mandatory pension, health and insurance contributions. Local-client residence eligibility remains separate from tax registration.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax framework is current and official; application to a hypothetical worker without a qualifying immigration route is necessarily scenario-dependent.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route exists for the stated ordinary foreign-contract profile, so a meaningful time-to-residence value cannot be assigned.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General minimum is 24 months for eligible temporary residents with no more than two months of absence. Longer absences can raise the requirement to 30, 36 or 48 months; this does not create eligibility for the current profile.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Approximate inference where permanent residence is obtained after two years and naturalization eligibility arises after five total years counted from the qualifying temporary-residence stamp.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General eligibility threshold from the qualifying temporary-residence stamp; applicant must hold valid permanent residence. Processing follows the eligibility period.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: SERMIG states that naturalization takes about three years on average.

key_conditions.value: A qualifying temporary-residence subcategory, physical residence with controlled absences, eligible permanent residence, livelihood and compliance evidence, valid permanent residence at naturalization, clean-enough criminal history and satisfaction of a discretionary nationalization review. Chile does not publish a general language-test requirement on the cited SERMIG page.
key_conditions.notes: These conditions describe the general settlement framework, not a path available through foreign-contract remote work alone.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Qualified naturalization requires valid permanent residence and two years of continuous Chilean residence; a spouse must also have been married to the Chilean citizen for at least two years with the marriage registered in Chile.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Chilean can support family-reunification temporary residence and, once the marriage-duration, continuous-residence and permanent-residence conditions are met, qualified naturalization after two years rather than the ordinary five.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not grant automatic permanent residence or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The relationship must be legally effective and documented. For qualified naturalization, the marriage must be registered in Chile and the spouses must comply with marital cohabitation duties during the relevant period. Criminal convictions and adverse background information can bar or undermine naturalization; false or sham relationships risk refusal and other sanctions.
requirements_and_risks.notes: SERMIG retains an adjudicative role even when minimum periods are met.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Chile’s Constitution grants nationality to persons born in Chile, with narrow exceptions for children of foreigners serving their government and children of transient foreigners; those excepted children may opt for Chilean nationality. Under the prompt’s classification rule, this broad jus soli system is treated as unconditional despite narrow exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Chile generally becomes Chilean even when both parents are migrants, unless the narrow foreign-government-service or transient-foreigner exception applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The constitutional exception and administrative classification of a parent as transient should be checked in an individual case.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Chile is ordinarily Chilean by birth; a child born abroad to a Chilean parent can also acquire Chilean nationality subject to the constitutional ancestry rule.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A migrant parent of a Chilean child can apply for family-reunification temporary residence from inside or outside Chile, may work under that permit, and may potentially use the two-year qualified-naturalization rule after obtaining permanent residence. The child’s citizenship does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The family link must be documented and maintained.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Chilean child may qualify independently for family-reunification temporary residence as the child’s parent. This can lead through eligible residence to permanent residence and potentially qualified naturalization, but neither status nor citizenship is automatic.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage, genuine family relationship, residence, compliance and later permanent-residence requirements remain relevant.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 44 visa-on-arrival and 11 eTA destinations shown by Passport Index. The index separately lists eVisa and other electronic-entry categories, so this is not the full mobility score.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 159 and world reach of 80%. Counts and ranks can change as entry rules change.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in Santiago, Valparaíso and international/IT settings, but Spanish remains important for government, housing, health care and everyday life. EF EPI 2025 ranks Chile 54th of 123 with medium proficiency; its IT-function score is stronger than the national result.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF data are based on voluntary test participants and are an indicator rather than a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official language, and no reliable national evidence of broad service availability in either language was found; Spanish should be assumed necessary outside community-specific support.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Kept qualitative because focused searches did not establish a reliable nationwide proficiency or service-availability measure.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of CLP 962,945 at CLP 913.20 per USD on 2026-08-14.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of CLP 680,000 at CLP 913.20 per USD on 2026-08-14.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory minimum wage, not an observed distribution minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of official 2025 mean net monthly labour income.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of official 2025 median net monthly labour income.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: INE publishes distribution shares and subgroup averages, not a meaningful national maximum salary; no maximum was inferred.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum for workers over 18 and up to age 65.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2025 mean net monthly labour income of employed persons.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2025 median net monthly labour income of employed persons.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Net monthly labour income for employed persons; minimum field is the statutory gross minimum-income floor
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 income survey, published 2026-07-14; minimum wage effective 2026-05-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: INE explicitly defines its mean as net income after pension and health deductions. USD conversions use the latest available observed exchange rate before the 2026-08-15 research date and are rounded.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official benchmark: average monthly household consumption spending was CLP 564,680 per person in urban regional capitals in 2021–2022, excluding imputed rent. This is a historical resident-household benchmark, not a current expat budget; INE’s July 2026 CPI rose 0.1% month on month, while the Ministry of Social Development separately updates renter/non-renter poverty thresholds monthly.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The prior null is resolved with official evidence. The spending estimate covers urban regional capitals and is not a 2026 single-person budget, an expat budget, or an immigration income threshold.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Chile has no confirmed digital-nomad status. Visitor stay, tax registration or remote work alone does not establish a residence-to-citizenship track.
settlement_track.summary: No qualifying route exists for the stated foreign-contract profile. Settlement becomes possible only after independently qualifying for a different temporary-residence basis, such as a Chile-linked services contract, genuine passive income, investment or family reunification.
settlement_track.notes: The general Chilean residence system can culminate in permanent residence and naturalization, but that does not make foreign-client remote work an eligible entry category.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The exhaustive current SERMIG subcategory list contains no digital-nomad or foreign-employer remote-work residence status, and the closest own-account route requires a Chilean citizen or permanent-resident client.

data.notes: Focused unexplained-null audit completed against the previous Chile record. At least 16 directly relevant pages were inspected, including six official URLs outside the previous source set; 26 distinct canonical sources are retained. The negative selection conclusion remains correct. The prior cost-of-living null is now filled with an official urban-household expenditure benchmark and current price context; remaining nulls are explained where no fixed official threshold, aggregate contribution rate, maximum wage or profile-specific route timeline can be established.

data.selection_summary: China is not eligible for this selector. Current official visa, residence, employment, and entrepreneurship materials do not provide a digital-nomad, ordinary foreign-client remote-worker, or generally available self-employed residence route. Visitor/business status is not a work or residence basis; qualifying routes instead require Chinese employment, study, family, genuine local innovation/entrepreneurship, talent, or investment.

visa_application.title: China Online VISA Application
visa_application.notes: This is the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' current general online visa portal. Applicants select their filing location and may be redirected to the responsible Chinese Visa Application Service Center. It does not offer a digital-nomad or remote-worker visa category.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor, business/exchange, or visa-free short stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists because this is not a remote-work residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker financial threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; short-stay status only
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial evidence may still be requested for an ordinary visa, but it does not establish eligibility to reside and work remotely in China.

income_proof_months.notes: No standardized number of remote-work income-proof months applies.

key_requirements.requirement: The visa or exemption must be used for its authorized short-stay purpose, such as tourism, business, family visit, exchange, or transit.
Extensions require purpose-specific evidence. F and M applicants generally need an inviting or receiving entity or individual in China.
Eligible nationals may use the current unilateral exemption for stays of up to 30 days for listed purposes; it is not a residence permit.

initial_validity.value: Nationality and visa-category dependent; the current unilateral exemption permits up to 30 days for eligible ordinary-passport holders.
initial_validity.notes: Other visas have category- and decision-specific validity and permitted-stay periods.

extension_rules.value: Apply to the competent exit-entry authority before expiry with evidence supporting the authorized purpose. Accumulated visa extensions generally cannot exceed the original duration of stay.
extension_rules.notes: An extension does not convert tourism or ordinary business travel into a remote-worker residence route.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No transition from visitor/business status to residence based solely on a foreign remote contract is provided. The employment rules' exceptional in-country change requires an employment license secured by an employer.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official permanent-residence categories do not include ordinary foreign-client remote work.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Short-stay status supplies no confirmed naturalization path.

rejected_routes.notes: Potentially useful for a visit, but it is neither authorization for ordinary remote employment nor a settlement route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Chinese employer-sponsored work and work-type residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No single national remote-worker threshold applies. Work-permit criteria and any salary requirements depend on the Chinese position, locality, and applicant category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The national employment rules require pay not below the applicable local minimum wage, but China has no universal national wage amount for all sponsored work permits.

income_requirement_display.value: No universal threshold; Chinese job and employer sponsorship required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least the applicable local minimum wage; additional work-permit criteria are category- and locality-specific
income_requirement_display.notes: This route is rejected because a Chinese employment basis and employer-led work-permit process are required.

income_proof_months.notes: No universal prior-income history is published; the relevant evidence is principally a qualifying job contract or employment certificate.

key_requirements.requirement: A work-type residence permit normally requires a foreigner's work permit and certification from the employer.
Work-permit materials include qualifications, authenticated degree or professional credentials, criminal-record certificate, medical evidence, and a job contract or employment certificate.
The employer processes the work-permit application; the national employment rules require a definite employing unit.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year for other personnel, up to 2 years for workers at qualifying registered entities, and up to 5 years for qualifying high-level talent, urgently needed professionals, or investors.
initial_validity.notes: Actual issuance is discretionary and tied to the qualifying Chinese basis.

extension_rules.value: Apply approximately 30 days before residence-permit and work-permit expiry with continued purpose-specific supporting evidence.
extension_rules.notes: Continued qualifying employment and work authorization are required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying work permit and Chinese employer can support a work-type residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is genuine temporary residence but does not fit independent foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate permanent-residence application may become possible for qualifying senior or equivalently salaried employees after at least four consecutive years of qualifying Chinese employment, at least three years' residence within those four years, and good tax records.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A work residence permit does not automatically become permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization remains discretionary for a person settled in China, a near relative of a Chinese national, or a person with another legitimate reason; approval requires giving up foreign nationality.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No fixed residence period guaranteeing naturalization is stated.

rejected_routes.notes: A potentially long-term route for locally hired professionals, but it fails the selection rule because it requires Chinese employment and employer participation.

rejected_routes.route_name: Graduate innovation or business-startup residence facilitation

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The national NIA guide does not publish a monthly income threshold. Some local procedures instead require business evidence and a bank deposit.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No nationwide minimum income or capital amount is established. Chongqing and Beijing currently publish local bank-deposit evidence above CNY 50,000 for specified entrepreneurship applicants, but that is not a national monthly-income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No national monthly-income threshold; local entrepreneurship evidence and deposit requirements may apply
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: National guidance states no monetary formula; Chongqing and Beijing publish local bank-deposit evidence over CNY 50,000 for specified applicants
income_requirement_display.notes: The CNY 50,000 figure is a local deposit/evidence requirement, not income, investment capital applicable throughout China, or proof that an ordinary foreign-client freelancer qualifies. National guidance requires genuine innovation/startup evidence, while local rules differ.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither national guidance nor the reviewed current Beijing procedure specifies a standardized number of prior-income months.

key_requirements.requirement: Outstanding foreign graduates of designated Chinese universities must be engaged in innovation or a startup in China and provide graduation and activity evidence.
Graduates of internationally renowned overseas universities may qualify when coming to China for innovation or a startup within two years after graduation.
Local procedures can require a business or investment plan, domestic bank evidence, intellectual-property or investment evidence, local-authority certification, or a host/partner guarantee.

initial_validity.value: Potentially 2–5 years for qualifying graduates of designated Chinese universities; up to 2 years for qualifying recent graduates of internationally renowned overseas universities.
initial_validity.notes: Local eligibility and documentary standards require confirmation.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary remote-work renewal rule exists; continued residence depends on retaining a qualifying innovation or startup basis and satisfying local authority requirements.
extension_rules.notes: The national guide does not establish automatic renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary private-affairs or locally designated entrepreneurship residence may be available to narrowly qualifying graduates or other applicants conducting genuine innovation, investment, or startup activity in China.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A foreign software contract alone does not meet the stated basis.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic graduate-startup-to-PR transition is published; the person must separately meet a permanent-residence category.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No direct or time-defined citizenship path from this facilitation is published.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this requires genuine China-based innovation, investment, or entrepreneurship and locally variable evidence. Shanghai expressly says there is no separate entrepreneurship visa in China's visa list; the available document is a residence permit for qualifying innovation/entrepreneurship cases.

summary.value: Narrow residence facilitation exists for certain outstanding graduates engaged in genuine innovation or startup activity in China, including some recent graduates of internationally renowned overseas universities. A degree by itself is insufficient, the route is not ordinary foreign-contract remote work, and no direct PR entitlement is published.
summary.notes: Available only in this restricted innovation/entrepreneurship sense; it is not an independent degree-based skilled-migration program.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual domiciled in China, or a non-domiciled individual present for at least 183 days in a tax year, is generally a resident individual. Special six-year and single-departure rules can exempt qualifying foreign-source income paid abroad for some non-domiciled residents.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Day count, domicile, work location, payment source, treaty position, and the six-year rule all require individual analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal screening rate for resident comprehensive income, not an expected effective rate. Business-operation income instead uses rates up to 35%, and classification of independent foreign-contract income needs professional review.

social_contributions_percent.notes: There is no single nationwide total percentage across all insurance branches. The tax authority states that participating freelancers pay basic pension insurance at 20% of a locally selected base between 60% and 300% of the provincial full-coverage average wage, but that general contribution rule does not create immigration eligibility for a foreign remote worker. Legally employed foreigners are subject to locally determined employee contributions, potentially modified by a social-security agreement.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No digital-nomad fixed monthly payment exists. Residence-permit charges are application fees rather than monthly payments. Social-insurance amounts depend on lawful status, locality, the selected or assessed contribution base, and treaty coverage, so no national USD monthly amount can be stated.

special_tax_regimes.value: Non-domiciled individuals may obtain the six-year foreign-source-income exemption when statutory conditions and filing requirements are met. No digital-nomad tax holiday was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is a general inbound-individual rule, not an immigration program.

taxes.caveats: China has no qualifying digital-nomad route, so these are general tax screening rules rather than a route-specific tax result. Services physically performed in China may be treated as China-source even when the payer is abroad. Contract characterization, deductions, foreign tax credits, VAT, treaties, and local social-insurance rules require professional advice.

taxation_system.value: China uses category-based individual income taxation. Resident comprehensive income is taxed annually at progressive rates from 3% to 45% after applicable deductions; business-operation income uses 5% to 35%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile in China or at least 183 days in a tax year generally creates resident-individual status; non-domiciled residents may benefit from the six-year rule for qualifying foreign-source income paid abroad.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxable on China and foreign income, subject to the non-domiciled six-year exemption and treaties. Non-residents generally pay tax on China-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Six-year foreign-source-income rule for qualifying non-domiciled individuals; no special digital-nomad regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Legally employed foreigners generally join the employee system under locally determined bases and rates, subject to social-security agreements. General rules allow participating freelancers to pay basic pension insurance at 20% of a locally selected base, but foreign eligibility and immigration status must be established separately.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 45% figure is the top marginal dashboard rate. Brackets apply to annual taxable comprehensive income after the CNY 60,000 basic deduction and other permitted deductions; they are not rates on gross income.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident annual comprehensive income after deductions
tax_brackets.notes: USD conversion omitted because tax is computed in CNY.

tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: Official law establishes the 3%–45% range, CNY 60,000 annual basic deduction, residence rule, and foreign tax credit. PwC's July 2026 review was used to transcribe bracket thresholds presented graphically on the official English law page.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because China has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence status.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; general individual income tax rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 45% top marginal rate for resident comprehensive income; actual treatment depends on income classification and deductions.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or at least 183 days generally creates tax residence, subject to the non-domiciled six-year rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident worldwide-income taxation can apply. Qualifying non-domiciled residents may exempt foreign-source income paid abroad until the six-year conditions are met, subject to filing and detailed sourcing rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad regime; the general non-domiciled six-year rule may apply independently of immigration category.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific contribution system. Legally employed or dispatched foreign workers generally participate under locally variable employee rules, subject to treaty exemptions. General freelancer pension rules cannot be treated as authorization for a foreigner to reside or work independently.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed-payment schedule exists; obligations arise only under another lawful employment or business structure.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No nomad-specific fixed amount applies. For legally employed foreigners, the employer and employee contribute under local rules and possible treaty exemptions. The national tax-authority overview states that participating individual businesses without employees and other freelancers pay basic pension insurance at 20% of a contribution base selected between 60% and 300% of the province's full-coverage average wage; it does not establish that an unsupported foreign remote worker may enroll or obtain residence through that mechanism.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad fee. Foreign residence-permit fees are CNY 400 for up to one year, CNY 800 for one to three years, and CNY 1,000 for three to five years, but only for applicants with a qualifying residence basis.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific flat tax, registration fee, or transaction tax is published. If a person separately establishes a lawful taxable business, the 2026 VAT Law applies to taxable transactions in China; current administration guidance sets the natural-person per-transaction VAT threshold at CNY 1,000. Whether remote software services fall within that rule, qualify for another treatment, or require invoicing/registration depends on the actual lawful structure and cannot be converted into a universal fixed monthly cost.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of a qualifying route means no reliable nomad-specific fixed-cost calculation can be provided. The cited pension and VAT rules describe general tax or social-insurance systems, not an immigration pathway.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being present under 183 days does not by itself make work performed in China tax-free or lawful under immigration rules; China-source and treaty analysis remains necessary.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days or with Chinese domicile, resident taxation may apply, potentially reaching a 45% marginal rate. The six-year exemption may protect qualifying foreign-source income paid abroad, but services physically performed in China may not qualify as foreign-source.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: No immigration pathway based merely on registering as a sole proprietor after visitor entry is published. Any lawful China business structure requires separate corporate, licensing, immigration, tax, VAT, invoicing, and social-insurance review.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax conclusions are general screening information because the requested immigration route does not exist.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying foreign-contract remote-work route grants temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: There is no remote-worker status from which to count. Separate categories have their own conditions: qualifying senior employment commonly requires four consecutive years of qualifying work and three years' residence within four, while the spouse category requires five years of marriage and residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: No fixed statutory number of years from permanent residence to naturalization is published.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and no qualifying remote-work starting route exists.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed official national naturalization guide does not publish a typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Naturalization requires approval and a statutory connection such as being a near relative of a Chinese national, being settled in China, or another legitimate reason. An approved applicant cannot retain foreign nationality. No automatic language-test or fixed-years formula is published in the reviewed national guidance.
key_conditions.notes: Settlement and approval are substantive, discretionary requirements; permanent residence does not guarantee citizenship.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For spouse-based PR, the marriage must have lasted at least five years and the applicant must also have resided in China for five consecutive years, at least nine months in each year, with stable income and domicile.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count toward the five-year marriage condition, but it does not remove the separate five-consecutive-year China residence requirement or create automatic citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to either a Chinese citizen or a foreign Chinese permanent resident can support the stated spouse PR category.

requirements_and_risks.value: Provide the marriage certificate, spouse's identity evidence, housing evidence, stable-income evidence, health certificate, and foreign criminal-record certificate. Naturalization as a near relative remains discretionary and requires loss of foreign nationality upon approval. False documents or a sham marriage can result in refusal, cancellation, and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Official authorities may verify the authenticity of relationships and submitted evidence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: China does not provide broad territorial birthright citizenship. A child born in China is Chinese when at least one parent is Chinese, or when both parents are stateless or of uncertain nationality and settled in China.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in China to two foreign-national migrant parents does not ordinarily acquire Chinese nationality merely by birth in China.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Article 6 creates a narrow exception where the parents are stateless or of uncertain nationality and have settled in China.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in China with one Chinese-national parent has Chinese nationality under Article 4.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: For a child born abroad, Article 5 contains an exception when the relevant Chinese parent is settled abroad and the child acquires foreign nationality at birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Chinese-citizen child does not automatically naturalize or permanently admit the foreign father. Family/private-affairs residence or later family-based PR may be possible only under a separately qualifying category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The exact family category depends on the child's circumstances, age, residence, and the sponsoring relationship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: Potential access to family-related visa or residence processes and, if the separate statutory conditions are eventually met, family-based permanent residence or discretionary naturalization. No automatic father citizenship or PR arises from the child's birth.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Documented kinship, genuine family life, income, domicile, residence history, and approval remain important.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the live China passport dashboard on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations in this index; the broader mobility score is 94.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance by the index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 46 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. The index treats eVisa destinations separately.

passport.notes: Passport-index values are dynamic. China does not recognize dual nationality for Chinese nationals.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only daily life is possible in parts of major international cities but is not broadly practical for government procedures and many ordinary services. The 2025 EF index ranked China 86th with a below-global-average score of 464, while official processes commonly require Chinese or Chinese translations.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF is a private, self-selected testing dataset and should be treated as an indicator rather than a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian is not a general working or administrative language in China. Russian-language immigration information exists on the NIA site, but daily life and official filings generally require Chinese; professional interpretation may be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide Ukrainian- or Russian-proficiency statistic was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2025 urban non-private average of CNY 129,441 annually, divided by 12 and converted using the retrieved July 2026 CNY/USD reference of about USD 0.1477 per CNY.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current NBS wage release publishes means by ownership, region, industry, and occupational group, but no national employee-wage median. The household release publishes median disposable income, which is not an employee salary and was not substituted.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: China has locally determined minimum wages and no single national figure. The current source confirms Shanghai's highest monthly standard of CNY 2,740 but does not establish one nationwide minimum for conversion to USD.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2025 urban private-unit annual average, CNY 71,590, divided by 12. This is a formal urban employee average, not universal resident income.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed 2025 NBS wage releases provide arithmetic average wages, including breakdowns by sector, region, registration type, and five occupational groups, but do not publish a national median employee salary. NBS separately reports median per-capita disposable household income of CNY 36,231 for 2025; that includes multiple income sources and is not a salary statistic, so it is not converted or placed here.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official releases publish averages, not an observed or statutory maximum salary. The highest occupational or sector average cannot be treated as a wage ceiling.

min_salary_local_currency.value: No single national minimum; locally determined. Shanghai's highest reported monthly minimum was CNY 2,740 as of January 1, 2026.
min_salary_local_currency.notes: CNY 2,740 is the highest reported local minimum, not the lowest salary nationally.

average_salary_local_currency.value: CNY 5,966/month urban private units; CNY 10,787/month urban non-private units
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Calculated from official 2025 annual averages of CNY 71,590 and CNY 129,441.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No national employee-salary median is published in the reviewed current NBS wage releases. The published CNY 36,231 figure is 2025 median per-capita disposable household income, not employee salary, and therefore is not substituted.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum salary or wage ceiling is published in the reviewed NBS releases. They report group averages; even the CNY 210,016 average for middle and senior management in enterprises above designated size is not a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2025 pre-tax average wages of employees in urban private and non-private legal-person units; excludes self-employed businesses and freelancers
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 annual figures converted to monthly
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are worker-wage statistics, not immigration income thresholds. USD conversions are approximate; local-currency figures are authoritative. Coverage is urban formal units and does not represent every worker. Current official sources do not publish a national employee median or maximum.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official 2025 household statistics report annual per-capita consumption expenditure of CNY 29,476, including CNY 35,869 for urban residents and CNY 20,259 for rural residents. These are population averages, not a recommended remote-worker budget, and costs vary substantially by city.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Per-capita household expenditure should not be read as the cost of maintaining a specific expatriate lifestyle.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor, business, and visa-free stays are not remote-worker residence statuses and do not provide a settlement clock.
settlement_track.summary: No current ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route was found. Settlement would require changing to a separately qualifying Chinese employment, family, genuine approved entrepreneurship, investment, talent, or other residence basis, and naturalization would remain discretionary.
settlement_track.notes: Official materials confirm other residence categories but no regular remote-work route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The national residence categories do not include independent residence based solely on foreign remote income. The employment rules require authorized employment and employer participation, while visitor categories cannot be used as ordinary employment status. Current Beijing, Chongqing, and Shanghai entrepreneurship procedures require genuine local innovation, investment, business planning, deposits, intellectual property, guarantees, or locally recognized entrepreneurship evidence; they do not establish that opening a bank account, registering a business after visitor entry, or retaining only an ordinary foreign software contract legalizes residence and remote work.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed using more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including multiple current official sources not present in the previous source set. Remaining nulls reflect facts that are inapplicable or not published as national statistics or route-specific obligations, rather than unsearched placeholders.

data.selection_summary: Colombia’s Visa V for digital nomads fits foreign-contract remote work but is expressly visitor status, does not constitute domicile, and provides no direct settlement or citizenship path. Visa M Profesional Independiente is independently filed and can lead to Visa R after five years, but software engineering is generally non-regulated and approval requires a discretionary finding that the proposed activity is of interest to Colombia. It is therefore a residence-oriented qualification route requiring filing-level review, not a confirmed ordinary remote-worker route.

visa_application.notes: Official electronic application form for Colombian visa categories. Applicants outside Colombia select the appropriate consulate; applicants legally present in Colombia select the Bogotá office.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximation of five 2026 statutory minimum monthly wages using COP 3,128.65 per USD on 2026-08-15.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: COP 8,754,525 per month (5 SMLMV in 2026)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The authoritative requirement is five Colombian statutory minimum monthly wages.

income_requirement_display.value: COP 8,754,525/month (about USD 2,798)
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: COP monthly income based on 5 SMLMV
income_requirement_display.notes: Six months of bank history are required. For a second or subsequent visa of this type, the income evidence must come from a Colombian bank.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank certificate must report the account opening date, products, average balance, and monthly movements for the preceding six months.

key_requirements.requirement: Letter explaining the profession or activity the applicant intends to perform in Colombia.
For a regulated profession, Colombian recognition of the degree plus the applicable professional card, licence, or provisional permit.
A non-regulated activity is admitted only exceptionally and must be considered of interest to Colombia; professional-experience evidence may be requested.
Average monthly income of at least five SMLMV, demonstrated through six months of bank records.
Colombian health coverage or comprehensive private insurance covering the planned stay, including accident, illness, maternity, disability, hospitalization, death, and repatriation.
General visa documentation, including a passport valid for at least six months, photograph, and apostille/legalization and official Spanish translation where required.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years
initial_validity.notes: The authority may grant a shorter period at its discretion.

extension_rules.value: Subsequent applications are possible while the qualifying professional activity, income, and health coverage continue; later applications must show income through a Colombian bank.
extension_rules.notes: The rules describe second and subsequent visa applications rather than an automatic extension. Every grant remains discretionary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The M visa is migrant status intended for a foreigner seeking to establish in Colombia and directly permits residence and work in the profession or activity authorized by the visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a residence-oriented category, unlike the Visa V digital-nomad category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After five years as a qualifying M Profesional Independiente visa holder, the applicant may apply for Visa R by accumulated time, subject to valid visas, movement records, continued circumstances, income, and absence limits.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Conversion is not automatic; a separate Visa R application is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: For an applicant who is not Latin American, Caribbean, or Spanish, naturalization normally becomes available after five continuous years counted from issuance of Visa R. The general screening timeline is therefore about ten years from the first qualifying M visa: five years to R plus five years holding R.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary. Shorter domicile periods apply to Latin American, Caribbean, and Spanish nationals and to applicants married to or parenting a Colombian citizen.

best_routes.notes: This is the strongest settlement option found that can be filed without a local employer. It is only a partial profile match: a foreign contract is not prohibited, but the official rules do not establish ordinary foreign-client software work as sufficient. Because software engineering is generally non-regulated, the exceptional Colombian-interest test should be confirmed with the visa authority before relying on this route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximation of three 2026 statutory minimum monthly wages at the 2026-08-15 official TRM.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: COP 5,252,715 per month (3 SMLMV in 2026)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The legal requirement is expressed as three SMLMV.

income_requirement_display.value: COP 5,252,715/month (about USD 1,679)
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: COP monthly income based on 3 SMLMV
income_requirement_display.notes: The earlier approximately USD 1,100 figure is outdated because the current minimum wage and exchange rate materially change the conversion.

income_proof_months.notes: The resolution expressly requires the minimum income during the preceding three months.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport from a country or territory exempt from a Colombian short-stay visa.

Letter in Spanish or English from one or more foreign companies explaining the relationship and remuneration, with the contract where available; foreign-company owners may document remote ownership and work.
Three months of bank statements showing income of at least three SMLMV.
Comprehensive health policy valid in Colombia for the planned stay.
No remunerated activity for a person or entity domiciled in Colombia.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Visa V is visitor status, not migrant or resident status.

extension_rules.value: No automatic extension or renewal entitlement is published; any later application remains discretionary.
extension_rules.notes: The rules specify a maximum grant of two years but do not include this Visa V category among the statuses eligible for Visa R by accumulated time.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None directly. It provides lawful temporary visitor status for foreign remote work but does not grant temporary-resident or migrant status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Cancillería expressly states that Visa V categories do not grant temporary or permanent resident status, and the visa resolution states that Visa V does not constitute domicile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Possible by separately qualifying for Visa M Profesional Independiente or another eligible M category; the independent-professional PR clock is five years after obtaining M status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Articles 24, 46, 76 and 90 establish in-country filing, nomad restrictions, professional eligibility and the M-to-R clock. A foreign remote contract does not itself secure acceptance of the regulated profession or exceptional activity. This is a conditional professional successor, not a requirement to accumulate nomad time.

path_to_citizenship.value: This Visa V has no citizenship path of its own: it is issued without constituting domicile, while naturalization requires a current Visa R and counts the ordinary five-year domicile period from issuance of that Visa R. Time on Visa V therefore does not count toward the statutory naturalization period; the holder must independently qualify for a settlement status and later Visa R.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is a legal-status distinction rather than merely an absence of published guidance. Visa V may support temporary living, but it supplies neither qualifying domicile nor accumulated time toward Visa R.

rejected_routes.notes: Excellent temporary fit for ordinary foreign-contract remote work, including Ukrainian and Russian passport holders because both appear on the short-stay exemption list. It is rejected for the citizenship-oriented selection because it is visitor status without a qualifying domicile or accumulated-time route to Visa R.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This route uses a capital threshold rather than a monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly-income threshold applies; at least 100 SMLMV of paid company capital or qualifying participation is required.

income_requirement_display.notes: Excluded because substantial local-company capital and active business evidence are required.

income_proof_months.notes: Later applications require evidence of active business and solvency, including recent bank statements; this is not personal income proof.

key_requirements.requirement: A functioning Colombian commercial company and paid ownership or foreign investment of at least 100 SMLMV.
Evidence of continued economic activity, solvency, taxes, social-security payments, premises, and employment generation for later applications.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years
initial_validity.notes: Validity depends on maintaining the qualifying ownership.

extension_rules.value: Further visas require continued capital ownership and proof of active, solvent business operations.
extension_rules.notes: A later grant remains discretionary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct Visa M migrant status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence-oriented but capital-dependent.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Eligible to apply for Visa R after five years of qualifying Visa M time.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate application is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially available after conversion to Visa R and completion of the applicable Visa R domicile period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not suitable for the stated profile because it requires substantial capital and local business substance.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a capitalized local-company route rather than ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No applicant monthly-income threshold was identified; the Colombian employer must meet a substantial solvency test.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The key financial condition concerns the Colombian employer rather than the applicant’s foreign income.

income_requirement_display.value: No applicant income threshold; Colombian employer sponsorship and solvency required
income_requirement_display.notes: Incompatible with independent foreign-contract remote work.

Employer bank evidence showing average monthly income of 100 SMLMV.
Degree or experience evidence and professional authorization where the profession is regulated.

initial_validity.notes: Work authorization is limited to the approved employer, role, profession, or activity.

extension_rules.notes: It cannot be renewed independently of the qualifying local employment.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct Visa M migrant status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The status is tied to the approved Colombian employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Visa R may be requested after five years of qualifying M Trabajador time.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate application is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially available after Visa R and the applicable naturalization domicile period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route remains outside the selection because it requires a Colombian employer.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Colombian employer and local employment contract are mandatory.

summary.value: Visa M Profesional Independiente can be sought without a local employer and grants migrant residence for up to three years. It requires professional qualifications, five SMLMV of monthly income, health coverage, and—especially for a non-regulated profession such as software engineering—an exceptional determination that the activity is of interest to Colombia. It can lead to Visa R after five years but is not a guaranteed degree-only route.
summary.notes: This is why Colombia is classified as partial rather than fully matched.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreign individual generally becomes Colombian tax resident after being present for more than 183 calendar days, continuously or discontinuously, in any consecutive 365-day period. Entry and exit days count; if the period spans two tax years, residence applies in the second year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Colombian nationals face additional family, income, asset, proof-of-foreign-residence, and tax-haven tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for a tax-resident individual, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For a locally obligated independent worker, health is 12.5% and pension 16% of the contribution base. The base is generally 40% of net income, subject to a minimum of one SMLMV; occupational-risk and solidarity amounts can add more. Whether a foreign-contract nomad must register and contribute requires case-specific review.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Conditional minimum health plus pension contribution for an independent worker subject to Colombian social security: approximately COP 499,008 monthly on the 2026 minimum contribution base. It excludes occupational-risk contributions, private visa health insurance, solidarity contributions, and filing costs.

special_tax_regimes.value: DIAN states that Colombia has no specific tax regime for digital nomads. Ordinary national taxes and formal obligations apply according to residence, income source, activity, and treaty position.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No digital-nomad tax holiday or blanket foreign-income exemption was found.

taxes.caveats: Immigration status and tax residence are separate. Work physically performed from Colombia can raise Colombian-source-income questions even when the payer is foreign. Actual liability depends on day count, source characterization, deductions, whether the relationship is employment or independent services, VAT status, social-security registration, permanent-establishment risk, and any applicable double-tax treaty.

taxation_system.value: Tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income under progressive rates from 0% to 39%; non-residents are generally taxed only on Colombian-source income. No special digital-nomad regime applies.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any consecutive 365-day period, with residence assigned to the second tax year when the period crosses years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: worldwide income and worldwide-assets reporting as applicable. Non-residents: Colombian-source income and Colombian assets.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad tax exemption or holiday. Treaty relief may apply case by case.
taxation_system.social_security: Locally obligated independent workers generally contribute health at 12.5% and pension at 16% on an IBC normally equal to 40% of net income, with an IBC floor of one SMLMV. Occupational-risk, solidarity-pension, and optional compensation-fund payments may apply.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 39% is the top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. Thresholds below are annual taxable-income bands. COP figures use the official 2026 UVT of COP 52,374; USD approximations use the 2026-08-15 TRM of COP 3,128.65 per USD.

tax_brackets.notes: Annual taxable-income band.
USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.
USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.
