USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.
Top marginal band; threshold is approximate in USD.

taxation_system.notes: PwC’s July 2026 page displayed COP 52,347 for the UVT, but official DIAN Resolution 238 fixes the 2026 UVT at COP 52,374; the official DIAN figure controls the conversions used here.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The Visa V digital-nomad category has no special tax exemption. A nomad can become tax resident under the ordinary 183-day test, after which worldwide income is generally within scope; non-residents remain subject to Colombian-source-income rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Visa V digital nomad or foreign-contract remote worker under ordinary Colombian tax rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 0%–39% if tax resident; 39% is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any consecutive 365-day period; residence applies in the second tax year if the period crosses years.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Tax residents are generally taxable on worldwide income. Non-residents generally face Colombian tax only on Colombian-source income, but services physically performed in Colombia require source analysis even when paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None. DIAN expressly states that no specific digital-nomad tax regime exists.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The visa itself requires comprehensive health insurance. If the person becomes a locally obligated independent worker, standard health and pension rules may apply; foreign-contract treatment should be confirmed with Colombian tax and social-security advisers.

fixed_payments.status: conditional_on_local_registration_and_activity
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: If Colombian independent-worker contributions apply, the minimum 2026 health and pension amount is about COP 499,008 monthly, before occupational-risk or solidarity additions. At higher income, contributions rise because they are percentages of the IBC.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Visa study and issuance fees apply and vary by visa category, nationality, and processing location. The official live fee page was inspected, but it does not publish one stable universal amount for this profile.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Colombia has a 0.4% financial-transactions tax on covered account disposals, subject to exemptions. VAT, municipal business taxes, and registration duties can arise if the person conducts taxable or registered local business.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health-insurance premiums are not government-fixed and were not reliably quantified. Immigration fees and private insurance therefore remain additional variable costs.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying at or below 183 days avoids the ordinary day-count residence test but does not by itself exempt Colombian-source income, locally performed services, VAT, or other registration obligations.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident should plan for Colombian reporting of worldwide income and progressive PIT, subject to deductions, credits, source analysis, and treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local independent registration can trigger health and pension contributions, possible occupational-risk coverage, income-tax filings, VAT analysis, municipal industry-and-commerce tax, invoicing duties, and the 0.4% financial-transactions tax.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: DIAN’s digital-nomad opinion expressly rejects the existence of a special nomad tax regime and confirms possible tax residence and worldwide taxation.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visa M Profesional Independiente directly supplies migrant residence once granted; no preliminary employer-sponsored status is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five years of qualifying M Profesional Independiente time are required before applying for Visa R by accumulated time.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General period for an applicant who is not Latin American, Caribbean, or Spanish and has no Colombian spouse, permanent partner, or child. It is counted from issuance of Visa R.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Screening total for the best partial route: approximately five years on qualifying Visa M plus five years on Visa R, excluding application-processing time. Latin American, Caribbean, Spanish, and qualifying Colombian-family cases may be faster.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official materials do not publish an average or guaranteed end-to-end processing time. The procedure includes document review, agency checks, possible domicile verification, examinations, a discretionary decision, and an oath, so a numeric estimate would be speculative.

key_conditions.value: Maintain valid qualifying M status and the professional activity, observe absence rules, convert separately to Visa R, then complete continuous Visa R domicile. Naturalization requires good conduct and lawful means, tax and authority checks, and examinations in Colombia’s Constitution, history, culture, geography, and Spanish when Spanish is not the applicant’s mother tongue. An absence of at least one year interrupts the continuous naturalization domicile period.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is sovereign and discretionary even when formal requirements are met; Colombia permits multiple nationalities.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For a non-Latin-American, non-Caribbean, non-Spanish foreigner married to or in a permanent partnership with a Colombian, the Visa R domicile period for naturalization is reduced from five years to two. This is residence after Visa R, not merely two years of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Colombian can support a Visa M spouse application once the Colombian civil record and required sponsorship documents are available. It does not itself grant residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. Marriage to another foreign migrant provides no Colombian citizenship acceleration, though dependent status may be possible.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The relationship need not be formed after immigration, but it must be current, genuine, documented, and accompanied by effective cohabitation intentions.

requirements_and_risks.value: Visa M spouse applicants need a recent Colombian marriage record, a request and cohabitation declaration from the Colombian spouse, notarized authority, and both spouses’ movement records. Officials may request further relationship evidence or interviews. The current accumulated-time rule permits Visa R after three years on Visa M spouse; naturalization then generally requires two years of Visa R domicile. Sham marriage can lead to refusal, cancellation, and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The dedicated spouse page contains an older reference to five years for Visa R; later Resolution 10434 of 2023 specifies three years for M Cónyuge.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Colombia is Colombian if a parent is Colombian or, where both parents are foreign, at least one parent was domiciled in Colombia at birth. Current law generally proves the foreign parent’s intent to remain through three continuous or uninterrupted years holding a visa authorizing establishment. An anti-statelessness exception applies without the domicile requirement.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically: the child qualifies only if at least one foreign parent satisfies the statutory domicile test at birth—generally three years of a valid visa authorizing establishment—or if the child would otherwise be stateless. A short-term Visa V digital nomad should not be treated as satisfying this test.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Because the result depends on each parent’s visa category, duration, and the anti-statelessness rule, the binary field remains null.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Colombian by birth if either parent is Colombian. Registration and proof of the Colombian parent’s nationality are still required.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This is citizenship by parentage and birth registration, not a benefit dependent on the migrant father’s status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Colombian-by-birth child can seek Visa M as the parent of a Colombian and may apply for Visa R after two years of qualifying M time. Having a Colombian child also reduces the general Visa R domicile period for naturalization to two years.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The child must actually hold Colombian nationality; birth in Colombia alone is insufficient where the domicile condition is not met.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child is Colombian by birth and paternity is legally recorded, the migrant father may qualify independently for a family-based Visa M and later Visa R after two years. The father does not receive automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship, and naturalization remains a separate discretionary process after the applicable Visa R domicile period.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A permanent-resident parent does not establish the child’s nationality solely by holding Visa R; the statutory domicile evidence must also be checked. The corresponding boolean therefore remains null.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when accessed on 2026-08-15. This index is used because it publishes a current category breakdown.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations categorized strictly as visa-free; this is not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations categorized as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 45 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately displays a mobility score of 135.

passport.notes: Index methodologies differ. The figures here consistently use Passport Index’s displayed breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable in some multinational, technology, tourism, and expatriate settings, especially in major cities, but is insufficient for many administrative and daily-life tasks. Spanish is strongly advisable for immigration, tax, housing, healthcare, and long-term integration. EF EPI 2025 ranked Colombia 76th of 123 and classified national proficiency as low.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected proficiency dataset and should be treated as a practical indicator rather than an official population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and no nationwide service-availability statistics were identified. Small community resources may exist in major cities, but relying on either language for government, legal, medical, or ordinary commercial dealings would be impractical; Spanish remains necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The inspected national legal and language sources do not quantify Russian- or Ukrainian-language availability, so the assessment is qualitative and cautious.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the OECD’s 2025 country estimate of COP 31,542,293 gross annual average wage, divided by 12 and converted at COP 3,128.65 per USD. This OECD full-time average-worker concept does not describe the median worker or the entire employed population.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected current DANE and OECD publications do not report a national median monthly wage. Producing one would require a weighted calculation from GEIH microdata with an explicitly chosen worker population.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory 2026 minimum monthly wage; it is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate current-TRM conversion of the OECD 2025 country estimate. The authoritative OECD national-currency amount is COP 31,542,293 gross annually, equal to COP 2,628,524.42 monthly.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national median monthly worker wage is published in the inspected current releases. A value cannot be derived defensibly without weighted GEIH microdata analysis and population-definition choices.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A finite national maximum wage is not a meaningful published statistic. DANE’s registered-labor distributions use an open-ended 'more than 10 SMLMV' category rather than a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: COP 1,750,905 statutory minimum monthly wage for 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Excludes the separate transport allowance and is not an observed minimum across every worker.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: OECD 2025 country estimate for an average worker, converted from annual to monthly by division by 12. It is an average-wage benchmark and not a household-survey median.

median_salary_local_currency.value: The inspected current DANE GEIH, DANE RELAB, and OECD releases do not publish a national median monthly wage; calculating it requires weighted GEIH microdata and a defined worker population.
median_salary_local_currency.notes: No private salary-site estimate was substituted because it would not be comparable to the national average-worker measure.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Not applicable as a finite national wage statistic: Colombian wage rules do not set a general maximum, and DANE RELAB publishes an open-ended category above 10 SMLMV rather than a maximum amount.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: This field describes the absence of a finite population maximum, not a missing statutory minimum or an unknown immigration threshold.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2026 statutory gross monthly minimum; OECD 2025 gross annual average-worker estimate divided by 12; median and maximum checked against current DANE and OECD publications
average_citizen_salary.period: 2026 minimum wage and 2025 OECD average wage; DANE releases inspected through 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum is a statutory benchmark for Colombian workers. The average is the OECD’s gross average-worker estimate and should not be read as the typical or median resident’s earnings. Current official statistical releases do not provide a directly transferable national median, while a national maximum is inapplicable because the published distribution is open-ended.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected national labor-statistics page does not publish a single nationwide cost-of-living amount suitable for this comparison. Living costs vary materially by city, and no crowdsourced figure was inserted.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Visa V digital-nomad route is temporary visitor status and is not the settlement route used for this classification. Settlement depends on separately qualifying for Visa M Profesional Independiente.
settlement_track.summary: Visa M Profesional Independiente is genuine migrant status that can lead to Visa R after five years and, for an ordinary non-Latin-American/non-Spanish applicant, naturalization after another five years holding Visa R. The citizenship track is legally credible, but entry to it is only a partial profile match because approval of non-regulated software work requires an exceptional Colombian-interest determination.
settlement_track.notes: The track is strong once the applicant secures and maintains Visa M Profesional Independiente. Visa V itself does not establish domicile or count toward the first five years.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Visa V fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work but is temporary-only. Visa M Profesional Independiente does not require a local employer or expressly require a local client, yet its exceptional activity-of-interest test means ordinary foreign-client software work is not a confirmed fit.

data.notes: Focused audit resolved the digital-nomad citizenship field and the national average-wage field. Visa V is expressly non-domiciliary visitor status with no direct citizenship path. OECD Taxing Wages 2026 supplies a 2025 gross average-worker estimate of COP 31,542,293 annually, or COP 2,628,524.42 monthly. Current DANE and OECD publications still do not publish a directly transferable national median monthly wage, and a finite national maximum is inapplicable because official distributions use an open-ended upper band. Other remaining uncertainties include citizenship processing duration, private insurance pricing, and whether non-regulated software engineering will receive the discretionary Colombian-interest finding under Visa M.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Visa M Profesional Independiente, followed by Visa R
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A Visa V nomad holder may independently apply for an eligible Visa M, including Profesional Independiente, and then accumulate five years toward Visa R. Visa V nomad time is excluded from that PR clock.
requirements: Obtain approval for a regulated profession, or exceptionally an accepted activity of interest to Colombia.
For the independent-professional category, provide degree recognition/licence where required, qualifying income history and health coverage.
Maintain qualifying M status for five years, the approved professional activity and applicable continuity/absence conditions.
reviewed_route_names: Visa V — Nómadas Digitales
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Articles 24, 46, 76 and 90 establish in-country filing, nomad restrictions, professional eligibility and the M-to-R clock. A foreign remote contract does not itself secure acceptance of the regulated profession or exceptional activity. This is a conditional professional successor, not a requirement to accumulate nomad time.

data.selection_summary: Comorian law contains a potentially independent residence route: a long-stay visa, annually renewable residence card, and a 10-year renewable resident card for an authorized liberal activity. No local employer is prescribed, but activity authorization and the resident card are discretionary Council of Ministers decisions. Current official materials do not confirm that foreign-client software work qualifies, so this is not a fully matched remote-work route.

visa_application.title: Visas — Embassy of the Union of the Comoros in Belgium
visa_application.notes: Official consular information page, not a direct online application. Applicants must ask specifically about a long-stay visa under Law 88-025 and authorization for a liberal activity; no dedicated remote-worker channel was found.

best_routes.route_name: Long-stay visa, residence card, and resident card for an authorized liberal activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Law 88-025 publishes no minimum income threshold. A filing authority may nevertheless require proof of means.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No KMF minimum was published in the governing law or reachable official consular material.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income threshold; verify proof-of-means requirements with the embassy and Ministry of the Interior
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No statutory KMF amount or income formula is published; filing-level proof-of-means expectations must be confirmed
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of a published threshold does not establish that financial evidence will not be requested.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither the residence law nor reviewed consular material states a bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through a Comorian diplomatic or consular representation for a long-stay visa when intending to remain more than three months; approval is decided by the Council of Ministers.
Within ten days after entry, the Ministry of the Interior issues a residence card; it is renewable annually.
Visas and the ordinary residence card do not themselves permit salaried or non-salaried gainful activity.
A residence-card holder wishing to work professionally must obtain a resident card. For liberal activity, the application goes to the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
If creating an activity, the resident-card application must include an activity-authorization application. Both authorization and the card are decided by the Council of Ministers.

For natural-person business registration, the published checklist requires a residence card for a foreigner, recent civil-status and criminal-record documents, a residence certificate, proof of business premises, and any required prior authorization; listed registration and printing charges total KMF 15,000.

initial_validity.value: Annual residence card after long-stay entry; a professional resident card, if approved, is valid for 10 years.
initial_validity.notes: The 10-year document is called a carte de résident. Its equivalence to permanent residence for every purpose is not established by the current sources.

extension_rules.value: The residence card is renewable annually. The 10-year resident card may be renewed and carries an annual charge set through finance legislation.
extension_rules.notes: No current renewal checklist, deadline, fee schedule, or approval standard was published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A Council-approved long-stay visa is followed by an annually renewable residence card issued within ten days after entry.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The long-stay visa and ordinary residence card do not themselves authorize gainful work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The law permits a 10-year renewable resident card for an approved professional activity, but does not label it permanent residence or establish automatic progression based on years lived in Comoros.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Treat permanent-residence equivalence as unconfirmed pending guidance from the Ministry of the Interior.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization is discretionary by decree and normally requires ten years of habitual residence immediately preceding application, plus lawful status, good character, specified health conditions, and assimilation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality code does not expressly confirm how every residence-card category is counted.

best_routes.notes: This residence-oriented route might accommodate a foreign-contract software engineer and does not prescribe a local employer. However, foreign-client software services are not expressly covered, local activity authorization is mandatory, approval is discretionary, and the business-registration checklist presupposes a residence card. The KMF 15,000 registration charge is not a residence or activity-authorization fee. Written confirmation is essential.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist visa, short-stay visa, or visa on arrival

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies to visitor entry.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No KMF remote-worker threshold applies to this visitor route.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker income threshold; this is visitor entry only
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status is not a residence or work route.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither Law 88-025 nor the reviewed official tourism/consular entry material specifies a bank-statement or income-history period for tourist or short-stay entry; because this is not a remote-worker route, no remote-work income-proof period applies.

key_requirements.requirement: The law provides a tourist visa for up to 45 days and a short-stay visa for up to three months, potentially renewable once.
Current secondary entry screening reports a 45-day visa on arrival, generally requiring six months' passport validity and onward or return travel.
Tourist, short-stay, and long-stay visa holders may not undertake gainful salaried or non-salaried activity unless the separate professional resident-card rules are satisfied.

initial_validity.value: Tourist stay up to 45 days; short stay up to three months. Secondary screening also reports a 45-day visa on arrival.
initial_validity.notes: Reconfirm entry rules with the embassy before travel.

extension_rules.value: The statutory short-stay visa may be renewed once; no visitor-to-independent-professional conversion procedure is published.
extension_rules.notes: Applicants intending to stay over three months are directed to the separate consular long-stay process.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No tourist-to-residence conversion was confirmed; the long-stay process is a separate consular procedure.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Do not assume an in-country change of status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor status has no confirmed permanent-residence path.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor stays are not established as habitual qualifying residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor entry does not authorize remote work, confer residence, or establish a settlement path.

summary.value: No independent degree-based, points-tested, or skilled-migration program was found. A software-engineering degree may support a discretionary liberal-activity application but creates no entitlement.
summary.notes: Reviewed official materials disclose no qualification-based route.

tax_residency_rule.value: The tax code does not use a simple 183-day test. Habitual residence includes accommodation available under ownership, usufruct, or a continuous rental of at least one year, or having one's principal place of stay in Comoros. Nonresidents remain taxable on Comorian-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence may begin before 183 days. Classification, service location, and treaty position require professional advice.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate under the progressive general schedule, not the expected effective rate. A separate 30% business-profits rate may also be relevant.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage applies to this applicant. The IMF/CRC table reports an 8% pension contribution for formal non-civil-servant employees (5% employer and 3% employee), while eRegulations lists employer social contributions of 2.5%, 3%, or 5% of remuneration by risk branch. Neither source establishes a mandatory rate or minimum for an independently registered foreign liberal professional.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No compulsory monthly minimum contribution or fixed freelancer payment for this independent-professional scenario is published.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, expatriate, remittance-basis, or tax-holiday regime applicable to an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer was confirmed.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Investment incentives require an approved qualifying investment and are not an ordinary freelancer regime.

taxes.caveats: The available tax code contains older provisions and later amendments, while the DGI code page was suspended during review. The 2026 IMF report corroborates the progressive rates. Local advice is required on whether receipts constitute salary, liberal-profession income, or business profits and on treaty or foreign-tax-credit relief.

taxation_system.value: Progressive general income tax with a top marginal rate of 30%; foreign-source income is included under the applicable category rules for persons subject to general income tax.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Habitual-residence/principal-stay test rather than a published 183-day threshold; a continuous rental of at least one year is one express criterion.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are assessed across global income categories, with foreign-source income determined under equivalent Comorian rules and foreign receipts separately declared. Nonresidents are taxable on Comorian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No ordinary digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime confirmed; approved investments may receive separate incentives.
taxation_system.social_security: Formal-sector employee affiliation is compulsory. The CRC non-civil-servant pension rate is 8% of pay (5% employer and 3% employee); eRegulations separately lists employer CNSPS contributions of 2.5%, 3%, or 5% of remuneration according to activity/risk branch. These payroll rates cannot be assigned to a self-employed foreign professional because no reviewed current source establishes compulsory self-employed coverage, a self-employed percentage, or a minimum payment.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value is the 30% top marginal rate, not an effective rate. Thresholds are annual taxable income in KMF; USD conversions are rough screening conversions using approximately KMF 424 per USD.

tax_brackets.notes: Annual threshold.

tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold approximate in USD.

taxation_system.notes: Income-tax rates and foreign-income rules are reasonably supported; classification and self-employed social contributions require local advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Comoros has no confirmed digital-nomad tax category. A person approved for liberal activity would likely fall under ordinary resident/general-income and professional-profit rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Potential independent liberal professional; no dedicated digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% top marginal personal income tax; professional-profit classification may also produce a 30% rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Habitual residence or principal place of stay; no simple 183-day safe harbor was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-source income is determined under equivalent Comorian income rules, and foreign receipts must be separately declared by persons subject to general income tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: There is no digital-nomad contribution category. Formal non-civil-servant pension contributions total 8% of pay (5% employer and 3% employee), while eRegulations publishes separate employer CNSPS rates of 2.5%–5% by activity/risk branch. No reviewed current source establishes whether or how these employee/payroll rules apply to a foreign-client independent liberal professional or publishes a self-employed minimum.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment is established for the proposed foreign-client liberal-professional scenario. Current sources publish employee payroll percentages and one-time business-registration charges, but no compulsory self-employed minimum contribution or flat monthly freelancer payment.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Formal non-civil-servant employee pension contributions total 8% of pay; employer CNSPS rates of 2.5%, 3%, or 5% are also published by risk branch. Applicability and any minimum for an independent foreign professional are unpublished.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Article 15 of Law 88-025 authorizes charges for visas, residence cards, resident cards, and renewals, but the reviewed law and official consular pages do not publish current amounts. Separately, natural-person business registration costs KMF 10,000 plus KMF 5,000 in printing fees; that KMF 15,000 total is not a visa or residence-card fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A professional licence/patente and activity-specific taxes may apply; current amounts for a software freelancer were not established.
fixed_payments.notes: Request the current fee schedule for the long-stay visa, annual residence card, 10-year resident card, renewals, activity authorization, patente, and any self-employed CNSPS/CRC liability. Only the KMF 15,000 business-registration total was directly published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no verified day-count safe harbor. A principal stay or qualifying long rental can create habitual residence, while Comorian-source income may be taxable without residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect declaration of foreign receipts and screening under the progressive schedule up to 30%, subject to classification and treaty or foreign-tax-credit relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: An authorized liberal activity may face professional-profit tax, patente/business registration, and possible social-security obligations in addition to residence-document charges.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No dedicated nomad guidance exists. Employee contribution rates are published, but self-employed fixed payments and professional-residence fees remain unresolved.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The residence card follows long-stay entry and is statutorily issued within ten days, subject to obtaining the discretionary long-stay visa.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No waiting period is stated before applying for the 10-year professional resident card, but prior residence-card status and professional/activity authorization are required. Permanent-residence equivalence is unconfirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization depends on habitual residence rather than a separately stated period after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General eligibility arises after ten years of habitual residence immediately preceding application; naturalization remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality code publishes no statutory or typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Habitual residence at filing and decree; normally ten preceding years of residence; lawful immigration compliance; good character; specified mental and physical health conditions; ability not to burden or endanger the community; and assimilation. No formal language level or general renunciation requirement is published.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is not automatic after the qualifying period.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For a foreign man married to a Comorian woman, the ordinary residence period is reduced from ten to five years. No minimum marriage duration is stated. A foreign woman marrying a Comorian man may acquire nationality at marriage, subject to exceptions and opposition rules.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Comorian woman can support the five-year residence reduction for a foreign husband. A foreign wife of a Comorian man may fall under the acquisition-at-marriage rule, but current registration procedures require verification.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The code is explicitly gender-asymmetric; do not generalize the automatic rule to a foreign husband.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage does not eliminate lawful-status, character, health, assimilation, investigation, and decree requirements for a foreign husband. Fraud can result in refusal, cancellation, and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Confirm current civil-status documentation and genuine-marriage evidence with the Ministry of Justice.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A person born in Comoros is Comorian unless both parents are foreigners; a child born abroad to a Comorian parent qualifies by descent. This is not unconditional jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Comoros to two foreign parents is excluded from automatic nationality. Special declaration, foundling, or anti-statelessness provisions may apply in limited cases.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parental temporary or permanent residence does not overcome the two-foreign-parent exclusion.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Comorian, subject to establishing legal parentage and completing civil registration.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Registration and proof of filiation remain important.

parent_benefit_summary.value: The nationality code does not grant a foreign parent automatic residence or citizenship merely because the child is Comorian; a separate family or residence basis must be established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Do not infer an automatic parent shortcut from the child's nationality.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic residence, permanent residence, or nationality was found. If married to the child's Comorian mother, the separate marriage rule may reduce his naturalization residence period to five years.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The benefit arises from marriage, not paternity alone.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings change frequently.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category; eVisa treatment varies by index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined value: 37 visa-on-arrival plus 4 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 60. Other indexes differ because of methodology and update timing.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only living is likely difficult outside internationally oriented businesses and tourism. French is more practical for administration and professional activity.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current nationwide English-proficiency measurement was found.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and no evidence of broad administrative or commercial use was found. French or an interpreter will generally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No dedicated Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking service network was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national mean employee wage is published in the reviewed sources. The World Bank gives a 2021 employee median of KMF 75,000, not a mean; INSEED released representative 2024 household and labour microdata in 2026, but the catalogue and reviewed aggregate publication do not state a validated national mean, so no USD average is calculated.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the World Bank's 2021 employee median of KMF 75,000 using roughly KMF 424 per USD. This is historical survey evidence.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The ILO Global Wage Report lists KMF 55,000 per month for 2015–2019, while Labour Code article 106 says the guaranteed inter-occupational minimum must be set by decree. No current decree or post-2019 official rate was located, so the historical figure is not converted into a current 2026 USD minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No validated current national mean employee wage is stated in the reviewed public sources.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of KMF 75,000 per month.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum wage or validated upper bound is published.

min_salary_local_currency.value: KMF 55,000 per month (ILO series for 2015–2019; current 2026 legal rate unverified)
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the latest directly located ILO series value, not proof that it remains legally in force in 2026. Article 106 requires a Council of Ministers decree; no current decree was found.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The World Bank publishes employee and self-employed medians, not a national mean. INSEED confirms representative 2024 labour and income microdata released in 2026, but no reviewed page states a validated current monthly mean.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: World Bank estimate for employees based on 2021 labour-market evidence.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A national maximum salary is not a statutory labour-market measure, and neither source publishes an upper bound. Sample outliers or advertised salaries are not substituted.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2021 employee median; historical 2015–2019 minimum-wage series; current national mean and maximum unpublished
average_citizen_salary.period: 2021 median and 2015–2019 minimum series, reviewed 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: This is labour-market context, not an immigration income threshold. The strongest aggregate is the World Bank's 2021 employee median of KMF 75,000 per month; self-employed workers had a KMF 43,000 median. The KMF 55,000 minimum is historical and its current legal force is unverified.

cost_of_living_note.value: INSEED reports cumulative consumer-price inflation of 28.1% from 2020 to 2024, including 31.8% for housing, water, electricity, and gas, and a 49.8% real increase in household rent spending. Its 2024 household survey reports a 46.1% national poverty rate. These are official affordability indicators, not an expatriate monthly budget; no reliable comprehensive 2026 household-cost figure was published.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Costs vary materially by island, housing tenure, imported-goods availability, and utilities. Price an actual local basket before relocation.

settlement_track.summary: A statutory long-stay/residence-card path and 10-year professional resident card exist, and habitual residence can support naturalization after ten years. The track remains weak because foreign-client software work is not expressly accepted, approval is discretionary, and no filing guidance confirms how time on this exact route counts.
settlement_track.notes: Manual verification with the embassy, Ministry of the Interior, Ministry of Economy and Finance, and a Comorian lawyer is essential.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The statute accommodates independently requested liberal activity without prescribing a local employer, but does not say whether a software engineer serving only foreign clients qualifies or what local business substance is required.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 2026-08-15 after inspecting more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including more than five not in the previous source set. New evidence clarifies natural-person registration documents and KMF 15,000 charges, formal-employee contribution rates, historical minimum-wage evidence, and official affordability indicators. Self-employed contributions, residence-document fees, a current national mean wage, and a national maximum wage remain unpublished in the reviewed sources.

data.selection_summary: Congo means the Republic of the Congo (Congo-Brazzaville), not the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The 2017 immigration law creates a one-year renewable ordinary resident card that can be requested personally and does not invariably require a local employer. However, any professional activity requires approval from the relevant Congolese ministry, and no official source expressly confirms that exclusively foreign-client software work qualifies. This is a settlement-oriented possibility requiring written pre-filing confirmation, not a confirmed digital-nomad or freelance route.

visa_application.title: GIRAFE — Demande de visa
visa_application.notes: This official Embassy of Congo in France platform supports account creation, document upload and payment for short visas. It is a general consular visa portal, not an online residence-card or digital-nomad application. The resident-card procedure occurs after lawful entry through the immigration authorities.

best_routes.route_name: Ordinary resident card for a non-salaried professional activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The law requires sufficient resources but publishes no numerical monthly minimum.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No numerical threshold is published; sufficient resources must be demonstrated
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Articles 19 and 28 make resources and the proposed professional activity relevant to the discretionary decision.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold — sufficient resources required
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: No quantified XAF or USD threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Resources assessed individually under Articles 19 and 28
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign contract may help demonstrate resources, but the statute does not identify foreign-contract remote work as a qualifying category.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither the law nor the current official residence guidance specifies a fixed bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Enter lawfully and apply personally to immigration for the resident card within 15 days of entry.
Valid passport and entry visa where required, criminal-record extract less than three months old, consular card and valid international vaccination record.
Repatriation-guarantee deposit where applicable, accommodation evidence, identity photographs and required taxes or stamps.
Approval from the relevant Congolese ministry for any professional activity; published guidance does not identify the ministry responsible for foreign-client software work.
Demonstrate sufficient resources; approval remains discretionary and may consider the activity and declarations supporting the residence request.

initial_validity.value: 1 year, renewable
initial_validity.notes: The ordinary resident card is residence status, not a visitor visa.

extension_rules.value: Renewal must be filed during the month before the one-year card expires. Article 29 makes renewal fee-bearing. The current online General Tax Code lists XAF 200,000 plus a XAF 5,000 stamp for an ordinary residence carnet, but still labels that carnet as valid for up to three years, conflicting with the 2017 immigration law’s one-year ordinary card. Immigration must confirm which tariff applies and whether it is charged on renewal.
extension_rules.notes: Late filing or refusal exposes the holder to removal. The deadline is clear, but the current tariff compilation has not been reconciled with the later one-year-card framework.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved ordinary resident card directly authorizes residence for one year.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Acceptance of the proposed foreign-client professional activity must be confirmed before relying on this route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least 10 years of uninterrupted residence, the applicant may seek a five-year renewable privileged resident card.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The statute calls this a privileged resident card rather than permanent residence, and issuance is not shown as automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after 10 years of habitual residence immediately preceding the application, but remains discretionary and is granted by decree after investigation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Residence must continue through the decree. Good character, assimilation, health or capacity and civic-oath conditions apply. The 2011 amendment abolished the former mandatory renunciation clause.

best_routes.notes: This is the only potentially relevant independent residence mechanism located. It is not a dedicated digital-nomad program. The wording may accommodate a self-directed professional, but professional work requires ministry approval and neither the responsible ministry, acceptance of exclusively foreign clients nor a software-professional checklist is published. Written confirmation from immigration and the competent ministry is essential.

rejected_routes.route_name: Short visitor or business visa / temporary professional mission

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Proof of sufficient means is required, but the reviewed consular pages publish no numerical minimum.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No numerical visitor threshold is published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Applicants must demonstrate means for the visit.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; sufficient means for the stay
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a visitor requirement, not a remote-worker income test.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed mission pages do not prescribe a fixed income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport, photograph, invitation or accommodation evidence, return travel and sufficient means.
Visitor status is limited to no more than three months and is legally distinct from residence.

initial_validity.value: Consular offerings vary by mission; the France portal offers 15-day and approximately three-month visas, while the statute limits visitor status to three months.
initial_validity.notes: Duration, entries and price depend on the consular mission and nationality.

extension_rules.value: France Diplomatie reports in-country visa renewal after three months at approximately XAF 106,000 for one year or XAF 206,000 for two years, but this does not turn visitor status into a confirmed settlement route.
extension_rules.notes: A visa extension and a resident card are legally distinct. A separate qualifying resident-card application is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence right; a separately approved resident card is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The short visa only facilitates entry.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from visitor status itself.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Any long-term outcome depends on a separate resident-card approval and qualifying residence thereafter.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path. A visitor is legally distinct from a resident, and a short stay does not establish the habitual residence required for naturalization. The person would first need a separately approved resident card, after which the general ten-year habitual-residence rule could potentially apply.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Neither the immigration law nor the nationality code treats a short visitor or business stay as qualifying residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this remains visitor or business status, even where a temporary professional mission is involved. It does not authorize ordinary ongoing foreign-contract remote residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration salary threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No immigration threshold is published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The national minimum wage is a labor rule rather than an immigration eligibility threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published immigration income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Local employment contract or approved-employer attestation required
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because substantive eligibility depends on local employment.

income_proof_months.notes: The immigration law does not specify a fixed evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Local employment contract or attestation signed by an approved employer.
General passport, criminal-record, consular-card, vaccination, accommodation, deposit and tax-stamp documents.

initial_validity.value: 1 year, renewable
initial_validity.notes: Ordinary resident card.

extension_rules.value: Apply during the month preceding expiry and pay the prescribed fee.
extension_rules.notes: The filing deadline is confirmed. The current General Tax Code publishes XAF 200,000 plus a XAF 5,000 stamp for an ordinary residence carnet, but its three-year validity label conflicts with the 2017 law’s one-year ordinary card; immigration must confirm the charge applicable to this salaried-card renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct one-year ordinary residence if approved.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential privileged resident card after 10 uninterrupted years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The status is a five-year renewable privileged card, not expressly permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: The general discretionary naturalization rule permits an application after 10 years of habitual residence, but this route is ineligible for the selector because it requires a local employer.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Personal filing of the card does not remove the underlying local-employment requirement.

rejected_routes.notes: The foreigner personally files the card application, but substantive eligibility as a salaried worker depends on a Congolese approved employer. Personal filing does not make it an independent route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numerical student-income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No numerical threshold is published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The general sufficient-resources assessment applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; local enrollment and sufficient resources required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Enrollment or attendance certificate from a Congolese institution
income_requirement_display.notes: An existing foreign software degree is not a substitute for local enrollment.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed period is prescribed.

key_requirements.requirement: Enrollment or attendance certificate from a school or university in the Republic of the Congo.
General resident-card documents and sufficient resources.

initial_validity.value: 1 year, renewable if the qualifying basis continues
initial_validity.notes: No student-specific renewal standard is published.

extension_rules.value: Use the general resident-card renewal procedure during the month before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: Continued enrollment would need to be demonstrated in practice, although a detailed current student-renewal checklist was not located.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct ordinary resident card when approved.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The general statute permits a privileged card after 10 uninterrupted years, but treatment of student time and post-study conversion is not specifically stated.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Manual legal verification is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: No education-specific citizenship pathway; only the general discretionary naturalization provisions apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant’s existing foreign degree does not independently create residence. The route requires actual study in Congo and does not confirm permission for continuing ordinary foreign-client work.

summary.value: A foreign student enrolled in a Congolese school or university can use an enrollment or attendance certificate to seek the one-year ordinary resident card without a local employer. No independent skilled-migration or foreign-degree route was found, and post-study conversion or treatment of student time toward privileged residence was not specifically established.
summary.notes: This requires local study; the applicant’s existing software-engineering degree alone is insufficient.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual has regular tax residence when their principal residence is in the Republic of the Congo; the current reviewed source does not state a standalone 183-day safe harbor.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence may arise from establishing a principal home rather than only after a day-count threshold. Treaty rules can alter the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: 30% is the 2026 top marginal employment-income rate, not an expected effective rate. PwC’s August 2026 summary also displays older general PIT bands up to 40% and a 20% rule for certain non-domiciled non-commercial income, so foreign-client income requires classification advice.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 4% value is the covered employee’s pension share on gross salary, not a complete self-employed burden. Separate 2024–2025 universal-health rules require independent workers and liberal professionals to pay monthly at 3.79% of a regulatory activity base; published category payments range from XAF 7,201 to XAF 22,740. The schedule includes conseils at XAF 22,740, but does not expressly classify freelance software engineering, so that category cannot be assumed.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: A single route-wide USD amount cannot be stated because universal-health contributions vary by assigned activity category from XAF 7,201 to XAF 22,740 monthly, and the category for a foreign software consultant is unpublished.

special_tax_regimes.value: PwC describes global flat taxation at 5% of annual turnover or 8% of annual margin for qualifying persons with annual income not exceeding EUR 152,449 who keep minimal cash accounts. No digital-nomad or inbound-expatriate exemption was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility of a foreign software professional and interaction with the 2026 Finance Law require local tax advice.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the contract is classified as employment, professional or non-commercial income, or business income; whether the individual establishes a principal residence; where work is physically performed; treaty relief; and local registration. Current secondary guidance has not fully reconciled every 2026 amendment.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income. Employment income uses a progressive 2026 scale topping at 30%; professional income can fall under different PIT or qualifying flat-turnover rules.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Principal residence in the Republic of the Congo creates regular residence; no general 183-day threshold was confirmed.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for domiciled residents; Congolese-source income for non-domiciled persons, subject to treaties and special provisions.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Possible global flat taxation of 5% of turnover or 8% of margin for qualifying smaller taxpayers; no remote-worker-specific regime.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees generally contribute 4% of gross salary for pensions, with employer CNSS branches reported at 20.28%. Independently registered workers and liberal professionals also fall under universal-health contributions at 3.79% of a prescribed activity base, with monthly amounts of XAF 7,201–22,740 depending on category.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard number is the top marginal rate for 2026 employment income, not the expected effective rate. The first band carries a fixed XAF 1,200 amount. Classification of non-employment foreign-client income needs professional advice.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable employment income per family-share or quotient
tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted using the 2026 budget assumption of approximately XAF 550 per USD.

tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable employment income per family-share or quotient
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable employment income per family-share or quotient
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The statutory employment scale and independent-worker health schedule are well supported. Overall confidence is lower because the immigration route does not define the tax or social-security classification of an ordinary foreign-client software professional.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax treatment exists because no dedicated digital-nomad status was found. A resident foreign professional may face worldwide-income taxation under employment, professional or business rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Unconfirmed independent-professional residence; not a digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% marginal rate for 2026 employment income; professional classifications may differ
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Principal residence in Congo can establish tax residence; no 183-day-only rule was confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is generally taxable for a domiciled resident; treaty relief may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found. A general smaller-taxpayer flat regime may be available but is not remote-worker-specific.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: There is no nomad-specific payroll rule. Covered employees generally bear a 4% pension contribution. If registered as an independent worker or liberal professional, current universal-health rules require direct monthly contributions at 3.79% of a prescribed activity base; published category amounts run from XAF 7,201 to XAF 22,740. Software consulting is not expressly named, so the fund must assign the category.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed: universal-health contributions for registered independent workers are fixed by activity category, but the immigration renewal tariff and the software professional’s category require official confirmation
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Registered independent workers and liberal professionals pay monthly universal-health contributions of XAF 7,201–22,740 by activity category. The highest listed group includes conseils at XAF 22,740, but the schedule does not expressly place freelance software engineering there. A separate 4% pension share applies to covered employees.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Through the France mission, the current short business-visa schedule is EUR 55 for 15 days or EUR 110 for three months. France Diplomatie reports in-country visa renewal at about XAF 106,000 for one year or XAF 206,000 for two years. The current General Tax Code lists XAF 200,000 plus a XAF 5,000 stamp for an ordinary residence carnet, but its three-year label conflicts with the 2017 one-year ordinary card, so immigration must confirm the applicable issuance or renewal charge.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: PwC reports an annual departmental tax of XAF 2,000, 18% VAT and a 0.5% universal-health solidarity contribution for specified high-income or business-tax bases; applicability depends on registration and income classification.
fixed_payments.notes: The universal-health schedule is current and official, but the category for software consulting is unpublished. Visa prices vary by consular mission, and the current residence-carnet tariff has not been reconciled with the 2017 terminology.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no confirmed day-count safe harbor. Establishing a principal home may create residence, while work physically performed in Congo can also create Congolese-source income.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A domiciled resident is generally taxable on worldwide income. Employment income uses the 2026 progressive scale up to 30%, while professional or business income may be classified differently.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registered independent workers or liberal professionals face category-based universal-health contributions. Qualifying smaller taxpayers may potentially use the 5%-of-turnover or 8%-of-margin regime, but eligibility and registration for a foreign software professional require local advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is scenario screening, not a confirmed digital-nomad regime. Congolese immigration, tax and social-security advice is necessary before establishing a home or performing work in the country.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: If the professional basis is accepted, the foreigner applies personally within 15 days after lawful entry; processing time is not published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Ten years of uninterrupted residence permits an application for the five-year privileged resident card. The statute neither labels it permanent residence nor guarantees issuance.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization and privileged-card eligibility both use approximately ten-year residence periods and are not stated as sequential. No additional post-privileged-card period is prescribed.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the earliest ordinary statutory application point after ten years of habitual residence. Naturalization remains discretionary and completion can take longer.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed nationality legislation and current naturalization decrees disclose no service standard or filing dates from which a reliable typical processing period could be calculated.

key_conditions.value: Ten years of habitual residence immediately before applying; residence in Congo at decree date; adulthood, capacity, health, good character, assimilation and civic oath. Naturalization is granted by decree after investigation. The former mandatory renunciation clause was abolished in 2011.
key_conditions.notes: No formal language-test level, published absence allowance or guaranteed decision period was located.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A resident card is available as of right to a foreign spouse after at least two years of marriage plus regular residence, subject to the continuing marriage, retained Congolese nationality of the spouse and transcription where required. The older nationality code separately provides nationality to a foreign woman after five years of common residence in Congo following civil registration.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can count toward the two-year card condition, but the applicant must also be regularly resident in Congo and satisfy transcription and document requirements. The nationality provision measures five years of common residence in Congo from registration, so years lived abroad are not shown as sufficient.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The nationality text is gendered toward a foreign wife. Current treatment of a foreign husband or same-sex spouse was not established.

requirements_and_risks.value: The union must continue, the citizen spouse must retain Congolese nationality, and a foreign-celebrated marriage must be transcribed in Congolese civil records. Civil-status evidence and any applicable repatriation deposit are required. Sham marriage can lead to refusal, loss of status and penalties; genuine relationship and residence evidence should be expected.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage-based nationality should be verified with the Ministry of Justice because the nationality code contains older gendered language.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship at birth includes descent from a Congolese parent and double jus soli where the child and at least one parent were born in Congo. A child born in Congo to two foreign-born parents generally acquires citizenship only at majority if resident then and habitually resident since age 16, subject to a right to decline.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Congo to two foreign-born migrant parents is not ordinarily a citizen at birth. The child may acquire nationality at majority if resident in Congo then and habitually resident there since age 16. Foundlings and children of unknown parents have protective rules; double jus soli applies if a parent was also born in Congo.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary case; statutory exceptions require individual assessment.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Congolese father or mother is Congolese under the descent provisions, provided filiation is legally established during minority.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Registration and proof of parentage remain important.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a child in Congo does not itself create a confirmed residence or citizenship shortcut for two foreign parents. If the child is Congolese through the other parent, family ties may support a discretionary immigration request, but no automatic parent status was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The immigration law expressly addresses qualifying spouses but does not publish an equivalent automatic card rule solely for parents of citizen children.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically obtain residence or citizenship through the child’s birth or citizenship. Any family application requires separate legal grounds and official confirmation.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Childbirth should not be treated as an immigration strategy.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s visa-required count; eVisa classifications may differ between indexes.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 33 visa-on-arrival plus 3 eTA destinations. The index also reports a mobility score of 57.

passport.notes: Passport-index methodologies and counts change. These fields consistently use Passport Index because it supplies the requested category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English may be usable within an international employer or technology team, but immigration, legislation and government administration operate primarily in French. Functional French is strongly advisable.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from the constitutional official language and the language of current procedures; no nationwide English-proficiency statistic was located.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and should not be expected in routine administration or local services. French would normally be required, with an interpreter where necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide evidence of Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the XAF 108,449 arithmetic mean monthly wage reported from provisional 2022 EHCVM results in the government’s 2024 Voluntary National Review, using the 2026 budget assumption of XAF 550 per USD. It is not a current 2026 wage or a software-engineer salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official EHCVM/VNR material publishes means by sex, residence and education but no national median. ILOSTAT’s topic catalog identifies median-earnings tables without displaying a Congo observation on the cited page, and a new employment survey was launched in 2026 after a long survey gap.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory XAF 70,400 monthly minimum using the 2026 budget assumption of XAF 550 per USD. This is a legal wage floor, not an observed minimum or average.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the nationally reported XAF 108,449 arithmetic mean monthly wage from provisional 2022 EHCVM results at XAF 550 per USD. It is an average for surveyed employees, not a 2026 wage quote or software-engineer average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national median amount is published in the reviewed current material. The government VNR gives arithmetic means from the 2022 EHCVM; ILOSTAT’s general wage page lists median tables but does not display a Congo value, while a replacement national employment survey was only launched in 2026.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No statistically meaningful national maximum wage is published. The official report gives subgroup means, including XAF 181,612 for employees with higher education, which is not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: National statutory SMIG effective 1 January 2025.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Arithmetic mean monthly wage reported from provisional nationally sampled 2022 EHCVM results in the government’s 2024 Voluntary National Review; not a current 2026 salary.

median_salary_local_currency.value: The reviewed official EHCVM/VNR results publish a mean wage but no national median amount
median_salary_local_currency.notes: A numeric median remains null because substituting the arithmetic mean or estimating a distribution would be misleading.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No nationally representative maximum wage statistic is published in the reviewed official or ILO material
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reported XAF 181,612 mean for higher-educated employees is a subgroup average, not a national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Provisional 2022 EHCVM arithmetic mean for surveyed employees plus the statutory national monthly minimum wage; no national median or maximum statistic
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly; survey mean relates to 2022 and SMIG is effective from 2025-01-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: The XAF 108,449 amount is the arithmetic mean monthly wage in provisional nationally sampled 2022 EHCVM results reported by the government in 2024; it is not a 2026 software-engineer salary. XAF 70,400 is the statutory wage floor. No national median or maximum was published, and a new employment survey was only launched in 2026.

cost_of_living_note.value: The Anker Research Institute estimated a 2025 gross rural living-wage reference of XAF 118,086 per month, including an estimated XAF 5,621 for tax and social security. This is a modeled decent-living benchmark for rural Congo, not a national price index or observed salary.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The report gives approximately USD 207 using its June 2025 exchange rate; Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire can differ materially.
