settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No dedicated nomad status exists. The possible route is a genuine resident card, but its availability for exclusively foreign-client remote work is unconfirmed.
settlement_track.summary: The ordinary resident card is settlement-oriented, and general law provides privileged residence and discretionary naturalization after approximately ten years. The track remains weak because professional activity needs ministry approval and no official filing guidance confirms acceptance of ordinary foreign-contract software work.
settlement_track.notes: If immigration and the competent ministry confirm the professional basis in writing, the route could become materially stronger. Without that confirmation it should not be ranked as a dependable remote-work citizenship route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The law permits personal resident-card applications and contemplates professional activity without invariably requiring a local employer, but requires ministry approval and never expressly authorizes exclusively foreign-client remote work. No dedicated program, software-professional checklist or responsible-ministry guidance was found.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit reviewed more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including nine canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. It established category-based universal-health contributions, current consular and residence-carnet tariffs with an explained legal inconsistency, and a provisional national mean wage. Remaining nulls reflect specific unpublished facts: the professional ministry and acceptance criteria for foreign-client software work, a quantified immigration income threshold and evidence period, the applicable software-professional contribution category, a national median or maximum wage, and a citizenship processing-time standard.

data.selection_summary: Costa Rica has an active, independently accessible digital-nomad stay for ordinary work for a foreign employer or client. It requires USD 3,000 monthly income, or USD 4,000 with dependants, but is legally a non-resident estancia rather than temporary residence and lasts at most two years. No official rule confirms that this status counts toward permanent residence or naturalization or converts directly into qualifying residence. The separate rentista residence can reach permanent residence after three years, but official law does not establish that ordinary foreign salary or freelance receipts constitute the required permanent and stable rent, and remunerated activity requires DGME authorization.

visa_application.title: Tramite Ya — DGME digital application portal
visa_application.notes: Official instructions direct digital-nomad applicants to Tramite Ya. The JavaScript-dependent portal was not text-readable during review; an in-person application is also available by DGME appointment.

best_routes.route_name: Estancia para Trabajadores y Prestadores Remotos de Servicios (Digital Nomad)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: USD 3,000 for an individual or USD 4,000 when requesting status for dependants.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold is denominated in USD and converted at the official BCCR selling rate; no fixed CRC threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 3,000/month individual; USD 4,000/month with dependants
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: CRC equivalent at the official BCCR USD selling rate
income_requirement_display.notes: Official instructions require stable net income originating outside Costa Rica.

income_proof_months.notes: Bank statements or an authorized professional's certification must establish qualifying payments during the previous year.

key_requirements.requirement: Provide paid remote services through digital or telecommunications technology to a person or entity located outside Costa Rica; the income must originate outside Costa Rica.
Show stable net foreign-source income of at least USD 3,000 monthly, or USD 4,000 when including dependants, during the previous year.
Maintain medical insurance throughout the authorized stay with at least USD 50,000 coverage; each dependant must also be insured.
Submit a valid passport, any required entry visa, signed application, and official Spanish translations of foreign-language documents.
Pass DGME criminal/police database checks and, when considered appropriate, biometric security checks.

Pay the USD 100 application fee and, after approval, complete documentation within three months, including the USD 90 document fee, the amount specified in the approval resolution, and a variable guarantee deposit.

initial_validity.value: 1 year
initial_validity.notes: This is a non-resident estancia, not temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: One renewal for 1 additional year; the applicant must maintain the income and insurance requirements and have been physically present in Costa Rica for at least 80 days during the first authorization.
extension_rules.notes: Maximum program duration is normally two years.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No official rule automatically converts or counts the non-resident digital-nomad estancia as temporary residence. A separate residence application requires independent qualification under another category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Conditional path through separately qualifying temporary residence, then three consecutive years in that status; nomad estancia time is not temporary-residence time.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: PGR pages redirected to a script-only portal and migration PDFs failed direct opening; their official indexed text supplied articles 80–87 and the 2024 category-change provisions. A current March 2026 Correos/DGME announcement independently confirms PR after three years of temporary residence. No specific in-country nomad-to-rentista procedure or exit requirement was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires five or seven years of official residence depending on origin. No inspected official source treats digital-nomad estancia as official residence for that clock.

best_routes.notes: Strong ordinary foreign-contract remote-work fit for a temporary stay, but not a citizenship-track route. It does not authorize work for Costa Rican clients or employers and is not temporary residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Law requires permanent and stable monthly rent generated abroad or by Costa Rican national-system banks. It does not expressly classify ordinary salary or freelance contract receipts as qualifying rent.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold is legally denominated as USD 2,500 or its equivalent.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 2,500/month in permanent, stable rent
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a rent requirement, not a published remote-worker salary threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The law fixes the monthly amount, but the current consolidated DGME filing resolution does not prescribe one universal number of bank-statement months for every way of proving permanent and stable rent. The evidentiary period therefore depends on the accepted documentary method and filing instructions.

key_requirements.requirement: Prove permanent and stable rent of at least USD 2,500 monthly arising abroad or from Costa Rican national-system banks.
Obtain DGME authorization before conducting remunerated or profit-making activity while holding temporary residence.
Maintain applicable CCSS insurance for residence renewal.

initial_validity.value: More than 90 days and up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: DGME determines the grant period within the statutory range.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for periods up to the statutory limit while category requirements and required CCSS coverage are maintained.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence if DGME accepts the applicant's income as permanent and stable rent and all filing requirements are met.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After three consecutive years holding qualifying temporary residence, the resident may apply to change category to permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence is not automatic at the three-year mark: article 208 of the immigration regulation requires a change-of-category application and compliance with the applicable filing requirements. This is a genuine settlement route for a qualifying rentista, but ordinary foreign-contract earnings have not been confirmed as eligible rent.

path_to_citizenship.value: Official residence may support naturalization after five years for Central American, Spanish, or Ibero-American citizens by birth, or seven years for other foreigners.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The naturalization clock is based on official residence, not a separate period beginning only after permanent residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because official law does not confirm that ordinary foreign employment or freelance income constitutes permanent and stable rent, and remunerated activity by a temporary resident requires DGME authorization. Filing-level confirmation is needed before treating it as a remote-work solution.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for professionals or specialized technicians

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general income threshold for a sponsor-free, degree-only application is published in the inspected law or consolidated DGME filing resolution.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general degree-only threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No general degree-only income threshold is published
income_requirement_display.notes: Occupation- and authorization-specific filing rules apply.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank-statement period is not applicable as a standardized criterion because the inspected law, immigration regulation, and consolidated DGME resolution do not establish this as a standalone degree-based route with a universal income test. Any financial or activity evidence instead depends on the particular professional authorization and filing basis.

key_requirements.requirement: Fall within the statutory professional, scientist, intern, or specialized-technician temporary-residence category.
Obtain DGME authorization for remunerated or profit-making activity; professional licensing or other occupation-specific evidence may apply.

initial_validity.value: More than 90 days and up to 2 years if approved

extension_rules.value: Potentially renewable for comparable periods while the approved conditions continue.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The statutory category is temporary residence, but current official sources do not establish an ordinary sponsor-free foreign-client application based only on a software-engineering degree.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Three consecutive years of qualifying temporary residence can support an application to change category to permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This later rule does not cure the absence of a confirmed initial route for ordinary foreign-contract work.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through the general five- or seven-year official-residence naturalization rules if qualifying residence is actually obtained and maintained.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because no current official source establishes a sponsor-free, degree-only route compatible with continuing ordinary foreign-client work. The professional category and remunerated-activity authorization require filing-level review.

summary.value: Costa Rican law lists professionals and specialized technicians among temporary residents, but it does not establish a general degree-only remote-worker route. Current official instructions do not establish whether an applicant can qualify without a Costa Rican role, professional licensing, or a specifically authorized activity.
summary.notes: A software-engineering degree is relevant evidence but is not, by itself, a confirmed residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: Under the ordinary regime, an individual generally becomes tax resident after more than 183 continuous or discontinuous days during the fiscal period; qualifying Law 10008 digital-nomad beneficiaries are specifically deemed not to be habitual residents for tax purposes.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The route-specific statutory rule is more relevant while valid digital-nomad status is maintained.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal 2026 rate for an individual carrying on a taxable profit-making activity. It is not the digital-nomad rate or an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Current employee CCSS share shown by CCSS: 5.50% SEM plus 4.33% IVM. This is a local-payroll comparison rate, not a confirmed digital-nomad charge; self-employed contributions vary.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly digital-nomad tax or social-security payment is published. Private insurance is mandatory, but its premium is market-priced.

special_tax_regimes.value: Law 10008 grants qualifying beneficiaries a complete profits-tax exemption, deems them not habitual tax residents, and treats qualifying foreign income as non-Costa-Rican-source. Dependants receive this treatment only if they independently qualify as beneficiaries.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The exemption is tied to valid beneficiary status and qualifying foreign remote income.

taxes.caveats: Treatment changes if the person loses or exceeds digital-nomad authorization, serves Costa Rican clients, earns Costa Rican-source income, registers a local business, or switches to ordinary residence. Home-country and treaty rules may still apply.

taxation_system.value: Costa Rica ordinarily uses a territorial, progressive personal-income-tax system. For 2026, individuals with taxable profit-making activities face annual net-income bands of 0%, 10%, 15%, 20%, and 25%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in the fiscal period under the ordinary rule, subject to the special Law 10008 rule for qualifying digital nomads.
taxation_system.income_scope: Primarily Costa Rican-source income; qualifying Law 10008 foreign remote income is expressly treated as non-Costa-Rican-source and exempt.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Digital-nomad exemption under Law 10008.
taxation_system.social_security: Local employees currently contribute 9.83% to CCSS for SEM and IVM. Self-employed rates depend on reported income and CCSS scales. No mandatory CCSS contribution was confirmed for the non-resident nomad category; private medical insurance is mandatory.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% dashboard figure is the top marginal screening rate for taxable local activity, not an effective rate or the rate on qualifying digital-nomad income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net income up to CRC 6,244,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Individuals with taxable profit-making activities, fiscal year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses the BCCR reference selling rate observed during review.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Individuals with taxable profit-making activities, fiscal year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate upper threshold in USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Individuals with taxable profit-making activities, fiscal year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate upper threshold in USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Individuals with taxable profit-making activities, fiscal year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate upper threshold in USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Individuals with taxable profit-making activities, fiscal year 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket begins at approximately this amount.

taxation_system.notes: Based primarily on official law, tax-authority, CCSS, and central-bank sources.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Qualifying Law 10008 beneficiaries owe 0% Costa Rican profits tax on qualifying foreign remote income. They are statutorily not habitual tax residents, and this income is not Costa Rican-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Special Law 10008 digital-nomad exemption
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% on qualifying foreign remote income while valid Law 10008 status is maintained
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: The ordinary more-than-183-day rule is displaced for the qualifying beneficiary by Law 10008's express non-habitual-resident rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Qualifying remuneration received from abroad is not Costa Rican-source and is fully exempt from Costa Rican profits tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Law 10008 and its implementing regulation.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No mandatory Costa Rican payroll or CCSS contribution was established for this non-resident foreign-employer/client status. Private medical insurance with at least USD 50,000 coverage is mandatory.

fixed_payments.status: Known state fees plus variable insurance and guarantee deposit
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed CCSS payment confirmed for the qualifying non-resident digital nomad.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: USD 100 application fee; after approval, USD 90 documentation fee, an additional amount specified in the approval resolution, and a variable guarantee deposit. An international transfer may incur a USD 15 receiving-bank charge.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed digital-nomad income tax. Private insurance is market-priced.
fixed_payments.notes: The approval-resolution and guarantee-deposit amounts cannot be stated as one universal figure.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Qualifying status supplies the statutory exemption regardless of the ordinary 183-day threshold; home-country taxation may continue.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Law 10008 says the beneficiary is not a habitual Costa Rican tax resident. Ordinary rules must be reassessed if status is lost or the work falls outside the law.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Serving Costa Rican clients, registering local taxable activity, or switching to ordinary residence can trigger progressive tax, VAT, CCSS, and filing obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The route-specific 0% treatment must not be confused with the ordinary 25% top marginal rate.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Digital-nomad approval immediately grants non-resident estancia, not temporary residence. No official conversion timetable is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General rule after three consecutive years of actual temporary residence, followed by a change-of-category application. It matters only after independently obtaining qualifying temporary residence; nomad estancia itself does not satisfy the rule.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalization is measured by five or seven years of official residence depending on origin, not by a separately published fixed period beginning after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No route-specific total can be calculated from digital-nomad estancia: it remains a non-resident status for at most two years, and no inspected law or current official procedure converts it to residence or counts that time. If the person later independently acquires qualifying official residence, the separate naturalization clock is five years for Central American, Spanish, or Ibero-American citizens by birth and seven years for other applicants; it is measured from qualifying official residence rather than added mechanically after permanent residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: TSE publishes a resolution period of 285 business days, approximately 13 working months. Elapsed time can be longer if requirements, publication, corrections, consultation, or appeals remain outstanding.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires five or seven years of qualifying official residence, good conduct, known means of support, Spanish speaking/reading/writing ability, knowledge of Costa Rican history and values, admissible identity and police documents, publication of the application notice, a promise to continue residing regularly and stably in Costa Rica, and an oath to respect the constitutional order. The application statement must renounce the previous nationality unless a dual-nationality treaty applies, although the effect of that statement under the applicant's home-country law requires individual advice.
key_conditions.notes: The TSE regulation says official residence is checked through DGME migration movements and certification of every immigration status, with additional evidence requested when necessary. This makes it inappropriate to assume that digital-nomad non-resident estancia counts. Current MEP materials confirm separate Spanish and Costa Rican history/values examinations, subject to published exemptions.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Naturalization by marriage requires both two years married to a Costa Rican and residence in Costa Rica for that same period.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage matters only if the spouse is Costa Rican and the marriage is registered in Costa Rica. Marriage to another foreigner does not shorten citizenship, although a spouse may be included as a digital-nomad dependant under the higher income threshold.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be registered with the Civil Registry, and the applicant must document the required Costa Rican residence and civil status. Foreign documents must be apostilled or legalized and translated where applicable. Citizenship is not automatic, and false or purely instrumental claims risk refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: TSE publishes a 285-business-day resolution period.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Costa Rica to foreign parents is Costa Rican by birth upon registration by either parent while the child is a minor, or by the child personally before age 25. Citizenship is broadly available by birthplace but not automatic without registration.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: If born in Costa Rica, the child may be registered as Costa Rican by either foreign parent while a minor, or personally before age 25.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The registration condition prevents classification as unconditional jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Costa Rica to a Costa Rican mother or father is Costa Rican by birth. A child born abroad to a Costa Rican-by-birth parent may be registered by that parent while a minor or personally before age 25.

parent_benefit_summary.value: After the child is registered as a Costa Rican citizen, a foreign parent is a first-degree relative of a citizen and may apply directly for permanent residence. The child's citizenship does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must still apply and satisfy DGME requirements.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father of a registered Costa Rican child can seek permanent residence as the citizen's first-degree relative. He does not receive citizenship automatically; naturalization remains a separate TSE process.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and the child's citizenship or registration must be legally documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank observed on 2026-08-15; this index-specific value changes dynamically.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined 44 visa-on-arrival and 8 eTA destinations. Passport Index reports a mobility score of 142; Henley's methodology and totals should not be mixed with this category breakdown.

passport.notes: Passport Index supplies the requested separated breakdown. Henley was retained as a methodology cross-check.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Remote work in English is practical in technology, tourism, and expatriate settings, and the official nomad program emphasizes connectivity. Immigration, tax, civil-registry, and citizenship procedures operate in Spanish, and foreign-language documents require official Spanish translation.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English can support daily remote work but is insufficient for many government filings and eventual naturalization.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian alone is not practical for official administration. No general DGME or TSE filing support in either language was identified; applicants should expect Spanish forms and certified translations.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national measure of Russian- or Ukrainian-language prevalence was published in the inspected sources.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Costa Rica has no statutory maximum salary, and the inspected official statistics do not publish a meaningful national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: General unqualified-worker minimum of CRC 12,436.41 per ordinary day multiplied by 30; occupation-specific schedules apply.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Weighted mean principal monetary salary from ENAHO 2025.

average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is an official weighted survey mean, not a software-engineer salary. The minimum is statutory, not an observed lower percentile.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The official household survey reports income, poverty, and distribution data but not a single defensible national remote-worker cost-of-living amount.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The digital-nomad authorization is a non-resident estancia for one year plus one renewal. Official law does not count it as temporary residence or establish that its time counts toward permanent residence or naturalization.
settlement_track.summary: Costa Rica is a strong temporary remote-work destination but not a citizenship-track match through the nomad route. Settlement requires independently qualifying for and switching to a separate residence category; no automatic conversion or counting rule is published.
settlement_track.notes: The focused audit confirmed the legal distinction between non-resident estancia and temporary residence and found no basis for a route-specific citizenship timeline.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The nomad estancia fits ordinary foreign-employer or foreign-client remote work without a local employer, but only for temporary living; this does not make it a settlement fit.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit using 33 distinct directly relevant URLs, including five new official legal or administrative sources. The rentista permanent-residence note now distinguishes eligibility from the required change-of-category application; the professional-route income-proof null is explained as inapplicable without a standardized degree-only route; and the citizenship timeline notes now reflect TSE rules on official-residence verification, nationality renunciation statements, examinations, and the absence of any nomad counting or conversion rule.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Qualifying temporary residence, for example rentista
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Nomad estancia is a non-resident category. PR can follow a separately approved temporary-residence basis after three consecutive years; ordinary remote salary has not been confirmed as sufficient for the rentista successor.
requirements: Independently qualify for temporary residence; rentista requires stable monthly qualifying rent of at least USD 2,500.
Maintain temporary residence and renew it for three consecutive years before requesting PR.
Comply with any work restrictions and applicable insurance/social-security requirements of the new category.
reviewed_route_names: Estancia para Trabajadores y Prestadores Remotos de Servicios (Digital Nomad)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: PGR pages redirected to a script-only portal and migration PDFs failed direct opening; their official indexed text supplied articles 80–87 and the 2024 category-change provisions. A current March 2026 Correos/DGME announcement independently confirms PR after three years of temporary residence. No specific in-country nomad-to-rentista procedure or exit requirement was confirmed. The unchanged remote-work profile is not confirmed; the conditional alternative requires an additional independently accepted eligibility basis.

data.selection_summary: A potentially usable self-employed pathway exists, but it is not documented as a single immigration program. Official sources separately confirm that a foreigner may register an individual enterprise using a passport, that non-ECOWAS foreigners residing in Côte d’Ivoire can apply for a resident card, and that resident-card renewals accept a commercial register plus tax-clearance certificate from traders. They do not expressly confirm that foreign-client software work is an accepted basis for the first resident card, that entry as a visitor may be converted in-country, or that all time on the resulting card counts toward naturalization. Filing-level confirmation from ONECI and CEPICI is therefore essential.

visa_application.title: ONECI resident-card pre-registration
visa_application.notes: The ONECI-validated resident-card site says pre-registration is mandatory before filing. This is the residence-card application channel, not proof that an ordinary foreign-client software engineer will be approved. Entry visas are separately obtained through SNEDAI.

best_routes.route_name: Individual enterprise / independent worker plus ONECI resident card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum income or bank-balance threshold is published on the official business-registration or resident-card pages checked.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published minimum. Business registration requires a local business address and residence certificate, while resident-card approval remains separate.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; ONECI/CEPICI confirmation required
income_requirement_display.notes: Absence of a published threshold is not assurance of approval or adequate means.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither page specifies a required history of income statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Register an individual enterprise through CEPICI; the official checklist accepts a passport as the manager's identity document.
Provide a local lease or property document, a residence certificate under six months old, birth record, criminal-record declaration and location plan for the business.
For a first resident-card application: passport identity page, visa, entry stamp, birth record, criminal record under three months old and residence certificate under six months old.
Resident-card renewal documentation expressly includes the commercial register and tax-clearance certificate for traders.

An active independent worker of any nationality must affiliate with CNPS; base coverage is 12%, currently XOF 3,600–21,600 per month, with an additional 9% retirement component above the base-income ceiling.

Confirm with ONECI and CEPICI before travel that foreign-client software development is accepted as the business activity and basis for the first resident card; the published sources do not explicitly join these procedures into a guaranteed immigration route.

initial_validity.value: Resident card; a UNCTAD review reports five-year validity since 2017
initial_validity.notes: The current ONECI pages inspected do not state the card's validity period, so the five-year figure should be reconfirmed at filing.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is available; a trader supplies the old card, passport/consular-card copy, commercial-register copy and tax-clearance certificate.
extension_rules.notes: The current checklist does not state renewal duration, filing window or absence limits.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply independently for the ONECI resident card after lawful entry. Published documentation recognizes traders at renewal, but does not expressly state that registering an enterprise guarantees the first card.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a reconstructed pathway from separate official procedures and needs manual confirmation.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The sources establish renewable residence documentation but do not identify a separate permanent-residence status, qualifying period or automatic conversion.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after five years of habitual residence, but it is discretionary, granted by decree after investigation, and the exact treatment of this reconstructed self-employed route is not expressly confirmed.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant must still be habitually resident when the naturalization decree is signed.

best_routes.notes: This is the strongest independently accessible possibility found. It is more promising than the previous record suggested, but it is not an official digital-nomad visa or a clearly named entrepreneur residence category. A passport can start business registration and ONECI accepts resident-card applications from foreigners, yet the published rules do not establish sequencing, conversion from an e-visa, foreign-client acceptability or settlement counting with enough certainty for a positive selection.

This is education attendance rather than a degree-based skilled migration route, provides no confirmed right to retain foreign remote work, and has no direct permanent-residence transition in the sources checked.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing software-engineering degree does not itself confer residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is treated as resident if Côte d’Ivoire is the principal residence or dwelling, if present for at least 183 days continuously or cumulatively, or in the specified case of an overseas employee paid by an Ivorian employer.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A home in Côte d’Ivoire can trigger residence independently of the 183-day test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for the published monthly salary scale, not an expected effective rate and not necessarily the correct classification for sole-proprietor business profits.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Base independent-worker CNPS rate. The official CNPS page also shows an additional 9% retirement contribution on income above the base-plan ceiling.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate minimum of the official XOF 3,600–21,600 monthly base-contribution range, using about XOF 574.8/USD. The upper end is about USD 37.6; additional retirement contributions may apply.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or inbound expatriate personal tax exemption was located. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaties may change source allocation or double-tax outcomes, but PwC reports no general foreign-tax credit under domestic rules.

taxes.caveats: The 32% figure is the top marginal salary rate. A registered sole proprietor may instead have business-income, withholding, VAT, turnover-regime and filing obligations depending on legal form, revenue and where the services are performed. Remote services physically performed from Côte d’Ivoire should not be assumed foreign-source merely because the client is abroad. Obtain Ivorian advice before relying on a treaty or classification.

taxation_system.value: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents generally on Côte d’Ivoire-source income. The official DGI salary scale is progressive from 0% to 32%, while the proper regime for an individual enterprise depends on business classification.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Principal residence or dwelling in Côte d’Ivoire, presence of at least 183 days, or specified Ivorian-employer circumstances.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Côte d’Ivoire-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad regime found; treaty relief is fact-specific.
taxation_system.social_security: Independent workers of any nationality must affiliate with CNPS. Base contribution is 12%, XOF 3,600–21,600 monthly; an additional 9% retirement rate applies above the base ceiling.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 32% is the top marginal salary rate, not the effective burden. Family reductions may apply. Business profits require separate classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax category exists. If the uncertain self-employed/resident-card combination is accepted, ordinary resident and business-tax rules apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: ordinary self-employed/business taxation; no nomad regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 32% on the published salary scale; self-employed business treatment requires classification
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Principal dwelling can trigger residence; otherwise 183 days is an express test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income. Foreign-client receipts should not be assumed exempt, and treaty relief depends on the relevant treaty and facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None located.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: CNPS says every active independent worker, regardless of nationality, must affiliate. Base rate 12%, XOF 3,600–21,600 monthly; additional 9% retirement contribution above the base ceiling.

fixed_payments.status: ordinary self-employed payments potentially applicable
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: CNPS base contribution XOF 3,600–21,600 per month, plus possible 9% complementary retirement contribution.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: SNEDAI lists EUR 73 for the ordinary three-month e-visa. The Service Public resident-card page lists XOF 150,000 for French nationals and XOF 300,000 for other foreigners; current amount should be reconfirmed.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business-registration, lease-registration, tax-clearance, VAT and turnover-regime costs depend on structure and activity; no complete fixed monthly amount was established.
fixed_payments.notes: The visa and resident-card fees are one-time/state-document costs, not monthly tax. No published renewal fee was found.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Even below 183 days, maintaining a principal dwelling can create tax residence; work performed physically in Côte d’Ivoire may also create local-source tax or business obligations.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide income is generally in scope. The 32% dashboard figure is only a top salary-rate screen; confirm whether receipts are employment income, professional profit or enterprise turnover.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect enterprise registration, tax registration/clearance and mandatory CNPS affiliation. The official CNPS base contribution is 12% with a stated monthly range of XOF 3,600–21,600.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No dedicated nomad regime exists; professional advice is required to classify foreign-client software income.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A first resident-card application can be filed after lawful entry, but the official page gives no processing time and no guaranteed self-employed approval timeline.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No separate permanent-residence category or qualifying period was established.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on habitual residence rather than a confirmed prerequisite of permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory residence period before applying for discretionary naturalization. This is not a guarantee and assumes the residence is accepted as habitual and continuous.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable current statutory or typical processing duration was found after checking the consolidated code and procedure materials.

key_conditions.value: Five years of habitual residence before filing; habitual residence must continue when the decree is signed. Naturalization is granted by decree after investigation and remains discretionary. Procedure materials call for identity, residence, conduct/criminal-record, health and means-related evidence.
key_conditions.notes: The sources checked do not provide a clear modern language-test requirement, absence allowance or guaranteed dual-nationality treatment for naturalized applicants.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse may declare for Ivorian nationality five years after celebration of the marriage if marital life has continued and the Ivorian spouse retains nationality.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Time is measured from celebration of the marriage. If celebrated abroad, the marriage must be transcribed in Ivorian civil-status registers before the declaration can be received.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing marriage to a non-Ivorian has no effect on this route.

requirements_and_risks.value: The spouses must maintain a genuine community of life, provable by any means, and the Ivorian spouse must retain nationality. The declaration requires governmental acceptance; annulment can cause loss of nationality acquired through marriage. Sham marriages or false evidence create rejection, loss and potential legal risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: This is a nationality-by-marriage route, not a remote-worker residence solution.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Côte d’Ivoire is Ivorian unless both legally established parents are foreign; therefore birth alone does not give citizenship to a child of two migrant parents. Descent from an Ivorian parent also applies.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child whose two legally established parents are foreign does not receive automatic Ivorian nationality merely by being born in Côte d’Ivoire.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Special rules concerning filiation, adoption or statelessness require case-specific review.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Côte d’Ivoire is Ivorian where one parent is Ivorian, and a child born abroad may acquire nationality by descent from an Ivorian parent, subject to legally established filiation.

parent_benefit_summary.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence for a foreign parent was found merely because the child is Ivorian. The parent would need a separate family/residence basis and may later use the ordinary naturalization framework if eligible.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A citizen child's status and the parent's immigration status are legally separate.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Ivorian, the child can be Ivorian, but the migrant father does not automatically become Ivorian or obtain permanent residence. He should verify family-based resident-card documentation with ONECI.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity/filiation must be legally established.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank on the source, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations in Passport Index's current breakdown.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count; eVisa destinations are treated separately by that index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 33 visa-on-arrival plus 2 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 63. Index methodologies differ: a separate 2026 Henley summary combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access and therefore should not be mixed with this breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Limited outside international-business and expatriate settings. Immigration, business-registration, tax and resident-card materials are primarily in French, and non-French resident-card documents must be translated and certified.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: A software engineer may work with a foreign client in English, but French is practically important for housing, registration, tax and government procedures.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. No official Russian- or Ukrainian-language immigration, tax or business-registration support was found in the government sources inspected; French translation and local assistance would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from the official-language rule and available government interfaces, not a measured speaker-population statistic.

cost_of_living_note.value: The government continues to describe cost-of-living pressure and reports subsidies and price-support measures. Abidjan housing and transport can consume a large share of household budgets, so the XOF 75,000 minimum wage should not be treated as a realistic expatriate or remote-worker budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: There is no dedicated digital-nomad status. The possible route depends on combining enterprise registration with a separately approved resident card.
settlement_track.summary: A renewable resident card could potentially support the five-year habitual-residence naturalization period, but official sources do not expressly confirm the first-card basis for a foreign-client software business or how this exact status is counted. Treat the route as filing-sensitive and not fully matched until ONECI confirms it in writing.
settlement_track.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and no separate permanent-residence milestone was confirmed.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreigners can register an individual enterprise and the resident-card checklist recognizes traders, but no official source expressly says that ordinary software services performed solely for foreign clients qualify for the first resident card or may begin after visitor entry.

data.notes: Major gaps in the previous record were improved with official residence-card, enterprise-registration, tax, social-security and updated nationality sources. Remaining uncertainty is substantive rather than merely missing research: Côte d’Ivoire does not publish a unified self-employed immigration route, first-card approval criteria for foreign-client professionals, a separate permanent-residence framework, or a typical naturalization-processing time.

data.selection_summary: Croatia independently grants qualifying third-country nationals temporary digital-nomad stay for up to 18 months while they work for a foreign employer, foreign client, or their own foreign company. It is an excellent temporary remote-work fit but not a confirmed citizenship-path fit: another digital-nomad application requires a six-month interval, and no compatible conversion route avoiding Croatian employment or substantial Croatian business requirements was confirmed.

visa_application.title: Online Application for Temporary Stay of Digital Nomads
visa_application.notes: MUP continues to list this as its direct online application. The portal returned an internal error during inspection, so applicants should also verify consular or police-station filing options. Visa-required applicants generally need a long-stay D visa after approval.

best_routes.route_name: Temporary stay of digital nomads

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,622.50 using about USD 1.1392 per EUR. The official EUR threshold controls.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,622.50 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The formula is 2.5 times the previous year's average monthly net salary, increased for accompanying family members.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,622.50/month (approximately USD 4,127)
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 3,622.50 monthly; alternatively EUR 43,470 for 12 months or EUR 65,205 for 18 months
income_requirement_display.notes: Verify the current amount displayed by MUP when filing because the wage-based threshold changes.

income_proof_months.notes: MUP accepts payslips for at least six months; a bank statement showing regular income or the full required lump sum is an alternative.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be a non-EU/EEA/Swiss third-country national.
Remote work must be for a foreign employer, foreign client under a service contract, or the applicant's own company registered outside Croatia.
The holder may not work for or provide services to Croatian employers.
Valid passport, private or travel health insurance covering Croatia, sufficient means, proof of purpose, accommodation, and a legalized criminal-record certificate are required.
Documents must be in Croatian or English or accompanied by an authorized translation.

initial_validity.value: Up to 18 months
initial_validity.notes: The permit may be granted for less than 18 months.

extension_rules.value: A permit initially granted for less than 18 months may be extended once, within the overall 18-month limit. A new digital-nomad application may be made only after six months have elapsed following expiry of the previous digital-nomad or legally defined 'other purposes' stay.
extension_rules.notes: This does not provide continuous indefinite renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval directly grants temporary stay; the holder must register an address and obtain a biometric residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A later qualifying work/residence status can lead to five-year long-term residence, but the 18-month nomad stay cannot by itself maintain the necessary continuous residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official long-term-residence page does not expressly exclude the separately named nomad category, but this review did not establish a nomad-specific counting decision or conversion filing sequence. Exit and accrued-time treatment therefore remain uncertain. An ordinary foreign contract alone does not demonstrate eligibility for the employer-based successor.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct route. Ordinary naturalization generally requires eight years of uninterrupted registered residence, permanent-stay status, Croatian-language and cultural knowledge, public-obligation compliance, no security obstacle, and normally release from prior citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Official sources do not establish an eight-year sequence based solely on digital-nomad permits.

best_routes.notes: Suitable for temporary foreign-contract remote work, but rejected for citizenship-oriented selection. Qualifying digital-nomad foreign-work income is exempt from Croatian PIT, and the category is exempt from compulsory Croatian health-insurance contributions while private coverage is maintained.

rejected_routes.route_name: Self-employment through a Croatian company or sole trade

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The applicable amount differs by structure: a self-employed company owner must meet 1.5 times the latest officially published average gross monthly wage, while a sole trader must demonstrate self-employment income of 1.5 times the latest average net monthly wage. Because the statutory reference period differs from the Blue Card's prior-calendar-year formula and changes whenever DZS publishes a new figure, no single stable USD threshold applies to both structures.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Company-owner gross salary or sole-trader net self-employment income of at least 1.5 times the applicable official Croatian average
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Separate investment and Croatian hiring requirements also apply.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 26,544.56 investment, three Croatian full-time employees, and a 1.5× wage/income formula
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR and official Croatian wage statistics
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 26,544.56 investment plus structure-dependent salary or income formula
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a local-business-substance route, not ordinary foreign-client freelancing.

income_proof_months.notes: The current law and MUP summary specify wage/income levels but not one universal number of historical proof months for every self-employment structure.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant generally owns at least 51% of the Croatian company or trade.
A sole owner must invest at least EUR 26,544.56.
At least three Croatian citizens must be employed permanently and full-time at the required wage level.
The applicant must meet the structure-dependent Croatian salary or self-employment-income formula.

initial_validity.value: Combined temporary stay and work permit
initial_validity.notes: No single validity period was established for every ownership structure from the route summary.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires continued compliance with ownership, investment, staffing, wage or income, tax, social-security, and immigration conditions.
extension_rules.notes: Filing-level requirements depend on the business structure.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying owner or sole trader may receive a combined temporary stay and work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially subject to the general five-year uninterrupted qualifying-residence rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a capital-, staffing-, and local-substance-intensive route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential ordinary naturalization after meeting permanent-status and eight-year residence requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not suitable for the supplied ordinary foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial Croatian investment, three Croatian employees, local business substance, and an applicant wage or income formula.

rejected_routes.route_name: EU Blue Card / highly qualified employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: For a standard 2026 application, the statutory threshold is 1.5 times Croatia's official 2025 average gross monthly wage: 1.5 × EUR 2,016 = EUR 3,024 gross per month, approximately USD 3,445 at about USD 1.1392 per EUR. A qualifying applicant whose higher-education qualification was obtained no more than three years before filing may use an 80% threshold, EUR 2,419.20 monthly (approximately USD 2,756). The official EUR formula and the authority's filing calculation control.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,024 gross per month standard threshold for 2026; EUR 2,419.20 under the qualifying recent-graduate exception
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Based on the official 2025 average gross monthly wage of EUR 2,016. The reduced threshold is 80% of the standard threshold and is subject to the statutory recent-qualification conditions.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,024 gross/month standard (approximately USD 3,445); EUR 2,419.20 for a qualifying recent graduate
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR; 1.5× prior-year official average gross wage, or 80% of that threshold for the statutory exception
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 1.5 × EUR 2,016 = EUR 3,024 monthly; possible 80% threshold = EUR 2,419.20
income_requirement_display.notes: The route still requires Croatian highly qualified employment and is not a foreign-contract remote-work option.

income_proof_months.notes: The requirement is a Croatian employment contract of at least six months whose stated salary meets the threshold; the checked sources do not impose a separate history of prior income proof.

key_requirements.requirement: Requires a highly qualified employment contract of at least six months with a Croatian employer.
Requires relevant higher-education qualifications or qualifying high-level professional skills; ICT specialists are among the occupations for which experience may be assessed.
The employment salary must meet the standard or applicable recent-graduate threshold.

initial_validity.value: 48 months, or the employment-contract term plus three months if shorter, capped at 48 months
initial_validity.notes: The current 2025-amended Croatian law supersedes older portal text describing a two-year standard validity.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while Blue Card employment and statutory requirements continue to be met.
extension_rules.notes: The applicant may submit the application personally, but the Croatian employment contract remains mandatory.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Blue Card directly grants temporary residence and Croatian work authorization.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: May lead to long-term residence under the general five-year rules and special EU Blue Card mobility provisions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: It is not a route for retaining the supplied ordinary foreign contract.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential ordinary naturalization after satisfying the separate permanent-status and eight-year residence conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Croatian highly qualified employment contract is mandatory. Personal filing is possible, but that does not remove the local-employment requirement.

summary.value: Admission to Croatian university study can support temporary residence without a local employer, and students may work or be self-employed for no more than 20 hours weekly. Only half of university-study residence counts toward the five-year long-term-residence period. An existing foreign degree alone creates no independent Croatian residence route; the EU Blue Card requires Croatian employment.
summary.notes: This requires Croatian enrollment and is not a route based solely on the applicant's existing software-engineering degree.

tax_residency_rule.value: Domestic tax residence can arise when an individual has Croatian real estate available for an uninterrupted period of at least 183 days in one or two calendar years or is physically present for at least 183 days in one or two calendar years. Treaty residence and tie-breaker rules may override the domestic result.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The domestic test is broader than a simple calendar-year day count.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Route-specific screening rate: qualifying foreign-employer or foreign-activity income earned while holding statutory digital-nomad status is exempt from Croatian PIT. Other income is not necessarily exempt.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Digital nomads are exempt from Croatian compulsory health-insurance registration and contributions but must maintain private insurance. No universal Croatian pension percentage applies to every foreign-contract arrangement; foreign coverage and social-security agreements can control. Ordinary Croatian employment generally uses 20% employee pension and 16.5% employer health contributions.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly Croatian tax or public-health contribution applies to the digital-nomad category. Private insurance is mandatory but market-priced rather than government-fixed.

special_tax_regimes.value: Qualifying foreign-work receipts earned under acquired digital-nomad status are exempt from Croatian PIT. Digital nomads are also exempt from Croatian compulsory public-health-insurance enrollment and contributions while maintaining private coverage.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The exemptions are status- and income-specific.

taxes.caveats: Treatment depends on valid digital-nomad status, payer and contract structure, income source, Croatian presence and accommodation, treaties, and obligations in the employer or home country. The PIT exemption does not eliminate possible foreign tax, payroll, pension, VAT, or permanent-establishment exposure.

taxation_system.value: Croatia has a mixed system: ordinary employment, self-employment, and non-final other income are taxed progressively at locally selected rates, while certain final income uses flat rates. Qualifying digital-nomad foreign-work income receives a 0% exemption.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domestic residence may arise from at least 183 days of presence or uninterrupted availability of Croatian real estate in one or two calendar years, subject to treaties.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally face worldwide taxation and non-residents Croatian-source taxation, except where a statutory exemption or treaty applies.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Qualifying foreign-work receipts earned under acquired digital-nomad status are exempt from Croatian PIT.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary employment generally carries 20% employee pension and 16.5% employer health contributions. Digital nomads are exempt from Croatian compulsory health contributions but need private insurance; pension treatment is contract- and treaty-dependent.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Local governments choose lower rates from 15% to 23% and higher rates from 25% to 33%. The 33% figure is a maximum marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate or the digital-nomad rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual tax base up to EUR 60,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Maximum locally selectable lower rate for ordinary annual income
tax_brackets.notes: The actual lower rate varies from 15% to 23%. USD conversion is approximate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Maximum locally selectable higher marginal rate for ordinary annual income
tax_brackets.notes: The actual higher rate varies from 25% to 33%. This does not override the digital-nomad exemption.

taxation_system.notes: General rates rely partly on current professional tax summaries; the route-specific exemption is supported by Croatian statutory and government material.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Qualifying foreign-work income earned under Croatian digital-nomad status is exempt from Croatian PIT. Croatian-source, property, investment, local-business, or other income may remain taxable.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Special digital-nomad PIT exemption
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% Croatian PIT on qualifying digital-nomad foreign-work income; ordinary Croatian annual income may otherwise reach a 33% top marginal rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domestic tax residence may still arise through the 183-day physical-presence or real-estate-availability tests, subject to treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Employment or activity receipts for an employer not registered in Croatia are exempt when earned under acquired statutory digital-nomad status. Other foreign income is not automatically covered.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Income Tax Act exemption for qualifying digital-nomad receipts and exemption from Croatian compulsory health-insurance contributions, conditional on private coverage.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No Croatian compulsory health contribution applies to this category. Private insurance is mandatory. Pension, foreign payroll, and home-country social security depend on the contract and applicable agreements.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed monthly Croatian tax or public-health contribution confirmed; private insurance and immigration fees remain.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Croatian compulsory health contribution is not payable. No universal Croatian pension payment applies to every foreign-contract arrangement.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: MUP lists EUR 55.74 for temporary stay through a mission or consulate, EUR 93 for visa D where required, and EUR 41.14 for the biometric card. Police-station filing lists EUR 46.45 for temporary stay, EUR 9.29 administrative fee, and EUR 31.85 for a regular card or EUR 59.73 for accelerated production.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No digital-nomad-specific fixed freelancer tax, VAT payment, or financial-transaction tax was established. Other activities or Croatian registration can create ordinary liabilities.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health-insurance premiums are mandatory but no government-set monthly price exists.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Qualifying route income remains covered by the exemption, but source, treaty, and foreign-country obligations still require review.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Croatian residence does not itself erase the status-specific exemption; other worldwide income may enter Croatian taxation.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Croatian trade or company, Croatian customers, or activity outside the digital-nomad definition can trigger ordinary PIT or corporate tax, VAT, payroll, and contributions.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The correct route-specific screening rate is 0%; 33% is only the maximum general marginal rate.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Approval directly grants temporary stay; no prior Croatian-residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Current law sets a general threshold of five uninterrupted years of qualifying temporary residence, asylum, or subsidiary protection. Digital-nomad residence is not among the periods expressly excluded, so an approved nomad period appears capable of contributing to that calculation. No route-specific number is stated because the nomad permit ends after at most 18 months and another nomad application requires a six-month interval; five uninterrupted years therefore require a timely switch to another qualifying status. The earliest general threshold would remain five years from the beginning of counted residence—about 3.5 additional years after a full 18-month nomad permit—but no compatible ordinary foreign-contract status covering that remainder was confirmed, and eligibility ultimately depends on MUP's continuity calculation.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires eight years of uninterrupted registered residence plus permanent-stay status at application; authorities do not state a separate mandatory number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Eight years is the ordinary statutory residence threshold, not confirmation that digital-nomad permits alone provide a viable eight-year sequence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: MUP says duration depends on case complexity and does not publish a reliable typical number of months.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalization requires adulthood, eight years of uninterrupted registered residence, permanent-stay status, Croatian-language and Latin-script knowledge, Croatian culture and social-order knowledge, compliance with public obligations, no security obstacle, and generally release from prior citizenship. Long-term residence generally requires five uninterrupted qualifying years, permitted absences, resources, insurance, and Croatian-language knowledge.
key_conditions.notes: Privileged naturalization grounds have different requirements.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Four years refers to uninterrupted family-reunification or life-partnership temporary residence normally required for permanent stay as a family member of a Croatian citizen. MUP states no separate minimum marriage duration for the later citizenship application.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage or recognized life partnership with a Croatian citizen can support family-reunification temporary residence. After four uninterrupted years on that status, permanent stay may be available; a spouse residing in Croatia with permanent stay may seek citizenship under simplified conditions.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not automatically create immediate permanent stay or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The relationship must be genuine and documented. Spouse citizenship requires permanent stay, Croatian residence, legal-order compliance, paid public dues, and no security obstacle. Authorities may investigate marriages of convenience using factors such as inconsistent personal information, no common language, lack of a marital relationship, or payment for the marriage.
requirements_and_risks.notes: MUP permits retention of foreign citizenship under this privileged ground, but the other country's nationality rules must also be checked.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Croatia alone does not generally confer citizenship; descent and limited protective provisions dominate.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Croatia to two foreign migrant parents does not ordinarily become Croatian by birthplace alone. Limited foundling, unknown-parentage, statelessness, adoption, or later-naturalization rules may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents must regulate the child's immigration status after birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Croatia with one Croatian parent acquires citizenship by origin. A child born abroad to one Croatian parent generally requires registration in the citizenship record by age 21.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a minor Croatian citizen may seek temporary family-reunification residence. Parenthood does not automatically confer permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Ordinary or family-status requirements still apply.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child is Croatian, such as through a Croatian mother, the migrant father may qualify for family-reunification residence as the parent of a minor citizen. He does not automatically acquire citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and the genuine parent-child relationship must be legally documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the research date; index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined 44 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. eVisa destinations are separately classified by the index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 172 and supplies the requested category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Highly practical in major cities, tourism areas, and international remote-work settings. EF EPI 2025 ranked Croatia second among measured non-native-English countries with a very-high-proficiency score of 617; official digital-nomad instructions accept English documents.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI uses a self-selected test-taking population and does not guarantee English service at every authority.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-language digital-nomad application service was identified. Croatian or English should be expected for filings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Local diaspora services may exist, but no reliable national prevalence statistic was published by the checked sources.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of official May 2026 average net earnings of EUR 1,552.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of official May 2026 median net earnings of EUR 1,324.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the EUR 1,050 statutory gross monthly minimum wage; this is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of average monthly net earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of median monthly net earnings.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official national wage release suppresses the open-ended highest decile and publishes no meaningful national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage for 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 1,552 net; EUR 2,178 gross per month
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average earnings for May 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 1,324 net; EUR 1,821 gross per month
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official May 2026 median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum was published. The ninth decile is a percentile threshold, not a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average and median figures are monthly paid earnings for employees in Croatian legal entities; the minimum is the statutory gross wage.
average_citizen_salary.period: May 2026 for average and median; calendar year 2026 for minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: USD values use an approximate ECB EUR/USD conversion and are not fixed amounts.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable official single monthly cost-of-living budget was published. Croatian consumer prices in June 2026 were 4.5% higher than a year earlier; actual housing costs vary substantially by location and tourist season.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Inflation is contextual and was not treated as a monthly living-cost estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The permit lasts no more than 18 months and cannot be renewed continuously. Although the period is not expressly excluded from long-term-residence counting, the route alone cannot provide five uninterrupted qualifying years.
settlement_track.summary: Croatia is a strong temporary-living option for a foreign-contract remote worker but not a confirmed citizenship track. Settlement requires a timely switch to another qualifying status; the ordinary alternatives identified require Croatian employment, Croatian enrollment, family eligibility, or substantial local investment and hiring.
settlement_track.notes: Digital-nomad time appears countable because it is temporary residence and is absent from the statutory exclusion list. That does not create a route-only settlement sequence because of the 18-month cap and six-month reapplication interval.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The status expressly fits work for a foreign employer, foreign client, or the applicant's own foreign company without Croatian employment. This is only a temporary-living fit, not a citizenship-path fit.

data.notes: Focused audit inspected more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including at least five not in the previous source set. The Blue Card income gap was resolved using the current Aliens Act formula and official 2025 wage data. The permanent-residence timeline remains null because no route-specific duration exists without identifying a later qualifying status; its note now explains that digital-nomad time appears countable but cannot independently provide the required five uninterrupted years.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Ordinary stay-and-work permit with a Croatian employer or another independently qualifying residence basis
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A later qualifying work/residence status can lead to five-year long-term residence, but the 18-month nomad stay cannot by itself maintain the necessary continuous residence.
requirements: Qualify independently for the successor permit, for example by obtaining a Croatian employment contract and the required employment authorization.
Arrange the successor before nomad stay expires; a new nomad application is subject to a six-month interval.
Meet continuity, means, insurance and Croatian-language requirements for long-term residence.
reviewed_route_names: Temporary stay of digital nomads
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The official long-term-residence page does not expressly exclude the separately named nomad category, but this review did not establish a nomad-specific counting decision or conversion filing sequence. Exit and accrued-time treatment therefore remain uncertain. An ordinary foreign contract alone does not demonstrate eligibility for the employer-based successor.

data.selection_summary: Cuba has no current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or independently accessible freelance residence route. The eVisa is exclusively for tourism, and foreigners may register as self-employed only after obtaining permanent residence. Published migration reforms expected to take effect 180 days after 5 May 2026 add qualification-based residence grounds, but the professional route requires endorsement by a Cuban state body and is not yet active, so it does not fit ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

visa_application.title: eVisa-Cuba
visa_application.notes: Official direct application portal for Cuba's tourist eVisa, not a remote-work or residence application. Longer-term purposes must be handled through a Cuban consulate or embassy.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies because this is a tourist visa.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published monthly income threshold applies to the tourist eVisa.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly income threshold; tourist use only
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of a remote-worker income test does not authorize employment or foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The official portal does not publish a recurring-income proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport and email for the electronic application.
Passport validity of at least six months, medical travel insurance, return ticket, and DViajeros declaration for entry.
The visa is a tourist visa and does not constitute residence or work authorization.

initial_validity.value: Single entry with a maximum tourist stay of 90 days
initial_validity.notes: The electronic visa may have a separate period within which it must be used.

extension_rules.value: One tourist extension of up to 90 additional days
extension_rules.notes: An extension remains visitor status and does not create a settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No current official source confirms conversion from the tourist eVisa to residence for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Tourist time is not identified as a direct permanent-residence pathway.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The tourist eVisa does not place its holder on a naturalization track.

rejected_routes.notes: Usable for a temporary tourist visit only; it is not a digital-nomad visa or citizenship-path status.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No newcomer residence threshold is applicable.

income_requirement_display.notes: Current rules restrict self-employment to Cuban effective residents and foreign permanent residents.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable to an ineligible newcomer.

Authorized workers must register with the tax administration and comply with income-tax and social-security obligations.

initial_validity.notes: This is an economic registration, not an immigration status.

extension_rules.notes: Not an immigration permission.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Registration follows permanent residence; it is not a route to temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence is a prerequisite, not an outcome.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Self-employment alone does not create a naturalization route.
