minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The published legislation requires lawful financial support but states no monthly threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly CUP threshold is stated.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly threshold published; USD/EUR 1,000 guarantee deposit required under forthcoming rules
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: USD, EUR, or another freely convertible currency
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Non-refundable USD/EUR 1,000 deposit per applicant and accompanying foreign national
income_requirement_display.notes: The deposit is not an income threshold; lawful funds, a Cuban bank account, and medical insurance are also required.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed historical income-proof period is published.

Professional-qualification applications require endorsement from the Cuban state body or entity making the request.
Passport, medical examinations, guarantee deposit, lawful income, Cuban bank account, insurance, acceptable conduct, and social integration.
The migration and foreigners rules were scheduled to take effect 180 days after 5 May 2026 and were not active on the research date.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year of provisional residence under the published future rules
initial_validity.notes: The reform was not yet in force on 2026-08-15.

extension_rules.value: After one year, the authority decides permanent residence within up to 60 business days
extension_rules.notes: Approval remains conditional and discretionary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: If accepted after commencement, provisional residence is the mandatory assessment stage.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The initial decision may take up to 180 business days.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: One year of provisional residence, followed by a permanent-residence decision.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The professional ground requires Cuban state-body endorsement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Published future rules require at least five years as a permanent resident for ordinary naturalization, plus authorized economic activity, integration, record checks, and an examination.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Procedures must be rechecked after commencement.

rejected_routes.notes: Residence-oriented but rejected: it was not active on 2026-08-15 and is not an independent ordinary remote-worker route.

summary.value: Published reforms create a provisional-to-permanent residence ground for advanced qualifications or expertise, but a professional application must be endorsed by a Cuban state body or requesting entity. The rules were not yet effective on 2026-08-15.
summary.notes: Current filing practice and the required endorsement must be rechecked after commencement.

tax_residency_rule.value: Cuban tax liability is status- and source-based in Law 113: Cuban and foreign permanent residents are taxed on income from any country, while persons without permanent residence are taxed on income obtained or generated in Cuba.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The forthcoming 180-day effective-migratory-residence concept is not itself the personal-income-tax rule in Law 113.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate under the general annual PIT scale, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For an authorized self-employed worker, the contribution is 20% of a selected contribution base, not 20% of all gross foreign income.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal USD amount exists: social security depends on a selected CUP base, tax advances depend on income, and exchange-rate segments diverge.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime was identified. Authorized self-employed workers use general rules, including annual PIT settlement, monthly advances, potentially sales or services tax, and social security.
special_tax_regimes.notes: These rules apply only after legal authorization to conduct the activity.

taxes.caveats: There is no lawful digital-nomad fact pattern to which definitive tax treatment can be attached. Treatment of foreign-client services performed physically in Cuba by a non-permanent visitor requires professional source analysis. Permanent residents are expressly within worldwide-income taxation.

taxation_system.value: Progressive PIT applies to covered income. Permanent residents have worldwide-income scope; non-permanent residents have Cuban-source scope under the captured law.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-residence status triggers worldwide taxation; persons without permanent residence are taxed on income obtained or generated in Cuba.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide for Cuban and foreign permanent residents; Cuban-source for persons without permanent residence.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker exemption was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Authorized self-employed workers contribute 20% of a selected contribution base.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 50% is the top marginal screening rate. Law 113 applies 15%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% marginal bands; deductions and exemptions can reduce the effective rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to CUP 10,000
tax_brackets.notes: Historic nominal bracket in Law 113; verify annual-budget modifications before filing.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Excess over CUP 10,000 up to CUP 20,000
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Excess over CUP 20,000 up to CUP 30,000
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Excess over CUP 30,000 up to CUP 50,000
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.
Top marginal band and dashboard screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: Core rates and income scope come from legislation; annual budget rules and taxpayer classification can change the practical computation.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated regime applies because Cuba has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. A permanent resident generally enters worldwide-income taxation; unauthorized work while visiting creates immigration and tax risk.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; visitor or, separately, authorized permanent-resident self-employment
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 50% top marginal PIT under the general scale; not a nomad-specific rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-residence status, not merely 183 days, is the explicit worldwide-income trigger in the captured tax law.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign income of permanent residents is within the tax base regardless of origin. Services performed from Cuba by a non-permanent visitor require professional source analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the current immigration and tax sources reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: An authorized self-employed permanent resident may owe 20% of a selected contribution base plus activity-related taxes. A tourist cannot use these rules to legalize work.

fixed_payments.status: No dedicated digital-nomad fixed-payment schedule applies because Cuba has no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker route. For an already authorized self-employed permanent resident, mandatory social security and tax advances are percentage-based and therefore variable, not a universal fixed monthly amount.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Authorized self-employed workers must contribute 20% of a selected CUP contribution base; the 2024 rules do not establish one universal fixed payment for every worker.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Tourist eVisa fees vary by consulate or payment channel. Forthcoming permanent-residence rules specify a non-refundable USD/EUR 1,000 guarantee deposit per applicant, which is not a monthly tax.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Authorized activity may face a 10% sales or services tax and a monthly PIT advance of 5% of monthly income above the applicable exempt amount, subject to activity-specific rules.
fixed_payments.notes: These are contextual self-employment obligations, not a nomad cost schedule.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe tax-free nomad scenario is established. A visitor is outside worldwide taxation unless permanently resident, but locally performed services may be Cuban-source and may violate visitor conditions.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A foreign permanent resident is within worldwide-income taxation and may face the general progressive scale up to 50%.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Only an already-authorized permanent resident can pursue self-employment registration; obligations may include annual PIT, monthly advances, sales or services tax, and 20% social security on a selected base.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax conclusions are contextual because the requested immigration route does not exist. Obtain Cuban tax advice before performing services from the country.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No current qualifying temporary-residence route exists for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No current selected route exists. Under the not-yet-effective qualification reform, provisional residence would normally be assessed for one year.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Published future ordinary naturalization rule; spouses and parents of Cuban citizens by birth have a published two-year permanent-residence rule.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Cannot be calculated because the applicant lacks a qualifying remote-worker residence route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The law specifies procedural steps but no reliable typical end-to-end processing period.

key_conditions.value: Published future framework: applicable permanent residence, effective presence, authorized economic activity, social integration, criminal-record clearance, citizenship examination, character references, housing evidence, and a declaration of intention.
key_conditions.notes: The package was not yet effective on the research date.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Two years of permanent residence for a spouse, mother, or father of a Cuban citizen by birth; not merely two years of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine marriage or recognized de facto union with an effectively resident Cuban citizen is a published ground for provisional-to-permanent residence. Marriage does not itself confer citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The expanded procedure was not yet active on the research date.

requirements_and_risks.value: Expect civil-registration and housing evidence, guarantee deposit under forthcoming rules, provisional residence, financial support, insurance, and integration review. A marriage contracted solely to obtain permanent residence is a serious migration offense.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Verify current consular instructions and genuine-relationship evidence requirements.

birthright_citizenship.notes: On 2026-08-15 the Constitution broadly covered births in Cuba apart from narrow foreign-government or international-organization exceptions. Law 172, scheduled to commence 180 days after 5 May 2026, would materially condition acquisition for children of nonresident foreigners; recheck after commencement.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Under the constitutional rule applying on the research date, a child born in Cuba generally acquired citizenship even if both parents were migrants, subject to narrow exceptions and registration. The forthcoming law would require regular parental stay and at least 180 continuous days before birth for nonresident parents.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Prospective parents should obtain current civil-registry advice because the published rule was scheduled to change.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Cuba is Cuban by birth, and a child born abroad to a Cuban parent can acquire citizenship after registration and required formalities. This does not automatically naturalize the foreign father.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Foreign-birth registration formalities apply.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Parenthood of a Cuban citizen by birth is a published provisional-to-permanent residence ground and reduces the published naturalization residence requirement to two years of permanent residence. Neither status is automatic.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The relevant migration procedure was not yet effective on 2026-08-15.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father may apply under the family ground after commencement and later use the two-year permanent-residence naturalization rule, but must complete all immigration and citizenship procedures.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, the child's status, residence, support, conduct, and other requirements must be documented.

rank.notes: Dynamic Passport Power Rank checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 42 visa-on-arrival plus 5 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a total mobility score of 72; the breakdown is not a Henley score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low. Government, immigration, banking, tax, and ordinary processes should be expected in Spanish. Remote work is also constrained by slow fixed internet and power-related outages.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: DataReportal reported median fixed download speed of 3.48 Mbps at the end of 2025; Internet Society documented nationwide outages in March 2026.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited. Russian may occasionally appear in tourism, but neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official administrative language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current national proficiency dataset was identified; Spanish remains necessary.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Rough conversion of CUP 6,930 using an informal-market reference near CUP 675/USD; the CUP figure is more meaningful because exchange segments diverge.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No national median is published in ONEI's current 2025 release. The 2026 measures provide a minimum and budget-sector scale, neither of which is a median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate informal-rate equivalent of the statutory CUP 3,210 minimum; not an observed minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate informal-rate conversion.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: ONEI's 2025 publication reports arithmetic means by territory and activity, not a national median. Resolution 15/2026 publishes minimum and budget-sector wage bands, so no defensible median or USD conversion can be supplied.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The CUP 14,535 budget-sector ceiling is not a nationwide maximum. No USD value is supplied because the figure is sector-specific and exchange segments diverge.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: National statutory minimum effective 1 July 2026, reflected in August salary payments.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: ONEI-reported national arithmetic mean for 2025, covering the state civil sector described in the publication.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No national median is published in the current ONEI 2025 release or 2026 salary measures. The value remains null rather than treating an average or scale midpoint as a median.

max_salary_local_currency.value: CUP 14,535 per month (top of the 44-hour budget-sector salary scale; not a nationwide maximum)
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Resolution 15/2026 sets CUP 14,535 for Group XXXII of the 44-hour budget-sector scale and CUP 13,215 for the comparable 40-hour scale. These are sector wage-band ceilings, not national wage caps.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory national minimum, ONEI arithmetic mean for the state civil sector, and the official 2026 budget-sector salary scale; gross/net distinction was not clearly identified
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum and scale effective July 2026; average for calendar year 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are worker wage statistics, not immigration thresholds. USD equivalents are illustrative because Cuba has multiple exchange-rate segments and limited convertibility.

cost_of_living_note.value: Nominal CUP wages convert to extremely low informal-rate USD values, while shortages, inflation, currency segmentation, blackouts, and connectivity costs make simple comparisons misleading.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No precise comprehensive national monthly cost estimate is supplied.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Cuba's eVisa is exclusively tourist entry and does not authorize ordinary remote work or count toward citizenship.
settlement_track.summary: Not eligible: no current ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route exists. Tourist entry cannot be converted through self-employment because foreign self-employment requires pre-existing permanent residence; the forthcoming qualification route is not active and requires state endorsement.
settlement_track.notes: Recheck after the reform package's scheduled early-November 2026 commencement, although its published professional ground still is not an ordinary independent remote-worker program.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Tourist permission is not work residence, self-employment requires prior permanent residence, and the pending professional route requires Cuban state endorsement.

data.notes: The negative remote-work conclusion is well supported, but overall confidence is medium because major migration, foreigners, and citizenship reforms were published in May 2026 and scheduled to take effect 180 days later.

data.selection_summary: Cyprus currently accepts independent applications under its Digital Nomad Scheme and clearly accommodates ordinary remote work for foreign employers or clients. However, the permit is limited to one year plus a renewal of up to two years, and no current official source confirms a digital-nomad-specific route to permanent residence or a renewable status capable of sustaining the general naturalization period. The previously suggested conversion path could not be substantiated. Cyprus is therefore useful for temporary remote residence but not a confirmed citizenship-path match for this profile.

visa_application.title: Digital nomads and family members
visa_application.notes: There is no online filing portal. The official page instructs applicants to file personally or through an authorized representative at the Migration Department's central offices in Nicosia within three months after arrival. Forms and document lists are published separately on the official forms page.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,500 using the retrievable ECB reference value of EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. The binding requirement is the euro amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,500 net per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Required after deduction of taxes and contributions. It increases by 20% for a spouse or partner and 15% for each child.

income_requirement_display.value: €3,500 net/month (approximately US$3,987)
income_requirement_display.notes: The euro threshold controls; the USD figure is only an approximate dashboard conversion.

income_proof_months.notes: The official document list requests detailed bank statements for the preceding six months, together with salary-payment evidence or the specified affirmation where net-income evidence is unavailable.

key_requirements.requirement: Non-EU/non-EEA nationality and location-independent work using telecommunications technology.
Employment by a company registered abroad or self-employment under contracts with clients established abroad; Cyprus employers and clients are excluded.
Employment or service contract lasting at least as long as the requested permit, plus evidence that the work can be performed remotely.
Valid passport, criminal-record certificate, specified medical tests, comprehensive private health insurance, and Cyprus accommodation evidenced by a title deed or rental agreement plus utility bill.
Documents must be officially translated and duly certified or authenticated; biometric data are required.
Application must be submitted in Nicosia within three months after lawful arrival, unless applying while already legally resident under another status.

initial_validity.value: 1 year
initial_validity.notes: This is a temporary residence permit, despite the scheme's use of the word visa.

extension_rules.value: Renewable once for a permit valid for up to a further 2 years; renewal should be filed at least one month before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: The published structure supports a maximum identified scheme period of three years. No further digital-nomad renewal cycle is stated.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The successful application directly produces a Digital Nomad temporary residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The permit is filed after lawful arrival and is not merely visitor permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The nomad permit does not establish an automatic PR path, but a separate permanent Immigration Permit application is possible if the applicant independently qualifies, including for approved self-employed professional activity.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official nomad scheme provides one year plus renewal for up to two years. The European Commission confirms that the self-employed Immigration Permit is permanent; it also requires a domestic need assessment. Official gov.cy pages were readable through search indexing but direct opening returned 403. No reliable nomad-specific five-year counting or guaranteed in-country transition was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: The permit cannot by itself cover the general naturalization residence period. A switch to a separate qualifying status would be necessary, but no ordinary foreign-contract remote-work conversion route was confirmed.
path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization requires a final continuous 12 months plus seven cumulative years in the preceding ten-year period. Whether all digital-nomad residence would be credited was not expressly addressed in the route materials.

rejected_routes.notes: Excellent fit for temporary foreign-contract remote work, but rejected under the citizenship-oriented selection rule because the published permit ends after the identified three-year period and no suitable settlement conversion is confirmed.

rejected_routes.route_name: Category F Immigration Permit for persons living on secured foreign income

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate monthly conversion of the published EUR 9,568.17 annual threshold. The official threshold is annual and denominated in euros.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 9,568.17 secured annual foreign income, plus EUR 4,613.22 per dependent
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Approximately EUR 797.35 per month for the principal applicant, but the official formulation is annual.

income_requirement_display.value: €9,568.17/year secured foreign income
income_requirement_display.notes: The published amount is not evidence that active remote work is permitted under this category.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed official summary states a secured annual-income threshold but does not specify a fixed number of bank-statement months.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must intend to remain as a permanent visitor and not work in Cyprus.
Applicant must have secured annual income from abroad at or above the published threshold.

initial_validity.value: Immigration permit/permanent-visitor status
initial_validity.notes: The reviewed official page categorizes this as an immigration permit for permanent visitors; detailed card-renewal and lapse rules were not established from that page.

extension_rules.notes: Current detailed renewal, absence, and lapse provisions were not located in the reviewed official summary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not the principal status; this is presented as an immigration permit for permanent visitors.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct immigration-permit status is possible for qualifying non-working applicants with secured foreign income.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not make the route compatible with active software work performed from Cyprus.

path_to_citizenship.value: Legal residence may potentially contribute to general residence-based naturalization, subject to all naturalization conditions and continuous lawful residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not usable for the stated profile because the official category is for people who will not work in Cyprus.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an active foreign-client software engineer would still be performing work while physically in Cyprus. The official wording that the holder will not work in Cyprus makes reliance on this route unsafe for ordinary remote work.

summary.value: Admission to a recognized full-time higher-education program supports a renewable student temporary residence permit without a local employer. The educational institution ordinarily applies for the entry permit, student work is restricted, and only graduates at EQF level 7 or higher may obtain up to 12 months after studies to seek employment or establish a business. This is an education route, not a foreign-contract remote-work or direct permanent-residence route.
summary.notes: It is independently relevant to a person pursuing further education, but an existing degree alone does not create residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence arises after more than 183 days in Cyprus in a calendar year, or under the 60-day rule when the person spends at least 60 days in Cyprus, no more than 183 days in another single state, maintains a permanent Cyprus home, and has the required Cyprus business, employment, or company-office tie. From 2026, the former condition of not being tax resident anywhere else was removed from Cyprus domestic law.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Another country may still treat the person as resident; a double-tax treaty tie-breaker and the precise characterization of foreign remote employment require professional analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for 2026, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Published self-employed share of social-insurance contributions on insurable/estimated earnings. The state adds 5.2%. A separate GHS contribution can apply at 4% to self-employed income; foreign employees may instead be affected by treaty, EU coordination, or foreign-system rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer payment was established. Social insurance and GHS are percentage-based, while the nomad permit fees are transactional rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: Cyprus non-domiciled tax residents may be exempt from Special Defence Contribution on dividend and interest income, generally until deemed domiciled after long-term residence. This does not exempt salary or service income from ordinary personal income tax. No special digital-nomad income-tax holiday was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Employment exemptions and corporate/non-dom planning have separate eligibility rules and should not be assumed for an ordinary foreign-employer contract.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on physical presence, whether services performed in Cyprus are Cyprus-source, employee versus self-employed classification, permanent-establishment exposure for a foreign employer, social-security coordination, applicable treaties, deductions, and whether the 60-day rule's Cyprus-tie conditions are met.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax on residents' worldwide income, with 2026 rates from 0% to 35%. Non-residents are generally taxed only on specified Cyprus-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days, or the qualifying 60-day rule with Cyprus ties.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for Cyprus tax residents; specified Cyprus-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Non-domiciled residents can receive Special Defence Contribution relief on passive income, but there is no verified digital-nomad exemption for employment or freelance income.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed persons generally pay 16.6% of insurable estimated earnings, with possible assessment on actual earnings, plus potentially 4% GHS. Foreign-employee coverage requires contract- and treaty-specific review.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 35% is the top marginal rate. It applies only to taxable income above EUR 72,000; lower slices are taxed at 0%, 20%, 25%, and 30%.

tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable income exceeding the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate; threshold approximately converted.

taxation_system.notes: Current 2026 brackets are supported by a Cyprus government business portal and Tax Department material. Cross-border treatment still requires individualized advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The scheme itself does not create a special tax exemption. Its official page says a holder exceeding 183 days in the same tax year is considered Cyprus tax resident, subject to its stated conditions; the wider Cyprus tax rules, including the revised 60-day rule, can also matter. A tax resident is generally taxed on worldwide employment or business income under progressive rates up to 35%.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary resident remote employee or foreign-client self-employed person; tax classification depends on the underlying contract.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–35% progressive PIT; 35% is the top marginal screening rate, not an effective-rate estimate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days, or potentially the separate 60-day rule with the required Cyprus home and economic tie.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is generally within Cyprus PIT for tax residents. Non-residents are taxed only on specified Cyprus-source income, but services physically performed in Cyprus require source analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad PIT holiday was verified. Non-dom relief concerns Special Defence Contribution on passive income and does not generally shelter salary or service income.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Coverage depends on employee/self-employed characterization and international coordination. Cyprus self-employed social insurance is published at 16.6% of insurable earnings, and GHS is 4% for self-employed income. Do not automatically apply those rates to a foreign employee remaining in a foreign social-security system.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly tax or contribution confirmed.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based obligations may apply; no route-specific monthly minimum was established.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: EUR 70 for issue or renewal of the temporary residence permit, plus EUR 70 for initial registration in the Aliens' Registry.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Private health insurance is mandatory but no official standard premium is fixed. VAT registration is generally required once taxable transactions exceed EUR 15,600 over the relevant period; cross-border place-of-supply rules may alter the result.
fixed_payments.notes: Permit fees are not monthly taxes. Insurance premiums depend on provider and coverage.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay below the domestic residence thresholds does not by itself eliminate Cyprus-source, payroll, permanent-establishment, or home-country tax questions.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect worldwide employment or service income to enter the progressive PIT computation, potentially reaching 35%, with treaty relief considered separately.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Self-employed registration can bring income-tax filing, 16.6% social insurance on assessed insurable earnings, possible 4% GHS, record-keeping, and VAT obligations. Digital nomads must not serve Cyprus clients.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Immigration eligibility is clear, but tax and social-security outcomes vary materially with the foreign contract and treaty position.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The approved digital-nomad application directly grants temporary residence; no preliminary years of residence are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No official digital-nomad-to-permanent-residence timeline or conversion was confirmed. The published digital-nomad permission ends after the identified maximum three-year period.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Cyprus naturalization is based on qualifying legal residence rather than a simple fixed number of years after permanent residence, so this breakdown would be misleading.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General screening timeline: seven cumulative years of legal residence in the relevant preceding period plus the final 12 months of legal and continuous residence. This is not a digital-nomad-only timeline because that permit does not last eight years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No general M127 processing-time commitment was published on the reviewed official route page. Faster timelines associated with specified highly qualified employment should not be applied to this ordinary remote-worker profile.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires the prescribed residence record, a final continuous 12-month period with no more than 90 days' absence, good character, Greek at B1, successful knowledge testing on Cyprus's contemporary political and social reality, suitable accommodation, and stable regular resources. Approval is not automatic merely because the time threshold is met.
key_conditions.notes: No suitable status allowing the applicant to remain an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker throughout this full period was confirmed.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Three years of marriage or civil partnership before applying. Couples residing in Cyprus must also show at least six months' residence in each year and at least two years' aggregate residence during the preceding three years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage or civil partnership counts toward the three-year requirement. Applicants permanently residing abroad may also apply after three years of marriage or partnership.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not confer citizenship automatically; an M125 application and approval are required.

requirements_and_risks.value: The application requires civil-status evidence, certified translations/authentication, a EUR 300 fee, two EUR 8.54 stamps, and a declaration of harmonious cohabitation after approval. False documents, sham relationships, or misleading cohabitation claims create rejection, revocation, and possible criminal or immigration risks.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official process expressly relies on proof of the qualifying relationship and harmonious cohabitation.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Cyprus alone is not a generally applicable grant of citizenship. The main rule is descent/registration through Cypriot origin, with narrow statutory cases rather than broad jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Cyprus to two foreign temporary or permanent residents does not ordinarily become Cypriot solely because of the place of birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth registration and a Cypriot birth certificate are distinct from citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Cypriot parent is generally eligible for citizenship by descent or registration, subject to the applicable form, date-of-birth rules, parentage evidence, and statutory exceptions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Complex cases involving contested parentage or the island's divided territory require individual legal review.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a minor Cypriot citizen may qualify for facilitated family-member residence as a direct ascendant if parental care and contact rights have not been removed by a court. Parent citizenship is not automatic.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The residence benefit depends on the child actually being a Cypriot citizen and on genuine parental responsibility.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father can potentially seek family-member residence where his child is Cypriot and he retains parental care/contact rights, but the child's citizenship does not directly naturalize the father or erase normal citizenship requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: If the other parent is merely a permanent resident rather than a citizen, local birth does not ordinarily make the child Cypriot.

rank.notes: The current Henley page is interactive; the Cyprus-specific 2026 figure was cross-checked against a secondary summary citing Henley.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's score combines destinations accessible without obtaining a visa before departure, including visa-on-arrival access; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The reviewed Henley presentation did not publish a Cyprus-specific visa-required-in-advance total, and no equally current authoritative separated count was established.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The 174-point Henley score does not provide a Cyprus-specific split between pure visa-free, visa on arrival, and eTA in the reviewed material.

passport.notes: Rank and access score are current screening figures. Entry rules change frequently and should be checked with the destination before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for daily remote-work practicality: an official Cyprus statistical publication says English is widely spoken, although government filings and certified documents may still require Greek or Turkish.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English is widely usable but is not constitutionally an official language of the Republic.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Official sworn-translation services are available for both Russian and Ukrainian, but no reliable current evidence established that either language is sufficiently widespread for government dealings or everyday nationwide use. English or Greek remains more practical.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Availability of certified translators should not be confused with general community-language coverage.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the reported 2025 average monthly wage of EUR 2,605.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the reported 2025 median monthly wage of EUR 1,968.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory EUR 979 full-time minimum during the first six continuous months with the same employer. This is a legal minimum, not the lowest observed salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 average for Cypriot-citizen employees, EUR 2,506 gross monthly.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 median for Cypriot-citizen employees, EUR 2,053 gross monthly.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Cyprus has no national maximum salary. Published sector averages and open-ended distribution groups are not individual maximum wages.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 979/month for the first 6 months; EUR 1,088/month thereafter
min_salary_local_currency.notes: National statutory gross minimum for covered full-time employees from 1 January 2026; exclusions can apply to specified occupations.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average for Cypriot-citizen employees in final 2024 data.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median for Cypriot-citizen employees in final 2024 data.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum was published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly employee earnings; minimum field is the statutory full-time minimum.
average_citizen_salary.period: Citizen-specific averages: 2024 final data; national minimum: effective 2026.
average_citizen_salary.notes: For the overall labor market, the government reported a 2025 average of EUR 2,605 and median of EUR 1,968. Citizen-specific finalized figures are retained separately because the schema asks for an average citizen salary.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No current official single-person cost-of-living budget or nationally comparable monthly figure was established. Private crowd-sourced city estimates were not substituted for an official national measure.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Digital Nomad permit is limited to one year plus up to two additional years. No suitable ordinary-remote-work status was confirmed for the remaining permanent-residence or naturalization period.
settlement_track.summary: Cyprus offers a genuine temporary residence permit for foreign remote workers, but the published route ends after the identified three-year period. The previous record's assumed conversion path was not supported by a named official mechanism, so the route should not be ranked as a citizenship path.
settlement_track.notes: Some lawful digital-nomad residence might potentially be relevant to a later naturalization residence calculation, but official materials do not confirm the credit or supply a compatible follow-on status. That uncertainty is insufficient under the selection rules.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The scheme expressly accepts employees of companies registered abroad and self-employed people serving clients abroad, without a Cyprus employer or client. This is a strong temporary-living fit but not a settlement fit.

data.notes: Audited against the prior Cyprus record. The active digital-nomad route, income threshold, document requirements, tax bands, wages, citizenship conditions, and family rules were refreshed. The material correction is downgrading the country to temporary-nomad-only because no official ordinary-remote-worker conversion to permanent or sufficiently long renewable residence was established.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Category-D self-employed professional Immigration Permit or another independently eligible Immigration Permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The nomad permit does not establish an automatic PR path, but a separate permanent Immigration Permit application is possible if the applicant independently qualifies, including for approved self-employed professional activity.
requirements: For Category D, prove appropriate professional qualifications, adequate funds and demand for additional members of the profession.
Obtain the Immigration Permit under its own admission criteria; foreign remote income alone is insufficient.
reviewed_route_names: Cyprus Digital Nomad Visa Scheme
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The official nomad scheme provides one year plus renewal for up to two years. The European Commission confirms that the self-employed Immigration Permit is permanent; it also requires a domestic need assessment. Official gov.cy pages were readable through search indexing but direct opening returned 403. No reliable nomad-specific five-year counting or guaranteed in-country transition was established.

data.selection_summary: Czechia has two relevant independent paths. The active Digital Nomad Programme directly covers foreign-employer remote workers and freelancers in IT, but only nationals of specified countries; the applicant’s nationality is unknown. The general business route can support genuine Czech-registered self-employment for a foreign client and counts toward settlement, but does not fit someone remaining solely a foreign employee. Confirm nationality and contract classification before treating Czechia as a match.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad Program
visa_application.notes: Official programme-information and admission page, not an online visa portal. The applicant emails the Ministry of Industry and Trade for programme inclusion and, if admitted, files the long-term visa or residence application at a Czech embassy or consulate.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Programme — foreign-employer IT specialist or IT freelancer

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion at CZK 21.076/USD. The programme requires at least 1.5 times the announced average gross salary; the 2026 reference of CZK 51,497 produces approximately CZK 77,246 monthly.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Approximately CZK 77,246 per month (1.5 × CZK 51,497)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Formula-based threshold that should be recalculated using the figure applicable when filing.

income_requirement_display.value: About CZK 77,246/month (approximately USD 3,665)
income_requirement_display.notes: Minimum contractual salary or prorated service-contract remuneration, not an account-balance requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: The official rules do not prescribe a minimum income-history period. They instead require a qualifying employment or client contract showing remuneration and continued remote work.

key_requirements.requirement: Nationality must be Australia, Brazil, Canada, India, Israel, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, the United Kingdom or the United States.
Applicant must perform highly qualified IT or marketing work; software engineering fits the IT category.
IT applicant needs relevant STEM tertiary education or at least three years of documented IT experience.
A foreign employee remains employed by a foreign employer with at least 50 employees worldwide and must have permission to work remotely.
A freelancer must obtain or undertake to obtain a Czech trade licence for IT or marketing and document a qualifying client contract.
The visa filing requires passport, purpose documentation, accommodation, funds, criminal-record documentation and insurance.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to 1 year through the applicable long-term visa
initial_validity.notes: Foreign employees generally use an 'other purpose' long-term visa; freelancers use a business-purpose long-term visa.

extension_rules.value: A foreign employee may seek renewed programme inclusion and follow-on long-term residence for the same purpose. A freelancer may continue through business-purpose long-term residence, generally issued for up to 2 years.
extension_rules.notes: Continued eligibility and fulfilment of the declared purpose must be documented.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Programme inclusion facilitates an embassy filing and 45-day processing for the applicable long-term visa or residence application.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Programme inclusion is discretionary and does not itself grant residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Long-term visas and subsequent long-term residence permits count toward the normal five-year continuous-residence requirement for permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Continuity and permitted-absence rules apply.

path_to_citizenship.value: After permanent residence, an ordinary third-country national may generally qualify after five years of permanent residence or when permanent residence plus immediately preceding lawful residence totals at least ten continuous years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation remains discretionary and requires language, civics, presence, income, criminal-record and tax-compliance conditions.

best_routes.notes: This is a direct ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route for eligible nationalities and is settlement-oriented rather than visitor-style. Eligibility remains uncertain solely because nationality and employee-versus-freelancer classification were not supplied.

best_routes.route_name: Long-term visa and residence for doing business — self-employed licensed trade

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no universal monthly salary threshold for the initial general business visa. It uses a lump-sum funds requirement, while follow-on residence applies a household-income formula.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Initial visa: CZK 156,500 in available funds; follow-on residence: stable household income sufficient under the statutory living-and-housing-cost formula
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: CZK 156,500 is a balance requirement, not monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: CZK 156,500 available funds initially; no universal monthly income floor for follow-on residence
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: CZK balance and statutory household formula
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: CZK 156,500 initial balance; later income must cover applicable subsistence and housing amounts
income_requirement_display.notes: The follow-on amount varies by household composition and housing circumstances.

income_proof_months.notes: Where regular income cannot be proved another way, the official portal permits bank statements showing stable income for at least the preceding six months. Established self-employed applicants normally use tax and contribution documents.

key_requirements.requirement: Carry on genuine business, licensed trade or self-employment in Czechia and maintain that purpose.
Register in the Trade Licensing Register, Commercial Register or relevant professional register.
Apply in person through an eligible Czech diplomatic mission; mission-specific business-visa quotas may apply.
Provide accommodation, funds, criminal-record documents where required, insurance and business-purpose evidence.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: A visa issued for less than one year can generally be extended only to one year in total.

extension_rules.value: Before expiry, the holder may apply in Czechia for business-purpose long-term residence, generally issued for up to 2 years and renewable while conditions remain satisfied.
extension_rules.notes: This is a staged visa-to-residence route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The independently filed business visa grants lawful long-term temporary residence and can transition to business-purpose long-term residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant must conduct genuine Czech-registered business rather than merely use a trade licence as a residence device.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The long-term business visa and subsequent long-term residence count toward permanent residence after five years of continuous qualifying residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The standard permanent-residence application normally requires Czech-language certification.

path_to_citizenship.value: The route can support the ordinary approximately ten-year naturalisation timeline: about five years to permanent residence and ten total years of qualifying lawful residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is discretionary, not automatic.

best_routes.notes: This route fits a genuine independent contractor willing to use Czech-registered self-employment and comply with Czech business, tax and insurance rules. It does not fit someone who will remain solely an employee of a foreign company.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visa-free or short-stay remote work followed by in-country legalisation

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No qualifying income threshold exists because visa-free presence is not an eligible work or long-term residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold applies to this rejected visitor-status scenario.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable — visa-free presence is not an ordinary business-residence legalisation route
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status is not the qualifying route.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history requirement applies because this is not a qualifying residence route.

key_requirements.requirement: Visa-free presence is limited to eligible short-stay purposes and generally cannot be converted into an ordinary long-term business visa inside Czechia.

initial_validity.value: Normally up to 90 days under Schengen or an applicable bilateral arrangement
initial_validity.notes: Nationality-specific rules apply.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary conversion to self-employed residence from visa-free status
extension_rules.notes: The initial long-term visa normally must be filed at an eligible Czech diplomatic mission.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No ordinary in-country route from visitor status
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate qualifying long-term application is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Visa-free presence does not count toward the standard five-year permanent-residence period.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Only qualifying long-term residence periods are relevant.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from the visitor stay itself
path_to_citizenship.notes: A separate qualifying residence track is required.

rejected_routes.notes: Entering as a visitor, opening accounts or obtaining a trade licence and then attempting ordinary in-country legalisation is not the verified route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employee Card or Blue Card for Czech employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The two employment permits have different salary tests, and both require Czech employment. No single USD threshold is applicable to this grouped rejected route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Employee Card: above the basic minimum wage; Blue Card: at least 1.5 times the applicable average gross salary
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The permits have different statutory tests.

income_requirement_display.value: Employee Card: above CZK 22,400/month in 2026; Blue Card: at least 1.5× the applicable average gross salary
income_requirement_display.notes: Excluded because both routes require Czech employment.

income_proof_months.notes: The official requirements use a qualifying employment or pre-employment contract rather than a prescribed history of prior income.

key_requirements.requirement: Requires qualifying employment with a Czech employer and the applicable vacancy or contract documentation.
A Blue Card requires highly qualified employment and salary of at least 1.5 times the applicable average gross salary.

initial_validity.value: Permit-specific and tied to the approved Czech employment
initial_validity.notes: A Blue Card may generally be valid three months beyond the contract, up to three years.

extension_rules.value: Continuation remains tied to qualifying Czech employment and permit conditions.
extension_rules.notes: This does not preserve the foreign-contract scenario.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Can grant employment-based long-term residence, but only for Czech employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not independently usable by an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Qualifying employment residence may count toward settlement, but requires abandoning the selected foreign-contract scenario.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Rejected on route-fit grounds, not because employment residence can never settle.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through ordinary settlement rules after qualifying residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: The employment permit does not directly confer citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the selection requires an independent route without a local employer or job offer.

summary.value: A foreign degree alone does not create an independent Czech residence entitlement. The nine-month job-seeking or starting-business permit is limited to people who completed an accredited university programme or qualifying research in Czechia while holding the corresponding Czech residence status.
summary.notes: The applicant’s foreign degree can satisfy the Digital Nomad Programme qualification criterion but does not independently grant residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally Czech tax-resident if they have a permanent home in Czechia in circumstances indicating an intention to live there, or spend at least 183 days there during a calendar year. Treaty tie-breakers can override domestic dual-residence results.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Every started day generally counts toward the 183-day test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate; the lower marginal rate is 15%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage accurately describes the self-employed scenario because pension and health contributions use different assessment bases, minimum advances and possible international-coverage exceptions.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate combined ordinary minimum advances for main self-employment from July 2026: CZK 5,005 social plus CZK 3,306 health, converted at about CZK 21.076/USD. Starter and international-coverage exceptions may change this.

special_tax_regimes.value: Eligible self-employed taxpayers may elect the Czech flat-rate regime. From July 2026 the three monthly bands are CZK 9,162, CZK 16,745 and CZK 27,139, combining income tax, pension and health components.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is an optional general self-employed regime, not a special digital-nomad exemption.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on whether the applicant remains a foreign employee or becomes Czech-registered self-employed, treaty residence, permanent-establishment exposure, social-security coordination, deductions and VAT place-of-supply rules. Cross-border professional advice is appropriate.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with 15% and 23% marginal rates. Czech residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents generally on Czech-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-home/intention test or at least 183 days in the calendar year, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for Czech residents; generally Czech-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Optional flat-rate self-employed regime when statutory conditions are met; no dedicated digital-nomad income-tax exemption was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: For main self-employment from July 2026, the standard minimum social advance is CZK 5,005 monthly and the 2026 minimum health advance is CZK 3,306. Actual liability may be higher and international coordination can change coverage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 23% is the top marginal screening rate, not an estimated effective rate. For 2026, the annual high-rate threshold is CZK 1,762,812.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Tax base up to CZK 1,762,812 annually in 2026
tax_brackets.applies_to: Taxable personal-income base within the lower bracket
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at CZK 21.076/USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Tax base above CZK 1,762,812 annually in 2026
tax_brackets.applies_to: Only the portion of the tax base above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not a flat rate on all income.

taxation_system.notes: Based on official Czech tax, social-security and health-insurance sources; individual treaty and worker-classification analysis remains fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special digital-nomad tax holiday was found. A Czech tax-resident participant should expect ordinary worldwide-income analysis. Czech-registered freelancers normally face PIT plus social and health obligations; foreign employees require individual payroll and social-security analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary foreign employment or Czech self-employment, depending on programme category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive PIT: 15%, then 23% above the 2026 high-income threshold; 23% is the top marginal screening rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-home/intention test or at least 183 days in a calendar year, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Czech tax residents generally report worldwide income, including foreign employment or client income; treaty relief depends on the other jurisdiction.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad exemption confirmed. The ordinary self-employed flat-rate regime may be available if its conditions are met.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary self-employed minimums from July 2026 are generally CZK 5,005 social and CZK 3,306 health monthly. Foreign employees require employer, treaty and applicable-legislation analysis.

fixed_payments.status: Confirmed ordinary Czech self-employment minimums; no special fixed nomad levy
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Main-activity self-employed minimum social advance CZK 5,005/month from July 2026 and minimum health advance CZK 3,306/month for 2026; qualifying new entrepreneurs may have different social advances.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Long-term business visa CZK 5,000; extension of a shorter business visa CZK 1,000; follow-on business long-term residence CZK 2,500.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Optional 2026 flat-rate payments are CZK 9,162, CZK 16,745 or CZK 27,139 monthly by band. VAT turnover thresholds are CZK 2,000,000 and CZK 2,536,500 per calendar year, with differing registration timing.
fixed_payments.notes: Actual-income calculations, foreign social-security coverage, starter exceptions and private-insurance requirements can materially change the amounts.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if the permanent-home/intention test is met. Czech-source income, local business, VAT or social-security obligations may still arise.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Assume Czech worldwide-income reporting and treaty analysis. Ordinary 15% and 23% PIT brackets apply unless another statutory treatment controls.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect Czech registration, tax records, PIT or eligible flat-rate tax, social and health contributions, debt-clearance evidence for residence renewal and VAT review.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No official special digital-nomad tax concession was identified.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The successful long-term visa itself grants temporary lawful residence; no preliminary years are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five years is the normal total continuous qualifying-residence requirement.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: An ordinary third-country national generally needs five years of permanent residence or permanent residence plus immediately preceding lawful residence totalling ten continuous years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Screening estimate assuming five years to permanent residence and ten total years of continuous lawful residence; naturalisation remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Ministry’s decision period is generally 180 days after receipt; transfer time and suspended proceedings may lengthen elapsed time.

key_conditions.value: Maintain the declared remote-work or business purpose, comply with continuity and absence rules, obtain permanent residence, meet Czech-language requirements, and demonstrate presence, civics knowledge, lawful income, clean record and tax/contribution compliance.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary and creates no legal entitlement.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A close family member of a Czech citizen permanently residing in Czechia may seek permanent residence after two years of continuous temporary residence if they have been that citizen’s family member for at least one year. This accelerates PR, not citizenship automatically.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Czech citizen can support family residence and accelerated permanent residence once the residence and family-duration conditions are met. Marriage alone does not confer citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Naturalisation residence conditions may only be waived under statutory discretion; no automatic fixed marriage-to-citizenship period was confirmed.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must prove the family relationship and qualifying residence. Authorities may examine whether the relationship and shared family life are genuine. Sham marriage or false documents can result in refusal, revocation and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage should not be treated as a guaranteed citizenship shortcut.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Czechia alone normally does not confer citizenship. Citizenship primarily follows a Czech parent, subject to narrow anti-statelessness and foundling provisions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Normally no Czech citizenship merely from birth in Czechia. Parents must arrange the child’s corresponding residence status, generally within 60 days. Narrow anti-statelessness rules may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Czechia does not have broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child generally acquires Czech citizenship by birth if at least one parent is a Czech citizen on the birth date, regardless of birthplace. Special paternity-establishment rules may apply in some cases.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The foreign parent does not acquire citizenship automatically.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent who is the primary carer of a Czech/EU-citizen child under 21 may qualify as a close family member for residence purposes. This can support residence and later permanent residence, but not automatic naturalisation.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must independently satisfy the applicable residence conditions.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no citizenship benefit merely because a child is born in Czechia. If the child is Czech through the other parent and the father is the primary carer, family-member residence may be available; citizenship remains separate and discretionary.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Legal parentage and genuine caregiving must be documented.

rank.notes: Guide Passport Index rank checked on 2026-08-15; index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Includes 27 eVisa destinations and 17 requiring a traditional visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 30 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 13 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: The index reports facilitated access to 185 destinations when visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA access are combined.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate. English is workable in international IT workplaces and major cities, but Czech is needed for many administrative matters and fuller integration; foreign documents generally require certified Czech translations.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Nationwide English practicality is lower than the experience in Prague or Brno technology workplaces may suggest.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The current official nationwide language and administrative sources do not quantify ordinary private-service availability in Russian or Ukrainian. Neither language substitutes for Czech in administrative proceedings.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of CZK 50,282 at about CZK 21.076/USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 structural wage median of CZK 44,337.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the statutory 2026 minimum wage, not an observed lowest salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate Q1 2026 national gross average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2025 national structural wage median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official earnings distribution reports quantiles rather than a meaningful national maximum. An observed sample maximum would be outlier-dependent, so no USD maximum is stated.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage for a standard 40-hour week in 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National-economy average for full-time-equivalent employees in Q1 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Structural wage median for 2025.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current official distribution does not publish a meaningful national maximum monthly wage; the value remains null rather than substituting a percentile or outlier.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly employee wages; minimum field is the statutory minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum: 2026; average: Q1 2026; median: 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are ordinary employee wage indicators, not immigration income thresholds. USD amounts are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: The Czech Statistical Office’s 2025 Household Budget Survey reports average household consumption expenditure of CZK 216,214 per person annually, approximately CZK 18,018 per person monthly. Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels accounted for CZK 54,042 annually, about CZK 4,504 per person monthly. A separate 2025 living-conditions survey found average housing expenditure of CZK 8,897 per household nationwide and CZK 10,872 in Prague; housing represented about 16% of net household income nationwide and 17.4% in Prague. These are resident-household averages, not a newcomer budget: rent, household size, tenure and city materially affect actual costs.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The flagged null is resolved using current official household-expenditure and housing-cost evidence. Per-capita monthly figures are annual survey totals divided by 12. The Prague and nationwide housing figures are household-level SILC measures and should not be added directly to the per-capita HBS total. Eurostat and the European Commission sources were checked as contextual affordability evidence; they show that housing burdens vary substantially by tenure, income group and region.

data.selection_summary: DRC has a three-year renewable ordinary establishment visa for profit-making liberal professionals that does not expressly require a local employer or client. It may accommodate an independently registered software professional, but official materials require professional approval or a licence, RCCM and tax registration, at least USD 5,000 in a local bank, and six months of prior lawful stay; they do not confirm that ordinary freelance software engineering qualifies. Permanent establishment may follow 15 years of uninterrupted lawful residence, while naturalization is highly discretionary. Written DGM confirmation is essential.

summary.value: A one-year renewable study establishment visa is available with admission, financial support, accommodation and sufficient resources. It is education-based rather than degree-based independent migration.
summary.notes: No official source confirmed that study time counts toward permanent establishment or permits unrelated remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: Residence is broadly factual: a real, effective and permanent home, family, centre of vital interests or business can establish residence. Authorities also examine presence exceeding 183 days, a local lease, business address and organizational role; residence may be treated as beginning on entry.
tax_residency_rule.notes: This is broader than a simple 183-day test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top statutory marginal screening rate. IPR on taxable salary is capped at 30% of taxable salary, so 40% is not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the worker pension share for covered employment, not a confirmed charge on a newly registered independent professional. Covered employers additionally bear 5% pension, 1.5% occupational-risk and 6.5% family-benefit contributions: 13% employer and 18% combined. The law covers specified employees and active company associates; voluntary continuation is limited to someone previously affiliated for at least three years, including the final six consecutive months. No reviewed source establishes that a first-time self-employed software professional must pay the employee rate.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed mandatory monthly CNSS, health-insurance or freelancer payment in USD is published for a first-time independent professional. Verified CNSS charges are percentage-based for covered employment. Voluntary contributors bear their contributions, but voluntary continuation requires prior insurance and no fixed amount for this applicant is published. Visa and registration fees are transactional rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker regime was found. Personal-income-tax reform took effect on 1 January 2026, leaving classification of an independent software professional uncertain.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Obtain advice on the 2026 IRPP classification before registering.

taxes.caveats: Treatment depends on classification as salary, foreign-source profit, locally performed service income or business income. PwC’s April 2026 summary reports foreign-source profits exempt and says non-salary income was historically not subject to IPR in practice, while the 2026 reform reorganizes taxation of personal income. Foreign payment alone does not establish foreign source.

taxation_system.value: Mixed territorial and progressive system: employment income has 3%, 15%, 30% and 40% marginal bands, with tax capped at 30% of taxable salary; PwC reports foreign-source profits exempt.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Broad factual test based on permanent home, family or economic interests; more than 183 days is one factor and residence can be treated as starting on entry.
taxation_system.income_scope: Employment connected with activity performed in DRC is taxable. Classification of foreign-client software revenue after the 2026 reform requires advice.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime; the 2026 IRPP reform reorganized personal-income taxation.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employment carries total CNSS contributions of 18%: 5% worker pension plus employer charges of 5% pension, 1.5% occupational risk and 6.5% family benefits. Employer-only INPP charges are 1%–3%. PwC reports ONEM at 0.2%, while ONEM’s current page states 0.5%, so that levy needs confirmation. The law and CNSS website contain inconsistent wording on the duration rule for foreign workers sent by overseas enterprises. An ordinary first-time sole professional is not expressly placed in the compulsory categories; voluntary continuation requires three prior years of affiliation, including the final six consecutive months. No mandatory self-employed percentage or fixed monthly contribution is therefore confirmed for this route.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 40% is the top marginal screening rate; salary IPR is capped at 30% of taxable salary.

tax_brackets.notes: USD conversion omitted because no reliable same-date official rate was established.
Salary tax remains capped at 30% of taxable salary.

taxation_system.notes: The exact treatment of a foreign-client software professional remains filing-dependent.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: DRC has no dedicated digital-nomad category. Anyone accepted as a liberal professional would need local registration and individualized ordinary-tax classification.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Prospective registered liberal professional; no digital-nomad regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 40% marginal IPR, with salary tax capped at 30%; self-employed treatment needs advice
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence can arise from a home or centre of interests and may begin on entry; 183 days is only one factor.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: PwC reports foreign-source profits exempt, but expatriate salary connected with activity in DRC taxable. Remote-service sourcing requires advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employees pay 5% pension and employers bear 13% CNSS. Compulsory treatment of a first-time independent professional is not established by the current sources; voluntary continuation requires prior affiliation.
