fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed monthly self-employed amount is published. Verified CNSS charges are percentage-based for covered employment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: A 2020 tariff lists USD 700 for an ordinary establishment visa for a merchant or profit-making liberal professional; confirm the current fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: RCCM, identification, licensing, banking and tax-registration costs apply, but current amounts were not published in the reviewed route materials.
fixed_payments.notes: There is no dedicated nomad payment schedule.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Under 183 days is not automatically non-resident because a home, lease, family or business centre may establish residence from entry.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Locally performed foreign-paid salary may be subject to IPR; classification of business profits requires advice under the 2026 reform.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The plausible route requires RCCM, identification, tax compliance, professional approval and USD 5,000 in a local bank. Confirm CNSS classification locally.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax conclusions do not resolve immigration eligibility.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Applicants generally need six months of prior lawful stay; processing time is additional and unpublished.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Permanent establishment requires 15 years of uninterrupted lawful residence in total; the exact post-temporary interval is not published.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The law requires seven years of “permanent residence” but does not clearly equate that phrase with holding the permanent establishment visa.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No reliable total can be calculated because naturalization is discretionary and requires national benefit or distinguished service.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the nationality law nor implementing order publishes a typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Adulthood, individual application, commitment to renounce other nationality, a Congolese language, good character, seven years of permanent residence, no disqualifying convictions and distinguished service or national benefit. Approval requires the Council of Ministers, National Assembly opinion and presidential decree.
key_conditions.notes: Congolese nationality is generally exclusive.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse may apply seven years after marriage; citizenship is not automatic.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage to a Congolese citizen can start the seven-year period if marital community continues and the citizen spouse retains nationality. Marriage to another foreign national gives no benefit.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The implementing order’s older five-year document reference conflicts with the controlling law’s seven-year rule.

requirements_and_risks.value: Continuing marital community, civil-status records, police records, medical and domicile documents and language evidence are required. Approval remains discretionary; fraud may cause refusal or loss of nationality.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A sham marriage is unlawful.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship primarily follows a Congolese parent. Birth alone does not generally confer citizenship; foundling, statelessness and later conditional-acquisition rules apply.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not ordinarily at birth. Exceptions apply to foundlings, children of stateless parents and children unable to acquire their parents’ nationality. Otherwise, a DRC-born child of foreign parents may request citizenship from age 18 while permanently resident.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is conditional acquisition, not broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Congolese from birth if either parent is Congolese and filiation is established during minority.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. No immediate parent-of-citizen settlement route was established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Confirm any family-residence application with DGM.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A child may be Congolese through the other Congolese parent, but the migrant father receives no automatic citizenship. Birth to two foreign migrants normally creates no settlement shortcut.

rank.notes: Current rank reported by this index; methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately lists 46 eVisa destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Visa-on-arrival destinations; eTA is not combined.

passport.notes: Passport-index counts change frequently; all values use one index for consistency.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: French should be expected for immigration, licensing, tax and registration. English may work in some international or technology workplaces, but no nationwide English public-service provision was found.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: A French-speaking adviser would be prudent.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and should not be expected in government procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable evidence of broadly available public services in either language was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current nationally representative mean monthly wage suitable for 2026 USD conversion was published. The official 2012 surveys contain only historical income figures.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median monthly wage or defensible 2026 USD equivalent was published.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The SMIG is a daily CDF rate; no universal monthly-day formula and reliable same-date official FX rate were established.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current nationally representative mean monthly earnings figure or defensible USD conversion is published in the current INS catalogue, ILO survey catalogue or 2024 World Bank Enterprise Survey. The official 2012 employment survey reported CDF 50,277 mean monthly main-activity income nationally and CDF 86,916 urban; the separate informal-sector survey reported CDF 62,741. These are historical, differently scoped income measures, not a 2026 average salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median salary or USD equivalent is published. The 2012 employment survey reported CDF 27,000 median monthly main-activity income nationally; the informal-sector survey reported CDF 30,000. Both are too old and differently scoped for a 2026 value.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful current national maximum salary is published.

min_salary_local_currency.value: CDF 21,500 per working day from January 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage, not an observed minimum or average salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national mean monthly salary in CDF is published. Historical official benchmarks are CDF 50,277 monthly main-activity income nationally and CDF 62,741 among informal-sector workers in separate 2012 surveys; neither is carried forward as a 2026 salary.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national median monthly salary in CDF is published. The 2012 employment survey gives CDF 27,000 and the separate informal-sector survey gives CDF 30,000; their age and different coverage make them unsuitable as a 2026 value.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No official current national maximum salary is published. Historical surveys report means, medians and quartiles rather than a national upper bound; the 2012 employment survey’s CDF 50,000 national 75th percentile is not a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Current statutory daily minimum; national mean and median unavailable
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective January 2026; exact national earnings benchmarks are from 2012
average_citizen_salary.notes: The exact national earnings amounts located are historical: the 2012 employment survey reported CDF 50,277 mean and CDF 27,000 median monthly main-activity income; a separate informal-sector survey reported CDF 62,741 mean and CDF 30,000 median. The current INS catalogue has no wage series, the ILO catalogue describes collected variables without publishing a current estimate, and the 2024 World Bank Enterprise Survey is firm-level rather than a national worker salary distribution.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No reliable current national cost-of-living basket was found; Kinshasa crowdsourced estimates were not used nationally.

data.selection_summary: Denmark has no current digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route for a non-EU/EEA applicant. Business registration, Danish tax liability, or remote work while visiting does not create residence rights. Alternatives require a Danish job, Danish study, family status, or an innovative founder business approved under Start-up Denmark.

summary.value: Admission to a full-time Danish higher-education program can support student residence without a local employer. A previously earned foreign degree alone does not qualify. Qualifying graduates may receive a job-seeking period but ordinarily need subsequent employment or another status.
summary.notes: This requires new Danish study and does not independently match ongoing foreign-contract remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: Full Danish tax liability generally begins when a person becomes resident or stays more than six consecutive months; in the latter case it applies from the beginning of the stay. Holiday-type presence of no more than three consecutive months or 180 days in 12 months may avoid full liability only when unconnected with employment.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence, availability of a home and the nature of the work can alter the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Approximate 2026 top marginal screening figure including the 8% labour-market tax. It is not an expected effective rate; deductions, municipality, income composition and church membership affect actual tax.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The labour-market contribution applies to salary, fees, self-employment profit and relevant non-Danish income. It is treated as a tax and is not a complete measure of pension or payroll costs.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer or nomad payment applies because Denmark has no nomad route. Under another lawful status, labour-market contribution and B-tax vary with income; ATP depends on classification, sole-proprietor registration is fee-exempt, covered public healthcare is not presented as a separate monthly premium, and VAT is transaction-based.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax regime exists. Qualifying Danish employees and researchers can use a separate 27% expatriate regime plus labour-market contribution for up to 84 months; highly paid employees require qualifying Danish employment and the applicable salary threshold.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This regime neither supports foreign-contract remote work nor creates immigration eligibility.

taxes.caveats: Tax and immigration are separate. Danish taxation, CVR registration or VAT registration does not authorize residence or work. Foreign-employer income earned while lawfully working from Denmark can require Danish reporting, B-tax, payroll, permanent-establishment, treaty and social-security analysis.

taxation_system.value: Progressive national and municipal taxation plus an 8% labour-market tax; the approximate combined top screening rate is 60.5% in 2026.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence or more than six consecutive months generally creates full liability, normally from the beginning of the stay.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxable on worldwide income, subject to treaty residence and double-tax relief. Foreign-employer wages for work done while living in Denmark remain reportable.
taxation_system.special_regimes: A 27% expatriate/researcher regime plus labour-market tax is available to qualifying Danish employees or researchers for up to 84 months; no nomad regime exists.
taxation_system.social_security: The 8% labour-market contribution applies broadly to earned and self-employment income. ATP, pension and foreign-payroll obligations depend on classification and coverage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 60.5% figure is a top marginal screen, not an effective-rate estimate. National brackets are layered with municipal tax and the labour-market contribution, and their tax bases differ.

tax_brackets.notes: Check the live filing-year personal allowance.

tax_brackets.notes: The actual rate depends on municipality.

taxation_system.notes: Official SKAT sources support residence, foreign-income and labour-market-tax claims. PwC is retained for the combined top-rate screen and expatriate-regime summary.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Denmark has no digital-nomad immigration or tax category. Someone who obtains another lawful residence basis and works from Denmark for a foreign employer is subject to ordinary Danish rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary employee or self-employed taxation applies under another lawful status.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to approximately 60.5% top marginal screening rate including labour-market tax; not an expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Full liability generally begins upon residence or after more than six consecutive months, normally from the beginning of that stay.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally report worldwide income. Wages from a foreign employer for work performed while living in Denmark are taxable and may require B-tax instalments when the employer does not withhold.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No nomad regime. The expatriate/researcher regime requires qualifying Danish employment or researcher status.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The 8% labour-market contribution covers salary, fees, self-employment profit and relevant foreign income. ATP, foreign-employer payroll and international social-security coordination require classification-specific review.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed payment applies because Denmark has no digital-nomad route.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No nomad-specific charge exists. The 8% labour-market contribution is income-based. ATP may apply according to worker classification; the published full-time employee contribution is DKK 3,408 annually, with two-thirds employer-funded, so it is not a universal freelancer payment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad application or renewal fee exists. The rejected Start-up Denmark founder route currently charges a DKK 3,060 SIRI processing fee; other lawful routes have their own fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Sole proprietorships are exempt from the Danish Business Authority company-registration fee. VAT registration is generally required above DKK 50,000 of taxable sales within 12 months, but VAT is transaction-based rather than a fixed monthly payment.
fixed_payments.notes: The prior vague marker is resolved as inapplicable. Ordinary tax, ATP, payroll, insurance, registration and VAT obligations depend on a separate lawful status and the actual work structure. Covered legally working residents receive public healthcare without a separately published universal monthly insurance premium.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Holiday-type presence may avoid full tax liability only when unconnected with employment. This is not authorization to work remotely as a visitor.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A person living lawfully under another status and paid by a foreign employer should expect Danish reporting and potentially B-tax instalments.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: CVR or VAT registration creates tax/reporting obligations but not immigration status. Start-up Denmark separately requires an approved innovative founder business.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This analysis is hypothetical for the selected profile because no qualifying Danish remote-work immigration route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying foreign-contract remote-work route exists, so no route-specific temporary-residence timeline applies.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Ordinarily 8 years of qualifying legal residence; 4 years is possible only when all supplementary requirements are met. This does not create a route for the current profile.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: An ordinary applicant generally must have held permanent residence for two years when the naturalisation bill is expected to be adopted.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: A practical ordinary minimum is about 10 years when permanent residence is obtained after 8 years and then held for 2 years. The separate general residence condition is 9 years, processing adds time, and this profile has no qualifying starting route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Published average; individual cases can be faster or substantially slower.

key_conditions.value: A qualifying immigration basis must come first. Permanent residence normally requires continuous legal residence, work or self-employment, Danish language, continued employment, self-support and other conditions. Naturalisation generally requires 9 years' continuous residence, permanent residence held for 2 years, Danish residence, language, employment, self-support, acceptable conduct and debt status, knowledge of Denmark and participation in a constitutional ceremony.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation occurs through legislation and remains subject to the rules applying when decided.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For the maximum residence reduction, both the marriage and the Danish spouse's citizenship must have lasted at least 3 years; the residence condition then becomes 6 years. One or two years of marriage results in 8- or 7-year residence conditions.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Danish citizen can count toward the marriage-duration requirement. Marriage to a non-Danish spouse does not accelerate citizenship, and marriage never grants citizenship automatically.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The Danish spouse must have held citizenship for the relevant period.

requirements_and_risks.value: Spousal reunification is a separate conditional residence process. The relationship must be legally valid and genuine; age, integration, housing, financial and other requirements can apply. Citizenship still requires the applicable residence, permanent-residence, language, employment and self-support conditions.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A sham or primarily immigration-motivated marriage can be refused and carry legal consequences.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Denmark alone generally does not grant citizenship. Special application rules protect certain stateless children.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Denmark to two non-Danish migrant parents does not automatically become Danish merely through birthplace; special rules apply to stateless children.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents must arrange the child's residence status under applicable family rules.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born on or after 1 July 2014 automatically acquires Danish citizenship when the father, mother or co-mother is Danish.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Earlier births are governed by the law then in force.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Danish-citizen child may support a derived family-residence claim for a foreign parent in particular circumstances, but residence is not automatic and citizenship is not transferred upward.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Individual eligibility requires assessment under the applicable family or derived-right rules.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is Danish, the child may be Danish from birth, but the migrant father receives neither automatic permanent residence nor citizenship. He may need family-reunification or derived-residence authorization and must prove the genuine family relationship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Birth to two temporary migrants provides no ordinary immigration shortcut for the father.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of DKK 51,675 at about DKK 6.53 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Statistics Denmark defines and charts the 2024 all-sector median, but the exact national-total amount is not stated in the inspected accessible text; only selected sector medians are explicit. Substituting a sector figure or estimating from the chart would be misleading.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Denmark has no statutory national minimum wage, and the inspected official earnings sources do not publish an observed national wage floor, so no USD minimum can be responsibly converted.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion; exchange rates fluctuate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official 2024 release defines and charts the all-sector median but its accessible text states exact medians only for selected sectors: state DKK 49,594, private DKK 47,920 and municipalities DKK 43,210. None is the national median, so no USD value is invented.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official wage-distribution sources publish quartiles, not a national maximum. A maximum would be outlier-dependent rather than a stable national statistic.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: No statutory national minimum wage exists; pay is generally set by collective agreement, and the inspected official earnings sources do not publish an observed national minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 standardized monthly earnings, including pension and bonuses and excluding overtime and absence payments.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Statistics Denmark's 2024 release defines and charts the all-sector median but does not state its exact national amount in the accessible text. Explicit sector medians cannot be substituted for the national figure.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Statistics Denmark publishes quartiles and selected sector distributions, not a national maximum salary; a maximum would be an unstable outlier rather than a meaningful benchmark.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average standardized monthly earnings of employees on the Danish labour market; gross, including pension contributions and bonuses
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024, monthly
average_citizen_salary.notes: The official 2024 average remains DKK 51,675 gross monthly. Denmark has no statutory minimum wage; the exact national median is charted but not textually exposed in the inspected release, and no national maximum is published. The nulls reflect inapplicable or unpublished national measures, not missing guesses.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Denmark has no digital-nomad status through which settlement residence can begin or accumulate. Visitor presence, taxation and company registration do not substitute for a residence and work permit.
settlement_track.summary: No qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists. Settlement requires changing the underlying circumstances and qualifying through a Danish job, approved innovative start-up, Danish education followed by another status, family residence or another lawful category.
settlement_track.notes: Start-up Denmark can be settlement-oriented for genuine innovative founders but is outside the applicant profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign contract can produce Danish taxable income when someone lawfully lives and works in Denmark, but it is not an immigration basis. Business registration does not supply residence authorization.

data.selection_summary: Djibouti is not a match for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker seeking a citizenship path. The current immigration law offers renewable residence cards, including for visitors with their own resources, but that visitor basis requires an undertaking not to conduct professional activity in Djibouti. Professional work requires a local employer or qualifying business/investment basis and work authorization. No dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or independently usable freelance residence category was found in the current law, official eVisa portal, or residence-permit enrollment portal.

visa_application.notes: This official form starts residence-permit enrollment and asks for entry details, professional situation, purpose, local address, photograph, and passport information. It is not evidence of a digital-nomad category; eligibility must still satisfy the 2019 immigration law. The separate official eVisa portal handles entry visas.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct application for a renewable residence card is possible on an own-resources visitor basis.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a residence card, but its no-professional-activity condition makes it unusable for the applicant's ongoing remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The 2019 law replaced the former temporary/permanent-card structure and expressly repealed the 2007 law. No current conversion from the own-resources card to permanent residence was found.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization law permits an application after at least 10 years of habitual residence, but it does not confirm that an own-resources visitor card can lawfully be used while working remotely.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and granted by decree. This does not cure the route's prohibition on professional activity.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest independent residence basis found, but it fails the profile because foreign remote work is professional activity and the law requires the visitor to undertake not to exercise professional activity in Djibouti. A filing should not be attempted on the assumption that foreign-paid remote work is exempt without written immigration and labor-authority confirmation.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only the separate discretionary naturalization route after the applicable habitual-residence period was found.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the profile does not assume founder, investor, licensed local-company, or substantial local-business status. Historical investor residence provisions must not be treated as current because the underlying 2007 law was repealed.

summary.value: A student may obtain a residence card after showing admission or pre-admission to an approved Djiboutian institution and sufficient stable means. This is education enrollment, not an independent skilled-migration route based on an already-held software-engineering degree, and no direct permanent-residence conversion was found.
summary.notes: The general residence card is valid for no more than one year at a time. Student status does not authorize local employment under the inspected law.

tax_residency_rule.value: No reliable 183-day tax-residence test was found. Djibouti's schedular system instead taxes salary for work physically exercised in Djibouti and professional profits from activities carried on in Djibouti; therefore foreign payment does not by itself establish an exemption.
tax_residency_rule.notes: This is a territorial/source rule, not a confirmed day-count residence rule. Individual domicile, business registration, contract characterization, and treaty position require professional advice.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal monthly salary rate in the 2024 consolidated-code copy. It is a screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Source reconciliation is imperfect: the official Ministry page still displays an older 30% top rate, while the 2024 IMF report states 40% even though the consolidated 2024 code displays 45%; current DGI confirmation is required.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the general formal-payroll total, not a remote-worker or self-employed rate: 15.7% is employer-borne and 6% employee-borne. The components are 5.5% family benefits paid by the employer, 1.2% work-accident coverage paid by the employer, 7% mandatory health insurance split 5% employer/2% employee, and 8% retirement split 4%/4%. The same 2020 decree separately lists only a 7% mandatory-health contribution under the independent regime. Because Djibouti has no qualifying remote-worker route, the independent classification and collection mechanics for a foreign remote contractor require confirmation from CNSS.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax or contribution for a foreign remote worker was established. The independent-regime contribution identified in the official decree is percentage-based at 7%, not a fixed amount, and no qualifying remote-work immigration category exists.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-remote-worker tax regime was found. Professional profits are generally taxed at 25% of net taxable profit; the annual minimum business tax is 1% of turnover with a DJF 120,000 floor. The 2024 finance law makes liberal professions subject to VAT without a turnover threshold.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business registration would not independently establish immigration permission.

taxes.caveats: Tax results are not a substitute for advice from Djibouti's Direction Générale des Impôts and CNSS. The current consolidated tax code was located through a secondary document host, while official government pages expose older or piecemeal legislation. The treatment of foreign-employer remote salary, employee versus independent-professional characterization, CNSS coverage, and any treaty relief should be confirmed before work begins.

taxation_system.value: Schedular, predominantly territorial system: salary for work exercised in Djibouti is taxed progressively; locally carried-on professional profits are generally taxed at 25%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No confirmed 183-day test; liability is principally linked to work or business activity carried out in Djibouti.
taxation_system.income_scope: Djibouti-source salary and professional/business profits. Salary paid by a foreign employer can still fall within the territorial rule when the work is performed in Djibouti.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad exemption found. Business and investment incentives exist but are not ordinary remote-worker regimes.
taxation_system.social_security: General formal payroll bears 21.7% in contributions, split 15.7% employer and 6% employee. The official 2020 contribution decree lists a separate 7% mandatory-health contribution for the independent regime; whether and how that regime could cover a foreign contractor must be confirmed because no qualifying remote-work status exists.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value is the 45% top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. The consolidated 2024 code says salaries not exceeding DJF 50,000 are exempt and applies marginal bands to taxable monthly salary above that level. Official and secondary sources conflict on the current top rate, so confidence is medium.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal portion of monthly taxable salary where total taxable salary exceeds the DJF 50,000 exemption ceiling
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses the fixed rate of DJF 177.721 per USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal portion of monthly taxable salary where total taxable salary exceeds DJF 50,000
Top marginal portion of monthly taxable salary
tax_brackets.notes: The 2024 IMF discussion instead states 40%; verify the live rate with DGI.

taxation_system.notes: The 2024 consolidated code is the most complete located tax schedule, but its non-government host and conflict with other sources prevent high confidence. Social-security percentages are better supported by the official 2020 decree, CNSS, and ISSA.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category: Djibouti has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. If work is nevertheless performed from Djibouti, the territorial salary or professional-profit rules may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary salary or professional-profit rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 45% marginal salary tax; or generally 25% professional-profits tax if validly registered as an independent business
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No confirmed day-count safe harbor; work physically exercised in Djibouti is within the salary-tax territorial rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign payment does not necessarily make employment income foreign-source when the work is performed in Djibouti. The inspected law taxes remuneration for work exercised in the territory.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No digital-nomad-specific payroll rule exists. Under the general formal-payroll regime, contributions total 21.7%: 15.7% employer and 6% employee. The official 2020 decree separately lists a 7% mandatory-health contribution for the independent regime, with no retirement, family-benefit, or work-accident percentage in that column. ISSA materials indicate that self-employed persons are excluded from the employee pension and work-injury schemes, reinforcing that the 21.7% employee-payroll total should not be applied automatically to an independent contractor. Applicability, contribution base, registration, and collection for a foreign remote contractor remain filing-level questions because immigration law supplies no qualifying remote-work category.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad-specific fixed payment exists; ordinary business and residence fees may apply in other categories.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed monthly social contribution was established. General payroll uses percentage contributions of 21.7%, while the official independent-regime column lists a 7% mandatory-health contribution. The decree does not publish a fixed monthly minimum for that independent contribution.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The tax-code schedule inspected lists residence-card issuance at DJF 25,000 for African nationals, DJF 30,000 for Asian nationals, and DJF 40,000 for European/American nationals; renewals are DJF 20,000, 25,000, and 35,000 respectively. Confirm the live portal quote because the schedule may have changed.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: For a registered professional business, the 2024 code states a 1% minimum turnover tax with an annual floor of DJF 120,000; patents and VAT obligations may also apply.
fixed_payments.notes: These charges do not authorize remote work. The separate 7% independent health contribution is a percentage, not a fixed payment, and its applicability to a foreign contractor requires CNSS confirmation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No reliable 183-day threshold was identified. A short stay should not be assumed tax-free if work is physically performed in Djibouti, and visitor/eVisa status is not work authorization.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No lawful ordinary remote-worker category was found. If work is authorized under another status, salary for work exercised in Djibouti may be taxed progressively up to the screening top rate, with general payroll contributions potentially applying if an employment relationship is recognized.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Professional profits realized through an activity carried on in Djibouti are generally taxed at 25%, with minimum-turnover tax and potentially VAT/patent obligations. The official contribution decree lists a 7% mandatory-health contribution for the independent regime, but local business or CNSS registration alone does not resolve immigration and work authorization.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The absence of a qualifying route makes these tax scenarios cautionary rather than an application plan. The independent 7% health rate is established in the decree, but its practical coverage of this applicant remains unconfirmed.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A residence card can be applied for directly, but no qualifying foreign-remote-work temporary-residence route exists; expressing this as a citizenship-path duration would be misleading.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No current permanent-residence conversion period was found. The 2019 law repealed the 2007 law that had described certain resident cards.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization depends on habitual residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence prerequisite.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory residence period before application. It is not a guaranteed outcome and is not linked to a valid remote-worker route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Interior Minister must transmit the complete file and opinion to the naturalization commission within six months, but no total decision deadline or reliable typical processing time is published in the inspected nationality law and implementing decree.

key_conditions.value: At least 10 years of habitual residence immediately before applying; age 18 or older; good character; qualifying criminal record; medical certificate; assimilation into the Djiboutian community, including sufficient knowledge of a language used in Djibouti; police investigation; favorable discretionary assessment; and naturalization by decree. The period can be reduced to five years for persons whose capacity or talent has rendered or can render important services, but that exceptional route does not fit an ordinary software engineer profile.
key_conditions.notes: The code does not establish an entitlement after ten years. No general renunciation requirement was found; the code says acquiring a foreign nationality does not itself remove Djiboutian nationality.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Ten years of common life with a Djiboutian spouse; reduced to five years if the union has produced at least one child.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage has no automatic effect on nationality. A foreign spouse may apply after the applicable period of common life, but the code does not clearly state whether time lived together abroad before establishing Djiboutian residence is fully creditable; obtain filing-level confirmation.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must remain in effect at the relevant date; the benefit is excluded where divorce has occurred and the foreign spouse has remarried a foreign national. Naturalization remains an application decided by decree, and normal character, health, investigation, and documentary requirements apply. Genuine relationship and common-life evidence should be expected; sham marriage or false documents can create criminal, immigration, and nationality consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No separate accelerated permanent-residence rule based on marriage was confirmed in the current 2019 immigration law.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Djibouti or abroad is Djiboutian if either parent is Djiboutian. Territorial birth alone does not confer citizenship; the narrow foundling rule covers a child born in Djibouti whose parents are unknown, subject to loss of that presumption if foreign parentage is established before majority.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship from birth in Djibouti when both known parents are foreign migrants. The exception for a child whose parents are unknown is not a general migrant-family route.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Djibouti or abroad is Djiboutian when either the father or mother is Djiboutian.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a child to two foreign migrants does not create citizenship for the child or an automatic residence, permanent-residence, or citizenship benefit for either parent. A child shared with a Djiboutian spouse can reduce the foreign spouse's citizenship application waiting period from ten to five years of common life.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic parent-of-citizen residence category was found in the current immigration law.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic status merely because a child is born in Djibouti. If the mother is Djiboutian, the child is Djiboutian by descent; the father's potential citizenship benefit is the marriage provision reducing the common-life period to five years when the union has a child, not automatic citizenship through the child.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on the research date; index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count, separate from visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 39 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 3 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 59. These figures should not be mixed with Henley's combined visa-free/visa-on-arrival access count.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only living is possible mainly in some international, logistics, diplomatic, or business settings, but official law and government processes are French/Arabic-first. Internet Society rates national internet resilience at 46%, indicating medium rather than strong resilience; this does not measure connection quality at a particular address.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide English-proficiency statistic was found, so English practicality should be treated as limited outside international workplaces.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and no general government-service or labor-market support in either language was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: An interpreter would likely be necessary for legal, immigration, tax, and administrative matters unless the applicant speaks French or Arabic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of ILOSTAT's DJF 95,504.295 average monthly earnings observation for employees in 2017. This is the latest defensible national employee-average amount located, but it is historical and must not be presented as a current 2026 salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected ILOSTAT earnings catalogue provides a median-earnings series in principle, but no national Djibouti median amount was exposed in the current country materials or the 2017 survey catalogue. The 2025 labor-force findings published in the 2026 World Bank update also do not report a national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the DJF 35,000 statutory SMIG, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the 2017 ILOSTAT national average monthly earnings observation for employees. No current 2025/2026 average wage amount was published in the inspected new labor-force materials.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national median monthly employee-earnings amount for Djibouti was published in the inspected current ILOSTAT country materials, 2017 public survey catalogue, or 2026 World Bank labor-market update.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum salary is not a standard labor-market statistic, and none is published in the inspected official/statistical sources. Survey record maxima were not used because they may be top-coded, erroneous, or sample-specific and do not establish a meaningful national salary ceiling.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory interprofessional guaranteed minimum wage reported by the Djiboutian government to the ILO supervisory process.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: ILOSTAT's total-sex observation for average monthly earnings of employees, derived from the 2017 Djiboutian Household Survey. It is a historical employee-average statistic, not a current 2026 salary. Djibouti's first dedicated labor-force survey covered the first two quarters of 2025, but the accessible 2026 economic update does not publish its national average earnings figure.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: ILOSTAT publishes a median-monthly-earnings indicator globally, but the inspected current Djibouti country profile and earnings materials did not expose a Djibouti total value. The public EDAM 2017 catalogue identifies income variables without publishing a national weighted median, and the 2026 World Bank analysis of the 2025 labor-force survey does not state one.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No official or internationally harmonized source inspected publishes a meaningful national maximum monthly salary in DJF. Microdata maxima and individual salary scales do not represent a national maximum and therefore were not substituted.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum wage plus historical 2017 national average monthly earnings of employees; current national average, median, and maximum are unpublished in the inspected 2025/2026 labor-market materials
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage reported in the 2025 government submission discussed by the ILO in 2026; average earnings observation from 2017; median and maximum unavailable
average_citizen_salary.notes: The DJF 35,000 amount is a statutory minimum, while DJF 95,504.295 is ILOSTAT's historical 2017 average monthly earnings of employees. Neither should be described as a current average-citizen salary for 2026. The first two quarters of Djibouti's 2025 labor-force survey are discussed in the 2026 economic update, but the accessible report publishes labor-force structure rather than a national average or median wage. No defensible national maximum was published.

cost_of_living_note.value: No comparable current household budget was found. The World Bank reports that regional transport disruptions and higher energy costs are placing upward pressure on household living costs, while many households remain close to the poverty line and informal earnings are unstable.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is a qualitative current warning, not a monthly cost estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The independent own-resources residence card requires the holder not to conduct professional activity in Djibouti. An eVisa or visitor residence card therefore cannot be treated as remote-work permission.
settlement_track.summary: Djibouti has renewable residence cards and a separate discretionary ten-year naturalization rule, but no current residence category was found that both permits ordinary foreign-contract remote work and provides a confirmed settlement track. Working lawfully requires an unrelated local-employment or qualifying local-business basis.
settlement_track.notes: The general ten-year naturalization benchmark is not assigned as this route's citizenship duration because there is no qualifying remote-worker route whose lawful residence time can be followed while continuing the applicant's foreign work.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category was found. The independent visitor residence basis expressly requires an undertaking not to exercise professional activity; authorized professional work is tied to local employment, work authorization, or a qualifying business structure.

data.notes: High confidence in the negative route finding because the current immigration law, official entry portal, residence enrollment form, and free-zone procedure were checked. Overall confidence is medium because Djibouti publishes limited implementation guidance, current tax sources conflict on the top salary rate, no explicit rule addresses foreign-paid remote work, and the 2025 labor-force survey materials inspected do not publish current national average or median earnings. The social-security split is now well supported: 21.7% for general payroll and a separate 7% health contribution in the independent-regime column.

data.selection_summary: Dominica is a match for a foreign-client contractor willing to register a local sole-trader/business activity and obtain a self-employed work permit. Official guidance supports self-employed filing with business-registration and bank evidence, without a local employer; a work permit exceeding six months confers residence, permits are renewable annually, permanent residence may be requested after five years, and the government publishes a citizenship application after seven years of residence. Filing is in-country and approval is discretionary. A salaried foreign employee should not assume this settlement route fits without written Labour Division confirmation; WIN is a separate temporary-only option.

visa_application.title: Dominica Labour Division forms — Work Permit (First Time)
visa_application.notes: The official forms page links to the eServices first-time work-permit application. The underlying eServices page was not independently readable during this audit, so start from the Labour page and confirm the self-employed filing category with the Labour Division.

best_routes.route_name: Self-employed work permit with business registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed minimum is published. Self-employed applicants are directed to provide a bank statement and business-registration evidence.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed XCD income or capital threshold is published for the ordinary self-employed work-permit category.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; bank statement and registered-business evidence required
income_requirement_display.notes: Approval remains discretionary. Confirm whether the proposed foreign-client software consultancy and financial evidence are sufficient.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank statement is required, but no official source specifies a mandatory lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: Normally be physically present in Dominica while the first work-permit application is processed and maintain lawful visitor status until approval.
Register the self-employed business and provide a Statement of Particulars or Certificate of Registration.
Provide a bank statement; confirm whether general employer-letter and vacancy-advertisement items are waived or replaced for self-employed applicants.
Provide medical and police certificates, passport, photographs, return-ticket evidence, testimonials and the applicable fee.
Register with Inland Revenue, keep business records and report taxable earnings, including overseas income.
Published non-CARICOM first-time work-permit fee is EC$800; the CARICOM fee is EC$250. Other registration, licence or renewal costs may apply.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: A work permit for a term exceeding six months automatically confers residence status.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually; residence permits may be renewed yearly through five years, after which permanent residence may be requested.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal and permanent residence remain discretionary and require continuing compliance.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A work permit exceeding six months automatically confers residence; the published self-employed category uses business-registration and bank evidence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a residence-oriented work route, unlike WIN.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Permanent residence may be requested after five years of residence or employment on the island, subject to ministerial discretion and documentary evidence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Retain every work/residence permit and evidence of physical residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: The government publishes a citizenship application after seven years of residence. Approval, supporting records, fees and an oath are still required.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Support the seven-year period with qualifying permits; do not assume WIN time counts.

best_routes.notes: This route can fit an independently contracting software engineer with foreign clients if the consultancy is registered in Dominica and the work permit is approved. Official materials do not impose a local-client or stated investment threshold, but do not expressly discuss a one-person software consultancy serving only foreign clients. Obtain written confirmation before restructuring a foreign contract. A salaried foreign employee is not clearly self-employed.

rejected_routes.route_name: Work in Nature (WIN) Extended Stay Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Official eligibility states expected income of US$50,000 or more over the next 12 months and/or sufficient means to support accompanying family.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Approximately XCD 135,000/year at the fixed XCD 2.70/USD peg
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The program publishes its threshold in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: US$50,000/year (about US$4,167/month), or sufficient supporting means
income_requirement_display.notes: The alternative sufficient-means test is not quantified.

income_proof_months.notes: The program requests an employment letter or, for non-salary income, a bank letter, recent bank statement and good-standing/credit evidence, but publishes no fixed lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: Be at least 18, of good character, without a criminal record and able to work remotely.
Work only for companies or individuals not registered in Dominica.
Provide passport, police records for jurisdictions lived in during the previous five years, bank reference, employment/income evidence, photographs and Dominica-valid health insurance.
Pay a US$100 non-refundable application fee plus US$800 individual or US$1,200 family visa fee.

initial_validity.value: Up to 18 months from the WIN stamp issued on arrival

extension_rules.notes: Official materials describe an 18-month maximum and an extension only of the post-approval payment deadline; they do not establish renewal beyond 18 months.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary extended-stay visa permitting foreign remote work; it is not described as a residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The official site characterizes WIN holders as tourists/remote workers.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Conditional PR path after an independently approved work/residence permit; the documented self-employed alternative requires business registration and qualifying permits.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Official pages allow in-country permit processing. They do not expressly confirm that an unchanged foreign-client arrangement qualifies for the self-employed permit, or that WIN time counts. Five years refers to the evidenced work/residence-permit route, not five years of WIN renewals.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official WIN source establishes conversion to residence, permanent residence or citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: WIN remains active and has an application portal, but it is temporary-nomad-only for this citizenship-oriented selection. It permits foreign-only remote work and provides a Dominica income-tax waiver.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary residence permit without work authorization

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum is stated; applicants provide a banker's statement or evidence from a responsible person.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; financial-position evidence required
income_requirement_display.notes: The financial-sufficiency decision is discretionary.

income_proof_months.notes: No lookback period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply while legally present as a visitor and maintain an extension of stay during processing.
Provide medical and police records, financial-position evidence, testimonials, return-ticket evidence and a local friend/family responsibility letter.
Obtain a separate work permit to engage in work in Dominica.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: Invest Dominica states residence permits are valid for one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewable yearly through five years
extension_rules.notes: Renewal requires continuing financial and sponsor evidence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct residence permit after an in-country application and approval.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential application after five years, subject to ministerial discretion.

path_to_citizenship.value: Residence can support the seven-year citizenship application, but the permit alone does not authorize remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as a standalone route because residence permission is not published as remote-work authorization. It should be paired with an approved self-employed work permit.

summary.value: No general independent degree-based or points-tested residence route for an ordinary non-CARICOM software engineer was located. CARICOM Skills Certificates are nationality-restricted.
summary.notes: A university degree may support the credibility of a software consultancy but does not itself grant residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: Residence for the personal allowance can arise through a permanent place of abode in Dominica, physical presence for 183 days in the assessment year, or presence in a year continuous with another qualifying 183-day year. IRD also states that persons physically present for more than 183 days continuously must file as residents.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence can arise through more than a simple day count; obtain advice for arrival and departure years.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Resident individuals receive a published EC$30,000 allowance before the 15%, 25% and 35% bands.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The official DSS 2012–2031 table sets the 2026 self-employed contribution at 13.75% of annual insurable earnings. This is the ordinary registered self-employed rate, not a WIN-specific charge.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: DSS self-employed contributions are percentage-based, not fixed. At the EC$84,000 annual insurable-earnings cap, 13.75% equals EC$11,550/year or EC$962.50/month (about US$356.48); a lower assessment produces a lower amount.

special_tax_regimes.value: WIN holders receive a Dominica income-tax waiver for qualifying foreign remote work. That waiver should not be assumed after switching to a locally registered self-employed work permit.
special_tax_regimes.notes: WIN holders remain responsible for tax in their normal residence or tax domicile.

taxes.caveats: The self-employed settlement route and WIN have materially different tax treatment. A locally registered consultant falls under ordinary business-income rules, including overseas income, while qualifying WIN work has a specific waiver. Contract classification, source of services, tax residence, double-tax relief, VAT and DSS coverage require individualized advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax. Published resident bands are 0% through EC$30,000, 15% on the next EC$20,000, 25% on the next EC$30,000 and 35% above EC$80,000. Self-employed persons calculate tax on business profits, and IRD expressly includes overseas income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of abode or qualifying physical presence, including 183 days in the assessment year or a continuous adjacent qualifying year.
taxation_system.income_scope: IRD states that taxable income includes earnings, business profits and overseas income. Deductions generally require expenses incurred wholly and exclusively in producing taxable income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: WIN foreign remote work receives a specific Dominica income-tax waiver; ordinary registered self-employment does not inherit it.
taxation_system.social_security: For ordinary registered self-employment, DSS sets 13.75% of annual insurable earnings in 2026, capped on EC$84,000, generally payable quarterly. WIN-specific coverage is not stated and requires DSS classification.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 35% dashboard figure is the top marginal rate, not the effective rate on all income.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD value uses the EC$2.70/USD peg.
USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.
Top marginal band.

taxation_system.notes: High confidence in the published tax bands and ordinary 2026 self-employed DSS rate; medium confidence in application to a particular foreign-client structure, and low confidence that general DSS rules can be applied to WIN without written classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Qualifying WIN remote workers receive a Dominica income-tax waiver while remaining responsible for tax in their normal country of residence or tax domicile.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary digital-nomad visa with a specific local income-tax waiver
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% Dominica income tax for qualifying WIN remote work; ordinary PIT up to 35% after switching to taxable self-employment
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Ordinary residence tests exist, but official WIN materials separately promise an income-tax waiver for qualifying holders.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign remote-work income is waived from Dominica income tax while WIN conditions are satisfied; permitted work is limited to businesses and individuals not registered in Dominica.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: WIN income-tax waiver plus limited import-duty/VAT concessions for personal and business effects imported during the first three months, subject to other charges and re-export conditions.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: WIN materials publish no DSS exemption, contribution rule or payroll classification. DSS separately says employees in Dominica, including non-nationals, must contribute and requires self-employed persons ordinarily resident and engaged in employment in Dominica to register. Neither authority states whether foreign-only WIN work is employment in Dominica or whether the holder is an employee or self-employed person; obtain written DSS classification.

fixed_payments.status: One-time WIN visa fees confirmed; no fixed monthly WIN tax or DSS amount is published
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No recurring WIN-specific amount is published. If DSS classifies the holder as self-employed, the 2026 rate is 13.75% of annual insurable earnings, not a fixed payment. If classified as an employee in Dominica, the 2026 employee share is 6.75%, plus an employer share of 8.00% with redundancy coverage or 7.75% without. WIN and DSS sources do not resolve which, if any, classification applies to foreign-only remote work.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: US$100 non-refundable application fee; US$800 individual, US$1,200 family, or US$800 plus US$500 per additional employee for qualifying business-group applications.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Customs Service Charge and Environmental Surcharge may remain payable on concessionary imports; amounts depend on the imported items.
fixed_payments.notes: The unresolved point is classification, not the rates: current DSS tables publish 2026 percentages, but neither DSS nor WIN guidance places foreign-only WIN work in a contribution category. Confirm coverage, the EC$84,000 insurable-earnings ceiling and reciprocal-agreement exceptions with DSS.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: The explicit WIN waiver is more relevant than merely staying below 183 days. Home-country tax obligations may continue.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: WIN promises a local income-tax waiver, but tax residence, DSS coverage and treaty consequences still require review in Dominica and the home jurisdiction.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: After switching to a registered Dominica business/work permit, model ordinary PIT up to 35%, DSS at 13.75%, business registration costs and potential VAT obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The WIN income-tax exemption is explicit. Social-security treatment is not: the law and DSS pages establish compulsory categories and rates but do not classify WIN foreign-only remote work. Home-country liability and treaty or reciprocal-agreement relief remain fact-specific.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: An approved work permit exceeding six months confers residence immediately; processing time is not published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Permanent residence may be requested after five years of residence or employment and remains ministerially discretionary.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the published five-year permanent-residence point and seven-year-residence citizenship form; it is not a guaranteed two-year PR-to-citizenship entitlement.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Government forms identify citizenship after seven years of residence; approval remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed official sources publish no service standard or typical processing duration.

key_conditions.value: Maintain lawful work/residence permits and records; seek permanent residence after five years if approved; document financial standing, police record, health, testimonials and residence history; then submit the citizenship application, fees and oath after the qualifying period. The reviewed materials publish no language test or mandatory renunciation rule.
key_conditions.notes: Confirm residence continuity, permitted absences and treatment of any WIN period in writing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Labour Ministry says a person married to a Dominican-born spouse must have resided in Dominica for at least three years and received three work or residence permits; three years of marriage alone is not stated to suffice.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Dominican citizen can support the marriage route, but at least three years of Dominica residence and three work/residence permits remain required. Marriage to another migrant does not shorten citizenship, although a spouse may accompany a WIN principal applicant.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not confer citizenship automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: Provide marriage and civil-status evidence and maintain the required residence permits. Citizenship is reviewed and approved by the competent minister; false documents or a sham arrangement can cause refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The reviewed official pages do not publish a detailed marriage-interview protocol; confirm genuineness procedures with the Labour Division.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Constitution section 98 grants citizenship at birth to persons born in Dominica, subject to narrow foreign-envoy and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Dominica is a citizen at birth even when both parents are migrants, subject to the narrow constitutional exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parental temporary or permanent status is generally irrelevant to territorial birth citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Dominica is a citizen by birth. A child born abroad may acquire citizenship by descent where the Dominican parent's constitutional citizenship category satisfies section 99; later-generation cases require checking the Citizenship Act.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The Labour Ministry states that third-generation citizenship by descent is not provided.

parent_benefit_summary.value: The child’s citizenship does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on a migrant parent. The parent must use a separate work, residence, family or naturalization process.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No official automatic parent-of-citizen residence route was located.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status. A migrant father may document the citizen child and family ties in a residence application, but published rules still require a separate permit and ministerial approval.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not treat birth of a citizen child as an immediate passport or permanent-residence route for the father.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English is official, government procedures and WIN materials operate in English, and the WIN portal advertises island-wide internet connectivity.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Connectivity quality still varies by accommodation and location.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low outside private or expatriate contacts. Official procedures reviewed operate in English, and applicants should expect certified English translations for non-English documents.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from official-service language, not a measured proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national average monthly wage is published in the official material reviewed. The Statistics Office labour page exposes only 2011 employment tables and 1997/1999 labour-force reports; its survey list names an Occupational Wage Survey without publishing current results. The ILO report uses a 2008 occupational-wage survey, too old and occupation-specific for a 2026 national mean.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 1997 official survey reported EC$840 median monthly income, but the current CSO labour and archive pages publish no newer national median; the historical figure is not treated as current.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximation from the statutory EC$240/week minimum for a home assistant receiving meals: EC$1,040/month divided by the EC$2.70/USD peg. This is a category-specific statutory minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A current reliable national mean was not established. Official CSO pages list the survey programs but publish only historical labour material, while the ILO source uses a 2008 occupational survey rather than a current national average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The located official median is from 1997. No newer national median is published on the current CSO labour or archive pages, so no current USD conversion is supplied.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed minimum-wage order establishes category floors, but the current statistical pages publish no national upper wage distribution or meaningful maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: Category-dependent: EC$6.52/hour for juveniles, trainees and apprentices; EC$7.75/hour for temporary assistants; EC$9.00/hour for many adult categories; EC$240/week for home assistants receiving meals
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Rates effective 1 December 2025; Dominica does not publish one uniform monthly minimum for all workers.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The current Statistics Office site lists Labour Force and Occupational Wage surveys, but its labour-data page publishes only 2011 employment tables and 1997/1999 labour-force reports. The additional ILO Dominica report reproduces occupation-by-sex hourly rates from a 2008 Occupational Wage Survey, not a current all-worker monthly mean. Therefore no defensible 2026 average salary in XCD can be stated.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The official EC$840/month median is from the 1997 Labour Force Survey. Current CSO labour and archive pages do not publish a newer national median, so the historical amount is not presented as current.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current minimum-wage order sets category floors, while the CSO labour and archive pages expose no current national upper wage distribution or meaningful maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory category-specific minimum wages; current national average and median unpublished in the reviewed official materials
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum rates effective 2025-12-01; researched 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: High confidence in the December 2025 statutory category-specific minimum rates. Current national mean, median and upper-distribution values remain null because current CSO pages publish no wage-results table; the newest located wage observations are occupation-by-sex hourly rates from a 2008 survey cited by the ILO.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official statistical material does not publish a sufficiently current countrywide household cost-of-living estimate. Accommodation and imported-goods costs vary, so a crowdsourced index was not substituted.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: WIN itself is temporary and does not establish settlement. The strong classification applies only to the registered self-employed work-permit/residence route.
settlement_track.summary: A registered self-employed work permit is a qualifying residence route: permits are annual, permanent residence may be requested after five years, and the government publishes citizenship filing after seven years of residence. The route is credible for a foreign-client contractor, subject to discretionary approval and confirmation that the proposed software consultancy is accepted as self-employment.
settlement_track.notes: Preserve permit and physical-presence evidence. WIN time should not be counted unless the authorities expressly recognize it.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True for a contractor or freelancer who registers the consultancy in Dominica and receives a self-employed work permit. It is not automatically true for a salaried foreign employee, who would need WIN temporarily or written approval of another structure.

data.notes: Official sources support business registration, self-employed work-permit evidence, residence effect, five-year permanent-residence eligibility and seven-year citizenship filing. Confidence remains medium because no official example expressly covers a one-person software consultancy serving only foreign clients, work-permit approval is discretionary, and the treatment of general checklist items and DSS coverage should be confirmed before filing.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Self-employed work permit with business registration, or another qualifying work/residence permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: WIN can be followed by an independently approved work or residence permit. A self-employed work-permit route is documented, and PR can be requested after five years of qualifying residence/employment, subject to ministerial discretion.
requirements: For self-employment, register a business or show that registration and the Statement of Particulars are being processed.
Obtain and maintain annual work permits; Labour guidance requires at least five work permits for the work-based PR application.
Maintain lawful stay while the new application is considered and document finances and good character.
reviewed_route_names: Work in Nature (WIN) Extended Stay Visa
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Official pages allow in-country permit processing. They do not expressly confirm that an unchanged foreign-client arrangement qualifies for the self-employed permit, or that WIN time counts. Five years refers to the evidenced work/residence-permit route, not five years of WIN renewals. The unchanged remote-work profile is not confirmed; the conditional alternative requires an additional independently accepted eligibility basis.

data.selection_summary: No current dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence route was found. Ordinary temporary residence RT-9 requires an RS residence visa, while MIREX lists qualifying RS bases such as family ties, investment, pension, and passive rentista income; salary income is expressly excluded from the rentista category. An ordinary software engineer working for a foreign employer or client therefore has no confirmed independent residence-to-citizenship route.

visa_application.notes: This is DGM's official online filing portal, but it does not offer a digital-nomad application. RT-9 applicants must first obtain an RS residence visa from a Dominican consulate and later submit original documents in person. The applicant profile does not match the RS qualifying bases confirmed by MIREX.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No recurring monthly-income threshold is published. DGM instead requests Dominican solvency evidence, including a Dominican bank certificate showing at least DOP 300,000 or qualifying Dominican property.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No monthly threshold; DOP 300,000 in a Dominican bank account or qualifying Dominican property may evidence solvency

income_requirement_display.notes: RT-9 is not a remote-worker category and requires a prior RS visa. Active work under an ordinary foreign contract is not a confirmed RS eligibility basis.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed period of remote-work income proof applies. Bank movements may be requested when the account is older than three months, but they do not independently establish RS eligibility.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain an RS residence visa before entering for the RT-9 filing.
Provide passport, apostilled civil-status records, criminal-record certificate, photographs, guarantee policy, and a DGM-authorized medical examination.
Provide Dominican economic-solvency evidence, such as the specified local bank balance or property.
File online and subsequently submit original documents in person; DGM lists a DOP 14,000 filing fee and DOP 6,300 adult medical-examination fee.
