initial_validity.notes: This is temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually. The ordinary residence ladder generally requires five years in qualifying temporary-resident status before permanent residence.
extension_rules.notes: The settlement ladder matters only after lawful admission on a qualifying RS basis.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: RT-9 directly grants temporary residence after an RS visa and DGM approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The target applicant lacks a confirmed qualifying RS basis.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying ordinary temporary resident may proceed to permanent residence after the prescribed temporary-residence period and renewals.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not cure the absence of an initial remote-worker eligibility basis.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may generally be requested after more than two continuous years as a permanent resident.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The indicative general sequence is approximately five years of qualifying temporary residence followed by two years of permanent residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the prerequisite RS visa is tied to separately qualifying family, investor, pensioner, or rentista circumstances. A foreign employment or client contract is not itself a confirmed RS basis.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official threshold is denominated in USD.

income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: US$2,000 monthly plus US$250 per dependent
income_requirement_display.notes: An active software-engineering contract cannot be treated as qualifying rentista income because MIREX excludes salaries.

income_proof_months.notes: MIREX requests bank movements for the preceding three months and documents proving the passive source.

RS rentista visa, passport, criminal-record certificate, civil-status records, guarantee policy, and medical examination.

initial_validity.notes: Residence remains dependent on continuing rentista eligibility.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct one-year residence for qualifying rentistas after the RS visa process.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Active salary or service income does not qualify.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A residence progression exists for qualifying rentistas, but the category is outside this active-worker profile.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No conversion based solely on an ordinary foreign work contract was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: A qualifying resident may eventually use the ordinary naturalization framework.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make active salary income eligible for rentista residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant earns active software-work income and the official consular rules expressly exclude salary income.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general route-level minimum salary is published; eligibility instead depends on qualifying local employment.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No general route-level minimum salary published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A Dominican employment contract is the decisive requirement.

income_requirement_display.value: No general salary threshold published; qualifying Dominican employment is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not independently available to a person working only for a foreign client or employer.

income_proof_months.notes: The official requirements do not state a standardized number of prior salary months.

key_requirements.requirement: Dominican employment contract registered with the Ministry of Labor.
Employer guarantee and corporate or employer documentation.
Passport, visa or lawful entry documentation, civil records, criminal-record certificate, and medical examination.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: Temporary labor residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually while qualifying local employment continues.
extension_rules.notes: Loss of the qualifying employment basis can affect renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence for a qualifying locally employed worker.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Requires local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Any later residence progression depends on continued lawful qualifying status and applicable migration rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: It is not an independent foreign-contract route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization may eventually be possible after separately satisfying permanent-residence requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route fails the no-local-employer selection requirement.

summary.value: No independent degree-only, qualification-only, or points-tested residence route was found. The migration rules contain discretionary treatment for professionals of high national interest, but this is not an ordinary application route for a degree-holding remote software engineer.
summary.notes: The applicant's university degree does not create an RS visa basis.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreign individual becomes tax resident after more than 182 days in the Dominican Republic during the fiscal year, continuously or intermittently.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Conducting registered Dominican economic activity may create obligations independently of the residence-day test; individual circumstances require advice.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 5.91% figure is the employee share under Dominican payroll: 3.04% for Family Health Insurance plus 2.87% for old-age, disability, and survivors insurance. The employer ordinarily pays 7.09% health and 7.10% pension, plus the employer-only occupational-risk charge. TSS states that salaried workers, including regularized foreigners, must be reported. This percentage is not a confirmed charge for an ordinary foreign-contract worker outside Dominican payroll: CNSS describes the contributory-subsidized regime intended for independent and own-account workers but states that the general regime has not begun, apart from limited pilot arrangements. Consequently, no universal current self-employed contribution percentage can responsibly be substituted for the payroll rate.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly social-security or freelancer payment applies in the documented foreign-contract scenario. The intended general contributory-subsidized regime for independent workers is not generally operational, and immigration charges are transaction-based rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime was found. The Dominican system is territorial in important respects: Dominican-source income is taxable, while specified foreign-source investment and financial income of a resident foreigner generally enters scope from the third resident tax year.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is not a blanket exemption for active services physically performed in the Dominican Republic.

taxes.caveats: Remote services performed while physically present in the Dominican Republic may be treated as Dominican-source even when the payer is foreign. Tax and social-security outcomes depend on work location, residence days, contract structure, local registration, payroll status, deductions, and treaty coverage. Dominican professional advice is necessary before filing.

taxation_system.value: Mixed territorial and progressive system. Dominican-source taxable income is subject to progressive personal rates up to 25%; specified foreign-source investment and financial income becomes taxable for resident foreigners from their third resident tax year.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 182 days in the fiscal year, continuously or intermittently.
taxation_system.income_scope: Dominican-source income is taxable. Specified foreign-source investment and financial income of resident foreigners is also taxable beginning with the third resident tax year; the official notice does not establish a general exemption for active services performed locally.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or remote-worker regime was confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: Dominican-payroll employees contribute 3.04% health plus 2.87% pension. No generally operational contribution rate was confirmed for an independent foreign-contract worker under the contributory-subsidized regime.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 25% is the top marginal screening rate. Actual liability is progressive and depends on annual net taxable income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Up to DOP 416,220.00 annual taxable income
tax_brackets.notes: Exempt band; approximate USD conversion uses DOP 64.1 per US dollar.
The USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: DOP 31,216 plus 20% of excess over DOP 624,329.01
tax_brackets.notes: The USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: DOP 79,776 plus 25% of excess over DOP 867,123.01
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band and dashboard screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official tax and social-security sources support the ordinary payroll rates. The remaining filing uncertainty concerns source characterization of active foreign-client services and the absence of a generally operational contribution schedule for independent workers.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special nomad tax rate exists in the reviewed official sources. Any person living and working in the country would require ordinary immigration authority and an ordinary tax analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary tax rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive PIT up to 25% on taxable income; no special nomad rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 182 days in the fiscal year, continuously or intermittently.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Dominican-source income is taxable. Specified foreign investment and financial income enters scope from the third resident tax year; active services performed from Dominican territory should not be presumed foreign-source or exempt.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Local-payroll employee deductions total 5.91%. CNSS states that the general contributory-subsidized regime intended for independent workers has not generally begun, so no universal independent-worker percentage was confirmed.

fixed_payments.status: no_nomad_route_and_no_general_remote_worker_fixed_charge_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed monthly amount or generally operational contribution percentage was confirmed for a foreign-contract worker outside Dominican payroll.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: RT-9 lists a DOP 14,000 filing fee and DOP 6,300 adult medical examination, but the route is not available on a confirmed remote-work basis. A single countrywide RS consular fee was not established.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: ITBIS is generally 18% on taxable goods and services. Exported-service treatment and invoicing require fact-specific confirmation. No nomad levy or fixed freelancer tax was found.
fixed_payments.notes: Immigration fees are application or renewal costs rather than monthly tax. Guarantee-policy premiums are not published as one universal official amount.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying no more than 182 days may avoid tax residence under the presence test, but Dominican-source service income and immigration authorization can still create obligations. Visitor status is not a settlement route.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary progressive PIT and income-source rules apply. Services physically performed in the Dominican Republic may be Dominican-source despite a foreign payer.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Tax or business registration may create local filing and ITBIS obligations, but the current official sources do not describe a route allowing tourist entry, sole-proprietor registration, and conversion to residence solely on that basis. A general independent-worker social-security contribution schedule is not established as operational by the current sources checked.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax discussion is hypothetical for this profile because no qualifying remote-worker immigration status was confirmed.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route is confirmed for the target remote-worker profile.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General ordinary-residence sequence. It is not usable unless the applicant first qualifies for RT-9 through a valid RS basis.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization generally requires more than two years as a permanent resident and continuous qualifying presence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Theoretical general sequence of about five years of temporary residence plus two years of permanent residence. This is not a remote-worker timeline.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: MIP publishes a four-to-six-month estimate; six months is the conservative upper end, not a guarantee.

key_conditions.value: A qualifying immigration basis, timely residence renewals, permanent residence, continuous presence, valid civil and identity records, clean criminal history, income and solvency evidence, migration-history certifications, the required Dominican-culture examination, executive approval, and oath. Naturalization is discretionary rather than automatic.
key_conditions.notes: No general renunciation requirement was established; the Constitution recognizes dual nationality.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Official filing material states at least six months of marriage and more than six months of provisional residence. Requirements should be reconfirmed immediately before filing.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage helps only when the spouse is a Dominican citizen. Marriage to another foreign national does not create this accelerated nationality option.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The Constitution permits a person married to a Dominican to opt for the spouse's nationality subject to statutory requirements.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant still needs lawful residence, a valid residence card, registered marriage evidence, Dominican and foreign criminal-record certificates, migration records, income and solvency evidence, Dominican domicile, and executive approval. False records or a sham marriage can lead to denial, cancellation, and civil or criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically confer citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants nationality to persons born in Dominican territory except children of diplomatic or consular personnel, foreigners in transit, and foreigners residing illegally.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in the country generally qualifies when both migrant parents are lawful residents and are not classified as in transit. A child of parents who are both in transit or residing illegally is excluded, so the result depends on the parents' documented status.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean remains null because migrant status alone does not determine the outcome; civil-registry treatment should be confirmed for the family's exact documents.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Dominican mother or father is Dominican by descent, including when born abroad. The migrant father's nationality does not prevent acquisition through the citizen parent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Civil registration and proof of parentage may still be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically regularize or naturalize a foreign parent. Any family or humanitarian benefit requires a separate filing and case-specific legal basis.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The child's citizenship is not a substitute for the parent's immigration status.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship was confirmed for the migrant father merely because the child is Dominican. The reviewed family-residence protocol does not expressly list parents among the defined eligible relatives.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Professional Dominican immigration advice is necessary before relying on parentage.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when reviewed; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 44 visa-on-arrival destinations plus six eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 82. Its categories differ from indexes that combine visa-free and visa-on-arrival access.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is useful in tourism and international-business settings, but immigration, tax, naturalization, and civil-status procedures are conducted in Spanish. A remote worker without Spanish should expect certified translations and local professional assistance.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No official nationwide English-proficiency measure was established in this focused pass.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian should not be relied upon for government procedures; Spanish-language assistance and certified translations are advisable.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No official evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public-service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2024 national average monthly primary-occupation income of DOP 26,459 at approximately DOP 64.1 per US dollar.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current ONE labor portal and 2024 yearbook publish averages but not a current national median monthly labor income. An official methodology paper reports a DOP 6,820 median for 2007, which is too old and methodologically unsuitable for a current conversion.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the DOP 17,701.25 lower non-sectorized private-enterprise minimum effective 1 June 2026. This is a statutory minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2024 national average monthly income in the primary occupation.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national median monthly salary was published in the reviewed current ONE sources. The only exact official median located was from a 2007 income survey and is too stale to report as current.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A single national maximum wage is not a meaningful published labor-market statistic in the current official sources. The old methodology paper's sample maximum is not a statutory ceiling or current representative maximum and was therefore not converted.

min_salary_local_currency.value: DOP 17,701.25/month for the lower non-sectorized private-enterprise category and DOP 21,000/month for the larger-enterprise category, effective 1 June 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Dominican minimum wages vary by sector and enterprise category; there is no single universal national minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: ONE's national total excludes unpaid family helpers. A separate government report gives a December 2025 formal contributory average of DOP 38,733.94.

median_salary_local_currency.value: No current national median monthly wage is published in the reviewed ONE 2024 yearbook or current labor-data portal; the only exact official median located, DOP 6,820 for 2007, is too old to use as a current salary statistic
median_salary_local_currency.notes: This is a precise publication gap, not an estimate. The 2007 figure came from an older household income methodology exercise and is not substituted into the current field.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No current official national maximum wage or upper salary-distribution endpoint is published in the reviewed ONE and formal social-security wage sources; the historical survey sample maximum is not a national wage ceiling
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Maximum individual earnings are open-ended and survey sample maxima vary by dataset. The field therefore remains nonnumeric rather than treating an outlier or category average as a national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: National average monthly income in the primary occupation; statutory category-specific minimum used only for the minimum field
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: 2024; minimum: effective 1 June 2026; formal-sector comparison: December 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are local worker-income statistics, not immigration income thresholds. The DOP 26,459 average is broad national worker context, while DOP 38,733.94 covers formal social-security contributors. Focused searches confirmed that current official publications do not provide a comparable national median or meaningful national maximum.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No sufficiently authoritative current national cost-of-living figure directly comparable with the wage basis was established; the field remains null rather than using a crowd-sourced estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No current digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence category was found. Visitor stay, tourist extensions, foreign-client work, tax registration, or sole-proprietor registration alone do not create a settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: The country has genuine settlement routes, but none fits ordinary active foreign-contract remote work. RT-9 depends on a separately qualifying RS visa, rentista status excludes salaries, and RT-3 requires Dominican employment.
settlement_track.notes: The general temporary-residence, permanent-residence, and naturalization ladder must not be attributed to this applicant unless another qualifying immigration basis is obtained.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No reviewed category accepts ordinary active work for a foreign employer or client as the independent substantive residence basis. Rentista excludes salaries, RT-3 requires local employment, and RT-9 requires a prior RS visa tied to another qualifying basis.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field audit reviewed more than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs, including more than five URLs absent from the previous source set. It resolves the social-contribution note by distinguishing the 5.91% Dominican-payroll employee deduction from the not-generally-operational independent-worker regime. Current official wage publications still do not supply a comparable national median or meaningful maximum, so those local-currency fields now state exactly what is unpublished and why the old 2007 survey values cannot be used.

data.selection_summary: Ecuador is a strong match. Its active Visa Nómada is a temporary-residence category expressly covering employees, independent professionals and business owners working remotely for foreign employers or clients. The 2026 threshold is USD 1,446 per month (three 2026 SBU) proven over the preceding three months. After at least 21 continuous months of temporary residence, the holder can apply for permanent residence; ordinary naturalization then requires at least three years holding permanent residence, Spanish and civic knowledge, lawful means and controlled absences.

visa_application.title: MREMH Servicios Digitales / e-VISAS
visa_application.notes: The official Visa Nómada procedure instructs applicants to register and submit through this platform. The portal is JavaScript-dependent; confirm the selected visa category, document list and payable amounts before submitting because the initial application fee is non-refundable.

best_routes.route_name: Visa de Residencia Temporal Rentista para Trabajo Remoto (Visa Nómada)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The rule is three Salarios Básicos Unificados. The 2026 SBU is USD 482, making the current monthly threshold USD 1,446.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 1,446 per month, or USD 17,352 for each requested year
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Ecuador uses the US dollar. The annual alternative is 36 SBU; for 2026 this equals USD 17,352.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 1,446/month (3 × 2026 SBU), shown for the previous 3 months; alternatively USD 17,352 per requested year
income_requirement_display.notes: Add USD 250 monthly income for each dependent. Because the threshold is indexed to the SBU, recheck it for the filing year.

income_proof_months.notes: International bank statements must show qualifying foreign-source income during the three months immediately preceding the application; the procedure also permits an annual-funds alternative.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign employer/client contract, service documents or proof of ownership of a company registered and domiciled abroad; the work must be remote, digital or telework.
Passport valid for at least six months, compliant photograph and lawful immigration status where applicable.
National-level criminal-record certificates from the country of origin and countries of residence during the preceding five years, translated and apostilled or legalized as applicable.
National or foreign health-insurance policy valid for the visa period and expressly covering Ecuador.
Pay USD 50 to submit and USD 270 upon grant; neither amount is subject to VAT.
Maintain the underlying foreign remote-work/income basis because permanent-residence filing requires documentation showing that the fact giving rise to the temporary visa continues.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence, ordinarily up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The current nomad procedure confirms temporary-resident status but does not print a separate validity line. The governing temporary-residence framework provides the two-year duration.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence may generally be renewed once for a further two-year period, subject to updated requirements and continued eligibility; applying for permanent residence after 21 continuous months is normally the more settlement-oriented step.
extension_rules.notes: Confirm the current renewal option in the e-VISAS filing flow because the nomad procedure itself does not state a route-specific renewal period.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved Visa Nómada itself grants temporary-resident status; no local-employer sponsorship or preliminary visitor-to-work conversion is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply before the temporary status expires after at least 21 continuous months as a temporary resident. The applicant must document the qualifying period, lawful means and continuation of the fact that supported the temporary visa.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The permanent visa is indefinite. Compliance with absence limits and continuity of the nomad visa's underlying basis are important.

path_to_citizenship.value: After conversion, ordinary naturalization requires at least three years of regular, continuous domicile while holding permanent residence, plus Spanish, Ecuador history/geography/culture knowledge, lawful means, an interview and good standing with the state.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The official procedure measures the three-year period from permanent residence, not from initial temporary residence. Naturalization is not automatic.

best_routes.notes: This is an unusually clear remote-worker fit because the official category expressly accepts foreign employment and foreign-client independent services. It is also residence—not visitor—status. The credible settlement sequence is Visa Nómada → permanent residence after 21 continuous months → naturalization after three years as a permanent resident.

best_routes.route_name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Profesional, Técnico, Tecnólogo o Artesano

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official procedure requires lawful means but does not publish a route-specific fixed monthly threshold in the material inspected.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No current route-specific numeric threshold was established after focused review.

income_requirement_display.value: Lawful means required; no current fixed amount confirmed
income_requirement_display.notes: Verify the means-of-life standard used by the filing office before applying.

income_proof_months.notes: The inspected procedure does not state a fixed bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Apostilled or legalized professional, technical or technological qualification.
Registration of the foreign qualification with Ecuador's competent higher-education authority.
Passport, criminal-record documentation, lawful means and applicable fees.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence, ordinarily 2 years

extension_rules.value: Subject to the general temporary-residence renewal framework and continued qualification; permanent residence becomes available after at least 21 continuous months.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The qualification-based visa directly grants temporary residence after the title is accepted and registered.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The general route permits application after at least 21 continuous months of temporary residence, before expiry and while the qualifying basis continues.

path_to_citizenship.value: Following permanent residence, ordinary naturalization requires at least three years as a permanent resident and the standard language, knowledge, lawful-means and continuity conditions.

best_routes.notes: Useful independent fallback for a degree-holding software engineer, but classified partial because it is a qualification-based residence category rather than a route specifically validating ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The Visa Nómada is the cleaner profile match.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor/tourist entry followed only by freelancer or RUC registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitor status has no qualifying residence income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not applicable to a visitor-only strategy.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—visitor status is not a residence route

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable.

key_requirements.requirement: RUC registration identifies a person conducting economic activity for tax purposes, but it does not itself grant immigration residence or work authorization.
A visitor would need to obtain a qualifying residence visa, such as the Visa Nómada, rather than rely on tourist status or tax registration.

initial_validity.value: Visitor stay only; not qualifying residence

extension_rules.value: Tourist extensions do not transform the stay into qualifying temporary residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path through bank-account, RUC or sole-proprietor registration alone; a separate residence-visa application is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Visitor time does not meet the requirement of at least 21 continuous months as a temporary resident.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path. Ordinary naturalization requires permanent residence and the subsequent qualifying period.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because opening accounts or registering for tax does not legalize residence. Use the dedicated Visa Nómada instead.

summary.value: A foreigner with an accepted professional, technical or technological title may independently seek the Professional temporary-residence visa without a local-employer sponsor. The title must be apostilled/legalized and registered with the competent Ecuadorian authority. It is an independent residence option and can use the general 21-month permanent-residence transition, but it is not a dedicated foreign-remote-work authorization.
summary.notes: Classified as partial because the degree is the qualifying basis, not the applicant's ordinary foreign contract.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence generally arises at 183 or more days in Ecuador, including sporadic absences, in the same fiscal year, or under the 183-day test across a rolling 12-month period spanning two fiscal years. Economic-interest, asset and close-family-tie tests can also establish residence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The official rule is broader than a simple day count. A residence visa and work physically performed in Ecuador may also create filing exposure before the user assumes it does.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal rate, not an expected effective rate. The progressive table begins at 0% and reaches 37% only above USD 109,956 of taxable annual income.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the voluntary-contributor rate over the declared contribution base. It is not established as a universal compulsory charge solely for holding the Visa Nómada, although participation is required when relying on the foreign-income branch of the temporary tax-residence regime.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Minimum 2026 voluntary IESS contribution: 17.6% of the USD 482 minimum base, rounded by IESS to USD 84.83. It is conditional/voluntary rather than an automatic Visa Nómada fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: A five-year temporary tax-residence regime may be elected once by qualifying first-time Ecuador tax residents. It limits income tax to Ecuador-source income, requires at least 183 days in Ecuador in each relevant fiscal year and timely proof/notification. The foreign-income qualification branch also requires continued social-security affiliation; an investment branch exists separately.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is not an automatic digital-nomad exemption. Because Ecuador defines income from activities executed in Ecuador as Ecuador-source regardless of payment location, professional advice is needed before assuming remote-service income is outside the regime's taxable scope.

taxes.caveats: Immigration classification and tax sourcing are separate. Ecuador treats income from activities executed in Ecuador as Ecuador-source regardless of where it is paid, while resident individuals can also face tax on foreign income. Foreign tax credits, treaty position, employee versus contractor characterization, RUC obligations, VAT and municipal patente rules can materially change the result. Obtain Ecuador tax advice before beginning work in-country or electing temporary tax residence.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax. For 2026 the annual zero-rate band ends at USD 12,208 and marginal rates rise through 5%, 10%, 12%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35% and 37%. Ecuador-source rules focus on where activity is performed, while tax residents can also be taxed on income generated abroad, subject to relief. A qualifying five-year temporary tax-residence regime taxes only Ecuador-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally 183 days, with additional economic-interest, asset and family-tie tests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Ecuador-source income for non-residents; residents can be taxed on Ecuador-source and foreign income. Services performed physically in Ecuador may be Ecuador-source even when the payer and bank account are foreign.
taxation_system.special_regimes: One-time five-year temporary tax residence for qualifying new residents, limited to Ecuador-source income; it is elective and conditional, not inherent in the nomad visa.
taxation_system.social_security: Voluntary IESS contributors pay 17.6% of a chosen base not below the SBU. Private employees normally contribute 9.45%, with 12.15% paid by the employer. Nomad-visa insurance is separately required for the visa period.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 37% is the top marginal screening rate. It should not be interpreted as the tax rate on all earnings or as the applicant's expected effective rate.

tax_brackets.notes: No base tax in this band.
Base tax USD 167.
Base tax USD 631.
Base tax USD 1,412.
Base tax USD 2,678.
Base tax USD 4,965.
Base tax USD 8,823.
Base tax USD 15,025.
Base tax USD 24,572; this is the top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official SRI sources establish the residence tests, special-regime framework and 2026 brackets. PwC's Ecuador summary, last reviewed 23 July 2026, was used to interpret income sourcing, foreign income, social security, VAT and municipal charges.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The Visa Nómada creates immigration residence but no automatic nomad tax holiday. Ecuador-source work income is taxed under the ordinary progressive system up to 37%; work performed in Ecuador can be Ecuador-source even if the client and payment are foreign. Tax residents may also face tax on foreign income. A separately elected five-year temporary tax-residence regime can limit tax to Ecuador-source income, but its conditions and Ecuador's broad service-source rule must be analyzed carefully.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary resident remote worker; ordinary individual tax rules unless a separate tax election applies
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–37% progressive; 37% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally 183 days, but economic-interest, asset and family-tie tests also apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents' foreign income can be taxable, with foreign-tax relief potentially available. Income from activity executed in Ecuador may be treated as Ecuador-source regardless of foreign payer or receipt location.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No visa-specific exemption. A general five-year temporary tax-residence regime for qualifying new residents taxes only Ecuador-source income and may require continued IESS affiliation under the foreign-income branch.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No local employer payroll is inherent in the visa. Voluntary IESS costs 17.6% of the declared base, minimum USD 84.83 monthly in 2026. Separate private or public health coverage is required for the immigration status.

fixed_payments.status: Conditional; no universal monthly nomad levy confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Voluntary IESS minimum USD 84.83/month in 2026; potentially mandatory when using the relevant temporary tax-residence qualification branch.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: USD 50 application plus USD 270 grant fee; permanent-residence transition currently lists USD 50 application plus USD 225 grant fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: An economically active independent professional may need RUC registration and a municipal patente, reported by PwC as approximately USD 10–700 depending on activity/accounting status. Professional services can attract 15% VAT depending on sourcing and export treatment.
fixed_payments.notes: Health-insurance premium is mandatory for the visa but no universal price exists; it depends on policy and applicant.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Do not assume zero Ecuador tax merely because presence is below 183 days. Services physically performed in Ecuador may be Ecuador-source; occasional non-resident work paid entirely abroad may have different treatment, requiring fact-specific advice.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary progressive PIT up to 37% can apply, including to foreign income. Check foreign-tax credits and whether the temporary tax-residence election is available.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: RUC, invoicing, expense records, possible 15% VAT, annual income-tax filing, municipal patente and optional/conditional IESS may apply. RUC registration does not itself grant immigration status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in statutory brackets and broad rules; medium confidence in an individual nomad's ultimate sourcing and special-regime result because that depends on where services are performed, employment structure, prior residence, election timing and treaty facts.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The visa itself directly grants temporary residence upon approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: At least 21 continuous months as a temporary resident, with the application filed before the status expires.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The current official procedure requires at least three years of regular domicile holding permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Minimum eligibility arithmetic from grant of temporary residence: 21 months plus three years as a permanent resident. Processing time and transition timing make the practical total longer.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official procedure describes review, examination, interview, fees and notification but does not publish a reliable typical or guaranteed end-to-end processing time. No sufficiently authoritative current statistic was found after focused searching.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous lawful residence and the visa's underlying basis; apply for permanent residence before temporary status expires; keep absences within applicable limits. Naturalization requires permanent residence for three years, Spanish speaking and writing, civic knowledge, lawful means, good standing with the state and an interview. Absence exceeding 180 days in a year during the first three permanent-resident years interrupts naturalization eligibility. Renunciation of the original nationality is not required.
key_conditions.notes: The official process remains an eligibility-based administrative determination, not automatic citizenship.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Two years from an Ecuador marriage celebration, or from Ecuador Civil Registry registration when the marriage occurred abroad; registered de facto unions use the registration date.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing foreign marriage counts only after it is registered with Ecuador's Civil Registry; the official two-year period for a marriage celebrated abroad runs from that Ecuador registration. Domicile must be established in Ecuador. If the Ecuadorian spouse was naturalized, the marriage/union must post-date that spouse's acquisition of Ecuadorian nationality.

requirements_and_risks.value: The foreign spouse must hold an eligible residence category; temporary visitors and protection applicants cannot use this naturalization procedure. Required elements include the registered civil-status record, identity/filiation documents, interview, good standing with the state, potentially proof of lawful means and fees. Both spouses/partners may need to participate. Authorities can verify the continuing genuine relationship; false documents or sham relationships carry refusal, cancellation and criminal/immigration risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage also supports permanent residence under the mobility framework, but citizenship is never automatic merely upon marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 7 grants Ecuadorian nationality by birth to persons born in Ecuador without a parental residence or nationality condition. The classification remains broad jus soli notwithstanding any narrow public-international-law exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Ecuador is Ecuadorian by birth even when both parents are foreign migrants; the Constitution does not condition territorial citizenship on either parent's status.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Ecuadorian if born in Ecuador and can also qualify by descent when born abroad to an Ecuadorian-born mother or father, within the Constitution's stated descent limits.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father's status does not prevent the child's nationality.

parent_benefit_summary.value: An Ecuadorian child can provide a family basis for the foreign parent to seek permanent residence as a close relative, subject to the immigration procedure and evidence. It does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Verify the current family-category checklist before filing.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father may qualify for family-based permanent residence through the Ecuadorian child, but must apply and satisfy identity, filiation, admissibility and other requirements. Father citizenship is not automatic; the ordinary or marriage-based naturalization rules remain separate.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on the date checked; index methodologies differ, so this should not be mixed with Henley ranking.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required category shown by the same index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 48 visa-on-arrival destinations and 6 eTA destinations. Other eVisa/pre-enrolment categories are treated separately by the index.

passport.notes: All passport figures use the same Passport Index 2026 methodology and snapshot. Destination rules can change without notice.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be workable within an international remote-work bubble and parts of Quito, but Spanish is needed for government processes, contracts and broad day-to-day integration. EF EPI 2025 ranks Ecuador 83rd of 123 with 'low' English proficiency, although its IT-function score is materially higher.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The EF index is a non-governmental, self-selected adult test dataset, so use it as a practical signal rather than a census measure.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or broadly documented working languages. A migrant should expect to rely primarily on Spanish, with English useful only in narrower professional and expatriate settings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current national dataset measuring Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found after focused searching; the conclusion is therefore cautious.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Official INEC national average monthly labor income for April 2026; urban average was USD 563 and rural average USD 388.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Official national median monthly labor income for all employed persons, salaried and independent, in Q1 2026, expressed in real December 2025 dollars.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statutory 2026 Salario Básico Unificado, not an observed minimum across all workers.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: National average labor income for April 2026.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: National median labor income for Q1 2026; includes employees and independent workers.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary was published in the inspected wage releases; a maximum would be distribution- and occupation-dependent.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: US dollar is Ecuador's circulating currency.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Minimum is statutory SBU; average is national monthly labor income; median covers all employed persons including salaried and independent workers.

settlement_track.summary: The Visa Nómada is genuine temporary residence and the general permanent-residence procedure expressly accepts holders after at least 21 continuous months. Citizenship requires a later switch to permanent residence and three further qualifying years, making the route a credible but multi-stage settlement track.
settlement_track.notes: The 4.75-year figure is minimum eligibility arithmetic, not a guaranteed passport date. Filing and processing delays extend the practical timeline.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official procedure expressly covers dependent employment and autonomous professional services for foreign employers, clients or companies, as well as ownership of a foreign company. No Ecuadorian employer or local client is required.

data.notes: The previous Ecuador record contained conflicting selection and settlement flags. This audit resolves them in favor of a full match: the current official Visa Nómada procedure confirms ordinary foreign-contract remote work, while the official permanent-residence and naturalization procedures confirm the 21-month temporary-to-permanent transition and three-year permanent-resident naturalization period. Tax treatment remains the main area requiring individual professional advice.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Visa de Residencia Temporal Rentista para Trabajo Remoto (Visa Nómada)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The nomad visa is qualifying temporary residence. Its holder can apply for permanent residence after at least 21 continuous months, before the current temporary status expires.
requirements: Maintain the temporary remote-work residence and its qualifying basis for at least 21 continuous months.
Apply before expiry with evidence of lawful means of support, temporary-residence history, the underlying visa basis and Ecuador criminal record.
reviewed_route_names: Visa de Residencia Temporal Rentista para Trabajo Remoto (Visa Nómada)
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The official nomad procedure and PR procedure both opened successfully. 1.75 years is the 21-month application threshold, not a promise of approval or processing duration. The PR filing can be made through offices within Ecuador; continuity and absence rules still apply.

data.selection_summary: Egypt does not currently offer a confirmed digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or qualification-based independent residence route for a software engineer working solely for a foreign client. Official channels cover tourism, legacy/special residence categories, locally sponsored foreign employment, and investment-based residence or citizenship; none satisfies the ordinary foreign-contract remote-work and citizenship-path criteria.

visa_application.title: Egypt Electronic Visa Portal
visa_application.notes: Official Ministry of Interior tourism-eVisa portal with online applications; it is not an application channel for remote-worker residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists because these are tourism/visitor permissions.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income requirement is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; tourism/visitor status
income_requirement_display.notes: The portal publishes USD 30 single-entry and USD 65 multiple-entry tourism-visa fees, not an income test.

income_proof_months.notes: No recurring-income proof period is specified for the tourism eVisa.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligible nationality, passport valid for at least six months, eVisa printout, itinerary, and relevant accommodation or supporting documents.
Temporary tourism residence is for tourism, visits, treatment, and similar purposes, for no more than one year at a time.

initial_validity.value: The eVisa is a tourism entry document; temporary tourism residence may be authorized for up to one year.
initial_validity.notes: Nationality-specific entry validity should be checked in the portal.

extension_rules.value: Temporary tourism residence is described as renewable, but renewal is not established by the current sources to authorize foreign-contract work or create a settlement route.
extension_rules.notes: Renewability does not turn tourism status into qualifying remote-worker residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary tourism residence may be obtainable but remains visitor-based and is not a remote-work residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion from tourism/eVisa status to permanent or ordinary long-term residence was established for this profile.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Published ordinary residence is a legacy category tied to residence before 26 May 1952, not progression from tourist status.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path arises from the eVisa or tourism residence itself.
path_to_citizenship.notes: General discretionary naturalization following qualifying residence is separate and does not validate visitor-based remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourism permission is neither work authorization nor qualifying citizenship-path residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker threshold applies; eligibility depends on local employment and work-permit approval.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No dedicated salary threshold for the target foreign-contract scenario is published in the inspected service material.

income_requirement_display.value: Local-employer work authorization required; no remote-worker income formula
income_requirement_display.notes: The Ministry describes Egyptian companies or qualifying business owners seeking authorization to employ foreigners.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not a foreign-income route.

key_requirements.requirement: An employing company or qualifying local business must pursue authorization to employ the foreign worker.
Foreign-worker licensing is governed by Egyptian labor legislation and implementing procedures.

initial_validity.value: Depends on the approved employment and work permit.
initial_validity.notes: The inspected official service index did not publish a complete generally applicable permit-duration rule.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continued local work authorization.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary residence may accompany authorized local employment but is not independently available to the target applicant.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The permit does not establish a direct permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only separate discretionary general naturalization rules could eventually apply; the work permit does not grant citizenship directly.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an Egyptian employer or locally established employing business is required.

income_proof_months.notes: Not an income-based remote-worker route.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Requires local business and investment substance.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent-residence entitlement was established; permission remains project-linked.

path_to_citizenship.value: Investor residence is distinct from the separate citizenship-by-investment program and general naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because founder, investment, and locally substantiated business routes are outside the profile; a foreign software contract alone is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Uses administrative fees and substantial investment rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Program amounts are structured in foreign currency.

income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Investment project, real estate, treasury contribution, or Central Bank deposit
income_requirement_display.notes: Not an ordinary income-based residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: Not an income route.

Execute an approved investment, real-estate, treasury-contribution, or deposit option.

initial_validity.value: Six months of temporary residence after preliminary approval to execute the investment.

extension_rules.value: Not an ordinary renewable route; citizenship follows only after investment completion and a Prime Ministerial decision.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Six-month implementation residence following preliminary approval.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The program proceeds toward citizenship rather than conventional permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship may be granted by Prime Ministerial decision after completing an approved investment.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Approval is discretionary and security-vetted.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because substantial investment is explicitly outside the target profile.

summary.value: No independent degree- or qualification-based residence route comparable to skilled migration was established. The public materials do not establish that a foreign university degree alone qualifies an applicant or that student residence authorizes ordinary foreign-client work.
summary.notes: Institution-sponsored student residence requires separate verification and would not itself match the applicant’s remote-work purpose.

tax_residency_rule.value: Resident if the person has a permanent home in Egypt or spends more than 183 days, continuously or intermittently, in a 12-month period. A separate rule covers Egyptians paid by the Egyptian treasury while abroad.
tax_residency_rule.notes: An applicable double-tax treaty can modify the analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 11% figure is the covered employee share, not a universal levy on an unsponsored foreign remote worker. The ordinary employer share is 18.75%. For 2026 the insured monthly salary is bounded at EGP 2,700–16,700, implying an employee amount of EGP 297–1,837 and an employer amount of EGP 506.25–3,131.25 where ordinary employee coverage applies. Egypt has no qualifying digital-nomad status, so contribution liability for the target scenario cannot be inferred from payroll rates; own-account and specified informal-worker categories can follow different rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment applies to the target scenario. Social insurance is percentage-based, and Egypt has no digital-nomad category from which a route-specific payment could arise.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, non-dom, or general inbound-worker tax holiday is published. Treaty relief may provide a credit or deduction for income taxed twice.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty eligibility and income characterization require case-specific advice.

taxes.caveats: Immigration permission and taxation are separate. Work physically performed in Egypt may create Egyptian-source or taxable professional income even below 183 days; permanent-home, centre-of-activity, treaty, contract, registration, and social-insurance facts can change the result.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax from 0% to 27.5%. Residents are taxed on Egyptian income and qualifying foreign income where their centre of commercial, industrial, or professional activity is in Egypt; non-residents are taxed on Egyptian-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home in Egypt or more than 183 days in a 12-month period, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Egyptian-source income, plus qualifying foreign income for residents whose centre of professional, commercial, or industrial activity is in Egypt.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad regime; treaty foreign-tax relief may apply.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees contribute 11% and employers 18.75% of insured salary. The 2026 insured monthly salary base is EGP 2,700–16,700. Certain registered managers/directors fall under a different employer-category treatment.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 27.5% dashboard figure is the top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. PwC also reports an EGP 20,000 annual salary-tax exemption; final liability depends on bracket-relief and income classification rules.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD upper boundary using about EGP 50.7/USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual earned income above the approximate USD threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The ETA supplies governing materials and 2026 payroll forms; current numerical interpretation also uses PwC’s February 2026 professional summary because a consolidated current official English bracket table was not located.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Egypt has no confirmed digital-nomad immigration or tax category. Anyone working there under another lawful status would need ordinary residence, source, professional-income, treaty, registration, and social-insurance rules analyzed.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary individual or business taxation only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive PIT up to 27.5% where taxable; top marginal rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home or more than 183 days in 12 months, subject to treaty analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign income can fall within Egyptian taxation for a resident whose centre of professional, commercial, or industrial activity is in Egypt; work physically performed in Egypt also requires source analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None published.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: There is no route-specific digital-nomad contribution. Covered employment ordinarily uses 11% employee and 18.75% employer rates on the insured salary; NOSI sets the 2026 insured-salary base at EGP 2,700–16,700. Different own-account or manager categories may apply under separate lawful registration.

fixed_payments.status: not_applicable_no_digital_nomad_route
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No route-specific fixed payment exists. Ordinary social insurance is percentage-based and depends on a separately lawful covered status; for covered employees the 2026 insured-salary base is EGP 2,700–16,700.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Tourism eVisa fees are USD 30 single entry and USD 65 multiple entry. These are visitor charges, not digital-nomad or remote-worker residence fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Ordinary tax, 14% VAT where registration applies, the 0.05% employee Martyrs Fund payroll deduction, stamp, or registration liabilities depend on the alternative structure; none is a universal digital-nomad payment.
fixed_payments.notes: The fixed-payment question is inapplicable because official visa, residence, labor, tax, and social-insurance materials do not define a digital-nomad status. This does not establish zero liability: work from Egypt would require analysis under another lawful employment, business, or residence status.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 183 days does not guarantee zero Egyptian tax because permanent-home, source, work-location, and treaty rules still matter; tourism status is not a settlement strategy.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Potentially subject to progressive PIT up to 27.5% and possibly foreign-income taxation depending on the centre of professional activity and treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Business, tax, VAT, social-insurance, and investor-residence rules may apply, but no simple foreign-client freelancer legalization route is published.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax screening does not create immigration eligibility.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: There is no qualifying independent remote-work residence route from which to calculate this stage.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No general permanent-residence progression from the rejected tourism scenario was established.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalization is framed around ten consecutive years of normal residence, not years following a defined permanent-residence stage.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum normal-residence period for discretionary general naturalization, not a timeline available through the rejected remote-worker scenario.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The law and electronic service directory publish no typical processing time for ordinary ten-year naturalization; the investor-program timeline is inapplicable.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization is discretionary after at least ten consecutive years of normal residence and requires adulthood, good conduct, Arabic ability, mental capacity, and lawful livelihood. The law does not establish that tourism/eVisa time or unauthorized remote work supplies a qualifying route.
key_conditions.notes: Continuous lawful residence and filing practice require confirmation with the nationality authority.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The accelerated provision is specifically for a foreign woman married to an Egyptian man; no equivalent two-year entitlement for a foreign husband was established.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage can support a foreign wife’s application, but she must notify her wish to acquire nationality; marriage alone is not automatic. The marriage generally must continue for two years after notification.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Gender-specific and unrelated to remote-worker eligibility.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be officially documented; the service procedure requires participation by both spouses and later confirmation that the marriage continues. The Minister may issue a reasoned refusal, and false documents or statements carry criminal and nationality risks.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sham marriage is legally dangerous.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Egypt primarily applies citizenship by descent. Birth in Egypt alone is generally insufficient, with narrow foundling, unknown/stateless-parentage, and specified Egypt-born provisions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Egypt to two foreign parents is not ordinarily Egyptian automatically. Narrow exceptions or later application provisions may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parent residence or permanent residence alone does not create automatic birthright citizenship under the inspected law.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with an Egyptian parent generally qualifies through descent; Ministry services expressly cover children of Egyptian mothers.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Registration and proof of the Egyptian parent’s nationality may be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically grant residence, permanent residence, or citizenship to a foreign parent; any family-residence benefit requires a separate application.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The inspected law contains no automatic parent-of-citizen naturalization entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Egyptian, the child can generally obtain Egyptian citizenship, but the migrant father does not thereby become Egyptian and no accelerated citizenship entitlement for him was established.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Possible family-residence treatment requires separate verification.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in parts of Cairo, Alexandria, tourism, technology, and international business, but nationwide proficiency is limited and government procedures should be expected in Arabic. EF’s 2025 index gives Egypt a score of 458 and rank 89; its IT subgroup scores 492.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF uses a self-selected adult testing dataset rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian may be encountered in some Red Sea tourism areas, but neither is official and no reliable nationwide service-availability evidence was established. Arabic remains necessary for government processes, with English the more practical second language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The inspected sources do not establish dependable Russian- or Ukrainian-language access to immigration, banking, tax, or legal services.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of CAPMAS’s EGP 5,005 monthly average using about EGP 50.7/USD. The wage observation concerns 2023.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The directly inspectable CAPMAS material reports arithmetic averages, while the inspected ILOSTAT interface did not expose a current Egypt median observation.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the EGP 7,000 statutory monthly minimum using about EGP 50.7/USD.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the EGP 5,005 official 2023 establishment-worker average. The older average is below the later minimum wage because the periods differ.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national monthly median can be converted: the CAPMAS establishment release reports arithmetic averages, the public 2024 labor-force catalog exposes a bulletin but no median in its inspectable metadata, and the ILOSTAT catalog defines median tables but did not expose a current Egypt observation through the inspected interface.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum wage is not a bounded labor-market statistic. CAPMAS publishes averages rather than a top observed wage; the EGP 16,700 social-insurance ceiling is not a maximum wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory private-sector minimum effective 1 March 2025; PwC identifies EGP 7,000 as current in its February 2026 review.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: CAPMAS 2023 average monthly wage for workers in public/public-business and private-sector establishments, published in 2024.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The directly inspected CAPMAS establishment release publishes arithmetic averages only. CAPMAS’s public 2024 labor-force catalog exposes the bulletin but does not state a national monthly median in its inspectable metadata, while ILOSTAT lists median-monthly-earnings tables but the inspected interface yielded no current Egypt observation. A current EGP median therefore remains unpublished in the named inspectable sources and is kept null.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Official wage materials report averages and a statutory minimum, not a national maximum. Wages have no general upper legal ceiling; EGP 16,700 is only the 2026 maximum salary base for social-insurance contributions and must not be represented as a maximum wage.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory 2025 private-sector minimum and CAPMAS 2023 establishment-worker average monthly wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly; minimum current in the February 2026 tax review, average observed in 2023
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are Egyptian-worker wage indicators, not immigration income requirements. The average is older than the minimum-wage figure and is not a current 2026 average.

cost_of_living_note.value: CAPMAS publishes consumer-price and household-expenditure material, but the inspected official sources do not supply a current comparable monthly basket for a single remote worker.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing and imported-goods costs vary sharply by city and exchange rate; no crowdsourced estimate was substituted.
