settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourism eVisa or renewable temporary tourism residence is visitor-based and must not be treated as remote-work or citizenship-path status.
settlement_track.summary: No current ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route was confirmed. Reaching Egypt’s discretionary ten-year naturalization threshold would require a different lawful qualifying residence basis; employment and investor bases do not fit this profile.
settlement_track.notes: The conclusion follows review of official visa, residence, labor, investment, and nationality inventories; none defines an ordinary digital-nomad or foreign-client freelance route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign-client work alone matches no published residence category. Tourism is visitor-only, foreign employment requires local authorization, and investor residence requires an Egyptian investment project.

data.notes: The previous ineligibility conclusion is preserved. This focused pass inspected current immigration, tax, social-insurance, payroll, and wage sources, including eight relevant URLs outside the previous source set. It resolves the digital-nomad fixed-payment marker as inapplicable because no such route exists, clarifies the 2026 contribution base and rates, and retains precise nulls for national median and maximum wages because the inspected current sources do not publish those statistics.

data.selection_summary: El Salvador has no dedicated digital-nomad visa, but temporary residence with work authorization expressly covers independent migrant workers. An applicant may self-apply without a local employer by documenting genuine self-employed activity, a business address, projected monthly income and any required permits. This can fit a foreign-client software consultant operating from El Salvador, but a person remaining solely a foreign employee should obtain filing-level confirmation. Temporary residents can generally seek definitive residence after three years, and most nationalities can seek naturalization after five total years of temporary and definitive residence.

visa_application.title: Residencias temporales
visa_application.notes: The official DGME page links to form F3 for temporary residence with authorization to work. It is route information and a downloadable-form index, not a complete online application. Filing is handled through DGME service offices; confirm the current form, appointment process and acceptance of foreign-client home-office software consulting before filing.

best_routes.route_name: Temporary Residence with Authorization to Work — Independent Migrant Worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numerical minimum is published. The applicant must declare projected monthly economic income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed minimum published; projected monthly income must be declared in USD
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The United States dollar is used by the official form and fee schedule.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum published; provide a projected monthly-income declaration
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Projected monthly economic income, without a published floor
income_requirement_display.notes: The official requirements demand a notarized declaration describing the activity, address, business location, start date and projected monthly income. They prescribe neither an income floor nor a historical income period.

income_proof_months.notes: The sources require projected monthly income and supporting documentation but do not state a fixed number of prior income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Application signed by the foreign applicant, legal representative, attorney or employer; an independent applicant may sign personally.
Valid passport and copies of used pages.
Police or criminal-record certificate from the country of origin or residence during the two years before entry, apostilled or authenticated and translated into Spanish when necessary.
Current Salvadoran police clearance if the applicant has stayed more than three months or entered more than twice during the preceding year.
Notarized declaration describing the independent activity, domicile, business location, start date and projected monthly income.
Municipal, professional, state or business-registration permits when the specific activity requires them.
Published processing target is 45 working days when all requirements are met.
Published residence fee for up to one year is USD 70 for Central Americans and USD 140 for non-Central Americans; confirm fees for a longer grant.

initial_validity.value: Up to two years, with multiple entry
initial_validity.notes: The migration law allows migrant-worker temporary residence for up to two years. The service sheet publishes fees specifically for a grant of up to one year, so the actual first grant should be confirmed with DGME.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for periods of up to two years while the qualifying activity and other requirements continue
extension_rules.notes: The renewal form requires an independent worker to restate the activity, domicile, business location and start date, support the declaration and provide a current business registration if the person is a merchant.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct application for temporary residence with work authorization as an independent migrant worker; no visitor-to-business conversion is required by the category itself.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: DGME states that applicants must identify the applicable category, submit the application and supporting documents, pay the fee and undergo document verification.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A non-Central-American temporary resident can generally apply for definitive residence after maintaining temporary residence for the preceding three years; Spanish and Hispanic-American nationals have a one-year rule.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Definitive residence is a separate filing. Continued lawful status, presence, income evidence and police checks matter.

path_to_citizenship.value: For a foreigner not covered by a special nationality rule, naturalization becomes available after five years of residence, counting both temporary and definitive residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is a separate application and is not automatic. The law requires definitive-resident documentation at filing, police clearance, supporting civil records, fees and an oath or declaration of adherence to Salvadoran law.

best_routes.notes: This is a residence-and-work category, not a digital-nomad visa. It is a credible fit where the applicant genuinely conducts software consulting as an independent business from a declared Salvadoran location. The rules do not require a local employer or expressly require local customers, but they also do not expressly mention remote foreign clients. Present the foreign contract, invoices or payment evidence, business description and projected income, and obtain written DGME confirmation. A person who remains exclusively an employee of a foreign company may not satisfy the independent-worker facts without genuine self-employment.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum income was identified.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed minimum published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility depends on a qualifying transfer and assignment rather than an income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum published
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility turns on an employer-directed temporary transfer and a Salvadoran entity requiring the services, not a general income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed historical period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Existing employment relationship with an enterprise established outside El Salvador and an employer-directed temporary transfer.
Confirmation from the representative of the entity in El Salvador that requires the applicant's activities.

initial_validity.value: Initially transitory and potentially temporary residence for up to two years
initial_validity.notes: The exact grant depends on whether the applicant enters the transitory or temporary subcategory.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence can be renewed for up to two years if the qualifying assignment continues
extension_rules.notes: Renewal requires confirmation that the in-country activities continue.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Possible where a foreign employer transfers the worker to perform an assignment required in El Salvador.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not an open-ended work-from-anywhere category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Temporary residence can fall within the general definitive-residence rule, but the initial transitory status itself generates no definitive-residence rights.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A qualifying temporary-residence grant would be necessary.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only qualifying residence time can support naturalization; a merely transitory assignment is not a confirmed settlement route.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not suitable for an ordinary foreign employee working remotely without an El Salvador assignment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the statute requires an employer-directed transfer and circumstances connecting the assignment to an entity or services in El Salvador. Ordinary remote employment for a foreign company, with no Salvadoran host or assignment, is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No current numerical threshold was established in the sources inspected.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No current fixed minimum published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Applicants must demonstrate resources or lawful external income.

income_requirement_display.value: External resources required; no current fixed minimum published
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a passive/support-income residence category and does not authorize ordinary remunerated remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Demonstrate external resources or lawful external income sufficient to support residence.
Declare that the resident will not undertake remunerated activity in El Salvador, subject to narrow public-sector specialist or teaching exceptions.

initial_validity.value: One year

extension_rules.value: Renewable while rentista conditions continue
extension_rules.notes: The renewal form sets a 45-working-day response target when complete.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence based on external resources

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A rentista may seek definitive residence after holding that status for one year
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The favorable settlement rule does not cure the prohibition on remunerated work.

path_to_citizenship.value: Definitive residence could ultimately support naturalization, but the route is incompatible with continuing remunerated foreign-client software work.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because DGME's rentista instructions expressly prohibit remunerated work, despite accepting income from abroad.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route uses a business-asset threshold rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least USD 2,500 in business assets
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is an asset requirement, not monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 2,500 minimum business assets
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Business assets of at least USD 2,500
income_requirement_display.notes: A registered mercantile enterprise, balance sheet and business and establishment registrations are required.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not an income-history route.

key_requirements.requirement: Own an individual mercantile enterprise with assets of at least USD 2,500.
Provide a notarized business declaration, certified balance sheet and current commercial registrations for the enterprise and establishment.

initial_validity.value: Up to two years

extension_rules.value: Renewable for up to two years while the enterprise remains qualifying

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct entrepreneur/merchant temporary residence

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The general three-year temporary-to-definitive-residence rule may apply

path_to_citizenship.value: Qualifying temporary and definitive residence can count toward the five-year naturalization period for most foreigners

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as the preferred route because it requires a formal Salvadoran mercantile enterprise, registered establishment and minimum business assets. The independent-migrant-worker subcategory is less capital-intensive and better aligned with professional consulting.

summary.value: Enrollment as a regular student in a recognized Salvadoran technical, university or specialized program can support temporary residence for up to one year, renewable. It requires enrollment and maintenance evidence rather than merely possessing a degree. Student residence itself does not qualify for definitive residence unless the person changes immigration status.
summary.notes: Academic and teaching categories generally require an institutional agreement or contracting institution and are not independent degree-based migration routes. Article 126 of the migration law expressly says student residence does not enable definitive residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is treated as tax resident if present temporarily or permanently for more than 200 consecutive days in a calendar year, or if the individual's main source of income is in El Salvador.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence and immigration residence are separate tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal/screening rate, not the applicant's expected effective rate. Current PwC guidance also reports 30% for non-domiciled individuals.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single mandatory percentage applies to the selected self-employed route. The previously displayed 10.25% combined the employee shares of general-regime ISSS health insurance (3%, capped under the payroll rules) and AFP pension (7.25%) and therefore described a dependent employee, not an independent consultant. ISSS instead publishes an opt-in special independent-worker health scheme with fixed charges of USD 40 monthly for individual coverage or USD 56 for family coverage. The pension law makes compulsory affiliation and monthly contributions explicit for subordinated employment; an independent worker may affiliate and, when contributing, pays the full 16% pension contribution on a self-selected contribution base no lower than the applicable legal minimum wage. Filing advice is required to determine which registrations the particular consultant should make.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal mandatory fixed monthly payment for every self-employed resident. The official ISSS special independent-worker scheme is opt-in and currently costs USD 40 monthly for individual coverage or USD 56 for family coverage. Pension contributions, when made by an independent worker, are percentage-based rather than fixed.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad or inbound-remote-worker income-tax exemption was identified. El Salvador generally taxes Salvadoran-source income; work physically performed in El Salvador can be taxable even when paid abroad.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign taxes generally do not produce a Salvadoran credit, and PwC identifies only Spain as having a double-tax treaty with El Salvador.

taxes.caveats: Tax and contribution classification depends on whether the relationship is employment or independent services, where services are performed or used, domicile, business registration, VAT status, payer location and treaty position. Work performed from El Salvador should not be assumed tax-free merely because the client and payment account are abroad. The ISSS and pension options for independent workers are distinct from employee payroll deductions.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax on Salvadoran-source income, with territorial/source-based scope and separate rules for non-domiciled individuals.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 200 consecutive days in a calendar year, or El Salvador is the individual's main income source.
taxation_system.income_scope: Citizens, residents and non-residents are taxed on income earned in El Salvador and other Salvadoran-source income. Current guidance says compensation for work performed in El Salvador remains taxable regardless of where paid or remitted.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad tax holiday or inbound remote-worker regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Dependent employees are subject to general-regime payroll contributions: ISSS is 3% employee and 7.5% employer, while AFP is 7.25% employee and 8.75% employer. Those employee rates do not automatically apply to the independent-worker route. ISSS publishes an opt-in independent-worker health scheme at USD 40 monthly individual or USD 56 family. An independent worker who contributes to the pension system pays the full 16% on a chosen base no lower than the applicable minimum wage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate. The bands below are annual net-income bands reported by PwC after the May 2025 amendment. PwC's displayed fixed-sum formula for the 10% band contains a legacy-base inconsistency, so only the published band edges and marginal rates are reproduced.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: USD 0 to USD 6,600 annual net income
tax_brackets.notes: Exempt band.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over USD 6,600 through USD 9,142.86 annual net income
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band; check the current statutory fixed-sum formula before filing.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over USD 9,142.86 through USD 22,857.14 annual net income
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.
Top marginal band.

taxation_system.notes: The tax statute is primary authority, while the February 2026 PwC summary provides the clearest current USD brackets and recent-amendment treatment. Official ISSS and pension-law sources resolve the distinction between employee payroll rates and independent-worker options. Professional advice remains important because a foreign-client service performed from El Salvador may be Salvadoran-source.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: El Salvador has no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. A qualifying applicant would be taxed as an ordinary self-employed resident or service provider under the general income-tax, VAT and registration rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Independent migrant worker / self-employed professional; not a statutory digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive, 0% to 30% top marginal rate; 30% is a screening ceiling, not expected effective tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 200 consecutive days in a calendar year, or El Salvador is the person's main income source.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: General rules are source-based, but services physically performed in El Salvador or used there can be Salvadoran-source regardless of foreign payment or remittance. Foreign-client income therefore requires contract-specific sourcing advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee payroll rates do not automatically apply. ISSS offers independent workers an opt-in fixed health scheme at USD 40 monthly individual or USD 56 family. Pension-system affiliation is compulsory for subordinated employment; an independent worker may affiliate and pays the full 16% contribution when contributing.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Official ISSS independent-worker coverage costs USD 40 monthly for an individual or USD 56 for family coverage, but the scheme is described as one workers elect to join rather than a universal immigration-route charge. Independent pension contributions are 16% of a chosen base no lower than the applicable legal minimum wage, not a fixed payment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: F3 service sheet: USD 70 for Central Americans or USD 140 for non-Central Americans for residence of up to one year. This is not monthly; renewal and card fees should be reconfirmed.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: An annual municipal transit tax of USD 3.43 is reported. Municipal business taxes may apply. VAT is generally 13%. A mercantile natural-person taxpayer may make a 1.75% monthly advance income-tax payment on gross receipts.
fixed_payments.notes: Notary, apostille, translation, municipal permit, professional authorization and business-registration costs vary and are not published as one fixed package. Whether the consultant must or should use the ISSS and pension options requires case-specific registration advice.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below 200 consecutive days does not guarantee non-residence if the main source of income is in El Salvador. Work physically performed there may still be Salvadoran-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident performing services from El Salvador should screen the income under the annual 0%–30% brackets even when the client and bank account are foreign.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A genuine independent worker should expect taxpayer registration, annual income-tax compliance and potentially VAT, municipal permits and the 1.75% gross-receipts advance payment if classified as a mercantile natural person. ISSS independent coverage is available at USD 40 individual or USD 56 family monthly; independent pension contributions use a 16% rate when made.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The immigration route has no special tax regime. The focused audit established the published independent-worker health and pension contribution options, but whether a particular consultant must register as a mercantile business, professional service provider or another taxpayer class remains case-specific.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The selected route directly grants temporary residence. DGME publishes a 45-working-day processing target for a complete F3 filing.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General rule for temporary residents. Spanish and Hispanic-American nationals can qualify after one uninterrupted year; Central Americans have more favorable rules.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: For an ordinary non-Hispanic foreigner, this is an inferred sequence: definitive residence after three temporary-residence years and naturalization eligibility after five total temporary-plus-definitive residence years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General rule for foreigners not entitled to a shorter nationality-specific period. Spanish and Hispanic-American nationals have a shorter rule, but nationality-specific legal review is advisable.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: DGME publishes application forms and an online case-status facility but no reliable typical or statutory processing duration.

key_conditions.value: Maintain lawful temporary residence and required physical presence, convert to definitive residence, preserve clean police and criminal records, document civil status, provide proof that the origin country permits dual nationality where requested, pay the fee and complete the naturalization oath or declaration. Temporary residents can lose status through excessive absence; DGME's current FAQ states more than three consecutive months or four accumulated months in one year.
key_conditions.notes: No separate language examination was identified in the official materials inspected, but proceedings and documents operate in Spanish.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Naturalization by marriage requires two years of residence before or after the marriage. Definitive residence is available after one uninterrupted year of temporary residence as the spouse or cohabiting partner of a Salvadoran.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Salvadoran supports temporary residence for up to two years, renewable. After one uninterrupted year of that temporary residence, the spouse can seek definitive residence; two years of residence can support naturalization.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A foreign marriage must be properly registered or recognized in El Salvador, and the Salvadoran spouse's civil-status records must reflect the relationship.

requirements_and_risks.value: Provide marriage and birth records, the Salvadoran spouse's identity document, maintenance declaration and other general residence requirements. Cohabiting partners use a notarized declaration. Residence obtained through a marriage entered solely for immigration benefits can be cancelled; marriage does not make citizenship automatic.
requirements_and_risks.notes: DGME may examine authenticity and continuity of the relationship. Sham marriage creates cancellation and enforcement risk.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 90 grants Salvadoran nationality by birth to persons born in El Salvador. No parental residence or citizenship condition is stated; narrow diplomatic exceptions, if applicable elsewhere in law, do not change the broad classification.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in El Salvador is Salvadoran by birth even when both parents are foreign migrants, because the Constitution grants nationality based on birth in the territory.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents must register the birth and obtain the child's civil documents.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Salvadoran by birth if born in El Salvador and also by descent if born abroad to a Salvadoran father or mother.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule is gender-neutral as to the Salvadoran parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize or confer residence on either foreign parent. The current migration law's definitive-residence categories include spouses or cohabiting partners of Salvadorans, qualifying temporary residents and other specified groups, but do not list parenthood of a Salvadoran child as a stand-alone category. A parent must therefore qualify through an independently available residence category unless DGME accepts another legally supported basis.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The focused audit checked Migration Law Article 152 and the regulation's definitive-residence provisions. Article 193 requests birth certificates when families with children apply for definitive residence, but it governs documentation for children and families already using an eligible category; it does not create an automatic or accelerated residence entitlement for the foreign parent of a Salvadoran child. No current DGME service sheet dedicated to such parents appears in the official temporary- or definitive-residence indexes.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father receives neither automatic citizenship nor an automatic residence status through the citizen child. He must qualify in his own right, although the child's birth certificate may document family ties in an otherwise eligible or discretionary filing.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not rely on the citizen-child relationship alone without written DGME confirmation of a specific statutory category.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; live indexes can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately lists eVisa destinations within its destination table; its headline visa-required figure is reproduced.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 43 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations. The index reports a mobility score of 130 when visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA access are combined.

passport.notes: Passport Index was used because it supplies a current, separated visa-free/visa-on-arrival/eTA breakdown. Its rank methodology differs from Henley.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be used within an international remote-work team, but Spanish is the official language and is the practical language for immigration forms, notarizations, tax registration, municipal permits and daily administration. An English-only applicant should expect translation or local professional help.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No authoritative national English-proficiency measure was identified in the focused searches; this assessment is based on the official-language rule and Spanish-language government procedures.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian should not be expected to work with government agencies or for routine daily administration. Spanish-language assistance and certified Spanish translations will normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No official evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: National mean monthly salary of employed people in the 2025 Household Survey. The tabulation excludes unpaid family workers.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current 2025 EHPM report and published tabulations provide national mean salaries by sex, education, occupation and area but do not publish a national median monthly salary. ONEC makes the 2025 microdata available through a registration-controlled repository, so a median could be calculated from weighted microdata, but no official calculated median was established from the named published sources.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Lowest published statutory monthly minimum among the cited sectors: agriculture, fishing, coffee harvesting and other agricultural activities, effective 1 June 2025.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official 2025 EHPM national average monthly salary of employed people; unpaid family workers are excluded.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The published 2025 EHPM report and tabulations state arithmetic means but not a national wage median. A private job-market median was not substituted for an official resident-worker statistic.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the statutory minimum-wage announcement nor the 2025 EHPM national tables publish a meaningful maximum salary. Occupational group means are not salary ceilings.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory sectoral minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: El Salvador uses the United States dollar. This is the 2025 EHPM national arithmetic mean monthly salary for employed people, excluding unpaid family workers.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Not published as a national monthly statistic in the 2025 EHPM report or tabulations
median_salary_local_currency.notes: The current official survey materials publish national mean salaries but no calculated national median. The downloadable microdata could support a weighted calculation, but that would be an analyst-derived result rather than a published official median.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No meaningful national maximum salary is published
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official sources provide sectoral minimum wages and average salaries, not a salary ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2025 EHPM national mean monthly salary for employed people, excluding unpaid family workers; statutory sectoral minimum wages effective 1 June 2025
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly; survey year 2025 and minimum wages effective 2025-06-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is the national average citizen/resident-worker salary from the 2025 household survey, not a remote-worker immigration income requirement. Official minimums range from USD 272.53 for agriculture/fishing and related activities, through USD 305.23 for sugar-cane harvesting and coffee processing, USD 402.32 for textile/apparel maquila, to USD 408.80 for industry, commerce and services. No official national median or maximum salary is published in the current report.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official ONEC statistics publish the urban and rural basic food basket monthly, but define it as the minimum caloric requirement for one person—not a complete cost-of-living budget. Housing, utilities, transport, health insurance and other spending must be budgeted separately; no current official all-in monthly amount for an individual foreign remote worker was established.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Focused unexplained-null pass. ONEC’s CBA definition and query tool, its economic-statistics and February 2026 IPC pages, the World Bank April 2026 macro outlook, and the 2026 decree commissioning a new household income-and-expenditure survey were checked. They support a reliable bounded note and current price context, but not a defensible all-in remote-worker budget. The 2026 household expenditure survey was underway and its results were not available on the research date.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: This is not a digital-nomad visa. It requires genuine independent economic activity documented as a local self-employed operation; ordinary foreign employment alone is insufficient.
settlement_track.summary: The independent-worker category grants real temporary residence and can convert to definitive residence after three years under the general rule. Temporary and definitive residence both count toward the general five-year naturalization period, making this a credible citizenship track, but it requires conversion and genuine self-employed business substance.
settlement_track.notes: The legal settlement chain is reasonably well supported. Filing-level confirmation remains prudent because official materials describe independent work and a business location but do not expressly name foreign-client remote software consulting.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The independent-worker requirements do not demand a local employer or local customer and can accommodate genuine foreign-client consulting operated from a declared Salvadoran business location. This does not automatically cover a conventional foreign employee who is neither independently established nor assigned to El Salvador.

data.notes: The focused audit resolves the flagged cost-of-living field with a bounded official-statistics note. ONEC publishes monthly urban and rural basic-food-basket data but defines that basket as a minimum caloric measure, not a complete living budget; the new 2026 household income-and-expenditure survey had not yet published results. Overall confidence remains medium because DGME does not publish a remote-work example or explicit confirmation of home-based foreign-client software consulting.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, freelance, or independently accessible self-employed residence route was confirmed. The eVisa is a short-stay visitor status, while residence requires a separate residence permit and, under the published government regularization rules, a work permit; no route accommodating ordinary work solely for a foreign client was found. General naturalization requires at least 40 years of continuous legal residence, so Equatorial Guinea is not a practical citizenship-path match for this profile.

visa_application.notes: This is the current visitor/eVisa application channel, corroborated as the official portal by 2026 ITU visitor instructions and linked by GOV.UK. It is not an application channel for digital-nomad, freelance, work, or residence status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No current official rule converting visitor status to permanent residence was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The process can produce a residence permit, but the published checklist requires a work permit and does not establish an ordinary foreign-client remote-work category.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not an independently confirmed route for the applicant profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No current official permanent-residence eligibility or conversion timeline was located.

path_to_citizenship.value: A person maintaining qualifying continuous legal residence may theoretically reach general naturalization after at least 40 years, subject to extensive integration, documentation and discretionary approval requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No evidence confirms that the applicant could first obtain this status through foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: The ordinary documented pattern is work authorization plus residence. Although business/legal-person documentation appears in the residence checklist, no current self-employed residence category allowing a software engineer to work solely for a foreign client was identified.

summary.value: No current official student, degree-based, points-tested, or independent skilled-migration residence route was found in the sources inspected. A university degree does not remove the published work-permit requirement for ordinary economic activity.
summary.notes: Publicly accessible filing-level rules for foreign students were not located after focused searches; the nulls are retained rather than assuming that admission independently produces residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is treated as tax resident after remaining in Equatorial Guinea for 183 days in a 12-month period; a person present for fewer than 183 days while performing activities is treated as non-resident.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence and immigration residence are separate determinations.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening personal income tax rate under the current PwC summary, not an expected effective rate. The older translated tax-code text contains a historical 35% scale; the fresher 2025-reviewed summary reports the current 0%–25% scale.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Combined employee-side contribution: 4.5% to INSESO plus 0.5% to the Work Protection Fund. Employer-side contributions are an additional 21.5% plus 1%. Applicability to a foreign employer or independently registered professional requires advice.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly freelancer, nomad, health-insurance or minimum social-security payment was established.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, freelancer, non-dom, remittance-basis or inbound-worker tax regime was identified. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on Equatorial Guinea-source income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign tax relief and treaty treatment should be checked for the applicant's citizenship and contract structure.

taxes.caveats: There is no qualifying remote-worker immigration route, so the tax analysis is hypothetical. Work performed while physically in Equatorial Guinea may create local-source, payroll, registration or permanent-establishment issues even when the payer is foreign. Obtain local advice before performing economic activity.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax from 0% to 25%. Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Equatorial Guinea-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in a 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Equatorial Guinea-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or inbound-individual regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee: 4.5% INSESO plus 0.5% Work Protection Fund. Employer: 21.5% INSESO plus 1% Work Protection Fund.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 25% is the top marginal rate. The applicable effective rate depends on annual taxable income and deductions.

tax_brackets.notes: Current bracket reported in the 21 November 2025-reviewed summary.

The translated tax code is useful primary-law context but displays an older 0%–35% scale and therefore should not override the fresher professional summary without confirmation from the tax administration.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status exists. If a person nevertheless becomes tax resident under another lawful status, ordinary progressive PIT and potentially social-security rules apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–25% progressive PIT; 25% is the top marginal screening rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in a 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is taxable for residents; non-residents are taxed on Equatorial Guinea-source income. Physical performance of services in the country requires source analysis even when payment comes from abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary employee rates are 4.5% INSESO plus 0.5% Work Protection Fund, with additional employer contributions of 21.5% and 1%. Application to foreign payroll or genuine self-employment was not established.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific recurring payment confirmed.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed minimum contribution was published; percentage-based employee and employer contributions exist.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Visitor fee information varies by context: 2026 ITU instructions quoted a common $75 eVisa charge, while Spanish travel advice referenced €105 for visas under 90 days. The live portal should control at filing.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Standard VAT is 15%, but no freelancer-specific fixed tax or registration charge was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Visitor visa fees do not create or evidence a lawful remote-work route.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below 183 days generally avoids tax residence, but it does not authorize work and does not necessarily eliminate Equatorial Guinea-source taxation for services physically performed there.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A lawfully resident person reaching 183 days would ordinarily face worldwide-income taxation at progressive rates up to 25%; however, no immigration status authorizing this ordinary remote-worker scenario was found.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Business or professional activity may require work authorization, tax registration and possibly entity/government documentation. No simple tourist-to-sole-proprietor legalization route was confirmed.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax rules are reasonably documented, but their application to a foreign-contract worker is hypothetical because the matching immigration route is absent.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No selected independent route exists. A separate one-year residence permit is reported, but eligibility for an ordinary foreign-contract worker was not established.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No current official permanent-residence threshold or conversion rule was found.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality law measures continuous legal residence rather than a confirmed period after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the statutory minimum for general residence-based naturalization, not a timeline from a qualifying remote-worker route. Approval remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality law supplies no ordinary processing-time commitment, and no reliable current administrative average was found.

key_conditions.value: At least 40 years of continuous legal residence; valid residence permit; no criminal record locally or serious foreign conviction; Spanish plus a national language and cultural integration; tax clearance; police good-conduct certificate; medical certificate; tax-roll and social-security registration; fees; and renunciation of previous nationality. Denial may be based on the general interest without reasons.
key_conditions.notes: These are general naturalization conditions and do not cure the absence of an eligible entry/residence route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The spouse may exercise the nationality option after ten years of marriage and cohabitation in Equatorial Guinea. The law provides a narrow exception to in-country marital domicile when the citizen spouse is abroad on an Equatoguinean government request or commission.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to an Equatoguinean citizen can begin satisfying the ten-year marriage/cohabitation requirement, but marriage does not produce immediate citizenship and is not a remote-work residence route.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Filing is made to the President through the Ministry of Justice.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage and cohabitation must be genuine and documentable. Nationality remains an application process; false documents or sham-marriage arrangements can lead to refusal, immigration penalties and later loss of naturalized nationality.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The captured law does not provide a processing-time guarantee or automatic permanent residence through marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The 2011 law grants nationality at birth through an Equatoguinean father or mother. A person born locally to foreign parents may opt only from age 18 after at least ten years of continuous prior residence, so this is not automatic jus soli at birth.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Equatorial Guinea to two foreign parents is not automatically a citizen under the 2011 law. From age 18, the child may exercise an option after demonstrating at least ten years of continuous residence before applying.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Separate anti-statelessness or foundling rules were not established in the captured current law.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Equatoguinean by birth when either the father or mother is an Equatoguinean citizen.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Birth registration and documentary proof remain necessary in practice.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. No current rule granting the migrant father automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship solely through the child was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any family-based residence benefit requires filing-level confirmation with National Security.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or confirmed residence benefit was established. The father must maintain his own lawful immigration basis unless authorities confirm a separate family permit.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not infer a parental immigration entitlement from the child's nationality.

passport.notes: The index reports a Mobility Score of 64. This differs from Henley-style totals that combine visa-free and visa-on-arrival access, so figures from different indexes should not be mixed.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low for administration and local daily life. English may work within a foreign remote team, but it is not an official language; Spanish is by far the most useful language for immigration, tax, banking and ordinary services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The 2026 UK factfile reports Spanish understood by about 87% of the population; French and Portuguese have substantially less everyday use.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Very low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official or documented as commonly used; Spanish-language assistance or a professional interpreter should be expected for filings and local services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No evidence of broadly available Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current nationally representative average monthly earnings figure was found. GDP or GNI per capita was not substituted for wages.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current nationally representative median wage was published in the inspected sources.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the listed XAF 117,304 private-sector statutory minimum using roughly XAF 576.76 per USD. This is a minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A defensible current national average was not established.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current median was established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum or reliable wage-distribution upper bound was found.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Private-sector statutory minimum shown as valid in June 2026, with effect from 1 January 2011. Spanish consular guidance rounds the minimum to XAF 120,000.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Not available in the inspected current statistics.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not available in the inspected current statistics.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory gross monthly private-sector minimum only; national average and median unavailable.
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage listed as valid June 2026; exchange-rate approximation uses a July 2026 BEAC indicative rate.
average_citizen_salary.notes: The previous record's wage gaps were investigated. Only the statutory minimum could be established; national average, median and maximum values remain cautious nulls because available GDP, poverty and expatriate-pay material is not a substitute for resident-worker earnings.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable current national or city-level household cost-of-living basket was established. The World Bank reports weak labor-market conditions, substantial poverty and a hydrocarbon-dependent economy, but those indicators cannot be converted into a monthly living-cost estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing and imported-goods costs can differ sharply between Malabo, Bata and other areas; verify locally.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The eVisa is visitor-only. It does not authorize ordinary remote work and is not a qualifying settlement status.
settlement_track.summary: Only visitor permission and a work-permit-dependent residence process were confirmed. No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists, and the separate general naturalization rule requires at least 40 years of uninterrupted legal residence.
settlement_track.notes: The 40-year naturalization rule does not make the visitor eVisa or an unavailable remote-worker status a citizenship path.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The visitor status does not authorize economic activity, and residence documentation requires a work permit. No independently accessible foreign-client freelance or remote-worker category was found.

data.notes: Audited against the previous record and more than 15 distinct relevant URLs. Material improvements include the current 40-year general naturalization rule from Law 3/2011, detailed residence-document requirements, the current 0%–25% PIT scale, 5% combined employee social contributions, a current passport-index breakdown, and a documented statutory minimum wage. Permanent-residence rules, student residence, independent self-employment eligibility, national average/median wages and citizenship processing time remain unresolved after focused searches and are therefore retained as explained nulls.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, independent freelancer, self-employed, or qualification-based residence route was confirmed. The available employment visa and work-linked residence permit require an Eritrean sponsoring/employing entity and Labour Office or government work authorization, so ordinary work for a foreign client does not qualify.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: After authorized entry for work, the foreign worker must register and obtain a residence permit supported by Labour Office or government work authorization.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The inspected legislation provides renewable one-year residence and foreigner registration but contains no permanent-residence transition rule.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization law refers to 20 years of domicile for post-1952 entrants, language ability, good character, self-support, permanent domicile, renunciation of other nationality, and an oath. No official source confirms that this employment residence automatically creates or counts as a guaranteed settlement track.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is legally separate and exceptionally long; neither the nationality legislation nor inspected current consular guidance publishes a processing procedure linking employer-sponsored residence to naturalization.

initial_validity.notes: The Melbourne consulate likewise states that tourist entry permits one month of stay. Longer fee categories do not establish residence or remote-work permission.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The immigration regulation requires separate work authorization for work-linked residence; it does not make visitor entry a temporary-residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The immigration regulation contains no visitor-to-permanent-residence transition.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Article 4 of Proclamation No. 21/1992 requires 20 years of domicile after legal entry for post-1952 applicants. The current embassy visitor pages and immigration regulation do not define a tourist stay or visitor extension as qualifying domicile, and the 2021 Horn of Africa study repeats the 20-year rule without identifying visitor time as creditable; therefore no citizenship credit can be assigned to this visitor route from the published rules.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because ordinary visitor or business entry is not a remote-work residence route and the inspected immigration, work-permit, and consular materials provide no tourist-to-self-employed legalization process.

summary.value: No independent degree-based, points-tested, or skilled residence route was identified in the inspected consular and immigration sources. A software-engineering degree does not remove the sponsoring-employer and work-authorization requirements for the published employment route.
summary.notes: A student visa is listed as an entry category, but the published material provides no education-to-independent-residence or citizenship transition.

tax_residency_rule.value: The accessible Income Tax Proclamation No. 62/1994 taxes income by Eritrean origin and does not state a general modern individual tax-residence test. IMF summaries identify an exemption for business representatives residing in Eritrea for less than 183 days, but that category-specific exemption is not evidence that all individuals become tax residents at 183 days.
tax_residency_rule.notes: No public current Eritrean tax-authority guidance defining resident, non-resident, habitual abode, or a universal day-count test was located. The ICAEW page confirms that specialist resident/expatriate/non-resident coverage exists in a subscription database but does not publish the rule; accordingly the 183-day business-representative exemption is reported narrowly and not promoted to a general residence threshold.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal employment-income rate in the IMF summary of Eritrean authorities' tax system; it is not an expected effective rate. The original 1994 proclamation available online contains an earlier schedule topping at 30%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The public portions of the legislation, IMF summaries, and ICAEW country page do not disclose a current mandatory social-security contribution percentage for a foreign remote worker or independent professional; ICAEW places detailed individual-tax coverage behind its subscribed database.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The immigration regulation refers to issuance and renewal service fees, but the inspected official sources publish no mandatory monthly amount or consolidated current residence-fee schedule.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, freelancer, expatriate, remittance-basis, or foreign-remote-worker tax regime was identified. Eritrea's separate 2% recovery and rehabilitation tax concerns eligible Eritrean citizens abroad, not an ordinary foreign applicant residing in Eritrea.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The diaspora levy should not be presented as the applicant's remote-worker tax rate. HMRC also treats Eritrean income tax and rehabilitation tax differently for UK unilateral-relief purposes.

taxes.caveats: The accessible tax legislation is old, historical schedules differ, and no current public Eritrean tax-authority portal or individual-residence guide was located. The source characterization of software services physically performed in Eritrea for a foreign client, business licensing, withholding, currency conversion, and treaty relief requires filing-level professional confirmation.

taxation_system.value: Schedular, predominantly source-based income taxation. Employment and individual business/professional income are progressive; one accessible IMF schedule reaches 38%, while the original individual business/professional schedule reaches 30%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No general current residence test is published in the inspected sources; the 1994 law defines taxable income by Eritrean origin, while the IMF's 183-day language is limited to an exemption for business representatives.
taxation_system.income_scope: The 1994 proclamation covers income having its origin within Eritrea, including employment, rent, trade, business, professional, vocational, farming, royalty, and certain service income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special foreign-remote-worker regime was identified. A separate 2% levy applies to eligible Eritreans abroad.
taxation_system.social_security: The inspected public sources provide no current mandatory contribution rate for the applicant scenario.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 38% is a top marginal screening rate from an IMF historical summary, not an effective rate. The original 1994 text and the IMF's December 2002 summary show schedules topping at 30%, so the applicable current schedule requires confirmation before filing.

ICAEW confirms that detailed resident/expatriate/non-resident material is held in a subscription database, while HMRC confirms only that Eritrean income tax is eligible for unilateral relief in the UK; neither supplies a public Eritrean residence definition. Conflicting historical rate schedules are disclosed rather than silently reconciled.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Inapplicable as a dedicated regime because Eritrea has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. If a foreigner nevertheless performed services while physically in Eritrea, source and licensing treatment would require a ruling or advice based on the facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; possible employment or professional/business income under general law
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Historical employment schedule up to a 38% top marginal rate; the original individual professional/business schedule tops at 30%. Neither figure is a confirmed effective rate for foreign-client remote income.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: The inspected public sources provide no universal residence threshold; the law instead defines taxable income by Eritrean origin, and the 183-day language concerns a narrow business-representative exemption.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The 1994 law is framed around income originating within Eritrea. No current public Eritrean guidance clarifies whether foreign-paid software services performed physically in Eritrea are Eritrean-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: The inspected immigration, tax-law, IMF, ICAEW, and diplomatic sources contain no dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-remote-worker tax regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The inspected public sources do not disclose a current contribution percentage or minimum contribution for this hypothetical scenario.

fixed_payments.status: No applicant-specific amount published
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The inspected public sources contain no minimum social-security or payroll contribution for a foreign remote worker.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Consulates publish entry-visa fees, and the immigration regulation refers to residence issuance and renewal fees, but no universal current residence-fee schedule is published.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The inspected public materials do not provide freelancer-specific business-license, municipal, sales-tax registration, or financial-transaction amounts.
fixed_payments.notes: The missing amounts are inapplicable to any dedicated nomad category because no such route exists, and no consolidated current fee or tax-administration publication covers a hypothetical foreign freelancer.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe tax-free day-count scenario can be stated. Visitor status does not authorize remote work, and the law's source-based wording may matter independently of duration.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No dedicated category exists; potential Eritrean-source employment or professional income could face progressive taxation, subject to classification and enforcement advice.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The inspected immigration, work-permit, registration, and consular sources provide no residence path based solely on registering as a freelancer or sole proprietor. Business registration would not itself replace immigration and work authorization.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: These are screening conclusions because the applicant cannot use a confirmed remote-worker route and the public sources do not provide current Eritrean administrative guidance for foreign-client services.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: There is no qualifying independent route. Employer-authorized workers may receive a one-year residence permit, but the regulation publishes no standard processing interval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The inspected immigration and foreigner-registration legislation contains no permanent-residence transition or qualifying period.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality law uses 20 years of domicile rather than a permanent-residence milestone, and no separate permanent-residence stage was identified.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No qualifying remote-work route exists from which to calculate a route-specific total. The general law and comparative study state 20 years of domicile for post-1952 entrants, but published sources do not establish how a visitor or this applicant could acquire qualifying domicile.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality legislation and current law guide identify the governing law but publish neither a service standard nor a representative processing-time statistic.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires legal entry, 20 years of domicile for modern entrants under the text, high integrity and no criminal conviction, ability to speak an Eritrean language, self-support, renunciation of other nationality, intention to remain permanently domiciled, and an oath of allegiance.
key_conditions.notes: The current law guide indicates that the 1992 proclamation remains the governing nationality legislation, but no current implementation guide connects foreign remote work or visitor status to qualifying domicile.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The law requires living in Eritrea with the Eritrean spouse for at least three years, not merely three years of marriage abroad.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legal marriage to an Eritrean citizen can support an application, but the applicant must still have lived in Eritrea with the spouse for at least three years.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage alone does not produce immediate citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The foreign spouse must apply, renounce foreign nationality, and sign the oath of allegiance. Nationality granted through marriage may be lost if the person chooses to reacquire the former nationality after death, divorce, or annulment. Genuine-marriage and documentary verification should be expected, although the law does not publish detailed evidentiary procedures.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The inspected law and current law guide provide no separate permanent-residence acceleration rule or current filing portal.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship follows Eritrean parentage whether birth occurs in Eritrea or abroad. Birth in Eritrea alone is insufficient; the law separately protects foundlings and children of unknown parents.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Eritrea to two known non-Eritrean parents does not acquire citizenship merely by birthplace. A child born in Eritrea of unknown parents is treated as Eritrean by birth until proven otherwise.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The proclamation contains no broader jus soli rule for children of known migrant parents.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If either the mother or father is of Eritrean origin, the child is Eritrean by birth whether born in Eritrea or abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule is gender-neutral as to the Eritrean parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A child's Eritrean citizenship does not automatically grant citizenship or permanent residence to a foreign parent. The inspected nationality and immigration rules provide no citizen-child family-residence entitlement for the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any discretionary or unpublished family-residence procedure would require direct confirmation from Eritrean immigration authorities.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or published permanent-residence entitlement applies to a migrant father solely because his child is Eritrean. Marriage-based naturalization may apply separately if the mother is an Eritrean spouse and its conditions are satisfied.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Child citizenship and spousal naturalization are legally distinct.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15; the index is dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required count displayed by the index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Sum of the source's separate 32 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA categories.

passport.notes: Passport Index displayed a mobility score of 48 on the research date. Its methodology differs from indexes that combine visa-free and visa-on-arrival access.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is a de facto working language and is used as a medium of instruction from middle school upward, so it can help in educated and formal settings. Eritrea legally designates no single official language, however, and local administration and daily life may require Tigrinya or Arabic.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The array lists the three de facto working languages because the schema requires language names; official Eritrean material says no language is formally designated official and all Eritrean languages are equal.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not identified as official or working languages in the inspected official materials and are unlikely to be practical for ordinary administration or remote-work logistics.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is an inference from the published working-language information, not a national proficiency measurement.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected ILO and World Bank pages publish no current representative Eritrean national average-wage amount.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected ILO country and wage portals provide no Eritrean national median-wage value.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The ILO review classifies Eritrea among countries without a generally applicable minimum wage, so no national statutory minimum amount exists to convert to USD from that source.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official and international statistical pages contain no current representative national average-wage amount.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected ILO pages contain no current Eritrean national median-wage amount.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum salary is not a standard labor-market statistic, and the inspected ILO sources publish no representative upper wage bound for Eritrea.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: The cited ILO review reports no generally applicable Eritrean minimum wage, so there is no national statutory ERN amount to record.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected ILO sources contain no current representative national average expressed in ERN.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected ILO sources contain no current Eritrean median expressed in ERN.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected ILO sources contain no representative national wage-distribution ceiling expressed in ERN.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: No representative current national wage statistic published in the inspected sources
average_citizen_salary.period: monthly
average_citizen_salary.notes: The ILO country and wage portals do not expose a usable current Eritrea wage series, and the ILO minimum-wage review indicates that Eritrea lacks a generally applicable minimum wage. Commercial salary aggregators were excluded because their sampling and national representativeness could not be established.

cost_of_living_note.value: The inspected sources contain no reliable current household cost-of-living budget. The World Bank instead reports severe data limitations and forecasts consumer-price inflation around 3.8% for 2026.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Inflation is not a household budget and cannot substitute for current rent, food, or household expenditure figures.
