settlement_track.summary: A genuine entrepreneur permit is a qualifying residence route rather than a nomad or visitor status. Migri expressly accepts entrepreneurship as an A-permit ground for permanent residence, and lawful permit residence can lead to citizenship; the route is strong only for a real Finnish business, not unchanged foreign payroll employment or invoicing-service freelancing.
settlement_track.notes: The earliest four-year PR path is conditional; otherwise a six-year PR path may apply. Citizenship can be possible after five years with the required language skills or eight years under the ordinary rule.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only for foreign-client contracting restructured as genuine work through the applicant's qualifying Finnish business. It is false for a person who merely remains a foreign employee or bills through an invoicing-service/light-entrepreneur arrangement.

data.notes: The previous record correctly identified the entrepreneur route but contained a contradictory false selection verdict and inconsistent remote-work flags. Current official sources support a true match for the foreign-client/self-employed version of the profile, with strict caveats about genuine Finnish business activity, profitability, and the exclusion of unchanged foreign payroll employment.

data.selection_summary: France has no dedicated digital-nomad visa, but it has an independent entrepreneur/profession libérale residence route. A software engineer genuinely working as a self-employed professional for a foreign client can potentially use it without a French employer, provided the activity is registered and carried on in France, is economically viable, and produces at least the full-time French minimum-wage equivalent. It does not cover simply retaining foreign salaried employment without establishing a French independent activity.

visa_application.title: Self employed person or liberal activity
visa_application.notes: Official route-information page. France-Visas directs applicants to start the visa process online and use its visa wizard for the filing-country-specific document list; it is not a standalone application form URL.

best_routes.route_name: Entrepreneur/profession libérale VLS-TS and residence card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the current EUR 1,867.02 gross monthly full-time SMIC using about USD 1.1392 per EUR. France-Visas defines the test by reference to full-time minimum wage rather than publishing a USD figure; the visa wizard should be checked for how gross income, net resources and business forecasts are evidenced.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Economic viability for a new activity, or resources at least equivalent to the full-time French SMIC; current benchmark EUR 1,867.02 gross per month from 1 June 2026.
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold changes when the SMIC is revalued. The route is project- and activity-based, not a simple digital-nomad salary test.

income_requirement_display.value: Viable activity or at least full-time SMIC: EUR 1,867.02 gross/month benchmark (about USD 2,127)
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Economic viability or full-time SMIC equivalent
income_requirement_display.notes: Verify the live SMIC and the visa-wizard evidence requirements immediately before filing.

income_proof_months.notes: No universal historical-income period is prescribed for the initial liberal-profession visa on the public route page. For renewal, Annex 10 requires an income-tax notice or accounting evidence for the latest three months, and in the absence of a tax notice may require twelve months; the exact initial filing list remains applicant- and consular-post-specific.

key_requirements.requirement: Carry on a genuine commercial, industrial, artisanal, agricultural or independent liberal activity in France; a liberal activity is habitual, independent and non-salaried.
Show economic viability for a new activity, or at least full-time-SMIC-equivalent resources for a liberal or existing activity.
Register the principal activity through the French business-formalities system and provide evidence that the enterprise or activity is genuine.
A foreign-client contract may support the project, but the status is not permission merely to remain on an unchanged foreign payroll.
Meet diploma, qualification and authorization rules if the proposed profession is regulated.
For the first four-year multiannual card, demonstrate A2 French and pass the applicable civic examination unless exempt.

initial_validity.value: One-year VLS-TS equivalent to a residence permit, followed by a residence-card process as applicable
initial_validity.notes: France-Visas says the VLS-TS is valid for one year and must be validated after arrival.

extension_rules.value: Continue satisfying the activity and viability conditions. At the end of the first temporary card, a four-year multiannual card may be requested; A2 French and a civic examination generally apply to the first multiannual card for applicants under 65.
extension_rules.notes: The official page lists EUR 250 for renewal of a temporary card and EUR 350 for a multiannual card as of the research date.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct: the long-stay visa is a VLS-TS equivalent to a residence permit marked entrepreneur/profession libérale.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least five years of legal and uninterrupted residence, an EU long-term resident card may be available if the residence, resources, insurance and integration conditions are met. The card is valid for ten years and renewable.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: CESEDA article L426-17 counts residence under temporary or multiannual cards, and article L426-18 does not list the entrepreneur/profession libérale card among excluded statuses. Permitted absences and all substantive conditions still apply.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation is possible after a five-year habitual-residence baseline. The applicant must still have lawful residence, a French centre of material and family interests, stable sufficient income, B2 French, civic-exam success, assimilation and good character.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary; meeting the minimum period does not guarantee approval.

best_routes.notes: This is a strong fit only where the applicant's foreign contract is an independent-client arrangement and the applicant will establish and operate a real French self-employed/liberal activity. It is not a digital-nomad visa and does not clearly accommodate an unchanged foreign-employer payroll relationship. The route itself is qualifying residence and can support five-year long-term-residence and naturalisation timelines.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: France does not publish a digital-nomad visitor income threshold because ordinary visitor status is not the professional residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No qualifying professional-residence income threshold applies to visitor status
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Visitor status is separate from the entrepreneur/profession libérale residence route.

income_requirement_display.value: Not a qualifying remote-work residence route
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: A separate professional residence basis is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Short-stay or visitor presence does not replace the required professional residence status.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period for a qualifying remote-work residence route exists because this rejected option is visitor status.

key_requirements.requirement: A visitor must not treat short-stay presence as authorization to establish the selected self-employed activity or as qualifying settlement residence.

initial_validity.value: Short stay only, according to nationality and Schengen rules

extension_rules.value: Ordinary visitor remote work has no confirmed conversion into the selected settlement route
extension_rules.notes: A separate qualifying application and professional basis are required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct qualifying residence from ordinary short-stay status

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from visitor status itself
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Long-term residence requires qualifying legal residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status itself
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation requires habitual qualifying residence and a French centre of interests.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because France does not publish a dedicated digital-nomad or visitor-based settlement route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route uses investment, project and qualification conditions rather than an ordinary remote-worker monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least EUR 30,000 investment for the business-creator category
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is capital investment, not monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 30,000 investment plus qualifying business project
income_requirement_display.notes: Excluded under the selection rules because it is a higher-threshold business-creator route, not ordinary foreign-client remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: No monthly proof period applies to the published investment test.

key_requirements.requirement: Real and serious French business-creation project and at least EUR 30,000 investment.
Master's-equivalent degree or at least five years of comparable professional experience.

initial_validity.value: Potential multiannual talent residence authorization tied to the project

extension_rules.value: Continued eligibility depends on the qualifying business project

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, if the higher-threshold talent conditions are met

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially through ordinary qualifying residence rules
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not selected for the ordinary remote-worker profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through ordinary naturalisation rules
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not selected for the ordinary remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a substantial investment and a French business-creation project. The lower-threshold entrepreneur/profession libérale route is the relevant alternative.

summary.value: Admission or pre-admission to French higher education can support a student VLS-TS without a local employer. From 1 August 2026 the official resource requirement is EUR 877.50 monthly. This is education-based temporary residence, not a benefit granted merely because the applicant already holds a university degree and not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.
summary.notes: The student VLS-TS lasts four months to one year; subsequent student cards can be renewed, including multiannual cards covering the remaining study cycle.

tax_residency_rule.value: French tax domicile can arise if France is the person's home or principal place of stay, principal salaried or self-employed activity, or centre of economic interests. Treaty residence rules can resolve dual-residence conflicts; this is broader than a mechanical 183-day test.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The tests apply to each household member separately.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top ordinary marginal rate in the 2026 schedule for 2025 income. It is a screening rate, not an expected effective rate; family quotient, deductions, surtaxes and social charges can change the result.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single defensible percentage applies across micro-entrepreneur, ordinary non-regulated liberal profession, regulated profession and company structures. URSSAF publishes component rates and income-dependent bases; filing-level modelling is required.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly fixed payment applies to every qualifying self-employed structure. URSSAF's 2026 first-year example for an ordinary non-regulated liberal professional shows EUR 3,473 annual contributions excluding the EUR 120 training contribution, but this uses prescribed bases and is not a universal bill.

special_tax_regimes.value: France has an impatriate regime lasting potentially through the end of the eighth year after taking up duties, but it is primarily for employees or qualifying executives recruited or transferred to an enterprise established in France. It should not be assumed available to the selected self-employed foreign-client route.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No special digital-nomad tax holiday was identified in the reviewed tax-authority materials.

taxes.caveats: French tax and social-security outcomes depend heavily on whether the contract is employment or genuine independent services, the chosen legal and micro/real tax regime, turnover, expenses, household composition, VAT position and the applicable double-tax and social-security treaties.

taxation_system.value: Progressive residence-based personal income tax, normally covering worldwide income for French tax residents, with separate social contributions and possible high-income charges.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Home or principal stay, principal professional activity, or centre of economic interests in France, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
taxation_system.income_scope: French tax residents generally report worldwide income subject to treaty relief; nonresidents are generally taxed on French-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: A qualifying employee/executive impatriate regime can apply for up to eight years after taking duties, but it is not an ordinary self-employed digital-nomad regime.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed liability is structure- and income-dependent. URSSAF publishes separate health, pension, disability, family, CSG-CRDS and training contributions rather than one universal rate.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 45% number is the top ordinary marginal rate, not an effective rate. The 2026 schedule shown by the tax authority applies per tax share to 2025 taxable income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Up to EUR 11,497 per tax share
tax_brackets.applies_to: 2025 taxable income assessed under the 2026 schedule
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: EUR 11,498 to EUR 29,315 per tax share
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: EUR 29,316 to EUR 83,823 per tax share
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: EUR 83,824 to EUR 180,294 per tax share
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.
Additional high-income charges may apply separately.

taxation_system.notes: Professional advice is important before selecting micro-entrepreneur, ordinary profession libérale or company treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: France has no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. A person using the selected route is taxed as an ordinary French self-employed/liberal professional according to the chosen structure.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary French self-employed/liberal-profession taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive PIT up to 45% ordinary top marginal rate, plus structure-dependent social contributions and possible high-income charges.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Tax domicile can arise from the home/principal-stay, principal-professional-activity or economic-interests tests, subject to treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A French tax resident generally reports worldwide income, including foreign-client income, subject to treaty characterization, foreign-tax credits and exemptions where applicable.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No nomad regime. The impatriate regime is generally tied to qualifying recruitment or transfer into a French enterprise and should not be assumed for this self-employed route.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: French registration normally triggers self-employed social contributions. The amount varies by activity, turnover or income, legal form and micro versus ordinary regime.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly amount applies across all qualifying self-employed structures
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: URSSAF's ordinary non-regulated-liberal 2026 first-year example totals EUR 3,473 excluding a EUR 120 training contribution, but actual liability is regime- and income-dependent; micro-entrepreneur treatment is turnover-based.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: France-Visas lists a standard EUR 99 long-stay visa application fee. The entrepreneur/profession libérale page lists EUR 350 for the first residence card, EUR 250 for temporary-card renewal and EUR 350 for a multiannual card; exceptions and service-provider fees may apply.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT, business-registration, accounting and local business-tax consequences depend on turnover, activity and legal form; the reviewed official sources do not establish one amount applicable to every applicant.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa and residence-card charges are state fees, not recurring monthly taxes. Late residence applications can attract an additional EUR 180 regularisation charge.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A brief stay may still create French tax issues if the principal professional activity, home or economic interests are in France. A day count alone is insufficient, and visitor status is not the selected immigration route.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Budget for worldwide-income reporting, progressive PIT up to the 45% marginal bracket and French social-security analysis, subject to treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The selected route normally entails French activity registration, tax returns and social filings. The micro regime may simplify administration if eligible, but should be compared with an ordinary BNC or company structure.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section describes the qualifying self-employed route, not a nonexistent French digital-nomad visa.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The approved VLS-TS itself is equivalent to a temporary residence permit; no prior years in France are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five years of legal and uninterrupted residence is the standard EU long-term-resident baseline; residence, resources, insurance, language and civic conditions apply.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: A long-term resident card is not a mandatory prerequisite to naturalisation. The ordinary naturalisation residence baseline is also five years, so an eligible applicant may apply without waiting additional years after obtaining long-term residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the statutory baseline, not a guaranteed grant date. Residence continuity, French centre of interests, stable income, B2 language, civic examination, assimilation and good character remain necessary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official maximum response period is generally 18 months after issuance of the receipt, reduced to 12 months after at least ten years of habitual residence; it may be extended once by three months.

key_conditions.value: Maintain lawful and genuine residence and the qualifying activity; observe long-term-residence absence limits; show stable sufficient resources and health coverage; meet A2 French/civic requirements for the first multiannual card, B1 for the first relevant resident card, and B2 plus the naturalisation civic examination for citizenship; retain a French centre of material and family interests and good character.
key_conditions.notes: France allows multiple nationality; the reviewed official naturalisation materials did not impose a general renunciation requirement.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Normally four years of marriage to a person who was French on the wedding date and remains French. It becomes five years in specified cases involving less than three years' continuous residence in France or lack of French consular registration while abroad.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a French citizen counts from the marriage date if the French spouse held and retained French nationality and an overseas marriage is transcribed into French civil-status records. Marriage to another foreign migrant does not accelerate French citizenship by itself.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marital and emotional/material community of life must have continued without interruption. The applicant generally needs lawful status, B2 French, supporting civil-status and cohabitation evidence and acceptable criminal/public-order history. False or sham-marriage evidence can lead to refusal, contestation and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage creates a declaration route; citizenship is not automatic on the wedding date.

birthright_citizenship.notes: France combines descent, double jus soli, anti-statelessness rules and residence-based acquisition. A child born in metropolitan France to two foreign-born migrant parents is generally not French immediately merely because of the birthplace.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Generally not French at birth when both parents are foreign-born migrants, unless a special rule such as statelessness applies. A France-born child normally acquires citizenship automatically at 18 if resident in France then and habitually resident for at least five years since age 11; earlier declarations are possible at 13 or 16 under conditions. A child born in France to a foreign parent who was also born in France is French from birth under double jus soli.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Special rules apply in Mayotte and for diplomatic or career-consular families.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is French by descent if at least one parent was French on the child's birth date, whether the child was born in France or abroad, subject to legally established parentage.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a non-citizen child in France does not automatically legalize either parent. If the child is French, a foreign parent may obtain a private-and-family-life residence card if the child is a minor residing in France and the parent effectively contributes to maintenance and education from birth or for at least two years.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent's residence benefit is conditional and does not itself confer citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic status simply because a child is born in France. If the child is French, he can potentially obtain residence and work authorization as the parent of a French minor residing in France, provided parentage is established and he proves effective financial and educational involvement; citizenship still requires a separate route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Fraudulent recognition of parentage or false evidence creates refusal and legal risks.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on the live France dashboard, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category. Passport Index separately reports visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required category on the live dashboard; eVisa destinations may be classified separately in the destination list.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 41 visa-on-arrival and 11 eTA destinations shown by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 173 and world reach of 87%. Index methodologies differ, so these category counts should not be mixed with Henley's broader visa-free/visa-on-arrival score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in international technology environments and major cities, but not sufficient for a low-friction long-term settlement strategy. EF EPI 2025 ranks France 38th of 123 with medium proficiency, while official residence and citizenship processes increasingly require French.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The EF index is based on a self-selected test-taking population and is a practical indicator rather than a census measure.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian may be useful within specific communities but is not an official or generally adequate administrative language. Immigration, tax, business-registration and settlement procedures should be expected in French; professional translation may be required.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The reviewed current sources do not establish broad national availability of Russian- or Ukrainian-language administrative services.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 2,733 net monthly average for private-sector employees in full-time-equivalent employment in 2024.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 annual net median EUR 26,279 divided by 12.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory gross monthly SMIC from 1 June 2026. This is a legal minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary and not net pay.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the 2024 private-sector net full-time-equivalent average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the 2024 private-sector annual net full-time-equivalent median divided by 12.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: INSEE publishes distribution thresholds, including a 99th-percentile threshold of EUR 10,261 net per month, but no finite national maximum. The 99th percentile is not a maximum and is therefore not converted into a maximum-salary value.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 1,867.02 gross per month statutory SMIC from 1 June 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: 35-hour week; not observed minimum pay after deductions.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 private-sector full-time-equivalent average, including apprentices and interns in the publication's stated scope.

median_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 26,279 net annually, or about EUR 2,190 per month
median_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 private-sector full-time-equivalent median; monthly figure is annual value divided by 12.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite national maximum is published; INSEE reports EUR 10,261 net per month as the 99th-percentile threshold for 2024, not as a maximum.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: A maximum is not a meaningful bounded national statistic because the top one percent extend above EUR 10,261 and individual salaries can be higher. This records the highest official distribution marker found without mislabeling it as a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Minimum is statutory gross SMIC for 35 hours weekly; average and median are net private-sector full-time-equivalent employee pay.
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 1 June 2026; average and median refer to 2024.
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average resident-worker labor-market figures, not software-engineer salaries. Gross statutory minimum wage is not directly comparable with the net private-sector average and median. INSEE publishes percentile thresholds rather than a finite maximum; the 99th-percentile marker is preserved only as context.

cost_of_living_note.value: The reviewed official sources do not publish one representative national monthly cost-of-living total. Salary levels vary substantially by territory—for example, the 2024 private-sector average in Île-de-France was 27.3% above the national average—so housing and daily-cost budgeting should be city-specific.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The territorial salary evidence supports the need for location-specific budgeting but is not itself a consumer-price budget.

settlement_track.summary: The entrepreneur/profession libérale VLS-TS is qualifying residence rather than visitor or nomad status. A genuine self-employed software professional can renew into a multiannual card and accumulate the five years ordinarily needed for EU long-term residence or naturalisation; permanent residence is not required before applying for citizenship.
settlement_track.notes: This classification is conditional on a genuine French-registered, principal self-employed activity rather than unchanged foreign salaried employment. CESEDA article L421-5 grants the entrepreneur/profession libérale temporary card; article L426-17 counts regular residence under temporary or multiannual cards toward the five-year EU long-term-resident test, and article L426-18 does not list this card among the excluded statuses. Civil Code article 21-17 separately establishes the ordinary five-year habitual-residence baseline for naturalisation. Both outcomes remain conditional: long-term residence requires continuity, sufficient resources, health insurance and integration, while naturalisation is discretionary and requires the other statutory conditions.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A genuine foreign-client independent-contractor arrangement can fit because the governing rule requires a principal, economically viable non-salaried activity in France and does not state a French-client requirement; registration and proof that the business is real and produces sufficient resources are required. An unchanged foreign-employer payroll relationship is not established as eligible by these sources and needs separate immigration, employment and social-security advice.

data.notes: Current official sources confirm the qualifying residence and five-year settlement framework. Confidence is medium rather than high because the public rules do not expressly discuss foreign-client software contracts, and eligibility depends on genuine self-employment rather than an employment relationship merely relabelled as contracting.

data.selection_summary: Gabon recognizes independent workers as a resident class and permits an independently filed, two-year renewable foreign-resident card. However, commerce approval is mandatory and current rules do not confirm that a software engineer serving only foreign clients qualifies. Ordinary naturalisation requires ten continuous years plus viable, durable investment of local or national interest and remains discretionary. Gabon is therefore not a confirmed foreign-contract remote-work citizenship route.

visa_application.title: Demande de carte de séjour
visa_application.notes: Official residence-card form, not an online adjudication portal. A person authorized to stay beyond 90 days must approach DGDI and request the card within one month after arrival; filing arrangements and the current repatriation-bond amount require direct confirmation.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign-resident card for an independent worker (travailleur indépendant)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The residence-card decree publishes no minimum-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No XAF income threshold is stated.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; commerce approval and repatriation bond required
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility depends on authorized independent professional or commercial activity rather than a stated foreign-income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No bank-statement or income-history period is prescribed in the inspected decree.

key_requirements.requirement: Regular entry and authorization to reside; request the resident card within one month after arrival.
Individually exercise a liberal, commercial, or industrial profession.
Criminal-record extract from the applicant's place of birth, commerce approval, and proof of the repatriation bond.
Statutory resident-card issuance or renewal charge of XAF 50,000; the separate bond amount was not established.
Ordinary independent-worker tax, patente, and social-protection rules may apply.

initial_validity.value: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Article 13 provides a two-year foreign-resident card.

extension_rules.value: Renewable; renewal should be completed in the month following expiry. Statutory late charges apply, and failure to regularize within six months can lead to removal.
extension_rules.notes: The same XAF 50,000 statutory card charge applies to renewal; current substantive renewal criteria are not published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying independent worker can apply directly to DGDI for a carte de séjour de résident étranger after regular entry.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is renewable temporary residence despite the word résident.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The inspected residence law and implementing decree establish renewable resident cards but no distinct permanent-residence class, qualifying period, or automatic conversion rule.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation may be requested after at least ten continuous years, subject to continued residence, viable durable investment of local or national interest, integration, admissibility, and presidential discretion.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Residence alone is insufficient; the investment condition prevents treating ordinary foreign-client software work as a confirmed citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: Closest independent option, but rejected for this selection because no current authority confirms that foreign-client-only software services can obtain the required commerce approval, and ordinary naturalisation separately requires qualifying investment.

rejected_routes.route_name: Salaried foreign-worker authorization and resident card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No route-specific immigration salary threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Ordinary wage rules apply, but no immigration-specific threshold was established.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration threshold published; authorized local employment required
income_requirement_display.notes: Employer-driven route rather than foreign remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: No applicant income-history period applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Local employer and individual employment authorization tied to the worker, position, and enterprise.
Criminal record, accommodation evidence, and repatriation-bond receipt for the resident card.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Both employment authorization and resident card can run for up to two years.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while authorized local employment continues.
extension_rules.notes: Detailed administrative review criteria should be confirmed at filing.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An authorized local employee can request a foreign-resident card.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic permanent-residence conversion is provided by the inspected law.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation is separately discretionary after ten continuous years and qualifying investment and integration.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Excluded because a local employer is required.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route requires local employment and employer-linked authorization.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Sufficient means are required, but no amount is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed XAF amount is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient means required; no amount published
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor requirement, not a residence income test.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport, application, photographs, travel-purpose and accommodation evidence, and sufficient means.

initial_validity.value: Up to 90 days
initial_validity.notes: Short-stay limit.

extension_rules.notes: No remote-work or settlement extension is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Residence beyond three months requires separate authorization and a resident-card application; the visitor visa itself grants no residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Short stays are capped at 90 days, while longer residence is a separate authorized category requiring a resident card. Neither the visa nor eVisa creates permanent residence, and the inspected statutes publish no visitor-to-permanent-residence conversion or qualifying visitor-time rule.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path from visitor status
path_to_citizenship.notes: The ten-year rule concerns continuous qualifying residence and additional conditions, not ordinary visits.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourist, business, visitor, and eVisa permissions do not create a remote-work residence or settlement track.

summary.value: Study is a recognized travel purpose, but no sufficiently clear current student-residence procedure, status duration, or post-study conversion route was established. A university degree alone creates no residence entitlement.
summary.notes: Current searches mainly returned procedures for Gabonese students studying abroad rather than inbound student residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: IRPP residence can arise from habitual residence or a home/main residence in Gabon, or from spending at least 183 days there during the year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The home test can apply before day 183.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Current screening rate reported for mandatory non-salaried health coverage; voluntary pension coverage is reported at 16%.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly total exists: health is percentage-based, the card fee is XAF 50,000 per two-year issuance or renewal, the patente is annual and activity-dependent, and the repatriation-bond amount is unpublished.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or general inbound remote-worker tax regime was identified.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary personal and business rules apply.

taxes.caveats: Foreign-paid work performed from Gabon may be taxable there depending on residence, source, employment classification, business registration, and treaty position. Salary, commercial profit, and non-commercial professional income can receive different treatment.

taxation_system.value: Progressive IRPP using taxable income and a family quotient, with marginal rates from 0% to 35%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Habitual home/main residence or at least 183 days in the year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents may be assessed on global income; non-residents remain taxable on Gabon-source income. Foreign-client work physically performed in Gabon needs source and treaty analysis.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime.
taxation_system.social_security: Current guidance reports mandatory non-salaried health contributions at 6.1% and voluntary pension contributions at 16%, subject to ceilings.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 35% display is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate; family-quotient calculations and statutory offsets apply.

tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: IRPP structure is well supported; filing-level social-security treatment should be reconfirmed because the independent-worker fund has been undergoing implementation.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax category exists. An approved independent worker would fall under ordinary individual, business, and social-protection rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad regime; ordinary self-employed taxation if registered
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive IRPP up to 35%—top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Habitual home/main residence or at least 183 days during the year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: No blanket foreign-income exemption was identified; foreign-paid work conducted from Gabon may be taxable there, subject to source and treaty analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Current guidance reports mandatory independent-worker health contributions at 6.1%; voluntary pension coverage is reported at 16%.

fixed_payments.status: Mixed ordinary charges apply; no universal monthly flat total is published
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Health contributions are percentage-based. CNAMGS describes a Fund 4 for independent workers, but its public rollout page says the forfait schedule was awaiting ministerial validation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad fee exists. Decree 999 sets the two-year residence-card issuance and renewal fee at XAF 50,000, plus a repatriation bond whose amount was not established. Visitor eVisa charges are not residence-route fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: An annual patente applies to non-exempt professions and businesses; its amount varies by statutory tariff, activity, operating means, and establishments. VAT and filing obligations can also apply depending on activity and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: Fixed costs apply but cannot be reduced to one monthly number: the card charge is biennial, patente is annual and variable, social protection is percentage-based, and the bond amount is unpublished. Confirm CNAMGS Fund 4 and DGDI amounts when filing.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 183 days does not guarantee non-residence because the habitual-home test is independent; Gabon-source income may remain taxable.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary IRPP may apply up to 35%; no nomad exemption exists.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect IRPP or business taxation, patente, possible VAT obligations, social coverage, commerce approval, and residence-card and bond costs.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax consequences describe the attempted independent-worker route, not a dedicated nomad program.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying independent worker may apply directly after regular entry.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No distinct permanent-residence transition or qualifying period is published.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality code uses continuous residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence prerequisite.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest ordinary statutory application point; investment, integration, continued residence, and discretion still apply.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No end-to-end service standard is published. Presidential silence for six months after ministerial transmission counts as rejection, not approval.

key_conditions.value: Ten continuous years; viable durable investment of local or national interest; continued residence; adulthood; good character; qualifying integration; no disqualifying convictions; individual presidential decree.
key_conditions.notes: Exceptional reductions are discretionary and not an ordinary remote-worker entitlement.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Current marriage-based citizenship waiting period.

existing_marriage_effect.value: The six years run from celebration of a subsisting marriage properly entered or transcribed in Gabonese civil-status records; spouses apply jointly.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Foreign marriage documentation must be regularized.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be genuine and remain in force. Fraud or sham arrangements can cause refusal or deprivation; divorce within six years after acquisition can create deprivation risk under the 2026 code.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates citizenship but does not make it automatic.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A foreign-parent child born in Gabon generally needs continuous residence to age 16 and judicial recognition between ages 16 and 18; this is not automatic jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship at birth solely from birth in Gabon. Conditional recognition and anti-statelessness rules may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Diplomatic-family exclusions apply.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a legally established qualifying Gabonese parent is Gabonese by origin.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage must be legally established.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalise a foreign parent. Marriage to a Gabonese citizen can support residence and the six-year marriage route; exceptional naturalisation reductions remain discretionary.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No general parent-of-citizen-child permanent-residence entitlement was established.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship through the child. A father married to the Gabonese mother may use spouse residence and marriage-based citizenship rules; no separate benefit was established for an unmarried father.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Marriage and parentage must be genuine and documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Index count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 34 visa-on-arrival plus 4 eTA destinations; eVisas are separate.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports mobility score 67; methodology differs from Henley.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English may work inside an international remote team, but French is required in practice for immigration, tax, commerce, housing, and most local administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Practical assessment inferred from French being the official working language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian should not be expected in public administration; French-language assistance would normally be necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official portal publishes formal-employment bulletins and ENEC 2024 reporting supplies labor-force indicators, but the inspected public materials do not publish a current national mean worker salary. GNI, payroll totals, and household expenditure were not substituted.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median wage is published in the inspected employment sources, so no USD conversion is possible.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: AU statistics report the 2024 nominal gross monthly minimum in USD; this is not a 2026 spot conversion.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national average wage was published.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median wage was published.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum salary is not a statutory measure; contribution ceilings are not wage maxima.

min_salary_local_currency.value: XAF 150,000 monthly minimum income (RMM); underlying SMIG XAF 80,000
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary or immigration threshold.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national mean monthly worker salary in XAF is published in the inspected official employment portal, accessible ENEC 2024 reporting, or AU pocketbook. Historical sector means were not treated as a current national average.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national median monthly worker salary in XAF is published. Public ENEC 2024 reporting gives employment indicators but not median pay.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No statutory or observed national upper salary endpoint is published. The XAF 1,500,000 amounts in social-security materials are contribution or benefit-calculation ceilings, not maximum salaries.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory nominal gross monthly minimum only; current national average, median, and maximum worker pay are unpublished in the inspected sources.
average_citizen_salary.period: RMM/SMIG reference current in 2026 materials; USD comparison reported for 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: Only the statutory minimum is populated. Current public employment sources do not supply national mean or median pay, while maximum salary is not a meaningful statutory measure.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No sufficiently current official national or Libreville household budget was established.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Not a nomad-only program: Gabon publishes no dedicated digital-nomad or remote-worker status. Short-stay visas and eVisas are visitor permissions and provide no settlement track; the separate two-year independent-worker resident card requires commerce approval and does not confirm foreign-client-only software work.
settlement_track.summary: An independent-worker resident card exists, but its fit for a foreign-client-only software contractor is unconfirmed. Even if granted, ordinary naturalisation requires ten continuous years plus viable durable investment and discretionary approval.
settlement_track.notes: No separate permanent-residence stage was established. A formal status switch is not expressly required, but qualifying local or national investment would have to be added to the ordinary remote-worker profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The law recognizes independent liberal, commercial, and industrial work but does not confirm commerce approval for software services supplied solely to foreign clients. Citizenship independently requires qualifying durable investment.

data.notes: Focused audit confirmed a two-year renewable independent-worker resident card and a statutory XAF 50,000 issuance/renewal charge. Gabon remains ineligible because foreign-client-only software work is not established by the current sources for commerce approval and naturalisation imposes a separate investment condition. Visitor status has no permanent-residence conversion rule. Current average and median wages are unpublished in the inspected sources, while a national maximum salary is inapplicable; these fields remain null with precise explanations.

data.selection_summary: The Gambia does not currently offer a qualifying route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Residence Permit A can be obtained without a local employer but expressly prohibits any paid or unpaid employment or business; Residence Permit B is for employment and is tied to immigration approval, an employer and the expatriate-quota system. Visitor visas likewise confer no residence or work authorization. A 2026 Immigration Bill remains at committee stage and cannot be treated as current law or an open route.

visa_application.title: Residential Permit – Gambia Immigration Department
visa_application.notes: This is the official permit-information page, not a direct online application portal. Applications are processed through designated issuing centres and bank counters. No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or ordinary freelance application channel was found.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The Act requires sufficient means appropriate to the applicant's station in life but publishes no numeric threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed amount published; applicant must demonstrate sufficient means.
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is a discretionary sufficiency test, not an income threshold for remote workers.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; sufficient means required
income_requirement_display.notes: The permit is unsuitable even if the means test is met because all paid or unpaid employment and business are prohibited.

income_proof_months.notes: The current official permit page does not state a required bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport, document establishing status and identity, and attestation from an embassy or high commission.
Good character and sufficient means to live in The Gambia; immigration may require a bank-guaranteed repatriation bond or cash deposit.
The holder must not undertake any employment or conduct any business whatsoever, whether paid or unpaid.
Non-ECOWAS Permit A is listed at GMD 5,700, with GMD 2,500 identified for the Alien Card; the page does not clearly state whether that card amount is included or additional.

initial_validity.value: From issue until 31 January immediately following the issue date
initial_validity.notes: The duration therefore varies according to the issue date.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is contemplated annually; the prior-year permit is required for renewal, but approval criteria and filing deadlines are not published on the current page.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains discretionary and does not remove the prohibition on work or business.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence is possible, but only on a residence-without-work basis.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It cannot lawfully support the applicant's continuing foreign employment or freelance business on the wording of the permit conditions.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Neither the current permit page nor the governing Act establishes a permanent-residence conversion rule for Permit A.

path_to_citizenship.value: The Constitution separately permits naturalisation after at least 15 continuous years of ordinary residence, but it does not confirm that every year on Permit A counts, and Permit A prohibits the applicant's remote work.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not create a workable citizenship track for the stated foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this residence category expressly prohibits employment and business of any kind, including wording broad enough to capture foreign remote employment. It could be relevant only to a financially self-sufficient person who does not work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general salary threshold is published; this is an employer/quota route rather than a foreign-income route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No general minimum salary published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A GRA payroll-tax receipt is required.

income_requirement_display.value: No published salary threshold; local employment and payroll evidence required
income_requirement_display.notes: Foreign-client income is not a substitute for the local employment and immigration approvals described by the official material.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Prospective employer application, expatriate-quota availability, employee application, passport and immigration permit.
Written immigration permission is required before employment begins.
Residence Permit B application requires a GRA payroll-tax receipt; renewal requires the prior-year permit.
The statutory permit form restricts the holder to employment with the named employer and requires permission to change employment or conduct another business.

initial_validity.value: From issue until 31 January immediately following the issue date
initial_validity.notes: The official non-ECOWAS Permit B fee is listed as GMD 7,700, with GMD 2,500 identified for the Alien Card; inclusion versus addition is unclear.

extension_rules.value: Annual renewal appears available with the prior-year permit and continuing employment/payroll evidence.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic renewal or permanent-residence conversion was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Grants temporary residence and authorization for the specifically approved employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not authorize ordinary independent foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence route or qualifying period was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Long-term ordinary residence may eventually support a separate naturalisation application after 15 continuous years, but the employment permit itself does not grant citizenship or permanent residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This route is excluded because a local employer and immigration employment approval are required.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route is employer-linked, subject to the expatriate-quota and immigration-permission system, and does not fit independent work for a foreign client or employer.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary visa, short visit or visa-exempt entry

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visible means of sustenance may be required, but no numeric threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed amount published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is entry evidence, not a residence income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; visitor entry only
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor entry does not provide work authorization or qualifying residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport and visa unless exempt; health documentation, entry clearance where applicable and visible means of sustenance may be requested.
Ordinary intended stay generally must not exceed 90 days unless referred to the Director General of Immigration.
London High Commission applications are submitted in person or by post; listed fees are GBP 40 single-entry and GBP 60 multiple-entry.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to 90 days for a short visit; a multiple-journey visa may have validity not exceeding 12 months, without authorizing continuous residence.
initial_validity.notes: Actual permission depends on nationality and the decision at the port of entry.

extension_rules.value: Stays exceeding 90 days require referral to the Director General; no remote-work or settlement conversion is published.
extension_rules.notes: An extension remains visitor status unless a separate permit is granted.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A visa or visa exemption is entry permission, not a residential permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No path from visitor status was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Short visits are not established as ordinary residence for the constitutional 15-year naturalisation rule.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor, visa-exempt and short-business entry do not confer residence or remote-work authorization and cannot be treated as a citizenship path.

summary.value: No independent degree-, points- or qualification-based residence route was found. Skilled-worker Residence Permit B is tied to approved employment rather than awarded independently for a software-engineering degree.
summary.notes: The applicant's degree may support an employer-sponsored skilled role but does not itself provide immigration status.

tax_residency_rule.value: Under the captured Income and Sales Tax Act, an individual is resident if the individual resides in The Gambia at any time during the tax year, is present for an aggregate 183 days or more, or is a Gambian government employee posted abroad. First- and final-year rules limit residence to the period beginning with first presence or ending with last presence in specified circumstances.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 'resides at any time' alternative means 183 days is not the sole test. Filing-level application should be confirmed with GRA because the consolidated source is the 2004 Act and subsequent amendments may affect details.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the current published top marginal employment-income rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee National Provident Fund contribution for covered local employment is 5% of basic salary; the employer pays another 10%. Applicability to a person employed solely by a foreign entity without a lawful Gambian employment arrangement is not established.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly nomad or freelancer payment exists because no such immigration category was found. Permit/card fees are event-based, while NPF is percentage-based.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, remote-worker or inbound expatriate regime was found. Ordinary employment or business-income rules apply if the activity is taxable.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The absence of a special regime does not imply tax exemption.

taxes.caveats: Immigration authorization and tax liability are separate. Work physically performed in The Gambia may be Gambian-source even when paid abroad. Classification as employment versus business income, residence, foreign withholding, treaty relief and permanent-establishment exposure require case-specific advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal employment-income tax with published rates from 0% to 25%. Individual businesses are subject to the higher of scheduled income tax or turnover-based minimum tax: 1% of turnover with audited accounts, 2% without audited accounts, while the GRA FAQ states 3% of turnover where annual business turnover is below GMD 500,000.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Resident if residing in The Gambia during the year, present for at least 183 aggregate days, or a Gambian government employee posted abroad, subject to first/final-year rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Employment carried out in The Gambia is Gambian-source wherever paid. Resident foreign-source employment income is exempt if foreign income tax was paid or withheld; statutory foreign-tax-credit rules apply to other included foreign-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or remote-worker special regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered NPF employment, 5% of basic salary is deducted from the employee and 10% is paid by the employer. Voluntary registration exists, but no fixed contribution for this unsupported foreign-remote-work scenario is published.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 25% figure is the top marginal rate. It applies only to the portion above the top threshold, not to all income. Business/self-employment may also face turnover-based minimum tax.

tax_brackets.notes: Official GRA employment-income schedule; no USD conversion used because exchange rates fluctuate.
Top marginal bracket and dashboard screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: The official GRA schedule improves the previous record's unsupported 30% value: the current GRA employment-income material shows a 25% top bracket.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because The Gambia has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. A person nevertheless working from The Gambia may fall under ordinary employment or business tax rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary PIT/business rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 25% progressive employment-income tax; this is a top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence can arise by residing in The Gambia during the year or reaching 183 aggregate days; the statutory tests require case-specific application.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Work performed in The Gambia is Gambian-source wherever paid. Resident foreign-source employment income is exempt if foreign income tax was paid or withheld; foreign-tax-credit rules may apply to other included foreign-source income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered local employees contribute 5% of basic salary to NPF and employers contribute 10%. No official rule was found applying a fixed contribution to an unsupported foreign-only remote-work arrangement.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payments
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: NPF is percentage-based for covered employment: 5% employee plus 10% employer; voluntary registrants declare a contribution level based on earnings.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Non-ECOWAS Residence Permit A is listed at GMD 5,700 and Permit B at GMD 7,700, with GMD 2,500 identified for an Alien Card; the official wording does not clearly establish whether the card amount is included or additional. A Non-Gambian ID Card is GMD 750.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax was confirmed. Individual businesses may instead face turnover-based minimum tax.
fixed_payments.notes: These fees do not make either permit suitable for foreign-contract remote work.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence because the Act also treats an individual who resides in The Gambia during the year as resident, and locally performed work may be Gambian-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary progressive PIT may apply, subject to source classification and foreign-tax relief. Immigration remains the primary blocker because no permit authorizes the stated arrangement.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: GRA requires income-generating individuals to register. Individual business tax may be the higher of scheduled tax or turnover minimum tax, but tax or business registration does not legalize residence or work.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax treatment is reported for screening despite the negative immigration result. Obtain GRA or professional advice before working from The Gambia.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Permit A or B can be issued directly, but neither fits the profile: A prohibits work and B requires approved employment. No waiting period or processing time is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No statutory permanent-residence conversion period was established for either permit.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Constitution measures naturalisation by continuous ordinary residence, not by a confirmed permanent-residence stage.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the general constitutional naturalisation residence period, not a timeline available through a qualifying foreign-remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official citizenship page describes eligibility and documents but publishes no typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: At least 15 years of continuous ordinary residence, full age and capacity, good character, intention to continue residing permanently, ability to support oneself and dependants, renunciation of other citizenship, and an oath of allegiance. Permit copies and alien cards may be required as residence evidence.
key_conditions.notes: The route is not usable for the applicant unless a separate lawful work-authorized residence basis is obtained.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution requires at least seven years of ordinary residence since the marriage to a Gambian citizen; marriage alone is insufficient.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A person presently married to a Gambian citizen may apply for registration after seven years of ordinary residence since the marriage. The provision also covers a former marriage to a person who was Gambian during the marriage, provided seven years of ordinary residence have accrued since the marriage ended.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing marriage between two non-Gambians provides no accelerated route.

requirements_and_risks.value: Application and proof of the qualifying marriage and residence are required. Fraud, false representation or concealment can support deprivation proceedings; applicants should expect documentary verification and must not rely on a sham marriage.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The Constitution states that later annulment does not undo citizenship already registered under the marriage provision, but this does not protect a fraudulent application.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A person born in The Gambia is presumed Gambian by birth only when at least one parent was a Gambian citizen at the time of birth; place of birth alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in The Gambia to two non-citizen migrant parents does not acquire citizenship automatically under the constitutional birth rule.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No generally applicable permanent-resident-parent or unrestricted jus-soli rule was found.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in The Gambia is presumed a citizen by birth when either parent is Gambian; a child born abroad is a citizen by descent when either parent is Gambian otherwise than solely by descent under the same provision.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Documentary registration may still be needed in practice.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Gambian child does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on a foreign parent. No published automatic parent-of-citizen route was found in the reviewed official immigration material.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any family-based discretion should be verified directly with GID.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Gambian, the child can be Gambian, but the migrant father receives no automatic immigration or nationality status from the child's citizenship. Marriage to the Gambian mother may create the separate seven-year residence-based registration route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and a citizen child should not be treated as an automatic shortcut.

rank.notes: Current Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change dynamically.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count, separate from visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index displayed count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 25 visa-on-arrival destinations and 3 eTA destinations shown by the source.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 71 and world reach of 36% at the time checked.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the official language and is used in government, education and formal settings, so English is practical for official interactions and remote-work logistics. Mandinka, Wolof, Fula and Jola are also widely used in daily life.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Language practicality does not overcome the absence of a lawful remote-work permit.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or widely documented working languages. They may be usable within private expatriate communities, but English is needed for official processes.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official 2025 Labour Force Survey was inspected but does not publish a national mean monthly earnings figure in its reported tables.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No official national median monthly wage was established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current reliable national minimum-wage amount or observed minimum monthly salary was confirmed; the previous record's dated secondary GMD 50/day figure was not retained.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey measures employment structure, informality and labour underutilisation but does not provide a national average salary suitable for this field.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Not published in the inspected official report.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A meaningful national maximum salary is not published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: No current official amount confirmed.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No current official national mean salary confirmed.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current official national median salary confirmed.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No official national maximum confirmed.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: No reliable national salary level established; official labour-force survey context only
average_citizen_salary.period: GLFS 2025 revised report available in 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: Nulls are retained deliberately. The focused salary search located a current official labour-force report but not defensible mean, median, minimum or maximum national monthly earnings.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No reliable official household cost-of-living amount comparable to a remote worker's monthly budget was established in this pass.

settlement_track.summary: Residence Permit A is independently obtainable but prohibits all employment and business, while Permit B requires approved employer-linked employment. General naturalisation after 15 years exists separately, but no lawful ordinary foreign-contract remote-work status was found from which this applicant could pursue it.
settlement_track.notes: The 2026 Immigration Bill was still at committee stage on the official tracker and therefore was not treated as enacted law or an available route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Permit A prohibits any employment or business; Permit B is tied to approved employment and the expatriate-quota system. No separate digital-nomad, remote-worker or ordinary freelance permit was found.

data.notes: The negative route conclusion has strong official support and materially improves the previous record by distinguishing the independently obtainable but non-working Permit A from employer-linked Permit B. Overall confidence remains medium because no permanent-residence framework, citizenship processing time or defensible national salary level could be established, and the pending 2026 Immigration Bill may later change the legal framework.

data.selection_summary: Georgia has a current residence-oriented route: the IT Residence Permit, effective since September 2025. A foreign software engineer can independently register as a Georgian individual entrepreneur, obtain Small Business Status, conduct qualifying IT activities, and apply without a local employer after documenting at least two years of IT experience and USD 25,000 of IT remuneration during the preceding year. The permit is initially valid for three years, can be extended within a 12-year ceiling, and can support permanent residence and ordinary naturalisation after 10 years, subject to physical-presence, business, tax, language and other conditions.
