settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor, visa-free, visa-on-arrival, and ordinary e-visa permission must not be treated as authorization to work remotely or as settlement residence.
settlement_track.summary: Ghana has general residence, purpose-specific self-employment authorization, indefinite residence, and citizenship procedures, but no current official source confirms that ordinary foreign-client remote work qualifies for the necessary initial permit. The applicant therefore cannot presently start a verified residence-to-citizenship track through this profile.
settlement_track.notes: A favorable written GIS determination confirming the proposed foreign-contract software activity, application classification, sponsor or business requirements, and settlement treatment could change the assessment. The current public rules do not support selection eligibility.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Self-employment is a recognized residence purpose, but official public material does not confirm that services supplied solely to a foreign employer or client qualify, identify a dedicated classification, or establish that the applicant may file without a Ghanaian sponsor or local business. This uncertainty does not support current selection eligibility.

data.notes: Focused audit completed against the previous Ghana record. More than 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including five new official GRA and GSS URLs outside the previous source set. The route conclusion remains negative. The flagged temporary-residence explanation now identifies the Form E mechanism and its unresolved filing conditions; fixed-payment treatment now distinguishes optional percentage-based SSNIT from inapplicable informal-sector fixed schemes; and the salary fields now contain exact, carefully delimited official Ghana-cedi observations instead of vague unresolved markers.

data.selection_summary: Greece has a current Digital Nomad Visa (Z.1) for non-EU employees, freelancers and self-employed people working exclusively for employers or clients outside Greece. It fits the applicant's foreign-contract remote work and can be followed by a renewable two-year residence permit. However, current sources do not establish that this digital-nomad status qualifies for EU long-term residence or naturalisation; official citizenship guidance excludes temporary permits and does not list the digital-nomad permit among the seven-year qualifying titles. Greece therefore needs immigration-law confirmation before being treated as a citizenship-path match.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad Visa – Hellenic Republic Ministry of Foreign Affairs
visa_application.notes: The MFA page is official route information, not the consular application form. Under the 2026 framework, the applicant should obtain the Z.1 national visa through the competent Greek consulate before travelling; the later residence-permit application is filed through the official migration portal.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Visa (Z.1) followed by digital-nomad residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,500 using the ECB reference rate of about USD 1.1715 per EUR shown for 14 July 2026. Exchange rates fluctuate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,500 net per month; add 20% for a spouse/partner and 15% for each child
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The statutory amount is net income after tax in the country where the work is provided. It may be demonstrated through the employment/service contract or a bank account.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,500 net/month (about USD 4,100); +20% spouse/partner, +15% per child
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR threshold with approximate USD conversion
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 3,500 × 1.20 with spouse/partner; add 15% of EUR 3,500 for each child
income_requirement_display.notes: The euro amount is statutory; the USD amount is only an exchange-rate approximation.

income_proof_months.notes: Article 68 and the current consular Z.1 checklist allow proof through the relevant employment/service relationship or a bank account, and permit assessment monthly or as an annual average, but prescribe no fixed number of historical statement months. The competent consulate may request case-specific evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Be a third-country national working remotely through information and communications technology for an employer or clients established outside Greece.
Declare an intention to reside in Greece for remote work and undertake not to provide work, services or projects to an employer established in Greece.

Provide a foreign employment or service contract covering the visa period; freelancers with multiple foreign clients provide the relevant contracts, while owners provide details of their foreign business.
Show net stable income of at least EUR 3,500 per month, increased for accompanying family members.
Satisfy the general national-visa documentation requirements, including a valid travel document and the health-insurance and admissibility documents requested by the consulate.
Apply for the initial Z.1 national visa through the competent Greek consular authority before travelling; the former visitor/visa-free in-country shortcut was removed in 2026.

initial_validity.value: National Digital Nomad Visa for up to 12 months; qualifying holders may apply before expiry for a two-year residence permit.
initial_validity.notes: The national visa is the entry stage. The subsequent residence permit is a distinct status.

extension_rules.value: The two-year residence permit may be renewed repeatedly in two-year increments while the foreign-work and income conditions continue. Absences not exceeding six months per year do not prevent renewal.
extension_rules.notes: Law 5275/2026 changed the entry/application procedure; applicants should verify the current renewal filing window in the electronic portal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Confirmed: obtain the consular Z.1 visa, enter Greece and file electronically for the two-year digital-nomad residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is genuine temporary legal residence, not ordinary visitor status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Greece has a general EU long-term-resident status after five years of lawful and continuous residence, but eligibility of this exact digital-nomad sequence remains unresolved. Current Article 68 converts Z.1 into an I.8 sufficient-resources permit; Articles 143-144 cover lawful residents but exclude persons enjoying a temporary residence status, and the reviewed current provisions do not expressly say whether an Article-68-derived I.8 permit falls inside or outside that exclusion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The uncertainty is classification, not the existence of Greece’s five-year long-term-resident regime. Obtain written confirmation from the Ministry or specialist Greek counsel that digital-nomad I.8 years are countable before treating this as a permanent-residence path.

path_to_citizenship.value: Uncertain. Ordinary naturalisation can use seven years for holders of specified qualifying residence titles, while other non-temporary titles may require twelve years. The official list does not name the digital-nomad permit and temporary permits are excluded.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A switch to EU long-term residence or another listed qualifying title may be necessary, but no ordinary foreign-contract conversion route was officially confirmed.

best_routes.notes: This is a strong temporary-living fit for an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer and does not require a Greek employer. It is not a confirmed settlement route: the digital-nomad visa and renewable permit are clear, while permanent-residence and citizenship counting remain unresolved.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor or visa-free entry followed by an in-country digital-nomad application

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The underlying income threshold remains EUR 3,500, but this in-country filing route is no longer available to new applicants.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,500 net per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Income is not the reason for rejection; the filing location/status is.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,500 net/month, but visitor-to-permit filing is closed
income_requirement_display.notes: A visitor must not rely on the former in-country shortcut.

income_proof_months.notes: The law prescribes no fixed historical income-proof period for this now-closed filing strategy.

key_requirements.requirement: New applicants must use the consular Z.1 national-visa route before travel.

initial_validity.value: Not available as a new visitor-to-residence route
initial_validity.notes: Visitor status itself remains subject to Schengen limits and is not a residence route.

extension_rules.notes: There is no visitor-based digital-nomad residence permit to extend.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No under this filing strategy; apply for Z.1 abroad instead.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time is not qualifying residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: No
path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor presence is not qualifying legal residence for naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because Law 5275/2026 removed the former ability to arrive under a short-stay visa or visa exemption and initiate this digital-nomad residence strategy from Greece.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence permit for persons with sufficient resources (I.8 / financially independent person)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 2,000 at about USD 1.1715 per EUR. The controlling threshold is EUR 2,000; exchange rates fluctuate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 2,000 per month; +20% for a spouse and +15% for each child
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Joint Ministerial Decision 41712/2014 is marked in force in the reviewed legal database and sets the minimum for financially independent persons. It permits proof through a foreign pension, bank account, or other evidence of sufficient lawfully obtained own resources.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 2,000/month (about USD 2,343); +20% spouse, +15% per child
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR threshold with approximate USD conversion
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 2,000 × 1.20 with spouse; add 15% of EUR 2,000 for each child
income_requirement_display.notes: The EUR amount is the published legal threshold. This route prohibits salaried work and independent economic activity in Greece and is therefore not used for the active foreign-contract profile.

income_proof_months.notes: The in-force decision specifies acceptable proof categories—a foreign pension, bank account, or other evidence of sufficient lawfully obtained own resources—but does not prescribe a fixed number of historical bank-statement or income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Demonstrate sufficient independent resources and comply with the I.8 conditions; the permit is not the dedicated remote-work route.

initial_validity.value: Three-year I.8 residence permit under the current consolidated Migration Code
initial_validity.notes: This is the general sufficient-resources I.8 permit, distinct from the special two-year Article 68 permit issued after a Z.1 digital-nomad visa.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for further three-year periods while the sufficient-resources conditions continue
extension_rules.notes: Renewal does not change the statutory prohibition on salaried work or independent economic activity in Greece.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, if its separate sufficient-resources conditions are met.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A general five-year EU long-term-residence framework exists, but this route is rejected for the applicant because it does not authorise the intended active foreign-contract work.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No claim is made here that every I.8 period necessarily qualifies; permit classification should be verified.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential only under the applicable qualifying-title and residence rules; it is not a suitable route for this active-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant intends to continue active foreign-contract work. The general I.8 permit expressly prohibits salaried work and independent economic activity in Greece.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Article 79C delegates the sufficient-resources amount to a joint decision under Article 176(51). No current implementing amount specifically applicable to Z.15 was located, so no USD threshold is asserted.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The enacted provision requires sufficient subsistence resources but does not state the euro amount; it refers to an implementing joint decision.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient resources required; current Z.15 euro amount not published in the reviewed implementing material
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a prospective Greek employment or business-activity search route, not a foreign-contract remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: Article 79C requires evidence of sufficient subsistence resources in the amount to be set under Article 176(51), but it states neither a historical proof period nor a bank-statement month count. No current implementing checklist specifying such a period was located.

key_requirements.requirement: Be a graduate of a qualifying foreign higher-education institution and hold a qualifying master’s, doctorate or postdoctorate obtained within the preceding five years; the institutions must appear in at least two designated international rankings.
Enter to seek employment or develop professional activity in Greece and demonstrate sufficient subsistence resources.

initial_validity.value: Twelve-month national Talent Visa (Z.15)
initial_validity.notes: The 12-month duration is express in Article 79C. Eligibility also requires both a qualifying foreign higher-education degree and a master’s, doctorate or postdoctorate obtained within the preceding five years.

extension_rules.value: No Z.15 renewal is provided; before expiry the holder may apply under Article 12 for another residence permit only if that permit’s separate conditions are met
extension_rules.notes: This is a conversion opportunity, not an automatic extension or residence permit. Without a qualifying employment, business or other residence basis, Z.15 supplies no continuing status after 12 months.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Only after obtaining a qualifying Greek employment, business or other residence basis.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through a later qualifying residence status, not the job-search visa itself.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the research profile is ordinary ongoing foreign-contract remote work, not prospective Greek employment or local entrepreneurial activity; the applicant context also does not establish the required recent postgraduate qualification.

rejected_routes.route_name: EU Blue Card / Greek employer-sponsored skilled employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current European Commission Greece page states a formula of 1.6 times average gross annual salary and reports EUR 31,918.83 only for 2024—about EUR 2,659.90/month or USD 3,116/month at the cited 2026 exchange rate. Because no 2026 numeric threshold is published there, the current USD minimum remains null rather than presenting the 2024 figure as current.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: 1.6 × Greece’s average gross annual salary; latest numeric amount on the reviewed Commission page is EUR 31,918.83 for 2024
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The formula is current on the Commission page, but its displayed euro amount is explicitly for 2024. A 2026 euro threshold was not published in the current official material reviewed, so no 2026 amount is asserted.

income_requirement_display.value: 1.6× average gross annual salary; Commission page lists EUR 31,918.83/year for 2024 (2026 amount not published there)
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 1.6 × average gross annual salary; last displayed threshold EUR 31,918.83/year for 2024
income_requirement_display.notes: The historical 2024 amount is context only. The route is rejected independently because it requires qualifying highly skilled employment in Greece.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable as a historical income requirement; qualification depends on the salary in the qualifying Greek employment contract.

key_requirements.requirement: Hold a valid national visa and qualifying highly skilled Greek employment contract meeting the applicable duration and salary conditions.
Show higher professional qualifications or the recognised equivalent experience, sickness insurance and admissibility.

initial_validity.value: Two years; if the employment contract is shorter, the contract term plus three months
initial_validity.notes: The European Commission’s Greece page states a standard 24-month validity period.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for three years by reapplying before expiry and continuing to meet the conditions
extension_rules.notes: The Commission page says renewal documents are resubmitted except those concerning whether the profession is regulated or unregulated.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, through qualifying Greek employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential EU long-term-residence pathway after qualifying residence, but not independently available to this profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential only after qualifying residence and naturalisation requirements.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Greek employer and qualifying local job contract are required.

summary.value: A third-country national admitted to a Greek educational institution can independently seek a study residence permit without an employer. Law 5275/2026 also lists a one-year post-study/research permit for job search or entrepreneurship and a highly qualified Z.15 job-search visa. These require enrolment, completed Greek study/research, or prospective Greek work/business; the applicant's existing foreign degree alone does not create a remote-work residence entitlement.
summary.notes: Education routes are genuine temporary residence but are not ordinary foreign-contract remote-work matches and do not grant permanent residence directly.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person is Greek tax resident if Greece is their permanent/principal residence, habitual abode or centre of vital interests, or if present for more than 183 cumulative days in any 12-month period; the 183-day rule generally applies from the first day of presence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Double-tax treaties and centre-of-vital-interests analysis can alter the practical result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for a single taxpayer without dependent children. It is not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage applies to the foreign-contract digital-nomad scenario. Locally registered self-employed people use fixed insurance categories; foreign employees may instead depend on EU coordination, a bilateral agreement or Greek payroll classification.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the 2026 first self-employed pension/health category, EUR 250.77, plus the EUR 10 unemployment contribution. This applies only if Greek self-employed insurance registration is required, not automatically to every digital nomad.

special_tax_regimes.value: Article 5C can exempt 50% of qualifying Greek employment and/or individual-business income from income tax for seven tax years after transferring tax residence, subject to its detailed eligibility rules. It is not a digital-nomad-visa exemption and should not be assumed to cover ordinary foreign employment automatically.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Article 5A is an investment-based high-net-worth regime and Article 5B concerns foreign pensioners; neither fits the ordinary applicant profile.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on days in Greece, centre of vital interests, where employment is physically exercised, contract and entity structure, the applicable double-tax treaty and social-security agreement. A digital-nomad immigration permit does not itself exempt foreign salary or business income from Greek tax.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax on employment, pensions and business profits, with a 44% top marginal rate; Greek tax residents generally report worldwide income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Greek residence can arise from permanent/principal residence, habitual abode, centre of vital interests, or more than 183 cumulative days during a 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Greek tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Greek-source income, subject to treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Article 5C provides a conditional 50% exemption for qualifying Greek employment or individual-business income for seven tax years. It is not automatic for digital nomads.
taxation_system.social_security: No universal DNV rate was confirmed. If registered as Greek self-employed in 2026, the first pension/health category is EUR 250.77 monthly plus EUR 10 unemployment contribution; higher categories are available and some professions incur supplementary contributions.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard number is the 44% top marginal screening rate, not the effective tax rate. From tax year 2026, the general childless scale is 9%, 20%, 26%, 34%, 39% and 44%. Lower rates can apply based on age and dependent children.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual employment, pension and business-profit income; general 2026 childless scale
tax_brackets.notes: USD ceiling approximated at EUR 1 = USD 1.1715.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual employment, pension and business-profit income; general 2026 childless scale
tax_brackets.notes: Age- and child-based reductions may apply.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual employment, pension and business-profit income; general 2026 childless scale
tax_brackets.notes: Child-based reductions may apply.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual employment, pension and business-profit income
Annual employment, pension and business-profit income
Annual employment, pension and business-profit income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: The general 2026 scale is well supported. Classification of a particular foreign employment or freelance arrangement and entitlement to Article 5C require individual advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special DNV tax exemption was found. A tax-resident digital nomad should expect Greek worldwide-income analysis and progressive PIT up to 44%, unless a treaty or a separately approved inbound regime changes the result.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Foreign-contract digital nomad; tax category depends on employment versus business structure
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive PIT up to 44% for 2026; top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 cumulative days in any 12-month period generally creates residence from the first day; permanent home, habitual abode and centre of vital interests can create residence independently.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Greek tax residents are generally taxable on worldwide income. Work physically performed from Greece can also require Greek-source and treaty analysis even before residence is settled.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No visa-specific exemption. Article 5C's seven-year 50% exemption is conditional and targets qualifying income from Greek employment or individual business activity, so a foreign-contract worker must not assume eligibility.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The visa law does not impose a fixed monthly DNV contribution. Liability depends on foreign payroll coverage, EU or bilateral coordination and whether a Greek sole proprietorship/self-employed registration is created.

fixed_payments.status: Route fees are confirmed; recurring social insurance is setup-dependent
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: If Greek self-employed insurance applies, the 2026 minimum general pension/health category is EUR 250.77 plus EUR 10 unemployment contribution per month; this is not automatically imposed merely by holding the DNV.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The establishing law specifies EUR 75 for the national visa and EUR 1,000 for the principal applicant's two-year residence-permit application. A residence-card printing fee may also apply; an official EU Blue Card page lists EUR 16 for the card.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Greek business registration can bring bookkeeping, VAT and presumptive-minimum-income issues. Standard VAT is 24%, with 13% and 6% reduced rates; actual VAT liability depends on place-of-supply and exemptions.
fixed_payments.notes: The EUR 75 and EUR 1,000 amounts are statutory route fees, not monthly taxes. Confirm the current consular fee schedule and electronic-payment codes before filing.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 184 days does not guarantee non-residence if Greece becomes the centre of vital interests. Greek-source income and treaty rules can still matter.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect a Greek return and worldwide-income review, with foreign tax credits or treaty relief considered case by case; the top marginal screening rate is 44%.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Greek sole proprietorship can trigger progressive business-profit tax, fixed e-EFKA categories, VAT/place-of-supply analysis, bookkeeping and the alternative minimum-income rules. Article 5C may help only after separate approval and satisfaction of its conditions.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: General law is well supported; DNV-specific payroll and social-security treatment remains contract- and treaty-dependent.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary status is obtained through the initial national visa and subsequent residence-permit application; no multi-year qualifying wait precedes it.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The general EU long-term-resident threshold is five years, but current law does not expressly confirm whether the Article-68 digital-nomad I.8 permit is excluded as temporary status. An exact DNV-to-PR timeline therefore cannot safely be stated.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: If the applicant validly reaches a listed long-term/permanent title after five qualifying years, the ordinary seven-year residence condition would nominally leave two years. This is a conditional arithmetic illustration, not confirmation that DNV years count.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Seven years applies to holders of specified qualifying titles, while twelve years may apply to other non-temporary titles. The DNV's classification and conversion path are not officially resolved, so no reliable route-specific total is available.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Official simplified guidance states a one-year legal target but approximately two to four years in practice; 36 months is the midpoint for display, not a guarantee.

key_conditions.value: Qualifying continuous lawful residence and an eligible title at filing; adequate Greek language plus knowledge of history, geography, culture and institutions; social and economic integration; tax and insurance compliance; no disqualifying conviction, removal issue or national-security ground. Greek law does not generally require renunciation, but the applicant's existing nationality law must also be checked.
key_conditions.notes: Physical-presence continuity and the DNV title's eligibility need formal confirmation.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Three years of prior continuous lawful residence applies to a spouse of a Greek citizen who has a child with that citizen, and to a person exercising parental responsibility for a Greek child born in Greece. Marriage alone is not an automatic three-year citizenship rule.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Greek citizen can support a family-member residence card. For accelerated naturalisation, official citizenship law additionally specifies the spouse-with-child or qualifying Greek-child-parent situation; marriage to another migrant does not change the DNV settlement analysis.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A family-member route is separate from the applicant's digital-nomad route.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship is not automatic through marriage. The applicant must hold an eligible residence title, maintain lawful residence, satisfy language/knowledge and integration requirements, and avoid criminal or immigration disqualifications. Authorities may verify cohabitation and family facts; false documents or a sham marriage risk refusal, revocation and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The three-year rule should not be represented as applying to every spouse of a Greek citizen.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Greece is automatically Greek only in limited cases, including where one parent was also born in Greece and has lived there permanently since birth, or where the child would otherwise be stateless/unknown nationality. A broader route for children of migrants requires an application, Greek-school attendance and parental residence/title conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Birth in Greece alone normally does not confer citizenship. A child may acquire it through declaration/application after enrolment in the first grade of a qualifying Greek school if one parent had at least five years of continuous lawful residence before birth, or after that parent reaches ten years where the five years were not completed before birth, and the parents/title conditions are met.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Anti-statelessness and second-generation automatic-birth exceptions remain possible.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Greek mother or father acquires Greek citizenship at birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage must be legally established and registered.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A non-Greek parent of a minor Greek citizen can seek a family residence card and, where the parent exercises parental responsibility for a Greek child born in Greece, may use the three-year lawful-residence naturalisation threshold. Citizenship is never automatic for the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Residence and naturalisation remain separate applications with their own eligibility checks.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is Greek and paternity is legally established, the child is Greek from birth. The migrant father may have a family-residence route as the parent of a Greek minor and potentially the three-year naturalisation residence threshold if he exercises parental responsibility and the child was born in Greece; he does not automatically become Greek.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: If neither parent is Greek, birth alone ordinarily gives the father no immediate immigration shortcut.

rank.notes: Current Henley interactive ranking accessed on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score combines destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance, including visa-on-arrival and certain electronic travel authorities; it is not a strict visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Henley's public ranking provides an access score but not a directly captured visa-required-in-advance total for Greece.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The current Henley ranking did not provide a separately captured visa-on-arrival/eTA subtotal.

passport.notes: The Greek passport is a very strong EU passport. Rank and access scores change as destination policies are updated.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is practical for remote work and daily life in Athens, Thessaloniki and major tourism/technology centres. EF EPI 2025 ranked Greece 20th globally with a score of 592, but government processes and naturalisation require Greek.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private proficiency index based on its test-taking population, not a government census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian may be useful within particular migrant or tourism communities but are not official administrative languages. No reliable nationwide evidence was found that either can replace Greek or English for routine remote-work life.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Kept cautious because no current authoritative nationwide proficiency dataset for Russian or Ukrainian was located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the government's statement that the mean full-time wage had reached EUR 1,500 in 2026. Gross/net treatment was not explicitly stated in that speech, so this is contextual rather than a statistical-series estimate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median monthly wage in EUR was published. Eurostat's available median is a 2022 gross hourly PPS measure, not a current monthly EUR salary.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the EUR 920 statutory monthly minimum salary effective 1 April 2026. Greece normally pays this salary in 14 instalments annually; it is a legal floor, not an observed minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 1,500. The source is an official government speech describing the mean full-time wage, not an ELSTAT distribution table.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national monthly median suitable for USD conversion was established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary exists or was published in the reviewed material.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 920 per monthly payment from 1 April 2026; generally 14 payments annually
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum for full-time salaried employees.

average_salary_local_currency.value: About EUR 1,500 per month for mean full-time wage in 2026, according to the Prime Minister's June 2026 statement
average_salary_local_currency.notes: The speech does not supply the detailed statistical methodology or explicitly label the figure gross versus net.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national median monthly salary in EUR was published in the reviewed ELSTAT quarterly wage-index release. Eurostat publishes a 2022 median gross hourly earnings measure, including Greece at 9.8 PPS, but PPS per hour is neither a current EUR monthly salary nor safely convertible into one without hours and coverage assumptions, so the dashboard value remains null.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither the reviewed ELSTAT wage-index release nor Eurostat’s earnings methodology publishes a national maximum monthly salary. A maximum is open-ended and not a meaningful national wage statistic, so no amount is supplied.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory minimum monthly salary and official-government mean full-time wage context; not the DNV immigration income threshold
average_citizen_salary.period: 2026 monthly context; minimum effective 2026-04-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe Greek resident employees, not software-engineer pay and not the EUR 3,500 net DNV threshold. The minimum is a statutory floor paid through Greece's 14-payment system; the EUR 1,500 mean lacks a detailed statistical table in the cited speech.

cost_of_living_note.value: Greece's aggregate prices are generally below the EU average, but housing affordability is difficult: Eurostat reported that 29% of city residents faced housing-cost overburden, the highest reported EU city rate in its 2025 housing publication. Athens and island/tourist markets can differ substantially from the national average.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is a national/EU comparison, not a personal monthly budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Z.1 visa and two-year renewable residence permit are confirmed, but neither the EU long-term-residence eligibility of this status nor its naturalisation counting is confirmed. Do not assume that renewability makes it a settlement permit.
settlement_track.summary: Greece works well for temporary foreign-contract remote residence, but its citizenship bridge is not established. Article 68 converts Z.1 into an I.8 permit, while Articles 143-144 do not expressly resolve whether that permit is excluded as temporary status; the citizenship code also does not list it among the seven-year qualifying titles.
settlement_track.notes: A written official response or specialist legal opinion is needed on whether the post-visa digital-nomad I.8 permit counts toward Article 144 long-term residence and which Citizenship Code residence-title rule applies.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route expressly covers remote employees, freelancers and self-employed people serving employers or clients outside Greece and prohibits Greek clients/employers. This is a strong work-profile fit but not a confirmed citizenship-path fit.

data.notes: The route, current consular-entry requirement, income threshold, temporary-residence stages, tax rules and citizenship-title restrictions are well supported. Overall confidence is medium because the decisive issue—whether the digital-nomad I.8 permit is qualifying residence for long-term status or naturalisation—remains unresolved after focused review of current migration law, citizenship law, official guidance and secondary legal analysis.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Digital-nomad Z.1 followed by the Article-68 sufficient-resources residence sequence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A renewable residence sequence exists after the digital-nomad visa, but this review could not establish that the exact nomad-derived status qualifies for long-term residence or identify a verified ordinary-remote-worker PR successor.
requirements: Resolve with the Migration Ministry whether the nomad-derived permit falls within the temporary-status exclusion from EU long-term residence.
If it does, qualify separately for a residence category that admits long-term settlement.
reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad Visa (Z.1) followed by digital-nomad residence permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Official 2023 Migration Code Articles 143–144 establish the five-year regime and exclude temporary residence statuses. The 2026 amending law was inspected, but did not resolve classification of the exact nomad-to-I.8 sequence. A foreign income stream and an available general five-year rule are not enough to mark this confirmed. No categorical prohibition is inferred.

data.selection_summary: Grenada does not currently offer a dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. A foreign national may obtain a one-year work permit, including as a self-employed person, but the official framework regulates work in Grenada, requires local business, tax and NIS documentation, and does not confirm that foreign-client remote work qualifies or that the permit enters the advertised work-to-residency pathway. Visitor status prohibits work, while citizenship by investment is outside this profile.

visa_application.title: Requirements for Processing Grenada Visa Applications Prior to Arrival
visa_application.notes: Official embassy visa-information page with a downloadable form, not an online residence or remote-worker portal. It expressly says a visa does not authorize work without Ministry of Labour permission.

rejected_routes.route_name: Individual or self-employed foreign-national work permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official requirements publish no numerical minimum-income threshold. Applicants instead submit evidence of sufficient finance, and self-employed applicants need local incorporation, tax and NIS documentation.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current official work-permit requirements specify sufficient funds rather than a fixed XCD threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; sufficient funds and local business-compliance evidence required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Proof of finance plus business incorporation, tax status and NIS registration
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a foreign-income digital-nomad test.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank statement is required, but the official page does not specify how many months it must cover.

key_requirements.requirement: Individual work permits authorize a named foreign national to engage in a specified occupation; the official guide separately recognizes self-employment.
Passport, photographs, original police clearance, notarized qualifications, two professional references and proof of sufficient finance.
Business incorporation, Inland Revenue tax-obligation status and NIS registration or compliance.
Approval is discretionary and tied to a specified occupation, industry or profession.
After work-permit approval, the applicant must separately obtain the appropriate entry visa from Immigration and Passport.

initial_validity.value: 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The official guide states that work permits are granted for one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is required; the guide describes renewal as continuing with the same employer and occupation, and the Labour page requires filing three months before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: How the same-employer rule applies to a self-employed permit should be verified with the Work Permit Unit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence grant. The work permit authorizes work, after which Immigration issues an appropriate time-limited entry visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The official sources do not equate the work-permit card with temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The guide describes a skilled Work to Residency category but does not confirm that a self-employed foreign-client software engineer qualifies or publish the conversion conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A permanent-residence form exists, but its official view page is login-gated and did not expose eligibility or qualifying-period rules.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path from this permit was confirmed. General naturalisation separately requires good character, adequate English, continuous residence for the final 12 months and at least five aggregate years of residence or government service during the preceding seven years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The law does not establish that every work-permit or entry-visa period counts as residence for naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest independently initiated option, but it is not an ordinary remote-worker route. It requires a locally incorporated and compliant business and regulates specified work in Grenada. Foreign-client remote software work and access to Work to Residency remain unconfirmed.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: A remote-worker income threshold is inapplicable because visitor status does not authorize work.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A remote-worker income threshold is inapplicable because visitor status does not authorize work.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold; visitor status does not authorize work
income_requirement_display.notes: Evidence of visitor funds is not a residence-route income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The official visitor-visa page does not prescribe a standardized income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Visa need and permitted visit length depend on nationality.
Passport generally must remain valid at least six months beyond departure.
Visa holders may not work without Ministry of Labour permission.
Travellers complete the online immigration and customs form within 72 hours before arrival.

initial_validity.value: Specified on the visa or entry permission
initial_validity.notes: No single duration applies to every nationality.

extension_rules.notes: The official visa page reviewed does not publish an extension rule that authorizes remote work.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Visitor permission is not temporary residence and creates no confirmed residence conversion.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No visitor-to-permanent-residence conversion right is published.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate permanent-residence form exists, but that does not create a conversion entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor status provides no confirmed citizenship path or qualifying-residence credit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status expressly does not authorize work and has no confirmed settlement conversion.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route uses a capital contribution or approved-project investment rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A monthly-income test is inapplicable to this capital-based route.

income_requirement_display.value: Minimum contribution advertised from USD 150,000; investment route excluded
income_requirement_display.notes: This is one-time capital, not income.

income_proof_months.notes: An income-history period is inapplicable to this investment route.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must use either a National Transformation Fund contribution or approved-project real-estate investment.
Applications are submitted through authorized agents.
Personal eligibility and due-diligence requirements apply.

initial_validity.value: Citizenship after approval
initial_validity.notes: The official site advertises processing in approximately three to four months.

extension_rules.value: Not applicable to citizenship

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not required

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct citizenship rather than a residence progression

path_to_citizenship.value: Direct citizenship through contribution or approved investment and due diligence
path_to_citizenship.notes: Excluded because substantial investment and authorized-agent filing are outside the applicant profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Excluded by the research criteria because it requires substantial capital investment and authorized-agent submission.

summary.value: The work-permit framework has a skilled Work to Residency category for skills in demand, and qualifications are assessed, but the guide is oriented to Grenadian labour-market needs and does not establish an independently selectable degree-based residence route for a foreign-client software engineer.
summary.notes: A relevant degree strengthens a work-permit application but does not itself confer residence or eliminate work and immigration approval.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is tax resident after spending more than 183 days in Grenada in a year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and tie-breaker rules may modify the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For a self-employed contributor, the 2026 NIS rate is 13.5% of insurable earnings. Employees contribute 6.25% and employers 7.25%.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: NIS is percentage-based. At the XCD 5,200 monthly insurable-earnings ceiling, 13.5% is XCD 702, approximately USD 260 monthly for a self-employed contributor.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad regime was identified. Grenada operates a territorial income-tax system; foreign-source income is generally outside Grenadian income tax, but the source of services physically performed from Grenada requires professional determination.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign clients or foreign payment accounts do not by themselves establish foreign-source income.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on source characterization, days present, employment versus self-employment, local registration, VAT and annual stamp-tax exposure, NIS coverage, treaty position and foreign-country rules. Lack of an eligible immigration route does not remove tax obligations.

taxation_system.value: Territorial, progressive personal income tax on Grenada-source income: exempt through XCD 36,000 annually, 10% from XCD 36,000 to XCD 60,000, and 28% above XCD 60,000.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in Grenada during the year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Grenada-source income, including gains or profits from business, employment, fees and commissions arising from sources in Grenada. Foreign-source income is generally exempt, subject to source classification.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No current digital-nomad or ordinary inbound-remote-worker tax holiday was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: 2026 NIS total is 13.5% of insurable earnings up to XCD 5,200 monthly: 6.25% employee plus 7.25% employer, or 13.5% for self-employed contributors. Non-nationals working in Grenada are included.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 28% is the top marginal screening rate. It applies only above XCD 60,000 annual income and is not the effective rate on total income.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses XCD 2.70 per USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual income over XCD 36,000 through XCD 60,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal personal income in this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal personal income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: The OECD review consolidates statutory rates and confirms territorial taxation; IRD material confirms the XCD 3,000 monthly liability threshold. Source characterization for foreign remote services remains filing-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Grenada has no confirmed digital-nomad status or special nomad tax regime. If a person instead obtains a self-employed work permit, ordinary territorial income tax, NIS, business registration, annual stamp tax and possibly VAT apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated route; ordinary self-employed or employee rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Territorial PIT, top marginal rate 28% on annual income above XCD 60,000
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Tax residence after more than 183 days in Grenada per year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-source income is generally exempt, but services physically performed in Grenada may be Grenada-source; no official remote-worker ruling was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the current official and OECD sources reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Self-employed persons, including non-nationals, generally pay 13.5% NIS on insurable earnings up to XCD 5,200 monthly. Employee payroll uses 6.25% employee and 7.25% employer shares.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed nomad payment; ordinary variable taxes and contributions apply
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: 13.5% for self-employed persons, capped at the XCD 5,200 monthly insurable-earnings ceiling; maximum approximately XCD 702 or USD 260 monthly.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Work-permit application fee XCD 100; nationality-based work-permit fees shown by Labour range from XCD 1,000 to XCD 5,000.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Annual stamp tax applies to gross business receipts above XCD 36,000 at 0.5% through XCD 300,000 and 0.70% above XCD 300,000. VAT registration threshold is XCD 300,000 annual taxable supplies.
fixed_payments.notes: Confirm fees and registrations with Labour, Immigration and IRD before filing.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Spending 183 days or fewer avoids residence under the published day test, but Grenada-source work or business income may still be taxable and visitor status does not authorize work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: After more than 183 days, ordinary territorial rules apply. Foreign-client service income should not be assumed foreign-source without an IRD determination.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local incorporation, tax status and NIS registration are requested for self-employed work permits; PIT, 13.5% self-employed NIS, annual stamp tax and potentially VAT can apply.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Screening analysis for a rejected route, not confirmation of permit eligibility or final tax treatment.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying remote-worker route grants temporary residence. A one-year work permit requires separate immigration permission and is not expressly identified as residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: A permanent-residence form exists, but its current eligibility, qualifying period and treatment of work-permit time are not published on the accessible official pages.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Citizenship Act uses residence and government-service tests rather than a fixed number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be assigned from the rejected work-permit route. General naturalisation contemplates continuous residence for the final 12 months plus at least five aggregate years in the preceding seven, but qualifying residence from this route is unconfirmed and approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The accessible official sources publish no typical processing time for ordinary naturalisation. The CBI programme's three-to-four-month estimate is inapplicable.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires full age and capacity, good character, adequate English, continuous residence during the final 12 months, at least five aggregate years of residence or government service during the preceding seven, intent to reside or serve the Government, and an oath of allegiance. Ministerial discretion applies.
key_conditions.notes: The reviewed Act does not specify a language-test format, general absence allowance, tax-compliance checklist or mandatory renunciation rule.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A spouse of a citizen may apply for registration without a stated minimum marriage or residence duration. Citizenship is not automatic on marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A current spouse of a Grenadian citizen may apply for citizenship by registration. The Constitution also covers a person who had been married to someone who was a Grenadian citizen during the marriage, subject to the prescribed process.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marriage must be legally documented.

requirements_and_risks.value: Official instructions require an application, reference letter, bank statement, police certificate, certified photographs, birth and marriage certificates, medical documentation, proof of the spouse's Grenadian citizenship and the spouse's concurrence. An alien must take the oath of allegiance. False or sham documentation can result in refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The instruction sheet reflects older administrative instructions; current fees and medical requirements should be reconfirmed with Home Affairs.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship at birth to every person born in Grenada, subject only to narrow diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Grenada is normally a citizen at birth even when both parents are migrants, subject to the narrow constitutional exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' visitor, temporary or permanent status is generally irrelevant to the ordinary constitutional birth grant.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Grenada is a citizen by birth. A child born abroad is also a citizen at birth when either parent is a Grenadian citizen otherwise than solely by descent under the specified constitutional provisions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: For overseas birth, the citizen parent's manner of acquiring citizenship can matter.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Grenadian citizen child does not automatically make a migrant parent a resident, permanent resident or citizen. The accessible current official sources publish no parent-of-citizen residence entitlement.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A parent needs an independent immigration basis or a discretionary option confirmed by Home Affairs.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically obtain residence or citizenship because his child is Grenadian. The reviewed law and official forms publish no accelerated father-specific route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Any discretionary family benefit requires direct confirmation.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 37 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations. eVisa destinations are listed separately.

passport.notes: The index displayed a mobility score of 139 and separately classified visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, eVisa and visa-required access.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for daily life and business communication because English is the official language. Work-permit documents must be submitted in English.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: French patois is listed as a major language but not as an official language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low as a standalone language. Current official information does not indicate broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services; English should be expected for government, legal and business dealings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Inference from official-language information, not a measured proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The newest publicly listed detailed official salary release, 2025 Q2, reports grouped gross-monthly-salary counts rather than an arithmetic mean. The World Bank methods paper explains that Grenada LFS income is interval-censored. No exact current mean or USD equivalent was inferred from midpoint assumptions or third-party estimates.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: For 2025 Q2, 34,171 of 51,159 employed respondents stated a salary. Their median lies in the XCD 1,200–1,999 monthly band, but an exact amount and USD equivalent cannot be recovered; 33.2% of all employed respondents did not state salary.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the XCD 1,200 monthly basic statutory minimum using XCD 2.70 per USD. Some occupations use hourly, daily or higher rates.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No exact current official national arithmetic mean is published. The LFS gives bands, including an open-ended XCD 6,000+ category, so calculating a mean would require unsupported distribution assumptions.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The median among stated 2025 Q2 responses falls within XCD 1,200–1,999 gross monthly, but no exact amount exists to convert to USD.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The highest published category is open-ended at XCD 6,000+ gross monthly, so it supplies neither a finite maximum nor a value that can be converted to USD.

min_salary_local_currency.value: Basic statutory minimum XCD 1,200/month or XCD 60/day from 1 January 2024; occupation-specific schedules also apply
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.value: The official 2025 Q2 table does not publish a national arithmetic mean; it provides grouped gross-monthly-salary counts, and 33.2% of employed respondents are recorded as salary not stated.
average_salary_local_currency.notes: A mean cannot be calculated exactly from interval-censored bands, particularly the open-ended XCD 6,000+ band. Current third-party figures reviewed were estimates or small-sample user submissions and were not substituted for an official statistic.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Median of stated 2025 Q2 responses: within XCD 1,200–1,999 gross per month; the exact median is not published or recoverable from the grouped table.
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Of 51,159 employed respondents, 16,988 did not state salary. Among the 34,171 stated responses, the cumulative grouped count crosses the midpoint inside the XCD 1,200–1,999 band. This is a band classification, not an exact median.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite national maximum is published; the official 2025 Q2 distribution ends with an open-ended XCD 6,000+ gross-per-month band.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: XCD 6,000 is the lower boundary of the top survey category, not the maximum salary or highest observed value. Multiple quarterly releases use the same open-ended structure.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory occupation-based minimum wage plus official grouped gross-monthly-salary distribution for employed persons
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 2024; newest publicly listed detailed salary distribution 2025 Q2
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe worker wages, not an immigration threshold. The survey does not identify citizenship, so it covers employed respondents rather than citizens only. Exact mean, median amount and maximum remain unavailable because earnings are published in bands, the upper band is open-ended and non-response is substantial.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The current official CSO publications reviewed do not provide a current standardized cost-of-living basket suitable for a comparable monthly household-budget figure, so no crowdsourced estimate is used.
