settlement_track.summary: Grenada recognizes self-employed work permits and advertises a separate skilled Work to Residency category, but official rules do not confirm that ordinary foreign-client remote work qualifies or that a self-employed permit enters that settlement path. Visitor status prohibits work, so no qualifying citizenship-oriented route is established for this profile.
settlement_track.notes: A filing-level opinion from the Work Permit Unit and Home Affairs is needed before treating locally incorporated self-employment as a potential conversion route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker status exists. The self-employed work permit regulates a specified occupation in Grenada and requires local business compliance; foreign-client remote software work is not expressly accepted.

data.notes: The negative selection result remains supported by current official visa and work-permit materials. This focused pass audited the flagged salary fields against the newest publicly listed detailed LFS tables through 2025 Q2, multiple earlier quarterly tables, current CSO publication listings and World Bank methodological evidence. No exact national arithmetic mean, exact median amount or finite maximum is published.

data.selection_summary: Guatemala now has a current, ordinary temporary-residence route expressly covering migrant workers with a foreign employer. The 2026 official form requires at least USD 2,000 per month from abroad, received throughout the previous year (USD 3,000 with dependants), and permits a personal application without a Guatemalan employer. It is qualifying temporary residence rather than visitor or digital-nomad status: after five continuous years the resident can apply for permanent residence, and ordinary naturalization generally requires a further five years as a permanently resident foreigner domiciled in Guatemala. Separate work-permit, tax, and possibly insurance requirements must be confirmed before filing.

visa_application.title: SICOE Web — solicitudes de residencias y visas guatemaltecas
visa_application.notes: SICOE is IGM's online application interface and lists temporary residence for migrant workers. The current 2026 form and supporting documents must subsequently be filed personally with the Subdirección de Extranjería.

best_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for migrant workers — foreign-employer branch

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official 2026 form requires foreign remuneration of at least USD 2,000 monthly, increasing to USD 3,000 when accompanied by dependants.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Threshold officially denominated in USD: USD 2,000 per month, or USD 3,000 with dependants
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: IGM does not state an equivalent quetzal amount.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 2,000/month from abroad for the preceding 12 months; USD 3,000/month with dependants
income_requirement_display.notes: Bank statements or a properly legalized/apostilled certification from a public accountant may establish the income.

income_proof_months.notes: The initial and extension forms require proof that the qualifying foreign remuneration was received throughout the previous year.

key_requirements.requirement: File the current residence form personally with a valid passport and legalized full copy, last-entry migration certificate, payment receipt, and foreign criminal or police record; foreign documents generally require apostille/legalization and Spanish translation.
Provide bank statements showing at least USD 2,000 every month during the preceding year, or USD 3,000 with dependants; an apostilled/legalized accountant certification is an alternative.

IGM's route summary says the Ministry of Labor work permit is a separate mandatory procedure. Filing-level confirmation is needed regarding how that permit applies to a foreign employer with no Guatemalan entity.

International medical insurance is listed by IGM's summary for the foreign-employer branch, while the detailed 2026 form expressly mentions insurance only for the international-NGO/international-organization exception; applicants should obtain written IGM confirmation.

Temporary residents must maintain tax compliance and update their migratory registration; the current extension form requires Guatemalan police and criminal records, DPI, and an application 30 days before expiry.

initial_validity.value: Applicant may request 1 year, 2 years, or 3–5 years; approval is discretionary within a maximum five-year temporary-residence period.
initial_validity.notes: Published state fees are USD 200 for one year, USD 300 for two years, or USD 500 for three to five years, plus the USD 25 application fee.

extension_rules.value: An extension must be filed approximately 30 days before expiry. The foreign-employer worker must again demonstrate qualifying foreign remuneration received during the previous year. Residence beyond five continuous years normally requires conversion to permanent residence.
extension_rules.notes: The extension form offers requested periods of one to four years, subject to the overall temporary-residence rules.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct qualifying temporary residence is available through the migrant-worker category's foreign-employer branch.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is ordinary residence, not a tourist permission or digital-nomad label.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply for permanent residence after maintaining temporary-resident status continuously for at least five years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The permanent-residence file requires proof of five years, a sworn declaration and proof of the applicant's activity, and an updated guarantor certificate unless exempt.

path_to_citizenship.value: After conversion to permanent residence and registration as an extranjero domiciliado, ordinary naturalization can be requested after at least five additional years in that domiciled status, subject to absence limits, Spanish/civics examinations, good record, livelihood proof, witnesses, presidential discretion, and the required renunciation oath.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The credible ordinary timeline is therefore about ten years from initial temporary residence, not five years total.

best_routes.notes: This route is a strong ordinary foreign-contract remote-work match even though Guatemala does not call it a digital-nomad visa. Current primary sources expressly include a foreign employer, require no Guatemalan employer or local-client contract, and create qualifying temporary residence. The main filing risk is the separate Ministry of Labor permit and inconsistent insurance wording, which should be clarified with IGM before committing funds.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold is published because this is only an entry or visitor status.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Economic solvency may be checked at entry, but IGM publishes no fixed amount for this purpose.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold published; visitor status is not a remote-work residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: A tourist extension does not substitute for qualifying residence.

income_proof_months.notes: The official entry page does not specify a fixed income-history period for visitor admission.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid travel document and any visa required for the traveller's nationality; admission may involve proof of solvency and accommodation.

initial_validity.value: Normally a short visitor admission, commonly up to 90 days depending on nationality and admission decision.
initial_validity.notes: Exact admission is determined at the border.

extension_rules.value: A tourist extension may be requested, but it remains visitor status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence rights; the person must separately qualify and file under a residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Visitor status itself does not establish the five years of temporary residence required for the ordinary permanent-residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time should not be treated as qualifying domiciled residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an ordinary visitor or tourist extension is not qualifying residence and does not independently authorize a settlement track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permanent residence for rentistas or pensionados

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: USD 1,250 in stable, permanent foreign income for the principal plus USD 300 for each dependant.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 1,250/month plus USD 300/dependant
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: IGM publishes the requirement in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 1,250/month permanent passive income + USD 300/dependant
income_requirement_display.notes: Ordinary salary or short-term client income is not safely equivalent to permanent rentista or pension income.

income_proof_months.notes: The official summary requires permanent income but does not state a bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Demonstrate stable and permanent income from abroad and re-establish its continuity every five years.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence
initial_validity.notes: Published one-time residence fee is USD 400.

extension_rules.value: Income continuity must be demonstrated every five years, and permanent residents pay an annual foreigner fee.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not required; this category grants permanent residence directly.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence for a qualifying rentista or pensionado.

path_to_citizenship.value: Permanent residence can establish domiciled status for ordinary naturalization if all naturalization conditions are met.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because the official category requires stable permanent passive/rent or pension income, not ordinary software-engineering compensation from a foreign contract.

summary.value: A foreign student admitted to a recognized Guatemalan educational institution can obtain temporary student residence without an employer, based on enrollment and financial support. It is not a degree-based skilled migration route and is unnecessary for the applicant's existing foreign-contract profile; official material does not establish direct permanent residence solely from the degree.
summary.notes: Student residence may be extended for the duration of studies, but it should not be substituted for the directly fitting foreign-employer worker residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreign individual is generally resident when present in Guatemala for more than 183 days during the calendar year; the statute also contains economic-interest/residence tests. PwC additionally identifies a fixed place of business in Guatemala as a residence indicator.
tax_residency_rule.notes: PwC's English page contains an apparent mistranslation saying 'not exceeding' 183 days; the Spanish tax statute uses more than 183 days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal resident employment-income rate, not the expected effective rate. The resident employment brackets are 5% through GTQ 300,000 taxable income annually, then GTQ 15,000 plus 7% of the excess.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Published employee social-security rate; the employer rate is 12.67%. Whether and how Guatemalan payroll contributions attach to a worker retained directly by a foreign entity requires advice on the contract and work-permit structure.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly immigration payment applies. Residence charges are application or period fees. IGSS voluntary continuation is 5.5% of a prior compulsory-contribution salary and is not a flat contribution available to every new foreign freelancer.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad or inbound-worker exemption was identified in the current SAT law and guidance reviewed. A self-employed person may potentially use an applicable business-income regime after SAT registration, including the optional simplified 5%/7% gross-income regime, but classification must be confirmed.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Do not assume foreign payment makes services performed physically in Guatemala foreign-source.

taxes.caveats: Tax residence and source are separate issues. Compensation for services performed in Guatemala may be Guatemalan-source even before the worker becomes tax resident and even if payment remains abroad. The appropriate employment, professional-services, VAT, invoicing, withholding, and social-security treatment depends on the actual contract and registration; obtain Guatemalan tax and labor advice.

taxation_system.value: Source-based system with progressive resident employment taxation and separate rates/regimes for non-residents and business or professional income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in the calendar year, with additional statutory economic-interest/residence tests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Guatemalan-source income. Services physically performed in Guatemala can be Guatemalan-source regardless of where the payer is located or payment is made.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad exemption identified. Optional simplified business-income taxation may apply to properly registered independent activity but is not automatic for a foreign employee.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees 4.83% and employers 12.67% of monthly payroll under the general published rates; direct foreign-employer applicability requires filing-specific review.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 7% is the top marginal resident employment rate. It is not an effective rate. Non-resident Guatemalan-source salary is reported separately at 10% withholding, and professional fees can follow different rules.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses about GTQ 7.66 per USD solely for display.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over GTQ 300,000 annual taxable employment income; GTQ 15,000 plus 7% of the excess
tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident employment income above the first bracket
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not the rate on all income.

taxation_system.notes: Primary SAT law was used for the 183-day rule; PwC's Guatemala summary, reviewed 9 June 2026, supplies the current bracket, income-source, and social-security presentation.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: There is no separate digital-nomad tax regime in the current sources reviewed. A resident foreign-employer worker is screened under ordinary Guatemalan-source employment rules at 5%/7%; before residence, services performed in Guatemala may still be taxable at the applicable non-resident rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary foreign-employer migrant-worker residence; not a digital-nomad tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Resident employment: 5% up to GTQ 300,000 taxable income and 7% above; non-resident Guatemalan-source salary: 10% withholding
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days during the calendar year, with additional statutory residence/economic-interest tests.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Guatemala is source-based, but remote services physically performed from Guatemala can be Guatemalan-source even when the employer and bank account are foreign. Foreign investment income is treated differently from remuneration for locally performed services.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No separate regime is stated in the current SAT law and guidance reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: General published payroll rates are 4.83% employee and 12.67% employer. Application to a direct foreign employer and responsibility for withholding require contract-specific advice.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment applies under the current immigration tariff and IGSS voluntary-continuation rules reviewed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No flat mandatory self-employed payment was established. IGSS voluntary continuation is 5.5% of the last compulsory-contribution salary and is limited by eligibility conditions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: USD 25 application fee plus USD 200 for one year, USD 300 for two years, or USD 500 for three-to-five-year temporary residence. Permanent residence after five years costs USD 700 under the published tariff; permanent residents also have a USD 40 annual foreigner fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT is generally 12% on non-personal services rendered or effected in Guatemala. Whether exported software services qualify for different treatment and which invoicing regime applies must be confirmed with SAT.
fixed_payments.notes: Translation, apostille/legalization, criminal-record, accountant-certification, medical-insurance, work-permit, DPI, and professional-service costs are variable rather than fixed state charges.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Do not assume zero Guatemalan tax. Non-residents can be taxed on salary or professional services sourced to work physically performed in Guatemala; PwC reports 10% withholding for non-resident Guatemalan-source salary.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary resident employment brackets of 5% and 7% are the starting screen, subject to deductions, withholding mechanics, and the actual characterization of the foreign contract.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The separate worker-residence branch for own-account activity requires an RTU and authorization to conduct commercial activity. A registered independent professional may face ISR, FEL invoicing and potentially VAT obligations; the optional simplified ISR regime applies 5% through GTQ 30,000 of monthly gross income and 7% above, if that regime is validly selected.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The immigration route is clear, but foreign-employer payroll, work-permit and withholding implementation should be confirmed with Guatemalan advisers before filing.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The qualifying route directly grants temporary residence once approved; there is no preliminary multi-year status.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five continuous years of temporary-resident status must be documented.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: MINEX requires at least five years as an extranjero domiciliado, a status that presupposes permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Approximately five years temporary residence plus five years as a permanent resident/foreign domiciliary before application. Processing time is additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official ordinary-naturalization materials reviewed do not publish a processing-time estimate. The government portal's 3–6 month estimate concerns the separate procedure for a foreign woman married to a Guatemalan and cannot be generalized.

key_conditions.value: Continuous qualifying residence; permanent-resident and extranjero-domiciliado registration; during the five domiciled years no absence longer than six consecutive months and aggregate absences under one year; personal application; Spanish and civics examinations; Guatemalan and relevant foreign criminal/police records; lawful livelihood; three witnesses; executive approval; publication and a renunciation/loyalty oath.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and the oath may affect retention of another nationality; obtain advice concerning the applicant's current nationality.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: At least one year of registered marriage or declared union with a Guatemalan creates a direct permanent-residence category.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage matters only if the spouse is Guatemalan and the marriage or declared union has been registered for at least one year. Marriage between two migrants does not create this benefit. Guatemala also has a special naturalization procedure for a foreign woman married to a Guatemalan; equivalent acceleration for a foreign husband is not established on the current government portal.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The gender-specific citizenship provision is legally sensitive and should be checked directly with MINEX for the applicant's sex and circumstances.

requirements_and_risks.value: For permanent residence, provide current RENAP marriage/union and Guatemalan spouse birth certificates plus the general residence file. The relationship and documents are verified. False statements, sham marriage, or a marriage entered only to evade immigration rules can cause refusal, cancellation and legal consequences. Marriage does not automatically naturalize the spouse.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The government portal estimates 3–6 months only for the special married-woman naturalization service, not ordinary naturalization or permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants Guatemalan nationality of origin to people born in Guatemala, with the narrow exception of children of diplomatic officials and legally equivalent officials. It also recognizes descent through a Guatemalan father or mother.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Guatemala to two migrant parents is generally Guatemalan from birth, regardless of their temporary, permanent, or visitor status, unless the narrow diplomatic-official exception applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth registration with RENAP remains necessary to document the status.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Guatemalan by birth if born in Guatemala and also has a constitutional descent basis through either a Guatemalan mother or father, including when born abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Guatemalan child can create a direct permanent-residence basis for a foreign parent as a qualifying family member of a Guatemalan, but the parent does not automatically become a citizen.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must document the legal relationship and satisfy the residence filing requirements.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Guatemalan child can potentially apply for permanent residence through the official family-link category. Citizenship remains a separate naturalization process with its own residence, examination, record, livelihood and discretionary-approval requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and the child's Guatemalan registration must be documented; the child's citizenship alone does not confer the father's citizenship.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change dynamically.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category, separate from visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Value displayed by Passport Index; its detailed country list also distinguishes electronic visas and other pre-travel permissions.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 44 visa-on-arrival destinations and 8 eTA destinations as separately displayed by Passport Index.

passport.notes: The mobility score was 130, comprising 78 visa-free, 44 visa-on-arrival and 8 eTA destinations. This source's methodology differs from Henley, so these numbers should not be mixed with a Henley-based rank.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only remote work is workable within an international employer and in selected business or tourist areas, but Spanish is the official language and will be important for immigration, tax, banking, housing and everyday administration. EF EPI 2025 gives Guatemala a score of 510 and global rank 61, with an IT-function score of 531.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected proficiency dataset rather than a population census; it supports only a general practicality assessment.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian should not be expected to work for government filings or ordinary daily life. The official sources reviewed provide no Russian- or Ukrainian-language service commitment; Spanish ability or a Spanish-speaking representative is advisable.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from Spanish being the constitutional official language, not a claim that no Russian or Ukrainian speakers live in Guatemala.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest official Q4-2025 average monthly labor income of GTQ 2,842 at about GTQ 7.66 per USD. This is average labor income of occupied persons, not an immigration threshold.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The latest official publications checked report arithmetic means and confidence intervals, not a national median; the INE portal provides microdata but no published weighted-median statistic.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the lowest 2026 statutory total monthly minimum identified: GTQ 3,471.10 for export/maquila work outside the Department of Guatemala, including the GTQ 250 incentive bonus. This is a legal wage floor, not an observed minimum income.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest official Q4-2025 national mean of GTQ 2,842. The average can be below formal minimum wages because ENEIC covers occupied persons across a labor market with extensive informality.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: INE’s latest 2025 bulletin publishes quarterly national mean labor income (GTQ 2,842 in Q4) and confidence intervals, while the current results presentation, earlier official report, and publication portal likewise provide no official national median. A median was therefore not inferred from the mean or recomputed from raw microdata without a documented weighting procedure.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: INE’s current national labor-income publications do not publish a maximum. A population salary maximum is not a bounded statutory measure, and neither the highest subgroup mean nor the upper confidence limit is an individual maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: GTQ 3,471.10/month total statutory minimum for 2026 export/maquila work in CE2, including GTQ 250 incentive bonus
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Other sectors and the Department of Guatemala have higher minimums.

average_salary_local_currency.value: GTQ 2,842/month average labor income in Q4 2025
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official national ENEIC estimate for occupied persons; the Q4 confidence interval is GTQ 2,803–2,881.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: INE’s latest 2025 bulletin publishes quarterly arithmetic mean labor income and confidence intervals, not the national median. The current results presentation, 2024 report, earlier 2025 bulletin, and ENEIC publication portal were also checked and do not publish a weighted national median, so no GTQ value can be reported without independently processing the survey microdata under INE’s weighting methodology.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The named official ENEIC publications report national and subgroup means plus confidence intervals but no maximum individual monthly labor income or upper endpoint of a national wage distribution. Because salaries are not capped and a sample maximum would be survey-specific and sensitive to outliers, neither a subgroup mean nor a confidence-bound endpoint is a valid national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly labor income of occupied persons; minimum field is the 2026 statutory sectoral wage floor including incentive bonus
average_citizen_salary.period: ENEIC Q4 2025 labor income and statutory minimum wages effective 1 January–31 December 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The latest official national mean is GTQ 2,842 for Q4 2025. INE does not publish a national median or maximum in the current summary products checked; those fields remain null with precise methodological explanations. Approximate USD conversion uses about GTQ 7.66 per USD and is rounded.

cost_of_living_note.value: INE's January 2026 expanded-basket estimate was GTQ 2,237.85 per urban person per month and GTQ 1,403.97 per rural person; the food-only baskets were GTQ 924.35 urban and GTQ 713.40 rural. These are statistical basket measures, not a complete expatriate or household budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Actual costs vary substantially by city, household size, housing standard, health insurance and imported consumption.

settlement_track.summary: The foreign-employer worker category is qualifying temporary residence and fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Five continuous temporary-residence years permit conversion to permanent residence; naturalization then generally requires five years as a permanent resident/foreign domiciliary, making the route a credible roughly ten-year citizenship track.
settlement_track.notes: The absence of a digital-nomad label does not invalidate an official foreign-employer residence route, while the citizenship estimate must include both the five-year temporary-residence stage and the subsequent five-year domiciled stage.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The current official category expressly accepts a foreign employer and foreign remuneration without a Guatemalan employer or local-client contract. The applicant must formalize residence and clarify the separate work-permit and insurance requirements.

data.notes: The core route, income history, temporary residence, five-year permanent-residence bridge, and ordinary naturalization prerequisites are supported by current primary sources. The focused wage pass inspected current and historical INE publications plus its data portal; they publish means but no national median or maximum. Confidence is not high because foreign-employer work-permit implementation, insurance wording, payroll treatment, and ordinary naturalization processing time still require filing-level confirmation.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Temporary residence for migrant workers with a foreign employer
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The foreign-employer route is ordinary temporary residence and can support PR after at least five years as a temporary resident.
requirements: Evidence foreign remuneration of at least USD 2,000/month, or USD 3,000 with dependants, over the previous year under the foreign-employer branch.
Maintain and renew temporary residence and complete required annual updates.
At PR filing, prove five years of temporary residence, current activity, criminal clearance and the required guarantor documentation.
reviewed_route_names: Temporary residence for migrant workers — foreign-employer branch
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: This is a remote-worker branch of ordinary migrant-worker residence, not a separately named digital-nomad visa. The 2026 worker PDF failed direct opening, but the current IGM portal and its 2025 residence regulation were accessible. Articles 11–12 explicitly cover foreign employers; the 2026 PR checklist proves the five-year route.

data.selection_summary: Guinea has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. The foreigners rules contemplate temporary residence for an authorized professional activity, but the official materials do not establish that a foreign software contract alone qualifies for the required professional authorization. Enterprise registration does not confer immigration permission, while the documented employee route requires a Guinean employer and work-permit sponsorship.

visa_application.title: Guinea Visa — ETA Electronic Travel Authorisation of Guinea
visa_application.notes: The official portal is the general online visa starting point, but it offers no dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category. France Diplomatie confirmed in June 2026 that visa applications are initiated through this DCPAF portal.

rejected_routes.route_name: Long-stay visa and temporary residence for an authorized liberal or economic activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Neither source publishes a numerical monthly threshold. Short-stay entrants must demonstrate sufficient subsistence and return means; professional residence instead depends on authorization for the proposed activity.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed GNF income threshold is published for this category.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; sufficient means and prior professional authorization apply
income_requirement_display.notes: The decisive unresolved issue is authorization to perform the activity, not a foreign-income test.

income_proof_months.notes: The portal does not prescribe a bank-statement or income-history period for this category.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport valid for at least six months, return travel evidence, yellow-fever certificate, accommodation or invitation evidence, and repatriation guarantee.
Authorization from the competent authority to practise the proposed liberal, commercial, industrial, agricultural, artistic, or other regulated activity.
A foreigner staying beyond three months must obtain the applicable residence card; professional activity subject to authorization requires proof that authorization was granted.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence card: up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The card cannot outlast the supporting visa or documents.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is legally available. The applicant must provide a valid passport or identity document, a criminal-record extract issued within the preceding 3 months where available, and a medical certificate issued within the preceding 2 months; documents must be translated into French and consularly authenticated where applicable. The renewed temporary card still cannot exceed 1 year or the validity of its supporting documents.
extension_rules.notes: The law supplies the renewal evidence and duration limits, but the ministry page does not publish a current form, filing window, fee, or service standard.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The foreigners rules recognize a temporary card for a person temporarily exercising an authorized professional activity. The applicant must first obtain the required professional authorization and long-stay permission.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No current official filing guide confirms approval solely on the basis of ordinary foreign-client software work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least 3 years of uninterrupted lawful residence, a foreigner may request a five-year resident card. Approval considers means of support, professional activity, and intention to settle and is not automatic for this category.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time and unauthorized remote work should not be assumed to qualify.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after 5 years of habitual residence, but it is discretionary, granted by decree after investigation, and presupposes lawful residence and assimilation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant cannot use this path without first securing a lawful qualifying residence basis.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because no official source establishes that an ordinary foreign software contract satisfies the competent-authority authorization requirement. Independent application availability therefore remains filing-dependent rather than confirmed.

rejected_routes.route_name: Individual-enterprise registration followed by residence legalization

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Enterprise formation has no immigration income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum capital is stated for an individual enterprise; that company-law rule is not an immigration concession.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration income threshold; stated individual-enterprise registration cost is GNF 212,500
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a formation charge, not a residence fee or monthly-income requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: APIP does not require or publish an immigration income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Biometric identity card or passport, photographs, residence certificate, and prior sector authorization where applicable.
RCCM registration and issuance of a tax identification number through APIP's one-stop shop.
Separate immigration permission and any required professional authorization remain necessary.

initial_validity.notes: Enterprise registration is not a residence status and consequently has no immigration validity period.

extension_rules.notes: There is no residence status to extend: APIP registration creates a business and tax record, while any visa or residence card must be obtained and renewed under the separate foreigners rules.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path. The entrepreneur must separately qualify for a visa, professional authorization, and residence card.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The residence-certificate formation requirement also prevents treating this as a documented simple tourist-to-resident sequence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Business registration alone grants no permanent-residence right; the separate resident-card rules require at least three years of qualifying lawful residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: There is no direct business-registration path. Naturalization would depend on separate lawful habitual residence and the nationality-law requirements.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because forming an enterprise is not permission to reside or work. APIP documents formation, but neither APIP nor the immigration sources confirm tourist-to-self-employed legalization for a foreign-client contractor.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign employee work permit and long-stay visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed employment rules do not establish a route-specific minimum salary.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No route-specific GNF salary threshold was identified.

income_requirement_display.value: No route-specific threshold published; an approved Guinean employment contract is required
income_requirement_display.notes: The employer-sponsored nature of this route excludes it from selection.

income_proof_months.notes: An independent income-history test is inapplicable because eligibility rests on an employer-filed contract and permit.

key_requirements.requirement: Written foreign-worker employment contract approved by the employment authority.
The employer submits the work-permit or contract-approval request; APIP also describes prior AGUIPE authorization for employers hiring non-ECOWAS foreigners.
Long-stay visa evidence includes the approved employment contract or work authorization.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence card up to 1 year; a foreign-worker employment contract cannot exceed 4 years
initial_validity.notes: The residence card and employment authorization are separate documents and may have different validity periods.

extension_rules.value: Work-permit renewal exists, and AGUIPE states that late renewal attracts a penalty equal to 50% of the applicable permit type. The renewed residence card remains limited to 1 year and requires the passport, recent criminal-record extract, and recent medical certificate described in the foreigners rules.
extension_rules.notes: Current official sources reviewed do not publish the normal work-permit renewal filing window, complete evidence list, or renewed permit duration; only the existence of renewal and the late-renewal penalty are currently exposed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approved local employment can support a long-stay visa and temporary residence card.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A five-year resident card may be requested after at least 3 years of uninterrupted lawful residence, subject to the statutory assessment.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization eligibility begins after 5 years of habitual lawful residence, subject to investigation and discretionary approval by decree.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Guinean employer must sponsor the contract and authorization. It does not fit independent foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: Institutional enrollment can support long-stay entry and a student temporary-residence card. Education does not directly grant permanent residence, and no independent degree-based skilled migration route was identified.
summary.notes: This is a study route, not a qualification-based route for continuing ordinary foreign-contract work.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is fiscally resident in Guinea if they have a permanent home there, stay more than six months in the year, exercise salaried or independent professional activity there unless it is ancillary to a principal activity abroad, or have their center of economic interests there.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Article 4 of the newer DGI-hosted 2021 code confirms that tax residence can arise without waiting for the six-month threshold.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Applicant-screening rate for plausible self-employed treatment: the 2021 code taxes BIC and BNC profits at 25%. Foreign-employer salary is instead taxed progressively from 0% to 20%. Classification must be confirmed with DGI; 25% is not an expected effective rate on gross receipts.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Five percent is the employee share for mandatory covered employment; CNSS states an 18% employer share and 23% total on the published monthly contribution base of GNF 550,000–2,500,000. CNSS describes mandatory coverage for workers principally employed in Guinea for one or more employers regardless of nationality, but its current pages do not specify collection mechanics for a foreign employer with no Guinean payroll. A new foreign-client freelancer is not shown as compulsorily covered, and voluntary insurance is limited to a former mandatory member with at least six consecutive months of affiliation who applies within six months after coverage ends.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universally applicable fixed monthly remote-worker or freelancer payment exists in the reviewed rules. Employee CNSS is percentage-based; qualifying voluntary insurance is assessed by CNSS and paid quarterly; GNF 212,500 is a one-time enterprise-registration cost.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, expatriate, remittance-basis, or ordinary inbound remote-worker concession is identified in the DGI materials reviewed.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The DGI published a 2026 fiscal précis, but its downloadable DOCX did not expose a searchable provision establishing such a regime. Narrow investment incentives are not ordinary remote-worker concessions.

taxes.caveats: The 2021 DGI-hosted code materially improves on the older code used previously: foreign-employer salary is expressly declarable and subject to the 0%–20% salary scale, while BIC and BNC profits are taxed at 25%. Services performed from Guinea may create residence, source, business-registration, VAT, and payroll issues even when the payer is abroad. Obtain DGI and CNSS advice on contract classification, deductions, treaty relief, VAT, employer registration, and social coverage before filing.

taxation_system.value: Mixed categorical system: progressive monthly tax of 0%–20% for employment income, including salary received from a foreign employer by a Guinean tax resident, and generally flat 25% tax on taxable BIC or BNC profits.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, more than six months' presence, professional activity in Guinea unless ancillary to a principal foreign activity, or center of economic interests in Guinea.
taxation_system.income_scope: The code taxes resident persons under the applicable income categories and expressly requires Guinean residents receiving salary from foreign employers to declare it. Nonresident and source rules may also apply to activity exercised in Guinea.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No ordinary digital-nomad or inbound foreign-remote-worker regime confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees: 5% employee plus 18% employer on the published GNF 550,000–2,500,000 monthly base. New independent contractors are not expressly brought into mandatory CNSS coverage by the reviewed pages; voluntary coverage is restricted to qualifying former insured workers.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The employment scale applies marginal monthly rates of 0%, 5%, 8%, 10%, 15%, and 20%. The displayed 25% dashboard figure is a conservative classification-screening rate for BIC/BNC profit, not a progressive top salary rate and not a rate on gross receipts.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly taxable employment income up to GNF 1,000,000

tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal salary rate, not the effective rate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Individual business or non-commercial professional profit, depending on classification
tax_brackets.notes: Flat categorical profit rate rather than an employment-income bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The newer DGI-hosted code directly supports the residence test, foreign-employer salary declaration, salary scale, and 25% BIC/BNC rates. The remaining uncertainty is how DGI would classify this particular foreign contract and whether post-2021 finance legislation changed a relevant provision; the 2026 précis page confirms a current précis exists but its DOCX contents were not browser-readable.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special digital-nomad taxation applies because Guinea has no confirmed digital-nomad status. Ordinary salary or business-profit rules would apply if the underlying work and residence were lawful.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; potentially foreign-employer salary, BNC professional profit, or BIC business profit
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Employment income: progressive 0%–20%; plausible BIC/BNC contractor treatment: 25% of taxable profit
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: A permanent home, more than six months' presence, Guinean professional activity unless ancillary to a principal foreign activity, or center of economic interests can create tax residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The code expressly requires Guinean tax residents receiving salary from foreign employers to declare it. Foreign-client fees require DGI classification and may be taxable as business or non-commercial professional profit.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the current official sources reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If treated as covered employment principally exercised in Guinea, CNSS publishes a 5% employee and 18% employer contribution on the GNF 550,000–2,500,000 monthly base, but it does not publish how a foreign employer without Guinean payroll must register or remit. A new independent foreign-client contractor is not expressly covered by the salaried collection page, and voluntary CNSS coverage is not open generally: it requires at least six prior consecutive months of mandatory affiliation and application within six months after that affiliation ends.

fixed_payments.status: No generally applicable fixed monthly payment can be stated for this profile: there is no digital-nomad route, salaried CNSS is percentage-based, and voluntary CNSS is a restricted continuation mechanism whose quarterly amount is individually notified by CNSS.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Covered employee contributions vary with the contribution base. Qualifying voluntary members pay quarterly at a CNSS-determined amount based on declared annual remuneration, not a published universal freelancer minimum.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The official visa and residence pages reviewed do not publish a reliable current visa or residence-card fee. APIP states GNF 212,500 for individual-enterprise registration, which is not an immigration fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No digital-nomad levy or universal fixed freelancer tax is published. Business registration, patent, VAT, withholding, or other obligations depend on classification and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: This replaces the vague prior status marker with the applicable legal distinction. The absence of a single fixed number reflects percentage-based employee contributions, restricted individually assessed voluntary coverage, and the lack of a lawful nomad category.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Six months or less does not ensure nonresidence because a permanent home, professional activity, or center of economic interests can independently establish tax residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Foreign-employer salary must be declared and is subject to the monthly 0%–20% scale. A contractor may instead face 25% BIC or BNC tax on taxable profit, depending on DGI classification.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Enterprise registration creates an RCCM record and tax number but does not legalize immigration status. DGI must confirm BIC/BNC classification, VAT, patent, deductions, and filing obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening analysis, not a filing calculation. Immigration authorization must be resolved separately.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying professional, study, family, or visitor category can receive a temporary card, but no processing duration or valid initial ordinary remote-worker route is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: A five-year resident card may be requested after at least three years of uninterrupted lawful residence; approval is assessed and this does not validate foreign-contract remote work as the initial basis.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived comparison only: resident-card eligibility starts after three years and ordinary naturalization eligibility after five years of habitual residence. The clocks overlap, and citizenship is not automatically granted two years after the resident card.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the ordinary eligibility period; acquisition remains discretionary and occurs by decree after investigation.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality code describes the decision mechanism, but neither it nor the government service portal publishes a representative or guaranteed processing duration.

key_conditions.value: The applicant must be lawfully resident when naturalization is granted, have five years of habitual residence before applying, satisfy character requirements, and demonstrate assimilation through sufficient knowledge of at least one national language, Guinean history, culture, society, and republican values. Naturalization is granted by decree after investigation.
key_conditions.notes: No general renunciation requirement was identified in the reviewed provisions; the applicant must separately check home-country nationality law.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship by declaration generally requires five years from marriage, including at least three years spent in Guinea. The marriage period is reduced to three years when a child with filiation established to both spouses was born before or after marriage. A resident card is available as of right to the foreign spouse.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage to a Guinean citizen can support resident-card eligibility. For nationality, qualifying time runs from the marriage date, but community of life must continue and the Guinean spouse must retain nationality when the declaration is made.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage itself does not automatically confer nationality.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must remain valid and the spouses' community of life must not have ceased. The President may oppose acquisition under the statutory procedure. Fraudulent documents, sham marriage, or misrepresentation can result in refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The route is declaration-based after the statutory conditions are met, not automatic at marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Guinea combines descent and conditional birth rules. Birth in Guinea confers nationality where at least one parent was also born there, and protective rules cover foundlings, unknown parents, and otherwise-stateless children. A child born in Guinea to foreign parents may later claim nationality under age and residence conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not ordinarily at birth solely because the child is born in Guinea. Citizenship can arise through double jus soli, statelessness or unknown-parent protections, or later residence-and-declaration provisions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for two temporary migrant parents neither of whom was born in Guinea where the child acquires another nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child is Guinean when at least one parent is Guinean, subject to proof of parentage and the code's limited repudiation rules for certain children born abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign father or mother of a Guinean child residing in Guinea is entitled to a resident card unless permanently deprived of parental authority. This is a residence benefit, not automatic citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Proof of the child's nationality, residence, parentage, and continuing parental status will be necessary.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Guinean child residing in Guinea can qualify for the parent-of-citizen-child resident card. He does not automatically become Guinean and must qualify separately for naturalization or a marriage declaration.

rank.notes: The 2026 Henley table reviewed on 2026-08-15 listed Guinea at rank 82.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's mobility score includes destinations accessible without a prior visa, including qualifying visa-on-arrival arrangements; it is not a strict visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Henley does not publish a separate visa-required total in the reviewed table, and the secondary country table was not sufficiently structured and current to support an audited count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The Henley score combines access types, while the secondary table did not yield a reliable current combined VOA/eTA count.

passport.notes: Current rank and mobility score are retained; separate access-category counts remain null because the reviewed sources do not provide an auditable current breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low outside a limited expatriate, university, or international-business environment in Conakry. French is the working and university-instruction language; U.S. commercial guidance says few Guineans use English in business discussions and even fewer do so outside Conakry.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This assessment concerns day-to-day administrative and business practicality, not the applicant's ability to work in English for a foreign client. The commercial guide, published in 2024, also reports no regular English-language publications; the U.S. State Department education profile confirms French university instruction and three years of required English instruction. The Constitution recognizes French and national languages, but the organic law needed for an exhaustive official-language list was not located, so the indigenous list reflects the principal national languages identified by the reviewed government sources.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Very low. Neither language has official status or documented broad administrative or commercial use; French or a major Guinean language is normally needed for local dealings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No Guinea-specific current source documents a substantial Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking service environment.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the survey's GNF 177,792 mean monthly income for employed persons using about GNF 8,774 per USD. The 2018/2019 survey is old and covers a predominantly informal labor market.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The national all-worker table publishes income bands rather than an exact median. It shows the median falls within the GNF 1,000,000–2,000,000 band, while the exact GNF 450,000 median belongs only to workers in informal production units.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the current GNF 550,000 CNSS contribution floor/SMIG. This is a statutory or contribution floor, not an observed minimum wage in the informal economy.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of GNF 177,792 mean monthly income of employed persons in the 2018/2019 survey; it is not a current formal-sector salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No exact median for all employed persons is published. The survey's exact GNF 450,000 median applies to informal-production-unit workers only.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No finite national maximum is published; the highest national all-worker income category is open-ended at GNF 8,000,000 or more.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: CNSS identifies this as the current SMIG and minimum monthly contribution base.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean monthly income of employed persons in the 2018/2019 national survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the exact median published in the survey's informal-sector worker analysis, not a national all-worker median. For all employed persons, the survey provides income bands showing that the median lies somewhere in the GNF 1,000,000–2,000,000 band but does not publish an exact value.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The national employed-person distribution ends with an open category of GNF 8,000,000 or more, representing 8.1% of employed persons; because that category has no upper bound, GNF 8,000,000 is not a maximum and no finite maximum can be reported.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: National survey mean monthly employment income; informal-sector median separately labelled; statutory CNSS/SMIG floor shown separately
average_citizen_salary.period: 2018/2019 survey; CNSS floor current on pages reviewed 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: The survey reports 95.6% informal employment, explaining why the national mean is not comparable with the current formal-sector contribution floor. The exact GNF 450,000 median is restricted to informal-production-unit workers; the all-worker distribution supports only a median band, not an exact point estimate. USD values are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable current national expatriate cost-of-living basket was identified. The World Bank's inflation and poverty indicators provide macroeconomic context but cannot be converted into a defensible remote-worker monthly budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Conakry housing and imported-goods costs can differ substantially from national worker-income data.
