settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: A visitor/eVisa stay, enterprise registration, or unauthorized foreign-client work is not a qualifying citizenship path. A separate authorized professional, employment, family, study, or other lawful residence basis is required.
settlement_track.summary: Guinea provides a general resident-card request after three years and ordinary naturalization eligibility after five years, but no confirmed initial residence route accepts ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The applicant would need a different authorized status, so Guinea is not valid for this selection.
settlement_track.notes: General settlement provisions do not cure the absence of a lawful initial remote-worker category.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: There is no dedicated remote-worker status. Local employment requires employer authorization, while independent professional activity requires competent-authority approval not shown to accept an ordinary foreign software contract. Company registration alone grants no immigration permission.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed using more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including more than five sources outside the prior set. The residence-renewal evidence, work-permit renewal status, current tax categories, social-security scope, English-practicality evidence, informal-sector median, and reason no maximum salary can be stated are now explicit. Remaining nulls reflect genuinely unpublished procedures, fees, processing times, or finite statistics rather than placeholder text.

data.selection_summary: A renewable general residence permit may be obtainable locally and, according to Spain’s embassy in Bissau, residence permits allow work after tax and social-security registration. Legal residence can support naturalization after six years. However, no current Guinea-Bissau immigration law or official route page was found establishing the residence-permit eligibility grounds, documentary requirements, treatment of foreign-client remote work, or permanent-residence transition. This is therefore a filing-level possibility requiring confirmation from the Direcção-Geral de Migração e Fronteiras, not a confirmed digital-nomad or freelance route.

visa_application.title: Pedido de Visto
visa_application.notes: This is an official Guinea-Bissau embassy page for an entry-visa application, not a residence-permit portal. Spain’s embassy reports that the former electronic visa site is not operating. Residence applications must be made to local authorities, but no official online residence application channel was found.

best_routes.route_name: General renewable residence permit with local work/tax registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No published minimum income was found for the general residence-permit application.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No XOF financial threshold was published by the sources inspected.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; eligibility and proof of means require confirmation
income_requirement_display.notes: The available residence guidance says to apply locally with a passport but does not publish comprehensive eligibility or proof-of-means rules.

income_proof_months.notes: No required bank-statement or income-proof period was found.

key_requirements.requirement: Enter with a valid passport and entry visa, then present a residence application and passport to the competent local authorities.
A residence permit reportedly permits employment or professional activity, but the resident must register as a taxpayer with the Ministry of Finance and with social security.
Confirm directly with the Direcção-Geral de Migração e Fronteiras whether foreign-employer or foreign-client software work is accepted as the residence purpose and which documents are required.
For eventual naturalization, maintain documented legal residence for at least six years, demonstrate minimum knowledge of Portuguese or Guinea-Bissau Creole, and provide criminal-record certificates.

initial_validity.value: 1 to 5 years
initial_validity.notes: Spain’s embassy describes residence permits as valid for between one and five years; the exact grant depends on the local authority and permit category.

extension_rules.value: Renewable, but renewal timing, absence limits, financial requirements and documentation were not published in the sources found.
extension_rules.notes: Obtain written current rules from migration authorities before relying on renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The locally issued general residence permit is itself temporary residence. Current secondary official guidance indicates a foreigner applies locally with a passport, but the complete statutory eligibility framework was not located.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not a dedicated remote-worker category.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No permanent-residence category, qualifying period or conversion procedure was established. Naturalization law instead refers to six years of legal residence under residence authorization.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization may be requested after at least six years of legal residence documented by the migration service, with Portuguese or Creole knowledge and qualifying criminal records. Approval involves administrative review and government decision.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The six-year citizenship rule is confirmed in primary legislation, but it does not resolve whether this applicant would first qualify for the general residence permit.

best_routes.notes: This route is materially more promising than the previous record indicated because current Spanish-government guidance says residence permits are renewable, last one to five years and allow work after registration. It remains uncertain because no current Guinea-Bissau primary immigration rules were found defining independent eligibility or expressly authorizing ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Verify before travel; do not treat an entry visa alone as work or residence authorization.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist/visitor visa, visa on arrival or consular entry visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies because this is entry permission rather than a residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published minimum income was found.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold; visitor entry permission only
income_requirement_display.notes: A visitor visa does not itself establish residence or authorization for continuing foreign-contract work.

income_proof_months.notes: The embassy page requests a passport, photograph and form but publishes no income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Visa required; it may be obtained at an embassy or, according to U.S. guidance, on arrival.
Passport generally needs at least six months remaining validity and travelers need proof of yellow-fever vaccination.
Spain’s embassy recommends obtaining the visa before travel because border issuance is unclear and unstable and the former electronic system is suspended.

initial_validity.value: Embassy/consular offerings include 30/45-day, 90-day and 180-day visas.
initial_validity.notes: Duration depends on the issuing post and is not residence status.

extension_rules.notes: No reliable visitor-extension rules were found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate local residence application may exist, but visitor status does not automatically convert or authorize work.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Any residence filing must be confirmed with local migration authorities.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence path arises from the visitor visa.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires documented legal residence; ordinary visitor time was not shown to qualify.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is visitor entry permission, not a remote-worker residence or settlement route.

summary.value: No separate degree-based, independent skilled-worker or points-tested residence route was found. A software-engineering degree may support a professional filing but does not create a documented immigration entitlement.
summary.notes: The general residence possibility is not qualification-based, and the investment framework is not an ordinary remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.notes: No current primary source establishing a general day-count or 183-day tax-residence test was found. The Portugal–Guinea-Bissau treaty guide discusses persons resident in Guinea-Bissau but does not define domestic residence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: IMF’s 2025 selected-issues report describes the statutory PIT rate as 20%. This is a screening statutory rate, not an estimated effective rate. A separate Macao government investment page describes professional tax for employees as 11–12%, so classification and liability for foreign remote income require local advice.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Published employee contribution rate. IMF also reports 14% employer social security and 2–10% work-accident insurance depending on sector. Treatment of a foreign-payroll worker or locally registered independent professional was not established.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly social-security, health-insurance or freelancer payment was found.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate or freelancer tax holiday was found. A Portugal–Guinea-Bissau tax treaty can provide exemption or foreign-tax credits in qualifying bilateral cases.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty benefits are relevant only when the applicant has a Portuguese tax connection and satisfies the treaty procedure.

taxes.caveats: Tax liability depends on whether the person becomes domestically tax resident, whether foreign employment is treated as work exercised in Guinea-Bissau, whether the worker is an employee or independent professional, registration status, and any applicable treaty. The available sources do not provide a complete current personal-tax code or self-employed contribution schedule.

taxation_system.value: The available evidence indicates a 20% statutory personal income-tax rate, alongside a professional-tax description of 11–12% for employees and payroll-related contributions. The precise relationship among these charges and the tax base for foreign-client income was not established.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Not established; no reliable domestic day-count rule was located.
taxation_system.income_scope: Work exercised in Guinea-Bissau and liberal-profession activity there are described as taxable even without permanent residence. The extent of worldwide taxation for residents was not established.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or general inbound-expatriate regime found; treaty relief may apply in Portugal-linked cases.
taxation_system.social_security: 8% worker and 14% employer; IMF additionally reports work-accident insurance of 2–10% depending on sector.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: No verified progressive bracket table was found. The dashboard’s 20% figure is the IMF-reported statutory PIT screening rate, not expected effective tax.
taxation_system.notes: The IMF is authoritative for the headline rate and contributions, but filing-level treatment should be confirmed with the Ministry of Finance or a local adviser because the underlying current tax code and remote-worker classification were not located.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax treatment exists in the sources found. A person admitted under general residence and working from Guinea-Bissau should assume local tax and registration exposure until advised otherwise.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: General resident worker or independent professional; no digital-nomad category confirmed
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 20% statutory PIT screening rate; a separate professional-tax source reports 11–12% for employees
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No domestic day-count rule confirmed. Tax exposure may arise from exercising work or a liberal profession in Guinea-Bissau even without permanent residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The Portugal treaty guide indicates independent work of a Guinea-Bissau resident is generally taxable in Guinea-Bissau, subject to treaty exceptions. Broader treatment of foreign-source income was not established.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Published formal-worker rates are 8% employee and 14% employer, plus 2–10% work-accident insurance depending on sector. Application to foreign payroll or self-employment is unresolved.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed monthly amount confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage contributions are reported, but no minimum monthly contribution base was found.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The Porto honorary consulate lists EUR 60 for 30/45-day visas, EUR 80 for 90 days and EUR 180 for 180 days. Spain’s embassy reports that residence permits may cost up to approximately EUR 70 in local currency. Fees vary and must be reconfirmed.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A Macao government investment page reports 0.3% stamp tax on salaries and 2% work-accident insurance in its summary; IMF reports accident insurance can range from 2% to 10% by sector.
fixed_payments.notes: These are not digital-nomad program fees and may change.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe tax-free short-stay threshold was established. Spain’s embassy states that work stays under three months have no professional-tax withholding and need no Guinea-Bissau social-security contribution when home-country coverage is proven, but this is not equivalent to a general exemption from all tax or immigration rules.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Budget using the 20% PIT screening rate and seek classification of the foreign contract, tax base, withholding mechanism and treaty position. Register with the Ministry of Finance and social security if directed.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Professional activity appears to require taxpayer and social-security registration. No simplified freelancer rate, minimum contribution or foreign-client exemption was found.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No dedicated nomad regime exists; figures describe the general tax and formal-work system.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: If approved, the general application directly produces a renewable residence permit; no prerequisite years were published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No permanent-residence timeline or category was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on six years of legal residence rather than a confirmed prerequisite period of permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum of six years of legal residence. This does not include application processing and depends on obtaining and continuously documenting qualifying residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The regulation gives a 30-day period for one registry opinion stage, but no reliable total end-to-end processing time was established.

key_conditions.value: At least six years of documented legal residence under residence authorization; adulthood; minimum Portuguese or Guinea-Bissau Creole knowledge; qualifying Guinea-Bissau and foreign criminal records; administrative review and government approval. No published permanent-residence prerequisite was found.
key_conditions.notes: Residence continuity and absence rules were not located.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The statute requires three years of continuing marriage and one year of residence in Guinea-Bissau.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage appears capable of satisfying the three-year marriage-duration element because the law refers to the duration of the subsisting marriage, but the applicant must also complete one year of residence and make an express declaration. Registration and documentary recognition should be confirmed.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The law does not say that all three marriage years must occur after entry.

requirements_and_risks.value: Submit an express declaration and civil-status evidence. The marriage must remain in force; the law protects nationality acquired through a later-annulled marriage only where the applicant married in good faith. Criminal records and evidence of an effective connection may be requested under the regulation. Fraudulent or sham marriage creates refusal, loss and criminal-law risks.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage is a family-based nationality route, not a substitute for the requested remote-work route.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Guinea-Bissau alone is insufficient. Citizenship at birth covers a child of a Bissau-Guinean mother or father and locally born children who have no other nationality; it also covers children born locally to stateless or unknown-nationality parents resident in the country and presumptively covers foundlings.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Normally no if both parents are foreign migrants and the child obtains either parent’s nationality. Citizenship may arise if the locally born child has no other nationality, or where both parents are stateless or of unknown nationality and reside in Guinea-Bissau.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is an anti-statelessness safeguard rather than general jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Guinea-Bissau to a Bissau-Guinean mother or father is a citizen of origin. A child born abroad to a citizen parent can acquire origin nationality through the prescribed declaration or civil-registration process, subject to the statutory details.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Document and register the parent-child relationship.

parent_benefit_summary.value: No automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship for a foreign parent follows merely from having a citizen child. A family-based residence possibility may exist in practice, but no current legal procedure was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Obtain case-specific confirmation from migration authorities.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically become a citizen through the child. If the mother is Bissau-Guinean, the child is a citizen, but any residence benefit for the father requires a separate immigration decision not established by the sources inspected.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Marriage to the citizen mother can create the separate three-years-of-marriage plus one-year-residence nationality route.

rank.notes: VISAXS’s 2026 global rank, whose methodology differs from Henley. A secondary Henley summary reports rank 82 with 50 destinations accessible visa-free or on arrival.

visa_free_destinations.notes: VISAXS visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: VISAXS visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: VISAXS combined non-visa-free mobility category shown between visa-free and visa-required counts; confirm whether individual destinations are visa on arrival, eVisa or eTA before travel.

passport.notes: The previous Henley-derived record combined visa-free and visa-on-arrival access into 50 destinations and rank 82. The normalized fields here use one named index, VISAXS, that publishes separate 2026 counts; ranks are not comparable across methodologies.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low outside a narrow international/business environment. Portuguese is the official administrative language, while Guinea-Bissau Creole is much more widely spoken in everyday life. English-only residence, tax and social-security filings are unlikely to be practical without local assistance.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The nationality regulation accepts minimum knowledge of Portuguese or Guinea-Bissau Creole for naturalization.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Very low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official or documented widespread administrative use; Portuguese or Creole interpretation would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from the documented language environment; no Guinea-Bissau-specific survey of Russian or Ukrainian speakers was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Very rough secondary estimate for formal-sector workers, reportedly based on World Bank/ILO material. It is not an official national average and should not be used for immigration eligibility.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No Guinea-Bissau national median observation was recoverable from the inspected ILO profile or other reliable source.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory XOF 19,030 monthly minimum wage, not an observed lower bound of salaries.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Secondary, low-confidence formal-sector estimate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median wage value was established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum or upper wage bound was published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Reported statutory nominal gross monthly minimum wage; the secondary source attributes its underlying series to ILOSTAT.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Very rough estimated formal-sector average, not a directly verified national-statistics release.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not established.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not established.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum plus a rough gross formal-sector average estimate
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 minimum-wage reporting and a 2022-based formal-sector average, published/updated in 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: Guinea-Bissau’s informal economy is dominant and current wage data are sparse. Preserve the values only as rough labor-market context; do not infer a national median or maximum.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable current expatriate cost-of-living basket was found. Economic context indicates limited purchasing power and exposure to food and fuel prices: the World Bank projects extreme poverty at 37.8% in 2028 and notes that food and fuel each account for about 30% of imports.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Low local wages do not necessarily imply that imported goods, reliable electricity, internet, healthcare or expatriate-standard housing are inexpensive.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: There is no dedicated digital-nomad status. The potential route is a general residence permit whose eligibility for foreign-contract remote work must be confirmed before applying.
settlement_track.summary: General legal residence can support naturalization after six years, and residence reportedly permits work after registration. The track remains weak and uncertain because no current primary immigration source confirmed that an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker can obtain or continually renew the initial residence permit, and no permanent-residence rules were found.
settlement_track.notes: This improves the previous conclusion that no residence possibility existed, but it is not strong enough to mark Guinea-Bissau as selected. Written confirmation from migration, tax and social-security authorities is essential.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Residence reportedly authorizes work and does not appear to require a separate employer-sponsored work permit, but the available guidance does not expressly address a foreign employer/client, independent software services, approval grounds or foreign-source income. Verify the exact filing category and whether local business registration is required.

data.notes: Twenty-three distinct country-relevant URLs were inspected. Strong primary support exists for nationality, marriage and child-citizenship rules, and credible institutional support exists for headline taxes. Immigration eligibility, permanent residence, tax residence, self-employed contributions, median wages and total citizenship processing time remain cautiously unresolved because no current primary rules or official application instructions establishing them were located.

data.selection_summary: Guyana does not currently publish a digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary freelance residence route. Its official system offers visitor, business, employment, and student visas: visitor status is temporary, employment requires an employment contract/sponsor, and the business route requires a registered business, Guyana tax and NIS compliance, and a sponsor permit letter. None is a confirmed independent residence-to-citizenship route for ordinary work under a foreign contract.

visa_application.title: Immigration Support Services — Apply for a Visa
visa_application.notes: This is the official general portal for visitor, business, employment, and student visas. It is not a digital-nomad or freelance-residence application portal.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No personal monthly-income threshold is published. The route instead requires local business-registration, tax-compliance, NIS-compliance, and sponsorship documents.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum income amount is stated.

income_requirement_display.value: No published personal-income threshold; registered-business and sponsor documentation required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a business/entrepreneur channel, not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker category.

income_proof_months.notes: The portal does not state a required number of months of personal income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Business registration and a mandatory business income-tax liability statement.
Business NIS compliance and a mandatory sponsor permit letter.
Police clearance, medical report, passport biodata, passport stamps, and applicant photograph.

initial_validity.value: An entry permit may initially be granted for up to three months; the Immigration Act permits extensions up to an aggregate maximum of three years from entry.
initial_validity.notes: Actual visa/permit duration and conditions remain discretionary and purpose-specific.

extension_rules.value: The Chief Immigration Officer may extend a permit up to three years from entry and may impose residence, occupation, security, or other conditions.
extension_rules.notes: Extension is discretionary and does not establish permanent residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The sources establish a temporary business visa/immigration permit, not a separately defined qualifying temporary-residence status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No published business-visa-to-permanent-residence transition was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation exists after qualifying residence, but no official source confirms that this business visa provides a dependable settlement transition for an ordinary foreign-contract worker.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the filing requires local business, tax, NIS, and sponsor documentation. Whether a foreign remote worker could establish the required local business and obtain the sponsor letter is unclear, and the route is not designed for ordinary foreign-client remote work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The inspected official employment-visa checklists prescribe an employment contract, sponsorship and employer compliance documents but publish no minimum salary.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The named official sources publish no minimum salary in GYD or another currency.

income_requirement_display.value: No published salary threshold; employment contract and employer sponsorship required
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign-client remote-work contract does not satisfy the official employer-processing requirements as published.

income_proof_months.notes: The official checklist requires a contract or employment letter but does not prescribe a past-income evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Mandatory contract or letter of employment, police clearance, medical report, passport, and photograph.
The sponsor/employer must provide its details to the Ministry before arrival; the workplace must be an established business registered and compliant with GRA and NIS.
The employer presents the worker to the Ministry, and work-permit approval is given to the employer and Immigration.
The employment-visa-on-arrival checklist requires a signed employment contract and evidence that the vacancy was advertised for three consecutive months.

initial_validity.value: The current visa-on-arrival employment advisory says employment visas are granted for three years.
initial_validity.notes: This does not remove employer sponsorship. A separate Ministry extension form refers to a five-year extension of stay, so the applicable term for a particular filing should be confirmed with Immigration Support Services.

extension_rules.value: The official portal provides an employment-visa extension/work-permit channel. A Ministry form states that an extension of stay will be granted for five years, although it does not explain its relationship to the three-year employment-visa rule.
extension_rules.notes: The current sources do not state whether five years is a renewal term, a category-specific term, or an outdated form instruction; confirm before relying on it.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Current official materials describe this status as an Employment Visa, Work Permit, and Extension of Stay—not as a separately named temporary-residence permit. The April 2025 visa-on-arrival advisory says the employment visa is granted for three years, while the Ministry extension form says an extension of stay is granted for five years; neither document explains whether the latter is a renewal term, a different filing type, or supersedes the three-year rule. The status is therefore confirmed as employer-dependent lawful temporary stay, but a distinct qualifying temporary-residence classification and the applicable duration must be verified with Immigration Support Services.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Immigration Act, current employment advisory, extension form and current ISS service description publish no employment-visa-to-permanent-residence procedure. The null reflects the absence of a published transition, not a claim that discretionary recognition is legally impossible.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may eventually be available after qualifying residence, but the route requires a local employer and therefore fails the target profile.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act states the general residence test—residence throughout the final 12 months plus at least five aggregate years in the preceding seven—while current consular guidance summarizes naturalisation as five years of ordinary residence. The Act and guidance do not identify employment-visa or work-permit time as included or excluded, and the current employment-visa, extension, and ISS-platform sources publish no route-specific naturalisation-counting or permanent-residence conversion rule. Accordingly, citizenship may be legally possible only if the Minister accepts the applicant’s actual stay as qualifying residence and all other discretionary requirements are met; that treatment is unpublished and must be confirmed with Citizenship and Immigration.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local established employer/sponsor and employment contract are required. Current sources also require employer compliance evidence and, for visa on arrival, a three-month vacancy advertisement.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor visa, visa exemption, or visitor permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visa-on-arrival guidance asks for finances covering 30 days but does not publish a numerical threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No numerical visitor-funds threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Evidence of funds for the visit may be required; no numerical threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: This is visitor evidence, not a remote-worker income requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank statement may be requested, but no history period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport, photograph, birth certificate, and visa-on-arrival request letter are mandatory in the online visitor-visa checklist; other family, medical, sponsor, character, and bank documents may apply.
Visa-on-arrival guidance requires accommodation or inviter details, invitation evidence, and finances for 30 days.
A visitor who breaches entry conditions may be liable to deportation.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to three months under the Immigration Act; the visa-on-arrival advisory discusses a 30-day visitor stay.
initial_validity.notes: The actual permission depends on nationality and the immigration endorsement.

extension_rules.value: Visa-on-arrival guidance allows at most two one-month visitor extensions; the Immigration Act gives broader discretionary extension authority subject to conditions.
extension_rules.notes: Visitor extensions do not create a remote-work or settlement right.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The reviewed sources provide visitor entry and discretionary extensions but publish no visitor-to-residence conversion for a foreign-contract worker.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed Immigration Act provisions publish no visitor-to-permanent-residence procedure.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act prescribes general residence requirements but does not state that temporary visitor permission is qualifying naturalisation residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor entry is temporary, does not expressly authorize ordinary remote work, and has no confirmed settlement conversion.

summary.value: A student visa can be applied for without an employer but requires an educational institution and is a temporary study/entry category. No independent degree-based skilled migration or direct permanent-residence route was found for a non-CARICOM applicant. The CSME framework separately permits qualified CARICOM nationals, including university graduates, to seek work without a work permit and its portal advertises definite and indefinite stay services, but eligibility depends on CARICOM nationality and therefore does not fit the assumed applicant merely because the applicant has a degree.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing software-engineering degree does not itself create a Guyanese residence entitlement. CSME is a nationality-limited regional mobility framework, not a general foreign graduate route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if permanently resident/intending permanent residence or present in Guyana for more than 183 days in the year; GRA return guidance operationally instructs taxpayers to mark resident at 183 days or more.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The statute says more than 183 days while the current return guide says 183 days or more. The boundary should be confirmed with GRA for a filing involving exactly 183 days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for 2026, not the expected effective rate. The first GYD 3,360,000 of chargeable income is taxed at 25%, with the excess at 35%, after applicable deductions.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The NIS page states that self-employed persons contribute 12.5% of declared income. Whether a foreign-contract worker without valid local self-employment status must register requires case-specific confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly remote-worker payment applies because there is no nomad route. NIS is percentage-based, and the reviewed page does not publish a current minimum self-employed monthly contribution.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or dedicated inbound remote-worker regime was found. Guyana's Income Tax Act provides a remittance limitation for foreign income that is earned income or belongs to a person not ordinarily resident or not domiciled in Guyana.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary residence, domicile, income source, and remittance require case-specific analysis; this is not a nomad tax exemption.

taxes.caveats: Tax outcomes depend on whether work performed physically in Guyana is Guyana-source, ordinary residence and domicile, whether foreign income is received or remitted in Guyana, deductions, NIS registration, and any applicable tax treaty. Immigration permission and tax registration are separate questions.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with worldwide-income language and a statutory remittance limitation for certain foreign income
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence/intention or presence over 183 days under the Act; the current return guide uses 183 days or more.
taxation_system.income_scope: The Act charges income arising in Guyana or elsewhere whether received in Guyana or not, but foreign earned income or foreign income of a person not ordinarily resident or not domiciled is taxed on the amount received in Guyana.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. A remittance limitation may apply based on ordinary residence, domicile, income character, and receipt in Guyana.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed persons are stated to contribute 12.5% of declared income; the reviewed NIS page does not establish a current minimum or updated insurable-income ceiling for this scenario.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For 2026, the annual personal deduction is GYD 1,680,000 or one-third of qualifying income, whichever is greater. The first GYD 3,360,000 of chargeable income is taxed at 25%; excess chargeable income is taxed at 35%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First GYD 3,360,000 of annual chargeable income
tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual chargeable income after applicable allowances and deductions
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses the Bureau of Statistics December 2025 mid-rate of GYD 221 per USD.
This is a marginal rate on the excess, not a flat rate on gross income.

taxation_system.notes: The rates and core residence rule are official. Application of the remittance provision and NIS to a particular foreign contract requires professional advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable: Guyana has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker visa.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary individual/self-employed rules would apply if the person had another lawful status.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Top marginal screening rate: 35%; lower bracket 25% after deductions.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Resident at 183 days or more under current GRA return guidance, although the underlying Act says more than 183 days; permanent-residence intention is also relevant.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The Act uses worldwide-income language, subject to a remittance limitation for certain foreign earned income or income of a person who is not ordinarily resident or not domiciled.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: NIS states that self-employed persons contribute 12.5% of declared income. Applicability depends on lawful local self-employment and registration.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment; ordinary percentage-based tax/NIS may apply.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: 12.5% of declared income for self-employed persons according to the NIS page; no current minimum monthly amount was established.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Ordinary visitor, business, employment, and student visa fees may apply, but there is no nomad-visa fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific fixed tax was found. Local business registration and compliance costs would apply if using a business structure.
fixed_payments.notes: The reviewed official sources did not establish a fixed monthly freelancer tax, mandatory private-health premium, or nomad renewal fee.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Tax non-residence does not itself authorize remote work. Guyana-source income and remitted foreign income can still require analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident may face 25%/35% progressive PIT, potentially 12.5% self-employed NIS, and worldwide/remittance rules, but must first possess lawful immigration and work status.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local business/TIN/NIS registration is possible administratively, but no official source confirms that registration converts visitor status into qualifying residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax rules are reasonably well supported; the hypothetical remote-worker treatment remains conditional because the immigration route itself is unavailable.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker temporary-residence route is among the current immigration categories. Temporary visas, work permits and extensions should not automatically be equated with a separately defined residence status.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The inspected Immigration Act and current ISS category description publish no general remote-worker or employment-visa permanent-residence transition.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The naturalisation law is based on residence history rather than a published permanent-residence milestone, so an interval measured specifically from permanent residence is inapplicable to the text reviewed.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The consolidated Citizenship Act requires residence throughout the final 12 months plus at least five aggregate years during the preceding seven years, implying at least six years of actual residence. Current consular guidance instead summarizes the requirement as five immediately preceding years, so filing practice should be confirmed.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Citizenship Act, current official consular guidance and ISS platform announcement publish no typical naturalisation processing duration.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation is discretionary and requires the statutory residence history, good character, intent to reside in Guyana, approval, and an oath of allegiance. The Minister may relax residence periods in special circumstances. No language-test requirement or general renunciation requirement was identified in the reviewed provisions.
key_conditions.notes: This general naturalisation framework does not cure the absence of a fitting initial remote-worker immigration route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Official consular guidance states that spouse registration has no specified years-of-residence requirement. Zero denotes no published waiting period, not automatic citizenship: legal entry, lawful presence, application, oath, and other legal requirements still apply.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A person already genuinely married to a Guyanese citizen may apply for registration as a citizen after legally entering and being legally present in Guyana; marriage alone is not automatic citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: This is a family route outside the target applicant's assumed profile.

requirements_and_risks.value: Application and an oath of allegiance are required. Registration may be refused for national-security or public-policy reasons. Documentary proof and genuine-marriage verification should be expected; sham marriage or false evidence can cause refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official sources do not promise approval merely because a marriage certificate exists.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 43 grants citizenship at birth to a person born in Guyana, subject only to narrow exceptions for children of qualifying foreign envoys when neither parent is Guyanese and enemy-alien births in enemy-occupied territory.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Guyana generally becomes a citizen at birth even when both parents are foreign migrants, subject to the Constitution's narrow diplomatic and enemy-occupation exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' temporary or permanent status does not change the broad territorial rule.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Guyana is a citizen by birth; a child born abroad is also a citizen at birth if either parent is Guyanese otherwise than solely by descent under Article 44.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Documentary registration may still be needed in practice for a foreign-born child.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's status does not automatically confer citizenship, permanent residence, or a remote-work right on a foreign parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed constitutional and citizenship provisions contain no automatic parent-of-citizen immigration entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic residence or citizenship benefit for the migrant father is created by the reviewed provisions. Any family-based permission would require a separate application and current Immigration Support Services guidance.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child's Guyanese citizenship should not be treated as automatic legalization of the father.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the live Guyana dashboard on 2026-08-15; real-time rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Live Passport Index category count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 40 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. The index separately lists other eVisa destinations that are not included here.

passport.notes: These values use Passport Index because it provides the requested categorical breakdown. They are not directly comparable to Henley's combined visa-free/visa-on-arrival score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for language: English is the official language, while Guyanese Creolese is widely spoken. Government forms and the visa portal are in English.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Language practicality does not overcome the lack of a suitable immigration route.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. The reviewed government language source identifies English as the official language and does not identify Russian or Ukrainian as languages of administration; English should be expected.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from official-language information, not a measured proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: GYD 151,923 average monthly income for all salaried workers in 2024 Q4, divided by the Bureau's December 2025 mid-rate of GYD 221/USD. Rounded approximate conversion.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official labour-force bulletin reports means but does not publish a national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Public-sector minimum wage of GYD 102,346 divided by GYD 221/USD. It is not an observed minimum across all workers.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 Q4 mean monthly income for salaried workers.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official bulletin does not publish a national median salary, so no value is inferred from the reported mean.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum wage is not published in the inspected labour-force bulletin and would not be a meaningful population statistic.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 public-sector minimum wage, not a national observed minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean monthly labour income for all salaried workers, 2024 Q4. The same bulletin reports GYD 161,846 for all self-employed workers.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official bulletin does not publish a national median salary.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official bulletin does not publish a meaningful national maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Mean monthly labour-related income for salaried workers; minimum field is the public-sector minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 Q4 average income; 2025 minimum wage; USD conversion uses December 2025 mid-rate
average_citizen_salary.notes: Official survey estimates are representative means with sampling error; they are not software-engineer salaries. The USD figures are approximate and exchange-rate-sensitive.

cost_of_living_note.value: The Georgetown CPI reached 153.47 in June 2026 and rose 1.2% from May, driven mainly by miscellaneous goods/services and food. CPI measures price change rather than the absolute monthly budget needed by a remote worker.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official source does not publish a single-person monthly cost-of-living budget, so none is estimated.

settlement_track.summary: Guyana has general naturalisation rules, but none of its current visitor, business, employment, or student visa channels is a confirmed independent ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route. Visitor permission is temporary, employment requires sponsorship, and the business route requires local business substance and sponsorship documents.
settlement_track.notes: Naturalisation law cannot be used without first obtaining and maintaining appropriate lawful status. The focused employment-route audit established lawful temporary stay terminology but found no published employment-visa permanent-residence transition or definitive rule stating whether work-permit time counts toward naturalisation.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The complete current official visa menu contains no digital-nomad/remote-worker category. Business filings require local compliance and a sponsor letter; employment requires an established employer, sponsorship and an employment contract; visitor status is not a work/residence route.

data.notes: The negative route conclusion is supported by the current official visa portal, category checklists, immigration and citizenship legislation, and eight additional official URLs inspected during the focused unresolved-field pass. Guyana remains unsuitable for the specified ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker citizenship-path selection.

data.selection_summary: Haiti has a current residence-permit procedure, and its labor rules contemplate work permits for self-employed foreigners. However, published rules do not expressly confirm that ordinary remote work performed solely for a foreign client qualifies, while the residence checklist requests an employment or financial-support letter. Written confirmation from the immigration and labor authorities is therefore needed before treating this as a reliable citizenship-oriented route.

visa_application.title: Obtention d’un permis de séjour en Haïti
visa_application.notes: Official residence-permit checklist, not an online application portal. The applicant writes to the Direction de l’Immigration et de l’Émigration, submits documents, attends an interview, completes a form and pays through the Treasury. Work authorization requires a separate labor-authority filing.

best_routes.route_name: Residence permit plus self-employed foreign-worker permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly income threshold is published. The residence checklist instead requires a Haitian-bank certificate showing at least HTG 7,500 or US$200.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly minimum is stated; HTG 7,500 is a minimum bank balance, not monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly-income threshold; the official checklist requires a Haitian-bank certificate showing at least HTG 7,500 or US$200.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: HTG 7,500 or US$200 minimum bank balance
income_requirement_display.notes: The alternative amounts are reproduced as published even though they are not equivalent at current exchange rates.

income_proof_months.notes: The checklist does not prescribe a bank-statement history or number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Write to the DIE explaining the reason for requesting residence and apply in Haiti.

Provide the passport bio-page, a medical certificate issued within 30 days, two photographs, the last arrival card, a birth certificate with mandatory French translation and a recent home-country criminal record.

Provide an employment letter or a letter from the person supporting the applicant that guarantees the stay and repatriation; the checklist requests the employer’s business licence or an NGO operating authorization where applicable.
Provide a certificate from a bank located in Haiti showing at least HTG 7,500 or US$200.
Attend an interview, complete the application form and pay HTG 5,000 by bank cheque to the Treasury.
Obtain a separate work permit before undertaking profitable self-employment. The labor-code guide requires a residence permit and contemplates qualification and non-competition evidence.
Obtain a Haitian tax number for tax filings and Treasury-related transactions.

initial_validity.value: The current DIE checklist does not state the residence permit’s duration. The associated foreign-worker permit may be issued for no more than one year.
initial_validity.notes: The residence document should not be assumed to be permanent or to have the same duration as the work permit.

extension_rules.value: The foreign-worker permit is renewable at the labor authority’s discretion for up to five consecutive years. The current DIE page does not publish a residence-permit renewal duration or procedure.
extension_rules.notes: Filing-level confirmation is important because the work-permit ceiling coincides with the five-year statutory naturalization period.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply directly to the DIE for a time-limited residence permit and obtain the separate self-employed work permit before carrying on profitable professional activity.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The residence permit is a genuine immigration status, but approval and duration remain discretionary.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No current official conversion procedure from this time-limited residence/work-permit combination to an unlimited or permanent residence status was established.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The older foreigners law describes an unlimited residence visa, but the current DIE site does not publish transition rules or current eligibility requirements.

path_to_citizenship.value: Articles 15 and 19–23 of the 6 November 1984 nationality decree provide for naturalization after five years of legal residence. The applicant petitions the Minister of Justice with a residence permit, identity card and locally certified residence certificate; the Interior Department investigates moral character, the President decides by published order, and the applicant takes the prescribed oath. The decree states a fixed HTG 5,000 naturalization charge. Current Haitian instructions do not separately identify qualifying permit categories, so continuous validity of this exact residence permit throughout the five years should be confirmed before reliance.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The primary decree establishes a five-year legal-residence route rather than requiring prior permanent residence. Its stated fee is historical legislation and the current amount and administrative practice should be verified with the Ministry of Justice.

best_routes.notes: Plausible self-employed route, not a digital-nomad visa. The decisive unresolved issue is whether a software engineer serving only a foreign client can receive the work permit and satisfy the residence support-letter and non-competition evidence without a Haitian employer or local client.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist visa or visa-exempt visitor entry

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: An income threshold is inapplicable to visitor entry.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; this is visitor entry, not work-authorized residence.
income_requirement_display.notes: A current-employer letter is among the tourist-visa documents for visa-required nationals, but it does not confer work authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: The tourist-visa page does not prescribe a period of income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Most tourists are visa exempt but need a passport valid for at least six months and pay US$10 on arrival.
Nationals listed by the embassy as visa-required must apply in advance and submit the specified tourist-visa documents.

initial_validity.value: The embassy fee schedule lists three-month and six-month tourist visas.
initial_validity.notes: These visas do not establish residence or work authorization.

extension_rules.value: A traveler staying beyond ordinary visitor admission must regularize through the separate DIE residence-permit procedure.
extension_rules.notes: This is a new residence application, not an automatic extension or conversion.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path. A separate discretionary residence-permit application is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor entry alone is not qualifying residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Tourist status creates no right to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality decree requires legal residence and requires a residence permit in an ordinary naturalization application. The reviewed tourist rules confer neither residence nor work authorization, so visitor time cannot be treated as satisfying the five-year residence period without an intervening grant of qualifying legal residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourist or visa-exempt entry does not authorize profitable remote work and is not itself qualifying settlement status.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign commercial registration or professional identity card alone

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The DGI states that a foreigner seeking residence authorization to trade must maintain HTG 50,000 at the central bank; this is a deposit, not income.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly income threshold; commercial rules mention a permanent HTG 50,000 deposit for a foreign trader seeking residence authorization.
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an ordinary foreign-contract software-freelancer income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed commercial-card sources do not prescribe an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: A foreign CIP applicant must already provide a passport and valid residence permit, plus applicable tax, patent and business-registration documents.
Foreign traders require the applicable residence authorization and commercial documentation.

initial_validity.value: Not a residence status.
initial_validity.notes: The CIP certifies commercial activity and requires a residence permit from a foreign applicant.

extension_rules.notes: The reviewed sources did not establish current renewal duration; renewal would not independently extend immigration status.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Commercial registration is downstream of, not a substitute for, residence authorization.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The commercial-card sources publish no direct permanent-residence path.

path_to_citizenship.notes: A commercial card is not legal residence and therefore cannot independently satisfy the nationality decree’s residence requirement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as a standalone route. It may be required for locally registered activity, but it does not legalize residence and introduces local commercial-substance requirements beyond ordinary foreign-client remote work.

summary.value: No education- or degree-only residence route was identified. A university degree or technical qualification supports a foreign-worker permit application but does not independently grant residence.
summary.notes: The software-engineering degree is supporting evidence for the uncertain self-employed route, not a separate immigration category.

tax_residency_rule.value: The DGI requires a definitive income-tax return from non-diplomatic foreigners staying in Haiti for more than 183 days during the same fiscal year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The DGI also requires returns from persons domiciled in Haiti and non-domiciled persons receiving Haitian-source income; 183 days is therefore not the only possible tax nexus.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate under the official five-band progressive schedule, not the expected effective tax rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This 12% figure is not a confirmed mandatory contribution rate for the target self-employed foreigner. ONA states that compulsory coverage applies to private-sector employees, with 6% withheld from the employee and another 6% paid by the employer. Any person choosing voluntary coverage pays the combined 12% of declared salary. ONA does not state on this page that a self-employed foreign permit holder must enroll, so mandatory status and the permitted declared-salary base require confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed ONA and DGI material publishes no mandatory fixed monthly payment for this foreign self-employed scenario. ONA voluntary coverage is percentage-based.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or inbound-expatriate income-tax regime was identified. Professionals must make three provisional installments based on 75% of the preceding year’s final income tax.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The provisional-payment rule changes payment timing, not the underlying rate.

taxes.caveats: Remote services physically performed from Haiti may create Haitian tax and work-permit exposure even when the client and payment account are abroad. Income sourcing, deductions, business taxes, ONA status, foreign tax credits and treaty availability require Haitian professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with official annual bands from 0% to 30%. Foreigners present for more than 183 days in a fiscal year are expressly listed as definitive-return filers.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in the same fiscal year is an express filing trigger for non-diplomatic foreigners; domicile or Haitian-source income can independently trigger filing.
taxation_system.income_scope: The DGI requires returns from persons domiciled in Haiti and non-domiciled persons receiving Haitian-source income, but the reviewed pages do not expressly classify services performed in Haiti solely for a foreign client.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker exemption was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: ONA compulsory employee coverage is 6% employee plus 6% employer. A person voluntarily enrolling pays the combined 12% of declared salary; mandatory treatment of the target self-employed foreigner is unpublished on the reviewed ONA page.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard’s 30% value is the top marginal rate. DGI also lists 1% CFGDCT on gross salary of at least HTG 5,000 and 1% FDU/CAS on employee gross salary; application to foreign self-employment is not established.

taxation_system.notes: Rates and filing categories are official. The exact source treatment of foreign-client services remains unpublished in the reviewed DGI guidance.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Haiti has no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. If the uncertain self-employed residence/work route is accepted, ordinary income-tax and professional filing rules would apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: ordinary_self_employed_taxation_if_route_approved
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–30% progressive PIT; 30% is the top marginal screening rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Foreigners staying more than 183 days in the same fiscal year are expressly required to file a definitive return; domicile or Haitian-source income may trigger filing earlier.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The DGI requires persons domiciled in Haiti to file and also covers Haitian-source income of non-domiciled persons, but it does not expressly classify the target foreign-client service arrangement.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the reviewed immigration and tax sources.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: ONA publishes compulsory coverage only for private-sector employees: 6% is withheld from the employee and the employer adds 6%. Voluntary participants pay the combined 12% of declared salary. The ONA page does not classify a self-employed foreign work-permit holder as compulsorily insured, and no employer payroll share applies where there is no Haitian employer; enrollment status and declared-income basis therefore require direct ONA confirmation.

fixed_payments.status: no_fixed_monthly_amount_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed amount is published. If voluntary ONA coverage is chosen, the published charge is 12% of declared salary; mandatory enrollment for the target foreign self-employed person is not stated.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The current DIE checklist charges HTG 5,000 for the residence-permit filing. Non-resident visitors pay a US$10 arrival tax, while the Washington embassy lists US$100 for a three-month tourist visa and US$200 for a six-month multiple-entry tourist visa where a visa is required. The 1984 nationality decree separately states a fixed HTG 5,000 naturalization charge, but its current collection amount should be verified. No current official filing page publishing a separate self-employed work-permit fee was located.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A NIF is needed for tax dealings. Professionals make three equal provisional income-tax installments based on 75% of prior-year tax. Patent, professional-card or business fees may apply if local commercial registration is required.
fixed_payments.notes: The residence and naturalization amounts are state filing charges, not monthly taxes. Tourist charges are included for completeness but do not legalize remote work. No digital-nomad levy or fixed freelancer tax was published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being under 183 days avoids the specific long-stay foreigner filing category, but domicile, Haitian-source income, business registration or withholding may still create obligations.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect ordinary progressive PIT up to 30% and local filing obligations; obtain advice on income sourcing and foreign tax relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A NIF is needed. Depending on structure, a patent, CIP, provisional income-tax installments and voluntary or compulsory ONA enrollment may also apply.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No dedicated nomad route or special tax regime exists. Core tax rates and identified fees are published, but the foreign-contract fact pattern, self-employed ONA status and work-permit fee are not addressed by current filing guidance.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant applies directly for a residence permit; zero means no prerequisite residence period, not immediate or guaranteed approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No current transition period to unlimited or permanent residence is published.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The naturalization rule is based on five years of legal residence, not on a confirmed period after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory legal-residence period for ordinary naturalization. Approval remains discretionary and current processing practice is unpublished.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The decree describes ministerial review, an Interior Department moral-character inquiry, presidential decision, publication and oath, but none of the current sources inspected publishes a normal processing time.

key_conditions.value: Complete five years of legal residence; petition the Minister of Justice with a residence permit, identity card and residence certificate; pass the Interior Department’s moral-character inquiry; receive presidential approval published in the official journal; and take the statutory oath. The decree states a fixed HTG 5,000 charge.
key_conditions.notes: The decree does not publish a language examination or quantified income requirement. Current filing forms and absence-tolerance rules were not located.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Article 16 of the 1984 decree allows the ordinary five-year legal-residence period to be reduced to two years for a foreigner who has married a Haitian woman. It does not state a separate minimum duration of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legally valid marriage to a Haitian woman can support a request for the discretionary reduction to two years of legal residence. Marriage itself does not grant nationality or eliminate the naturalization procedure.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The statutory wording is gender-specific. A historical Haitian CEDAW report states that women and men have equal rights concerning residence and work permits for foreign spouses, but current official guidance applying the naturalization reduction to every gender combination was not located.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must still establish legal residence and submit a naturalization petition to the Minister of Justice with a residence permit, identity card and residence certificate. The Interior Department conducts an inquiry into the applicant’s moral character, the President decides the application, and an approved applicant must take the statutory oath and pay the applicable charge. Article 16 says the residence period may be reduced, so the two-year treatment is discretionary rather than automatic. The decree does not publish a cohabitation period, language test or separate sham-marriage test. The marriage and Haitian nationality of the spouse must nevertheless be legally established to invoke the reduction; no current Haitian source inspected specifies documentary standards or consequences particular to a non-genuine marriage beyond loss of eligibility and possible refusal under the ordinary inquiry.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The rule comes from primary 1984 legislation, but current Ministry of Justice filing guidance was unavailable. Its gender-specific text and present-day equal-treatment application require direct confirmation.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Haiti does not provide broad automatic jus soli. Citizenship is principally by descent, with limited territorial or declaration-based categories, including protection for children of unknown or undetermined-nationality parents.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Haiti to two known foreign parents is not generally an automatic citizen. Limited statutory categories may apply where parents are unknown or their nationality cannot be established, while the 1984 decree contains historical declaration-based provisions requiring specialist review.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The false value describes the ordinary two-known-foreign-parent case, not foundlings or statelessness-related exceptions.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child has Haitian nationality by origin when born to a qualifying Haitian father or mother, regardless of birthplace.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Civil registration and proof of the citizen parent’s status may still be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Haitian child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. IOM material reports a work-permit exemption for a foreigner with Haitian children after five years of continuous residence, but this is not automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Verify the exemption and any family-residence option directly with the DIE and labor authority.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent-residence benefit. A migrant father may potentially receive the reported work-permit exemption after five years of continuous residence if he has a Haitian child, subject to authority confirmation.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, the child’s citizenship and lawful residence would need documentation.

settlement_track.summary: Primary nationality legislation confirms a naturalization mechanism after five years of legal residence, without a stated prior permanent-residence requirement. The track remains uncertain because current authorities do not expressly confirm foreign-client-only software work as eligible self-employment or publish filing guidance confirming uninterrupted use of this exact residence/work-permit combination.
settlement_track.notes: Written pre-filing confirmation is needed from the DIE, labor authority and Ministry of Justice. No current naturalization processing standard or self-employed work-permit fee was published.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Self-employed foreigners are contemplated, but published rules do not expressly address services supplied exclusively to a foreign client. The non-competition evidence and residence support-letter requirement may be interpreted as requiring local economic or employer ties.

data.notes: Focused audit added the primary 1984 nationality decree and corroborating constitutional and UN materials. The five-year legal-residence naturalization mechanism and procedural requirements are now substantially clearer, but ordinary foreign-contract remote-work eligibility, current Ministry of Justice practice, self-employed ONA treatment and the separate work-permit fee still require direct confirmation.

data.selection_summary: Honduras has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker visa. The strongest independent alternative is a temporary Permission of Special Stay for exercising a university profession: a degree holder may apply without a local employer by proving capacity to establish a professional practice, but the degree must be incorporated by UNAH and the category appears oriented to practicing locally. Special-permission holders may seek immigrado residence after five consecutive years, while the official naturalization procedure accepts a special-stay permit and the general constitutional threshold is more than three years of legal residence. This is an independent qualification-based settlement possibility, not a confirmed match for simply continuing a foreign software contract.

initial_validity.notes: The category-specific material does not promise a universal initial term.

extension_rules.notes: The underlying authorization and the foreigner identification card have separate administrative renewal requirements.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved Permission of Special Stay permits the foreign professional to reside temporarily and legally in Honduras; registration in the National Registry of Foreigners and issuance of a card follow approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a special-stay permit rather than permanent immigrado residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least five consecutive years with a valid Permission of Special Stay, the holder may apply for immigrado residence, subject to continued compliance and discretionary approval.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate conversion application is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: The official naturalization procedure accepts applicants holding either a residence resolution or a Permission of Special Stay. Most non-Central-American, non-Ibero-American foreigners become constitutionally eligible after more than three consecutive years of legal residence, subject to substantive requirements and discretionary approval.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Central Americans by birth have a one-year threshold; Spaniards and Ibero-Americans by birth have a two-year threshold. Eligibility does not guarantee approval.

best_routes.notes: This route is independent only through the professional-office alternative. It requires Honduran recognition of the degree and is framed around exercising the profession in Honduras. Official sources do not establish that merely working remotely under an unchanged foreign contract, without establishing a Honduran professional practice, satisfies the category. It is settlement-oriented but is a qualification-based alternative rather than an ordinary remote-work match.
