summary.value: A foreign university graduate may seek a temporary Permission of Special Stay to exercise a university profession without a local employer if the applicant incorporates the degree through UNAH and proves financial capacity to establish a professional office. Alternatively, an authenticated services or employment contract can support the category. Immigrado residence is a later conversion after five consecutive years.
summary.notes: This is a local professional-practice category, not a general degree-holder or digital-nomad permit. Applicability to software engineering and a foreign-only client base requires INM and UNAH confirmation.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is treated as tax resident after spending more than 90 days in Honduras during a fiscal year, continuously or cumulatively.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence is distinct from immigration residence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: IHSS publishes current contribution rules for workers and employers, but the reviewed material does not establish one mandatory percentage for an independently practicing foreign professional. Applicability and contribution bases require IHSS confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed sources identify annual or per-filing immigration charges, not a mandatory monthly fixed tax or social-security payment for this independent-professional scenario.

special_tax_regimes.value: Honduras applies territorial taxation. The reviewed current tax and immigration sources do not establish a special digital-nomad, remote-worker or inbound-professional income-tax regime.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Whether services performed physically from Honduras for a foreign client constitute Honduran-source income requires professional source-of-income analysis.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on where services are performed, whether the worker operates personally or through a Honduran business, tax residence, municipal registration, invoicing, IHSS status and foreign-country obligations. Territoriality should not be interpreted as automatically exempting foreign-paid remote work performed in Honduras.

taxation_system.value: Territorial personal-income-tax system with progressive 2026 rates of 0%, 15%, 20% and 25% on taxable Honduran-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 90 days in Honduras during the fiscal year, continuously or cumulatively.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income earned or accrued in Honduras is taxable under the territorial system. The source characterization of foreign-paid services physically performed in Honduras needs professional confirmation.
taxation_system.special_regimes: The reviewed sources do not establish a dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-professional regime.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee and employer IHSS regimes exist, but the current official material reviewed does not establish one mandatory self-employed rate for the independent-professional scenario.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard figure is the 25% top marginal rate, not an effective rate. The official thresholds are annual taxable-income bands for 2026.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax regime was identified. A professional-permit holder is screened under ordinary Honduran territorial and progressive-tax rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: qualification-based professional permit with no nomad regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–25% progressive tax on taxable Honduran-source income; 25% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 90 days in Honduras during the fiscal year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Honduras is territorial, but payment by a foreign client does not by itself establish foreign-source income. Services performed while physically in Honduras may require Honduran-source analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: The reviewed current sources do not establish a special digital-nomad or inbound-professional regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No route-specific exemption was identified. IHSS or payroll obligations depend on whether the applicant is employed, operates a local practice or qualifies for independent affiliation; the reviewed source does not publish one fixed self-employed percentage for this case.

fixed_payments.status: partially confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No single mandatory independent-professional amount is published for this scenario in the reviewed current IHSS material; obtain an IHSS classification before commencing local practice.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Professional special-permission fee USD 100 per approved year; certification HNL 200; foreigner registration USD 20; resident or special-stay card USD 20 per year; stamps and authentication or representation costs are additional.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: First RTN issuance is officially described as free. Municipal industry, commerce and services tax may apply to a local professional business, but the amount varies by municipality and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: Immigration fees are not monthly taxes. Legal-representation, translation, apostille, degree-incorporation and professional-registration expenses are not quantified in the reviewed sources.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Presence of 90 days or less may avoid tax residence, but Honduran-source income and non-resident rules can still apply. Visitor status remains unsuitable for settlement-oriented remote work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: After more than 90 days, ordinary territorial tax rules apply; confirm whether services performed from Honduras for the foreign client are Honduran-source.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A local professional office or individual-merchant activity may require RTN, municipal registration, invoicing, business tax and possibly IHSS compliance. This is materially different from merely retaining a foreign contract.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No route-specific tax concession was identified. Local advice is particularly important for determining the source of remote-service income.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The professional Permission of Special Stay directly grants temporary legal stay upon approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The immigrado category requires at least five consecutive years with a valid special-stay permit and continued card compliance.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization can become available after more than three years of legal residence, and the official procedure accepts a Permission of Special Stay. Immigrado status is not stated as a prerequisite, so eligibility may arise before the five-year conversion.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: For most foreigners, the constitutional rule is more than three consecutive years, so practical eligibility is just after year three. Central Americans by birth require one year; Spaniards and Ibero-Americans by birth require two.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official procedure lists administrative stages but publishes no standard or typical completion time.

key_conditions.value: Continuous legal residence for the nationality-specific period; civil capacity; lawful means of support; good conduct and criminal-record compliance; Spanish literacy and speaking ability; written examination on Honduran history, geography and the Constitution; municipal and income-tax solvency; filing through counsel; and prior renunciation of original nationality unless an applicable dual-nationality treaty removes that requirement. Naturalization is discretionary rather than automatic.
key_conditions.notes: The reviewed sources do not express absence limits as a simple annual day count; continuous residence and migration-movement records are examined.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution creates a naturalization category for a foreign person married to a Honduran by birth without stating a minimum marriage or residence period. This does not make citizenship automatic or immediate.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Honduran by birth can support both a family-link residence application and a constitutionally accelerated naturalization application. Marriage itself does not change either spouse's nationality.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marriage must be documented and, if celebrated abroad, legalized for use in Honduras.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must file and satisfy the naturalization requirements, including documentation, good conduct, lawful support, the knowledge and Spanish examination and generally prior renunciation unless a treaty applies. A marriage certificate does not itself confer nationality. False documents or a sham relationship can lead to refusal, cancellation and other legal consequences; obtain filing advice because the official sources do not publish a simple marriage-duration safe harbor.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The zero-year field records the absence of an express minimum period in the constitutional category, not a promised processing timeline.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution treats persons born in Honduran territory as Hondurans by birth, with narrow exceptions for children of diplomatic agents and transient foreigners who are not subject to Honduran jurisdiction.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Honduras generally acquires Honduran nationality at birth even when both parents are migrants, subject to the narrow constitutional exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' temporary or permanent status is generally not the controlling factor for territorial birthright nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Honduran parent has a descent-based claim and, if born in Honduras, also normally acquires nationality through jus soli.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This does not automatically naturalize the migrant father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Honduran by birth is expressly eligible to seek residence through family connection. The child does not automatically confer permanent residence or citizenship on the parent, and an application with supporting family documentation is still required.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Ordinary naturalization timelines and requirements remain separate.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Honduran-born child can use the parent-child relationship as an independent residence basis. No automatic or constitutionally accelerated citizenship category for a parent of a Honduran child was identified.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The Constitution expressly accelerates naturalization for a spouse, not for a parent merely because the child is Honduran.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15; index positions can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category in Passport Index, not its broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified by the index as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined total of 43 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations. The index separately lists eVisa destinations, which are not included in this combined figure.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 128 and world reach of 64%. Its methodology differs from the Henley index.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only remote work is workable in parts of Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula and the Bay Islands, and EF EPI 2025 places Honduras in the high-proficiency band with a score of 553. Nevertheless, government, immigration, tax, legal and degree-recognition procedures operate in Spanish, so Spanish ability or professional assistance is practically important.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI reflects participating adult test takers and should not be read as universal population fluency.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian cannot be relied on for government procedures or everyday administration. The reviewed official materials provide no Russian- or Ukrainian-language administrative channel; Spanish interpretation and certified translation will generally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Official immigration material requires foreign-language documents to be officially translated into Spanish.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the July 2025 national average monthly income of HNL 9,682 at roughly HNL 26.78/USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current INE releases inspected publish means by worker category, education, sex, activity and location but no national median. ILOSTAT lists a median-monthly-earnings indicator and identifies the 2024 Honduran household survey, but the reviewed public country profile and catalogue did not expose a verifiable current Honduras observation. No USD median is therefore reported.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the lowest monthly statutory minimum shown in the 2026 table, HNL 9,596.64. This is a legal minimum for one employer-size and activity category, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the July 2025 national mean labor income of HNL 9,682.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current, directly verifiable national median amount was published in the reviewed INE bulletins or displayed in the accessible ILOSTAT Honduras profile, so no USD conversion is made.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum salary is not a bounded statutory labor-market measure, and the reviewed official wage publications provide averages, minimum-wage schedules and distribution categories rather than a maximum attainable salary. The highest sectoral mean or highest minimum-wage category is not a national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Lowest monthly statutory minimum in the 2026 table; the applicable minimum varies by economic activity and employer size.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National average monthly labor income of employed persons reported by INE's July 2025 EPHPM. INE's separate employee-only mean is HNL 10,465, so these populations should not be conflated.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Unpublished as a current national amount in the reviewed official releases
median_salary_local_currency.notes: INE's July 2025 labor-market and income bulletins report arithmetic means by category, education, sex, economic activity and urban or rural location, but no national median. INE makes the underlying 2025 EPHPM microdata available in SPSS, meaning a median could be calculated with the survey weights, but the database page does not publish that computed statistic. ILOSTAT's catalogue includes a median-monthly-earnings series, yet the accessible Honduras profile did not display a current numeric observation; an exact value is therefore not inferred.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Not applicable as a national cap; no maximum salary is established or published
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official sources publish average incomes, statutory minimum wages, wage-range distributions and category breakdowns. None defines a maximum possible national salary, and treating the highest observed category mean or highest statutory minimum as a maximum would be misleading.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: National mean monthly labor income of employed persons from INE EPHPM July 2025; minimum is the lowest 2026 statutory monthly minimum-wage category. Median and maximum fields describe the publication status of national statistics, not estimates.
average_citizen_salary.period: July 2025 average income; statutory minimum effective in 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures concern average citizen or resident worker labor income and statutory minimum wages, not immigration income requirements. INE reports HNL 18,483 for public employees, HNL 9,776 for private employees, HNL 8,491 for own-account workers and HNL 18,995 for persons with higher education. The separate INE income bulletin reports an employee-only mean of HNL 10,465. USD conversions are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The labor-market sources are not household-budget measures. Although the labor ministry publishes historical food-basket material, this focused review did not establish a current, consistently comparable national total monthly living-cost budget, so the wage figures should not be treated as a complete cost-of-living estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Not a nomad-only case: the selected university-professional Permission of Special Stay is a temporary legal status that the official naturalization procedure recognizes and that can later support an immigrado application. The material warning is instead that Honduras has no dedicated remote-worker category and an unchanged foreign software contract is not established by the current sources to satisfy the local professional-practice basis.
settlement_track.summary: The university-professional special-stay permit is legal temporary status expressly accepted by the official naturalization procedure, making naturalization potentially available after the applicable constitutional residence period. Immigrado residence is a separate conversion after five consecutive years, and the route remains only a partial fit because its degree-recognition and professional-practice requirements are not equivalent to ordinary foreign-contract remote work.
settlement_track.notes: The route may lead toward citizenship without first obtaining immigrado status, but naturalization is discretionary. Before applying, confirm with INM that software engineering qualifies under the incorporated-profession category and that a foreign-client practice satisfies its professional-office alternative.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker route was identified. The qualification-based professional permit may be filed without a local employer, but it requires UNAH degree incorporation and financial capacity to establish a professional office in Honduras. The official sources do not establish that an unchanged foreign contract alone qualifies.

data.notes: Focused audit retained the independent university-professional special-stay category and clarified its settlement implications. Honduras remains a partial selection because the route is qualification and local-practice based, not designed for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The current INE wage releases do not publish a national median, while a nationwide maximum salary is not an applicable bounded statistic. Exact initial permit duration, self-employed IHSS treatment, source classification of remote-service income, citizenship processing time and acceptance of software engineering under the professional category require filing-level confirmation.

data.selection_summary: Hungary has a potentially qualifying independent route for this profile: the residence permit for guest self-employment covers independently performed remunerated activity and accepts private service or business contracts as evidence. It grants temporary residence and may plausibly lead to an EU residence card after five years because guest self-employment is not among that card’s published exclusions. Filing-level confirmation is still advisable that successive permits and the applicant’s foreign-client software contract satisfy the five-year continuity rules. The White Card fits foreign remote employment but is temporary-only and is not the selected settlement route.

visa_application.title: Enter Hungary electronic immigration application platform
visa_application.notes: Enter Hungary is the official electronic filing platform. Visa-exempt third-country nationals may file an initial guest-self-employment application while lawfully in Hungary; applicants requiring an entry visa generally apply through the competent Hungarian mission.

best_routes.route_name: Residence permit for guest self-employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: NDGAP does not prescribe one fixed monetary minimum for every initial application. Sufficient lawful resources must be demonstrated.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed initial amount; established self-employment may be evidenced by annual income exceeding HUF 7,747,200 (24 × the 2026 monthly minimum wage), equivalent to more than HUF 645,600 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is an accepted evidentiary formula for an already registered self-employed person, not an unequivocal universal initial-application threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed first-application minimum; established self-employment may be evidenced by more than HUF 7,747,200/year (about HUF 645,600 or USD 2,054 per month)
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: HUF formula converted at HUF 314.36 per USD
income_requirement_display.notes: Bank balances, regular income, annual tax evidence or other credible proof may be relevant depending on the application stage.

income_proof_months.notes: The factsheet does not specify a uniform number of prior income or bank-statement months for this route; established applicants may instead need annual tax-authority evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Perform remunerated activity independently or act as chief executive of a qualifying business organisation.
Document the activity through self-employed registration, a detailed activity declaration, a private service or business contract, or other credible evidence.
Demonstrate lawful resources for subsistence, accommodation, healthcare and onward travel.
Provide accommodation, comprehensive healthcare coverage or adequate healthcare funds, a valid passport, onward-travel means and a photograph.
For extension, maintain reporting compliance and at least 90 days of Hungarian residence in the relevant 180-day period.
Obtain a Hungarian tax identification number when Hungarian taxable income exists and register as a private entrepreneur where the activity requires it.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Passport validity can limit the approved period.

extension_rules.value: Extendable for up to 2 additional years, with the initial permit and extension capped at 3 years. NDGAP states that a person wishing to remain longer may file a new issuance application in Hungary at least 40 days before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: A change to another residence purpose generally cannot be filed from within Hungary during or immediately after this status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval directly grants a temporary residence permit for guest self-employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visa-exempt nationals may make an initial application during lawful stay; others normally apply abroad.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential EU residence card after at least 5 years of continuous lawful residence. Guest self-employment is not listed among the EU-card exclusions, although holders are excluded from the separate national residence card.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Because the initial permit and extension cover at most three years, timely reissuance and continuity counting should be confirmed with NDGAP before relying on the five-year pathway.

path_to_citizenship.value: After qualifying long-term residence and registration of a Hungarian domicile, ordinary naturalisation generally requires eight years of continuous residence plus livelihood, housing, criminal-record, security, Hungarian-language and constitutional-knowledge conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The conservative planning timeline is approximately five years to an EU residence card followed by eight years on qualifying residence.

best_routes.notes: This route is a better settlement-oriented fit than the White Card for a genuine foreign-client software freelancer. It does not expressly require a Hungarian employer or client, but contract classification, entrepreneur registration, reissuance and EU-card residence counting merit filing-level confirmation.

rejected_routes.route_name: White Card – residency for digital nomads

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,000 using the official 14 August 2026 MNB rates of HUF 363.28 per EUR and HUF 314.36 per USD.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,000 net per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official threshold is denominated in euros.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,000 net monthly for the preceding 6 months (about USD 3,467)
income_requirement_display.notes: The qualifying income must continue throughout the stay.

income_proof_months.notes: Evidence may include six months of bank statements or employer/tax-authority certification.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment outside Hungary allowing remote electronic work, or ownership of a profitable foreign company managed remotely.
No gainful activity for a Hungarian employer and no ownership interest in a Hungarian company.
Accommodation, healthcare coverage, valid passport and onward-travel means.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year

extension_rules.value: Extendable once for one additional year
extension_rules.notes: Extension requires at least 90 days’ residence during the preceding 180 days.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence as a White Card holder.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The White Card cannot itself reach settlement and an in-country change of purpose is barred. A later settlement path requires leaving and independently qualifying for another permit, such as an EU Blue Card.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: OIF expressly caps White Cards at two years, bars another-purpose applications on this status and excludes holders from the national residence card. The separately published Blue Card and EU residence-card regimes do not make this a remote-contract-only route. Preservation of White Card time was not established; the five-year figure describes the successor qualifying-residence rule.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official conversion from this exact temporary status to qualifying permanent residence or citizenship was established.

rejected_routes.notes: A strong temporary-living fit for foreign remote employment, but expressly temporary-only and therefore rejected for citizenship-oriented selection.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No independent remote-worker income threshold applies because qualifying employment or a domestic-employer arrangement is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The route is employment-based rather than an independent foreign-contract route.

income_requirement_display.value: No independent remote-worker threshold; qualifying employment is required
income_requirement_display.notes: A degree alone does not establish eligibility.

income_proof_months.notes: A prior-income period is not the relevant eligibility test for this rejected route.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying remunerated work and an eligible professional qualification or another listed professional category.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years

extension_rules.value: Extendable for up to 3 years

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct employment-oriented temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential only through general long-term-residence rules after maintaining qualifying employment-based status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not usable for the target foreign-contract profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through a separate qualifying long-term-residence history.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route requires qualifying employment or a domestic-employer arrangement, not ordinary remote work solely for a foreign client.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence permit for seeking a job or starting a business

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The applicant is ineligible without prior qualifying study or research residence in Hungary, so no profile-relevant threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Inapplicable to the current profile.

income_requirement_display.value: Available only following qualifying studies or research completed in Hungary

income_proof_months.notes: A uniform prior-income period was not needed to determine the route’s inapplicability.

key_requirements.requirement: Hold a Hungarian study or research residence permit and complete the corresponding studies or research.

initial_validity.notes: Not material to the current profile’s rejection.

extension_rules.notes: Not material to the current profile’s rejection.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Post-study or post-research transition status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: May lead to another qualifying status, but only after Hungarian studies or research.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through a later qualifying residence route and permanent residence.

rejected_routes.notes: A foreign university degree alone does not qualify; prior Hungarian study or research status is mandatory.

summary.value: No independent degree-only migration route was established for a person educated abroad. The post-study route requires prior Hungarian study or research, while the Hungarian Card requires qualifying work.
summary.notes: The software-engineering degree may support employment eligibility but does not independently create residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: Residence is determined through nationality or permanent-settlement rules, permanent home, centre of vital interests and, where earlier tests do not decide residence, at least 183 days in the calendar year. Treaty tie-breakers may override domestic treatment.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Remaining below 183 days does not by itself prevent Hungarian residence or Hungarian-source taxation.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Flat personal income-tax rate for ordinary income; it is not the all-in effective burden.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Standard insured-person contribution. Cross-border coordination, treaty coverage and the worker’s classification can alter applicability.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly charge applies to every White Card or guest-self-employment holder. Percentage contributions, entrepreneur minimum bases or an eligible business-tax regime depend on registration and contract structure.

special_tax_regimes.value: Private-entrepreneur, flat-rate and KATA regimes exist under separate eligibility conditions. NAV’s 2026 summary describes a 9% entrepreneurial income-tax rate and a HUF 50,000 monthly KATA amount for eligible taxpayers, but neither is a digital-nomad exemption and eligibility is not assumed for foreign-client work.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Professional advice is needed before selecting an entrepreneur regime.

taxes.caveats: Immigration and tax status are separate. Work physically performed in Hungary may be taxable there even when paid from abroad. Liability depends on residence, income classification, social-insurance coverage, foreign-payer obligations, treaty relief, entrepreneur registration and possible permanent-establishment exposure.

taxation_system.value: Hungary generally applies flat 15% personal income tax. Residents are normally taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on Hungarian-source income, subject to treaties.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-home, centre-of-vital-interests and 183-day tests apply, subject to domestic nationality/settlement rules and treaty tie-breakers.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Hungarian-source income for non-residents, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No White Card or digital-nomad tax holiday was identified. Entrepreneur and KATA regimes have separate eligibility rules.
taxation_system.social_security: The standard insured-person contribution is 18.5%; entrepreneur minimum bases or cross-border social-security coordination may apply.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable: ordinary PIT is flat at 15%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: From the first taxable HUF of ordinary personal income
tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary taxable personal income, subject to exemptions and allowances
tax_brackets.notes: Flat PIT; deductions and income classification affect the taxable base.

taxation_system.notes: The 15% headline rate is well supported, but the applicant’s total burden cannot be stated without resolving insurance, registration, deductions and treaty treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The selected guest-self-employment route receives no special nomad exemption: ordinary Hungarian personal and business tax rules apply, generally including 15% PIT on the applicable tax base plus social-security or entrepreneur obligations where applicable.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Guest self-employment under ordinary Hungarian personal and business tax rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 15% flat PIT screening rate; social security and business taxes may be additional
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-home, centre-of-interests and 183-day tests apply, with treaty tie-breakers where relevant.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are generally taxable on worldwide income; services performed from Hungary may be taxable there even when paid by a foreign client.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No official White Card, digital-nomad or general inbound-worker PIT exemption was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The standard insured-person contribution is 18.5%; exact liability depends on employment/self-employment classification and cross-border coverage.

fixed_payments.status: structure_dependent_not_universal
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed amount. Percentage contributions and entrepreneur minimum bases may apply; HUF 50,000 monthly KATA applies only if separately eligible.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: EUR 110 when filed abroad with an entry visa; HUF 39,000 for an in-person domestic application; HUF 26,000 for electronic filing or extension.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Tax-number, private-entrepreneur, VAT and local-business-tax obligations require case-specific review.
fixed_payments.notes: Private healthcare coverage is also an immigration requirement, but no official fixed insurance premium is prescribed.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 183 days does not automatically eliminate Hungarian tax because permanent-home, centre-of-interests, source and treaty rules remain relevant.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident generally reports worldwide income at the 15% PIT rate, with possible treaty relief and separate social-security analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Obtain a tax number and, where required, private-entrepreneur registration; determine expense, flat-rate, contribution, VAT and local-business-tax treatment before invoicing.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Official sources establish the headline rates and registration duties; exact freelancer contributions remain contract- and registration-specific.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is granted directly on approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The EU residence card generally requires five years of continuous lawful residence. Successive guest-self-employment permit counting should be confirmed before relying on it.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation generally follows eight years of qualifying residence after permanent residence and domicile registration prerequisites are met.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Conservative planning estimate: approximately five years to an EU residence card plus eight years under the ordinary naturalisation route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: An official embassy page provides a statutory period for simplified naturalisation, but no reliable typical processing duration for ordinary residence-based naturalisation was established; the simplified procedure’s timing was not generalized.

key_conditions.value: Maintain lawful continuous residence, renew or reapply on time, satisfy presence and reporting duties, obtain the EU residence card, register a Hungarian domicile and meet livelihood, housing, criminal-record, security, Hungarian-language and constitutional-knowledge requirements.
key_conditions.notes: The EU residence-card process also requires the current cultural-knowledge documentation specified by NDGAP.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Preferential residence-based naturalisation may be available after three years of qualifying residence where the applicant has been married to a Hungarian citizen for at least three years or has a minor Hungarian child. A separate simplified route recognizes ten years of marriage, reduced to five years where the couple has a child.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage counts toward the applicable duration condition. Marriage alone does not automatically grant citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The applicable shortcut depends on whether the applicant uses residence-based preferential naturalisation or simplified naturalisation.

requirements_and_risks.value: Criminal-record, security and Hungarian-language conditions remain relevant; the residence-based route also requires livelihood, housing and qualifying residence. Marriage and child documents may require Hungarian registration, legalization and translation. False documents or a sham relationship can cause refusal or withdrawal.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The relationship must be genuine and properly documented.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Hungary to foreign parents does not generally confer citizenship. Narrow safeguards exist for foundlings and certain children who would otherwise lack established citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Hungary to two foreign parents normally does not acquire Hungarian citizenship. Narrow anti-statelessness and foundling presumptions may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A child may qualify for immigration residence through family rules, which is distinct from citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child is Hungarian by descent if either parent is a Hungarian citizen.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This does not automatically naturalise the migrant parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a minor Hungarian child can support family residence and may reduce the qualifying residence period for preferential naturalisation to three years; it does not automatically grant the parent permanent residence or citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A legally recognized migrant father of a Hungarian minor may qualify for family residence and, after satisfying the preferential residence period and other conditions, naturalisation. Fatherhood alone creates no automatic citizenship.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Do not substitute the White Card for guest self-employment. The White Card is capped at two years and blocks an in-country change of purpose and the national residence card.
settlement_track.summary: Guest self-employment is an independent temporary-residence route that can plausibly reach an EU residence card after five years because it is not among that card’s published exclusions. Citizenship then requires qualifying permanent residence and the ordinary naturalisation period; confirm that successive guest-self-employment permits count continuously.
settlement_track.notes: The route requires conversion to the EU residence card. Confidence is reduced because the immigration pages do not expressly state in one place that successive reissued guest-self-employment permits count toward the five-year period.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route accepts independently performed remunerated activity and private service or business contracts and does not publish a mandatory Hungarian employer or client requirement. Genuine self-employment, registration and adequate resources must still be documented.

data.notes: The focused unresolved-field audit replaces the previous non-schema maximum-salary marker with a documented null. Current KSH sources publish averages, medians, subgroup averages and an open-ended top earnings band, but no nationwide maximum. Related USD salary and income-display conversions were refreshed using the official 14 August 2026 MNB exchange rate. The immigration conclusion remains medium-confidence because the guest-self-employment-to-EU-residence counting issue merits confirmation before filing.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The White Card cannot itself reach settlement and an in-country change of purpose is barred. A later settlement path requires leaving and independently qualifying for another permit, such as an EU Blue Card.
requirements: End the White Card route and use the appropriate application procedure abroad.
For an EU Blue Card, obtain qualifying employment in Hungary and meet qualification and salary requirements.
Meet the later EU residence-card requirements, including five qualifying years, subsistence, insurance and the applicable cultural-knowledge requirement.
reviewed_route_names: White Card – residency for digital nomads
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: OIF expressly caps White Cards at two years, bars another-purpose applications on this status and excludes holders from the national residence card. The separately published Blue Card and EU residence-card regimes do not make this a remote-contract-only route. Preservation of White Card time was not established; the five-year figure describes the successor qualifying-residence rule.

data.selection_summary: Iceland no longer has a current ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route. The former long-term visa for remote workers was repealed in May 2026. Its replacement short-term residence permit is limited to specified visits, does not authorize ordinary work, cannot be renewed, does not establish legal domicile, and cannot lead to permanent residence. Work-based residence requires a specific Icelandic employer and job. Iceland therefore does not fit the requested independent remote-work-to-citizenship profile.

summary.value: Admission to full-time study at an Icelandic university can support an independently filed student residence permit, normally granted and renewed for up to one year at a time. It is education-based rather than a route based merely on an existing foreign degree. Student residence ordinarily is not itself a permanent-residence basis, although limited combined counting may apply after at least two years on a qualifying permit and at least two previous student years. Graduates of Icelandic degree programs may renew for up to 18 months to seek qualifying employment.
summary.notes: Useful only with genuine Icelandic enrollment. It is not an independent skilled-migration or foreign-contract remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: A stay of six months or longer in any 12-month period generally creates Icelandic residence and unlimited tax liability from arrival; residents are taxed on worldwide income. A shorter stay generally creates limited liability on Iceland-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Income sourcing, treaty residence, foreign-employer payroll duties, and foreign-tax credits require case-specific analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top 2026 marginal withholding rate including the published standard municipal component. It is a screening ceiling, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Published mandatory employee pension contribution. The 2026 general employer payroll tax is separately listed as 6.35%; foreign-employer and self-employed treatment may differ.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the ISK 22,200 annual broadcasting fee and ISK 14,614 Senior Citizen’s Construction Fund fee, using ISK 125.53/USD. These charges apply only above the published income threshold and are not nomad fees.

special_tax_regimes.value: An approved foreign expert employed by an Iceland-domiciled entity or a foreign company with an Icelandic permanent establishment may have only 75% of employment income included in the taxable base during the first three years.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Requires committee approval and scarce expertise. It does not fit an ordinary employee of a foreign company without an Icelandic permanent establishment and does not create immigration eligibility.

taxes.caveats: Iceland has no current digital-nomad route. Results depend on physical work location, income source, employee versus contractor status, the foreign employer’s Icelandic presence, pension and social-security coordination, VAT or business registration, and treaty provisions.

taxation_system.value: Progressive state and municipal personal income taxation. The combined published 2026 withholding brackets are 31.49%, 37.99%, and 46.29%, with a monthly personal tax credit of ISK 72,492.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Six months or longer in a 12-month period generally creates unlimited liability from arrival; shorter stays generally produce limited liability on Iceland-source income.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Iceland-source income for persons with limited liability, subject to treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Approved foreign experts may exclude 25% of qualifying remuneration from the taxable base for their first three years, subject to employer and approval conditions.
taxation_system.social_security: Published ordinary rules include a 4% employee pension contribution and 6.35% general employer payroll tax; cross-border and self-employed treatment needs individual review.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Rates are marginal. The personal tax credit reduces computed tax, so the top rate must not be interpreted as the expected effective rate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment-income withholding in the first monthly bracket
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold uses ISK 125.53/USD; the personal credit can materially reduce effective tax.

tax_brackets.applies_to: The portion of monthly employment income within the second bracket
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount is the approximate upper threshold; the lower threshold is about USD 3,968.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Only the portion exceeding the top threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax.

taxation_system.notes: Official 2026 figures; individual cross-border classification remains fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No current digital-nomad tax category exists because the remote-worker visa was repealed. A person lawfully living in Iceland under another status is subject to ordinary residence, source, payroll, pension, and business-tax rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No current digital-nomad route; ordinary tax rules only under another lawful status
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 46.29% top marginal ordinary rate; not a nomad-specific or expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Six months or more in a 12-month period generally creates unlimited tax liability from arrival.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is taxable for residents. For shorter stays, the sourcing of compensation for services performed in Iceland and treaty treatment require professional review.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad regime. The foreign-expert reduction requires a qualifying Icelandic employer or Icelandic permanent establishment and approval.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary published rules include a 4% employee pension contribution and 6.35% employer payroll tax; cross-border coordination is fact-specific.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed tax or contribution
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed nomad contribution; ordinary percentage-based rules may apply under another lawful status.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No current remote-worker visa fee. Other published fees include ISK 80,000 for a first work-residence application, ISK 70,000 for a student application, ISK 60,000 for permanent residence, and ISK 60,000 for citizenship.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Qualifying taxpayers may face the annual broadcasting and Senior Citizen’s Construction Fund fees. VAT is 24% standard and 11% reduced; business obligations require separate review.
fixed_payments.notes: General charges do not establish eligibility to live or work remotely in Iceland.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay under six months generally leaves limited liability on Iceland-source income, but immigration permission and work-income sourcing must be determined separately. The short-term permit does not authorize ordinary remote work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If lawfully resident under another status for at least six months, expect worldwide-income reporting from arrival and ordinary progressive rates, subject to treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Business registration does not legalize immigration status. Someone already entitled to independent activity must separately assess income tax, pension, social security, VAT, payroll, and presumptive-remuneration rules.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence that no current nomad-specific regime exists; individual cross-border tax outcomes require contract, treaty, and residence details.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker temporary-residence route exists, so a numeric value would misleadingly imply current eligibility.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General rule for someone already holding a residence permit that qualifies as a permanent-residence basis; it does not apply to the repealed visa or short-term permit.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Illustrative arithmetic where permanent residence follows four qualifying years and ordinary naturalization requires seven years. There is no universal separate three-year PR-holding requirement.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General ordinary naturalization residence requirement, not a timeline available through a current remote-worker route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Directorate publishes a changing queue/status page rather than a stable typical citizenship-processing duration. No reliable fixed number could be established.

key_conditions.value: A third-country applicant normally needs permanent residence, seven years of legal domicile and continuous residence, an Icelandic-language test, satisfactory identity, support and tax compliance, and acceptable criminal history. Permanent residence generally requires four continuous qualifying years, absence limits, Icelandic study or testing, and secure means.
key_conditions.notes: Iceland permits dual citizenship, but consequences under the applicant’s other nationality require separate verification.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship may be available after four years of Icelandic domicile since marriage if the Icelandic spouse has held citizenship for at least five years. Permanent residence may be available after three continuous qualifying years living with the Icelandic spouse.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support spouse residence but does not itself grant permanent residence or citizenship. The citizenship shortcut counts Icelandic domicile since marriage.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Registered cohabitation has distinct rules, including five years of legal residence for the citizenship shortcut.

requirements_and_risks.value: The couple must intend to share a permanent address, and the marriage must qualify for Icelandic registration. Authorities may require evidence of a genuine relationship and compliance with residence, support, language, and other requirements.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Misrepresentation or a sham marriage can cause refusal, revocation, immigration consequences, and possible criminal liability. Marriage between two migrants does not create the citizen-spouse shortcut.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Iceland alone does not generally confer citizenship. Citizenship is primarily transmitted by an Icelandic parent, with limited foundling and statelessness protections.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Iceland to two non-Icelandic migrant parents does not ordinarily become Icelandic automatically. Narrow foundling and statelessness provisions may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Citizenship by descent under each parent’s national law must also be checked.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: For a child born after 1 July 2018, one Icelandic-citizen parent is sufficient for automatic Icelandic citizenship at birth, subject to parentage and registration.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This does not automatically naturalize the migrant parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen or lawfully resident minor child can support a parent-residence application only in defined custody, contact, residence, or necessity circumstances. Birth of a child does not automatically grant a parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Special permanent-residence treatment for a child of a permanent-resident custodial parent benefits the child, not automatically the parent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence. A migrant father may seek parent residence only where the statutory custody, access, residence, and necessity conditions are met.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: If the Icelandic parent normally cares for the child in Iceland, the migrant father may not satisfy the necessity requirement.

rank.notes: Current Henley online ranking captured during this review.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley access score includes destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance, including visa-on-arrival categories Henley counts.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Neither inspected index supplied a reliable, mutually exclusive visa-in-advance total consistent with Henley’s methodology.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Henley does not expose a separate Iceland VOA/eTA total in the inspected ranking, and Passport Index did not provide a dependable summarized breakdown.

passport.notes: Rank and access figures can change when destination entry rules change.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is highly practical for many daily interactions, international technology work, tourism, and major government information pages. Icelandic remains important for long-term integration, courts, permanent residence, and citizenship testing.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current official population-wide English-proficiency percentage was established; this is a qualitative assessment.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and cannot be assumed sufficient for ordinary work or government dealings. Interpreters in both languages and dedicated Ukrainian information services exist, but Icelandic or English is substantially more practical.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Dedicated Ukrainian services are substantially connected to collective protection and are not a general remote-worker route.

cost_of_living_note.value: Iceland is exceptionally expensive by European standards: preliminary 2025 PPP data put household-consumption prices at 173.5 with EU27=100, including food and non-alcoholic beverages at 155.8 and housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels at 178.0. HMS reports that rent averaged 40% of renter households’ disposable income in 2025 and that 47% of renters faced housing costs above 40% of disposable income. Immigrant renters averaged just over ISK 243,000 monthly rent in January 2026, versus just under ISK 213,000 for native renters, partly reflecting location and landlord mix.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The 2025 international price-level figures are preliminary and compare price levels rather than affordability after wages. Statistics Iceland’s CPI page confirms current price-change monitoring but does not publish a universal household budget. Rent figures describe surveyed or registered renter households, not a standard budget for every remote worker.

data.selection_summary: India does not offer a current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or self-employed residence route for a software engineer working solely for a foreign client.
