Tourist visas are not extendable under the general visa-provision table.

initial_validity.value: The portal lists 30-day, one-year and five-year e-Tourist variants; actual permitted stay and entry conditions depend on nationality and the issued authorization.
initial_validity.notes: Long visa validity does not itself authorize continuous residence or employment.

extension_rules.value: The official general table marks Tourist Visas as non-extendable.
extension_rules.notes: Exceptional emergency powers should not be treated as a planned residence route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed. A tourist or e-Tourist authorization remains a visitor category.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No ordinary visitor-to-freelancer legalization procedure was found.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: India's identified Permanent Residency Status is an investor scheme, not a conversion from tourism.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from this status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation requires qualifying residence and does not make tourist status a settlement route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected: this is a visitor category, not a lawful foreign-contract remote-work residence or citizenship track.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No ordinary foreign-remote-worker monthly income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A ₹1 crore annual gross-sales/turnover condition is associated with certain in-country Business Visa extensions, but it is not a remote-worker income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold; certain extensions require ₹1 crore annual business turnover
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: ₹1 crore annual gross sales/turnover for the relevant business activity in specified extension cases
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a genuine-business requirement, not permission to reside as a foreign-client contractor.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-income lookback period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Documents proving a bona fide business purpose, such as company correspondence, are required.
Registration with FRRO/FRO is required when aggregate Business Visa stay exceeds 180 days in a calendar year.
A Business Visa is generally non-convertible to another visa category except specified cases.

initial_validity.value: Up to five years under the general visa-provision table, subject to nationality, mission decision and stay conditions.
initial_validity.notes: Visa validity is not equivalent to permanent or qualifying residence.

extension_rules.value: Potential extension up to five years is described for shorter grants, subject to conditions including qualifying business turnover; the category is generally non-convertible.
extension_rules.notes: The applicant's ordinary foreign software contract does not by itself establish the required Indian business purpose.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No separate ordinary temporary-residence status or foreign-remote-worker conversion was confirmed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: FRRO registration records authorized stay; it does not transform the visa into a qualifying freelance residence route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Only the separate capital-intensive foreign-investor PRS scheme was identified.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Ordinary Business Visa holders do not thereby qualify for PRS.

path_to_citizenship.value: No confirmed citizenship path from an ordinary Business Visa.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation remains discretionary and residence-based; the exact visa-time treatment would require case-specific confirmation.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected: the category is for bona fide business activities and is generally non-convertible, not an ordinary digital-nomad or foreign-client freelance residence route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Derived from the general US$25,000 annual salary floor. Listed exceptions include ethnic cooks, certain language teachers/translators and embassy staff.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official FAQ expresses the benchmark in US dollars.

income_requirement_display.value: More than US$25,000 per year (about US$2,083 per month)
income_requirement_display.notes: This threshold applies to sponsored employment and does not create eligibility for an independent foreign-contract worker.

income_proof_months.notes: The official material requires proposed employment documents rather than a historical remote-income period.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment or appointment by an Indian registered organization, or by a foreign organization executing a project in India.
The sponsoring employer or organization is identified on the visa.
Proof of employment, appointment terms and contract conditions.
The role generally must be skilled or qualified rather than routine work for which qualified Indians are available.

initial_validity.value: Generally one year or the contract period under the official visa-provision table.
initial_validity.notes: Actual validity is mission- and contract-dependent.

extension_rules.value: Extendable in India subject to continuing eligible sponsored employment and immigration approval.
extension_rules.notes: The route remains tied to India-connected employment.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Provides an employment-authorized visa stay, not an independently obtained remote-worker residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It fails the selection because sponsorship and India-connected work are required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No general employment-to-permanent-residence transition was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The PRS material concerns qualifying foreign investors.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may theoretically be considered after the statutory residence history, but no automatic Employment Visa-to-citizenship track exists.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the local-sponsor mismatch.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant's ordinary contract is with a foreign client outside India and does not constitute the required sponsored India-connected employment.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permanent Residency Status for Foreign Investors

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Eligibility is investment- and job-creation-based, not monthly-income-based.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: ₹10 crore within 18 months or ₹25 crore within 36 months
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Substantial FDI-route capital investment is required.

income_requirement_display.value: ₹10 crore within 18 months or ₹25 crore within 36 months, plus 20 Indian jobs annually
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an investor program outside the ordinary remote-worker profile.

income_proof_months.notes: The scheme tests invested capital and ongoing job creation, not prior personal income.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying foreign direct investment of ₹10 crore within 18 months or ₹25 crore within 36 months.
Creation of at least 20 jobs for resident Indians every financial year.
Security clearance and annual investment/compliance documentation.

initial_validity.value: An initial B-4 Investor Visa for 18 or 36 months, followed—after satisfying the conditions—by PRS for 10 years.
initial_validity.notes: Despite its name, PRS is issued for a renewable fixed period.

extension_rules.value: PRS may be renewed for another 10 years, subject to continued compliance.
extension_rules.notes: Annual filings and scheme conditions continue to matter.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Initial B-4 Investor Visa while completing the investment conditions.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Available only to a qualifying investor.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct application for 10-year PRS after fulfilling the investment and employment conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is the only explicit PRS route located, but it is excluded by the applicant profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: No automatic PRS-to-citizenship entitlement was confirmed; general naturalisation remains separately discretionary.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Whether all PRS time qualifies should be verified before relying on it.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial investment and local job creation, which the applicant context expressly excludes.

summary.value: A Student Visa can be obtained without an employer after admission to an Indian institution, but it is an education-specific visa rather than an independent degree-based skilled residence route. No points-tested or university-degree-only permanent-residence route comparable to skilled-independent migration was found.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing degree does not independently qualify them for Indian residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally resident for a financial year after at least 182 days in India, or at least 60 days in that year plus at least 365 days during the preceding four years. Special substitutions apply mainly to Indian citizens and persons of Indian origin.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence is tested separately each financial year. Treaty residence and source-of-income rules can modify the practical result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top ordinary marginal slab under the default new regime for AY 2026-27, before surcharge and 4% health and education cess; it is not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No mandatory self-employed or digital-nomad contribution rate was established because no such immigration route exists. EPF commonly uses a 12% employee and 12% employer rate for covered employment, subject to coverage and social-security-agreement exceptions, but that cannot safely be assigned to an independent foreign contractor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly social-security, health-insurance or freelancer payment applies to a nonexistent remote-worker category. Visa fees vary by nationality and category.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker tax regime was found. Resident and ordinarily resident individuals are generally taxable on worldwide income; RNOR and nonresident scopes are narrower.
special_tax_regimes.notes: RNOR treatment can be important for newcomers but depends on prior residence history and whether a business is controlled or profession set up in India.

taxes.caveats: Physical presence, where services are performed, receipt of income in India, RNOR status, business/profession characterization, permanent-establishment issues and an applicable double-tax treaty can change the result. Obtain Indian tax advice before working from India.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax. Under the default new regime for AY 2026-27, ordinary taxable income progresses from 0% to 30%; resident rebate, surcharge and 4% cess can materially alter liability.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally 182 days, or 60 days plus 365 days in the preceding four years, subject to statutory exceptions.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident and ordinarily resident individuals are generally taxed on worldwide income. RNOR individuals generally exclude foreign income unless derived from a business controlled or profession set up in India; nonresidents are generally taxed on Indian-received or Indian-accruing/deemed income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated nomad regime. RNOR is a general residence classification, not a digital-nomad concession.
taxation_system.social_security: No self-employed nomad contribution regime was identified. Covered employment can trigger EPF obligations, commonly 12% from employee and employer, subject to establishment coverage and international-worker/SSA rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 30% value is the top base marginal slab, not an effective rate. The official page also identifies surcharge at high incomes and a 4% health and education cess on tax plus surcharge.

tax_brackets.notes: USD conversion uses approximately ₹96.3665 per US$ from the cited July 17, 2026 reference-rate archive.
Upper threshold shown approximately in USD.
Surcharge and 4% cess may apply in addition.

taxation_system.notes: Rates shown are for AY 2026-27 and should be rechecked for the applicant's actual assessment year and income classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because India has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status. If a person is otherwise lawfully present and taxable, ordinary residence, source and progressive-rate rules apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No qualifying digital-nomad route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive, 0%–30% base slabs; 30% is the top screening rate before surcharge and 4% cess
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally 182 days, or 60 days plus 365 days over the preceding four years, with statutory exceptions.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: ROR residents are generally taxable on worldwide income. RNOR and nonresident treatment is narrower, but services physically performed in India and Indian receipt/source rules require professional analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific contribution. EPF rules concern covered employment and international workers; an independent foreign-client arrangement was not assigned a contribution percentage.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal amount confirmed; covered employment may trigger percentage-based EPF.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Visa fees vary by nationality and category; no remote-worker residence-card fee exists.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific fixed tax or municipal freelancer levy was identified. GST and business-registration consequences depend on actual activities and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: Absence of a route-specific payment does not mean a person can legally work under a visitor visa.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Nonresident status does not automatically mean zero Indian tax: Indian-received, Indian-accruing or deemed income can remain taxable, and immigration authorization is a separate issue.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: An ROR remote worker could face Indian tax on worldwide income at ordinary progressive rates, with treaty/foreign-tax-credit analysis required.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Tax or business registration cannot by itself legalize immigration status; no visitor-to-self-employed residence conversion was found.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is tax screening, not advice. The immigration route fails independently of tax treatment.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker temporary-residence route exists, so no route-specific time can be stated.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No ordinary remote-worker temporary-to-permanent transition was found. The separate investor PRS route is excluded.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Indian naturalisation is based on statutory residence history rather than a general PR-plus-fixed-years formula.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation requires residence/service throughout the 12 months immediately before applying plus an aggregate 11 years during the preceding 14 years. This is a general minimum residence history, not a path available from the rejected remote-work scenario.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable official typical end-to-end processing duration was published on the materials inspected; naturalisation is discretionary and security/document checks can vary.

key_conditions.value: For general naturalisation: full age and capacity; lawful residence history; good character; adequate knowledge of an Eighth Schedule language; intention to reside in India or enter qualifying India-connected service; oath of allegiance; and an undertaking to renounce existing citizenship if accepted. India does not generally retain dual citizenship after voluntary acquisition of another nationality.
key_conditions.notes: A valid residential permit is required for the online naturalisation filing. No qualifying permit exists for the ordinary remote-worker profile identified here.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The statutory route is for a person married to an Indian citizen who is ordinarily resident in India for seven years. The official definition requires residence throughout the final 12 months and at least six years during the preceding eight years; it is not simply seven years of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can establish the relationship element, but does not waive the required ordinary residence or valid immigration status.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage alone does not confer citizenship or permanent residence automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must provide a valid foreign passport, residential permit/LTV, proof of the spouse's Indian citizenship and a registered marriage certificate. Registration remains governmental rather than automatic; false documents, sham marriage or unlawful residence can lead to refusal and immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official materials inspected do not establish an automatic PR grant merely through marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For births in India on or after 3 December 2004, citizenship by birth generally requires both parents to be Indian citizens, or one Indian-citizen parent and the other parent not to be an illegal migrant. Earlier cohorts have different rules.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in India on or after 3 December 2004 does not acquire citizenship merely from birth when neither parent is an Indian citizen.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Diplomatic and enemy-alien exceptions also exist; anti-statelessness or exceptional facts require separate review.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is an Indian citizen, a child born in India on or after 3 December 2004 is generally a citizen by birth provided the other parent is not an illegal migrant.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This describes the child's status, not automatic citizenship for the migrant father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of an Indian-citizen child does not automatically naturalize the foreign parent or create a general permanent-residence entitlement. Any family/dependent visa must be applied for separately under the applicable immigration rules.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No specific automatic parent-of-citizen settlement rule was confirmed in the official sources inspected.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or PR benefit. A migrant father may have a basis to seek an appropriate family/entry status depending on the other parent and child, but filing-level eligibility requires confirmation from the Indian mission or FRRO.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not rely on the child's citizenship as an independent shortcut for the father.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank reported by Passport Index on the research date; index methodologies and ranks can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index separates visa-free access from visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index also separately lists destinations requiring eVisas or other prior electronic permissions, so this is not the complement of the mobility score.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 42 visa-on-arrival plus 5 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 72, composed of 25 visa-free, 42 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations. Figures are index snapshots rather than guarantees of admission.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is used for Union official purposes alongside Hindi and is widely usable in technology and major urban business environments, but proficiency varies sharply by region. EF EPI 2025 ranked India 74th with a score of 484; several major technology cities scored materially higher than the national score.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: India has no constitutionally declared national language; Hindi is the Union's official language and English continues for Union official purposes. State official languages vary.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not Union official languages and cannot be expected for routine administration or daily life. English or the relevant regional Indian language is substantially more practical.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national dataset quantifying Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of ₹22,699 average monthly earnings for regular wage/salaried workers in PLFS 2025 using ₹96.3665 per US$ from July 17, 2026. It is not an all-worker or software-engineer average.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official PLFS publication reports averages but not a directly comparable national median monthly regular salary.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: India does not have one directly comparable national statutory minimum wage in the inspected source; wage floors vary by jurisdiction, occupation and skill category.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the official ₹22,699 monthly average for regular wage/salaried employees in 2025.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No comparable official national median was established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A national maximum salary is not meaningful and the official summary does not publish one.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: No single national minimum applicable to all workers was established from the inspected official data.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: All-India rural-plus-urban average for persons in regular wage/salaried employment, current weekly status, 2025.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published in the inspected PLFS summary.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published and not inferred from raw survey outliers.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average nominal monthly earnings of regular wage/salaried employees in current weekly status
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 annual PLFS
average_citizen_salary.notes: This is the best current official wage measure located, but it excludes self-employed and casual-worker earnings and is not a software-engineering salary benchmark.

cost_of_living_note.value: India's purchasing power and household-consumption conditions differ substantially from nominal USD comparisons, and costs vary greatly by city. No defensible single current national monthly remote-worker budget was established from the official sources inspected.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A cautious qualitative note is retained instead of inserting a crowdsourced city budget as a national figure.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourist/eVisa or ordinary business presence must not be treated as a digital-nomad settlement route. No visitor-to-self-employed legalization path was confirmed.
settlement_track.summary: India has no qualifying independent route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. General naturalisation exists, but the applicant would first need a different lawful status—normally sponsored employment, family eligibility or excluded substantial investment—and no conversion from the rejected visitor/business scenario is confirmed.
settlement_track.notes: The general 12-year statutory naturalisation history is not entered as route-specific years because the selected profile has no qualifying entry/residence route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The current official category set contains no dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence option. Tourist status is visitor-only; business status requires a bona fide business purpose and is generally non-convertible; employment requires India-connected sponsorship.

data.notes: The previous result's negative selection is preserved but substantially strengthened with current official visa, citizenship, tax, language and labor-market sources. Remaining nulls are limited to facts that are inapplicable without a route or not defensibly published, including a route income threshold, general employment-to-PR timing, citizenship processing time, comparable median wage and national maximum wage.

data.selection_summary: Indonesia’s active E33G Remote Worker Visa fits an ordinary employee working remotely for a company established outside Indonesia. It is independently filed without an Indonesian sponsor, grants a one-year limited-stay permit (ITAS), is renewable, and is officially described as transferable to another stay permit. E33G is classified as a second-home remote-worker category, and current immigration rules allow eligible second-home ITAS holders to convert to permanent stay (ITAP) after three consecutive years. Citizenship law counts residence on an ITAS or ITAP toward the general five-consecutive-year naturalization requirement, making this a credible citizenship track, although Indonesian-language ability, stable income, good character, and avoidance of adult dual nationality are required.

visa_application.title: Indonesia eVisa portal — E33G Remote Worker Visa
visa_application.notes: The official E33G instructions require an individual eVisa account and online application. No Indonesian sponsor is required. The public portal sometimes blocks automated access, so the detailed checklist was verified through an Indonesian immigration-office page reproducing the current national visa classification.

best_routes.route_name: E33G Remote Worker Visa / Limited Stay Permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official threshold is US$60,000 per year, equivalent to US$5,000 per month. A separate bank balance of at least US$2,000 must be shown through statements covering the preceding three months.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Approximately IDR 89,180,000 per month (IDR 1.070 billion per year)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Approximation uses Bank Indonesia’s 14 August 2026 JISDOR rate of IDR 17,836 per US dollar. The published threshold remains denominated in US dollars.

income_requirement_display.value: US$5,000/month (US$60,000/year), plus a US$2,000 bank balance shown over 3 months
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Approximately IDR 89.18 million/month at IDR 17,836 per US$1
income_requirement_display.notes: The US$2,000 amount is a minimum available balance, not additional monthly income.

income_proof_months.notes: The general financial-evidence requirement is a personal bank statement covering the preceding three months. The page separately requires proof of annual salary or income of at least US$60,000.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment agreement with a company established outside Indonesia; because the published route is framed around employment, a pure independent-contractor agreement should be confirmed with Immigration before filing.
Valid national passport, recent color photograph, curriculum vitae and itinerary.
Personal bank statements for the preceding three months showing at least US$2,000 or equivalent.
Proof of salary or income of at least US$60,000 per year.
No Indonesian sponsor is required; the applicant files through an individual eVisa account.

The holder may perform assignments for the overseas company but must not undertake unauthorized Indonesian work, sell goods or services locally, or receive remuneration from Indonesian persons or entities.

initial_validity.value: 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The e-ITAS and re-entry permit are issued automatically upon admission at the immigration checkpoint.

extension_rules.value: Renewable online, generally in one-year increments; the current ITAS classification table places E33G among one-year permits whose aggregate ITAS duration may not exceed six years.
extension_rules.notes: Continued eligibility and updated supporting documents must be maintained. Conversion to ITAP may become available before the six-year ITAS ceiling.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct: entry on E33G produces an electronic Limited Stay Permit (ITAS), which is qualifying legal residence rather than visitor status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Years to temporary residence is effectively zero once admitted on the visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: E33G expressly permits transfer to another stay permit. PR is possible through a separately qualifying ITAS category; a direct three-year E33G-to-ITAP entitlement is not sufficiently established.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Bengkalis labels E33G second-home, but the implementing ITAP list at Depok names second-home, special expertise, world figures and seniors, without remote workers. PP 40/2023 also describes second-home as a five/ten-year facility, while E33G is annual. Therefore nomad-time credit and the ordinary remote-worker PR path remain uncertain; changed-profile routes are conditional.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization may be requested after five consecutive years or ten non-consecutive years residing in Indonesia. Immigration guidance states that this period is counted from obtaining an ITAS or ITAP, so citizenship does not appear to require waiting five additional years after ITAP.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Applicants must satisfy Indonesian-language, health, character, stable-income, allegiance and anti-dual-nationality conditions. Naturalization is discretionary and becomes effective only after approval and the oath or pledge.

best_routes.notes: E33G directly grants ITAS, is renewable and transferable, and current law supplies a plausible ITAP and citizenship pathway. The strongest fit is a salaried remote employee; contractors should request written pre-filing confirmation because the official checklist specifically requests an employment agreement with an overseas company.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not applicable to visitor status.

income_requirement_display.notes: Visa-on-arrival and visa-exemption status cannot be converted to ITAS. Other visit permits can convert only for listed qualifying purposes, not merely by opening a bank account or informally registering as a freelancer.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time is not established as qualifying ITAS/ITAP residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employer-sponsored ITAS
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Does not fit the foreign-client remote-work profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Workers may potentially convert after qualifying residence, but only while meeting the sponsored-worker rules.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may eventually apply, but the route is outside the selection because it requires local employment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected despite the applicant’s occupation because an Indonesian employer and local work authorization are required.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The controlling requirement is qualifying investment or corporate activity, not ordinary foreign remote income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Route-specific investment thresholds vary by subclass and are outside the ordinary remote-worker profile.

income_requirement_display.value: Substantial investment or Indonesian corporate activity required
income_requirement_display.notes: Not treated as an ordinary entrepreneur or freelancer option.

income_proof_months.notes: A monthly-income history is not the controlling test.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying investment, shareholding or Indonesian company activity depending on subclass.

initial_validity.value: Subclass dependent, including multi-year golden-visa options

extension_rules.value: Subject to maintaining the investment commitments.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Investor ITAS

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Investor ITAS can potentially convert to ITAP after qualifying residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization rules may eventually apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant profile does not include substantial investment, Indonesian company formation or founder activity.

summary.value: Indonesia offers education visas that produce an ITAS without a local employer, but admission to and support from an Indonesian educational institution are required. A foreign university degree alone does not create an independent residence entitlement, and education status does not directly grant ITAP.
summary.notes: Education is an alternative purpose-specific stay, not a degree-based skilled-migration route and not a better fit than E33G for this applicant.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is an Indonesian domestic tax subject if residing in Indonesia, present for more than 183 days in any 12-month period, or present during a tax year with an intention to reside. A VITAS/ITAS lasting more than 183 days and a long residence lease may evidence that intention before day 184.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Because E33G provides a one-year ITAS, the holder should not assume non-residence merely because fewer than 184 days have elapsed.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Resident individual taxable income is taxed progressively at 5%, 15%, 25%, 30% and 35%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Foreigners working in Indonesia for at least six months generally fall within BPJS rules, but the official material reviewed does not conclusively establish how a sponsor-free E33G holder employed only by an overseas company must register or which contribution base applies. Route-specific advice is required.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly fixed tax or social-security payment for E33G was established. The official immigration charge is IDR 7,000,000 for the initial one-year visa/ITAS/re-entry package, approximately US$392 at the 14 August 2026 JISDOR rate; it is not a monthly payment.

special_tax_regimes.value: A foreign tax resident with approved specified expertise may elect Indonesian-source-only taxation for up to four tax years. Software-development occupations appear among the listed expertise, but eligibility requires a DGT application and additional employment, qualification and knowledge-transfer criteria. Foreign-paid services performed in Indonesia can still be treated as Indonesian-source income, and the election cannot be combined with treaty treatment for the relevant foreign income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Do not assume E33G automatically grants this regime. A sponsor-free remote employee may not satisfy all specified-expertise employment and knowledge-transfer conditions.

taxes.caveats: Tax source, residence, treaty tie-breakers, the legal identity of the overseas employer, place where services are performed, and approval for the four-year expertise regime can materially change the outcome. The visa itself is not a tax exemption.

taxation_system.value: Progressive resident personal income tax, ordinarily on worldwide income, with a limited application-based territorial regime for qualifying foreign experts.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence, more than 183 days in 12 months, or presence plus intention to reside; a long-duration VITAS/ITAS can evidence intention.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally report Indonesian and foreign income. Nonresidents are taxed on Indonesian-source income. Approved qualifying foreign experts may receive Indonesian-source-only treatment for up to four tax years, but work physically performed in Indonesia may itself be Indonesian-source even when paid abroad.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Application-based four-tax-year territorial treatment for qualifying foreign experts; not automatic for digital nomads and unavailable where the taxpayer instead uses treaty treatment for the relevant foreign income.
taxation_system.social_security: BPJS participation generally covers foreigners working in Indonesia for at least six months, but the registration and contribution treatment of an E33G overseas employee is not clearly resolved by the official general guidance.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Annual taxable-income brackets: 5% through IDR 60 million; 15% above IDR 60 million through IDR 250 million; 25% above IDR 250 million through IDR 500 million; 30% above IDR 500 million through IDR 5 billion; 35% above IDR 5 billion. The displayed 35% is only the highest marginal rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Up to IDR 60,000,000 annual taxable income
tax_brackets.notes: Approximation at IDR 17,836 per US$1.
USD value is the approximate upper threshold.
USD value is the approximate upper threshold.
USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident individual taxable income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: The current Indonesian-language DGT page and consolidated amended law support the five current brackets.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: E33G has no automatic digital-nomad tax holiday. A one-year ITAS can establish tax residence through intention to reside, and ordinary resident rates reach 35%. A qualifying software professional may apply for the four-year foreign-expert territorial regime, but remote salary for duties performed while in Indonesia may remain Indonesian-source and taxable.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Resident remote employee unless facts or a treaty establish otherwise
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 5%–35%; 35% is the top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence, more than 183 days in 12 months, or presence plus intention to reside; E33G’s one-year ITAS is relevant evidence of intention.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Ordinarily worldwide for residents. Potential Indonesian-source-only treatment for approved specified experts for four tax years, subject to application and restrictions; services performed in Indonesia may still be Indonesian-source despite offshore payment.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No E33G-specific exemption. The separate specified-expertise regime may be relevant to software developers but must be approved by DGT and may not fit a sponsor-free overseas employment arrangement.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: General rules require BPJS coverage for foreigners working in Indonesia for at least six months, but official sources do not clearly allocate employer/employee obligations where the only employer is overseas and the worker holds E33G.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potential BPJS obligation after six months; route-specific amount and registration method require confirmation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: IDR 7,000,000 for the one-year E33G package: IDR 500,000 visa, IDR 2,000,000 verification, IDR 3,000,000 ITAS and IDR 1,500,000 re-entry permit.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No E33G-specific municipal tax, fixed freelancer tax or mandatory monthly levy was identified in the cited official sources. Ordinary tax registration and reporting may apply.
fixed_payments.notes: Private insurance, accommodation and agent fees are not included; direct self-application is available.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Do not assume tax non-residence: a one-year VITAS/ITAS and other facts can show intention to reside before 184 days. If genuinely nonresident, only Indonesian-source income is ordinarily taxable, subject to source and treaty analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary resident brackets and worldwide reporting apply unless an approved expertise election or treaty changes the result. Foreign tax credits may be relevant.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: E33G is framed as overseas employment, not local freelance business. Registering an Indonesian business or performing local-client work changes immigration, tax, VAT and social-security analysis and may require another status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax-residence and rate rules are well supported. Confidence is lower for BPJS and special-regime eligibility because official general rules do not expressly address every sponsor-free E33G payroll configuration.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The E33G entry produces an e-ITAS immediately upon admission.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The regulation permits qualifying second-home ITAS holders to apply for ITAP after at least three consecutive years. Approval is not automatic.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: This is a derived timeline: citizenship eligibility arises after five consecutive residence years counted from ITAS/ITAP, while ITAP may be sought after year three. ITAP is not stated to restart the clock.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum residence is five consecutive years, alternatively ten non-consecutive years. Eligibility does not guarantee approval.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The cited citizenship law provides procedural deadlines but does not publish an empirical typical-processing duration. Ministerial forwarding and a presidential decision are tied to three-month limits, notification follows within 14 days, and the oath may be scheduled within three months after the decision; those statutory stages are not a proven typical total.

key_conditions.value: Age 18 or married; five consecutive or ten non-consecutive residence years; physical and mental health; Indonesian-language ability; recognition of Pancasila and the Constitution; no disqualifying conviction; stable work or income; payment of the naturalization charge; oath or pledge; and no resulting adult dual citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Long absences or departure for good can affect whether residence is treated as consecutive. Maintain ITAS/ITAP validity, tax compliance and evidence of actual residence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Two years refers to eligibility for ITAS-to-ITAP conversion based on a genuine marriage to an Indonesian citizen. Citizenship by declaration still requires five consecutive or ten non-consecutive years residing in Indonesia.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A marriage to an Indonesian citizen that already satisfies the two-year duration can support family ITAS and an ITAP application once the immigration requirements are met. A pre-existing marriage to another foreign national does not accelerate the applicant’s own citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage duration alone does not automatically confer ITAP or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid and documented. Citizenship by declaration is available after the residence period only if it does not create dual nationality; otherwise the law allows permanent residence instead. False records can cancel citizenship, and sham-marriage or misrepresentation can cause refusal, cancellation, prosecution or removal.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The citizenship law does not provide a shorter residence clock merely because the applicant is married; the clear acceleration is to ITAP after two years of marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Indonesia is primarily descent-based. Territorial citizenship is limited to cases such as unknown or stateless parents and certain uncertainty-of-status situations, not ordinary children of two foreign migrants.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Indonesia to two foreign parents does not ordinarily acquire Indonesian citizenship solely by birth. Exceptions include parents who are stateless, unknown or of unclear citizenship status.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A parent’s ITAS or ITAP does not itself create citizenship for the newborn.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born within a lawful marriage with either an Indonesian father or Indonesian mother is Indonesian. Limited dual citizenship may apply during childhood, followed by a requirement to choose after age 18 or marriage, with the declaration due within three years.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The result is based on descent, not place of birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a child does not benefit two foreign parents because the child is normally not Indonesian. Where the child is Indonesian through the other parent, the migrant parent may have family-residence options, but parent citizenship is never automatic.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Some parent-joining categories depend on the Indonesian child’s age and legal family relationship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically acquire residence, ITAP or citizenship from the child’s citizenship. If married to the Indonesian mother, the clearer route is spouse-sponsored family residence and potential ITAP after two years of marriage. Immigration also lists a parent-joining-child category for an Indonesian child aged at least 21.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, marriage and civil-registration documents must be legally recognized.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on 15 August 2026. Henley’s 9 January 2026 edition separately ranked Indonesia 64th with a score of 73; index methodologies and update dates differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s strict visa-free count. Its mobility score is 89 after adding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 40 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 7 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport rankings change frequently. Passport Index supplies the requested visa-free/arrival/eTA/required breakdown; Henley’s January 2026 PDF is retained as a separate methodology cross-check.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable in Bali, Jakarta, technology workplaces and established tourism/expatriate areas, but it should not be assumed nationwide. EF EPI 2025 ranked Indonesia 80th of 123 with a score of 471, classified as low proficiency. Indonesian is important for government, tax, long-term integration and citizenship.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a non-governmental index based on test participants and is used only as a practical screening indicator.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or generally used administrative languages. They may be available through expatriate communities and private services in Bali, but daily administration and citizenship integration require Indonesian; English is the more practical bridge language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national source quantified Russian- or Ukrainian-language availability, so no broader claim is made.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: IDR 3.29 million divided by the 14 August 2026 JISDOR rate of IDR 17,836 per US dollar.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of BPS’s latest located national employee median, IDR 2,750,136 for August 2025. It is older than the February 2026 average-wage observation and should not be read as a February 2026 median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Indonesia sets minimum wages provincially or locally, so there is no single defensible national minimum. For context only, Jakarta’s 2026 provincial minimum is IDR 5,729,876, approximately US$321, but it is not nationally applicable.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the February 2026 national average employee wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: IDR 2,750,136 divided by the 14 August 2026 JISDOR rate. The underlying median is from Sakernas August 2025, not February 2026.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected BPS sources publish averages and breakdowns, not a meaningful nationwide maximum salary; a sample maximum would also be unstable and unsuitable as a national benchmark.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: There is no single national minimum wage; provincial and regency/city minimums vary. Jakarta’s 2026 UMP is IDR 5,729,876 only as an example.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official BPS average employee wage for February 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: BPS’s Decent Work Indicators in Indonesia 2025, released 30 April 2026, publishes this nationwide monthly median for employees based on the August 2025 Sakernas. The newer February 2026 employee release, Laborer Situation publication and Sakernas booklet publish averages rather than a February 2026 national median; the February 2026 Income Statistics publication concerns non-employee income, while the labor-market-indicator publication and current average-wage table do not supply a newer directly comparable national employee median. Accordingly, IDR 2,750,136 is retained as the latest exact official national employee median located, with its August 2025 period stated explicitly.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current BPS wage products publish national/provincial averages and characteristics but no meaningful nationwide maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Employee wages: February 2026 national average from Sakernas; August 2025 national median from BPS Decent Work Indicators. USD values use the 14 August 2026 official JISDOR rate.
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: February 2026; median: August 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The BPS figures describe employees and are not software-engineer salaries. The median and average come from different Sakernas reference periods because no February 2026 national employee median was published in the inspected current products.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official socioeconomic source does not provide one directly comparable nationwide monthly cost-of-living figure suitable for this field. Costs vary sharply between Bali/Jakarta and smaller cities, so no crowdsourced estimate was inserted.

settlement_track.summary: E33G directly creates an ITAS rather than visitor status, and official immigration material confirms renewal and status transfer. Its second-home classification supports ITAP conversion after three consecutive years, while citizenship residence is counted from ITAS or ITAP and reaches the statutory minimum after five consecutive years.
settlement_track.notes: ITAP conversion and naturalization are applications, not automatic entitlements. Before planning around the three-year conversion, obtain filing-level confirmation that the issued E33G ITAS remains classified as a qualifying second-home facility under the then-current ministerial classification.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route expressly permits living in Indonesia while performing assignments for a company established outside Indonesia, requires no Indonesian sponsor and prohibits local remuneration. The official wording is strongest for an employment relationship; foreign-client contractors need manual pre-filing confirmation.

data.notes: The focused audit resolved the salary-median gap: BPS’s latest located nationwide employee median is IDR 2,750,136 for August 2025. The February 2026 wage products publish a fresher average but no directly comparable national median. E33G remains a qualifying ITAS route with a credible, though filing-dependent, ITAP and naturalization track; tax and BPJS treatment still require individualized professional confirmation.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Qualifying worker, investor, family or eligible second-home ITAS followed by ITAP
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: E33G expressly permits transfer to another stay permit. PR is possible through a separately qualifying ITAS category; a direct three-year E33G-to-ITAP entitlement is not sufficiently established.
requirements: Meet the full requirements of a qualifying ITAS category, such as sponsored work, investment or eligible second-home residence.
For worker, investor and qualifying second-home ITAS, PP 40/2023 requires three consecutive years from ITAS issuance before ITAP conversion.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Bengkalis labels E33G second-home, but the implementing ITAP list at Depok names second-home, special expertise, world figures and seniors, without remote workers. PP 40/2023 also describes second-home as a five/ten-year facility, while E33G is annual. Therefore nomad-time credit and the ordinary remote-worker PR path remain uncertain; changed-profile routes are conditional.
reviewed_route_names: E33G Remote Worker Visa / Limited Stay Permit

data.selection_summary: Iran has no dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or independently accessible freelance residence route for an ordinary software engineer working only for a foreign client. The official temporary-work category requires an Iranian sponsor employer and labour approval; tourist/eVisa status is temporary travel only, while the independent study and USD 100,000 investment options do not match the profile.

visa_application.title: Iran Online Non-immigrant Visa Application
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct application portal for Iranian non-immigrant visas, not a remote-worker residence application. It lists entry, tourist, work, education, investment, marital and other categories; applicants from some countries may instead be directed to an Iranian embassy.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum monthly income was published. Eligibility depends on Iranian employer sponsorship and labour approval rather than foreign income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying salary threshold was found in the official visa directory or labour law.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; Iranian employer sponsorship and labour approval are required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an independently accessible foreign-contract route.

income_proof_months.notes: No separate income-history period was published.

key_requirements.requirement: Sponsor employer in Iran and a labour certificate approved by the Ministry of Labour.

Labour approval generally requires showing that no suitable Iranian worker is available, that the foreigner has the required expertise, and that the expertise can be transferred to an Iranian replacement.

initial_validity.value: Work permits may be issued for no more than one year.
initial_validity.notes: The official eVisa portal describes this as a non-immigrant temporary-work visa.

extension_rules.value: Renewal or extension is possible for periods not exceeding one year, subject to renewed labour approval.
extension_rules.notes: The employment relationship remains central; the employer must report termination and the foreign worker must surrender the permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary lawful work and stay are possible only through the Iranian sponsor-employer process.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This fails the independent-application requirement.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence entitlement from the work visa was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: Iran's general naturalization law permits an application after five years of residence, but approval is discretionary and the employer-sponsored work route does not fit this applicant.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The law does not make citizenship automatic after five years.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the temporary-work visa requires an Iranian sponsor employer and labour-market approval. A foreign-client contract alone is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income requirement applies to the tourist category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying residence-income threshold exists for this visitor category.

income_requirement_display.value: No qualifying remote-worker income threshold; tourist status is for tourism
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status is not a residence or work category.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker income-history rule was found.

key_requirements.requirement: Online visa application and possible consular interview; passport must generally remain valid for at least six months beyond travel.
The official directory defines category B specifically for tourism.

initial_validity.value: Temporary non-immigrant travel only; duration is determined in the issued visa.
initial_validity.notes: The portal does not establish residence rights for tourist applicants.

extension_rules.notes: No extension rule capable of converting tourist status into an independent remote-work residence route was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No tourist-to-freelancer or tourist-to-self-employed residence conversion was confirmed.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Tourist status is not a direct permanent-residence route.

path_to_citizenship.notes: A tourist visa authorizes tourism, not residence under a residence permit. Article 979 naturalization requires five years of residence, and the foreign-residence regulation treats residence as legally qualifying only when supported by a residence permit; no current source confirms that tourist-visa days alone count or that tourist status converts to a remote-worker residence permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an eVisa or tourist visa permits temporary travel, not ordinary foreign-contract remote work or a residence-to-citizenship track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Five-year residence through investment or long-term deposit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route uses a capital threshold, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Investment or long-term deposit equivalent to at least USD 100,000
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The rule is denominated by reference to USD and equivalent foreign currency, so no stable rial conversion is supplied.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 100,000 minimum investment or long-term deposit
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a substantial-capital route and is excluded by the applicant criteria.

income_proof_months.notes: No monthly income-history requirement applies.

key_requirements.requirement: At least USD 100,000 or equivalent placed in an approved long-term deposit or investment, with confirmation from the economic authorities.
Investment-visa applicants require approval from Iran's investment authority.

initial_validity.value: Five-year residence permit after the qualifying investment or deposit is confirmed.
initial_validity.notes: This is residence based on capital, not foreign remote work.

extension_rules.notes: Current renewal conditions were not established from the reviewed text.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct five-year residence is available after the qualifying investment or deposit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Excluded because it requires substantial capital.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed decision describes a five-year permit, not direct permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after five years of residence, but no automatic investor-to-citizenship entitlement was confirmed.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization remains discretionary.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the profile excludes investor/golden-visa routes and substantial capital requirements.

summary.value: A foreign student admitted by an accredited Iranian institution can obtain an education visa and a residence permit covering the study period, including multiple exit and re-entry. It requires actual enrollment, is not a degree-based skilled migration route, and no direct permanent-residence outcome was found.
summary.notes: This is an education-based temporary status, not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: No reliable general day-count test for a foreign individual was identified. The Direct Taxation Act instead subjects non-Iranians to income earned in or collected from Iran; whether foreign salary for work physically performed from Iran is Iranian-source income requires filing-level advice.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The six-month rule in Article 180 addresses when an Iranian national may be treated as resident abroad and should not be mechanically applied to foreign nationals.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening figure: the top 1405 Iranian-year marginal salary-tax rate is 30%, not an expected effective rate. Self-employed/business income under Article 131 has a separate top rate of 25%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 7% value is the employee share under Article 28 of the general Social Security Law, within a 30% statutory total (20% employer and 3% state). The newer ISSA country profile separates programme components and reports self-employed old-age/survivor options of 12%, 14% or 18%, plus health-related amounts; none of these rates is confirmed as mandatory for a foreign-contract remote worker who lacks a recognized Iranian work or self-employment status.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No route-specific USD monthly payment applies because Iran has no digital-nomad route. ISSA reports general self-employed contribution options and an IRR 1,196,000 monthly health amount, plus the same amount per covered dependent, but its table does not establish that those amounts apply to a foreign remote worker or remain the operative 1405 assessment; therefore no USD fixed-payment value is stated.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, non-dom, remittance-basis or inbound-worker tax regime was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary source and income-category rules apply.

taxes.caveats: Iran has no qualifying remote-worker residence category. Tax treatment depends on whether the arrangement is characterized as employment or independent business, whether services performed from Iran create Iranian-source income, registration status, treaty availability, and the official exchange rate used. Obtain current Iranian tax advice before working from Iran.

taxation_system.value: Mixed progressive system: 1405 salary income has annual brackets from 0% to 30%, while general natural-person business income under Article 131 uses 15%, 20% and 25% brackets. Non-Iranian persons are generally liable on income earned in or collected from Iran.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No general foreign-individual day-count rule was confirmed; non-Iranian liability is framed primarily by Iranian-source income.
taxation_system.income_scope: Non-Iranians are taxed on income earned in Iran or collected from Iran. Foreign salary received for services performed while physically in Iran may require local-source analysis.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: General employees have a 7% employee share under the Social Security Law. ISSA separately reports self-employed pension options of 12%, 14% or 18% and a stated monthly health amount, but foreign remote-worker eligibility and the current 1405 assessment are not established.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal 1405 salary-tax rate. It is not the expected effective tax rate. General business/professional income has a separate 25% top rate under Article 131.

tax_brackets.notes: Equivalent to Toman 40,000,000 per month. No USD conversion is supplied because Iran's multiple and volatile exchange rates make a single conversion misleading.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual salary above IRR 4,800,000,000 through IRR 9,600,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The 1405 salary brackets are current for the research date. The source and category treatment of foreign-contract remote income remains uncertain because Iran has no corresponding immigration or tax category.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special regime: Iran has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence category. Ordinary Iranian-source rules could nevertheless apply if work is physically performed in Iran.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: not_applicable_no_qualifying_route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% top marginal salary tax; up to 25% for general natural-person business income
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No general foreign-individual day-count rule was confirmed. Non-Iranian liability is based on income earned in or collected from Iran.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-paid income is not automatically exempt. Services performed from Iran may create Iranian-source income, but the precise treatment of a foreign remote contract needs local advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No digital-nomad payroll rule exists. Under the general system, an employee share of 7% is stated by law; ISSA reports voluntary/self-employed pension options of 12%, 14% or 18% and a stated health amount, but applicability to a foreign remote worker without Iranian work/self-employment status is not established.

fixed_payments.status: Not applicable to a digital-nomad route because no such route exists; current foreign-remote-worker liability under the general self-employed system is unestablished.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: ISSA reports self-employed pension contribution options of 12%, 14% or 18% of monthly earnings, with a minimum earnings base tied to the legal minimum wage, and IRR 1,196,000 per month for health coverage plus the same amount per dependent. The profile does not confirm that a foreign remote worker may enroll or that the fixed health amount is current for Iranian year 1405.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Iran charges visa and residence-permit fees, but the 1404 consular-tariff rule makes visa pricing nationality/reciprocity-dependent and its accessible text does not publish one universal remote-worker amount. The foreign-residence law also provides for permit fees, but no digital-nomad permit or route-specific fee exists.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed digital-nomad levy was found. Business licensing, VAT or banking charges would depend on an independently valid local registration, which was not established.
fixed_payments.notes: The route-specific fixed-payment question is inapplicable because Iran has no digital-nomad status. General self-employed contribution figures are recorded only as context and must not be treated as proof that this applicant can register or obtain residence.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short tourist stay remains non-qualifying for work or settlement. Absence of a verified day-count rule does not make work tax-free or immigration-compliant.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No immigration category authorizes this scenario. If treated as working in Iran, Iranian-source tax and possibly registration obligations may arise.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: No official visitor-to-sole-proprietor or independent freelancer residence conversion was found. Do not assume local business registration would legalize immigration status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax rates are better documented than the classification of a foreign remote contract. Filing-level professional advice is essential.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker temporary residence route exists.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No route-specific timeline exists for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. The residence regulation lists discretionary permanent-residence eligibility after five years of lawful residence generally, or after two years for specified categories including applicants whose personal income, salary or pension is verified by an authorized Iranian bank; however, it defines qualifying residence as residence under a residence permit, and no initial independent remote-worker permit or current filing channel was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Article 979 uses five years of residence and does not state a separate number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory minimum residence for a naturalization application: five years, continuous or intermittent. This is not a route-specific promise and approval remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the reviewed current Civil Code texts nor the nationality materials publish a typical or statutory processing period for a completed naturalization application.

key_conditions.value: Age 18 or older; five years' residence; not a military-service deserter; no conviction for serious non-political offences; police evidence of residence, clean record and sufficient property or livelihood. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs completes the file and the Council of Ministers decides whether to approve naturalization.
key_conditions.notes: No statutory Persian-language test or automatic approval deadline was identified in the reviewed provisions. Renunciation of prior nationality was not stated as a general precondition in Articles 979–983, but dual-nationality consequences require specialist advice.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No uniform number applies. A foreign woman marrying an Iranian man is treated as Iranian under Article 976(6). A foreign man married to an Iranian woman does not receive automatic citizenship; Article 980 may waive residence only where he has an Iranian wife and children, subject to government discretion.

existing_marriage_effect.value: The result is gender-specific. A foreign woman who marries an Iranian man acquires Iranian nationality by statute. A foreign husband of an Iranian woman may use the marital visa, but marriage alone does not grant citizenship; if they have an Iranian child, residence and discretionary naturalization advantages may arise.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: For the target applicant as a migrant father, an existing marriage matters only if the spouse is Iranian and the legal marriage and family relationship can be documented.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally recognizable and documented. For a foreign father, residence based on an Iranian child is subject to a written request and security clearance and can be cancelled following divorce or separation. Naturalization under Article 980 remains discretionary and requires Council of Ministers approval; sham or fraudulent documentation can lead to denial, cancellation and legal action.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No automatic citizenship benefit should be assumed for a foreign husband.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Iran is primarily descent-based but has conditional birth rules: a child born in Iran to foreign parents is Iranian if one parent was also born in Iran; another category can qualify after age 18 and an additional year of residence. This is not broad jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically in the ordinary case. Citizenship at birth applies where the child is born in Iran and one foreign parent was also born in Iran. A person born in Iran to a foreign father may also qualify after age 18 and at least one further year of residence. Foundlings and children of unknown parents are Iranian.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Because the outcome depends on parental birthplace and later residence, the boolean remains null rather than implying a universal result.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If the father is Iranian, the child is Iranian whether born in Iran or abroad. If the mother is Iranian and the father foreign, the mother may apply before the child turns 18, subject to proof of the qualifying marriage and security review; the adult child may apply independently.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The maternal route is application-based and administratively reviewed, unlike the Civil Code's direct paternal-descent rule.

parent_benefit_summary.value: An Iranian child can support a foreign father's residence when the mother is Iranian, but it does not automatically make the father Iranian or a permanent resident.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Security review and a written residence application are required.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: After the child's Iranian nationality is confirmed, the foreign father may request an Iranian residence permit, subject to no security objection. That family-based permit can be cancelled if he separates or divorces the Iranian mother. A foreign man with an Iranian wife and children may also be considered for discretionary naturalization without the normal residence requirement under Article 980.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Neither residence nor citizenship is automatic for the father.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the source when accessed on 2026-08-15; index values can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as visa required by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard figure: 33 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 50, comprising 13 visa-free, 33 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations. This methodology differs from Henley's combined-access count.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Limited to moderate linguistically, and poor operationally for reliable foreign remote work. EF's 2025 index places Iran near the global average for tested adult English, but Persian is the sole national official language and severe internet filtering and shutdowns materially undermine remote-work reliability.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English may be usable among some educated urban residents, but government procedures and authoritative legal texts are commonly Persian.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official status, and no evidence was found that either is broadly usable for administration or daily services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Persian is required for most local-government interaction; interpreters may be necessary.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Crowdsourced average monthly net salary after tax, updated May 2026; it is not an official national wage statistic.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the current Numbeo page nor the statutory minimum-wage decision publishes a national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The 1405 statutory base wage is confirmed in rials, but no USD value is supplied because Iran's official, exchange-centre and open-market rates diverge substantially.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Crowdsourced net salary after tax, not an official formal-sector average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed Numbeo country page publishes an average net salary but not a national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither source publishes a meaningful national wage ceiling or maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory base minimum wage for Iranian year 1405, excluding housing, child and seniority allowances.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Wage.is reports this as a 2026 national average gross monthly salary. It is a non-official secondary estimate with limited published methodology and should not be conflated with Numbeo's separate crowdsourced net-salary figure.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Wage.is reports this 2026 monthly median, but does not expose an official national survey table or sufficiently detailed methodology; use as a low-confidence secondary benchmark, not an official statistic.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum monthly salary is published by the reviewed current sources. IranTalent publishes occupation-, seniority- and location-specific percentiles, such as a Tehran administrative-expert range, which cannot be used as a nationwide maximum; Wage.is publishes average and median figures but no national ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.currency: Iranian rial (IRR); local prices are commonly quoted in tomans, where 1 toman equals 10 rials
average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly base minimum wage; separate non-official national gross average/median estimates; separate crowdsourced net-salary estimate
average_citizen_salary.period: Iranian year 1405 / current pages reviewed August 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum is the statutory 1405 worker base wage. Wage.is supplies low-confidence gross national average and median estimates in rials; Numbeo supplies a separate crowdsourced net figure in USD. IranTalent confirms that its current 1405 data are based on employee self-reports and anonymized company payrolls but publishes detailed values by occupation and location, not a single defensible national maximum. Multiple exchange rates make cross-source USD reconciliation unreliable.

cost_of_living_note.value: Numbeo's May 2026 crowdsourced data reported an average net salary of about USD 249, a one-bedroom rent of about USD 280 in city centres and USD 188 outside them. These figures are indicative only and can shift rapidly with inflation and exchange-rate assumptions.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Crowdsourced secondary data, not official statistics.
