settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourist/eVisa status is temporary non-immigrant travel and is not a remote-work or settlement status.
settlement_track.summary: Iran has a general discretionary naturalization rule after five years' residence, but no independent ordinary foreign-contract remote-work status with which this applicant can establish that residence. Available work status requires an Iranian sponsor; study and investment routes require a materially different purpose.
settlement_track.notes: The previous record's negative selection result is retained: current visa and residence categories exist, but none is a regular remote-worker route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official visa directory and consular rules contain no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category, and foreign nationals working in Iran require work authorization. Although the residence regulation includes discretionary permanent-residence categories based on prior lawful residence and bank-verified personal income, it does not create the prerequisite initial remote-worker residence status or authorize work for a foreign client.

data.notes: Thirty-four distinct directly relevant URLs are listed, including nine newly inspected URLs outside the previous source set. The negative selection result remains: no current ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route or prerequisite independent residence permit was confirmed. The focused pass clarifies tourist-time treatment, current social-insurance context and fixed-payment inapplicability, and replaces salary placeholders with sourced low-confidence estimates or precise explained nulls.

data.selection_summary: Iraq does not currently offer a dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary foreign-client freelancer residence route. The official framework permits visitor entry, employer-linked work residence, study, family residence, and renewable residence for investors, businesspeople, or people providing useful services to Iraq, but none fits ordinary independent work for a foreign client while providing a confirmed citizenship track.

visa_application.title: Iraqi Electronic Visa
visa_application.notes: This is Iraq's official general eVisa application portal, not a digital-nomad or remote-worker application. Visa eligibility and conditions must be searched by nationality and passport type.

rejected_routes.route_name: Iraqi eVisa / visit or tourist visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly income threshold is published; the law instead requires proof of financial ability for the intended stay.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed law and current eVisa instructions publish no fixed IQD threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published fixed threshold; sufficient funds for the visit are required.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Proof of financial ability during the stay
income_requirement_display.notes: The eVisa portal determines requirements by nationality and passport type.

income_proof_months.notes: The current instructions publish no standard number of income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligible passport, valid travel document, and nationality-specific eVisa requirements.
The residence law requires financial ability, no applicable entry bar, and compliance with health and security requirements.
Visit and tourist visa holders may not work in Iraq, whether paid or unpaid.

initial_validity.value: Nationality and visa-type specific; the 2017 law describes a 30-day stay for visit and tourist visas.
initial_validity.notes: Portal-generated conditions should be treated as controlling for the applicant's passport. A UK government page reports a 60-day visa for British visitors, but that should not be generalized to other nationalities.

extension_rules.value: Specified visit and tourist categories may be extended once for a double fee; the authorities may change a visit or tourist visa to a regular visa, but no entitlement or remote-work conversion criteria are published.
extension_rules.notes: This discretionary visa amendment is not a confirmed route for foreign-client remote work.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying remote-work residence path. Any change to a regular visa remains discretionary and requires a separate lawful justification for residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor status itself is not temporary residence for this selection.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed from visitor/eVisa status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The law describes renewable residence cards but does not establish visitor-to-permanent-residence conversion for remote workers.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from eVisa or visitor status. General naturalization requires at least ten consecutive years of legal residence, which a short visitor stay does not establish.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A separate qualifying residence basis would be necessary.

rejected_routes.notes: Entry permission does not authorize employment or establish a settlement route. Remote work should not be assumed lawful merely because the client and payment are foreign.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employer-sponsored foreign worker permit and residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed labour law and current government procedure publish no immigration salary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Employment must comply with applicable wage law, but no foreign-worker immigration minimum was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published foreign-worker immigration income threshold.
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer-driven process, not an income-qualified remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: The current employer-led procedure does not state a monthly income-history test.

key_requirements.requirement: A valid Ministry of Labour work permit is required before a foreign worker starts an occupation.
The Iraqi employer or project submits the recruitment or employment request and supplies company and project documents.
A labour-market check may reject recruitment when registered Iraqi workers are available for the occupation.
Residence card, health documentation, qualifications, security approval, and social-security enrollment or a qualifying home-country exemption may be required.

initial_validity.value: Work-permit duration was not clearly published; the general residence card may be issued for up to one year.
initial_validity.notes: Permit and residence validity must be confirmed in the individual case.

extension_rules.value: The employer or project requests work-permit renewal; general residence may be extended for another year while its justification remains.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal is not independent of the employment basis.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A lawful local-employment basis can support a residence card for up to one year, renewable while the justification remains.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This fails the no-local-employer criterion.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent residence. Three-year renewable residence may be considered after six years under a government employment contract, or after fifteen years of lawful continuous residence under specified conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: These are discretionary grounds for renewable three-year residence, not an ordinary private foreign-worker permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after at least ten consecutive years of legal residence, subject to ministerial acceptance and other conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The work route is unsuitable for the selected profile because sponsorship and local employment are required.

rejected_routes.notes: The official procedure is employer-led, includes labour-market review, and is not usable solely on the basis of a foreign software contract.

rejected_routes.route_name: Investor, businessperson, or useful-service three-year residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No ordinary income threshold is published; qualifying local investment, business, or useful service is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The federal residence sources publish no general minimum investment amount. The KRG company-registration service requires at least IQD 1,000,000 company capital, but that incorporation threshold is not a federal or residence-route investment minimum.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly-income test; qualifying Iraqi investment, commercial business, or useful service is required.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Local investment, business, or useful-service basis
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a passive foreign-income or freelancer route.

income_proof_months.notes: The current residence information publishes no standard income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Investors and businesspeople must have investment or commercial business inside Iraq.
The useful scientific, cultural, or artistic service category normally requires three prior years of Iraqi residence.
Business registration, local premises, capital, tax registration, and substantive local commercial activity may be required.

initial_validity.value: Up to three years per grant.
initial_validity.notes: Granting is discretionary.

extension_rules.value: Renewable on request for further three-year periods while the qualifying basis continues.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic permanent status follows.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct discretionary three-year residence is possible for qualifying investors, businesspeople, and specified useful-service cases.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: An ordinary foreign software contract is not enough.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No distinct direct permanent-residence entitlement was found.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Article 21 of the 2017 Foreigner Residence Law authorizes discretionary three-year residence renewable for further three-year periods; it does not call that status permanent residence. Its separate fifteen-year lawful-continuous-residence category is only an eligibility ground for the same renewable three-year permission, not an automatic or indefinite permanent-residence grant. The KRG company-registration page likewise treats incorporation and a foreign manager's residence card as separate matters and publishes no company-to-permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially relevant lawful residence could contribute to the general ten-year naturalization residence period, but naturalization remains discretionary.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This route is rejected because it requires local investment, business substance, or special service rather than ordinary remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: Although independently initiated in some cases, this category is incompatible with the ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker profile and cannot be treated as a freelancer visa.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed federal and Kurdistan Region sources publish no nationally standardized monthly threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current sources state fees and institutional requirements but no fixed monthly financial-sufficiency amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No published standardized monthly threshold; admission and financial sufficiency may be assessed.
income_requirement_display.notes: Institution-specific requirements must be checked.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither current student source publishes a standard number of financial-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: Admission to an Iraqi university, college, institute, religious seminary, or qualifying training or specialized course.
Valid passport and institution-supported study-visa or residence process.
In the Kurdistan Region, applicants aged 18 or older need educational-center support, residential support, a health test, and a passport valid for at least six months.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year; the Kurdistan Region service specifies six months or one year.
initial_validity.notes: Tied to the study basis.

extension_rules.value: Under the federal residence law, a residence card may be extended for another year, repeatedly, while the study justification remains. In the Kurdistan Region, the official student card is valid for six months or one year and is renewable with continuing educational-center support.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal is tied to continuing enrollment or institutional support, not to graduation. The Kurdistan Region procedure requires filing before expiry and imposes an IQD 20,000 daily late penalty; neither the federal law nor the current KRG service page publishes a post-study extension, job-search period, or student-to-permanent-residence conversion.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying student may receive a renewable residence basis of up to one year.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This does not authorize ordinary foreign-client remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent-residence route from study was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The federal law and current KRG student-residence procedure do not provide a general student-to-permanent-residence transition.

path_to_citizenship.value: No study-specific citizenship path was confirmed; only the general ten-year lawful-residence rule is stated in nationality law.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Whether every period of student residence is accepted for naturalization should be verified before relying on it.

rejected_routes.notes: Available without a local employer, but it is an education route rather than an ordinary remote-work route and has no confirmed direct settlement conversion.

summary.value: Admission to an Iraqi university, college, institute, religious seminary, or qualifying training course can support renewable student residence without a local employer. No independent degree-recognition or skilled-migration residence route, direct permanent residence, or confirmed student-to-permanent-residence conversion was found.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing software degree alone does not create eligibility; actual Iraqi study admission and continuing institutional support are required. The current KRG procedure confirms renewable six- or twelve-month student residence but publishes no post-study settlement conversion.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person is tax-resident after a continuous stay of four months or an aggregate six months during the fiscal year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax residence are separate tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee contribution on net salary after allowances; the ordinary employer contribution is 12%, or 25% for employers categorized as prime. Application to an unsupported foreign-client freelancer arrangement is not established.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly payment can be stated for a digital nomad because no such route exists. Employer-sponsored work procedures have transaction fees rather than a confirmed monthly fixed charge.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, freelancer, or inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. Federal Iraq uses progressive personal income tax; the reviewed PwC business guide reports a separate 5% fixed taxable-income rate in the Kurdistan Region, requiring location-specific advice.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Federal and Kurdistan Region rules can differ.

taxes.caveats: A foreign payer does not by itself establish foreign-source income. Work physically performed from Iraq may be treated as Iraqi-source; the official tax law also states that foreign income of a non-Iraqi resident is generally not taxed, creating a sourcing question that requires advice from the General Commission for Taxes. Residence, work authorization, payer location, place of performance, Kurdistan versus federal Iraq, and treaty or foreign-tax-credit availability all matter.

taxation_system.value: Federal Iraq applies progressive personal income tax at 3%, 5%, 10%, and 15%. Iraqi-source income is taxable regardless of residence. The tax law says foreign income of non-Iraqi residents is not taxed, but classification of services physically performed in Iraq for a foreign client needs professional determination.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Four continuous months or six aggregate months in the fiscal year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Iraqi-source income is taxable regardless of residence. Foreign-income rules depend on nationality, residence, source, and whether funds or deposits in Iraq generate the income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No federal digital-nomad or ordinary freelancer regime found; Kurdistan Region treatment can differ.
taxation_system.social_security: For local and expatriate employees, PwC reports 5% employee and normally 12% employer contributions after allowances; certain prime employers contribute 25%.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Thresholds are annual taxable-income bands after applicable allowances. The 15% dashboard value is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate.

tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses the CBI rate of IQD 1,310 per USD observed on 2026-08-15.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess within this federal individual personal-income-tax band
tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted at IQD 1,310 per USD.

tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted at IQD 1,310 per USD.

tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: Tax rates and residence rules are well supported, but the source characterization of foreign-client services performed from Iraq is filing-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special visa category: Iraq has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. If a foreigner nevertheless becomes lawfully resident under another basis, federal personal income tax and source rules must be analyzed normally.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary federal personal income tax or applicable Kurdistan Region rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 15% federal personal income tax (top marginal screening rate; sourcing must be determined)
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Four continuous months or six aggregate months in the fiscal year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The official tax law states that foreign income of a non-Iraqi resident is not taxed, while Iraqi-source income is taxable regardless of residence. Services physically performed in Iraq may present an Iraqi-source risk even when paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For employees, 5% employee and normally 12% employer social-security contributions are reported. No freelancer-specific contribution rule was confirmed for a foreign remote worker without an authorized route.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed-payment schedule exists.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed monthly freelancer amount confirmed; employee contributions are percentage-based.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: General eVisa fees vary by passport and type. Employer-sponsored procedures list IQD 100,000 and IQD 250,000 checks or fees, including IQD 250,000 for renewal, but they do not apply to an independent nomad route.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The reviewed federal sources publish no VAT-style freelancer registration threshold or fixed municipal freelancer tax for this unsupported scenario.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of a route prevents a reliable route-specific fixed-cost calculation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Short visitor presence does not authorize work. Iraqi-source income may still be taxable regardless of tax residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Potentially subject to federal personal income tax up to 15%, but the foreign-versus-Iraqi source of services must be resolved; lawful immigration and work authorization remain separate problems.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local business registration may create corporate, licensing, accounting, and social-security obligations and does not independently confer a suitable residence status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No route-specific nomad tax guidance exists; the scenarios are cautious applications of ordinary rules, not filing advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No temporary-residence route fitting ordinary foreign-contract remote work was found. Other qualifying bases can provide residence after approval, so no waiting-period number applies to the selected profile.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed federal law provides renewable one- and three-year residence but no generally defined permanent-residence milestone for this profile. Fifteen years of lawful continuous residence is a ground for discretionary renewable three-year residence, not a statutory permanent-residence conversion.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on at least ten consecutive years of legal residence rather than a confirmed number of years after permanent residence; the law does not establish the intervening permanent-residence stage assumed by this field.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory minimum before applying, assuming ten consecutive years of qualifying legal residence. The selected remote-worker profile has no confirmed route with which to begin this period.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality law and current Iraqi consular procedural guidance state conditions and documents but publish neither a statutory decision deadline nor a reliable current typical processing-time benchmark.

key_conditions.value: Legal entry and residence at application; at least ten consecutive years of legal residence; adulthood; good conduct; no dishonourable felony or misdemeanor; a clear means of living; freedom from communicable disease; ministerial acceptance; and an oath after approval. The law does not state a general Arabic or Kurdish test or require renunciation of an existing nationality, but case-specific practice should be verified.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and Palestinians are excluded under the cited law.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For a foreign man married to an Iraqi woman, the ordinary ten-year residence condition is reduced to at least five years while the marriage continues. A foreign woman married to an Iraqi must also generally complete five years of marriage and residence in Iraq.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to an Iraqi citizen can support renewable three-year family residence and may use the five-year naturalization provisions; time merely married abroad without the required Iraqi residence is insufficient.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marital relationship generally must continue through the application date, subject to the limited widow-or-divorce-and-child exception stated for foreign women.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally recognized and genuine. The foreign spouse still needs lawful entry and residence and must satisfy the applicable naturalization conditions. Residence and citizenship are discretionary, and false documents or sham marriage can cause refusal, loss of status, or other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The residence law imposes additional checks when a foreign man seeks approval to marry an Iraqi woman, including lawful entry and health-related requirements. The KRG family procedure requires an Iraqi-recognized or properly authenticated foreign marriage contract.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is primarily by descent from an Iraqi father or mother. Birth in Iraq alone is insufficient, except for foundlings or unknown parents and a discretionary double-generation rule for a child born in Iraq whose non-Iraqi father was also born and habitually resident there.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship merely from birth in Iraq. A foundling or child of unknown parents is Iraqi; a person born in Iraq may later apply under the narrow rule where the non-Iraqi father was also born and habitually resident in Iraq.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent or long-term residence of the parents alone is not a general jus-soli condition.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Iraqi if either the father or mother is Iraqi.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Birth and nationality must still be documented through the applicable civil-status and nationality procedures.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize a foreign father. Marriage to the Iraqi mother can support family residence and the five-year married-naturalization provision; parenthood without marriage was not established as an independent residence or citizenship basis.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The nationality law's exception for a widowed or divorced foreign woman with an Iraqi child must not be generalized to foreign fathers.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence. If married to the Iraqi mother, the foreign father may seek renewable three-year family residence and, after at least five years of qualifying residence with the marriage continuing, apply for discretionary naturalization.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Article 11's child-based exception applies only to a non-Iraqi woman who is divorced from or widowed by her Iraqi husband and has his child; it does not extend to a foreign father. A foreign husband instead relies on continuing marriage to an Iraqi woman under Nationality Law Article 7 and Residence Law Article 21. The current KRG family-reunification procedure also requires an Iraqi spouse and marriage documentation. None of the checked law, Iraqi government reporting, nationality guidance, or current family-residence material creates a father-only residence, permanent-residence, or naturalization entitlement based solely on having an Iraqi citizen child.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; live rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category in Passport Index, not the broader Henley score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 29 visa-on-arrival plus 4 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports mobility score 41. For comparison, the official Henley ranking page showed Iraq at rank 101 with a score of 29 in its 2026 table; the methodologies and category groupings differ.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Limited. English can be used in some professional, IT, university, and major-city contexts, but it is not official and should not be assumed sufficient for government procedures or everyday life. EF EPI 2025 gives Iraq a score of 406 and global rank 113, within EF's very-low proficiency range.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Arabic is important in federal administration; Kurdish is important in the Kurdistan Region.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official language, and no reliable evidence of broad practical use was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Focused research did not establish a general Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking service environment.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximation of the survey average IQD 671,177 at the CBI rate of IQD 1,310 per USD. The earnings observation is from the 2021 Labour Force Survey, not a 2026 wage measurement.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximation of the 2021 median IQD 614,400 at IQD 1,310 per USD.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate federal statutory minimum wage of IQD 350,000, not an observed minimum salary. WageIndicator reports a separate IQD 450,000 minimum for the Kurdistan Region effective August 2025.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: 2021 national employee average, converted using the 2026 official exchange rate solely for comparison.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: 2021 national median monthly earnings at employees' main job, converted at the 2026 official exchange rate.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The national survey publishes an open-ended top earnings category rather than a meaningful maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.value: IQD 350,000 per month (federal statutory minimum); IQD 450,000 in the Kurdistan Region
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The federal amount has applied since 2018; the Kurdistan amount is reported effective 2025-08-01.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly earnings of employees in the 2021 Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly earnings of employees at their main job in the 2021 Labour Force Survey.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The survey does not publish a national maximum; its top distribution band is open-ended.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly earnings of employees at their main job; gross, cash-and-kind employment-income concept in the 2021 national Labour Force Survey. Minimum is statutory.
average_citizen_salary.period: 2021 earnings; minimum-wage page valid June 2026; USD conversions use the 2026-08-15 CBI rate
average_citizen_salary.notes: The Labour Force Survey is the strongest national source located but is dated 2021. It reports employee earnings, not all citizens, freelancers, or household income. USD figures are approximate and do not represent 2026 purchasing-power adjustments.

cost_of_living_note.value: A reliable current standardized rent-and-expense basket was not published by the reviewed official statistical sources. As broader context, the World Bank reports a 17.5% national poverty rate in 2023/24, with substantial regional differences, so national salary figures can conceal large geographic disparities.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The poverty rate is contextual and should not be interpreted as a monthly cost-of-living estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: An eVisa or visitor stay does not authorize work and does not begin a confirmed remote-worker settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: Iraq has no current ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route. General naturalization is possible after ten consecutive years of qualifying legal residence, but the applicant would first need a different lawful basis such as sponsored local work, family, study, or substantive local investment or business.
settlement_track.notes: The absence conclusion is based on the official visa portals, the current residence law's enumerated residence categories, and the employer-driven foreign-worker procedure. No official digital-nomad or foreign-client freelancer category was located after focused English and Arabic searches.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Visitor visas prohibit work; work permits are employer-driven; and longer independent residence requires local investment, commercial business, special useful service, study, or family status. A foreign software contract alone is not a qualifying basis.

data.notes: The prior rejection remains correct. This focused audit inspected current federal law and visa, labour, nationality, tax, statistical, passport, and language material, plus six relevant Iraqi-government, KRG, and UN URLs absent from the previous source set. It clarifies that Article 21's repeatable three-year residence is not statutory permanent residence; student renewal remains tied to active study and has no published post-study settlement conversion; and Iraqi parentage gives the child nationality but gives a foreign father no independent automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship entitlement. Remaining nulls are retained only where the named current sources publish no standardized amount, permanent-residence concept, or processing benchmark.

data.selection_summary: Ireland does not offer a current digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route for a non-EEA applicant. Stamp 1 business permission requires a prior employment permit or a specific ISD permission letter; employment permits require qualifying Irish employment or, for Contract for Services, an Irish client contract. STEP is independently accessible but requires an innovative start-up and €50,000 funding, so it does not fit an ordinary software engineer continuing foreign remote work.

visa_application.title: Automated Visa Application and Tracking System (AVATS)
visa_application.notes: AVATS is Ireland's official general visa/preclearance application portal, not an application route for digital nomads. An applicant must first identify an eligible immigration category; the employment option normally requires an employment permit or qualifying ISD permission.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general income threshold exists because ISD does not publish Stamp 1 as an independently accessible freelancer route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No generally applicable freelancer income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No independent freelancer threshold or general application route is published
income_requirement_display.notes: Stamp 1 may permit business activity, but the applicant must already have an employment permit or an ISD letter expressly authorising work and, where applicable, self-employment.

income_proof_months.notes: Not published for a general route because no ordinary independent freelancer application category was identified.

key_requirements.requirement: A valid employment permit or an ISD letter confirming that work without an employment permit is permitted.
Business, trade or self-employment is prohibited unless the permission letter expressly authorises it.

initial_validity.value: Depends on the underlying permission; no standalone freelancer validity period is published
initial_validity.notes: Stamp 1 records conditions arising from another qualifying permission.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on retaining the underlying permission and applying before expiry
extension_rules.notes: There is no published ordinary foreign-client freelancer renewal track.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Stamp 1 is registered temporary immigration permission, but it cannot be obtained merely by entering as a visitor and registering a sole proprietorship
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Prior substantive authorisation is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No path was confirmed for a hypothetical general freelancer Stamp 1; employment-permit residence has separate long-term-residence rules
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The long-term-residence scheme is principally tied to qualifying employment-permit residence and lawful employment.

path_to_citizenship.value: Stamp 1 time is generally reckonable for naturalisation, but no independently accessible Stamp 1 freelancer route exists for this profile
path_to_citizenship.notes: Reckonability does not create eligibility for the underlying immigration permission.

rejected_routes.notes: Stamp 1 can authorise business activity, but it is not a self-standing freelancer visa. The official page requires an employment permit or specific ISD authorisation and prohibits business activity unless expressly allowed.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The applicable remuneration threshold depends on the occupation and permit rules; it is not an ordinary remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No single route-wide monthly amount was extracted.

income_requirement_display.value: Occupation-specific employment-permit remuneration rules; no remote-worker income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least the applicable employment-permit threshold and statutory minimum wage
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employment permit for an employee assigned to perform a foreign contractor's contract with an Irish entity.

income_proof_months.notes: No personal-income look-back period applies as for a nomad visa.

key_requirements.requirement: The foreign undertaking must have won a one-to-one services contract with an Irish entity.
The applicant remains an employee of the foreign contractor and must be required for the Irish contract.
An employment-permit application and signed employment contract are required.

initial_validity.value: Up to 24 months
initial_validity.notes: Limited to the contract term.

extension_rules.value: Extensions may permit an aggregate stay of up to 5 years
extension_rules.notes: Continued eligibility and the Irish services contract are required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employment permit followed by the appropriate employment visa, entry and Stamp 1 registration
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is assignment-based employment, not location-independent remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential long-term residence may become relevant after qualifying employment-permit residence, but the route requires an Irish client assignment throughout its own eligibility period
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: It does not fit the stated ordinary foreign-client profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Qualifying registered Stamp 1 residence can be reckonable toward general naturalisation
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant must first satisfy the non-fitting Irish-contract permit rules.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the foreign employer must hold a services contract with an Irish entity and transfer the employee to work on that Irish contract. An unrelated foreign-client remote contract is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: STEP uses a funding requirement rather than a monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: €50,000 available funding
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is start-up funding, not recurring personal income.

income_requirement_display.value: €50,000 start-up funding plus an innovative business proposal
income_requirement_display.notes: Approximately US$57,835 at the ECB reference rate of €1 = US$1.1567 on 14 August 2026; it is not a monthly threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The applicant proves available funding and its source, not a prescribed number of income months.

key_requirements.requirement: At least €50,000 available funding.
An innovative business proposal assessed by an evaluation committee.
Good character and no criminal convictions.
The approved business must be established and pursued full time; other employment is prohibited.

initial_validity.value: Residence permission is issued following approval; the current page does not state a single initial duration
initial_validity.notes: Exact permission dates are set in the approval and registration documentation.

extension_rules.value: Continued permission depends on establishing and working full time in the approved business and satisfying programme conditions
extension_rules.notes: The official page states that status may be withdrawn if conditions are breached.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct residence permission after STEP approval, followed by registration
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a genuine entrepreneur residence route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic direct permanent residence is granted; later status depends on applicable residence rules and continued lawful permission
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A precise STEP-to-long-term-residence entitlement was not established from the reviewed official pages.

path_to_citizenship.value: Lawful reckonable residence may ultimately support naturalisation, subject to the stamp issued and general five-year rules
path_to_citizenship.notes: This alternative is rejected for profile fit, not necessarily because settlement is impossible.

rejected_routes.notes: Independently accessible and residence-oriented, but rejected because it requires an innovative funded start-up pursued full time. Continuing ordinary software work for a foreign employer or client is insufficient and other employment is prohibited.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The programme is based on a recent qualifying Irish award.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly income threshold; requires a qualifying Irish higher-education award
income_requirement_display.notes: The applicant's existing foreign university degree does not satisfy the requirement to graduate under the Irish programme.

income_proof_months.notes: Not an income-based route.

key_requirements.requirement: A qualifying award from a recognised Irish institution under the Third Level Graduate Programme.
Stamp 1G graduates may work but may not operate a business or be self-employed.

initial_validity.value: Generally 12 months for Level 8 graduates and up to 24 months in two 12-month periods for Level 9 or above
initial_validity.notes: Subject to the programme's award and timing conditions.

extension_rules.value: Level 9-or-above graduates may obtain a second 12-month period if programme conditions are met; the status is intended to facilitate obtaining qualifying employment
extension_rules.notes: It is not an indefinitely renewable remote-work permission.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Requires completing qualifying higher education in Ireland first
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant's foreign degree alone does not directly grant residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Requires conversion to another qualifying status, normally employment-based permission
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Stamp 1G itself is not permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Graduate Stamp 1G can be reckonable, but the applicant must first study in Ireland and later obtain another sustainable permission
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not a direct degree-recognition immigration route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a new qualifying Irish qualification and expressly bars self-employment. It is not available merely because the applicant already holds a relevant foreign university degree.

summary.value: A foreign software-engineering degree alone does not create an independent Irish residence route. Study permission requires admission to an Irish programme, while the post-study Stamp 1G route requires a qualifying Irish award and does not permit self-employment.
summary.notes: Education can form a separate study-to-employment pathway, but it is not a direct qualification-based residence route for the current foreign-contract profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Irish tax resident if present for at least 183 days in a tax year, or for at least 280 days across that year and the preceding year, provided presence is at least 30 days in each relevant year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence, ordinary residence and domicile can alter the final result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal Income Tax rate, not an expected effective rate. A single person pays 20% up to €44,000 and 40% on the balance before credits; USC and PRSI can apply additionally.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening value for ordinary Class S self-employed PRSI on gross income after capital allowances. Cross-border employee social-security treatment may differ.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the published €650 annual minimum Class S PRSI contribution, converted at €1 = US$1.1567. PRSI is assessed annually, not paid as a universal fixed monthly nomad charge.

special_tax_regimes.value: Ireland has residence, ordinary-residence and domicile rules, including potentially different treatment for non-Irish-domiciled individuals; no special digital-nomad tax regime was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Remittance-basis and treaty questions require individual advice and depend on domicile, income character and remittance facts.

taxes.caveats: Ireland has no selected nomad route. Tax exposure can arise even for a non-resident when foreign employment duties are physically performed in Ireland. Income Tax, USC and PRSI are separate charges; credits, deductions, domicile, treaty residence and social-security coordination materially affect the effective burden.

taxation_system.value: Progressive Income Tax of 20% and 40%, plus progressive USC and potentially PRSI. For a single person in 2026, the 20% Income Tax band ends at €44,000; USC reaches 8% above €70,044, with a further 3% USC surcharge on relevant self-employed income above €100,000.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in one tax year or 280 days over the current and preceding tax years, subject to the 30-day minimum in each year for the two-year test.
taxation_system.income_scope: Irish-resident and domiciled individuals are generally taxable on worldwide income, subject to treaty relief. Non-residents can still be taxed on Irish-source income and foreign employment income attributable to duties performed in Ireland.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad concession. Domicile and remittance-basis rules may affect certain foreign income for non-Irish-domiciled residents and require fact-specific advice.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed individuals with at least €5,000 annual income generally pay Class S PRSI at 4.1%, subject to a €650 annual minimum under the currently published rule. Employee and cross-border cases differ.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard screening rate is the 40% top Income Tax rate, not the effective total. USC can add up to 8%, Class S PRSI 4.1%, and a 3% USC surcharge can apply to self-employed relevant income above €100,000.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First €44,000 annually for a single person without qualifying children in 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at €1 = US$1.1567.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Balance above €44,000 annually for that single-person category
tax_brackets.notes: Other family-status bands differ.
If total income is within the USC exemption, separate exemption rules may apply.
2026 standard USC band.
This brings the cumulative threshold to €70,044.
A further 3% surcharge can apply to self-employed relevant income above €100,000.

taxation_system.notes: Official 2026 rates were used. This describes screening exposure and not a personalised effective-tax calculation.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No Irish digital-nomad immigration or tax category was identified. If a person nevertheless performs employment or self-employment duties while physically in Ireland, ordinary Irish tax rules may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad regime; ordinary employment or self-employment rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 20%/40% progressive Income Tax, plus USC up to 8% and potentially PRSI; 40% is the dashboard Income Tax screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183-day annual test or 280-day two-year test, with the statutory qualifications.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident and domiciled individuals are generally taxed on worldwide income. Even a non-resident may be taxed on foreign employment income for duties performed in Ireland; domicile and treaties can change the result.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found. Domicile/remittance-basis treatment is a general tax concept, not a nomad concession.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Class S self-employed PRSI is generally 4.1% with a €650 annual minimum where applicable. Foreign-employer payroll and international social-security coordination require separate analysis.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed tax or contribution exists; ordinary charges depend on work classification.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: For qualifying Class S self-employment, the published minimum PRSI contribution is €650 annually.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: General visa fees are €60 single-entry, €100 multi-entry and €25 transit; the IRP registration card is generally €300. These do not create nomad eligibility.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No mandatory fixed freelancer tax or nomad levy was identified. Business registration, VAT and professional costs depend on the actual structure.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa, registration and tax obligations are distinct. Paying tax or registering a business does not legalise residence or work.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 183 days does not guarantee no Irish tax: the 280-day test and taxation of duties physically performed in Ireland must also be checked.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary Income Tax, USC and potentially PRSI/payroll rules apply; worldwide-income or remittance-basis treatment depends particularly on domicile and treaty facts.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Tax or sole-trader registration cannot substitute for immigration permission. Stamp 1 must expressly permit business or self-employment.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax information is provided for context only because the immigration profile is not eligible for an Irish nomad route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists, so there is no route-specific time to temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Ireland's employment-based long-term residence framework cannot be assigned to a nonexistent nomad permission. Qualifying employment-permit holders may have separate five-year rules.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Irish naturalisation does not generally require first obtaining permanent residence, so a PR-to-citizenship interval would be misleading.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation commonly requires five years of reckonable residence, but the current profile has no qualifying entry/residence route from which to start that clock.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed current official pages did not expose a stable numeric service time. Processing is case-specific, so no number is inferred.

key_conditions.value: For ordinary adult naturalisation: 1,825 or 1,826 days of reckonable residence, including one continuous year immediately before applying; normally four additional years within the preceding eight; registered permission without gaps, good character, intent to reside, ceremony attendance and declaration of fidelity. Up to 70 days' absence is normally allowed in the final year, with a discretionary additional 30 days in exceptional cases.
key_conditions.notes: The Minister retains discretion even where statutory conditions are met.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must have been married to or in a civil partnership with the Irish citizen for at least three years and have three years of legal residence on the island of Ireland during the preceding five, including the continuous final year.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage counts toward the three-year marriage-duration condition, but it does not remove the separate Irish residence requirement or automatically confer citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The couple must be living together when the application is made and when citizenship is granted.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage or civil partnership must be genuine and enduring; the applicant must live with the Irish spouse, prove both partners' residence, be of good character, intend to reside in Ireland and make the declaration of fidelity. False documents or a sham relationship risk refusal and immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage can also support a separate Stamp 4 application, but immigration permission is not automatic merely from marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For a child born on the island on or after 1 January 2005, citizenship at birth generally requires at least one parent to be Irish, British, entitled to reside without restriction, or a foreign national legally resident on the island for three of the four years immediately before birth, subject to statutory exclusions and details.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically. A child born in Ireland can qualify if at least one migrant parent has the required three years of qualifying legal residence during the four years immediately before birth; otherwise birth alone is insufficient.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Certain residence categories and periods may be excluded by nationality law, so the parent's exact status must be checked.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child is entitled to Irish citizenship where one parent is Irish, subject to proof and the detailed birth/descent rules.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This does not automatically make the migrant father an Irish citizen.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A non-EEA parent of a dependent Irish citizen child may apply for permission to live and work in Ireland, including under applicable Zambrano/Irish Citizen Child principles, but parentage does not itself confer citizenship and each case is assessed against dependency, involvement, conduct and family circumstances.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The child must actually be an Irish citizen; being merely born in Ireland is insufficient.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father may seek a change to residence permission as the parent of an Irish citizen child and, if qualifying Zambrano criteria are met, may receive permission to live and work without an employment permit. There is no automatic permanent residence or citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Active and continuous involvement and genuine emotional or financial support may be relevant; adverse conduct can weigh against permission.

rank.notes: Ireland was tied at rank 4 in the Henley table accessed on 15 August 2026.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score counts destinations accessible without obtaining a conventional visa before departure, including categories such as visa on arrival where Henley's methodology treats them as visa-free access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Calculated as 227 destinations evaluated by Henley minus Ireland's access score of 186. This is an inferred remainder, not a separately displayed Henley category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The inspected Henley ranking did not provide a separate Ireland-specific combined visa-on-arrival/eTA count, so no unsupported breakdown is supplied.

passport.notes: The July/August 2026 Henley ranking showed Ireland tied fourth with an access score of 186. Scores and destination rules change over time.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. English is an official language and is practical for administration, daily life and professional software work throughout Ireland.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The Constitution identifies Irish as the first official language and English as the second official language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages; relying on either alone is not practical for mainstream administration or professional work. English remains the normal practical language for this profile.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national source quantified Russian- or Ukrainian-language service coverage, so the statement is limited to official-language status and practical inference.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate gross monthly equivalent of €1,075.58 average weekly earnings multiplied by 52 and divided by 12, then converted at €1 = US$1.1567.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate gross monthly equivalent of €44,816 median annual earnings in 2024, the latest official annual median located.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the 2026 statutory annual minimum of €28,696.20; this is a statutory floor for a full-rate worker, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Converted from preliminary Q1 2026 average weekly employee earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Converted from the latest located official median annual earnings, covering 2024.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD conversion is supplied because the reviewed current official sources do not publish a national maximum employee salary. Published upper bands and percentile thresholds are distribution measures, not the largest observed salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage from 1 January 2026, expressed as the official annual equivalent divided by 12.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Preliminary whole-economy average employee earnings for Q1 2026, annualised by multiplying weekly earnings by 52 and dividing by 12.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median annual employee earnings for 2024 divided by 12. Employments active fewer than 50 weeks were excluded from the annual analysis.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Current official sources publish means, medians, open-ended earnings bands, deciles and percentile thresholds, but none publishes the largest observed national employee salary. The €1,600-or-more weekly band and top-1%/top-0.1% thresholds are not maxima, so a national maximum monthly salary is not a defined published statistic and the value remains null.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross employee earnings: statutory full-rate minimum for the minimum field, preliminary Q1 2026 whole-economy weekly mean for the average, and 2024 administrative-data annual median for the median
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly equivalents; underlying periods differ as explained
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are employee earnings for workers/residents and a statutory minimum, not immigration income thresholds. USD conversions use the ECB 14 August 2026 reference rate of €1 = US$1.1567 and are rounded. Five additional official earnings/distribution sources were checked for a national maximum; they publish averages, open-ended bands or percentile thresholds rather than a maximum.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No single official current national cost-of-living amount comparable to the salary fields was established. Housing and household circumstances vary substantially, so no unsupported estimate is provided.
