settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Ireland has no digital-nomad permission to use as an entry status. Visitor presence, tax registration or sole-trader registration does not authorise residence or remote work.
settlement_track.summary: Ireland has a well-defined five-year naturalisation framework for people who first obtain qualifying reckonable residence, but no current ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route supplies that residence. The applicant would need a materially different basis such as qualifying Irish employment, an innovative funded start-up, Irish family rights or study followed by another status.
settlement_track.notes: The previous false result is confirmed and the focused unresolved-field audit adds official evidence explaining why no national maximum salary is reported.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No ordinary route permits a non-EEA software engineer to reside in Ireland solely while serving an unrelated foreign employer or client. Available alternatives introduce Irish employment/client, start-up, study or family requirements.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed using 34 distinct canonical source URLs, including five newly added official earnings-distribution sources and inspection of at least 15 directly relevant URLs in this pass. Ireland remains ineligible because no ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route exists. Remaining nulls are explained where a route or stable published statistic does not exist; specifically, official earnings sources do not publish a national maximum salary.

data.selection_summary: Israel has no confirmed digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, independent freelance, or self-employed immigration status for an ordinary software engineer working under a foreign contract. Registering a business or National Insurance file does not legalize immigration status; available alternatives depend on an Israeli employer, study, a genuine family relationship, or eligibility under the Law of Return.

visa_application.title: Visas and status in Israel
visa_application.notes: This is the official general visa and status portal. No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker application channel was found. The applicant must instead determine whether a separate employer, family, study, or Law of Return category applies.

rejected_routes.route_name: B/1 foreign-expert work visa and permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The foreign-expert rules include employer-side wage requirements, including a double-average-wage standard for relevant expert cases, but no independent remote-worker income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Applicable foreign-expert wage requirement, commonly at least twice the average wage for the relevant expert category
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The precise applicable wage and category must be verified by the Israeli employer under the current permit procedure.

income_requirement_display.value: Employer-sponsored wage requirement; no remote-worker income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Applicable expert cases generally require at least twice the average wage
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employment condition, not an independently provable foreign-income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No applicant-controlled foreign-income history requirement applies; the sponsoring employer supplies the employment and permit documentation.

key_requirements.requirement: A licensed Israeli employer must first obtain authorization to employ the foreign expert.
The worker may work only for the registered, licensed employer and in the authorized role.
A valid B/1 work and stay license, employment contract, passport, insurance, and category-specific documentation are required.

initial_validity.value: Determined by the approved employer permit and B/1 license
initial_validity.notes: The official service does not state one universal initial term for every expert category.

extension_rules.value: Employer-led extensions may be requested, normally subject to a cumulative 63-month limit for foreign-expert work authorization unless an exception applies.
extension_rules.notes: Extensions remain tied to the authorized employer and category.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved B/1 license permits temporary stay and work for the sponsoring Israeli employer.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not an independent remote-worker residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No ordinary transition from this temporary employer-specific work route to permanent residence was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence requires a separate legal basis.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct citizenship path exists from the B/1 expert route; ordinary naturalization first requires permanent residence under a separate basis.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Temporary employer-sponsored work does not itself satisfy that prerequisite.

rejected_routes.notes: This route can fit a locally hired software expert, but it fails the selection because the application is employer-led, employment is restricted to the licensed Israeli employer, and it is not a settlement route for ongoing foreign-contract work.

rejected_routes.route_name: A/1 temporary residence for persons eligible under the Law of Return

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum monthly income is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published income threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility is ancestry/status based rather than income based.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; proof of Law of Return eligibility is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Foreign employment or freelance income is not the eligibility basis.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligibility for Aliyah under the Law of Return must be established.
Applicants provide a valid passport, photographs, an explanation letter, and original authenticated evidence of eligibility.
The application is submitted in person to the Population and Immigration Authority.

initial_validity.value: Up to 5 years
initial_validity.notes: The holder may live and work in Israel while deciding whether to make Aliyah and become a citizen.

extension_rules.value: After five years, an eligible holder may choose Israeli citizenship or apply for A/5 temporary residence.
extension_rules.notes: The official page describes this decision point rather than an ordinary remote-worker renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A/1 directly provides temporary residence and permission to work for eligible persons.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Eligibility is based on the Law of Return.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The official page identifies possible conversion to A/5 temporary residence, not direct permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate status decision is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: An eligible holder may choose to become an Israeli citizen after the A/1 period, subject to the Law of Return process.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This special ancestry/status route cannot be assumed from the supplied software-engineer profile.

rejected_routes.notes: This route is independently usable and settlement-oriented only for applicants who separately qualify under the Law of Return. Because no such eligibility was supplied, it is an alternative rather than a match for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.route_name: B/2 visitor or tourist status followed by self-employed registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold exists because this is not a residence or work route.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published remote-worker income threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Visitor eligibility is not a freelance-residence program.

income_requirement_display.value: No qualifying income threshold; visitor and tax registration do not create work residence
income_requirement_display.notes: Opening a tax or National Insurance file is an administrative tax step, not immigration authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker income-proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: A B/2 visa or ETA is for visitor entry and does not provide a qualifying work-residence route.
Tax and National Insurance registration does not change immigration status.
A separate visa or residence basis is required to live and work lawfully in Israel.

initial_validity.notes: Permitted stay depends on the entry authorization and border decision; no universal remote-work term was established.

extension_rules.value: Any visitor extension remains visitor status and does not convert the person into an independently authorized remote worker.
extension_rules.notes: No visitor-to-freelancer legalization procedure was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic or confirmed conversion from visitor entry plus business registration to qualifying temporary residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Tax registration cannot substitute for immigration permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No path from this scenario is published.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate family, Law of Return, employer, or other lawful status would be needed.

path_to_citizenship.value: No path from this scenario exists.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires permanent residence, which this scenario does not provide.

rejected_routes.notes: Entering as a visitor and opening a self-employed or bank account does not legalize foreign-contract remote work or establish a citizenship-oriented residence track.

summary.value: A/2 student status can be obtained for qualifying study without a local employer and provides temporary study residence, but a university degree by itself creates no independent skilled residence route. No direct transition from A/2 study status to permanent residence or citizenship for an ordinary foreign-contract worker was confirmed.
summary.notes: Study requires acceptance and compliance with the student-visa procedure. It is not a points-tested or degree-based settlement program and is not a substitute for work authorization.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence is determined principally by the individual's center of life. Rebuttable residence presumptions apply at 183 or more days in Israel in a tax year, or at least 30 days in the current year and at least 425 aggregate days in the current and preceding two tax years.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The center-of-life test can establish residence even when a day-count presumption is not met; treaties may apply tie-breaker rules.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal screening rate: 47% ordinary graduated tax plus a 3% surtax above ILS 721,560. It is not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Top combined 2026 National Insurance and health-insurance rate for a self-employed person below retirement age, on income above ILS 7,703 and up to ILS 51,910 monthly. The lower combined rate is 7.7%.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Indicative minimum screening amount: income below ILS 3,442 is assessed from that minimum income; applying the 7.7% lower rate gives about ILS 265, approximately USD 87 at ILS 3.057/USD. Actual liability requires individual confirmation.

special_tax_regimes.value: New immigrants and qualifying veteran returning residents can receive substantial relief, including a ten-year exemption on qualifying foreign-source income. Special 2026-2030 relief also exists for qualifying new immigrants and returning residents who arrived in the specified 2025-2026 window. These regimes do not apply merely because someone is a remote worker.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility depends on obtaining the relevant immigrant or returning-resident status and detailed sourcing rules.

taxes.caveats: Israel has no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. Tax results depend on legal immigration status, center of life, income sourcing, employee or self-employed classification, National Insurance residence, and applicable treaties.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal taxation. Israeli tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are generally taxed on Israeli-source income. Ordinary 2026 employment/business rates run from 10% to 47%, with a 3% surtax producing a 50% top marginal rate.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Center of life, with rebuttable 183-day and 30/425-day presumptions.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for Israeli tax residents; Israeli-source income for non-residents, subject to sourcing rules, exemptions, and treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Ten-year foreign-source-income relief for qualifying new immigrants and veteran returning residents, plus detailed 2026-2030 relief for certain eligible arrivals.
taxation_system.social_security: For a 2026 self-employed resident below retirement age, combined National Insurance and health rates are 7.7% up to ILS 7,703 monthly and 18% above that amount up to the ILS 51,910 contribution ceiling. A resident employed by a foreign employer that does not contribute must declare the income and generally pay at self-employed rates.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 50% dashboard value is a maximum marginal screening rate, not an estimate of effective tax. Tax credits and deductions may materially reduce actual tax. Thresholds are annual.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to ILS 84,120
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at ILS 3.057/USD.
USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure is the approximate upper threshold.
Top marginal screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: Current 2026 brackets and contribution rates were captured. PwC is a current reputable secondary tax summary; National Insurance and immigrant-relief sources are official.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No route-specific digital-nomad taxation exists because Israel has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker immigration status. A person lawfully resident through another basis is subject to ordinary Israeli residence, sourcing, income-tax, and National Insurance rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 10%-47%, potentially 50% including the top surtax; 50% is a maximum marginal screening rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Center of life, with rebuttable 183-day and 30/425-day presumptions.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Israeli tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are generally taxed on Israeli-source income. New-immigrant relief can apply only where the separate status and detailed conditions are satisfied.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad regime. Special inbound relief is limited to qualifying new immigrants and veteran returning residents.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A resident working for a foreign employer that does not pay Israeli contributions must declare the income and generally pay contributions at self-employed rates. Self-employed combined 2026 rates are 7.7% and 18% within the published bands.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed nomad payment; ordinary self-employed minimum-assessment rules may apply under another lawful status.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Income below ILS 3,442 monthly is assessed from the published minimum income for contribution purposes; an indicative lower-rate amount is about ILS 265/USD 87 monthly, subject to the NII calculation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad visa fee exists. Other visa fees are category specific; for example, the A/1 and ordinary naturalization service pages each state ILS 195.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Small businesses may qualify for VAT-exempt-dealer registration where expected 2026 turnover does not exceed ILS 122,833 and the occupation is not excluded. Registration itself does not confer immigration status.
fixed_payments.notes: Contribution liability and VAT treatment require confirmation based on residence, business form, profession, turnover, and treaty position.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Spending fewer than 183 days in Israel does not guarantee non-residence because center of life remains decisive and the alternative 30/425-day presumption may apply.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A lawful Israeli tax resident working for a foreign employer is generally exposed to worldwide-income taxation and may need to declare and pay National Insurance personally if the foreign employer does not contribute.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Opening Tax Authority and National Insurance files can establish tax compliance but does not grant a visa, work permission, temporary residence, permanent residence, or citizenship path.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The taxation description is contextual only; it does not cure the absence of a qualifying immigration route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary remote-worker route exists, so there is no route-specific time to temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No transition from ordinary foreign-contract remote work to permanent residence was found.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: A permanent resident may apply after residing in Israel for 3 of the preceding 5 years, but this is a look-back condition rather than a guaranteed number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated for this profile because no qualifying initial status exists and naturalization is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official service page does not publish a typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalization requires current permanent residence, presence in Israel, residence during 3 of the preceding 5 years, settlement or intention to settle, some Hebrew, and relinquishment or prospective cessation of other citizenship. Approval is discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: These conditions do not create an initial immigration route for a foreign-contract remote worker.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The official pages confirm a graduated status procedure and later naturalization for qualifying permanent-resident spouses, but do not publish one universal completion period on the pages inspected.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage or qualifying life partnership with an Israeli citizen or permanent resident can support an application for status through a graduated family procedure. Marriage alone does not immediately confer permanent residence or citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Naturalization as a spouse requires the applicant already to be a permanent resident, share a household, be settled in Israel, and apply while in Israel.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must document a sincere, real, exclusive family unit and a shared center of life. Required civil documents must be properly authenticated, incomplete applications can be rejected, and sham relationships can result in refusal, loss of status, removal, and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The family route is separate from the evaluated remote-worker profile.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship principally follows an Israeli parent. A person born in Israel who has never held any nationality may apply only between ages 18 and 21 after five consecutive years of Israeli residence, subject to statutory conditions; this is not automatic citizenship at birth.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Birth in Israel to two non-citizen migrant parents does not automatically confer Israeli citizenship. A narrow later application route exists for a person who has never held any nationality and meets the age and five-year-residence requirements.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Other humanitarian or statelessness facts require individual legal review.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with an Israeli citizen mother or father generally derives citizenship through that parent, subject to registration and proof of parenthood. Citizenship by descent can be limited for a second generation born abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Where the Israeli citizen is the father, evidence of the parents' relationship or a court determination of parenthood may be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having an Israeli citizen child does not automatically make a foreign parent a citizen or permanent resident. The parent needs a separate family-status, humanitarian, or other legal basis.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic parent-of-citizen naturalization route was found.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship solely because his child is Israeli. If the other parent is Israeli, the father may have a separate genuine-partner or humanitarian case, which remains individually examined.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parenthood can be relevant evidence but is not itself automatic status.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank reported by Passport Index on the Israel dashboard.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category; it excludes visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 40 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. The index separately reports other eVisa and non-admission outcomes.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 153. Rankings and access rules change frequently and should be rechecked before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Hebrew is the state language; English is not official. English is commonly encountered in international technology and business settings, but the official sources inspected do not quantify nationwide English proficiency, so Hebrew remains important for government forms and long-term integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The naturalization service requires some Hebrew and notes that its forms are provided in Hebrew.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is practically useful in sizeable immigrant communities: an official CBS social-survey publication reported Russian as the mother tongue of about 15% of the surveyed population. Ukrainian is not an official language and no current nationwide Ukrainian-use measure was established.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The language survey is older contextual evidence and should not be treated as a current population percentage or an immigration advantage.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the CBS March 2026 average monthly wage of ILS 15,921 at ILS 3.057/USD. This is an average wage indicator, not an immigration threshold.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the first-half 2025 median per salaried employee, ILS 10,586.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the statutory monthly minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the CBS March 2026 average monthly wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the first-half 2025 median wage per salaried employee.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD value is calculated because current official sources do not publish a finite national maximum salary in ILS. The top wage decile is open-ended, and the social-insurance contribution ceiling is not a salary cap.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum for an adult full-time monthly employee from 1 April 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: CBS average monthly wage indicator for March 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median per salaried employee for the first half of 2025.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No finite national maximum salary is published. The National Insurance wage-distribution table leaves the maximum blank, shown as a dash, for both all salaried employees and the open-ended tenth decile. CBS publications report averages, medians, deciles, or subgroup averages rather than the highest individual wage. The ILS 51,910 National Insurance figure is a contribution-assessment ceiling, not a legal or observed salary maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross/current-price wage indicators: CBS average monthly wage, NII median per salaried employee, and statutory adult minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: March 2026; median: first half of 2025; minimum: effective 1 April 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are employee-earnings statistics, not immigration thresholds. The focused audit reviewed current CBS releases and publications, household-income distributions, NII wage tables, statutory-average-wage material, and contribution ceilings. None establishes a finite national maximum salary; the NII total and tenth-decile maximum cells are expressly left open with a dash.

cost_of_living_note.value: Israel has a high comparative price level: the OECD's 2025 economic survey placed it among the five highest-priced OECD economies and above the level expected from its GDP per capita.
cost_of_living_note.notes: National comparative context; actual costs vary substantially by city and household.

settlement_track.summary: Israel has no confirmed ordinary digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or independent freelance residence route. Employer-sponsored work, study, family status, and the Law of Return are separate categories, so the supplied foreign-contract profile has no qualifying starting route to permanent residence or citizenship.
settlement_track.notes: Switching would require an independently qualifying basis such as a genuine family relationship, Law of Return eligibility, or authorized Israeli employment; business registration alone is insufficient.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official visa inventory contains no dedicated status for ordinary work performed remotely for a foreign employer or client. The work route inspected is tied to a licensed Israeli employer, while tax registration does not grant immigration permission.

data.notes: The previous record was audited through a focused unresolved-field pass using current official immigration and labor-market sources. The ineligibility conclusion remains unchanged. For the flagged maximum-salary field, current CBS and NII materials establish that published wage statistics provide averages, medians, decile boundaries, and subgroup averages but no finite national maximum: the NII table shows a dash for the overall and open-ended tenth-decile maximum. The null is therefore intentional and is not a missing-research marker.

data.selection_summary: Italy has an active, independently filed digital-nomad/remote-worker route for highly qualified non-EU professionals. It fits a software engineer working for a foreign employer or client, grants a renewable one-year residence permit, and the Italian government expressly confirms eligibility to apply for EU long-term residence after five years; ordinary naturalisation is available after ten years of continuous legal residence.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad / Remote Worker VISA
visa_application.notes: This is an official Italian consulate route and filing-instructions page, not a centralized online application. Applicants apply through the Italian embassy or consulate responsible for their place of legal residence; the general Visa for Italy portal should be used to identify the competent post and current national-visa form, appointment procedure and fee.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad / Remote Worker Visa and Residence Permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 24,789 annually, or EUR 2,065.75 monthly, using an ECB screening rate of about USD 1.138 per EUR. A salaried remote worker also needs contractual pay satisfying the applicable collective agreement and not below the approximately EUR 33,500 annual ISTAT floor cited by the government.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 24,789 per year for the general income test; salaried remote workers also need approximately EUR 33,500 per year or the higher applicable collective-agreement salary
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold is formula-based—three times the income level used for exemption from participation in health expenditure—so the competent consulate must confirm the amount at filing. EUR 24,789 is the government's published single-applicant example.

income_requirement_display.value: At least EUR 24,789/year (about USD 2,351/month); salaried remote-worker floor about EUR 33,500/year
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR annual formula, approximately converted to USD monthly
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 3 × the health-expenditure exemption income; published example EUR 24,789/year. Remote employees also face an approximately EUR 33,500/year remuneration floor.
income_requirement_display.notes: The lower figure is relevant to self-employed digital nomads. A foreign-employed software engineer should screen against the higher contractual-remuneration rule, approximately EUR 2,792/month or USD 3,177/month at the cited exchange rate.

income_proof_months.notes: The New York consulate accepts the three most recent bank statements, but also lists pay slips, tax returns and other evidence. This is a documentary option, not a universal rule that only three months of income history will suffice.

key_requirements.requirement: Non-EU national performing highly qualified work remotely as a self-employed digital nomad or salaried/collaborating remote worker; the employer or client may be established abroad.

A relevant university degree or qualifying professional experience. The government FAQ states five years generally, reduced to three years for ICT professionals; the applicant's software-engineering degree is the cleaner qualification route.
At least six months of prior experience performing the relevant digital-nomad or remote-work activity.
Health insurance covering medical treatment and hospitalization in Italy for the intended stay.
Suitable accommodation, commonly evidenced by a registered lease, rental contract or ownership document; individual consulates may impose stricter documentary rules.
Remote employees must provide an employment contract or binding offer meeting the remuneration rule and an employer declaration concerning specified immigration and labor-law convictions.
Apply at the competent Italian embassy or consulate; no prior work authorization/nulla osta is required. Apply for the residence permit at the Questura within eight working days after arrival.
Self-employed digital nomads must obtain an Italian VAT number (partita IVA); tax and social-security compliance can affect continued immigration status.

initial_validity.value: National visa up to 365 days, followed by a digital-nomad/remote-worker residence permit lasting one year
initial_validity.notes: The residence permit must be requested within eight working days after entry.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually while minimum income, qualifying remote work, health insurance and the other issuance conditions continue
extension_rules.notes: The government FAQ confirms annual renewal while the issuance conditions remain satisfied. It also identifies a specific absence limitation: renewal may be refused when residence was interrupted continuously for more than six months unless serious, proven reasons justify the interruption. The rule is conditional rather than an automatic or unlimited extension entitlement.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The national visa is followed directly by a work-based residence-permit application at the local Questura; work may begin once that permit is requested.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence status, not visitor or workcation permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The government expressly confirms that digital-nomad and remote-worker residence permits can lead to EU long-term residence after five years of regular stay. Annual renewal can preserve the foreign remote-work basis.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The government FAQ distinguishes eligibility for EU long-term residence from conversion to other ordinary permits: the latter is not allowed under the ministry interpretation described there. That conversion restriction does not remove the expressly stated five-year long-term residence path.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation may be requested after ten years of continuous legal residence by a non-EU national. The route supplies legal residence and is expressly capable of reaching long-term residence after five years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary rather than automatic and requires continuous registration, qualifying income, B1 Italian, tax compliance and a satisfactory record.

best_routes.notes: This route directly fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work and does not require an Italian employer, local customer, investment, startup or exceptional-talent award. It is settlement-oriented: the government expressly confirms a five-year path to EU long-term residence, although the permit generally cannot be converted to another temporary-permit category.

rejected_routes.route_name: EU Blue Card / locally employed highly qualified worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly USD threshold is inserted because the current official rule is dynamic: the Italian employment contract or binding offer must pay at least the applicable national collective-agreement remuneration and in all cases at least the latest ISTAT annual average gross remuneration per employee work unit. The reviewed official Blue Card pages do not state a stable current euro amount from which a defensible monthly USD figure can be calculated. This route is also excluded from selection because the Italian employer must initiate it.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least the applicable national collective-agreement remuneration and no less than the latest ISTAT annual average gross remuneration per employee work unit
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The governing circular points to a periodically updated ISTAT measure instead of fixing a permanent euro threshold. The exact applicable floor should therefore be verified when the Italian employer files.

income_requirement_display.value: Dynamic Italian-employment salary floor; no stable current euro amount confirmed
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Applicable collective agreement and latest ISTAT annual average gross remuneration
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: The higher applicable constraint is the relevant collective-agreement remuneration, subject to an absolute floor equal to the latest ISTAT annual average gross remuneration per employee work unit.
income_requirement_display.notes: This employer-sponsored threshold is not the digital-nomad income test and is not applicable to the supplied foreign-employer/client selection scenario.

income_proof_months.notes: The official procedure relies on an Italian employment contract or binding offer and employer filing, not a stated number of months of the applicant's historical income.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying Italian employment contract or binding job offer; the Italian employer presents the residence-contract proposal or work-authorization filing.
Higher professional qualification through qualifying education or professional experience and remuneration satisfying both the collective-agreement and ISTAT-based floors.

initial_validity.value: Two years for an indefinite employment contract; otherwise the contract term plus three months
initial_validity.notes: The entry visa itself cannot exceed 365 days; the subsequent Blue Card residence permit follows the stated employment-contract rules.

extension_rules.value: Renewable only while the applicant continues to satisfy the Blue Card conditions through qualifying Italian employment; permit duration remains two years for an indefinite contract or the fixed contract term plus three months
extension_rules.notes: The reviewed official sources do not publish a separate universal number of permitted renewals. They establish contract-linked validity and provide for refusal, non-renewal or revocation when the statutory Blue Card conditions cease to be met. Continued qualifying local employment is therefore essential.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available through qualifying Italian employment after employer-initiated authorization, entry visa and residence-permit filing.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The employer, rather than the foreign worker acting independently, initiates the core work-authorization procedure.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: EU long-term residence may generally be available after five years of qualifying continuous legal residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not cure the local-employer mismatch.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially contributes to ordinary legal-residence naturalisation, but only through a local-employment route.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary non-EU residence-based naturalisation generally requires ten years of legal residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Attractive for skilled software engineers seeking Italian employment, but it is not independently usable for the supplied foreign-employer/client profile and is unnecessary because Italy has a dedicated remote-work route.

summary.value: No separate residence route was confirmed that grants residence merely because the applicant holds a relevant degree. The degree is valuable because it can establish the highly qualified status required for the independently filed digital-nomad/remote-worker route.
summary.notes: This field excludes the digital-nomad route itself and asks whether education alone supplies a distinct residence basis.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Italian tax resident when, for most of the tax year—normally at least 183 days, counting fractions of days—any one of the statutory tests is met: civil-law residence, personal/family domicile, physical presence, or registration in the resident-population register, the latter being rebuttable.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Remote work physically performed in Italy for most of the year is sufficient for tax residence. A treaty may resolve dual residence differently.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top national IRPEF marginal/screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Regional and municipal surtaxes and social-security contributions may apply in addition.

social_contributions_percent.notes: 2026 Gestione Separata rate for a self-employed professional with a VAT number and no other compulsory pension coverage: 25% pension contribution plus 0.72% additional contribution and 0.35% ISCRO. Remote employees, persons already insured elsewhere, treaty-covered workers and regulated professionals can have different treatment.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly INPS payment applies to the profiled self-employed professional; the cited contribution is percentage-based. Insurance premiums, visa fees and residence-card charges depend on provider, consulate and filing stage.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax exemption exists. A qualifying new resident may potentially use the impatriate-worker regime, generally taxing only 50% of eligible Italian employment or professional income for five tax periods, subject to prior non-residence, highly qualified work, Italian work-presence and minimum-residence commitments. A separate EUR 300,000 annual substitute tax for foreign income is aimed at very high-income new residents and is not an ordinary nomad benefit.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility of a particular foreign-employer or foreign-client arrangement for the impatriate regime requires professional filing-level analysis.

taxes.caveats: Immigration status does not itself determine tax classification. Liability depends on days and personal ties, whether the person is an employee or self-employed professional, where services are physically performed, partita IVA and VAT treatment, social-security agreements, permanent-establishment/payroll exposure for the foreign employer, treaty tie-breakers and foreign tax credits.

taxation_system.value: Italian tax residents are generally subject to progressive IRPEF on worldwide income. For 2026 the national brackets are 23%, 33% and 43%, with regional and municipal additions potentially payable. Self-employed digital nomads normally need a partita IVA and may owe percentage-based INPS contributions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Tax residence generally arises when any statutory residence, domicile, physical-presence or registration test is met for most of the tax year, normally 183 days.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are generally taxed on Italian-source income, subject to treaties and source rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Potential impatriate-worker relief can reduce the taxable portion of qualifying work income, but it is conditional and not specific to the digital-nomad visa. The high-net-worth foreign-income substitute tax is EUR 300,000 annually for qualifying moves from 2026.
taxation_system.social_security: Italian social-security law generally applies irrespective of the employer/client's nationality unless a bilateral agreement preserves foreign coverage. A self-employed professional without other compulsory coverage generally faces 26.07% Gestione Separata contributions in 2026.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 43% is the top national marginal rate, not an effective rate. Regional and municipal surtaxes are additional and location-dependent. Deductions, credits, special regimes and social contributions materially change the final burden.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold using about USD 1.138 per EUR; local surtaxes are separate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over EUR 28,000 and up to EUR 50,000
tax_brackets.notes: The USD figure represents the upper threshold. Italy reduced this bracket from 35% to 33% from 2026.
Top marginal national rate; regional and municipal additions are not included.

taxation_system.notes: Current parliamentary, statutory and INPS material was used. Individual outcomes still require Italian tax and social-security advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The digital-nomad permit has no visa-specific tax holiday. A tax-resident remote worker is screened under ordinary progressive IRPEF, potentially with impatriate relief if all independent tax conditions are met. Self-employed permit holders must obtain a partita IVA and ordinarily address VAT, income tax and INPS.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital nomad/remote worker residence permit; ordinary employee or self-employed taxation according to contract structure
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive national IRPEF: 23% / 33% / 43%; 43% is the top marginal screening rate, before local surtaxes and social contributions
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Most-of-year statutory tests, including 183 days of physical presence; treaty rules can resolve dual residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident is generally taxable on worldwide income. Compensation for services physically performed from Italy may be Italian work income even when paid by a foreign employer or client; treaty credits may relieve double taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No special nomad exemption. Conditional impatriate-worker relief may exclude 50% of qualifying work income from the tax base for five periods, but eligibility must be separately established.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Italian coverage generally applies unless a bilateral social-security agreement preserves foreign coverage. A foreign employer may need Italian payroll analysis. Self-employed digital nomads require a VAT number; the 2026 Gestione Separata screening rate is 26.07% where no other compulsory coverage applies.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly tax or social-security payment confirmed; percentage contributions and filing fees apply
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: For an unprotected self-employed professional, 26.07% of the applicable contribution base in 2026. Different employee, treaty or prior-coverage rates may apply.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: A non-refundable national-visa fee is payable and changes periodically; residence-permit/card and stamp charges also apply. No single current worldwide amount was published by the reviewed route pages, so the competent consulate must confirm it.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Self-employed nomads must open a partita IVA. VAT obligations and any accountant, registration or insurance costs depend on turnover, regime and activity; no universal fixed amount was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health-insurance cost is mandatory for immigration but market-priced rather than a state tax. The absence of a universal fixed monthly figure should not be read as absence of tax, social-security or administrative costs.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence because the residence, domicile or registration tests can independently apply. Italian-source work income, payroll, VAT and treaty issues can also arise before tax residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Plan for an Italian return and worldwide-income reporting, progressive IRPEF up to 43%, local surtaxes and social-security/payroll analysis. Investigate impatriate relief before the move rather than assuming eligibility.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A self-employed digital nomad must obtain a partita IVA and ordinarily invoice, file income/VAT returns as applicable and pay INPS. The 26.07% Gestione Separata rate is the relevant 2026 screen for an unprotected freelance professional.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax residence and special-regime eligibility are fact-sensitive. Obtain advice concerning the applicant's nationality, foreign employer/client, treaty and social-security agreement before filing.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The route directly produces a one-year residence permit after entry and the required Questura filing; it does not require years on another status.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: After five years of regular stay, the digital-nomad/remote-worker permit holder may apply for EU long-term-resident status. This is application eligibility, not automatic issuance.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: For an ordinary non-EU applicant, the naturalisation threshold is ten years of continuous legal residence. Reaching long-term residence around year five therefore leaves approximately five more years before eligibility.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary residence-based naturalisation threshold for a non-EU national; grant is discretionary and processing follows the eligibility period.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: This is the statutory ordinary maximum completion period for applications filed since 20 December 2020, not an observed median. It may be extended to 36 months.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous legal and registered residence, avoid residence-registration gaps and disqualifying absences, document adequate taxable income and tax compliance, satisfy B1 Italian, and pass security/good-character review. Naturalisation is not automatic after ten years.
key_conditions.notes: The nomad permit generally cannot convert into another temporary permit, but conversion is unnecessary for the expressly confirmed five-year EU long-term-residence path.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse of an Italian citizen may apply after two years of legal residence in Italy following marriage, or after three years of marriage when residing abroad. These periods are halved when the couple has children.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A pre-existing genuine marriage to an Italian citizen can count: the relevant two-year Italian-residence or three-year overseas-marriage period runs from marriage, subject to registration and continuing marital status. Marriage to another non-Italian migrant does not shorten naturalisation, although the spouse may qualify for family reunification.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: If the spouse becomes Italian later, official guidance indicates the period runs from the spouse's naturalisation oath.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage or civil union must be valid and registered in Italy and must continue, without separation, through the citizenship decree. B1 Italian and criminal/security checks apply. Authorities may scrutinize civil-status records and the genuine continuation of the relationship; sham marriage can lead to refusal, loss of status and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage creates an accelerated application route, not automatic citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Italy primarily follows descent. Birth in Italy alone does not confer citizenship, except residual protections for children of unknown/stateless parents or parents unable to transmit citizenship. A child born in Italy to foreign parents may elect citizenship after continuous legal residence from birth to adulthood under the statutory procedure.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Italy to two foreign migrant parents normally receives the parents' transmissible nationality, not Italian citizenship automatically. Residual jus-soli/statelessness safeguards and the later continuous-residence election rule may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' national laws must also be checked to determine whether citizenship is transmitted.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born to an Italian mother or father is generally Italian by descent. For children born abroad, 2025 reforms introduced additional limits and declaration/residence conditions in some cases; a child born in Italy to an Italian parent remains the straightforward case.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage and civil-status registration must be established.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a child in Italy does not help merely because of the birthplace, since the child is normally not Italian. Where the child is Italian through the other parent, the foreign parent may have a family-residence basis, but citizenship is neither automatic nor immediate.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The exact family permit should be verified with the Questura for the family's circumstances.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship from the child's birth. If the other parent is Italian and the child is Italian, parentage may support family residence and marriage/family naturalisation planning, but the father must independently satisfy the applicable procedure.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No accelerated father-specific naturalisation rule was established beyond ordinary marriage, family and residence provisions.

rank.notes: Italy is tied at fourth in the current 2026 ranking.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley access score, which combines destinations accessible without a prior visa, including visa-on-arrival and similar qualifying access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The reviewed Henley ranking does not publish a separate reliable visa-in-advance count for Italy.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Henley publishes a combined access score rather than a separate current visa-on-arrival/eTA subtotal on the reviewed ranking page.

passport.notes: Italy has a very strong EU passport, but the 186 figure should not be interpreted as strictly visa-free only because Henley's methodology combines several no-prior-visa access categories.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is practical in international technology teams and major cities, but not a substitute for Italian in immigration, leases, healthcare, taxation and long-term integration. EF's 2025 self-selected test dataset gives Italy a score of 513 and global rank 59, while Italian IT respondents scored considerably higher at 599.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected testing dataset rather than a representative census. B1 Italian is required for ordinary naturalisation.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and no reliable nationwide evidence was found that either is broadly usable for administration or daily services. Community support may exist locally, but applicants should expect to rely on Italian and, in international settings, English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The focused additional-source review did not identify an official nationwide Russian/Ukrainian proficiency measure, so no unsupported prevalence claim is made.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the OECD 2025 average gross wage of EUR 36,594 annually, or EUR 3,049.50 monthly, at about USD 1.138 per EUR.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of ISTAT's 2022 median gross annual remuneration of EUR 12,550 per non-agricultural private-sector job position: EUR 1,045.83 per month by simple annual division, or about USD 1,190. This measure includes job positions without contribution coverage for every week and is not a full-time-equivalent national employee median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Italy had no national statutory minimum wage on 1 January 2026; sectoral collective agreements set wage floors, so no single national USD figure is valid.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly conversion of the OECD 2025 gross average wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2022 ISTAT median gross annual remuneration per private-sector job position. It is an observed job-position measure containing partial-year or low-intensity positions, not a full-time-equivalent median salary for all Italian residents.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: There is no meaningful statutory national maximum wage. ISTAT reports that the highest-paid employee decile earned more than EUR 26.60 per hour in 2022, but that is an open-ended decile boundary, not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: No national statutory minimum wage; sectoral collective-agreement floors apply
min_salary_local_currency.notes: A software engineer's applicable minimum depends on classification and collective agreement.

average_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 36,594 gross per year (EUR 3,049.50 per month)
average_salary_local_currency.notes: OECD 2025 average-wage measure, not household income and not the immigration income threshold.

median_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 12,550 gross per year per non-agricultural private-sector job position in 2022 (EUR 1,045.83/month by simple division)
median_salary_local_currency.notes: ISTAT publishes this as the median annual remuneration per job position. Nearly 60% of the measured positions lacked contribution coverage for every week of the year, the median position lasted 348 days, and one worker may hold multiple positions. It is therefore a precise official median for private-sector job positions, but not a full-time-equivalent national monthly median for individual workers.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No national maximum salary published
max_salary_local_currency.notes: ISTAT's highest decile boundary is not a maximum and is therefore not inserted as one.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: OECD 2025 annual gross average wage for a single average worker; ISTAT 2022 median annual gross remuneration per non-agricultural private-sector job position, including partial-year positions; supporting ISTAT employee-earnings distribution covers establishments with at least 10 employees
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 OECD average; 2022 ISTAT median and distribution published in 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are resident-worker labor-market figures, not digital-nomad visa income requirements. Italy lacks a single statutory minimum wage. The newly populated median is an official private-sector job-position median and should not be compared directly with the OECD full-year average without accounting for its partial-year and job-position basis; no national maximum was invented.

cost_of_living_note.value: Costs vary substantially by city and region. ISTAT reports average resident-household net income of EUR 39,501 in 2024 and median household income of EUR 31,704, while 22.6% of people were at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2025. Consumer prices rose by an average 1.5% in 2025. These figures provide affordability context but are not a personal remote-worker budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Household income should not be confused with an individual wage or visa threshold.
