settlement_track.summary: Italy's digital-nomad/remote-worker permit is qualifying work residence, not a visitor-like nomad stay. The Italian government expressly states that five years on these permits can lead to EU long-term-resident status, while ordinary non-EU naturalisation is available after ten years of continuous legal residence.
settlement_track.notes: The Ministry considers the permit non-convertible into other temporary permit categories, but no switch is required for the confirmed long-term-residence path. Long-term residence and citizenship remain applications subject to continuity, income, language, integration, tax and character requirements.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official rules expressly allow highly qualified remote employees and collaborators whose employer or client is established abroad, as well as self-employed digital nomads. No Italian employer, local customer, investment or startup is required.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including six newly added canonical sources. The rejected Blue Card income note now explains the official dynamic salary formula instead of treating the field as unresearched; its renewal field now states the contract-linked duration and why no universal renewal count is published. The labor-market median now uses ISTAT's exact EUR 12,550 gross annual median per private-sector job position, with explicit warnings that partial-year positions make it unlike a full-time-equivalent national worker median. The independently filed digital-nomad/remote-worker route remains a strong match, while consulate-specific documents, tax-regime eligibility and social-security treaty treatment still require filing-level verification.

reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad / Remote Worker Visa and Residence Permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: EU long-term residence permit
requirements: Maintain annual residence-permit renewals and the highly qualified remote-work conditions.
Meet the ordinary EU long-term residence requirements, including qualifying continuity and sufficient resources.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The government expressly confirms that digital-nomad and remote-worker residence permits can lead to EU long-term residence after five years of regular stay. Annual renewal can preserve the foreign remote-work basis.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The government FAQ distinguishes eligibility for EU long-term residence from conversion to other ordinary permits: the latter is not allowed under the ministry interpretation described there. That conversion restriction does not remove the expressly stated five-year long-term residence path.

data.selection_summary: Jamaica does not currently offer an implemented digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. A 2024 government Green Paper proposes a 1–3 year Nomad Visa, but it remains a policy proposal with no active application channel or published income amount. Existing work-permit rules cover gainful work performed in Jamaica; ordinary applications require a prospective employer, while self-employed applications require an investment proposal and proof of investment. Those conditions do not fit ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

visa_application.title: Immigration | Passport, Immigration and Citizenship Agency
visa_application.notes: No application for a digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status was found. PICA is the official immigration starting point. Work-permit applications use the Ministry of Labour process, but that route is rejected for this profile.

rejected_routes.route_name: Proposed Nomad (Live a Yard, Work Abroad) Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The Green Paper says the amount will be prescribed by the Ministry of National Security but does not state it.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The Green Paper does not publish a prescribed local-currency amount.

income_requirement_display.value: Proposed threshold is unpublished and would be prescribed by the Ministry of National Security
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Amount prescribed by the Ministry of National Security
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a proposed policy, not an open program.

income_proof_months.notes: Proposed proof of employment and monthly income for the three months before application.

key_requirements.requirement: Proposed foreign employment, self-employment, or business must be registered and domiciled outside Jamaica.
Proposed proof of sufficient means and adequate health insurance.
PICA and the Ministry policy page do not publish active rules, an application form, an application channel, or a prescribed income amount.

initial_validity.value: Proposed 1 to 3 years; not currently implemented
initial_validity.notes: The Ministry continues to publish the document as a Green Paper rather than an implemented visa program.

extension_rules.notes: The proposal does not establish renewal or extension rules.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No current status is granted because the proposal has not been implemented.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: PICA's current immigration categories do not list a nomad visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion or counting rule is established; the proposal describes a stay without the obligations of ordinary or permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Proposed nomad time should not be treated as qualifying settlement residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path is established for the proposed visa.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation requires qualifying residence, but no rule confirms that proposed nomad time would count.

rejected_routes.notes: The proposal conceptually matches foreign remote work but is not an available visa as of the research date. Planned programs cannot qualify for selection.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current instructions publish no minimum personal-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current instructions publish no minimum personal-income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; investment evidence required
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Investment proposal and supporting financial evidence
income_requirement_display.notes: Absence of a numerical threshold does not make this an ordinary freelancer route.

income_proof_months.notes: The instructions require bank statements and investment evidence but specify no fixed look-back period.

key_requirements.requirement: Non-Jamaicans engaging in gainful work in Jamaica generally need a work permit.
Self-employed applicants complete both applicant and employer sections and explain the nature and duration of the work.
An investment proposal and documentary proof of proposed investment, such as ownership evidence and bank statements, are required.
Academic or professional qualifications, or evidence of foreign commercial or professional activity, are required.
The processing fee is JMD 17,250, excluding the work-permit fee payable after approval.

initial_validity.value: For the designated period stated in the work-permit approval
initial_validity.notes: No universal initial term is published; authorization is case-specific.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires a further work-permit process and supporting documents.
extension_rules.notes: A new application is required when changing employers; self-employed renewals remain subject to the permit process.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: After work-permit approval, PICA endorses or extends the holder's stay for the work period.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is work-authorized immigration status, not an ordinary foreign-remote-worker permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: PICA accepts employment-category permanent-residence applications from foreign nationals working in Jamaica for more than three years; business owners must provide registration, tax-compliance, tax-return, and audited-financial-statement evidence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Whether a foreign-client software consultancy with sufficient Jamaican investment would be approved requires filing-level review. The investment and business-substance requirements make the route incompatible with the stated ordinary remote-work profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation is generally possible after five years' residence in aggregate, including the 12 months immediately before application, subject to good character and documentary requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary, and PICA requests a work-permit card or exemption, tax compliance, income evidence, bank statements, and community evidence.

rejected_routes.notes: This is independently fileable on a self-employed basis, but it is an entrepreneur/investment work-permit route. It is rejected because investment evidence and Jamaican business substance are material requirements, not because a local employer is mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitor status has no remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Visitor status has no remote-worker income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold; visitor status is not work authorization
income_requirement_display.notes: A visitor extension cannot substitute for a work permit or qualifying residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: PICA publishes no fixed income-history period for a visitor extension.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport, return ticket, explanation for extension, entry visa if applicable, and fee.
Gainful employment in Jamaica generally requires a work permit.

initial_validity.value: Visitor extensions allow up to 12 months for Commonwealth citizens and up to 6 months for non-Commonwealth citizens.
initial_validity.notes: Initial visa-free or visa-required admission depends on nationality.

extension_rules.value: Apply before the authorized stay expires; approval is discretionary.
extension_rules.notes: PICA lists JMD 10,000 as the ordinary extension processing fee and JMD 50,000 for extension beyond a visa-exemption period.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None; this remains visitor status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not qualifying temporary residence for this selection.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: PICA publishes no visitor-to-permanent-residence conversion for an ordinary foreign remote worker.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Published permanent-residence categories are employment, retirement, marriage, dependency, and certain former unconditional-landing holders.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor status alone creates no citizenship path.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation residence requirements do not turn a visitor extension into a lawful remote-work route.

rejected_routes.notes: Visitor status is temporary and does not authorize the proposed ordinary foreign-contract remote-working arrangement.

summary.value: Enrollment at a Ministry of Education-registered institution supports a student extension or endorsement without a local employer. It requires the institution's registration letter, passport, one-year return ticket, visa if applicable, and fee. PICA does not present study as a direct permanent-residence category, and the reviewed official pages publish no study-to-PR conversion.
summary.notes: This is available for genuine study, not because the applicant already holds a degree, and it is not a foreign-remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual may be Jamaican tax resident by spending at least six months in Jamaica during the calendar year, by visiting with intent to establish residence and doing so, by having an available Jamaican abode and visiting during the year, or through habitual substantial visits; TAJ generally treats three-month visits in four consecutive years as habitual and substantial.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The rule is broader than a simple 183-day test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Resident chargeable income is generally taxed at 25% up to JMD 6 million annually and 30% above it, after the applicable resident threshold.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening aggregate for an ordinary locally registered self-employed person: NIS 6% up to JMD 5 million annual earnings, NHT 3% under current NHT self-employed guidance, and Education Tax 2.25% after relevant deductions. PwC instead states 2% NHT for self-employed persons, while NHT distinguishes 3% for ordinary self-employed contributors and 2% for specified domestic-worker, gardener, and caregiver categories. The official category-specific NHT figure is used, but the applicant's classification and assessment must be confirmed with NHT or TAJ.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer payment is published. NIS, NHT, and Education Tax are earnings-based; self-employed income tax and NHT payments are generally estimated and paid quarterly, although NHT permits monthly payment. Applicable ceilings, minimum or stamp-card mechanics, and contributor classification require case-specific confirmation.

special_tax_regimes.value: Jamaican resident and domiciled individuals are generally taxed on worldwide income. A non-Jamaican-domiciled individual is generally not taxed on foreign-source income unless remitted, but compensation for services rendered in or in relation to Jamaica may still be taxable. No implemented digital-nomad tax holiday was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Domicile, income source, place where services are performed, remittance, treaty residence, and contract structure are decisive. The reviewed 2026/27 revenue measures establish no digital-nomad or general inbound-worker PIT holiday.

taxes.caveats: Immigration permission and taxation are separate. Performing services while physically in Jamaica can create Jamaican taxable income even where the payer and contract are foreign. Obtain Jamaican advice on source, domicile, permanent-establishment or business-registration exposure, GCT, treaty relief, and statutory contributions before working from Jamaica.

taxation_system.value: Progressive national personal income tax with domicile/remittance features for foreign-source income and separate statutory contributions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Calendar-year residence may arise at six months, through an available abode plus a visit, intended residence, or habitual substantial visits.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident and domiciled individuals are generally taxed worldwide; non-residents are taxed on Jamaican-source income; non-Jamaican-domiciled residents are generally taxed on foreign income when remitted, subject to taxation of services rendered in or in relation to Jamaica.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No implemented digital-nomad tax regime was identified. Non-domicile/remittance treatment is general tax law, not a nomad exemption.
taxation_system.social_security: For ordinary local self-employment, screening rates are NIS 6% up to JMD 5 million annual earnings, NHT 3% under current NHT guidance, and Education Tax 2.25% after relevant deductions. PwC reports 2% NHT for self-employed persons, so the NHT contributor category must be confirmed.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For resident individuals, the 2026 calendar-year tax-free amount is JMD 1,876,614 because the monthly threshold changed on 1 April 2026. Income above the threshold is generally taxed at 25%, with chargeable income above JMD 6 million taxed at 30%. Non-residents generally receive no annual threshold and pay 25% from the first dollar, with the upper rate applying where relevant.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate conversion uses roughly JMD 159 per USD from Bank of Jamaica mid-2026 rates.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Chargeable income up to JMD 6,000,000 per year
tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident chargeable income above the tax-free amount and up to the upper-rate boundary
tax_brackets.notes: The JMD 6 million boundary concerns chargeable income; this is a marginal bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Chargeable income over JMD 6,000,000 per year
tax_brackets.notes: This is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The April 2026 TAJ/JIS notice confirms the JMD 1,876,614 resident calendar-year nil-rate amount, while PwC corroborates the 25% and 30% marginal bands. The Income Tax Act is controlling, but its public consolidation does not itself present every 2026 threshold introduced through later annual measures. Foreign-source/remittance and services-performed-in-Jamaica treatment therefore relies on PwC's 31 December 2025 technical review alongside the Act because the current TAJ materials reviewed do not publish an equally detailed interpretation. Contribution guidance is not fully aligned: current NHT guidance says ordinary self-employed persons pay 3%, with 2% for specified domestic-worker, gardener, and caregiver categories, whereas PwC states 2% for self-employed persons generally. This record uses 3% for an ordinary self-employed screening total of 11.25%, but the applicant's NHT classification must be confirmed with NHT or TAJ. The reviewed current Ministry revenue measures and tax summaries publish no implemented digital-nomad PIT exemption.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special route: Jamaica's nomad visa remains a Green Paper proposal, and no nomad-specific tax exemption or contribution regime was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No implemented digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 30% top marginal screening rate under ordinary Jamaican PIT rules; not a nomad rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Ordinary Jamaican residence tests apply and can be triggered by more than physical presence alone.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Non-Jamaican-domiciled persons are generally taxed on foreign-source income when remitted, but compensation for services rendered in or in relation to Jamaica may be taxable regardless of the foreign payer.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No implemented special digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime is published.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If treated as locally self-employed, NIS, NHT, Education Tax, income-tax filing, and potentially business-tax obligations may apply. The ordinary screening aggregate is 11.25%, but NHT category guidance conflicts with PwC and requires confirmation.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment is published
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: NIS 6% up to its earnings ceiling, NHT generally 3% under current official self-employed guidance, and Education Tax 2.25% are percentage-based screening obligations. PwC reports 2% NHT, so actual classification must be confirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad-visa fee exists. Existing fees include JMD 17,250 work-permit processing, JMD 10,000 ordinary extension processing, JMD 100,000 permanent-residence application, and JMD 2,000 registration for non-Commonwealth nationals over 16 staying more than six months.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: GCT, business registration, work-permit issuance fees, and tax-compliance costs depend on activity and structure; no reliable universal monthly amount is published.
fixed_payments.notes: The post-approval work-permit fee varies with the permit and cannot be reduced to a universal monthly amount.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay does not create a lawful remote-work immigration category. Tax residence may still arise through abode, intention, or habitual-visit tests, and services physically performed in Jamaica may be Jamaican-taxable.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary PIT rules apply; 30% is only the top marginal rate. Foreign-source and remittance treatment requires analysis of domicile and where the services are rendered.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect income-tax filing plus possible NIS, NHT, Education Tax, business registration, GCT, and work-permit obligations. The immigration route also requires investment evidence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Because no active nomad route exists, this section screens ordinary Jamaican law rather than a special visa tax package.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary remote-worker temporary residence is currently available.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: This applies only to the alternative employment category: PICA says foreign nationals working in Jamaica for more than three years may apply. It does not apply to visitor status or the unimplemented nomad proposal.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Jamaican naturalisation is based on total residence history rather than a specified number of years after permanent residence, so a separate post-PR number is inapplicable.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Generic naturalisation minimum: five years in aggregate, including continuous residence during the 12 months immediately before filing. This is not a timeline from a qualifying remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: PICA says compliant naturalisation applications are prepared for ministerial submission within 24 months; final approval may take longer.

key_conditions.value: Age 18+, prescribed residence history, good character, intention to reside, work permit or exemption evidence, four Jamaican-born sponsors, newspaper notices, tax compliance, income and bank evidence, and community-activity evidence. Jamaica accepts dual citizenship. PICA's naturalisation requirements do not list a formal language test.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation remains ministerial and discretionary; five years is an eligibility threshold, not guaranteed citizenship.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: PICA states there is no waiting period before the spouse of a Jamaican may submit a citizenship-by-marriage application. This does not mean immediate approval.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Jamaican citizen can support a marriage exemption or extension, permanent residence, and direct application for citizenship by virtue of marriage. Both spouses must provide original civil-status and identity documents.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: For a work-permit marriage exemption, the Ministry says the marriage must be at least six months old before processing; citizenship filing has no waiting period.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship by marriage requires the official marriage certificate, both spouses' birth or citizenship evidence and passports, a police certificate, and other original documents. The Constitution permits refusal where the marriage was entered primarily to obtain citizenship; false evidence or a sham marriage carries serious immigration and legal risk. PICA reports preparation for ministerial approval within 24 months.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage must be legally valid and genuine. Citizenship is not automatic upon marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship to persons born in Jamaica, subject to narrow exceptions for specified diplomatic-immunity and enemy-alien births during occupation.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Jamaica is ordinarily a citizen even when both parents are migrants, unless a narrow constitutional exception applies, principally specified diplomatic-immunity or enemy-occupation circumstances.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' temporary or permanent immigration category ordinarily does not alter territorial birth citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is ordinarily Jamaican if born in Jamaica and can also acquire citizenship by descent when born abroad if the Jamaican parent qualifies under the constitutional descent rule.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Registration and proof of parentage may be required for an overseas birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically give either migrant parent permanent residence or citizenship. PICA's published permanent-residence categories do not expressly list parent of a Jamaican citizen as a standalone category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any discretionary family application should be confirmed directly with PICA.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father receives no automatic citizenship or published automatic PR entitlement. The child's citizenship may be relevant to a discretionary family case, but PICA's listed dependency category concerns persons dependent on a permanent-resident holder, not parents deriving status from a citizen child.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The father must maintain his own lawful immigration status and obtain case-specific advice.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the research date; index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category only.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index count; the index treats eVisa destinations separately.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 37 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations, which the source reports separately.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports mobility score 97, comprising 53 visa-free, 37 visa-on-arrival, and 7 eTA destinations. It is used because the current Henley interactive result did not expose a stable Jamaica breakdown during the audit.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for daily life and business: English is the official language, while Jamaican Patois is widely spoken.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Internet quality and location-specific reliability should still be checked separately.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low without English. The reviewed official-language source does not indicate broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services; English is the practical language for government, contracts, banking, and professional life.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical inference from the official-language environment, not a measured proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: STATIN exposes employment-and-earnings table categories, but the accessible official page does not publish a usable current national average amount. A secondary 2026 estimate was reviewed but not adopted as an official national figure.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The accessible STATIN page publishes no current national median monthly wage. The secondary source estimates JMD 80,000, but its national dataset and methodology are insufficiently transparent for this normalized field.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the statutory JMD 16,000 weekly minimum wage, using 52/12 weeks and roughly JMD 159 per USD. This is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed accessible sources do not establish a sufficiently supported current national average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed accessible sources do not establish a sufficiently supported current national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither source publishes a meaningful national maximum salary; one should not be inferred from job-site ranges.

min_salary_local_currency.value: JMD 16,000 per 40-hour week; approximately JMD 69,333 per month
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum effective 1 June 2025.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: STATIN confirms that official large-establishment earnings series exist, but its accessible page does not expose a usable current national aggregate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The secondary estimate of JMD 80,000 monthly is not adopted because the underlying national dataset and methodology are unclear.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed sources publish no reliable national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory gross minimum wage for the minimum field; national average and median unresolved after official and secondary-source review
average_citizen_salary.period: Weekly minimum converted to monthly equivalent
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum-wage figure is high confidence. Average and median remain null because the official STATIN interface exposes table categories but not a usable current national figure. The USD approximation uses mid-2026 Bank of Jamaica rates.

cost_of_living_note.value: The reviewed official source publishes no household cost-of-living budget. As context only, STATIN reported 6.7% year-on-year CPI inflation in June 2026; CPI measures price change, not the monthly cost of maintaining a household.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing and lifestyle costs vary substantially between Kingston, other urban centres, and rural areas.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The proposed nomad visa is not open and, even as proposed, no rule confirms that its time would count toward permanent residence or naturalisation.
settlement_track.summary: Jamaica is not currently valid: its foreign-remote-worker visa exists only in a Green Paper, not as an implemented application route. The self-employed work permit can potentially feed employment-based PR and naturalisation, but it requires investment evidence and Jamaican business substance inconsistent with ordinary foreign-contract remote work.
settlement_track.notes: Reclassify only if final legislation, operational rules, an application channel, and a confirmed settlement-counting or conversion rule are published.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The conceptually matching nomad visa is pending, while the active self-employed work-permit route requires investment evidence and Jamaican business substance.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed. The tax-system note now distinguishes controlling legislation, current thresholds, foreign-income interpretation, and the unresolved NHT contribution-rate conflict. Jamaica remains ineligible because its nomad proposal is not implemented and active alternatives do not fit ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

data.selection_summary: Japan's Designated Activities status fits eligible foreign-contract digital nomads only for a temporary six-month stay. It cannot be extended, provides no residence card, and has no confirmed route to permanent residence or citizenship. Ordinary software-engineer and highly skilled statuses require qualifying Japan-based activity or a Japanese contracting organization.

visa_application.title: Designated Activities — Digital Nomad / Spouse or Child
visa_application.notes: Official route and document page. Applicants outside Japan generally file through the Japanese embassy or consulate responsible for their residence; this is not a universal online application.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion at JPY 150/USD of the official JPY 10,000,000 annual threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: JPY 10,000,000/year (JPY 833,333/month equivalent)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The applicant's personal annual income must meet the threshold at application.

income_requirement_display.value: JPY 10,000,000/year (about USD 5,556/month)
income_requirement_display.notes: USD value is illustrative and exchange-rate dependent.

income_proof_months.notes: The route requires a foreign tax or income certificate but prescribes no fixed number of bank-statement or income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Citizenship of a listed visa-exempt country or region covered by an applicable Japanese tax convention.
Remote employment for a foreign organization or online services or sales to persons outside Japan; Japanese employment is prohibited.
Personal annual income of at least JPY 10,000,000.
Private medical/travel insurance for the entire stay, including at least JPY 10,000,000 of injury and illness treatment coverage and required death-related cover.
Passport, photograph, activity schedule, current employment or contract evidence, and the documents required by the chosen consular or Certificate of Eligibility procedure.

initial_validity.value: Six months
initial_validity.notes: No residence card is issued; the holder is not a mid-to-long-term resident.

extension_rules.value: Not renewable; another grant can be sought after at least six months outside Japan.
extension_rules.notes: The status cannot support continuous residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct lawful six-month Designated Activities stay without mid-to-long-term resident status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary immigration permission only.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After the digital-nomad stay, PR is possible only after independently qualifying for a settlement-capable status, such as work based on a contract with a Japanese organisation.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The nomad stay is capped at six months without extension. A continuous ordinary foreign-employer remote-work path was not established. Whether an in-country change is accepted and any nomad period is credited remains unconfirmed; ten years refers to the general successor route, not ten years on the nomad visa. Original ISA pages failed to load, so official indexed ISA documents and MOFA were used.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The nonrenewable six-month status cannot establish the generally required five consecutive years of Japanese domicile.

rejected_routes.notes: Valid for temporary foreign-contract remote work, but rejected under the citizenship-oriented selection criteria.

rejected_routes.route_name: Engineer / Specialist in Humanities / International Services

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No single universal threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility instead depends on qualifying work and remuneration comparable to a Japanese worker.

income_requirement_display.value: No universal threshold; Japanese-organization contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign client does not replace the required Japanese contracting organization.

income_proof_months.notes: No route-wide fixed proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying technical, humanities, or international-services activity under a contract with a Japanese public or private organization.
Relevant education or experience and supporting documents from the Japanese organization.

initial_validity.value: Five years, three years, one year, or three months

extension_rules.value: Renewable while qualifying Japan-based activity continues.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Qualifying work status after securing the required Japanese contract.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No single route-wide threshold; points depend on activity, education, experience, age, salary, and other factors.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Category-specific salary requirements and points apply.

income_requirement_display.notes: Not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed route-wide period applies.

Qualifying professional activity connected to an accepting or contracting organization in Japan.

extension_rules.value: Continuation requires qualifying highly skilled activity.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Residence through approved highly skilled activity in Japan.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: PR may be available after three years with 70 points or one year with 80 points.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential naturalization under the general nationality rules.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is points-based and tied to qualifying Japan-based activity, not ordinary foreign-client remote work.

summary.value: Admission to an eligible Japanese educational institution can support Student status without an employer, for a designated period not exceeding four years and three months. It is temporary education-based residence, not direct PR, and does not authorize unrestricted full-time foreign-contract work. An existing foreign degree alone confers no residence status.
summary.notes: Enrollment, financial support, and institutional documents are required.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person is generally resident for Japanese tax purposes if they have a domicile in Japan or maintain a residence continuously for at least one year. A six-month digital nomad is normally a nonresident absent facts establishing domicile, but work physically performed in Japan may still produce Japan-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 183-day concept arises mainly through tax-treaty exemptions, not Japan's basic domestic residence test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top resident national marginal rate, not an expected effective rate; reconstruction surtax and local inhabitant tax are separate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage applies. The official digital-nomad FAQ says holders cannot join Japanese public medical insurance. National Pension is resident-based, and no route-specific pension contribution is imposed by the inspected digital-nomad rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly state payment applies to this route. Mandatory private insurance is market-priced. The FY2026 JPY 17,920 National Pension amount applies to covered Category I residents and is not assigned to this no-residence-card status.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax holiday or rate exists. Applicable tax conventions may exempt qualifying short-stay remuneration when all treaty requirements are satisfied.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty relief is conditional and may require procedural filings.

taxes.caveats: Liability depends on domicile, physical work location, employee versus contractor characterization, payer and permanent-establishment facts, remittances, the applicable treaty, and filing procedures.

taxation_system.value: Residents face progressive national income tax from 5% to 45%, reconstruction surtax, and generally local inhabitant tax. Nonresidents are taxed on Japan-source income, commonly at 20.42% for covered remuneration when treaty relief is unavailable.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile in Japan or residence continuously maintained for at least one year; otherwise generally nonresident.
taxation_system.income_scope: Full residents generally face worldwide-income taxation. Non-permanent residents have restricted foreign-source treatment based on payment and remittance rules. Nonresidents face Japan-source taxation.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special nomad regime; ordinary treaty relief may apply.
taxation_system.social_security: Digital nomads cannot join Japanese public medical insurance and must hold private insurance. National Pension compulsory coverage is resident-based; no route-specific fixed pension contribution was established.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 45% dashboard number is the top national marginal rate. The relevant nonresident screening rate for a short-stay worker may instead be 20.42%, potentially reduced to zero by treaty.

tax_brackets.notes: Before reconstruction surtax and local tax.
Top marginal national rate.

taxation_system.notes: Treaty and contractor analysis requires filing-specific professional advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: A six-month holder is normally a domestic-law nonresident unless a Japanese domicile is established. Work performed physically in Japan may nevertheless be Japan-source. Without treaty relief, covered nonresident remuneration may face 20.42% national tax; many treaties can exempt qualifying short stays.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary digital nomad; normally nonresident screening
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 20.42% nonresident Japan-source remuneration screening rate; potentially treaty-exempt
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or at least one year of continuous residence; the six-month immigration limit is below the latter test, but domicile remains fact-dependent.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign payment does not automatically make remuneration foreign-source when the work is physically performed in Japan.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated tax rate or holiday; ordinary treaty relief may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The official FAQ expressly states that holders cannot join Japanese public medical insurance because they are not mid-to-long-term residents. No Japanese-employer payroll applies to the permitted foreign work, and no route-specific National Pension payment was identified.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed monthly state payment applies. Public medical insurance is unavailable; mandatory private medical/travel insurance has a market-priced premium. Any visa charge is one-off, not monthly.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: JPY 0 identified as a route-specific fixed public contribution. National Pension's fixed Category I amount applies to covered residents, not automatically to this no-residence-card status.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: MOFA's general schedule lists approximately JPY 3,000 for a single-entry visa, subject to nationality, exemptions, local-currency schedules, and mission practice.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific municipal fee, fixed freelancer tax, financial-transaction tax, or automatic consumption-tax registration charge was identified.
fixed_payments.notes: Private insurance must cover the full stay, at least JPY 10,000,000 of injury and illness treatment, and required death-related cover; the premium varies by insurer.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person without Japanese domicile is generally nonresident, but Japan-source remuneration and treaty filing still require review.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If domicile or later residence creates tax residency, progressive national tax, reconstruction surtax, local tax, and resident reporting can apply.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local business activity, a Japanese permanent establishment, or resident registration can change income-tax, consumption-tax, pension, health-insurance, and immigration treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The 20.42% figure is a conservative screening rate, not a prediction of final liability.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The approved status directly permits a six-month stay, but not mid-to-long-term residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No conversion or PR clock begins from this status; a separate qualifying status is required.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Japanese naturalization does not generally require PR first.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No continuous citizenship timeline exists from the nonrenewable digital-nomad status.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official standard or national average processing time is published in the inspected material.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization ordinarily requires five consecutive years of domicile, valid status, legal capacity, good conduct and tax compliance, financial support, and generally loss or renunciation of foreign nationality. Permission is discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: No precise statutory Japanese-language test level is specified.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Naturalization and PR have distinct spouse exceptions; both require additional Japanese residence or domicile conditions.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage to a Japanese citizen can count toward the marriage period, but marriage alone grants neither citizenship nor PR.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid and genuine. Authorities may examine civil records, cohabitation, finances, and inconsistencies; fraud can lead to refusal, revocation, removal, or prosecution.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Japan alone does not confer nationality. A child is Japanese at birth if a parent is Japanese, or exceptionally if both parents are unknown or stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Japan-born child of two foreign migrant parents does not ordinarily become Japanese; the statutory exception concerns unknown or stateless parents.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Japanese at birth if either legally recognized parent is Japanese at that time, subject to special parentage and overseas-birth rules.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer nationality or PR on a foreign father. Spouse status or a discretionary family-based assessment requires a separate application.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father receives no automatic citizenship. If genuinely married to the Japanese mother, he may separately seek spouse status and later use applicable spouse exceptions.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child's citizenship and the father's status are separate.

rank.notes: Joint second in Henley's January 2026 release.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's score includes destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance and is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Inferred as 227 destinations minus the Henley score of 188.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The inspected Henley release does not separately state VOA and eTA counts.

passport.notes: Index figures are methodology-dependent and may change.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only remote work is feasible in major cities and international settings, but Japanese is often needed for administration, leases, healthcare, and local services. EF classified Japan's 2025 adult English proficiency as very low.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a nongovernmental self-selected testing index.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not practical general-purpose languages for Japanese administration or daily services; Japanese is primary and English is generally the more useful fallback.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide proficiency statistic for Russian or Ukrainian was located.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official JPY 296,600 median scheduled cash earnings at JPY 150/USD.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Japan has prefectural hourly minima rather than one national monthly minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion at JPY 150/USD.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: The applicable legal rate depends on prefecture and sometimes industry.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Published 2025 national median scheduled cash earnings for general workers, industry total, both sexes, education total, enterprise-size total; establishments with at least 10 regular employees.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite national maximum is published; the official distribution uses an open-ended highest wage band and reports the 90th percentile rather than a maximum.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: This is a limitation of the published statistic, not a missing currency conversion.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average: gross total cash earnings for regular employees in establishments with at least five regular employees. Median: scheduled cash earnings for general workers in establishments with at least 10 regular employees, excluding overtime and annual bonuses. Minimum: weighted average of prefectural hourly legal minima.

average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and median use different official series and populations, so they are not a matched mean/median pair. Local-currency figures are authoritative.

cost_of_living_note.value: Living costs vary materially by city, housing, and short-term accommodation. No single official monthly budget matching a solo remote worker was established.
cost_of_living_note.notes: OECD price-level data support cross-country comparison but not a personal monthly budget.

data.selection_summary: Jordan has online visa and residence services, but no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route was found. Work residence follows Jordanian employer/work-permit rules, while independently accessible workless residence requires substantial capital and does not establish remote-work authorization. Jordan therefore does not fit the requested remote-work-to-citizenship profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual becomes resident after at least 183 days of actual presence during the tax year, consecutively or intermittently.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Jordan-source income may be taxable even before tax residence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Published total for a covered self-employed person, employer or working partner in their own enterprise; applicability to an unregistered foreign remote worker is not established.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly payment for a foreign remote worker is published because no corresponding immigration category exists.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker personal tax regime was identified.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical presence, where services are performed, income-source characterization, exemptions, local registration, social-security coverage and treaty position. Immigration authorization must be analyzed separately.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with source-based rules and a 183-day residence definition.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 days of actual presence during the tax year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income incurred in or from Jordan is taxable regardless of where payment occurs; the reviewed sources do not establish that work physically performed in Jordan for a foreign client is exempt.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or ordinary remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered self-employed persons, employers and working partners may face total contributions of 21.75% of contributory wage; applicability requires registration-level verification.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% figure is the top marginal rate on taxable income above JOD 1 million, not an estimated effective rate. A 1% national contribution also applies above the statutory threshold.

fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Local registration, licensing and sales-tax obligations would depend on legal form and turnover.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining under 183 days prevents tax residence but does not automatically exempt Jordan-source income or authorize work as a visitor.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days, ordinary progressive PIT may apply if services are treated as Jordan-source.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registration may trigger licensing, tax and social-security rules, but no source confirms that it legalizes remote work for a visitor or workless resident.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: There is no qualifying remote-worker route. Workless deposit residence is direct but rejected for this profile.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No general permanent-residence transition for the rejected categories was established.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The law uses ordinary residence rather than a confirmed route-specific permanent-residence sequence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: A discretionary application may be possible after four years of ordinary residence, but no qualifying remote-work residence route exists and four years is not a reliable route-specific outcome.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality law does not publish a typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires four years of ordinary residence, intent to remain, Arabic literacy, good character, mental capacity and lawful means of earning; approval is discretionary and the law generally contemplates loss of the previous nationality.
key_conditions.notes: These conditions do not confirm that visitor or workless-residence time creates a dependable citizenship path.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For the male applicant contemplated here, marriage to a Jordanian woman does not provide the accelerated nationality rule. A foreign wife of a Jordanian man may apply after three years if Arab or five years if non-Arab.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can count toward the three- or five-year period only for a foreign wife married to a Jordanian man; no parallel accelerated rule was found for a foreign husband.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Approval remains required.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must prove a legally valid, continuing and genuine marriage. False documents or sham arrangements can cause refusal, cancellation and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No official detailed sham-marriage checklist or processing time was located.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Jordan does not grant general citizenship merely for birth in Jordan. Citizenship principally follows a Jordanian father, with limited protections for foundlings and certain children of Jordanian mothers where the father is unknown, stateless or paternity is not legally established.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Jordan to two known non-Jordanian parents does not ordinarily become Jordanian.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Narrow foundling and statelessness-related exceptions do not create general jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Jordanian father is Jordanian wherever born. A child of a Jordanian mother and known foreign father does not ordinarily receive citizenship automatically, subject to narrow statutory exceptions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The result is sex- and circumstance-dependent, so the general one-citizen-parent boolean remains null.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Jordanian child does not automatically naturalize the foreign father; any family residence benefit must be pursued separately.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A non-citizen child born locally creates no citizenship-based parental shortcut.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence; the father must rely on separate immigration rules.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No exact national median amount is published. The official 2024 distribution establishes only that the median lies in the JOD 300-499 band.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate equivalent of the statutory JOD 290 monthly private-sector minimum wage, effective 2025-2027; this is a legal floor, not an observed minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the directly published JOD 551 total monthly establishment wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No exact official median amount is published. In 2024, 3.1% earned under JOD 200, 16.7% earned JOD 200-299 and 55.6% earned JOD 300-499, placing the median in JOD 300-499; grouped data cannot support an exact USD value.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No finite national maximum is published. The official distribution uses an open-ended above-JOD-500 category, while establishment tables report group averages rather than individual maxima.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory private-sector minimum wage effective from 2025-01-01 through 2027-12-31.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Directly published total average monthly wage per paid employee across surveyed public- and private-sector establishments in October 2023.

median_salary_local_currency.value: JOD 300-499 per month (official median wage band; exact median unpublished)
median_salary_local_currency.notes: The 2024 distribution places 19.8% below JOD 300 and another 55.6% in JOD 300-499, so the 50th percentile falls in this band. No exact dinar median is published.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite maximum published; highest official 2024 wage band is above JOD 500 per month
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The Central Bank distribution has an open-ended above-JOD-500 category, and Department of Statistics tables publish averages rather than the highest individual wage.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly establishment-survey wage; grouped wage-distribution band for employed Jordanians; separate statutory private-sector minimum
average_citizen_salary.period: 2023 establishment average; 2024 median band; minimum valid 2025-2027
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe ordinary workers, not software engineers or an immigration threshold. The focused review resolved the median only to an official JOD 300-499 band and confirmed that no finite national maximum is published.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official CPI data measure price changes rather than a single-person monthly budget; no official current absolute monthly cost figure was established.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No unsupported budget estimate is supplied.
