settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor status and bank-deposit workless residence must not be treated as remote-work authorization or a confirmed citizenship track.
settlement_track.summary: Jordan has no confirmed ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Visitor status is temporary, work residence requires the employer/work-permit process, and workless or investment residence does not establish remote-work permission.
settlement_track.notes: The previous negative result remains supported after the focused current-source audit.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category was identified. The closest independent residence is workless and capital-based; lawful work routes use employer/work-permit rules.

data.notes: The audit inspected at least 15 directly relevant URLs and added six official labor-market URLs absent from the previous source set. The focused salary pass established an official median band of JOD 300-499 but no exact median, and confirmed that no finite national maximum wage is published.

data.selection_summary: Kazakhstan is a strong residence-to-citizenship option for a qualifying software engineer, but only a partial match for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The independently initiated Digital Nomad Residency process screens applicants against listed in-demand IT professions and can grant permanent residence directly without a local employer; it is therefore a qualification-based IT route rather than an unrestricted remote-worker route. The separate Neo Nomad B12-1 visa fits foreign remote work but is a temporary tourist visa and is not itself a settlement route.

visa_application.title: Issuance of permit to foreign IT specialists for permanent residence in the Republic of Kazakhstan
visa_application.notes: Official online permanent-residence service. The applicant first completes IT-profession screening through Astana Hub and obtains the sectoral-government petition, then files the permanent-residence request through eGov. Authentication, an IIN and an electronic signature may be required; the government states that IINs and signatures can now be arranged through foreign missions.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Residency for foreign IT specialists

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is stated for the current IT permanent-residence pilot. The government reported that income verification was removed. The general service page still displays the standard 1,320-MCI solvency rule or a statutory exemption, and explicitly identifies foreigners in listed in-demand professions as exempt; filing-level confirmation is prudent.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No recurring monthly-income threshold was confirmed. The generic PR checklist refers to KZT 5,709,000 (1,320 MCI at the 2026 MCI of KZT 4,325) or an exemption, but listed in-demand professionals are expressly within the exemption.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income threshold confirmed; listed in-demand IT professionals are exempt from the generic PR solvency requirement
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Generic PR test: 1,320 MCI = KZT 5,709,000, unless exempt
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a qualification-screened IT route. An official 2025 government update says income verification is no longer required, while the current generic service checklist preserves the 1,320-MCI alternative and the in-demand-profession exemption.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period applies if the in-demand-profession exemption is accepted. The six-month bank-statement rule belongs to the separate Neo Nomad B12-1 tourist visa and must not be imported into this PR route.

key_requirements.requirement: Be verified as a foreign IT specialist matching Kazakhstan's current in-demand occupation list; software architect, software developer, application programmer and several other software occupations appear on the official list.
Astana Hub screening requires a passport copy, CV, portfolio, motivation letter, criminal-record certificate and photo, followed by a video interview and a sectoral-government petition.

The PR stage requires the eligibility certificate or petition, passport valid for more than 180 days, legalized criminal-record evidence, housing evidence, medical certificate, photo, fingerprinting and applicable legalized translations; the service also lists evidence permitting departure for permanent residence abroad.
No local employer or Kazakhstan job offer is listed, but approval is qualification-screened and requires a petition from the competent digital-sector authority.
Official service fee is 4 MCI, or KZT 17,300 in 2026, about USD 37 using the cited National Bank rate.

initial_validity.value: Permanent-residence permit; residence card issued for up to 10 years, limited by passport validity
initial_validity.notes: The government service result is permanent residence, not merely a temporary visa. The physical residence card is normally valid for ten years or the remaining passport term.

extension_rules.value: Apply for a replacement or renewed residence card no later than one month before expiry
extension_rules.notes: Renewing the document does not ordinarily interrupt permanent-resident status. PR can be annulled for insufficient presence, including residence in Kazakhstan for fewer than 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period, subject to statutory exceptions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No temporary-residence stage is required by the Digital Nomad Residency service; preliminary approval is completed online and the applicant then completes PR registration.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A B9-1 visa may be used by qualifying IT specialists entering to complete PR, but the current program also describes a fully remote preliminary process.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct application for permanent residence after Astana Hub qualification verification and issuance of the sectoral-government petition; official processing period is 45 calendar days after the document package is filed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Approval is not automatic. The IT qualification and occupation match are substantively screened.

path_to_citizenship.value: After obtaining PR, ordinary naturalization is available following at least five years of continuous permanent residence, subject to citizenship testing, compliance and termination or renunciation of prior citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Kazakhstan does not recognize dual or multiple citizenship. The five-year period should not be treated as running during a Neo Nomad tourist stay.

best_routes.notes: This route is independently initiated and directly settlement-oriented, but it is classified as partial because it depends on government verification of an in-demand IT occupation, skills, diploma or experience and portfolio. It is not an unrestricted visa for anyone holding a foreign remote-work contract. A software engineer with a relevant degree may fit, but must obtain the Astana Hub or sectoral petition.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Official threshold is stable foreign-source income of at least USD 3,000 per month.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Approximately KZT 1,420,770 per month at KZT 473.59/USD
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Approximate conversion for comparison only; the legally displayed threshold is in US dollars.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 3,000 per month from foreign sources
income_requirement_display.notes: Six months of bank statements are required.

income_proof_months.notes: Bank statements for the preceding six months must show stable qualifying income.

key_requirements.requirement: Remote work and permanent income from sources outside Kazakhstan.
Tax return from the applicant's country, criminal-record certificate and medical insurance covering the visa term.
Invitation is waived only for citizens of the specified 48 states; other applicants require an approved invitation.
Employment by a Kazakhstan company is not permitted on this visa.

initial_validity.value: Multiple-entry tourist visa valid for up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Official materials expressly describe B12-1 as a tourist visa.

extension_rules.value: May be extended once for up to 1 additional year through the Ministry of Internal Affairs
extension_rules.notes: Maximum described total is two years.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No separate temporary-residence permit is granted; the visa authorizes an extended tourist stay.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The visa is not equivalent to Kazakhstan permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate IT-specialist permanent-residence application is available after independent professional assessment and a sectoral-authority petition. The Ministry explicitly permits foreign-company work on the B9-1 Digital Nomad route leading to DNR; B12-1 alone does not establish eligibility.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: B12-1 is the selected tourist/remote-work visa; B9-1/DNR is a separate screened IT route. Ministry guidance connects foreign-company work with a PR application; Article 6 gives permanent residents equal labour rights. Neither source expressly explains how foreign-only work is evidenced for the post-grant in-demand occupational test, so remote-profile support remains uncertain. A local employer, marriage or major investment is not listed as mandatory, but qualification recognition cannot be assumed. The B12-1 change/exit procedure is unverified. Zero years denotes no prior-residence wait; published processing is 45 days.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The official B12-1 page classifies this status as a tourist visa, while ordinary naturalization expressly requires at least five years of continuous permanent residence. The reviewed citizenship law and guidance contain no rule treating B12-1 tourist-visa time as permanent residence, so this visa itself does not establish a citizenship-qualifying period.

rejected_routes.notes: This route is a good temporary-living fit for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker, but it fails the citizenship-oriented selection because it is expressly a tourist visa and has no confirmed direct settlement chain.

rejected_routes.route_name: Independent-employment qualification certificate and C4 visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current official service applies a qualification and six-point assessment rather than a monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The certificate service is free and the reviewed qualification rules do not impose a recurring monetary income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No monetary income threshold; qualification, education, experience and priority-sector scoring apply
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Not applicable — eligibility is qualification- and points-based, not income-based
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No KZT income formula; at least 6 qualification points are required
income_requirement_display.notes: The official service states that the certificate is free and refusal follows if the applicant scores below six points. It is an employment-qualification instrument rather than a residence permit.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is part of the published certificate test.

key_requirements.requirement: Occupation must be on the priority-sector list and the applicant must obtain a certificate confirming qualifications for independent employment.
The applicant must meet education and occupational requirements and obtain at least six assessment points.
Listed computer-related occupations include programmer, database administrator, system architect, systems analyst and software-support specialist.

The associated C4 visa rules require the qualification certificate and petition; the published multiple-entry C4 documentation also lists an employment contract, making this unsuitable as a simple foreign-client remote-work route.

initial_validity.value: Qualification certificate issued for up to 3 months; associated C4 visa can be issued separately under the visa rules
initial_validity.notes: The certificate is issued within six working days and does not itself grant residence. C4 can be single-entry for up to 90 days or multiple-entry for up to three years, but visa documentation and employment-contract conditions apply.

extension_rules.value: Certificate extension service is available and processed within 3 working days; continued immigration status requires a separate valid C4 visa or other status
extension_rules.notes: Extension of the certificate is not an automatic settlement transition.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate C4 visa filing is required; the qualification certificate alone grants no residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The reviewed sources do not establish a stand-alone temporary-residence permit for ordinary work solely for a foreign client.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Neither the certificate service nor the C4 visa rules publish an automatic PR conversion. The separate in-demand-IT permanent-residence service is the more relevant settlement route.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship requires qualifying continuous permanent residence. A qualification certificate or C4 visa is not identified as permanent residence and therefore does not independently start the ordinary five-year naturalization period.

rejected_routes.notes: Although software occupations appear in the independent-employment rules, this is an employment-qualification and visa channel rather than a complete foreign-client remote-work settlement route. The certificate service is independently accessible, but the separate immigration documentation and employment-contract conditions prevent treating it as an ordinary remote-worker route.

summary.value: Digital Nomad Residency permits a foreign IT specialist to initiate an application without a Kazakhstan employer and obtain PR directly after occupation and qualification verification. A sectoral-government petition is mandatory, and the current in-demand list includes multiple software-development professions. A relevant degree helps establish the required occupation and skill match but does not guarantee approval.
summary.notes: This qualification screening is why Kazakhstan is marked partial rather than a full ordinary-remote-work match.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally resident after 183 or more days in Kazakhstan in any rolling 12-month period ending in the reporting period, or earlier if the statutory center-of-vital-interests test is met.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The center-of-interest test considers residence or citizenship status, close family in Kazakhstan and available Kazakhstan real estate together. Treaty tie-breaker rules may override domestic residence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for most individual income in 2026. Income up to 8,500 MCI annually is taxed at 10%; only the excess is taxed at 15%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening figure combining 10% employee pension and 2% employee medical-insurance deductions where both apply. Applicability depends on PR, nationality, local employment or payroll and contract structure; it should not be assumed for every foreign-employer payment. Employer-side charges are additional.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal fixed monthly payment for every Digital Nomad Residency holder. If registered as an individual entrepreneur, 2026 category-specific amounts include KZT 5,950 monthly medical insurance and fixed social tax of 2 MCI, KZT 8,650, plus percentage-based pension and social contributions. A qualifying independent payer instead pays KZT 4,250 monthly medical insurance. Exact applicability to a foreign-contract PR holder depends on registration and contract classification, so one USD total is not stated.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special Neo Nomad or Digital Nomad Residency personal-income-tax exemption was found. Kazakhstan residents are generally taxed on worldwide income and may claim properly documented foreign-tax credits.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business or Astana Hub entity incentives should not be assumed to exempt the individual's foreign employment or freelance income. The 2026 self-employed special regime described by the tax authority is limited to Kazakhstan citizens and therefore is not assumed available to a foreign resident.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical presence, the center-of-vital-interests test, whether work performed from Kazakhstan is Kazakhstan-source, foreign-employer permanent-establishment exposure, local business registration, social-insurance status and the applicable double-tax treaty. Professional advice is warranted before working from Kazakhstan under PR.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax: 10% on annual taxable income through 8,500 MCI and 15% on the excess. Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents generally only on Kazakhstan-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in a rolling 12-month period or an earlier statutory center-of-vital-interests finding.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Kazakhstan-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special personal tax holiday or nomad exemption confirmed. Foreign-tax credits may be available with legalized supporting evidence. The new individual self-employed regime is not assumed available to foreigners because the official description limits it to Kazakhstan citizens.
taxation_system.social_security: Where applicable, employee deductions include 10% pension and 2% obligatory medical insurance. Employers may face social tax, social insurance, medical insurance and employer pension contributions. Individual entrepreneurs face category-specific fixed and percentage payments.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 15% value is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. In 2026, 8,500 MCI equals KZT 36,762,500 annually, about USD 77,625 using KZT 473.59/USD; only income above that amount bears 15%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to and including 8,500 MCI (KZT 36,762,500 in 2026)
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion using the cited early-August 2026 National Bank rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion of annual taxable income exceeding 8,500 MCI (KZT 36,762,500 in 2026)
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not a flat 15% on all income.

taxation_system.notes: Rates and residency rules are current to August 2026. Exact liability and social-payment category for foreign-contract software work require source-of-income, registration and treaty analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The qualification-based Digital Nomad Residency route has no special personal tax exemption. Once tax resident, the holder should screen worldwide foreign salary or freelance income under the ordinary 10%/15% PIT scale; local registration may also trigger social or business obligations.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Qualification-screened IT permanent resident; ordinary resident taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% through KZT 36,762,500 annual taxable income; 15% on the excess (top marginal screening rate)
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in any rolling 12-month period, or an earlier center-of-vital-interests finding.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Kazakhstan tax residents are taxed on worldwide income. Foreign-tax credits may be claimed with legalized or apostilled evidence and Russian or Kazakh translation, subject to treaty and filing rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No personal tax exemption or reduced nomad rate was confirmed for Digital Nomad Residency or Neo Nomad B12-1 holders.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: PR holders on local payroll may be subject to 10% employee pension and 2% employee medical deductions, with employer-side charges. Individual entrepreneurs have percentage contributions plus category-specific fixed payments. Treatment of payments directly from a foreign employer or client depends on employment, source and registration facts.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific recurring nomad payment; category-specific fixed payments apply if the holder registers or pays locally as an individual entrepreneur or independent medical-insurance payer
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: For 2026, an individual entrepreneur pays KZT 5,950 monthly obligatory medical insurance and fixed social tax of 2 MCI, KZT 8,650, plus percentage-based pension and social contributions. An eligible independent medical-insurance payer pays KZT 4,250 monthly. These categories do not automatically apply merely because a person holds Digital Nomad Residency.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The IT permanent-residence service lists a one-time fee of 4 MCI: KZT 17,300 in 2026, approximately USD 37. Separate document, legalization, medical, translation and card costs can apply. Neo Nomad consular fees vary by mission; the London mission lists GBP 170 for multiple entry.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No special municipal nomad levy or financial-transaction tax was published in the reviewed official sources. Individual-entrepreneur registration can introduce fixed social tax, medical insurance, percentage social contributions and potentially VAT or other business obligations.
fixed_payments.notes: The fixed-payment position is conditional rather than absent: immigration status alone does not create one universal monthly amount, but official 2026 schedules publish fixed payments for particular local registration and insurance categories. Filing advice is needed to determine which category covers a PR holder paid directly by a foreign client.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person below 183 days who does not meet the center-of-vital-interests test may remain non-resident, but Kazakhstan-source treatment of work physically performed in Kazakhstan and treaty rules still require analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident should assume worldwide foreign-contract income is reportable and subject to the ordinary progressive PIT scale, with possible foreign-tax credit relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registering as an individual entrepreneur can trigger KZT 5,950 monthly medical insurance, 2-MCI monthly social tax and percentage pension and social contributions. The separate 2026 self-employed special regime is described as limited to Kazakhstan citizens and should not be assumed available to a foreign PR holder.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in headline PIT, residence rules and published 2026 payment amounts; medium confidence in which social-security category applies to a foreign-employer arrangement because that depends on contract, payroll and registration structure.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The selected route applies directly for permanent residence rather than first granting a temporary residence permit.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence period is required. The official PR service states a 45-calendar-day service period once the complete application is filed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary eligibility requires at least five years of continuous permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest ordinary statutory timeline from direct PR is approximately five years, excluding application preparation and citizenship processing. It is not a guarantee of approval.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The ordinary procedure is officially capped at six months across the reviewing bodies; facilitated cases are generally three months.

key_conditions.value: Maintain permanent residence continuously and generally spend at least 183 days in Kazakhstan in each consecutive 12-month period to avoid PR cancellation; after five years, pass elementary Kazakh-language, Constitution and history testing, demonstrate legal compliance, pay the fee and provide evidence of termination or renunciation of prior citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Kazakhstan does not permit dual or multiple citizenship. Absences and continuity should be checked before travel.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The official guidance states that a person married to a Kazakhstan citizen and residing for at least three years may qualify. Permanent residence and the facilitated filing requirements still apply.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage to a Kazakhstan citizen can be relevant toward the three-year marriage or residence condition, but marriage to another foreigner has no acceleration effect. The foreign spouse must be permanently residing in Kazakhstan when using the facilitated process.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The exact treatment of time married before Kazakhstan residence should be confirmed with migration authorities before relying on it.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage can support family residence and facilitated citizenship but does not confer citizenship automatically. Applicants still provide identity, residence and citizenship-status documents and must address prior citizenship. A marriage used as a migration basis can lead to residence cancellation if judicially annulled or found invalid.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Only a genuine, legally recognized marriage should be relied upon; sham or invalid marriages expose the applicant to refusal or cancellation.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Kazakhstan is principally jus sanguinis. Birth in Kazakhstan does not make a child of two foreign citizens Kazakh, while a locally born child of two stateless permanent residents is a citizen and foundlings are protected.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child whose parents were both foreign citizens at birth is not a Kazakhstan citizen regardless of birthplace. A child born in Kazakhstan to two stateless parents who permanently reside there is a citizen.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the stated two-foreign-migrant-parent scenario; anti-statelessness rules are a separate exception.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is a Kazakhstan citizen, a child born in Kazakhstan is a citizen. A child born abroad is also a citizen when either parent permanently resided in Kazakhstan; if both parents permanently lived abroad, they determine citizenship by written agreement. A Kazakhstan-citizen father and stateless mother can transmit citizenship under the law's paternity rule.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Citizenship by descent is strong but the foreign-birth rule can require parental agreement.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Kazakhstan-citizen child does not automatically naturalize or grant PR to a foreign father. Family-reunification status may be possible only where the parent falls within the statutory family categories, such as a dependent incapacitated parent; ordinary citizenship rules otherwise continue to apply.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A minor child generally cannot be treated as an unrestricted sponsor for an able-bodied foreign parent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence follows from the child's citizenship. A foreign father may rely on marriage, another qualifying residence route, or a specifically applicable family-reunification category.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity may establish the child's citizenship when the father is Kazakh, but that rule concerns the child, not automatic status for a foreign father.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed by Passport Index when checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free; this excludes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance by the index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined 42 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. The index's overall mobility score is 90.

passport.notes: Passport-index classifications change frequently and may treat eVisas or other electronic permissions separately. Verify the destination's official entry rules before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable within international technology teams and for remote work, but it is not a reliable standalone language for government procedures or everyday life nationwide. EF's 2025 index places Kazakhstan 107th with a score of 417, in the very-low-proficiency band.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected adult proficiency dataset and should be treated as an indicator rather than a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is highly practical: it is constitutionally used officially alongside Kazakh in state institutions and local self-government, and government services commonly accept Russian documents or translations. Ukrainian is not official, though Ukrainian speakers may find Russian linguistically useful if they know it.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Kazakh is the state language and is required at an elementary level for ordinary naturalization.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official Q1 2026 average monthly nominal wage of KZT 461,486 using KZT 473.59/USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official estimated Q1 2026 median wage of KZT 331,527.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory 2026 minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the official Q1 2026 average monthly nominal employee wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the official estimated Q1 2026 median employee wage.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: An exact national maximum cannot be calculated from the official releases. The detailed 2025 wage distribution uses an open-ended highest band above KZT 1,500,001 per month and reports employees in that band, but does not publish its upper endpoint or the largest observed wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage effective 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly nominal wage, Q1 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Estimated median wage, Q1 2026.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Exact maximum unpublished; the official wage distribution's highest band is open-ended at over KZT 1,500,001 per month
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official 2025 distribution reports 62,749 employees in the over-KZT-1,500,001 band but publishes neither an upper boundary nor the maximum observed individual salary. KZT 1,500,001 is therefore a band threshold, not a national maximum, and no maximum is invented.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official monthly nominal employee wage; minimum field is the statutory minimum wage; maximum discussion uses the official employee wage-distribution survey
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 for average and estimated median; 2026 statutory minimum; 2025 detailed distribution for the open-ended top band
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe Kazakhstan employees generally and are not the immigration income threshold. USD values are rounded using the National Bank's early-August 2026 official rate of KZT 473.59 per USD. The official distribution confirms why an exact maximum is unavailable rather than treating the highest band's lower boundary as a maximum.

cost_of_living_note.value: No official comparable household budget was captured. As a price-pressure indicator, official annual consumer-price inflation was 10.4% in May 2026, including 10.7% for food and 11.7% for non-food goods, so current housing and living costs should be checked immediately before relocation.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Inflation is not a cost-of-living total and does not show differences between Almaty, Astana and smaller cities.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Do not confuse Digital Nomad Residency with the Neo Nomad B12-1 tourist visa. Only the qualification-screened IT route directly grants PR; B12-1 alone is temporary.
settlement_track.summary: For an approved in-demand IT specialist, Digital Nomad Residency directly grants permanent residence and creates a credible five-year ordinary naturalization track. The country remains only a partial profile match because entry to this track depends on skills, occupation and government-petition screening rather than merely holding a foreign remote-work contract.
settlement_track.notes: Direct PR makes the settlement track strong after approval. The principal uncertainty is applicant-level qualification approval, not the legal existence of the PR-to-citizenship chain.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The settlement route is not available merely because the applicant has a foreign contract: it requires in-demand IT qualification verification and a government petition. The unrestricted foreign-contract fit is the Neo Nomad tourist visa, which is temporary and does not itself establish the citizenship track.

data.notes: Focused re-audit confirms the partial classification. The qualification-screened Digital Nomad Residency service directly grants PR and supports a five-year citizenship track, while the ordinary foreign-contract Neo Nomad visa remains tourist-only. The four flagged gaps were resolved or precisely bounded: tourist time is not permanent residence for citizenship; the independent-employment certificate uses qualifications and points rather than an income currency; nomad status has no universal recurring fixed payment but published category-specific local payments may apply; and the official wage distribution has an open-ended top band rather than a published national maximum. Applicants should still confirm PR solvency exemption and foreign-contract tax or social-payment classification at filing.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Separate Digital Nomad Residency / IT-specialist permanent-residence application
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A separate IT-specialist permanent-residence application is available after independent professional assessment and a sectoral-authority petition. The Ministry explicitly permits foreign-company work on the B9-1 Digital Nomad route leading to DNR; B12-1 alone does not establish eligibility.
requirements: Pass the immigrant eligibility assessment and obtain recognition of an occupation on the in-demand list, qualifications and relevant experience.
Obtain the sectoral-authority petition, housing evidence, police/medical documents and other required documents; prove solvency unless exempt.
After PR, meet the minimum 183-day presence and in-demand occupational-activity conditions in each consecutive twelve-month period.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: B12-1 is the selected tourist/remote-work visa; B9-1/DNR is a separate screened IT route. Ministry guidance connects foreign-company work with a PR application; Article 6 gives permanent residents equal labour rights. Neither source expressly explains how foreign-only work is evidenced for the post-grant in-demand occupational test, so remote-profile support remains uncertain. A local employer, marriage or major investment is not listed as mandatory, but qualification recognition cannot be assumed. The B12-1 change/exit procedure is unverified. Zero years denotes no prior-residence wait; published processing is 45 days.

data.selection_summary: Kenya has an active Class N Digital Nomad work/residence permit for foreign-company employees and freelancers serving companies outside Kenya. The 2025 amended Immigration Regulations require assured foreign annual income of USD 55,000, although the public Class N checklist omits the numerical threshold. The independently filed permit is issued for one or two years and is renewable. General valid-permit rules can support citizenship after seven years and work-permit rules can support Category B permanent residence after seven years, but later approvals require substantive contribution to Kenya and are not automatic.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is not automatic conversion. The application also requires tangible socioeconomic contribution, interview, tax compliance and substantial fees.

path_to_citizenship.value: A person lawfully and ordinarily resident under valid permits for the seven years immediately before applying may seek citizenship by registration; permanent residence is not stated as a prerequisite.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Additional requirements include final-12-month residence, Kiswahili or a local dialect, knowledge of Kenya, good character, intended continued residence and substantive contribution to national development.

best_routes.notes: Strong ordinary foreign-contract remote-work fit. The amended Regulations cover foreign-company remote employees and freelancers, require USD 55,000 annual foreign income and prohibit Kenyan-domiciled employment. The settlement link follows from Class N being a work/residence permit and the generally worded PR and citizenship provisions; later approvals remain substantive and discretionary.

summary.value: Class C can be independently sought by members of specifically prescribed regulated professions intending to practise in Kenya. A university degree alone is insufficient, and ordinary software engineering is not established as a prescribed profession. Class N is the directly fitting route.
summary.notes: Class C is professional-membership based, not a general degree-based migration program.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they have a permanent home in Kenya and are present during the year; otherwise residence arises at 183 days in the year or when presence in that year and each of the preceding two years averages more than 122 days per year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and the meaning of permanent home may change the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax. Individual bands run from 10% to 35%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single Class N percentage exists. A non-Kenyan ordinarily resident beyond 12 months is liable to SHIF: 2.75% of gross salary for salaried households, or 2.75% of means-tested household income for non-salaried households with a KES 300 monthly minimum. NSSF separately uses 6% employee and 6% employer contributions on pensionable earnings for covered employees; foreign-payroll Class N implementation requires confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal USD fixed monthly amount applies. Non-salaried SHIF has a KES 300 monthly minimum when the non-Kenyan is ordinarily resident beyond 12 months; salaried SHIF and payroll levies are percentage-based. Class N also costs USD 200 processing plus USD 1,000 issuance per permit year.

special_tax_regimes.value: No official Class N income-tax exemption, reduced rate or tax holiday was identified.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Immigration eligibility does not imply tax exemption.

taxes.caveats: Kenya is mainly source-based but has specific foreign-income exceptions. Work physically performed from Kenya may be Kenyan-source despite a foreign payer; resident foreign employment income and partly foreign business can also be taxable. Contract classification, treaty relief, permanent-establishment exposure, VAT, SHIF, NSSF and the Affordable Housing Levy require Kenyan professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax from 10% to 35% within a mainly source-based system, with exceptions for resident foreign employment income and business carried on partly inside and outside Kenya.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home plus presence, 183 days in a year, or average presence exceeding 122 days across the current and preceding two years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income accrued in or derived from Kenya is taxable for residents and non-residents. KRA also identifies resident foreign employment income and business conducted partly inside and outside Kenya as foreign-income exceptions.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-individual regime was confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: For non-Kenyans ordinarily resident more than 12 months, SHIF is mandatory: 2.75% of gross salary for salaried households, or 2.75% of means-tested household income for non-salaried households with a KES 300 monthly minimum. NSSF law prescribes 6% employee plus 6% employer on pensionable earnings for covered employees; self-employed participation is voluntary.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 35% dashboard figure is a top marginal screening rate. Monthly bands are 10% on the first KES 24,000; 25% on the next KES 8,333; 30% on the next KES 467,667; 32.5% on the next KES 300,000; and 35% above KES 800,000. Resident personal relief is KES 2,400 monthly.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at about KES 129.5/USD.

tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate cumulative upper threshold.

tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate cumulative upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next KES 300,000; cumulative income up to KES 800,000 per month
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate cumulative upper threshold.
Top marginal band.

taxation_system.notes: Immigration and tax status are separate. Physical work location and contract structure are particularly important.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Class N has no confirmed tax holiday. Services performed from Kenya require Kenyan tax analysis; individual rates are progressive up to 35%, and Kenyan-source gross income may also attract the 1.5% Affordable Housing Levy.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital-nomad work/residence permit without a special tax regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10%–35% progressive PIT; 35% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent-home test, 183-day test, or average presence exceeding 122 days across the current and two preceding years.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Kenya is primarily source-based, but KRA identifies resident foreign employment income and business conducted partly in Kenya and abroad as exceptions. Remote services physically performed in Kenya may independently be Kenyan-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No official Class N exemption, reduced rate or tax holiday was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A non-Kenyan ordinarily resident for more than 12 months is liable to SHIF. Salaried households contribute 2.75% of gross salary; non-salaried households contribute 2.75% of means-tested household income, with a KES 300 monthly minimum. NSSF separately prescribes 6% employee and 6% employer contributions on pensionable earnings for covered employees, while self-employed membership is voluntary. Class N guidance does not explain registration and remittance by a foreign employer without Kenyan payroll.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: SHIF is mandatory once a non-Kenyan is ordinarily resident in Kenya for more than 12 months: 2.75% of gross monthly salary for salaried households; for non-salaried households, 2.75% of means-tested household income with a minimum of KES 300 per month, paid annually. NSSF is not a single fixed Class N payment: covered employees and employers each contribute 6% of pensionable earnings, while self-employed membership is voluntary and the NSSF voluntary page describes a KES 200 initial contribution. The official materials do not specify how a foreign employer without Kenyan payroll must remit for a Class N employee.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Class N: USD 200 non-refundable processing fee plus USD 1,000 issuance fee per year. The service charter also lists KES 5,000 per year for foreign-national registration.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Affordable Housing Levy is variable: 1.5% of gross salary for an employee or 1.5% of Kenyan-accrued gross income for other persons, subject to the Act. VAT and registration obligations depend on activity and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: SHIF liability depends on ordinary residence beyond 12 months and salaried versus non-salaried classification. NSSF coverage and foreign-employer remittance require filing-level confirmation; AHL, PAYE and VAT are separate.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 183 days does not guarantee exemption: a permanent home can establish residence, and work performed in Kenya may be Kenyan-source even for a non-resident.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Budget using the progressive 10%–35% schedule unless treaty relief or classification changes the result. Resident foreign employment income is among KRA's stated exceptions.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Assess individual business income, 1.5% AHL on Kenyan-accrued gross income, VAT, local registration, SHIF after the residence threshold and voluntary NSSF. Class N itself does not require a Kenyan company.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: General rules are official, but KRA, SHA and NSSF have not published Class N-specific foreign-payroll guidance.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Residence begins upon approval; the service charter lists a 21-working-day target.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Category B requires seven years of work permits and continuous Kenyan residence during the three years immediately before applying. The service charter lists 24 months for PR processing.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Citizenship can be sought after seven years of qualifying permit residence; PR is not stated as a prerequisite.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Seven years is the legal eligibility floor, not guaranteed approval or completion.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current service charter lists citizenship fees but no general processing period for lawful-resident registration.

key_conditions.value: Maintain valid permits and ordinary residence for seven years; reside in Kenya throughout the final 12 months; understand Kenya and citizens' duties and rights; speak Kiswahili or a local dialect; have no disqualifying serious conviction or bankruptcy; intend continued residence; and demonstrate substantive contribution to national development.
key_conditions.notes: Dual citizenship is constitutionally permitted; general renunciation was not identified as a condition.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Three years of marriage supports Category D PR. Citizenship by marriage requires at least seven years of marriage and acquired residence status.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A pre-existing legally recognized marriage can count toward the three-year PR and seven-year citizenship periods if it remains subsisting and genuine. Marriage to another non-citizen does not accelerate citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Document the continuing marriage and shared family life.

requirements_and_risks.value: Spousal PR requires extensive proof and may involve interview. Citizenship requires a recognized, subsisting marriage, residence status, no prohibited-immigrant finding and no disqualifying serious conviction. A marriage entered mainly for status is disqualifying.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sham marriage can cause refusal and wider immigration or criminal consequences.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Kenya alone does not confer citizenship. Citizenship follows a Kenyan mother or father; a narrow presumption protects a found child under eight whose nationality and parents are unknown.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Kenya to two known foreign parents does not automatically become Kenyan merely by birthplace.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The foundling rule is not general migrant-family jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Kenyan by birth if either parent was Kenyan on the date of birth, whether born inside or outside Kenya.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This does not automatically change the migrant father's status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not itself provide an automatic parent-to-PR or parent-to-citizenship route. A foreign parent may qualify through marriage to the Kenyan parent or an independent permit/residence category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Current PR categories cover spouses and specified children or dependants, not a general parent-of-citizen category.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A Kenyan-citizen child does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on a foreign father. The Constitution makes the child Kenyan when either parent is Kenyan, but the Immigration Act and current Regulations list spouse-based and work-permit-based routes, not a general parent-of-Kenyan-child route. If the father is legally married to the Kenyan parent, he may use the separate spouse route: PR eligibility after at least three years of marriage and citizenship by marriage after at least seven years plus acquired residence status. If unmarried, he must qualify under another permit or residence category.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parenthood may matter factually in an individual case, but no automatic or accelerated father-specific status appears in the current provisions inspected.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index aggregate; eVisas may be classified separately in destination details.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English is official and is used throughout immigration and government procedures. Long-term citizenship applicants must nevertheless speak Kiswahili or a local dialect.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Practicality is inferred from official status and English-language government processes.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low outside private expatriate or diaspora circles. Neither language is official or substitutes for English or Kiswahili in government procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-usage statistics were established.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2026 Economic Survey reports modern-sector average earnings, not a national median. ILOSTAT lists median-monthly-earnings indicators, but its current public pages did not expose a Kenya observation suitable for this record, so no USD median is calculated.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the lowest general-labourer basic monthly minimum, KES 8,596.49 in other areas. This is a statutory minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate provisional modern-sector nominal average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median monthly salary is published in the 2026 Economic Survey material inspected. ILOSTAT provides a median-earnings series in principle, but no current Kenya value was exposed in the inspected interface; converting an absent or older unverified observation would be misleading.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the current Economic Survey nor the inspected KNBS household-microdata metadata publishes a defensible national maximum salary. A survey-variable maximum would be sample-specific and may include top-coded or special values, so it is not converted to USD.

min_salary_local_currency.value: KES 8,596.49–16,113.75 per month for a general labourer, depending on location
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Basic statutory minimum excluding housing allowance: KES 16,113.75 in Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru and Eldoret; KES 14,866.92 in former municipalities and specified towns; KES 8,596.49 elsewhere.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Calculated from provisional 2025 modern-sector nominal average annual earnings of KES 988,200.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The current KNBS Economic Survey publishes a modern-sector mean, not a national median. KNBS 2020 household microdata exposes wage variables but not a weighted national median on the inspected variable page, and the ILOSTAT public catalog did not surface a current Kenya observation.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Kenya has no statutory maximum wage, and the current Economic Survey does not publish a national maximum. The inspected 2020 KNBS microdata variable has a coded range rather than a population maximum; reporting the code or largest sample response as a national maximum would be statistically invalid.

average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 provisional average earnings; minimum-wage order effective 1 November 2024
