settlement_track.summary: Class N is a renewable work/residence permit rather than visitor status. Kenya's citizenship law counts valid-permit residence, permitting application after seven qualifying years; Category B PR is also available after seven years of work permits but is optional for citizenship.
settlement_track.notes: This conclusion reads the Class N permit classification together with generally worded work-permit PR and valid-permit citizenship provisions. Applicants must meet residence, language, conduct, tax-compliance and national-contribution requirements.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Class N expressly covers foreign-company remote employment and freelance remote work for a foreign company without a Kenyan employer, local client, investment or exceptional-talent requirement.

data.notes: The active Class N route remains a strong fit and settlement-capable under Kenya's general valid-permit rules. This focused audit restored the USD 55,000 annual threshold from the amended Regulations, clarified SHIF/NSSF exposure and replaced vague salary gaps with precise explanations. Confidence remains medium because Class N-specific foreign-payroll guidance is unpublished and later PR/citizenship decisions require substantive contribution.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Renewable Class N work/residence permit, then Category B permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Class N is a renewable work/residence permit. Category B PR accepts holders of Kenyan work permits for at least seven years, including three continuous years of residence immediately before applying.
requirements: Maintain qualifying work permits and the continuous-residence period.
Demonstrate tangible socioeconomic contribution and supply police clearance, tax compliance and the PR documentation; an interview may be required.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The conclusion applies the general work-permit PR rule to Class N, which Immigration lists among those permits. It is eligibility to apply, subject to assessment, not automatic PR. The original Category B webpage failed to load; its official eFNS version was reviewed.
reviewed_route_names: Class N Digital Nomad Work/Residence Permit

data.selection_summary: Kiribati has no dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary freelance residence route. Its immigration rules treat any activity for gain or reward as work, while available work visas require a job offer, Kiribati employer, local assignment, sponsorship, or specific local purpose. An indefinite residence visa becomes possible after three years of ordinary residence, but no lawful temporary route fitting ordinary work for a foreign client was confirmed; consequently, the residence and seven-year naturalisation provisions do not make Kiribati eligible for this profile.

visa_application.title: Visa – Ministry of Foreign Affairs & Immigration
visa_application.notes: Official visa-information page rather than an online application portal. It links downloadable visitor, work, student, investment, and other application forms. Applicants are directed to contact visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki regarding submission and fees.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient maintenance and onward-travel funds, but the current procedures and form publish no fixed amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current visitor materials require sufficient funds or sponsorship but specify no AUD threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed amount published; sufficient maintenance and onward-travel funds required
income_requirement_display.notes: A visitor financial-support requirement, not a remote-worker income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The official visitor form does not prescribe a fixed bank-statement history.

key_requirements.requirement: Bona fide temporary purpose, acceptable health and character, financial support, and means of onward travel.
Visitor status does not authorize ordinary paid remote work: Kiribati defines work as any activity undertaken for gain or reward.

initial_validity.value: Normally up to 4 months in a 12-month period; total visitor presence may not exceed 9 months in an 18-month period, subject to visa conditions.
initial_validity.notes: A multiple-journey visitor visa may remain current for travel for up to three years, but each stay remains limited.

extension_rules.value: Further visitor permission is discretionary, and total presence is normally capped at 9 months in an 18-month period.
extension_rules.notes: An extension does not create work authorization or residence status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct path; this is temporary visitor status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A temporary visa holder may later satisfy general residence prerequisites, but visitor status cannot lawfully support the applicant's ordinary foreign-paid remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate indefinite residence visa may be requested after three years of ordinary residence, but visitor status cannot lawfully support ordinary paid remote work during that qualifying period.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not establish a viable visitor-to-residence strategy for the applicant profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation generally requires seven years of ordinary residence and additional statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No viable lawful bridge from visitor status while continuing ordinary foreign-contract remote work was established.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is visitor status and paid foreign remote work falls within Kiribati's broad definition of work. It is neither a remote-work route nor a qualifying settlement route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Essential Skills Work Visa / Specific Purpose or Event Work Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed immigration salary threshold is published; a qualifying job offer must state pay and conditions, and the proposed salary must be sufficient.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current procedures and form specify no fixed AUD immigration salary.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; qualifying Kiribati job offer and sufficient proposed salary required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Salary stated in local job offer
income_requirement_display.notes: A local-employment requirement, not a foreign-income route.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed prior-income history is prescribed.

key_requirements.requirement: Signed job offer specifying the employer, job description, pay, hours, conditions, and duration.
Qualifications and experience relevant to the offered job.
Essential Skills cases require evidence that no suitable Kiribati citizen or resident is available.
Specific Purpose cases require a time-bound Kiribati purpose, assignment, or service rather than ordinary location-independent foreign work.

initial_validity.value: Essential Skills: initially up to 1 year.
initial_validity.notes: Specific Purpose validity is tied to the approved purpose or event.

extension_rules.value: Further Essential Skills visas may be granted for the offered employment, up to three years; Specific Purpose extensions must remain necessary to complete the original purpose.
extension_rules.notes: Essential Skills permission is restricted to the specified employer, occupation, and location.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The work visa is temporary entry status, not a residence visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It may provide lawful ordinary-residence time, but only through qualifying local employment or a Kiribati-specific assignment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate indefinite residence visa may be requested after three years of ordinary residence if language, character, support, and other criteria are met.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This settlement possibility does not remove the route's local-job or assignment requirement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation may be requested after seven years of ordinary residence, subject to language, support, integration, renunciation, and other requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: It is unusable for the supplied profile without changing to qualifying local employment or a local assignment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the official checklist requires a job offer, while Essential Skills cases require employer recruitment and a local labour-availability assessment. Specific Purpose status is restricted to a Kiribati-specific, time-bound purpose or assignment.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no ordinary monthly-income test; the decisive prerequisite is an approved Foreign Investment Certificate.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The investment materials specify no monthly-income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income threshold; approved Foreign Investment Certificate required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Investment approval rather than an income test
income_requirement_display.notes: Required investment and local business approval make this incompatible with ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The application form prescribes no standardized income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Approved Foreign Investment Certificate from the Investment Promotion Division.
Health, character, passport, photographs, applicable fee, and relationship evidence for accompanying family.
A foreign business also needs relevant registration and annually renewed local business licensing.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years.
initial_validity.notes: Duration remains subject to the underlying investment approval.

extension_rules.value: Further investment visas may be granted while the applicant continues to satisfy investment requirements.
extension_rules.notes: A current standardized renewal-fee schedule was not published by the official visa pages inspected.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary investment visa only.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not itself residence status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate residence visa may be considered after three years of ordinary residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Investment status is excluded from selection because the applicant profile does not assume a qualifying local investment.

path_to_citizenship.value: The general seven-year ordinary-residence naturalisation rule may eventually apply.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This remains a separate discretionary naturalisation application.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires approved foreign investment and local business substance, which the applicant context excludes.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence Visa after three years of ordinary residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The law requires means of support but publishes no fixed amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current Act and procedures state no fixed support threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold published; sufficient means of support required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Means of support for applicant and dependants
income_requirement_display.notes: The principal barrier is three years of prior ordinary residence, not an income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The current Act and procedures prescribe no fixed financial-evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Three years of ordinary residence in Kiribati immediately before applying.
Intention to continue residing, good character, conversational Kiribati language, respect for customs and traditions, and means of support.
Approval is discretionary: the Residence Visa Commission recommends, and the Minister decides whether to grant the application.

initial_validity.value: Indefinite residence, work, and study rights if granted.
initial_validity.notes: This is substantively permanent residence.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary renewal period; residence is indefinite, subject to immigration law and potential deportation grounds.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; this is indefinite residence reached only after prior ordinary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct indefinite residence upon grant, after satisfying the three-year prerequisite.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation is legally possible after seven years of ordinary residence in total, subject to all statutory requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Residence-visa approval at year three does not guarantee later naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: Although independently filed and settlement-oriented, this is not an entry route. No qualifying temporary status permitting the applicant to accumulate the required three years while continuing ordinary foreign-client remote work was identified.

summary.value: A student visa can be obtained without a local employer for study exceeding three months, but it requires admission to a Kiribati education provider and remains temporary-entry status. The applicant's existing degree does not independently qualify them for residence or permanent residence.
summary.notes: Current immigration materials publish no independent degree-based or points-tested skilled residence program.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident for Kiribati tax purposes if they have a permanent home available in Kiribati, are physically present for periods totalling at least 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending in the tax year, or fall within the specified overseas-official rule.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The current tax-return instructions describe this rule under the Income Tax Act 2023.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Resident chargeable income is taxed at 0%, 20%, 25%, and 30% under the latest official individual-return instructions located.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 7.5% figure is the employee contribution for a covered employee, with a separate 7.5% employer contribution. Provident Fund legislation defines covered employment around a contract of service in Kiribati, while the 2018 ISSA profile says certain foreign nationals working under specified contracts are excluded and coverage for persons without mandatory coverage, including self-employed persons, is voluntary. Because Kiribati has no digital-nomad route and the current KPF website publishes no foreign-remote-worker coverage determination, 7.5% must not be treated as a confirmed charge on ordinary foreign-client self-employment.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly payment applicable to a digital-nomad route exists because Kiribati has no such route. The 2018 ISSA profile reports voluntary self-employed Provident Fund contributions from AUD 5 monthly, but the current KPF website publishes no updated self-employed schedule; this older voluntary amount is not treated as a mandatory remote-worker charge.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, expatriate, or remote-worker tax holiday was identified. Resident individuals report income from sources inside and outside Kiribati and may claim limited foreign-tax credits.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Tax treatment should be confirmed with the Kiribati Tax Division before relocation.

taxes.caveats: The immigration route is invalid for this profile, but a person living and performing services from Kiribati may still create Kiribati tax exposure. Classification as employment versus business income, income-source rules, foreign-tax credits, Provident Fund coverage, VAT, and treaty relief require professional review.

taxation_system.value: Progressive residence-based personal income taxation. Residents include domestic and foreign-source income; non-residents generally include Kiribati-source income only.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home in Kiribati or at least 183 aggregate days in a relevant 12-month period, plus a special rule for specified Kiribati officials abroad.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: income from sources inside and outside Kiribati. Non-residents: Kiribati-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime was established; foreign-tax credits may be available within statutory limits.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees generally contribute 7.5% to the Kiribati Provident Fund, with employers contributing another 7.5%. Current sources do not establish mandatory coverage for ordinary foreign-client self-employment; older ISSA material describes voluntary self-employed participation.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% figure is the top marginal screening rate, not the effective rate on total income. The official 2023 individual-return instructions, published on the tax site in 2025, were the freshest official rate schedule located.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate conversion at AUD 1 = USD 0.697.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over AUD 5,000 up to AUD 15,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over AUD 15,000 up to AUD 30,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate upper boundary.
Top marginal rate begins above the stated approximate USD amount.

taxation_system.notes: The official tax portal's freshest downloadable individual instructions located concern the 2023 return. Filing-level confirmation is advisable in case later rate changes have not been posted.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Kiribati has no digital-nomad tax category. A person otherwise lawfully living and working from Kiribati would be screened under ordinary residence, income-tax, business-registration, VAT, and Provident Fund rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary individual employment or business-income rules would apply if lawful work status existed.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 0%–30%; 30% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home in Kiribati or at least 183 aggregate days in a relevant 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The official instructions state that a resident's gross income includes income from sources inside and outside Kiribati, with foreign-tax-credit relief potentially available.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the current immigration and tax materials inspected.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered employees generally contribute 7.5% to the Provident Fund, matched by employers. Mandatory coverage of an ordinary foreign-contract worker or locally registered sole proprietor is not established by the current sources.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory digital-nomad-specific fixed payment applies because Kiribati has no digital-nomad route. For a hypothetical self-employed person, mandatory KPF coverage was not established: the 2018 ISSA profile describes voluntary coverage with contributions of at least AUD 5 monthly, while the current KPF website publishes no updated self-employed contribution schedule.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No mandatory fixed remote-worker amount is established. The older ISSA profile describes voluntary self-employed Provident Fund contributions from AUD 5 monthly; covered employment instead generally triggers percentage contributions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The official visa pages and forms inspected do not publish a current standardized visa or residence-fee schedule and direct applicants to the Visa Officer.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A local business may face registration and annual licensing; the business-licence application submission fee shown is AUD 5, while the VAT threshold is AUD 100,000 in annual taxable supplies and the standard VAT rate is 12.5%.
fixed_payments.notes: The AUD 5 Provident Fund amount is an older voluntary minimum, not a confirmed current mandatory remote-worker payment. Covered employment may instead trigger percentage contributions. Business registration, annual licensing, VAT, immigration, and income-tax obligations are separate and do not create work or residence permission.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short visitor stay may avoid residence under the day-count test, but a permanent home can independently trigger residence, and services performed physically in Kiribati can still create source or business issues. Visitor status does not authorize ordinary paid remote work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If lawfully resident and working, worldwide income would generally enter the resident tax base under the official instructions, with progressive rates up to 30% and possible foreign-tax credits.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: TIN, VAT, and local business licensing may apply to a genuine local business, but foreign-investment approval and immigration authorization are separate. Registration alone does not create residence or work permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: There is no route-specific tax guidance because Kiribati has no digital-nomad route. The remaining uncertainty concerns how the Provident Fund would classify an independently contracted foreign worker in a hypothetical lawful-work scenario.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Kiribati publishes no independent temporary residence route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Visitor, work, student, and investment permissions are temporary-entry visas.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The residence visa requires three immediately preceding years of ordinary residence. This is a general legal threshold, not a confirmed pathway from foreign-remote-work status.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the three-year residence-visa threshold and seven-year naturalisation threshold, assuming all residence counts continuously. It is not a guaranteed processing sequence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Seven years of ordinary residence immediately before application; no qualifying starting route exists for the supplied remote-worker profile.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Citizenship Act and constitutional material inspected publish no typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: Naturalisation requires seven years of ordinary residence, intention to continue residing, good character, conversational Kiribati, respect for customs and traditions, means of support, citizenship knowledge, renunciation of other citizenship, and an oath of allegiance. Approval is discretionary through the Citizenship Commission.
key_conditions.notes: Residence time spent in custody awaiting deportation is excluded.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution specifies no minimum marriage or residence period for a qualifying woman to apply for registration, but the rule is explicitly gender-specific.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A foreign woman married to a male Kiribati citizen is constitutionally entitled to apply for registration as a citizen. The text does not provide a reciprocal registration entitlement for a foreign husband married to a female Kiribati citizen.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing genuine qualifying marriage can therefore matter immediately for a female applicant, subject to prescribed application procedures.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship is not automatic upon marriage; an application in the prescribed manner is required. The constitutional wording is gender-discriminatory, no current processing standard is published in the materials inspected, and genuine identity and relationship evidence should be expected. False statements or sham arrangements can cause refusal and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Current filing practice should be confirmed directly with citizenship or immigration authorities.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Kiribati is a citizen at birth unless the child is not of I-Kiribati descent, the father is not a citizen, and the child acquires another country's citizenship at birth. Diplomatic and enemy-occupation exceptions also apply.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Kiribati-born child of two migrant parents becomes a citizen only if the constitutional exclusion does not apply. If the child automatically acquires either parent's foreign citizenship, Kiribati citizenship is generally not acquired; if the child would otherwise lack another citizenship, Kiribati birth citizenship may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The answer depends on the parents' nationality laws, so an unconditional boolean would be inaccurate.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The constitutional text automatically covers a child whose father is a Kiribati citizen. For a child born out of wedlock, references to the father are construed as references to the mother. The consolidated text does not establish a fully gender-neutral rule for every child of a citizen mother, so case-specific registration advice is required.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The historical gender distinction prevents a universal true/false answer for every one-citizen-parent case.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a citizen child does not automatically grant a migrant parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. The immigration procedures establish no general parent-of-citizen settlement shortcut.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A dependent-child visitor category exists, but the reverse parent-of-child benefit is not established.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic immigration or citizenship status through the child's citizenship. If the other parent is a Kiribati citizen, marriage rules assist only a foreign woman married to a male citizen; the Constitution provides no equivalent citizenship-registration entitlement to a foreign husband.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Family-specific advice is essential because the constitutional rules retain gender distinctions.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; index values can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's advance-visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Calculated from 43 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 5 eTA destinations reported separately by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index also displayed a mobility score of 127. Its methodology differs from Henley, so ranks and access totals should not be mixed across indexes.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is official, and the national tourism authority says it is widely understood, particularly for services. Remote work remains operationally challenging because Internet Society data characterizes international upstream diversity as poor and reports access costs of about 7.97% of average income for a low-consumption basket.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English practicality is stronger in South Tarawa than on remote islands; connectivity quality and backup power should be checked at the exact accommodation.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. The documented official and commonly used language environment provides no basis to expect widespread Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services; English or Gilbertese would normally be necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: A cautious practical assessment based on the documented language environment, not a measured proficiency survey.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official-survey average employee wage of AUD 538 per month using AUD 1 ≈ USD 0.697.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official-survey median employee wage of AUD 430 per month.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the statutory AUD 1.30 hourly minimum for locally funded private-sector work, assuming 40 hours weekly and 52/12 weeks monthly. This is a statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of AUD 538.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of AUD 430.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The national labour monograph publishes no nationwide maximum wage, upper percentile, or top-of-distribution statistic. The underlying microdata catalog identifies an employee-earnings variable but does not publish a computed maximum, while a public-service salary scale would not represent a nationwide maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: AUD 1.30 per hour; approximately AUD 225 per month at 40 hours weekly
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum for local businesses/private construction. Foreign-funded projects have a separate AUD 3.00 hourly minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly wage in employees' main jobs from the 2023 HIES-based labour monograph.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly employee wage from the same national survey.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The 2023–2024 national labour monograph publishes averages and medians, including subgroup averages, but no nationwide maximum wage, upper percentile, or top-of-distribution statistic. The ILO public HIES catalog confirms that monthly employee-earnings variables exist in the underlying microdata but does not publish a computed national maximum; the government employment portal links a public-service salary scale, which is not a nationwide maximum for all citizen/resident workers. A numeric maximum would therefore be misleading and remains null.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average and median monthly wages in employees' main jobs from the 2023–2024 HIES labour-market monograph; minimum is a statutory hourly wage converted to a monthly equivalent.
average_citizen_salary.period: 2023 wages, report published 2025; minimum-wage page checked 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average citizen/resident worker wage statistics, not immigration income thresholds. USD conversions use approximately AUD 1 = USD 0.697 as available near the research date.

cost_of_living_note.value: The inspected official sources do not publish a reliable nationwide remote-worker monthly budget. CPI material measures price changes rather than an absolute household budget, while actual costs are highly location-dependent.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No monthly cost estimate is inferred from CPI data.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor or visa-waiver status cannot be used as a digital-nomad substitute because paid activity is broadly defined as work and requires appropriate work authorization.
settlement_track.summary: Kiribati has an indefinite residence visa after three years of ordinary residence and naturalisation after seven years, but it has no lawful temporary route fitting ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Available bridge statuses require local employment, a Kiribati-specific assignment, study, investment, or another non-fitting purpose.
settlement_track.notes: The current negative assessment is supported by the Immigration Act, procedures, and official application forms.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign-client software work performed from Kiribati falls within the broad definition of work. No dedicated foreign-remote-worker category exists, and ordinary work applications require a job offer or qualifying Kiribati-specific purpose.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field audit inspected more than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs, including seven URLs absent from the previous source set. The social-contribution note now distinguishes covered employment from voluntary self-employed participation; the digital-nomad fixed-payment status explains why no route-specific mandatory amount applies; and the national maximum-salary field remains null because the named current statistical sources publish no nationwide maximum.

data.selection_summary: Kuwait is not a match for an ordinary foreign-contract remote software engineer. The current Article 24 source-of-income residence is the closest route, but the official service requires a sponsor-signed application and does not establish independent self-sponsorship, a published foreign-income threshold, permanent residence, or a citizenship path. Article 19 requires a sponsor, work permit, and Kuwaiti commercial documentation; visitor status prohibits work.

visa_application.title: Residence for those with Source of Income Article 24
visa_application.notes: This is the official information and filing-route page for the closest residence category. Applications may be handled through the Sahel app or in person, but the page requires the residence application to be signed by a sponsor. It is not a confirmed independent remote-worker application channel.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence for Those with Source of Income — Article 24

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official page requires proof of a source of income but publishes no minimum amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum income in KWD is published.

income_requirement_display.notes: The source-of-income wording should not be converted into an invented threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The official service page does not specify a bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Sponsor-signed residence application; the official page does not confirm that an applicant may self-sponsor.
First-time applicants need a passport, photographs, criminal-record clearance, and health-insurance certificate.
Applications may be presented through the Sahel app or in person to the relevant nationality and travel-documents department.
The published fixed first-time fee is KWD 500, with possible variable fees.

initial_validity.notes: The official page does not publish the permit duration.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is available, subject to circulars in force when the application is reviewed.
extension_rules.notes: No maximum renewal count or renewal period is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The service issues a residence permit directly after approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence rather than visitor status, but sponsorship remains mandatory on the published instructions.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No conventional permanent-residence conversion for this category was identified in the official immigration directory or current nationality materials.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No citizenship path from Article 24 is confirmed. Decree-Law 52/2026 repealed the former general-naturalization provisions, including Article 4.

rejected_routes.notes: This route is operational, not merely planned. It nevertheless fails selection because current official instructions require a sponsor and do not confirm self-sponsorship for an ordinary foreign-client remote worker. Filing-level confirmation from the General Department of Residency Affairs would be needed to determine who may sponsor an Article 24 applicant.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Tourist admission is not qualifying residence. Obtaining a later residence permit would be a separate, category-specific approval rather than a residence entitlement created by the tourist visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The visitor status itself has no permanent-residence conversion. The limited in-country status changes identified require eligibility for a separate sponsored or family category and do not establish permanent settlement for an ordinary foreign remote worker.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Tourist or visit status itself has no citizenship path. Current Ministry of Interior rules prohibit work and require departure when the authorized visit ends; Decree-Law 114/2024 treats any later residence as a separately obtained permit, not as continuation of visitor status. The limited visit-to-residence cases reviewed are enumerated family, government/work-process, domestic-service, or exceptional/humanitarian conversions subject to Residence Affairs approval and do not create an ordinary foreign-remote-worker category. Separately, Decree-Law 52/2026 repealed former general-naturalization Articles 2 through 6, including the old residence-based Article 4. Therefore no statutory period of tourist presence can be credited toward ordinary naturalization: the null value reflects that citizenship is inapplicable from this route, not an unpublished waiting period.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourist status prohibits work and is not a settlement route. A visitor who independently qualifies for a separately regulated residence category may seek Ministry approval where current conversion rules permit, but that does not make tourism a remote-work or citizenship route.

summary.value: Article 23 grants sponsored student residence, but it requires a government educational institution to sign the application and specify the residence period. A pre-existing software-engineering degree creates no independent residence entitlement.
summary.notes: No independent degree-recognition, graduate, points-tested, or qualification-only settlement route was found.

tax_residency_rule.value: Kuwait does not levy personal income tax on individuals, so there is no operative domestic personal-income-tax residence threshold for employment or freelance income. A 183-day test appearing in Ministry of Finance tax-clearance procedures concerns corporate-tax administration and should not be treated as a personal PIT rule.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence, treaty residence, and a foreign client's possible Kuwaiti corporate taxable presence remain separate questions.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Zero reflects the absence of Kuwaiti personal income tax on individual income, including income of non-Kuwaiti employees; it is not a temporary incentive rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For the modeled non-Kuwaiti, non-GCC remote worker, ordinary PIFSS pension contributions were not identified. PIFSS defines the insured employee as Kuwaiti and separately covers GCC portability. Kuwaiti insured employees can bear multiple contributions, so 0% must not be generalized to Kuwaiti or qualifying GCC nationals.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No recurring monthly amount can be stated reliably. Residence applicants need health insurance; an older KPMG guide reports a KWD 50 expatriate health levy, but current route pages do not confirm its period or whether that amount remains current.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, expatriate, remittance-basis, or freelancer personal-income-tax regime was identified; the ordinary individual rate is already 0%.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A foreign enterprise may acquire a Kuwaiti corporate taxable presence through activity or representation in Kuwait.

taxes.caveats: The 0% figure concerns Kuwaiti personal income tax only. The worker may remain taxable in another country under that country's residence rules, and a foreign client's corporate-tax or permanent-establishment exposure requires separate advice. Residence fees, health insurance, customs, and departure tax are not personal income tax.

taxation_system.value: Kuwait does not impose personal income tax on individual employment or freelance income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No operative domestic PIT-residency threshold because individuals are not subject to personal income tax.
taxation_system.income_scope: Individual employment and personal freelance income are not subject to Kuwaiti personal income tax; foreign-company activity may create separate corporate-tax exposure.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-individual regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: PIFSS's ordinary insured definition is Kuwaiti-focused; no mandatory PIFSS percentage was established for the modeled non-Kuwaiti, non-GCC remote worker. GCC nationals can fall under protection-extension rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable; there are no individual PIT brackets.
taxation_system.notes: The personal-tax conclusion is well established, but contract structure and foreign-company presence can change the corporate-tax analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special nomad tax regime exists. If a foreign individual lawfully resides under another category, Kuwait's individual personal-income-tax rate remains 0%, subject to foreign-country taxation and possible corporate-presence issues.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% personal income tax; not a special nomad rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No operative Kuwaiti individual PIT threshold; residence and treaty analysis may still matter outside Kuwait.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Kuwait does not impose personal income tax on individual income, but another jurisdiction may tax it.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No mandatory PIFSS contribution was established for the modeled non-Kuwaiti, non-GCC foreign worker. Local employment can carry other labor obligations and end-of-service benefits.

fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No PIFSS percentage was established for the modeled foreign remote worker.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Article 24 publishes a KWD 500 fixed fee plus possible variable fees; Article 19 publishes KWD 50; Article 18 and Article 23 publish KWD 20. These are route fees, not monthly taxes.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: KPMG reports a KWD 3 airport departure tax included in the ticket and an older KWD 50 expatriate health levy; current applicability and frequency of the health amount require confirmation.
fixed_payments.notes: Health-insurance proof is mandatory for the residence categories reviewed.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No Kuwaiti individual PIT is due merely because the person is below a day-count threshold; another country may still treat the person as tax resident.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Kuwait levies no individual PIT, but there is no qualifying independent remote-worker residence route, and the foreign client could face separate corporate-presence questions.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Article 19 requires a sponsor, work permit, and Kuwaiti commercial documents. PIFSS self-employed rules are designed around persons within the statutory insurance system and should not be assumed available to a foreign remote worker.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax treatment does not cure the immigration problem: lawful work authorization must be established independently.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Article 24 would grant residence upon approval, but no processing timeline is published and it is not independently applicable on the current evidence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No conventional permanent-residence stage or qualifying period for Article 24 was identified.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: No permanent-residence-to-citizenship timetable exists for this profile. Decree-Law 52/2026 repealed former general-naturalization Articles 2 through 6.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No current statutory ordinary-residence citizenship timeline can be supplied for this applicant.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current sources publish no typical processing period applicable to this profile; nationality decisions are sovereign and, under amended Article 22, not subject to judicial review.

key_conditions.value: No qualifying citizenship route is confirmed. Current nationality rules emphasize discretionary sovereign decisions, renunciation of other nationality within three months when naturalization is granted, and broad withdrawal or revocation powers.
key_conditions.notes: The older 20-year or 15-year naturalization rule in historical Article 4 is obsolete for current planning because Article 4 was repealed by Decree-Law 52/2026.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A current marriage-based citizenship waiting period is inapplicable: the 2024 reform states that a foreign woman marrying a Kuwaiti is not eligible to acquire nationality, and the 2026 materials do not restore automatic or ordinary acquisition through marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage to a Kuwaiti may support family residence where family-sponsorship rules are met, but it does not confer or accelerate citizenship under the current nationality rules.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The older Article 8 rule and its 15-year period shown in historical legal reproductions are superseded and should not be used for a new application.

requirements_and_risks.value: Family residence requires a qualifying sponsor and supporting kinship, identity, and salary or business documents. Citizenship is not acquired through marriage; nationality decisions are sovereign, and fraud or false-document allegations can lead to serious penalties and revocation consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Genuine-marriage and document verification should be expected. Sham marriage is not a lawful immigration strategy.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The 2026 law places nationality by descent through a Kuwaiti father in amended Article 1. Birth in Kuwait to foreign parents does not generally confer citizenship; prior general foundling and naturalization provisions in Articles 2 through 6 were repealed.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic Kuwaiti citizenship merely from birth in Kuwait to two foreign parents.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No broad jus soli rule exists.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born inside or outside Kuwait to a Kuwaiti father is Kuwaiti under the amended paternal-descent rule. A Kuwaiti mother alone does not create the same generally automatic rule on the sources reviewed; limited protective treatment may exist in specified family circumstances.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The boolean is true only where the citizen parent is the Kuwaiti father. Parent sex and legal filiation matter.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a child in Kuwait does not itself give migrant parents residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. A citizen child may be relevant to separately regulated family residence, but no automatic parent status was identified.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any family application remains sponsor- and category-dependent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically obtain residence or citizenship from the child's birth. Where the mother is Kuwaiti, current law does not generally make the child automatically Kuwaiti through her alone, and no automatic status benefit to the father was identified.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Case-specific humanitarian or family-residence discretion should be verified directly with the Ministry of Interior.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This remains a cautious qualitative conclusion after focused searches found no directly relevant authoritative evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language availability.

The citizen average is not representative of an incoming foreign worker: the same Q1 2025 reporting gives KWD 1,567 for Kuwaitis and KWD 344 for non-Kuwaitis. cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing, household size, schooling, transport, and employer benefits can dominate expatriate costs; a precise budget requires a city- and household-specific source.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourist or eVisa status prohibits work and is not qualifying residence. Article 24 is residence, but its sponsor requirement prevents it from being treated as an independent remote-worker route.
settlement_track.summary: Kuwait documents an operational Article 24 source-of-income residence, but the application must be sponsor-signed and no self-sponsored foreign-remote-worker eligibility or settlement conversion is confirmed. Current citizenship law also repeals the former general-naturalization provisions, leaving no credible citizenship track for this profile.
settlement_track.notes: Classification is not pending implementation because Article 24 is operational. It remains invalid because the published route is sponsored and does not establish ordinary independent foreign-contract remote work.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No current route permits this applicant to self-apply for residence solely on the basis of an ordinary foreign employment or client contract. Article 24 requires a sponsor-signed application; Articles 18 and 19 require local sponsorship and work authorization; tourist status prohibits work.

data.notes: Focused audit of the previous Kuwait record used 31 distinct canonical URLs, including six directly relevant URLs outside the prior source set. The flagged tourist-route citizenship note is resolved factually: tourist presence is a nonworking visitor status, any later residence requires a separate category and approval, and the 2026 repeal of former general-naturalization Articles 2 through 6 leaves no ordinary residence-based naturalization period to which tourist time could contribute. Kuwait remains invalid because independent self-sponsorship, an ordinary remote-worker filing basis, permanent residence, and a citizenship path are not established.

data.selection_summary: Kyrgyzstan has an active Digital Nomad status and direct online application portal. It fits an independently applying software engineer with foreign contracts: initial approval authorizes lawful remote work for 60 days, and renewal for one year—annually for up to 10 years—requires registration as a Kyrgyz individual entrepreneur or through a local entity. General citizenship rules accept visa-based continuous residence and allow ordinary naturalization after five years without first obtaining permanent residence. This is a credible citizenship track, but the applicant should obtain written confirmation that the complete DN status, visa and registration history will be accepted as five years of continuous residence.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad Program
visa_application.notes: The active official portal accepts online applications. The applicant first requests activation of a personal account; the substantive application becomes available after activation. Nationals requiring a visa may also need a DN visa through the separate e-Visa system.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Monthly equivalent of the actual rule: bank evidence of at least USD 5,000 earned from contract services over the preceding year. The regulation does not state a separate monthly threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official requirement is denominated in US dollars, not KGS.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 5,000 of contract-service income during the preceding year (~USD 416.67/month equivalent), plus at least USD 3,000 held in a bank account
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: USD annual income and bank-balance tests
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 5,000 / 12 months; separate USD 3,000 bank balance
income_requirement_display.notes: The USD 3,000 balance is a separate liquidity requirement, not monthly income.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank statement must evidence at least USD 5,000 of income from performed contract services during the year preceding application.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport and compliant digital facial photograph.
Employment, client-service, works or services contracts concluded during the previous two years and/or covering a future period.
Evidence of at least USD 5,000 in contract-service income over the preceding year and at least USD 3,000 in a bank account.
Evidence of professional activity in an eligible digital field, such as a degree, professional qualification, course certificate or recommendation letter; software development is covered.

For the one-year extension: local medical examination and HIV test, continuing professional income, and registration as a Kyrgyz individual entrepreneur and/or through a locally registered legal entity, branch or representative office.
Visa-required nationals must hold a valid DN visa when applying for the one-year extension.

initial_validity.value: 60 days
initial_validity.notes: This is the first-stage Digital Nomad status.

extension_rules.value: Extension to one year, followed by annual renewals for up to 10 years
extension_rules.notes: The first one-year extension must be requested during the initial 60-day period. Local individual-entrepreneur/entity registration and medical documents are required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The status itself authorizes lawful residence and remote professional activity. For visa-required nationals, the DN visa is issued for up to one year. It is not described as an ordinary temporary-residence-permit card.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The temporary-residence flag is true because this is an independently obtained, renewable lawful-residence status, not because it automatically issues a conventional residence-permit card.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Digital Nomad status permits renewable remote-work stay, but a PR pathway retaining that profile is not verified. General guidance refers to more than five years of lawful stay without expressly establishing how DN status qualifies.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The DN programme can be renewed annually for up to ten years. That duration and the general five-year PR threshold do not independently prove a DN-to-PR entitlement or an eligible remote-work successor. DN-time credit, the filing procedure and the applicable PR timeline remain unconfirmed. Ministry PR pages were reviewed through official indexed text.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization is available after five years of continuous residence. Official citizenship guidance says a visa is acceptable evidence of continuous residence for visa-required nationals and permanent residence is not mandatory. A five-year DN history can therefore support naturalization if continuity, renewals and residence evidence are accepted.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This combines the general visa-evidence rule with the DN visa rules; no DN-specific naturalization ruling was located. Obtain written confirmation concerning evidence for visa-free nationals and any period during which DN holders were exempt from address registration.

best_routes.notes: The route fits ordinary foreign-client software work and is renewable beyond the ordinary five-year naturalization period. Continued status requires local individual-entrepreneur or entity registration during the initial 60 days, but it does not require a Kyrgyz employer or client.

income_requirement_display.notes: The official grounds listed are local employment with work authorization, local study or investment.

extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains dependent on the underlying qualifying ground.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant's existing foreign software contract alone is not one of the listed grounds.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General permanent residence may be available after more than five years of lawful stay.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: All substantive permanent-residence conditions still apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Potentially useful for a local student, employee or investor, but not the best route for the supplied foreign-contract software-engineer profile.

summary.value: Admission to a Kyrgyz educational institution can support a student visa and ordinary temporary residence without an employer, but it requires the local institution's contract or petition and is not a degree-holder migration route. A relevant software degree or qualification separately helps prove Digital Nomad eligibility but does not by itself grant residence.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing foreign university degree is evidence for the Digital Nomad application, not an independent qualification-based residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally tax-resident after physical presence in Kyrgyzstan for at least 183 days during any consecutive 12-month period ending in the current tax period.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax residence are separate tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the standard flat personal-income-tax screening rate. A locally registered individual entrepreneur may instead fall under a turnover-based unified-tax regime.

social_contributions_percent.notes: There is no single percentage of actual remote-work income applicable to every DN holder. Individual-entrepreneur obligations use statutory categories and an average-wage base, whereas employees and employers use different rates and bases. The applicant's precise classification and registration locality must be established first.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No nationwide fixed USD monthly amount exists that can safely be assigned to every Digital Nomad individual entrepreneur. The generally published IP rule uses a minimum contribution calculated as a percentage of an official average monthly wage for the relevant city or district, rather than a fixed national amount; separate categories use different percentages or bases. The Social Fund page checked on 2026-08-15 linked locality-specific bases for 2025 but did not publish a DN-specific classification or a complete 2026 amount that would allow one universal monthly USD figure. The value therefore remains null because the amount is formula- and locality-dependent, not because social-insurance obligations are absent.

special_tax_regimes.value: Individual entrepreneurs may use a unified turnover-tax regime instead of ordinary PIT. Published guidance identifies 2% for non-cash and 4% for cash receipts from software development, while a later reform introduced a 0.1% unified-tax rate for qualifying activity outside Kyrgyzstan and a 0.1% tax on transactions through a foreign bank. Whether foreign-client software performed physically in Kyrgyzstan qualifies as activity outside the country requires a tax ruling or local advice.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The 0.1% provision should not be assumed automatically merely because the client is foreign.

taxes.caveats: Tax results depend on whether the contract is treated as employment or entrepreneurship, whether services are Kyrgyz-source, whether the DN holder is treated as holding a residence permit for Tax Code purposes, the selected unified-tax category, payment channel, social-insurance classification, registration locality and any applicable treaty. IP registration for the immigration extension creates local filing obligations even when the client and payment account are foreign.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system for this profile: standard personal income is generally taxed at a flat 10%, while a registered individual entrepreneur may use turnover-based unified-tax rates. Digital Nomad renewal requires IP or entity registration, so entrepreneur rules may be more practically relevant than ordinary PIT.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 days during any consecutive 12-month period ending in the current tax period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Professional guidance describes residents as generally taxable on worldwide income and non-residents on Kyrgyz-source income. Tax Code treatment of resident foreigners also depends on immigration status. DN status is not expressly identified as a residence permit, and services performed physically in Kyrgyzstan may be Kyrgyz-source.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Unified turnover tax for registered entrepreneurs; published software-development rates are 2% for non-cash and 4% for cash receipts. A later reform introduced 0.1% for qualifying activity outside Kyrgyzstan and 0.1% for transactions through foreign banks, subject to classification.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee, employer, entrepreneur and foreigner rules use different rates and bases. An IP contribution may be formula-based on a locality-specific official average wage; no universal DN monthly amount is published.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Ordinary PIT is flat, not progressive. Unified-tax percentages apply to turnover and should not be compared directly with a net-income PIT rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Standard taxable personal income; no progressive threshold
tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary personal income outside an applicable entrepreneur regime
tax_brackets.notes: Flat screening rate; deductions, source rules and special regimes can change the result.

taxation_system.notes: The standard 10% rule is well supported. Confidence is lower for the DN/IP effective burden because current official material does not publish a route-specific tax example and the social-insurance base varies by classification and locality.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Initial DN status does not publish a special tax exemption. The one-year extension requires local IP or entity registration, after which unified turnover tax and social-insurance filings may apply. Standard PIT is 10%; potential IP rates are lower but depend on activity, payment and source classification.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: digital nomad with mandatory self-employed/local-business registration for renewal
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% standard PIT screening rate; potentially 2% non-cash/4% cash unified tax for software-development turnover, or 0.1% only if the outside-Kyrgyzstan activity rule is confirmed to apply
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in any consecutive 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Professional guidance says tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income, but current Tax Code wording distinguishes some resident foreigners by immigration status. Foreign-client work physically performed from Kyrgyzstan and locally booked IP revenue may be treated as Kyrgyz-source; obtain local advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No standalone Digital Nomad tax holiday was located. The relevant favorable provisions are general individual-entrepreneur and unified-tax rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Local IP registration can trigger social-insurance obligations under a statutory category and locality-specific average-wage formula. No official DN example states one universally applicable rate or amount.

fixed_payments.status: amount_not_confirmed_route_dependent
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potential mandatory IP social-insurance contribution. Public rules indicate formula-based minimums tied to an official average-wage base, while the applicable percentage, base and locality depend on classification. No universal DN amount is published.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The public DN portal does not display a complete fee schedule. Any status, DN-visa or document charges must be checked inside the authenticated application and e-Visa payment flow.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A 0.1% tax on qualifying transactions through a foreign bank was enacted in the later tax reform; its application to a DN's particular receipts requires confirmation.
fixed_payments.notes: The public sources establish that formula-based or category-specific payments can apply, but they do not establish one nationwide monthly amount for every DN/IP applicant.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Spending fewer than 183 days avoids tax-resident status, but locally performed services, Kyrgyz-source income, IP turnover and transaction or social-insurance rules may still create liability.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Use 10% as the conservative ordinary-PIT screen until a Kyrgyz adviser confirms source, immigration-status treatment and whether an entrepreneur regime displaces PIT.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: This is the expected renewal scenario. Register the IP or entity, select the correct unified-tax category, issue required fiscal documents, file returns and obtain the locality-specific social-insurance assessment. Do not assume the 0.1% outside-country rate solely because the client is foreign.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Professional filing advice is particularly important before the initial 60-day status expires because local business registration is an immigration-renewal requirement.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The independently obtained DN status immediately authorizes lawful residence and remote work during its initial 60-day period.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Official guidance says permanent residence is available after lawful presence exceeding five years, subject to permanent legal income. It does not expressly name DN status, so filing eligibility should be confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Permanent residence is not a prerequisite. General naturalization can be requested after five years of continuous residence, so no additional waiting period after becoming PR-eligible is established.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the ordinary eligibility period, followed by application processing. The DN-specific residence-evidence issue should be confirmed before relying on this timeline.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The law permits up to one year for a general-order decision. This is a statutory maximum rather than a guaranteed typical completion time.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous lawful residence for five years; annual absences must not exceed three months; retain every DN status, visa and residence record; demonstrate sufficient command of Kyrgyz or Russian, lawful means of support, legal compliance, and the required criminal-record evidence.
key_conditions.notes: Permanent residence is not a prerequisite. No general mandatory renunciation rule was established for this ordinary case, but dual-nationality and nationality-specific documentation should be reviewed at filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage to a Kyrgyz citizen reduces the ordinary five-year residence period to three years. Official guidance describes eligibility after three years of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Kyrgyz citizen can support the reduced three-year naturalization period and preferential permanent-residence treatment. Marriage to another non-citizen does not accelerate either spouse's citizenship, although dependent immigration documentation may be available.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not grant citizenship automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant still needs documented lawful residence, adequate Kyrgyz or Russian, lawful means of support, legal compliance and the required criminal-record evidence. Authorities may require marriage and cohabitation evidence; false documents or a sham marriage can cause refusal and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Document the three-year period from the marriage date and reconcile it with the residence evidence required at filing.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Kyrgyzstan alone does not generally confer citizenship. Citizenship at birth applies through a Kyrgyz parent and in limited territorial cases involving stateless parents, foreign ethnic-Kyrgyz parents or unknown parents.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Kyrgyzstan to two ordinary foreign-citizen migrants is not automatically Kyrgyz. Exceptions include a child whose foreign parents are ethnic Kyrgyz, a child whose parents are stateless, and a foundling with unknown parents.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth registration is distinct from acquisition of citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with one Kyrgyz-citizen parent and one foreign-citizen parent is generally Kyrgyz at birth. The law provides an exception where both parents jointly decline Kyrgyz citizenship for a child who acquires foreign citizenship by birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule applies regardless of whether the Kyrgyz parent is the mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. A parent of a Kyrgyz citizen is listed among persons with preferential permanent-residence treatment and may apply after six months of lawful stay, subject to income, housing, medical, criminal-record and documentary requirements.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: This is accelerated eligibility to apply for permanent residence, not automatic approval or citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father may use the same parent-of-a-Kyrgyz-citizen preferential permanent-residence ground after six months of lawful stay. He does not automatically receive residence, permanent residence or citizenship merely because the child is Kyrgyz.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, the child's citizenship and the family relationship must be legally documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 42 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations. Passport Index also reported a mobility score of 72. Henley uses a broader no-prior-visa methodology, so its figures should not be mixed with this breakdown.

passport.notes: Passport Index was selected because it separately reports visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA and visa-required categories. Henley is retained as a methodological cross-check.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable in international and technology circles in Bishkek but weak for routine administration and life outside those circles. EF's 2025 index ranked Kyrgyzstan 101st with a score of 443, below its global average of 488.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: A remote worker can work in English for a foreign client, but Russian or Kyrgyz is advisable for tax registration, healthcare, housing and government procedures.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is an official language and remains widely used in larger cities and business, making it highly practical for daily life and administration. Ukrainian has no official status and should not be assumed to substitute for Russian in formal procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Kyrgyz is the state language and is increasingly required in public administration; long-term residents should not rely exclusively on Russian.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official May 2026 organized-sector wage/income figure of KGS 60,816 using about KGS 87.4 per USD. The statistic is partial and excludes small enterprises.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official current wage sources publish averages but no national median-wage series; the average cannot be presented as a median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 statutory minimum monthly wage of KGS 3,280 using about KGS 87.4 per USD. This is a statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary or a realistic living-wage benchmark.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of KGS 60,816.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official wage releases checked publish arithmetic averages and sector or territorial figures, but no national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official national statistics do not define or publish a meaningful maximum individual salary; sector averages are not nationwide maxima.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the statutory national minimum monthly wage set for 2026 for an unskilled employee performing simple work during normal full working hours. It is distinct from the KGS 7,040 minimum base rates established by separate 2026 decrees for calculating salaries in particular public-sector systems; those sector-specific base rates are not the national minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: May 2026 partial organized-sector wage/income statistic excluding small enterprises. January 2026's broader territorial average was KGS 45,797.3, illustrating period and coverage sensitivity.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The named current official statistics publish average wages but no national median amount.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The named official statistics do not publish a nationwide maximum individual monthly salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory national minimum wage plus monthly organized-sector average wage/income; the average is partial and excludes small enterprises
average_citizen_salary.period: 2026 statutory minimum; May 2026 average
average_citizen_salary.notes: KGS 3,280 is a statutory minimum wage, not an observed low-end salary or living wage. KGS 60,816 is the current organized-sector average and is not the earnings of every citizen; excluding small enterprises may raise it relative to an all-worker average.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official statistics maintains a subsistence-minimum series. The Q2 2026 national figure reported from that series was KGS 9,873.28 per person per month. This is a basic-needs statistical benchmark, not a realistic expatriate or Bishkek rental budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing, private healthcare, imported goods and a remote worker's lifestyle can make actual costs substantially higher.
