settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The route is not merely a short visitor program: it can be renewed annually for up to 10 years. Nevertheless, obtain written confirmation that DN status and visa records—especially for visa-free nationals exempt from address registration—will be accepted as five years of continuous residence.
settlement_track.summary: The active Digital Nomad route authorizes lawful residence, fits foreign software contracts and can be renewed beyond the five-year naturalization period. General citizenship guidance accepts visas as continuous-residence evidence and does not require prior permanent residence, making this a credible direct citizenship track subject to careful preservation and pre-confirmation of DN residence evidence.
settlement_track.notes: The connection is supported by general visa-residence rules rather than a published DN-specific naturalization decision. A conventional permanent-residence application after more than five years is an optional backup, not a stated citizenship prerequisite.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The program expressly accepts employment and client-service contracts, requires documented professional income and covers software or ICT activity without a Kyrgyz employer. Renewal requires local IP or entity registration, but the client may remain foreign.

data.notes: Current primary sources confirm the active program, online application portal, financial evidence, professional evidence, initial period and renewals up to 10 years. The focused audit established that the 2026 statutory minimum wage is KGS 3,280 and that KGS 7,040 is a separate public-sector base rate. It also established why no single fixed monthly USD social-insurance amount can be reported: IP contributions depend on statutory classification, a locality-specific average-wage base and current assessment. The remaining material uncertainty is how a DN holder—especially a visa-free national—should document continuous residence for naturalization.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Digital Nomad status permits renewable remote-work stay, but a PR pathway retaining that profile is not verified. General guidance refers to more than five years of lawful stay without expressly establishing how DN status qualifies.
requirements: Verify that DN residence meets the permanent-residence legal-stay test and how exempt-from-registration periods must be documented.
If eligible, substantiate sufficient legal income, housing, police clearance and medical requirements.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The DN programme can be renewed annually for up to ten years. That duration and the general five-year PR threshold do not independently prove a DN-to-PR entitlement or an eligible remote-work successor. DN-time credit, the filing procedure and the applicable PR timeline remain unconfirmed. Ministry PR pages were reviewed through official indexed text.
reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad status and DN visa

data.selection_summary: Laos has no confirmed digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary freelance residence route. The official eVisa is tourist-only. Foreigners can establish Lao enterprises and qualifying investors can obtain business visas and renewable stay permits, but this requires genuine local business registration, investment, licensing, tax and social-security compliance rather than merely continuing a foreign software contract. A discretionary permanent-residence category also exists for experts required by Laos, but a university degree alone does not qualify.

visa_application.title: Lao Official Online Visa application
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct application portal, but it currently accepts only tourist-visa applications. The resulting single-entry eVisa permits a 30-day stay and is not a remote-work or residence route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official tourist-eVisa materials publish no remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is published for the tourist eVisa.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; tourist entry only
income_requirement_display.notes: Absence of an income threshold does not authorize employment or foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The official pages do not specify a recurring-income evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Online application, passport biodata page and recent 4×6 cm photograph.
The online system currently accepts only tourist-visa applications.
The approval letter must be printed and presented with the passport at an authorized entry point.

initial_validity.value: Approval letter valid for entry for up to 60 days; single-entry stay limited to 30 days
initial_validity.notes: The 60-day approval-letter validity is not the permitted stay. The stay begins on entry and is limited to 30 days.

extension_rules.notes: The official eVisa and immigration materials checked do not publish an extension or conversion into remote-worker residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None from the tourist eVisa
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A tourist eVisa is entry permission, not a Lao stay-permit category for remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No tourist-eVisa path
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence has separate statutory criteria; tourist stays do not establish a qualifying route.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path from this eVisa
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires qualifying permanent residence and the nationality-law conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Useful only for a short tourist visit. It does not fit ordinary foreign-contract remote work and is not settlement-oriented.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign-owned enterprise, NI-B2 investor visa and stay permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This route is based on establishing and operating a Lao business, not monthly foreign income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly-income threshold applies. An older implementation rule cited on the trade portal specifies at least LAK 1 billion of registered capital for general foreign investment, but its application under the amended 2024 Investment Promotion Law requires confirmation.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly income test; genuine Lao enterprise and investment required
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Business capital and local regulatory compliance, not personal income
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Older implementing rule: at least LAK 1 billion registered capital for general foreign investment; verify current applicability
income_requirement_display.notes: At the Bank of the Lao PDR reference rate captured near the research date, LAK 1 billion was approximately USD 44,300. This is capital, not monthly income.

income_proof_months.notes: No recurring-income proof period is published; authorities instead require investment, enterprise, tax and licensing records.

key_requirements.requirement: Register and genuinely operate a Lao enterprise, subject to sector and licensing rules.
Obtain an enterprise registration certificate and taxpayer identification number; some activities also require a business or investment licence.
For NI-B2 and the investor stay permit, provide investment or enterprise registration, tax registration, passport and company proposal documents.
Complete social-security registration as part of the official business-start process.
The 2024 investment law routes foreign-investor visa, work and residence-permit processing through investment one-stop services.

initial_validity.value: Ordinary investor stay permit and multiple-entry visa generally up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Three-to-five-year validity is described for concession investors with government agreements lasting at least ten years; ordinary registered businesses generally receive no more than one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewable year by year while the qualifying Lao investment and enterprise remain compliant
extension_rules.notes: Renewal depends on continuing business, registration, tax and permit compliance.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: NI-B2 entry followed by an investor stay-permit card through the investment one-stop service
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is available to qualifying investors, not someone solely working under a foreign contract.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The general decree permits an application after at least 10 years of continuous lawful residence; a separate investor criterion applies after more than 5 years where registered capital exceeds USD 500,000 and the investment remains stable and tax-compliant
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Neither criterion converts an ordinary foreign remote-work arrangement into residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: After permanent residence, naturalization generally requires 10 years of continuous permanent residence plus Lao-language, integration, economic-status and renunciation conditions
path_to_citizenship.notes: This theoretical route depends on genuine local investment and is not a foreign-contract remote-work path.

rejected_routes.notes: Potentially self-initiated, but excluded because it is a genuine local entrepreneur/investor route with capital, local-business substance and regulatory obligations.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permanent residence for an expert required by Lao PDR

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The decree states no income threshold for this expert criterion.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No local-currency income threshold is specified.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; applicant must be an expert required by Lao PDR
income_requirement_display.notes: Qualification is based on special expertise required by the country, not ordinary foreign-contract earnings.

income_proof_months.notes: The decree specifies no income-evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Professional knowledge at expert level required by Lao PDR.
No prior intentional-offence custodial sentence.
Application and supporting documentation through the designated Lao diplomatic or governmental channel.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence, if discretionarily approved
initial_validity.notes: The decree creates eligibility to request permanent residence, not an automatic entitlement.

extension_rules.value: Permanent residence is without a fixed time limit, subject to continued legal compliance
extension_rules.notes: The reviewed sources do not establish the detailed card-renewal administration.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not required by the wording of the expert criterion, but filing practice requires official confirmation
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The decree lists expert status as a separate permanent-residence criterion.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct discretionary application under the expert-needed criterion
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No points system or degree-only qualification was found.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization generally requires 10 years of continuous permanent residence and all nationality-law conditions
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality law has a three-year exception for outstanding experts needed by the Party and State, but this is not an ordinary software-engineer route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a relevant degree and foreign software contract do not establish that the applicant is an expert specifically required by Lao PDR.

rejected_routes.route_name: LA-B2 technical foreign-employee visa and stay permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official investor visa and stay-permit page publishes no salary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum salary is stated.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; Lao company sponsorship and labour approval required
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility depends on a Lao enterprise's approved need for foreign technical labour.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: A Lao company must request authorization to use foreign technical labour.
Directors without shares, technicians and technical officers use the LA-B2 category and require company documentation.
Work and stay permits are tied to the Lao enterprise and approved employment.

initial_validity.value: Generally no more than 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Foreign directors and technicians follow annual validity rather than the longer concession-investor privilege.

extension_rules.value: Renewable year by year while sponsored employment and company approvals continue
extension_rules.notes: Renewal is employer-dependent.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employer-supported LA-B2 visa and stay permit
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not independently available to a foreign-contract remote worker.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General permanent-residence rules may become relevant after long lawful residence, but no direct conversion from LA-B2 is stated
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The initial route remains employer-sponsored.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct route; general naturalization requires qualifying permanent residence and nationality-law conditions
path_to_citizenship.notes: Employment-visa time is not itself stated to count as permanent residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Lao employer/company proposal, labour approval and local technical role are required.

summary.value: A university degree by itself creates no confirmed Lao residence route. The permanent-residence decree has a discretionary category for experts whose professional knowledge is required by Lao PDR, but this is not an ordinary degree-based program.
summary.notes: The expert category can directly result in permanent residence when approved, but it provides no general software-engineer eligibility, points test, occupation list or degree-only test.

tax_residency_rule.value: The current income-tax definition treats a person with permanent residence, living, earning a living or conducting business in Laos as resident. Separately, a foreigner staying more than 183 aggregate days in a one-year period and receiving remuneration from abroad is obligated to pay Lao PIT.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The residence definition is broader than a simple day-count test. Treaty position, domicile, business presence and the nature and place of work require individual analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal monthly PIT rate under the new Income Tax Law effective 1 July 2026, not an expected effective rate. Lower bands range from 0% to 20%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The displayed 5.5% is the employee rate; the employer contributes another 6%, producing an 11.5% combined payroll rate. Current summaries apply both percentages to monthly insurable earnings capped at LAK 4.5 million, giving maximum monthly amounts of LAK 247,500 for the employee and LAK 270,000 for the employer. The Social Security Law separately defines self-employed people as voluntary insured persons and sets their contribution at 9% of a selected insurable-earnings amount between the statutory minimum wage and the applicable ceiling. PwC states that expatriates working in Laos for more than 12 months must register. None of these rules creates immigration permission for foreign remote work.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal fixed monthly digital-nomad payment because Laos has no such route. Contributions are percentage-based. For an employee at the LAK 4.5 million ceiling, the 5.5% employee share is LAK 247,500, approximately USD 11 at the cited exchange rate. A lawfully registered voluntary/self-employed insured person pays 9% of a selected base, not a single fixed amount.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or general inbound-expatriate tax exemption was found. Sole traders and independent contractors are subject to profit tax on Lao-derived business income; exact treatment depends on registration and income characterization.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The 2026 law introduced a 5% net-profit tax for qualifying microenterprises and a 10% withholding rate for consultancy and service fees, but these provisions should not be applied to a foreign remote worker without professional classification advice.

taxes.caveats: Tax liability depends on physical presence, whether work is performed in Laos, residence or permanent-business ties, whether payments are salary or independent-service income, Lao registration, withholding, social-security coverage and any applicable treaty. Immigration permission and tax liability are separate questions.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax on remuneration, with separate profit-tax and withholding rules for business or service income
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Resident status may arise from permanent residence, living, earning a living or conducting business in Laos; foreign remuneration becomes expressly taxable after more than 183 aggregate days in a one-year period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Lao remuneration is taxable; foreign remuneration is taxable for foreigners staying more than 183 days. Lao-derived sole-trader and independent-contractor business income is subject to profit-tax rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary inbound-remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees contribute 5.5% and employers 6% on a contribution base currently reported as capped at LAK 4.5 million. Expatriates working in Laos for more than 12 months must register. The law treats self-employed people as voluntary insured persons subject to a 9% contribution on a selected base between the minimum wage and applicable ceiling.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% dashboard figure is the top marginal screening rate, applying only to the monthly slice above LAK 65 million. It is not the effective rate on total income.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Monthly remuneration up to the upper threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted at approximately LAK 22,564 per USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Income slice within this monthly band
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Income slice within this monthly band
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Income slice within this monthly band
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Income above the band entry point
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate lower threshold; this is the top marginal band.

taxation_system.notes: Rates and caps are a screening summary. The 2018 Social Security Law was under government review in 2024–2025; no enacted replacement changing the cited rates was located, and current 2026 tax and payroll summaries continue to report 5.5%, 6% and the LAK 4.5 million ceiling.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a dedicated regime: Laos has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker immigration category.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; tourist stays, Lao employment and locally registered business are treated under their ordinary rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 25% progressive PIT on remuneration; separate business-income rules may apply
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: A broad residence definition applies, and foreign remuneration is expressly taxable after more than 183 aggregate days in a one-year period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign remuneration is taxable when a foreigner stays more than 183 days. Shorter presence does not guarantee exemption where the person lives, works, earns a living or conducts business in Laos.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No digital-nomad-specific payroll rule exists. For lawful Lao employment, the employee rate is 5.5% and employer rate is 6% on monthly insurable earnings capped at LAK 4.5 million; PwC states expatriates working in Laos for more than 12 months must register. The Social Security Law defines self-employed people as voluntary insured persons and sets a 9% contribution on a selected insurable-earnings base between the minimum wage and applicable ceiling. Whether a particular foreign contractor can register in that category depends on lawful Lao business and immigration status and should be confirmed with the Lao Social Security Organisation.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed digital-nomad payment because no such route exists; ordinary social-security contributions are percentage-based
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: At the current LAK 4.5 million ceiling, maximum monthly employee and employer shares are LAK 247,500 and LAK 270,000. A voluntary/self-employed insured person pays 9% of a selected base: using the cited LAK 2.5 million minimum wage and LAK 4.5 million ceiling, this corresponds to LAK 225,000–405,000 per month. This is a conditional contribution range, not a digital-nomad fee, and foreign-contractor eligibility requires local confirmation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Tourist-eVisa fees are collected online and can depend on nationality; no universal amount was established. Investor-page fees include LAK 300,000, 600,000 and 1,200,000 for 3-, 6- and 12-month multiple-entry visas, respectively, plus other service fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Stamp taxes generally range from LAK 2,000 to LAK 20,000. Enterprise-registration issuance fees range from LAK 20,000 to LAK 5 million by registered capital, plus form and administrative charges.
fixed_payments.notes: The voluntary-insurance range is calculated from the statutory 9% rate, cited current minimum wage and cited contribution ceiling. Investor, enterprise and social-security payments do not create a remote-work immigration route; current filing amounts should be verified before payment.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A sub-183-day stay does not legalize remote work and is not automatically tax-free: Lao-source remuneration, work performed locally, residence facts or business activity may still trigger tax.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A person living in Laos and receiving foreign remuneration after more than 183 days is expressly subject to Lao PIT, potentially up to the 25% marginal band, but currently lacks a matching remote-worker immigration route.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A genuinely registered Lao enterprise must obtain a TIN, complete relevant licensing and social-security steps, and apply ordinary profit-tax or withholding rules. A self-employed person may voluntarily insure at 9% of a selected insurable base, but foreign-client software revenue and foreigner eligibility require local classification advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening analysis, not a claim that tourist status permits remote work. Social-security rules were separately checked against the official English Social Security Law, a current tax summary, OECD analysis and a 2026 payroll-compliance summary.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No temporary-residence route fitting ordinary foreign-contract remote work exists in the reviewed sources. Qualifying investors can obtain stay permits only through a genuine Lao enterprise or investment.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The general decree permits foreigners to request permanent residence after at least ten years of continuous lawful residence. This is not a confirmed conversion path from tourist or remote-worker status.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The 2017 nationality law generally requires ten years of continuous permanent residence before naturalization.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Theoretical general sequence: ten years of continuous lawful residence to become eligible to request permanent residence, followed by ten years of continuous permanent residence before requesting nationality. Approval at both stages is discretionary, and no suitable initial remote-work status exists.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The nationality law specifies staged administrative review periods totaling at least 80 days before the Ministry of Justice proposes a case to the government, but it gives no complete filing-to-final-decision deadline.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires age 18+, respect for the Constitution and laws, fluent spoken/read/written Lao, social and cultural integration, good health, acceptable criminal history, prior-nationality renunciation, contribution to national protection and development, no harm to national interests, qualifications, stable economic status and ten years of continuous permanent residence.
key_conditions.notes: Laos generally does not authorize multiple nationality. Exceptional three-year treatment exists for outstanding persons needed by the Party and State, but it is not an ordinary migration route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreigner legally married to a Lao citizen may request permanent residence after continuously residing in Laos for more than two years. This accelerates permanent-residence eligibility, not automatic citizenship.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage to a Lao citizen can support permanent-residence eligibility after more than two years of continuous Lao residence, but marriage itself does not change either spouse's nationality.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing foreign marriage must be valid and accepted for Lao administrative purposes; filing and registration requirements should be confirmed locally.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legal and the foreign spouse must continuously reside in Laos for more than two years. Permanent residence remains subject to application and approval. Citizenship still requires the nationality-law conditions, including Lao language, integration, stable economic status, continuous permanent residence and renunciation. Genuine-marriage evidence should be expected; sham marriage can create immigration and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The current nationality law contains no marriage-specific reduction of the naturalization residence period.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Laos alone is insufficient. Children of two foreign citizens do not automatically acquire Lao nationality. Limited provisions cover children of a Lao parent, foundlings, and children born in Laos to permanently resident, socially integrated stateless parents upon parental request.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Laos to two foreign-citizen migrant parents does not automatically become Lao. If both parents are stateless, permanently resident and integrated into Lao society and culture, the child may acquire Lao citizenship upon the parents' request.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is restricted, anti-statelessness-oriented jus soli rather than general birthright citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is Lao and the child is born in Laos, the child is Lao by birth. A child born abroad also qualifies where either parent has a permanent address in Laos; if both parents permanently reside abroad, the parents decide the child's nationality.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Where the other parent is stateless, the child is Lao regardless of birthplace.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A child's Lao citizenship does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on a foreign father. Marriage to the Lao parent may create a separate permanent-residence application after more than two years of continuous Lao residence.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No standalone parent-of-Lao-child naturalization shortcut was found.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic nationality or residence. Any benefit must arise through a separate valid family, marriage, employment, investor or permanent-residence provision.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The nationality of one spouse or child does not automatically change the father's nationality.

rank.notes: Index methodologies differ. Guide Passport Index ranked Laos 98th when accessed in August 2026.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Guide Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Guide Passport Index groups destinations requiring a physical visa or an eVisa in this figure, so it is broader than consular-visa-only destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 20 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 3 eTA destinations, excluding separately categorized eVisa destinations.

passport.notes: Guide Passport Index reports 43 combined visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations. Figures change frequently and should be rechecked before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Possible in Vientiane and international business or tourism settings, but Lao remains necessary for government procedures and broader daily life. EF EPI 2025 ranked Laos 88th with a score of 461, indicating limited-to-moderate practical English rather than universal proficiency.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is based on test participants rather than a complete population census, so it is a directional indicator.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official language, and the reviewed sources provide no evidence of broad public or administrative use.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Individual expatriate communities may exist, but nationwide practicality is not established.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximately LAK 2.504 million per month from the 2022 Labour Force Survey, converted at roughly LAK 22,564 per USD. This is an employee average, not an immigration threshold.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2022 labour-market profile reports arithmetic-average wages, while the Lao Statistics Bureau earnings indicator is also defined as an arithmetic average. Neither reviewed source publishes a national median monthly employee wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the LAK 2.5 million statutory monthly minimum wage cited in the July 2026 tax-law update. This is a legal minimum wage, not the lowest observed salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2022 Labour Force Survey's LAK 2.504 million average monthly employee wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed national sources provide arithmetic means and disaggregated average earnings but do not publish a national median salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official and UN-supported wage sources publish average earnings and subgroup averages, not a national maximum salary or upper wage-distribution endpoint.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage cited as current in the July 2026 tax update.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly wage of employees in the 2022 Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The UNDP/UNFPA labour-market profile reports the national arithmetic-average monthly employee wage and breakdowns by sex, location, sector and education, but no median. The Lao Statistics Bureau earnings indicator is likewise defined and presented as an arithmetic average. Therefore no national median amount in LAK can be stated from the current named sources.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A national maximum is not a statutory wage measure, and the reviewed Labour Force Survey profile and Lao Statistics Bureau earnings materials publish averages rather than a maximum observation, percentile ceiling or reliable upper wage-distribution bound. Therefore no national maximum salary amount in LAK can be stated.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory minimum wage for the minimum field; average monthly employee wage from the national 2022 Labour Force Survey for the average field
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly; minimum current in 2026, average based on 2022 survey data
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are labour-market figures, not an immigration income threshold. The survey average is dated and nearly equals the newer statutory minimum, illustrating inflation and wage-policy changes; it should not be treated as a current software-engineer salary. Focused checks established that the named sources publish arithmetic averages, not national median or maximum values.

cost_of_living_note.value: Living-cost pressure remains significant. The World Bank reported that inflation rose again to nearly 10% in April 2026 and that fuel prices in early June remained 38–40% above pre-shock levels, eroding household purchasing power.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official sources do not publish a single monthly expatriate cost-of-living budget, so none is inferred.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The tourist eVisa is limited to a 30-day tourist stay and is not a residence or remote-work status.
settlement_track.summary: No regular foreign-contract remote-work route exists. Settlement is theoretically possible only through materially different statuses such as a genuine Lao investment/business, sponsored employment, marriage or a discretionary expert category; the general path can require ten years to permanent-residence eligibility and another ten years of permanent residence before naturalization.
settlement_track.notes: Enterprise registration alone does not legalize residence or make a foreign contract a Lao immigration basis.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Official sources identify tourist, investor, technical-employee, student and other conventional categories, but no digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or ordinary freelance stay-permit category. A foreign contract is not a qualifying basis.

data.notes: Twenty-nine distinct directly relevant URLs were reviewed. The focused pass added five sources outside the previous set: the official Lao Social Security Law, the ILO's 2025 law review, Lao Statistics Bureau earnings metadata, OECD social-contribution analysis and a 2026 Laos payroll-compliance review. The social-security fields are materially resolved; national median and maximum salary values remain null because the named statistical sources publish arithmetic averages and subgroup means, not those statistics. Confidence remains medium because English-language Lao administrative guidance is fragmented and the absence of a remote-work route is harder to prove than a published program.

data.selection_summary: Latvia has a genuine independent self-employed-person temporary residence permit that can support a foreign-client software business without a Latvian employer or a stated local-client requirement. It is demanding: the applicant must present an auditor-approved business plan, startup funds and EUR 2,554 monthly subsistence, renew annually, conduct active Latvian economic activity providing economic benefit, and meet substantial Latvian tax-payment tests. Five years of continuous lawful residence can lead to EU long-term-resident/permanent status, followed by five years holding permanent residence before naturalisation. Latvia's separate remote-work D visa fits OECD-linked foreign remote work but is temporary for at most two consecutive one-year visas and is not itself a confirmed settlement route.

visa_application.title: Self-employed person
visa_application.notes: Official OCMA checklist for the selected self-employed residence-permit route. It links to the residence-permit form but is not a complete online application portal. First applications are normally filed through a competent Latvian mission abroad; filing location and whether an invitation is needed should be confirmed with OCMA before submission.

best_routes.route_name: Temporary residence permit as a self-employed person

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the currently displayed EUR 2,554 monthly subsistence requirement using 1 EUR = USD 1.1392. This is a maintenance threshold, not necessarily the revenue needed to satisfy the business plan and annual tax-payment tests.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 2,554 per month in personal subsistence, plus sufficient funds to commence the business-plan activities
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: OCMA's English checklist remains dated 22 April 2022 but was still live and displayed this amount when checked. Confirm the figure with OCMA before filing because subsistence amounts may be revised.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 2,554/month subsistence (about USD 2,909), plus business startup funds and renewal tax-payment tests
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 2,554/month; renewal generally requires at least EUR 9,960 Latvian state and municipal taxes in the preceding reporting year, or EUR 800/month during the first incomplete reporting year
income_requirement_display.notes: The business may require materially more revenue than the maintenance threshold because the permit depends on an auditor-approved business plan, active Latvian economic activity and documented Latvian tax payments.

income_proof_months.notes: The official initial checklist requires proof of subsistence and sufficient startup funds but does not publish a fixed number of historical income-statement months for this route.

key_requirements.requirement: Register/qualify as a self-employed person and request a Latvian residence permit; no Latvian employer or local-client contract is stated as a requirement.
Submit passport copy, residence-permit form, photograph, proof of subsistence, state-fee payment and, where applicable, a criminal-record statement.
Submit a business plan approved by a sworn auditor and evidence of sufficient personal funds to commence the planned activities; regulated activities also require the relevant licence or certificate.
Starting with the second year, submit an auditor-checked business plan and show that the previous plan was fulfilled.
For renewal, show at least EUR 9,960 in Latvian state and municipal tax payments in the preceding reporting year, or at least EUR 800 per month during the first incomplete reporting year.
The activity must remain active and provide economic benefit to Latvia; unpaid taxes, tax debt, inactivity or failure to provide economic benefit can cause refusal.

For EU long-term-resident status after five years, maintain continuous lawful residence, generally limiting absences to six consecutive months and ten months total, show stable taxed income for the preceding 12 months, have accommodation and demonstrate Latvian at A2 level.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Immigration Law Section 23(1)(4) limits the self-employed temporary residence permit to one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewable through repeated residence-permit applications while the business-plan, active-economic-activity, economic-benefit and tax-payment conditions remain satisfied
extension_rules.notes: Annual renewal is compliance-heavy. OCMA's published renewal threshold for a self-employed person is EUR 9,960 of preceding-year state and municipal taxes, or EUR 800 per month for the first incomplete reporting year.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The route directly grants a temporary residence permit for up to one year; no preliminary digital-nomad visa is required as the legal basis for this route.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Initial filing location and procedural requirements should be confirmed with the competent Latvian mission or OCMA.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After five years of continuous and lawful qualifying residence, the applicant may apply for EU long-term-resident status, which is documented by a permanent residence permit, subject to absence, stable taxed-income, accommodation and A2 Latvian requirements.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The EU long-term-resident page states the general five-year rule and excludes current students, but does not exclude self-employed permit holders. Maintaining uninterrupted qualifying self-employed permits and tax compliance is essential.

path_to_citizenship.value: A third-country national generally becomes eligible for naturalisation after holding permanent residence in Latvia for five years, passing Latvian-language and constitutional/history/culture tests, showing legal maintenance, meeting loyalty and security conditions, and resolving prior citizenship where required.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Combined with the usual five-year route to permanent/EU long-term-resident status, the screening timeline is about ten years plus processing.

best_routes.notes: This is the strongest match overlooked by the previous record. Foreign clients are not prohibited, but merely possessing a foreign contract is insufficient: the applicant must establish and substantiate Latvian self-employed economic activity, pay Latvian taxes and show economic benefit. A filing-level review of the business plan and proposed foreign-client structure is prudent.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the current Latvian-language OCMA threshold of EUR 4,538 using 1 EUR = USD 1.1392. The English page displayed EUR 4,213, so the fresher Latvian update governs this screening value.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 4,538 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Current Latvian OCMA page updated 16 June 2026 states 2.5 times the previous year's average gross wage, currently EUR 4,538. The English version lagged at EUR 4,213.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 4,538/month (about USD 5,169); six months of qualifying OECD employment or self-employed income
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 2.5 × Latvia's preceding-year average monthly gross wage, currently EUR 4,538
income_requirement_display.notes: This route is a national D visa rather than a residence permit and is rejected only for the citizenship-path selection; it remains useful for temporary remote living.

income_proof_months.notes: Employees must document at least six months with the OECD-state employer; self-employed applicants must document income from the preceding six months.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must not be a Russian citizen and must work remotely for an employer registered in another OECD member state or be self-employed and registered in an OECD member state.

Employee applicants need tax/social-insurance confirmation of current employment and an employer certificate confirming at least six months of prior employment, remuneration and remote-work permission.
Self-employed applicants need an OECD-state tax-administration document confirming the preceding six months of qualifying self-employed income.
Provide travel document, signed visa form, recent photograph, accommodation, health insurance valid in Latvia and Schengen with at least EUR 42,600 coverage, and state-fee payment.
The visa does not permit employment in Latvia.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: A national long-stay D visa, not a temporary residence permit.

extension_rules.value: One further long-stay remote-work visa of up to 1 year may be issued; after the repeat visa, another visa on the same ground is unavailable for the following 6 months.
extension_rules.notes: Maximum continuous sequence is ordinarily two one-year visas.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Immigration Law allows a visa holder to request a temporary residence permit before the visa expires, but the applicant must independently qualify under a separate residence-permit ground such as self-employment, employment or family.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The law does not create an automatic remote-worker residence permit or conversion entitlement.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A nomad can apply independently for Latvian self-employed residence and later EU long-term residence. The remote-work D visa itself is not a substitute for the successor residence permit.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: OCMA publishes both the self-employed permit and five-year long-term-resident route. An ordinary foreign-client professional can use the self-employed category if its business criteria are satisfied; an employee would need to restructure into eligible self-employment or obtain another qualifying basis. Nomad-visa time and a universal right to file the successor in-country were not established, so neither is assumed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No direct citizenship path exists from the D visa. A switch to a qualifying temporary residence basis, then permanent residence, is required.

rejected_routes.notes: A good temporary foreign-remote-work fit, including an optional 15% Latvian PIT rate for the first 365 days after becoming a Latvian tax resident, but not a qualifying settlement route by itself.

rejected_routes.route_name: Locally sponsored employment or EU Blue Card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Occupation-specific salary conditions were not needed for this rejection because the decisive issue is mandatory Latvian employer sponsorship.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not established for this profile; thresholds vary by employment category.

income_requirement_display.value: Local-employment remuneration rules apply; no single remote-worker threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because it requires a Latvian job/employer process.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable as a pre-existing foreign-income route.

key_requirements.requirement: The Latvian employer normally registers the vacancy, obtains the required State Employment Agency opinion and arranges an invitation before the foreigner applies.

initial_validity.value: Generally tied to the employment period; ordinary employment permits may be issued for up to 5 years and an EU Blue Card for up to 2 years

extension_rules.value: Requires continued qualifying Latvian employment and immigration compliance

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Can directly grant temporary residence based on Latvian employment
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not independently usable by the foreign-contract applicant.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially available under the general five-year continuous lawful-residence rules
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Separate from the selected profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially follows permanent residence and naturalisation requirements
path_to_citizenship.notes: Separate from the selected profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the selection rules exclude Latvian employer sponsorship, job offers and labour-market procedures.

summary.value: Admission to an accredited Latvian institution and a study contract can support a temporary residence permit without an employer. A foreign degree alone does not create a Latvian residence right. Current students cannot obtain EU long-term-resident status on the study basis; after switching to work or family residence, only half of the Latvian study period counts toward the five-year long-term-resident period.
summary.notes: Education residence is available but is not the selected route for an applicant who already has a degree and intends to keep ordinary foreign-client work.

tax_residency_rule.value: A natural person is Latvian tax resident if their declared residence is in Latvia, they stay in Latvia for at least 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending in a tax year, or they are a Latvian citizen employed abroad by the Latvian government. Treaty tie-breaker rules can alter the practical result.
tax_residency_rule.notes: For a person not resident in the preceding year, domestic law generally treats residence as beginning on the first arrival date in the qualifying tax year.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate: ordinary annual taxable/business income is taxed at 25.5% up to EUR 105,300 and 33% above that, with an additional 3% on annual income over EUR 200,000. This is not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: General self-employed MSSIC rate. In 2026, profit of at least EUR 780 triggers 31.07% on a chosen base of at least EUR 780 plus at least 10% pension contribution on the difference between actual profit and the chosen base; lower profit generally attracts 10% pension contributions. Coverage and treaty coordination may change the result.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universally fixed monthly payment applies. At the minimum EUR 780 contribution base, 31.07% is EUR 242.35 before any additional 10% pension contribution, but the actual base and foreign social-security coordination vary.

special_tax_regimes.value: Remote-work D-visa holders who transfer tax residence to Latvia may elect 15% PIT on qualifying OECD foreign-employment or OECD-registered self-employment income for 365 days from becoming resident, subject to treaty residence. This concession does not apply merely because someone holds the selected Latvian self-employed residence permit. Latvian self-employed persons may also assess the 25% micro-enterprise turnover-tax regime if eligible.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The digital-nomad 15% option is route-specific and temporary; it should not be projected over the settlement timeline.

taxes.caveats: Tax outcome depends on residence start, treaty tie-breakers, whether the applicant remains a foreign employee or registers Latvian economic activity, permanent-establishment exposure for a foreign employer, deductible expenses, VAT obligations and social-security coordination. Obtain Latvian advice before changing contract structure or using the self-employed permit.

taxation_system.value: Progressive worldwide-income-oriented resident taxation, with a temporary optional 15% rate for qualifying tax-resident remote-work D-visa holders and a separate 25% micro-enterprise turnover regime for eligible businesses.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Declared Latvian residence or at least 183 days in any 12-month period, subject to treaty rules; a newly qualifying resident can be treated as resident from first arrival.
taxation_system.income_scope: Latvian residents generally report taxable Latvian and foreign income, with treaty relief where applicable; non-residents are taxed on Latvian-source income defined by law.
taxation_system.special_regimes: 15% for qualifying remote-work D-visa income for the first 365 days of Latvian tax residence; 25% micro-enterprise tax on turnover for eligible registered taxpayers.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed MSSIC is generally 31.07% on a selected base not below EUR 780 when monthly profit reaches that amount, plus at least 10% pension contribution on excess profit; below EUR 780, generally 10% of actual profit. Foreign coverage/treaties can affect liability.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: 25.5% applies through EUR 105,300 annual taxable or business income; 33% applies above EUR 105,300; an additional 3% applies above EUR 200,000, producing a 36% top marginal screening rate. Effective tax is lower and depends on deductions and income level.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable/business income up to EUR 105,300
tax_brackets.applies_to: Annual taxable income and business-activity income
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at 1 EUR = USD 1.1392.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable/business income above EUR 105,300 up to EUR 200,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion above EUR 105,300 before the additional high-income rate begins
tax_brackets.notes: Threshold converted approximately; 33% is marginal, not the rate on all income.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Top portion where the 33% rate and additional 3% rate overlap
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate inferred by combining the published 33% bracket with the published additional 3% above EUR 200,000.

taxation_system.notes: Official 2026 tax-authority and statutory sources replace the previous record's obsolete 31.4% top-rate figure.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: A remote-work D-visa holder who becomes Latvian tax resident may elect 15% PIT on qualifying remote income for 365 days. Otherwise ordinary progressive Latvian PIT and the applicable social-security/treaty analysis apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: temporary digital-nomad special regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 15% elective PIT for 365 days after becoming Latvian tax resident; thereafter ordinary rates up to a 36% top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: The concession requires Latvian tax residence under domestic law and the applicable treaty; ordinary residence indicators include declared residence or at least 183 days in a 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The 15% election covers qualifying income from remote work for an employer registered in another OECD member state or OECD-state-registered economic activity. Treaty residence in the other contracting state prevents use of the election.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Elective 15% PIT for 365 days from the date Latvian tax residence begins.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No universal D-visa social-security exemption was confirmed. Liability depends on employee/self-employed classification, home-country coverage and EU or bilateral coordination; foreign-employer registration or Latvian self-registration may be required.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed route-wide amount; ordinary MSSIC rules or foreign-coverage coordination may apply.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: EUR 90 for a national long-stay D visa; EUR 180 for a late in-country application submitted less than three working days before lawful stay expires.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No digital-nomad-specific municipal fee or transaction tax was found. Health insurance with at least EUR 42,600 coverage is mandatory, but the premium is market-priced.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa fees are official as of 18 March 2026. Insurance cost depends on provider and coverage.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay below 183 days may still create Latvian tax residence through declared residence or other facts, and work physically performed in Latvia can have source/treaty implications. Do not assume zero Latvian tax solely from day count.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If the D-visa holder becomes treaty-resident in Latvia, qualifying remote income may use the 15% election for 365 days; ordinary progressive PIT applies afterward.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Switching to the selected Latvian self-employed residence permit means operating and documenting Latvian economic activity, normally using ordinary business-income PIT/MSSIC rules or an eligible micro-enterprise regime rather than the D-visa-only 15% concession.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The special 15% rule is officially confirmed, correcting the previous record's statement that no special digital-nomad regime was confirmed.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The selected self-employed application is directly for a temporary residence permit; no preceding residence period is prescribed.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: EU long-term-resident status requires five years of continuous lawful residence and results in a permanent residence permit, subject to absence, income, accommodation and A2-language conditions.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: A third-country national generally must independently live in Latvia with permanent residence for the most recent five years before naturalisation.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Screening total: approximately five years of qualifying temporary residence to permanent/EU long-term-resident status, then five years holding permanent residence. Application processing is additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: OCMA states a typical 6–12 month naturalisation process and a legal service deadline within one year. Nine months is the midpoint used for dashboard screening, not a guarantee.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous qualifying residence and annual self-employed permits; comply with business-plan and tax-payment obligations; for EU long-term residence, satisfy absence limits, stable taxed income, accommodation and A2 Latvian; for citizenship, hold permanent residence for five years, demonstrate Latvian, constitutional/history/culture and anthem knowledge, legal maintenance and loyalty, have no disqualifying security/criminal/tax issues, and renounce prior citizenship when Latvian dual-citizenship rules require it.
key_conditions.notes: The ten-year estimate assumes uninterrupted approvals and that each self-employed permit year qualifies for EU long-term residence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A spouse of a Latvian citizen ordinarily receives a one-year temporary permit on first filing, a four-year temporary permit on second filing and permanent residence on the third filing—approximately five years. Marriage does not create a separate accelerated naturalisation rule.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Latvian citizen can immediately support the family-reunification residence-permit sequence. Marriage to another migrant does not independently accelerate citizenship, though dependent residence may be available through the principal permit.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Citizenship of either spouse does not automatically change because of marriage.

requirements_and_risks.value: Family-reunification applicants must prove the relationship, subsistence and other residence-permit requirements. The spouses must live together in a monogamous marriage and maintain a common household. A marriage that does not exist in fact can cause refusal or cancellation; divorce before permanent residence normally ends the route, subject to limited protections involving a Latvian-citizen/non-citizen child.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates access to permanent residence compared with repeatedly proving a commercial basis, but not the five-permanent-residence-year naturalisation condition.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Latvia primarily grants citizenship by descent. Birth in Latvia is not enough for ordinary foreign parents; special recognition rules protect children of stateless persons or Latvian non-citizens under residence and registration conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Latvia to two ordinary foreign citizens does not automatically become Latvian. Conditional recognition exists when both parents are stateless persons or Latvian non-citizens and the statutory residence/registration conditions are met.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Anti-statelessness and Latvian non-citizen provisions should not be generalized to all migrants.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child belongs to Latvian citizenship when one or both parents are Latvian citizens, subject to the Citizenship Law's registration and dual-citizenship provisions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This rule applies irrespective of whether the Latvian citizen is the mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically naturalise a migrant parent. Family and custody circumstances can support or preserve residence—for example, specified divorce/death situations involving a minor Latvian citizen—but the parent must use the applicable residence procedure.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A foreign parent of a Latvian citizen is not automatically entitled to citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic citizenship merely because his child is Latvian. If he is the spouse of a Latvian citizen, he may use the spouse residence route; limited permanent-residence protection can arise after divorce or the spouse's death when a minor Latvian-citizen child is involved and statutory conditions are met.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity, custody, genuine family life and the precise Immigration Law ground must be documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed by Passport Index on 15 August 2026. Latvia's OCMA separately reported rank 4 earlier in 2026; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Pure visa-free count as separated by Passport Index, not the broader Henley-style visa-free-or-arrival score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index advance-visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index separates 44 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations; combined here because the schema provides a combined field. Its mobility score is 172.

passport.notes: Passport data change frequently. The Latvian Foreign Ministry also maintains a destination-by-destination visa-free list, updated 25 May 2026; travelers should verify each destination before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Good for remote professional life in Riga and the technology sector, but Latvian is necessary for many official procedures and long-term integration. EF's 2025 index ranked Latvia 16th globally with a high-proficiency score of 598; Riga scored 611.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF is a reputable but self-selected private proficiency index, so it supports practicality rather than a legal conclusion. Naturalisation requires Latvian.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian remains practically useful with part of the population: official survey results say 34.6% of adults aged 18–69 used Russian for home communication in 2022. Russian and Ukrainian are legally foreign languages, not official languages; neither should be relied on for government processes or citizenship requirements. Ukrainian is much less widely used, though community and refugee-support services exist.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Language use is socially and politically sensitive. Use Latvian for official interaction and English where available.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 1,815 gross monthly average earnings in 2025 at 1 EUR = USD 1.1392.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 1,462 gross monthly median earnings in 2025.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory EUR 780 gross monthly minimum wage effective 1 January 2026; it is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2025 full-time-equivalent gross monthly average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2025 full-time-equivalent gross monthly median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary is published. The official release gives sector averages, not a maximum wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum for normal full-time work from 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National 2025 average in full-time units; average net earnings were EUR 1,346.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: National 2025 median in full-time units; net median was EUR 1,117.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No official national maximum wage was established. The highest sector average reported was EUR 3,077 in finance and insurance, but that is not a maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly gross wages and salaries in full-time units; minimum is statutory
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 average/median; 2026 statutory minimum
average_citizen_salary.notes: Official statistics replace the previous record's salary nulls. USD amounts are approximate dashboard conversions, not immigration thresholds.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No current official, nationally representative cost-of-living basket suitable for a concise cross-country comparison was established in the inspected sources; salary and minimum-wage context is provided instead of an unsupported estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The strong classification applies to the self-employed residence permit, not to Latvia's remote-work D visa. The D visa remains temporary and requires switching to a separately qualifying residence ground.
settlement_track.summary: The independent self-employed permit is a qualifying temporary residence route, not merely a nomad visa. With annual renewals, real Latvian economic activity, tax compliance and continuous residence, it can lead after five years to EU long-term-resident/permanent status and after another five permanent-residence years to naturalisation.
settlement_track.notes: The route is credible but substantially more demanding than passive foreign remote work because OCMA can test the business plan, economic benefit and tax payments.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No Latvian employer or local-client contract is required, so a software engineer may serve foreign clients through Latvian self-employment. The applicant must nevertheless convert the arrangement into genuine Latvian economic activity, use an auditor-approved business plan, pay Latvian taxes and demonstrate economic benefit; a bare foreign contract with no Latvian registration or substance is insufficient.

data.notes: This audit materially improves the previous record by identifying the independent self-employed temporary residence permit and its confirmed settlement track, updating the remote-work threshold to EUR 4,538, confirming the D-visa 15% tax concession, replacing obsolete PIT rates, and filling official salary, passport and family/citizenship fields. Filing-level confirmation is still advisable because the self-employed checklist's subsistence page is older and OCMA has discretion when assessing economic benefit.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Latvian self-employed temporary residence permit, followed by EU long-term residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A nomad can apply independently for Latvian self-employed residence and later EU long-term residence. The remote-work D visa itself is not a substitute for the successor residence permit.
requirements: Register and qualify as self-employed, submit an auditor-checked business plan and demonstrate resources for the activity.
Maintain the approved business and meet repeated-permit requirements.
Meet five years of qualifying residence, stable lawful means and Latvian A2 for EU long-term status.
reviewed_route_names: Long-stay visa for remote work
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: OCMA publishes both the self-employed permit and five-year long-term-resident route. An ordinary foreign-client professional can use the self-employed category if its business criteria are satisfied; an employee would need to restructure into eligible self-employment or obtain another qualifying basis. Nomad-visa time and a universal right to file the successor in-country were not established, so neither is assumed.

data.selection_summary: Lebanon does not currently offer a digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary independent freelance residence route. Its independently obtainable bank-income residence expressly requires a notarized undertaking not to work, while work-based residence requires a Lebanese work permit and normally an employer or other qualifying local basis. The cash-guarantee permit is capital-intensive and also prohibits work, so none fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work or provides a confirmed route-specific citizenship track.

visa_application.title: Lebanese General Security
visa_application.notes: General Security is the official residence and immigration authority. Applications for the relevant residence categories are made using the prescribed form at an authorized General Security office; no dedicated remote-worker application channel exists.

rejected_routes.route_name: Annual residence based on monthly income or bank balance

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of LBP 50,000,000 at the Banque du Liban USD/LBP rate of 89,500. The alternative is a qualifying blocked balance rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: LBP 50,000,000 monthly income, or LBP 1,000,000,000 in a blocked account established at least three months earlier
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A comparable amount in foreign currency is accepted. A joint blocked account of at least LBP 2,000,000,000 is listed for accompanying family.

income_requirement_display.value: About USD 559/month, or LBP 1 billion blocked balance
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: LBP 50,000,000 monthly income or LBP 1,000,000,000 blocked for at least three months
income_requirement_display.notes: This financial residence is not a work authorization: the applicant must undertake not to work.

income_proof_months.notes: The three-month condition expressly applies to the blocked-account evidence. The authority does not state a separate look-back period for recurring monthly-income statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Application form, passport valid for at least one year, and three photographs.
Notarized undertaking that the applicant will not work.
Qualifying bank statement or monthly-income evidence.
Lease or title deed for accommodation.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year
initial_validity.notes: Validity follows passport validity where more than six months remain, capped at one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewal appears possible through the ordinary residence-renewal process, but the current page does not publish an automatic renewal entitlement or maximum number of renewals.
extension_rules.notes: Continued compliance and fresh General Security review should be expected.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct annual residence after approval by General Security.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a no-work financial residence, not a remote-work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion from this annual financial residence to a permanent permit is confirmed by the current official pages.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Lebanon separately lists a capital-backed three-year permit under its 'permanent residence' heading.

path_to_citizenship.value: Lebanese nationality law separately permits discretionary naturalization after five consecutive years of residence, but no official source confirms that this no-work permit creates an assured or routine citizenship track.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires a Head-of-State decree and is not automatic after five years.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the mandatory undertaking not to work is incompatible with an ordinary software engineer performing foreign-contract remote work from Lebanon.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no monthly-income threshold; the route instead requires a very large cash guarantee.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No monthly threshold; LBP 4,500,000,000 cash guarantee
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The General Security page describes a cash deposit or qualifying fresh bank cheque lodged with the Ministry of Finance.

income_requirement_display.value: LBP 4.5 billion cash guarantee (about USD 50,279), not monthly income
income_requirement_display.notes: The official category is headed 'permanent residence – three years,' but the document itself has a three-year validity period and prohibits work for applicants under 64.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period applies; a cash guarantee is required.

LBP 4.5 billion cash guarantee deposited with the Ministry of Finance.
Lease or property title.
Applicants under 64 must undertake not to work.

initial_validity.value: Three years
initial_validity.notes: The permit is officially listed under permanent residence but is issued for three years, or shorter if constrained by passport validity.

extension_rules.value: No automatic renewal or indefinite-status rule was located on the current official page.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal and continued treatment as 'permanent residence' require confirmation from General Security.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct three-year legal residence after approval and deposit of the guarantee.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The authority labels the category permanent residence, although the issued document is limited to three years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This field reflects Lebanese administrative terminology; it should not be assumed equivalent to an indefinite permanent-resident status.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after five consecutive years of residence, but approval is discretionary and no route-specific entitlement is confirmed.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial tied capital and expressly prohibits work for applicants under 64; it therefore cannot support the applicant's ordinary remote-work activity.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No generally applicable salary threshold was established from the reviewed official material.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The route depends on the relevant work-permit category and employment arrangement rather than a remote-worker income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No universal published income threshold found; Lebanese work permit and qualifying employment basis required
income_requirement_display.notes: Not an independent foreign-contract route.

income_proof_months.notes: No general income-history period was confirmed.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreigners carrying on work or a profession in Lebanon must obtain authorization from the Ministry of Labour.
Work-permit residence documentation normally includes the employer's identity or commercial registration and an employment contract.
Two- or three-year 'permanent residence' categories are limited to specified first- or second-class work permits.

initial_validity.value: Depends on work permit; official residence examples include annual, two-year, and three-year documents

extension_rules.value: Continuation depends on a valid work permit and qualifying employment basis.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Work permit followed by the corresponding work residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Specified two- and three-year work-permit holders can receive permits listed under General Security's permanent-residence category.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not remove the local employment/work-permit dependency.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only the separate discretionary five-consecutive-year naturalization rule was found.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No employer-route citizenship entitlement is established.
