summary.value: General Security lists annual residence for enrolled religious students, based on institutional confirmation, accommodation/financial evidence, prior authorization where applicable, and a no-work condition. No independent residence route based merely on possessing a software-engineering degree or professional qualification was found.
summary.notes: Enrollment-based student residence is not a qualification-based settlement route and does not fit the applicant's current remote-work purpose.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Lebanese tax resident if they have a place of business in Lebanon, have a permanent home available as their or their family's usual residence, or spend more than 183 days in Lebanon during any consecutive 12 months, excluding qualifying transit and medical-treatment days.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence may therefore begin before day 184 if the business-place or permanent-home test is met.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Wages and salaries and individual business profits are progressive; the actual result depends on characterization, deductions, brackets, residence, and where services are performed.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Current employee medical-scheme contribution rate, capped at the applicable monthly base. Employer contributions are separately listed as 8% sickness/maternity, 6% family benefits, and 5% end-of-service. Applicability to a foreign worker can depend on registration, employment structure, and reciprocity; no digital-nomad category exists.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly digital-nomad or self-employed payment exists because there is no such immigration category. Employee NSSF contributions are percentage-based and capped; business tax and possible VAT/stamp duties depend on activity.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, remote-worker, non-dom, or inbound-professional tax regime was found. Lebanese salary taxation applies territorially where the beneficiary is resident, the services are performed in Lebanon, the services benefit a Lebanese company, or funding comes from Lebanon.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign funding alone does not establish exemption.

taxes.caveats: The immigration rules do not authorize ordinary remote work under the financial-residence categories. If a person nevertheless performs services from Lebanon, tax exposure can arise even with a foreign payer. Professional advice is necessary regarding salary versus business-profit treatment, permanent establishment, foreign-tax credits or treaties, NSSF eligibility, VAT, and currency conversion.

taxation_system.value: Lebanon uses a mixed territorial and progressive system. Employment income and individual business profits can reach a 25% top marginal rate. Foreign-funded salary can be taxable where the beneficiary is resident or services are performed in Lebanon.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Place of business, permanent home available to the individual/family, or more than 183 days in any consecutive 12 months.
taxation_system.income_scope: Territorial nexus is broad for salary: residence, performance of services in Lebanon, benefit to a Lebanese company, or Lebanese funding can trigger tax. Individual business profits are taxed progressively.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or ordinary inbound-remote-worker exemption found.
taxation_system.social_security: For registered employment, the employee medical contribution is 3% up to the applicable ceiling. Employer rates are 8% for sickness/maternity, 6% for family benefits, and 5% for end-of-service; foreign-worker coverage requires case-specific review.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: PwC's July 2026 summary reports wage and salary rates from 2% to 25% and individual business-profit rates from 4% to 25%. The Ministry of Finance pages still display older nominal brackets, while later budget laws substantially increased bracket amounts; therefore the current PwC summary is used for screening and the precise filing-year table must be confirmed.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Lowest payroll-tax rate; current filing-year threshold must be checked against the applicable budget law
tax_brackets.notes: PwC confirms a 2%-25% progressive payroll range but the reviewed current page does not reproduce every 2026 bracket boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Top payroll bracket; PwC reports the payroll schedule extending through annual brackets introduced at up to LBP 675,000,000 under the 2022 Budget Law
tax_brackets.notes: The stated LBP 675 million figure comes from the budget-law schedule summarized by PwC; filing-year inflation adjustments should be verified.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Lowest individual business-profit rate; 2024 schedule starts with substantially increased LBP brackets
tax_brackets.applies_to: Sole proprietorship and individual professional/business profit
tax_brackets.notes: Current summary confirms the 4%-25% range.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Top of the current individual business-profit schedule; PwC states the 2024 annual schedule extends to LBP 13.5 billion
tax_brackets.applies_to: Sole proprietorship and individual professional/business profit
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official Ministry of Finance pages establish the tax categories but retain some older nominal bracket displays. The July 2026 PwC summary was used to capture later budget-law changes; exact 2026 filing brackets should be verified with a Lebanese tax adviser.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Lebanon has no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. A Lebanese tax resident working for a foreign payer may nevertheless owe progressive salary tax, and a self-employed individual may fall under progressive business-profit taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; likely employment income or individual professional/business profit depending on facts
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 2%-25% progressive employment tax or 4%-25% progressive individual business-profit tax; 25% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Place of business, permanent home, or more than 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-funded salary is not automatically exempt. Tax can arise where the beneficiary is Lebanese resident or the work is performed in Lebanon.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Registered employees generally bear a 3% medical contribution up to the cap; employer contributions are additional. Coverage of foreign employees and foreign-employer arrangements requires individual analysis.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed-payment system
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based if NSSF-covered; no fixed self-employed amount confirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Residence fees vary by category. The annual financial-residence page did not render a reliable fee amount; the three-year cash-guarantee route lists a LBP 54,000,000 residence fee plus the LBP 4.5 billion guarantee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Potential 11% VAT, registration obligations above the applicable turnover threshold, and stamp duties can apply to an actual Lebanese business activity or contracts.
fixed_payments.notes: These are not a substitute for work authorization.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 184 days does not guarantee non-residence if the person has a Lebanese place of business or permanent home. Work performed physically in Lebanon can also create Lebanese-source salary exposure.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident foreign-payroll worker may need a Lebanese tax number, returns, and progressive payroll tax even though the employer is abroad; the Ministry of Finance specifically addresses resident employees of non-resident employers.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Individual professional or business profit can be taxed progressively at 4%-25%; VAT registration may arise when applicable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold. Immigration permission to perform the activity remains a separate unresolved barrier.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax analysis is hypothetical because no qualifying remote-worker immigration route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work exists. Financial residence can be obtained directly but prohibits work.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No conversion from the annual no-work financial residence to a qualifying permanent status was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Lebanese nationality law uses a five-consecutive-year residence criterion rather than a clearly defined number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five consecutive years is the statutory threshold to request discretionary naturalization, not a guaranteed route-specific timeline. It cannot make the currently non-fitting remote-work options eligible.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable official typical processing time for ordinary discretionary naturalization was found after reviewing the nationality law and civil-status procedures.

key_conditions.value: A foreigner may request naturalization after five consecutive years' residence, but citizenship is granted only by Head-of-State decree. No automatic entitlement, routine processing timetable, or confirmed treatment of the no-work financial residence as a remote-worker citizenship track was found.
key_conditions.notes: The law does not turn mere satisfaction of the residence period into citizenship.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Rules are gender-specific. A foreign man married to a Lebanese woman may request discretionary naturalization after one consecutive year of Lebanese residence from the marriage date. A foreign wife of a Lebanese man may request citizenship one year after the marriage is registered.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can qualify once the relevant one-year period and registration/residence conditions are satisfied. General Security also lists courtesy residence for the foreign husband of a Lebanese woman where the marriage is at least one year old and for a non-working foreign wife of a Lebanese man.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not create an ordinary remote-work authorization.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally valid and registered, with civil-status and identity evidence. The foreign husband's naturalization remains discretionary and requires consecutive residence; the foreign wife's route is legally more direct. Genuine-marriage verification and accurate civil registration are essential, and sham marriage can lead to refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Lebanese nationality rules remain gender-discriminatory.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Lebanon primarily follows paternal jus sanguinis. Birth in Lebanon confers citizenship only in narrow cases, principally where the child acquires no foreign nationality by descent or where parents are unknown or of unknown nationality.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: An ordinary child born in Lebanon to two foreign migrant parents does not automatically become Lebanese. Narrow anti-statelessness and unknown-parent rules may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The result can change if the child acquires no foreign nationality at birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If the local parent is the Lebanese father, the child is generally Lebanese from birth regardless of birthplace. A Lebanese mother generally cannot transmit nationality to a child on equal terms where the father is foreign, subject to narrow rules concerning filiation outside marriage.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because the answer depends on which parent is Lebanese, the generic boolean is left null rather than implying gender-neutral transmission.

parent_benefit_summary.value: General Security lists annual residence for the mother or father of a Lebanese citizen, subject to proof of family relationship, financial support by the Lebanese citizen, and a no-work undertaking for applicants under 64. This is a residence benefit, not automatic permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A minor child's ability to act as financial sponsor may require case-specific confirmation.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically obtain citizenship through a child. If the mother is Lebanese and the father foreign, the child ordinarily does not automatically become Lebanese through the mother; where the child is otherwise a Lebanese citizen, the father may seek the parent-of-citizen annual residence category but must not assume a citizenship shortcut.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Family-residence eligibility should be confirmed directly with General Security.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on the live Lebanon dashboard on 2026-08-15; rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined display: 35 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 55. Its methodology and category totals differ from Henley's combined visa-free/visa-on-arrival measure.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in Beirut and some professional settings, but nationwide proficiency is uneven. EF EPI 2025 gives Lebanon a score of 477 and rank 78, below the reported global average; Beirut scores 523 and Mount Lebanon 536, while several other regions score materially lower. Remote work also requires contingency planning for electricity and connectivity interruptions.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF is a non-governmental proficiency index based on participating test takers, so it is indicative rather than a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No reliable evidence was found that Russian or Ukrainian is broadly usable for government procedures or everyday administration. Arabic is the official language; English or French is generally more practical in internationally oriented settings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The negative practicality assessment is cautious because no current national proficiency dataset for Russian or Ukrainian was located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: January 2022 survey-time conversion of LBP 2,284,100 at the survey's market rate of LBP 25,000 per USD. This is stale and should not be interpreted as a current 2026 wage because Lebanon subsequently experienced major inflation, exchange-rate, and wage adjustments.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current, reliable national median monthly wage was established. Regional income medians and non-comparable salary websites were not substituted for a national employee median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory private-sector minimum wage of LBP 28,000,000 at USD 1 = LBP 89,500. This is a legal minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Survey-time USD equivalent for the January 2022 national employee average. It is retained only because no fresher comparable national average was found.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A current national median salary was not published in the reviewed official sources.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary or upper wage-distribution boundary was published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory private-sector minimum effective from August 2025.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average earnings of employees at their main job in the January 2022 follow-up Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not established from the reviewed national survey.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published as a meaningful national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum for the minimum field; average monthly earnings at employees' main job for the average field
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage: effective August 2025; average earnings: January 2022
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum wage is current, but the only comparable official national average found is from January 2022. Currency collapse, dollarized pay, informal employment, and rapid inflation make direct comparison hazardous.

cost_of_living_note.value: Lebanon's wage and cost environment remains distorted by the currency crisis and partial dollarization. CAS reports average inflation of 14.58% in 2025; current household costs vary sharply by location, currency of payment, electricity arrangements, and imported-goods exposure.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No single official current monthly cost-of-living budget was found.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The independently obtainable bank-income residence is a no-work status and cannot be treated as a digital-nomad visa. Performing remote work would conflict with the notarized non-work undertaking.
settlement_track.summary: No residence category currently permits an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker to live and work independently in Lebanon. The general five-year discretionary naturalization rule does not cure the absence of a lawful qualifying work/residence route for this profile.
settlement_track.notes: Financial, investment, family, student, and employer/work-permit categories were separately reviewed. None provides the required ordinary independent remote-work fit.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker visa exists; financial residence prohibits work, and lawful work generally requires a Ministry of Labour permit and qualifying employment or professional basis.

data.notes: The negative route conclusion is supported by current official General Security residence categories and the statutory work-permit requirement. Tax, salary, and nationality details include clearly identified secondary-source or staleness caveats where official current data were incomplete.

data.selection_summary: Lesotho does not currently publish a digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or independently accessible self-employment residence route for a software engineer working only for a foreign client. The closest business residence category requires a Lesotho business structure, trader’s licence, tax compliance and a work permit; the 2024 Labour Act makes the prospective employer submit a foreign worker’s application and requires a labor-market check. Visitor/eVisa status is not a residence or work route. Lesotho is therefore not valid for this selection, although independently obtained lawful residence through a genuinely qualifying business, family, study or sponsored-work basis may support a separate citizenship application after five continuous years.

visa_application.title: Ministry of Home Affairs eServices
visa_application.notes: The official eServices page links to the residence-permit application system. It says the eVisa system is suspended and directs visa applications to VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls. No dedicated remote-worker application was found. The linked permit portal contains two-year and indefinite permit categories but displays visibly stale operational notices, so applicants should verify the filing channel with Home Affairs before paying or submitting documents.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum personal monthly income threshold is published. A six-month bank statement is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum amount is stated for the business residence category.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; six months of bank statements required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an entrepreneur/business category, not a foreign-remote-worker income route.

income_proof_months.notes: The residence-permit service charter requires a six-month bank statement.

key_requirements.requirement: Lesotho trader’s licence and genuine local business structure
Certified work permit, personal and company tax-clearance certificates
Personal and company application letters, employment contract and company memorandum where applicable
Medical form, police clearance, passport and certified educational records
Under the Labour Act, a prospective employer submits a non-citizen work-permit application and the authority must certify that no qualified citizen is available

initial_validity.value: Two years
initial_validity.notes: Home Affairs lists a two-year residence permit. The service charter states a four-week target and an M3,000 fee for the business category.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is possible; an indefinite permit category also exists, but no automatic conversion rule or qualifying period is published on the reviewed pages.
extension_rules.notes: The business-category service charter lists M25,000 for an indefinite permit. Grant remains discretionary and subject to scrutiny; this is not evidence of automatic permanent residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying local business applicant may apply directly for the two-year business residence permit after satisfying work-permit, licensing, tax and company requirements.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Ordinary work solely for a foreign client does not satisfy the published business package by itself.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: An indefinite permit category is available, but the reviewed official material does not establish an automatic time-based transition from the business permit.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Manual Home Affairs verification is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: General citizenship service guidance permits an application after at least five continuous years in Lesotho with a valid residence permit, but business applicants must also provide extensive business, work-permit and tax evidence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make the business permit suitable for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires genuine Lesotho business substance, licensing and a work-permit process tied to a prospective employer/company and labor-market availability. Creating a shell company merely to legalize foreign-client remote work is not supported by the official rules.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign-worker work permit and employment residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold was published in the reviewed current law.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Compensation is governed by the employment contract and applicable wage rules, not a published immigration threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published immigration income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: A local job and prospective-employer filing are required.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed employee categories generally require a six-month bank statement.

key_requirements.requirement: Prospective employer submits the work-permit application
Authority must certify that no qualified Lesotho citizen is available in the labor-market database
Local employment contract and employer/application letters
Work permit, tax clearance, police clearance, medical form, passport and qualifications

initial_validity.value: Residence permits are generally issued for two years for the listed employment categories; work-permit duration is set by regulations.

extension_rules.value: Work permits may be renewed or cancelled by the Director, National Employment Service; residence renewal remains a separate immigration process pending full work-visa harmonization.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Local sponsored employment can support a work permit and a corresponding residence-permit application.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: An indefinite residence category exists, but no automatic sponsored-worker conversion timeline was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Five continuous years with a valid residence permit can support a general citizenship application, subject to category-specific evidence and discretion.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local prospective employer, sponsorship and labor-market certification are mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly threshold is published; sufficient sponsorship for tuition and the study duration is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed amount is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient study funding; no fixed amount published
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Tuition and living sponsorship for the study duration

income_proof_months.notes: The study guidance requires proof of sponsorship but does not state a fixed bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Admission letter and applicant’s application letter
Proof of tuition fees and sufficient sponsorship
Passport, prior educational certificates, medical documentation and police clearance where applicable

initial_validity.value: Up to four years
initial_validity.notes: Home Affairs lists a four-year study permit.

extension_rules.value: The permit portal requests the previous permit for renewal applications but does not publish a maximum cumulative study-permit period or detailed renewal criteria.
extension_rules.notes: Confirm continuation requirements with Home Affairs and the educational institution.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Admission to a recognized institution can support a study permit allowing residence for study.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct or automatic transition from study status to an indefinite permit is established by the reviewed current sources.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Aliens Control Act makes indefinite and temporary permits discretionary and supplies no study-specific conversion entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: The 1971 Citizenship Order’s general naturalisation rule requires five years of lawful sojourn and does not expressly exclude study status. However, the current Government citizenship service requires five continuous years with a valid residence permit, while Home Affairs separately describes the four-year instrument as a study permit. The reviewed current sources therefore do not establish that time held only under a study permit satisfies the current residence-permit requirement; obtain a written determination from Home Affairs before relying on study years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is a source-defined ambiguity, not a claim that study time is categorically excluded: the older statute uses broad lawful-sojourn wording, but the current administrative rule uses residence-permit wording and does not state whether a study permit qualifies.

rejected_routes.notes: Available without a local employer but rejected because it requires genuine study and is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is a visitor-funds requirement, not a remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: M10,000 bank balance for the reviewed visitor application category
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The entry-visa service charter requests a three-month bank statement showing M10,000.

income_requirement_display.value: M10,000 visitor funds; not a monthly-income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status does not authorize a settlement-oriented remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: Three months of applicant or sponsor bank statements are requested.

key_requirements.requirement: Application or invitation letter, passport, return ticket, medical report and insurance
Visitor funds shown by applicant or sponsor
The official eVisa application system is currently marked suspended; email filing is directed by Home Affairs

initial_validity.value: Single-entry visa: three months; multiple-entry visa: six months. Visa-free periods vary from one to three months by nationality.
initial_validity.notes: Visa validity is not necessarily the same as authorized stay on every entry.

extension_rules.value: No visitor-to-business/self-employment legalization rule is published by the reviewed immigration sources.
extension_rules.notes: The Aliens Control Act permits discretionary in-country temporary or indefinite permit applications in some circumstances, but this is not a published conversion entitlement or a remote-worker category.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None directly. A separate qualifying residence category and supporting basis would be required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None directly; an indefinite permit is a separate discretionary status rather than a visitor benefit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time is not established as satisfying the current citizenship service’s requirement for five continuous years with a valid residence permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status is temporary entry, not permission for ordinary foreign-contract remote work or a qualifying residence path.

summary.value: A study permit is available following admission and proof of sponsorship. It can provide temporary residence for genuine study, but no independent degree-based skilled-migration route or direct permanent residence was found. Whether study-permit-only time satisfies the current citizenship service’s five-year valid-residence-permit requirement is not stated and requires written Home Affairs confirmation.
summary.notes: The applicant’s existing software-engineering degree does not independently qualify them for residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident for the entire assessment year if they have a normal place of abode in Lesotho and are present for part of the year, are present for more than 182 days in any consecutive 12-month period overlapping the assessment year, are an overseas Lesotho official, or are otherwise resident under the Act.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can arise through the abode test before day 183; treaty residence may alter the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for resident individuals from 1 April 2026, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No universal employee/self-employed contribution percentage was established. OECD Revenue Statistics records Lesotho social-security contributions as null under its classification, but that is not conclusive proof that no occupational pension, insurance or sector-specific payment can apply.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No digital-nomad or universal self-employed monthly state payment is published. Business licensing, tax registration, insurance and immigration fees depend on the actual structure and are not reducible to a confirmed monthly USD amount.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remittance-basis or special foreign-remote-worker tax regime was found. Ordinary resident-individual rules expressly cover sole traders.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Specific expatriate exemptions and foreign-tax credits can depend on income character and contract facts; professional advice is required.

taxes.caveats: A foreign contract does not prevent Lesotho taxation. Residents generally include income from all geographical sources, while non-residents include only Lesotho-source income; services physically performed in Lesotho may also be Lesotho-source. Classification as employment, sole-trader business or a technical-services contract, available deductions, foreign-tax credits and treaty residence can materially change liability.

taxation_system.value: Progressive residence-based personal income tax. From 1 April 2026, resident individuals, including sole traders, pay 20% on the first M77,760 annual chargeable income and 30% above that amount, less a non-refundable personal credit of M12,240 per year.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Normal-place-of-abode plus presence, more than 182 days in a consecutive 12-month period, or other statutory residence tests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: income from all geographical sources. Non-residents: Lesotho-source income only.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: No general percentage confirmed. OECD’s comparable revenue data classifies Lesotho social-security contributions as null, which should not be treated as a filing-level exemption from every pension, insurance or sector obligation.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal rate. The personal credit means the effective zero-tax point is about M5,100 per month for an otherwise straightforward resident individual, while chargeable income up to M6,480 per month is calculated at 20% before the M1,020 monthly credit.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First M6,480 per month / M77,760 per year
tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident-individual chargeable income, including sole traders
tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses the World Bank’s 2024 average official exchange rate of 18.33 LSL per USD; it is illustrative, not a 2026 filing conversion rate. The monthly M1,020 personal credit applies after calculating tax.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Amount above M6,480 per month / M77,760 per year
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket, not a flat rate on total income.

taxation_system.notes: Current 2026/27 thresholds come from Revenue Services Lesotho. The underlying residence and worldwide-income rules come from the Income Tax Order hosted by LesLII.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Lesotho has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. If a person nevertheless becomes tax resident while lawfully present under another status, ordinary progressive resident-individual taxation can reach 30% on worldwide income.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary resident/non-resident rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 20% then 30% top marginal rate, less the resident personal credit
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Normal place of abode plus presence, more than 182 days in a consecutive 12-month period, or another statutory residence basis.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident gross income includes all geographical sources; non-resident gross income includes only Lesotho-source income. Work physically performed in Lesotho may itself be locally sourced.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No universal digital-nomad/self-employed contribution rate was established. Employment, pension, insurance and withholding treatment depends on the contract and registration structure.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed-payment regime exists; business and immigration fees are route-specific.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal monthly amount confirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The business residence service charter lists M3,000 for a two-year permit and M25,000 for an indefinite permit; these are application/status fees, not monthly taxes.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Trader’s-licence, company registration, VAT and other business obligations may arise for a genuine Lesotho business, but no universal monthly amount for the profile was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Do not infer permission to work from tax registration.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short-term visitor may remain non-resident under the day-count test, but the normal-place-of-abode test and Lesotho-source services rule still require review. Visitor status does not itself authorize work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide employment or business income generally enters the resident tax base and is screened at the 20%/30% brackets, subject to deductions, credits, exemptions and treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A resident sole trader uses the resident-individual brackets. Tax registration or a trader’s licence does not replace the immigration residence and work-permit requirements.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is high on general tax law but lower for a hypothetical remote worker because no qualifying immigration route exists and contract classification is fact-specific.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists, so there is no route-specific time to temporary residence. Other categories can issue a two-year permit, generally with a four-week published service target.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: An indefinite permit exists, but no automatic conversion period for a qualifying remote-work route is published; the Aliens Control Act makes issuance discretionary.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The published rule is at least five continuous years with a valid residence permit; it is not framed as a fixed number of years after obtaining an indefinite permit.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General eligibility can arise after five continuous lawful-residence years, but no suitable starting route exists for this profile, so a route-specific total is inapplicable.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Published government service target; actual timing may vary because approval is discretionary and document scrutiny can be extensive.

key_conditions.value: General administrative guidance requires at least five continuous years in Lesotho with a valid residence permit. Depending on category, applicants may need a passport, original permit, police clearance, chief’s consent, medical certificate, six-month bank statements, tax clearance, work permit and business/employment evidence. The older Citizenship Order also states English-or-Sesotho knowledge, good character, financial solvency, allegiance and permanent-residence intent conditions. No suitable remote-work starting route exists.
key_conditions.notes: Five years establishes eligibility to apply, not guaranteed approval. The current administrative page and older statutory text should be reconciled with Home Affairs for a filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The current constitutional text provides registration after five years of cohabitation in Lesotho and continuous lawful stay with the Lesotho citizen. This is not numerically faster than the published five-year general residence threshold, although it creates a distinct registration basis.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support spouse residence and later citizenship registration, but time married abroad alone does not satisfy the stated requirement of five years’ cohabitation and continuous lawful stay in Lesotho.

requirements_and_risks.value: Expect marriage certificate, applications from both spouses, proof of relationship, permits/passports, police and medical documents, financial statements and local verification. Entry guidance also requests family affidavits for the marriage category. False documents or a sham marriage can lead to refusal and immigration enforcement; approval is not automatic.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official pages do not publish a comprehensive sham-marriage adjudication test, so filing-level requirements should be confirmed directly.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The current constitutional text grants citizenship to persons born in Lesotho, with narrow diplomatic/enemy-occupation exceptions and an anti-statelessness safeguard. Pew’s 2026 GLOBALCIT-based review also classifies Lesotho’s territorial-birth rule as generally applicable and automatic. Older citizenship instruments and reports have produced inconsistent descriptions and implementation concerns, so parents should obtain written civil-registration confirmation.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Under the current constitutional rule, a child born in Lesotho generally becomes a citizen even if both parents are foreign migrants, apart from narrow exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Practical registration should be confirmed because older statutory wording and historical practice have not always been described consistently.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Lesotho is a citizen by territorial birth; a child born abroad also acquires citizenship at birth if either parent is a Lesotho citizen otherwise than by descent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically make either foreign parent a citizen or permanent resident. Home Affairs has family residence categories such as joining parents and joining relatives, but the reviewed rules do not clearly confirm that a minor citizen child can independently sponsor a foreign parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Treat any parent-of-citizen residence benefit as requiring direct Home Affairs confirmation.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship, indefinite residence or shortened naturalisation period for the migrant father was found. A family-based residence application may be arguable, but eligibility, custody/maintenance evidence and whether a minor citizen can serve as the anchor require manual verification.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately categorizes eVisa and other facilitated-entry destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined for this schema from 29 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations. Passport Index reports these categories separately.

passport.notes: Passport Index shows a mobility score of 79. Its mobility score includes additional facilitated categories, so it should not be confused with the 43 strictly visa-free destinations.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is an official language and can support government, professional and remote-work dealings, especially in Maseru. Practical remote work is constrained by infrastructure: the Central Bank notes that internet availability is limited and nearly absent in rural areas, while international-card acceptance is concentrated in major towns.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The 2025 constitutional amendment expanded the official-language list. Verify reliable fixed or mobile connectivity at the exact accommodation before relocating.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and no evidence of broad public-service or commercial use was found. A Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking resident should expect to operate mainly in English and Sesotho and use interpretation when needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official-language framework; no reliable national proficiency statistics for Russian or Ukrainian were located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximation: the 2024 LFS mean of M5,664.89 for paid employees divided by the World Bank’s 2024 average official exchange rate of 18.33 LSL/USD. It is not a current exchange quote.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed 2024 LFS tables publish means but no national median monthly earnings figure was identified.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 general minimum wage of M2,242 for employees with under 12 months’ service, using the World Bank 2024 average exchange rate. This is a statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the national mean monthly earnings for persons in paid employment on their main job.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official 2024 Labour Force Survey tables reviewed publish mean earnings but not a national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary is published. Occupational mean values are not maximum salaries.

min_salary_local_currency.value: M2,242 per month for general-minimum-wage employees with under 12 months’ continuous service; M2,448 after more than 12 months
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Effective wage notice dated 28 March 2025. Sector-specific minima differ.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 Labour Force Survey mean monthly earnings for persons in paid employment on the main job, averaged across occupations and settlement types.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official report does not publish a national median monthly earnings value.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A national maximum is not a meaningful published statistic. The report’s highest occupational mean was M12,231.74 for managers, but that is not a maximum and is therefore not entered here.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Mean monthly earnings of persons in paid employment on the main job; minimum field is the statutory general minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 LFS for average earnings; 2025 wage notice for minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average applies to paid employees rather than all citizens or all employed/self-employed people. USD conversions use the matching 2024 annual-average exchange rate for comparability and are rounded.

cost_of_living_note.value: A reliable current nationwide household cost basket was not published in the reviewed official sources. Practical infrastructure costs may be material outside Maseru because official Central Bank guidance describes internet access as limited and nearly absent in rural areas and ATMs as limited and unreliable.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is an infrastructure caveat, not a quantified cost-of-living index.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Lesotho publishes no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker permit, so there is no nomad status whose time can count toward settlement. Visitor/eVisa status is not a residence permit, and no official visitor-to-remote-worker conversion is published; settlement would require obtaining a separate qualifying residence basis.
settlement_track.summary: Lesotho has a general citizenship application after five continuous years with a valid residence permit, but no ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route was found from which this applicant could begin that clock. Business residence requires genuine local business, licensing and work-permit substance; sponsored work requires a local employer.
settlement_track.notes: The negative selection result is preserved after a focused 2026 audit. Current immigration and Aliens Control sources confirm that visitor status is distinct from temporary or indefinite permits, no digital-nomad/foreign-remote-worker category is published, and the general citizenship service requires five continuous years with a valid residence permit. The study-time issue remains a precise legal/administrative ambiguity rather than an assumed exclusion.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category is published. The business route requires local business substance and a work permit; the employee route requires a prospective local employer and labor-market certification. Visitor entry is not a qualifying substitute.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field audit inspected at least 21 directly relevant URLs, including six canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. The negative remote-work conclusion remains high confidence. Study-permit time is not marked as counting or excluded: the 1971 Citizenship Order uses broad lawful-sojourn wording, while current administrative guidance requires a valid residence permit and does not say whether a study permit qualifies.

data.selection_summary: Liberia has an online resident-permit system and official rules covering self-employed foreign workers, but current filing materials do not confirm that foreign-client software work is an acceptable first-time residence basis. The work-permit procedure asks for a Liberian business or institution, entity documents, staffing information, and potentially labor-market evidence. No dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker category was identified, so Liberia does not meet the citizenship-oriented selection criteria.

visa_application.title: Liberia Resident Permit Application
visa_application.notes: Official online resident-permit application. It is not a digital-nomad application, and the public portal and current service charter do not establish foreign-client remote work as a first-time eligibility category.

rejected_routes.route_name: Resident permit plus self-employed alien work permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current resident-permit and self-employed work-permit materials publish fees but no minimum monthly income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official filing materials prescribe no income threshold or bank-balance formula.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income threshold
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: No income threshold published; separate permit fees apply in USD
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of an income threshold does not establish eligibility for foreign-client remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The current portal, service charter, work-permit regulation, and checklist do not prescribe a number of months of prior income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: A resident permit is required for a stay exceeding 90 days. The application is filed online, followed by in-person document verification and biometric enrollment.

The current LIS service charter describes residence-permit change of status after lawful entry and requires a valid travel document, entry stamp, application letter, photographs, bond/notary documentation, and a completed change-of-status form.
Aliens working in Liberia generally require a work permit; the employment-permit regulation expressly includes self-employed aliens in its formal-sector category.
The published Category A work-permit fee for formal-sector and self-employed aliens is US$1,000 for one calendar year.

The general work-permit checklist asks for a business or institution, business-registration evidence, job description, staff lists, and, where applicable, advertising and certification that no qualified Liberian is available.
A sole proprietorship can be registered with identification and a photograph, must obtain a TIN, and renews its business registration annually.

Certain activities are legally reserved for Liberian citizens or Liberian-owned businesses; the government announced active enforcement in 2026. Software consulting is not identified in the reviewed notice, but the proposed activity must be checked against the reserved-business rules.
The resident-permit fee table recognizes adjustment from employee to self-employed status but does not expressly list a first-time self-employed category.

initial_validity.value: Resident-permit duration for this category is not published; work permit is valid for one calendar year
initial_validity.notes: The resident materials describe fixed or indefinite residence and renewal procedures but do not state the duration granted to a first-time self-employed applicant.

extension_rules.value: Work permit reviewed annually; resident-permit renewal must be filed before 60 days remain on the current permit
extension_rules.notes: The Ministry of Labour expressly reserves discretion not to renew a work permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: After lawful entry, apply for a resident permit/change of status and separately satisfy business-registration and alien work-permit requirements if self-employed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The current service charter confirms a general change-of-status process but does not confirm foreign-client software services as the qualifying ground; filing-level confirmation from LIS and the Ministry of Labour remains necessary.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed resident-permit portal, current LIS service charter, and nationality law do not publish a separate permanent-residence entitlement, qualifying period, or conversion rule for a self-employed foreign worker.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization law permits an eligible applicant to petition after at least two years of continuous lawful residence, but naturalization is judicial, is not a route-specific remote-worker entitlement, and remains restricted by current constitutional and statutory text to persons described as Negro or of Negro descent.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant must maintain continuous lawful residence, have been lawfully admitted, and document a resident permit. An absence exceeding six months breaks continuity unless the court is satisfied that Liberian residence was not abandoned. No automatic citizenship consequence follows from holding a self-employed work permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because current official materials do not identify ordinary foreign-contract remote work as an eligible first-time resident/self-employed category. The general work-permit checklist contains local-entity and labor-market elements, no permanent-residence conversion was established, and naturalization has a statutory racial restriction.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies because this is entry permission, not a remote-work residence category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: An income threshold is inapplicable to the route assessed; the portal does not confer remote-work residence status.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—ordinary entry permission
income_requirement_display.notes: Visa-on-arrival approval facilitates entry only.

income_proof_months.notes: The official visa-on-arrival service does not prescribe a remote-work income-history requirement.

key_requirements.requirement: Visa-on-arrival approval is an entry service, not residence or work authorization.
A stay beyond 90 days requires a separate resident permit, while work requires separate work authorization.

initial_validity.notes: The entry portal does not create a remote-worker status or publish a route-specific residence period.

extension_rules.notes: Continued residence requires a separate resident-permit/change-of-status process rather than extension of a remote-worker category.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic transition; a separate resident-permit/change-of-status application is required for residence beyond 90 days.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: LIS retains approval authority, and the applicant must establish a valid residence ground.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current entry, residence, and nationality materials publish no permanent-residence conversion entitlement arising from ordinary visa or visa-on-arrival entry.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality law requires continuous lawful residence and lawful admission, while the official naturalization checklist requires a resident permit. The sources do not state that time held solely under ordinary visitor or visa-on-arrival permission satisfies the naturalization residence requirement; entry permission alone therefore cannot be treated as qualifying citizenship-path residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because ordinary visitor or visa-on-arrival permission is not a remote-work, residence, permanent-residence, or settlement category.

summary.value: No independent degree-based or software-engineer residence route was identified. A foreign-worker application generally proceeds through a work permit connected to a business or institution and may require evidence that no qualified Liberian is available.
summary.notes: A university degree may support the applicant's credentials but does not independently confer immigration status.

tax_residency_rule.value: A natural person is resident for a tax year if the person has a normal place of abode in Liberia and is present at any time, or is present for more than 182 days in a 12-month period ending during the tax year, subject to statutory exclusions.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A person who was not resident in the preceding year is not treated as resident for the period before first presence in Liberia during the tax year.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for resident natural persons, not an expected effective rate. A qualifying small business may instead fall under a 4% turnover-based presumptive regime.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For an employee, the published total is 10% of remuneration: 4% employee pension, 4% employer pension, and 2% employer employment-injury contribution. This 10% is not the rate for a solo self-employed person. The Act makes self-employed membership application-based and subject to NASSCORP approval; the current employer guide publishes 7% of gross monthly earnings for a formerly insured employee approved to continue pension contributions after becoming self-employed. It does not publish an automatic mandatory rate for a newly arrived solo foreign freelancer.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly fixed payment applies across the assessed scenario. Relevant non-monthly or percentage charges include a US$1,000 annual self-employed work-permit fee, nationality-dependent resident-permit fees, annual business registration, and—if NASSCORP approves voluntary self-employed membership—percentage contributions rather than a published fixed minimum.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, non-dom, remittance-basis, or inbound-worker concession was identified. A small taxpayer carrying on business with annual turnover below LRD 3,000,000 is generally subject to 4% of turnover unless electing regular income tax.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility and classification of software consulting should be confirmed with the Liberia Revenue Authority.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on physical work location, tax residence, whether the contract is employment or independent services, business registration, deductions, foreign tax credits, and any applicable treaty. Services physically performed in Liberia are Liberia-source even if payment comes from abroad. NASSCORP treatment differs materially between an employee, a business with employees, and an approved voluntary self-employed member.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax for resident natural persons, with a separate presumptive turnover regime for qualifying small businesses.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Normal place of abode plus presence, or more than 182 days in a relevant 12-month period, subject to statutory exclusions.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident natural persons are taxed on annual taxable income. The Code treats services or employment exercised in Liberia as Liberia-source regardless of where payment is received; nonresidents are taxed on Liberia-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Small taxpayers below LRD 3,000,000 annual turnover generally face 4% presumptive tax on turnover unless they elect the regular regime. No nomad-specific regime was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees working for an employer with at least one employee are generally covered by NASSCORP. Published employee-system contributions total 10% of remuneration: employee 4% pension, employer 4% pension, and employer 2% employment-injury coverage. Self-employed membership is not automatically treated the same: section 89.13 of the 2017 Act permits enrollment only on written application and approval by the Director General, with the applicable rate set by regulations. NASSCORP's current employer guide states that a previously insured employee who becomes self-employed may request permission to continue National Pension Scheme contributions at 7% of gross monthly earnings. The reviewed current NASSCORP sources do not publish a compulsory contribution rate or fixed minimum for a newly arrived solo foreign freelancer with no employees.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Annual resident-natural-person brackets are 0%, 5%, 15%, and 25%. The dashboard value of 25% is the top marginal rate. Business income below the small-taxpayer ceiling can instead be taxed at 4% of turnover.

tax_brackets.notes: No tax in this band.
Annual bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: LRD 200,001–800,000; LRD 6,500 plus 15% of excess over LRD 200,000
tax_brackets.notes: Annual bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Above LRD 800,000; LRD 96,500 plus 25% of excess over LRD 800,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal annual bracket, not the effective rate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Qualifying small natural or legal person carrying on trade or business
tax_brackets.notes: Presumptive tax on turnover in lieu of regular income tax unless the taxpayer elects regular taxation; separate petty-trader fixed amounts apply below LRD 200,000.

taxation_system.notes: The Revenue Code and LRA tables support the tax-residence test and rates. The 2017 NASSCORP Act, current official guide, and FAQ clarify the employee contribution split and application-based self-employed coverage. Classification of a particular foreign contract and approval of voluntary self-employed NASSCORP membership remain filing-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Liberia has no confirmed digital-nomad status or tax regime. A person physically performing remote services in Liberia can generate Liberia-source income even when paid abroad, and a resident natural person may face progressive tax up to 25%; a qualifying registered small business may instead fall under 4% presumptive turnover tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; analyze as employment income or registered self-employed business income
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 25% top marginal PIT screening rate; qualifying small-business alternative may be 4% of turnover
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Normal place of abode plus presence, or more than 182 days in a relevant 12-month period, subject to statutory exclusions.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign payment does not by itself make income foreign-source: services or employment exercised in Liberia are Liberia-source whether or not the gains are received in Liberia.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax regime was identified in the current immigration and tax materials.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee coverage totals 10%, split between employee and employer. A solo self-employed person may apply for NASSCORP membership subject to approval; the current guide states a 7% pension rate for an approved formerly insured employee who becomes self-employed, but does not establish that rate as a mandatory charge for every newly arrived foreign freelancer.

fixed_payments.status: No monthly nomad charge; annual, percentage-based, and transaction-specific charges may apply
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No compulsory fixed self-employed minimum was published for a newly arrived solo freelancer. Employee-system contributions apply where there is Liberian employment/payroll; approved voluntary self-employed pension participation may be charged at 7% of gross monthly earnings in the circumstance described by NASSCORP.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Resident permit: US$750 first application and US$350 renewal for a non-African citizen; employee-to-self-employed status adjustment: US$350. Formal-sector/self-employed alien work permit: US$1,000 for one calendar year.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Small petty-trader fixed annual amounts exist below LRD 200,000 turnover. Business registration renews annually, but the reviewed current sources do not establish one universal registration fee for the assessed software-consulting structure.
fixed_payments.notes: Fees are not monthly equivalents and can change. Resident-permit charges vary by nationality and family status; social-security treatment depends on employment structure and NASSCORP approval.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Even before tax residence, services physically performed in Liberia are expressly Liberia-source; nonresident withholding or filing consequences therefore require advice.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident natural person is generally screened under progressive PIT up to 25%, with foreign-tax-credit and treaty analysis where applicable.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A qualifying small business below LRD 3,000,000 turnover may face 4% presumptive turnover tax unless regular taxation is elected. Registration, TIN, quarterly payments, work permit, and resident permit may also be required. NASSCORP participation for a solo self-employed applicant is application-based rather than a confirmed universal fixed monthly charge.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax law is clear on Liberia-source services and headline rates, but no digital-nomad administrative guidance exists. Contract classification, foreign-employer payroll obligations, and approval/rate details for a new solo self-employed NASSCORP applicant remain fact-dependent.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A resident permit/change of status, if approved, authorizes residence beyond 90 days without a prior multi-year waiting period. The current service charter gives a seven-working-day service target for listed change-of-status applications.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The current resident-permit portal, service charter, and nationality law do not publish a permanent-residence entitlement or qualifying timeline.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Liberian naturalization law uses continuous lawful residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence prerequisite, so an after-permanent-residence interval is inapplicable to the published statutory test.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum continuous lawful residence before filing. This is not available to every applicant: current law restricts naturalization to persons described as Negro or of Negro descent, and judicial approval is not automatic.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official naturalization page, nationality law, and current LIS service charter do not publish a typical end-to-end naturalization processing period.

key_conditions.value: At least two years of continuous lawful residence immediately before filing; continued residence through admission; lawful admission; absence over six months can break continuity unless rebutted; good moral character; constitutional allegiance; resident permit; passport; four recommendations; police/security clearance; health certificate; autobiography; legal representation; and racial eligibility under current constitutional and nationality-law text.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is judicial and discretionary. The reviewed materials do not identify a language test or a prerequisite permanent-residence stage.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Two years is the general naturalization residence minimum, not a shortened marriage period. No special spouse timeline was established.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage to a Liberian citizen affects resident-permit fees, and a married naturalization applicant must provide a marriage certificate; it does not remove the general naturalization restrictions found in current law.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Current sources do not provide automatic citizenship or accelerated naturalization merely because the marriage already exists.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid and documented. Residence, work authorization, naturalization eligibility, security clearance, and current statutory citizenship restrictions remain separate issues. Fraudulent documents or a sham marriage can result in refusal, revocation, or prosecution.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The reviewed official and legal sources publish no cohabitation substitute or marriage-duration concession.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The nationality statute historically attributes citizenship to a child born in Liberia who is of Negro descent and subject to Liberian jurisdiction, while the 1986 Constitution frames citizenship at birth through at least one Liberian parent and restricts citizenship by race. This conflict makes the jurisdiction restricted rather than unconditional jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Potentially under the statutory birthplace rule if the child is of Negro descent and subject to Liberian jurisdiction, but the Constitution's parent-citizenship language creates legal uncertainty; citizenship should not be assumed without an official determination.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The result depends on racial eligibility, parental citizenship, diplomatic status, and resolution of the constitutional/statutory tension. The reviewed law does not make a parent's permanent-resident status independently sufficient.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Liberian mother or father qualifies as a citizen at birth under the Constitution and the 2022 gender-equal transmission amendment, subject to Liberia's constitutional citizenship restrictions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2022 amendment allows either a Liberian mother or father to transmit citizenship to a child born abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Liberian citizen child does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. Any family residence or naturalization application remains separate and subject to ordinary eligibility requirements.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed sources publish no automatic parent residence, permanent-residence, or citizenship entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent-residence benefit was established for a migrant father. If the other parent is Liberian, the child may be Liberian, but the father must independently maintain lawful immigration status.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child's nationality and the father's immigration status are legally separate.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-free category; its methodology differs from Henley's combined-access count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required category displayed by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 28 visa-on-arrival plus 2 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately counts eVisas and other authorizations.

passport.notes: A current single-index breakdown is used so the rank and access categories are methodologically consistent.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the official language and is practical for administration and business. Remote work remains operationally challenging because electricity access is low and dry-season load shedding is frequent; dependable backup power and connectivity are advisable.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English-language usability is high, but infrastructure quality is materially weaker than the language environment.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and no evidence of broad everyday use was identified; English would be necessary for administration and most business dealings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable source quantified Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking communities, so practicality beyond isolated individuals remains unquantified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The recent census labor report describes employment status but does not publish a current national mean wage. The 2025 labor-statistics document is a data-collection questionnaire rather than completed wage results.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the census labor report nor the 2025 labor-statistics questionnaire publishes a current national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Screening equivalent derived from the cited statutory US$5.50 daily minimum for ordinary workers multiplied by 26 workdays. It is not an observed minimum monthly salary, and entitlement depends on days and hours worked.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed recent official labor publications do not provide completed national average monthly earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed recent official labor publications do not provide completed national median monthly earnings.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum wage is published in the reviewed labor sources, so no ceiling is inferred.

min_salary_local_currency.value: US$5.50 per day for an ordinary worker; US$3.50 per day for a domestic or casual worker
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The cited Liberian statutory minimum is expressed in US dollars rather than LRD. The ordinary-worker screening equivalent is approximately US$143 for 26 workdays.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official reports do not publish a current national average in LRD.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official reports do not publish a current national median in LRD.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official reports do not publish a national maximum earnings figure.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory daily minimum only; no completed current official national average or median earnings result
average_citizen_salary.period: Daily statutory minimum, with a 26-workday monthly screening conversion
average_citizen_salary.notes: The only defensible current wage floor identified is US$5.50 per day for ordinary workers and US$3.50 for domestic or casual workers. Mean, median, and maximum earnings remain null because the named recent official sources do not publish those completed statistics.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable current household cost basket was established. Infrastructure costs can be significant: electricity access remains low, residential tariffs were reported at about US$0.24/kWh in 2024, and frequent dry-season load shedding makes backup power important for remote work.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is an infrastructure-cost warning rather than a numerical cost-of-living estimate.
