settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Liberia does not publish a digital-nomad or remote-worker status, so there is no nomad residence period that can be credited toward settlement. A visa, visa on arrival, or re-entry card is only entry/travel permission; lawful residence beyond 90 days requires a separate resident permit/change of status, and remunerated activity requires an applicable work permit. Even after those separate approvals, current sources do not confirm foreign-client remote work as an eligible first-time basis or publish a permanent-residence conversion.
settlement_track.summary: Liberia has general resident-permit, self-employed work-permit, and naturalization mechanisms, but current official rules do not confirm ordinary foreign-client remote work as a first-time qualifying residence category. Entry permission is not a settlement route, no permanent-residence conversion was established, and naturalization remains subject to restrictive statutory eligibility rules.
settlement_track.notes: The field is not describing a temporary nomad program: no such Liberian program was identified. It warns that ordinary entry cannot substitute for separate residence and work authorization. Even if local self-employment is approved, no permanent-residence entitlement was found, and current constitutional/statutory text restricts naturalization by race.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Self-employed aliens are recognized, but current filing rules do not identify foreign-client software work as a first-time residence basis and include local-entity, business-registration, and potentially labor-market requirements. No official digital-nomad category was identified.

data.notes: The negative nomad finding, resident-permit process, work-permit fees and conditions, tax rates, employee social-security contribution split, application-based self-employed social-security coverage, and nationality restrictions are supported by current official or legal sources. Overall confidence remains medium because the resident-permit system does not publish a complete first-time self-employed eligibility taxonomy; LIS, the Ministry of Labour, LRA, and NASSCORP would need to confirm the treatment of a particular foreign-client consulting arrangement.

data.selection_summary: No current ordinary digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, freelance, or independently accessible self-employed residence route was confirmed. Libya's official eVisa is an entry channel, while the current foreign-worker framework requires a Libyan employer, authenticated employment contract, work approval, and purpose-specific residence; it does not fit ordinary work for a foreign client without a local employer.

visa_application.title: Libya eVisa
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct eVisa application portal. It is an entry-visa channel, not an application for digital-nomad, independent freelance, or foreign-contract remote-worker residence. Libya launched the second implementation phase of E-VISA LIBYA and Wafed in June 2026, but the reviewed current materials publish no qualifying remote-work category.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold is published because this is not a remote-worker residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying-route income threshold applies to ordinary eVisa entry.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold published; ordinary entry only
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No income formula applies to ordinary remote-work residence because the eVisa does not create that status.
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of a threshold does not make the entry visa an independent work or residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: The current sources do not prescribe a remote-worker income-history period because no remote-worker category is offered.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through the official eVisa platform for an available entry purpose; nationality-specific availability and supporting documents must be checked in the portal.
An entry or residence authorization may be used only for its stated purpose unless written permission to change purpose is obtained.
Foreigners must register with the passport authority within seven days of arrival under the general foreigners law.

initial_validity.value: The 1987 law describes an entry visa issued for its stated purpose, with issuance validity not exceeding 45 days and a stay of up to three months from entry; the live portal's category-specific terms control a current application.
initial_validity.notes: These are general statutory entry-visa rules, not a guaranteed eVisa duration or residence permission.

extension_rules.value: Tourist and visitor entry may be extended for no more than three months under the reviewed implementing decree, but no remote-work extension category exists.
extension_rules.notes: Extension does not authorize foreign-contract remote work or create a settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path. A separate purpose-specific residence authorization is required; work residence remains linked to approved employment or another recognized purpose.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The sources do not establish conversion from ordinary visitor entry to independent foreign-contract remote-work residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed immigration and anti-settlement laws publish no permanent-residence conversion entitlement from ordinary eVisa entry.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path arises from the eVisa itself. General naturalization requires a separate lawful-residence basis for ten consecutive years and remains discretionary.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time should not be assumed to qualify as continuous legal residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: This route is independently accessible for entry but is visitor-like, purpose-restricted, and not settlement-oriented. It does not authorize the applicant's ordinary foreign-contract remote-work scenario.

rejected_routes.route_name: Locally sponsored foreign-worker work and residence route

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed current hiring procedure and foreign-worker rules do not prescribe a generally applicable immigration salary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The employment contract must state the wage and benefits, but the reviewed rules do not specify a universal minimum salary for work-permit eligibility.

income_requirement_display.value: No statutory work-permit salary threshold or salary formula; an employer-sponsored contract stating remuneration is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No universal amount or formula is prescribed. The employer submits a contract stating the worker's wage, allowances, and benefits, and the authorities assess the employer-linked work approval.
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer-linked foreign-employment requirement, not an income route for foreign-client remote work. The statutory national minimum wage is a labor standard and should not be misrepresented as an immigration eligibility threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed rules require an employment contract and employer application rather than a prescribed number of months of prior income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: A foreigner may not work without approval from the competent labor authority, and the employer must obtain prior authorization to recruit or employ the foreign worker.
The employer submits the work-approval application; the foreign worker may work only for the authorized employer, occupation, and workplace.
Current regularization rules require registration on Wafed, an authenticated employment contract, and a health certificate.
A purpose-specific work-residence authorization and residence documentation are required.

initial_validity.value: Work approval is generally valid for one to two years from the foreign worker's arrival under Decision No. 392 of 2021.
initial_validity.notes: The older work-card regulation described one-year cards, with up to three years for designated work; the current employer-specific approval controls the filing.

extension_rules.value: The employer may request renewal for one or more equivalent periods before expiry, subject to continuing compliance with the foreign-worker conditions.
extension_rules.notes: Decision No. 392 provides for renewal filings no more than 60 days before expiry. Continued approved employment is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying Libyan employer obtains the work approval and supports purpose-specific work residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This requires local employment and therefore fails the applicant profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No general direct permanent-residence entitlement for ordinary foreign workers is published in the reviewed laws.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ten consecutive years of lawful residence can satisfy the general residence condition for discretionary naturalization if every other statutory condition is met.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality law does not guarantee naturalization or define a separate permanent-residence milestone.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Libyan employer, authenticated employment contract, and work approval are required. It is not an independent foreign-contract remote-work route, even for a qualified software engineer.

summary.value: Nationality Law No. 24 of 2010 exempts persons with special expertise or higher qualifications needed by Libya from several ordinary naturalization conditions. This is discretionary nationality relief, not a published skilled-migration or degree-based residence route, and no independent application channel or objective software-engineer eligibility criteria were found.
summary.notes: The applicant's degree alone does not create an immigration route. Whether Libya formally determines that a particular qualification is needed requires case-specific government confirmation.

tax_residency_rule.value: Income Tax Law No. 64 of 1973 treats an individual as resident when presence exceeds six months during the taxable year, even non-continuously, or when Libya is the person's principal residence or center of main interests.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The six-month rule is not expressed as an exact 183-day test. Treatment of remotely performed services and foreign income requires professional interpretation.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for employment income, not an expected effective rate. The lower bracket is 5%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee contribution on gross covered earnings for persons working in Libya. ISSA separately reports 20.425% for covered self-employed residents; employer contributions are additional.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conditional minimum social-insurance contribution for a covered self-employed resident: 20.425% of the published LYD 900 minimum contribution base equals LYD 183.825, approximately USD 29 at the 13 August 2026 official exchange rate. This is not a digital-nomad fee and does not create immigration eligibility.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate remittance-basis, or inbound tax-holiday regime was identified in the reviewed tax materials.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This negative finding should be verified with the Libyan Tax Authority or a local adviser before reliance.

taxes.caveats: The immigration framework does not authorize ordinary foreign-client remote work. Tax residence, where services are physically performed, source characterization, contract structure, payer presence, social-insurance registration, and any applicable treaty can change the result. The statutory external-income provisions and current secondary tax guidance should be reconciled by a Libyan tax professional.

taxation_system.value: Progressive employment-income tax with resident external-income rules and source-specific exemptions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Resident after more than six months' presence in the taxable year, or when Libya is the principal residence or center of main interests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Current PwC guidance states that Libyan and foreign nationals are taxed on employment income derived from employment in Libya. The Income Tax Law also addresses residents' external income and exempts wages paid for work performed abroad; services physically performed from Libya should not automatically be characterized as work abroad.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees contribute 5.125% of gross covered earnings. Employers generally contribute 14.35%, or 15.375% for foreign employers. ISSA reports 20.425% for covered self-employed residents, based on covered earnings with a published LYD 900 monthly minimum base. A 1% Social Unity Fund contribution and 0.5% salary stamp duty are also reported for employment.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 10% figure is the top marginal screening rate. Employment PIT is 5% through LYD 1,000 monthly and 10% above, after applicable deductions and exemptions; it is not a 10% effective rate on every dinar.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Up to LYD 1,000 gross salary per month (LYD 12,000 per year)
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment income after applicable deductions and exemptions
tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses the Central Bank of Libya's 13 August 2026 USD buy/sell range of LYD 6.3539–6.3858 per USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over LYD 1,000 gross salary per month (over LYD 12,000 per year)
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment income above the lower-bracket threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not the expected effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Current rate and contribution information comes from PwC's May 2026 review and ISSA's February 2026 country profile; residence and external-income rules are supported by the published income-tax law. Filing treatment of foreign-contract remote services remains uncertain because no dedicated immigration or tax category exists.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special digital-nomad tax category applies because Libya has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker status.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No qualifying digital-nomad or remote-worker route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% top marginal employment-income screening rate; no nomad-specific rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than six months' presence during the taxable year, or principal residence/main interests in Libya, under the published income-tax law.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The statutory external-income chapter applies to residents' foreign income while exempting wages for work performed abroad; current guidance emphasizes employment income derived from employment in Libya. Services physically performed from Libya require professional source-characterization advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No such regime was identified in the reviewed law, tax summaries, eVisa portal, or current foreign-worker rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employees working in Libya are reported subject to 5.125% employee social security, while ISSA reports 20.425% for covered self-employed residents. Employer contributions, a 1% Social Unity Fund contribution, and 0.5% salary stamp duty may apply depending on structure.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed payment is applicable because no digital-nomad route exists; a conditional minimum self-employed social-insurance contribution can arise only after lawful resident self-employed coverage.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: ISSA reports self-employed contributions of 20.425% of covered earnings, with a LYD 900 monthly minimum contribution base. That implies a minimum contribution of LYD 183.825 per month, approximately USD 29, but it is not a nomad fee and does not provide residence.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No remote-worker visa or residence-card fee exists. The current government labor-import procedure is marked free of charge, while the still-published 1974 work-card regulation states LYD 5 for a card or LYD 10 when valid for more than one year; the applicable current charge requires filing-level confirmation.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No VAT is reported. Employment-related charges include a 1% Social Unity Fund contribution on gross salary and 0.5% stamp duty on net salary; other stamp duties depend on transaction type.
fixed_payments.notes: The only quantified minimum found is the conditional social-insurance amount for a covered self-employed resident. It must not be treated as a digital-nomad, freelancer-visa, municipal-registration, or immigration-renewal fee. Current work-procedure and older work-card fee sources are not fully aligned.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below the six-month residence threshold can still create Libya-source income or work-authorization issues. Visitor status is not an authorized remote-work solution.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: The general 10% top marginal employment rate is only a screening figure. Source rules, resident external-income provisions, social insurance, and lack of an authorized remote-work status make professional advice essential.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Social insurance rules contemplate covered self-employed residents, but no immigration process was found by which a visitor can register as self-employed and thereby legalize residence for foreign-client work.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section describes hypothetical tax and contribution exposure only; it does not imply that immigration permission for remote work exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-work route exists. Locally sponsored workers may obtain purpose-specific temporary residence, but that is a rejected employer route.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed laws publish no general permanent-residence milestone or entitlement for the applicant's scenario.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality law measures ten consecutive years of legal residence rather than years after a separately defined permanent-residence status.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated from a qualifying remote-work route because none exists. General discretionary naturalization has a ten-year consecutive legal-residence condition.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the nationality law nor the reviewed index of its implementing regulation publishes a typical processing-time service standard.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization is discretionary and ordinarily requires adulthood and capacity, lawful entry, ten consecutive years of legal residence, a legitimate and proven steady income, good character, no disqualifying conviction, freedom from infectious or communicable disease, and age not exceeding 50 at filing. Additional public-interest conditions may be imposed.
key_conditions.notes: The law does not state a general language test. Libya may withdraw naturalized nationality in specified circumstances, including certain security grounds or two consecutive years abroad within the first ten years after naturalization without an accepted excuse.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Gender-specific rule: a foreign woman married to a Libyan man is exempted from ordinary naturalization conditions 2 through 6 after at least two years of marriage at filing.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can count toward the statutory two-year duration if it is legally recognized and still subsists at filing. Marriage alone does not automatically confer nationality; a government decision is still required.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The reviewed law does not publish a separate cohabitation substitute.

requirements_and_risks.value: The accelerated rule applies to foreign wives of Libyan men and specified widows or divorcees of Libyan citizens; no equivalent accelerated citizenship rule was found for a foreign husband of a Libyan woman. The application remains discretionary, and current documentary practice must be checked under the implementing regulation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A genuine, legally documented marriage should be expected. False information or counterfeit documents can cause loss of nationality; the reviewed sources do not publish a quantified sham-marriage test.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Libya primarily uses descent through a Libyan father. Birth in Libya alone is insufficient; narrow territorial protections cover a child born in Libya to a Libyan mother and an unknown or stateless father, and a child whose parents are unknown.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Libya to two known non-Libyan migrant parents does not automatically become Libyan merely by birthplace. The unknown-parent rule is a narrow exception.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No unconditional or ordinary conditional jus soli applies.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child is Libyan through a Libyan father under Article 3, subject to timely registration when born abroad. A child of a Libyan mother and non-Libyan father may be granted nationality under Article 11, so transmission through the mother is not stated as equally automatic.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because the result depends on which parent is Libyan and the father's status, the country-level boolean remains null rather than overstating equal transmission.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A child's Libyan nationality does not automatically grant a migrant parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. The parent needs an independently recognized family or immigration basis.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The foreigners rules allow specified dependants to share a foreign resident's status but do not establish automatic status for every parent of a Libyan child.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or residence benefit was confirmed for a foreign father. If the mother is Libyan, the child's nationality may itself require a grant under Article 11, and the foreign-wife marriage exemption does not apply to the husband.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A case-specific family-residence inquiry with the passport and nationality authority is necessary.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank observed on 15 August 2026. A separate January 2026 Henley report placed Libya 93rd, illustrating methodology and update differences.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category; eVisa destinations are not included in the requested VOA/eTA field.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reports 30 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 49. Henley instead reported 39 destinations accessible without a prior visa and rank 93 in January 2026; the indexes use different category groupings and should not be combined.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Limited. Arabic is the sole official language under the current constitutional framework. English may be usable in some international-business settings, but no reliable current nationwide proficiency evidence or dedicated remote-worker ecosystem was identified.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical inference from official-language status and the lack of stronger current evidence, not a measured proficiency score.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, and the reviewed sources provide no evidence of broad day-to-day public-service or business usability.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Arabic-speaking assistance would likely be needed for legal and administrative processes.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate current-rate conversion of the 2022 National Labour Force Survey mean of LYD 1,306 per worker per month, using the Central Bank's 13 August 2026 official USD rate range. The wage observation itself is from 2022.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2022 National Labour Force Survey listing and the 2025 World Bank assessment publish a national mean wage, not a median. The separate official 2022–2023 household-income dataset reports average income by quintile and cannot establish a national median worker wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the LYD 1,000 statutory national minimum using the Central Bank's 13 August 2026 rate. ISSA records LYD 900 as of 1 July 2024 and cautions that the legislated LYD 1,000 increase may not then have been fully implemented.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate current-rate conversion of the LYD 1,306 mean monthly earnings reported from the 2022 National Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD median can be calculated: the reviewed National Labour Force Survey material and World Bank assessment publish only the LYD 1,306 arithmetic mean for workers. The official household-income-by-quintile dataset measures household income rather than a national median worker wage.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD maximum can be calculated because the reviewed national labor and household-income sources publish neither a national maximum worker wage nor an upper endpoint for the worker-wage distribution.

min_salary_local_currency.value: LYD 1,000 per month statutory minimum; ISSA recorded LYD 900 in July 2024 while noting incomplete implementation of the increase
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is a statutory labor standard, not an observed minimum salary or immigration income threshold.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Arithmetic mean reported by the World Bank from Libya's Bureau of Statistics and Census 2022 National Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_local_currency.value: The reviewed national worker-wage sources publish the LYD 1,306 arithmetic mean but do not publish a median monthly worker wage.
median_salary_local_currency.notes: The official 2022–2023 household-income dataset provides average income by quintile, which is a different measure and cannot substitute for a national median worker salary.

max_salary_local_currency.value: The reviewed national sources publish no national maximum worker wage or upper endpoint of the worker-wage distribution.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: A household income quintile table and a national arithmetic mean do not establish an observed or statutory maximum salary; no value is inferred.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory national minimum wage and 2022 National Labour Force Survey arithmetic mean monthly earnings per worker
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum-wage law enacted in 2023; wage-survey reference year 2022; USD conversions use 13 August 2026 official exchange rates
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average citizen/resident labor-market figures, not an immigration income threshold. The worker mean is dated, the minimum-wage increase had reported implementation uncertainty in July 2024, and no national median or maximum worker wage is published in the reviewed current sources.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official and international sources do not provide a sufficiently current, methodologically comparable individual cost-of-living budget. Salary figures should not be treated as a living-cost estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The official eVisa is an entry channel, not qualifying remote-worker residence. It cannot be treated as a citizenship-track status.
settlement_track.summary: Libya has no confirmed ordinary remote-worker, freelance, or independently accessible self-employed residence route. The eVisa is purpose-restricted entry, while current work and residence procedures require authorized local employment; general ten-year discretionary naturalization does not cure the missing qualifying route.
settlement_track.notes: A switch to an independently qualifying status would be necessary, but no such status for ordinary foreign-contract remote work was identified.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No published status fits ordinary work for a foreign client or employer without a Libyan employer, local work approval, investment, or discretionary special-expertise treatment. Visitor/eVisa entry is purpose-restricted and is not a settlement route.

data.notes: The negative route conclusion is supported by the current eVisa channel, 2026 implementation announcement, current foreign-worker procedure, 2021 recruitment rules, 2025 regularization requirements, and published immigration and anti-settlement laws. Confidence remains medium because Libya's online immigration materials are fragmented and the expanded Wafed/E-VISA systems do not publish a complete English category catalogue. Focused research found no digital-nomad, independent freelance, visitor-to-self-employed, direct permanent-residence, or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route.

data.selection_summary: Liechtenstein has no dedicated digital-nomad visa. A potentially qualifying exception is the EEA residence-permit lottery for applicants not gainfully employed in Liechtenstein: it expressly permits employment abroad, grants a B residence permit, and can lead to permanent residence after five years. Eligibility is limited to EEA nationals, excludes Swiss and UK nationals, and only eight non-employed permits are drawn annually. Because the applicant's nationality was not supplied, eligibility cannot be confirmed; a non-EEA applicant relying on an ordinary foreign software contract would not have a generally available matching route.

visa_application.title: Residence permit draw (B) — without gainful employment
visa_application.notes: This is the official route and application-information page. The time-limited online form was accepting preliminary-lottery submissions from 1 to 31 August 2026 when checked. It is usable only by eligible EEA nationals and is not a general digital-nomad application channel.

best_routes.route_name: EEA residence-permit lottery (B), non-employed in Liechtenstein

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed income threshold is published. Applicants must prove sufficient financial means so that social assistance is unnecessary.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed CHF amount published; sufficient financial means required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Proof of assets or financial means is requested after preliminary selection.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient financial means; no published minimum
income_requirement_display.notes: The authority applies a sufficient-resources test rather than a stated monthly-income floor.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page requires proof of financial means but does not state a prescribed number of statement or income months.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be an EEA national; Swiss and UK nationals cannot participate in this lottery.
No gainful activity may be undertaken in Liechtenstein, but employment abroad is expressly permitted.
Participation is through preliminary and final draws held twice yearly; only eight permits are drawn annually for the non-employed group.

After preliminary selection, provide requested documents including passport copy and proof of financial means; false declarations, an entry ban, or threats to public safety, order, or health are exclusion grounds.
Preliminary-draw fee CHF 100 and final-draw fee CHF 500.

initial_validity.value: B residence permit, authorizing residence for more than 12 months
initial_validity.notes: The route page does not state the precise initial card expiry. Residence permits are quota-limited and winning the draw is required.

extension_rules.notes: The reviewed route pages did not publish a complete renewal schedule. Renewal must be confirmed with the Migration and Passport Office before relying on the route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Winning the final draw results in assurance of a B residence permit, which authorizes residence for more than 12 months.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is qualifying residence, not visitor status, but access is restricted by nationality and lottery.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: An EEA national may apply for a permanent-residence permit after five years of continuous residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The permit holder must continue satisfying the applicable residence rules and observe absence limits.

path_to_citizenship.value: General simplified naturalization based on long-term residence requires 30 years of ordinary residence, with years from birth through age 20 counted twice and continuous residence during the last five years. Ordinary discretionary naturalization may be sought after at least ten years but requires municipal citizenship approval and is not treated here as a predictable ten-year entitlement.
path_to_citizenship.notes: German/civics, good-character, financial-capacity and prior-citizenship renunciation requirements apply.

summary.notes: This is an education-enrollment route, not an independent qualification-based migration program.

tax_residency_rule.value: Individuals are subject to unlimited taxation on their entire wealth and income when they have a Liechtenstein domicile or habitual residence. Domicile means presence with an intention to remain permanently; a continuous stay exceeding six months is deemed habitual residence from the beginning, subject to statutory exceptions.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A residence-permit holder who establishes a domicile may become fully taxable before six months; 183 days is not a universal safe harbor.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening maximum: the top national rate is 8%, and municipal tax is a surcharge of 150%–250% of national tax. At the maximum 250% surcharge, national plus municipal tax equals 28% of the national taxable-income base before considering deductions and the tariff formula. This is not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Current total for locally classified self-employed income: AHV 8.25%, IV 1.35%, FAK 2.1% and administration cost 0.585%. An ordinary employee's direct employee share is 4.9%, with 7.385% borne by the employer. Cross-border and foreign-employer coverage depends on social-security coordination and classification.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the CHF 368.55 annual minimum AHV/IV/FAK contribution when locally classified self-employed income is below CHF 3,000. It does not establish that the selected residence holder must register as locally self-employed.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker or general inbound tax holiday was identified. Ordinary wealth and earned-income taxation applies to resident individuals.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty relief and social-security coordination must be reviewed for the specific foreign employer/client country.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the foreign contract is employment or self-employment, where the employer is established, treaty residence, permanent-establishment risk, municipal residence, deductions, wealth taxation and applicable EEA/Swiss social-security coordination. The EEA lottery prohibits gainful activity in Liechtenstein but permits employment abroad; that immigration wording does not itself exempt foreign earnings from Liechtenstein tax.

taxation_system.value: Progressive national wealth-and-earned-income tax plus municipal surcharge. Single taxpayers receive a CHF 15,855 basic allowance; the national tariff rises through eight positive-rate bands to 8% above CHF 211,400. Municipalities add 150%–250% of the national tax, producing a maximum combined marginal screening rate of 28%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Unlimited liability arises with Liechtenstein domicile or habitual residence; a continuous stay over six months is habitual residence from its beginning.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide wealth and income for unlimited taxpayers, subject to statutory exclusions and tax treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees: 4.9% employee plus 7.385% employer for AHV/IV/FAK/VK. Locally classified self-employed persons: 12.285% including administration costs, with a CHF 368.55 annual minimum below CHF 3,000 income.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Bracket rates below are national statutory rates for single taxpayers. Municipal tax is added as 150%–250% of the computed national tax; therefore the combined marginal equivalent ranges from 2.5 times to 3.5 times the national marginal rate. USD thresholds use the approximate 22 July 2026 XE midpoint of USD 1.2293 per CHF.

tax_brackets.notes: Basic allowance; municipal surcharge on zero national tax remains zero.
Formula: 0.01 × taxable income minus CHF 159; municipal surcharge applies to computed tax.

taxation_system.notes: The 28% dashboard value is deliberately a maximum marginal screening rate, not an estimate of effective tax.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: There is no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. An eligible EEA lottery resident working abroad is taxed under ordinary resident rules if Liechtenstein domicile or habitual residence is established.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary resident individual; foreign employment or self-employment classification must be determined separately
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive; up to 28% combined national and maximum municipal marginal equivalent
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile triggers unlimited taxation; otherwise a continuous stay over six months is deemed habitual residence from the beginning.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Unlimited taxpayers are taxed on their entire income and wealth, subject to statutory exclusions and applicable double-tax treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Potentially 4.9% employee share for locally covered employment or 12.285% for locally classified self-employment. Foreign-employer and EEA coordination require an individual coverage determination.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed nomad tax. A self-employed AHV minimum and lottery fees may apply in their respective circumstances.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: CHF 368.55 annual minimum for locally classified self-employment below CHF 3,000 annual income; not automatically applicable to a foreign employee.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: CHF 100 preliminary-lottery fee plus CHF 500 final-lottery fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No route-specific fixed tax found. VAT registration is generally exempt below CHF 100,000 worldwide taxable turnover and also where a Liechtenstein-established business supplies services exclusively abroad, subject to the detailed VAT rules.
fixed_payments.notes: Mandatory health insurance is required in practice for residence, but no universal premium amount was established because premiums vary by insurer, plan, deductible and subsidies.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no assured six-month tax-free period if the person establishes a Liechtenstein domicile with an intention to remain. Without domicile, habitual residence is deemed from the beginning once continuous presence exceeds six months.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary worldwide-income rules apply; the maximum combined marginal screening rate is 28%, with treaty relief and municipal variation requiring calculation.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: If activities are classified as Liechtenstein self-employment, ordinary income tax, AHV/IV/FAK contributions and possible business/VAT obligations apply. Local self-employment may also conflict with the non-employed lottery permit's prohibition on Liechtenstein gainful activity.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Immigration permission for employment abroad and tax/social-security classification are separate legal questions.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Winning the final lottery leads directly to a B residence permit; no prior visitor-to-residence conversion is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: EEA nationals may apply for permanent residence after five years of continuous qualifying residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the 30-year long-residence naturalization rule minus the standard five-year permanent-residence point. This is a nominal sequence; age-based double-counting can shorten the calendar period for younger residents, while ordinary discretionary naturalization is a separate process.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Predictable simplified route based on long residence. Years from birth to age 20 count twice, and the last five years must be continuously resident.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official naturalization procedure says applicants are informed as decisions are made but publishes no typical total processing duration; no dependable current duration was found.

key_conditions.value: Continuous qualifying residence; German-language and civics knowledge; good character; economic self-sufficiency; cooperation with the authorities; and generally renunciation of prior citizenship. Permanent residence after five years requires continued eligibility and, for third-country applicants, A2 German and a civics test. The selected EEA lottery route is available only after winning a highly limited draw.
key_conditions.notes: Ordinary naturalization after ten years is discretionary and involves municipal citizenship approval, so the 30-year simplified long-residence route is used for the principal timeline.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The marriage must have been genuinely maintained for at least five years, and the applicant needs ten weighted years of ordinary Liechtenstein residence; years after marriage count twice, making five years the theoretical minimum when all qualifying residence occurs after marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage itself neither automatically grants nor removes Liechtenstein citizenship. An existing foreign marriage can support the facilitated route once recognized and once the residence, five-year maintained-marriage and other conditions are met.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Foreign civil-status events involving a Liechtenstein citizen must be recognized by the Civil Registry Office; the published recognition fee is CHF 150.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicant must be married to a Liechtenstein citizen whose citizenship was not itself acquired through marriage, maintain the marriage for at least five years, meet weighted residence, German/civics, character and financial-capacity requirements, and generally renounce prior citizenship. Separation, divorce, invalidity or false declarations can affect eligibility; documentary recognition and substantive review prevent reliance on a sham marriage.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage can accelerate naturalization but is not automatic citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Liechtenstein alone does not confer citizenship. Citizenship at birth follows from either parent being a Liechtenstein citizen; foundlings of unknown nationality are a narrow statutory exception.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Liechtenstein to two non-citizen migrant parents does not ordinarily become a citizen merely by birth. Narrow protections exist for foundlings and a facilitated application route for a person born stateless in Liechtenstein.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is not general jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Liechtenstein citizen from birth if either the father or mother is a Liechtenstein citizen, regardless of the other parent's migrant status.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage and civil-registration evidence may be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize either migrant parent. A migrant parent may have a separate family-reunification or family-life residence basis depending on custody, relationship and the sponsoring citizen parent's circumstances.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any parent application requires an independent immigration assessment.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is a Liechtenstein citizen, the child is a citizen by descent, but the migrant father does not automatically acquire citizenship or permanent residence. He may pursue family reunification and, if married to the citizen mother, the facilitated marriage-naturalization route after satisfying all requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Fatherhood of a citizen child and marriage to a citizen are legally distinct bases; neither creates automatic citizenship.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in international business and official information is often translated, but German is the sole national and official language and the English government pages have no legal force. Long-term settlement and naturalization require German, so English-only living is not a reliable integration strategy.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current official national English-proficiency percentage was found.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and no dependable evidence of broad administrative or workplace use was found. Applicants should expect German for government, integration and long-term settlement, using interpreters where necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: A country-specific proficiency or speaker-share statistic could not be established from the reviewed official sources.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the official CHF 7,401 median gross monthly wage using CHF 1 = USD 1.2293.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Liechtenstein has no generally applicable statutory minimum wage captured here, and the published first quartile is not an observed minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official publication reports median rather than arithmetic-average wages.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official statistics show an average gross rent of CHF 1,963 per month for a four-room dwelling in 2020 and a 3.6% unoccupied-dwelling rate at the end of 2025. The rent figure is useful context but stale and should not be treated as a current market quote.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: There is no digital-nomad visa. The potentially usable status is an ordinary B residence permit obtained through an EEA-only lottery, with just eight non-employed permits drawn annually.
settlement_track.summary: For an eligible EEA national who wins the non-employed lottery, the B permit is genuine qualifying residence: employment abroad is permitted, permanent residence is available after five continuous years, and long-residence naturalization is available under the general 30-year rule. The result remains uncertain for this applicant because nationality was not supplied; non-EEA ordinary remote workers lack a generally available equivalent.
settlement_track.notes: Conversion from B residence to permanent residence is required. The route is highly capacity-constrained but not temporary visitor or workcation status.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The EEA non-employed lottery expressly allows employment abroad and therefore fits the activity itself, but only eligible EEA nationals can apply. Swiss and UK nationals are excluded from the draw, and no generally available third-country remote-worker route exists.

data.selection_summary: Lithuania does not currently offer a dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Registering individual activity is a tax/business step, not an immigration status; the Startup Visa requires an approved innovative startup; ordinary work permits require Lithuanian employment. Lithuania therefore does not fit this selection, although study, startup, employment and family routes can independently lead to residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires the employment basis to continue; the Migration Department recommends applying four months before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying Lithuanian job can support a work-based temporary residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not independently usable with only a foreign employer.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General long-term residence may be possible after five years of qualifying continuous residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may be possible after 10 years and all other statutory requirements.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Lithuanian employer/job basis is required.

summary.value: Admission to full-time studies or a doctoral programme at a Lithuanian institution can support a temporary residence permit without a local employer. It is an education route, not a degree-holder residence route based merely on the applicant's existing foreign degree, and it does not grant permanent residence directly.
summary.notes: The applicant must actually enroll. The Migration Department states that study-based TRPs may be issued for two years; post-study or later employment options require a separate status analysis.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person can be Lithuanian tax resident through a permanent home, a stronger centre of personal/social/economic interests in Lithuania, presence for at least 183 days in a tax period, or presence for at least 280 days over successive tax periods with at least 90 days in one of them. Treaty tie-breakers may alter the result.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence may arise before day 183 through the home or centre-of-interests tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate for 2026, not an expected effective rate. The main aggregated-income brackets are 20%, 25% and 32%; individual-activity income can receive a credit producing a lower effective rate at modest profit levels.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Nominal 2026 combined individual-activity rates before optional pension accumulation: 12.52% VSD plus 6.98% PSD, generally assessed on 90% of taxable individual-activity income. This is not 19.5% of gross receipts.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 minimum monthly PSD contribution of €80.48 at €1 = US$1.1392. Exceptions apply when PSD is paid on another basis or the person is state-insured.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime was found. From 2026, individual-activity taxable profit up to €20,000 can produce a 5% PIT after the tax credit; the effective rate rises between €20,000 and €42,500 until reaching 20%. Above €42,500, the credit is unavailable and income is integrated with the main annual-rate rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This individual-activity mechanism is ordinary domestic taxation, not an immigration concession or nomad exemption.

taxes.caveats: Immigration eligibility and tax registration are separate. Classification depends on whether the arrangement is employment or genuine independent activity, where the work is physically performed, tax residence, permanent-establishment/fixed-base issues, social-security coordination and the applicable double-tax treaty. A foreign payer does not by itself prevent Lithuanian tax.

taxation_system.value: Lithuania applies progressive personal income taxation to aggregated annual income, with special category rules and credits. Residents generally report worldwide income, subject to treaty relief; non-residents are taxed on specified Lithuanian-source and fixed-base income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home or Lithuanian centre of interests; alternatively 183 days in a tax period, or 280 days over successive tax periods with at least 90 days in one period, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally: Lithuanian and foreign-source income. Non-residents: specified Lithuanian-source income and income attributable to a Lithuanian fixed base.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Individual-activity PIT credit can reduce effective PIT to 5% at taxable profit up to €20,000 and phases out through €42,500; no dedicated nomad regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: For 2026 individual activity, VSD is generally 12.52% and PSD 6.98% on 90% of taxable income, with caps, exceptions and optional additional pension accumulation. Minimum monthly PSD is €80.48 when applicable.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For 2026, the principal annual aggregated-income bands are 20% up to €83,237.40 (36 VDU), 25% from €83,237.40 to €138,729 (60 VDU), and 32% above €138,729. Certain non-employment income has separate 15% treatment up to category limits before aggregation rules apply.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Main aggregated annual income for 2026, subject to category-specific rules
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses €1 = US$1.1392.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual income over €83,237.40 and up to €138,729 (36–60 VDU)
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper boundary.
Top marginal rate, not effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The 2026 tax law and current tax-authority explanations materially improve the previous record, which lacked current brackets and self-employment contributions.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Lithuania has no confirmed digital-nomad residence route. A person living and working from Lithuania under another lawful status is subject to ordinary Lithuanian residence, source, PIT and social-insurance rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; ordinary employment, civil-contract or individual-activity treatment applies according to facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 32% top marginal PIT; individual activity may have a 5%–20% effective PIT range at taxable profit up to €42,500 before the main aggregation rules become relevant.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Home/centre-of-interests tests or the 183-day/280-day presence tests, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Lithuanian residents generally declare Lithuanian and foreign income; double-tax relief may exempt or credit tax depending on the income and treaty.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Individual activity generally carries 12.52% VSD and 6.98% PSD on 90% of taxable income; employment has different employee/employer payroll rules and cross-border coordination may apply.

fixed_payments.status: Applicable only if the person is validly registered and liable under ordinary rules; not a nomad-route fee.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Minimum monthly PSD is €80.48 in 2026 when applicable; annual reconciliation may increase the total.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: General TRP examination is €160 or €320 urgent, plus €45 or €90 for card personalisation. These fees relate to an actual qualifying residence application, not a nonexistent nomad application.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No dedicated fixed nomad tax or financial-transaction tax was identified. VAT and business-registration consequences depend on turnover, activity and legal form.
fixed_payments.notes: External-provider service charges may be additional and country-dependent.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Spending fewer than 183 days does not automatically make income tax-free: a Lithuanian home, centre of interests, Lithuanian-source work or fixed base can still matter, and immigration permission remains independently required.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident generally declares worldwide income. The payer being abroad does not by itself remove Lithuanian PIT; treaty relief and contract classification must be reviewed.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Genuine individual activity can be registered with VMI and generally triggers PIT plus VSD/PSD, but registration does not create a right of residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: These are ordinary-tax scenarios only. They should not be read as confirmation that a person may immigrate as a remote worker.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No matching ordinary remote-work route exists, so there is no meaningful time-to-TR for the supplied profile. Startup, study, family and Lithuanian-employment routes can give TR under their separate requirements.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General long-term-resident benchmark after five years of uninterrupted qualifying residence with a TRP. Absence, continuity, resources, insurance, language/integration and status-specific conditions must be verified.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the ordinary 10-year naturalisation residence requirement and the general five-year long-term-residence benchmark; citizenship law tests legal permanent residence, not simply possession of a PR card for exactly five years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation benchmark from qualifying residence. It is not reachable from a nonexistent remote-work route without first obtaining another lawful qualifying status.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Statutory workflow indicates up to three months to prepare and submit a naturalisation case to the Citizenship Affairs Commission and up to six months for consideration/decision. Suspensions or document defects can extend elapsed time.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalisation requires 10 years of lawful permanent residence, the right to permanent residence at filing/decision, Lithuanian-language and Constitution examinations, a legal source of support, oath/loyalty, no disqualifying circumstances and generally renunciation or loss of the other nationality unless an exception applies. Residence continuity and absences matter.
key_conditions.notes: Lithuania restricts dual citizenship outside statutory exceptions.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The facilitated rule generally requires seven years of marriage to and residence together in Lithuania with a Lithuanian citizen; narrower five-year treatment exists in specified cases such as marriage to certain deportee/political-prisoner descendants or after the citizen spouse's death, subject to the law.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support family-based residence and the facilitated naturalisation clock, but elapsed marriage abroad alone should not be assumed to satisfy the required period of living together in Lithuania.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Family residence and citizenship are separate applications.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants still face lawful-residence, Lithuanian-language, Constitution knowledge, oath, criminal/security and nationality requirements applicable to the facilitated provision. Authorities can verify cohabitation and whether the marriage is genuine; sham marriage, false documents or misleading statements can lead to refusal, cancellation and liability.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically confer PR or citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child acquires Lithuanian citizenship when either parent is Lithuanian. Birth in Lithuania alone does not normally confer citizenship; limited anti-statelessness rules cover children of stateless habitual residents and foundlings/children whose parents are unknown.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child of two foreign-citizen migrants does not acquire Lithuanian citizenship merely by being born in Lithuania. A child born in Lithuania to stateless parents habitually resident there can acquire citizenship under the statutory anti-statelessness rule.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary case of migrant parents who possess another nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Lithuanian citizen by descent if either parent was a Lithuanian citizen at birth, regardless of whether the migrant parent is the father or mother.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The birth must be properly registered; the migrant parent does not automatically become Lithuanian.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent whose Lithuanian-citizen child lives in Lithuania has an identified family-based temporary-residence application ground. This is a separate residence application, not automatic PR or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Custody, residence, dependency, genuine family life and documentary requirements can be examined.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Lithuanian-citizen child may apply for family-based temporary residence when the child lives in Lithuania. Fatherhood alone does not automatically grant residence, permanent residence or citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The same principle is not gender-specific.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard value: 44 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 10 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately lists eVisa destinations, which are not included here.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 170. Its methodology and rank differ from Henley, so figures should not be mixed across indexes.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in Vilnius and other urban/international settings, but not universal. The migration information centre reports 31.1% of residents speaking English as a foreign language, so Lithuanian remains important for government procedures and long-term integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The source is the IOM-linked Lithuanian Migration Information Centre rather than a commercial proficiency index.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is comparatively widespread: the migration information centre reports 60.6% of residents speaking it as a foreign language. No comparable current percentage for Ukrainian was established, so Ukrainian should not be assumed sufficient for routine services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian-language practicality varies by age, region and context. Lithuanian is required for official integration and naturalisation.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of €2,447.40 gross monthly earnings in May 2026 at €1 = US$1.1392.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national monthly median amount was extracted from the official sources. Eurostat published only a band showing Lithuania's 2024 minimum wage was between 50% and 60% of median earnings, which is insufficient for a precise median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the 2026 statutory gross minimum monthly wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of May 2026 gross average earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A precise current median was not established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary is published; earnings are unbounded and occupation-specific.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: 2026 statutory minimum monthly wage, payable only for unskilled work under the cited official explanation.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Whole-economy average for May 2026, excluding individual enterprises.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Current exact national monthly median not established from the inspected official pages.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No official national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly earnings before employee taxes; average excludes individual enterprises. Minimum is statutory gross minimum for unskilled work.
average_citizen_salary.period: May 2026 average; calendar-year 2026 minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: USD conversions are indicative ECB-rate conversions, not purchasing-power adjustments. Average earnings should not be interpreted as a software-engineer salary.

cost_of_living_note.value: Eurostat confirms wide price-level differences across the EU and provides Lithuania-specific data in its PPP dataset, but the inspected summary did not expose a reliable Lithuania headline value. No precise cost-of-living figure is asserted.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This cautious null-equivalent narrative avoids substituting a commercial crowdsourced city index for official national data.
