settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Lithuania has no confirmed nomad status to use even temporarily as a residence route. Visitor presence or individual-activity registration must not be treated as a settlement pathway.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route exists, so there is no route-specific path to permanent residence or citizenship. The applicant would need to qualify independently under a materially different status such as an approved startup, Lithuanian study, family reunification or Lithuanian employment.
settlement_track.notes: Lithuania's general five-year long-term-residence and 10-year naturalisation rules do not supply the missing initial immigration basis.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: An ordinary foreign employer/client contract is not a confirmed independent Lithuanian residence ground. Startup, local-employment and study routes materially change the applicant's activity and therefore are not matches.

data.notes: Audit result: the previous conclusion of ineligibility is preserved, but unsupported search-result and Wikipedia references were replaced with current migration, tax, social-insurance, citizenship, statistics and passport sources. At least 15 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected. Current filing rules, nationality-specific restrictions and live MIGRIS document lists should still be checked immediately before any application.

data.selection_summary: Luxembourg has a settlement-oriented permit for genuine self-employed businesses, but it requires a viable activity benefiting Luxembourg, local establishment, and the applicant’s physical presence for day-to-day management. The official residence categories reviewed contain no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route, while the EU Blue Card requires a Luxembourg employment contract. Luxembourg therefore does not fit the requested profile, even though a qualifying local self-employed business could eventually reach long-term residence and naturalisation.

visa_application.title: Conditions of residence for self-employed third-country workers
visa_application.notes: This is the official start page for the closest independent route, not a digital-nomad route. The temporary authorisation to stay normally must be requested and approved from abroad before entry. After arrival, the residence-permit application may be submitted through MyGuichet.lu or by post.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence permit for self-employed third-country workers

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly-income threshold is published. The applicant must instead demonstrate sufficient resources for the proposed Luxembourg activity and a viable business and financing plan.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed euro threshold is stated for initial admission.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published; sufficient resources and a viable Luxembourg business project are assessed
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a foreign-salary digital-nomad test.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page does not prescribe a fixed number of historical income months for initial admission; it requires project financing and supporting business evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply for temporary authorisation to stay from abroad before entering Luxembourg; in-country applications are generally inadmissible.
Possess the qualifications and professional permissions required for the proposed activity.
Show sufficient resources, a business and financing plan, viability and sustainability, and economic, social or cultural benefit to Luxembourg.
The activity must require the applicant’s presence in Luxembourg for day-to-day management.
Where a business permit is required, maintain a physical Luxembourg establishment and effective, permanent local management.
After entry, declare arrival, complete the medical check, provide an address, pay the EUR 80 residence-card fee, and apply for the residence permit.
Register with Luxembourg social security and personally pay self-employed contributions.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years
initial_validity.notes: The initial residence permit is valid for at most 3 years from the declaration of arrival.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for additional periods of up to 3 years while all conditions remain satisfied; apply within 2 months before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal evidence includes continuing activity, tax/VAT filings where applicable, Luxembourg social-security affiliation and an EUR 80 fee.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence after pre-entry authorisation, entry formalities and issuance of the self-employed residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The permit is available only for a qualifying Luxembourg self-employed project.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying holder may apply for EU long-term resident status after 5 years of continuous lawful residence, subject to resources, housing, insurance, integration and absence rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The self-employed permit is temporary residence; permanent/long-term status is a later application.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may be requested after 5 years of legal residence, with the final year uninterrupted, Luxembourgish-language and civic-knowledge requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This path applies to someone actually admitted on a qualifying residence status, not to an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker who does not meet the self-employed-project criteria.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this is a locally established business route rather than an ordinary foreign-client or foreign-employer remote-work route. A software consultant with foreign clients might attempt it only if the authorities accept a genuine Luxembourg-based business satisfying the national-interest, viability, establishment and physical-management tests; filing-level advice would be prudent.

rejected_routes.route_name: EU Blue Card for highly qualified salaried workers

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the published EUR 65,652 annual threshold, converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1567 on 14 August 2026.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 65,652 gross/year (EUR 5,471/month equivalent)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official page states an annual threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 65,652 gross/year
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR annual salary under a Luxembourg employment contract
income_requirement_display.notes: Conversion is informational and changes with exchange rates.

income_proof_months.notes: Eligibility is based on a signed employment contract lasting at least 6 months, not historical income statements.

key_requirements.requirement: A signed employment contract of at least 6 months with a Luxembourg employer.
Highly qualified work, the prescribed salary and proof of relevant higher professional qualifications.
Employer declaration of the vacancy to ADEM, although the Blue Card route is exempt from the labour-market test.

initial_validity.value: Temporary EU Blue Card residence
initial_validity.notes: Exact validity depends on the employment contract and statutory Blue Card rules.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continued qualifying highly paid Luxembourg employment.
extension_rules.notes: It is not usable for the applicant’s existing foreign contract.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, following approval and Luxembourg employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential EU long-term residence after qualifying residence periods and satisfaction of Blue Card aggregation rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not assessed as an independent foreign-contract route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential naturalisation after meeting the general 5-year legal-residence and integration requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The current applicant would first need qualifying local employment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Luxembourg employment contract and employer involvement are mandatory.

rejected_routes.route_name: Third-country student residence permit and post-study conversion

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The threshold is 80% of the current social-inclusion income; a stable current dollar amount was not extracted from the reviewed official page.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: 80% of the current social-inclusion income
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official route page states a formula rather than a fixed amount in the reviewed text.

income_requirement_display.value: 80% of current social-inclusion income
income_requirement_display.notes: Six months of bank statements may be used as evidence.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page requests a bank certificate and statements for the past 6 months when personal or parental funds are used.

key_requirements.requirement: Full-time enrolment in an eligible Luxembourg higher-education programme.
Sufficient resources, health coverage, passport and criminal-record documentation.
Post-study job-search or entrepreneurship conversion is limited to qualifying Luxembourg graduates and subsequent work must relate to their Luxembourg academic education.

initial_validity.value: At least 1 year, or the shorter duration of the study cycle

extension_rules.value: Renewable while enrolment and other conditions continue; apply within 2 months before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct student temporary residence after pre-entry authorisation and arrival formalities.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Student status is not itself a direct permanent-residence route; conversion to employment or qualifying self-employment is required, and the long-term-resident rules exclude students from applying while in student status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The treatment of study time in every later residence calculation should be verified for the individual conversion.

path_to_citizenship.value: Possible only through continued legal residence and satisfaction of the general naturalisation requirements, usually after conversion to another status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This route would require new study in Luxembourg and does not fit the existing foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for selection because it requires full-time Luxembourg study and any later professional conversion is separate and qualification-linked.

summary.value: Admission to eligible full-time higher education can support an independently requested student residence permit without a local employer. It is not direct permanent residence. Certain Luxembourg graduates may request a post-study job-search/entrepreneurship status or convert to qualifying salaried or self-employed activity, but this requires new Luxembourg study and does not validate ongoing ordinary foreign-contract remote work.
summary.notes: The applicant’s existing foreign university degree alone does not create an independent residence route. The degree may support a Blue Card application only together with qualifying Luxembourg employment.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident under domestic law when their tax domicile or habitual abode is in Luxembourg; treaty residence and the centre of vital interests can override a simple address analysis. A stay exceeding 6 months generally characterises habitual abode retroactively from arrival, but residence-permit ownership alone does not establish tax residence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The precise outcome depends on permanent home, habitual abode, centre of vital interests and any applicable double-tax treaty.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal base income-tax rate, not an expected effective rate. The employment-fund surcharge can increase the tax charged.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Indicative aggregation for a self-employed person in 2026: health care 5.60%, sickness cash benefits 0.50%, pension 17%, accident 0.65%, occupational health 0.14% and dependency 1.40%. Dependency insurance uses a reduced base, accident rates can be adjusted, and optional Employers’ Mutual Insurance is excluded, so 25.29% is not applied uniformly to one unadjusted base.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate initial minimum monthly social-security burden for a main self-employed activity: about EUR 691, using the EUR 2,771.33 June 2026 minimum contribution base, the listed mandatory rates, the dependency allowance equal to one quarter of that base, and EUR 1 = USD 1.1567. Actual CCSS billing is reconciled to professional income.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax regime was found. Luxembourg has an inbound highly skilled worker relocation-expense regime, but it concerns qualifying workers recruited or posted from abroad and does not make a foreign-contract remote worker immigration-eligible.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility and exempt expense caps under the inbound regime require professional tax advice.

taxes.caveats: Luxembourg tax depends on actual residence, source and character of income, permanent-establishment risk, business form, social-security coordination and treaty position. Foreign income may be exempt under a treaty but still used to determine the rate. The 42% figure is a top marginal screening rate, not the effective tax burden.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with a 0% band and marginal rates from 8% to 42%, plus the employment-fund surcharge. Residents report worldwide income; treaty-exempt foreign income may influence the applicable rate.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Tax domicile or habitual abode in Luxembourg, subject to centre-of-vital-interests and treaty analysis; more than 6 months generally indicates habitual abode.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident taxpayers report worldwide exempt and non-exempt income. Non-residents normally pay Luxembourg tax on Luxembourg-source income; treaties may exempt foreign income with progression.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. A separate inbound highly skilled employee expense regime exists but is not an ordinary foreign-contractor regime.
taxation_system.social_security: A Luxembourg self-employed person pays both sides personally. Mandatory 2026 rates include health 6.10%, pension 17%, accident 0.65%, dependency 1.40% on its adjusted base and occupational health 0.14%; first affiliation is provisionally billed using at least the minimum wage when no better income estimate exists.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Rates shown are the class-1 base schedule applicable from tax year 2025. The employment-fund surcharge and tax class affect final liability.

tax_brackets.notes: Employment-fund surcharge is additional.

taxation_system.notes: The rate schedule is official and current for tax year 2025 onward as displayed on the tax authority page. Individual effective taxation requires calculation using tax class, deductions, surcharge, treaty and business structure.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Luxembourg has no confirmed dedicated digital-nomad immigration or tax category. If an applicant independently qualifies as a Luxembourg self-employed resident, ordinary progressive income tax and self-employed social-security rules would apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; closest comparison is ordinary Luxembourg self-employment
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–42% progressive base rates; 42% is the top marginal screening rate, plus employment-fund surcharge
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Tax domicile or habitual abode, commonly indicated by a stay exceeding 6 months, subject to centre-of-vital-interests and treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents report worldwide income. Treaty-exempt income may remain exempt but affect the rate applied to taxable Luxembourg income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad regime. The inbound highly skilled worker expense regime is tied to qualifying recruited or posted workers and does not cure the immigration mismatch.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A qualifying self-employed resident registers with CCSS, personally pays mandatory health, pension, accident and dependency contributions, and is provisionally assessed on at least the minimum wage when no better initial professional-income estimate exists.

fixed_payments.status: No universal digital-nomad fixed tax. A main self-employed activity has a contribution floor and administrative fees.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Approximately EUR 691/month (about USD 799) at the June 2026 minimum contribution base under the stated assumptions; reconciled to actual professional income.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: EUR 80 residence-permit fee; normally EUR 50 stamp duty if a business permit is required.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT, municipal and business obligations depend on activity and turnover; no universal monthly amount was established.
fixed_payments.notes: The social-security estimate excludes optional mutual insurance and may change with accident adjustment, dependency-base rules and subsequent income reconciliation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay does not itself authorise ordinary foreign-contract work or create a digital-nomad residence route. Tax residence is fact-specific and can arise from domicile or centre-of-vital-interests considerations, not only day counting.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no confirmed remote-worker permit. A person nevertheless lawfully resident and tax-resident would normally report worldwide income, with treaty relief assessed separately.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A person accepted under the self-employed permit registers the activity and social security locally, pays ordinary progressive tax and self-employed contributions, and may need a EUR 50 business permit plus EUR 80 residence-card fee.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax treatment is described for the closest lawful self-employed scenario, not for a nonexistent Luxembourg digital-nomad status.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying self-employed applicant receives temporary residence through the initial admission process; there is no multi-year prerequisite. This does not mean an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker qualifies.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: EU long-term resident status generally requires 5 years of continuous lawful residence. Temporary absences under 6 consecutive months and no more than 10 months total in 5 years normally do not interrupt continuity.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalisation eligibility also starts after 5 years of legal residence, so acquisition of long-term residence is not stated as a prerequisite and no additional post-PR waiting period is prescribed.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest general eligibility after 5 years of legal residence, assuming the final year is uninterrupted and all language, civic and good-repute requirements are met. This timeline applies only after admission to a qualifying status.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official page states that the Minister of Justice grants or rejects naturalisation within 8 months after submission.

key_conditions.value: For long-term residence: 5 years of continuous lawful residence, stable and sufficient resources, suitable housing, health insurance, social-security history, integration evidence and public-order compliance. For naturalisation: 5 years of legal residence with the final year uninterrupted, Luxembourgish-language test, Vivre ensemble course or test, and acceptable criminal history. Luxembourg permits multiple nationality; the official naturalisation page does not require general renunciation.
key_conditions.notes: The five-year settlement timeline is credible for a person who genuinely qualifies for the self-employed residence permit, but not for the requested ordinary foreign-contract profile.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A spouse residing in Luxembourg has no stated minimum marriage-duration waiting period for nationality by option. A spouse who is not resident in Luxembourg normally needs 3 immediately preceding years of marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing valid marriage to a Luxembourgish citizen can support nationality by option. If the applicant resides in Luxembourg, the official page does not state a minimum marriage duration; if living abroad, 3 immediately preceding years of marriage are generally required.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not itself make the spouse automatically Luxembourgish.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must pass the Luxembourgish-language evaluation and complete or pass the Vivre ensemble civic requirement, provide the marriage certificate and spouse’s nationality certificate, and satisfy statutory good-repute rules. The marriage must be legally valid and accurately documented; fraudulent or sham arrangements can cause refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The option route accelerates nationality eligibility but should not be treated as automatic citizenship or as a substitute for a genuine relationship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Luxembourg combines descent with restricted birth-based rules: immediate double jus soli when a parent was also born in Luxembourg, safeguards for statelessness or unknown parents, and automatic acquisition at age 18 subject to child- and parent-residence conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically at birth in the ordinary case. Immediate citizenship applies if a parent was also born in Luxembourg or under statelessness/unknown-parent safeguards. Otherwise, a Luxembourg-born child of foreign parents automatically acquires nationality at 18 if they lived legally and habitually in Luxembourg for the preceding 5 years and, for births after 1 July 2013, one parent lived legally and habitually there for the 12 months before birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Therefore the simple boolean is false for two ordinary first-generation migrant parents, despite important conditional exceptions.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Luxembourgish by descent when either parent is Luxembourgish at birth or when filiation is established.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father does not automatically acquire citizenship from the child.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A parent of a Luxembourgish minor may acquire nationality by option after at least 5 years of legal residence, with the final year uninterrupted, plus Luxembourgish-language and civic requirements. Parenthood is not automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any separate family-residence right must be assessed under the applicable family and EU-law provisions.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child is Luxembourgish, the migrant father may use the parent-of-a-Luxembourgish-minor nationality option only after 5 years of legal Luxembourg residence, the final year uninterrupted, and completion of language and civic requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A citizen child does not automatically naturalise the father; legal parentage and all option conditions must be established.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026 for rank/access; Passport Index 2026 for separated entry categories

rank.notes: Current 2026 Henley ranking page reviewed on 15 August 2026: Luxembourg is joint 4th.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley access score counts destinations accessible without obtaining a prior visa and therefore includes visa-on-arrival and similar qualifying access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category count; methodology differs from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index lists 41 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. Its separate visa-free count is 122 and mobility score is 173, so these category counts should not be combined with Henley’s 186 score.

passport.notes: Henley is used for the headline rank and access score. Passport Index is used only because it separately reports visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA and visa-required categories.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High in international, financial, EU-institution and many business settings. The government describes English as the lingua franca of the large international community and frequently used in business and finance, although French, Luxembourgish or German remains important for administration and daily integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English-only living is most practical in Luxembourg City and international workplaces, but it does not remove immigration or Luxembourgish-language naturalisation requirements.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited compared with Luxembourgish, French, German and English. No reviewed official source identified Russian or Ukrainian as a generally used administrative or business language, so either language should be treated as community support rather than a dependable standalone language for work or government procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official description of Luxembourg’s language environment; no reliable nationwide Russian/Ukrainian proficiency rate was established.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of Eurostat’s EUR 83,000 annual full-time-adjusted 2024 salary: EUR 6,916.67/month × 1.1567 USD/EUR.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current directly comparable nationwide median monthly employee wage was established. Eurostat reports a 2022 median gross hourly figure, while STATEC’s 2025 publication reports household disposable-income and living-standard measures; neither is substituted for a current monthly salary.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the EUR 2,771.33 gross monthly statutory minimum for an unqualified adult employee from 1 June 2026.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: 2024 annual full-time-adjusted salary divided by 12 and converted at the 14 August 2026 ECB reference rate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Eurostat confirms median gross hourly earnings of EUR 24.0 for October 2022, but no current comparable national monthly employee median was confirmed. An hourly figure cannot be converted to a monthly value without imposing an assumed hours basis.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No authoritative national maximum salary is published, so there is no factual maximum to convert to USD. STATEC’s 2022 Structure of Earnings Survey reports EUR 135,797 gross/year as D9—the threshold above which the top 10% earn—not the highest salary. Eurostat likewise defines D9 as the minimum earnings of the highest-paid decile, while detailed employee-level earnings are protected or researcher-access microdata rather than a published national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 2,771.33 gross/month for an unqualified adult employee; EUR 3,325.59 for a qualified adult employee, from 1 June 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: These are statutory minimum wages, not observed minimum earnings.

average_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 83,000 gross/year, equivalent to about EUR 6,916.67/month
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Eurostat annual full-time-adjusted salary per employee for 2024.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed sources do not provide a current comparable national monthly median salary. Eurostat’s EUR 24.0 figure is gross hourly earnings for October 2022, and STATEC’s newer report concerns household-income measures.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Official sources publish no national maximum
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Luxembourg has no statutory salary ceiling, and the reviewed official wage-distribution publications do not report a national maximum. The closest authoritative upper-tail statistic is 2022 D9 of EUR 135,797 gross/year, but D9 means one employee in ten earns more than that amount and therefore cannot be labelled a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory gross monthly minimum wage and Eurostat annual full-time-adjusted average salary per employee; official 2022 earnings-distribution sources checked separately for a maximum
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 1 June 2026; average reference year 2024; earnings-distribution reference year 2022; USD conversion at 14 August 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is a full-time-adjusted macroeconomic indicator and may be influenced by Luxembourg’s high-wage sectors and cross-border workforce. It is not an immigration income threshold. Focused review of official wage-distribution data found deciles and medians but no publishable national maximum; D9 was not misrepresented as a maximum.

cost_of_living_note.value: Housing is a major affordability constraint. STATEC reported that dwelling prices stabilised in late 2025 after earlier declines and rose 1.6% over 2025, while its social-cohesion report continued to identify substantial housing-related pressure and inequality. No single national monthly cost-of-living figure was used because household size and location materially change the result.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Salary comparisons should account for unusually high housing costs, especially around Luxembourg City.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Luxembourg has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status. Visitor or Schengen short-stay permission is not a settlement route and does not legalise this residence-and-work scenario.
settlement_track.summary: A genuine Luxembourg self-employed business permit can support long-term residence and naturalisation, but the official criteria require local economic substance, benefit and day-to-day management. Because ordinary work under the applicant’s existing foreign contract is not a confirmed qualifying activity, there is no citizenship track from the requested remote-work scenario.
settlement_track.notes: A switch is required in the practical sense: the applicant must obtain qualifying Luxembourg employment, undertake qualifying Luxembourg study followed by conversion, or establish a self-employed project that independently satisfies the substantive local-business tests. Simply registering a nominal sole proprietorship after visitor entry is not a valid route; initial self-employed authorisation normally must be approved before entry.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker route was found among the current official categories. The closest independent permit requires a substantive Luxembourg self-employed project, local establishment and physical day-to-day management; the Blue Card requires a Luxembourg employer.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Luxembourg result using 32 distinct directly relevant canonical URLs, including 6 focused official earnings URLs not present in the previous source set. The route and selection conclusions remain unchanged. The unexplained maximum-salary null was resolved cautiously: official STATEC and Eurostat sources publish deciles, medians and averages but no national maximum, so the USD maximum remains null with evidence and the local field is explicitly marked Official sources publish no national maximum rather than inventing a ceiling or mislabelling D9.

data.selection_summary: Madagascar has transformable immigrant visas for specified purposes, including locally authorized employment, investment or company management, study, retirement, family reunification and missions. Current official route lists do not provide a digital-nomad, foreign-contract remote-worker or ordinary freelancer category; tourist status is expressly non-transformable. The applicant’s foreign software contract therefore does not establish a qualifying independent residence or citizenship route.

visa_application.title: Visas d’entrée et de séjour à Madagascar
visa_application.notes: This official page identifies the eligible immigrant purposes and links to the government submission system for applicants residing where Madagascar lacks a diplomatic mission. It is not an application route for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist eVisa, visa on arrival or other non-immigrant stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists because this is visitor status.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying income requirement was published for remote work.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; visitor status only
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial requirements for ordinary visitors are not a substitute for residence eligibility.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker income-history requirement applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport and ordinary visitor-entry documentation appropriate to the applicant’s nationality and intended stay.
Non-immigrant purposes include tourism, conferences, family events, medical visits and business visits, but not residence.

initial_validity.value: Non-immigrant stays may be extended only up to a cumulative three months.
initial_validity.notes: The exact initial visa duration and fee depend on the requested visitor period.

extension_rules.value: Extendable locally up to a cumulative maximum of three months.
extension_rules.notes: Extension does not make the status transformable into long-stay residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None from this status: the official EDBM instructions expressly state that non-immigrant visas are not transformable into long-stay status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying immigrant visa must be obtained through the appropriate procedure instead.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No permanent-residence path exists from ordinary visitor status.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Madagascar’s official consular instructions make short-stay status non-transformable and require a resident-card application only after entry on a qualifying immigrant visa. Articles 27–28 of the current Nationality Code require five years of habitual residence maintained through the naturalisation decree. The reviewed law and immigration rules do not classify a maximum-three-month visitor stay as habitual residence or provide any conversion chain from that stay; accordingly, no visitor-to-citizenship path can be stated.

rejected_routes.notes: This is independently obtainable for travel, but it neither authorizes a remote-worker residence category nor converts into qualifying residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum salary threshold was published on the reviewed official route page.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum salary amount was identified; employment authorization and an endorsed contract are required.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; locally authorized employment required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a sponsorship-based employment route, not a foreign-contract remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period was published.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment contract endorsed by the Malagasy labor ministry.
Receipt confirming an employment-authorization application.
Employer certificate and the Malagasy employing company’s commercial, tax and statistical registration documents.

initial_validity.value: One-month immigrant visa, transformable and extendable into long-stay residence.
initial_validity.notes: The immigrant must complete the resident-card procedure after arrival.

extension_rules.value: Renewal must be filed three months before expiry and is subject to the same substantive conditions as the initial visa.
extension_rules.notes: Continued local employment authorization remains material.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply for a resident card with the Ministry of Interior within one month after arrival using the original supporting documents.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This pathway is unavailable on the applicant’s foreign contract alone.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The finance law lists fees for stays exceeding five years and definitive-stay visas, but the reviewed sources did not establish an automatic eligibility timeline from the worker category.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalisation may be requested after five years of habitual residence if all statutory conditions are met.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No automatic citizenship entitlement follows from employment residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant must have locally authorized employment and employer documentation.

rejected_routes.route_name: Transformable immigrant visa — investor or Malagasy company manager

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No personal monthly-income threshold was published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility is based on a registered Malagasy company or investment activity rather than a stated monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly threshold; registered local company/investment required
income_requirement_display.notes: Company formation and local business substance make this unsuitable for ordinary remote work under the selection rules.

income_proof_months.notes: No personal income-history period was published.

key_requirements.requirement: Registered company statutes, existence declaration, statistical card, commercial-register extract and tax-identification documents.
Company bank certificate and evidence of tax payment.
A corporate manager must also provide the registered appointment resolution.
The 2023 Investment Law limits the investor visa to an associate or shareholder of a local company; professional and specific-skill worker visas likewise require a local-company role or employment.

initial_validity.value: One-month immigrant visa, transformable and extendable into long-stay residence.
initial_validity.notes: The transformable-visa fee published by EDBM is MGA 140,000.

extension_rules.value: Long-stay renewal remains subject to the applicable investment or company-management conditions.
extension_rules.notes: The reviewed sources did not establish automatic renewal or permanent residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The transformable visa supports a post-arrival resident-card application.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This requires a genuine locally registered business basis.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Long-duration and definitive-stay fees exist, but no automatic investor-to-permanent-residence timeline was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalisation may become available after five years of habitual residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Investment does not create an automatic citizenship entitlement in the reviewed law.

rejected_routes.notes: Independently initiated in principle, but rejected because it requires a Malagasy company, investment activity and local business substance rather than ordinary services for a foreign client.

summary.value: A long-study transformable visa is available without a local employer and requires a diploma, enrollment certificate and scholarship or proof of resources. It can support a resident-card application after arrival, but no direct permanent-residence or degree-based skilled-migration route was confirmed; it does not fit continued ordinary foreign-contract remote work.
summary.notes: Study must be the genuine immigration purpose. A university degree by itself does not qualify the applicant for residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person is treated as resident if they have a home available in Madagascar as owner, usufructuary or tenant, or if Madagascar is their main place of stay. Residence can therefore arise before a simple 183-day threshold in practice.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The current individual summary does not present 183 days as the sole test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal IRSA salary-income rate, not an expected effective rate. Business or service income may be taxed under different rules.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For an ordinary employee, the reviewed rules show 1% employee CNaPS plus 1% statutory health contribution, each subject to the applicable ceiling. Employer-side contributions are additional. No mandatory equivalent for an unsupported foreign-contract freelancer was confirmed.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal USD-denominated monthly payment applies. IRSA has a minimum MGA 3,000 tax, while business minimum taxes and contributions depend on classification and registration.

special_tax_regimes.value: An individual business below MGA 400 million annual turnover may be subject to synthetic tax at 5% of turnover, potentially reduced by 70%, with a minimum tax of MGA 16,000 or MGA 150,000 depending on activity. This is a small-business regime, not a digital-nomad concession.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Filing-level advice is required before treating foreign software services as salary, Malagasy business income or foreign-supplier income.

taxes.caveats: Madagascar has no special digital-nomad tax status. A person living and performing work in Madagascar may incur Malagasy tax even when paid by a foreign employer; contract characterization, local business registration, permanent-establishment issues and any applicable tax treaty must be reviewed professionally.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: progressive IRSA on employment income, with separate IR or synthetic-tax treatment for individual business income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Home available in Madagascar or main place of stay in Madagascar.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident employment income is subject to IRSA on a worldwide basis. Salary received in Madagascar remains taxable even when paid by a foreign employer; business income performed in Madagascar can be subject to IR or synthetic tax.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Synthetic tax may apply below MGA 400 million annual turnover; no digital-nomad or inbound-worker exemption was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary employees generally bear 1% CNaPS and 1% statutory health contributions, subject to ceilings; employer-side pension, health and training contributions are additional. Applicability to an independently registered foreign contractor was not established.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: IRSA is 0% through MGA 350,000 per month, then 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% marginal bands. The dashboard’s 20% figure is the top marginal screening rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly taxable income up to MGA 350,000
tax_brackets.notes: A minimum salary-income tax of MGA 3,000 applies notwithstanding the scale.
Top marginal rate, not the effective rate on the whole salary.

taxation_system.notes: PwC’s Madagascar individual pages were last reviewed on 18 November 2025. The official 2026 DGI code repository was also checked, but its document interface did not expose an easily verifiable freelancer-specific calculation.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad immigration or tax category was identified. A resident remote employee may fall under IRSA up to 20%; an independently registered service business may instead fall under IR or synthetic tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary employment or business classification applies
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–20% progressive IRSA; 20% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: A home available in Madagascar or Madagascar as the main place of stay can establish residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident employment income is taxable on a worldwide basis, and salary received in Madagascar can be subject to IRSA even when the employer is established abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If treated as an employee, employee-side CNaPS and statutory health contributions generally total 2%, subject to ceilings. The foreign-employer filing mechanism and any self-employed contribution obligation require local advice.

fixed_payments.status: No universal digital-nomad fixed payment
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed freelancer contribution was confirmed; employee contributions are percentage-based and capped.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The official transformable immigrant-visa fee is MGA 140,000 for several immigrant categories. The 2026 finance law lists MGA 292,500 for stays over three months through three years, MGA 390,000 for more than three through five years, and MGA 487,500 for more than five years or definitive stay. These fees do not create remote-worker eligibility.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: IRSA has a minimum MGA 3,000 payment; synthetic-tax minimums can be MGA 16,000 or MGA 150,000 depending on activity.
fixed_payments.notes: Amounts are state or tax charges, not monthly remote-worker income requirements.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe tax-free day-count assumption is available because having a home available or Madagascar as the main place of stay may establish residence independently of a simple 183-day threshold.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Foreign-paid salary received while resident and working in Madagascar may be subject to progressive IRSA up to 20%, with local filing potentially required when the employer is not established in Madagascar.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Locally performed business services may be subject to ordinary IR or the turnover-based synthetic tax; tax registration, VAT and social-security consequences require classification-specific advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax analysis is contextual only because the applicant has no confirmed immigration route authorizing this remote-work arrangement.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying foreign-contract remote-worker route exists. Other eligible immigrant categories can seek a resident card within one month after arrival.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Fees exist for long-duration and definitive stays, but an automatic permanent-residence timetable was not established for the rejected routes.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on five years of habitual residence before application, not a clearly defined number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: There is no total timeline from the applicant’s foreign-contract profile because no qualifying residence route was found. Under another lawful status, ordinary naturalisation generally requires five years of habitual residence and remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current Nationality Code states that naturalisation is granted by decree but does not prescribe or report a typical processing duration; no current official service standard or aggregate processing-time statistic was published in the official nationality and justice materials reviewed.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalisation generally requires five years of habitual residence maintained through the decree date, adulthood, good character, qualifying health, no disqualifying serious conviction and assimilation into the Malagasy community, including sufficient Malagasy-language knowledge. Grant remains discretionary by decree.
key_conditions.notes: The reviewed law does not make naturalisation automatic after five years. Treatment of an applicant’s existing nationality should be verified before filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The operative reviewed code provides a declaration-at-marriage mechanism specifically for a foreign woman marrying a Malagasy man; the declaration must be made no later than the marriage ceremony or transcription abroad. This is not a gender-neutral zero-year route.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage supports a family-reunification immigrant visa. For nationality, the special provision reviewed is narrow: a foreign woman must declare her intention no later than the marriage or foreign-marriage transcription. A foreign husband of a Malagasy woman was not shown to receive the same direct marriage declaration route and may need ordinary naturalisation.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A pending legislative comparison contains proposed gender-neutral reforms, but proposals were not treated as current law.

requirements_and_risks.value: Family-reunification residence requires the marriage certificate and the applicable sponsor documents. The government may oppose marriage-based nationality acquisition, and a marriage contracted in bad faith can lose its nationality effect; genuine-marriage and civil-registration evidence are essential.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not create an automatic residence-to-citizenship shortcut for every foreign spouse.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is principally transmitted by a Malagasy parent. Birth in Madagascar alone is insufficient; the law separately protects certain children of unknown parents and foundlings. The 2026 exceptional birth-registration law expressly confirms that registration of a birth does not itself attribute Malagasy nationality.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Madagascar to two ordinary foreign parents does not acquire Malagasy citizenship merely by birth. Special provisions may protect a foundling or a child of unknown parents presumed to have a Malagasy parent.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent residence of the parents was not identified as a substitute for Malagasy parentage.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Malagasy when either the father or mother is Malagasy, regardless of whether the child was born inside or outside marriage, subject to establishing filiation and civil registration.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2016 reform equalized transmission through Malagasy mothers and fathers.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent does not automatically obtain residence, permanent residence or citizenship because the child is Malagasy. Current official family-reunification materials cover a spouse of a Malagasy citizen and spouses or dependent children joining a principal immigrant or resident parent; they do not establish reverse sponsorship by a Malagasy child.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The Ministry of Interior checklist requires a birth or marriage record plus the resident documents of parents or a spouse already established in Madagascar, and the EDBM checklist likewise asks for the visa of parents or a spouse already in Madagascar. Article 14 of the 2023 Investment Law defines family-reunification beneficiaries as the principal visa holder’s spouse and dependent children. The current Nationality Code provides ordinary discretionary naturalisation rules but no automatic or shortened nationality rule for a foreign parent of a Malagasy child. Because none of these current official sources publishes a standalone parent-of-Malagasy-child category, any residence request based on the child’s best interests or dependency would require case-specific confirmation from the Ministry of Interior rather than being represented as an entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Malagasy, the child can be Malagasy by descent. The foreign father gains no automatic citizenship from the child and would need an independently valid family-residence or naturalisation basis.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A foreign husband should not assume he qualifies for the female-spouse nationality declaration provision.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on the review date; methodology differs from Henley.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 35 visa-on-arrival destinations and 4 eTA destinations shown by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 68. These figures can differ from Henley because the indexes classify electronic and arrival permissions differently.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be workable within international businesses, tourism and an English-speaking remote team, but Malagasy and French are the official and broadly relevant administrative languages. French is much more practical for immigration, tax, housing and local services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The assessment of day-to-day practicality is an inference from the documented official-language environment; no nationwide current English-proficiency measure was located.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official or generally documented working language, so a migrant should expect to rely on French, Malagasy or translation assistance.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official-language sources; no reliable national statistics for Russian or Ukrainian usage were found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximation: the 2021–2022 EPM reports MGA 2,747,374 annual average salaried-employment income, or about MGA 228,948 monthly; conversion uses the report’s later official average exchange-rate series near MGA 4,578 per USD. It is not a current 2026 wage.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official household survey reports an average, but no nationwide median salaried-worker income was located.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current statutory minimum is available in MGA, but no same-date official USD exchange rate was captured, so an approximate USD value is withheld.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Historical survey approximation, not a 2026 salary estimate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The EPM 2021–2022 publishes average salaried-employment income but no nationwide median employee-income statistic in the reviewed tables.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official survey publishes averages and sector measures, not a meaningful nationwide maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.value: MGA 300,000 per month (non-agricultural general regime); MGA 304,300 agricultural, effective 1 March 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: These are statutory minimum hiring wages, not observed minimum earnings.

average_salary_local_currency.value: MGA 2,747,374 annual average salaried-employment income, approximately MGA 228,948 per month
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Based on the EPM 2021–2022 and published in 2024; it predates the current 2026 minimum wage.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed national household survey does not publish a nationwide median salaried-worker income amount.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Sector averages are available, but the official report does not define or publish a national maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum for 2026; separate historical annual average salaried-employment income from the EPM 2021–2022
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 2026-03-01; average measured in 2021–2022 and published in 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: The historical survey average is below the current statutory minimum because the measures refer to different periods and may reflect informality, incomplete employment and different coverage. Neither figure is an immigration income threshold.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The household survey reports expenditure and living-condition indicators but does not publish a current standardized monthly cost-of-living budget for a foreign remote worker; such a figure is therefore not inferred.
