settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route was found. Citizenship would require first qualifying under a different immigrant category, maintaining habitual residence and then seeking discretionary naturalisation; tourist status cannot be converted.
settlement_track.notes: The general five-year naturalisation condition does not cure the absence of a qualifying initial residence basis for this applicant.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official immigrant purposes require another substantive basis, such as locally authorized employment, a registered Malagasy investment/company, study, retirement, family reunification or mission work. A foreign software contract alone is not listed.

data.notes: This focused audit inspected 17 distinct directly relevant URLs, including six official URLs not present in the previous source set. The negative route conclusion is supported by current official immigration pages and the 2023 Investment Law. The two flagged citizenship notes are now tied to precise rules: visitor status is non-transformable and cannot be mapped to the Code’s five-year habitual-residence requirement, while current family-reunification sources do not publish a reverse sponsorship category for the foreign parent of a Malagasy child. Confidence remains medium overall because Madagascar’s online material still does not provide a consolidated general permanent-residence timetable, an official typical naturalisation processing time, or a freelancer-specific tax and social-security calculation.

data.selection_summary: Malawi does not publish a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Its independently accessible Business Residence Permit is for productive-sector investors/self-employed proprietors and requires at least USD 50,000 in external investment funds; the general permanent-residence page does not confirm that foreign remote work alone qualifies or is authorized. Visitor, temporary-residence, student, and employer-sponsored permits therefore do not satisfy the requested citizenship-oriented remote-work profile.

visa_application.title: Malawi e-Permit Portal
visa_application.notes: Official online permit portal. It lists temporary residence, study, employment, business residence, permanent residence, diplomatic, and technical-assistance permits, but no digital-nomad or dedicated foreign-remote-worker category.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is published. The route instead requires at least USD 50,000 in externally sourced investment funds.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No MWK monthly-income threshold; minimum USD 50,000 external investment funds
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is capital for a qualifying business or investment, not recurring remote-work income.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 50,000 minimum external investment funds; no monthly-income test published
income_requirement_display.notes: The requirement is not comparable to a digital-nomad monthly-income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page does not prescribe a monthly income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Carry on a business, profession, or occupation for gain as a self-employed person, partner, or proprietor.
Invest at least USD 50,000 originating from a legal source outside Malawi.
Operate in manufacturing, mining, agriculture, fisheries, tourism, financial services, or another productive sector.
Submit supporting business information; the Minister decides, and operations must not begin before approval.

initial_validity.value: 5 years
initial_validity.notes: Validity runs from approval.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for successive 5-year periods; apply about 3 months before expiry and demonstrate that the business remains viable and exists.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The permit itself authorizes residence for the approved business, profession, or self-employment activity.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Ordinary software work for a foreign client without qualifying investment and productive local business substance is not the published target.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate Permanent Residence Permit may be requested after at least 5 years of ordinary residence, but approval is ministerial and conversion from a BRP is not guaranteed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This possible path does not cure the entry route's mismatch with ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_citizenship.value: General alien naturalisation becomes available after more than 7 years' residence, subject to language, character, solvency, valid-status, and discretionary requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is separate from BRP approval and is not guaranteed.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected: although independently applicable and residence-oriented, this is a substantial-investment/productive-business route rather than an ordinary foreign-client freelancer or remote-worker permit.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permanent Residence Permit, including assured-income category

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The page mentions people of assured income but publishes no amount, calculation, or evidence period.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monetary assured-income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Assured income mentioned for retirees; no threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: The official page does not establish an ordinary remote-worker category or financial threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No evidence period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Potential categories include foreign nationals seeking permanent residence, foreign wives of Malawians, elderly assured-income retirees, over-age dependants of PRP holders, and persons ordinarily resident for at least 5 years.
Submit a PRP application with supporting information and processing fee; the Minister decides.

initial_validity.value: Permanent
initial_validity.notes: The permit authorizes permanent residence if approved.

extension_rules.notes: No ordinary renewal rule is stated because the status is permanent.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; this is described as a permanent-residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence if the Minister approves the application.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The broad description does not establish that an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer can qualify directly or work remotely under this status.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially subject to general naturalisation rules after more than 7 years' qualifying residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No special citizenship entitlement follows from PRP approval.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because no current official rule confirms that foreign remote-work income alone qualifies under the broad PRP/assured-income wording or that the status authorizes that work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No relevant minimum salary was found on the permit notice.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; local employment and labour-market conditions apply

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Specified employment in Malawi and application while the foreign worker is outside Malawi.
The vacancy must first be offered to qualified Malawians, with evidence of local advertising and inability to recruit a suitable Malawian.
Applications should identify a qualified Malawian understudy who can eventually take over the post.

initial_validity.value: 6 months to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The precise period depends on the approved employment.

extension_rules.value: May be renewed while the holder remains in approved employment; ordinary TEPs other than key posts may generally be renewed only twice, and renewal is not automatic.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, for the specified Malawi employment and approved area or occupation.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct conversion is promised; the general PRP page separately mentions eligibility after at least 5 years of ordinary residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not relevant to this profile because local employment sponsorship is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only the separate general naturalisation rules could eventually apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a local-employment permit with labour-market testing, not independent foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary Residence Permit after visitor/business-visitor stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is published on the general permit page or the dedicated Temporary Residence Permit page.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: This absence does not imply permission to perform regular foreign remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Hold a valid visitor or business-visit permit and have completed the maximum 90-day visitor period.
Show legitimate and justifiable reasons for continued residence.

initial_validity.notes: The reviewed official pages do not publish a standard validity period.

extension_rules.notes: The decision and duration appear case-specific; no remote-worker renewal framework is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A temporary-residence permit can be requested after the maximum visitor stay for justified continued residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not a dedicated remote-worker legalization mechanism.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path is published for this temporary visitor-related status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The PRP's separate 5-year ordinary-residence category does not confirm that this short-term status counts.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official source confirms that time on this visitor-derived temporary status counts toward naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a visitor-derived, justification-based temporary status, not an ordinary digital-nomad or freelancer route. Entering as a visitor and registering as self-employed is not established as a lawful conversion strategy.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor permit, business visit permit, or eVisa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numerical remote-work or visitor-maintenance threshold in USD is published. The requirement is discretionary sufficient funds for the planned stay.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed minimum amount in MWK is published. Current Immigration guidance requires sufficient funds to maintain the visitor for the duration of the visit, while the Immigration Act requires sufficient means to support the entrant and accompanying dependants; neither states a numerical threshold. Published visa fees—USD 75 single entry, USD 150 six-month multiple entry, and USD 250 twelve-month multiple entry—are application charges, not income or maintenance thresholds.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient funds for the visit; no numerical MWK or USD threshold published
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sufficient funds for the duration of the visit
income_requirement_display.notes: The requirement is not a remote-worker income test. Visa fees are separate application charges.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: The visa is entry permission rather than permission to stay, work, or conduct an ongoing business.
A visitor/business-visit permit is normally valid for 30 days and may be extended by another 60 days.
Possess sufficient funds for the visit and a return or onward ticket.
Apply online where a visa is required and submit passport, travel, photograph, and related documents.

initial_validity.value: Visitor/business-visit permit: 30 days
initial_validity.notes: Visa validity varies by entry category; the tourist visa page describes a single-use visa valid for 3 months.

extension_rules.value: Visitor/business-visit permit may be extended for a further 60 days upon application and payment of the applicable fee.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying remote-worker residence is granted by the visa or visitor permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None directly.

path_to_citizenship.value: None directly.

rejected_routes.notes: A visitor visa or permit is for short tourism, visiting relatives, or business and is not a work or settlement route. Official guidance requires sufficient funds and a return/onward ticket but publishes no numerical maintenance threshold in MWK or another currency.

summary.value: A foreign student may independently obtain a study permit for study or research at an approved educational institution. The official permit catalog does not present a degree-based independent skilled residence route, post-study remote-work route, or direct permanent residence based solely on qualifications.
summary.notes: The study permit is education-specific and is not valid for the applicant's existing foreign-contract remote work unless separate work authorization is obtained.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident when present in Malawi for an aggregate of at least 183 days in any 12-month period commencing or ending in the relevant year of assessment.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breakers may change the result for dual residents.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for general individual taxable income above the annual MWK 2,040,000 exemption. Employment PAYE has additional 35% and 40% marginal brackets; 30% is not necessarily the effective rate for every contract structure.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The mandatory occupational pension minimum is 5% for an employee and 10% for an employer. Applicability to a foreign-contract remote worker or genuinely self-employed proprietor was not established, so no single remote-worker percentage is asserted.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly tax, health-insurance payment, or self-employed social-security minimum was confirmed for a nonexistent digital-nomad route.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, expatriate, remittance-basis, or remote-worker tax holiday was found in the reviewed current MRA measures and tax legislation.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary source, residence, business-registration, and contract-classification rules apply.

taxes.caveats: Malawi taxes income from sources within Malawi or deemed within Malawi. Professional services physically performed in Malawi may be treated as Malawi-source even when the payer is abroad; treaty and contract analysis is required. Local advice is necessary on employment versus independent-business classification, deductions, withholding, VAT, pension coverage, and treaty relief.

taxation_system.value: Progressive/mixed individual system: general personal taxable income is exempt up to MWK 2,040,000 annually and taxed at 30% above that amount, while employment PAYE uses 0%, 30%, 35%, and 40% monthly brackets.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Resident at an aggregate 183 days or more in any 12-month period commencing or ending in the assessment year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income received or accrued from sources within Malawi or deemed within Malawi. Services performed in Malawi may be Malawi-source even when paid from abroad.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered employees, minimum occupational-pension contributions are 5% employee and 10% employer. Coverage of a foreign-contract remote worker or self-employed person requires classification advice.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 40% figure is the top employment PAYE marginal rate, not an expected effective rate. General individual taxable income outside PAYE is shown as 0% then 30%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First MWK 170,000 per month / MWK 2,040,000 annually
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment PAYE; the same annual exempt amount is shown for general personal income.
tax_brackets.notes: Effective 30 December 2025. USD conversion is omitted because a dependable current official exchange-rate observation was not established.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next MWK 1,400,000 per month; general personal income above MWK 2,040,000 annually
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment PAYE and general personal taxable income, respectively.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly employment income above MWK 10,000,000 / annual employment income above MWK 120,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate only.

taxation_system.notes: The March 2026 MRA notice also introduced a 0.05% levy on bank electronic transfers and mobile-money transfers over MWK 100,000, and increased VAT to 17.5%. These are transaction or consumption taxes, not fixed monthly remote-worker charges.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Malawi has no confirmed digital-nomad status. A person nevertheless working from Malawi must examine ordinary Malawi-source income and residence rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary individual, employment, or business taxation depending on facts
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 30% general PIT screening rate; employment PAYE top marginal rate 40%
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183 aggregate days in the relevant 12-month test period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Malawi applies source-based rules. Remuneration for professional services performed in Malawi may be Malawi-source notwithstanding a foreign payer; treaty relief and the precise contract must be checked.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered employment carries minimum pension contributions of 5% employee and 10% employer. Application to a foreign employer without Malawi payroll or to genuine self-employment is unresolved.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed monthly payment confirmed.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed amount; percentage-based pension contributions may apply if the relationship is covered employment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Permit and citizenship fees exist, but no digital-nomad fee exists. The citizenship department publishes USD 20,000 after successful alien naturalisation or spouse registration.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A 0.05% levy applies to bank electronic transfers and mobile-money transfers exceeding MWK 100,000 under the current MRA notice.
fixed_payments.notes: Business registration, VAT, permit, and professional costs depend on the structure and cannot safely be reduced to one monthly amount.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 183 days does not automatically eliminate Malawi tax: income from services performed in Malawi may still be Malawi-source. Confirm treaty and non-resident rules.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 aggregate days, residence is triggered. Ordinary PIT and source rules apply; no nomad exemption exists.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally operated business or profession may require business and tax registration and the USD 50,000 BRP conditions for immigration purposes. PIT, deductions, VAT, and pension treatment require local classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax treatment is for screening only because no qualifying immigration route exists and foreign-contract work can be recharacterized based on how and where services are performed.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary remote-work temporary-residence route exists, so a route-specific time-to-residence cannot be stated.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The PRP page permits an application by a person ordinarily resident for at least 5 years. It does not guarantee approval or confirm that visitor-derived temporary residence counts.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on more than 7 years' residence rather than a stated number of years after PR. A separate post-PR interval could not be established.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: More than 7 years' residence is the published alien-naturalisation eligibility point. This is a general rule, not a confirmed timeline from an ordinary remote-worker route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official current processing-time commitment was found. Ministerial or discretionary review and payment after approval make estimation unsafe.

key_conditions.value: Alien naturalisation requires more than 7 years' residence, adequate English and one prescribed vernacular language, good character, financial solvency, a valid permit, and prescribed documentation. The published dual-citizenship facility is limited to citizens by birth or descent.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary and currently carries a published USD 20,000 fee after approval.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The department states that a woman married to a Malawian may obtain citizenship after at least 5 years in Malawi on a valid permit. It does not clearly state that the marriage itself must have lasted 5 years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Malawian can support a married-woman citizenship registration application and may support the foreign-wife PRP category, but citizenship is not automatic.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The published guidance remains gender-specific. A male foreign spouse should obtain current legal advice rather than assume equal processing.

requirements_and_risks.value: Published requirements include a marriage certificate and proof of the Malawian husband's citizenship or passport; the 5-year guidance also requires residence on a valid permit. Genuine-marriage scrutiny applies, and sham marriage can cause refusal and immigration or criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official pages do not publish a complete current checklist, language test, processing time, or gender-neutral spouse rule.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Malawi alone is insufficient. Citizenship at birth generally requires at least one Malawi-citizen parent. Foundlings and certain stateless persons have separate protective rules.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Malawi to two non-citizen migrant parents does not ordinarily become Malawian automatically. Foundlings and persons who have always been stateless have limited protective registration rules.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent residence of the parents alone is not stated as sufficient.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Malawi becomes a citizen at birth if either parent is a Malawi citizen. A child born abroad becomes a citizen by descent if either parent is a Malawi citizen by birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Documentary registration and proof of parentage and citizenship may still be needed.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Malawian citizen child does not automatically grant either migrant parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. A separate family, residence, or naturalisation basis must be established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed PRP page lists foreign wives and dependants but no automatic parent-of-citizen entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father gains no automatic status from the child's citizenship. If the mother is Malawian, the child may be a citizen, but the father must independently qualify for an immigration permit or citizenship route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The official spouse guidance is gender-specific and does not establish an equivalent automatic benefit for a foreign husband.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown by Passport Index on the research date; index methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 29 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index is used because it provides separate visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA, and visa-required counts.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is official and the reviewed immigration, tax, and government application materials are available in English, making it practical for administration and professional remote work. Chichewa is useful for everyday integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Internet reliability and power availability were not separately quantified.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or commonly listed working languages. Reliance on either without English or Chichewa would be impractical for government procedures and most daily interactions.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the government's official and common-language listing; no reliable nationwide proficiency statistics were found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2024 Labour Force Survey metadata was located, but the reviewed official publications did not expose a national mean monthly wage suitable for this field.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No official national median monthly wage was established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official general minimum is MWK 125,000.16 per month from 1 June 2025. A USD conversion is withheld because no reliable current official exchange-rate observation was established.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor, visitor-derived temporary residence, and eVisa status are not remote-worker residence routes and have no confirmed settlement counting rule.
settlement_track.summary: Malawi has investor/business and general permanent-residence mechanisms, but no current official route authorizes ordinary foreign-contract remote work without substantial investment, local employment, or another separate basis. The general 5-year PR and more-than-7-year naturalisation rules therefore do not create a usable citizenship track from the rejected visitor/remote-work scenario.
settlement_track.notes: A BRP holder with a genuine USD 50,000 productive-sector investment may build an independent settlement history, but that materially different investor/business profile is outside the requested selection.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The complete official permit catalog contains no dedicated foreign-remote-worker or digital-nomad category. The self-employed BRP requires at least USD 50,000 in outside investment funds and productive-sector business activity.

data.notes: Focused unexplained-null audit preserved the high-confidence rejection and resolved the flagged visitor-route income field as a cautious null: current official guidance requires sufficient funds but publishes no numerical MWK maintenance threshold. Twenty-eight distinct directly relevant canonical URLs were inspected and retained, including seven relevant URLs absent from the previous source set. Remaining nulls are limited to facts not safely published or inferable, inapplicable measures, or discretionary requirements.

data.selection_summary: Malaysia’s DE Rantau Nomad Pass independently fits a software engineer working for a foreign employer or foreign clients, but it is a temporary Professional Visit Pass limited to 24 months. No official DE Rantau-to-permanent-residence conversion is published, and Malaysia’s Constitution normally excludes residence under a temporary immigration pass from citizenship-residence calculations unless the Minister consents. Malaysia is therefore useful for temporary remote work but not valid for this citizenship-oriented selection.

visa_application.notes: Official MDEC portal for DE Rantau applications and status checking. The MDEC FAQ says complete applications are normally processed in 6–8 weeks; applicants should verify current timing in the portal.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: For tech talent, including software engineers, MDEC requires annual income of more than USD 24,000; the threshold is therefore more than USD 2,000 monthly.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Threshold officially stated as more than USD 24,000 per year; no prescribed MYR equivalent

income_proof_months.notes: Remote employees provide three months of payslips and matching bank statements; freelancers provide three months of invoices and bank statements. The contract must have commenced at least three months before submission.

key_requirements.requirement: Software engineers are expressly included in the eligible tech-talent category.
A remote employee needs a signed remote-work contract with a foreign company that is not registered in Malaysia; the contract should preferably remain valid for at least six months from application.
A freelancer needs client contracts, three months of invoices, proof of payment and matching bank statements.
Passport with at least six empty pages and 14 months’ validity, CV, good-conduct letter, personal bond and highest education certificate.
Medical insurance valid in Malaysia and an LHDN tax-registration slip are required before pass issuance.
Documents must be in English or accompanied by a certified English translation.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: DE Rantau does not itself establish a PR pathway. A holder may seek a separate Entry Permit only with independent qualifying grounds; the official PR categories expressly include spouses and children of Malaysian citizens.

No verified ordinary foreign-only remote-work successor to PR was established. The official Entry Permit e-book link opened a Drive folder without readable content, so no unverified professional/points threshold or waiting period is asserted.

path_to_citizenship.notes: DE Rantau has no published citizenship transition. The Constitution normally excludes residence under a temporary immigration pass from naturalisation residence calculations unless the Minister specifically consents.

best_routes.notes: This is a strong ordinary foreign-contract remote-work fit for temporary living. It fails the selection because the exact status is capped at 24 months and is not a confirmed settlement route.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: RP-T is a renewable long-term immigration pass, not an Entry Permit, which is Malaysia’s permanent-residence document. Current TalentCorp materials direct holders nearing ten years to a separate discretionary RP-T Post-10-Years application; they do not publish an automatic RP-T-to-permanent-residence conversion. The Immigration Department lists Entry Permit applications separately, so any PR outcome would require a distinct application and approval under prevailing criteria.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Any eventual naturalisation would be a separate discretionary process; TalentCorp does not describe RP-T as direct citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected: tax, banking or business registration is not a substitute for an immigration pass, and no official legalization route matching this scenario is published.

summary.value: No degree-only independent residence route matching the profile was found. RP-T recognizes degrees and professional qualifications but also requires three years of Malaysian Employment Pass work, MYR 15,000 monthly basic salary, five years’ experience and Malaysian tax compliance.
summary.notes: The applicant’s degree helps only after substantial local-employment prerequisites are met.

tax_residency_rule.value: The primary test is physical presence in Malaysia for at least 182 days in a basis year, supplemented by linked-period and other statutory tests under section 7.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence is separate from immigration status; fewer than 182 days does not invariably determine the result because linked-period rules may apply.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening value only: residents use progressive rates up to 30%, while non-resident individuals generally pay 30% on taxable chargeable income. This is not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Covered non-Malaysian employees generally have a 2% employee EPF share and 2% employer share, but the current sources do not establish universal application to a DE Rantau holder employed solely by an overseas entity without Malaysian payroll. PERKESO coverage also depends on employment classification.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly fixed payment is prescribed. Immigration charges are transaction-based, while insurance premiums and security bonds vary.

special_tax_regimes.value: No DE Rantau-specific income-tax exemption or preferential rate is published; general source, residence and treaty rules apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A foreign payer does not by itself make services performed from Malaysia foreign-source.

taxes.caveats: Foreign remote employees working in Malaysia for no more than 60 days may qualify for the statutory short-employment exemption; longer stays may create Malaysian taxation even before tax residence begins. Freelancers may face business-income and withholding rules. Source classification, treaty relief, deductions, foreign-employer presence and social-security coverage require individual Malaysian advice.

taxation_system.value: Mixed source-based system: residents face progressive rates up to 30%, while non-residents generally face 30% on taxable Malaysian-source income. Qualifying foreign-source income received in Malaysia may be exempt, but work physically performed in Malaysia can be Malaysian-source.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Primary 182-day test, supplemented by linked-period and other section 7 tests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income accruing in or derived from Malaysia is taxable. Qualifying foreign-source income received in Malaysia may be exempt, but employment exercised and services performed in Malaysia can be Malaysian-source even when paid from abroad.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated DE Rantau tax holiday or digital-nomad rate is published.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered non-permanent-resident foreign employees generally contribute 2% to EPF, matched by the employer. Application to an overseas employer without Malaysian payroll and PERKESO coverage requires case-specific confirmation.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard value is the top resident marginal rate and usual non-resident flat rate, not an expected effective rate. Verify the applicable assessment-year brackets before filing.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: DE Rantau has no blanket tax exemption. Remote employment physically exercised in Malaysia can become taxable after the short-employment exemption ceases, subject to treaty rules; resident rates apply when residence tests are met. Freelancers may have business-income and withholding issues.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Professional Visit Pass holder working as a foreign remote employee or freelancer
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Residents: progressive 0–30%; non-residents: generally 30% on taxable income; qualifying employment of no more than 60 days may be exempt
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Primary 182-day test plus linked-period and other section 7 rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Qualifying foreign-source income received in Malaysia may be exempt, but employment exercised or services performed in Malaysia can be Malaysian-source. The payer’s foreign location is not decisive.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No DE Rantau-specific tax holiday or reduced income-tax rate is published.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered foreign employees generally have 2% employee and 2% employer EPF contributions. Application to an overseas employer without Malaysian payroll and PERKESO coverage requires confirmation.

fixed_payments.status: Route fees and document obligations are published; recurring insurance and social-security amounts vary or require classification.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal DE Rantau amount is published. Covered foreign employees generally have 2% employee and 2% employer EPF contributions; PERKESO depends on coverage.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The FAQ states MYR 1,080 for the principal’s processing fee including SST, MYR 540 per dependent, plus MYR 90 per three months or MYR 360 per year for the immigration pass. Multiple-entry visa charges and refundable security bonds vary by nationality.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Medical insurance valid in Malaysia is mandatory, but no fixed premium is prescribed. A bond may apply. No universal monthly freelancer levy or municipal fee is published.
fixed_payments.notes: The route page displays headline fees of MYR 1,000 for the principal and MYR 500 per dependent, while the FAQ gives SST-inclusive totals. Confirm the live checkout amount before payment.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Tax non-residence does not automatically mean no tax. Employment exercised in Malaysia for no more than 60 days may qualify for exemption; a 61–181-day stay can produce non-resident taxation, generally at 30%, subject to treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Once section 7 residence conditions are met, taxable Malaysian-source employment income is generally subject to progressive resident rates up to 30%, with relief eligibility depending on the facts.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Foreign freelancers may be treated as carrying on business in Malaysia, with source, business-income, withholding and treaty issues. The current MDEC checklist also requires an LHDN registration slip.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the screening framework; an individual liability determination requires the contract, working-day count, treaty, payer and business structure.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The Professional Visit Pass is the initial approved status; no prior Malaysian residence is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No DE Rantau-to-PR conversion or qualifying waiting period is published. A separate status and eligibility basis would be required.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on qualifying residence—10 of the preceding 12 years, including the final 12 months—not a published fixed period after PR. Approval remains discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the general naturalisation residence threshold, not a DE Rantau timeline. Temporary-pass residence normally does not count without ministerial consent.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current Article 19 page publishes conditions and filing procedures but no standard or typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires age 21+, qualifying residence for at least 10 of the preceding 12 years including the immediately preceding 12 months, permanent intent, good character, adequate Malay and two adult citizen sponsors. Temporary-pass residence normally does not count without ministerial consent.
key_conditions.notes: Meeting the conditions does not guarantee approval.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Article 15(1) provides a citizenship-registration route only for a foreign woman married to a Malaysian male citizen and requires residence throughout the two years immediately before application. A foreign husband has no equivalent two-year citizenship route.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine marriage to a Malaysian citizen can support a Long-Term Social Visit Pass for either foreign spouse and, after at least three years on a valid long-term pass, possible Residence Pass eligibility. The accelerated Article 15(1) citizenship route is limited to wives of Malaysian citizens.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to another migrant does not accelerate citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must remain subsisting and be lawfully registered. Spouse applications require civil-status evidence and both parties’ participation; Immigration may conduct visits, observation, interviews and document checks. Residence and citizenship remain separate approvals, and false statements can result in refusal, cancellation or prosecution.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically grant permanent residence or citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A Malaysia-born child is generally a citizen if at least one parent is a Malaysian citizen or permanent resident at birth, or under the constitutional anti-statelessness provision if the child would otherwise have no citizenship. Narrow exceptions and parentage rules apply.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Malaysia-born child of two temporary foreign migrants normally does not acquire citizenship solely by birth. The result changes if a parent is a Malaysian permanent resident or the child would otherwise be stateless.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parentage, marriage registration and proof of another nationality can affect the determination.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: For a child born in Malaysia, citizenship generally arises by operation of law when at least one legally recognized parent is a Malaysian citizen at birth. JPN provides an Article 14 status-confirmation procedure.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Special rules can affect children born before registration of their parents’ marriage and births abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Malaysian-citizen child can create potential family-based Residence Pass eligibility for a biological foreign parent, but only through a separate sponsored application after the required lawful long-term residence. It does not automatically grant PR or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The published category includes biological mothers and fathers of Malaysian citizens.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign biological father of a Malaysian-citizen child may apply for a family-ties Residence Pass after at least three years on a valid long-term pass and with an eligible Malaysian sponsor. Citizenship remains a separate Article 19 process.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child’s birth alone does not legalize the father’s stay or confer nationality.

rank.notes: Bernama’s 23 July 2026 report states that Malaysia shared seventh place in the then-current Henley update.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley’s access score combines destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance, including visa-on-arrival access; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The inspected current report does not provide a separate count of destinations requiring an advance visa.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The inspected current report combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access and does not publish a separate visa-on-arrival/eTA subtotal.

passport.notes: Current passport rank and combined access score are available, but the requested category breakdown is not published by the cited current report.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High in major cities and business or remote-work contexts. The government identifies Malay as the official language and states that English dominates trade and industry; MDEC also accepts English-language submissions.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Malay remains important for government interaction and is required at an adequate level for naturalisation.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low as general working languages. No official role or broad institutional support is published for Russian or Ukrainian; applicants should expect to use English for remote work and Malay or English for local services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Community availability may vary by city but should not be relied upon for administration.

Work visas require a Maldivian work permit and employer action; business and tourist visas are temporary; the corporate resident route is for qualifying investors; and the resident visa is based on marriage to a Maldivian citizen. None is a qualifying independent remote-work citizenship track.

The employer or authorized representative must obtain the Work e-Visa through Xpat Online within 15 days after arrival.

initial_validity.value: Tied to the approved work permit.
initial_validity.notes: The visa is invalid when the linked work-permit fees expire.

extension_rules.value: Renewed Work e-Visas are issued for no more than one year at a time and remain tied to the work permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Authorizes the sponsored expatriate to reside and work while the linked permit remains valid.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is temporary employer-linked status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Neither the current Work Visa page nor the Immigration Act identifies a permanent-residence conversion for work-visa holders.

path_to_citizenship.value: No route-specific citizenship transition is published. General discretionary naturalization has separate conditions, including long residence, Dhivehi, Islam and distinguished service.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Employer-sponsored residence should not be assumed to satisfy every naturalization condition.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Maldivian work permit and employer or authorized representative are required.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current Business Visa page publishes duration and approval rules but no personal-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current Business Visa page publishes duration and approval rules but no personal-income threshold in MVR.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; the proposed business or work must be permitted and approved by the relevant Maldivian authority.
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a short business-visit permission rather than a remote-worker residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: The published Business Visa criteria do not prescribe a standard income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Application initiated through the Ministry of Economic Development's Business Portal.
Passport valid for at least six months, recent photograph and ministerial/immigration verification.
Business or work must be permitted and approved by the relevant Maldivian government authority.

initial_validity.value: 30 to 90 days per grant.

extension_rules.value: Total Business Visa stay may not exceed 180 days in a calendar year.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The visa permits a time-limited business visit but is not identified as residence status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current Business Visa rules and Immigration Act provide no published conversion from this visitor-like permission to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The citizenship material provides no naturalization transition tied to a Business Visa, and temporary business visits are not established as qualifying settlement residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a temporary business-visit permission requiring government approval for the activity, not ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route is based on qualifying investor status rather than monthly remote-work income, so an ordinary monthly-income minimum is inapplicable.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The route is based on qualifying investor status rather than monthly remote-work income, so an ordinary monthly-income minimum in MVR is inapplicable.

income_requirement_display.value: Investor eligibility and approved investment required; no ordinary remote-worker income threshold.
income_requirement_display.notes: The official description identifies this as a route for eligible investors.

income_proof_months.notes: A remote-income history is not the eligibility basis; the applicant instead needs the prescribed investor and corporate evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Must qualify as an eligible investor under the Corporate Resident Visa Regulation.
Online application through the government Business Portal using an eFaas account.
Passport, compliant photograph, health/travel insurance and investment/corporate evidence appropriate to the applicant category.

initial_validity.value: 5 years.
initial_validity.notes: The official ministry announcement gives a standard processing target of 14 days.

extension_rules.notes: The reviewed current English ministry announcement and regulations index do not state the renewal duration or renewal eligibility rules.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct five-year corporate resident status for eligible investors.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is investment-based, not an ordinary self-employed or remote-worker route.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed current ministry announcement and regulations index do not identify conversion to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: No route-specific citizenship transition was identified; general discretionary naturalization is separate.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant profile excludes investor and substantial-capital routes.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: A remote-worker income threshold is inapplicable because tourist permission is visitor status, not a remote-work route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A remote-worker income threshold in MVR is inapplicable because tourist permission is visitor status, not a remote-work route.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable; visitor status is not a remote-work residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: The visitor rules do not prescribe remote-income history because they do not create a remote-work category.

key_requirements.requirement: Visitor status under the Immigration Act is for a visiting foreign national without the intention to be employed or work to earn income in Maldives.
Tourist extensions are processed digitally under the revised procedure effective 23 April 2026.

initial_validity.value: Up to 30 days under the Immigration Act.
initial_validity.notes: Immigration has discretion to allow a total stay of up to 90 days after payment of the applicable fee.

extension_rules.value: Discretionary extension up to a maximum total of 90 days from entry under the cited Act.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Visitor permission only; the Immigration Act does not characterize it as residence status.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Immigration Act contains no tourist-to-permanent-residence conversion.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No citizenship transition from tourist status is published.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourist/visitor status is temporary, and the statutory visitor definition is incompatible with treating it as permission to work for income while in Maldives.

rejected_routes.route_name: Resident Visa based on marriage to a Maldivian citizen

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current Resident Visa service page lists marriage and documentary requirements but no income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current Resident Visa service page lists marriage and documentary requirements but no income threshold in MVR.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; valid marriage to a Maldivian citizen is required.

income_proof_months.notes: The published marriage-based Resident Visa requirements do not prescribe an income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Legally registered marriage to a Maldivian citizen.
Court-stamped application, marriage certificate, citizen spouse's ID, passport documents, photograph, and initially a medical report and health insurance.
Pre-arrival sponsorship is required when travelling to marry or register the marriage.

initial_validity.value: 1 year initially.

extension_rules.value: Renewals of up to 5 years; extension may be filed through IMUGA during the three months before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct Resident Visa after the qualifying marriage is legally registered.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Despite its title, the published visa remains time-limited and renewable.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current service page provides one-year initial validity and renewals of up to five years but does not identify a separate permanent-residence grant.

path_to_citizenship.value: No marriage-specific accelerated naturalization rule was identified; the general statutory conditions remain separate and discretionary.

rejected_routes.notes: A genuine family route exists, but it does not fit the supplied applicant profile and is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

summary.value: Maldivian law recognizes a Student Visa, and Maldives National University publishes a current process for admitted international students: obtain pre-arrival immigration approval, enter Maldives, and apply through IMUGA for the Student Visa within 30 days using the university offer letter, medical report, health insurance and passport evidence. This study permission does not require a local employer, but no independent degree-based, skilled-graduate or qualification-based residence route leading to permanent residence was identified for a foreign software engineer.
summary.notes: The current university instructions resolve the earlier procedural gap: admission and an institutional offer letter are required, pre-arrival approval must be obtained, and the post-arrival Student Visa application is filed through IMUGA. The Immigration Act and university instructions describe temporary study permission; they do not publish post-study work rights, permanent-residence conversion, or a citizenship-counting rule. Consequently, this is not a qualification-based settlement route for the supplied profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if their permanent place of living is in Maldives, or they are present or intend to be present for at least 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending in a tax year, or are an overseas-posted Maldivian government employee. A foreign resident legally present under the Immigration Act and not married to a Maldivian is classified as a temporary resident for income-scope purposes.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Temporary residents are taxed only on Maldives-source income, despite meeting the residence test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening individual rate, not an expected effective rate. The first MVR 720,000 of annual taxable income is taxed at 0%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The Maldives Retirement Pension Scheme contribution for covered local employment totals 14% of basic salary—7% employee and 7% employer. The Pension Office describes mandatory participation for local employees; no mandatory contribution for an unsupported foreign-contract remote-worker category was established.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: A route-specific amount is inapplicable because Maldives has no digital-nomad route. Unrelated visa categories have differing fees, and the reviewed pension material does not establish a fixed monthly freelancer contribution.

special_tax_regimes.value: Foreign individuals who meet the residence test while legally present and are not married to a Maldivian are treated as temporary residents and taxed only on Maldives-source income. This is a general statutory classification, not a digital-nomad tax holiday.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Employment exercised in Maldives is expressly Maldives-source remuneration. Classification of a particular foreign-client contracting arrangement should be confirmed with MIRA.

taxes.caveats: There is no qualifying immigration status for the proposed activity. Taxability depends on whether the relationship is employment or business, whether work performed physically in Maldives creates Maldives-source income or a permanent establishment, the temporary-resident rules, deductions, and any foreign tax credit or treaty position.

taxation_system.value: Progressive individual income tax. Ordinary residents are taxed on worldwide income, while non-residents and statutory temporary residents are taxed on Maldives-source income. Rates range from 0% to 15%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of living, or at least 183 days in any rolling 12-month period beginning or ending in a tax year; special rule for overseas-posted government employees.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide for ordinary residents; Maldives-source only for non-residents and temporary residents. A foreigner legally present under the Immigration Act who meets residence criteria and is not married to a Maldivian is a temporary resident.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Temporary-resident source-only treatment; no dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-worker exemption found.
taxation_system.social_security: MRPS is 7% employee plus 7% employer for covered local employees. Coverage and contribution liability for a hypothetical foreign-contract worker were not established.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Annual brackets are cumulative. The dashboard value of 15% is the top marginal rate, not the effective rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income not exceeding MVR 720,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Individual taxable income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at MVR 15.42 per USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of individual taxable income in this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of individual taxable income in this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of individual taxable income in this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of individual taxable income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band begins at approximately USD 155,642 annually.

taxation_system.notes: Tax law and rates are well supported by MIRA. Application to remote work remains hypothetical because immigration sources do not authorize the proposed status.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Maldives has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker visa. If a foreigner nevertheless performs employment in Maldives, the Income Tax Act treats remuneration from employment exercised there as Maldives-source; individual rates can reach 15%.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; hypothetical temporary-resident individual taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–15% progressive; 15% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183-day/permanent-place test, with legally present unmarried foreign residents generally classified as temporary residents.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Temporary residents are taxed only on Maldives-source income. However, employment exercised physically in Maldives is Maldives-source even when the employer is foreign; treatment of independent foreign-client business income requires filing-specific advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found. Temporary-resident source-only taxation is a general Income Tax Act rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: MRPS totals 14% of basic salary for covered local employment, split 7% employee and 7% employer. No remote-worker contribution rule was found.

fixed_payments.status: Not applicable—no digital-nomad status exists.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed amount; covered local employment uses percentage contributions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad visa fee. Unrelated resident, dependent, work, business and investor statuses have their own fees or approval processes.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax or nomad levy was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Health insurance is required for some unrelated visa categories, but no standardized monthly premium is published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 183 days does not alone eliminate tax: Maldives-source income can be taxable for non-residents, and visitor status does not authorize the proposed work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: An unmarried foreigner legally present for at least 183 days would generally be a temporary resident taxed on Maldives-source income. Employment physically exercised in Maldives is expressly Maldives-source.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Professional services can constitute business under the Income Tax Act, but current business-registration and immigration sources did not establish that a foreign visitor can register a sole proprietorship and thereby legalize residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the general tax law; lower confidence in any hypothetical remote-worker application because the immigration route itself does not exist.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent temporary-residence route exists for ordinary foreign-contract remote work, so a route-specific time to temporary residence is inapplicable.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed immigration categories and regulations index publish no permanent-residence conversion timeline for the supplied profile.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The naturalization law uses residence rather than a published permanent-residence prerequisite and states no PR-to-citizenship interval.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization screening only, not a timeline from any selected remote-work route. The statute requires 12 years' continuous residence, with a limited aggregate-residence alternative, and citizenship remains presidentially discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The ministry service charter provides administrative review or notification targets but does not publish the total elapsed time for the President's discretionary citizenship decision.

key_conditions.value: Applicant must be Muslim, at least 21 and of sound mind; meet the long-residence rule; know the Constitution; speak Dhivehi; have adequate education; meet criminal-history restrictions; have rendered distinguished service to Maldives; and renounce prior citizenship. Final grant is discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: The distinguished-service requirement makes naturalization substantially more restrictive than a routine residence-duration pathway.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage immediately supports an application for a renewable Resident Visa after legal registration, but the reviewed visa page and citizenship law state no special marriage-duration rule accelerating permanent residence or citizenship.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A foreign national already legally married to a Maldivian can apply for the marriage-based Resident Visa through IMUGA, subject to marriage registration/document requirements and any required visa transfer. Initial validity is one year and renewals may be granted for up to five years.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage creates a family residence option, not automatic citizenship or confirmed permanent residence.

requirements_and_risks.value: The application requires a court-stamped form, marriage certificate, citizen spouse's ID and supporting identity, medical and insurance documents. Authorities can verify legal registration and supporting evidence; false or sham documentation can result in refusal and legal consequences. General citizenship requirements still apply.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official sources reviewed do not publish a separate expedited citizenship track for spouses.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship to children born to a Maldivian citizen, not generally to every child born on Maldivian territory.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Maldives to two foreign parents does not acquire citizenship merely by birth there under the constitutional rule reviewed.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The reviewed constitutional text does not set out a broad territorial-birth rule. Any narrow foundling or statelessness protection would require separate case-specific verification.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. The Constitution states that children born to a citizen of Maldives are citizens, without limiting the rule to the mother or father.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The constitutional text supports citizenship through either citizen parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. The published Resident Visa is based on marriage to a Maldivian citizen, while citizenship requires a separate discretionary application.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed immigration services do not publish an independent parent-of-citizen residence category.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child's other parent is Maldivian, the child is a citizen. The foreign father may qualify for the marriage-based Resident Visa if legally married to the citizen parent, but the child's citizenship alone was not shown to grant residence, permanent residence or citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No automatic derivative citizenship for the father.

rank.notes: Current secondary country-specific reporting summarizes the 2026 Henley result as rank 49. Henley's main interactive page confirms its methodology but did not expose the Maldives row in the captured text.

visa_free_destinations.notes: This is the reported 2026 Henley-style mobility score combining destinations accessible without a prior visa, rather than a strict visa-free-only count. The Maldivian Foreign Ministry separately listed 64 strictly visa-free countries and territories as of March 2024.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The official Maldivian page supplies an older strict visa-free list, while the current Henley-style source supplies a combined mobility score. Neither reviewed source publishes a current separate count of destinations requiring an advance visa, and subtracting the mobility score would incorrectly combine eVisa and other categories.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The current 92-destination score combines access categories, while the official 2024 page lists only strict visa-free access; the reviewed sources do not publish a current separated visa-on-arrival/eTA total.

passport.notes: Rank and mobility score use the 2026 Henley summary. The only directly published Maldivian government count found was an older strict visa-free total of 64 as of March 2024.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in tourism, business-facing services and the principal immigration/tax portals, and current broadband coverage is substantial. Dhivehi remains the sole national language, and connectivity quality and affordability vary between Malé, resorts and outer atolls.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The assessment is practical rather than an assertion that English has official status. A government connectivity source reports nationwide mobile broadband availability and fixed broadband coverage of about 80% of the population.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and no reliable evidence of broad institutional use was found. They should not be relied upon for government, tax or legal procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The constitutional language rule does not recognize Russian or Ukrainian, and the reviewed government service portals provide no evidence of nationwide service availability in either language.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Historical benchmark only: the official HIES 2016 employment report gives average monthly main-job earnings of MVR 10,229 for employed persons. The USD value uses MVR 15.42 per USD and must not be read as a current 2026 average; the 2024–2025 Malé Labour Force Survey publishes employment indicators but no earnings estimate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No combined all-worker median was published in the current 2024–2025 Malé Labour Force Survey, the 2022 census employment tables or the 2023 Statistical Yearbook. The older HIES 2016 report separates median main-job earnings for Maldivian and foreign workers rather than publishing a combined resident-worker median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The minimum-wage order uses employer-category hourly rates and a separate public-sector monthly floor, so one national monthly USD minimum would be misleading.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Historical benchmark only: the official HIES 2016 employment report gives mean monthly main-job earnings of MVR 10,456 for Maldivian workers. The approximate USD conversion uses MVR 15.42 per USD. No newer representative citizen-specific mean was published in the reviewed 2022 census, 2023 Yearbook or 2024–2025 Malé Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Historical benchmark only: the official HIES 2016 employment report's nationality breakdown gives median monthly main-job earnings of MVR 10,000 for Maldivian workers. The approximate USD value is MVR 10,000 divided by the cited MVR 15.42 reference rate. The newer 2022 census employment tables, 2023 Statistical Yearbook and 2024–2025 Malé Labour Force Survey do not publish a representative citizen-specific median, so this must not be presented as a current 2026 salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed labour survey, historical earnings report and Statistical Yearbook publish indicators or salary distributions but no meaningful national maximum salary; an observed maximum would also be sample-dependent rather than a statutory ceiling.

min_salary_local_currency.value: MVR 21.63/hour for 'other employers'; category rates include MVR 33.65/hour for medium enterprises, MVR 38.46/hour for larger private businesses, and a public-sector floor of MVR 7,000/month for permanent employees working at least 30 hours weekly.
min_salary_local_currency.notes: These are statutory minimum-wage figures from the 2021 order, not observed minimum earnings. Applicability depends on employer category.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Historical mean monthly main-job earnings for Maldivian workers in HIES 2016, not a current national salary estimate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Historical median monthly main-job earnings for Maldivian workers in HIES 2016. Newer reviewed official publications do not provide a replacement citizen-specific median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official publications do not define or publish a representative national maximum monthly salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Historical HIES 2016 main-job earnings by nationality; statutory minimum wage by employer category
average_citizen_salary.period: Earnings: HIES 2016; minimum wage: order dated 8 November 2021; newer sources checked include Census 2022, Statistical Yearbook 2023 and the October 2024–September 2025 Malé Labour Force Survey
average_citizen_salary.notes: The focused audit found an official historical citizen-specific mean and median, resolving the absence of any documented benchmark. Those values remain dated: the newer census and labour-force publications reviewed do not report representative earnings, while the Yearbook's salary table covers civil servants rather than all Maldivian workers. USD amounts are approximate conversions at MVR 15.42 per USD and are not inflation-adjusted.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official CPI data are available through the Maldives Bureau of Statistics, but the reviewed official sources do not publish a standardized single-person monthly cost-of-living budget. Costs vary materially between Malé, inhabited atolls and resort islands.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No crowdsourced cost estimate was substituted for an official figure.
