settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourist and business permissions are temporary and do not create a remote-worker settlement path. Working under visitor status should not be assumed lawful.
settlement_track.summary: Maldives has no confirmed ordinary digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, freelance or independent-professional residence route. Every reviewed alternative is visitor-like, employer-sponsored, investment-based, study-based or family-based, so the supplied profile has no route from foreign-contract remote work to permanent residence or citizenship.
settlement_track.notes: General naturalization may be considered after demanding statutory residence and eligibility conditions, but no qualifying initial status for this profile was found and the grant remains discretionary. Student status does not cure this gap because no post-study settlement conversion was published.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated visa authorizes residence for ordinary work performed remotely under a foreign contract. Work status requires a Maldivian permit and employer action; business and visitor visas are temporary; investor, student and marriage routes do not match the profile.

data.notes: The focused audit confirmed the previous negative selection result. It resolved the education-procedure gap with current Maldives National University and Immigration evidence and resolved the salary-note gap with the official HIES 2016 Maldivian earnings breakdown, while explicitly labeling those earnings as historical because newer official sources do not publish a representative citizen-specific median.

data.selection_summary: Malian law provides a potentially independent establishment route for an immigrant conducting non-salaried activity: proof of means and medical clearance can support a five-year renewable resident card without a local employer. Foreigners may own a Malian company and ordinary professional activity requires tax registration, but foreign software contracting may require prior ministerial authorization as a liberal profession. Current official portals do not state whether ordinary software consulting is regulated, identify the competent approving ministry, or publish a resident-card filing page and current fee. Written confirmation from Mali's immigration authority and API-Mali is therefore necessary before treating this as a usable citizenship track.

visa_application.title: Official Missions Diplomatiques et Postes Consulaires portal — Venir au Mali
visa_application.notes: The diplomatic portal routes applicants to the competent Malian mission and covers ordinary visa categories. The Ministry of Security publishes a procedures index with an immigration section, but the reviewed current page did not expose a resident-card form, filing instructions, fee schedule, or online application. Establishment authorization and the resident card are governed by the 2004 law and 2005 decree and appear to require in-country filing with the immigration authority after lawful entry.

best_routes.route_name: Immigrant establishment authorization and resident card — non-salaried activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The decree requires evidence of sufficient means but supplies neither a numerical minimum nor a conversion formula.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The decree does not specify a minimum amount in XOF.

income_requirement_display.value: No numerical minimum published; evidence of sufficient means is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Toutes justifications sur les moyens d'existence
income_requirement_display.notes: The immigration authority evaluates means without a published threshold. The decree also does not prescribe the number or age of bank statements, invoices, or contracts.

income_proof_months.notes: The decree requires evidence of means but does not prescribe a look-back period.

key_requirements.requirement: Enter lawfully and apply to the immigration authority; an immigrant is a foreigner intending to fix residence or conduct a permanent gainful activity or profession.
Provide a valid passport, a criminal-record extract issued within three months, and certified French translations where necessary.
Provide evidence of means and a medical certificate from an approved doctor resident in Mali confirming absence of contagious disease or an incapacity incompatible with the intended activity.

A foreigner's liberal, commercial, industrial, or artisanal profession requires prior authorization from the competent minister. The current API-Mali authorization page lists several regulated professions but does not list ordinary software consulting or identify its competent ministry.
Apply for the resident card on stamped paper within 15 days after entry and pay the prescribed card tax; neither the decree nor the current official procedure pages publish the present amount.

Obtain a NIF for gainful activity and, where applicable, a professional patente. The DGI requires an existence declaration, address information, and tax-registration documents; patente liability and charges depend on classification and turnover.

Foreign investors may own up to 100% of a Malian company, subject to restrictions governing regulated sectors; this corporate right does not itself grant immigration status or remove professional-authorization requirements.

initial_validity.value: Five-year renewable resident card
initial_validity.notes: This is a time-limited carte de résident for an approved immigrant, not a separately defined indefinite permanent-residence status.

extension_rules.value: Renewable; the same card tax is payable on renewal. The card becomes invalid after more than six consecutive months outside Mali.
extension_rules.notes: The decree does not state a maximum number of renewals.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval for immigrant establishment leads directly to a five-year resident card after lawful entry and filing.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Although the statute calls it a resident card, its five-year validity means it is treated here as renewable long-term temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed law and implementing decree provide a renewable five-year card but do not establish a separate indefinite permanent-residence status or automatic conversion after a specified period.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after at least ten years of habitual residence in Mali. It is discretionary and requires integration, good character, mental capacity, and an acceptable criminal record.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality provisions require establishment à demeure but do not require a separately named permanent-residence stage. The current sources do not expressly address whether a foreign-client software contractor holding this card satisfies that concept, so filing-level confirmation remains necessary.

best_routes.notes: This is the strongest potentially matching statutory route, not a digital-nomad program. The law permits establishment for non-salaried activity without a local employer, and separate official sources confirm that foreigners can own a company, obtain tax registration, and become liable for professional patente. However, the immigration decree requires professional authorization, while API-Mali's current authorization page lists regulated sectors without classifying ordinary software consulting. No current official page identifies the resident-card filing desk, publishes the card fee, or confirms foreign-client remote software work as an accepted activity. The applicant should obtain written classification and filing instructions before entering or working.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary entry visa or visitor stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitor rules do not define a remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Entry requires evidence appropriate to the purpose and conditions of the stay, but the law does not state a standard XOF amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold applies to visitor status
income_requirement_display.notes: An ordinary visa is an entry instrument, not a foreign-remote-work residence category.

income_proof_months.notes: Visitor provisions do not prescribe an income-evidence look-back period.

key_requirements.requirement: Unless exempt, obtain an entry visa and documents showing the purpose, conditions of stay, means, and repatriation guarantee.
An entry visa is valid for at most 90 days and may be renewed once; it does not itself confer a right of residence or establishment.

initial_validity.value: Up to 90 days
initial_validity.notes: The particular visa issued may authorize a shorter stay.

extension_rules.value: An entry visa may be renewed once; a non-immigrant stay visa may be issued for up to one year and renewed.
extension_rules.notes: Neither instrument authorizes professional activity that otherwise requires approval.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic transition exists; immigrant establishment requires a separate application and approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor status alone is not a qualifying residence route.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The immigration law gives visitors no entitlement to indefinite or permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: A visitor stay does not by itself establish the habitual, permanent settlement required for ordinary naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an ordinary visa or visitor stay is neither permission for foreign-contract remote work nor a settlement status.

rejected_routes.route_name: Locally salaried employment and work authorization

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The immigration decree does not impose a numerical salary threshold for this route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The decisive requirement is a locally validated employment contract, not a published immigration income floor.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration income threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: A locally validated employment contract controls eligibility.

income_proof_months.notes: The employment route does not prescribe a prior-income evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: An immigrant seeking establishment for salaried work must submit a labor contract endorsed by the Direction nationale du travail.
A foreigner may not conduct salaried professional activity in Mali without authorization.

initial_validity.value: Five-year renewable resident card if approved as an immigrant
initial_validity.notes: Employment authorization remains necessary.

extension_rules.value: The resident card is renewable and becomes invalid after absence exceeding six consecutive months.
extension_rules.notes: The decree does not state a maximum number of renewals.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Possible through approved local employment and immigrant establishment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This does not fit the applicant's foreign-contract profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed immigration law does not create a distinct indefinite-residence conversion for locally employed residents.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential naturalization after ten years of habitual residence, subject to discretion and statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The underlying immigration route is rejected for this selection because it requires locally validated employment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires local employment authorization and an endorsed employment contract.

rejected_routes.route_name: Investment Code company or approved investment project

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The Investment Code uses project-capital thresholds rather than monthly personal income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The lowest ordinary preferential investment regime starts at 12,500,000 XOF of qualifying investment, which is a capital requirement rather than monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: Qualifying investment generally starts at 12,500,000 XOF for Code incentives
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least 12,500,000 XOF qualifying investment for Regime A
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an investor/project threshold and is incompatible with the ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker profile.

income_proof_months.notes: The Code assesses an investment program, not a period of personal income.

key_requirements.requirement: Create or develop an eligible enterprise and meet the applicable investment-program threshold and approval conditions.
Comply with company, accounting, employment, environmental, and sector-specific regulation.

initial_validity.notes: The Code provides investment incentives and automatic professional residence treatment for specialized expatriate employees of approved enterprises, but it does not itself state a residence duration for a foreign founder.

extension_rules.notes: Residence-card renewal rules for an individual investor are not specified in the Investment Code page.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate immigration basis and approvals are still required for a foreign founder or independent operator.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Company ownership alone does not grant residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Investment Code does not establish direct permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Owning an enterprise does not shorten the ordinary nationality residence period in the reviewed sources.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is an investment/founder route with material project-capital and approval requirements, not ordinary foreign-client remote work. The Code's permission for 100% foreign ownership is useful only as supporting context for the non-salaried establishment route.

summary.value: Students are classified as non-immigrants. A foreign adult remaining beyond three months can obtain temporary stay authorization and a stay visa valid for up to one year and renewable without a local employer. The reviewed immigration and administrative sources do not create a degree-only skilled route, direct permanent residence, or confirmed student-to-citizenship conversion.
summary.notes: This is ordinary study-based temporary stay, not qualification-based migration for an already qualified software engineer.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence can arise through domicile, residence, principal stay exceeding six months/183 days, or exercise of salaried, professional, or other activity in Mali.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The activity test means professional work from Mali may create residence even before 183 days. Applicable treaty tie-breakers can modify the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal employee ITS rate, not an expected effective rate. Independent business income may fall under separate rules, including a possible 3% turnover-based synthetic regime.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share: 3.6% old-age plus 3.06% compulsory health insurance. Employer contributions are approximately 18.9%–21.9%, including the ANPE levy. Application to a foreign employer without Malian payroll and to a self-employed contractor requires professional advice.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed sources do not establish a universal monthly freelancer payment. NIF registration is free apart from a 200 XOF fiscal stamp on the application. Patente charges are assessed from the submitted activity and revenue information rather than published as one universal monthly amount; current resident-card and professional-authorization charges also remain unpublished in the reviewed procedure pages.

special_tax_regimes.value: A 3% annual turnover-based impôt synthétique applies to qualifying enterprises below 50,000,000 XOF annual turnover, but statutory exclusions and election into the real regime can apply. No digital-nomad or inbound-expatriate exemption is identified in the reviewed DGI material.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The correct classification of foreign software-contract revenue and eligibility for the synthetic regime require filing-level advice.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the contract is employment or independent services, where the work is physically performed, whether the foreign payer creates Mali payroll obligations, the business form, VAT/export-of-services treatment, and any applicable treaty. DGI guidance expressly includes Mali residents working for an employer established abroad within the taxable employee population and treats professional activity as a residence criterion.

taxation_system.value: Progressive ITS for employment income, with separate business-income regimes for independent activity.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile, residence, principal stay over six months/183 days, or exercise of salaried, professional, or other activity in Mali.
taxation_system.income_scope: DGI guidance states that persons domiciled or habitually resident in Mali remain taxable where their activity is exercised abroad or their employer is established abroad. Residents must declare taxable employment, independent, pension, and property income; category-specific rules and treaty relief still require analysis.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Impôt synthétique at 3% of annual turnover for qualifying enterprises below 50,000,000 XOF; no dedicated digital-nomad regime is published.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee contribution is 6.66%; employer burden is approximately 18.9%–21.9%. The reviewed sources do not state a universal fixed self-employed contribution amount.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Annual taxable employment income is taxed by bands from 0% to 37%, followed by family reductions. The 37% dashboard value is a top marginal screening rate, not the effective rate.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses about 576 XOF per USD; exchange rates fluctuate.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
Top marginal band; the USD figure approximates its starting threshold.

taxation_system.notes: Statutory rates and the foreign-employer employee rule are supported by current DGI pages. The proper employee-versus-independent regime, patente amount, VAT treatment, and social-security position remain contract- and registration-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Mali has no separately published digital-nomad tax category. A resident foreign employee may face progressive ITS up to 37%; a registered independent business may potentially use the 3% turnover-based synthetic regime if eligible.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: General resident employee or registered independent professional/business
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 37% progressive ITS; potentially 3% of turnover under the qualifying synthetic business regime
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Professional activity in Mali can establish residence; principal presence above six months/183 days is an additional trigger.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: DGI guidance expressly treats a Mali-domiciled or habitually resident employee as taxable even where the employer is established abroad. Independent foreign-client revenue requires classification under the applicable business-income rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: The reviewed DGI, visa, immigration, and administrative portals publish no distinct digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee share is 6.66% and employer burden about 18.9%–21.9% under local rules. The position of an unregistered foreign employer and a genuinely self-employed contractor requires confirmation.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly remote-worker payment is specified in the reviewed tax and social-security sources
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Employee contributions are percentage-based; the current official material does not publish a universal minimum monthly contribution for an independent software contractor.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Entry visas and resident cards require duties or taxes, but the reviewed general official pages do not publish a current resident-card amount. Mission-specific entry-visa fees should not be generalized nationally.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A NIF application uses a 200 XOF fiscal stamp. A professional patente also begins with a 200 XOF stamped application, after which the DGI calculates the activity-specific charge. VAT and other business taxes depend on registration and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: The 3% synthetic tax is turnover-based rather than a fixed monthly payment.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying under 183 days does not ensure non-residence because exercising salaried or professional activity in Mali is independently listed as a residence criterion. Immigration authorization is a separate issue.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A foreign employee should screen progressive ITS up to 37%; DGI guidance covers Mali residents whose employer is abroad. The foreign employer's payroll and social-security obligations need professional determination.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Obtain immigration/professional classification, a NIF, and any required business or patente registration before invoicing. Confirm synthetic-regime eligibility and VAT/export-of-services treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax treatment of foreign-employer salary is clearer after this audit, but no route-specific tax guidance exists because Mali does not publish a dedicated digital-nomad program.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: If approved as an immigrant, the applicant receives a five-year resident card without completing a prior minimum residence period.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed law and decree establish renewable five-year residence but no separate indefinite-residence stage or statutory conversion interval.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization eligibility is measured from ten years of habitual residence rather than from a separately defined permanent-residence date.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the earliest ordinary eligibility point after ten years of habitual residence; naturalization remains discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official administrative page describes issuance of the naturalization decree one year after the filing receipt. Individual processing may exceed that administrative indication.

key_conditions.value: Maintain habitual residence and establishment à demeure; integrate into the Malian community; be an adult or emancipated, mentally capable, and of good character; make the prescribed declaration of submission to the Republic; and have no disqualifying unrehabilitated criminal conviction. A resident card becomes invalid after more than six consecutive months abroad.
key_conditions.notes: The reviewed provisions do not prescribe a formal language-test level or general renunciation requirement. A July 2026 government communiqué announced amendments concerning nationality deprivation and marriage-related provisions, but the final consolidated ordinance was not available through the current official sources reviewed.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Nationality may be acquired through marriage, subject to a one-year government opposition period. The year is an opposition/processing period rather than a minimum pre-application marriage-duration requirement.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing valid marriage to a Malian citizen supports temporary residence and nationality procedures. A marriage celebrated abroad must first be transcribed in the Malian civil-status register; the government's one-year opposition period runs from transcription.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A foreign spouse married to a Malian for at least three months is entitled to temporary stay authorization under the immigration law.

requirements_and_risks.value: File a stamped request with the Ministry of Justice, marriage record, spouse's nationality certificate and birth record, and the prescribed attestation concerning non-repudiation. The government may oppose acquisition within one year, and nationality is lost if the marriage is judicially annulled. False documents or a simulated marriage can lead to refusal, annulment, and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The July 2026 government communiqué announced changes affecting nationality deprivation and marriage-related rules, but the final consolidated ordinance was not retrievable from the current official publications reviewed. Applicants should verify the enacted text before filing.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Mali combines descent with restricted territorial rules. Birth in Mali generally requires an additional statutory connection, such as a parent also born in Mali; foundlings and children of unknown parents receive separate protection.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born to two newly arrived foreign parents does not ordinarily become Malian automatically. A Mali-born child may qualify through double jus soli if at least one foreign parent was also born in Mali, or may acquire nationality around majority after the statutory habitual-residence period.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean represents the ordinary case of two migrant parents. Foundling, unknown-parent, statelessness, and double-jus-soli provisions can produce a different result.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Mali or abroad to a Malian father or mother and a foreign parent is Malian, subject to the Code's filiation and repudiation provisions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Filiation and civil registration must be legally established.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign father or mother of a Malian child residing in Mali is entitled to temporary stay authorization when exercising parental authority, even partly, or effectively supporting the child. The child's citizenship does not automatically confer nationality on the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent separately needs authorization for employment or independent professional activity.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Malian child can obtain temporary stay authorization by proving parentage, the child's residence in Mali, and parental authority or actual support. No automatic permanent residence or citizenship follows.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: If the mother is Malian, the child is Malian by descent; the father's immigration benefit remains a separate application.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed by Passport Index on the research date. Different indexes and refresh dates can produce different ranks.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index includes eVisa destinations within its visa-required total.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reports 28 visa-on-arrival and 3 eTA destinations; eVisa destinations are excluded from this combined figure.

passport.notes: Passport access changes frequently. Passport Index reports a mobility score of 61, comprising 30 visa-free, 28 visa-on-arrival, and 3 eTA destinations. The July 2026 Henley release confirms an index refresh but its accessible public release does not provide Mali's complete category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low outside international organizations and some technology or business settings. The Constitution makes national languages official and French the working language, making French substantially more useful for immigration, tax, banking, and professional authorization.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English may be usable within a foreign remote team, but current official procedures and governing statutes are primarily in French.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official or working language, and the reviewed official material provides no evidence of broad administrative use.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: French and locally relevant official languages are needed for most daily administration.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest published 2023 mean monthly income in principal employment, 55,857 XOF, using about 576 XOF per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2023 median monthly income in principal employment, 32,500 XOF.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 40,000 XOF statutory SMIG reported for 2023. This is a legal minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of 55,857 XOF monthly mean income in principal employment.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of 32,500 XOF monthly median income in principal employment.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed INSTAT tables publish mean, median, and minimum-wage indicators but no national maximum salary statistic; such an economy-wide maximum would not be a stable wage benchmark.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory interprofessional minimum for 2023; the reviewed 2024 table marks the corresponding entry unavailable.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean monthly income in principal employment for 2023, the latest numerical value in the reviewed table.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly income in principal employment for 2023.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed national statistical tables do not report an economy-wide maximum monthly salary or upper wage bound.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly income in principal employment across the labor market; SMIG is a separate statutory formal-sector floor
average_citizen_salary.period: 2023 values published in a 2026 INSTAT statistical yearbook; the reviewed 2024 wage entries did not contain numerical values
average_citizen_salary.notes: The observed median is below the statutory SMIG because the income measure covers principal employment in an economy with extensive informal work. These figures are not a formal-sector software-engineering salary range.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official statistical publications do not provide a current household budget or cost basket tailored to a foreign remote worker. Wage statistics alone are insufficient to estimate accommodation, utilities, security, insurance, and imported-goods costs.

settlement_track.summary: The non-salaried immigrant route grants a five-year renewable resident card, and ordinary law permits naturalization after ten years of habitual residence. The link remains uncertain because current official sources do not classify foreign-client software work under the required professional-authorization system or expressly confirm this activity as establishment à demeure.
settlement_track.notes: This is a genuine residence-oriented statutory route rather than a visitor or temporary nomad permission. It nevertheless requires written, case-specific confirmation from immigration and API-Mali concerning professional classification, competent authority, filing location, and fees.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The statutes permit independent non-salaried establishment and foreign company ownership without a local employer. However, foreign professional activity requires authorization, and the current API-Mali list neither includes ordinary software consulting nor says that unlisted services are exempt. Foreign payroll remote work is also not expressly addressed by the immigration guidance.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field audit inspected more than 15 directly relevant current URLs, including five new official canonical sources covering the Ministry-hosted immigration law, foreign-employer income, professional patente, API-Mali activity approval, the Investment Code, and the Ministry of Security procedures index. Those sources confirm that foreigners may conduct and tax-register professional activity, may own a Malian company, and are taxable on foreign-employer salary when resident. They do not publish a resident-card application page or current card fee, identify the minister competent for ordinary software consulting, state whether that activity needs sector-specific approval, or expressly approve foreign-client remote software work for immigrant establishment. The result therefore remains review-only rather than selected. No dedicated digital-nomad program or route-specific application channel appears in the current official visa, administration, tax, investment, or security sources reviewed.

data.selection_summary: Malta's active Nomad Residence Permit independently accommodates ordinary remote work for a foreign employer or foreign clients. However, the official programme FAQ expressly says it does not lead to permanent/long-term residence or citizenship, and it is capped at four years. Malta is therefore suitable only for temporary remote living, not the requested citizenship-oriented selection. The separate self-employed route requires major investment, local hiring, an endorsed project, or an overseas-company branch and does not fit an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer.

visa_application.title: Residency Malta Agency online application system
visa_application.notes: Official application portal linked from the Nomad Residence Permit FAQ. Applicants should verify nationality eligibility before paying: the current FAQ excludes several nationalities and expressly states that Russian and Belarusian applications are currently ineligible.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,500 per month using the ECB-displayed reference rate of EUR 1 = USD 1.1392; exchange rates fluctuate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 42,000 gross annually (EUR 3,500 monthly)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Current threshold for applications submitted from 1 April 2024. Earlier applicants retained the former EUR 32,400 annual threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 42,000 gross/year (EUR 3,500/month; approximately USD 3,987/month)
income_requirement_display.notes: The euro figure is controlling; the USD amount is an approximate screening conversion.

income_proof_months.notes: The current FAQ requires a guaranteed source of income meeting the threshold for at least five cumulative months from the application date. The Agency may request supporting documentation.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be at least 18, a qualifying third-country national, and capable of location-independent work using telecommunications technology.

Qualifying work must be employment with a foreign-registered employer, activity through a foreign company in which the applicant is a partner/shareholder, or freelance/consulting contracts with foreign-established clients.
Services for Malta-based companies or individuals, including indirect services through a Maltese subsidiary, are ineligible.
Valid passport, health insurance, background screening, and qualifying Malta accommodation covering the permit are required; the residence card requires qualifying residential accommodation.
Application documentation includes forms, letter of intent, employment/business/client contracts, bank evidence, and supporting identity documents.
The programme is discretionary; adverse information, criminal history, eligibility failures, or relevant prior visa refusals may cause rejection.

initial_validity.value: 1 year from issuance of the residence card

extension_rules.value: Renewable three times, for a maximum cumulative stay of four years, at Residency Malta Agency's discretion. Renewal requires continued eligibility and evidence of at least five cumulative months' residence in Malta during the preceding 12 months; apply approximately 2–3 months before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: Previous stays under the programme count toward the four-year cap.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved programme issues a Nomad Residence Permit and residence card allowing the holder to reside in Malta while retaining qualifying foreign work.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is temporary residence only.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A Nomad Residence Permit holder may apply separately for MPRP or another local permit and renounce the nomad permit when approved. This is a conditional successor route, even though nomad residence itself does not lead to PR.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current official FAQ expressly allows a nomad holder to submit an MPRP application and discusses changing to another local permit. This corrects the misleading inference that no direct conversion means no later PR path. Foreign remote income alone does not satisfy either successor route. The old v12 FAQ PDF now returns 404; current v14.1 web FAQ was used.

path_to_citizenship.value: None through this permit. A holder would need to qualify separately for another residence basis whose time counts toward settlement and naturalisation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: General residence-based naturalisation is discretionary and must not be presented as an extension of the Nomad Residence Permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Excellent fit for temporary foreign-contract remote work but rejected because the exact status has no permanent-residence or citizenship transition. Current nationality restrictions must be checked immediately before application.

rejected_routes.route_name: Self-Employed Residence Permit for third-country nationals

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No ordinary monthly-income threshold was found because eligibility instead depends on restrictive business/investment categories.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No ordinary income-only qualification; one route requires EUR 500,000 in fixed Maltese business assets.

income_requirement_display.value: No ordinary income threshold; restrictive business criteria apply, including a possible EUR 500,000 fixed-asset investment
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 500,000 fixed business assets under the investment category
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an income-based freelance route.

income_proof_months.notes: The official FAQ does not establish a general income-history period for an ordinary foreign-contract freelancer.

key_requirements.requirement: A Jobsplus self-employment licence must be obtained before applying for residence.

Applicant must qualify through at least one restrictive category: EUR 500,000 fixed-business-asset investment; highly skilled innovator with a viable plan and commitment to hire at least three Maltese/EU/EEA/Swiss nationals within 18 months; Malta Enterprise-endorsed project leader; or sole representative opening a branch of an overseas company.
The licence and application are personal; an ordinary foreign-client freelance contract alone is insufficient.

initial_validity.value: Up to the expiry date of the underlying Jobsplus employment licence
initial_validity.notes: The official FAQ reviewed did not publish one uniform initial duration.

extension_rules.value: Continued residence depends on renewal/continued validity of the Jobsplus licence and satisfaction of the relevant business conditions.
extension_rules.notes: No ordinary foreign-contract renewal track was identified.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A temporary residence permit may be issued after obtaining the qualifying Jobsplus self-employment licence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially only under the separate general long-term-residence rules after qualifying legal and continuous residence; the official sources do not establish that an ordinary foreign-contract worker can enter this route without meeting its restrictive business criteria.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not cure the initial profile mismatch.

path_to_citizenship.value: Any eventual citizenship claim would be under Malta's separate, discretionary residence-based naturalisation rules, not directly through the self-employment permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is not Malta's equivalent of an ordinary freelancer visa. The applicant's foreign software contract alone does not meet the published eligibility categories.

rejected_routes.route_name: Study residence permit and nine-month post-study permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official study guidance requires sufficient resources but the reviewed page did not establish a single universal monthly amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Financial evidence depends on the study application; no single reliable threshold was captured.

income_requirement_display.value: No single universal amount confirmed; sufficient study and living resources must be documented
income_requirement_display.notes: Do not infer eligibility merely from the applicant's existing foreign income.

income_proof_months.notes: No universal income-history period was confirmed.

key_requirements.requirement: Acceptance into a full-time course, normally MQF Level 5 or higher, at a licensed Maltese institution is required.
The applicant needs the appropriate study visa where applicable, a valid passport, financial resources, insurance, accommodation, and supporting documents.
The one-time post-study permit lasts up to nine months and permits job or qualifying-business seeking; it does not itself authorise full-time employment.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to one year or the expected end of studies if sooner; the post-study permit is up to 9 months

extension_rules.value: Study permits may be renewed while genuine full-time studies and other conditions continue. The nine-month post-study permit is not renewable.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Admission to qualifying full-time study can support a study residence permit without a local employer.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This requires new enrolment in Malta; possessing an existing foreign university degree is not enough.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The official long-term-residence FAQ states that time under a student or vocational-training permit does not count toward the five-year requirement; a switch to a qualifying regular permit is required.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The post-study bridge normally leads to employer-sponsored status or a separately qualifying business, neither of which matches the current profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct citizenship path. A switch to another qualifying residence basis would be required.

rejected_routes.notes: Available without a local employer only if the applicant undertakes qualifying full-time Maltese studies. It is rejected for this profile because an existing degree does not itself grant residence and study time is officially excluded from long-term residence.

summary.value: A third-country national accepted into qualifying full-time Maltese study can independently obtain temporary study residence. An existing foreign degree alone creates no residence entitlement. The reviewed official long-term-residence FAQ excludes student/vocational-training time from the five-year calculation, and the post-study permit is a non-renewable nine-month job/business-search bridge rather than permanent residence.
summary.notes: Useful only if the applicant genuinely enrols in a new Maltese programme; subsequent local employment normally requires employer involvement.

tax_residency_rule.value: Presence in Malta for more than 183 days in a calendar year generally makes an individual tax-resident for that year. A person arriving to establish residence can become resident from arrival regardless of duration. Domicile and ordinary residence separately determine whether worldwide or remittance-basis taxation applies.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence is fact-specific, dual residence is possible, and treaty tie-breaker rules may alter the practical result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Special Nomad Residence Permit rate on chargeable income from authorised work—not an expected effective rate and not the general top marginal rate. A statutory initial 12-month no-tax period and foreign-tax interaction can apply.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Malta's general Class 2 system commonly uses income-based self-occupied contributions, but the reviewed official nomad tax guidance did not establish a universal Maltese social-security percentage for every foreign-employed or foreign-client nomad. Applicable-country social-security rules, EU coordination where relevant, bilateral agreements, and employment structure require individual verification.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal mandatory monthly fixed payment was established for every nomad. The programme instead charges application/card fees and requires private health insurance and accommodation.

special_tax_regimes.value: A valid Nomad Residence Permit holder is taxed at 10% on chargeable income from authorised foreign-employer or foreign-client work. Generally no tax is chargeable on that authorised work before the end of the first 12 months, unless the holder elects immediate taxation or another rule/treaty outcome applies. Foreign tax of at least 10% can remove the Maltese return requirement for that authorised income under the conditions in the official guidance; otherwise foreign-tax relief may apply through a Malta return.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Other income remains governed by the ordinary Income Tax Act and may be taxed at progressive rates.

taxes.caveats: The special 10% rule is limited to authorised work under a valid nomad permit. Residence, ordinary residence, domicile, remittances, source of income, employer permanent-establishment risk, foreign taxes, treaties, and social-security coordination can materially change the result. Obtain Malta tax advice for the actual contract and home-country position.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: a special 10% nomad rate applies to authorised work, while other or non-qualifying income is governed by Malta's ordinary progressive income-tax and residence/domicile rules.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in a year, or from arrival when the facts show that the person came to establish residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Ordinarily resident and domiciled individuals are generally taxed worldwide. Individuals who are not domiciled or not ordinarily resident generally fall under a remittance basis: Malta-source income plus foreign income received in Malta, subject to legislation, special nomad rules, treaties, and exceptions.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Nomad authorised work: 10% special rate, with the statutory first-12-month treatment and foreign-tax provisions described in the official 2026 guidance.
taxation_system.social_security: No universal nomad contribution was confirmed. General Maltese Class 2 contributions apply to qualifying ordinarily resident self-occupied persons and are based on prior-year net profit/income, but cross-border nomad coverage must be determined separately.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 35% general number is the top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate. The 2026 single-person brackets shown here are illustrative; married and parent schedules have different thresholds.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD value is the upper bound using EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.
Approximate USD value is the upper bound.
Approximate USD value is the upper bound.
Approximate USD value is the lower bound; this is a marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: The 10% nomad rate is better supported than the prior generic progressive-tax description because the March 2026 MTCA guidance directly addresses this permit.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Qualifying authorised work is subject to a special 10% rate. Generally, no Maltese tax is chargeable on such work before the end of 12 months from the later statutory date, unless the holder declares that residence was not casual and elects immediate taxation. Other income follows ordinary Maltese rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Special Nomad Residence Permits (Income Tax) Rules regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% special rate on authorised work; statutory initial 12-month and foreign-tax rules may reduce or defer Maltese liability
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: General residence can arise after more than 183 days, or from arrival when residence is being established; the special nomad charging rules must be applied alongside this factual residence test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Authorised foreign-employer/client work receives the special treatment. Other foreign income depends on source, residence, domicile, remittance, treaty, and ordinary Maltese tax rules. Official proof of at least 10% foreign tax on authorised work may remove the Maltese return requirement for that income under the stated conditions.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: 10% on chargeable authorised-work income under S.L. 123.210, effective for qualifying permit holders from 1 January 2024, with the initial 12-month rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The official tax guidance says eligible foreign employers are not subject to Malta's Final Settlement System while the qualifying foreign-employment arrangement continues. It does not conclusively determine social-security coverage; that requires contract- and country-specific review.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed tax or social-security payment confirmed for all nomads.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No Malta FSS payroll obligations for the qualifying non-resident employer under the official nomad tax guidance; social-security coverage remains case-specific.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: EUR 300 non-refundable application fee per person plus EUR 100 residence-card fee per person; other visa fees may apply.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: EUR 50 administrative charges can apply to specified card/address replacement procedures. No universal financial-transaction tax or fixed freelancer levy was established for this scenario.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health insurance and qualifying accommodation are mandatory costs but have no government-fixed universal amount.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being under 183 days does not automatically eliminate Malta tax. Treaty conditions, source of services, an intention to establish residence, and the special nomad rules must all be checked. The special rules generally provide their own initial 12-month treatment for authorised work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A qualifying permit holder generally uses the 10% authorised-work regime rather than treating 35% as the expected rate. Other income can enter the ordinary progressive/remittance framework.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Foreign-client freelance work qualifying as authorised work can receive the nomad regime. Ordinary Malta self-occupation outside it may require tax registration, Jobsplus/business compliance, and Class 2 contributions; it must not be conflated with the restrictive immigration self-employment licence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The precise social-security result remains intentionally unresolved because the official nomad tax material does not provide a universal answer across foreign employment, freelance work, EU coordination, and treaty situations.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence begins when the Nomad Residence Permit/residence card is issued; no preliminary years of residence are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: There is no permanent-residence transition from the Nomad Residence Permit. A separate qualifying status must be obtained, so no defensible route-specific number exists.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Malta's residence-based naturalisation eligibility is based on residence history rather than a fixed number of years after permanent residence, and grant remains ministerially discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No citizenship timeline exists from the nomad route. General naturalisation may be applied for after residence throughout the immediately preceding 12 months plus at least four aggregate years in the prior six, but the nomad permit expressly does not lead to citizenship and approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official citizenship page reviewed does not promise a typical or statutory processing duration for ordinary residence-based naturalisation.

key_conditions.value: For ordinary naturalisation, statutory screening includes adulthood, residence throughout the 12 months immediately before application, at least four aggregate years during the preceding six, good character, adequate Maltese or English, and suitability as a Maltese citizen. Grant is discretionary. These rules do not turn nomad-permit time into a confirmed citizenship path.
key_conditions.notes: Long-term residence separately requires five years of legal continuous qualifying residence, stable resources, accommodation, integration measures, restricted absences, and qualifying status. The nomad permit is officially excluded as a direct settlement route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship by registration is available to a spouse of a Maltese citizen after at least five years of marriage while still married and living together. The official guidance does not state a parallel five-year Malta-residence requirement.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count toward the five-year marriage period. The applicant must still be married to and living with the Maltese citizen when applying. A qualifying widow or widower may also register if the five-year marriage/cohabitation condition was met.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to a non-Maltese spouse has no Maltese citizenship acceleration.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must provide a joint affidavit confirming at least five years of marriage and continued cohabitation, a Malta-registered marriage certificate, identity and civil-status records, and related supporting documents. False affidavits or sham arrangements risk refusal and legal consequences; citizenship is not automatic merely upon marriage.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Current official guidance permits dual Maltese citizenship but advises checking whether the applicant's existing nationality would be lost under the other country's law.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For births on or after 1 August 1989, birth in Malta alone is insufficient: at least one parent normally must be a Maltese citizen or fall within a narrow statutory category. Foundlings who would otherwise be stateless receive protection.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Malta to two foreign temporary migrants does not ordinarily acquire Maltese citizenship solely from local birth. Narrow foundling/statelessness and other statutory exceptions must be assessed separately.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: For a child born in Malta on or after 1 August 1989, having a Maltese-citizen mother or father normally satisfies the parental citizenship condition. Citizenship for a child born abroad can involve additional descent limitations depending on how the Maltese parent acquired citizenship.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This does not automatically give citizenship to the foreign parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A non-EU parent of a dependent Maltese-citizen child may apply for a temporary parent-of-a-Maltese-national residence permit if the dependency, custody/contact, resources, and main-residence requirements are met. This is not automatic and does not itself confer citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The first parent permit is generally one year, with later renewals subject to continuing dependency and the child's age.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father gains no citizenship merely because his child is born in Malta. If the child is independently Maltese and dependent on him, he may seek the conditional parent residence permit on the same basis as a mother, subject to proof of parentage, custody/contact, dependency, resources, and residence in Malta.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Where both parents are foreign nomad-permit holders, the child is normally not Maltese, so this benefit ordinarily does not arise.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's separately labelled visa-free count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 40 visa-on-arrival plus 10 eTA destinations. The index reports these separately; the combined value is calculated for this schema.

passport.notes: The cited index also reports a mobility score of 172. Its methodology and rank are not directly interchangeable with the Henley Passport Index.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. English is constitutionally official, people may address the administration in an official language and receive a reply in that language, and the immigration/tax application material is available in English.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Maltese remains the national language and is the default language of the courts, subject to statutory English-language provisions.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status. No reliable national source reviewed established broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language availability for administration or daily services, so English should be treated as the practical working language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Separately, the current Nomad Residence Permit FAQ says applications from the Russian Federation are currently ineligible; nationality eligibility is distinct from language practicality.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official EUR 2,270 average monthly basic salary using EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed Q1 2026 Labour Force Survey publishes average basic salary tables but did not establish a national median monthly wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly conversion of the statutory adult minimum wage: EUR 229.44 weekly × 52/12 = EUR 994.24 monthly, then converted at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. This is a statutory minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of EUR 2,270.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No official national median was confirmed in the reviewed Q1 2026 release.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary was published; inventing a maximum from occupational averages would be misleading.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 229.44 per week; approximately EUR 994.24 per month using 52/12
min_salary_local_currency.notes: 2026 statutory national minimum for a full-time employee aged 18 or over; sectoral minima and statutory bonuses/allowances may also apply.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly basic salary of employees in the main occupation, Q1 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not established in the reviewed official release.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful official national maximum found.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly basic employee salary and statutory gross minimum wage; not net disposable income
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 average; 2026 minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average covers employees rather than only Maltese citizens and is not a remote-software-engineer salary. USD figures are approximate screening conversions.

cost_of_living_note.value: A fresh official universal monthly cost-of-living amount was not available. Malta's latest Household Budget Survey fieldwork covered November 2024–December 2025, but the NSO said the resulting expenditure data would be used by the end of 2026; therefore no premature monthly budget estimate is supplied.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing and household composition can dominate actual costs; private crowd-sourced estimates were deliberately not substituted for official data.
