settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Nomad Residence Permit fits foreign-contract remote work only as a temporary stay. It is capped at four years and officially provides no permanent/long-term-residence or citizenship path.
settlement_track.summary: Malta's nomad permit is a genuine residence-and-remote-work status, but the official FAQ expressly excludes permanent residence, long-term residence, the separate MPRP, and citizenship. A holder must qualify independently for another status; no ordinary foreign-contract conversion route was confirmed.
settlement_track.notes: The statutory five-year naturalisation screening period must not be applied to nomad-permit time when the programme authority expressly says the status does not lead to citizenship.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True as a temporary remote-work fit: foreign employment and foreign-client freelancing are expressly supported without a Maltese employer. It is not a citizenship-path fit.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Malta record and more than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs. The prior temporary-nomad-only conclusion remains correct. Material improvements include the current EUR 42,000 threshold and five-month income requirement, four-year cap, 2026 special 10% tax rules, separated passport breakdown, current salary/minimum-wage data, stronger citizenship-by-birth analysis, and cautious unresolved treatment of nomad social-security coverage and citizenship processing time.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: MPRP with independent financial eligibility, or a local employment Single Permit followed by long-term residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A Nomad Residence Permit holder may apply separately for MPRP or another local permit and renounce the nomad permit when approved. This is a conditional successor route, even though nomad residence itself does not lead to PR.
requirements: Meet all MPRP property, capital/contribution and eligibility criteria through a licensed agent, or qualify for employment and a Single Permit.
Notify Residency Malta and surrender/revoke nomad status when changing permits.
For the employment route, accrue five qualifying years and satisfy long-term-residence integration and resource conditions.
reviewed_route_names: Nomad Residence Permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The current official FAQ expressly allows a nomad holder to submit an MPRP application and discusses changing to another local permit. This corrects the misleading inference that no direct conversion means no later PR path. Foreign remote income alone does not satisfy either successor route. The old v12 FAQ PDF now returns 404; current v14.1 web FAQ was used.

data.selection_summary: No active independent digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or self-sponsored professional residence route was found. Official rules tie ordinary work visas to an RMI employer's work permit; the self-employed foreign-investor permit requires a licensed local investment business, and statutory time spent as a foreign worker is expressly excluded from the ten-year general-naturalisation residence calculation.

visa_application.title: RMI Division of Immigration — Applications
visa_application.notes: Official forms and checklist page. Its online WebApp is still marked “Coming Soon,” and no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category is listed.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor visa, visa waiver, or visa on arrival

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists; sufficient visitor funds may be requested, but no fixed amount is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The Marshall Islands uses USD. The current visitor material does not publish a fixed funds threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published fixed income threshold; visitor status does not authorize employment
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor entry is not an independent remote-work or residence category.

income_proof_months.notes: The current visitor rules do not prescribe a number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport generally valid for at least six months, onward or return travel, and documents applicable to the nationality and entry category.
The official waiver schedule expressly prohibits employment and, for listed waiver categories, change of status and extensions.

initial_validity.value: Common visitor periods include 30 or 90 days depending on nationality; Compact-country exemptions can differ.
initial_validity.notes: This is visitor permission, not temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: No remote-worker extension route; the official waiver schedule prohibits extensions for listed categories.
extension_rules.notes: Nationality-specific rules must be checked before travel.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No ordinary visitor-to-freelancer or visitor-to-remote-worker conversion is provided in the current official categories.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: In-country work-permit issuance is allowed only exceptionally and is not a dependable self-employment conversion route.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current categories and Immigration Act do not establish permanent-residence progression from visitor status.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time that is not legal residence as an immigrant cannot satisfy naturalisation residence requirements.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is visitor-only and does not authorize employment, qualifying residence, permanent residence, or a credible citizenship path.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employment visa and non-resident worker permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The legislation does not impose an immigration income threshold; local employment is instead subject to employment and minimum-wage rules.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: USD is the local currency; the law does not prescribe a visa-specific monthly threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No visa income threshold published; requires an RMI employer and approved work permit
income_requirement_display.notes: The statutory minimum wage is a labor standard, not an immigration threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The work-permit legislation does not prescribe an applicant income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Except for narrow family and exceptional cases, the employer submits the work-permit application while the worker is outside the country.
The Labor Division requests the employment visa only after approving the work permit.
Professional-shortage and general permits remain employer-led; general permits fill positions where citizens are unavailable or cannot readily be trained.

initial_validity.value: Work-permit validity is tied to the approved employment or contractual obligation; the corresponding work visa cannot exceed two years and follows the permit duration.
initial_validity.notes: The law also requires repatriation or exit after two years from hire, subject to the statutory framework.

extension_rules.value: The employer may apply at least 30 days before expiry; ordinary renewal periods are limited to one year.
extension_rules.notes: Extension uses substantially the same criteria as the initial application.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Allows temporary presence for the approved RMI employment only.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not independent residence for a foreign-client remote worker.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current statutes do not provide an automatic or time-based PR progression from this work permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Not a qualifying naturalisation path: residence while admitted as a foreign worker under the non-resident-worker legislation is expressly excluded from the ten-year residence calculation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This exclusion is decisive for the citizenship-oriented selection.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because sponsorship by an RMI employer is required and the route does not fit an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. Foreign-worker time is expressly excluded from general naturalisation residence.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign investor work permit and business visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The legislation does not prescribe a monthly personal-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: USD is the local currency; the route instead requires a licensed local investment business.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly threshold published; valid Foreign Investment Business License and local business registration required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an investor/entrepreneur route, not ordinary foreign-client freelancing.

income_proof_months.notes: The foreign-investor permit provisions do not prescribe a historical income-evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid Foreign Investment Business License identifying the applicant as owner or legal representative.
Police and health clearances covering the applicant's place of residence during the preceding five years.
Clearance from Finance, Social Security, and local government showing that the company is registered, plus the application fee.

initial_validity.value: Tied to the approved investment business license and work permit; the associated visa may be issued for up to two years.
initial_validity.notes: Exact approval duration is discretionary and fact-dependent.

extension_rules.value: Ordinary work-permit renewals are limited to one year and depend on continuing eligibility and the business license.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal is not an automatic permanent-residence progression.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary presence may be authorized to implement the licensed local investment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This requires local business substance beyond the applicant's ordinary foreign software contract.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current official categories and statute do not create a direct PR entitlement or published investor-to-PR progression.

path_to_citizenship.value: Foreign-worker residence is excluded from the ordinary ten-year naturalisation calculation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No separate investor-to-citizenship track was established.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires founder/investor status, a licensed and registered local enterprise, and local regulatory clearances. It is not an ordinary remote-worker or lightweight sole-proprietor route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official category and regulations require evidence of financial ability but do not prescribe a fixed monthly amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: USD is the local currency; the current official material does not specify a fixed amount.

income_requirement_display.value: Financial ability required, but no fixed amount is published
income_requirement_display.notes: Admission and student documentation must be verified from the current checklist.

income_proof_months.notes: The current checklist page and regulations do not prescribe a fixed number of months.

key_requirements.requirement: Purpose must be study at a college-level academic institution, with evidence of acceptance and the official student-visa form and checklist.
The student visa does not permit employment or business activities.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year.
initial_validity.notes: This is study permission rather than a degree-based skilled residence program.

extension_rules.value: Any renewal is discretionary under immigration rules; no graduate residence track is established in the current categories.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic post-study status is provided.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary study stay only.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not authorize the applicant's ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current categories and statute do not provide an education-to-PR route.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act does not establish student status as a direct citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because possessing a relevant degree does not create an independent skilled or qualification-based residence entitlement.

summary.value: A student visa exists, but no independent degree-based, points-tested, graduate, or skilled residence program was found. The occupational-shortage professional permit still requires an employer to apply.
summary.notes: The applicant's software-engineering degree does not independently confer residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: No general day-count tax-residence test was identified. The OECD jurisdiction sheet states that individual tax liability is determined by Part II of the Income Tax Act, whose wage rules focus on compensation for personal services; treatment of a foreign payer and offshore contract requires filing-level advice.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Do not import the U.S.-territory 183-day rule: the Marshall Islands is an independent state in free association with the United States.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening wage-tax rate effective from October 2025, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee payroll share: 8% retirement plus 3.5% health, subject to separate quarterly earnings caps. Employers contribute an equivalent share. A self-employed person can therefore bear both sides, effectively 23% of the prescribed contribution base.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: MISSA publishes percentage-based quarterly contributions rather than a fixed monthly minimum.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. Defined U.S.-contractor personnel may qualify for a separate 5% wage-tax treatment, but that does not apply to an ordinary foreign client contract.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The special U.S.-contractor rule should not be generalized.

taxes.caveats: Tax exposure depends on where services are physically performed, employee-versus-independent-contractor classification, whether a local business is operated, the foreign payer's presence, social-security registration, and any treaty or Compact rule. No immigration route authorizes the target remote-work scenario, so the tax analysis is hypothetical and not evidence of work authorization.

taxation_system.value: Wage tax uses a conditional exemption and two positive rates. From October 2025, annual wages of USD 8,320 or less are exempt; if wages exceed USD 8,320, the first USD 10,400 is taxed at 8% and the excess at 12%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No general day-count test was established; individual liability is governed by Part II of the Income Tax Act and the source/classification of compensation.
taxation_system.income_scope: Wages and salaries attributable to personal services are covered; the precise treatment of foreign-paid remote services and independent business receipts requires advice from the RMI Division of Revenue and Taxation.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Defined U.S.-contractor personnel may be taxed at 5%; no digital-nomad exemption or inbound regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Employee: 8% retirement plus 3.5% health, with an equal employer contribution and separate quarterly caps. Self-employed reporting uses a statutory base, generally 75% of quarterly gross revenue for a person with no employees.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 12% value is the top marginal wage-tax screening rate. The USD 8,320 exemption creates a discontinuity: a worker at or below that annual total is exempt, while a worker above it is not eligible for the exemption.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual wages and salaries of USD 8,320 or less
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employees whose total annual wages do not exceed USD 8,320
tax_brackets.notes: This exemption does not function as an ordinary tax-free first bracket once total wages exceed USD 8,320.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First USD 10,400 of annual wages where total wages exceed USD 8,320
tax_brackets.notes: Applies to the first USD 10,400 when the employee is ineligible for the low-income exemption.
Top marginal/screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: Current wage rates and payroll contributions are well supported. Confidence is lower for an offshore-payer remote contractor because neither an authorized remote-work route nor sufficiently specific official sourcing guidance was found.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special nomad tax treatment exists in the reviewed official material. A person actually performing services in RMI could face wage/business and social-security rules even when paid abroad, but classification must be confirmed with the tax authority.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No route; hypothetical foreign-paid worker or locally registered independent contractor
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 12% wage tax, plus potentially 11.5% employee payroll contributions or both contribution shares for self-employment
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No confirmed day-count rule; liability is determined under the Income Tax Act based on the relevant compensation and activity.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The current tax sources do not conclusively determine the treatment of ordinary remote services paid by a foreign client or employer with no RMI presence.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No such regime appears in the current immigration and tax sources.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee share is 8% retirement plus 3.5% health, with an equal employer share. Independent contractors are liable in their own right under self-employment procedures.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed monthly minimum is prescribed in the reviewed MISSA material; percentage-based quarterly liabilities may apply.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: 8% retirement and 3.5% health per employee side; self-employed persons may bear both sides on the prescribed base, subject to caps.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee is applicable because RMI has no digital-nomad visa. The published Immigration Regulations fee schedule lists USD 100 for a visitor visa, USD 200 for a work visa, USD 300 for a business visa, USD 150 for a provisional business visa, and USD 50 for an alien registration card; these categories do not legalize ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The Immigration application page does not display fee amounts, so applicants should confirm the regulation amounts with Immigration before payment. A separate USD 20 international-airport departure fee applies to travelers aged 13–59.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business licensing, gross-revenue, local-government, or registration liabilities may arise if operating a local enterprise; the reviewed official sources do not prescribe a universal fixed remote-freelancer payment.
fixed_payments.notes: There is no route-specific nomad charge. Published visa and registration charges are category-specific state fees, not monthly payments and not a substitute for work authorization. MISSA liabilities are percentage-based and reported quarterly.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no verified day-count safe harbor. Visitor rules prohibit employment, so a short stay should not be treated as work authorization or automatic tax exemption.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No dedicated category exists. Services physically performed in RMI may fall within wage or business taxation and payroll rules regardless of a foreign payer; obtain written authority guidance.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally operating self-employed person generally needs the foreign-investor/business framework and may owe both social-security and health contribution sides on a statutory contribution base.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a hypothetical tax screen, not confirmation that foreign remote work is legally permitted.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker temporary-residence route exists.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The current official sources do not establish a remote-worker-to-PR transition or general time-based PR progression applicable to this profile.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The law uses ten years of qualifying ordinary residence rather than a published number of years after PR.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the general naturalisation residence requirement, not a usable timeline from the target profile. Time admitted as a foreign worker is expressly excluded.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current Citizenship Act and legislation index do not publish an administrative processing-time standard.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation is discretionary and requires ten immediately preceding years of qualifying ordinary residence, domicile, good character, conversational Marshallese, understanding of customs and the Constitution, means of support, a written test, oath, and normally renunciation. The annual general-naturalisation quota is ten persons including dependants, and foreign-worker residence is excluded.
key_conditions.notes: Because the available employment route does not generate countable residence, the ten-year rule does not rescue this country for the selected profile.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The current Citizenship Act does not provide a spouse-specific citizenship or PR acceleration. A separate family work permit requires at least one year of marriage, but it is not citizenship or PR.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A person legally married to an RMI citizen for at least one year and lawfully present may apply for a family work permit, subject to the required employer/spouse declaration, marriage certificate, entry or residence document, and fee.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing marriage shorter than one year does not yet satisfy this work-permit condition.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally documented and genuine. The family work permit does not grant automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship, and the Citizenship Act provides no spouse shortcut. False statements can lead to refusal, penalties, visa cancellation, or removal.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Citizenship eligibility should not be inferred from eligibility for a family work permit.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in RMI confers citizenship only when the child is not entitled at birth to be or become a citizen of another country. Otherwise citizenship is primarily by descent.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Normally no. A child born in RMI becomes a citizen only if the child is not entitled at birth to be or become a citizen of any other country.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is an anti-statelessness safeguard, not broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born on or after the Constitution's effective date is a citizen when either parent is an RMI citizen at the date of birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The citizen parent may be the mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A non-citizen parent of an RMI-citizen child may apply for citizenship by registration after at least three years of legal residence, subject to High Court review, national-security clearance, oath, and generally renunciation. The child's citizenship does not automatically legalize or naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: This benefit applies only if the child is actually an RMI citizen and the parent has qualifying legal residence.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic status merely from the child's birth. If the child is an RMI citizen, the father can potentially use the parent-of-citizen registration ground after three years of legal residence; if the other parent is only a permanent resident, the child is not automatically a citizen unless otherwise stateless.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: High Court and national-security requirements remain, and renunciation is generally required.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026; category breakdown cross-checked with AbroadPilot

rank.notes: The current 2026 Henley ranking page showed Marshall Islands at joint 40th with a mobility score of 128 when checked.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's score counts destinations accessible without obtaining a visa before departure, including visa-on-arrival categories; it is not a literal visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Secondary open-dataset breakdown; methodology differs from Henley and separately lists 40 eVisa destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The secondary breakdown reports 33 visa-on-arrival and 3 eTA destinations, combined here. Entry rules change frequently.

passport.notes: Henley rank and mobility score are preferred for headline comparison. The category breakdown comes from a current secondary open-dataset source because Henley's public ranking does not expose a simple visa-required/VOA/eTA breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is an official language, so government-facing and professional communication is comparatively practical. Connectivity remains uneven: about 66% of the population used the internet in 2024, provider choice was rated poor, and the IMF reported that RMI lagged peers despite Starlink becoming available in 2025 and continuing infrastructure investment.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Most realistic in Majuro and other connected population centers; verify accommodation-level speed, latency, power reliability, and backup connectivity before relying on remote work.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, and the reviewed sources do not show broadly available public services or professional support in either language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: English would generally be required for immigration, business, and professional interactions.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: USD 1,499.50 monthly equivalent of the directly published FY2024 average annual wage of USD 17,994. This is a payroll/formal-sector average, not a median and not an immigration income threshold.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Current payroll statistics publish average annual wages, while the 2021 census publishes median household income rather than median pay per worker. The ILO HIES catalogue, ILOSTAT profile, and ADB indicator collection do not provide a defensible national median individual salary in their public country summaries; the value therefore remains null.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the statutory USD 4.50 hourly minimum in force on 2026-08-15, assuming 40 hours per week and 52 weeks per year. The law states an hourly, not monthly, amount.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Monthly equivalent of the directly published FY2024 average annual wage of USD 17,994. It covers payroll/formal-sector employment and is not restricted to citizens.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national median individual employee wage is published in the current public payroll review or the checked census, HIES catalogue, ILOSTAT, and ADB summaries. The census median is household income and cannot be substituted for an individual salary median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The checked official and international datasets publish averages, employment totals, minimum-wage rules, or household-income statistics, but no national maximum employee salary or upper endpoint of an employee-wage distribution. A true maximum is not a stable labor-market statistic, so no value is inferred.

min_salary_local_currency.value: USD 4.50 per hour (approximately USD 780/month at 40 hours/week)
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage effective from 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30, unless a legislated halt is adopted. The scheduled rate is USD 5.00 from 2026-10-01.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: RMI uses USD, so no currency conversion is needed. This is the FY2024 average annual payroll wage converted to a monthly equivalent.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: USD is the local currency, but no national median individual wage amount is published in the current payroll statistics or the checked census, HIES, ILOSTAT, and ADB public materials. The published median household-income figure measures a different unit and is not inserted here.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: USD is the local currency. No national maximum salary or published upper endpoint of an individual wage distribution appears in the current payroll review, census, HIES catalogue, ILOSTAT profile, or ADB indicators, so the field remains null rather than using a sector average as a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory minimum wage plus the directly published FY2024 average annual payroll wage; median household income is deliberately not treated as median individual salary.
average_citizen_salary.period: FY2024 average wage; statutory minimum wage effective on 2026-08-15.
average_citizen_salary.notes: Salary figures describe resident/formal-sector workers, not a digital-nomad income threshold. The minimum is the statutory hourly wage converted at 40 hours per week; the average is a direct FY2024 payroll statistic. Focused checks of the current payroll release, census, HIES catalogue, ILOSTAT, and ADB materials found no national median individual salary and no meaningful maximum salary, so both remain null with the statistical-unit limitation explained.

cost_of_living_note.value: The IMF describes RMI as highly import-dependent and expected inflation to remain elevated, while connectivity and geographic remoteness can increase practical living costs.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is qualitative; the reviewed sources do not provide a current national monthly cost-of-living basket suitable for a budget estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No official digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor permission does not authorize employment or settlement.
settlement_track.summary: The official framework provides no qualifying independent route for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. Although general naturalisation nominally requires ten years of qualifying residence, time admitted as a foreign worker is expressly excluded and no remote-worker-to-PR conversion is provided.
settlement_track.notes: A different legal basis producing countable residence would be required, but no ordinary route matching the applicant was established.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker status exists; visitor categories prohibit employment, employer-sponsored permits require an RMI employer, and the independent investor permit requires a licensed local investment business.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit preserves the prior negative selection. It resolves the fee field with the published Immigration Regulations schedule and replaces the inferred wage average with the directly published FY2024 payroll average. Median and maximum individual salary values remain null because the newest payroll release reports averages, the census reports household income, and the checked HIES, ILOSTAT, ADB, IMF, and World Bank materials do not publish those individual-wage statistics. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including eight URLs outside the previous source set.

data.selection_summary: Mauritania has an official eVisa and residence-card procedures, but no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route was found. Employment requires a Mauritanian employer and work permit; independent gainful activity or company-owner residence requires local business registration, tax compliance and ministerial authorization, so it is not a confirmed fit for an ordinary software engineer continuing only a foreign contract.

visa_application.title: ANRPTS eVisa application
visa_application.notes: This is the official electronic visitor-visa application, offering 30-, 90- and 360-day visa options. It is not an application for remote-work residence or permission to work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly income threshold is displayed by the official eVisa application.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is published on the application page.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; visitor eVisa only
income_requirement_display.notes: Absence of an income threshold does not make the eVisa a work or residence route.

income_proof_months.notes: The public application page does not state a required income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Complete the official electronic application using passport and traveller details before travel.
The issued eVisa must be printed; applicable fees are paid on arrival according to current government travel guidance based on Mauritanian rules.

initial_validity.value: The application offers 30-, 90- and 360-day visa options.
initial_validity.notes: These are visa options, not residence permits.

extension_rules.notes: The official application and tracking pages publish no eVisa extension rule. Overstayers must regularise before departure, but that penalty process is not an extension or residence conversion.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic conversion. A separate residence-card basis and supporting documents are required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor status alone is insufficient.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The inspected law establishes renewable resident cards but no permanent-residence progression from an eVisa.

path_to_citizenship.notes: An eVisa is not a confirmed qualifying residence basis for the five-year habitual-residence naturalisation rule.

rejected_routes.notes: This is independently available for entry but is visitor status only. It neither authorizes ordinary foreign-contract remote work nor supplies a confirmed settlement track.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign-worker permit and employment-based residence card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general immigration salary threshold was found; eligibility is tied to a Mauritanian job and employer filing.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The statutory SMIG is a labour-law floor, not a published immigration eligibility threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No general immigration income threshold; Mauritanian employer required
income_requirement_display.notes: The decisive condition is employer sponsorship and labour approval, not foreign income.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history requirement was established.

key_requirements.requirement: A Mauritanian employer completes and signs the application.
The employer must explain why the position cannot be filled by a Mauritanian worker.
Qualifications, CV, passport and employment documents are required.
The residence card requires an approved work permit or employment contract and a passport valid for more than six months.

initial_validity.value: Work permit A: one year, renewable; permit B: up to four years; permit C: indefinite employment authorization after qualifying long residence.
initial_validity.notes: A work permit is distinct from the one-to-five-year biometric resident card.

extension_rules.value: Permit A is renewable. Permit B may cover up to four years. Permit C may be available after at least ten years of uninterrupted lawful residence and work, subject to additional conditions.
extension_rules.notes: These rules remain employer/local-work oriented.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A worker can apply separately for a resident card using an approved local employment contract or work permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The work permit does not itself constitute the resident card.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permit C provides indefinite employment authorization, but the inspected material does not establish that it is legal permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalisation may be requested after at least five years of habitual residence, but this does not cure the route's local-employer requirement.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A residence card, criminal record and morality investigation are required for the naturalisation filing.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the application is employer-led, requires local employment and includes a labour-market justification. A foreign client or foreign employer does not satisfy this route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence card for personal gainful activity or local company owner

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum personal income threshold was published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum income or capital figure was established.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; local business evidence and authorization required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a passive foreign-income or digital-nomad route.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed income-history period was published.

key_requirements.requirement: A company owner must provide a commercial-register extract; associates must provide company rules and the commercial register.
Evidence of continuing payment of Mauritanian taxes is required.
A person undertaking personal gainful activity needs authorization from the responsible minister.
Residence-card applicants may need a medical certificate, vaccination certificate, recent criminal record, tax stamp and fingerprints.

initial_validity.value: Resident cards are valid for one to five years under Decree No. 2024-042.
initial_validity.notes: The decree gives a general range for biometric resident cards; it does not assign a specific term to the company-owner or personal-gainful-activity category.

extension_rules.value: A biometric resident card may be renewed in person at a Resident Reception Centre—or, where unavailable, the local Citizen Reception Centre—or remotely through Houwiyeti after biometric authentication.
extension_rules.notes: Decree No. 2024-042 confirms the one-to-five-year card-validity range and renewal channels, but it does not publish a category-specific renewal term, automatic-renewal right or approval test for company owners or personal gainful activity. Continued local-business, tax-payment and ministerial-authorization evidence therefore remains subject to current filing practice.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The official residence-card procedure recognizes local company owners and associates when commercial-registration and tax evidence is supplied.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Ministerial authorization is additionally described for personal gainful activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current decree establishes resident-card validity and renewal mechanics but no statutory conversion from this category to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Habitual lawful residence could potentially support a discretionary naturalisation request after five years, but whether this exact status continuously qualifies requires filing-level verification.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is by decree after investigation, not automatic.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because the evidence supports a locally registered and tax-compliant business or specifically authorized gainful activity, not ordinary remote work conducted solely under a foreign contract. No simple visitor-to-freelancer legalization process or confirmed settlement progression was found.

summary.value: Students enrolled in public universities or institutes can obtain a resident card using a valid enrolment certificate and passport; private-school enrolment must be certified by the supervising ministry. This is education-based temporary residence, not an independent skilled-worker or degree-based migration route, and no direct permanent-residence outcome was found.
summary.notes: A pre-existing software-engineering degree alone does not confer residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: There is no simple 183-day-only rule in the current summary. Tax residence can arise from maintaining a permanent home, having one's primary residence or centre of vital interests in Mauritania, or performing a principal professional activity there, subject to an applicable tax treaty.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence may therefore arise before 183 days depending on facts.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for employment income, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For locally registered salaried work, the employee-side total reported by CLEISS is 5%: 4% health on the full salary plus 1% for CNSS branches on salary capped at MRU 70,000 per month. The employer-side total is 20%: 5% health, 13% CNSS and 2% occupational medicine, with the MRU 70,000 ceiling applying to the latter two components. The CNSS declaration form independently displays 13%, 1% and 2%. PwC's narrower summary reports only 1% employee and 15% employer social-security contributions with an older MRU 15,000 ceiling; the 5% dashboard value includes health and uses the more detailed 2025 contribution breakdown. The sources do not state whether an overseas employer without Mauritanian payroll must register or withhold for a remote worker.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal fixed monthly freelancer or digital-nomad payment. Employee contributions are percentage-based; voluntary CNASS health coverage for non-salaried workers and business minimum taxes are annual rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, inbound-worker or remittance-basis regime was found. Personal business income under actual-income regimes may be taxed at 30% of the tax base or 2.5% of revenue, whichever is higher, with stated minimum tax amounts.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business classification and current filing rules require professional verification.

taxes.caveats: Mauritania has no confirmed remote-worker immigration category. Tax treatment depends on whether the foreign contract is employment or independent business income, when tax domicile begins, local registration, treaty coverage and whether foreign tax was paid. Professional advice is necessary before working from Mauritania.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income, although foreign income can be excluded where the taxpayer proves it was taxed abroad. Employment income is progressive at 15%, 25% and 40%; business income uses separate regimes.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, primary residence or centre of vital interests, or principal professional activity in Mauritania; treaty rules may override.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident worldwide income, with relief where foreign taxation is proven; non-residents are taxed only on Mauritanian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or general inbound exemption found. Personal business regimes have separate profit/revenue formulas and minimum tax amounts.
taxation_system.social_security: For local payroll, employees pay 5% in total—4% health on full salary plus 1% CNSS on salary capped at MRU 70,000—and employers pay 20% in total—5% health, 13% CNSS and 2% occupational medicine, with the MRU 70,000 ceiling applying to the latter two components.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 40% figure is the top marginal dashboard screening rate. It applies only to the portion of taxable monthly remuneration above MRU 21,000 and is not an effective-rate estimate.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate upper boundary converted at about MRU 40.21 per USD; the current tax table begins at MRU 6,000.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Above MRU 9,000 through MRU 21,000 per month
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure approximates the upper boundary.
Top marginal bracket begins at approximately USD 522 monthly.

taxation_system.notes: PwC's Mauritania individual pages were reviewed on 7 August 2026 and are current professional summaries rather than primary tax legislation; the tax authority's business-regime page, CNSS form and CLEISS contribution table were used as cross-checks.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax category exists. If a person nevertheless becomes resident while working for a foreign employer, employment income can be taxed at progressive rates up to 40%; independent business income can fall under separate business regimes.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated route; fact-dependent employment or personal business income
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 40% top marginal employment-income rate; this is not the expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Potentially from a permanent home, centre of vital interests, primary residence or principal professional activity rather than a fixed day count alone.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident worldwide income is generally taxable, but foreign income is not taxed where the taxpayer proves it was taxed abroad; treaty mechanics and documentation matter.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No digital-nomad payroll rule exists. For ordinary local payroll, the published employee total is 5% and employer total 20%, with component-specific bases and an MRU 70,000 ceiling for CNSS and occupational-medicine contributions. A foreign employer without Mauritanian payroll needs case-specific registration advice.

fixed_payments.status: No dedicated digital-nomad fixed-payment schedule applies because Mauritania has no digital-nomad route. For a genuinely self-employed person, the checked social-security source identifies voluntary CNASS health coverage of MRU 700 per year per enrolled person, of which MRU 250 is paid by the insured and MRU 450 by the state; business minimum taxes are annual and regime-dependent, not a universal monthly nomad charge.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Local employees face percentage-based payroll contributions rather than a fixed amount. Non-salaried workers may voluntarily join CNASS health coverage at MRU 700 per person per year—MRU 250 paid by the insured and MRU 450 state-funded—subject to the family or collective-enrolment conditions described by CLEISS.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The Mauritanian Foreign Ministry publishes visa charges by duration and region, but no remote-worker visa or dedicated remote-worker residence fee exists.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Personal business regimes can impose minimum annual tax: PwC reports MRU 125,000 under the normal regime and MRU 75,000 under the intermediary regime. VAT is generally 16%, with exports of services stated at 0%, subject to classification.
fixed_payments.notes: The current sources publish visa charges, local-payroll percentages, voluntary CNASS health coverage and annual minimum business taxes, but no residence-card fee, municipal charge or mandatory fixed freelancer payment specifically applicable to a foreign-contract remote worker. A digital-nomad tariff is inapplicable because no such immigration or tax category exists.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short visitor stay does not authorize work. Tax domicile may still depend on home, vital interests and professional activity rather than days alone.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Foreign-employer remuneration can be taxable in Mauritania when the employee is tax resident, even if work is performed inside or outside Mauritania and the employer is abroad.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Personal business income may face 30% of taxable profit or 2.5% of revenue, whichever is higher, plus minimum-tax and registration obligations depending on regime.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening analysis because there is no matching immigration route and no published digital-nomad tax guidance.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A resident card may be requested at least 15 days before visa or entry authorization expires after satisfying a recognized basis, but no standard processing period or qualifying ordinary remote-work basis is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No general permanent-residence status or conversion timeline for the target profile was established. A renewable one-to-five-year resident card and an indefinite work permit are not proven to equal permanent residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on habitual residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence stage.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The general five-year habitual-residence rule cannot be treated as a route-specific total because no qualifying initial remote-work residence route exists and naturalisation is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official procedure publishes no fixed processing period; completion follows presidential approval.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires at least five years of habitual residence unless a statutory waiver applies, an application by the individual, investigation, a residence card, criminal record and morality inquiry. Grant is by decree and remains discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: Current official guidance did not establish language, absence, income, tax-compliance or prior-nationality renunciation rules sufficiently for a numeric dashboard timeline.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The nationality-code text waives the five-year habitual-residence period for a person married to a Mauritanian woman. It also contains an immediate rule for a foreign woman marrying a Mauritanian man, but the gender-specific interaction with the 2021 amendment requires current legal confirmation.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A documented marriage to a Mauritanian citizen is an express resident-card basis. The nationality code also provides marriage-related acquisition or waiver rules, although current application should be verified against the 2021 amendment.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A biometric Mauritanian marriage certificate, court decision or properly authenticated foreign marriage certificate may support residence.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally documented and genuine. Residence or nationality is not automatic for every foreign spouse: the historical code uses gender-specific rules, naturalisation can require investigation and decree, and sham or undocumented marriages should not be relied on.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The inspected 2021 amendment record confirms later legislation exists, but its full consolidated effect on every marriage provision was not text-searchable; obtain current advice before relying on immediate acquisition.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Mauritania to two foreign parents does not ordinarily grant citizenship automatically. The code provides a later option near majority after at least five years' residence, alongside descent, foundling and anti-statelessness-related rules.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Mauritania to two foreign parents is not ordinarily Mauritanian at birth. Under the code, the child may opt for nationality during the year before majority if resident in Mauritania for at least five years.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Narrow rules for foundlings, unknown parents or avoidance of statelessness may produce different results.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Citizenship by descent is available through a Mauritanian parent, subject to the detailed place-of-birth, filiation and election provisions of the nationality code and its amendments.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Filiation must be legally established. The 2021 amendment should be checked for the current treatment of maternal transmission in the specific case.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship on a foreign father. Any residence benefit requires a separate recognized residence basis and documentation.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The inspected residence procedure lists marriage and a documented family relationship but does not establish automatic parent-of-citizen residence.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic nationality or permanent residence arises for the migrant father merely because his child is Mauritanian.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Family-based discretionary relief should be checked with ANRPTS and the Ministry of Justice.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank reported by Passport Index; its separate Individual Power Rank was 156.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free count on 15 August 2026.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count. Methodologies differ between indexes, especially in their handling of eVisas.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 34 visa-on-arrival and three eTA destinations reported by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported mobility score 64. VisaIndex independently reported 26 visa-free, 26 visa-on-arrival and one eTA destination and rank 85, illustrating methodology or update differences.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low outside international, technical and tourism settings. Arabic is the sole official language, while French is widely used as a practical working language; English alone is unlikely to be sufficient for government, immigration and routine local administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The official eVisa interface is available in English, but the residence and labour procedures inspected were principally Arabic or French.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. No evidence was found that Russian or Ukrainian is routinely usable for immigration, business registration or daily administration; Arabic or French assistance would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practicality assessment based on the documented language environment, not a measured proficiency survey.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of Numbeo's crowd-sourced Nouakchott average net salary of MRU 22,775 at about MRU 40.21 per USD. This is city-level and low-confidence, not an official national mean.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The Labour Ministry materials publish a minimum wage, not a median; ILOSTAT's accessible Mauritania profile does not expose a current national median-wage observation, and Numbeo reports a Nouakchott mean only.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the derived current SMIG of MRU 5,040 per month at about MRU 40.21 per USD. This is a statutory wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate crowd-sourced net salary for Nouakchott, not a reliable national citizen average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current Labour Ministry materials publish the SMIG, not a national median; the inspected ILOSTAT country profile does not expose a current Mauritania median-wage observation, and Numbeo reports a Nouakchott mean rather than a median. A national monthly median therefore cannot be stated from these named sources.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the Labour Ministry wage materials nor the inspected ILOSTAT and Nouakchott sources publish a national maximum wage. Earnings are not capped by the SMIG decree, so no defensible USD maximum can be calculated.

min_salary_local_currency.value: MRU 5,040 per month (derived 2026 SMIG for a 40-hour workweek)
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The ministry published Decree No. 2026-064 setting the SMIG and separately stated that the 2026 increase is 12%. Applying that enacted increase to the previously published MRU 4,500 monthly SMIG gives MRU 5,040. The amount is explicitly presented as a transparent derivation because the scanned decree attachment did not expose searchable amount text.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Crowd-sourced average net salary for Nouakchott, updated June 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No national monthly median is published in the inspected Labour Ministry wage-law page or exposed by the ILOSTAT Mauritania profile; the available Nouakchott crowd-sourced page reports an average only. The field remains null because a minimum wage or mean cannot substitute for a median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither the Labour Ministry wage-law page nor the inspected ILOSTAT profile publishes a national maximum salary, and the Nouakchott crowd-sourced page supplies no statistically meaningful upper bound. Because earnings are not legally capped and a sample maximum would be unstable, this field is inapplicable as a national salary statistic.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Nouakchott crowd-sourced average monthly net salary plus the national statutory SMIG; no official national mean, median or maximum series was established
average_citizen_salary.period: April-August 2026 for the SMIG; June 2026 for the Nouakchott average
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum is the statutory national SMIG, transparently derived as MRU 5,040 from the official 12% 2026 increase and the previously published MRU 4,500 base. The MRU 22,775 average remains a small-sample Nouakchott net-salary estimate. No current national mean, median or maximum was published in the inspected official and international sources.

cost_of_living_note.value: Numbeo's June 2026 Nouakchott sample reported approximately MRU 8,700 monthly for a one-bedroom city-centre apartment, MRU 6,000 outside the centre and MRU 2,400 for broadband. The page had only nine contributors in the preceding 12 months, so figures are indicative rather than authoritative.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Crowd-sourced secondary data with a small sample.
