settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The eVisa is visitor status only. No official digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was confirmed.
settlement_track.summary: Mauritania's general law permits discretionary naturalisation after at least five years of habitual residence, but the applicant first needs a lawful qualifying residence basis. The available visitor, employer-sponsored and locally authorized business categories do not provide a confirmed ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.
settlement_track.notes: Company-owner residence might support lawful residence for a genuine local business, but it requires local registration, ongoing Mauritanian tax compliance and authorization; it was not established as a foreign-contract remote-work route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker visa was found. The eVisa is visitor status, local employment requires employer sponsorship, and personal gainful activity requires authorization and local business evidence.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field audit retained the supported ineligibility conclusion and added the 2024 resident-card decree, 2026 SMIG materials, CNSS/CNAM contribution evidence, current visa guidance and migration-administration sources. Resident cards are now confirmed as valid for one to five years with formal renewal channels; employee-side payroll contributions total 5%; and the current monthly SMIG is transparently derived as MRU 5,040. National median and maximum wage fields remain null with source-specific explanations because the current official, ILOSTAT and city-salary materials do not publish those statistics.

data.selection_summary: Mauritius independently permits foreign-source remote work through the renewable Premium Visa, but that visa is a temporary long-stay status with no confirmed permanent-residence or citizenship clock. The separate Self-Employed Occupation Permit requires USD 50,000 investment and prospective Mauritian clients, while the Professional Occupation Permit requires local employment. No citizenship-oriented route therefore fits the ordinary foreign-contract software-engineer profile.

visa_application.title: National Electronic Licensing System — Premium Visa application
visa_application.notes: The official EDB Premium Visa page directs applicants to this electronic licensing platform. Registration or login is required, and the Premium Visa has no application or processing fee.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly-income threshold is published; applicants instead submit proof of monthly income and recent bank statements.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed MUR threshold is published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official checklist requires sufficient-funds evidence but states no minimum income or bank balance.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; proof of monthly income and three months of bank statements required
income_requirement_display.notes: An unofficial income estimate should not be substituted for the official documentary test.

income_proof_months.notes: The checklist requests bank statements for the preceding three months and proof of monthly income.

key_requirements.requirement: The main place of business and source of income or profits must remain outside Mauritius, and the holder must not enter the Mauritian labour market.
Travel and health insurance covering the intended stay.
Accommodation evidence and a return ticket covering a stay exceeding six months.
Passport, photograph and evidence supporting the purpose of the long stay.

initial_validity.value: More than six months and up to one year
initial_validity.notes: Official sources describe it as a renewable one-year long-stay visa.

extension_rules.value: Renewable through another online application with updated documents
extension_rules.notes: The reviewed official material specifies neither a maximum number of renewals nor an entitlement to renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: It authorizes a temporary long stay but is not presented as an Occupation Permit or residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A holder may make a separate application for an Occupation Permit or qualifying Residence Permit but must independently meet that route's requirements.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The official Premium Visa FAQ expressly permits an Occupation Permit application during the stay. A qualifying self-employed OP holder can apply for the renewable 20-year PRP after five years meeting the prescribed business-income/turnover test.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This requires investment and a locally established professional business, so it is conditional for an ordinary foreign-only remote worker. Premium Visa time does not substitute for the required OP years. Five years starts on the qualifying OP; the PRP is legally named permanent residence but has renewable 20-year validity.

path_to_citizenship.value: No confirmed citizenship path from the Premium Visa itself.
path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation is discretionary and residence-based. The Citizenship Act does not confirm that Premium Visa time qualifies and restricts ordinary naturalisation while an applicant holds temporary-residence status.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a strong temporary-living fit for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker, including a Ukrainian applicant, but it fails the citizenship-oriented selection because it is not established by the current sources as qualifying residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route uses investment and business-income tests rather than a monthly salary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Announced criteria: MUR 2 million annual business income from year 3 and MUR 3 million from year 5
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: These correspond to approximately MUR 166,667 and MUR 250,000 per month but are business-performance tests, not salary requirements.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 50,000 investment plus local-client and escalating business-income requirements
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Capital investment and annual business income
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: MUR 2 million/year from year 3; MUR 3 million/year from year 5
income_requirement_display.notes: The EDB route page and July 2026 policy material contain different renewal figures; the operative regulations should be confirmed before filing.

income_proof_months.notes: No ordinary income-history period is stated; the application instead relies on investment, a business plan and client commitments.

key_requirements.requirement: USD 50,000 investment in the professional activity.
Three contracts or letters of intent, including two from potential Mauritian clients.
Business plan, qualifications, CV, business registration and transfer of investment funds to a Mauritian bank account.

initial_validity.value: 10 years
initial_validity.notes: The official residency portal describes the permit as renewable.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on business-income performance; July 2026 material states MUR 3 million annual income from year 5.
extension_rules.notes: Filing-level confirmation is advisable because older and newly announced figures coexist.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Occupation Permit authorizes professional activity and residence in Mauritius.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate 20-year PRP may be requested after five qualifying years if the prescribed business-income or aggregate-turnover test is met.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence is not automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through separate qualifying residence and discretionary naturalisation, subject to the Citizenship Act.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The status sequence required before naturalisation needs individual legal confirmation.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because it requires substantial investment and prospective Mauritian clients; an existing foreign software contract alone is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the MUR 50,000 local basic-salary requirement at MUR 47.43 per USD.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: MUR 50,000 basic monthly salary
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The July 2026 EDB update states that this threshold applies across sectors.

income_requirement_display.value: MUR 50,000/month from a Mauritian employer
income_requirement_display.notes: USD conversion is approximate.

income_proof_months.notes: Eligibility depends on a Mauritian employment contract rather than prior foreign-income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment in Mauritius by a multinational or local company.
A local employment contract satisfying the current minimum basic salary.

initial_validity.value: Up to 10 years, normally subject to the employment contract
initial_validity.notes: Continued validity depends on the qualifying local professional activity.

extension_rules.value: Continued qualifying Mauritian employment and compliance with current permit criteria are required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Occupation Permit authorizes local work and residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A 20-year PRP may be available after five years, subject to a MUR 400,000 monthly basic salary throughout five consecutive years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The local-employment and high-salary requirements make it unsuitable for this profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separate qualifying residence and discretionary naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a Mauritian employer and local employment contract.

summary.value: Study permission is temporary, and post-study professional status depends on qualifying local employment. No employer-free points-tested or qualification-only permanent-residence route was identified for an overseas software engineer.
summary.notes: A university degree alone does not establish residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if domiciled in Mauritius unless the permanent abode is outside Mauritius, is present for at least 183 days in the income year, or is present for at least 270 days across the two preceding income years.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and individual domicile facts can change the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top ordinary marginal personal income-tax rate, not an expected effective rate. A separate 15% Fair Share Contribution can affect leviable income above MUR 12 million.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Route-specific result: the MRA FAQ says CSG, NSF and Training Levy are not applicable to a Premium Visa holder. This 0% does not apply after switching to Mauritian employment or registered local self-employment.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The visa and route-specific social contributions are zero, but mandatory travel and health insurance has no prescribed fixed price, so no single monthly total can be calculated.

special_tax_regimes.value: Premium Visa guidance taxes remote-work income to the extent it is remitted to Mauritius. Foreign-card spending is not treated as a remittance, and a Mauritian bank deposit may be protected where the holder declares that the income was already taxed in the country of origin or residence.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is a remittance rule, not a blanket digital-nomad tax exemption.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on physical presence, domicile, income sourcing, remittances, tax already paid abroad, treaty relief and the contractual structure. Switching from the Premium Visa to local work or business registration changes the tax and contribution analysis.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax combined with special remittance treatment for Premium Visa remote-work income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile test, 183 days in the income year, or 270 days across the two preceding income years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on Mauritius-derived income and income remitted to Mauritius; non-residents are taxed on Mauritius-derived or accruing net income. Premium Visa remote work performed from Mauritius is taxed when the income is remitted under the special rule.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Foreign-card spending is not deemed remitted. Deposits in Mauritius may avoid further Mauritius tax where the required declaration establishes that the income was already taxed in the country of origin or residence.
taxation_system.social_security: Premium Visa holders are expressly outside CSG: the consolidated Social Contribution and Social Benefits Act excludes a non-citizen holding that visa, and the MRA FAQ states that CSG, NSF and Training Levy are inapplicable. A person who switches to registered local self-employment is instead subject to MRA's ordinary CSG schedule: MUR 150 per month up to MUR 10,000 net income; 1.5% of 90% of monthly net income above MUR 10,000 through MUR 50,000, subject to the MUR 150 minimum; and 3% of 90% above MUR 50,000. Local employees and employers are governed by separate payroll contribution rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 20% is the top ordinary marginal rate, not an estimated effective rate. From 1 July 2025, the first MUR 500,000 is taxed at 0%, the next MUR 500,000 at 10%, and the remainder at 20%. A temporary 15% Fair Share Contribution can apply above MUR 12 million.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First MUR 500,000 of annual chargeable income
tax_brackets.notes: Local-currency statutory threshold retained without an additional exchange-rate estimate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next MUR 500,000; cumulative income through MUR 1,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: The threshold is cumulative.
Top ordinary PIT bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The prior social-security uncertainty is resolved by current legislation and the official MRA Premium Visa FAQ. The exemption is specific to the Premium Visa and must not be carried into a different employment or business status.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Premium Visa holders have no blanket income-tax holiday. Remote-work income is subject to Mauritius tax to the extent remitted under the special Premium Visa rule, while the visa holder is expressly exempt from CSG, NSF and Training Levy.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary foreign-remote-worker/long-stay visa
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%/10%/20% progressive PIT; 20% is the top ordinary screening rate, not the expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Resident under the domicile test, at 183 days in an income year, or at 270 days across the two preceding income years.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-card spending is not treated as a remittance. Funds deposited in Mauritius can be taxable unless declared as already taxed in the country of origin or residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Premium Visa remittance treatment applies, but there is no general tax holiday.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A Premium Visa holder is expressly exempt from CSG, NSF and Training Levy. Ordinary employee payroll or self-employed CSG rules apply only after entering a different local employment or business arrangement.

fixed_payments.status: No visa fee and no CSG, NSF or Training Levy for a Premium Visa holder; mandatory insurance remains a variable cost
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: MUR 0 per month while remaining a Premium Visa holder. Registered local self-employment under a different status can instead require at least MUR 150 monthly CSG and higher income-based contributions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Premium Visa application and processing fee: zero.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No universal fixed monthly transaction or freelancer tax is imposed merely by holding the Premium Visa.
fixed_payments.notes: The zero contribution result is confirmed specifically for Premium Visa holders. Mandatory travel and health insurance has no official fixed premium.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying fewer than 183 days does not automatically eliminate Mauritius tax because work performed from Mauritius may still fall within the Premium Visa remittance rule.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Progressive PIT and filing should be assessed for taxable remittances; foreign-card spending and income already taxed abroad receive the specific treatment described by MRA.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registered local self-employment is a different scenario and can trigger ordinary PIT filing plus CSG of MUR 150 minimum, 1.5% of 90% of monthly net income between MUR 10,000 and MUR 50,000, or 3% of 90% above MUR 50,000.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the published Premium Visa rules. Individual income-tax outcomes still depend on remittances, sourcing, foreign tax, residence and treaty facts.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Approval grants a temporary long stay immediately but not a qualifying temporary residence permit, so no qualifying-residence start year is assigned.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Premium Visa time is not listed as qualifying for PRP. The applicant would need to obtain a separate qualifying status.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is residence-based and discretionary rather than a fixed number of years after PR.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No citizenship timeline can be assigned to the Premium Visa. The general alien provision includes residence requirements but does not establish this visa as qualifying residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official citizenship page and Citizenship Act do not publish a typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires qualifying residence, good character, adequate knowledge of English or another language current in Mauritius and citizen responsibilities, and an intention to continue residing. Approval remains discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: These are general rules, not a Premium Visa settlement promise.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Registration generally requires four years living with the Mauritian spouse under the same conjugal roof in Mauritius immediately before application; special permit-sequence rules can apply.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage to a Mauritian citizen does not itself confer citizenship; the qualifying co-residence and applicable permit conditions must still be completed.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to another migrant does not accelerate naturalisation.

requirements_and_risks.value: The authorities assess qualifying co-residence, good character, language or civic knowledge and security or public-policy considerations. A genuine shared household must be documented; sham marriage can lead to refusal, cancellation and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Registration is not automatic after four years.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For a birth in Mauritius after 1 October 1995, territorial birth alone is insufficient; at least one parent must be a Mauritian citizen.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Mauritius to two non-citizen migrant parents does not automatically become Mauritian merely through territorial birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Narrow foundling or statelessness safeguards do not create a general jus soli rule.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Mauritius after 1 October 1995 is Mauritian if either parent is a Mauritian citizen.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: A non-citizen permanent-resident parent does not satisfy the citizenship-parent condition.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Mauritian-citizen child does not automatically naturalise or permanently admit a foreign parent. The parent must qualify under an applicable family or discretionary immigration category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The official material reviewed establishes no automatic parent-of-citizen PR or citizenship entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically receive citizenship because his child or the other parent is Mauritian. Marriage-based registration is a separate possibility if its requirements are met.

rank.notes: Henley's current ranking was cross-checked against a secondary table identifying Mauritius at rank 25.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's mobility score includes destinations accessible without a prior visa, including visa-on-arrival categories; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The detailed secondary index combines physical-visa and eVisa destinations, so a strict visa-in-advance-only count compatible with Henley's methodology cannot be stated reliably.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The secondary index reports 25 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. Its methodology differs from Henley, so the figures should not be combined with Henley's 147 score.

passport.notes: Henley supplies the headline rank and mobility score; VisaIndex is used only for the separately categorized VOA/eTA breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English is the official language of the National Assembly, is used throughout official Premium Visa materials and is practical for immigration and professional administration. French and Mauritian Creole are widely used socially.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The constitutional provision specifically defines the Assembly's official language rather than declaring an exhaustive national-language code.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited compared with English or French. Ukraine and Russia appear among Premium Visa-eligible nationalities, but the reviewed official services do not establish Russian- or Ukrainian-language administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Applicants should expect to use English or French.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of MUR 45,794 at MUR 47.43/USD. This is March 2025 average monthly earnings in establishments employing at least ten people, not a national median.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official earnings release publishes a mean, the labour-force release focuses on employment, and the Household Budget Survey reports household rather than individual-worker income. None publishes a comparable national monthly employee median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 statutory national minimum wage; it is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official large-establishment mean.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statistics Mauritius publishes an overall mean of MUR 45,794 for establishments with at least ten workers. Its labour-force release reports employment and unemployment, while the HBS publishes household income classes and household-level wage income. No comparable individual-worker median is available to convert to USD.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The earnings survey publishes averages, not the highest individual salary. The HBS open-ended household-income class of MUR 100,000 and above is neither an employee salary nor a maximum, so no national maximum can be converted to USD.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Premium Visa is a renewable long-stay remote-work visa, not established by the current sources qualifying residence. Its time should not be counted toward permanent residence or citizenship.
settlement_track.summary: The Premium Visa is a genuine foreign-remote-work option but not a confirmed settlement route. Conversion requires a new Occupation Permit application, and the independent self-employed category requires substantial investment and prospective Mauritian clients.
settlement_track.notes: General naturalisation rules do not transform the Premium Visa into qualifying residence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only as a temporary-living fit: the visa supports remote work where the main business and income source remain abroad, but it is not a citizenship-path fit.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed. Current legislation and the official MRA Premium Visa FAQ resolve the social-security uncertainty: CSG, NSF and Training Levy do not apply to Premium Visa holders. Official earnings and household-survey sources publish means and household distributions, not a national individual-worker median or finite maximum, so those salary values remain null with precise scope explanations.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Self-Employed Occupation Permit, then 20-year Permanent Residence Permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The official Premium Visa FAQ expressly permits an Occupation Permit application during the stay. A qualifying self-employed OP holder can apply for the renewable 20-year PRP after five years meeting the prescribed business-income/turnover test.
requirements: Self-employed OP: invest USD 50,000 and supply three client letters, including two from potential local clients.
PRP: five qualifying OP years and MUR 3 million annual business income for those years, or MUR 15 million aggregate turnover over five consecutive years.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: This requires investment and a locally established professional business, so it is conditional for an ordinary foreign-only remote worker. Premium Visa time does not substitute for the required OP years. Five years starts on the qualifying OP; the PRP is legally named permanent residence but has renewable 20-year validity.

data.selection_summary: Mexico fits the profile through the ordinary Temporary Resident Visa based on economic solvency. It is not branded as a digital-nomad visa, but official SRE guidance says it can be requested independently, does not depend on a Mexican job offer, and permits work when remuneration is paid abroad. Temporary residence can change to permanent residence after four consecutive years; maintaining status through that conversion provides a credible five-year ordinary naturalization track.

visa_application.notes: The official route page contains the digital appointment starting point, but the applicant must attend an interview at a Mexican consular office. Solvency documentation and the operational monetary threshold should be confirmed with the selected consulate before filing.

extension_rules.value: Temporary-resident status may be maintained only up to the four-year statutory maximum. After four consecutive years, the holder can apply to change to permanent residence.
extension_rules.notes: Renewals and the eventual change of status are handled with INM and require valid status, applications, and current government fees.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply independently at a Mexican consular office under economic solvency, enter Mexico after approval, and exchange the visa for a temporary resident card.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence, not visitor or workcation permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Change to permanent residence after four consecutive, uninterrupted years as a temporary resident.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The 2026 government procedure requires a valid temporary resident card, supporting declaration, application, and fees.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization generally requires five immediately preceding years of qualifying residence. Temporary or permanent resident cards qualify, while temporary student residence is expressly excluded; because temporary residence is capped at four years, the practical track normally converts to permanent residence for the fifth year.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Spanish and Mexican history/culture examinations, absence limits, documentation, and continued lawful residence apply.

best_routes.notes: This route is a strong substantive match despite lacking a digital-nomad label: it is independent economic-solvency residence and official SRE guidance expressly accommodates remuneration paid abroad. The principal filing risk is consulate-specific solvency implementation.

summary.value: Mexico offers a temporary student resident visa for studies longer than 180 days without a local employer. It is not a useful citizenship route for this selection because SRE expressly states that temporary student residence does not create residence rights for naturalization.
summary.notes: A university degree by itself does not create an independent skilled-worker residence category. The student route requires admission to an accredited Mexican educational institution and is separate from the applicant's existing degree.

tax_residency_rule.value: Mexico does not use a simple 183-day statutory test as its primary domestic rule. An individual is resident when a home is established in Mexico; if homes exist in Mexico and another country, Mexico applies the center-of-vital-interests test. Mexican vital interests include cases where more than 50% of annual income has a Mexican source or the principal center of professional activities is in Mexico.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A treaty tie-breaker can change the result where the applicant is also resident elsewhere. Physical presence remains practically relevant but is not a safe standalone domestic threshold.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal annual personal ISR rate for 2026. This is a screening ceiling, not the applicant's expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No universal employee or self-employed contribution percentage could be established for the exact foreign-employer/foreign-client arrangement. Liability depends on whether the relationship creates Mexican employment, payroll, voluntary coverage, or locally registered independent activity.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax or social-security payment applies solely because a person holds this residence status. Visa, residence-card, status-change, tax, and professional-compliance costs are separate and may change annually.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax exemption was found. Ordinary resident/nonresident ISR rules and any applicable treaty or foreign-tax credit rules apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A locally registered independent professional should obtain advice about business/professional activity, provisional payments, invoicing, VAT, and available regimes.

taxes.caveats: Immigration permission to receive pay abroad does not create a tax exemption. Tax residence, source of services, employee versus independent-contractor status, permanent-establishment risk, foreign tax credits, VAT, treaties, and social security must be evaluated separately.

taxation_system.value: Mexican-resident individuals are subject to ISR on their income, including foreign-source income, under a progressive annual tariff reaching 35%. Foreign income can be relevant to annual filing and foreign-tax-credit calculations.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Home in Mexico; if homes exist in multiple countries, center of vital interests, including the statutory income-source and professional-activity indicators. No general domestic 183-day safe harbor is stated.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for Mexican tax residents; nonresidents are generally subject to Mexican tax on Mexican-source income or income attributable to a Mexican permanent establishment.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated nomad tax holiday or exemption found.
taxation_system.social_security: Fact-dependent. Residence status alone does not establish a single compulsory contribution percentage for a foreign-paid employee or contractor.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 35% is the top marginal rate. Annual tax equals a fixed quota plus the applicable percentage of income above the bracket's lower limit; deductions, credits, and characterization affect effective tax.

taxation_system.notes: Official domestic-law screening. Individual advice is required for treaty residence, source, deductions, credits, VAT, and worker classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The financial-solvency resident is not placed in a special nomad tax category. If Mexican tax resident, the applicant should expect ordinary progressive ISR on worldwide income, subject to characterization, deductions, foreign-tax credits, and treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary financial-solvency temporary resident; foreign-paid remote worker
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive ISR up to 35%; 35% is the top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Home and center-of-vital-interests test rather than a simple 183-day rule.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident individuals are generally required to include foreign-source income; the law provides mechanisms and limits for crediting qualifying foreign income tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No universal fixed contribution was established for this arrangement. Mexican payroll, locally registered professional activity, or other factual links can change the result.

fixed_payments.status: No universal recurring fixed amount confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Fact-dependent; do not assume either zero liability or a fixed percentage without classifying the work relationship.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The 2026 consular visa application fee is USD 56. The 2026 permanent-residence change procedure lists MXN 1,847 for review/authorization and a further MXN 13,579 for the permanent-resident document after approval; temporary-card and renewal fees should be checked when due.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No special nomad levy found. Independent activity may create invoicing, provisional ISR, and VAT obligations rather than a single fixed nomad payment.
fixed_payments.notes: Immigration and naturalization fees are not monthly taxes and change annually.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: There is no reliable domestic 183-day safe harbor. Even a shorter stay can require analysis of whether a Mexican home was established, where vital interests lie, the source of services, and treaty residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Plan for Mexican registration and annual/provisional reporting analysis, with worldwide income potentially taxable under progressive ISR up to 35% and possible foreign-tax credits.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local independent-professional registration can require RFC enrollment, CFDI invoicing, provisional ISR filings, annual filing, and VAT analysis; social-insurance treatment must be determined separately.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No official source was found creating a special tax exemption merely because the immigration authority permits remuneration from abroad.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is obtained through the consular visa and post-entry card exchange; there is no preliminary multi-year status.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Four consecutive years as a temporary resident.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: This represents the practical ordinary sequence: four temporary-resident years, conversion to permanent residence, then completion of five total qualifying years. Naturalization law counts qualifying residence rather than imposing a separate minimum period as a permanent resident.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five immediately preceding years for ordinary naturalization, subject to lawful residence and absence limits.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: SRE publishes a maximum response period of three months after INM has issued its opinion, but does not establish a reliable typical total elapsed time from initial filing. Appointment availability and the INM-opinion stage can add time.

key_conditions.value: Maintain qualifying temporary/permanent residence; temporary student status does not count. During the two years before filing, total absences must not exceed six months. Applicants generally need Spanish ability, Mexican history/culture knowledge, complete civil and criminal-record documentation, biometrics, and the current fee.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is an application requiring approval, not an automatic consequence of five years' residence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The foreign spouse must have resided and lived together with the Mexican spouse at the marital home in Mexico for the two years immediately before filing, except where the Mexican spouse is abroad on a Mexican government assignment.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Mexican can support the reduced two-year naturalization category once the statutory residence and cohabitation period is satisfied. Marriage to another foreign national does not independently accelerate Mexican citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage alone does not confer citizenship automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: The Mexican spouse must accompany the applicant in the marriage category, and the applicant must meet the applicable residence, cohabitation, document, examination, and good-conduct requirements. Mexican law penalizes marriages entered solely to obtain nationality and false or fraudulent evidence.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Authorities can scrutinize whether the marriage and shared marital home are genuine.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 30 grants Mexican nationality by birth to everyone born in Mexican territory regardless of the parents' nationality.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Mexico is Mexican by birth even when both parents are foreign nationals and regardless of their residence category.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Civil registration remains the practical step for obtaining the birth certificate and identity documents.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Mexican mother or father is Mexican by descent if born abroad and is also Mexican by territorial birth if born in Mexico. This does not automatically give the foreign father Mexican citizenship.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Mexican child by birth can use the statutory two-year residence naturalization category. Family unity may also support immigration status, but the parent's citizenship remains application-based.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The child must be Mexican by birth for the reduced naturalization category cited.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father can potentially naturalize after two years of qualifying residence because he has a Mexican-by-birth child, but paternity and the child's Mexican status must be documented and citizenship is not automatic.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Residence continuity, absence, examination, documentation, and approval requirements remain.

passport.notes: Passport Index was selected because it provides the requested visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA, and visa-required breakdown. Its methodology and rank differ from Henley.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable inside some multinational technology teams and major expatriate or tourist areas, but Spanish is the practical language for immigration, tax, banking, health care, housing, and most daily administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from Mexico's legal language framework, not an official guarantee of English-language public services. Mexican law describes Spanish and recognized Indigenous languages as national languages rather than designating a single exclusive federal official language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low for routine administration outside private diaspora, interpreter, or community support; Spanish is normally needed for independent daily life and government procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No official nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-language service framework was found.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: INEGI's current ENOE dissemination system includes medians and income data, but the reviewed public outputs expose a median income per hour and income-band counts rather than a directly comparable national median monthly wage. No USD value was derived by multiplying an hourly median by assumed hours or by applying an unsourced exchange rate.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official average is retained in MXN rather than converted using an unsourced exchange rate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official ENOE sources reviewed do not publish a directly comparable national median monthly worker salary in USD. INEGI provides an hourly-income median and downloadable microdata, but converting those into a monthly USD median would require analyst assumptions and an exchange-rate source.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official nationwide maximum salary exists in the reviewed sources.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: INEGI's current InfoLaboral framework reports medians, including income in pesos per hour worked, and the current occupation table reports workers by broad income bands. Neither reviewed interface publishes a single national median monthly worker salary in MXN. ENOE microdata could support a separately calculated estimate, but no analyst-derived monthly figure is substituted for an official published statistic.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No defensible national maximum was published; high-earner observations would not constitute a meaningful wage ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 Q3 average; 2026 minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and statutory minimum are different concepts and should not be compared as if they came from the same wage distribution. Current INEGI ENOE resources publish income bands, an hourly-income median framework, and microdata, but not a directly comparable national median monthly worker salary in the reviewed outputs; median monthly and maximum fields therefore remain cautious nulls.

cost_of_living_note.notes: INEGI's ENIGH publishes household income and expenditure statistics, but no single nationally representative personal cost-of-living amount suitable for this remote worker was adopted; household size and location produce large differences.

settlement_track.summary: Economic-solvency temporary residence is qualifying residence and fits foreign-paid remote work. Because temporary residence is capped at four years while ordinary naturalization requires five qualifying years, the practical track converts to permanent residence after year four and completes the fifth year before naturalization.
settlement_track.notes: The required conversion is routine and officially documented, so this is a credible citizenship path rather than a temporary nomad-only stay.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Official SRE guidance expressly permits the independently requested temporary-residence visa holder to work where remuneration is paid abroad. The applicant must still meet the filing consulate's economic-solvency implementation and should not receive Mexican-source salary without the appropriate employment authorization.

data.notes: Immigration, settlement, naturalization, birthright citizenship, tax rates, minimum wages, and passport data are strongly supported, primarily by current official sources. Overall confidence is reduced from high because consular solvency implementation varies, tax/social-security characterization is fact-specific, citizenship's total processing time is not officially established, and national median/max wage figures remain unavailable after focused searches.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Ordinary Temporary Resident status based on economic solvency
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A qualifying temporary resident working for foreign-paid income can apply to change to permanent residence after four consecutive years in temporary-resident status.
requirements: Obtain the temporary-resident visa through a consulate, meet its economic-solvency evidence and obtain the resident card after entry.
Maintain temporary-resident status continuously for four years.
Submit the in-country PR change application with valid card, identity documents, declaration and fees.
reviewed_route_names: Temporary Resident Visa based on economic solvency
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: This is ordinary solvent temporary residence, not a separate statutory digital-nomad visa. The official Omaha consular PDF expressly permits work when salary is paid abroad. requires_exit=false describes temporary-resident-to-PR conversion; an initial tourist-to-temporary-resident strategy normally requires a consular visa application abroad.

data.selection_summary: The Federated States of Micronesia has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Visitor status does not authorize a settlement track, alien-worker permits depend on authorized local employment, and conducting a business requires a foreign-investment permit. Ordinary foreign residents also lack a general naturalization path: the standard five-year provision is limited to a child of an FSM citizen or an FSM national, while a citizen's spouse faces a discretionary congressional-bill and presidential process.

visa_application.title: FSM Code Title 50, Chapter 1 — Immigration
visa_application.notes: This is the official legal-information page describing entry-permit categories and applications, not an online application portal. No dedicated remote-worker application channel or current general immigration application portal was found.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists for visitor entry.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: FSM uses the US dollar; no visitor income threshold was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker income threshold; visitor status is not a remote-work residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial means may be examined administratively, but no statutory monthly threshold was established in the reviewed sources.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed visitor provisions do not prescribe a historical income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: A permit is not required for visits of 30 days or less; a further visitor period of up to 60 days may be issued to most non-US visitors.
A valid passport and round-trip ticket are expected for ordinary visitors.
Remaining longer requires an appropriate permit; visitor status is not a dedicated authorization for ongoing foreign-contract remote work.

initial_validity.value: Up to 30 days without a permit for ordinary visitors
initial_validity.notes: US citizens have special Compact rights that must not be generalized to other nationalities.

extension_rules.value: A visitor permit may extend an ordinary visit by up to 60 additional days; other visitor permits may be issued for a specified lawful purpose
extension_rules.notes: Extensions do not create a qualifying remote-worker or settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No independent remote-worker temporary-residence conversion confirmed
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A change of status normally requires departure and re-entry unless written authorization is granted.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Title 50 publishes no general progression from visitor status to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time does not overcome the restricted statutory eligibility for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Visitor entry may be convenient for short visits but is not valid for this citizenship-oriented foreign-contract remote-work selection.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed national statutes publish no general route-wide salary threshold; occupational minimums may be imposed administratively.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: FSM uses USD, but the reviewed labor statute publishes no nationwide route-specific amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No general published minimum; authorized local employment and an employer agreement are required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a local-employer route, not a foreign-client remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: This route is based on authorized employment rather than a prescribed period of historical income.

key_requirements.requirement: An authorized employment contract and compliance with national employment laws are required.
The employer-driven process assesses whether resident workers are available and requires a nonresident employment agreement.
The worker is tied to the authorized employer and may not work for another employer under the same contract.

initial_validity.value: For the authorized employment-contract period, generally subject to the one-year maximum applying unless otherwise specified
initial_validity.notes: The permit is renewed when lawful employment is extended or renewed.

extension_rules.value: Renewable upon extension or renewal of authorized lawful employment
extension_rules.notes: Continued local employment remains necessary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Provides a temporary alien-worker entry permit linked to authorized employment
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not independent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed immigration and labor provisions publish no general permanent-residence progression for alien workers.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary employment and residence alone do not satisfy the restricted naturalization eligibility rules.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires authorized local employment and an employer-driven process.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign investor entry permit and Foreign Investment Permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No ordinary remote-worker monthly-income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: FSM uses USD, but capital, sector, state and permit requirements are business-specific and cannot be reduced to a single national income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income test; a qualifying permitted foreign investment or business is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Foreign Investment Permit requirements vary by activity and state
income_requirement_display.notes: Opening a bank account alone is expressly excluded from engaging in business, but it does not create residence or work authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: The foreign-investment provisions do not prescribe a period of historical foreign income.

key_requirements.requirement: A noncitizen engaging in business in FSM must hold a valid national or state Foreign Investment Permit.
The entry permit depends on the underlying foreign-investment or business permit.
The route is for a genuine permitted business or investment, not ordinary remote work for a foreign client.

initial_validity.value: Specified duration tied to the foreign-investment permit
initial_validity.notes: Entry permits are generally limited to one year unless otherwise specified.

extension_rules.value: Renewable when the underlying business permit is renewed or extended
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains dependent on the qualifying business or investment authorization.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A foreign-investor entry permit can authorize temporary stay while the qualifying business permit remains valid
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Business approval is substantive and cannot be treated as simple freelancer registration.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed immigration and foreign-investment provisions publish no general permanent-residence progression from this permit.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Business residence alone does not satisfy the restricted naturalization eligibility rules.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a qualifying local business or investment framework and is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route.

summary.value: An enrolled foreign student may receive a student entry permit for the specified duration of the educational program. No degree-based independent skilled migration, permanent-residence route or post-study settlement progression was identified.
summary.notes: This is an education-attendance permit, not residence awarded merely because the applicant already holds a university degree.

tax_residency_rule.value: The reviewed national tax law does not state a general 183-day or domicile-based personal tax-residency test. FSM taxation instead focuses on wages received by employees and business revenue generated by activities or transactions within FSM; filing-level advice is required for a foreign employer or contractor.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Do not infer tax exemption merely from the absence of a conventional residence-day test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top statutory wage-and-salary rate, not an expected effective rate. Six percent applies to the first USD 11,000 of annual wages and 10% to the excess.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee rate for covered employment; the employer separately contributes 7.5%. Coverage turns on an FSM employer-employee relationship and possible other-system exceptions, so this is not automatically applicable to a foreign-contract remote worker.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no mandatory monthly digital-nomad or foreign-freelancer payment because no such route exists. A low-revenue self-employed person may make voluntary social-security contributions, but that does not legalize remote-worker residence.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, non-dom, remittance-basis or inbound-worker tax regime was identified.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business gross-revenue taxation is a general regime, not a nomad concession.

taxes.caveats: FSM uses the US dollar. Wage tax, business gross-revenue tax, social-security coverage and state-level licensing can produce different results depending on whether the person is legally an employee, independent contractor or permitted local business. Foreign-contract income earned through activity physically performed in FSM needs professional classification and apportionment advice.

taxation_system.value: Mixed source/activity-based system: progressive wage tax plus a separate business taxable-gross-revenue tax.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: The reviewed statutes state no general day-count rule; they focus on wages and the source or location of business activity.
taxation_system.income_scope: Wages and salaries received by employees are taxed at 6% and 10%. A business pays USD 80 per year on the first USD 10,000 of taxable gross revenue and 3% on taxable gross revenue above USD 10,000, with source apportionment available for activity inside and outside FSM.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees pay 7.5% and covered employers separately pay 7.5%. Low-revenue self-employed persons may elect voluntary coverage by paying both sides on deemed annual remuneration of USD 5,000.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 10% dashboard figure is the top marginal wage-tax rate. It is not the effective rate and is not the rate for permitted self-employed business revenue.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First USD 11,000 of annual wages and salaries
tax_brackets.notes: Annual statutory wage-tax bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual wages and salaries over USD 11,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Wages and salaries above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal wage-tax bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: USD 80 per year on taxable business gross revenue up to USD 10,000
tax_brackets.notes: Fixed annual amount rather than a percentage bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable business gross revenue over USD 10,000 annually
tax_brackets.applies_to: Taxable business gross revenue above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Separate business tax, not personal wage tax.

taxation_system.notes: The statutory rates are well supported. Application to an unauthorized foreign-contract remote-work arrangement remains fact-specific because no immigration or tax category was created for that scenario.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a dedicated category because FSM has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status. If activity is lawfully structured as employment, the 6% and 10% wage tax and potentially 7.5% employee social-security contribution are screening figures; a permitted business may instead face gross-revenue tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; possible wage-employee or permitted-business treatment only after immigration and tax classification
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 6% on the first USD 11,000 of annual wages and 10% above; permitted business revenue follows a separate USD 80 and 3% regime
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: The reviewed legislation states no conventional day-count rule; source and location of activity are central.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The reviewed statutes do not conclusively classify an ordinary foreign employer or client arrangement. Business revenue generated by activity within FSM may be FSM-source, while the statute allows apportionment when business activity occurs both within and outside FSM.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered employee rate is 7.5%, with a separate 7.5% employer contribution. Applicability to a foreign employer with no FSM business presence requires advice.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory nomad-specific fixed payment applies because there is no nomad status
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Covered employment uses percentage contributions rather than a fixed monthly amount. Voluntary low-revenue self-employed coverage can require both 7.5% sides on deemed USD 5,000 annual remuneration, equivalent to USD 750 annually or USD 62.50 monthly, but it is voluntary and does not legalize residence.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The immigration law authorizes entry-permit application and renewal fees, but the reviewed current official material does not provide a consolidated current fee schedule or any nomad fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A permitted business owes USD 80 annually on the portion of taxable gross revenue not exceeding USD 10,000, then 3% on the excess.
fixed_payments.notes: State business registration, licensing or municipal charges may also apply and cannot be reduced to one national amount from the reviewed sources.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Short visitor presence does not itself authorize ongoing remote work. The reviewed tax legislation states no official tax-safe day threshold.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no dedicated status or tax regime. Wage, business-revenue and social-security classification must be resolved before relying on foreign-contract income while physically working in FSM.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A noncitizen conducting business generally needs a Foreign Investment Permit; bank-account opening alone neither constitutes engaging in business nor grants residence. The business gross-revenue tax may then apply.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is high that there is no special nomad regime and in the statutory rates, but only medium for hypothetical foreign-contract classification because that arrangement has no specifically authorized route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker residence route exists. Visitor, employer and investor entry permits should not be normalized into a remote-worker residence timeline.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed immigration and citizenship laws establish no general permanent-residence progression for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: FSM law establishes no ordinary PR-to-citizenship timeline; naturalization eligibility is restricted to specified family or national categories.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the statutory lawful-residence minimum for eligible children of citizens, FSM nationals and citizen spouses; it is not a general foreigner pathway. A spouse additionally needs an individual congressional recommendation by bill and presidential action.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither current Public Law 23-140 nor the reviewed official individual spouse-recommendation bill publishes a generally applicable processing deadline or typical elapsed time.

key_conditions.value: Standard naturalization requires five immediately preceding years of lawful residence, status as a child of an FSM citizen or an FSM national, an oath of allegiance, competence in an indigenous FSM language and no felony conviction. Under current Public Law 23-140, a citizen spouse remains a separate discretionary category: the spouse must meet the five-year residence, oath, language and no-felony conditions, must renounce every prior citizenship with positive verifiable documentary evidence, and may be naturalized by the President only after Congress recommends the individual by bill.
key_conditions.notes: Public Law 23-140, signed December 11, 2024, removed foreign-citizenship renunciation from the child-of-citizen or FSM-national track but expressly retained it for the spouse track.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The naturalization condition is five years of lawful FSM residence immediately before filing, not five years of marriage. Separately, paid work on a spouse permit generally requires five years of FSM residence and/or five years of marriage unless regulations provide otherwise.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A lawful spouse of an FSM citizen is entitled to a spouse entry permit upon adequate evidence of the marriage. The immigration regulations describe an initial one-year permit, annual renewal on a reasonable showing that the marriage remains intact, and the statute permits renewals of up to five years. Marriage does not waive the normal departure and re-entry rule for changing status, does not create permanent residence and does not automatically grant citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: An existing lawful marriage supports the spouse permit and creates eligibility for the separate spouse-naturalization process, but all statutory conditions and discretionary congressional and presidential steps remain.

requirements_and_risks.value: Current spouse naturalization requires five years of lawful FSM residence immediately before filing, an oath of allegiance, competence in at least one indigenous FSM language proven by the prescribed examination, no felony conviction, renunciation of every prior citizenship and foreign allegiance supported by positive verifiable documents, an individual recommendation by Congress through a bill, and presidential approval. The spouse entry permit requires adequate evidence of a lawful marriage and annual proof that the marriage remains intact; divorce or irreconcilable separation can support denial or revocation, while death of the citizen spouse triggers statutory waiting and hardship protections.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The reviewed national immigration regulations require adequate evidence of marriage and, for renewal, a reasonable showing that the marriage remains intact, but they do not publish a single national documentary checklist or a separate statutory sham-marriage test. Marriage validity and records are governed at state level; for example, Chuuk requires a license for a citizen–noncitizen marriage, disclosure of identity, citizenship, residence and prior-marriage dissolution, a licensed ceremony with two witnesses, and registration. False, incomplete or misleading material information can support entry-permit denial, revocation or deportation under 50 FSMC 107, and naturalization obtained through concealment of a material fact or willful misrepresentation can be cancelled by court order under 7 FSMC 205. These are the supported fraud risks; no more specific current national sham-marriage offence or verification checklist was published in the sources reviewed.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution and current amended citizenship law grant citizenship by birth when at least one parent is an FSM citizen. Birth in FSM alone is not a generally applicable citizenship rule.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in FSM to two noncitizen migrant parents does not automatically become an FSM citizen solely by birthplace.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The current provisions establish citizenship through citizen parentage rather than broad jus soli or a permanent-resident-parent rule.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is an FSM citizen when either parent is an FSM citizen.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Public Law 23-140 implements the constitutional dual-citizenship amendment and no longer supports carrying forward the former general renunciation-at-adulthood warning.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically give a noncitizen parent citizenship or create an ordinary remote-worker settlement route. The immigration statute provides a dependent permit for a citizen's minor child, not a parent permit based solely on the child's citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed statutes publish no general parent residence category based solely on having an FSM-citizen child.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship merely because his child is an FSM citizen. The naturalization phrase “child of a citizen” describes the applicant's own parentage, not the applicant being the parent of a citizen child.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Marriage to the citizen mother could create a separate spouse-permit and discretionary spouse-naturalization route.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 45 visa-on-arrival destinations and six eTA destinations. The index separately lists eVisa and other categories, so this is not the overall mobility score of 120.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the official and common national language, so government and ordinary professional communication are comparatively practical in English. Connectivity and service reliability vary substantially across the widely dispersed islands and should be checked for a specific location.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Indigenous languages remain important locally; naturalization requires competence in at least one indigenous FSM language, not merely English.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. The reviewed official material does not identify Russian or Ukrainian as commonly used languages; English and local Micronesian languages predominate.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services should not be assumed.

cost_of_living_note.value: The cost of living is high relative to local wages because FSM is remote and import-dependent. Current 2026 reports identify elevated delivered fuel, freight and insurance costs as pressure on household purchasing power.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor entry is temporary and is not a digital-nomad, permanent-residence or citizenship route. Special Compact rights for US citizens cannot be generalized to other foreign nationals.
settlement_track.summary: No independent ordinary remote-worker route exists. Employer and investor permits require materially different local employment or business circumstances, and ordinary residence alone cannot satisfy FSM's restricted naturalization eligibility.
settlement_track.notes: Switching from visitor status normally requires departure and re-entry, but switching would still require qualification for a separate employer, investor, student or family category; no qualifying remote-work conversion is provided by the reviewed laws or regulations.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No current dedicated foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor status is not a settlement route, local employment is employer-linked, and self-employed business activity requires a substantive foreign-investment permit.

data.notes: The negative remote-work selection remains supported. This focused unresolved-field audit inspected 15 distinct directly relevant URLs, including seven URLs absent from the previous source set. It replaced the vague marriage-risk caveat with the published evidentiary, renewal, state-law validity, immigration-misrepresentation and naturalization-cancellation rules, and updated the citizenship discussion for Public Law 23-140 signed December 11, 2024. Explained nulls remain where current sources publish no national median wage, consolidated current immigration fee schedule, conventional tax-residency day test, general permanent-residence timeline or typical citizenship processing time.

data.selection_summary: Moldova has an active digital-nomad route granting temporary residence to employees, service providers, and company owners working exclusively for foreign legal entities. It requires no Moldovan employer. General immigration rules allow other temporary-residence categories to seek permanent residence after five years, while naturalisation generally requires ten years of continuous legal residence and permanent residence at filing. Because the nomad route opened only in September 2025, applicants should obtain filing-level confirmation that nomad residence and foreign-employment contribution records will satisfy the later permanent-residence checklist.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomads Q&A
visa_application.notes: Official route information with eligibility rules, documents, and filing instructions. It directs applications to the General Inspectorate for Migration in person or through an authorised representative. The reviewed material did not establish that an individual digital-nomad application can be completed entirely online.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of MDL 52,200, equal to three forecast average salaries for 2026, using MDL 17.528/USD. The formula and exchange-rate conversion change over time.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: MDL 52,200 per month; MDL 313,200 received over the preceding six months
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The law requires at least 18 forecast average salaries over the preceding six months, equivalent to three per month. The 2026 forecast average salary is MDL 17,400.

income_requirement_display.notes: Formula-based threshold; recalculate using the official forecast average salary applicable in the filing year.

income_proof_months.notes: A Romanian- or English-language bank statement must demonstrate the required receipts during the six months preceding filing.

key_requirements.requirement: Work remotely through information and communication technology exclusively for a legal entity registered outside Moldova, under an employment or service contract or as a shareholder/administrator of that entity.
Provide a passport, Moldovan accommodation evidence, valid health insurance, and an apostilled or legalised criminal-record certificate translated into Romanian or English.
Provide an apostilled or legalised foreign employment/service contract translated into Romanian and a remote-work declaration; owners need recent evidence concerning the foreign company's status.
Maintain qualifying foreign remote activity, income records, accommodation, and health coverage throughout the residence period.

initial_validity.value: Requested period, up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The authority may grant the requested shorter period; the statutory maximum is two years.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for further periods of up to 2 years while all eligibility conditions continue
extension_rules.notes: A new application and updated evidence are required before expiry; the criminal-record certificate is not required for extension.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval directly grants temporary residence as a digital nomad.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a residence category, not visitor or eVisa permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply separately for permanent residence after five years of temporary residence under the general rule for other categories.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Digital nomads are not among the published exclusions, but the route is too new to have produced a five-year case. The PR checklist requests five years of social, salary, and tax contribution evidence; the General Inspectorate for Migration should confirm how this applies to foreign-employed nomads.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation is available after at least ten years of continuous legal residence, provided the applicant holds permanent legal residence when filing.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Romanian and Constitution knowledge, legal income, personal filing, and statutory refusal-ground screening apply.

best_routes.notes: Directly fits ordinary foreign-contract software work without a Moldovan employer, investment, or elite-talent requirement. Its settlement chain is credible but not yet tested through the five-year permanent-residence stage.
