minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is Moldova's general statutory minimum wage effective 1 January 2026, not an additional migrant-worker immigration threshold. The route page requires the local employment contract to state monthly salary but does not prescribe a higher ordinary migrant-worker amount.

income_requirement_display.value: At least MDL 6,300/month for full-time local employment under the general 2026 wage floor; no separate ordinary migrant-worker threshold is published
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Moldovan employment contract and national minimum wage
income_requirement_display.notes: The amount is the general statutory wage floor. Special work categories, such as highly qualified workers or company managers, can have higher formula-based thresholds. This route does not fit a foreign-only contract.

income_proof_months.notes: The route requires a local employment contract stating monthly salary but does not prescribe a prior bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Individual employment contract for work for a Moldovan employer.
Passport, criminal record, accommodation evidence, application, and photograph.

initial_validity.notes: The reviewed ordinary migrant-worker page lists granting and extension documents but does not state a uniform initial permit duration.

extension_rules.value: Extension requires the Moldovan employment contract and existing residence documentation.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employer-linked provisional residence for work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially subject to the general five-year rule, but the route requires local employment.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through the general residence framework, but it is outside the applicant's foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a local employment contract and does not satisfy the independent foreign-contract profile.

summary.value: No independent degree-only or qualification-only residence route was established. Qualifications and experience support the temporary independent-professional exemption, but that status does not issue a residence permit; ordinary work residence requires local employment.
summary.notes: The software degree is potentially useful evidence but is unnecessary for the better-fitting digital-nomad route.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person is resident if they have permanent domicile in Moldova or are physically present for more than 183 days during the fiscal/calendar year; a tax treaty may override domestic residence through tie-breaker rules.
tax_residency_rule.notes: PwC's current summary uses both 'exceeding 183 days' and, elsewhere, 'at least 183 days'; obtain advice when near the boundary.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Flat standard 2026 rate for resident employment, professional, entrepreneurial, and other ordinary taxable income. This is a screening rate rather than estimated effective tax.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage accurately describes the foreign-employed digital-nomad scenario. Current CNAS guidance imposes 24% employer-funded state social insurance on ordinary Moldovan private-sector payroll, while registered independent entrepreneurs allocate 53.3% of their 15% unified tax to social insurance. The current payer guidance does not identify a foreign-employed digital nomad as either category; only the route-specific fixed health-insurance premium is expressly confirmed. Payroll, voluntary coverage, and social-security-agreement treatment require individual review.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Monthly equivalent of the mandatory 2026 digital-nomad health premium: MDL 12,636 annually divided by 12 and converted at MDL 17.528/USD. It is an annual fixed premium, not normally a monthly bill.

special_tax_regimes.value: No enacted digital-nomad PIT exemption or flat nomad tax was established. A separate 2026 independent-entrepreneur regime applies a unified 15% tax up to MDL 1.2 million annual revenue and 35% above that threshold, but it requires resident registration and is not the immigration basis of the nomad permit.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Proposal-stage descriptions of a special nomad tax were not treated as enacted without confirmation in current law or tax-authority guidance.

taxes.caveats: Remote work physically performed in Moldova may be Moldova-source or otherwise taxable there before tax residence begins. Employee, contractor, and foreign-company-owner structures can produce different payroll, permanent-establishment, VAT, social-security, and treaty outcomes.

taxation_system.value: Moldova applies a flat 12% standard PIT rate to ordinary employment, professional, and entrepreneurial taxable income. Digital nomads also owe a fixed mandatory health-insurance premium; no special nomad income-tax holiday was confirmed.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent domicile in Moldova or physical presence exceeding 183 days in the fiscal year, subject to applicable tax treaties.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on Moldova-source income and foreign-source income for work activity effectively performed in Moldova. Non-residents remain taxable on Moldova-source income, including remuneration for activity performed in Moldova.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No enacted special digital-nomad PIT regime confirmed. Registered independent entrepreneurs may use the 15% unified regime up to MDL 1.2 million revenue, with 35% on the excess.
taxation_system.social_security: The ordinary 2026 Moldovan private-sector payroll contribution is 24% of salary and remuneration, paid through the employer; registered independent entrepreneurs instead allocate 53.3% of their 15% unified tax to state social insurance. Current CNAS payer guidance does not list foreign-employed digital nomads as either payer category and publishes no nomad-specific state-social-insurance percentage. Digital nomads are expressly required to buy fixed individual health insurance of MDL 12,636 for 2026. Foreign payroll, voluntary coverage, and any bilateral social-security agreement must be reviewed case by case.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Ordinary PIT is flat. Special or final rates for dividends, gambling, and other income are outside the standard remote-work screening rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: All standard taxable employment, professional, entrepreneurial, and other ordinary income
tax_brackets.notes: Allowances and deductions can alter effective tax; this is the statutory screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: The state-social-insurance distinctions are supported by current official CNAS guidance. The remaining uncertainty is not the ordinary local rate but whether and how a foreign-employed nomad becomes a Moldovan state-social-insurance payer.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Screen on a 12% flat PIT rate plus the annual fixed health premium. No special nomad tax holiday is confirmed, and work physically performed in Moldova can be taxable even before tax residence begins.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital-nomad temporary-residence holder working for a foreign legal entity
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 12% flat standard PIT screening rate; not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent domicile or more than 183 days in a fiscal/calendar year, subject to tax-treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are taxable on foreign-source income attributable to work effectively performed in Moldova. Non-residents are taxable on Moldova-source income, potentially including remuneration for work performed there. Properly documented foreign tax may be creditable within Moldovan limits.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No enacted digital-nomad PIT exemption or special fixed nomad tax was confirmed as of the research date.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A digital-nomad resident must pay the fixed 2026 individual health-insurance premium of MDL 12,636. Current CNAS materials set 24% employer-funded social insurance for ordinary Moldovan private-sector payroll and allocate 53.3% of the 15% unified tax to social insurance for registered independent entrepreneurs, but they do not identify a foreign-employed digital nomad as either payer category or publish a nomad-specific pension contribution. Whether a foreign employer creates Moldovan payroll duties, or foreign social coverage remains applicable under an agreement, requires case-specific advice.

fixed_payments.status: confirmed_route_specific_health_payment_and_variable_state_fees
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: MDL 12,636 annual mandatory health-insurance premium in 2026. No separate compulsory state-social-insurance percentage specifically applicable to an unregistered, foreign-employed digital nomad is published in the reviewed current CNAS guidance.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The official 2026 fee table lists separate temporary-residence examination and residence-card charges, including MDL 90 for standard 30-day examination and MDL 350 for a 20-working-day card. Confirm the exact nomad total and available processing speed before payment.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No separate digital-nomad municipal tax, financial-transaction tax, or fixed freelancer tax was established in the reviewed current sources.
fixed_payments.notes: Translation, apostille/legalisation, accommodation, and insurance costs may be additional. The health premium is updated annually.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Do not assume zero Moldovan tax. A non-resident may still be taxed on remuneration for activity performed in Moldova; an employment treaty's 183-day article may protect some foreign employees only when all conditions are met.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Budget for 12% flat PIT on taxable remote-work income, annual health insurance, filing obligations, and possible foreign-tax credits. Obtain advice on foreign-employer payroll and permanent-establishment exposure.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The registered independent-entrepreneur regime uses a unified 15% tax up to MDL 1.2 million annual revenue and 35% on the excess; 53.3% of the unified tax is allocated to state social insurance. Registration changes the analysis and is not required for digital-nomad immigration eligibility.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The official sources clearly distinguish health insurance, ordinary local payroll, and registered independent entrepreneurship. They do not publish a digital-nomad-specific state pension contribution rule, so no percentage has been invented.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is the direct result of approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General rule for temporary residents in other categories. Digital nomads are not listed among exclusions, but treatment of their contribution evidence should be confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: If permanent residence is obtained after five years, ordinary naturalisation eligibility at ten years total residence leaves approximately five additional years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory eligibility period, not guaranteed approval.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Official processing is up to one year, potentially extended by up to six months for verification.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous legal residence; obtain permanent residence before filing; know Romanian and the Constitution; demonstrate legal income; submit personally; and avoid statutory refusal grounds. Permanent residence additionally requires accommodation, language evidence, criminal-record documents, insurance, subsistence, and contribution records.
key_conditions.notes: Verify absence and continuity limits before extended travel.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Naturalisation requires at least three years of marriage to a Moldovan citizen and continuous legal residence in Moldova during the preceding three years. Family-reunification residents can generally seek permanent residence after three years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A pre-existing genuine marriage can count toward the three-year marriage duration, but does not replace the separate three-year continuous legal-residence requirement.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Permanent legal residence is still required when filing for citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage does not confer citizenship automatically. Romanian and Constitution knowledge, legal income, permanent residence at filing, personal submission, and refusal-ground screening remain applicable. Authorities can investigate authenticity, and sham marriage can cause refusal, cancellation, or other immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Apply the rule to the couple's precise marriage and residence history.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child is Moldovan when at least one parent is a citizen. Birth in Moldova to two foreign citizens does not ordinarily suffice; territorial acquisition mainly protects children of stateless or protected parents and children who would otherwise be stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Moldova to two ordinary foreign-citizen parents does not receive citizenship merely because of birthplace or parental temporary/permanent residence. Citizenship at birth can apply where the parents are stateless or protected persons or anti-statelessness conditions apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parental residence alone is not the trigger under the law effective from 24 December 2025.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Moldovan citizen at birth when at least one parent is Moldovan, whether born in Moldova or abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: A foreign birth may need transcription or registration before identity documents are issued.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent continuously and legally residing for at least three years at the domicile or temporary residence of a Moldovan-citizen child may qualify for an accelerated naturalisation limb. The child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Permanent residence at filing and general language, Constitution, income, and refusal-ground requirements remain applicable.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father may potentially use the three-year citizen-child co-residence condition if the child is Moldovan, but must independently maintain lawful residence and satisfy every general naturalisation condition.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and genuine family/co-residence evidence may be examined; the child's citizenship does not automatically confer paternal citizenship.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the research date. Different indexes use different methodologies.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index count; eVisas are classified separately and excluded from the requested VOA/eTA field.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Sum of 43 visa-on-arrival and six eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 123: 74 visa-free, 43 visa-on-arrival, and six eTA destinations; power rank 40.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in Chișinău and international technology settings, but insufficient for immigration integration or citizenship. EF EPI 2025 ranked Moldova 43rd with a score of 531, while the 2024 census found 13.4% self-reported English knowledge; Romanian is needed for permanent residence and naturalisation.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF uses a self-selected testing population, while census self-reporting measures a different concept. Both support planning for Romanian outside international professional circles.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian remains widely practical for daily communication: 68.2% of the census population reported knowing it and 15.9% reported it as their usual language. Ukrainian is useful in Ukrainian communities but less universal; 6.4% reported knowing it.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Neither replaces Romanian for official integration and citizenship. Transnistria was outside the census coverage described by the source.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q1 2026 gross average of MDL 15,987.1 at MDL 17.528/USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The latest official distribution available by 15 August 2026 reports salary bands rather than a numeric median. Its cumulative percentages place the September 2025 median within MDL 7,000–15,000 gross/month, approximately USD 399–856 at the cited exchange rate, but do not support a single median amount.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 statutory minimum wage of MDL 6,300; this is a legal floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q1 2026 gross average monthly earning.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No exact national median is published in the latest official wage-distribution release available by the research date. That release only locates the September 2025 median inside the MDL 7,000–15,000 gross monthly band, approximately USD 399–856; a single USD median would therefore be invented.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official releases publish averages and open-ended distribution bands, not a bounded national maximum salary. No maximum was inferred.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory nationwide full-time minimum effective 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official Q1 2026 gross average for economic units with four or more employees and all budgetary institutions.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Between MDL 7,000 and MDL 15,000 gross/month; exact median unpublished
median_salary_local_currency.notes: For full-month, full-time September 2025 employees in real-sector units with at least four employees and all budgetary institutions, 20.4% earned no more than MDL 7,000 and another 46.9% earned MDL 7,000–15,000. The 50th percentile therefore lies within that band, but the banded release cannot identify a single median value.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No bounded national maximum is published
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official distribution's upper category is open-ended, and the earnings releases report averages rather than a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory gross minimum; official gross average; and banded distribution for full-month, full-time employees
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage: 2026; average: Q1 2026; median band: September 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The exact median remains numerically null because the current official source publishes only bands. This is distinct from the Q1 2026 mean and from the forecast average used for immigration thresholds.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official earnings sources do not publish a comprehensive current national household cost-of-living budget. Private crowdsourced estimates were not substituted for an official measure.

settlement_track.summary: Digital-nomad status is qualifying temporary residence rather than visitor permission. The holder must later obtain permanent residence—generally after five years—and hold permanent legal residence when applying for naturalisation after ten years of continuous legal residence.
settlement_track.notes: The statutory chain is credible and digital nomads are not among published permanent-residence exclusions. However, the route opened in September 2025, so no nomad has completed the five-year stage and the contribution-record checklist requires filing-level clarification.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The legislation expressly covers remote employees and service providers contracted with legal entities registered outside Moldova, without requiring a Moldovan employer or local client.

data.notes: Focused audit resolved the employer-sponsored salary display using the general 2026 wage floor, clarified that the current social-insurance sources publish local-payroll and registered-entrepreneur rules but no digital-nomad-specific state-pension percentage, and replaced the vague median marker with the official MDL 7,000–15,000 band. Confidence remains medium because the nomad route has not yet produced a five-year permanent-residence case.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Renewed digital-nomad temporary residence followed by permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Digital-nomad residence is renewable, and the general rule permits other temporary-resident categories to apply for permanent residence after five years.
requirements: Continue foreign remote activity and renew the up-to-two-year permits on time.
Meet the permanent-residence language, accommodation and criminal-record requirements.
Provide the contribution and income documentation requested by the permanent-residence checklist.
reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad temporary residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Counting nomad time is an inference from the general five-year rule and the published exclusions, which do not name digital nomads. The agency’s provisional-stay page clearly distinguishes three years for family reunification from five years for other categories. The PR checklist asks for five years of social/salary/tax records; how foreign-employed nomads satisfy that evidence should be confirmed. The programme is new; this is a legal route, not evidence of completed five-year cases. The checklist PDF direct fetch was blocked by the site; its requirement was available through the official search index.

data.selection_summary: Monaco does not offer a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker status. Financially self-sufficient residence is available independently but is expressly based on living without gainful employment; working from Monaco requires separate professional authorisation. A foreign national can seek authorisation for a Monaco sole-trader business, but this is a locally authorised, locally established business route with effective-substance requirements and discretionary sector regulation, not a regular foreign-contract remote-work route.

visa_application.title: How to apply for a residence permit
visa_application.notes: Official Monaco residence-permit procedure, not a digital-nomad application. Applicants who require a long-stay visa must first use France-Visas; the visa is issued only after Monaco approves the application.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence permit based on sufficient financial resources

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No statutory monthly threshold is published. A recent Monaco-bank reference or other accepted evidence must demonstrate sufficient resources.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No official minimum euro amount was found; widely reported private-bank deposit figures are not statutory thresholds and were not adopted.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; sufficient resources must be proved
income_requirement_display.notes: Evidence may include a Monaco-bank reference, qualifying income or support. The self-sufficient category does not itself authorise gainful remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: The official procedure requires current evidence but does not state a fixed number of historical income months.

key_requirements.requirement: Accommodation in Monaco suitable for the household, through ownership, qualifying company ownership, rental or permitted hosting.
Sufficient resources established through accepted evidence, including a recent Monaco-bank reference where applicable.
Criminal-record evidence and a good-character assessment.
Non-EEA applicants generally obtain a French-issued Monaco long-stay establishment visa before applying for the Monaco permit.
This resources-based ground is for an applicant who does not intend to engage in professional activity; professional work requires separate authorisation.

initial_validity.value: Temporary resident permit, up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: First issuance is discretionary and validity cannot exceed the underlying entry documents or visas.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while effective residence, accommodation, sufficient resources and other conditions continue; after more than 3 years an ordinary three-year card may be granted and after at least 10 years a privileged ten-year card may be granted.
extension_rules.notes: Progression uses discretionary language and is not an entitlement.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct application for a Monaco temporary residence permit after satisfying entry/visa, accommodation, resources and character requirements.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence, but not remote-work permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least 10 years of effective residence, a privileged residence card valid for 10 years may be granted.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Monaco law does not label this permanent residence, and grant or renewal remains discretionary.

path_to_citizenship.value: A foreigner may request naturalisation after 10 years of habitual residence in Monaco after age 18, but naturalisation is granted by sovereign ordinance and is not a right.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Loss of the prior nationality is generally required, subject to the statutory sequencing exception.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the exact financial-means ground does not authorise gainful work. A foreign employment contract may help show resources only if accepted by the authorities; it does not establish permission to perform that work from Monaco.

rejected_routes.route_name: Foreign-national sole trader or independent professional

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No generally applicable minimum income was found. Business authorisation and residence each require their own substantive assessment.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed euro income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; business authorisation and effective local activity required
income_requirement_display.notes: The applicant must obtain ministerial authorisation and establish the authorised activity in specified Monaco premises. This is not a lightweight foreign-remote-worker registration.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed look-back period was found in the current official rules.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign natural persons must obtain administrative authorisation from the Minister of State before carrying on covered economic activities.
Authorisation defines the permitted activities, premises and any operating conditions and is personal and non-transferable.
Maintain an installation or personnel capable of effective activity in Monaco; lack of effective local substance can support withdrawal.
Complete applicable business, NIS, tax and social-security registrations after authorisation.
For a long-stay visa, provide the business-authorisation application receipt and detailed bank-account information, including an account in Monaco.

initial_validity.value: Business authorisation has no general fixed term stated in the reviewed law; the linked first residence permit is valid for up to 1 year.
initial_validity.notes: The authorisation is activity- and premises-specific and can be conditioned or withdrawn.

extension_rules.value: Residence may renew while authorised professional activity and effective residence continue; business changes or relocation require a new authorisation.
extension_rules.notes: Residence-card progression is possible but discretionary.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A receipt for the business-authorisation application can support a Monaco long-stay visa; after approval and establishment, authorised professional income can support the Monaco residence-permit application.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Business authorisation and immigration permission are separate decisions.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Effective residents may be considered for an ordinary three-year card after more than 3 years and a privileged ten-year card after at least 10 years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Neither progression is automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ten years of habitual residence after age 18 permits a naturalisation request, subject to sovereign discretion, character review and prior-nationality rules.
path_to_citizenship.notes: There is no guaranteed citizenship outcome.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because it requires a specifically authorised and effectively established Monaco business. Official sources do not confirm that an ordinary software engineer merely continuing one foreign contract, without meaningful Monaco business substance, would be authorised. Foreign-client activity may also bring business-profit tax and cross-border VAT reporting obligations.

summary.value: No independent degree- or qualification-based immigration route comparable to a skilled-migrant permit was found. Education may establish a temporary purpose of stay in an individual case, but a university degree alone does not grant Monaco residence, permanent residence or work permission.
summary.notes: Focused official searches did not establish a separate post-study, points-based or degree-based residence track.

tax_residency_rule.value: For a Monaco residence certificate used for tax formalities, the applicant declares one of the applicable connections: more than 183 days per year in Monaco, principal centre of activities, longest annual stay, or, failing those, the home in Monaco.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence-card status and treaty tax residence are not necessarily identical; another state may assert residence under its domestic law or a treaty.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for most individuals genuinely and effectively established in Monaco. French nationals governed by the 1963 convention are the principal exception, and other countries may still tax under their own residence, source or anti-avoidance rules.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The reviewed self-employed schemes use fixed quarterly CAMTI and CARTI contribution amounts/classes rather than one general percentage of income.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate lowest combined monthly CAMTI plus CARTI burden: (€1,101 + €550.08) per quarter ÷ 3, converted at the accessible ECB reference rate of USD 1.1380 per EUR. CARTI class 1 is a derogatory category subject to average monthly resources below €3,014; a typical higher-income software professional would generally face a higher class.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax regime exists. Most genuine non-French individual residents face no Monaco personal income tax, but an industrial or commercial business deriving at least 25% of turnover from operations outside Monaco is generally within the business-profit-tax regime, whose normal rate is 25%.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Whether independent software consulting is industrial/commercial or another professional classification requires filing-specific advice.

taxes.caveats: Zero personal income tax does not legalise unauthorised remote work. A foreign-contract worker must resolve immigration, Monaco business authorisation, business-profit tax, VAT, social security, source-country taxation and treaty residence separately. French nationality is a major exception to the usual Monaco PIT treatment.

taxation_system.value: No personal income tax for most individuals genuinely established in Monaco, with nationality, foreign-law and business-tax exceptions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days, principal centre of activities, longest annual stay or home may support the Monaco tax-residence certificate; treaty analysis can differ.
taxation_system.income_scope: Monaco generally imposes no personal income tax on qualifying residents, but other states may tax foreign employment or business income and Monaco business-profit tax can apply to qualifying enterprises.
taxation_system.special_regimes: French nationals governed by the Franco-Monegasque convention are generally taxed under French rules; no special digital-nomad regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Authorised self-employed workers must join CAMTI and CARTI. For 2025–2026 CAMTI is €1,101 quarterly; from 1 October 2025 CARTI ranges from €550.08 to €2,200.32 quarterly, with class 1 restricted by a resources test.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable to Monaco personal income tax. The displayed 0% is not a promised all-in rate; a foreign-contract business may instead face 25% business-profit tax plus fixed social contributions.
taxation_system.notes: The personal and enterprise tax layers must not be conflated.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a dedicated regime. Monaco has no confirmed digital-nomad status; financially self-sufficient residence carries no work authorisation, while authorised local self-employment enters the ordinary Monaco business and social-security framework.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; potential financially self-sufficient resident or authorised Monaco sole trader
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% Monaco PIT screening rate for most genuine non-French residents; potentially 25% business-profit tax for a qualifying foreign-turnover enterprise
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days, principal centre of activities, longest annual stay or Monaco home can support the residence certificate, subject to treaty and foreign-law analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Monaco generally levies no personal income tax on qualifying individuals, but foreign states may retain taxing rights. A Monaco industrial or commercial enterprise with at least 25% qualifying outside-Monaco turnover can be subject to 25% business-profit tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Authorised self-employed activity requires CAMTI and CARTI membership. The lowest reviewed combined amount is €1,651.08 quarterly, but the lowest CARTI class is income-tested; higher classes materially increase the payment.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed tax; ordinary residence-card fees and, if locally self-employed, CAMTI/CARTI contributions apply.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: CAMTI €1,101 quarterly for 2025–2026; CARTI €550.08–€2,200.32 quarterly from 1 October 2025.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Residence cards: first temporary card €80 and renewal €40; ordinary card €100/€50; privileged card €160/€80. Late renewal costs €50.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business, VAT and registration obligations depend on activity. EU customer services can require the Monaco EC Sales List for Services; no universal monthly municipal or freelancer tax was confirmed.
fixed_payments.notes: Professional authorisation, premises and accounting costs are not fixed by a single official tariff.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay or residence card does not by itself eliminate tax residence elsewhere, and visitor status does not authorise routine remote work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No dedicated lawful category was confirmed. A self-sufficient resident should not assume that the 0% PIT rule permits continued foreign employment from Monaco.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: After ministerial business authorisation and registration, 0% personal PIT may coexist with fixed CAMTI/CARTI charges, VAT obligations and potentially 25% business-profit tax for qualifying foreign-turnover activity.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax results depend heavily on nationality, legal form, activity classification, source of revenue, effective management and treaty residence.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying applicant applies directly for a temporary residence permit; no prior Monaco-residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: After at least 10 years of effective residence, a privileged ten-year residence card may be granted. Monaco does not describe it as unconditional permanent residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation eligibility and eligibility for the privileged card can both arise around 10 years; citizenship does not require first holding that card. Naturalisation remains entirely discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest ordinary statutory point to request naturalisation: 10 years of habitual residence after age 18. This is eligibility to ask, not a guaranteed processing or approval timeline.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official standard or typical processing time was found after focused searches; sovereign naturalisation is discretionary.

key_conditions.value: Habitual and effective residence, acceptable character and situation, sovereign approval, and generally loss of the prior nationality. Residence-card progression and citizenship are discretionary rather than automatic accrued rights.
key_conditions.notes: No statutory language-test requirement was identified in the reviewed nationality provision, but that does not limit the sovereign assessment.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Nationality by declaration is available after 20 years of marriage. For marriages celebrated before 1 July 2022, the transition rule reduces the period to 10 years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage counts from its celebration date. The 10-year transitional period applies only to marriages celebrated before 1 July 2022; later marriages use 20 years.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage can support a five-year spouse residence card after more than one year of Monaco residence, but it is not faster than the ordinary 10-year point for requesting discretionary naturalisation.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marital community must continue at application, unless the Monaco spouse has died and the applicant has not remarried; the Monaco spouse must retain nationality and must not have acquired it through an earlier marriage. The acquisition must not automatically cause loss of the applicant's original nationality under foreign law or treaty. Fraud, sham marriage or cessation of marital community can defeat the declaration.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Nationality by marriage is a separate declaration mechanism, not automatic citizenship at marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Monaco alone does not generally confer nationality. The law includes a narrow rule for a child born in Monaco to unknown parents.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Monaco to two known foreign parents does not automatically become Monegasque solely by birth. The unknown-parent exception is narrow.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Long residence or recognition as an Enfant du Pays is distinct from nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child generally acquires Monegasque nationality through a qualifying Monegasque parent under the statutory descent rules.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The detailed transmission rules depend on the parent's mode of acquiring nationality and filiation.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Monegasque child may be considered for a privileged ten-year residence card after one year rather than the usual ten years. This does not confer automatic citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Actual residence, profession or means and administrative approval remain required.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Monegasque child can benefit from the one-year reduced residence period for consideration of a privileged card and may receive certain protected-housing priority when supporting and educating the child. He does not automatically become Monegasque.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Filiation, actual care, residence and administrative conditions must be documented.

passport.index_name: Passport Index 2026; Henley Passport Index 2026 cross-check

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank. Henley uses a different methodology and placed Monaco 12th with access to 177 destinations in the current 2026 table.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category in Passport Index, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 classification.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 51 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. Henley's broader access score is not directly comparable.

passport.notes: Passport strength is high, but naturalisation is discretionary and generally requires surrender of the prior nationality.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is used and understood in Monaco's international population and business environment, but French is the sole official language and is the language to expect for laws, authorisations and much administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English can be practical socially and commercially, but relying on English alone for immigration or business filings is risky.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No official or reliable current evidence was found that Russian or Ukrainian is broadly usable for government procedures or everyday independent living. French should be assumed necessary, with English sometimes useful.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practicality inference from the official-language rule after focused searches found no supported Russian- or Ukrainian-language provision.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 private-sector gross FTE mean of €4,931 at USD 1.1380 per EUR.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 private-sector gross FTE median of €3,339.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the June 2026 statutory monthly minimum plus the required 5% exceptional allowance: €2,184.41. This is a wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of €4,931 monthly gross.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of €3,339 monthly gross.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary was published.

min_salary_local_currency.value: €2,080.39 per month for 169 hours, plus a mandatory 5% exceptional allowance (€2,184.41 total)
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Applicable from 1 June 2026 for adult workers; the 5% allowance is excluded from specified social deductions.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 private-sector gross full-time-equivalent mean.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 private-sector gross full-time-equivalent median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published as a meaningful national figure.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Private-sector gross monthly full-time equivalent; minimum field is the statutory adult wage floor
average_citizen_salary.period: Mean and median: 2024; minimum wage: from 2026-06-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: Monaco's workforce includes many non-resident cross-border employees, so these figures are worker salaries, not income earned only by Monegasque citizens. USD conversions use the latest accessible ECB reference rate captured during research and are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: No comparable official cost-of-living index or representative household budget was found. The residence rules nevertheless require household-appropriate accommodation in Monaco and individually sufficient means, with no published universal amount.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Private real-estate quotations and anecdotal bank-deposit figures were deliberately not converted into an official cost threshold.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Financially self-sufficient residence is not permission to work remotely. To perform professional activity, the applicant must obtain a separate Monaco business or employment authorisation.
settlement_track.summary: Monaco has long-term residence-card progression and discretionary naturalisation after long habitual residence, but no qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route was confirmed. The applicant would have to stop working, obtain a locally authorised substantive business status, or secure local employment before the settlement timeline could be relevant.
settlement_track.notes: The ten-year naturalisation rule is not assigned as a route timeline because the profile's ordinary foreign-contract work is not lawfully matched to the resources-based residence ground.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The self-sufficient residence ground assumes no professional activity. The alternative sole-trader route requires ministerial approval, specified Monaco premises and effective local business substance, so it is not ordinary continuation of a foreign contract under a remote-worker status.

data.notes: Audit improved the previous result by correcting the financial-means route's direct temporary-residence flag, adding the foreign-national sole-trader alternative and its 2025-amended authorisation timeline, current self-employed contributions, current residence fees and minimum wage, detailed tax caveats, nationality rules, child-parent residence benefit, passport-category breakdown and complete settlement analysis. At least 24 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected; 24 canonical sources are retained. Unresolved figures—especially a universal resources threshold, income-history period, citizenship processing time and maximum salary—remain null because no authoritative fixed value was established.

data.selection_summary: Mongolia does not currently publish a digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary freelance residence category. The C2 information-technology route requires an inviting Mongolian organization, job description, and work permit; B1 requires investment; H1 requires outstanding contribution or achievement; H3 does not expressly authorize remote work; and G immigrant status requires three prior consecutive years of lawful residence. None supplies a qualifying entry-to-citizenship route for an ordinary software engineer working only under a foreign contract.

visa_application.title: Reside for an official and private purpose
visa_application.notes: This is the official residence-service page. No dedicated remote-worker application route or application channel was found in the current category list.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The threshold is stated as a formula in MNT. No authoritative current exchange-rate source was established during this review, so no USD conversion is asserted.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: MNT 3,960,000 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The G page requires monthly income exceeding five times Mongolia's minimum wage. Using the official MNT 792,000 minimum effective April 1, 2025 gives MNT 3,960,000; the wording says '5 times more,' so filing-level confirmation of whether the authority interprets this as at least or strictly above that amount is advisable.

income_requirement_display.value: More than 5× the Mongolian minimum wage (currently about MNT 3,960,000/month)
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an entry route: the applicant must already have resided legally in Mongolia for three consecutive years.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page requires proof of sufficient funds and a monthly-income threshold but does not state a bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Three consecutive years of prior lawful residence in Mongolia.
Undergraduate or graduate degree, or specialization in a field considered essential in Mongolia.
No criminal history, prior deportation, or entry ban.
Address evidence, three-generation biography, police certificate, medical certificates, funding evidence, diploma, photographs, passport, application, and fee.
Immigrant status is discretionary and subject to national and nationality-specific quotas.

initial_validity.value: Up to 5 years
initial_validity.notes: The Foreign Nationals Law places permanent residence within private-purpose residence and provides permits of up to five years.

extension_rules.value: Extensions of up to 3 years; status may be cancelled after more than 180 days outside Mongolia in one year
extension_rules.notes: The permit is called immigrant/permanent residence, but the residence document itself has a renewable validity period.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying foreign-remote-work status supplies the required three years of prior lawful residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A person would first need another lawful category, such as locally sponsored work, investment, study, or family residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The G application is the immigrant/permanent-residence application after three consecutive years of lawful residence, but approval remains discretionary.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Meeting the published eligibility conditions does not establish an entitlement to approval.

path_to_citizenship.value: After obtaining permanent residence, ordinary naturalization generally requires five years of permanent residence plus livelihood, Mongolian-language, customs, Constitution, conduct, policy, and renunciation conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the absence of a qualifying initial route for the foreign-contract remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Potentially important as a later permanent-residence application, but invalid for selection because the applicant cannot use ordinary foreign remote work to obtain the prerequisite three years of lawful residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum salary was published on the official C2 page.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum salary was published on the official C2 page.

income_requirement_display.value: No published route-specific minimum; local sponsored employment is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Absence of a stated minimum does not remove the work-permit and inviting-organization requirements.

income_proof_months.notes: The official C2 page does not publish a required income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Official request from an inviting organization or legal entity.
Organization registration documents and a job description.
Work permit from the competent labor authority.
Passport, application, fee, and supporting documents.

initial_validity.value: Entry visa permission for up to 90 days; residence must be applied for after entry when required
initial_validity.notes: The visa permission itself is valid for use for 60 days after issuance.

extension_rules.value: Employment residence may be extended through the competent authorities; published transition rules allow employment status to change only to investment status.
extension_rules.notes: No conversion from C2 to an independent remote-worker status is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Local sponsored C2 employment can support a residence permit after entry.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not cover ordinary work solely for a foreign employer or client.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A later G immigrant application may become possible after three lawful years if all discretionary eligibility requirements are met.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a separate application, not an automatic C2 conversion.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential only after separately obtaining permanent residence and then meeting the five-year naturalization conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Outside the selected profile because local sponsorship and a work permit are mandatory.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Mongolian inviting organization and work permit are mandatory even though information technology is expressly covered.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No personal-income threshold is published; this is an investment route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No personal-income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No personal-income threshold published; qualifying foreign investment and enterprise documentation required
income_requirement_display.notes: The official page does not establish a capital threshold, so none is inferred.

income_proof_months.notes: The official B1 page does not publish an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Inviting organization or legal entity and its registration documents.
Statement from the competent development authority and supporting tax/social-insurance documents.
Applicant must qualify as an investor of a foreign-invested enterprise.

initial_validity.value: Investor entry visa up to 90 days, followed by the applicable residence process
initial_validity.notes: Visa permission is valid for 60 days after issuance.

extension_rules.value: Private-purpose residence permits may be issued for up to five years and extended for up to three years, subject to category rules and approval.
extension_rules.notes: The B1 page does not establish an automatic settlement timeline.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available to qualifying investors through the B1 investment category.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not available merely because the applicant has foreign freelance income.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate discretionary G immigrant application may be considered after three years of lawful residence and satisfaction of its conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic investor-to-permanent-residence conversion was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separate permanent residence followed by ordinary naturalization conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not a route for the ordinary foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires investor and enterprise status, which is outside the applicant context.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; exceptional merit or achievement is required
income_requirement_display.notes: A relevant software degree alone does not satisfy the stated exceptional-achievement test.

income_proof_months.notes: The official H1 page does not publish an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Outstanding contribution to Mongolia, or a profession/specialization in great demand together with great achievements in science or another qualifying field.
Application, address evidence, passport, photograph, fee, and residence documentation.

initial_validity.value: Up to 5 years under the private-purpose residence framework
initial_validity.notes: The H1 page reviewed primarily describes extension requirements.

extension_rules.value: Up to 3 years per extension
extension_rules.notes: Extension application is generally due 30 days before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: H1 is a private-purpose residence category for exceptional/high-demand achievement cases.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Eligibility is discretionary and materially exceeds the ordinary software-engineer profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic H1-to-G conversion was published; the separate G criteria may potentially be relevant after three lawful years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Manual legal confirmation would be required.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship law contains a Presidential exceptional-contribution/high-demand-achievement discretion, but this is not ordinary naturalization or a predictable route.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Exceptional discretion is excluded by the selection criteria.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as an elite or exceptional-achievement route rather than ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: The category is defined residually as other private purposes and does not say that foreign remote work is authorized.

income_proof_months.notes: The official H3 materials do not publish an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Official invitation and documents supporting the specific private purpose.
Local address evidence, passport, photograph, application, fee, and in-person biometric registration for a first permit.
The English page contains relationship and H2-document references that make its standalone scope unclear.

initial_validity.value: Up to 5 years under the private-purpose residence framework
initial_validity.notes: Actual duration is determined by the authority and supporting purpose.

extension_rules.value: Extensions may be available under the private-purpose framework; the current Mongolian H3 service page states up to one year per extension
extension_rules.notes: A refused application in the same category generally cannot be refiled for one year.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: H3 can produce private-purpose residence when the authority accepts the documented purpose.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The official materials do not establish foreign remote work as a qualifying purpose or authorized activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion is published. The separate G immigrant application requires three consecutive lawful years and satisfaction of its other discretionary criteria.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The published G criteria do not expressly exclude H3 residence, but no current source guarantees that the authority will accept H3 time toward G eligibility.

path_to_citizenship.value: H3 does not itself confer permanent residence or citizenship. If H3 is granted and continuously renewed for a genuine private purpose, those years may satisfy the separate G immigrant-permit rule requiring three consecutive years of lawful residence; the published G criteria do not exclude H3, but no current source guarantees that H3 time will be accepted or that G will be approved. Only after separately obtaining G/permanent-resident status could ordinary naturalization be pursued, after at least five years of permanent residence and satisfaction of the livelihood, Mongolian-language, customs, Constitution, conduct, foreign-relations, and prior-citizenship-renunciation conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is a contingent H3-to-G-to-citizenship sequence, not an automatic conversion. H3 is a residual private-purpose category requiring an inviting citizen; it does not publish foreign remote work as an authorized purpose, and unauthorized employment or activity inconsistent with the admitted purpose can trigger deportation. Accordingly, this possible sequence remains invalid for the ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a residual private-purpose category is not sufficient evidence of permission to reside and work remotely for a foreign client. The current visa table and forms confirm that an inviting citizen is involved, so this is not an independent self-application route.

summary.value: E1-E5 categories cover higher education, undergraduate/graduate study, vocational or language study, state/research internships, and innovation or research activities. A student does not need a local employer, but does need a qualifying educational or research purpose and institution; education is not an ordinary remote-work route and no direct permanent residence entitlement was confirmed.
summary.notes: The later G route separately requires three consecutive years of lawful residence, sufficient income, education or essential specialization, and discretionary approval. The official sources do not confirm that study alone guarantees G approval.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is a Mongolian resident taxpayer after residing in Mongolia for at least 183 days during 12 consecutive months, or when at least 50% of total taxable income is earned in or derived from Mongolia, applying the law's stated sequential test. Days are cumulative across the relevant tax year and preceding year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A resident is taxed on Mongolian and foreign income; a nonresident is taxed on Mongolian-source income.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the principal screening rate for relevant employment, operational/business, and covered foreign income—not the maximum rate for every statutory income category.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The law states a 13.5% voluntary-insurance rate on self-declared income. Compulsorily insured employees pay 9.5%, with employers paying 10.5%, 11.5%, or 12.5% depending on workplace risk. Health insurance is governed separately.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable USD amount is asserted. If the statutory minimum-wage floor applies to a voluntary contract, 13.5% of MNT 792,000 equals MNT 106,920 monthly, but applicability to a foreign remote worker without a qualifying residence category requires confirmation; health insurance may be additional.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate, territorial, remittance-basis, or foreign-income tax holiday was found in the reviewed official materials.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Category-specific PIT rates still apply to specified income types.

taxes.caveats: The immigration route is absent, so these figures describe hypothetical tax treatment rather than a digital-nomad regime. Contract classification, source of services income, permanent establishment or local business registration, social-insurance status, health insurance, treaty residence, and foreign tax credits require case-specific advice.

taxation_system.value: Resident individuals are taxed on Mongolian and foreign income. A 10% rate applies to principal employment and operational-income categories, while specified categories carry 1%, 2%, 5%, 20%, or 40% rates.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 days in 12 consecutive months, or at least 50% of total taxable income earned in or derived from Mongolia, under the statutory sequential test.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for resident taxpayers; Mongolian-source income for nonresidents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary inbound-remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Voluntary insurance is 13.5% of declared income; compulsory employee contributions are 9.5%, plus employer contributions. Health insurance is regulated separately.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The system is not presented here as a progressive wage schedule. The 40% figure is a special category rate and should not be interpreted as the expected rate on remote software income; the practical screening PIT rate is 10%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No general threshold stated for the relevant employment/operational categories
tax_brackets.applies_to: Relevant employment income, operational income, and covered foreign income classifications
tax_brackets.notes: Income classification and deductions determine the actual liability.

tax_brackets.applies_to: The specific income category referenced in Article 19.1.2
tax_brackets.notes: Included only to explain the statutory maximum category rate; it is not the ordinary remote-worker rate.

taxation_system.notes: The statutes are official but displayed as unofficial English translations.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special regime because Mongolia has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence category. Hypothetically, a resident taxpayer's covered foreign employment or operational income would generally be screened at 10%.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; hypothetical resident individual with foreign employment or operational income
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% principal screening PIT rate; category-specific rates may differ
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Resident after at least 183 days in 12 consecutive months or under the 50%-of-income test in the PIT law.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident taxpayer's income earned abroad is taxable and covered foreign income is generally self-reported by February 15 following the tax year.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific exemption was found. Voluntary social insurance is 13.5% of declared income; compulsory employee insurance is 9.5%. Health insurance is separate.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed tax or contribution established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potential voluntary minimum approximately MNT 106,920 per month if the minimum-wage contribution floor applies; legal applicability and separate health insurance must be confirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad fee exists. Category fees vary; the G page publishes a MNT 135,000 standard processing fee, while other residence-category extension pages publish separate state and card fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No remote-worker-specific municipal fee, transaction tax, VAT threshold, or freelancer levy was established from the reviewed sources.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of a qualifying route makes a precise nomad fixed-payment total impossible.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A nonresident is generally taxed only on Mongolian-source income, but services physically performed in Mongolia may create source or compliance questions even when paid abroad.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Resident taxpayers are subject to tax on foreign income; relevant foreign employment or operational income is generally screened at 10%, subject to classification and treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Operational income may be taxed at 10%, and voluntary social insurance may be available at 13.5% of declared income, but tax or business registration does not independently create immigration permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in statutory headline rules; lower confidence in their application to a fact pattern for which no immigration category exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary residence is available for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Three consecutive lawful years are a published eligibility condition for the separate G immigrant application, not an automatic conversion and not achievable through an identified remote-worker status.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Immigration Agency states that ordinary naturalization requires at least five years of permanent residence, alongside other conditions.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: A theoretical minimum could exceed eight years, but no total is stated because there is no qualifying initial route, acceptance of H3 time toward G is not guaranteed, and G approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The law states that receiving, examining, and deciding citizenship matters must not exceed six months; the Immigration Agency separately displays a six-to-twelve-month service estimate, so actual timing should be confirmed at filing.

key_conditions.value: Obtain a qualifying lawful status, meet the separate G requirements after three consecutive years, maintain permanent residence, and then satisfy livelihood, Mongolian-language, customs, Constitution, conduct, state-policy, and renunciation requirements. G status may be cancelled after more than 180 days abroad in a year. Citizenship decisions are Presidential.
key_conditions.notes: Mongolia does not recognize dual citizenship in ordinary naturalization and generally requires renunciation of the former citizenship.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No separate shortened naturalization period based solely on marriage is published in the current reviewed law and official residence materials.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A legally registered existing marriage to a Mongolian citizen supports an F1 family-purpose residence application. Marriage does not automatically change either spouse's citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: F1 residence can be extended for up to three years at a time within the private-purpose framework.

requirements_and_risks.value: The relationship must be legally registered and genuine. Counterfeit marriage is an express ground for refusing or cancelling family residence, and finalized divorce can affect the permit. Ordinary citizenship conditions, including permanent residence and language/integration requirements, remain applicable because no spouse exception was identified.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A genuine spouse route is outside the applicant's stated independent remote-work profile.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Mongolia alone does not confer citizenship on a child of foreign parents. Narrow rules cover foundlings and allow a Mongolia-born child of permanently resident stateless parents to opt for citizenship after reaching age 16.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Mongolia to two foreign-citizen parents does not automatically become Mongolian. A child of permanently resident stateless parents may choose Mongolian citizenship after age 16; an unidentified-parent foundling in Mongolia is Mongolian.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A Mongolian birth certificate issued to a child of foreign or stateless parents proves birth, not citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is Mongolian and the other foreign, a child born in Mongolia is Mongolian. If born abroad, the parents determine citizenship by written agreement. If the other parent is stateless, the child is Mongolian regardless of birthplace.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Thus the result depends on birthplace and the second parent's status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. The reviewed category list did not establish a general parent-of-Mongolian-child residence category; a foreign spouse of a Mongolian citizen can instead use F1 if legally married.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Direct confirmation from the Immigration Agency is advisable for an unmarried foreign parent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or confirmed independent permanent-residence entitlement arises merely because the child is Mongolian. If the father is married to the Mongolian mother, F1 spouse residence may apply; otherwise a specific parent-based benefit was not established.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A citizen child's status should not be treated as automatically conferring citizenship or residence on the father.

rank.notes: Current Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; index rankings can change frequently.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Pure visa-free destinations in this index, not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately lists eVisa destinations, so this number should be read using the index's classification.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 38 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations. The index reports a mobility score of 78.

passport.notes: Passport Index categories differ from Henley's combined prior-visa-free-access methodology. These figures consistently use one current index and should not be mixed with the previous record's Henley rank/access count.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Remote work is technically feasible in connected urban areas, but English-only daily life is limited. EF's 2025 index ranks Mongolia 95th with a score of 447, and Mongolia's Education Ministry describes national English proficiency as low; government and legal processes operate in Mongolian. World Bank data reports 85% internet use in 2024, which supports connectivity but not language access.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English is more likely to be usable in Ulaanbaatar and international or technology settings than in government procedures or outside major urban areas.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no sufficiently authoritative current source quantified their day-to-day usefulness. Russian may help with some individuals, but it should not be treated as a dependable substitute for Mongolian; Ukrainian-specific practicality was not established.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Kept cautious after focused language searches because available claims about Russian use were mainly anecdotal or outdated.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Official Q4 2025 mean is MNT 2,877,800 monthly. No authoritative contemporaneous exchange-rate source was established, so no USD conversion is asserted.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Official Q4 2025 median is MNT 2,482,200 monthly. No authoritative contemporaneous exchange-rate source was established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: MNT 792,000 statutory monthly minimum; no USD conversion is asserted because no authoritative contemporaneous exchange-rate source was established.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: MNT 2,877,800 official nominal monthly average; no USD conversion is asserted because no authoritative contemporaneous exchange-rate source was established.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: MNT 2,482,200 official monthly median; no USD conversion is asserted because no authoritative contemporaneous exchange-rate source was established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official wage bulletin does not publish a meaningful national maximum wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory nationwide minimum effective April 1, 2025, not the lowest observed salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official national nominal average wage for Q4 2025.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official national median wage for Q4 2025.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official national wage bulletin does not publish a meaningful maximum employee wage.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official nominal monthly employee wages; statutory minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Q4 2025 wages; minimum effective April 1, 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: This is average citizen/resident employee wage data, not an immigration income threshold. The NSO bulletin reports a Q4 2025 national mean of MNT 2,877.8 thousand and median of MNT 2,482.2 thousand; the minimum is the statutory wage rather than an observed wage-distribution minimum.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official wage and labor sources do not publish a current household cost-of-living benchmark suitable for this field, so no estimate is invented.
