settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Mongolia has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. Visitor entry, H3 private-purpose residence, or tax registration must not be treated as remote-work authorization or a settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: Mongolia has a discretionary immigrant/permanent-residence application after three lawful years and ordinary naturalization after five years of permanent residence, but no qualifying initial status for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The applicant would have to switch to an unrelated sponsored-employment, investment, study, family, or exceptional route before any settlement path could begin.
settlement_track.notes: The negative selection result is retained. The focused audit establishes a possible but unguaranteed H3-to-G-to-naturalization sequence for a genuine non-work private purpose; it does not make H3 a remote-work or automatic settlement route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No category expressly permits an ordinary foreign employee or freelancer to reside in Mongolia while working solely for a foreign counterparty. C2 is locally sponsored; B1 is investment; H1 is exceptional; H3 requires an inviter, is defined only as a residual private purpose, and lacks remote-work authorization.

data.notes: Thirty-three distinct canonical, directly relevant URLs were inspected, including nine relevant URLs not present in the previous source set. The focused H3 audit confirms only a contingent H3-to-G-to-naturalization sequence, not an automatic conversion or a remote-work route. Remaining nulls precisely identify unpublished thresholds, conversion guarantees, exchange-rate conversions, cost benchmarks, or language-use measures rather than substituting guesses.

data.selection_summary: Montenegro has an active digital-nomad temporary-residence permit for ordinary remote work for a foreign company or the applicant’s own foreign company. Current 2026 Foreigners Law text treats granted temporary residence as counting toward permanent residence and does not exclude digital-nomad residence, but the nomad permit lasts only 2+2 years. Reaching the five-year PR threshold therefore requires changing to another qualifying residence basis before the fourth year expires without a residence gap. This is a credible conversion-based settlement route, but the future replacement basis must be planned and verified with the Ministry.

visa_application.title: How to get the visa?
visa_application.notes: Official government route page and filing checklist, not an online application portal. The applicant enters Montenegro lawfully and files personally at the competent Ministry of Internal Affairs regional unit or branch.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Temporary Residence Permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official checklist requires financial means but publishes no fixed monthly immigration threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Proof of sufficient financial means; no fixed EUR amount published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The separate tax-exemption test involving prior-year average earnings is not stated to be the immigration threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient financial means; no fixed permit amount officially published
income_requirement_display.notes: Do not substitute the tax exemption formula for an immigration threshold without written Ministry confirmation.

income_proof_months.notes: The official route page does not prescribe a specific bank-statement or payslip history.

key_requirements.requirement: Enter Montenegro lawfully and apply personally to the Ministry of Internal Affairs before the permitted short stay expires.
Provide an employment contract or other evidence of electronic work for a foreign company, or evidence of owning and working through a company not registered in Montenegro.
Provide proof of financial means, accommodation and health insurance.
Hold a valid passport or qualifying identity document, normally valid at least three months beyond the requested permit period.
Provide criminal-record evidence showing no relevant unconditional prison sentence exceeding six months, subject to cessation of legal consequences.
A photograph, two fingerprints and digitized signature are collected when filing.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The stated decision period is 40 days after submission of a complete application.

extension_rules.value: One extension for up to 2 additional years; file personally no later than 30 days before expiry. A new nomad permit may be issued only six months after the previous nomad residence expires.
extension_rules.notes: A settlement-oriented applicant must switch to another qualifying residence basis before expiry rather than take the six-month gap.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The route directly issues a temporary-residence permit after an in-person application in Montenegro.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A complete application filed before the lawful short stay expires permits the applicant to remain until an enforceable decision.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After nomad residence, a qualifying entrepreneur or owner-director work/residence permit can continue residence toward PR. A switch is needed before the four-year nomad maximum because PR normally requires five continuous years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The 2026 government-hosted consolidated law was inspected: Article 86 uses temporary-residence time and does not exclude digital nomads; Article 70 supplies the entrepreneur successor and its renewal condition. Counting prior nomad residence is a statutory inference, not an automatic conversion guarantee. Confirm the change-of-basis filing sequence; no universal no-exit promise is made.

path_to_citizenship.value: After ten years of legal and continuous residence, ordinary naturalisation may be requested if the applicant satisfies income, accommodation, language, criminal-record, security, tax-compliance and nationality-release requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nomad permit cannot cover the full period itself. Ordinary naturalisation generally requires release from prior citizenship, subject to statutory exceptions.

best_routes.notes: This route fits an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer and requires no Montenegrin employer. It is settlement-oriented only through conversion: nomad residence can contribute to the five-year PR period, but another lawful residence basis is required before the four-year cap. No automatic successor status is reserved for nomads.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker residence threshold applies to ordinary short stay.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Not applicable
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Visitor status is not qualifying residence.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable to visitor status
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status is not a settlement route.

income_proof_months.notes: Requirements depend on nationality and visa procedure, not a remote-work program.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid travel document and, where required, a short-stay visa; stay is generally limited to 90 days in 180 days.

initial_validity.value: Generally up to 90 days in a 180-day period

extension_rules.value: No recurring remote-work residence or settlement extension is provided.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None directly; a separate residence application is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Visitor time does not establish the temporary-residence history required for PR.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status is not a residence or citizenship path, even if incidental remote activity is practically possible.

rejected_routes.route_name: Local IT-sector employment residence and work permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No applicant-profile threshold is supplied because the route requires Montenegrin employment.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Employment remuneration under a Montenegrin employment contract
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current provision requires an IT-sector contract with a local employer for at least 12 months.

income_requirement_display.value: Local employment contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an ordinary foreign-client remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable as an independent-income test.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment contract in Montenegro’s IT sector with a Montenegrin employer, concluded for at least 12 months.
Tax and contribution compliance for renewal.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years under the current IT-sector provision

extension_rules.value: May be extended for up to 3 additional years, subject to continuing local employment and compliance.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence and work permit tied to local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially counts toward the general five-year PR rule if continuity and other requirements are met.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential ordinary ten-year residence route, but only through local employment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a Montenegrin employer and employment contract.

summary.value: Enrollment in a Montenegrin secondary or higher-education institution can support temporary residence without a local employer. A pre-existing software-engineering degree alone does not qualify. Only half of residence spent studying, specializing, in professional training or practical instruction counts toward the five-year PR period.
summary.notes: This is enrollment-based residence, not an independent qualification-based migration program. It may serve as a successor status after nomad residence, but discounted counting and genuine-study requirements make it inefficient.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is tax resident if domiciled in Montenegro, if the centre of personal and economic interests is there, or if present for at least 183 days in a tax year; treaty tie-breaker rules may override domestic residence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can arise before 183 days through domicile or centre-of-interests facts.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top ordinary PIT screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Qualifying digital-nomad earnings may be exempt; municipal surtax can add 13% or 15% of PIT assessed.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 10.5% figure is the ordinary employee burden: 10% pension/disability plus 0.5% unemployment, with another 0.5% unemployment borne by an ordinary employer. It is not the expected charge on qualifying nomad income: Article 18d of the current 2026 law exempts personal-income or self-employment income received from an employer not registered in Montenegro when earned on the basis of digital-nomad status.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly nomad-specific tax or social-security payment applies to covered income. A numeric amount remains null because private health-insurance premiums vary and the current official route and visa pages do not publish a consolidated permit/card fee amount.

special_tax_regimes.value: An official investment-agency guide states that individual digital nomads are exempt from PIT when working for an employer that does not operate or register as a legal entity in Montenegro and earnings exceed three official average gross earnings reported for the previous year.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Obtain tax-authority confirmation that the applicant’s employee, contractor or own-company arrangement qualifies.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on employee versus contractor status, tax residence, income source, the foreign employer’s Montenegro presence, treaty relief and the exact exemption conditions. The immigration permit does not itself conclusively establish exemption eligibility or eliminate filing obligations.

taxation_system.value: Mixed progressive and proportional PIT system with a special digital-nomad exemption. Salary and entrepreneurial income use 0%, 9% and 15% bands; other taxable personal income is generally taxed at 15%, plus municipal surtax on PIT assessed.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or centre of personal/economic interests in Montenegro, or at least 183 days in the tax year, subject to treaty tie-breaker rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents on Montenegro-source income. Qualifying nomad income may be exempt.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Conditional digital-nomad PIT exemption for qualifying work for a foreign employer/entity not operating or registered in Montenegro, where earnings exceed three prior-year official average gross earnings.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary salary payroll is 10% employee pension/disability plus 0.5% employee unemployment and 0.5% employer unemployment. Article 18d of the current 2026 law expressly exempts covered nomad personal or self-employment income from an employer not registered in Montenegro.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 15% is the top ordinary PIT rate, not an effective rate. Municipal surtax is 13% of PIT in most municipalities and 15% in Podgorica and Cetinje. A qualifying nomad may instead have 0% PIT on covered income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Salary income up to EUR 700 gross per month
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate conversion at USD 1.139 per EUR.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Salary income from EUR 700.01 to EUR 1,000 gross per month
tax_brackets.applies_to: Salary income up to the upper threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted approximately.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Salary income above EUR 1,000 gross per month
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate; municipal surtax applies separately.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Entrepreneurial earnings up to EUR 8,400 annually
Entrepreneurial earnings from EUR 8,400.01 to EUR 12,000 annually
tax_brackets.applies_to: Entrepreneurial income up to the upper threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted approximately.

taxation_system.notes: Ordinary rates are supported by PwC’s 7 August 2026 review and current Tax Administration publications. Official materials support the conditional PIT exemption, and the current contribution law separately confirms a contribution exemption. Filing treatment and treaty interaction require individual advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Qualifying foreign-employer digital-nomad earnings may receive a 0% PIT exemption and statutory social-contribution exemption. Otherwise, ordinary PIT reaches 15% plus municipal surtax. Tax residence can still arise through domicile, centre of interests or 183 days.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital-nomad temporary residence with conditional PIT exemption and statutory contribution exemption
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% on qualifying exempt nomad earnings; otherwise up to 15% ordinary PIT plus municipal surtax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Tax residence arises through Montenegro domicile or centre of personal/economic interests, or at least 183 days in the tax year, subject to treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are ordinarily taxable on worldwide income, but covered nomad earnings may be exempt when the statutory foreign-entity and income tests are satisfied.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Conditional PIT exemption where the individual works for an employer that does not operate or register as a legal entity in Montenegro and earnings exceed three prior-year official average gross earnings.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Article 18d of the current 2026 law exempts personal-income or self-employment income received from an employer not registered in Montenegro when earned on the basis of digital-nomad status. Ordinary payroll rates describe non-exempt payroll, not covered nomad income.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory fixed monthly nomad-specific tax or social-security charge was identified. Covered income is contribution-exempt; PIT is percentage-based and its separate exemption is conditional. Private insurance and filing/card charges remain separate.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: EUR 0 fixed monthly contribution on income satisfying Article 18d because the statute grants an exemption rather than setting a minimum. Ordinary payroll or locally registered self-employment outside the exemption can trigger percentage-based contributions.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The official visa page requires proof of payment of a consular fee, but neither it nor the current residence page states a consolidated digital-nomad visa, permit or card amount. Obtain current amounts from the relevant consulate and MIA office.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Private health insurance, translations, legalisation/apostille and residence-registration costs vary. The general VAT rate is 21% if local business registration and taxable supplies become relevant.
fixed_payments.notes: The contribution exemption is confirmed. Private insurance premiums and current one-time filing/card charges remain variable or unpriced on the reviewed official route pages.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence because domicile or centre of interests can independently create tax residence. Montenegro-source income and treaty rules also require review.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident is ordinarily taxed on worldwide income but should test and document the nomad PIT and contribution exemptions. If PIT exemption fails, ordinary PIT reaches 15% plus municipal surtax.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registering a Montenegro business or undertaking local entrepreneurial activity can trigger entrepreneurial PIT, SSC, VAT and compliance rules and may undermine the foreign-entity condition.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Official materials support the PIT and contribution exemptions. Exact one-time filing/card fees are not stated on the current route pages; contractor classification and treaty consequences require individual advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The application directly seeks temporary residence; no preliminary residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five uninterrupted years of qualifying temporary residence. The nomad permit covers at most four continuous years, so another qualifying basis is needed before expiry.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation requires ten years of legal continuous residence. PR normally being available after year five implies about five additional years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory eligibility period for ordinary admission, excluding processing time.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Statutory maximum decision period in Article 29, not a guaranteed practical time.

key_conditions.value: Preserve uninterrupted qualifying residence; for PR maintain regular means, accommodation, insurance, basic Montenegrin and tax compliance, with absences generally limited to ten months total or six continuous months during five years. Citizenship requires ten years’ legal continuous residence, adulthood, accommodation, permanent income, basic Montenegrin, acceptable criminal record, security clearance, settled taxes and generally release from prior citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: A six-month gap between nomad permits would undermine continuity, so conversion must occur before the four-year period expires.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Requires at least three years of marriage to a Montenegrin citizen and five years of legal continuous residence. The numeric field records the longer residence requirement.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count toward the three-year marriage requirement but does not remove the five-year legal-residence requirement.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The provision can also apply where a qualifying marriage ended through the citizen spouse’s death.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage does not confer citizenship automatically. The spouse must be an adult, have accommodation and permanent income, meet criminal-record and security conditions, and complete five years’ lawful continuous residence. Residence can be refused or cancelled for a marriage of convenience.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Expect evidence of a genuine shared relationship. False statements or a sham marriage create refusal, cancellation and legal risks.

birthright_citizenship.notes: No broad jus soli. Territorial citizenship is limited to a child born or found in Montenegro whose parents are unknown, of unknown citizenship, stateless, or where the child would otherwise remain stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Montenegro to two foreign migrant parents does not automatically become a citizen, except under anti-statelessness or unknown-parent rules.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A child may qualify for permanent residence where a parent has permanent residence, but that is not citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Montenegro with one Montenegrin-citizen parent acquires citizenship by origin. For birth abroad, acquisition can depend on registration and the child’s other-citizenship position.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Foreign-birth cases should be registered promptly and checked against detailed statutory conditions.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A child’s citizenship or permanent residence does not automatically naturalise a foreign parent. Family residence may be possible, but the reviewed family definition does not establish an unconditional parent-of-citizen route.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Seek written MIA confirmation of the appropriate family or humanitarian basis.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father receives no automatic citizenship from the child. If the other parent is Montenegrin and the child is a citizen, family facts may support residence, but ordinary or spousal naturalisation requirements remain.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No official source reviewed confirmed an automatic PR or citizenship shortcut solely from having a citizen child.

rank.notes: Real-time Passport Power Rank checked on 2026-08-15; positions can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free category, not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Category displayed on the research date.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 44 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations; eVisa destinations are separate.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 128. Its categories differ from Henley’s broader access score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in remote-work centres: 37.97% of residents aged 15 or older reported English knowledge. English should work in Podgorica, coastal tourism centres and international services, but formal filings and long-term integration require Montenegrin or assistance.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Self-reported ability to understand, speak, read and write, not a standardized proficiency score.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is practically useful in a meaningful minority community: 38,126 residents aged 15 or older reported Russian knowledge. Ukrainian proficiency was not separately measured in the language release, but another census release counted 3,049 residents holding only Ukrainian citizenship, including 1,003 in Budva and 941 in Bar. This supports some Ukrainian-community practicality on the coast, not nationwide Ukrainian-language service coverage.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian is not official and cannot replace Montenegrin for formal settlement. Ukrainian-citizenship counts demonstrate community presence, not proficiency among the wider population.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the June 2026 gross monthly average of EUR 1,237 at about USD 1.139 per EUR.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: MONSTAT publishes arithmetic means only. Its published series uses aggregate paid-wage mass and employee count, so a national median cannot be calculated.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the EUR 600 statutory net minimum. The EUR 800 minimum for qualification level VI or higher is about USD 911.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate gross-average conversion; the EUR 1,036 net average is about USD 1,180.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The release, wages page and metadata publish arithmetic means, not a national median. No employee-level distribution is released from which a USD median could be derived.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: MONSTAT does not publish a national employee-level maximum. Industry amounts are sector averages, not maximum salaries, and individual data are confidential.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 600 net monthly for positions up to qualification level V; EUR 800 net for positions requiring level VI or higher
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wages, not observed minimum earnings.

average_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 1,237 gross and EUR 1,036 net monthly
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official national average earnings for June 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No EUR median is published in MONSTAT’s June release, wages page or metadata. The sources disseminate arithmetic averages; individual data needed for a median are confidential.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national employee-level maximum is published. Sector figures are averages and cannot be relabeled as maximum salaries; individual records are confidential.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official monthly earnings paid to employees in enterprises, organisations and institutions with 10 or more employees; minimum fields use statutory net minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: June 2026 average earnings; statutory minimum current for 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are resident-employee wages, not immigration thresholds. Entrepreneurs and independent professions are excluded from MONSTAT’s wage population. The series supplies arithmetic gross and net averages, not a national median or employee-level maximum.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The official investment guide describes Montenegro as relatively low-cost but supplies no quantified household budget, so no precise figure is provided.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The nomad permit is limited to four continuous years. Convert to another qualifying temporary-residence basis before expiry and obtain Ministry confirmation that continuity will be preserved.
settlement_track.summary: Current 2026 law supports counting nomad temporary residence toward the general five-year PR period. Because the permit ends after 2+2 years, settlement depends on a timely switch to another qualifying residence basis; ordinary citizenship eligibility is generally reached after ten years of continuous legal residence.
settlement_track.notes: The conclusion is based on Article 86 covering granted temporary residence and not excluding nomad time. No automatic successor status is reserved, so the conversion basis must independently qualify.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route expressly covers electronic work for a foreign company or the applicant’s own company not registered in Montenegro. It requires neither a local employer nor local client.

data.notes: The remote-work fit, active filing route and statutory counting of temporary residence are well supported. Confidence remains medium because the nomad permit cannot cover the full five-year PR period, no automatic successor status is guaranteed, current official pages do not state every one-time filing/card fee, and the conversion plan should receive filing-level confirmation. The 2026 contribution law resolves the prior uncertainty over covered nomad social contributions by expressly granting an exemption.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Temporary residence and work as a registered entrepreneur or owner-director, followed by permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: After nomad residence, a qualifying entrepreneur or owner-director work/residence permit can continue residence toward PR. A switch is needed before the four-year nomad maximum because PR normally requires five continuous years.
requirements: Establish and operate a genuine registered business and obtain the appropriate residence/work permit.
For relevant non-EU entrepreneurs and majority owner-directors, renewals require at least EUR 5,000 in annual paid taxes/contributions under Article 70.
Preserve residence continuity and meet PR resources, insurance, housing, language and compliance conditions.
reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad Temporary Residence Permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The 2026 government-hosted consolidated law was inspected: Article 86 uses temporary-residence time and does not exclude digital nomads; Article 70 supplies the entrepreneur successor and its renewal condition. Counting prior nomad residence is a statutory inference, not an automatic conversion guarantee. Confirm the change-of-basis filing sequence; no universal no-exit promise is made.

data.selection_summary: Morocco has no confirmed digital-nomad visa or ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route. Its visitor registration card requires sufficient resources and a commitment not to perform professional activity requiring authorization, while professional registration requires prior authorization for the work or business activity. Although a general residence card may be requested after four continuous lawful years and ordinary naturalization starts after five years, the applicant still lacks a qualifying initial status for foreign-contract remote work.

visa_application.title: Access Maroc eVisa portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official visitor eVisa application portal. It is not an application channel for remote-work authorization or a residence card; residence-card applications are handled by the competent Moroccan security services.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Law 02-03 requires sufficient means of subsistence but does not publish a fixed monthly threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed MAD amount is stated in the reviewed law.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient own resources; no fixed amount published
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a discretionary resources test, not a digital-nomad income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed law and government stay guide do not specify a uniform number of bank-statement months.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid entry and application for a registration card when staying beyond the permitted short stay.
Evidence of sufficient means of subsistence.
Commitment not to exercise in Morocco a professional activity subject to authorization.
Accommodation/address and identity documentation are handled at filing level by the competent security service; a complete current national checklist was not published in the reviewed sources.

initial_validity.value: 1 to 10 years
initial_validity.notes: The statutory registration-card range depends on the accepted basis and administrative decision; it is not a guaranteed ten-year grant.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is possible while the approved basis and statutory conditions continue.
extension_rules.notes: No visitor-specific online renewal channel or uniform renewal-document checklist was confirmed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The registration card is a temporary lawful-residence document.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not itself authorize ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A general residence card may be requested after at least four years of continuous lawful residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Grant is not automatic, and this rule does not cure work performed without the required authorization.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after at least five years of habitual and regular residence, subject to additional statutory conditions and discretion.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No source confirms that unauthorised remote work can form the lawful qualifying residence history.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the visitor card is based on own resources and a non-professional-activity undertaking, not permission to work remotely for a foreign employer or client.

rejected_routes.route_name: Professional registration card for authorized work or activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general income threshold is published; requirements depend on the underlying employment, commercial, professional or other authorization.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No uniform minimum applies across the different underlying authorized activities.

income_requirement_display.value: No uniform threshold; underlying activity authorization controls
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Not applicable as a general threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: No general income floor applies to this category. Labour Code article 516 governs an employer recruiting a foreign employee and requires government authorization as a visa on that employment contract; the current TAECHIR guidance is employer-led and requires employer records and, in the normal case, an ANAPEC certificate on the absence of Moroccan candidates. A contract only with an overseas client or employer is therefore not the Moroccan employer-filed contract described by these sources and does not establish eligibility.

income_proof_months.notes: The applicable materials prescribe authorization and activity-specific documents, not a uniform number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Prior authorization to exercise the relevant professional activity in Morocco.
For ordinary salaried work, appropriate Moroccan employment/work authorization is required rather than merely a foreign remote-work contract.
An independently operated local business or regulated profession requires its own registration and authorization; no ordinary foreign-client freelancer residence category was found.

initial_validity.value: 1 to 10 years for a registration card, subject to the underlying authorization
initial_validity.notes: Actual validity is discretionary and tied to the approved activity.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continuation of the authorized activity and residence conditions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Professional registration card after the required underlying authorization is accepted.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A residence card may be requested under the general four-year continuous-lawful-residence rule.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is not direct permanent residence and remains discretionary.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through general naturalization after five years of habitual and regular lawful residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make the route suitable for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because no official source confirms that an ordinary foreign software contract, without a Moroccan employer or separately authorized local business activity, qualifies for this card. Employer-sponsored work and local-business routes fall outside the selection profile.

rejected_routes.route_name: Short-stay, long-validity or electronic visitor visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Means of support may be checked, but no remote-worker threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The general visitor-visa materials do not publish a fixed MAD threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Visitor means-of-support test; no fixed amount published
income_requirement_display.notes: The reviewed visa materials require or permit scrutiny of means of support but do not state a uniform numerical amount or create a remote-worker income test.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed general visa materials do not prescribe a uniform bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport, applicable visa, stated visit purpose, means of stay and repatriation guarantees.
Short stays are normally limited to 90 days; a long-validity visa can be valid for multiple entries but each stay remains limited to 90 days.
A visa type cannot ordinarily be changed after entering Morocco; a new visa must be requested from the country of residence.

initial_validity.value: Short-stay visa: up to 90 days; long-validity visa: validity up to one year, with each stay up to 90 days
initial_validity.notes: The eVisa is also a visitor entry permission, not residence.

extension_rules.value: No remote-work extension route; a person intending to stay beyond three months must pursue an eligible registration-card basis.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None directly; a separate qualifying registration-card application is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor status itself is not permanent residence and no visitor-to-remote-worker conversion is provided by the reviewed sources.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor status is not a confirmed citizenship-track residence status.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor entry, including the eVisa, is not an independent remote-work residence route.

summary.value: A foreign student admitted to a Moroccan educational institution can use a student registration-card basis without a local employer. A foreign university degree or software qualification alone creates no independent skilled residence route; the student route is study-based, temporary and not a match for continuing ordinary foreign-contract work.
summary.notes: The general four-year residence-card and five-year naturalization rules may become relevant only if the person maintains lawful qualifying residence and satisfies all other conditions. No official source reviewed confirms that study residence authorizes unrestricted foreign remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence is determined, in order, by permanent home, centre of economic interests, or presence exceeding 183 days during any 365-day period.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A permanent home or centre of economic interests can establish residence before day 184; an applicable tax treaty may provide tie-breaker rules.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate under the progressive individual income-tax scale, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share shown for standard CNSS employment: 4.48% social allocation plus 2.26% mandatory medical care. Employer charges are separate. This is not a confirmed contribution rate for a nonexistent digital-nomad route or every self-employed category.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment applies to the requested ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker scenario because no such immigration category exists and self-employed CNSS treatment depends on registration and occupational category.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or general foreign-remote-worker tax regime was found. A 20% regime can apply to eligible employees of Casablanca Finance City-status companies, but it requires employment by a qualifying local-status company and does not fit this profile.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The foreign-pension relief and sector-specific regimes are likewise not ordinary remote-worker regimes.

taxes.caveats: Immigration permission and tax liability are separate. A person can become Moroccan tax-resident without having a lawful remote-work immigration basis. Contract classification, income sourcing, permanent-establishment risk, VAT, CNSS status and treaty relief—including under Morocco's treaties with Ukraine and Russia—require case-specific advice.

taxation_system.value: Moroccan tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income under a progressive individual income-tax scale; non-residents are taxed on Moroccan-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, then centre of economic interests, then more than 183 days in any 365-day period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Moroccan-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No general digital-nomad regime. The 20% Casablanca Finance City employee regime is employer/status-specific and unsuitable here.
taxation_system.social_security: Standard employees contribute 4.48% for social allocation and 2.26% for mandatory medical care; corresponding employer portions are 8.98% and 4.11%, plus 6.40% family allocation and 1.60% professional training. Treaty exemptions may apply to qualifying foreign assignees.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 37% is the top marginal rate. Annual taxable income up to MAD 40,000 is exempt; intermediate bands are taxed at 10%, 20%, 30% and 34%.

tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses about MAD 9.34 per USD from July 2026 market data.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
USD figure approximates the upper threshold.
Top marginal rate, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: PwC's Morocco pages were reviewed on 30 April 2026 and cross-checked against the Ministry of Finance tax overview. The Ministry overview is authoritative but does not expose every filing-level detail in searchable text.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Morocco has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence category. If the person nevertheless becomes tax-resident, ordinary worldwide-income and progressive-rate rules can apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary employment or professional-income classification would depend on the facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–37% progressive; 37% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, centre of economic interests, or presence exceeding 183 days in any 365-day period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-source income of a Moroccan tax resident is generally taxable in Morocco, subject to treaty relief and available foreign tax credits.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found for ordinary remote workers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No route-specific fixed contribution exists. Standard employee CNSS contributions total 6.74% for the employee under the cited rates, but classification of a foreign-employer worker or locally registered self-employed person requires advice.

fixed_payments.status: No universal remote-worker fixed payment applies
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The amount depends on whether the person is treated as an employee, self-employed professional, foreign assignee or otherwise insured; no ordinary nomad category exists.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Visitor visa and residence-card fees may apply, but the reviewed official materials do not publish a uniform current residence-card fee for this fact pattern.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Potential professional tax, VAT and registration obligations depend on local business activity. Standard VAT is 20%, but no fixed monthly freelancer payment applies uniformly across legal forms and activity categories.
fixed_payments.notes: Uniform numerical amounts are inapplicable because Morocco has no qualifying remote-worker route and business/social-protection charges vary by legal form and activity classification.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying fewer than 184 days does not by itself prevent Moroccan tax residence if the permanent-home or centre-of-economic-interests tests are met. Non-residents remain potentially taxable on Moroccan-source income.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident is generally taxed on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 37%. Employment income from a non-resident entity generally requires an individual return by 28 February of the following year.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Professional income is generally taxable on net trading income. Business registration, professional tax, VAT and social-protection obligations depend on the chosen legal form and activity; registering a business does not itself establish immigration eligibility.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax rules are current, but their application to the requested scenario remains hypothetical because no lawful digital-nomad or ordinary remote-worker immigration route was found.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: An eligible applicant can apply directly for a registration card; however, the requested foreign-remote-work basis is not an eligible category confirmed by the law.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: After at least four continuous lawful years, a general residence card may be requested. The decision is not automatic.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on at least five years of habitual and regular residence, not a separately stated number of years after obtaining the residence card. It could overlap with the four-year residence-card timeline.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum residence before a discretionary naturalization application; it is not a guaranteed citizenship date and does not validate the requested remote-work activity.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Nationality Code and official stay guide do not publish a typical or guaranteed processing duration for ordinary discretionary naturalization.

key_conditions.value: Adult status, at least five years of habitual and regular residence immediately before filing and continued residence until decision, good conduct, absence of disqualifying convictions, sufficient knowledge of Arabic, sufficient means of existence and satisfaction of the other Nationality Code conditions. Naturalization is discretionary and granted by decree; no general renunciation requirement was identified in the reviewed code.
key_conditions.notes: Physical-presence/absence tolerances and filing-level evidentiary standards were not quantified in the reviewed official sources.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The special declaration route applies to a foreign woman married to a Moroccan man after at least five years of habitual and regular joint residence in Morocco. It is not a gender-neutral shortcut.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support family residence. For nationality, the express marriage declaration in the reviewed code benefits a foreign wife of a Moroccan husband after five years of qualifying joint residence in Morocco; time married abroad alone does not satisfy that condition. No equivalent special declaration route was confirmed for a foreign husband of a Moroccan woman.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A foreign husband may still pursue family residence and ordinary discretionary naturalization.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally documented and genuine. Family residence and nationality require civil-status records, lawful residence and administrative review. Fraudulent or sham marriages can lead to refusal, cancellation and legal consequences. Applicants should verify the continuing gender-specific wording before filing.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically confer Moroccan citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Moroccan nationality is principally acquired through a Moroccan mother or father. Birth in Morocco alone to two foreign parents is not broad automatic jus soli; limited birth-based declaration, double-birth and anti-statelessness provisions exist.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Morocco to two foreign migrant parents does not ordinarily become Moroccan automatically. Narrow provisions may apply for statelessness, foundlings or specified birth/declaration circumstances, so individual civil-status facts matter.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent residence of the parents alone is not a general birthright-citizenship condition.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Moroccan mother or Moroccan father is Moroccan by descent, subject to civil-registration and proof requirements.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Being the foreign parent of a Moroccan child can support a family-based residence-card claim under the foreigners law, subject to the statutory conditions. It does not automatically confer permanent residence or citizenship on the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent's own lawful residence and nationality requirements remain relevant.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child's mother is Moroccan, the child is Moroccan by descent and the foreign father may have a family-residence basis as the parent of a Moroccan child. The father does not automatically become Moroccan and no special husband-by-marriage nationality declaration equivalent to the foreign-wife provision was confirmed.

passport.index_name: Passport Index 2026 (Arton Capital); Henley July 2026 cross-check

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank. A separate July 2026 Henley update reported Morocco at rank 67, illustrating that methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's separately classified visa-free destinations. Henley's July 2026 score was 71 destinations without a prior visa, combining visa-free, visa-on-arrival and eTA access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index classification. The Henley universe and counting methodology differ.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-on-arrival component; its displayed data did not clearly separate eTA from visa on arrival in the extracted table.

passport.notes: Passport figures are index snapshots and can change immediately when destination policies change. For comparability, the separate-category fields use one index consistently; the July 2026 Henley cross-check reported rank 67 and a combined mobility score of 71.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate-to-low overall. The 2025 EF English Proficiency Index gave Morocco a score of 492 and global rank 68, with stronger results in major cities and IT than the national average. English can be workable in technology, tourism and major urban centres, but French and Arabic remain more dependable for administration, housing and local services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF uses a self-selected test-taking population and should be treated as a practical indicator rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or broadly used administrative languages. No reliable national proficiency statistics were found; relying on either language alone would be impractical outside limited expatriate or tourism contexts.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The conclusion is a cautious inference from the official-language framework; no current nationwide Russian/Ukrainian proficiency dataset was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of MAD 10,100. This is the announced average net public-sector salary for early 2026, not a national all-worker average.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current HCP labour publications do not report a national median individual employee wage. Household-income measures and the older World Bank labour-market analysis are not interchangeable with a current employee-wage median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the statutory non-agricultural minimum wage: MAD 17.92/hour × 191 hours, converted near MAD 9.34/USD. It is a statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Public-sector-only net average; the reviewed sources do not publish a directly comparable national all-worker average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official labour releases do not publish a national individual employee-wage median that can be reliably converted to USD.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed national statistical and government salary sources do not publish a meaningful economy-wide maximum employee wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory non-agricultural minimum effective 1 January 2026; actual monthly pay varies with legally counted hours.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Government-announced early-2026 public-sector average, not an economy-wide employee average.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The value remains null because the current HCP 2025 annual and quarterly labour-market publications report employment counts, employment status, salaried shares, unemployment and underemployment, but do not publish a national median of individual employee wages in MAD. HCP's 2022/23 living-standards series measures household income and consumption rather than employee wages, while the World Bank labour report uses 2019 survey data chiefly for workforce composition and does not supply a current national wage median; none is interchangeable with the requested statistic.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed national sources do not publish an economy-wide upper wage bound; individual wages are not subject to a meaningful national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory private non-agricultural minimum wage and announced average net public-sector salary
average_citizen_salary.notes: The reviewed sources do not provide one clean, current and directly comparable national series for average and median employee wages. HCP's 2025 labour releases publish workforce and employment-status indicators but no national earnings median; its 2022/23 living-standards survey reports per-person household income, which includes non-wage income and is not salary. The public-sector average and statutory private non-agricultural minimum are retained with their distinct bases.

cost_of_living_note.value: HCP's 2022/23 household living-standard survey reported average consumption expenditure of MAD 20,658 per person per year, about MAD 1,722 per month. This is a national survey consumption benchmark, not a current single-person urban budget; rent and city-level costs can differ substantially.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official sources do not provide a current city-by-city cost-of-living index, so the older national survey benchmark is retained with a clear limitation.
