average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2018 Labour Force Survey mean of N$7,935 using the Bank of Namibia’s May 2026 average of about N$16.48/USD. The wage observation is old and should not be treated as a current 2026 mean.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2016 median gross monthly wage of N$2,600. No newer exact national median was established; the 2023 census publishes income bands rather than a clean national median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Illustrative monthly equivalent of the general N$18/hour statutory minimum using 195 ordinary hours per month, converted at about N$16.48/USD. It is not an observed minimum salary. Domestic, agricultural and security workers have phased 2026 rates.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official 2018 paid-employee gross mean converted approximately; dated.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official 2016 paid-employee gross median converted approximately; substantially dated.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum wage is published; the available open-ended upper income band is not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: N$18/hour general statutory minimum; 2026 exceptions: domestic N$15/hour, agricultural N$14/hour, security N$16/hour
min_salary_local_currency.notes: General minimum effective since 1 January 2025, with sector phase-ins through 2027.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Gross mean for paid employees in the 2018 Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Gross median for paid employees in the 2016 Labour Force Survey; no newer exact national median was confirmed.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The official survey and census sources checked do not publish a finite national maximum wage.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly wages of paid employees; statutory hourly minimum for the minimum field
average_citizen_salary.period: 2018 mean, 2016 median, current statutory minimum checked 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: Current wage-level evidence remains incomplete. The 2023 census confirms a broad distribution and reports that fewer than 3% earned over N$40,000 monthly, but it does not provide a directly usable mean or exact median. Old survey figures are retained with explicit dates rather than presented as current.

cost_of_living_note.value: The latest published official household-expenditure benchmark located is the 2015/16 NHIES average annual consumption of N$28,434 per person, equivalent to about N$2,370 per person per month in 2015/16 prices. National household consumption averaged N$119,065 annually. These are historical consumption measures, not a current 2026 expatriate or single-person budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The 2015/16 NHIES reports actual household consumption and shows food and beverages at 36% and housing at 32% of national consumption; urban households allocated about 35% to housing. The 2025/26 NHIES completed data collection on 22 April 2026 and entered processing, validation and statistical analysis, but no final 2025/26 expenditure benchmark was published in the NSA sources inspected by 15 August 2026. The July 2026 CPI release is suitable for measuring price change, not the cash amount needed for a household budget, so the dated expenditure figure was not mechanically inflated into a purported current living-cost estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The strong track applies only to the independently filed direct PR route. The Digital Nomad Visa is temporary-only, non-renewable, cannot change condition and does not count toward naturalisation.
settlement_track.summary: The qualification/sufficient-means route directly grants permanent residence and can support naturalisation after ten years of qualifying ordinary residence, so its legal settlement track is strong. It remains only a partial profile match because approval is highly discretionary and ordinary foreign-contract remote work is not expressly accepted under the PR criteria.
settlement_track.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary. Do not confuse the direct PR route with the separate six-month Digital Nomad Visa.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The DNV expressly fits foreign-contract remote work but is temporary-only. The direct PR route supplies the citizenship track but does not expressly confirm that an applicant continuing exclusively foreign-client work satisfies its occupational and local-labour criteria.

data.notes: Focused re-audit preserved the partial selection based on the independent direct-PR route. The social-contribution note now distinguishes compulsory covered employment, voluntary sole-self-employed registration, both contribution shares, current floors and caps, and unresolved DNV classification. The cost-of-living note now supplies the latest published official consumption benchmark while explaining why it cannot be presented as a current 2026 budget.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Discretionary permanent residence under Immigration Control Act section 26
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A separate section 26 permanent-residence application is legally available based on means or qualifications and the Immigration Selection Board assessment. A digital-nomad visa does not need to accumulate a PR residence period.
requirements: Satisfy means or professional-qualification requirements, character, assimilation and welfare criteria, plus the occupational-saturation test.
Obtain a separate PR decision; do not treat the six-month nomad visa as permission for indefinite residence.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: NIPDB prohibits changes of condition on the nomad visa, while section 26(6) generally permits PR applications by persons already lawfully admitted. Their application together to this visa is not clarified, so exit requirements and approval for foreign-only remote work remain uncertain. Zero years denotes no statutory residence waiting period, not guaranteed approval.

data.selection_summary: Nauru has no dedicated digital-nomad visa or confirmed residence-to-citizenship route for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. A Business Visa (General) may authorize independently conducting a business, profession, or non-employee consultancy for up to 12 months and may be renewed, but current law does not expressly confirm routine offshore remote employment and provides no conversion to the family-only Residence Visa, permanent residence, or citizenship. Local-business and public-service visas require a Nauruan employer, public body, or government consultancy; the 30-year Long Term Stay Visa requires a state-to-state arrangement; investment citizenship is excluded.

visa_application.title: Immigration Division — visa classes and application forms
visa_application.notes: The official page provides downloadable forms, including the Business Visa form, but no functioning direct online application portal was confirmed. The consolidated regulations refer to an old online-application URL that could not be verified as operational; contact the Immigration Division before paying or filing.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Neither the current Immigration Division fee page nor the consolidated regulations prescribe a minimum monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Neither source prescribes an AUD income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; AUD 6,000 visa fee plus AUD 50 processing fee
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: AUD 6,000 for a multiple-entry Business Visa (General), plus AUD 50 processing
income_requirement_display.notes: The AUD 6,000 amount is a visa fee, not an income requirement. No reliable application-date USD conversion was established.

income_proof_months.notes: The prescribed form does not specify an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: State the proposed business, profession, or consultancy activity and provide a proposed residential address in Nauru.

Provide a passport copy and photograph; a multiple-entry application also requires police clearance covering the applicant's recorded history in jurisdictions lived in during the preceding 12 months and a medical-fitness certificate.
Obtain a Nauruan business licence if the proposed activity falls within the licensed-business schedule.
Pay the applicable visa and processing fees before filing.

initial_validity.value: Multiple entry for up to 12 months
initial_validity.notes: The published fee table does not list a three-month single-entry option for the General subclass.

extension_rules.value: May be renewed
extension_rules.notes: No automatic renewal, maximum cumulative duration, or settlement entitlement is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The visa permits the holder to stay in Nauru while conducting the approved business or profession for up to 12 months, but it is a business visa rather than the statutory family Residence Visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is temporary lawful stay, not qualifying permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion is provided. The ordinary Residence Visa is restricted to dependants of Nauruan citizens.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Renewing a Business Visa does not create permanent residence under the reviewed legislation.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path exists for a foreign-born Business Visa holder under the current ordinary citizenship categories. Those categories cover descent, marriage, adoption, former citizens, minors/dependants, and an application after 20 continuous years for a person born in Nauru to noncitizen parents.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The consolidated Naoero Citizenship Act, including amendments through 2024, and the Citizenship Division's current route list provide no naturalisation category based on Business Visa residence or years spent in Nauru by a foreign-born unrelated adult. Business Visa time therefore has no statutory citizenship route in the current sources.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest independently filed category because the regulations expressly cover conducting a profession and consultancy services otherwise than as an employee. It is rejected because the law does not expressly authorize ordinary employment for an offshore employer, no foreign-income criterion exists, and no settlement conversion is available.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The regulations do not specify a minimum salary.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The regulations do not specify an AUD salary threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Nauruan employer and employment contract required; no published salary threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer-dependent route rather than an income-history route.

income_proof_months.notes: The route requires a local employment contract, not evidence of prior monthly income.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment by a Nauruan citizen or wholly Nauruan-owned licensed business.
Employer must justify the foreign hire through a skills shortage, legally required qualification, or need to provide goods or services in Nauru.
Employment contract or accepted offer and employer letter showing that a Nauruan worker is not disadvantaged.

initial_validity.value: Up to 12 months, multiple entry
initial_validity.notes: The visa is tied to the named employer and approved work.

extension_rules.value: Renewable subject to continued qualifying local employment
extension_rules.notes: The visa is deemed cancelled when the employment ends or unauthorized work is undertaken.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Authorizes residence and work for the named Nauruan employer for the visa period.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Employer-linked temporary status only.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion or permanent-residence entitlement is provided.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The separate Residence Visa is for dependants of Nauruan citizens.

path_to_citizenship.value: Current citizenship legislation provides no employment-based naturalisation category for a foreign-born unrelated worker.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Years of locally sponsored employment are not listed as a citizenship basis.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local Nauruan employer and labor-market justification are mandatory; employment by a foreign business in Nauru is expressly ineligible.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The regulations prescribe no minimum remuneration.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The regulations prescribe no AUD remuneration threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Public-service employment or consultancy contract required; no published income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility derives from the public-service contract, not prior income.

income_proof_months.notes: The route requires a qualifying contract rather than an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment or consultancy contract with a Nauruan department, statutory authority, public enterprise, instrumentality, or qualifying government contractor.
Application must be submitted by the head of the public-service body.
Contract or terms letter, authenticated identity, medical examination, and police report.

initial_validity.value: At least the term of the public-service employment or consultancy contract
initial_validity.notes: The regulations use contract duration rather than a fixed maximum.

extension_rules.value: Dependent on the qualifying contract
extension_rules.notes: The visa may be cancelled following abandonment, termination, or resignation.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Permits remaining in Nauru for the approved public-service contract.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Contract-tied temporary status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion is provided.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The ordinary Residence Visa remains a dependant category.

path_to_citizenship.value: Current citizenship legislation provides no public-service-employment naturalisation category.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Contract duration is not listed as qualifying citizenship residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the public-service body, rather than the applicant, submits the application and a Nauruan public-sector employment or consultancy contract is compulsory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The regulations prescribe no applicant-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The regulations prescribe no applicant-income threshold in AUD.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; AUD 1,000 annual fee paid by the requesting state
income_requirement_display.notes: The fee is normally the responsibility of the requesting state.

income_proof_months.notes: Eligibility is based on an inter-state arrangement rather than personal income.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligibility under an arrangement between Nauru and another state.
Application submitted by an official of that state.
Authenticated identity, medical record, and criminal-history information.

initial_validity.value: Minimum 30 years
initial_validity.notes: Unlimited multiple entry is permitted, but the visa remains based on the inter-state arrangement.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary personal renewal process is published
extension_rules.notes: The category is controlled through the requesting state and can be cancelled in specified circumstances.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Allows long-term presence under the relevant state-to-state arrangement.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not open to ordinary self-applicants.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The regulations state no permanent-residence conversion or entitlement.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Long visa validity is not equivalent to statutory permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: The regulations and ordinary Citizenship Act state no citizenship connection for this visa.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No residence-counting rule links the visa to naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: Despite its unusually long duration, this is not a generally available long-stay or nomad route; an official of a state having an arrangement with Nauru must submit the application.

rejected_routes.route_name: Nauru Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is contribution/investment citizenship, not an income-qualified remote-worker route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Monthly income is not the eligibility basis.

income_requirement_display.value: Substantial program contribution required; excluded from profile
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: The temporary Iruwa Initiative reduced the main-applicant contribution from USD 115,000 to USD 90,000 only through 30 June 2026; that promotion had expired by the research date.
income_requirement_display.notes: Current contribution levels must be reconfirmed with the Program Office. Applications must be submitted through an authorized agent, so this is not direct self-filing.

income_proof_months.notes: The program requires financial information, contribution, and due diligence rather than a prescribed number of monthly income statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Application through an authorized agent, due diligence, qualifying contribution, supporting financial and medical information, police certificates, Cabinet approval, and oath or affirmation.

initial_validity.value: Direct citizenship if approved
initial_validity.notes: This is not a residence visa.

extension_rules.value: Not applicable
extension_rules.notes: Citizenship, rather than renewable immigration status, is granted if all approval conditions are completed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No temporary-residence stage is required by the program.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The program is structurally separate from the Business Visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No separate permanent-residence stage; the program concerns direct citizenship.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: It is not a residence-to-naturalisation route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Direct citizenship through the economic and climate-resilience program, subject to contribution, authorized-agent filing, due diligence, Cabinet approval, and completion of post-approval requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Excluded by the applicant profile because it is citizenship by contribution/investment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because substantial contribution programs are not ordinary foreign-contract remote-work routes and the application must be submitted through an authorized agent.

summary.value: Nauru lists a Business Visa (Education) for engaging in education, and the general Business Visa form can be filed by the applicant. No degree-based skilled residence program, post-study residence path, or education-to-permanent-residence conversion is provided in the reviewed immigration sources. It is therefore purpose-limited temporary permission, not qualification-based residence.
summary.notes: The current Immigration Division page does not separately publish comprehensive eligibility documentation or duration rules for the Education subclass.

tax_residency_rule.value: Nauru does not use a general 183-day rule for individuals. Under the Employment and Services Tax Act, resident individuals are principally Nauruan citizens without a permanent home abroad, resettled refugees or asylum seekers, and persons married to such resident Nauruan citizens; everyone else is nonresident. Business-tax residents are taxed on worldwide business income, while nonresidents are taxed on Nauru-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A foreign Business Visa holder does not become a domestic-law tax resident merely by spending 183 days in Nauru. Nevertheless, services physically performed in Nauru are Nauru-source wherever payment is made.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for an ordinary nonresident independent service provider: 20% services tax on gross Nauru-source service fees. This is a flat final withholding rate, not an expected effective rate after deductions.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 5% figure is the member contribution for eligible resident employees. Sections 5, 22, and 23 of the Nauru Superannuation Act define a resident for this scheme as a Nauruan citizen residing permanently in Nauru, restrict mandatory membership to resident employees aged 18 or over under a contract of service, and expressly exempt a nonresident individual employed in Nauru from mandatory contributions. Finance reports a 10% employer rate from 1 February 2026. An unrelated foreign Business Visa holder and an independent contractor therefore have no mandatory NSS contribution under the reviewed law.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly nomad tax, social-security payment, or health-insurance payment applies under the reviewed sources. The modeled nonresident contractor is outside mandatory NSS; the material charges instead are non-monthly visa and possible business-registration/licensing fees denominated in AUD.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax exemption was identified. Nonresident independent service providers are generally taxed at 20% on Nauru-source gross service fees; services connected with a Nauru permanent establishment move into business-tax treatment. NRO also publishes a 2.5% small-business tax for qualifying nonresident individuals conducting business solely in Nauru with annual gross revenue not exceeding AUD 250,000.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Classification between services tax, small-business tax, and business-profits tax requires NRO advice before operating.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on whether the relationship is employment or independent services, whether services are physically performed in Nauru, whether a permanent establishment or local business is created, and any available foreign-tax credit. Offshore payment does not prevent Nauru-source taxation. Confirm current rates, registration and withholding mechanics, and treaty relief directly with the Nauru Revenue Office.

taxation_system.value: Mixed residence-and-source system: resident persons are within worldwide business-income taxation, while nonresidents are taxed on Nauru-source employment, services, or business income. The ordinary nonresident contractor screening rate is 20% on gross service fees.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No general day-count test; statutory status is based chiefly on Nauruan citizenship/permanent home, refugee status, or qualifying marriage. Other foreign individuals are nonresident.
taxation_system.income_scope: Services exercised or performed in Nauru are Nauru-source wherever paid. Residents are taxable on worldwide business income; nonresidents on Nauru-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Potential small-business tax is 2.5% of gross revenue for a qualifying nonresident individual conducting business solely in Nauru with annual gross revenue not exceeding AUD 250,000.
taxation_system.social_security: NSS mandatory membership is limited to resident employees aged 18 or over under a contract of service; for this Act, resident means a Nauruan citizen residing permanently in Nauru, with a posted-government-employee exception. A nonresident employee is expressly exempt, and an independent contractor is not an employee-member. Covered members contribute 5%; Finance reports a 10% employer rate from 1 February 2026.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The relevant nonresident services rate is flat. Resident employment and services income has a 0% monthly band through AUD 9,240 and 20% above it, but an ordinary unrelated foreign applicant normally remains nonresident under the statutory definition.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: From AUD 0 of Nauru-source service fees
tax_brackets.applies_to: Ordinary nonresident independent service provider not directly contracted to the Government of Nauru
tax_brackets.notes: Final tax on gross fees; no expense deduction under services tax.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident individual employment or services income
tax_brackets.notes: The resident category is narrowly defined and generally does not include an unrelated foreign Business Visa holder.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident individual employment or services income
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not the expected effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The statutory Superannuation Act resolves the previous coverage gap: nonresident employees are expressly exempt from mandatory NSS contributions, and an independent contractor is outside employee membership. NRO also confirms worldwide business-income taxation for residents from 2021, while nonresidents remain source-taxed.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Nauru has no dedicated nomad tax category. If Immigration approves a foreign contractor under Business Visa (General), services physically performed in Nauru are Nauru-source and an ordinary nonresident independent service provider is screened at 20% services tax on gross fees, even when paid offshore.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad regime; general nonresident independent-services or business taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 20% flat screening rate on gross Nauru-source service fees for an ordinary nonresident independent contractor
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: An unrelated foreigner does not become tax resident merely through a day count; statutory resident categories are narrow. Source taxation still applies to work performed in Nauru.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: For a nonresident, genuinely foreign-source income is outside Nauru tax, but service fees become Nauru-source when the services are exercised or performed in Nauru, wherever paid. Resident persons' foreign business income is taxable with foreign-tax-credit rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax regime is listed in the current NRO legislation, forms, or guidance sources.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No mandatory NSS contribution applies to the modeled unrelated foreign remote worker: the Superannuation Act limits eligible mandatory members to resident employees, defines scheme residence by Nauruan citizenship and permanent residence, and expressly exempts nonresident employees. An independent contractor also is not an employee under a contract of service. If the facts instead create covered resident employment, the published rates are 5% employee and 10% employer from 1 February 2026; EST withholding can still apply independently of NSS.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed monthly nomad payment applies under the reviewed sources
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: AUD 0 mandatory NSS for the modeled nonresident independent contractor. Covered resident employees instead contribute 5% of superannuable salary and their employers 10% from 1 February 2026.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Business Visa (General): AUD 6,000 for multiple entry up to 12 months, plus AUD 50 processing. The regulations permit renewal but do not publish an automatic renewal entitlement or discounted renewal fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: If the activity is operated as a Nauru sole-trader business, the Justice Division publishes AUD 200 for business-name registration and AUD 300 for a business licence, with an extra AUD 300 for each additional business nature or district. These are registration/licensing charges, not monthly tax; whether an offshore-contract activity must register should be confirmed before filing.
fixed_payments.notes: The substantial visa fee and possible business charges do not create a settlement right.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay does not itself create tax residence, but services performed from Nauru may still be Nauru-source and taxable. Visitor status does not expressly authorize remote work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: An unrelated foreign worker ordinarily remains nonresident under the domestic definition. If a person falls within a resident category, worldwide business income can enter Nauru's tax base.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect possible Business Visa, business-name registration, business licence, TIN, and tax-classification requirements. Services tax is generally 20% of gross Nauru-source fees unless permanent-establishment, small-business, or other business-tax rules apply.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Superannuation treatment is established for the modeled facts, but Immigration still has not expressly confirmed that routine offshore remote work qualifies for Business Visa (General). Obtain written immigration and NRO classification before relying on the scenario.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Business Visa (General) provides temporary lawful stay upon grant for up to 12 months; this is not qualifying residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The Immigration Act and regulations provide no Business-Visa-to-permanent-residence conversion or general permanent-residence entitlement. The statutory Residence Visa is for dependants of Nauruan citizens.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The consolidated Citizenship Act and current Citizenship Division route list contain no general residence-plus-years naturalisation rule for a foreign-born unrelated applicant.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No citizenship timeline exists for the applicant's foreign-contract route because that route is not a statutory citizenship basis.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the consolidated Act nor the Citizenship Division publishes a typical processing-time statistic for ordinary citizenship applications.

key_conditions.value: The ordinary family-related citizenship route relevant to an adult foreigner is discretionary citizenship after seven continuous years lawfully married to and residing in Nauru with a citizen. A Nauru-born child of two noncitizens may apply after 20 continuous years. Current sources provide no general foreign-born worker naturalisation route.
key_conditions.notes: Citizenship applications involve ministerial and Cabinet consideration; satisfying threshold conditions does not remove statutory discretion.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must be lawfully married and residing with the citizen spouse in Nauru continuously for seven years; Cabinet may waive this condition.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage does not eliminate the residence requirement. The seven-year period concerns continuous lawful marriage and co-residence with the Nauruan spouse in Nauru. A spouse may separately qualify for a Residence Visa as a dependant of a Nauruan citizen.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Residence-visa eligibility and citizenship remain separate processes.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship requires commitment to permanent residence, good health and character, no criminal convictions, means of support, police clearances, medical evidence, marriage proof, two citizen character references, and Cabinet approval. Fraud, misrepresentation, or concealment can lead to cancellation; marriage-based citizenship can also be affected by remarriage to a non-Nauruan after divorce or the citizen spouse's death.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Applicants should obtain local legal advice regarding the Act's deprivation provisions and demonstrate a genuine continuing marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Nauru alone is insufficient. Citizenship is automatic when at least one parent is a citizen. A person born in Nauru to two noncitizens may apply only after 20 continuous years of residence; stateless children have a discretionary Cabinet-application safeguard.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No citizenship is acquired at birth solely because the child is born in Nauru. The Nauru-born person may apply after 20 continuous years of residence; a child who would otherwise be stateless may be considered through the constitutional and Cabinet process.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Both alternatives are application-based or discretionary rather than broad automatic jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Nauru is a citizen when either parent is a citizen at birth. A child born outside Nauru is a citizen by descent when either parent is a citizen at birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence on a migrant father. A Residence Visa is available only if the father independently qualifies as a dependant of a Nauruan citizen; marriage to the citizen mother may provide that separate basis.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Current citizenship legislation provides no parent-of-citizen naturalisation shortcut.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status. If married to the Nauruan parent, the father can seek a dependant Residence Visa and may later apply for marriage-based citizenship after the statutory co-residence period. A citizen child alone is not an automatic route.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the live Nauru dashboard on 2026-08-15; passport indexes use different methodologies and may report different ranks.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category, not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required category on the live dashboard.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 40 visa-on-arrival destinations and 5 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: The same index displayed a mobility score of 86. Values are a live snapshot and can change when destination policies change.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is an official language and is used for government and commercial purposes, making English-language administration workable. Remote-work practicality is nevertheless constrained by the absence of a dedicated visa and limited published infrastructure data.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The official HIES identifies both Nauruan and English as official languages.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. The reviewed official sources provide no evidence of routine Russian- or Ukrainian-language government, business, or community services; applicants should expect to operate in English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from official-language evidence, not a measured language-proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current HIES publishes household and per-capita income aggregates, not a mean wage per employed person. Combining it with the 2021 worker count would mix periods and produce a misleading figure.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2021 census and 2024–2025 HIES do not publish a national median individual wage, so no USD median can be calculated responsibly.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The available amount is the bottom of an official public-service pay scale, not a national minimum wage. No reliable research-date AUD/USD conversion was captured.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The HIES publishes household employment-income aggregates rather than an official mean individual salary, so no USD worker average can be derived.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The 2024–2025 HIES and 2021 census do not publish a national median individual salary, so no USD median can be derived without inventing a statistic.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official public-service scale has an upper band, not a national maximum salary, and no reliable research-date USD conversion was established.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Lowest point in the public-service salary scale effective 1 July 2022; not a statutory national minimum wage or observed economy-wide minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The HIES reports average annual household employment income of AUD 39,227, not an average salary per worker, so it is not placed in this field.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither the HIES nor the census publishes a national individual median wage in AUD.

max_salary_local_currency.value: AUD 6,958.67/month (AUD 83,504/year)
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Highest point in the published 2022 public-service scale; not an economy-wide maximum salary. Later gazettes reference the same band framework but do not publish a complete replacement scale.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official public-service annual salary-band endpoints; national mean and median individual wages unavailable
average_citizen_salary.period: Public-service scale effective 2022; HIES fieldwork March 2024–March 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The endpoints are public-sector wage-band context only and must not be interpreted as national minimum, average, or maximum wages. The 2024–2025 HIES found average annual household employment income of AUD 39,227 and average total household income of AUD 69,828, but these are household aggregates.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2024–2025 HIES reports average annual household expenditure of AUD 64,192, approximately AUD 5,349 per household per month, including imputed rent and non-cash components. Nauru is import-dependent, particularly for food and fuel, so this is household-budget context rather than a single-person nomad budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The household figure is not directly comparable with an individual salary.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Business Visa (General) is renewable temporary permission to conduct an approved profession or consultancy. Current sources do not expressly confirm ordinary offshore remote employment and provide no conversion to residence, permanent residence, or citizenship.
settlement_track.summary: Nauru's Business Visa (General) may support temporary independent professional or consultancy activity, but it is not a confirmed foreign-remote-worker settlement route. The ordinary Residence Visa is for dependants of Nauruan citizens, and current consolidated citizenship law contains no Business-Visa or general foreign-born worker naturalisation category.
settlement_track.notes: Employer visas, the state-arrangement Long Term Stay Visa, investment citizenship, visitor status, and family residence do not make the applicant's ordinary foreign contract a qualifying citizenship track.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The General Business Visa expressly covers conducting a profession and non-employee consultancy, but neither the current official page nor regulations expressly states that routine remote work for an offshore employer or client qualifies. Even if Immigration approves it, the visa has no settlement path under the reviewed law.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against 30 distinct directly relevant URLs, including seven URLs outside the previous source set. The key resolution is statutory: mandatory Nauru Superannuation Scheme coverage does not apply to the modeled nonresident independent remote contractor because membership is limited to resident employees and nonresident employees are expressly exempt. The Business Visa has no citizenship route under the current consolidated citizenship categories. Remaining nulls identify specific unpublished or inapplicable figures rather than estimates.

data.selection_summary: Nepal has no current digital-nomad, remote-worker, or ordinary foreign-contract freelance residence route. Official immigration material says only Working Visa holders may work, and that visa requires a Nepal-side appointment or contract, labour permit, government recommendation, and hiring-organisation tax documents. Tourist and relationship visas do not authorize work; the independent residential category is limited to retirees aged 60+ living without business activity, while business and investor routes require investment or a Nepal business. An ordinary software engineer continuing a foreign contract therefore has no qualifying residence-to-citizenship route.

visa_application.title: Nepali Port Online Services
visa_application.notes: This is the Department of Immigration's official general online application portal for ETA and listed visa services. It does not offer a digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category.

rejected_routes.route_name: Working Visa / Non-Tourist Visa for Foreign Workers

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed official immigration pages publish no minimum salary threshold; eligibility instead depends on authorized Nepal-side work.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official route requirements prescribe no immigration income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; Nepal-side appointment, labour permit, and government recommendation required
income_requirement_display.notes: A foreign-client contract performed independently does not replace the Nepal-side work-authorization requirements.

income_proof_months.notes: The requirements list appointment, contract, and tax documents but prescribe no fixed number of income-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: Recommendation from the relevant Nepal government line agency.
Work or labour permit and Ministry of Home Affairs work agreement.
Appointment or contract with the Nepal-side organization and tax-clearance documents for the organization and applicant.
For industrial expatriates, evidence that appropriate skilled labour was unavailable locally, including a vacancy notice and industry agreement.

initial_validity.value: Generally one year at a time for industrial expatriates
initial_validity.notes: The Department of Industry says the related work permit may continue for up to five years through annual renewal; other Working Visa cases depend on the recommendation and work authorization.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires continuing recommendation, work authorization, contract, and applicable tax-clearance documentation; industrial expatriate work permits may be renewed annually for up to five years.
extension_rules.notes: This creates no permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved Working Visa permits temporary stay and authorized local work.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is employer or institution dependent and does not fit independent foreign-contract work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed official immigration material provides no general conversion from a Working Visa to permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Nepal's separately named Residential Visa is category-specific and annually renewable; it is not presented as a work-visa conversion or general permanent-residence status.

path_to_citizenship.value: The reviewed law establishes no ordinary work-visa citizenship track. The Citizenship Act's 15-year naturalization provision is discretionary and additionally requires exceptional contribution, business in Nepal, language ability, reciprocity, good character, and relinquishment of other citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not an entitlement arising from continuous Working Visa residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Nepal-side employer or institution, labour authorization, and government recommendations are required. The applicant's ordinary foreign software contract does not qualify.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official requirement is at least USD 20,000 in regular annual income, equivalent to approximately USD 1,666.67 per month, plus a separate USD 20,000 bank statement.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 20,000 annual regular income plus USD 20,000 bank balance
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The government publishes this threshold in USD, not NPR.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 20,000/year regular income + USD 20,000 bank balance
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 20,000 annual income and USD 20,000 bank statement
income_requirement_display.notes: This category is for a person aged at least 60 or retired who intends to live in Nepal without carrying on business.

income_proof_months.notes: The official material requires a regular-income certificate and bank statement but specifies no fixed number of prior monthly statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Age 60 or older, or proof of retirement, and intention to live in Nepal without carrying on business.
USD 20,000 bank statement and certificate of at least USD 20,000 regular annual income.
Character certificate, embassy no-objection letter, health certificate, passport, and current Nepal visa.
Renewal requires evidence of USD 20,000 expenditure.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: Official fee information lists USD 700 for the first year.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually; official renewal fee USD 1,200 and an expenditure statement are required.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains category-dependent and is not permanent residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Residential Visa authorizes renewable residence for the qualifying retiree/non-business category.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not authorize the applicant's continuing business or professional activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed rules establish no automatic permanent-residence conversion or permanent status; the visa is renewed annually.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The name 'Residential Visa' should not be interpreted as permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: The reviewed law establishes no ordinary citizenship pathway from this visa.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act's 15-year exceptional-naturalization provision is discretionary and requires business in Nepal and exceptional contribution, which conflicts with treating this retiree route as a routine settlement track.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this software-engineer profile involves ongoing professional work, while the category is for applicants aged 60+ or retired who live without carrying on business.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Eligibility is investment- and business-based rather than based on monthly remote income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Investor Residential Visa: more than USD 100,000 one-time investment stated by the Department of Industry
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The Department of Immigration's consolidated page states a minimum USD 100,000 investment. Filing-level confirmation is advisable because older investment publications contained higher figures.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly income threshold; requires Nepal business/foreign investment, with at least USD 100,000 stated for investor residential status
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: More than USD 100,000 one-time convertible-currency investment for the investor residential category
income_requirement_display.notes: Business Visa fees vary with investment amount, but fee bands are not eligibility substitutes.

income_proof_months.notes: Investment evidence and company records are required; a fixed income-history period is inapplicable.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign-investment approval and recommendation from the Department of Industry or other competent line agency.
Nepal company and industry registration, PAN/VAT, investment or share evidence, and tax clearance for renewal.
Business performance, employment generation, tax paid, and investment level may affect the recommended visa period.

initial_validity.value: Business Visa: one month to one year or up to five years; investor Residential Visa: one year at a time
initial_validity.notes: Duration depends on the route, investment, and agency recommendation.

extension_rules.value: Business Visa renewal requires continued investment/business documentation, progress information, recommendation, and tax clearance; investor Residential Visa is renewed annually.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic permanent status is created.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved investor or business applicant can obtain a renewable visa tied to the Nepal investment or enterprise.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a substantive entrepreneur/investor route, not ordinary remote work for a foreign client.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed material establishes no direct permanent-residence entitlement or ordinary conversion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The investor Residential Visa is stated to be granted one year at a time.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization after at least 15 years may only be considered under the Citizenship Act's discretionary exceptional-contribution conditions; it is not an investor entitlement.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The law also requires business in Nepal, language ability, reciprocity, good character, and relinquishment of other citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a Nepal enterprise and substantial investment. Merely serving a foreign software client does not satisfy this route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist Visa / ETA used for remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Tourist eligibility is not based on remote income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-work income threshold applies to visitor status.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; tourist status does not authorize work
income_requirement_display.notes: The official immigration warning says foreigners on tourist or relationship visas may not work for an industry, business, or institution, whether paid or unpaid.

income_proof_months.notes: Income-history proof is inapplicable to tourist eligibility.

key_requirements.requirement: Tourist visa or ETA requirements only; this status does not legalize employment, business, or professional work in Nepal.

initial_validity.value: Tourist visas are issued for 15, 30, or 90 days and may be extended up to 150 total days in a visa year.
initial_validity.notes: This is visitor permission, not qualifying residence.

extension_rules.value: Tourist extensions are limited to 150 total days per visa year.
extension_rules.notes: Extension does not convert the status into a work or residence route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Tourist presence remains visitor status and does not directly confer qualifying temporary residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not treated as direct temporary residence for settlement purposes.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed Immigration Act and Regulations provide no tourist-to-permanent-residence conversion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate qualifying visa would be required.

path_to_citizenship.value: None under the reviewed law. Tourist stay is visitor permission capped at 150 days per visa year, not a qualifying residence category; the Immigration Regulations prohibit work on tourist status and provide no tourist-to-residence or tourist-to-naturalization conversion. The Citizenship Act's 15-year clause belongs only to discretionary exceptional-contribution naturalization and does not make tourist time an ordinary citizenship track.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A tourist would first need a separate lawful visa/status. No reviewed current source establishes that tourist days accrue toward an ordinary naturalization entitlement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status neither authorizes the proposed work nor provides a qualifying settlement path.

summary.value: A foreign student admitted to a Nepal educational institution may obtain a Study Visa without a local employer. It requires an education-ministry recommendation, admission receipt, recent bank statement, and other documents; ordinary students may not work. The route is education-based temporary stay, and the reviewed sources establish no direct permanent-residence or ordinary citizenship conversion.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing university degree alone creates no residence eligibility. New enrollment would be required, and the route does not fit continuing foreign-contract work.

tax_residency_rule.value: A natural person is resident if the person's normal place of abode is in Nepal or the person is present in Nepal for 183 days or more during a continuous 365-day period; specified Nepal-government foreign postings are also covered.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Visa status and tax residence are separate tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the FY 2026/27 top marginal screening rate for resident natural persons under the Finance Bill schedule, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The first resident remuneration band is described as a 1% social-security tax. It does not apply identically to qualifying sole-proprietor or pension income or to employment income where the taxpayer contributes to the Social Security Fund. Broader employer/employee SSF obligations are structure-dependent.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment applies to a foreign remote worker. Nepal has no matching digital-nomad status; the reviewed tax and Social Security Fund material instead describes transaction-based withholding, annual tax, or remuneration-linked contribution percentages.

special_tax_regimes.value: Nepal has no digital-nomad, expatriate, non-dom, or remittance-basis regime. Current tax material instead describes activity-specific treatment: a 5% withholding on qualifying foreign-currency receipts of a resident natural person not carrying on business for software/electronic or consultancy services supplied outside Nepal, and a 50% exemption of applicable tax for qualifying foreign-currency IT-service export income through FY 2084/85. These provisions depend on taxpayer and income classification and do not create immigration eligibility.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The 5% item is described in the current TDS schedule and grouped among final-withholding payments; the separate 50% IT-export concession reduces otherwise applicable tax. A Nepal tax adviser should confirm whether a foreign employee, independent consultant, or registered business satisfies the statutory category.

taxes.caveats: These tax rules are hypothetical for this profile because Nepal provides no matching immigration status. Classification of the contract as employment, consultancy, or business income, source rules, foreign tax credits, registration, treaty position, and Social Security Fund coverage can materially change liability.

taxation_system.value: Resident individuals are generally assessed progressively, with Nepal's Income Tax Act bringing resident income into the tax base regardless of source and allowing foreign-tax-credit mechanisms. FY 2026/27 resident remuneration rates run from 1% to a 29% top marginal rate.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Normal abode in Nepal or at least 183 days in a continuous 365-day period, subject to the statutory definitions.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally assessed on employment, business, and investment income regardless of source; non-residents are generally assessed on Nepal-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad, expatriate, non-dom, or remittance-basis regime was identified. Activity-specific rules may apply instead: current FY 2083/84 material lists 5% withholding on qualifying foreign-currency software/electronic or consultancy receipts of a resident natural person not operating a business, while qualifying foreign-currency IT-service export income may receive a 50% exemption of the applicable tax through FY 2084/85. Classification and filing treatment require case-specific confirmation and do not legalize immigration status.
taxation_system.social_security: A 1% social-security tax applies to the first remuneration band under the FY 2026/27 schedule, with stated exceptions; separate SSF contributions depend on employment and registration structure.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 29% is the top marginal screening rate, not the effective rate. FY 2026/27 unified resident remuneration bands are: first NPR 1,000,000 at 1%, next NPR 500,000 at 10%, next NPR 1,000,000 at 20%, next NPR 1,500,000 at 27%, and income above NPR 4,000,000 at 29%.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximately converted using the 2026-08-15 NRB USD buying rate of NPR 152.39. Described as social-security tax and subject to exceptions.
USD figure is the approximate cumulative upper threshold.

USD figure is the approximate cumulative upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident natural-person remuneration income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate under the FY 2026/27 Finance Bill schedule.

taxation_system.notes: The progressive 29% figure remains the general top marginal screening rate. The activity-specific 5% withholding/final-payment treatment and IT-export concession are narrower alternatives, not a universal foreign-income or nomad rate.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Nepal has no dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker visa. For tax purposes only, a qualifying resident natural person not carrying on business may face 5% final withholding on foreign-currency software/electronic or consultancy receipts; otherwise ordinary resident rules can apply up to the 29% top marginal rate. Tax compliance does not cure the immigration problem.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; hypothetical resident employment, consultancy, or business income
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Qualifying non-business foreign-currency software/consultancy receipts: 5% withholding; otherwise up to 29% top marginal resident rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Normal abode in Nepal or at least 183 days in a continuous 365-day period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are generally assessed regardless of source. Current material separately lists 5% withholding on qualifying foreign-currency software/electronic or consultancy receipts of a resident natural person not carrying on business, subject to exact classification and filing rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None. The reviewed rules contain activity-specific foreign-currency software, consultancy, and IT-export tax treatment, but no immigration-linked digital-nomad, expatriate, non-dom, remittance-basis, or inbound-worker regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A 1% social-security tax appears in the first remuneration band with exceptions. Full SSF/payroll obligations depend on whether the arrangement is employment or registered business activity.

fixed_payments.status: Not applicable as a digital-nomad package: Nepal has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker visa/status, so no route-specific mandatory monthly contribution, health payment, residence-card fee, or renewal payment exists. Tourist visa fees are visitor charges only; reviewed Social Security Fund material describes employment-based contributions rather than a compulsory fixed charge for an ineligible foreign remote worker.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No mandatory fixed monthly social-security amount was established for this profile. The Social Security Fund's formal-employment scheme is contribution-based, using employee and employer percentages of basic remuneration, but no source makes it applicable to a foreign tourist/remote worker who lacks a lawful Nepal employment route.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad visa or residence-card fee applies because no such route exists. Tourist visa and extension fees remain visitor fees and do not purchase work authorization or qualifying residence.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No route-specific municipal, freelancer, or monthly flat payment was identified. A 5% bank withholding can apply transaction-by-transaction to qualifying foreign-currency software/electronic or consultancy receipts of a resident natural person not carrying on business; this is tax collection on receipts, not a fixed monthly payment.
fixed_payments.notes: Status is inapplicable rather than unknown: there is no matching immigration category to which a fixed-payment package could attach. Business registration, VAT, payroll, and Social Security Fund obligations would depend on switching to a different lawful structure.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining under 183 days does not by itself guarantee non-residence because normal abode is an alternative test, and Nepal-source income may remain taxable. Tourist status also does not authorize work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A qualifying resident natural person not carrying on business may have 5% final withholding on foreign-currency software/electronic or consultancy receipts; other classifications may face ordinary worldwide-income assessment up to the 29% top marginal rate. Immigration eligibility remains absent.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registering a Nepal business or qualifying investment changes the immigration and tax facts. It is not a simple visitor-to-freelancer legalization route and can require company, industry, PAN/VAT, investment, and recommendation documentation.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a cautious hypothetical tax screen, not confirmation that remote work is permitted. The 5% treatment requires precise statutory classification.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent ordinary remote-worker route exists, so a route-specific time to temporary residence is inapplicable.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed sources establish no general permanent-residence conversion from work, study, tourist, business, or annually renewed Residential Visas.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Nepal's reviewed nationality law does not establish an ordinary PR-to-citizenship timeline for this profile.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The Act mentions at least 15 years of residence only inside a discretionary exceptional-contribution naturalization provision; this is not a reliable ordinary timeline for the applicant.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed Citizenship Act, Constitution, regulations page, and Ministry of Home Affairs materials publish no typical processing duration for this discretionary category.

key_conditions.value: Exceptional naturalization can require an exceptional contribution or capacity to contribute, ability to speak and write Nepali or another language used in Nepal, conducting business in Nepal, relinquishment of other citizenship, at least 15 years' residence, reciprocity, good character, mental fitness, and Nepal-government discretion. These conditions do not form an ordinary remote-worker entitlement.
key_conditions.notes: Because no matching immigration route exists, these conditions should not be treated as a usable settlement plan.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The express provision for a foreign woman married to a Nepali citizen states no minimum marriage duration, but citizenship is application-based and not automatic.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A foreign woman married to a Nepali citizen may apply for naturalized citizenship with marriage evidence and proof that she has begun relinquishing her foreign citizenship. No equivalent straightforward statutory route was confirmed for a foreign husband of a Nepali woman.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The law is gender-asymmetric; an existing genuine marriage supplies eligibility evidence but does not itself confer citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must document the genuine marital relationship and, for the express foreign-wife provision, action to relinquish foreign citizenship. False documents or sham arrangements can cause refusal, cancellation, and legal consequences; a foreign spouse should obtain case-specific advice because gender, descent rules, and administrative discretion matter.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Nepal generally requires relinquishment rather than ordinary dual nationality for naturalization.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Nepal is primarily jus sanguinis. Birth in Nepal alone does not generally grant citizenship; the Act preserves a historical birth-based category for persons born by a past cutoff and contains protections for foundlings, while children with a foreign parent face additional conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Nepal to two foreign parents does not automatically become a citizen merely by birth. A minor found in Nepal whose parents are unknown is treated as a citizen by descent until a parent is identified.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is restricted rather than general jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Citizenship may be available through a Nepali parent, but the result depends on the Nepali parent's sex, the foreign parent's identity and nationality, the child's birthplace and residence, and whether the child acquired foreign citizenship. A child born in Nepal to a Nepali mother and foreign father may fall under conditional naturalization rather than automatic descent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because one-Nepali-parent cases are not uniform, the boolean remains null rather than overstating a non-uniform rule.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child can potentially support a foreign parent's application for a relationship visa as Nepali kin, but it does not automatically grant the parent permanent residence or citizenship, and work still requires a labour permit.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Relationship eligibility and documents should be confirmed with the Department of Immigration.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically acquire Nepali citizenship or permanent residence because his child is Nepali. A relationship visa may be possible upon proof of kinship and the citizen relative's participation, but the visa does not itself authorize work without a labour permit.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The child's own citizenship can also be conditional where the Nepali citizen is the mother and the father is foreign.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index, May 2026; VisaIndex breakdown cross-check

rank.notes: Henley's 7 May 2026 ranking placed Nepal at 97 with a mobility score of 35; rankings can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: VisaIndex's separated breakdown lists 11 strictly visa-free destinations. Henley's broader score of 35 combines destinations accessible without obtaining a traditional visa in advance.

visa_required_destinations.notes: VisaIndex combines physical-visa and eVisa destinations into a group of 194, so its current categorization does not provide a defensible visa-in-advance-only count separate from eVisas.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: VisaIndex lists 22 visa-on-arrival and 2 eTA destinations. This excludes its 11 strictly visa-free destinations.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is reasonably practical in Kathmandu and other major urban or professional settings but is not an official federal language. EF's 2025 index scored Nepal at 514, rank 58, with Kathmandu at 531; this supports moderate practical usability but is a self-selected-test dataset rather than a census.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Nepali remains important for government procedures, local contracts, and daily life outside internationally oriented settings.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and the reviewed language sources provide no evidence of broad practical use. A speaker should expect to rely on Nepali or English and use translation or local assistance for formal procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The cited Constitution and proficiency index do not publish Nepal-wide Russian- or Ukrainian-proficiency figures.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2022 distributive-trade survey's NPR 17,374 average monthly wage using the 2026-08-15 NRB buying rate of NPR 152.39/USD. It is a trade-sector average, not an economy-wide current salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Nepal Labour Force Survey 2017/18 paid-employee median of NPR 15,208. The figure is official but historical.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory NPR 19,550 monthly minimum wage effective from 17 July 2025. It is a legal wage floor for covered non-tea sectors, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of NPR 17,374 per month from the 2022 Nepal Distributive Trade Survey. This covers paid employees in trade establishments and is not a national all-worker average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the official 2017/18 paid-employee median of NPR 15,208; retained as historical context because the newer reviewed survey does not publish a directly comparable economy-wide monthly median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD value is calculated because the reviewed official surveys do not publish a nationwide maximum salary in NPR. Their highest category or province averages are not individual maximum salaries.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory monthly minimum effective 17 July 2025 for covered sectors other than tea plantations.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly wages and salaries per paid employee in the 2022 distributive-trade survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly earnings of paid employees in the 2017/18 Nepal Labour Force Survey.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The Nepal Labour Force Survey publishes mean and median earnings by worker group; the Distributive Trade Survey publishes category and province averages; and the 2022/23 Living Standards Survey publishes mean annual earnings by daily, long-term, and contractual work. None publishes an observed or statutory nationwide maximum salary. A highest group average is not an individual maximum, so no NPR maximum can be reported without invention.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory minimum wage; 2022 trade-establishment average wage; and historical 2017/18 paid-employee median
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly; minimum effective July 2025, average based on reference year 2022, median based on 2017/18
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are labor-market indicators, not immigration income thresholds. The average is sector-specific and the median is historical. The 2022/23 Living Standards Survey provides newer mean earnings by job arrangement but no national maximum; therefore the maximum fields remain null. USD conversions for retained figures use the NRB 2026-08-15 buying rate of NPR 152.39 per USD.

cost_of_living_note.value: The reviewed official statistics do not provide a single comparable national monthly household budget suitable for this profile. Wage figures should not be treated as proof that a foreign remote worker's household costs would be covered; location and housing costs vary substantially.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A cautious factual explanation is retained rather than substituting a crowdsourced city estimate.

data.notes: The prior false verdict is retained. This focused audit inspected current immigration, citizenship, tax, social-security, and wage sources, including eight relevant canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. It resolves the flagged tourist-citizenship wording and tax-regime/fixed-payment descriptions; the national maximum-salary fields remain null because the named official surveys publish means and medians but no nationwide maximum.

data.selection_summary: The Netherlands has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. Its independently filed self-employed permit requires essential Dutch economic interest and, for freelancers, one or more commissions in the Netherlands; a foreign contract alone is insufficient. The orientation year is limited to recent qualifying graduates and is temporary, while highly skilled migrant and EU Blue Card routes require Dutch employment. The country therefore does not match the applicant’s ordinary foreign-contract remote-work profile, even though a materially different Dutch-facing business or local-employment route can eventually lead to permanent residence and citizenship.

visa_application.notes: This is the official application form for the closest independently filed route, not a digital-nomad application. Applicants normally apply for the MVV and residence permit through a Dutch embassy or consulate and then send the completed application to the IND. The route is rejected for this profile because it requires Dutch economic interest and Dutch commissions for freelancers.

summary.value: The one-year orientation permit can be applied for without a local employer after qualifying recent Dutch study/research or a qualifying recent foreign master’s, doctorate, or post-master’s credential. Foreign institutions must satisfy the top-200 rule in at least two specified rankings, and the diploma requires Nuffic evaluation. It is temporary and requires conversion to Dutch employment, a qualifying business, or another permit; an unspecified university degree alone does not establish eligibility.
summary.notes: This route is not marked partial because it neither provides permanent residence directly nor independently supports continued ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: Moving to and living in the Netherlands generally makes the person a resident taxpayer from the move date. Residents declare Dutch and foreign income as worldwide income; treaties and double-tax relief determine final taxing rights.
tax_residency_rule.notes: There is no simple universal 183-day safe harbor. Residence, employment location, treaty tie-breakers, and social-security coverage require individual analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top 2026 Box 1 marginal screening rate for a person below state-pension age, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Combined 2026 national-insurance rates for AOW 17.90%, Anw 0.10%, and Wlz 9.65%, calculated up to EUR 38,883; maximum stated contribution is EUR 10,751. Coverage can differ for cross-border workers.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Dutch basic health insurance is generally compulsory for people who live or work in the Netherlands, but no universal fixed monthly premium applies because insurers and policies vary. Foreign-employer and cross-border exceptions require SVB review.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax regime exists. The inbound employee facility may apply only in qualifying employment situations, not as a general concession for an independently resident foreign-contract remote worker.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No special remote-worker exemption was found.

taxes.caveats: The selected profile has no qualifying immigration route, so these figures are hypothetical screening information for someone who obtains another lawful status. Employment location, contract classification, permanent-establishment risk, treaty residence, double-tax relief, VAT, Dutch social insurance, and healthcare coverage need tailored advice.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally taxed under the Dutch box system. Work, salary, and self-employment income generally falls in progressive Box 1; resident worldwide income is declared with treaty relief where applicable.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: A person who moves to and lives in the Netherlands becomes a resident taxpayer from the move date; treaty analysis may modify cross-border taxing rights.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident worldwide income, subject to treaty allocation and double-tax relief.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Any employee-focused inbound facility requires separate eligibility and does not make foreign-contract remote residence permissible.
taxation_system.social_security: For 2026, national-insurance contributions total 27.65% up to EUR 38,883, with a stated maximum of EUR 10,751. Cross-border coverage may differ.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 49.50% dashboard figure is the top marginal Box 1 rate, not an effective rate. Tax credits, deductions, business classification, age, and treaty relief affect the result.

tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 Box 1 income for a person below state-pension age
tax_brackets.notes: Includes 8.10% income tax and 27.65% national insurance.
