digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because the Netherlands has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence permit. A person who lawfully relocates under another status should expect Dutch resident filing and declaration of worldwide income, subject to treaty relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: not_applicable_no_regular_remote_work_route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 49.50% top marginal Box 1 rate; not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Moving to and living in the Netherlands generally creates resident-taxpayer status from the move date; treaty residence must be checked separately.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents declare worldwide income, including foreign employment or business income, with double-tax relief where treaty or domestic rules allocate taxation elsewhere.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad regime confirmed. Employee-focused inbound relief is not a general remote-worker regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Dutch national insurance may apply; 2026 national-insurance rates total 27.65% up to the contribution ceiling. Foreign-employer and cross-border rules can change coverage.

fixed_payments.status: Route-dependent; no universal nomad payment
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: National insurance is percentage-based and capped, not a universal monthly flat amount.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee. The rejected self-employed permit costs EUR 423 in 2026; permanent residence costs EUR 254.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT and business-registration obligations depend on activities. The voluntary Dutch small-business VAT exemption has a EUR 20,000 annual turnover ceiling for qualifying Netherlands-established businesses.
fixed_payments.notes: Basic Dutch health insurance is usually compulsory for residents/workers, but premiums vary by insurer. A stated foreign-employer exception and other cross-border rules require confirmation with SVB.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No reliable day-count-only exemption should be assumed. Immigration permission, Dutch work activity, treaty residence, payroll, social-security, and permanent-establishment issues may arise before 183 days.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A lawful resident generally declares worldwide employment or business income and applies treaty relief where available; the top Box 1 marginal rate is 49.50%.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Dutch business may face Box 1 taxation, national insurance, health-insurance, Chamber of Commerce, and VAT obligations. The rejected immigration permit additionally requires Dutch economic interest and Dutch commissions.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax treatment is provided for screening only because no matching digital-nomad immigration route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route exists for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Other routes can grant temporary residence immediately only after materially changing to a Dutch-facing business, qualifying recent-graduate strategy, start-up, or Dutch employment.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The general rule is at least 5 consecutive qualifying years, but the applicant cannot start that clock through the stated foreign-contract profile.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation does not generally require first obtaining permanent residence; eligibility can arise after 5 qualifying lawful years while holding an accepted non-temporary residence purpose.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be assigned from the rejected foreign-contract profile. Under a different qualifying route, the ordinary naturalisation residence period is generally 5 consecutive years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The statutory IND decision period is 12 months and can be extended if additional time is needed; citizenship is completed only after approval and the naturalisation ceremony.

key_conditions.value: For ordinary naturalisation: 5 consecutive years of lawful residence, timely permit renewals, an accepted permanent or non-temporary residence purpose during application and ceremony, civic integration, identity/nationality evidence, public-order compliance, declaration of solidarity, and usually renunciation of the prior nationality unless an exception applies.
key_conditions.notes: Physical continuity and the precise permit purpose must be verified before relying on residence time.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Naturalisation may be available after 3 years of marriage/registered partnership and continuous cohabitation with the same Dutch citizen; qualifying pre-marriage cohabitation can sometimes count.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage or registered partnership can count toward the 3-year cohabitation period. The Dutch partner must be Dutch when the application is submitted, and the relationship and cohabitation normally must continue through the procedure.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage may also create an exception to renouncing the prior nationality, but it does not automatically grant residence, permanent residence, or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must satisfy the applicable lawful-residence or non-temporary-residence conditions, civic integration, identity, public-order, and continuing-relationship requirements. Authorities can request evidence of shared residence; false or sham relationships can lead to refusal, withdrawal, and enforcement consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The 3-year rule concerns naturalisation and should not be treated as automatic citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Dutch nationality is primarily by descent, with a narrow automatic multigenerational rule when the child and a parent reside in the Kingdom at birth and one of that parent’s parents also resided there when the parent was born. Stateless children and long-term residents may have option routes.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in the Netherlands to two foreign migrant parents does not ordinarily become Dutch merely by birth. The narrow multigenerational residence rule, statelessness provisions, or a later option/naturalisation procedure may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parental permanent residence alone does not create automatic Dutch nationality for the newborn.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child is generally Dutch automatically if the mother is Dutch at birth, or if the Dutch father is married to or the registered partner of the non-Dutch mother, or acknowledged the child before birth. Additional acknowledgement rules apply after birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule applies regardless of whether the child is born in the Netherlands or abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Dutch minor child can support a residence document for a genuinely caring, dependent non-EU parent under Chavez-Vilchez principles. The child must already be born, live or plan to live in the Netherlands, and be so dependent that refusal would effectively force the child to leave the EU.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The residence document is usually valid for up to 5 years or until the child turns 18. It does not automatically make the parent Dutch.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father who is a genuine caring parent of a dependent Dutch minor may qualify for Chavez residence and free access to work. After at least 5 years on that residence document, permanent residence may be possible; citizenship remains a separate application with its own conditions.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Biological parenthood alone or occasional care is insufficient, and birth of a Dutch child does not automatically grant the father residence or citizenship.

rank.notes: Tied fourth place in the live 2026 ranking checked on 15 August 2026.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley access score. Henley includes destinations accessible without a prior visa, including qualifying visa-on-arrival and electronic travel-authorisation access, rather than publishing a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The inspected Henley ranking did not publish a separate total for destinations requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Henley aggregates these categories into its access score; a separate combined VOA/eTA total was not established from the inspected current source.

passport.notes: The access score should not be interpreted as 186 strictly visa-free destinations because Henley’s methodology also credits specified visa-on-arrival and eTA access.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very practical in major cities and technology/international workplaces. The 2025 EF English Proficiency Index ranked the Netherlands first globally with a score of 624, although Dutch remains the official national language and is important for government procedures, integration, and long-term settlement.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF is a reputable private proficiency index based on self-selected adult test takers, not an official census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian may be useful within diaspora communities but is not a realistic primary language for government administration or the general labor market. Dutch or English should be expected for ordinary daily and professional life.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable national source quantifying general Russian or Ukrainian service availability was found; this conclusion is a cautious inference from the official-language position and high English proficiency.

average_citizen_salary.notes: The CBS income measure is per person receiving employee income and differs from a full-time-equivalent job salary. USD conversions are approximate and exchange-rate-sensitive.

cost_of_living_note.value: Housing is a significant expense. CBS reported 2023 median monthly housing costs of EUR 806 for owners, EUR 617 for social-housing tenants, and EUR 1,045 for tenants outside housing associations; corresponding median housing-cost ratios were 17.1%, 25.4%, and 30.2%. These are national historical medians, not current Amsterdam asking rents.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Use only as a broad affordability indicator.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor or short-stay presence must not be treated as the start of a Dutch settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: No qualifying settlement clock starts from ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Dutch-facing self-employment or Dutch-sponsored employment can lead to permanent residence and naturalisation under general rules, but each requires a material change from the applicant’s current profile.
settlement_track.notes: The rejected self-employed route can be settlement-capable for a genuinely qualifying Dutch business, but mandatory Dutch economic interest and Dutch commissions prevent treating it as a foreign-remote-worker route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated foreign-remote-worker permit was identified in the current official route portfolio. The independently filed self-employed permit requires essential Dutch economic interest and Dutch commissions for freelancers; other plausible routes require recent qualifying education, innovative founder activity, or Dutch employment.

data.notes: Audit updated the prior record with a direct application form, current 2026 fees and income threshold, a separate orientation-year analysis, clearer employer-versus-independent filing distinctions for the Blue Card, current tax and contribution brackets, worldwide-income treatment, health-insurance and VAT caveats, corrected route enums, a cautious conditional-jus-soli classification, current passport figures, and official wage/median data. At least 30 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected; 30 canonical sources are retained. Nulls remain where the official source does not publish a universal value or where a value would be misleading for a nonexistent remote-worker route.

data.selection_summary: New Zealand permits unlimited remote work for overseas employers or overseas clients while the person holds qualifying visitor status, but this is visitor permission rather than a residence visa and does not count as a settlement route. Skilled residence requires a skilled New Zealand job or job offer, while the independent business-investor route requires substantial local investment. No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker, freelance, or self-employed residence route was confirmed.

visa_application.title: Immigration New Zealand — Visitor Visa online application
visa_application.notes: The Visitor Visa page links to this official application portal. This is visitor status, not a digital-nomad or residence visa; eligible nationalities may instead use an NZeTA.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor Visa or NZeTA with overseas remote-work permission

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the NZD 1,000 monthly visitor maintenance-funds requirement at 1 NZD = USD 0.58045. This is accessible funding, not a remote-work earnings threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: NZD 1,000 per month, or NZD 400 per month if accommodation is prepaid
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Ordinary visitor maintenance funds; no separate digital-nomad income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: NZD 1,000/month visitor funds, or NZD 400/month with prepaid accommodation; no remote-work income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: NZD 1,000/month or NZD 400/month with prepaid accommodation
income_requirement_display.notes: Approximately USD 580 or USD 232. These are accessible funds rather than required salary or client income.

income_proof_months.notes: Recent bank or credit-card statements are required, but the official page does not prescribe a fixed historical number of months.

key_requirements.requirement: Remote work must be for an overseas employer, overseas business, or clients outside New Zealand.
The visitor cannot work for a New Zealand employer, provide goods or services to New Zealand persons or businesses, or perform work requiring physical presence in New Zealand.
The applicant must be a genuine visitor, intend to leave, meet health and character rules, and show maintenance and onward-travel funds.

initial_validity.value: Up to 6 or 9 months depending on visa conditions; generally no more than 9 months in an 18-month period
initial_validity.notes: Multiple-entry conditions and nationality-specific NZeTA rules may differ.

extension_rules.value: A new Visitor Visa may be requested before expiry, but total stay remains subject to visitor limits and discretionary approval.
extension_rules.notes: An extension remains visitor status and creates no residence rights.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None from this permission
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The remote-work condition is attached to visitor status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No conversion path was confirmed; the person must independently qualify for a separate resident visa.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time does not satisfy the resident-visa prerequisite for a Permanent Resident Visa.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status; qualifying presence must be accumulated while holding visas permitting indefinite residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A separate resident visa is required first.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a clear temporary fit for foreign-contract remote work: coding, testing, overseas employment, and overseas-client self-employment are permitted without a work-hour limit. It fails selection because it is visitor-only and has no settlement conversion.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no single route-wide monthly threshold; eligibility depends on skilled New Zealand employment, points, and applicable remuneration rules.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No universal monthly amount applies. A skilled local job or offer from an accredited employer is mandatory.

income_requirement_display.value: No universal monthly threshold; skilled New Zealand employment is mandatory
income_requirement_display.notes: The decisive mismatch is the local-employment requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: No universal historical income-proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Generally age 55 or younger with a skilled full-time job or job offer from an accredited New Zealand employer.
Six skilled-resident points, English, health and character requirements, an expression of interest, and an invitation to apply.

initial_validity.value: Resident visa permitting indefinite residence, subject to travel and any section 49 conditions
initial_validity.notes: It is a residence-class visa but not initially an unconditional Permanent Resident Visa.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary stay extension is needed; after at least 2 years the holder may qualify for a Permanent Resident Visa if all conditions are satisfied.
extension_rules.notes: Initial travel and employment conditions still matter.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; this route grants a resident visa

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Normally possible after holding a resident visa for at least 2 years and demonstrating commitment to New Zealand.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially after at least 5 years living with qualifying resident status and meeting presence, English, character, and intention requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The applicant's foreign contract does not meet the initial New Zealand-employment condition.

rejected_routes.notes: Residence-oriented but rejected because the current Skilled Migrant Category requires a skilled New Zealand job or offer. Changes scheduled for 24 August 2026 do not remove that mismatch.

rejected_routes.route_name: Business Investor Work Visa to Business Investor Resident Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This route uses investment capital, reserve funds, business experience, and employment requirements rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least NZD 1 million investment plus NZD 500,000 reserve funds
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A NZD 2 million investment offers the faster residence timetable; these are capital requirements.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly threshold; NZD 1 million or NZD 2 million investment plus NZD 500,000 reserve funds
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: NZD 1,000,000 or NZD 2,000,000 investment; NZD 500,000 reserve funds
income_requirement_display.notes: Excluded because it requires substantial capital and operation of an established New Zealand business.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not an income-proof route.

key_requirements.requirement: Invest at least NZD 1 million or NZD 2 million in an acceptable established New Zealand business and actively operate it.
Show relevant business experience, be no older than 55, hold NZD 500,000 reserve funds, and meet English, health, and character rules.
For residence, maintain at least five full-time-equivalent jobs and create at least one new full-time job for a citizen or resident.

initial_validity.value: Up to 4 years, including an establishment stage
initial_validity.notes: The work visa is tied to operating the approved local business.

extension_rules.value: Residence may be requested after 3 years under the NZD 1 million pathway or after 12 months under the NZD 2 million pathway, subject to all conditions.
extension_rules.notes: The business must continue meeting operating and employment conditions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The initial work visa provides temporary status for up to 4 years.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A Business Investor Resident Visa follows qualifying operation and investment; an unconditional Permanent Resident Visa is a later step.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially after subsequently meeting the normal 5-year resident-status and physical-presence rules.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The investment route is outside the ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: A genuine independent work-to-residence route, but it requires substantial investment and active operation of a local business rather than ordinary foreign-client remote work.

summary.value: A degree may contribute Skilled Migrant Category points, but a degree alone does not provide residence; the route also requires a skilled full-time job or offer from an accredited New Zealand employer.
summary.notes: The software-engineering degree does not create an independent residence route based on the existing foreign contract.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence generally begins upon acquiring a permanent place of abode or being present for more than 183 days in any 12-month period; the day-count result is backdated. A qualifying non-resident visitor can remain non-resident for up to 275 days in an 18-month period if every published condition is met.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration and tax residence are separate; treaties and short-stay rules may change the outcome.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: 2026/27 employee ACC earners' levy. Self-employed levies vary, so this is not a universal freelancer rate.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly social-security or freelancer payment is published; ACC depends on earnings and classification.

special_tax_regimes.value: Qualifying new or returning residents may receive a temporary exemption from tax on most overseas income for approximately four years.
special_tax_regimes.notes: There is no special digital-nomad tax rate, and the transitional exemption does not automatically exempt every employment or service-income category.

taxes.caveats: Remote visitor work can be taxable even before tax residence. Short-stay, income-source, permanent-place-of-abode, treaty, GST, and ACC treatment require individual analysis.

taxation_system.value: Progressive individual income tax; residents generally face worldwide-income taxation subject to exemptions and treaties.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of abode or more than 183 days in 12 months, subject to applicable exceptions.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally report worldwide income; non-resident liability depends on New Zealand source and treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Approximately four-year transitional-resident exemption for most overseas income may apply.
taxation_system.social_security: No single general social-security rate; ACC levies apply and self-employed rates vary.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 39% dashboard value is the top marginal screening rate, not an average effective rate.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: There is no dedicated digital-nomad tax regime; visitor remote workers remain subject to ordinary residence, source, short-stay, and treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Foreign remote work performed during visitor status
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 39% top marginal rate if taxable under ordinary rules; qualifying short-stay or treaty relief may eliminate liability.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of abode or more than 183 days in 12 months, with a conditional non-resident-visitor exception of up to 275 days in 18 months.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally face worldwide-income taxation, subject to treaties and the transitional-resident exemption.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No nomad-specific regime; a qualifying transitional-resident exemption may apply to most overseas income.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No universal fixed contribution for all visitor remote workers; ACC treatment depends on liability and classification.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly digital-nomad payment is published
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: ACC may apply, but no single fixed self-employed monthly amount exists.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Visitor Visa cost starts from NZD 441; NZeTA charges differ.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: GST registration is generally required when taxable-activity turnover reaches or is expected to reach NZD 60,000 in 12 months.
fixed_payments.notes: Medical insurance is recommended rather than universally mandatory; no fixed municipal freelancer or nomad tax was identified.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Short-stay or treaty relief may apply; Inland Revenue's 275-day non-resident-visitor rule requires every condition to be satisfied.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary progressive rates up to 39% may apply to worldwide taxable income.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Self-employed taxpayers generally use an IRD number, file an IR3 on net profit, and may need GST registration. Tax registration does not legalize or convert visitor status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Treaty, source, and contract classification require individual review.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The matching permission grants visitor status, not temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: There is no progression from visitor remote work; a separate resident visa is required.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Citizenship is measured from qualifying resident status, not visitor status or necessarily the later Permanent Resident Visa date.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total exists from the visitor route. After separately obtaining qualifying resident status, the normal citizenship period is at least 5 years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Current official data say 90% receive an outcome within 3 months; ceremony scheduling may add time.

key_conditions.value: Normally at least 5 years on visas permitting indefinite residence, at least 240 days present in each 12-month period and 1,350 days across 5 years, English ability, good character, intention to continue living in New Zealand, and compliance with visa conditions.
key_conditions.notes: New Zealand permits dual citizenship, although the other country may not.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Partner residence normally requires at least 12 months living together in a genuine and stable relationship, not merely 12 months of legal marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage is evidence but is insufficient by itself; the couple normally must prove 12 months of genuine and stable cohabitation and obtain partner support.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not shorten the ordinary citizenship presence requirement.

requirements_and_risks.value: Immigration New Zealand examines shared residence, finances, public recognition, relationship duration, and credibility. Unsupported or sham relationships may be declined; citizenship retains its normal residence, presence, English, and character requirements.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The acceleration concerns access to partnership residence, not automatic citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For births from 1 January 2006, at least one parent generally must be a citizen or entitled to remain indefinitely, subject to statutory exceptions and an anti-statelessness rule.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A New Zealand-born child is not automatically a citizen if both parents only hold temporary or visitor status. Citizenship is possible if at least one parent may remain indefinitely or the anti-statelessness rule applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' exact immigration status is decisive.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in New Zealand ordinarily becomes a citizen when the other parent is a New Zealand citizen; an overseas-born child may qualify by descent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Overseas descent registration and transmission limits should be checked.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically give the migrant father residence, permanent residence, or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any benefit requires a separate qualifying family or partnership application.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status. Partnership residence may be available through a qualifying New Zealand citizen or resident partner, but the child's birth does not replace visa requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A filing-specific assessment is required.

rank.notes: Guide Passport Index rank accessed on 15 August 2026.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations; total mobility is higher when VOA and eTA are included.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Physical visa required; the index separately lists 28 online-visa destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 37 visa-on-arrival plus 10 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: All breakdown figures consistently use the Guide Passport Index rather than mixing methodologies with Henley.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high; English is predominant in government, business, education, and everyday communication.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English is fully practical for software work and daily life.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited outside migrant communities and private interpretation services; English is normally needed for government and business matters.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Inference from the official-language environment; no official nationwide service-availability measure was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Constructed gross full-time equivalent from June 2026 average hourly earnings of NZD 44.72, assuming 40 hours/week and 52/12 weeks/month.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the June 2025 national HLFS median weekly wage-and-salary earnings of NZD 1,380. The measure covers employed wage-and-salary recipients and is not full-time-only.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate full-time monthly equivalent of the statutory adult minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Constructed gross full-time monthly equivalent from the June 2026 official average hourly earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximately USD 3,471 per month, derived from the latest published national HLFS median weekly wage-and-salary earnings of NZD 1,380 in June 2025 using 52/12 weeks per month and the official 30 July 2026 exchange rate. This is a gross survey median for employed wage-and-salary recipients, not a full-time-only salary or the June 2026 QES average.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No finite USD maximum can be converted because the official 2025 wage-and-salary distribution has an open-ended NZD 1,000,000-and-over annual band and does not identify the highest salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory adult minimum wage effective 1 April 2026, before tax.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Constructed from official June 2026 QES average hourly earnings.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The latest published national HLFS median is NZD 1,380 per week as at June 2025. The monthly amount is an arithmetic equivalent; the survey covers employed wage-and-salary recipients and is not restricted to full-time workers. Stats NZ research supports the HLFS methodology and shows close alignment with linked administrative data.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite national maximum is published; the official 2025 distribution ends with an open-ended NZD 1,000,000-and-over annual wage/salary band
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Inland Revenue reports counts and total wage/salary income by bands rather than the highest individual salary. The open-ended top band cannot establish a maximum monthly salary, so the numeric USD value remains null.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross statutory minimum; constructed QES full-time average; and gross HLFS median weekly wage-and-salary earnings converted monthly
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 1 April 2026; QES average June 2026; HLFS median June 2025; FX 30 July 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are national worker wage indicators, not immigration thresholds. The minimum is statutory, the average is constructed from an enterprise-survey hourly mean, the median is an HLFS survey measure, and no national maximum is published.

cost_of_living_note.value: No single current official national remote-worker budget was established; costs vary substantially by city, household, housing tenure, and transport.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The NZD 1,000 visitor maintenance requirement is not a realistic comprehensive cost-of-living estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Remote work is lawful only within visitor conditions. Visitor time does not create residence, permanent-residence eligibility, or citizenship presence; a separate resident visa is required.
settlement_track.summary: New Zealand is a strong temporary-living fit for foreign remote work but not a citizenship-path fit. The matching permission is visitor-only; available settlement routes require New Zealand employment, partnership, or substantial local business investment.
settlement_track.notes: Classified as temporary_nomad_only because explicit remote-work permission exists solely under visitor status.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only for temporary visitor use; it is not a settlement match.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit resolved the national salary median using the latest published June 2025 HLFS wage-and-salary median and established that no finite national maximum is published because the 2025 official distribution has an open-ended top band. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including five canonical URLs absent from the previous source set; Figure.NZ was used only as a transparent presentation of Stats NZ and Inland Revenue data.

data.selection_summary: Nicaragua has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route. The implementing regulation makes the independent-worker category Nicaragua-facing: it requires merchant registration, a municipal commercial licence, DGI/RUC registration, and a notarized declaration of income sources; independent consultants must also provide a State Supplier Certificate. Rentista status grants permanent residence but requires stable, permanent foreign rent and should not be assumed to accept an ordinary salary or services contract. Nicaragua therefore does not meet the selection criteria.

visa_application.title: Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería
visa_application.notes: No functioning official online application form for rentista or independent-worker residence was confirmed. The migration-law text says applications may be filed with DGME while in Nicaragua or through a Nicaraguan diplomatic or consular official abroad. Rentista applicants also require INTUR involvement. The authority page was intermittently inaccessible during this audit, so applicants should confirm the filing location and current document checklist directly.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Minimum stable and permanent foreign-generated rent for the principal applicant. The statute specifies an additional USD 150 monthly for each included dependent.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Equivalent of US$1,250 per month in Nicaraguan córdobas (approximately C$45,780.38 at the official 2026 rate)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The legal threshold is denominated in USD; the córdoba figure is an approximate conversion at C$36.6243 per USD.

income_requirement_display.value: US$1,250/month in stable, permanent foreign rent; ordinary employment or freelance-contract income is not expressly listed
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Approximately C$45,780.38/month at the 2026 official exchange rate; add US$150/month per dependent
income_requirement_display.notes: The law describes qualifying income as distributions of profits, rent, or analogous lawful businesses. It does not expressly classify a terminable foreign software-employment or services contract as stable, permanent rent.

income_proof_months.notes: The law and regulation require certification of stable, permanent income, but no fixed number of bank-statement months was established from the reviewed official material.

key_requirements.requirement: Stable and permanent foreign-generated income meeting the statutory threshold.
Application through INTUR or a Nicaraguan consulate, followed by the permanent-residence process before DGME.
Supporting income certification and the documents prescribed by the implementing regulation; current legalization, apostille, translation, and validity requirements should be confirmed before filing.
Maintain the residence conditions and comply with absence restrictions; an unjustified absence exceeding one year is a cancellation ground.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence; the permanent-residence card is valid for 5 years
initial_validity.notes: The immigration category is permanent, but the implementing regulation gives permanent residence a five-year documentary validity and requires renewal.

extension_rules.value: Renew the permanent residence before the five-year card expires. The regulation requires a renewal form, conduct certificate, copy of the residence card, two passport photos, and the items applicable to the subcategory; continued rentista eligibility must be supported because loss of the qualifying foreign rent is a cancellation ground.
extension_rules.notes: The law requires renewal to be requested 30 days before expiry. The regulation does not publish a separate rentista-only renewal checklist or a fixed renewed-card processing time; DGME decides renewal by administrative resolution.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; qualifying applicants proceed toward permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent-residence category after INTUR approval and DGME processing.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a genuine settlement category for qualifying rentiers, but it is rejected for the supplied profile because ordinary foreign-contract remuneration is not clearly qualifying rent.

path_to_citizenship.value: The general rule permits naturalization after four continuous years counted from issuance of the permanent-resident card, subject to lawful means, good conduct, criminal-record, Spanish, history, geography, and civic-knowledge requirements and the applicable renunciation rule.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route could provide a citizenship track to a genuine rentista. It is not a confirmed route for the applicant's ordinary foreign software contract.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile, despite direct permanent residence. The income definition is aimed at stable, permanent foreign rent such as profit distributions and rentals. A rentista may seek a separate INTUR-endorsed permit for remunerated activity (the official fee schedule lists US$200), but that does not make an ordinary foreign software contract qualifying rent or create a digital-nomad route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence as an independent worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Article 69 requires a notarized declaration of income sources but states no minimum USD amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Article 69 states no minimum córdoba amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum is published; applicants must document Nicaragua-side business registration and provide a notarized declaration of income sources
income_requirement_display.notes: Article 69 of the implementing regulation requires merchant registration, a municipal commercial licence, DGI/RUC registration, and a notarized declaration of income sources. It states no monetary floor or number of proof months. For independent consultants it additionally requires a State Supplier Certificate, making this materially different from an ordinary offshore-only remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: The regulation requires a notarized declaration of income sources but does not prescribe a fixed bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Register a merchant declaration in the Mercantile Registry.
Provide the commercial licence issued by the relevant municipality.
Register with the Dirección General de Ingresos and provide a RUC copy.
Provide a notarized declaration identifying the sources of income.
Independent consultants must additionally provide a copy of the State Supplier Certificate.
Obtain temporary residence authorizing the approved activity; foreigners may not perform activities beyond those authorized.

initial_validity.value: One to three years, or the duration of the authorized activity
initial_validity.notes: The statute defines temporary residence as one to three years, renewable, or for the duration of the admitted activity.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while the authorized cause or activity continues, subject to DGME approval.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic-renewal rule applies. The regulation requires a renewal form, conduct certificate, residence-card copy, two photographs, and subcategory-specific evidence such as commercial registration, RUC/DGI documentation, and a declaration of income sources.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence if DGME approves the locally registered independent activity.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not a dedicated foreign-contract remote-worker category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Temporary residents with more than three years of legal stay may apply for permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is an application opportunity, not automatic conversion. Because the independent-worker route requires Nicaragua-side commercial substance, it does not establish a regular offshore-only remote-work settlement path.

path_to_citizenship.value: If permanent residence is later granted, the ordinary naturalization period is four continuous years from the permanent-resident card.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Potential total is more than seven years from temporary residence, but only if the locally registered activity is accepted, status is maintained, permanent residence is approved, and naturalization requirements are met.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. The regulation confirms that this is a locally registered commercial/self-employment route, not a simple residence category based only on a foreign software contract. The State Supplier Certificate requirement for independent consultants creates an additional mismatch.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Not a residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not a residence route.

income_requirement_display.value: No residence-route income threshold; visitor status does not authorize ordinary remunerated activity
income_requirement_display.notes: Non-residents may not undertake profitable activity for their own account or as employees unless specially authorized.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable.

key_requirements.requirement: Remain within the authorized non-resident stay and do not undertake unauthorized remunerated activity.
Obtain an appropriate residence and activity authorization before treating Nicaragua as a remote-work base.

initial_validity.value: Category A: 90 days, extendable up to 180 days; Categories B and C: 30 days, extendable up to 90 days
initial_validity.notes: The exact initial stay depends on the nationality-based visa category. The regulation gives the category limits above; because applicant nationality was not supplied, no single duration applies. These are non-resident stays and do not authorize ordinary remunerated activity.

extension_rules.value: Any visitor extension remains non-resident status and does not itself legalize remote work or create a settlement route.
extension_rules.notes: An extension requires the prescribed form, a passport valid at least six months, and the applicable fee. A residence applicant must keep extending non-resident stay while the residence request is pending; an extension does not itself authorize work.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate qualifying residence application would be required; no tourist-to-remote-worker conversion route was confirmed.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None directly.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time is not established as qualifying permanent-residence time for ordinary naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Visitor status is not a valid remote-work or citizenship-path solution.

summary.value: Students are listed as temporary residents and therefore can obtain residence without a local employer when admitted for study. The status is education-dependent, not a degree-based independent skilled route for an existing software engineer. Temporary residents with more than three years of legal stay may apply for permanent residence, but no automatic student conversion or permission for ordinary foreign remote work was confirmed.
summary.notes: This alternative is not valid for the supplied foreign-contract profile unless the applicant genuinely studies and separately resolves work authorization.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is tax resident after spending more than 180 days in Nicaragua in a calendar year, whether continuously or not, or when the individual's main centre of economic interest is in Nicaragua unless qualifying foreign tax residence is proved.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence and source are separate questions: Nicaragua applies a reinforced territorial system, and services physically performed in Nicaragua may be treated as Nicaraguan-source even when paid by a foreign client.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for resident individual income, not an expected effective rate. The resident employment-income scale is progressive from 0% to 30%; business or professional income classification and deductions may differ.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The official INSS page lists 22.25% of declared income, using at least the established minimum salary base, for the voluntary comprehensive regime. Employees instead contribute 7%, with employers contributing 21.5% or 22.5% depending on workforce size. Applicability to a foreign-contract resident requires individual confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal USD fixed payment applies. Voluntary INSS is percentage-based, and its minimum monetary contribution depends on the applicable minimum-salary base.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime was found. Nicaragua uses a reinforced territorial-source system. Rentista legislation offers specified import and migration incentives, but it is not a general exemption for active remote-work income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign payment location alone does not prove exemption if services are performed from Nicaragua.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether remuneration is classified as work income or economic-activity income, where services are performed, residence and economic-interest tests, registration status, deductible expenses, withholding, VAT, and any applicable treaty. Nicaragua's reinforced territorial-source concept can reach income connected with services performed in Nicaragua. Obtain Nicaraguan tax advice before relying on foreign-source treatment.

taxation_system.value: Reinforced territorial taxation. Residents pay progressive individual income tax on Nicaraguan-source income, with a top marginal rate of 30%; non-residents receiving Nicaraguan-source income generally face 20% definitive withholding.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 days in a calendar year, continuous or not, or main centre of economic interest in Nicaragua unless qualifying foreign residence is proved.
taxation_system.income_scope: Nicaraguan-source income, including income derived from goods, services, rights, or activities in Nicaragua and certain economic links abroad under the reinforced territorial principle.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime found. Statutory rentista incentives are category-specific and do not clearly exempt active remote-work earnings.
taxation_system.social_security: Official INSS rates include 7% employee contributions; employer rates of 21.5% or 22.5%; voluntary comprehensive coverage at 22.25% of declared income subject to a minimum-salary base; and voluntary IVM at 14%.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The brackets are annual. The dashboard's 30% figure is the top marginal rate applied only to taxable income over C$500,000, plus the bracket's base charge; it is not the effective rate on total income.

tax_brackets.notes: No tax through C$100,000 annually.
USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold at C$36.6243/USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over C$200,000, plus C$15,000 base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over C$350,000, plus C$45,000 base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over C$500,000, plus C$82,500 base tax
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket begins at approximately USD 13,652 annual taxable income.

taxation_system.notes: The rate table and residence test were current as reviewed on 4 August 2026. Filing-specific classification of foreign-client services remains the main uncertainty.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special visa regime because Nicaragua has no confirmed digital-nomad status. A person nevertheless working from Nicaragua may enter the ordinary tax and registration system.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; potentially work income or economic-activity income under ordinary law
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–30% progressive resident scale on relevant Nicaraguan-source individual income; 30% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 days in the calendar year or main centre of economic interest in Nicaragua.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Nicaragua is territorial, but the source rules focus on activities and services in Nicaragua. Foreign-client remuneration for work physically performed in Nicaragua cannot safely be treated as exempt merely because the payer and bank account are abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Potential INSS, tax registration, withholding, and invoicing consequences depend on worker classification. Voluntary comprehensive INSS is listed at 22.25% of declared income with a minimum-salary base; employee coverage uses a 7% employee rate plus employer contributions.

fixed_payments.status: No universal remote-worker fixed tax or contribution confirmed.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based INSS regimes exist; the exact monthly minimum depends on the applicable declared/minimum salary base.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: There is no digital-nomad fee. The migration fee schedule includes category-specific residence services and a US$200 permit for an INTUR-endorsed rentista or pensionado to undertake remunerated activity.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Ordinary VAT, tax registration, municipal, stamp, or business obligations may arise depending on activity; no universal freelancer fixed-payment amount was established.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of a dedicated route prevents a reliable all-in monthly cost calculation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining under 181 days does not automatically eliminate Nicaraguan tax on services sourced to Nicaragua, and visitor status does not authorize ordinary remunerated activity.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident performing services from Nicaragua should screen the income under the territorial source rules and the progressive scale up to 30%, despite a foreign payer.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The independent-worker route requires merchant registration, a municipal commercial licence, DGI/RUC registration, and declared income sources. Tax, invoicing, VAT, municipal, and INSS treatment require local professional confirmation.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax law is clearer than immigration eligibility, but no official worked example specifically addresses a foreign software contract performed remotely from Nicaragua.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying temporary-residence category grants temporary residence directly after approval. This does not mean the supplied offshore-only foreign-contract profile qualifies.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Temporary residents with more than three years of legal stay may apply for permanent residence; approval is not automatic. Rentistas instead have a direct permanent-residence category.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires four continuous years from issuance of the permanent-resident card. Two-year exceptions apply to specified groups, including qualifying spouses of Nicaraguans.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Indicative minimum for a generic temporary-resident path: more than three years before applying for permanent residence plus four continuous years as a permanent resident. Processing gaps are excluded. This is not a confirmed timeline for ordinary foreign-contract remote work; a qualifying rentista begins with permanent residence and could use the four-year rule.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The migration law states a maximum 30-day approval-or-denial period under the ordinary nationality provision, but the reviewed sources do not establish a current typical end-to-end duration including examination, decision, publication, and documentation. The statutory decision period is therefore not presented as a typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Maintain the relevant lawful residence, obtain permanent-resident documentation, show lawful means of life, good conduct and no criminal record, demonstrate sufficient Spanish plus knowledge of Nicaragua's geography, history, and political and social organization, and address the applicable prior-nationality renunciation rule. Naturalization is not automatic.
key_conditions.notes: The 2025 Constitution states that foreigners may be naturalized after renouncing their nationality, while treaty, reciprocity, Central American, Spanish, and marriage exceptions require individual review.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The spouse of a Nicaraguan may naturalize after two years of continuous residence under the migration law while maintaining the qualifying marital link. This is an accelerated residence period, not citizenship immediately upon marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A marriage validly concluded with a Nicaraguan inside or outside Nicaragua can support residence by marital or family link. An already existing marriage therefore can matter, but the foreign marriage must be legally recognized and documented.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The implementing regulation requires at least two years' duration for the marriage or stable union when applying under the specified permanent-residence family-link provision.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage or stable union must be legally valid and subsisting. Residence, continuous-presence, lawful-means, good-conduct, criminal-record, Spanish/civic-knowledge, and nationality-renunciation requirements may still apply. Authorities can investigate authenticity, and false documents or sham relationships can cause denial, cancellation, removal, and potential criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No current official checklist quantifying cohabitation evidence or interview practice was located; obtain a filing-specific DGME checklist.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Nicaraguan law broadly grants nationality to persons born in national territory, with narrow exceptions involving children of foreign diplomats, international-organization officials, or persons sent by foreign governments to work in Nicaragua unless they opt for Nicaraguan nationality. Under the prompt's classification rule, these narrow exceptions remain unconditional jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Nicaragua generally acquires Nicaraguan nationality even when both parents are foreign migrants, subject to the narrow diplomatic, international-organization, and foreign-government-service exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A permanent-resident parent is not required for ordinary territorial birth citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Nicaraguan mother or father is Nicaraguan by descent; a child born in Nicaragua also normally qualifies territorially.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Nicaraguan child may apply for residence based on the family link. The child's citizenship does not automatically confer permanent residence or citizenship on the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must complete the applicable DGME procedure and independently satisfy later naturalization conditions.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Nicaraguan child may seek family-link residence, but paternity and the family relationship must be legally documented. He does not acquire Nicaraguan citizenship automatically through the child.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on 15 August 2026; live index values can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified by Passport Index as visa-free.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa; eVisas are treated separately by the index and therefore are not included in this number.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 43 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately displayed a mobility score of 121.

passport.notes: This uses Passport Index because it publishes the requested separated visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, and visa-required counts. It should not be compared directly with Henley's broader access score, which uses different categories.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Spanish is the nationwide official language. English Creole and several Indigenous languages have official or community status on the Caribbean Coast. English can support remote work and some activity in tourism or Caribbean communities, but Spanish is normally necessary for government procedures, housing, banking, taxation, healthcare, and broad daily integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The practicality assessment is an inference from the constitutional language distribution; no current nationwide English-proficiency dataset was used.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and should not be expected to work for routine administration or daily life. A Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking migrant should plan to use Spanish or arrange interpretation.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current national data measuring Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 annual-average nominal wage of INSS affiliates, C$15,877.2 per month, using C$36.6243/USD. This covers formal insured employment, not every citizen or informal worker.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed BCN publications report average formal-sector wages but do not publish a current national monthly median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of C$6,188.02, the lowest 2026 sectoral statutory minimum wage for agriculture, at C$36.6243/USD. This is a legal wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2025 formal-sector annual average, converted at the fixed 2026 official rate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official publications reviewed report means but not a national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official statistics do not publish a meaningful national maximum salary or reliable upper wage-distribution bound. A highest sectoral average or minimum wage is not treated as a maximum citizen salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Lowest 2026 sectoral statutory minimum, for agriculture, effective 1 March 2026 through 28 February 2027; it is not an observed minimum salary. The reviewed MITRAB-linked reporting identifies Commission Minute No. 1 CNSM-05/03/2026, but an inspectable copy of that current minute was unavailable on the MITRAB public site.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 annual-average nominal wage of INSS affiliates. The separate December 2025 point estimate was C$16,692.4.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed BCN and INSS materials publish averages but no current national median wage in córdobas.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official wage publications do not define or publish a meaningful national maximum wage.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Nominal monthly formal-sector wage of INSS affiliates; minimum field is the lowest sectoral statutory minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 formal-sector average wage; 2026 statutory minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average covers INSS-affiliated formal employment and excludes much informal employment; it is not a household-income or all-citizen measure. The minimum is the current lowest sectoral statutory floor, not an observed distribution minimum. USD conversions use C$36.6243 per USD. No current official national median or meaningful maximum wage was published in the inspected sources.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official wage publications do not provide a comparable individual monthly cost-of-living budget. No value is supplied rather than mixing an unofficial crowd-sourced estimate with official salary data.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor status is non-resident and does not authorize ordinary remunerated activity. The independent-worker category requires Nicaragua-side merchant, municipal, and tax registration—and a State Supplier Certificate for independent consultants—so it is not a regular foreign-contract remote-work route. Rentista permanent residence requires a materially different stable, permanent foreign-rent profile.
settlement_track.summary: Nicaragua has genuine residence-to-citizenship rules, including direct permanent residence for qualifying rentistas, but no current route fits the applicant's ordinary offshore-only foreign software contract. The independent-worker category requires Nicaragua-side commercial substance, while rentista status requires a materially different stable, permanent foreign-income profile.
settlement_track.notes: Ordinary naturalization is generally available after four continuous years as a permanent resident, but that general rule does not cure the lack of a matching initial immigration and work category.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad route exists. The implementing regulation requires independent workers to establish Nicaragua-side merchant, municipal, and DGI/RUC registrations and requires independent consultants to show a State Supplier Certificate. Rentista status instead requires stable, permanent foreign rent and should not be assumed to accept salary or ordinary freelance-contract revenue.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 15 August 2026. The implementing migration regulation resolves the independent-worker route as Nicaragua-side commercial/self-employment rather than ordinary offshore-only remote work; it also supplies the five-year permanent-residence renewal rule and nationality-category visitor durations. The 2026 statutory minimum was updated. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including seven canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. Remaining nulls are deliberate where the named official/current sources publish no fixed proof-month period, national median or maximum wage, typical end-to-end citizenship processing time, or universal remote-worker fixed payment.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary foreign-contract freelance residence route was confirmed. Niger’s entry-and-stay decree recognizes residence based on a separately authorized non-salaried professional activity, but the current sources inspected publish no application category, eligibility rules, or filing channel showing that ordinary work for a foreign client qualifies. The clearly documented work route remains employer-led: a Niger employment contract must be approved before entry and the employer files the contract-visa request.

visa_application.title: Note on obtaining a work visa for foreign workers in Niger
visa_application.notes: This official embassy page explains the employer/approved-contract route; it is not an online application portal and is not usable as an independent remote-worker application. No official digital-nomad or independent remote-work application channel was found.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker or general minimum-income threshold is published. The approved employment contract must state remuneration.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No route-specific minimum was found. Ordinary covered employment is subject to applicable wage rules, including the XOF 42,000 monthly SMIG from 1 January 2026.

income_requirement_display.value: No published route-specific income threshold
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Approved employment contract must state salary; ordinary wage rules apply
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No visa threshold; national SMIG is XOF 42,000/month from 2026
income_requirement_display.notes: The SMIG is a wage floor, not an immigration eligibility threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The route is based on an approved employment contract, not a specified number of prior income months.

key_requirements.requirement: A Niger-based employer must request approval of a written foreign-worker employment contract before the worker enters Niger.

The employer's file includes five contract copies, the worker's CV, legalized employment certificates and/or diplomas, nationality evidence, birth record, criminal-record certificate, job description, five photographs, and a medical certificate; several documents must be less than three months old.
The employer must prepare a Nigerien worker to replace the foreign worker by the end of the maximum authorization period.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: This is the validity of the foreign-worker contract visa. The sources reviewed do not establish that it is itself a residence card.

extension_rules.value: Renewable once, for a maximum combined period of 4 years; renewal must be requested two months before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: The employer must document measures for replacement by a Nigerien worker.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The contract authorization and entry visa do not themselves constitute the residence permit. Foreigners remaining beyond three months generally apply separately to the local police for a two-year renewable permit, but the sources do not establish an automatic entitlement through this employment authorization.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No permanent-residence transition was confirmed for this employment authorization.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The employment authorization is capped at four years and anticipates replacement of the foreign worker. The general residence permit is renewable, but no permanent-residence category or automatic conversion from this route was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: No route-specific citizenship transition. Separate discretionary naturalization generally requires at least 10 years of habitual residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The sources do not confirm that the four-year employment authorization can support ten years of continuous qualifying habitual residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the employer files the authorization request and the route concerns employment in Niger. It does not accommodate ordinary remote work solely for a foreign client or foreign employer. A separate residence-permit application may be required, but that does not remove the employer requirement.

summary.value: No degree-only or qualification-based independent residence route was found. Diplomas and employment certificates are supporting documents in the employer-filed foreign-worker contract process, not an independent immigration category.
summary.notes: A software-engineering degree may support an employer's application but does not remove the employer and approved-contract requirements.

tax_residency_rule.value: The 2025 General Tax Code subjects salary income to Niger tax where an employee has habitual residence or fiscal domicile in Niger; it also taxes certain Niger-source remuneration received without habitual residence. No universal 183-day test was identified in the provisions reviewed.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence, source, employment status, treaty protection, and whether foreign-client remuneration is treated as salary or business income require case-specific advice.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal monthly employment-income rate, not an expected effective rate. Lower portions of taxable monthly salary are taxed at rates from 1% through 34%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share for covered salaried workers. The employer bears an additional 16.40%, producing a 21.65% CNSS total, plus a 0.5% employer-only ANPE levy. Applicability to an independently registered foreign remote worker is not established because no corresponding immigration and registration route was confirmed.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no route-specific monthly digital-nomad payment because no such route exists. Salaried CNSS contributions are percentage-based and capped; visa, residence, and professional-authorization duties are event-based rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, non-dom, remittance-basis, or comparable inbound individual regime was identified in the 2025 General Tax Code review.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business incentives and ordinary corporate provisions are not a substitute for a remote-worker immigration route.

taxes.caveats: Tax results depend on fiscal domicile, habitual residence, where duties are performed, income characterization, contract structure, treaty availability, deductions, and registration status. No immigration route was confirmed for the modeled independent remote-work scenario, so the tax discussion is screening information rather than confirmation that the activity is lawful.

taxation_system.value: Progressive employment-income taxation with a top monthly marginal rate of 35%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Habitual residence or fiscal domicile triggers Niger taxation of salary income under the reviewed code; some Niger-source remuneration is taxable even without habitual residence. No general day-count threshold was confirmed.
taxation_system.income_scope: The code expressly covers salaries and similar remuneration. Ordinary foreign-client remote income may instead fall under business or professional-income rules and requires classification advice.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered employees, CNSS is 21.65% of salary: 16.40% employer and 5.25% employee, on an annual salary base capped at XOF 6,000,000. An additional 0.5% ANPE levy is employer-only.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The schedule is monthly and marginal. The dashboard's 35% figure is the top screening rate, not the effective tax burden.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly taxable income up to XOF 25,000
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal monthly bracket; USD conversion omitted because no authoritative research-date exchange-rate source was captured.
