taxation_system.notes: The tax code is official and current through the 2025 finance-law update. Application to foreign remote work remains hypothetical because no corresponding immigration status or official income classification was found.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime: Niger has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. A person otherwise lawfully present and working may face ordinary progressive income tax and, if an employee, payroll contributions.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; ordinary tax rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 35% top marginal employment-income rate; effective tax depends on brackets and classification.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Habitual residence or fiscal domicile rather than a confirmed universal 183-day rule in the provisions reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: No route-specific rule is published. Salary for duties performed while habitually resident in Niger may be taxable, while foreign-client freelance receipts may require treatment under business or professional-income provisions.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the 2025 General Tax Code.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered employees contribute 5.25%; employers contribute 16.40% plus a 0.5% ANPE levy. No fixed or percentage-based contribution rule was established for an independently registered foreign remote worker.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad-specific fixed payment; ordinary event-based state charges apply where relevant
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based for covered employees; the inspected CNSS materials do not publish a fixed freelancer minimum applicable to this hypothetical foreign-remote-worker scenario.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee applies because Niger has no confirmed digital-nomad route. Ordinary statutory charges in the 2025 General Tax Code are: foreign-passport visa stamp duty of XOF 20,000 for a stay up to one month, XOF 40,000 for more than one and up to six months, or XOF 70,000 for more than six months and up to one year, subject to reciprocity; for a non-ECOWAS residence carnet, XOF 50,000 on issue or renewal plus XOF 20,000 for the annual visa; and XOF 50,000 stamp duty for an authorization allowing a foreign person or entity to conduct an industrial, commercial, artisanal, or liberal activity. The labour regulations separately require remuneration for the initial or renewed foreign-worker contract visa, but delegate the amount to a joint ministerial order that was not located. Consular application charges also vary by post: the Niger Embassy in Türkiye lists EUR 60 for one month and EUR 120 for three months from 15 September 2025, while the Niger Embassy in Senegal lists XOF 35,000, XOF 60,000, and XOF 100,000 for one-, three-, and six-month visas respectively. Applicants must confirm with the responsible post which consular and statutory charges are cumulative.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Naturalization sources list a XOF 25,000 chancery duty and XOF 1,500 municipal tax; these are nationality-application costs, not monthly remote-worker taxes. No fixed digital-nomad tax or mandatory nomad-insurance payment applies because no such route exists.
fixed_payments.notes: The fee gap is narrowed but not eliminated: statutory visa, residence-carnet, annual-visa, and foreign professional-authorization duties are published, while the separate labour-contract visa remuneration is legally required but its current amount is absent from the inspected decree and official consular fee pages. None of these charges creates or proves eligibility for a remote-worker immigration category.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe day-count threshold was established. Tourist status prohibits professional activity unless later authorized, so a short stay does not create a confirmed lawful remote-work solution.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Potential exposure to ordinary Niger tax exists if habitually resident or fiscally domiciled, but immigration authorization and income classification must be resolved first.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The residence decree contemplates separately authorized non-salaried professional activity, but no current source establishes that visitor entry followed by sole-proprietor registration authorizes foreign-client remote work or guarantees residence. Business and tax registration should not be treated as immigration permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Ordinary tax and statutory fee rules are supportable. Their application to foreign remote work remains hypothetical because no corresponding immigration status, application process, or income classification was confirmed.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-work route exists. The general decree provides a two-year renewable residence permit, but no current application channel or decision timeline was found for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The decree provides renewable two-year residence permits but does not establish a distinct permanent-residence category or a fixed conversion period. The foreign-worker contract authorization is limited to two years plus one renewal.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality rules use habitual residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence prerequisite, so an after-PR interval cannot be stated.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General minimum habitual residence before discretionary naturalization, not a timeline from a remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The code states that a naturalization decree must issue within one year of the request or the request is considered rejected. This is a statutory decision window, not a verified current average.

key_conditions.value: Naturalization is discretionary and requires at least 10 years of habitual residence, good character, supporting civil-status and residence evidence, medical and criminal-record documents, fees, and an administrative investigation. No standardized language test or detailed absence-counting rule was identified. Current law permits dual nationality, but the applicant's original-country law must also be checked.
key_conditions.notes: Lawful residence under an appropriate status remains essential; no qualifying remote-worker route was confirmed.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Current sources describe at least three years of legally valid marriage, uninterrupted marital community, and at least three years of habitual and lawful residence in Niger.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage to a Nigerien spouse can count, provided it is legally recognized and the required three-year marriage, continuous marital community, and Niger residence conditions are documented.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage alone does not confer citizenship automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: The foreign spouse must show a legally valid marriage, continuous affective and material marital community, three years of habitual and lawful Niger residence, good conduct, sufficient means, social integration, and that the Nigerien spouse retained nationality. Authorities may investigate the application; separation, sham marriage, false evidence, or loss of marital community can cause refusal or later consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The 2014 reform made the marriage route gender-neutral. This is a citizenship acceleration, not confirmation of permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Niger applies double jus soli: a child born in Niger is Nigerien when a direct first-degree parent was also born in Niger. Foundlings and children of unknown parents have protective rules. Birth in Niger alone to two known foreign-born parents is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Niger to two known foreign-born migrant parents does not automatically acquire Nigerien nationality solely by birthplace. Citizenship may arise if the double-jus-soli condition is met or under anti-statelessness or foundling provisions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent residence of a parent is not stated as an independent birthright condition.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Nigerien mother or father generally acquires Nigerien nationality by descent once filiation is legally established.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2014 reform removed gender discrimination in transmission through a Nigerien parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. No current official source reviewed establishes an automatic permanent-residence or citizenship grant to the foreign father solely because the child is Nigerien.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The entry-and-stay decree does not state a parent-of-citizen residence entitlement. Any family-based administrative practice requires direct confirmation.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship benefit. If the mother is Nigerien, the child can be Nigerien by descent, but the foreign father must independently qualify for residence or citizenship, including potentially through marriage if applicable.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage of a citizen child should not be confused with automatic status for the parent.

rank.notes: Dynamic Passport Index power rank checked 2026-08-15. The January 2026 Henley snapshot separately ranked Niger 80th with a score of 55, illustrating index and date differences.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 classification.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is designated a working language alongside French under the 2025 Charter, but that legal label does not establish broad everyday English availability. French remains important in administration and formal documentation, while Hausa is the national language.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English-only living and administration should be expected to be difficult outside limited professional settings. The 2023 UN core document reflects the superseded constitutional position under which French was official.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No official or reliable source reviewed identified Russian or Ukrainian as institutionally supported languages. Neither should be expected to work for routine administration or daily life.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical inference from the Charter's language designations, not a measured proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate midpoint of the source's broad US$90–120 monthly range, corresponding to XOF 55,000–75,000. It is a screening estimate, not an official national mean.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ILOSTAT provides wage datasets and Niger's INS publishes employment and informal-sector survey materials, but the inspected pages do not publish a current Niger-wide median monthly wage figure.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the XOF 42,000 statutory monthly minimum effective 1 January 2026. This is a wage floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Dashboard midpoint of a secondary source's approximate US$90–120 range; substantial informal employment makes the figure uncertain.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the current ILOSTAT topic page nor the inspected INS survey landing page publishes a current national median monthly wage figure.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The labour profile and INS survey page do not publish a meaningful national maximum or reliable upper wage-distribution bound.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory SMIG effective 1 January 2026 for covered parapublic and private workers and auxiliaries governed by the Labour Code and collective agreement.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Secondary labour-market profile estimate; not an official INS national mean and potentially unrepresentative of informal and seasonal work.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected ILOSTAT and INS pages do not state a current national median monthly amount.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected sources do not define or publish a defensible national maximum wage.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly statutory gross wage floor and approximate economy-wide monthly salary range; formal and informal coverage is incomplete
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 profile; SMIG effective 2026-01-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: The XOF 42,000 figure is authoritative as a statutory minimum. The average is a reputable secondary estimate and should not be treated as an official mean; median and maximum remain null because the named wage and survey sources do not publish those current national statistics.

cost_of_living_note.value: Niger's statistics institute publishes consumer-price index series, but the inspected source does not provide a national monthly living-cost budget for a remote worker. Salary figures alone should not be used as a cost-of-living estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: CPI measures price change, not the amount a particular household needs each month.

settlement_track.summary: Only an employer-filed, pre-approved foreign-worker contract route was confirmed. It is capped at four years, anticipates replacement by a Nigerien worker, and does not provide a verified independent remote-work-to-settlement path.
settlement_track.notes: The general nationality code permits a discretionary naturalization application after at least 10 years of habitual residence; it does not require a separately identified permanent-resident status. The entry-and-stay decree provides a two-year renewable residence permit, requires an appropriate ministerial authorization for non-salaried professional activity, conditions renewal on continued resources or activity, and permits withdrawal after more than six months abroad or more than three months without employment or resources. Those rules show how lawful residence can exist in principle, but the current official sources inspected do not establish that ordinary foreign-client remote work is an authorized non-salaried activity, publish a filing route for it, or confirm that the employer-contract visa capped at four years can bridge to ten years of habitual residence. Accordingly, the rejected employment route is not a verified settlement track; any future claim based on separately authorized self-employment requires case-specific confirmation from the competent ministry and immigration police.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign contract or foreign-source income alone is insufficient. The confirmed salaried procedure requires a Niger employment contract and employer-filed approval before entry. Although the residence decree contemplates ministerial authorization for non-salaried professional activity, the inspected current sources do not show that ordinary foreign-client remote work qualifies or provide an application route.

data.notes: The negative selection conclusion is supported by the official employer-led work rules, the prohibition on tourist professional activity without later authorization, and the absence of a dedicated remote-worker application channel. The focused pass established ordinary visa, residence-carnet, annual-visa, and professional-authorization duties and clarified the general renewable residence-permit framework. The separate labour-contract visa fee remains unpublished in the inspected sources because the implementing decree delegates its amount to another ministerial order. Median and maximum national wages and an automatic family-based status for a citizen child's foreign father also remain null because the named current sources do not publish those facts.

data.selection_summary: Nigeria has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker visa. Its N4A Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa is a potentially useful independent skills-based alternative: no Nigerian employer or job offer appears in the published requirements, and it grants a five-year renewable residence permit within the permanent-residence visa category. However, it requires an Industrial Training Fund recommendation based on Nigeria's skills-gap assessment, so a software degree and foreign contract alone do not establish eligibility. This is therefore a partial skilled-residence option, not a normal remote-work match.

visa_application.title: Nigerian Immigration Service regular visa application portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official regular-visa portal linked by the Nigeria Immigration Service. Prospective N4A applicants should first verify how to obtain the mandatory Industrial Training Fund skills-gap recommendation; the public route page does not provide a separate ITF application link.

best_routes.route_name: Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa – N4A

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official N4A requirements publish no minimum income or salary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published minimum income threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility turns on specialized expertise and an ITF skills-gap recommendation, not a stated naira income amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; ITF skills-gap recommendation required
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of a stated threshold does not make eligibility automatic. The Industrial Training Fund must recommend the applicant based on Nigeria's economic skills needs.

income_proof_months.notes: The official requirements do not state a prescribed income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Specialized knowledge or technical expertise relevant to Nigeria's current or future economic needs.
Recommendation based on the Nigerian Skills Gap Assessment under the Industrial Training Fund.
Vetted academic/professional credentials, CV and documented skills profile.
Valid passport, photograph and police report or clearance from the country of residence.
Online application followed by embassy enrolment or processing under the current NIS procedure.

initial_validity.value: Entry visa valid for 90 days; five-year multiple-entry residence permit
initial_validity.notes: The NIS page calls N4A a Permanent Residence Visa but publishes a five-year permit rather than indefinite residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewable after five years if continuing requirements are met
extension_rules.notes: The NIS renewal FAQ confirms that N4A is renewable, but does not publish a guaranteed renewal test or filing window.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: N4A grants residence directly and is listed under the Permanent Residence Visa category; no preliminary temporary-residence period is stated.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The official terminology is unusual because the resulting residence permit has a five-year duration.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Directly classified by NIS as a Permanent Residence Visa, with a five-year renewable residence permit.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is not necessarily indefinite permanent residence. Applicants should verify the legal effects of the NIS 'Permanent Residence Visa' classification before relying on it.

path_to_citizenship.value: A lawful resident may separately seek discretionary naturalisation after satisfying Nigeria's constitutional residence and integration conditions, including 15 years of qualifying residence under either prescribed residence pattern.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is not automatic. The Constitution also requires good character, domicile intent, community acceptance and assimilation, a useful contribution to Nigeria, and the oath of allegiance.

best_routes.notes: This is a residence-oriented skilled/qualification route and may be relevant to a software engineer, but it is not designed around continued work for a foreign client. The published requirements do not list a Nigerian employer or job offer, yet the mandatory ITF skills-gap recommendation introduces a selective national-needs assessment. Application-level confirmation is essential.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No salary floor is published on the route page.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published salary threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A Nigerian employment contract and employer quota are mandatory regardless of salary.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; Nigerian employer and expatriate quota required
income_requirement_display.notes: The disqualifying condition is sponsorship, not income.

income_proof_months.notes: No income history period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Confirmed employment contract with a Nigerian employer holding an approved expatriate quota.
Employer accepts immigration responsibility and sponsors the application.
Educational certificates, CV and police clearance or other requested security documentation.

initial_validity.value: 90-day entry visa followed by a two-year renewable residence/work permit
initial_validity.notes: Work is restricted to the sponsoring employer.

extension_rules.value: The resulting two-year residence/work permit is renewable under the sponsoring arrangement.
extension_rules.notes: The 90-day entry visa itself is not extendable.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Regularisation or e-CERPAC processing produces a temporary residence/work permit tied to the sponsoring employer.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion to permanent residence was confirmed for an ordinary sponsored employee.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Separate NIS permanent categories have their own eligibility requirements.

path_to_citizenship.value: Long-term lawful residence may eventually support a separate naturalisation application, but this does not make R2A independently usable for the profile.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The route remains rejected because Nigerian-employer sponsorship is mandatory.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a Nigerian employer, approved expatriate quota and employer sponsorship, and employment is limited to that sponsor.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is stated.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published income threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: An invitation from a Nigerian company is required.

income_requirement_display.value: No published threshold; short business visit only
income_requirement_display.notes: This visa cannot be used for employment or residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Invitation and corporate registration evidence from a Nigerian host company.
Return ticket and accommodation or host address.
Activities limited to meetings, negotiations, conferences, marketing and similar business-visitor purposes; employment is prohibited.

initial_validity.value: Valid for 90 days for a single stay of up to 30 days
initial_validity.notes: The visa is non-extendable.

extension_rules.value: Not extendable

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a short business-visitor visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None for ordinary business visitors
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Only applicants independently satisfying another permanent category could change route.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from this visitor status

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a non-extendable visitor status, prohibits employment and does not create a qualifying settlement track.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: These routes use capital-investment requirements, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Not applicable; substantial retained investment capital required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: For example, N3C requires USD 1 million to USD 10 million of imported and retained investor capital.

income_requirement_display.value: Investment route; N3C requires USD 1,000,000–10,000,000 retained capital
income_requirement_display.notes: Thresholds vary by investor subclass and are capital requirements, not income tests.

income_proof_months.notes: The requirement concerns verified imported and retained capital rather than recurring income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying investment capital retained in Nigeria; N3C requires USD 1 million to USD 10 million.
Nigerian business registration, business plan and proof of investment.
Relevant prior business-visa history and security clearance for the examined N3C category.

initial_validity.value: Varies by category; N3C provides a six-year multiple-entry residence permit after a 90-day-valid entry visa
initial_validity.notes: Other investor subclasses have different capital and duration rules.

extension_rules.value: Investor visas are generally renewable while continuing investment conditions are met.
extension_rules.notes: Subclass-specific renewal requirements must be checked.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable to N3C; it is classified as a permanent-residence category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct residence under an NIS Permanent Residence Visa investor subclass.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The permit can nevertheless have a fixed multi-year duration.

path_to_citizenship.value: Some investors may separately apply after meeting constitutional residence and other naturalisation conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is discretionary and not automatic from investment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the profile does not include substantial investment or operation of a Nigerian enterprise. This is not an ordinary freelance or foreign-contract remote-work route.

summary.value: The N4A Highly Skilled Immigrant Visa is an independently filed, qualification/skills-based Permanent Residence Visa. The published requirements do not list a Nigerian employer or job offer, but an ITF recommendation based on Nigeria's skills-gap needs is mandatory. It is therefore a selective partial match rather than a normal degree-only or remote-worker route.
summary.notes: The official page does not explain ITF recommendation procedures or confirm that every software specialty appears on the skills-gap assessment.

tax_residency_rule.value: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, an individual is resident if any listed connection applies, including Nigerian domicile, a permanent domestic-use home, habitual abode, substantial economic and immediate-family ties, or at least 183 days in a 12-month period including annual leave or temporary absence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can therefore arise before the 183-day threshold through other statutory connections.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Annual chargeable income is taxed progressively from 0% to 25%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the statutory employee pension contribution rate on monthly emoluments under the contributory pension scheme; the employer minimum is 10%, producing 18% total. Application to a foreign employer without Nigerian payroll or to a self-employed N4A holder requires professional confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment for an N4A foreign-contract worker was established. NIS publishes substantial permit-related fees for some CERPAC employment categories, but the reviewed pages did not establish an N4A-specific recurring fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker tax concession was found. N4A holders fall under ordinary individual tax rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligible documented pension, health-insurance, housing-fund and other statutory deductions may reduce chargeable income.

taxes.caveats: Nigeria taxes resident individuals on income, gains and profits wherever arising, whether remitted to Nigeria or not. Employment duties performed in Nigeria can also create Nigerian-source income issues for a nonresident. Contract classification, treaty relief, foreign tax credits, payroll obligations and the applicability of pension or health contributions require Nigerian professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive worldwide taxation for resident individuals, with annual chargeable-income rates of 0%, 15%, 18%, 21%, 23% and 25%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence can arise through domicile, an available permanent home, habitual abode, substantial economic/family ties, or 183 days in a 12-month period including specified absences.
taxation_system.income_scope: A resident individual's income, gains and profits are taxable in Nigeria wherever they arise and whether or not remitted. Employment income can also be Nigerian-source where duties are performed in Nigeria under the statutory conditions.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No N4A, digital-nomad or ordinary inbound remote-worker tax holiday was found.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered employees, minimum contributory pension rates are 8% employee and 10% employer of monthly emoluments. Applicability to foreign payroll and independent contracting is structure-dependent.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 25% is the top marginal rate. It applies only to annual chargeable income above NGN 50 million after allowable deductions; it is not an estimated effective tax rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First NGN 800,000 of annual chargeable income
tax_brackets.notes: No USD conversion is supplied because a reliable research-date official exchange rate was not captured.
Top marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 applies from 2026 and the Joint Revenue Board issued implementing PIT Guidelines in 2026. Individual facts still depend on residence, source, deductions, treaty position and work classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Nigeria has no dedicated digital-nomad route. A resident N4A skilled-visa holder is screened under ordinary Nigerian personal income tax rules, with a 25% top marginal rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Ordinary resident individual taxation for an N4A skilled resident; no digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 0%–25%; 25% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence may arise from specified personal/economic connections or 183 days in a 12-month period; 183 days is not the only test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income, gains and profits of a resident individual are taxable whether or not remitted to Nigeria.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found for N4A holders or foreign-contract remote workers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered employment generally carries an 8% employee and 10% employer pension contribution. Foreign-employer payroll and independent-contractor treatment require individual confirmation.

fixed_payments.status: No universal N4A recurring fixed payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potential 8% employee and 10% employer pension contributions where the contributory scheme applies; health and housing-fund deductions depend on actual participation and status.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: An N4A-specific visa or residence-card fee was not established from the reviewed public route pages. NIS should be checked at filing because fees may be nationality- and category-dependent.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax was found. Registration, withholding, VAT or business obligations may arise if the individual conducts a Nigerian trade or registers a local business.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of a confirmed fixed amount should not be read as a fee exemption.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying fewer than 183 days does not automatically prevent residence because domicile, a permanent home, habitual abode, or substantial economic/family ties can independently qualify. Work physically performed in Nigeria can also create Nigerian-source employment income.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide foreign salary or professional income is potentially taxable under the ordinary progressive 0%–25% schedule, subject to deductions, treaty relief and foreign-tax-credit analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A self-employed taxable person may need a Tax ID, direct assessment and annual filing. Local business, VAT, withholding and pension consequences depend on the actual legal structure.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a tax screening summary, not a filing calculation. The immigration route itself is not a digital-nomad program.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: N4A provides residence directly and is officially placed in the Permanent Residence Visa category rather than requiring preliminary temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: NIS labels N4A a Permanent Residence Visa, although the published permit is five years and renewable rather than indefinite.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation generally requires either 15 continuous years immediately before application, or continuous residence during the preceding 12 months plus at least 15 aggregate years during the preceding 20 years. It remains discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest statutory residence measure identified for ordinary naturalisation; approval and processing add additional time and are not guaranteed.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed NIS citizenship guidance and constitutional materials do not publish a representative processing-time statistic for successful naturalisation applications.

key_conditions.value: Full age and capacity, good character, intention to be domiciled in Nigeria, acceptance and assimilation into the local community, capacity to contribute to Nigeria's advancement and wellbeing, the prescribed residence history, and the oath of allegiance. Naturalisation is discretionary, and constitutional dual-citizenship restrictions apply to citizens other than by birth.
key_conditions.notes: Physical presence and residence evidence should be maintained throughout the long qualifying period.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution states no fixed marriage-duration threshold for citizenship by registration. The benefit is gender-specific: it applies to a woman who is or has been married to a Nigerian citizen.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing or even past marriage can make a foreign woman eligible to seek citizenship by registration, subject to presidential satisfaction regarding good character, domicile intent and the oath. A spouse of a Nigerian citizen may also apply for the N1A permanent-residence category. The Constitution does not provide the same registration shortcut to a foreign husband.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not itself confer citizenship automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must prove a genuine, legally valid marriage and separately satisfy the applicable immigration or citizenship procedure. Registration is discretionary, and false documents or a sham marriage can cause refusal, loss of status and legal consequences. The constitutional citizenship-by-registration wording is expressly limited to women married to Nigerian citizens.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The reviewed Constitution and current NIS materials do not prescribe a fixed cohabitation period.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Nigeria alone does not confer citizenship. A post-independence child born in Nigeria is a citizen by birth if a parent or grandparent is Nigerian.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Nigeria to two foreign parents does not automatically become Nigerian merely by birthplace, unless a Nigerian parent or grandparent connection independently exists.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The reviewed constitutional provisions establish citizenship through Nigerian parentage or grandparentage rather than birthplace alone; exceptional statelessness questions require separate legal review.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Nigerian by birth when either parent is a Nigerian citizen, including where the father is foreign and the mother is Nigerian.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The Constitution also recognizes a Nigerian grandparent connection for a child born in Nigeria.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Nigerian citizen child does not automatically grant the foreign parent residence, permanent residence or citizenship. The public NIS permanent-residence list includes spouses of Nigerian citizens, not a general parent-of-citizen-child category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The 2026 NIS service standards, current permanent-residence category list and Immigration Act 2015 text were checked. They provide a spouse-of-Nigerian-citizen permit and other expressly defined categories, but publish no parent-of-Nigerian-citizen-child visa or residence entitlement. The Act gives the immigration authority general discretion to issue residence permits subject to conditions; that discretion is not a child-based right. A foreign parent must qualify through a separate category such as spouse, employment, skills, investment or another individually applicable status.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically acquire Nigerian citizenship or permanent residence through his Nigerian child. If he is married to the Nigerian mother, he may investigate spouse residence, but the Constitution's marriage-based citizenship-registration shortcut is written for foreign women, not foreign husbands.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The inspected current NIS visa catalogue contains no automatic or father-specific parent-of-citizen residence category.

rank.notes: Nigeria ranked 90th among 199 passports in the July 2026 Henley release.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score counts destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance and can include visa-on-arrival access; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The reviewed Henley material does not publish a Nigeria-specific count limited to destinations requiring a visa in advance, so it is not inferred by subtraction.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The current Henley ranking does not provide a separate Nigeria-specific visa-on-arrival/eTA breakdown in the inspected material.

passport.notes: Henley tracks 227 destinations and updates its ranking periodically. Rank and access score should be rechecked immediately before use.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for professional and remote work: English is Nigeria's official and common national working language, while Nigerian Pidgin is also widespread in many urban areas.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Infrastructure reliability, especially electricity and internet quality, varies materially by city and accommodation.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low for everyday administration and business. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official or broadly documented working language in Nigeria; English is the practical default.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The reviewed official language source documents English as the practical national working language and does not identify Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current NBS sources collect wage amounts or broad earnings bands, but none publishes a weighted national mean monthly worker wage. Respondents report hourly, daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly or annual pay, so a defensible monthly mean would require record-level normalization and survey weights; it is not inferred from unweighted catalogue case counts.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No inspected NBS publication reports a weighted national median monthly worker wage. The available pages are metadata or unweighted case distributions across mixed pay periods, not a published population median, and no USD conversion is attempted.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: NGN 70,000 is the statutory monthly minimum wage, but no reliable official research-date USD exchange rate was captured, so no USD conversion is invented.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official weighted national average monthly salary is published in the inspected NBS labour-force, household-panel or time-use materials; USD conversion is therefore inapplicable.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official weighted national median monthly salary is published in the inspected sources; USD conversion is therefore inapplicable.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official earnings-band metadata ends in an open-ended NGN 500,000-and-above category and does not publish a finite national salary maximum, so no USD maximum exists to convert.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the statutory national minimum wage, not an observed minimum or average salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No weighted national monthly mean salary is published in the inspected NBS sources. The labour-force and time-use catalogues disclose broad wage bands and explicitly warn that their displayed case counts are not population summary statistics; the household-panel dictionary identifies a raw naira earnings variable but publishes no national aggregate. Mixed reporting periods and survey weights would have to be handled using microdata, so a mean is not invented.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No weighted national monthly median salary is published in the inspected NBS materials. The visible wage-band case counts combine hourly, daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly and annual responses and are expressly not population estimates; calculating a median would require record-level pay-period normalization, survey weights and treatment of the open-ended top band.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A finite national maximum is neither a stable labour-market statistic nor published by the inspected official sources. The NBS banded data top-codes earnings at NGN 500,000 or above, while the household-panel dictionary exposes respondent-level earnings rather than an official ceiling; NGN 500,000 is therefore not reported as a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory national minimum wage plus an audit of current NBS labour-force, time-use and household-panel sources; no weighted national mean, median or finite maximum is published
average_citizen_salary.period: Statutory minimum current as reviewed on 2026-08-15; official earnings materials cover 2023 through 2025 and catalogue updates through March 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: Only the statutory NGN 70,000 monthly minimum is numeric. Current NBS sources collect respondent-level earnings or ranges, but the inspected publications do not provide population-weighted national monthly mean, median or maximum salary figures. Their catalogue case counts cannot be used as national statistics without microdata analysis.

cost_of_living_note.value: No sufficiently current, official national cost-of-living benchmark suitable for this record was established. Costs vary sharply between Lagos, Abuja and other locations.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected household-panel catalogue describes underlying expenditure and welfare data but does not publish a single current national cost-of-living amount suitable for this field.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: N4A is not a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract route. It is usable only if the applicant passes the selective Nigerian skills-gap and ITF recommendation process.
settlement_track.summary: N4A is officially a renewable five-year Permanent Residence Visa and lawful residence can feed into Nigeria's general 15-year discretionary naturalisation framework. The settlement track is credible for an applicant who independently qualifies as highly skilled, but it is only a partial profile match because foreign remote work and a university degree alone are insufficient.
settlement_track.notes: NIS terminology calls a fixed-duration five-year permit 'permanent residence.' Naturalisation remains discretionary and requires extensive residence, integration and character evidence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No ordinary foreign-employer or foreign-client remote-work route was found. N4A eligibility depends on nationally relevant specialized skills and an ITF recommendation, not on the applicant's foreign contract.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field pass preserves the N4A partial skilled-residence conclusion and resolves the flagged fields without inventing salary figures. Current NIS materials disclose no parent-of-Nigerian-citizen-child residence category or automatic parental status. Current NBS sources collect wage amounts or bands but do not publish a weighted national monthly mean, median or finite maximum; those fields are precise nulls, while the statutory minimum remains. At least 20 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected during this pass, including more than five URLs absent from the previous source set.

data.selection_summary: No current independent digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, freelance, self-employed, or qualification-based residence route was found. Current government guidance says every visit requires a visa, independent travelers need a sponsor and Foreign Ministry permission, business travelers need a North Korean organizational sponsor, foreigners must register, and travel and internet access are severely restricted. The applicant’s ordinary foreign-client software work therefore has no confirmed lawful immigration or settlement route; sanctions and banking restrictions create additional material risk.

visa_application.notes: No public DPRK online visa or immigration portal was identified. Article 20 of the reviewed DPRK Immigration Law says foreigners apply through a DPRK diplomatic or consular mission and that personal-purpose applicants must attach immigration-agency travel consent. Current French, German, and Chinese government directories provide mission contact details but no online filing channel. UK and Canadian guidance likewise direct applicants to a DPRK mission and describe prior approval from Pyongyang. Accordingly, application_url remains null and application_url_type retains the schema unavailable-page enum: embassy contact is the documented process, not a direct public application URL.

rejected_routes.route_name: Sponsored business, work, or other approved foreigner stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed entry rules base admission on purpose, sponsorship, and state approval rather than a published income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed entry rules do not prescribe a KPW income threshold for sponsored foreigner stays.

income_requirement_display.value: No public independent-income route or threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Entry depends on governmental approval, purpose, and sponsorship rather than a published income test.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period applies because this is not an income-qualified immigration route.

key_requirements.requirement: A visa is required; independent travelers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs.
Business travelers generally need sponsorship by a North Korean organization and Foreign Ministry permission.
Canadian guidance separately lists business visas, work permits, and student visas as required and says issuance follows approval from Pyongyang.
Foreigners staying more than 24 hours must register through the authorities, host organization, or hotel.
Residence requires approval of the institution concerned, and movement or a change of residence is controlled through immigration procedures.

initial_validity.value: Purpose-specific and discretionary; no generally published residence term
initial_validity.notes: The reviewed general immigration law and current government guidance do not establish a standard temporary-residence duration for an ordinary sponsored foreigner.

extension_rules.value: Article 25 of the reviewed DPRK Immigration Law requires an expired foreigner immigration certificate to be extended, but it does not publish eligibility criteria, a filing deadline, documents, fees, the extension period, or a renewal entitlement for an ordinary sponsored stay. Separate 1994 rules limited to the former Free Economic and Trade Zone required stay or residence certificate applications 10 days before expiry with an inviting-body document.
extension_rules.notes: The zone-specific ten-day procedure cannot be generalized to sponsored stays elsewhere in North Korea.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Immigration Law recognizes long-term-stay and residence registration certificates, but accessible materials do not establish an independent application route, objective qualification rules, or a defined remote-worker residence permit. Admission and residence remain tied to institutional or governmental approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Institutional approval is not equivalent to a generally available remote-worker residence program.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed immigration and nationality materials do not publish an ordinary permanent-residence eligibility period, independent application procedure, or conversion entitlement from a sponsored stay.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A residence registration certificate mentioned in the Immigration Law should not be equated with a transparent permanent-residence category.

path_to_citizenship.value: A foreign citizen or stateless person may petition for DPRK nationality, but the reviewed law does not publish approval criteria, required residence, processing time, or an entitlement arising from sponsored stay.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is a discretionary nationality petition, not a confirmed residence-to-citizenship track.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant cannot independently establish eligibility and no ordinary foreign-contract remote-work authorization is identified. A North Korean sponsor or host is required for the entry situations described; that sponsor is not necessarily an employer, so local_employer_required remains null. Severe communications, movement, payment, and sanctions constraints also make remote software work impractical.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitor entry is not an income-qualified route, so no monthly USD threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Visitor entry is not an income-qualified route, so no KPW threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; visitor status is not a residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Admission depends on the approved visit, sponsor or tour arrangements, and government permission rather than income.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is prescribed because visitor entry is not an income-based route.

key_requirements.requirement: Tourists normally travel only as part of an organized or official tour; other independent travelers require sponsorship and government permission.
A visa is generally required for travel; the reviewed Immigration Law also recognizes state-issued tourist certificates and any applicable visa-free agreement.
Travel inside the country is severely restricted and an official guide may be required.

initial_validity.value: Visit-specific; current government guidance and the reviewed general Immigration Law do not publish a standard tourist stay period
initial_validity.notes: The validity shown on the issued visa or tourist certificate controls the approved visit.

extension_rules.value: Article 25 of the reviewed DPRK Immigration Law requires an expired foreigner immigration certificate to be extended, but it does not publish eligibility criteria, filing deadline, documents, fee, extension length, or a general tourist-extension entitlement. Separate 1994 rules for the former Free Economic and Trade Zone require stay or residence certificate extension applications 10 days before expiry with the certificate and an inviting-body document; those zone-specific rules cannot be generalized to an ordinary tourist visit.
extension_rules.notes: The existence of a certificate-extension requirement is established, but the accessible general law does not establish a standardized visitor-renewal procedure. Current government travel guidance warns that entry conditions are discretionary and can change at short notice.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No conversion from a tourist visa or tourist certificate to qualifying temporary residence is published. The Immigration Law separately recognizes long-term-stay and residence registration certificates, but it does not create a tourist-to-residence entitlement or application path.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Recognition of separate long-term certificates does not establish that a visitor can change status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed Immigration Law and nationality law do not create a conversion from visitor status to permanent residence or publish an ordinary permanent-residence eligibility procedure.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time therefore cannot be treated as qualifying permanent-residence time.

path_to_citizenship.value: The nationality law permits a foreigner to petition for nationality but creates no citizenship entitlement from a tourist or visitor stay and publishes no rule counting visitor time toward naturalization.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A discretionary nationality petition is separate from visitor status.

rejected_routes.notes: A visitor or tour visa is not a work authorization or qualifying residence path and cannot satisfy the citizenship-oriented selection criteria.

summary.value: Canadian government guidance confirms that a student visa is required, but the current sources reviewed do not establish an independently accessible student-residence application, duration, work rights, conversion to permanent residence, or degree-based migration route.
summary.notes: The existence of a required student visa must not be treated as evidence of a qualification-based settlement route.

tax_residency_rule.value: The available translated foreign-tax law says a foreign individual earning income inside the DPRK is taxable and a foreign individual staying or residing for more than one year is also taxed on income earned outside the DPRK.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The accessible compilation is old and no current DPRK tax-authority publication was identified; current application requires filing-level verification.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top screening rate from an older translated foreign-tax law. Remuneration was stated as taxable at 5%–30%; this is not an expected effective rate, and the current schedule could not be verified.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The reviewed foreign-tax compilation and current labor reporting do not publish a mandatory social-insurance contribution rate applicable to a foreign remote worker.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed legislation does not establish a fixed monthly USD-equivalent payment. It instead describes a percentage-based city-management tax.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or remote-worker tax regime is contained in the reviewed legislation. The older foreign-tax rules contain exemptions or credits based on intergovernmental agreements, foreign tax paid, certain bank interest, and tax-authority approval for wages received abroad.
special_tax_regimes.notes: These provisions do not create immigration eligibility, and their current operation is not documented by a current tax-authority source.

taxes.caveats: Tax evidence is materially weaker and older than the immigration evidence. The cited translated legislation targets foreign-invested businesses and foreign individuals and does not establish how an unauthorized foreign-client remote-work arrangement would be characterized. Sanctions, payment restrictions, nationality, contract structure, source-of-income rules, and any applicable treaty must be reviewed before relying on the figures.

taxation_system.value: Older translated foreign-tax legislation describes progressive personal tax of 5%–30% on remuneration, 20% on interest, dividends, qualifying lease income, intellectual-property royalties and management services, 25% on property-sale income, and a 1% city-management tax on a foreign resident’s monthly income. Foreign-source income becomes taxable after more than one year of stay or residence.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Worldwide-income taxation is described after more than one year of stay or residence; DPRK-source income is taxable without that one-year condition.
taxation_system.income_scope: DPRK-source income for foreign individuals, expanding to foreign-source income after more than one year under the older translated law.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Limited exemptions, treaty treatment, and foreign-tax deductions appear in the older foreign-individual tax rules.
taxation_system.social_security: The reviewed sources do not publish a current foreign-worker social-security rate.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The source gives only a 5%–30% range for remuneration and does not provide the thresholds needed to reconstruct brackets. The displayed 30% is therefore a top marginal screening rate, not an effective-rate estimate.
taxation_system.notes: The tax compilation reproduces older DPRK legislation and implementing regulations but is not a current tax-authority portal. Exact brackets, current KPW thresholds, administration, and enforceability remain unpublished in the current sources reviewed.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as an immigration route: no digital-nomad or lawful ordinary foreign-remote-worker status was identified. If a foreigner were otherwise lawfully present, older foreign-tax legislation could potentially tax DPRK-source remuneration at 5%–30% and foreign income after more than one year, but current treatment is not documented by a current tax-authority source.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; hypothetical foreign-individual taxation only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 5%–30% on remuneration under older translated law; 30% is a top screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Older law: foreign-source income becomes taxable after more than one year of stay or residence; temporary exits count toward the period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Older regulations describe quarterly payment on foreign income after the one-year threshold and allow a deduction for tax already paid abroad, subject to documentary proof.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: The reviewed immigration and tax sources contain no separate digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The reviewed sources do not publish a social-security rule for this nonexistent route. The older law describes a separate 1% city-management tax on a foreign resident’s monthly income.

fixed_payments.status: The reviewed legislation prescribes no fixed monthly payment for a digital nomad or foreign remote worker.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The reviewed sources publish neither a mandatory amount nor a percentage applicable to this nonexistent route.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: There is no public digital-nomad visa or residence-card fee; the current sources reviewed do not publish a generally applicable ordinary visa-fee schedule.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The older law describes a 1% city-management tax, which is percentage-based rather than fixed.
fixed_payments.notes: No defensible USD conversion is possible because the legislation is old and official and unofficial KPW exchange rates are not comparable.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: The older law still taxes income earned inside the DPRK. Whether foreign-client remote work would be treated as DPRK-source income is not specified, and the work itself lacks a confirmed immigration basis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: After more than one year, the older law would extend taxation to foreign income, but no ordinary remote-worker residence route permits reaching this scenario.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The reviewed sources contain no independent sole-proprietor or freelancer registration-and-residence route. Foreign-investment tax legislation should not be treated as evidence that ordinary self-employment is available.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section is a cautious hypothetical tax screen, not confirmation that remote work is permitted.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The reviewed sources do not provide an independent qualifying temporary-residence route or standardized eligibility timeline.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed immigration and nationality materials do not publish an ordinary permanent-residence conversion period.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Nationality law permits a petition but publishes no permanent-residence prerequisite or years-based naturalization entitlement.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The reviewed nationality law publishes no objective residence-to-citizenship timeline.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed nationality materials publish neither a statutory decision period nor a reliable typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: A foreign citizen or stateless person may petition for nationality, but the reviewed law does not state residence duration, language, integration, income, physical-presence, absence, renunciation, or processing criteria. Immigration residence itself requires institutional approval.
key_conditions.notes: The absence of published criteria does not imply that naturalization is readily available.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The reviewed nationality law provides no fixed marriage-based acceleration period.

existing_marriage_effect.value: DPRK nationality does not automatically change because of marriage, divorce, adoption, or dissolution of adoption. An existing marriage therefore does not itself confer nationality under the reviewed law.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The reviewed materials do not publish a separate spouse-residence or expedited-naturalization procedure.

requirements_and_risks.value: Any immigration stay remains subject to state and institutional approval, and nationality acquisition by a foreigner is petition-based and discretionary. The reviewed sources do not publish immigration-specific genuine-marriage adjudication rules or a marriage-based exception from visa, residence, or security controls.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Applicants must not infer that marriage bypasses immigration approval. The conclusion is limited to the legal materials accessible in English.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is mainly parent-based. Birth in the DPRK confers citizenship where one parent is a DPRK citizen and the child resides in the DPRK, where both resident parents are stateless, or where parents are unknown. Birth to two foreign-national parents is not broad jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in the DPRK to two foreign-national parents does not acquire citizenship solely by birthplace. A child born to two stateless parents residing in the DPRK does acquire citizenship, as does a foundling whose parents are unknown.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary case of two foreign-national migrant parents; the anti-statelessness and foundling exceptions are stated separately.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is a DPRK citizen and the child resides in DPRK territory, citizenship is acquired at birth. If the DPRK-citizen parent resides abroad and the other parent is foreign, the parents choose the child’s nationality; if no choice is declared within three months for a child under 14, DPRK citizenship applies.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The statute distinguishes the DPRK-resident and foreign-resident parent situations.

parent_benefit_summary.value: The reviewed immigration and nationality laws do not create automatic residence, permanent residence, or citizenship for a foreign parent merely because the child is a DPRK citizen.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The nationality law regulates the child’s nationality but does not create a parent-based residence entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically acquire DPRK nationality or residence through the child. If the mother is a DPRK citizen, the child may qualify under the parentage rules, but the father still requires separately approved immigration status and any nationality petition remains discretionary.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No published parent-of-citizen residence category or accelerated naturalization period appears in the reviewed sources.

passport.index_name: Passport Index 2026 (Arton Capital), with Henley Passport Index cross-check

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank displayed on 2026-08-15. Henley’s live July 2026 ranking separately placed North Korea 96th with a score of 36; methodologies differ.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s strictly visa-free category, not its broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 36 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 3 eTA destinations. The Passport Index mobility score is 47 when these are combined with 8 visa-free destinations.

passport.notes: Henley combines destinations accessible without a prior visa and reported North Korea at rank 96 with a score of 36 in the live July 2026 table. Arton Capital’s Passport Index is used for the requested category breakdown because it separately reports visa-free, visa-on-arrival, eTA, and visa-required counts.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Extremely poor. Government travel guidance reports severely restricted and monitored internet and communications, no network connectivity through an international SIM, and unreliable international communications. English may be used with designated guides or official hosts, but it does not make independent remote work practical.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The current sources reviewed do not publish a reliable nationwide English-proficiency statistic suitable for this scenario.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Not established as practical for ordinary daily life or remote work. Korean is the sole national language in DPRK reporting; Russian may have limited diplomatic or institutional use, but the reviewed sources do not support general Russian- or Ukrainian-language accessibility.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No current nationwide survey of Russian or Ukrainian use is available in the reviewed sources.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed human-rights and World Bank sources do not publish a credible, comparable national average monthly wage.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed sources do not publish a national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The 2024 human-rights report states that DPRK law does not provide a minimum wage and that reliable state-enterprise minimum-wage data are unavailable.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No defensible national mean can be derived: formal wages may be unpaid or partly in kind, and exchange-rate distortions prevent reliable USD conversion.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither source publishes a national median worker wage.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The report provides no meaningful national maximum or reliable wage-distribution endpoint.

min_salary_local_currency.value: DPRK law provides no statutory minimum wage
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This describes the legal minimum, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither source publishes a reliable national average in KPW.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither source publishes a reliable national median in KPW.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The report publishes no national maximum wage in KPW.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: No credible comparable national worker-salary statistic available
average_citizen_salary.period: Latest reliable wage statement reviewed: 2024 reporting; research date 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: The state controls formal employment and wages; wages may be paid partly in kind, wage nonpayment is reported, and unofficial-market exchange rates diverge sharply from official rates. Nulls are retained rather than presenting misleading USD estimates.

cost_of_living_note.value: The reviewed sources do not publish a reliable general resident cost-of-living index. Government travel guidance instead reports shortages of food, electricity, clean water, and medicines; foreigners generally use foreign currency, cannot rely on cards or ATMs, and may face high or arbitrary travel and permit charges.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Visitor-facing costs are not representative of citizen household living costs.
