settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status exists in the sources reviewed; visitor and sponsored entry cannot be treated as a settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: No active independent route exists for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. Although nationality law permits a foreigner to petition for nationality, no qualifying residence route, permanent-residence conversion, objective naturalization period, or entitlement from the reviewed sponsored stays is established.
settlement_track.notes: The correct classification remains no current route confirmed, rather than employer-only, because the reviewed material also describes official, diplomatic, humanitarian, student, tour, and other institution-approved stays that are not necessarily employment relationships.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The reviewed sources contain no dedicated remote-worker status, independent self-employment route, or visitor-to-self-employment legalization process. Sponsorship, state approval, restricted movement, severely constrained internet, and sanctions exposure are incompatible with the specified ordinary foreign-client arrangement.

data.notes: The negative immigration conclusion is supported by multiple current government sources, the reviewed DPRK Immigration Law, and DPRK-reported immigration provisions. Confidence is not high because North Korea has no transparent public immigration portal and accessible immigration, tax, residence, and nationality materials are incomplete or dated. Twenty-five distinct directly relevant canonical URLs were reviewed, including five new focused sources for the public application-channel and visitor-extension questions. Remaining nulls are retained where no defensible current figure, entitlement, or generally applicable rule is published.

data.selection_summary: North Macedonia has no current dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. Its Foreigners Law recognizes self-employment under employment residence, and the foreigner may lodge the application independently, but the route requires a locally registered hiring/business entity, an explanation of local hiring necessity, an Employment Agency opinion, and evidence of employment mediation; the public rules do not confirm that a solo business serving only foreign clients is accepted. Because that local-substance and labor-market framework is incompatible with treating an ordinary foreign contract as a confirmed route, North Macedonia is not valid for this selection. If a self-employed filing is nevertheless accepted, employment residence is generally renewable annually, is not excluded from the five-year permanent-residence rule, and seven years of lawful continuous residence can support naturalization.

visa_application.title: Guidelines and Procedure for Specific Rights (Requests) of Foreign Nationals
visa_application.notes: This is the Ministry of Interior's official residence-information page, not a direct online self-employment application. For an initial application from abroad, the Foreigners Law links the temporary-residence request to a long-stay visa D application at a North Macedonian diplomatic or consular post. No dedicated online self-employed or digital-nomad application channel was found.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for employment through self-employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The inspected law requires sufficient means of subsistence but does not publish a fixed self-employed monthly income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No numeric MKD subsistence benchmark or self-employment revenue floor was established from the inspected official materials.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient means of subsistence; no fixed public threshold found
income_requirement_display.notes: A filing-specific subsistence benchmark should be confirmed with the Ministry of Interior and Employment Agency.

income_proof_months.notes: The sources inspected do not prescribe a standard number of bank-statement or income-history months for self-employed applicants.

key_requirements.requirement: The foreigner may lodge the employment-residence application, but a positive Employment Agency opinion is mandatory.

The opinion file requires registration of the legal entity hiring the foreigner, proof of identity, an explanation of the need to hire the foreigner, and recent proof of an employment-mediation request. For self-employment, only the employment-contract and education-proof items are expressly omitted.
General residence conditions include sufficient subsistence, accommodation, medical insurance, the purpose-specific conditions, and no public-order, security, or public-health bar.
The activity must be registered locally and social-insurance obligations must be settled for renewal.
The residential address must be reported; accommodation providers report within 12 hours and other hosts within 48 hours.

initial_validity.value: Employment Agency opinion for the requested period, not exceeding 1 year; 6 months if no period is stated
initial_validity.notes: The residence decision follows the period supported by the Agency opinion.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for periods not exceeding 1 year while the residence purpose and conditions continue
extension_rules.notes: The renewal review includes employment registration and settlement of social-insurance obligations. Unjustified absence for more than one-quarter of the authorized period can prevent renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct combined temporary residence and work authorization after a positive Employment Agency opinion and Ministry of Interior approval
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant can lodge the request personally, but approval remains embedded in the local employment/self-employment system.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially after 5 consecutive years of qualifying temporary residence
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Ordinary employment is not among the excluded grounds. Permanent residence also requires stable resources, accommodation, insurance, good character, Macedonian-language ability, and compliance with the absence limit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential naturalization eligibility after at least 7 years of lawful continuous residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: Housing, permanent income, good character, Macedonian-language ability, security checks, and normally renunciation of the prior citizenship apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because the law does not establish a clean foreign-client freelancer route. Although self-employment is mentioned, the retained requirements for a locally registered entity, local hiring justification, employment mediation, quota/labor-market review, and Agency opinion mean that a foreign-client-only solo structure cannot be treated as confirmed ordinary remote work. A written pre-filing determination from both the Employment Agency and Ministry of Interior would be needed before relying on this route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employment residence with a North Macedonian employer

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration-specific salary threshold was established; employment and labor-law pay rules apply.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No separate permit salary floor was found in the inspected residence sources.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration-specific salary threshold established
income_requirement_display.notes: The statutory wage floor is an employment-law figure, not an independent immigration income route.

income_proof_months.notes: Not expressed as historical income months; the route instead requires an employment contract and Agency opinion.

key_requirements.requirement: North Macedonian hiring entity and signed employment contract
Positive Employment Agency opinion, quota availability, labor-market assessment, and recent employment-mediation request
Proof of appropriate education or vocational training

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: Six months if the application does not state an employment period.

extension_rules.value: Renewable in periods not exceeding 1 year while employment and residence conditions continue
extension_rules.notes: Employment registration and social-insurance compliance are reviewed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct employment temporary residence/work permit
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Approval requires the local-employer and Employment Agency process.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Normally eligible after 5 consecutive years of qualifying residence
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Ordinary employment residence is not listed among the excluded grounds.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization eligibility after at least 7 years of lawful continuous residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: Subject to all naturalization conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer, local employment contract, and labor-market process are required.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No active program or income threshold was found.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No active program or local-currency threshold was found.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—no current route confirmed
income_requirement_display.notes: The current enumerated residence purposes do not include a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker ground.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable because no active route was confirmed.

key_requirements.requirement: No stable official program rules or application channel were found.

initial_validity.notes: No active status exists in the sources inspected.

extension_rules.notes: No active status exists in the sources inspected.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad residence ground was found.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No route exists whose time could be assessed for permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No digital-nomad route exists to connect to naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Announcements or unofficial references to a digital-nomad concept do not amount to a currently open program. The law, current-amendment reference, public residence guidance, and application channels inspected did not establish one.

summary.value: A foreigner may obtain temporary residence for studies without a local employer, normally for one year and renewable while study conditions continue. It is not an independent skilled-worker route, does not authorize unrestricted ordinary foreign-contract work, and study residence is expressly excluded from permanent residence under the five-year rule.
summary.notes: A university degree already held by the applicant does not itself create a residence route. Scientific-research residence requires a hosting arrangement and is also excluded from the ordinary five-year permanent-residence rule.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is tax resident if they have a permanent home in North Macedonia or stay there for more than 183 days, continuously or intermittently, in any 12-month period. Treaty rules and the center of vital interests can alter the result for foreign individuals.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence-permit status and tax residence are separate. First-year and dual-residence cases require treaty-specific analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the flat personal-income-tax screening rate, not an expected all-in effective burden. Independent-activity tax is generally charged on net income.

social_contributions_percent.notes: From July through December 2026, the published statutory rates total 28.0%: pension/disability 19.9%, health 7.5%, occupational-injury health 0.5%, and unemployment 0.1%. Liability and the applicable base depend on registration and insured status.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate screening estimate only: 28% of the published 2026 minimum contribution base of MKD 34,570 is about MKD 9,680, or roughly USD 179 using an approximately MKD 54/USD reference rate. This is not a universal freelancer bill; category, insurance status, treaty coverage, and the actual assessment base require accountant confirmation.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, remittance-basis, non-dom, or inbound-worker tax holiday was found. Resident foreign freelance and employment income is reportable under the ordinary system.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign tax may generally be credited only up to the domestic 10% amount when supporting official evidence is supplied.

taxes.caveats: The tax outcome depends on whether the person is tax resident, whether services performed physically in North Macedonia create North Macedonian-source income before residency, whether the person registers a sole proprietorship or company, deductible business expenses, social-insurance coverage, VAT status, and the applicable double-tax treaty. The calculated minimum contribution amount is a screening estimate, not individualized advice.

taxation_system.value: Flat 10% personal income tax on taxable income, with worldwide taxable income reportable by residents and North Macedonian-source income taxable for nonresidents.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home in North Macedonia or more than 183 days in any 12-month period, subject to treaty and center-of-vital-interests analysis.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: domestic and foreign taxable income. Nonresidents: income sourced in North Macedonia.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or general inbound-remittance exemption found.
taxation_system.social_security: Current July–December 2026 published rates total 28.0%. Local self-employment can trigger mandatory contributions, with a 2026 minimum calculation base of MKD 34,570 and a self-employed maximum base of MKD 829,692.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 10% is a flat PIT rate, not a top progressive bracket and not the total burden after social contributions.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable personal income generally; no progressive threshold established
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment, freelance/foreign work income, and net independent-activity income unless a specific exemption applies
tax_brackets.notes: Independent-activity income is generally calculated as revenue less allowable expenditure.

taxation_system.notes: Official July 2026 contribution changes supersede older rate summaries for payments from July through December 2026.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special route because North Macedonia has no confirmed digital-nomad status. A resident working for a foreign payer falls under ordinary foreign-income and, if locally self-employed, independent-activity and social-contribution rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad regime; ordinary resident foreign income or registered self-employment
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% flat PIT screening rate; social contributions may be additional
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home or more than 183 days in any 12-month period, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident foreign salary, freelance, intellectual-service, and other taxable income must be reported. Foreign tax credit is limited to the North Macedonian tax calculated at 10%, subject to proof.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Registered local self-employment can create mandatory pension, health, injury, and unemployment contributions totaling 28.0% under the July–December 2026 rates; the assessment base is fact-specific.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed nomad payment; a minimum-base social-contribution exposure may apply to registered self-employment.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Screening estimate around MKD 9,680 (about USD 179) monthly if the 28% total applies to the MKD 34,570 minimum contribution base.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No dedicated nomad fee exists. Current residence-card, visa-D, and self-employed filing fees were not established from the inspected public pages.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax or financial-transaction tax specific to remote workers was established. VAT and business-registration obligations depend on turnover and legal form.
fixed_payments.notes: The minimum contribution estimate must not be treated as a guaranteed invoice; obtain a current payroll/accounting calculation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person who remains nonresident is generally taxed on North Macedonian-source income only, but services physically performed in the country can raise sourcing and permanent-establishment questions. Visitor status also does not supply work authorization.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Foreign employment or freelance income becomes reportable under the ordinary worldwide-income rule, generally at 10%, with treaty relief or foreign-tax credit where available.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Net business income is generally subject to 10% PIT, advance payments and annual accounts; local registration may also trigger social contributions and other business compliance.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence in the headline tax-residence, PIT, and current contribution rates; medium confidence in an individual's minimum monthly contribution because classification and assessment bases vary.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying employment/self-employment approval directly grants temporary residence; there is no preliminary multi-year stage. This does not mean instant processing.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five consecutive years of qualifying temporary residence. Absence normally must not exceed six consecutive months or ten months total during the five-year period.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Approximate arithmetic relationship between five-year permanent-residence eligibility and seven-year naturalization residence eligibility. Citizenship law uses total lawful continuous residence and does not state a separate mandatory two-year period after PR.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest ordinary naturalization eligibility based on residence, not guaranteed grant or completion.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current Ministry of Interior citizenship guidance specifies the application method, conditions, and EUR 100 administrative fee but does not publish a reliable typical decision time.

key_conditions.value: For permanent residence: five qualifying years, stable regular means, accommodation, medical insurance, good character/security compliance, Macedonian-language ability, and strict absence limits. For ordinary naturalization: age 18+, seven years' lawful continuous residence, housing, permanent sufficient income, no disqualifying convictions or proceedings, communicative Macedonian, no residence ban or security concern, and normally renunciation or proof of future renunciation.
key_conditions.notes: The self-employed route's admission requirements remain the principal uncertainty for this applicant profile.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The official archived Ministry guidance states that a spouse married to a citizen for at least three years may use facilitated naturalization after at least one year of lawful continuous residence in North Macedonia. A separate route exists after eight years of marriage for a spouse legally and permanently living abroad.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legally valid marriage can count toward the three-year or eight-year marriage duration; it does not itself grant residence or citizenship. A citizen spouse can sponsor renewable family temporary residence.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Civil-status documents, the citizen spouse's status, domicile, and genuine family relationship must be proved.

requirements_and_risks.value: The three-year-marriage/one-year-residence route waives the ordinary seven-year residence, Macedonian-language, and renunciation requirements identified in the official guidance. The eight-year-marriage route can apply while residing abroad. The Foreigners Law authorizes detailed marriage-of-convenience checks, including cohabitation, consistent personal histories, prior meetings, a shared language, payments, and previous immigration anomalies.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sham marriage, false documents, or non-genuine cohabitation can lead to refusal, nonrenewal, revocation, and other legal consequences.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in North Macedonia alone does not normally confer citizenship. A foundling or child born in the country to unknown or stateless parents acquires citizenship subject to a limited loss rule if foreign parents are established before age 15 and the child will not become stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in North Macedonia to two foreign parents does not acquire citizenship solely by birth. During the first six months no residence permit is required; afterward the child can receive residence linked to a parent's status.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The anti-statelessness/foundling exception is distinct from ordinary migrant-parent births.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with one North Macedonian parent can acquire citizenship by descent. For a child born in North Macedonia, consent from the foreign parent is required under the Ministry guidance; for a child born abroad, registration or return-to-reside rules and age limits apply.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Citizenship is based on the citizen parent, not on the migrant father's residence status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a minor North Macedonian citizen may qualify as a family member for temporary residence when this is in the child's best interests. The citizen child does not automatically confer permanent residence or citizenship on the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The citizen parent normally lodges the family application, and the best-interest and genuine-family-relationship requirements remain relevant.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is a North Macedonian citizen, the child may obtain citizenship by descent and the migrant father may seek family temporary residence. If both parents are foreign, birth in North Macedonia supplies no citizenship-based shortcut. In neither case is the father's citizenship automatic.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Any later naturalization must use the applicable spouse, residence, or other statutory route.

rank.notes: Live Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard display of 45 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations. The index separately lists eVisa and other electronic/pre-enrollment cases, so this is not the full mobility score.

passport.notes: Passport Index displayed a mobility score of 130, comprising 79 visa-free, 45 visa-on-arrival, and 6 eTA destinations. Entry classifications and rank are live and should be rechecked before travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Generally practical in Skopje and professional/technology settings. EF EPI 2025 ranked North Macedonia 17th globally with a score of 595, while Skopje scored 600; this supports relatively strong English availability but does not guarantee service in English in every government office or smaller community.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI uses a self-selected online test population and should be treated as a practical indicator, not a census. Macedonian remains necessary for the statutory permanent-residence and ordinary naturalization language requirements.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited and not reliable for administration or daily services. Macedonian is a South Slavic language, but no authoritative current source inspected established widespread functional Russian or Ukrainian use; English or Macedonian is the safer working language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This cautious assessment is retained because targeted searches did not produce a reliable national proficiency or service-availability dataset for Russian or Ukrainian.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the May 2026 official average monthly net wage of MKD 49,544 using roughly MKD 54 per USD. Exchange-rate movement changes the USD figure.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The numeric value remains null because no current national monthly net median wage series was established. The State Statistical Office monthly wage product publishes arithmetic mean gross and net wages. MAKSTAT offers median annual gross earnings in structural tables, including 2024 administrative-source data updated in July 2026, but that concept is not a current monthly net median comparable with the dashboard mean. Eurostat's July 2026 minimum-wage note says harmonized SES 2022 data are unavailable for North Macedonia.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the 2026 statutory minimum net wage of MKD 26,046. This is a legal wage floor for full-time employment, not an observed minimum across all earners.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the May 2026 official average monthly net wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The value remains null: current official monthly releases publish arithmetic means, not a national monthly net median. MAKSTAT's July 2026 structural tables contain median annual gross-earnings dimensions, but that annual-gross measure is not a current monthly net median. A secondary fact sheet labels MKD 36,572 as median, but its cited source identifies MKD 36,572 as the official June 2023 average; it is therefore not used. Eurostat also states that harmonized SES 2022 data are unavailable for North Macedonia.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful statutory or official national maximum wage exists in the inspected sources.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Applies from the March 2026 wage payment under the annual legal adjustment.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official average monthly net wage paid per employee for May 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national monthly net median in MKD was established. Official current monthly releases report means; MAKSTAT publishes annual-gross structural median dimensions instead. The secondary MKD 36,572 claim was rejected because its cited source describes that amount as the June 2023 arithmetic average.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published and not a meaningful national statistic.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly net wage paid per employee; minimum field is the statutory full-time minimum net wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: May 2026; minimum: March 2026 through February 2027
average_citizen_salary.notes: The official current mean and statutory minimum remain usable. Median fields remain null because the official structural medians are annual gross measures, not a current monthly net median comparable to the dashboard average. USD figures use an approximate late-July 2026 reference rate near MKD 54/USD and are for comparison only.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official household data indicate a high basic-needs burden: in 2024 the average household devoted about 69.5% of consumption expenditure to food, clothing, housing and household equipment. Food and non-alcoholic beverages alone represented 50.8%, while housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels represented 7.9%. Prices were still rising in 2026: the official Consumer Price Index for May 2026 was 4.8% above May 2025.
cost_of_living_note.notes: These are national household expenditure shares and an inflation measure, not a monthly budget for one remote worker or a Skopje rental estimate. The official sources inspected do not publish a directly comparable current all-in monthly cost-of-living amount, so no speculative cash budget was inferred.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-work status is currently confirmed. Visitor or visa-free presence must not be treated as work authorization or a citizenship track.
settlement_track.summary: North Macedonia has statutory five-year permanent-residence and seven-year naturalization rules for qualifying residence, but no confirmed ordinary foreign-contract remote-work entry route. Settlement would require obtaining a separate qualifying status, such as genuinely accepted local self-employment or local employment, under the Employment Agency framework.
settlement_track.notes: The self-employment provisions do not omit local entity registration, hiring-necessity explanation, employment mediation, quota/labor-market review, or the positive Agency opinion. That prevents a foreign-client-only structure from being treated as a confirmed selection route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker route exists. The self-employment provision remains tied to a locally registered entity and Employment Agency process, and current public sources do not confirm approval for a solo foreign-client-only business.

data.notes: This focused cost-of-living null pass inspected 15 distinct directly relevant URLs, including five cost-of-living, household-budget, poverty, inflation, and comparative-price URLs not present in the previous source set. The flagged cost-of-living field is now supported by official household expenditure shares and current CPI evidence; no unsupported monthly remote-worker budget was inferred.

data.selection_summary: Norway has no dedicated digital-nomad visa, and visitor status does not permit ordinary remote work. A qualified software contractor may independently apply as a skilled self-employed person operating a Norwegian sole proprietorship; that permit is issued one year at a time and can support permanent residence after three years. However, the applicant must genuinely operate only through the Norwegian business, demonstrate that living in Norway is necessary for its establishment or operation, and show likely annual business profit of at least NOK 341,373. UDI does not expressly confirm on its public page that a one-client foreign contract is sufficient, and a continuing foreign employment relationship is incompatible with the restriction against other work. Eligibility therefore needs filing-level confirmation and likely contract restructuring.

visa_application.title: UDI skilled workers — self-employed persons with a company in Norway
visa_application.notes: Select the self-employed-person-with-a-company-in-Norway category and the applicant's citizenship. UDI then provides the appropriate electronic application and personalised checklist. The public route page is safer than linking to a session-dependent application form.

best_routes.route_name: Skilled self-employed person with a company in Norway

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The binding threshold is in NOK. An exact 2026-08-15 USD conversion was not stated because Norges Bank's accessible page did not expose the applicable dated observation.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: NOK 341,373/year pre-tax business profit
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Equivalent to approximately NOK 28,448 per month. This is expected business profit, not gross turnover or salary.

income_requirement_display.value: NOK 341,373/year pre-tax business profit (approximately NOK 28,448/month)
income_requirement_display.notes: UDI must consider it likely that the Norwegian business will generate this profit. No binding USD threshold exists.

income_proof_months.notes: UDI publishes no universal number of historical income months. The personalised checklist and assessment instead focus on the proposed business, contracts and likely future profit.

key_requirements.requirement: Hold completed higher education, qualifying vocational education or sufficiently documented special qualifications; the software-engineering degree can meet the higher-education limb.
Establish and actively operate a Norwegian business, normally the applicant's own sole proprietorship; a limited company does not qualify under this category.
Show that residence and active participation in Norway are necessary for establishing and continuing the business.
Work only through the qualifying Norwegian business. Separate employment or other remote work is prohibited.
The business work must require the applicant's skilled-worker qualifications and must be likely to produce at least NOK 341,373 annual pre-tax profit.

A genuine sole proprietorship must operate for profit, with duration, scope and activity at the applicant's own expense and risk; an employment relationship merely relabelled as contracting may be reclassified.
The sole proprietorship needs a Norwegian physical business address. Registration may require a Norwegian identity number or D-number and identity verification.
Pay the work-residence application fee and submit the personalised evidence requested by UDI.

initial_validity.value: One year at a time
initial_validity.notes: This is a temporary skilled-worker residence permit, not permanent residence on approval.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for one year at a time while the applicant continues to meet the skilled qualifications, qualifying-business, active-operation and profit requirements; the current work-permit fee also applies to renewals.
extension_rules.notes: The work-residence fee shown by UDI on the research date was NOK 6,300 for an adult initial application or renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: UDI approval directly grants a temporary skilled-worker residence permit authorising work only in the qualifying Norwegian sole proprietorship.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor entry or registration of a business alone does not legalise work. Work normally cannot start before the permit is granted.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: UDI expressly states that the applicant can apply for permanent residence after three years. The permits must continue to form a basis for permanent residence, and all income, continuity, language, social-studies and conduct requirements must be met.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current PR income requirement shown for an adult was NOK 341,373 in the preceding year. Other personalised conditions and absence rules apply.

path_to_citizenship.value: The permit is a qualifying skilled/self-employed status. Ordinary naturalisation currently requires residence for eight of the previous eleven years, or six of ten for applicants meeting the sufficient-income rule, plus identity, continued-residence, permanent-residence eligibility, language, citizenship-test and conduct conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A July 2026 government announcement proposed changing residence calculations, but the official January 2026 summary still states the eight-of-eleven current rule. Verify legislation again before applying.

best_routes.notes: This is a credible settlement route for a genuinely independent contractor who transfers the foreign-client relationship into a Norwegian sole proprietorship. It is not a permit to remain employed by a foreign company and work remotely. Public UDI guidance does not expressly resolve whether a single foreign client and the applicant's particular business plan satisfy the necessity and genuine-self-employment tests, so a pre-filing UDI or Norwegian immigration-law review is advisable.

rejected_routes.route_name: Self-employed person with a company abroad carrying out an assignment in Norway

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general USD threshold; remuneration must meet normal Norwegian conditions.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No single fixed threshold published; normal Norwegian remuneration required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Assessment depends on the occupation and assignment.

income_requirement_display.value: Normal Norwegian remuneration for the specific assignment; no universal fixed amount
income_requirement_display.notes: This route is rejected because it requires a specific Norwegian assignment and does not count toward permanent residence.

income_proof_months.notes: No universal prior-month requirement was published.

key_requirements.requirement: Operate an established sole proprietorship abroad and hold a contract for an assignment with one specific Norwegian enterprise having a registered Norwegian business address.
The assignment must require the applicant's skilled qualifications and remuneration must be normal for Norway.

initial_validity.value: Up to two years at a time
initial_validity.notes: Maximum aggregate use is generally six years, followed by two years outside Norway before a new permit.

extension_rules.value: May continue within the six-year maximum for the approved assignment; changing the assignment or enterprise requires a new permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary assignment-based residence permit

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No path from time on this permit; UDI expressly states that it does not count toward permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A switch to a separate qualifying status would be required, with the qualifying residence clock beginning under that status.

path_to_citizenship.value: No confirmed citizenship track from this assignment permit itself.
path_to_citizenship.notes: It is temporary and does not build the qualifying PR period.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant needs a specific Norwegian business assignment and the permit does not count toward permanent residence.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor or visa-free stay for ordinary foreign remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Not applicable; visitor status is not a remote-work residence route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not applicable.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable — visitor status cannot authorise ordinary remote work
income_requirement_display.notes: Incidental emails, calls or digital meetings may be allowed only when remote work is not the main purpose and creates no value in or connection to Norway.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable.

key_requirements.requirement: Visitor status does not permit work, including ordinary remote work, and cannot be used to apply for a residence permit in Norway.

initial_validity.value: Short Schengen visit only
initial_validity.notes: Not a residence status.

extension_rules.value: No conversion or work-authorising extension for this scenario

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None from visitor status

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None

path_to_citizenship.value: None

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because regular work for a foreign employer or client is not authorised during a visit.

rejected_routes.route_name: Skilled worker with an employer in Norway

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: UDI publishes NOK salary floors; no exact dated USD conversion used.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Generally NOK 545,400/year for a bachelor's-level position or NOK 624,700/year for a master's-level position where no collective agreement applies
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Lower pay may be accepted with substantial proof that it is normal for the occupation and location.

income_requirement_display.value: Generally NOK 545,400/year for bachelor's-level work or NOK 624,700/year for master's-level work
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Approximately NOK 45,450 or NOK 52,058 per month
income_requirement_display.notes: Occupation and collective-agreement rules can alter the applicable amount.

income_proof_months.notes: A concrete confirmed job offer is required rather than a fixed history of income.

key_requirements.requirement: Concrete job offer from a specific employer in Norway, with the employer confirming the offer for a self-filed overseas application.
The job must require and use the applicant's skilled-worker qualifications and meet Norwegian pay and working-condition rules.

initial_validity.value: Normally up to three years for a university-degree position; sometimes one year where closer review is needed

extension_rules.value: Renewable while qualifying employment continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct skilled-worker residence permit after approval

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential application after three years on qualifying skilled-worker permits

path_to_citizenship.value: Can lead to ordinary naturalisation after the statutory residence period

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this selection because a specific Norwegian employer and confirmed local job offer are mandatory, despite the strong settlement track.

summary.value: Admission to full-time accredited Norwegian higher education can support a study residence permit without an employer. The permit allows up to 20 hours of work per week, including remote work, but prohibits self-employment and does not count toward permanent residence. A graduate may seek a separate job-seeker permit, but that period also does not count; settlement normally requires later switching to qualifying skilled employment or qualifying self-employment.
summary.notes: This is an education route, not an independent citizenship track for the existing foreign-contract profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: Domestic tax residence begins after more than 183 days in any 12-month period or more than 270 days in any 36-month period. If more than 183 days are spent in the first income year, residence starts on the first day; where the days span income years, it generally starts on 1 January of the second year. The 270-day test starts residence on 1 January of the year in which the limit is exceeded.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax-treaty residence can modify Norway's taxing rights. Operating a Norwegian sole proprietorship can create Norwegian-source business taxation even before domestic worldwide-residence status begins.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Maximum effective marginal rate published for business income, not an expected effective or flat tax rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: 2026 national-insurance contribution rate for ordinary business income. A lower-limit and 25% limiting formula apply; treaty or EEA social-security coverage can change liability.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly self-employed tax or social-security payment was found. Contributions are percentage-based. One-time or per-application registration and immigration fees apply instead.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker tax exemption was found. A Norwegian sole proprietorship falls under ordinary Norwegian business, personal-income and national-insurance rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaties and foreign-tax credits may prevent double taxation but are not a nomad concession.

taxes.caveats: Norwegian sole-proprietorship profit, personal-income calculations, deductions, VAT treatment of exported services, National Insurance membership, foreign tax credits and treaty residence require individual analysis. The 50.6% dashboard number is the maximum marginal business-income rate, not the expected effective burden.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income and wealth. For a sole proprietor, net general income is taxed at 22%, progressive bracket tax applies to calculated personal income, and ordinary business income carries a 10.8% National Insurance contribution. The published combined maximum effective marginal rate for business income is 50.6%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in 12 months or more than 270 days in 36 months, with commencement rules depending on the year in which the threshold is crossed.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income and wealth for Norwegian tax residents, subject to tax treaties and double-tax relief; Norwegian-source business income may remain taxable for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or freelancer tax holiday identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary business income is subject to a 10.8% National Insurance contribution for 2026, subject to the lower-limit formula and possible international social-security coordination.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The five-step bracket tax is additional to 22% tax on net general income and National Insurance contributions. The 50.6% figure is a maximum marginal screening rate.

tax_brackets.notes: General-income tax and potentially National Insurance still apply.

tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 bracket tax on the portion in this band
2026 bracket tax on the portion in this band
2026 bracket tax on the portion in this band
2026 bracket tax on the portion in this band
2026 bracket tax on the portion above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: This bracket rate is not the complete marginal burden.

taxation_system.notes: USD bracket conversions were intentionally omitted because no exact research-date Norges Bank observation was exposed by the accessible page.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Norway has no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. A successful applicant under the skilled self-employed route operates a Norwegian sole proprietorship and is screened under ordinary progressive Norwegian tax and social-insurance rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: skilled self-employed residence / Norwegian sole proprietorship
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 50.6% maximum effective marginal rate for business income; not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in 12 months or more than 270 days in 36 months, subject to commencement and treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Norwegian tax residents generally report worldwide income and wealth. Foreign tax paid may qualify for relief, while treaty residence may limit Norway to source-state taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified for this route.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary self-employed business income carries a 10.8% National Insurance contribution in 2026, subject to thresholds and international coordination. A sole proprietor does not pay employer contributions on their own qualifying self-employment remuneration.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly payment identified
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based 10.8% National Insurance contribution on ordinary business income; no universal monthly minimum found.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: UDI work-residence application and renewal fee: NOK 6,300 for an adult on the research date. Sole-proprietorship electronic registration cost: NOK 2,185 for the Central Coordinating Register alone or NOK 3,883 when also registering in the Register of Business Enterprises.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration normally becomes mandatory when VAT-taxable turnover exceeds NOK 50,000 over 12 months. Whether exported software services attract Norwegian VAT requires transaction-specific review.
fixed_payments.notes: Registration and immigration fees are one-time or per application, not monthly taxes.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A Norwegian sole proprietorship and work physically performed in Norway can produce Norwegian-source business tax and reporting obligations even before worldwide tax residence begins; the 183-day rule is not a tax-free work allowance.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Assume worldwide income and wealth reporting, 22% general-income tax on net income, progressive bracket tax and applicable National Insurance contributions, with treaty relief for double taxation.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Register the Norwegian business, maintain accounts, assess VAT after NOK 50,000 of taxable turnover, make advance-tax arrangements and verify National Insurance membership. The contract must also reflect genuine independent business activity rather than disguised employment.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: There is no dedicated nomad regime; this section models the potentially usable Norwegian self-employed route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The approved self-employed skilled-worker permit directly grants temporary residence; no preliminary years are required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Three years is the route-specific UDI statement, subject to continuous qualifying permits and all PR requirements.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the ordinary eight-year naturalisation rule minus the earliest three-year PR point. Citizenship does not legally require waiting five years after receiving PR; total qualifying residence is what matters. The sufficient-income rule can reduce total residence to six years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Current general rule is eight of the last eleven years. Applicants with sufficient income may qualify after six of the last ten years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: UDI's current waiting-time tool requires applicant-specific answers and did not publish one reliable universal month figure. Processing may also be automatic or manual, so no generic number was inferred.

key_conditions.value: Maintain qualifying legal residence and the underlying business conditions; meet PR continuity, income, A2 oral Norwegian and social-studies requirements; for citizenship, satisfy identity, intention to remain, PR eligibility, generally B1 oral Norwegian, citizenship/social-studies testing and conduct/waiting-period rules. Norway permits dual citizenship, although the other country may not.
key_conditions.notes: Absences and any criminal penalties can delay eligibility. Proposed 2026 citizenship amendments had not displaced the current official eight-of-eleven summary as of the research date.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: At least five of the last ten years must still be qualifying residence in Norway. Residence plus marriage/cohabitation with a Norwegian citizen must total at least seven years; overlapping years count toward both components.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage or documented cohabitation can count toward the combined seven-year citizenship calculation, including qualifying shared residence abroad, but only for periods when the spouse was Norwegian. The applicant must still have at least five years of qualifying Norwegian residence and remain together when UDI decides the case.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not confer citizenship automatically and does not eliminate residence, language, testing, identity or conduct requirements.

requirements_and_risks.value: The couple must document a genuine continuing shared household. A foreign marriage must be recognised under Norwegian rules. Depending on the family-immigration scenario, both partners may need to be at least 24, with exceptions for established relationships. Inconsistent relationship evidence, non-recognition, separation or misrepresentation can defeat family-based eligibility and create serious immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The accelerated rule concerns marriage or cohabitation with a Norwegian citizen, not marriage to another migrant.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Norway alone does not grant Norwegian citizenship. A child born to two foreign citizens must obtain an appropriate residence status.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Norway to two foreign-citizen parents does not become Norwegian at birth. The parents must promptly apply for the child's residence permit, EEA registration or residence card as applicable.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Narrow statelessness or later-naturalisation provisions do not amount to general jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: For a child born on or after 1 September 2006, having a Norwegian mother or father at birth automatically confers Norwegian citizenship, regardless of birthplace or the parents' marital status, subject to legally established parentage.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: If only the father is Norwegian, paternity must be properly established.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Norwegian child may have a family-immigration category, including where the parent will live permanently with a Norwegian child under 18, but the child does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The exact route depends on custody, residence, access arrangements and the other parent's status.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father receives no automatic citizenship or permanent residence from the child's Norwegian citizenship. He may qualify to apply under the relevant parent-of-a-Norwegian-child family rules if he meets custody, co-residence or access and other requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage and family relationship documentation are required.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category in this index, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 46 visa-on-arrival destinations and 11 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 173 and power rank 4. These categories differ from Henley's access score, which combines visa-free and certain arrival-authorisation categories; figures from different indexes should not be mixed.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for daily life and technology work: EF's 2025 proficiency index ranked Norway fifth of 123 countries and classified proficiency as very high. Nevertheless, Norwegian is important for government administration, local business integration and the mandatory PR/citizenship language tests.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF is a reputable secondary proficiency index based on a self-selected test population, not an official census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Current official statistics confirm a substantial Ukrainian-origin immigrant population, but no directly relevant authoritative source established that Russian or Ukrainian can be relied upon for nationwide services, administration or business. Plan to use English initially and learn Norwegian.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The freshest comparable annual value is NOK 62,070 gross monthly earnings in 2025. No exact research-date USD conversion was used because the accessible Norges Bank page did not expose the dated rate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2025 median was NOK 55,800 per full-time equivalent. USD conversion intentionally omitted for the same FX reason.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Norway has no nationwide general statutory minimum wage; binding minimum rates exist only in ten specified sectors.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official NOK figure retained without an imprecise research-date FX conversion.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official NOK figure retained without an imprecise research-date FX conversion.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful nationwide maximum salary exists or was published by SSB.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Ten sectors have legally binding sectoral minimum rates; software development is not listed as a generalised-minimum-wage sector.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 gross monthly earnings across all sectors and occupations, including agreed earnings, irregular payments and bonuses but excluding overtime.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 median monthly earnings per full-time equivalent.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published as a meaningful national ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly employee earnings; average covers all employees, while the median is expressed per full-time equivalent
average_citizen_salary.notes: Fresh Q2 2026 quarterly data showed average monthly earnings of NOK 63,700 and average basic earnings of NOK 58,970, but the audited 2025 annual average and median are used together for consistent distribution comparison.

cost_of_living_note.value: Norway's 2025 household final-consumption price level was 128.6 with EU27=100. Food and non-alcoholic beverages were 133.1, transport 132.1 and restaurants/accommodation 139.7, indicating materially above-EU-average living costs.
cost_of_living_note.notes: 2025 figures published in June 2026 were preliminary.
