settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: This is not a digital-nomad permit. It works only if UDI accepts the applicant as a genuinely self-employed skilled person operating exclusively through a Norwegian sole proprietorship.
settlement_track.summary: If granted, the Norwegian-company self-employed permit is itself a qualifying residence route: UDI expressly permits permanent-residence application after three years, followed by ordinary naturalisation eligibility under the national residence rules. The uncertainty concerns initial fit for an ordinary foreign-client contract—not the settlement quality of the permit once granted.
settlement_track.notes: No status conversion is required, although obtaining permanent residence remains conditional. The applicant may potentially use the six-of-ten citizenship residence rule after demonstrating sufficient income.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign-client contractor may fit after moving the contract and invoicing into a genuine Norwegian sole proprietorship. Continuing foreign employment, performing separate remote work, or merely relabelling an employment relationship does not fit. UDI's public page does not expressly confirm whether a single foreign client satisfies the necessity and genuine-business assessment.

data.notes: The existing Norway record correctly identified the skilled self-employed route and its strong settlement potential but was internally inconsistent: it alternated between false and true selection conclusions and treated the foreign-client fit as both true and false. This audit classifies Norway as uncertain because the legal route is active and independent, but the exact foreign-contract profile requires contract restructuring and discretionary filing-level confirmation. Unresolved fields—exact research-date USD conversions, a universal citizenship processing time, fixed monthly self-employed payments and nationwide Russian/Ukrainian practicality—remain cautious nulls after focused additional searches.

data.selection_summary: No active Omani digital-nomad, ordinary freelance, self-employed, or foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was confirmed. Omani work visas require a local employer and labour permit; visitor status cannot be converted to residence; Golden Residency is limited to investors, entrepreneurs, business owners, qualifying property or financial investments, major employers, and nominated talent. Oman therefore does not fit an ordinary software engineer working for a foreign client, despite its long-residence naturalisation provision.

visa_application.title: Royal Oman Police eVisa portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official general visa portal, not a remote-worker application. No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker application channel was found. Golden Residency has a separate portal but is excluded because it requires investment, entrepreneurship, qualifying property or financial assets, major local employment, company nomination, or talent eligibility.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official program publishes qualifying investment, business, property, securities, deposit, employment, nomination, and talent categories rather than an ordinary monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No salary-based threshold applicable to an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No ordinary income threshold; qualifying investment, business ownership, property, assets, nomination, or talent is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an income-based remote-worker route.

income_proof_months.notes: No ordinary remote-worker income-proof period applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Start or invest in a business, own qualifying tourism-zone property, buy bonds or listed shares, hold a fixed-term deposit, employ at least 50 Omanis, receive nomination from an invested company, or qualify through the separate talent category.
Investor-linked family visas require the sponsor's residence permit and proof of relationship.

initial_validity.value: 10 years for the current Golden Residency program; an investor joining visa may be issued for 5 or 10 years
initial_validity.notes: Long validity is not permanent residence.

extension_rules.value: The official Golden Residency portal presents long-term residency; renewal conditions must be checked against the qualifying investment or talent category at filing.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic conversion to permanent residence was identified.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct long-term residence is possible only through a qualifying investor, entrepreneur, property, financial-asset, major-employer, nomination, or talent category.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Excluded for this ordinary remote-worker profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic permanent-residence entitlement was confirmed; the program is described as 10-year residency.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Renewable long residence should not be treated as permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation is a separate, discretionary process after at least 15 years of continuous lawful residence under the 2025 Nationality Law; the Golden Residency portal does not promise citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Whether every period under a particular Golden Residency category will satisfy all nationality-law requirements should be verified with the Ministry of Interior.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant profile excludes investor, founder, entrepreneur, substantial-capital, property, elite-talent, and major-local-employment routes.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No generally published visa salary threshold; eligibility depends on local employment and a labour permit.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No generally applicable visa salary threshold was established.

income_requirement_display.value: No general visa income threshold published; local employment and labour permission required
income_requirement_display.notes: Salary is not a substitute for sponsorship.

income_proof_months.notes: Not published as a standalone income-history requirement.

key_requirements.requirement: Application must be requested and accepted under the responsibility of a local employer.
A Ministry of Labour permit is normally required; the visa application is signed by the employer or authorised signatory.
For engineers, the Royal Oman Police page identifies an additional Ministry of Labour letter among the documents.

initial_validity.value: 2 years, multiple entry
initial_validity.notes: Validity runs from passport stamping.

extension_rules.value: Employer-led renewal; the ROP page states an OMR 50 fine for each month of renewal delay.
extension_rules.notes: Continued status remains tied to authorised local employment.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A sponsored work visa permits temporary residence for authorised local employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not independently available to a foreign-client remote worker.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic permanent-residence path was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Long lawful residence may eventually support a discretionary citizenship application, but that does not make this an independent route.

path_to_citizenship.value: A foreigner may separately apply after at least 15 years of continuous lawful residence if all nationality-law conditions are met; approval is discretionary and by Royal Decree.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not remove the need for employer sponsorship during the work-status period.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer, labour permit, and employer-filed application are mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitors need sufficient funds, but no residence-route monthly threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No residence-route threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No residence income threshold; visitor must show sufficient trip funds
income_requirement_display.notes: This is entry permission, not residence or work authorisation.

income_proof_months.notes: Not specified.

key_requirements.requirement: For the 14-day facility: passport valid for at least six months, return ticket, confirmed hotel, health insurance, and sufficient funds.
Eligibility depends on nationality and, for the second list, qualifying residence or a visa from specified countries.

initial_validity.value: Up to 14 days for the cited visa-exempt facility; other visitor visas vary
initial_validity.notes: Check the ROP portal for nationality-specific options.

extension_rules.value: The 14-day facility cannot be extended or transferred to any residence visa.
extension_rules.notes: This expressly blocks a visitor-to-residence strategy for that facility.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None through the 14-day facility; it is non-transferable to residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time is not a permanent-residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor status
path_to_citizenship.notes: A visitor stay does not establish the qualifying continuous lawful residence track.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor/eVisa status is not a remote-work residence status and the official 14-day facility is expressly non-extendable and non-transferable.

summary.value: A software-engineering degree does not create an independent residence route. Ordinary engineering employment requires local-employer sponsorship, a labour permit, and potentially an additional Ministry of Labour letter. The Golden Residency talent category is not an ordinary degree-based skilled-migration route and its eligibility criteria require category-specific assessment.
summary.notes: No employer-free points-based, degree-based, or skilled-independent residence program comparable to a skilled-migration visa was found.

tax_residency_rule.value: The enacted Personal Income Tax Law, effective 1 January 2028, treats an individual as tax resident after more than 183 continuous or intermittent days in Oman during the calendar tax year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: This statutory PIT residence rule is future-effective. In 2026 Oman has no general personal income tax.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Current screening rate for 2026: no general PIT. From 1 January 2028, the enacted law applies 5% to taxable income after the OMR 42,000 annual threshold and permitted deductions/exemptions.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single current percentage applicable to this nonexistent remote-worker route could be established. The Social Protection Law provides phased compulsory employment-related coverage and a defined-contribution savings system for non-Omani workers, but official implementation dates and contribution parameters must be checked for the worker category.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory monthly payment for a digital nomad or independently resident foreign freelancer exists because no such route was found. Employment, insurance, business, and savings obligations depend on the actual legal structure.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. Current general PIT is 0%; the enacted 2028 regime uses a 5% rate above the OMR 42,000 annual net-income threshold, with statutory deductions, exemptions, and foreign-tax-credit rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Local business activity may separately trigger income-tax registration, VAT, licensing, and other obligations.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical presence, income source, whether activity creates an Omani business or permanent establishment, the 2028 PIT regulations, and any applicable treaty. A 0% current PIT rate does not legalise remote work on visitor status or eliminate corporate, VAT, employment, insurance, or licensing obligations.

taxation_system.value: No general personal income tax applies in 2026. Royal Decree 56/2025 introduces PIT from 1 January 2028 at 5% on taxable income above the OMR 42,000 annual threshold. Tax residence will begin after more than 183 days in the calendar tax year.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No operative general PIT residence test is needed for 2026 individual income; from 2028, more than 183 days in Oman during the calendar year makes an individual tax resident.
taxation_system.income_scope: No general individual PIT in 2026. From 2028, resident individuals are subject under the new law, including relevant foreign income subject to statutory rules, exemptions, deductions, and foreign-tax credits; nonresident scope is source-based.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Future general PIT: 5% after the OMR 42,000 annual net-income threshold.
taxation_system.social_security: Employment-related social-protection and provident-savings rules are separate from PIT. Non-Omani coverage is being introduced by program and category; no remote-freelancer rate was confirmed.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's current 0% is the applicable 2026 screening rate. The enacted 5% from 2028 applies only above the annual threshold and is not the expected effective rate on total income.

tax_brackets.notes: No general PIT is currently levied.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: From 1 January 2028: first OMR 42,000 of annual gross income before further statutory calculation
tax_brackets.applies_to: Individuals under the enacted PIT law
tax_brackets.notes: The law defines net income as the amount exceeding OMR 42,000 and then permits exemptions, costs, losses, and treaty relief in calculating taxable income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: From 1 January 2028: taxable income after the OMR 42,000 threshold and permitted deductions/exemptions
tax_brackets.notes: Future statutory rate, not a 2026 liability or an effective rate on total income.

taxation_system.notes: Current and future rules are separated because the previous record risked making the enacted 2028 rate look current.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable: Oman has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence category. A visitor cannot rely on the current 0% PIT rate as work authorisation.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; general individual tax rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% general PIT in 2026; enacted 5% above OMR 42,000 annually from 2028
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: From 2028, tax residence begins after more than 183 days in Oman during the calendar tax year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: No general PIT in 2026. From 2028, the enacted law covers resident income under its worldwide-income, exemption, deduction, and foreign-tax-credit provisions; obtain advice once regulations are final and for treaty sourcing.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific contribution exists. Local employment requires employer-linked compliance; non-Omani social-protection and provident coverage is program-specific and phased.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Not applicable to a nonexistent nomad route; employment-related obligations depend on local employment and implementation of the Social Protection Law.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Work visa fee shown by ROP: OMR 20; investor-joining visa: OMR 50 for five years or OMR 100 for ten years. These are rejected routes, not digital-nomad fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration is generally mandatory for a resident economic activity once taxable supplies reach or are expected to reach OMR 38,500 over the relevant rolling 12-month test; local businesses must also register for income tax.
fixed_payments.notes: These amounts do not create eligibility for remote-worker residence.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short visitor stay is not subject to general PIT in 2026, but visitor status is not a remote-work residence authorisation and the 14-day facility cannot convert to residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no legal remote-worker residence route to model. From 2028, a person present for more than 183 days would meet the PIT residence test, but immigration legality must be established independently.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Operating an Omani establishment may require commercial and tax registration, licensing, VAT registration at the threshold, and an investor or other qualifying residence basis. That is a local-business route, not ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The 0% figure describes current general PIT only; it is not a special incentive and does not cure the absence of a qualifying immigration route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker route exists. Employer and investor routes can grant residence directly but are excluded.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No ordinary permanent-residence entitlement or conversion timeline was confirmed. Golden Residency is long but time-limited.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Nationality Law uses continuous lawful residence rather than a confirmed PR-plus-years sequence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Current general statutory minimum before a foreigner may apply: 15 years of continuous lawful residence, with no more than 90 days' absence in each year. This is a discretionary eligibility benchmark, not a route-specific guarantee.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Gov.om displays a 36-month service time, but that page still reproduces superseded 20/15-year conditions despite a July 2026 update. Treat 36 months as indicative and verify with the Ministry of Interior under Royal Decree 17/2025.

key_conditions.value: At least 15 years of continuous lawful residence; no more than 90 days' absence per year; Arabic reading and writing; good conduct; no qualifying criminal conviction; medical fitness; sufficient lawful income; written commitment to renounce other nationality. The Ministry may reject without giving reasons, and citizenship is granted by Royal Decree.
key_conditions.notes: Dual nationality is generally prohibited unless authorised by Royal Decree.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Under the current 2025 law, a foreign husband of an Omani woman may apply after at least 10 years of marriage and continuous lawful co-residence in Oman, provided they have a child. A foreign wife of an Omani man has an eight-year rule; this field uses the migrant-father scenario.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage matters only when the spouse is an Omani citizen and the couple satisfies the statutory co-residence, duration, child, language, conduct, and other conditions. An existing marriage to another foreigner gives no acceleration.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The prior record's 15-year husband figure is superseded by Article 18 of Royal Decree 17/2025.

requirements_and_risks.value: For a foreign husband: 10 years of marriage and continuous lawful residence with the Omani wife, no more than 90 days' absence per year, a child from the marriage, Arabic reading and writing, good conduct, no specified conviction, health fitness, adequate lawful income, and renunciation of other nationality. Approval remains discretionary; false information or documents can lead to imprisonment and substantial fines.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A genuine qualifying marriage and actual co-residence are essential; marriage does not automatically grant citizenship or permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Oman does not grant general citizenship merely for birth in Oman. The law principally transmits original nationality through an Omani father and covers narrow cases such as a child of unknown parents born in Oman or a child of an Omani mother whose paternity is not legally established.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic Omani citizenship solely because the child is born in Oman. The narrow unknown-parent/foundling rule does not cover ordinary identified migrant parents.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in or outside Oman to an Omani father who is an original citizen is Omani by origin. An Omani mother does not transmit citizenship on the same unconditional basis when the father is a known foreigner; separate statutory conditions and procedures may apply.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The boolean is true for at least one local-parent configuration, specifically an original Omani father; it is not a gender-neutral rule.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a citizen child does not automatically grant the migrant parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. For a foreign husband of an Omani woman, having a child is one mandatory condition for the separate ten-year marriage/co-residence naturalisation route.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must independently maintain lawful residence and satisfy all naturalisation conditions.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father married to an Omani woman may use the special ten-year naturalisation provision only after ten years of qualifying marriage and continuous lawful co-residence and only if they have a child; the child alone creates no automatic status.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Where the father is a known foreigner, the child is not automatically Omani merely through the Omani mother in the ordinary case.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on the country dashboard; passport-index methodologies differ from Henley.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category on Passport Index 2026, not the combined mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as visa required by the index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 40 visa-on-arrival plus 6 eTA destinations. The index reports a total mobility score of 95.

passport.notes: The prior record's Henley value of 84 combined visa-free and visa-on-arrival access. This audit uses Passport Index because it supplies the schema's separate visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA, and visa-required counts.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is widely used, particularly in business, higher education, expatriate-facing services, and Muscat, so day-to-day remote work in English is practical. Arabic remains the official language, governs many formal processes, and is required for naturalisation.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English practicality does not change immigration eligibility.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian alone is unlikely to be sufficient for government procedures or broad daily interaction; no reliable current nationwide proficiency data was found. English or Arabic should be expected.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical inference from official Arabic and widespread English use, not a measured Russian/Ukrainian proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Focused review of the current official yearbook, publication portal, labour datasets, and insured-worker bulletins did not yield a single current whole-workforce mean that safely combines citizens and expatriates.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median wage was established from the inspected official sources.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the OMR 325 minimum wage using the rial's roughly USD 2.60 peg. This floor applies to Omanis in the private sector, not all residents or foreign workers.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A comparable current all-citizen or all-worker mean was not extractable without mixing government, private, Omani, expatriate, and contribution-wage series.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable current national median was found after focused official-source review.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum wage is published; an open-ended top wage band is not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Current minimum reported for Omani private-sector workers; the proposed OMR 360–400 increase remained under review in the cited report. It is not a universal expatriate minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Not established on a comparable whole-workforce basis.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published in the inspected current official material.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Not meaningful or published as a national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory Omani private-sector minimum only; national mean and median left unresolved because available official series separate worker groups and sectors
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum current as reviewed 2026; official statistical material reviewed through 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The OMR 325 figure must not be presented as the average resident salary. Current official publications provide headcounts and wage bands but did not yield a defensible single national mean or median in the accessible material.

cost_of_living_note.value: No current official household-budget amount suitable for a remote software engineer was established. NCSI publishes current CPI data, but a price index is not a monthly living-cost budget; housing, schooling, insurance, transport, and location can materially change expenditure.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Left unquantified rather than substituting crowdsourced estimates.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Oman has no confirmed nomad status. Visitor/eVisa time is not a qualifying remote-work residence route, and the official 14-day facility cannot be transferred to residence.
settlement_track.summary: Oman has no ordinary independent foreign-contract remote-work route. Citizenship can be requested after 15 years of separate continuous lawful residence under the current Nationality Law, but the applicant would first need a non-fitting employer, investor, family, or other lawful status and naturalisation remains discretionary.
settlement_track.notes: The previous result correctly rejected Oman but used the superseded 20-year ordinary naturalisation benchmark. Royal Decree 17/2025 now states 15 years generally and 10 years for a qualifying foreign husband of an Omani woman.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker or ordinary freelance residence category was found. Local work requires employer authorisation, visitor status does not convert, and long independent residence is investment, business, property, financial-asset, nomination, or talent based.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Oman record and more than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs. The false selection verdict is retained. Material improvements include the current 15-year general naturalisation rule, the 10-year migrant-husband marriage rule, explicit separation of current 0% PIT from the enacted 2028 tax, a fully separated passport-index breakdown, and cautious salary nulls where no comparable current official mean or median could be established.

data.selection_summary: Pakistan has no current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or independent-professional residence route. Its work visa requires a Pakistani job offer and company documentation; tourist and business visas are entry permissions rather than qualifying remote-work residence. General naturalisation exists after a statutory residence period, but no fitting immigration status was found through which this applicant could independently establish that residence.

visa_application.title: Pakistan Online Visa System
visa_application.notes: This is the official application portal for Pakistan's existing visa categories. The official category list and application guide do not contain a digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category. The portal itself returned an automated-access error during this audit, but DGI&P and the Board of Investment continue to direct applicants to it.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum salary threshold is published; eligibility instead depends on a valid Pakistani job offer and employer documentation.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum PKR salary was found in the official route requirements.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum; Pakistani job offer required
income_requirement_display.notes: Absence of a numerical threshold does not make the route independent.

income_proof_months.notes: The official pages require an employment agreement or letter showing salary and assignment duration but do not specify a prior-income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid job offer and employment agreement from a Pakistani employer.
Employer undertaking or sponsorship/guarantee letter, company profile, and generally SECP company-registration evidence.
Passport, photograph, CV, and company covering letter.

initial_validity.value: Entry work visa: up to 3 months, single entry
initial_validity.notes: The entry visa permits temporary lawful stay for sponsored employment; it is not permanent residence.

extension_rules.value: Extension may be granted for up to 2 years with multiple entries, subject to security clearance and a mandatory Board of Investment recommendation.
extension_rules.notes: Continued employer/company support remains integral.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The work visa permits temporary stay for the sponsored Pakistani assignment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Pakistan does not present this as an independent residence permit for foreign-client remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No general permanent-residence entitlement arising from the work visa was published in the reviewed official sources.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalisation may be available after separate qualifying residence, but the work-visa page does not confirm that visa extensions create an assured settlement track.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not a route available to the applicant without a local employer.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Pakistani job offer and employing/sponsoring-company evidence are mandatory. The official fee page states a USD 100 single-entry fee for business and work categories, with 200% of that fee for multiple entry, but reciprocal or portal-calculated fees should be checked before filing.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No personal monthly-income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No personal monthly-income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No personal income threshold; business recommendation or invitation required
income_requirement_display.notes: Extensions depend on evidence of substantial investment, exports, imports, or other business activity.

income_proof_months.notes: No prior-income history is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Recommendation from a foreign chamber of commerce, qualifying business invitation, or other specified trade/investment recommendation.
For extension, business documentation showing substantial investment, export, or import activity during the preceding year.

initial_validity.value: Up to 5-year multiple-entry business visa for eligible Business Visa List nationalities; a qualifying visa-in-your-inbox business authorization may allow 30 days.
initial_validity.notes: Validity and permitted stay are not the same, and eligibility depends on nationality and supporting business documentation.

extension_rules.value: Regional offices may grant a one-year extension on business evidence; longer extensions are decided by the Ministry of Interior.
extension_rules.notes: The published rules require substantive Pakistani business activity.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No separate temporary-residence status is granted; this remains a business-entry visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The official material characterizes it as a visa rather than a residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No business-visa-to-PR entitlement is published in the reviewed official sources.

path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation law is separate; no official source confirms the business visa as a settlement route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is intended for qualifying business visits or substantive Pakistani business activity, not ordinary remote work for a foreign client. Investor/founder-style use is also outside the applicant profile.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income requirement exists because this is not a remote-worker route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A route-specific income threshold is inapplicable because this is visitor status.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—visitor category
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial or travel evidence requested in an individual application should not be confused with a remote-worker income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-work income-history rule is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Online application under the appropriate tourist or visit category and category-specific supporting documents.

initial_validity.notes: Duration varies by nationality and subcategory; the official materials do not publish one universal duration.

extension_rules.value: Extensions exist for some visa categories, but no conversion to remote-worker residence is published.
extension_rules.notes: An extension remains an extension of visitor status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The reviewed sources describe visitor status rather than a separate temporary-residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It should not be treated as remote-work residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed official sources publish no visitor-to-PR entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.notes: A visitor stay should not be treated as qualifying residence without case-specific legal confirmation.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status is not authorization for ordinary ongoing foreign-contract remote work and does not provide a confirmed settlement path.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This route uses a capital-transfer requirement rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: PKR 5,000,000 foreign-exchange transfer
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Restricted to qualifying Commonwealth citizens and subject to confirmation and security/formality checks.

income_requirement_display.value: PKR 5,000,000 capital transfer
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an income threshold and is excluded as an investment route.

income_proof_months.notes: Prior monthly income is inapplicable because the requirement is a lump-sum capital transfer.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying Commonwealth citizenship, prescribed Form R, and transfer of PKR 5 million through normal banking channels.
State Bank confirmation, arrival in Pakistan, security clearance, and completion of formalities.

initial_validity.value: Immigrant visa followed by citizenship-certificate processing after arrival and required checks
initial_validity.notes: The official page describes direct citizenship processing rather than a standard PR stage.

extension_rules.notes: Visa renewal is not presented as a stage of the described citizenship procedure.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary residence is not the route's stated purpose.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The procedure is investment-linked and excluded from the applicant profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The process uses an immigrant visa before citizenship, but no separate general PR status is described.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The schema's direct-PR flag reflects the immigrant/settlement character, not a separately documented PR card.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship certificate after entry, State Bank confirmation, security clearance, and completion of formalities.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Discretionary checks apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a nationality-restricted investment route, not ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: A foreign student may apply for a study entry visa without a local employer, normally using an admission/bonafide letter and relevant NOCs. The official policy allows a two-year study visa, but no independent degree-based skilled residence or direct permanent-residence route was found for a graduate software engineer.
summary.notes: This is education-based temporary stay, not a qualifying remote-work or post-degree settlement route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident for a tax year if present in Pakistan for at least 183 days, or for at least 120 days in that year plus at least 365 days in aggregate during the preceding four tax years. Government employees posted abroad are covered by a separate limb.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Pakistan's tax year generally runs from 1 July through 30 June.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for non-salaried individuals/business income, not an expected effective rate. A foreign remote employee could instead fall under salary rules depending on the facts; the 2026-27 salaried top marginal rate is 35% above PKR 7 million.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The reviewed sources do not publish a uniform mandatory self-employed social-contribution percentage applicable to a hypothetical foreign remote worker. Employee social-security and pension obligations are employment-, scheme-, wage-, and province-dependent, while no digital-nomad route exists.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory monthly digital-nomad or foreign-freelancer payment applies because there is no such immigration category. Visa fees are transactional rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: The 2026-27 official budget materials extend a 0.25% reduced tax rate for qualifying exporters of IT and IT-enabled services through Tax Year 2029. This is an export-tax measure, not a digital-nomad immigration or general inbound-expatriate regime; registration and eligibility require separate verification.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A foreign individual working remotely should not assume automatic eligibility.

taxes.caveats: Physical work performed in Pakistan can affect whether salary or business income is Pakistan-source even when the payer is abroad. Residence, employment versus independent-business classification, receipt location, permanent-establishment issues, registration, foreign tax credits, treaties, and provincial sales tax on services can materially change the result. The absence of an applicable immigration route is separate from tax liability.

taxation_system.value: Progressive federal personal income tax. Residents are generally within the worldwide-income framework, while non-residents are taxed on Pakistan-source income, subject to exemptions and treaties.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183 days, or 120 days plus 365 days over the preceding four tax years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents and Pakistan-source income for non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Salary is Pakistan-source to the extent employment is exercised in Pakistan, wherever paid.
taxation_system.special_regimes: A narrow short-term-resident exemption applies where residence arises solely from employment and presence does not exceed three years, but not to a Pakistan business or foreign income brought into or received in Pakistan. Foreign tax credits may be available. A 0.25% qualifying IT/ITeS export rate is extended through Tax Year 2029.
taxation_system.social_security: No single self-employed percentage was established from the reviewed current sources. Local payroll and social-insurance rules depend on the employment arrangement and applicable provincial/federal schemes.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For a non-salaried individual, the published structure reaches 45% above PKR 5.6 million annually; high-income surcharge rules may also apply. The table is a screening summary based on the operative non-salaried schedule and 2026-27 materials, which changed salaried rates but did not announce a replacement non-salaried table.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to PKR 600,000
tax_brackets.notes: Zero-rate band.
15% of the amount exceeding PKR 600,000.
PKR 90,000 plus 20% of the amount exceeding PKR 1.2 million.
PKR 170,000 plus 30% of the amount exceeding PKR 1.6 million.
PKR 650,000 plus 40% of the amount exceeding PKR 3.2 million.
PKR 1,610,000 plus 45% of the amount exceeding PKR 5.6 million; possible surcharge is not represented in this marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The top 45% is a conservative screening rate for the most plausible self-employed classification, not the applicant's effective rate. The exact Tax Year 2027 return and classification should be confirmed after FBR publishes or updates all consolidated rate cards.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a route-specific regime because Pakistan has no digital-nomad visa. If a person nevertheless works from Pakistan under another lawful status, ordinary salary or business-income rules may apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; a hypothetical foreign remote worker may be salaried or non-salaried depending on contract facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 45% top marginal rate for non-salaried income; not an effective-rate estimate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183 days, or 120 days plus 365 days in the preceding four years.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally face worldwide-income rules. Section 50's short-term foreign-employment exemption is narrow and excludes foreign income brought into or received in Pakistan and income from a Pakistan business; foreign tax credits may be available.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None. The 0.25% qualifying IT/ITeS export rate is not a nomad regime and requires separate eligibility verification.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No route-specific contribution exists. Employee payroll and social-insurance obligations depend on the relationship and applicable schemes; the reviewed sources do not publish a uniform foreign-freelancer percentage.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed-payment regime.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The reviewed sources do not publish a uniform monthly self-employed amount.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: DGI&P publishes USD 100 for single-entry business/work visas and 200% of that fee for multiple entry; reciprocal and portal calculations should be checked.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Possible registration, provincial sales-tax-on-services, withholding, and banking consequences require fact-specific advice; no universal monthly amount is published.
fixed_payments.notes: These payments are not substitutes for immigration eligibility.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident is generally taxed on Pakistan-source income. Work physically exercised in Pakistan may be treated as Pakistan-source even when paid abroad, so fewer than 183 days does not automatically mean zero Pakistani tax.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident may be taxable on worldwide salary or business income, with foreign tax credits or narrow exemptions depending on the facts.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A sole proprietor would generally be screened under non-salaried progressive rates up to 45%, plus possible registration, withholding, and provincial service-tax obligations. Registration would not itself create immigration status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax analysis is hypothetical because no qualifying digital-nomad or independent foreign-freelancer immigration route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No fitting independent remote-worker temporary-residence route exists. Employer-sponsored and study visas provide temporary stay only for their stated purposes.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed official sources do not publish a general PR stage or remote-worker conversion timeline.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Pakistan's naturalisation framework is based on qualifying residence and government approval rather than a published PR-plus-years formula.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation conditions require the 12 months immediately before application plus four years in aggregate during the preceding seven years. This does not create an immigration route, and approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed official citizenship, forms, and legislation sources do not publish a typical processing-time statistic.

key_conditions.value: Naturalisation generally requires the statutory residence history, good character, adequate knowledge of a language of Pakistan, intention to reside in Pakistan or enter qualifying public service, an oath of allegiance, and federal approval. Dual-nationality restrictions may require renunciation unless an exception or bilateral arrangement applies.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation eligibility is separate from obtaining a lawful visa that permits the applicant's remote work.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The official citizenship route is expressly for a foreign woman married to a Pakistani man and requires documentary evidence of five years' aggregate stay in Pakistan. It is not a gender-neutral five-year marriage rule.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support the official citizenship application when the applicant is a foreign woman married to a Pakistani man, but she must still document the required aggregate stay and other formalities. A foreign husband of a Pakistani woman can seek spouse-based POC and family-visa benefits, while citizenship remains subject to the general naturalisation process rather than the section 10 shortcut.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to a non-Pakistani has no immigration effect.

requirements_and_risks.value: The official citizenship process for foreign wives requires Form F, marriage and passport evidence, the husband's citizenship and identity evidence, residence-permit/visa records, affidavits, photographs, fee payment, and in some cases domicile and an oath. POC and family-visa applications have separate document and nationality rules. Security and authenticity checks remain possible; fraud or a sham marriage can lead to refusal, cancellation, and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The gender-specific citizenship shortcut is a major limitation for a male applicant, although current POC eligibility is framed for a foreign spouse of either sex.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Section 4 grants citizenship to every person born in Pakistan, with narrow exceptions for children of certain foreign envoys and enemy aliens born in enemy-occupied territory.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Pakistan is generally a citizen even if both parents are foreign migrants, subject to the narrow statutory exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This answer assumes birth in Pakistan; a parent's permanent-resident status is not the source of citizenship because section 4 generally grants citizenship by place of birth.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Pakistan is a citizen by birth. A child born abroad is generally a citizen by descent if a parent is Pakistani; consular registration is required where the Pakistani parent is a citizen by descent only, subject to the statutory details.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Since the 2000 amendment, the descent rule uses 'parent' rather than only 'father'.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Pakistani citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship, permanent residence, a Pakistan Origin Card, or another confirmed settlement status on a foreign parent. If the father is married to a Pakistani citizen, he may qualify separately as that citizen's foreign spouse for a POC and family-visit visa; those benefits arise from the intact marriage, not from parenthood of the citizen child.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The current official POC eligibility page lists foreign spouses of Pakistani citizens but not foreign parents of Pakistani citizens as a standalone eligibility class. Official family-visa materials likewise describe eligibility through Pakistani origin or a Pakistani spouse/parent and do not publish an automatic parent-of-citizen settlement entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The child's Pakistani citizenship does not itself make the migrant father a citizen or give him confirmed permanent residence. If the child's mother is Pakistani and the marriage is valid and intact, the father may separately apply as the foreign spouse of a Pakistani citizen for a Pakistan Origin Card, subject to nationality exclusions, and for a family-visit visa. A POC supports visa-free entry and facilitates property, business, and banking, while the family visa may be valid up to five years with stays up to one year per entry; neither is citizenship or an automatic permanent-residence grant. General naturalisation remains a separate, discretionary process.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The identified benefit is marriage-based, not child-based. The official POC eligibility page and official family-visa materials do not list the foreign father of a Pakistani citizen as eligible solely because of that parent-child relationship. Therefore, where both parents are foreign migrants and the child is Pakistani only by birth in Pakistan, the named current sources publish no automatic visa, POC, permanent-residence, or citizenship benefit for the father; any individual relief requires another legal basis or case-specific government or court action.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English may constitutionally be used for official purposes and is practical for professional, government, higher-education, and software-sector interactions, although Urdu and provincial languages dominate much everyday life.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The Constitution names Urdu as the national language and permits English for official purposes; it does not label both identically.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status and should not be expected to work for administration or ordinary daily life; no reliable source establishing broad local use was published in the reviewed materials.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the constitutional language framework, not a measured proficiency statistic.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourist and business visas are temporary entry permissions, not a digital-nomad residence status or confirmed settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists. Although general naturalisation law uses a roughly five-year residence pattern, the applicant would first need a different lawful qualifying status—normally sponsored employment, family circumstances, study followed by an unconfirmed route, or an excluded investment/business basis.
settlement_track.notes: Official visa categories were re-audited and again showed no digital-nomad, freelance, independent-professional, or degree-based skilled-migration category.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign employment or client contract does not qualify the applicant for Pakistan's work visa; that route requires Pakistani employment/company evidence. Visitor and business categories are not substitutes.

data.notes: The previous false selection verdict is retained. This focused pass resolves the flagged father-benefit note: a citizen child does not itself confer status on a migrant father, but a father married to a Pakistani citizen can seek marriage-based POC and family-visit benefits; those are not citizenship or confirmed PR. Current research inspected at least 15 directly relevant URLs, including seven URLs outside the previous source set. Remaining nulls concern facts that are inapplicable or not officially published, including a nonexistent remote-worker income threshold, a general PR timeline, citizenship processing time, uniform self-employed social contributions, and a single nationwide minimum or maximum salary.

data.selection_summary: Palau does not offer a qualifying ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route. Its Digital Resident Tourist Visa only extends tourist status, while tourist and business visas expressly prohibit employment, commercial, and business activities. A discretionary two-year Resident Visa exists, but no published entitlement for an ordinary remote worker, unrestricted remote-work authorization, permanent-residence progression, or settlement accrual was confirmed. More decisively, Palauan law restricts naturalization to people with recognized Palauan ancestry, so none of the reviewed routes supplies the requested citizenship path.

summary.value: A Student Visa can be requested with a school acceptance letter and class schedule, without a local employer, but it is study-specific immigration permission rather than qualifying residence. No independent degree-based or skilled-migration residence route was found for a software engineer.
summary.notes: Student status does not match ordinary foreign-contract remote work and no education-to-PR or citizenship progression was confirmed.

tax_residency_rule.value: No general individual tax-residence day-count test was located in the current official materials reviewed. Palau instead publishes wage, business-profit, gross-revenue, consumption-tax, and source/activity-specific rules; the RNS operator's digital-resident terms are not a general tax-residence statute.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Physical performance of work in Palau may affect source and business characterization even when the payer is foreign. Obtain a written determination from the Bureau of Revenue and Taxation.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Dashboard screening value: the top wage-and-salary marginal rate and the Business Profits Tax rate. It is not an expected effective rate for every remote contractor.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share for covered local wages: 7% Social Security plus 2.5% Healthcare Fund. Employers match both, producing a combined employer-and-worker burden of 19%. Owner and self-employed treatment depends on business structure.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment applies to a lawful digital-nomad route because no such route exists. Immigration renewals, Digital ID charges, business fees, and percentage-based contributions are separate and variable.

special_tax_regimes.value: RNS states that Digital Residents receive a 0% Palau rate on income earned outside Palau, but this is a program-operator term, does not create immigration work authorization, does not displace tax obligations in the person's actual country of residence, and does not establish how work physically performed in Palau is sourced.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No official tax-authority ruling confirming a special physical-resident digital-nomad regime was found.

taxes.caveats: Palau has no qualifying remote-worker visa. Tax depends on whether activity is wages, a local business, Palau-source services, or genuinely foreign-source income, as well as the worker's home-country residence and treaty position. RNS marketing should not be treated as a tax-residency certificate or permission to work while visiting.

taxation_system.value: Mixed category-based system: progressive wage and salary tax, 12% Business Profits Tax for covered businesses, Gross Revenue Tax for certain non-PGST-registered persons, 10% PGST, and Social Security/Healthcare Fund contributions.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No general statutory day-count rule was confirmed in reviewed current sources.
taxation_system.income_scope: Wages, Palau business profits or gross revenue, consumption, and other activity/source categories. RNS claims a 0% rate for Digital Residents' income earned outside Palau.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No verified immigration-linked digital-nomad tax regime; only the RNS operator's foreign-income statement.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered wages carry 7% employee Social Security plus 2.5% employee Healthcare Fund, matched by the employer. Owner/self-employed reporting may also apply.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 12% is the top marginal wage rate, not an estimated effective rate. Annual wage bands are 6% through USD 8,000, 10% from USD 8,001 through USD 40,000, and 12% above USD 40,000.

tax_brackets.notes: Rate applies to the first published annual band.
Middle published annual band.
Top marginal band; 12% is also the published Business Profits Tax rate for covered businesses.

taxation_system.notes: Rates are well supported, but the absence of a clear individual tax-residence test and uncertainty over the source of foreign-paid services performed physically in Palau prevent high confidence for a remote-worker scenario.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: There is no lawful digital-nomad immigration category. RNS advertises 0% Palau tax on income earned outside Palau, while the immigration authority classifies the physical-stay benefit as a tourist extension that does not authorize employment or business activity.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital identity plus tourist extension; not a remote-worker residence status
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% operator claim for genuinely non-Palau income; otherwise up to 12% screening rate depending on wage/business characterization
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No general day-count test confirmed; Digital Residency alone is not evidence of physical tax residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: RNS claims 0% on income earned outside Palau. Income from services physically performed in Palau requires tax-authority advice and cannot safely be assumed foreign-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No tax-authority-confirmed physical digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If treated as covered Palau wages, employee Social Security and Healthcare Fund contributions total 9.5%, with a matching 9.5% employer share. Business-owner rules may differ.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly digital-nomad payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based rather than fixed: employee 7% SS plus 2.5% HCF for covered local wages; self-employed/owner treatment requires classification.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Ordinary tourist renewal is USD 50. The immigration page does not clearly state the Digital Resident extension fee because its fee sentence appears mislabeled. Resident Visa issuance is USD 200; FIAC filing is generally USD 500, or USD 2,500 for lodging.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Small-business license, GRT, BPT, PGST, foreign-investment filing fees, and annual non-citizen employment fees may apply depending on local registration and activity.
fixed_payments.notes: No fixed payment should be inferred for an unlawful visitor-remote-work arrangement.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short visitor stay does not authorize remote employment or business activity. Remaining below an unconfirmed day threshold does not cure the immigration prohibition.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: No ordinary route or general residence-day rule was confirmed. A person working physically from Palau should obtain immigration authorization and a written tax/source assessment.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local operation may require company registration, physical premises, FIAC approval, business licensing, tax registration, and compliance with Social Security/Healthcare Fund rules. This is not a lightweight foreign-client freelancer route.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The official immigration prohibition is clear. Tax confidence is lower because the 0% foreign-income statement comes from RNS terms and no tax-authority ruling for services performed during a tourist stay was found.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A discretionary Resident Visa can be issued directly for up to two years, but it is not an ordinary remote-worker entitlement. The Digital Resident tourist extension is not residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No fixed conversion period from the reviewed visas to an indefinite permanent-resident status was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Not applicable to an ordinary applicant without recognized Palauan ancestry.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Palau has no residence-by-years naturalization path for a person lacking recognized Palauan ancestry.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No meaningful processing time applies to the applicant profile because the ancestry eligibility condition is not met.

key_conditions.value: Naturalization is restricted to persons born of at least one parent of recognized Palauan ancestry. Residence duration, employment, marriage, business ownership, or Digital Residency does not substitute for ancestry.
key_conditions.notes: Dual citizenship is permitted for eligible Palauan citizens under current Title 13, but that does not expand eligibility to applicants without Palauan ancestry.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No marriage-duration route to citizenship was found; recognized Palauan ancestry remains required.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage to a Palauan citizen does not independently make a spouse eligible for naturalization. A genuine marriage may support a dependent/family immigration application, but no automatic permanent residence was confirmed.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The immigration criteria request a valid marriage license, joint affidavit, sponsorship evidence, and financial support for relevant dependent applications.

requirements_and_risks.value: Family/dependent status requires documentary proof of the genuine relationship and sponsorship. Sham marriage or false affidavits can lead to denial, revocation, and other legal consequences. Marriage cannot overcome the constitutional ancestry restriction on naturalization.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No accelerated spousal-citizenship timeline exists for an ordinary non-ancestry applicant.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Palau alone is insufficient. Citizenship at birth depends on a citizen parent or recognized Palauan ancestry, subject to the governing constitutional amendments and Citizenship Act.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Palau to two non-Palauan migrant parents does not acquire citizenship solely from birthplace.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The parents' own nationality laws and anti-statelessness considerations should be checked separately.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Palauan-citizen parent qualifies for Palauan citizenship by descent under the constitutional rule.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Documentary registration requirements should be confirmed with the Ministry of Justice, especially for a child born abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Palauan citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. A parent may investigate dependent or family immigration, but no automatic PR or citizenship benefit was established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The ancestry restriction continues to apply to the parent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically gain residence, permanent residence, or citizenship because his child is Palauan. If the other parent is Palauan, the child may be a citizen, while the father must qualify separately for immigration status.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No special father-of-citizen naturalization provision was found.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is an official language and is used in government and statistical publications, making day-to-day administration reasonably practical in English. Immigration status and island connectivity remain separate practical constraints.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No national broadband-quality guarantee was established in the inspected sources.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no evidence of broad public-service availability in either language was found. English would be the practical working language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian citizens receive a 30-day visa-free entry arrangement according to Immigration, but that does not imply Russian-language services or work authorization.

The 2020 census contains citizenship and annual wage/salary variables, but its report presents mean income tabulations and the catalog states that public microdata access is unavailable; the 2023/24 HIES catalogs do not publish the requested citizen-worker median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum wage is published; government pay scales are not a national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: USD 5.00 per hour; approximately USD 866.67 per month at 40 hours/week
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Monthly equivalent of the FY2023 Palauan-citizen average annual wage.

median_salary_local_currency.value: No published national median for Palauan-citizen employee wages
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Palau uses USD. The official 2020 census report defines wage and salary income and says its income tabulations present means rather than a national citizen-worker median. Its catalog confirms separate citizenship and annual gross wage/salary variables, but public row-level data access is disabled, so a citizen-only median cannot be calculated reproducibly. The 2023/24 HIES dataset and ILO-derived catalog include employee monthly-earnings variables, yet neither inspected published output reports a Palauan-citizen median. Household income, public-sector occupation medians, and unsupported salary-site estimates were not substituted.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No published national maximum salary measure
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The national government pay scale is not a maximum for the entire labor market.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Citizen average: FY2023 nominal average annual wage divided by 12. Minimum: statutory hourly rate converted using a 40-hour week.
average_citizen_salary.period: FY2023 average wage; minimum wage current from 2025-10-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average citizen-worker and statutory minimum-wage indicators, not immigration income thresholds. The citizen average is more relevant to the requested average-citizen measure than the lower economy-wide average, which includes foreign workers. A focused official-source audit did not find a published Palauan-citizen median; the relevant census microdata are not publicly downloadable, so the median remains expressly unpublished rather than estimated.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2023/24 HIES reported average annual household expenditure of USD 32,834, about USD 2,736 per household per month, and annual per-capita expenditure of USD 12,712, about USD 1,059 per month. Food represented roughly 35% of consumption expenditure; Palau's import dependence contributes to high living costs.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Household expenditure includes cash spending, gifts, home production, imputed rent, and transfers, so it is not a single-person expatriate budget.
