settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Digital Residency provides a government-recognized ID and eligibility for tourist extensions, not work authorization, immigration residence, permanent residence, or a citizenship path.
settlement_track.summary: Only visitor-like, discretionary, employer-sponsored, locally established business, and high-fee elite options were found; none is a confirmed ordinary foreign-contract remote-work settlement route. Naturalization is additionally unavailable to an ordinary applicant without recognized Palauan ancestry.
settlement_track.notes: The discretionary Resident Visa may provide renewable temporary residence, but published rules do not establish a remote-worker entitlement, PR progression, or any way around the ancestry-based citizenship restriction.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: RNS markets Digital Residency to global remote workers, but the official physical-stay benefit is a tourist extension and Palau's immigration authority expressly prohibits work, commercial activity, and business activity on tourist status. No separate ordinary remote-worker visa was found.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit retained the ineligible immigration and citizenship conclusion and rechecked the citizen-median salary field against seven additional canonical URLs not in the previous source set. The official 2020 census report defines wage/salary income and states that its income tabulations present means; its data catalog exposes citizenship and annual wage/salary variables but says public microdata access is unavailable. The 2023/24 HIES and ILO-harmonized catalogs expose employee-earnings variables, but no inspected published table reports a Palauan-citizen employee median. Accordingly, no household median, public-sector occupation median, or unsupported salary-site estimate was substituted. Other unresolved legal and tax fields remain as previously qualified.

data.selection_summary: Panama has an independent Professional Foreigner residence category that begins with provisional residence and can progress to permanent residence. However, it is qualification-based rather than an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route, foreign credentials require homologation, and engineering and allied regulated professions are excluded. The applicant must confirm that the exact software-related degree qualifies. The dedicated Remote Worker Short-Stay Visa fits foreign employment or clients but is a non-resident status capped at 18 months with no confirmed settlement conversion.

visa_application.title: Professional Foreigner provisional and permanent residence requirements
visa_application.notes: Official document checklist, not a public online application form. Filing requires a notarized power and application; no direct public filing portal for this category was confirmed.

best_routes.route_name: Provisional/Permanent Residence as a Professional Foreigner

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current official checklist publishes no minimum-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum income is stated in the current checklist.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; qualification eligibility is the principal test
income_requirement_display.notes: Government fees and later tax or social-security compliance are separate from an income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The checklist does not prescribe a prior income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: University bachelor's, master's or doctoral diploma, apostilled or authenticated; a foreign diploma requires official homologation.
The profession must not be constitutionally or legally reserved to Panamanians.
Engineering, architecture and allied technical professions are treated as reserved; eligibility of the applicant's exact software-related credential must be confirmed before filing.
Notarized power and application, passport copy, photographs, criminal-record certificate, health certificate and personal-background declaration.
Initial government checks of B/.250 to the National Treasury and B/.800 to the National Migration Service.

initial_validity.value: 2 years of provisional residence
initial_validity.notes: The category begins with a provisional stage; permanent residence requires a separate application.

extension_rules.value: After the provisional stage, apply for permanent residence under the same professional category
extension_rules.notes: Permanent residence is not automatic.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The first approval grants provisional residence directly.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence rather than a visitor or non-resident visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply for permanent residence after the two-year provisional period.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Eligibility remains dependent on a recognized degree in a non-reserved profession.

path_to_citizenship.value: A qualifying resident may seek naturalization under the general constitutional rule after five consecutive years of residence, subject to permanent-resident documentation and other requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Official sources do not expressly state how every day of professional provisional residence is counted; confirm the residence-counting date with SNM.

best_routes.notes: Potential independent qualification-based settlement route, not an ordinary remote-worker route. No local-employer document appears in the checklist, but the applicant's exact diploma title is decisive. A credential classified as engineering or an allied regulated profession may be rejected.

rejected_routes.route_name: Short-Stay Visa as a Remote Worker

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: B/.36,000 annually; the balboa is numerically at parity with USD.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: B/.3,000 monthly or B/.36,000 annually

income_requirement_display.value: B/.3,000 (USD 3,000) monthly; B/.36,000 annually

income_proof_months.notes: Bank certification or statements are required, but no universal number of prior months is prescribed.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign-company employment or autonomous telework, with functions producing effects abroad and income from foreign sources.
Employees provide foreign-company and employment/income evidence; independent applicants provide evidence of a foreign-registered business and client relationships.
Passport, photographs, criminal record, health certificate, medical insurance covering Panama, application forms and an undertaking not to accept Panamanian work or services.
B/.250 migration payment and B/.50 card fee.

initial_validity.value: 9 months
initial_validity.notes: Created within the No Residente category.

extension_rules.value: One extension of 9 months; maximum 18 months

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The visa authorizes remote work and presence but is legally non-resident, not temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Conditional separate professional-residence route with a later PR stage; engineering and other reserved professions are excluded, so the applicant’s exact degree must be accepted.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The current professional checklist and official engineering-exclusion notice were readable. The decree opened only as a scanned PDF with no usable text, and its two-year period was not independently extracted in this review, so years_to_pr remains null. No generic remote-worker conversion or exit rule was established. Short-stay time is not the professional provisional-residence period.

path_to_citizenship.notes: This visa is expressly classified as No Residente, while the current naturalization checklist requires an authenticated permanent-resident card and permanent-resident migration-status certification. Neither the remote-worker decree nor the immigration and naturalization materials provide a conversion rule or say that No Residente time counts toward the constitutional residence period; a separate qualifying residence and permanent-resident status are therefore required before citizenship can be presented as available.

rejected_routes.notes: A strong temporary-living match for foreign-contract remote work, but rejected because it is non-resident, capped at 18 months and lacks a confirmed settlement pathway.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed minimum is published; adequate study and subsistence funding must be shown.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed amount is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed amount; scholarship, financing or adequate bank solvency required

income_proof_months.notes: No universal prior-month period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Full-time regular study at a recognized institution, admission and enrollment evidence, funding, domicile, health certificate and criminal record where applicable.
Employment is prohibited except required professional practice or internships.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence tied to the approved study program
initial_validity.notes: The checklist does not state one universal duration.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires the prior requirements and official academic credits showing the previous year was passed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence for full-time study.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct permanent-residence conversion is stated in the official education checklist.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The education permit is a temporary-resident category, but the current naturalization checklist requires a permanent-resident card and permanent-resident status certification at filing. The education checklist and migration law publish no direct conversion to permanent residence and do not state whether student temporary-residence time is credited toward Article 10's consecutive-residence period; that credit remains unresolved rather than assumed.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for the working software-engineer profile because it requires full-time study and generally prohibits employment, including ordinary remote work.

summary.value: The Professional Foreigner category begins with provisional residence without a local-employer document in the current checklist, followed by a permanent-residence application. It requires diploma homologation and excludes professions reserved to Panamanians; whether the applicant's exact software degree qualifies needs confirmation. A full-time student permit also grants temporary residence but prohibits ordinary employment and has no confirmed direct PR path.
summary.notes: The professional route, rather than the student permit, is the potentially relevant qualification-based settlement option.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is a Panamanian tax resident after spending more than 183 days, consecutive or non-consecutive, in Panama during the fiscal year or immediately preceding year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence is distinct from immigration residence and does not alone determine whether income is Panama-source.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate on Panama-source net taxable personal income, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Article 71 of the amended CSS law broadly requires national and foreign workers providing services inside Panama, including employees and independent workers, to participate. Mandatory independent-worker coverage is limited to disability, old-age and death at 9.36% of contributable income; health and maternity are voluntary at 8.5% of declared income on a minimum B/.800 base. The remote-worker rules do not publish how CSS classifies or collects from a non-resident employee paid solely by an offshore employer.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No fixed monthly amount applies: an independent worker's mandatory CSS pension contribution is percentage-based at 9.36%. Optional health and maternity cost 8.5% of voluntarily declared income of at least B/.800, equal to B/.68 monthly only if elected at that minimum base. Mandatory private medical insurance is market-priced.

special_tax_regimes.value: Panama generally uses territorial-source taxation. No specific digital-nomad income-tax exemption or holiday was found in the remote-worker decree or current checklist.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A foreign payer does not necessarily make services foreign-source when the work is physically performed in Panama.

taxes.caveats: Panama-source characterization is crucial. DGI states that income from activities carried out in Panama is taxable regardless of nationality, domicile or residence, so remote services physically performed in Panama require professional source analysis. Contract structure, tax-residence certificate eligibility, permanent establishment, social-security registration and treaty position may change the outcome.

taxation_system.value: Territorial taxation with progressive personal-income-tax rates on Panama-source net taxable income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in Panama during the fiscal year or immediately preceding year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Panama-source income; DGI describes income from activities performed in Panama as taxable regardless of nationality, domicile or residence.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No route-specific tax exemption was confirmed for remote-worker visa holders.
taxation_system.social_security: The amended CSS law makes affiliation compulsory for national or foreign employees and independent workers providing services inside Panama. Independent workers owe 9.36% of contributable income for disability, old-age and death; health and maternity are optional at 8.5% on declared income of at least B/.800. Published remote-worker rules do not explain offshore-employer payroll registration or collection.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 25% is the top marginal screening rate. The first B/.11,000 of annual net taxable income is exempt; 15% applies to the excess through B/.50,000; above B/.50,000, tax is B/.5,850 plus 25% of the excess.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net taxable income up to B/.11,000
tax_brackets.notes: Balboa amounts are numerically equivalent to USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Excess over B/.11,000 through B/.50,000 annually
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net taxable income above B/.50,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over B/.50,000 after B/.5,850 tax on the first B/.50,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket, not effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official DGI and CSS sources support the rates and residence threshold. Treatment of a particular foreign contract requires individualized tax and CSS analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The remote-worker visa does not publish a special tax holiday. Panama's territorial system may exclude genuinely foreign-source income, but DGI states that activities carried out in Panama generate taxable income; work physically performed in Panama should not automatically be treated as exempt merely because the payer and clients are foreign.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: non-resident remote-worker visa under ordinary territorial tax rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–25% progressive tax on Panama-source net taxable income; 25% is the top marginal screening rate, with no confirmed nomad exemption.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in Panama in the fiscal year or immediately preceding year. Because the visa can last up to 18 months, tax residence can arise.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-source income is generally outside territorial income tax, but DGI ties taxable source to activities performed in Panama. Foreign payment alone is insufficient to establish foreign-source treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No official digital-nomad income-tax exemption or preferential rate was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Article 71 of the current CSS law broadly makes affiliation compulsory for every national or foreign worker providing services inside Panama. A remote worker treated as independent is within the stated mandatory scope for disability, old-age and death at 9.36% of contributable income; health and maternity are voluntary at 8.5% on declared income of at least B/.800, and independent workers have no occupational-risk coverage. For an employee of an offshore company, the law defines employees by reference to employers operating in Panama, while the remote-worker decree authorizes work without another state permit but contains no CSS exemption, foreign-employer payroll-registration rule or collection procedure. That employee-payroll classification requires CSS confirmation and should not be reported as automatically exempt.

fixed_payments.status: one-time_visa_fees_and_variable_private_insurance
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: For an independent worker, CSS is percentage-based rather than fixed: mandatory 9.36% pension-related coverage; optional health and maternity are 8.5% on at least B/.800 declared income, or B/.68 monthly at the minimum if elected. Offshore-employer payroll treatment for a non-resident remote employee is not specified in the route materials and requires CSS confirmation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: B/.250 migration payment plus B/.50 card fee; one extension is available. Any additional extension filing charge should be reconfirmed.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No special fixed freelancer tax, municipal fee, VAT threshold or transaction tax specific to this visa was established from the official route materials.
fixed_payments.notes: Private medical insurance covering Panama for the whole stay is mandatory, but no standardized premium is published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 183 days may avoid Panamanian tax-resident status, but it does not automatically exempt Panama-source income from work physically performed in Panama.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect territorial source analysis and potentially progressive filing on Panama-source services; do not assume a foreign employer or client makes the income tax-free.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: An independent worker providing services while in Panama falls within Article 71's compulsory CSS scope and owes 9.36% of contributable income for disability, old-age and death; health and maternity may be elected at 8.5% on a declared base of at least B/.800. CSS stated that independent affiliation is obligatory, while its May 2025 notice said implementation processes under the reform were still being operationalized; no newer route-specific implementation guidance was located.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Rates and general statutory coverage are clear. The unresolved point is the CSS/payroll treatment and collection mechanism for a non-resident employee paid only by an offshore employer.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: If eligible, the professional category directly grants provisional residence; zero does not represent processing time.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Permanent residence requires a separate filing after the provisional professional stage.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Constitution uses five consecutive years of residence rather than a fixed number of years after PR. The checklist requires a permanent-resident card but does not expressly confirm how preceding provisional residence is credited.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General constitutional residence benchmark if the entire qualifying period is accepted. It is unavailable through the non-resident remote-worker visa alone.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Current official sources publish requirements and case tracking but no reliable typical or statutory processing duration.

key_conditions.value: Five consecutive years of qualifying residence; permanent-resident documentation at filing; express renunciation of existing nationality; Spanish ability; basic knowledge of Panamanian geography, history and political organization; criminal-record, tax-clearance, economic-solvency and interview documentation. The checklist also requests evidence concerning absences exceeding three months during the relevant period.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization remains discretionary, and the exact residence-counting date should be confirmed before relying on the timeline.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The constitutional shortcut is three consecutive years of residence for a foreigner with a Panamanian spouse or qualifying Panamanian children. Separately, spouse residence permits a PR application after two provisional years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Panamanian citizen can support provisional spouse residence and the three-year naturalization residence category. Marriage to another foreigner creates no shortcut.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage alone does not automatically grant residence or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The couple must live together with singularity, stability and continuity, document the marriage and common domicile, and may be interviewed. Permanent residence may be requested after two provisional years. Naturalization still requires residence, Spanish, civic knowledge, renunciation and supporting documentation. Sham marriages risk refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: SNM expressly states that marriage to a Panamanian does not by itself create a right to residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 9 grants Panamanian nationality by birth to persons born in the national territory without a general parental-residence condition.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Panama is Panamanian by birth even when both parents are foreign migrants; the Constitution states no general parent-status condition.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Panama is Panamanian by territorial birth. A child born abroad to a Panamanian parent by birth can qualify after establishing domicile in Panama; additional election rules apply when the Panamanian parent was naturalized.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Panamanian child may use the dedicated family-reunification residence category once the child is at least five years old, initially provisionally and then for permanent residence after two years. The Constitution also reduces the naturalization residence benchmark to three years for a foreigner with qualifying Panamanian children.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The child's citizenship does not automatically make the parent a citizen.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father can seek the Panamanian-child residence route once the child is at least five and must show fulfillment of parental duties. After two provisional years he may apply for PR. He may also qualify for the three-year naturalization residence category, but citizenship remains an application subject to all other conditions.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No automatic residence or citizenship arises at the child's birth.

rank.notes: Current Passport Power Rank displayed by this index; it should not be mixed with Henley's different scoring method.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category reported separately by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 42 visa-on-arrival and 8 eTA destinations; the index separately reports a mobility score of 138.

passport.notes: Figures use one named index so the separated categories remain internally consistent. Henley did not expose the requested category breakdown on its ranking page.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate in international-business and tourism settings, but Spanish is the constitutional official language and is required for naturalization. Immigration, tax and local administration should be expected to require Spanish or professional assistance.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No authoritative nationwide English-use measurement was found; the assessment is cautious.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low for routine administration: neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, and no reliable evidence of broad public-service availability in either language was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: An interpreter or Spanish-speaking adviser is likely to be needed for official procedures.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: INEC's September 2025 Labour Market Survey catalog identifies salary Tables 25 and 26 as median-and-distribution tables; it does not publish a national arithmetic mean monthly employee salary. The reference to a representative weekly average describes survey coverage, not an average wage.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: National monthly employee median for September 2025. Balboas are numerically at parity with USD.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Panama has no single national monthly minimum: the 2026 decree contains 59 activity- and region-specific rates, many expressed hourly.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The September 2025 EML publishes a national median and percentage distributions, but no national arithmetic mean monthly salary for employees or citizens specifically; median B/.755.8 must not be relabeled as an average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official national median monthly salary of employees aged 15 and over, September 2025.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official distribution has an open-ended B/.3,000-and-over band and therefore establishes no meaningful maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: No single amount; 59 region/activity-specific rates under Executive Decree 13 of 31 December 2025
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Rates became applicable in 2026 and must be queried by activity, region and province.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: INEC's September 2025 publication directory lists salary Tables 25 and 26 as medians with percentage distributions and supplies no national arithmetic mean in balboas. It covers habitual residents aged 15 and over in private dwellings, not a citizenship-only population; therefore neither an employee mean nor an average-citizen salary is published in these named current sources.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: National employee median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No maximum is published; the top distribution category is open-ended.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Monthly salary received by employees aged 15 and over in the national Labour Market Survey
average_citizen_salary.period: September 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The official median is well supported. Mean and maximum remain null because the reviewed tables do not publish them, while the statutory minimum varies by region and activity.

cost_of_living_note.value: As a current official food-cost benchmark, the MEF calculated the May 2026 basic family food basket at B/.367.00 per month in the districts of Panama and San Miguelito and B/.346.09 in the rest of urban Panama. This is a family food basket only, not a complete cost-of-living budget: it excludes housing, utilities, transport, health care and other household spending.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Balboas are numerically at parity with USD. Use these figures only as regional food-basket benchmarks, not as a single-person or all-expenses budget. The June 2026 INEC CPI measures price change rather than the monetary cost of a standard household budget, and the ENIGH 2024–2025 publication page does not expose a concise comparable monthly total suitable for this field.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Remote Worker Short-Stay Visa is non-resident and cannot serve as the confirmed settlement track. Settlement instead depends on qualifying for the separate Professional Foreigner residence category.
settlement_track.summary: The Professional Foreigner category can progress from provisional to permanent residence and potentially naturalization, but it is qualification-based rather than a remote-work route. The applicant must confirm that the exact software-related diploma is not treated as a reserved engineering profession and that provisional residence will be credited as expected.
settlement_track.notes: The remote-worker visa itself has no confirmed settlement track. Classification reflects the separate professional-residence route and its required conversion to PR.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign-contract remote work is expressly permitted only under the temporary non-resident remote-worker visa. The settlement-capable professional route does not require a local-employer document but is degree-based, not designed for foreign-contract remote work, and may exclude a software-engineering credential.

data.notes: Focused unexplained-null audit completed against the previous Panama record. At least 17 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected in the current pass, including five official/statistical URLs absent from the previous source set. The flagged cost-of-living field is now filled with the freshest official regional family food-basket benchmark and expressly warns that it is not a full household or single-person budget. The applicant-specific professional-route issue remains because official sources exclude engineering and allied professions but do not conclusively classify every software or computer-science diploma.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Professional Foreigner provisional/permanent residence, if degree and profession are eligible
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A remote-worker short-stay holder needs a separate qualifying residence application. The Professional Foreigner route has a PR stage, but its degree and reserved-profession restrictions can exclude an engineering qualification.
requirements: Hold a recognized/homologated degree in a profession not reserved for Panamanian nationals.
Obtain provisional residence and later meet the permanent-stage checklist.
Resolve the exact classification of a software/computer-engineering degree before treating this route as available.
reviewed_route_names: Short-Stay Visa as a Remote Worker
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The current professional checklist and official engineering-exclusion notice were readable. The decree opened only as a scanned PDF with no usable text, and its two-year period was not independently extracted in this review, so years_to_pr remains null. No generic remote-worker conversion or exit rule was established. Short-stay time is not the professional provisional-residence period.

data.selection_summary: Papua New Guinea has no current digital-nomad, remote-worker, freelance, or ordinary self-employed residence route for a software engineer working solely under a foreign contract. Paid work generally requires a sponsor/employer-filed work permit and Working Resident Visa; business, investor, and permanent-residence classes require substantive PNG business activity, investment, local work history, or another narrow connection. Visitor and business visas do not create a qualifying remote-work or settlement route.

visa_application.title: PNG ICA eVisa application
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct application portal for available eVisa classes, not a remote-worker application. Employer-sponsored work applications instead use the sponsor process and combined work-permit/Working Resident procedure.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The current official materials do not publish a generally applicable minimum salary; the employment contract and position are assessed.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The inspected official work-permit material does not prescribe a general PGK salary threshold for all employment permits.

income_requirement_display.value: No published general minimum; employer-sponsored employment contract required
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Employment contract rather than a fixed threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an independent foreign-contract route.

income_proof_months.notes: The official work-permit handbook requires a signed employment contract but does not prescribe a fixed number of prior salary or income-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: A sponsor or employer must apply for the work permit on the worker's behalf.
Requires a signed employment contract, job description, qualifications, CV, employer incorporation evidence, fee receipt, and other supporting documents.
The permit is employer- and occupation-specific and is not transferable.
Relevant tertiary qualifications, experience, and language proficiency are generally required.

initial_validity.value: Short-term work permits: up to 6 months; long-term permits: 1–3 years, or up to 5 years for qualifying Good Corporate Citizens
initial_validity.notes: The accompanying Working Resident Visa is also required.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is employer-linked and normally must be requested three months before expiry for the same position and company.
extension_rules.notes: Changing employer or position requires a new permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved work permit supports a Working Resident Visa, but only through the sponsor/employer process.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Permanent residence may become possible after at least five years of continuous PNG residence only if the applicant also satisfies one of the narrow PR classes.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Software engineering alone is not among the listed skilled-professional PR fields.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation can be requested after at least eight years of continuous residence, but this does not remove the need for a qualifying initial immigration status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Minister retains discretion.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the sponsor or employer applies and the permit is tied to PNG employment. A foreign-client contract alone does not qualify.

rejected_routes.route_name: Business Person or Investor Working Resident Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No ordinary monthly-income test is published; the route concerns establishing or conducting a PNG business or investment.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The inspected official materials require business, investment, work-permit, and corporate documentation but publish no monthly PGK income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income threshold published; substantive PNG business or investment required
income_requirement_display.notes: Foreign remote work by itself is not the stated purpose.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed look-back period for personal income or bank statements is prescribed. Current business-visa material requires financial maintenance or sufficient funds, and the foreign-enterprise process may require a latest balance sheet or bank statement and a projected first-year budget, but neither source converts this into a set number of income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: The visa class is for a person investing in or establishing a business in Papua New Guinea.

A foreign individual or foreign-controlled enterprise transacting business must obtain Foreign Investor Certification and provide proposed activities, investment, employment, budget, financial, identity, and CV documentation.

Official High Commission guidance identifies a valid work permit, incorporation documentation, IPA certification where applicable, a maintenance guarantee bond, qualifications, and CV among the requirements.

initial_validity.value: 3 months
initial_validity.notes: The current IPA investment guide's Working Resident Visa table gives three months for the Business Person/Investor class. The 2025 ICA fee booklet lists the class and fees but does not independently state a universal duration.

extension_rules.value: The 2025 ICA booklet lists a USD 700 extension fee; continued eligibility remains dependent on the visa, work-permit, and genuine business or investment circumstances.
extension_rules.notes: The booklet also lists a USD 380 application fee and USD 1,350 late-extension fee.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Can provide Working Resident status for genuine PNG business or investment activity, subject to the business, immigration, and work-permit requirements.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A majority business owner can seek PR after at least five years in a registered resident business, with net assets and turnover exceeding PGK 2 million, or qualifying PNG property investment of at least PGK 10 million.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: These substantial local-business and investment conditions are incompatible with ordinary foreign-client remote work.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may be requested after eight years of continuous residence if all constitutional requirements are met.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No ordinary remote-worker route exists at the beginning of this pathway.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires genuine PNG business or investment substance, Foreign Investor Certification where applicable, and work-permit compliance rather than merely working remotely for a foreign client.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Only sufficient support funds are required; no fixed amount is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed PGK threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; sufficient funds and financial-maintenance evidence may be required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a short business-visitor permission, not residence.

income_proof_months.notes: The current eVisa class page requires sufficient funds and a sponsorship letter stating financial maintenance. It says a personal bank statement is not mandatory but may be requested; it publishes no required statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Activities are limited to permissible business activities and meetings that do not constitute labour or employment.
Applicant must be a genuine business person, have sufficient funds, intend to leave, be a full-time employee of the represented company, and normally provide an invitation from a PNG-based sponsor.

initial_validity.value: Multiple entry for 12 months, with stays of up to 60 days per arrival
initial_validity.notes: Not available on arrival.

extension_rules.value: The 2025 booklet lists a USD 500 extension fee, but an extension does not convert the visa into work-authorised residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None; this is a temporary business-visitor visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct or confirmed conversion path.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor/business time is not established as a qualifying route to citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because permissible activities exclude labour or employment and the applicant must leave after the permitted stay.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is an asset, turnover, or property-investment test, not a monthly-income test.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: PGK 2 million net assets and turnover, or PGK 10 million qualifying property investment
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The business must have been a registered resident business for at least five years.

income_requirement_display.value: PGK 2 million business assets/turnover or PGK 10 million property investment
income_requirement_display.notes: These are not monthly income requirements.

income_proof_months.notes: A monthly income-proof period is inapplicable; the published substitute is at least five years of qualifying registered-resident-business history plus the capital or turnover evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: At least five years as majority owner of a registered resident business in PNG.
Net assets and turnover exceeding PGK 2 million, or qualifying PNG property investment of at least PGK 10 million.
General PR rules require five years' continuous residence, a valid long-term visa and work permit, criminal-record checks, and character references.

initial_validity.value: Indefinite residence, but the visa document is issued with the same validity as the holder's passport
initial_validity.notes: A replacement PR visa is needed when the passport expires; PR remains revocable for breach of conditions.

extension_rules.value: PR visa renewal may take up to seven business days; continuous absence exceeding 12 months without reasonable cause can breach conditions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Requires prior qualifying long-term residence and business activity; it is not an entry-level temporary route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct PR is possible upon satisfying the five-year residence, business-history, and capital requirements.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Normal processing is stated as approximately three to four months.

path_to_citizenship.value: A PR holder may later apply under the general eight-year continuous-residence naturalisation rule.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial PNG investment and five years of local business activity, not ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: A degree supports an employer-sponsored work-permit application, but PNG has no independent degree- or points-based route for a software engineer. The skilled-professional PR class is limited to medical doctors, specialists, and educationists with at least five years of work in PNG. A student visa requires full-time admission to a recognised PNG institution and is not an employment or direct PR route.
summary.notes: The applicant's software-engineering degree does not independently confer residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is normally treated as tax resident when present in Papua New Guinea for more than six months during the tax year; visits need not be continuous, and treaty rules may alter the result.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can also arise under broader statutory concepts, so individual advice may be needed.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective tax rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee superannuation contribution for covered employment; the covered employer contributes a further 8.4%. Compulsory coverage applies to employers engaging at least 15 employees and to their paid employees continuously employed for at least three months; smaller employers and their employees can participate voluntarily. The inspected law and regulator notice do not establish compulsory coverage for a self-employed foreign remote contractor without a PNG employer.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly social-security, payroll, or freelancer payment applies to the target scenario in the inspected sources. Percentage superannuation is employment-based, while foreign-contractor withholding is transaction-based and relevant only where its statutory PNG-contract conditions are met.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. A small-business regime exists, but it excludes employment income and professional-services income, so it is unlikely to cover software consulting.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The small-business regime otherwise uses a PGK 250 annual fee below PGK 60,000 turnover or quarterly/turnover formulas at higher eligible turnover.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on residence, where services are physically performed, income character, local business presence, the foreign-contractor rules, and any applicable treaty. PNG-source services may be taxable even when paid by a foreign client. Professional advice is advisable before working from PNG.

taxation_system.value: Progressive individual income tax, with residents taxed on worldwide income and non-residents generally taxed on PNG-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Normally more than six months' presence in a tax year, subject to statutory and treaty analysis.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: worldwide income with possible foreign-tax credit; non-residents: generally PNG-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. The small-business regime excludes employment and professional-services income.
taxation_system.social_security: The compulsory superannuation regime covers employers engaging at least 15 employees and their paid employees after three months of continuous employment: 6% is deducted from employee base salary and the employer contributes 8.4%. Employers below 15 employees may elect voluntary participation. The Act and Bank of PNG notice frame contributions through an employer-employee relationship and do not establish a mandatory fixed or percentage contribution for an independent foreign remote contractor without a PNG employer.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 42% is the top marginal screening rate. Resident rates are 0% through PGK 20,000, then marginal rates of 30%, 35%, 40%, and 42%; effective tax will be lower than 42% below the highest band.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses about USD 0.2274 per PGK from the Bank of PNG exchange-rate series inspected.
Threshold USD figure represents approximately PGK 33,000.
Threshold USD figure represents approximately PGK 70,000.
Threshold USD figure represents approximately PGK 250,000.
Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: Current rates were cross-checked against the government budget, Bank of PNG superannuation notice, governing superannuation Act, and PwC's PNG summary reviewed 10 August 2026. The National Trade Portal supplies the government day-count summary.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category: PNG has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker visa or tax regime. General residence, source, progressive-tax, and potentially foreign-contractor rules would need to be analysed if services were physically performed in PNG.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; general individual or professional-services taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive, up to 42% top marginal rate; this is a screening rate, not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Normally more than six months' presence in the tax year, subject to treaty and statutory analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents generally on PNG-source income. Services physically performed in PNG require source analysis even when paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The official 6% employee and 8.4% employer superannuation rates concern covered employer-employee arrangements. The inspected law and regulator notice do not impose that contribution on an independent foreign contractor with no PNG employer.

fixed_payments.status: Inapplicable as a nomad-specific schedule: PNG has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker category, and the inspected general tax and superannuation sources publish no universal fixed monthly payment for this hypothetical arrangement.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed remote-worker contribution is published. Percentage superannuation applies to covered local employment; employers with fewer than 15 employees may instead participate voluntarily.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad visa fee exists. Fees depend on an unrelated visa class; the 2025 booklet lists USD 380 for Working Resident classes and USD 50 online-lodgement fees for many visitor or business applications.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No universal monthly charge applies. The simplified small-business regime's PGK 250 annual charge excludes professional-services income. A 12% foreign-contractor withholding mechanism exists for qualifying payments under PNG contracts, but it is transaction-based rather than a fixed monthly fee and is not automatically applicable to every foreign remote contract.
fixed_payments.notes: Because there is no eligible remote-worker route, there is no nomad-specific fixed-payment schedule. Any PNG business registration, withholding, GST, or payroll obligation would depend on the actual legal and contractual structure.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining under six months does not itself establish tax exemption. PNG-source treatment depends on where services are performed, the contractual arrangement, and treaty rules.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident would generally face worldwide-income taxation at progressive rates up to 42%, with possible foreign-tax credits, but immigration permission to work would still be missing.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Local business registration does not independently legalise residence or work. Professional-services income is excluded from the simplified small-business regime, and qualifying PNG foreign-contract payments may attract 12% withholding.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section is hypothetical because no qualifying remote-worker route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No independent temporary-residence route exists for the target profile. Employer-sponsored Working Resident status can start after approval, but it is rejected for selection.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five years is the general minimum continuous-residence prerequisite, but an applicant must also meet a narrow PR class. It is not a universal entitlement.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Inferred from PR eligibility after at least five years and naturalisation after eight years of continuous residence. This assumes all residence counts continuously and is not a guaranteed three-year post-PR rule.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation eligibility; there is no qualifying initial route for the target profile, and approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official form describes extensive checks, Citizenship Advisory Committee consideration, and ministerial decision but provides no typical processing duration.

key_conditions.value: At least eight years of continuous residence; the long-term-resident form states no absence longer than 180 days during that period. Applicants need good character, intent to reside permanently, self-support, citizenship knowledge, cultural respect, and conversational Tok Pisin, Hiri Motu, or a vernacular. Renunciation is generally required unless approved dual citizenship is available with a prescribed country.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For citizenship by marriage, the official C6 form requires legal marriage to a PNG citizen and at least 12 months of residence in PNG during the preceding three years. Separately, spouse-class PR requires the relationship to have existed for at least five years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage helps only if the spouse is a PNG citizen. It may support citizenship by marriage after the residence condition or spouse-class PR after a five-year relationship; marriage to another migrant creates no special route.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must document the legal marriage, PNG residence, good character, and genuine relationship. Police clearances and references from PNG citizens are required for citizenship; sham or undocumented relationships risk refusal and possible immigration consequences. Citizenship remains subject to government checks and approval and is not automatic through marriage.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The C6 form lists a PGK 10,000 naturalisation fee or PGK 15,000 when also seeking approved dual citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Section 66 of the Constitution grants citizenship to a child born in PNG when at least one parent is a citizen. Birth in PNG alone to two known foreign parents is insufficient; unknown-parent cases receive protective presumptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in PNG to two known foreign parents does not acquire PNG citizenship solely by birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Unknown-parent presumptions or other exceptional protective provisions may apply.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in PNG on or after Independence Day is a citizen when one parent is a PNG citizen. A child born abroad to a PNG-citizen parent qualifies subject to prescribed birth registration.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A PNG-citizen child does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence, or citizenship on a foreign parent. The current ICA material describes the Dependent of Citizen class for a citizen's children, while the published PR classes cover a citizen's qualifying spouse and adult non-citizen child—not the foreign parent of a citizen child. A foreign parent who is also the spouse or de facto partner of a PNG citizen may have a partner-based class, but that benefit arises from the partner relationship rather than parenthood.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No dedicated parent-of-minor-PNG-citizen residence or PR class was published in the current ICA visa booklet, visa catalogue, PR-class list, or official High Commission category guidance inspected. Discretionary consideration cannot be excluded, but no automatic parent benefit should be inferred.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father gains no automatic status merely because the child's mother is a PNG citizen and the child is therefore a citizen. If he is the citizen mother's spouse or recognised de facto partner, he may need to qualify under the applicable partner/dependent, employment, PR, or citizenship-by-marriage rules.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the source when inspected on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations, not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately lists eVisa destinations; its visa-required count is reproduced as displayed.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 42 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: The same index reports a mobility score of 86. Passport-index methodologies differ, so these figures should not be mixed with Henley's combined-access score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the principal language of government and commerce, making professional communication feasible, although Tok Pisin is the main everyday lingua franca in much of the country.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Internet and infrastructure practicality varies substantially by location and was not treated as an immigration entitlement.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or commonly documented working languages; relying on either without English or Tok Pisin would be impractical.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No authoritative population-level usage data for Russian or Ukrainian was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of PGK 1,564 mean monthly monetary earnings using about USD 0.2274 per PGK.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of PGK 763 median monthly monetary earnings.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the statutory PGK 3.50 hourly minimum at 40 hours per week and 4.33 weeks per month; it is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate mean among Papua New Guineans with monetary earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate median among Papua New Guineans with monetary earnings.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The 2024 labour-market report publishes an open-ended top band of more than PGK 5,000 per month, not a maximum observation or national maximum. The official NSO survey page and SPC labour-force-survey collection page inspected do not publish a national maximum salary from which a USD amount could be calculated.

min_salary_local_currency.value: PGK 3.50 per hour; approximately PGK 606 per month at 40 hours/week
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage, not an observed lower bound.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean monetary earnings among Papua New Guineans with monetary earnings.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monetary earnings among Papua New Guineans with monetary earnings.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No finite national maximum salary is published in the current sources inspected. The 2024 BCFW distribution ends with an open-ended 'more than PGK 5,000 per month' bracket, which establishes neither the survey maximum nor a meaningful economy-wide maximum. The NSO survey page lists labour-force tables without a maximum-pay statistic, and the SPC 2025 labour-force-survey page identifies the collection but publishes no maximum earnings result.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Mean and median monthly monetary earnings from PNG labour-market survey analysis; minimum is the statutory hourly wage converted to a monthly equivalent; no finite maximum is published
average_citizen_salary.period: Labour-market analysis published November 2024; NSO survey resources and the SPC 2025 labour-force-survey collection were checked for newer maximum-pay data on 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average-citizen earnings, not immigration income thresholds. The mean and median apply to respondents with monetary earnings. The available distribution's top category is open-ended above PGK 5,000, so it must not be represented as a maximum. USD conversions are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: The government was reviewing the PGK 3.50 hourly minimum because of increased living costs and inflation, but no reliable nationwide monthly cost-of-living basket was established in the inspected sources.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Cost varies sharply between Port Moresby, other urban areas, and rural communities.
