settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor and business eVisas are temporary and do not authorise ordinary remote employment or provide a confirmed settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: No regular foreign-contract remote-work route exists. Settlement is available only through materially different statuses such as employer-sponsored work, substantial PNG business/investment, marriage, or another narrow PR class, so this profile cannot begin a qualifying citizenship track independently.
settlement_track.notes: Although general naturalisation is available after eight years of qualifying continuous residence, that rule does not cure the absence of a suitable entry and residence route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official visa catalogue contains no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker class. Business visits exclude labour or employment, while paid work requires the applicable PNG work authorisation, sponsor/employer process, or genuine local business/investment structure.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous record. Thirty-six distinct canonical sources are retained, including eleven sources outside the previous source set. The business-route income-evidence note now states exactly what current ICA and investment material require; superannuation scope is tied to the statutory employer-employee rules; the nomad fixed-payment field is marked factually inapplicable rather than unconfirmed; the foreign-parent consequence is distinguished from spouse and child-dependent classes; and the salary maximum remains null because the current distribution is open-ended above PGK 5,000 and no inspected official statistical source publishes a finite national maximum.

data.selection_summary: Paraguay has no separate digital-nomad visa, but its ordinary temporary residence is independently available for lawful activity and is a statutory route to permanent residence. The current permanent-residence conversion rules expressly recognize remote workers/digital nomads and accept an apostilled foreign work certificate stating income and payment method. This makes the route suitable for an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer without a Paraguayan employer, although genuine residence, local tax compliance and eventual conversion to permanent residence are required for citizenship.

visa_application.title: Residencia Temporal establecida por la Ley N° 6984/2022 de Migraciones
visa_application.notes: This is the official route and document-checklist page, not a complete online application. The residence application is personal and generally filed in Paraguay; whether a consular visa is needed before filing depends on nationality.

best_routes.route_name: Ordinary temporary residence followed by permanent residence under the remote-worker/digital-nomad solvency category

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numeric monthly minimum is published for either initial temporary residence or the remote-worker evidence used at permanent-residence conversion.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed PYG threshold is published. At conversion, a remote worker must document the work relationship, income received and payment method.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed minimum published; at permanent-residence conversion, provide an apostilled work certificate stating income and how salary or fees are received
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Evidence-based, with no published numerical threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Foreign work certificate showing income and payment method
income_requirement_display.notes: The current official conversion page separately lists trabajadores a distancia o nómadas digitales. It does not state a minimum income or a mandatory number of bank-statement months.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed history is stated for the remote-worker category. Other independent-professional categories use three recent IVA returns or the last annual IRP return, but those periods should not be imposed on the separate remote-worker category without filing-level confirmation.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport or identity document, lawful-entry evidence and any required consular visa.
Apostilled/legalized birth certificate, civil-status document where applicable, and foreign criminal or police certificate covering the relevant country of residence.
Paraguayan Interpol and police records, sworn commitment to comply with the Constitution and laws, and a declared Paraguayan address.

For permanent-residence conversion as a remote worker, a certificate or employment confirmation supporting the foreign work relationship, stating income and the means through which salary or professional fees are received; foreign documents require apostille/legalization and Spanish translation.
Personal filing in Paraguay and payment of the residence fee; document acceptance does not guarantee approval.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: The law and current checklist state that temporary residence may be granted for up to two years.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for an equal period; alternatively, change to permanent residence after completing the temporary-residence period
extension_rules.notes: The current fee schedule separately lists temporary-residence extension. A late change-of-category filing can force an extension and penalties, so conversion timing should be confirmed before the card expires.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply directly for ordinary Law 6984 temporary residence to settle and perform a lawful activity. Temporary/precarious status during processing permits work, study, exit and re-entry.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is residence rather than visitor or workcation permission.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Change category after the temporary-residence term. The official solvency rules expressly include remote workers/digital nomads and accept documented foreign work, income and payment method.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent status is indefinite, with the physical card renewed every ten years. This conversion, rather than temporary residence alone, is the critical settlement step.

path_to_citizenship.value: After at least 3 years of permanent residence, apply to the Supreme Court for a naturalization letter and prove adulthood, genuine residence, good conduct, and actual exercise in Paraguay of a profession, trade, science, art or industry.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Eligibility is not automatic approval. The court checklist requires permanent-residence evidence and proof of work, business, study or professional activity.

best_routes.notes: This is a relevant remote-work settlement route even though Paraguay does not label the initial permit a digital-nomad visa. The official permanent-residence checklist expressly recognizes remote workers/digital nomads. Before filing, confirm the acceptable wording and apostille requirements for the foreign contract or employer certificate and establish Paraguayan tax invoicing correctly.

rejected_routes.route_name: Paraguay Investor Pass / direct investor permanent residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route is investment-based rather than income-based.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly income test is applicable to this rejected route.

income_requirement_display.value: Investment-based; excluded for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker
income_requirement_display.notes: The official announcement confirms direct permanent residence through an investor certificate, but the applicant profile excludes investor routes.

income_proof_months.notes: A monthly income-history period is inapplicable to the route's investment criterion.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying foreign investment and a Constancia de Inversionista Extranjero under the Investor Pass framework.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence
initial_validity.notes: The route bypasses temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: Permanent-residence card renewal rules apply
extension_rules.notes: Not assessed further because the route is outside the applicant profile.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not required
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The investment exception permits direct permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence after qualifying investment certification

path_to_citizenship.value: Permanent residence can eventually support ordinary naturalization eligibility
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make the investment route suitable for the specified profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because substantial investment is a core condition. The applicant does not need this route because the ordinary temporary-to-permanent remote-worker path is available.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income test exists for visitor admission.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A residence-income threshold is inapplicable to visitor admission.

income_requirement_display.value: No qualifying residence income threshold; visitor status is not the selected route
income_requirement_display.notes: Visa-free or tourist admission must not be confused with residence authorization.

income_proof_months.notes: An income-history period is not published for visitor admission.

key_requirements.requirement: Entry permission depends on nationality and the official visa table.

initial_validity.value: Normally up to the visitor period authorized at entry
initial_validity.notes: Nationality-specific rules apply.

extension_rules.value: A visitor extension does not itself create a settlement route

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate residence application is required

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path from visitor status
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Use ordinary temporary residence first unless a statutory exception applies.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time alone is not a confirmed naturalization track

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourist or visa-free presence is not qualifying residence, even if foreign work can technically continue online.

summary.value: There is no separate degree visa. At permanent-residence conversion, a professional may use a Paraguayan-registered university degree plus evidence of actual professional income, without necessarily having a local employer. The separate remote-worker category is simpler for a foreign-contract engineer because it accepts foreign work and income evidence directly.
summary.notes: A degree alone is explicitly insufficient proof of solvency, and the qualification evidence is used during conversion from temporary to permanent residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: Paraguayan tax domicile is presumed after more than 120 days of habitual presence, but residence is not the only trigger: services physically performed in Paraguay can be Paraguayan-source, and nonresident rules may apply before tax residence is established.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 120-day rule is a statutory tax-domicile presumption, not a blanket exemption for the first 120 days. RUC registration, activity in Paraguay and treaty residence can change the practical result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal/screening IRP rate on net Paraguayan-source personal-service income, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Independent workers may opt into IPS pension coverage at 13% on a declared base not below the legal minimum wage. The official page describes this as optional and pension-only, without IPS health coverage; it should not be treated as a universal mandatory payroll charge.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly tax or social-security payment was established for every foreign remote worker. Optional IPS contributions use a minimum contribution base, while residence fees are one-off state charges rather than monthly payments.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad or inbound-worker income-tax exemption was identified in the current tax sources. Paraguay applies territorial/source rules, but work physically performed in Paraguay is generally Paraguayan-source even when the client or payer is abroad.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Territorial taxation does not make remote services performed from Paraguay automatically foreign-source.

taxes.caveats: Remote-work tax treatment depends on physical work location, tax domicile, RUC registration, deductions, the foreign payer's country and any applicable treaty. Independent services performed in Paraguay can attract both progressive IRP and 10% IVA invoicing; obtain Paraguayan advice before issuing foreign-client invoices.

taxation_system.value: Territorial/source-based personal taxation with progressive IRP rates for personal services and separate IVA obligations for independent services
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Tax domicile is presumed after more than 120 days of habitual presence, but locally performed services can be taxable earlier under source and nonresident rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Principally Paraguayan-source income. Personal services performed in Paraguay are locally sourced regardless of the payer's foreign location.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad exemption or tax holiday was identified in the current DNIT materials reviewed.
taxation_system.social_security: Optional IPS pension insurance for independent workers is 13% of a declared base not below the minimum wage and does not include IPS health coverage. Confirm whether another professional fund or employment classification applies.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 10% is the top marginal screening rate. IRP applies progressively to annual net personal-service income at 8%, 9% and 10%; gross personal-service income not exceeding PYG 80,000,000 annually is not subject to payment under the cited law, although formal obligations can remain.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net personal-service income up to PYG 50,000,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: The portion of annual net IRP personal-service income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses roughly PYG 6,000 per USD around the research date.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net personal-service income from PYG 50,000,001 to PYG 150,000,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: The portion of annual net IRP personal-service income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure shows the approximate upper threshold, not tax due.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual net personal-service income of PYG 150,000,001 or more
tax_brackets.applies_to: The portion of annual net IRP personal-service income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate; the threshold is approximately USD 25,000 at PYG 6,000 per USD.

taxation_system.notes: Official DNIT material supports the territorial source rule, progressive brackets and the treatment of services performed from Paraguay. IVA is a separate transaction tax and should not be added mechanically to the 10% top IRP rate when estimating effective personal tax.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The immigration route is ordinary residence with a remote-worker category at permanent conversion, not a special tax visa. A resident remote engineer working physically in Paraguay should plan for progressive IRP up to 10% and potentially 10% IVA invoicing on services supplied from Paraguay to a foreign client.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: ordinary_resident_remote_worker
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 10% progressive IRP on annual net Paraguayan-source personal-service income; this is a top marginal screening rate, not an effective-rate estimate. Independent services performed from Paraguay can also be subject to 10% IVA.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Tax domicile is presumed after more than 120 days of habitual presence; however, Paraguayan-source and nonresident taxation can arise before that threshold when services are physically performed in Paraguay.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Passive or genuinely foreign-source income is generally outside territorial IRP, but foreign-client fees are not automatically foreign-source. Official DNIT opinions treat services performed from Paraguay for foreign customers as locally performed and taxable.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No special digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime was identified in the current official tax materials reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No Paraguayan employer payroll is required for the residence route. Independent workers may voluntarily contribute 13% to IPS for pension-only coverage on a base not below the minimum wage; private health coverage remains a separate practical expense.

fixed_payments.status: No universal mandatory monthly fixed payment established; one-off residence fees and activity-based tax obligations apply.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Optional independent-worker IPS contribution: 13% of a declared base not below PYG 3,044,000, approximately PYG 395,720 or USD 66 monthly at about PYG 6,000/USD. It provides pension coverage, not IPS health coverage.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: From 1 July 2026, temporary residence costs PYG 2,926,925 in cash, approximately USD 488; permanent-residence conversion costs the same. Card payments cost slightly more, and extensions, certificates, translations, apostilles and identity documents are additional.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Independent services performed from Paraguay may require RUC registration, invoices and monthly 10% IVA treatment. IRP is annual and progressive once applicable.
fixed_payments.notes: The IPS amount is optional rather than a mandatory minimum contribution for every remote worker. USD conversions use approximately PYG 6,000 per USD and should be refreshed when paying.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Do not assume zero Paraguayan tax. Work physically performed in Paraguay can be Paraguayan-source, and nonresident or IVA rules can apply before the 120-day tax-domicile presumption is reached.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Register and file as advised locally; expect Paraguayan-source foreign-client service income to enter progressive IRP and assess 10% IVA invoicing separately.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: RUC registration, compliant invoices, monthly IVA returns and annual IRP may be required. Optional IPS pension contributions do not provide health coverage.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The immigration label remote worker/digital nomad does not create a tax exemption. Exact IVA credit, invoicing currency, treaty relief and foreign tax credit treatment require case-specific advice.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is the initial application; no prior residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The temporary card is issued for up to two years, after which the applicant changes category. Actual timing depends on the card term and filing window.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Supreme Court checklist requires three years of permanent residence counted from the permanent-admission resolution.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Planning estimate: up to two years of temporary residence plus three years of permanent residence before filing. Processing time is additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official court page provides requirements but publishes no typical or guaranteed processing time. A current official processing-time statistic was not available from that court source.

key_conditions.value: Maintain genuine residence and lawful activity, convert to permanent residence on time, avoid unjustified absences, remain tax-compliant, and prove good conduct and actual professional, commercial, educational or other qualifying activity in Paraguay. Temporary residence may be cancelled after more than one year of unjustified absence and permanent residence after more than three years.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is judicial and discretionary. Paraguay's Constitution restricts multiple nationality to constitutional-reciprocity treaties, so retention of the prior nationality requires individualized legal advice.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse of a Paraguayan can obtain direct permanent residence without first completing temporary residence. No separate shortened naturalization rule was identified; the official court page still requires three years of permanent residence.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Paraguayan citizen can support direct permanent residence. Marriage to another foreign national does not accelerate the route.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The documentary procedure and possible fee exemption differ depending on where the marriage was celebrated and whether a repatriation certificate is available.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must remain genuine and legally documented. Expect authenticated identity, marriage and civil-status records, criminal checks and personal filing. False documents or a simulated relationship can cause denial, cancellation and immigration sanctions; marriage does not automatically confer citizenship.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Direct permanent residence accelerates the settlement stage, not the three-year permanent-residence requirement stated by the court for naturalization.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 146 grants natural Paraguayan nationality to persons born in the Republic. The constitutional text states the territorial rule without a parent-status condition, so it is classified as broad/unconditional jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Paraguay is a natural-born Paraguayan even when both parents are foreign; no parental residence condition appears in Article 146.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth registration must still be completed. Diplomatic or unusual official-service cases should be checked separately.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Paraguay is Paraguayan by birth. If born abroad to a Paraguayan parent, constitutional descent rules also apply when the parent is serving the Republic abroad or when the child later settles permanently in Paraguay and formalizes the right.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically make a foreign father a citizen. The current general migration-law family exceptions reviewed expressly cover foreign spouses, children and certain grandchildren of Paraguayans, but no automatic direct-permanent-residence category for the foreign parent of a Paraguayan child was established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The father can still use the ordinary residence route. Obtain filing-level advice before relying on the child's nationality as an independent family-residence basis.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship and no clearly published direct parent-of-citizen permanent-residence entitlement appears in the current official pages reviewed. Parenthood may be relevant factually to family unity and genuine residence, but the father should plan on an independently valid residence status unless Migraciones confirms another category.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: This cautious conclusion avoids extending spouse/child provisions to parents where the official beneficiary list does not do so.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank shown on the current Paraguay passport dashboard. Rankings are live and may change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index, not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count; its methodology can place complex eVisas in this category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 48 destinations shown in the visa-on-arrival/easy-eVisa grouping and 8 eTA destinations. Passport Index's broader mobility score is 142.

passport.notes: Use the named Passport Index breakdown consistently: it differs from Henley, which combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access into a single score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable inside an international remote team and Paraguay scored 531, rank 43, in EF EPI 2025. However, immigration, tax, court and most daily administrative dealings require Spanish; English alone is not a reliable settlement language.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private proficiency index based on participating test takers, not a guarantee of English access to government services.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages. The constitutional language rules do not provide for nationwide government service in either language, so Spanish should be treated as necessary for documents, filings and integration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The official sources reviewed do not publish a nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-proficiency measure; private-community availability therefore is not quantified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate lower-bound conversion of the official statement that employed workers earned more than PYG 3,400,000 per month in Q1 2026. The conversion uses roughly PYG 6,000 per USD, so the true average and USD equivalent are slightly higher.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current INE income catalogue and EPHC earnings tables publish means, while the MTESS registry study describes median-remuneration tables as a proposed future output rather than publishing a current national median. The Atlas mentions medians used to impute outliers, but those are preprocessing values, not a published national median worker salary. Consequently, no defensible USD median can be calculated.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory PYG 3,044,000 monthly minimum wage at about PYG 6,000 per USD. This is a legal floor, not an observed minimum or average salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The latest directly published official amount states that employed workers earned an average exceeding PYG 3,400,000 per month in Q1 2026. PYG 3,400,000 converts to approximately USD 567 at roughly PYG 6,000 per USD, so 567 is a rounded lower-bound approximation rather than an exact converted mean. The underlying MTESS profile is based on INE EPHC data and reports about 43 weekly work hours.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current nationwide median monthly earnings statistic is published in the inspected INE income catalogue, EPHC mean-income table, Atlas indicator or MTESS registry study. References to a median in the INE sources describe values used to replace atypical observations during imputation, not the median salary of Paraguay's workers. The MTESS registry document proposes future mean-and-median tabulations but does not provide a current national median, so the numeric field remains null.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current national earnings sources publish averages and disaggregations, not a meaningful maximum worker salary. Because earnings are open-ended, inventing a national upper bound would be misleading.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum for unspecified private-sector activities, effective 1 July 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official MTESS Labor Observatory summary based on the INE EPHC for Q1 2026. It describes the average current monthly income of employed workers and states only that the amount is above PYG 3.4 million; it does not publish the exact underlying mean on that page. This is therefore preserved as an official lower-bound display rather than rounded into a falsely exact local-currency figure.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected current INE catalogue lists average monthly principal-occupation income and related income-distribution tables, but no national median worker-earnings series. The EPHC data-catalogue table is explicitly a mean-income table. The Atlas's PYG 2,500,000 median reference for 2024 is an outlier-imputation value and cannot be relabeled as the national median salary. The MTESS administrative-data study recommends that future registered-worker tables include medians but does not publish the requested current statistic.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current official earnings sources do not define or publish a national maximum salary. Worker earnings are open-ended, so no meaningful maximum local-currency value is supplied.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average current monthly income in the principal occupation of employed workers; statutory private-sector minimum wage; zero-income observations are excluded from the referenced EPHC mean-income tables
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: Q1 2026; statutory minimum: effective 1 July 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: This focused audit resolves the average-salary gap with the freshest directly published official figure: more than PYG 3.4 million monthly in Q1 2026, approximately more than USD 567. It does not manufacture an exact amount from the official lower-bound wording. The median remains null because the current sources publish means, use medians only for outlier imputation, or merely propose future median tables; none publishes a current nationwide median salary.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official poverty and income-distribution report publishes poverty lines and per-capita income distribution, but these are not a standardized cost-of-living budget for a remote-working household. No comparable national household-budget amount was substituted.

settlement_track.summary: Ordinary temporary residence is genuine residence, not visitor or workcation status, and the current permanent-residence conversion rules expressly accommodate remote workers with foreign work and income evidence. Citizenship requires changing to permanent residence and then completing three years of permanent residence, so the route requires conversion but has a credible settlement track.
settlement_track.notes: Temporary-residence time is useful for reaching permanent residence, but the official naturalization checklist measures the three-year citizenship clock from the permanent-admission resolution.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The initial ordinary residence permits lawful activity without a Paraguayan employer, and the conversion checklist explicitly accepts remote workers/digital nomads through foreign work confirmation stating income and payment method. No local client, startup, investment or elite-achievement condition is published for that category.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit: the route, tax and settlement conclusions remain supported. The salary average is improved using the official Q1 2026 MTESS/INE-based worker profile. The current official source states only that the average exceeds PYG 3.4 million, so the record preserves that lower-bound wording and uses approximately USD 567 as a lower-bound conversion. A national median remains null because the inspected INE and MTESS sources publish means, cite medians only for outlier imputation, or propose future median tables without publishing a current nationwide median worker salary.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Ordinary temporary residence under Law 6984/2022, then permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Ordinary temporary residence can be changed to permanent residence after its term. The current PR solvency annex expressly accepts remote workers/digital nomads and documented foreign work income.
requirements: Complete the ordinary temporary-residence term, normally two years.
File the category change during the three months before expiry; later filing is subject to the published limited grace/multas rules.
Document the foreign work relationship, income and how payment is received; provide current identity and background documents.
reviewed_route_names: Ordinary temporary residence followed by permanent residence under the remote-worker/digital-nomad solvency category
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: This is ordinary residence with a digital-nomad solvency category, not a separate short-stay nomad visa. Both current official pages opened successfully. Two years describes the standard temporary-residence term; application may begin in its final three months. PR is indefinite and its card is renewed periodically.

data.selection_summary: Peru enacted a digital-nomad migration category for remote employees of foreign companies, nominally for up to 365 days and renewable. However, the current consolidated migration regulation, Migraciones procedure catalogue, Agencia Digital, and updated TUPA materials still provide no digital-nomad filing procedure, checklist, fee, or income threshold. Peru therefore remains ineligible under the current-route rule. The operational worker-resident route requires a Peruvian contracting entity, while rentista residence requires permanent passive income rather than ordinary foreign-contract earnings.

visa_application.title: Trámites y servicios — Superintendencia Nacional de Migraciones
visa_application.notes: This is Migraciones’ official general procedure catalogue, which links to Agencia Digital and the available immigration applications. It is not a digital-nomad application: no dedicated nomad procedure appears in the current catalogue, Agencia Digital procedure list, consolidated regulation, or reviewed TUPA updates. The country-level application link is therefore classified as an official general visa/immigration portal, not a direct application for the unavailable route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad migration status — enacted but not operational

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The enacted law and all current official procedure materials reviewed through 2026-08-15 establish no operational income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No PEN threshold is published because the implementing procedure and checklist remain unavailable.

income_requirement_display.value: No operational income requirement published
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Pending implementing rules and an active TUPA procedure
income_requirement_display.notes: Unofficial estimates were excluded because current Migraciones sources do not publish a filing threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No operational checklist specifies a bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: The enacted category is for subordinate remote work through digital or telecommunications tools under an employment relationship created abroad with a company domiciled outside Peru.
The holder may not undertake remunerated or lucrative activity producing Peruvian-source income.
Current official procedure catalogues and TUPA materials do not provide an application, document checklist, fee, or implementation date for this category.

initial_validity.value: Up to 365 days once operational
initial_validity.notes: This is the statutory design, not a currently obtainable status.

extension_rules.value: Statutorily renewable, with operating conditions still unpublished
extension_rules.notes: No current procedure establishes renewal limits, fees, or evidence requirements.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The statute creates a migration category allowing a stay of up to 365 days, but no application can currently be filed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The legal category exists, but its operational residence classification and application process remain incomplete.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Article 93 of the consolidated regulation states a general three-consecutive-year rule for permanent residence, but the permanent-change procedure contains category-specific conditions and does not address digital nomads. Because the nomad category is not operational, official sources do not establish that its time would count or that it could convert.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official source confirms that time in the unimplemented nomad category would constitute qualifying continuous legal residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: The route fits foreign-employer remote work in concept but is excluded because it cannot currently be applied for. Even after implementation, its permanent-residence and citizenship treatment would require confirmation. Tax treatment also requires clarification because SUNAT can treat services physically performed in Peru as Peruvian-source while the migration category prohibits Peruvian-source income.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route page does not publish a personal monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No applicant-level PEN threshold is stated.

income_requirement_display.value: No personal monthly threshold published; qualifying Peruvian contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: The decisive mismatch is the required service or employment relationship in Peru and registered contracting entity.

income_proof_months.notes: Initial filing has no fixed income-history period; renewal for an independent worker requires the three latest electronic fee receipts.

key_requirements.requirement: A Peruvian employment contract, administrative relationship, or service contract is required.
The contracting company must have active and compliant RUC status with SUNAT.
An independent worker’s service contract must generally last at least one year for resident rather than temporary status.
Police, criminal, and judicial record documentation is required.

initial_validity.value: 365 days
initial_validity.notes: Worker-resident status is renewable.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while the qualifying relationship continues; independent workers must provide the current service contract and three latest electronic fee receipts.
extension_rules.notes: Tax and record documentation must also remain compliant.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct worker residence after approval
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not an ordinary foreign-client remote-work route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying resident can seek permanent residence after three consecutive years, subject to presence, records, contract, tax, and category-specific requirements.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not remove the initial requirement for a Peruvian contracting entity.

path_to_citizenship.value: Qualifying legal residence can support naturalization under the residence period in force, but this route does not fit the supplied foreign-only contract.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The active procedure still states two years; Law 32421 would raise the ordinary period to five years after its implementing regulation activates the new regime.

rejected_routes.notes: Despite permitting independent services, this is not independent self-sponsorship: the official rules require a service relationship in Peru and an active locally registered contracting entity.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This threshold applies to permanent foreign-source pension or passive income, not active employment or service-contract compensation.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official foreign-income threshold is denominated in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: US$1,000 net permanent income per month
income_requirement_display.notes: The income must be a pension or permanent rent and must enter Peru through an SBS-supervised financial institution.

income_proof_months.notes: Documentation establishing permanent income is required, but no fixed number of bank-statement months is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must receive a pension or permanent income from a Peruvian or foreign source; active software-engineering earnings are not established as qualifying rent.
Foreign-source applicants must prove at least US$1,000 net monthly and declare that the funds enter through an SBS-supervised institution.
The initial visa applicant must be outside Peru and provide passport and criminal-record documentation.

initial_validity.value: Indefinite resident stay
initial_validity.notes: Approval remains discretionary and depends on evidence that the income is qualifying permanent rent.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary annual residence extension is described because the status has indefinite stay
extension_rules.notes: Document renewal and continued compliance may still apply.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct resident status
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is independently available but does not fit active foreign-contract earnings.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No separate conversion is necessary for continued indefinite rentista residence, but official sources do not equate rentista automatically with the separately named permanent-resident category.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The legal distinction matters for any benefit specifically requiring Calidad Migratoria Permanente.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential naturalization after the generally applicable continuous legal-residence period if all requirements are met
path_to_citizenship.notes: The active procedure states two years; the pending new nationality-law regime would increase the ordinary period to five years.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a genuine independent residence route for retirees or people with qualifying permanent passive income, but it does not match the supplied applicant’s active earned income.

summary.value: Peru offers formation/student residence without a local employer to applicants admitted to recognized studies or training and able to demonstrate solvency. A university degree by itself does not create an independent skilled-migration route, and formation residence is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work solution.
summary.notes: This is enrolment-based rather than qualification-recognition based; work authorization and permanent-residence counting require separate verification.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreign individual generally acquires Peruvian tax domicile after spending more than 183 calendar days in any 12-month period. A change in domicile status generally takes effect from the following tax year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax domicile are separate. Even before tax domicile, services physically performed in Peru can be Peruvian-source.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening figure only: 30% is the top marginal rate for domiciled individuals’ net work plus relevant foreign-source income and the published rate applicable to net fourth-category income of non-domiciled independent workers. It is not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No universal mandatory contribution percentage is published for the unimplemented nomad route. The standard 9% EsSalud contribution applies principally to covered dependent employment and is employer-paid; independent-worker treatment depends on registration and insurance arrangements.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No operational nomad fee, compulsory insurance premium, or fixed monthly contribution is published.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad exemption or special inbound regime was found. Domiciled individuals generally combine relevant foreign-source income with taxable work income; non-domiciled individuals are taxed on Peruvian-source income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The immigration category’s prohibition on Peruvian-source income is not a tax exemption.

taxes.caveats: Remote services performed while physically in Peru may be Peruvian-source even when paid by a foreign client. That potentially conflicts with the future nomad category’s prohibition on Peruvian-source income. Contract characterization, domicile timing, deductions, foreign-tax credits, treaty position, RUC and receipt obligations, and social insurance require individualized advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive taxation of net work income combined with relevant foreign-source income for domiciled individuals; Peruvian-source-only taxation for non-domiciled individuals.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 calendar days in any 12-month period, with the domicile-status change generally effective from the following tax year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for domiciled individuals subject to category rules; Peruvian-source income only for non-domiciled individuals. Services physically performed in Peru can be Peruvian-source regardless of payer domicile.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No operational digital-nomad exemption or special remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: The standard EsSalud contribution for covered employees is 9% of remuneration and employer-paid, subject to the minimum base. No equivalent mandatory rate was established for an ordinary foreign-client remote worker.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For 2026, one UIT is S/5,500. Rates apply cumulatively after applicable deductions; 30% is the top marginal dashboard screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Net taxable work income plus relevant foreign-source income
tax_brackets.notes: Approximation uses about S/3.364 per US dollar.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal band of net taxable work plus relevant foreign-source income
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal band of net taxable work plus relevant foreign-source income
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal band of net taxable work plus relevant foreign-source income
tax_brackets.notes: USD amount approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Marginal excess of net taxable work plus relevant foreign-source income
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band, not effective tax.

taxation_system.notes: General rules are well supported, but no operational nomad tax guidance exists and a particular foreign contract requires professional classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime is operational. General source and domicile rules would need to be reconciled with the future immigration category.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Pending immigration category; general individual income-tax rules would likely require analysis
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% top marginal rate; non-domiciled independent Peru-source services may face 30% taxation on net income
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in a rolling 12-month period, generally changing domicile status from the following tax year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Domiciled individuals generally combine relevant foreign-source income with net work income under the progressive scale. Non-domiciled individuals owe tax only on Peruvian-source income, but work physically performed in Peru can itself be Peruvian-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None published.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific payroll or social-security rule is published. Standard EsSalud employment rules should not automatically be applied to a foreign-contract worker without analyzing employment and local-registration status.

fixed_payments.status: Not applicable operationally because the nomad procedure has not been implemented
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed mandatory nomad contribution is published
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad application or renewal fee is published
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific fixed tax, stamp duty, or business-registration payment is published
fixed_payments.notes: Private health insurance could be required by future rules, but no current checklist or fixed premium exists.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining non-domiciled does not necessarily mean zero Peruvian tax: personal services performed in Peru can be Peruvian-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Once domiciled, net work and relevant foreign-source income generally fall within the cumulative 8%–30% scale, subject to deductions, credits, and treaty analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered independent professional generally needs a RUC, electronic fee receipts, monthly payments or retentions where applicable, and an annual return. Tax registration alone does not legalize immigration residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is reduced because the enacted nomad category lacks operational immigration and tax guidance.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No obtainable nomad status exists, so there is no current timeline to temporary residence for this profile.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The consolidated regulation states that permanent residence generally requires three consecutive years of residence and limits absences during that period. However, the operative permanent-change provisions contain category-specific conditions and do not address digital nomads, while the nomad category itself still lacks an application procedure. Consequently, three years can be stated for established qualifying resident categories but cannot responsibly be assigned as a nomad-to-permanent-residence timeline until Migraciones confirms that nomad status is qualifying residence and its time counts.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on qualifying continuous legal residence rather than a separately published waiting period beginning only after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the minimum stated by the currently active general naturalization procedure for qualifying legal residents, not a confirmed nomad-route timeline. Law 32421 would raise the ordinary minimum to five years after its regulation activates the new regime.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The active procedure states a nominal maximum of 30 business days subject to suspensions and verification, while the not-yet-effective new law provides a substantially longer statutory framework. Neither source publishes an observed typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Under the active procedure: adulthood, at least two consecutive years of qualifying legal residence, a current resident card, evidence of lawful income or activity appropriate to the migration category, good conduct, and required criminal and Interpol documentation. The pending Law 32421 regime would require five continuous immediate years, minimum annual lawful income, formal tax compliance, language and Peru-knowledge testing, and expanded security review.
key_conditions.notes: Verify which nationality-law regime is effective immediately before filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The active procedure requires at least two continuous years residing in Peru while married to a Peruvian. Law 32421 would change the marriage period to four years after its regulation activates the law.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Peruvian can support family-resident status and citizenship by marriage after the continuous in-country residence and marriage period is met. Marriage to another foreigner does not accelerate citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Time married outside Peru alone does not replace the required residence in Peru.

requirements_and_risks.value: Maintain a genuine marriage to a Peruvian and continuous lawful residence; hold a current foreign-resident card; provide a recent RENIEC marriage record, clean-record documents, good-conduct evidence, and the remaining checklist documents. False documents or a sham marriage can result in refusal, cancellation, and sanctions.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Approval remains subject to verification, and the future Law 32421 rules are pending implementation.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 52 of the Constitution makes persons born in Peruvian territory Peruvian by birth. This is broad jus soli, subject to any narrow public-law exceptions in implementing legislation.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Peru is Peruvian by birth even when both parents are foreign migrants, subject to narrow legal exceptions and civil registration.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A child born abroad to two foreign residents does not become Peruvian merely through the parents’ residence.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Peru is Peruvian by territory. A child born abroad to a Peruvian father or mother is also Peruvian by birth when registered as provided by law.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The cited overseas-registration procedure concerns children of a parent who is Peruvian by birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Peruvian child may qualify for family-resident status, which permits dependent or independent work. The child’s citizenship does not automatically naturalize the parent or waive residence requirements.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Proof of parentage and the correct filing variant must be confirmed with Migraciones.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Peruvian child can potentially obtain family-resident status and later pursue citizenship under the applicable residence rules. Citizenship for the father is not automatic.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and the family relationship must be legally documented, and residence remains subject to approval.

rank.notes: Power rank displayed for Peru when checked; live rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 48 visa-on-arrival and 8 eTA destinations; ordinary eVisa-only access is not included.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 147. Its methodology differs from Henley’s combined access score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical in Lima, international companies, and technology settings, but Spanish remains important for housing, banking, taxes, healthcare, and government procedures. EF EPI 2025 classified Peru’s English proficiency as moderate.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected adult-test dataset, not a census measure.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low for everyday administration and local services. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, so Spanish or professional translation would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is an inference from the official-language framework; no reliable national proficiency statistic was located.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official S/1,925.9 national average monthly labour income using about S/3.364 per US dollar.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official national labour-market release publishes averages but no national median monthly wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory full-time private-sector minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate currency conversion; exchange rates fluctuate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official release does not publish a national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary is published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory full-time private-sector minimum wage effective from 1 January 2025.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National average monthly income from principal and secondary work.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No national median is published in the reviewed release.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly labour income from principal and secondary work; minimum is statutory full-time private-sector RMV
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: April 2025–March 2026; minimum wage checked through 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average represents the national employed population, not software-engineer pay or an immigration threshold. USD amounts are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official labour-market material does not publish a comparable national household cost-of-living budget, so a commercial city estimate was not substituted.
