settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The enacted digital-nomad category cannot currently be applied for, and current official sources do not establish that future time in the category will count toward permanent residence or naturalization.
settlement_track.summary: Peru’s foreign-remote-worker category remains pending operational implementation, so it cannot establish qualifying residence today. The consolidated three-year permanent-residence rule does not resolve whether future nomad time will count, and the operational worker route requires a Peruvian contracting entity.
settlement_track.notes: General naturalization is currently available after two years of qualifying legal residence, but that does not create a path from a migration category that cannot currently be obtained.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The enacted nomad category conceptually fits foreign-employer remote work but has no active application. The operational worker route requires a contract in Peru and a locally registered contracting entity.

data.notes: The negative current-selection conclusion is supported by the enacted law, current consolidated regulation, Migraciones procedure catalogue, Agencia Digital, TUPA updates, and worker-route requirements. Implementation could change the result, so the status should be rechecked before relying on it.

data.selection_summary: The Digital Nomad Visa (DNV) is authorized by Executive Order No. 86 and an official Philippine embassy page publishes eligibility requirements. However, no verifiable application workflow, DNV fee schedule, reciprocity-country list, or central eVisa category was found. A June 2026 legal guide states that implementing guidelines were still being finalized, while the central eVisa catalogue and the Washington Embassy's live August 2026 visa catalogue still omit the DNV. It is therefore treated as not currently open. Even if implemented as designed, it would be a temporary non-immigrant visa with no confirmed conversion to permanent residence or citizenship. The independent quota immigrant visa requires at least USD 100,000 of capital or investment and does not fit an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)
visa_application.notes: This official Foreign Service Post page lists DNV eligibility and an inquiry contact but provides no application workflow, documentary checklist, fee, processing time, or reciprocity-country list. The central eVisa catalogue and the Washington Embassy's current visa catalogue list other visa categories but no DNV. Written confirmation from the responsible Philippine Foreign Service Post is therefore necessary before attempting to apply.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Visa (DNV)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official materials require sufficient income generated outside the Philippines but publish no numerical threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No PHP threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient foreign-generated income; no official numerical threshold published
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sufficient income generated outside the Philippines
income_requirement_display.notes: No official minimum amount, assessment formula, or required bank-statement period was published in the current route materials.

income_proof_months.notes: The public eligibility page does not state how many months of income must be demonstrated.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be at least 18 and work remotely using digital technology for an employer or clients outside the Philippines.
Income must be generated outside the Philippines, but no minimum amount is published.
Clean criminal record and health insurance valid for the DNV period are required.
The applicant must not be employed in the Philippines and must remain compliant throughout the visa period.

Nationality reciprocity is mandatory: the applicant must be a national of a country that offers a comparable DNV to Filipinos. If that country has no Philippine Foreign Service Post, EO 86 permits filing at the nearest country with one. Neither EO 86 nor the official route page publishes a country-by-country eligibility list, so nationality eligibility must be confirmed with the responsible post.

As of 2026-08-15, the central eVisa catalogue and the Washington Embassy's current visa catalogue and fee schedule contain no DNV category, DNV filing workflow, or DNV fee. The Hague route page supplies eligibility bullets and an inquiry contact only. Operational filing therefore cannot be treated as available without written confirmation from the responsible Foreign Service Post.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year if implemented
initial_validity.notes: The EO describes a temporary non-immigrant, multiple-entry visa; this is not permanent or qualifying residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for the same duration under the EO
extension_rules.notes: The EO does not publish detailed renewal mechanics. Current implementing guidelines were not located.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying temporary-residence conversion confirmed; the contemplated status is a temporary non-immigrant visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Permission to stay temporarily should not be equated with a qualifying residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Neither EO 86 nor the current BI visa catalogue establishes DNV conversion to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The DNV creates no naturalization track. Judicial naturalization requires separate lawful permanent-residence evidence and lengthy continuous residence.

best_routes.notes: This route matches foreign-contract remote work in its legal design, but it is not usable for current selection because an operational application channel and complete rules remain unverified. It would also be temporary-only unless future rules create a qualifying settlement conversion.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This is a capital/investment requirement rather than monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current checklist states the principal threshold in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: At least USD 100,000 inward remittance or qualifying investment/property evidence
income_requirement_display.notes: Substantial investment is incompatible with the ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker profile.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not a recurring-income test.

key_requirements.requirement: Nationality must qualify under diplomatic-relations and reciprocity rules, with no more than 50 quota immigrants of one nationality per calendar year.
Applicant must demonstrate sufficient capital for a viable and sustainable Philippine investment.
Current evidence includes at least USD 100,000 inward remittance, qualifying condominium ownership, or at least USD 100,000 invested in an existing Philippine business.
Medical fitness, NBI clearance, BI clearance, valid admission, and a hearing are required.

initial_validity.value: Quota immigrant/permanent-resident status if approved
initial_validity.notes: Approval is quota-limited and discretionary.

extension_rules.value: Immigrant status rather than a normal fixed-term remote-worker visa
extension_rules.notes: Annual alien-reporting and re-entry formalities may still apply.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not applicable; the route is an immigrant category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct quota immigrant status if approved
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is not an ordinary remote-work route and currently demands substantial capital.

path_to_citizenship.value: Could support a separate judicial-naturalization case after the statutory residence period and other conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is not automatic.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the November 2025 checklist imposes a substantial USD 100,000 capital/investment requirement.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No generally applicable salary threshold was established on the route page.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No generally applicable salary threshold was established.

income_requirement_display.value: No general published salary threshold; Philippine employer petition required
income_requirement_display.notes: Not independently usable by a foreign-client remote worker.

income_proof_months.notes: The route page does not state a generally applicable proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must have pre-arranged employment with a Philippine-based employer that acts as petitioner.
The statutory framework includes a labor-availability test for pre-arranged employment.

initial_validity.value: Generally 1, 2, or 3 years, tied to employment

extension_rules.value: Renewable for 1, 2, or 3 years while qualifying employment continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employment-linked non-immigrant stay
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not an independent residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic 9G-to-permanent-residence path was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: A separate qualifying permanent-residence and naturalization basis would be required.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Philippine employer and employer petition are required.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitor proof of financial capacity is case-specific.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general visitor threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Case-specific visitor financial capacity; not a remote-work residence threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: The visitor financial-capacity test is not a DNV or settlement income requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: The eVisa policy lists a latest-six-month bank statement as one possible proof for certain visitor applications; this is not a DNV rule.

key_requirements.requirement: Temporary purpose, valid passport, onward or return travel, and proof appropriate to the visit.
eVisas cannot be converted to another visa type or extended.
Tourist extensions remain visitor status and do not legalize ordinary ongoing work or create settlement rights.

initial_validity.value: Varies by nationality and visitor category
initial_validity.notes: Many visa-exempt nationalities receive 30 days initially.

extension_rules.value: Regular visitor extensions may be available through BI, but issued eVisas are non-extendible and non-convertible.
extension_rules.notes: Extension does not convert visitor status into qualifying residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The reviewed eVisa rules establish no qualifying residence path.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No tourist-to-self-employed or tourist-to-PR route was found.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time is not established as lawful permanent residence for naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status and extensions are not qualifying remote-work residence routes.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Pensioners must show a lifetime pension of USD 800 monthly when single or USD 1,000 with dependants, but non-pensioners qualify through deposits instead.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Requirements are expressed mainly in USD.

income_requirement_display.value: Age 40+ plus USD 15,000–50,000 Classic deposit depending on age/pension status; pension requirements may also apply
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Lifetime pension USD 800/month single or USD 1,000/month with dependants for pensioner option
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a retirement/deposit route, not an ordinary software-engineer remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: The route requires lifetime-pension evidence rather than a stated number of recent income months.

key_requirements.requirement: Principal applicant must be at least 40.
Classic deposit ranges from USD 15,000 to USD 50,000 depending on age and pension status.
Police, medical, BI clearances and a USD 1,500 processing fee are required.

initial_validity.value: Multiple-entry indefinite-stay special non-immigrant status while program conditions are maintained
initial_validity.notes: PRA describes a permanent-residency benefit, but the legal category remains a special non-immigrant visa.

extension_rules.value: Maintained through continued program membership, required deposit/investment and annual fee

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Long-term special non-immigrant stay

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No conversion from SRRV into an Immigration Act immigrant visa was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official source confirmed SRRV time alone as lawful permanent residence for judicial naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is age-restricted and deposit/retirement-based, outside the supplied ordinary remote-worker profile.

summary.value: A 9(f) student visa can be obtained without a local employer after acceptance by a BI-accredited higher-education institution. The school participates in the petition, the status is temporary and study-specific, and no direct student-to-permanent-residence or citizenship route was confirmed.
summary.notes: Having an existing software-engineering degree does not itself create a skilled or qualification-based residence route.

tax_residency_rule.value: Philippine law taxes an alien, resident or nonresident, only on Philippine-source income. A nonresident alien present for more than 180 aggregate days in a calendar year is deemed engaged in trade or business. Resident-alien classification is fact-specific rather than a simple published DNV day-count rule. Compensation for services physically performed in the Philippines is Philippine-source even if paid by a foreign client.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration status, domestic tax classification, treaty residence, income source and business-registration duties must be analyzed separately.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for individuals subject to the graduated schedule, not an expected effective rate. A nonresident alien not engaged in Philippine trade or business may instead face 25% final tax on gross Philippine-source income, subject to treaty analysis.

social_contributions_percent.notes: SSS describes compulsory coverage for self-employed persons and a contribution schedule, but the reviewed sources do not establish that a DNV holder working only for foreign clients must or may register in that category. No reliable DNV-specific percentage is therefore stated.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No DNV-specific monthly government payment, health-insurance minimum premium, or contribution was published. The general 2025 SSS self-employed table ranges from PHP 760 to PHP 5,280 monthly, but applicability to a foreign DNV holder is not established.

special_tax_regimes.value: No enacted or official DNV tax exemption or special inbound regime was found. Alien taxpayers remain subject to ordinary Philippine-source rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Proposed DNV bills containing tax exemptions were not treated as law because EO 86 and the current enacted tax legislation reviewed do not create that exemption.

taxes.caveats: Remote services performed while physically in the Philippines can be Philippine-source notwithstanding a foreign payer. The 180-day rule changes the category of a nonresident alien but is not a blanket tax exemption below 180 days. Treaty protection may exempt qualifying short-term foreign employment when all treaty conditions are met. Permanent-establishment risk, deductions, VAT/business registration and social-security coverage require professional advice. The DNV itself is not verifiably operational.

taxation_system.value: Territorial/source-based taxation for aliens, with progressive individual rates up to 35% when the graduated schedule applies; certain nonresident aliens can instead be taxed at 25% on gross Philippine-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Aliens are taxed on Philippine-source income. More than 180 aggregate days makes a nonresident alien engaged in trade or business; resident-alien status remains fact-specific.
taxation_system.income_scope: Philippine-source income only for resident and nonresident aliens. Services are sourced where physically performed.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No official DNV-specific exemption or reduced rate was confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: General SSS rules make coverage compulsory for self-employed persons, with contributions based on declared earnings, but applicability to an unimplemented DNV/foreign-client arrangement is unresolved.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 35% value is the top marginal screening rate. The current graduated schedule is 0%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30% and 35%; it is not a flat 35% tax.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income not over PHP 250,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Individual graduated income-tax schedule effective 2023 onward
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses PHP 61.432 per USD, BSP reference at 2026-07-31.
USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: PHP 22,500 plus 20% of excess over PHP 400,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: PHP 102,500 plus 25% of excess over PHP 800,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: PHP 402,500 plus 30% of excess over PHP 2,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: PHP 2,202,500 plus 35% of excess over PHP 8,000,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket, not the effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Core source and rate rules are supported by legislation and BIR materials. DNV-specific treatment remains uncertain because no operational DNV tax, registration, fee or social-security guidance was published in the current official sources reviewed.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No DNV-specific tax holiday was confirmed. Under ordinary law, payment by a foreign client does not by itself make remote-service income foreign-source: services physically performed in the Philippines are Philippine-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Unimplemented DNV category; ordinary alien source, classification and treaty rules would apply unless future implementing guidance provides otherwise.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 35% graduated tax when that schedule applies; potentially 25% gross final tax for a nonresident alien not engaged in trade or business, subject to treaty and classification.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 aggregate days makes a nonresident alien engaged in Philippine trade or business. Resident-alien status and treaty residence remain fact-specific.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Aliens are taxed only on Philippine-source income, but compensation for work physically performed in the Philippines is Philippine-source even when the payer is abroad. A qualifying treaty may provide short-stay employment relief when all treaty conditions are satisfied.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No DNV-specific enacted exemption, reduced rate or tax holiday was published in the official law and guidance reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No DNV-specific payroll or SSS rule was published. General SSS self-employed coverage cannot safely be applied to a foreign DNV holder without registration and eligibility advice.

fixed_payments.status: No DNV-specific fixed-payment schedule is published in the current official materials reviewed as of 2026-08-15.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The general self-employed SSS table ranges from PHP 760 to PHP 5,280 per month effective January 2025, but the reviewed SSS and DNV materials do not establish that this schedule applies to a foreign DNV holder working solely for foreign clients.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Neither the official DNV information page, the central eVisa catalogue, nor the Washington Embassy's current visa catalogue and fee schedule publishes a DNV application, renewal, entry or exit fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: EO 86 requires private health insurance but publishes no minimum premium or coverage amount. No DNV-specific fixed tax, municipal charge, VAT rule or stamp duty was published.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence is category-specific, not an assertion that living or doing business in the Philippines is cost-free. Current official catalogues publish fees for visitor, employment and immigrant categories but omit the DNV. General visitor/eVisa fees and general SSS contribution amounts are not valid proxies for a DNV fee. BIR guidance requires foreign nationals who work, render services or conduct business in the Philippines to assess TIN and registration obligations, but it publishes no recurring DNV charge.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay of 180 days or less is not automatically tax-free. A nonresident alien not engaged in trade or business may face 25% final tax on gross Philippine-source income. Qualifying treaty employment relief may apply when the relevant day-count, foreign-employer and permanent-establishment conditions all hold.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident alien or a nonresident alien treated as engaged in trade or business can be taxed on Philippine-source remote-service income under the graduated schedule up to 35%, subject to deductions, registration and treaty position.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: If the activity is registered as a Philippine profession or business, graduated income tax, possible alternative small-business rules, VAT/percentage-tax registration and SSS may arise. EO 86 prohibits Philippine employment, and the reviewed sources do not establish that the contemplated DNV authorizes local sole-proprietor registration.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Ordinary Philippine-source and foreign-national registration rules are published, but no official DNV-specific fee, fixed tax, insurance premium floor, SSS classification or filing guidance was found. The DNV information page gives eligibility criteria only; the central eVisa catalogue and the Washington Embassy's current visa and fee pages omit the category, while the June 2026 legal guide states that implementing guidelines were still being finalized. Consequently, no DNV fixed-payment amount can be stated without inventing or borrowing fees from unrelated visa and contributor categories.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The DNV is not verifiably open and is legally a temporary non-immigrant visa, not qualifying temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No DNV-to-permanent-residence conversion or qualifying period was found.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The statute requires ten years of continuous Philippine residence in the ordinary case but does not express this as a fixed number of years after a generic PR grant.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory ordinary judicial-naturalization residence baseline on a separate qualifying basis, not a DNV timeline. Special statutory qualifications can reduce it to five years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable current official typical processing-time statistic was published. Judicial naturalization includes court proceedings, publication, and statutory procedural steps.

key_conditions.value: Judicial naturalization generally requires continuous lawful residence, lawful entry for permanent residence before the declaration of intention, age 21 at hearing, good moral character, a lawful and lucrative occupation or qualifying property, ability to speak and write English or Spanish and one principal Philippine language, qualifying schooling for minor children, social integration, reciprocity and absence of statutory disqualifications.
key_conditions.notes: The DNV does not itself establish lawful permanent residence or confirm that its time counts.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: CA 473 reduces the ordinary ten-year residence requirement to five for a petitioner 'married to a Filipino woman.' This historic gendered wording is not automatic citizenship and should be confirmed with Philippine counsel for the applicant's facts.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing valid marriage to a Philippine citizen can support a probationary 13(a) non-quota immigrant application, subject to reciprocity and BI adjudication. Marriage to a non-Philippine citizen has no immigration or naturalization acceleration.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage must remain valid and legally recognized.

requirements_and_risks.value: The 13(a) route requires a valid marriage to a Philippine citizen, admissibility, clean law-enforcement record, health eligibility and sufficient family support; reciprocity affects permanent-resident eligibility. BI requires a joint process and hearing. Naturalization remains separate. Fraudulent or sham marriage can lead to denial, revocation, deportation and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The published BI fee page warns that displayed fees date from 2014 and may change.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship through a Philippine father or mother, not through birth in Philippine territory alone. Narrow historical, naturalization and anti-statelessness questions do not create general jus soli.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in the Philippines to two foreign parents does not generally become a Philippine citizen solely because of birthplace.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Separate protection may be relevant in an individual statelessness case, but no general birthright rule applies.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Philippine citizen from birth if either parent is a Philippine citizen.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically give a foreign parent residence, permanent residence or citizenship. The Immigration Act gives quota-number preference to parents of Philippine citizens only when the citizen child is at least 21; marriage to the Philippine parent may independently support a 13(a) route.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any parental application remains subject to eligibility and adjudication.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father is not automatically naturalized or granted residence through the child's citizenship. If married to the Philippine-citizen parent, he may pursue the marriage-based immigrant route; a citizen child aged 21 or older may create quota preference, not automatic status.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026 for rank/access score; Passport Index 2026 for category breakdown

rank.notes: July 2026 Henley position reported by a current secondary source; the interactive Henley page confirms the current index but did not expose a stable country row in extracted text.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's score combines destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance, including some visa-on-arrival arrangements; it is not the strict visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 category count. Its methodology and destination universe differ from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reports 37 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations, combined here. This breakdown should not be added to the separate Henley score.

passport.notes: Henley and Passport Index use different methodologies. Rank 72 and access score 65 use the July 2026 Henley reporting; detailed category counts use Passport Index 2026.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English and Filipino are constitutionally official for communication and instruction, and English is widely usable in government, education and business-facing services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Local-language ability remains valuable for deeper integration outside internationally oriented settings.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low compared with English. Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and no reliable official source reviewed established widespread availability in daily services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: A Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking migrant should expect to rely primarily on English.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of PHP 21,544 at PHP 61.432 per USD. The wage figure covers time-rated full-time workers in establishments with at least 10 workers, not all citizens or workers.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed national Occupational Wages Survey table publishes an average, not a national median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The Philippines has regional and sector-specific minimum wage orders; no single nationally applicable monthly minimum was established in the reviewed national wage source.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of PHP 21,544.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed national table does not publish a national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed source does not publish a meaningful national maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: There is no single national statutory monthly minimum; wage floors vary regionally and by sector.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed national table does not publish a median.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The DNV is not verifiably open. Even if issued under EO 86, it is a temporary non-immigrant visa with no confirmed PR or citizenship conversion.
settlement_track.summary: The DNV is authorized and has published eligibility criteria, but current filing mechanics and final implementation remain unconfirmed. Its legal design is temporary non-immigrant stay only, so settlement would require an independently qualified immigrant status.
settlement_track.notes: The independent quota immigrant route is not a workaround for this profile because its current checklist requires at least USD 100,000 of qualifying capital or investment.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The contemplated DNV fits foreign-contract remote work on paper, but no currently usable filing channel or complete rules were verified. It also lacks a confirmed settlement conversion.

data.notes: More than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected, including five current official URLs absent from the previous source set. The principal unresolved facts—operational DNV filing, reciprocity-country list, numerical income threshold, DNV fees, processing time, DNV-specific tax/social-security treatment and settlement conversion—remain null or cautiously described because the named current official sources do not publish them.

data.selection_summary: Poland does not offer a dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-client remote-worker residence category. A non-EU national generally cannot use visitor status to register a sole proprietorship unless already holding an eligible residence title, while the business-residence permit requires genuine Polish business activity and substantial income, employment, investment, innovation or job-creation evidence. Employer-linked work permits and the Polish-graduate route do not match the supplied profile.

visa_application.title: MOS — Module for Handling Cases
visa_application.notes: Since 27 April 2026, applications for Polish temporary, permanent and EU long-term residence permits are generally submitted electronically through MOS. There is no digital-nomad application category; this portal is relevant only if the applicant qualifies under another statutory purpose such as genuine business, local employment, studies or family residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No qualifying category exists, so there is no published income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying category exists, so a local-currency threshold is inapplicable.

income_requirement_display.value: No dedicated remote-worker residence category
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No threshold is published because no such permit is listed
income_requirement_display.notes: The official catalogue instead lists employment, posting, business, study, research and family purposes.

income_proof_months.notes: Inapplicable because the route does not exist.

key_requirements.requirement: No digital-nomad or foreign-client-only purpose appears in the official temporary-residence catalogue.
Visa-free or visitor presence does not itself provide a residence purpose or unrestricted right to work or establish a sole proprietorship.

initial_validity.notes: There is no permit whose validity period could be stated.

extension_rules.notes: There is no permit capable of extension.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None from foreign remote work alone; another statutory residence purpose is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A foreign contract by itself is not a listed residence purpose.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct or conversion path exists from foreign-client remote work alone.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: EU long-term residence requires at least five years of qualifying legal and continuous residence, stable regular income, health coverage and Polish-language evidence. Ordinary foreign remote work supplies no Polish residence title from which that period could accrue, and Article 212 expressly excludes time as a posted worker or cross-border service provider. A separately obtained Polish business-residence permit can potentially count, but that is a different route with genuine Polish-business requirements, not a conversion from remote-worker status.

path_to_citizenship.value: No path from this nonexistent status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship can follow other qualifying residence statuses, but foreign remote work alone cannot initiate the route.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the decisive rejection: Poland may be attractive for remote work in practice, but the inspected official sources do not establish a residence permit for an ordinary non-EU software engineer working solely for a foreign employer or client.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence permit for conducting business activity

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The test concerns annual Polish-business performance, employment or future economic contribution, not a personal monthly foreign-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Annual business income of at least 12 times the relevant voivodeship average monthly gross wage, or an alternative employment/economic-potential test
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The precise PLN amount varies by voivodeship and reference year.

income_requirement_display.value: Polish business substance/performance test
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Prior-year income ≥12× the relevant regional average monthly wage; or at least two qualifying full-time employees for 12 months; or credible resources/actions showing future investment, innovation, technology transfer or job creation
income_requirement_display.notes: This is materially different from merely showing foreign freelance income.

income_proof_months.notes: The income test uses the preceding tax year; the alternative employment test examines at least 12 months.

key_requirements.requirement: The declared and actual principal purpose of stay must be conducting business in Poland.
Meet the Polish-business income or employment test, or substantiate a credible future economic-contribution forecast.
Provide corporate, financial, insurance, accommodation and other documents required by the procedure.

A non-EU national may register a sole proprietorship on Polish-citizen terms only with an eligible residence title; certain company forms remain available, but company formation alone does not guarantee residence.

initial_validity.value: More than 3 months and up to 3 years, with the individual grant limited to the period needed for the stated business purpose
initial_validity.notes: The EU Immigration Portal confirms the statutory range; the actual duration remains case-specific.

extension_rules.value: A subsequent permit may be requested, subject to the same business-purpose and economic-performance conditions.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal is not automatic.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, if genuine Polish business activity satisfies the statutory test.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Foreign-client contracting alone is insufficient without the required Polish business structure and substance.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential EU long-term resident status after five years of qualifying uninterrupted residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official EU self-employed guidance confirms that a qualifying business permit can feed the EU long-term-resident route. The result is not automatic: the applicant must satisfy continuity and absence limits, stable regular income, health insurance and Polish-language requirements.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially about eight years through the ordinary sequence of five qualifying years to EU long-term residence plus three years on permanent or EU-long-term status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is an illustrative alternative-business timeline, not a route available from remote work alone.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a settlement-oriented independent business route, but it is rejected for the supplied ordinary foreign-contract profile because it requires genuine Polish economic substance. A filing based only on a foreign software contract needs specialist review and should not be treated as a digital-nomad route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of PLN 4,806 using the NBP average rate of PLN 3.7300 per USD published on 2026-08-14.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: PLN 4,806 gross per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official work-permit page identifies this as the 2026 minimum remuneration floor.

income_requirement_display.value: PLN 4,806 gross/month (about USD 1,288)
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer-linked remuneration requirement, not a remote-worker income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed retrospective proof period applies; the employer states the proposed employment conditions.

key_requirements.requirement: A Polish employer must complete and electronically sign the employer annex.
The employment must justify residence exceeding three months and remuneration must meet statutory requirements.
The permit is tied to the specified employment conditions.

initial_validity.value: More than 3 months and up to 3 years
initial_validity.notes: The actual period follows the employment purpose.

extension_rules.value: A new or further application is required when the employment-based residence period expires or material permit conditions change.
extension_rules.notes: Continued eligibility depends on lawful qualifying employment.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence through qualifying Polish employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Not independently usable by a foreign-contract remote worker.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Qualifying residence can count toward the five-year EU long-term resident route.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Subject to continuity, income, health-insurance and Polish-language requirements.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially after EU long-term or permanent status and the additional citizenship-recognition period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Irrelevant to selection because a local employer is required.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant's foreign employer or client cannot substitute for the required Polish employment basis and employer annex.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for graduates of Polish universities

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the PLN 1,010 monthly subsistence amount for a person without dependants using the NBP average rate of PLN 3.7300 per USD on 2026-08-14; additional return-travel funds are required.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: PLN 1,010 per month without dependants, or PLN 823 for the applicant and each supported family member, plus return-travel funds
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: These are subsistence-funds requirements, not employment income.

income_requirement_display.value: PLN 1,010/month plus return funds for a single applicant
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: PLN 1,010 monthly; lower per-person formula for supported family members; return funds vary by destination
income_requirement_display.notes: Only recent graduates of Polish institutions qualify.

income_proof_months.notes: Funds should cover the nine-month permit period, although the official guidance describes the monthly amount rather than a nine-month bank-history requirement.

key_requirements.requirement: A qualifying degree must have been obtained from a Polish university immediately before applying.
The applicant must be legally staying in Poland in connection with those studies when applying.
Purpose must be seeking local employment or preparing to commence business activity in Poland.
Accommodation, health insurance, subsistence and return funds are required.

initial_validity.value: 9 months, granted once
initial_validity.notes: It is a post-study transition permit.

extension_rules.value: Not renewable in the same category; the graduate must switch to another residence basis.
extension_rules.notes: A foreign degree obtained before moving to Poland does not qualify.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct nine-month temporary residence only after completing qualifying studies in Poland.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant's existing foreign degree is insufficient.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent residence; another qualifying status is required.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Study residence is only partly counted under specified circumstances, while periods spent in Poland merely for education are excluded; the subsequent graduate status and any proposed transition require case-specific verification.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only after switching to and completing another qualifying residence track.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not a direct citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: Interesting only to someone who first studies in Poland. It does not fit the supplied software engineer merely because the applicant already holds a relevant foreign university degree.

summary.value: Poland offers a one-time nine-month permit to recent graduates of Polish universities for job search or preparation to start a business, without requiring an employer at filing. A foreign university degree alone creates no comparable residence right, and employment-oriented skilled or Blue Card routes require qualifying local employment.
summary.notes: The supplied applicant's existing degree does not satisfy the Polish-graduate condition, so this does not make Poland a partial match.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally Polish tax-resident if Poland is the centre of personal or economic interests or if presence in Poland exceeds 183 days in the tax year. Treaty tie-breaker rules may change the result in dual-residence cases.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The centre-of-interests test can establish residence before day 184.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal rate of the ordinary progressive scale, not an expected effective rate. Eligible business taxpayers may use different regimes.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single meaningful percentage applies to this profile. Self-employed social contributions use statutory assessment bases and fixed minimum amounts, while health contributions depend on the tax regime and income or revenue.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed amount applies. In 2026 standard self-employed social contributions are PLN 1,926.76 monthly including voluntary sickness insurance, or PLN 1,788.29 without it, before health insurance. Preferential contributions may be lower; health insurance is additional and regime-dependent.

special_tax_regimes.value: Eligible sole proprietors may use the progressive scale, a 19% business flat-tax regime, or revenue-based lump-sum taxation. Official guidance lists a 12% lump-sum rate for specified software and IT services, but precise PKWiU activity classification is essential.
special_tax_regimes.notes: These are general business regimes, not a digital-nomad concession.

taxes.caveats: Poland has no special digital-nomad tax regime. Tax treatment depends on residence, where work is physically performed, employee versus contractor status, permanent-establishment risk, social-security coordination and the applicable double-tax treaty. Immigration eligibility and tax registration are separate questions.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: the ordinary personal scale is progressive, while qualifying business activity may elect alternative flat or revenue-based regimes.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Centre of personal or economic interests in Poland, or more than 183 days in the tax year; treaty tie-breakers may apply.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally report worldwide income; non-residents generally report Polish-source income, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Potential 19% business flat tax or revenue-based lump-sum rates, including 12% for specified software/IT classifications; no digital-nomad exemption.
taxation_system.social_security: A locally registered business generally creates ZUS obligations. Standard 2026 social contributions are PLN 1,926.76 including voluntary sickness insurance or PLN 1,788.29 without it, before health insurance. Preferential and small-business schemes have separate eligibility rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard screening value is the 32% top marginal rate. Under the ordinary scale, 12% applies up to PLN 120,000, reduced by the PLN 3,600 tax-reducing amount, and 32% applies only to the excess.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Tax base up to PLN 120,000 annually
tax_brackets.notes: Tax is reduced by PLN 3,600; USD figure uses the NBP average rate of PLN 3.7300 per USD on 2026-08-14.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess above the threshold under the ordinary PIT scale
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not the rate on all income; USD threshold uses the 2026-08-14 NBP rate.

taxation_system.notes: The ordinary scale is well supported by the Ministry of Finance. Selecting a business regime and determining social-security liability requires contract- and activity-specific advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a visa category. A person nevertheless living and physically working from Poland may create Polish income-tax and social-security obligations despite having a foreign payer.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No Polish digital-nomad route; analyze as a cross-border employee or locally registered business if another lawful residence basis exists.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Ordinary scale: 12% then 32% top marginal rate; eligible businesses may have alternative regimes.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Centre of interests or more than 183 days, subject to tax-treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Polish residents generally report worldwide income. A non-resident physically working in Poland may still have Polish-source employment or service income depending on the facts and treaty.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad exemption or holiday was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Foreign employment and cross-border social security require case-specific coordination. A Polish sole proprietorship generally pays ZUS social and health contributions.

fixed_payments.status: No universal digital-nomad fixed payment; self-employed amounts depend on ZUS relief eligibility and tax regime.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Standard 2026 social contributions: PLN 1,926.76/month including voluntary sickness insurance or PLN 1,788.29 without it, before health insurance. Preferential social contributions can be PLN 456.18 or PLN 420.86 respectively. Health insurance is additional and regime-dependent.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Residence applications through MOS carry stamp duty generally ranging from PLN 340 to PLN 640 depending on permit type, plus PLN 100 for the residence card. No digital-nomad fee exists.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The 2026 domestic VAT small-business exemption threshold is generally PLN 240,000 of qualifying sales, subject to exclusions and place-of-establishment rules.
fixed_payments.notes: Amounts describe local-business scenarios and do not create immigration eligibility.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 184 days does not guarantee non-residence because a Polish centre of personal or economic interests is an independent test. Polish-source taxation and treaty rules can still apply.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A Polish tax resident generally reports worldwide income. Foreign-employer payroll, permanent-establishment, treaty and social-security issues require review.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: If legally entitled to register and genuinely operating a Polish business, the person must select an eligible PIT regime, address ZUS and health contributions, and examine VAT obligations. Registration does not by itself satisfy the business-residence permit.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section is included for screening even though Poland lacks a qualifying nomad route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Foreign-client remote work alone never produces temporary residence. A qualifying alternative purpose must exist first.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: EU long-term residence generally requires five years of qualifying uninterrupted residence in total, not five additional years after every temporary permit. Certain statuses are excluded or only partly counted.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The ordinary recognition criterion requires three continuous years on permanent residence, EU long-term residence or permanent-residence rights, plus stable Polish income and a dwelling title.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Illustrative ordinary minimum after first obtaining a qualifying residence basis: about five years to EU long-term status plus three years on that status. It is not available from foreign remote work alone and processing time is additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current Polish government return portal states that the statutory handling period for recognition cases was extended to six months. Presidential discretionary grants are separate and commonly take longer.

key_conditions.value: Qualifying and sufficiently continuous residence; stable and regular income; legal title to housing; at least B1 Polish for EU long-term residence and recognition as a citizen; compliance with absence rules; and no public-security bar. Ordinary recognition does not state a general renunciation requirement.
key_conditions.notes: The five-year EU long-term calculation excludes or discounts some residence categories and normally limits absences to six consecutive months and ten months total.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For citizenship recognition through marriage, the person must have been married to a Polish citizen for at least three years and have resided continuously for at least two years on permanent residence, EU long-term residence or permanent-residence rights. Before permanent residence, a non-EU spouse generally needs at least three years of marriage and two years of qualifying temporary residence based on that marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Polish citizen can count toward the three-year marriage-duration requirement, but it does not automatically confer residence or citizenship. Marriage to another foreign national provides no Polish-nationality shortcut.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The necessary Polish residence and status periods remain separate.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be recognized under Polish law, genuine and adequately documented. Authorities examine whether it was contracted to circumvent immigration rules. Sham marriage can cause refusal or status consequences; B1 Polish remains required for adult citizenship recognition.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage is an independent family route, not a way to validate an otherwise non-qualifying remote-work stay.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Poland alone does not normally grant citizenship. Territorial acquisition is restricted to a child born or found in Poland whose parents are both unknown, stateless or of undetermined citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Poland-born child of two foreign citizens does not ordinarily acquire Polish citizenship solely by birth. The narrow exception covers unknown, stateless or undetermined parents.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The child may need a separate residence permit; the parent's permit does not automatically cover the child.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child automatically acquires Polish citizenship at birth when at least one parent is a Polish citizen, regardless of birthplace.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This is citizenship by descent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A genuine family relationship with a Polish-citizen child may support a fact-specific temporary family-life residence application, but parenthood does not automatically give the foreign parent permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must use the appropriate MOS family category and prove the required genuine family ties or dependency.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Polish child may seek residence based on genuine protected family life where the statutory facts are met. He does not automatically become Polish, and the ordinary permanent-residence and citizenship requirements are not waived merely because his child is Polish.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage, actual care, dependency and family-life evidence may be scrutinized.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank as displayed on 2026-08-15; this is not a Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strict visa-free count. Its broader mobility score is 172 after including visa-on-arrival and eTA access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 43 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. Electronic visas are treated separately by the index and are not included.

passport.notes: Passport-index methodologies differ. Passport Index was used because it publishes a current separated breakdown; Henley combines several access categories in its mobility score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Generally practical in international technology and major-city environments. EF EPI 2025 ranked Poland 15th of 123 with very high adult English proficiency and reported a particularly strong IT score, but Polish remains necessary for many administrative processes and B1 Polish is required for the main settlement milestones.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected proficiency dataset and should not be interpreted as universal fluency.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Ukrainian and Russian assistance is available on parts of the Office for Foreigners and MOS ecosystem, which helps with immigration information. Neither language is nationally official, and everyday or professional usability varies substantially by city and institution.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Polish should be expected for formal integration and long-term settlement.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 national-economy average monthly gross wage of PLN 8,903.56 using the NBP average rate of PLN 3.7300 per USD on 2026-08-14.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the February 2026 national-economy gross median of PLN 7,690.82 using the 2026-08-14 NBP rate.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 statutory minimum wage; this is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 national-economy average monthly gross wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the February 2026 national-economy median monthly gross wage.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A numeric nationwide maximum is inapplicable: Poland has no statutory maximum wage, and current Statistics Poland publications report averages, medians, subgroup medians and distribution or decile measures rather than a finite national wage ceiling. A top observed individual salary would be sample-dependent and is not published as a representative national statistic.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage effective throughout 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average for the national economy during 2025.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median for February 2026; half of covered employees earned no more and half no less.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite national maximum applies; official wage statistics publish distribution measures rather than a maximum salary or wage ceiling
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Statistics Poland's current national releases provide averages, medians, subgroup medians and decile-based distributions. The upper tail remains open above the highest published decile, so treating a decile cutoff, occupational subgroup median or isolated observed salary as the national maximum would be misleading.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly wages in the national economy; minimum field is the statutory employee minimum
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 annual average, February 2026 median, and 2026 statutory minimum
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average citizen/resident-worker wage indicators, not immigration income thresholds. USD conversions use the official NBP average exchange rate of PLN 3.7300 per USD published on 2026-08-14.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official labor-statistics sources do not publish a single current monthly cost-of-living budget comparable across household types. Wage statistics were not used as a proxy.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Poland has no dedicated nomad status. Visitor or visa-free presence should not be treated as a remote-work residence or citizenship track.
settlement_track.summary: Foreign-client remote work alone is not a qualifying Polish residence purpose and therefore cannot start a confirmed settlement clock. A genuine Polish business, local employment, study, family or other statutory status may create a separate residence-to-citizenship path, but switching requires independently satisfying that route.
settlement_track.notes: The business route can be settlement-oriented, but its Polish economic-substance requirements make it unsuitable for treating an ordinary foreign software contract as a nomad route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated residence permit fits ordinary work solely for a foreign employer or client. The sole-proprietor and business-residence rules create circular or substantive eligibility barriers rather than a visitor-to-freelancer legalization route.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Poland result with focused searches for both flagged fields. The remote-worker permanent-residence note now distinguishes the nonexistent remote-work route from the separate qualifying business route and incorporates the statutory exclusion for posted and cross-border service-provider periods. The salary maximum field now explains that no finite national maximum applies and that official Polish wage releases publish distribution measures rather than a representative maximum. Thirty-nine distinct relevant canonical URLs are retained, including eight URLs outside the previous source set; current February 2026 wage data and the official 2026-08-14 NBP exchange rate were also incorporated.

data.selection_summary: Portugal's D8 residence route fits an ordinary software engineer working remotely for a foreign employer or client. It is independently available without a Portuguese employer, requires average income of four Portuguese minimum wages—EUR 3,680 per month in 2026—and leads to an ordinary two-year temporary residence permit renewable for three-year periods. Permanent residence is available after five years. Under nationality rules effective 19 May 2026, naturalization generally requires ten years of legal residence for non-EU/non-CPLP nationals or seven years for EU/CPLP nationals.

visa_application.title: E-Visa — Portuguese visa application portal
visa_application.notes: This is the Foreign Ministry's online visa portal. Select the residence visa for professional activity performed remotely outside Portugal and follow the instructions of the Portuguese consular post responsible for the applicant's residence. The portal blocked automated inspection, so its current jurisdiction-specific checklist and any external-service-provider charges must be confirmed manually.

best_routes.route_name: D8 residence visa and residence permit for remote work outside Portugal

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 3,680 using the ECB reference rate of EUR 1 = USD 1.1567 on 14 August 2026, the latest available working day before the research date. This is not a consular conversion rate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,680 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The formula is four times the Portuguese guaranteed minimum monthly remuneration. The 2026 minimum is EUR 920.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,680/month average over the previous 3 months (about USD 4,257)
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Four times Portugal's 2026 minimum monthly remuneration
income_requirement_display.notes: The euro threshold changes when the statutory minimum wage changes. Consulates may apply their own exchange-rate methodology.

income_proof_months.notes: Applicants must demonstrate average monthly income over the three months preceding the application.

key_requirements.requirement: Perform subordinate employment or independent professional services remotely for a person or entity domiciled or headquartered outside Portugal.
Provide an employment contract or employer declaration or, for independent work, a service contract, proposed service contract, company contract, or evidence of services performed.
Provide evidence of tax residence and average income of at least four Portuguese minimum wages during the preceding three months.

At the residence-permit stage, provide a valid passport and residence visa, means of subsistence, Portuguese accommodation evidence, criminal-record documentation, and the other general evidence requested by AIMA.

initial_validity.value: Residence visa followed by a two-year temporary residence permit
initial_validity.notes: The visa enables entry and the AIMA residence-permit process; the qualifying settlement status is the temporary residence permit.

extension_rules.value: The temporary residence permit is renewable for successive three-year periods.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains subject to continued eligibility and general residence requirements.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct: obtain the D8 residence visa abroad, enter Portugal, and complete the residence-permit process with AIMA.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is different from the temporary-stay version of the remote-work visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The D8 residence permit is renewable and can lead to permanent residence after five years holding temporary residence. Foreign employment or foreign-client services can continue; no local employer or investment route is required.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The five-year period refers to temporary residence permits, not merely a D8 temporary-stay visa. Someone entering on the temporary-stay variant must separately obtain the residence visa/permit; that visa period is not certified here as qualifying. The AIMA pages were verified through their current indexed official text; direct page retrieval returned an error.

path_to_citizenship.value: Legal D8 residence feeds the ordinary naturalization track. Applications filed after 19 May 2026 generally require ten years of legal residence for nationals outside the EU and CPLP, or seven years for EU/CPLP nationals.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is separate from permanent residence and has language, civic-knowledge, subsistence, security, sanctions, and criminal-record conditions. Pre-19-May-2026 pending cases are governed by transitional rules.

best_routes.notes: This is a strong settlement-oriented match for ordinary foreign-contract remote work: no Portuguese employer, local client, investment, startup, or elite-talent condition is inherent in the D8 route. The principal drawback for most third-country nationals is the ten-year citizenship horizon.

rejected_routes.route_name: D8 temporary-stay visa for remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the same four-minimum-wage formula used for remote-worker visa applications, using EUR 1 = USD 1.1567 on 14 August 2026.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,680 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Four times the 2026 minimum monthly remuneration.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 3,680/month average over the previous 3 months
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Four times Portugal's 2026 minimum monthly remuneration
income_requirement_display.notes: The income condition is documented, but this temporary-stay option does not itself issue an ordinary residence permit.

income_proof_months.notes: Average monthly income over the preceding three months.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign employment or independent service relationship and proof of remote activity.
Tax-residence and income evidence meeting the four-minimum-wage formula.

initial_validity.value: Temporary-stay visa for a professional stay shorter than one year
initial_validity.notes: The official general temporary-work service describes this visa category as covering a professional activity for less than one year. The D8-specific duration should still be verified with the responsible consular post.

extension_rules.value: Extensions are possible only through Portugal's general extension-of-stay procedure and remain case-specific; no D8-specific automatic renewal entitlement was identified.
extension_rules.notes: The current AIMA fee schedule contains a charge for extending a temporary-stay visa, but publication of a fee does not establish that every requested extension must be granted.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: This visa authorizes temporary stay but does not directly issue an ordinary temporary residence permit. A settlement applicant should use the D8 residence-visa version or separately qualify for another residence-permit procedure.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary lawful stay and temporary residence authorization are legally distinct statuses.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path from the temporary-stay visa itself: the official permanent-residence rule requires at least five years as the holder of a temporary residence authorization, and a temporary-stay visa is not such an authorization.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A later independently approved switch to a qualifying residence permit could start the permanent-residence track, but no automatic conversion from this D8 temporary-stay variant was identified.

path_to_citizenship.value: Time in Portugal under a valid temporary-stay visa may potentially count as legal residence for nationality purposes because Article 15 of the current Nationality Law expressly includes regularized stay under qualifying titles, visas, or authorizations. Ordinary naturalization still requires seven years for EU/CPLP nationals or ten years for other nationals, together with all substantive conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not equivalent to a permanent-residence pathway. The applicant should obtain official confirmation that every visa and extension period is recorded as qualifying legal residence; the D8 residence-permit route is materially safer for continuous settlement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it does not itself create the temporary residence authorization required for permanent residence. It may suit a shorter stay, and valid visa periods may be relevant to nationality counting, but the D8 residence visa is the clearer settlement-oriented route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tech Visa residence for a highly qualified worker employed by a certified company

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 1,342.83, calculated as 2.5 times the 2026 monthly IAS of EUR 537.13, using EUR 1 = USD 1.1567 on 14 August 2026. The governing instrument phrases the contract condition as minimum remuneration equivalent to 2.5 IAS, while AIMA describes a minimum salary; the certified company should confirm payroll presentation.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 1,342.83 per month (2.5 × the 2026 IAS of EUR 537.13)
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold changes when Portugal updates the IAS.

income_requirement_display.value: At least 2.5 × IAS, currently about EUR 1,342.83/month (about USD 1,553)
income_requirement_display.notes: The income threshold does not remove the requirement for a contract and responsibility statement from a certified company.

income_proof_months.notes: The official sources require a contract of at least 12 months but do not specify a separate number of historical payslip or income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: A contract or service contract of at least 12 months and a responsibility statement issued by a company certified under Tech Visa.
Minimum qualification at ISCED level 6, or level 5 plus at least five years of exceptional specialized technical experience.
Adequate command of Portuguese, English, French, or Spanish and compliance with criminal-record and tax/social-security requirements.

initial_validity.value: Two-year temporary residence permit

extension_rules.value: Renewable for successive three-year periods

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employer-supported temporary residence through a certified company.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not independently usable with only a foreign employer or client.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially through the ordinary five-year temporary-residence rule, but entry requires a certified participating company.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The settlement potential does not cure the route's incompatibility with the supplied independent remote-worker profile.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through ordinary legal-residence naturalization after seven or ten years depending on nationality, but it is not a match for the supplied independent remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the certified company must issue the responsibility statement and contract. It is not independently available to an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

summary.value: Admission to a recognized Portuguese higher-education institution can support a study residence visa and temporary residence permit without an employer. Applicants need admission or enrolment, tuition evidence where applicable, subsistence, accommodation, health coverage, and general immigration documents. Graduates of qualifying higher-education or research programs may obtain up to one year to seek work or establish a compatible business, but study residence is a separate education route and does not grant permanent residence directly.
summary.notes: This alternative is unnecessary for the applicant because the D8 already fits the active foreign contract. Post-study conversion and residence-time counting should be checked for the specific program before relying on it for settlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: Portuguese tax residence generally begins when a person spends more than 183 days, consecutive or not, in a relevant 12-month period beginning or ending in the tax year, or has a dwelling in Portugal under circumstances indicating an intention to maintain and occupy it as a habitual home.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breakers, split-year rules, and the precise date a habitual home becomes available can change the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Maximum screening marginal burden: the ordinary continental Portugal IRS schedule reaches 48%, and an additional 5% solidarity rate applies to taxable income above EUR 250,000. This is not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening rate for a locally registered self-employed worker. For services, the relevant contribution base is generally derived from 70% of declared service revenue. Foreign employees may instead be governed by Portuguese payroll rules, EU coordination, a bilateral agreement, or continued foreign coverage.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the EUR 20 minimum monthly self-employed contribution when there is no income or the calculated contribution is lower. Exemptions or foreign social-security coverage may alter the result.

special_tax_regimes.value: The D8 itself provides no tax exemption. IFICI can impose a 20% special IRS rate for ten years on qualifying Category A/B income, but only for narrowly defined research, innovation, highly qualified, startup, export-company, or other eligible activities and entities; a foreign-contract software engineer should not assume eligibility.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The former broad NHR regime should not be assumed available to a new 2026 arrival. IFICI eligibility requires a separate activity, entity, and registration review.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on residence dates, whether the arrangement is employment or self-employment, income sourcing, permanent-establishment and payroll exposure, VAT place-of-supply rules, social-security coordination, and the applicable double-tax treaty. The D8 is an immigration status, not a tax regime.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income under progressive IRS rates. The 2026 ordinary schedule runs from 12.5% to 48%, with additional solidarity rates of 2.5% and 5% at high income levels.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in a relevant 12-month period, or a dwelling indicating habitual residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Portuguese tax residents must declare Portuguese and foreign income; foreign tax may qualify for double-tax relief. Non-residents are generally taxed only on Portuguese-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: IFICI offers a 20% rate for ten years only to qualifying new residents performing specifically eligible activities for eligible entities; it is not an automatic digital-nomad concession.
taxation_system.social_security: Locally registered independent workers generally face a 21.4% contribution rate, normally calculated using 70% of service revenue under the quarterly method, with a EUR 20 minimum contribution in low/no-income cases. Employee and cross-border coverage can differ.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value of 53% is a maximum screening marginal rate, combining the 48% top ordinary rate with the 5% solidarity rate above EUR 250,000. It is not an estimate of effective tax. The ordinary brackets below apply to continental Portugal; autonomous-region rates may differ.
