taxation_system.notes: High confidence in the statutory rates and residence rule; only medium confidence in an applicant-specific result because contract characterization, deductions, treaties, and social-security coordination were not supplied.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: D8 holders receive no automatic tax holiday. Once Portuguese tax resident, a remote worker generally declares worldwide employment or professional income and faces the ordinary progressive system unless independently eligible for IFICI or treaty relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital-nomad residence holder taxed under ordinary resident rules; employment or Category B self-employment treatment depends on the contract structure.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive IRS: 12.5%–48%, plus solidarity additions producing a maximum 53% screening marginal rate; this is not an expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in a relevant 12-month period or maintenance of a habitual home in Portugal.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents must declare income obtained both in Portugal and abroad; documented foreign tax may receive double-tax credit relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No D8-specific tax regime. IFICI's 20% rate for ten years is possible only if the person and activity or entity independently satisfy its narrow statutory conditions.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A locally registered independent professional generally contributes at 21.4% on the applicable contribution base, commonly derived from 70% of service revenue. A foreign employee requires a separate payroll and social-security coordination analysis.

fixed_payments.status: Current official visa and AIMA charges are partly quantified; they are transactional rather than monthly fixed taxes.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: For locally registered self-employment, the official guide describes a minimum EUR 20 monthly contribution when there is no income or the calculated contribution is below EUR 20. Foreign mandatory coverage or an exemption may change this.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The current official professional-visa pages list EUR 90 for a residence visa and EUR 75 for a temporary-stay visa. AIMA's current schedule separately lists EUR 133 for reception and analysis of an ordinary residence application, or EUR 99.80 through the qualifying digital channel, and EUR 114.30 for concession or renewal of temporary residence, or EUR 85.80 digitally. If both AIMA items apply, the listed components total EUR 247.30 in person or EUR 185.60 digitally. The responsible consulate and AIMA should confirm the D8 classification, exemptions, applicable channel, and final total before payment.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The domestic small-business VAT exemption threshold is EUR 15,000 of annual turnover in Portugal, subject to statutory conditions. Cross-border B2B services may follow different place-of-supply and reverse-charge rules, so the threshold alone does not determine VAT liability.
fixed_payments.notes: The EUR 90/EUR 75 official fee page describes professional-activity visa categories rather than a D8-only fee table. External visa-center charges, insurance, accommodation, document legalization, translations, postage, and criminal-record certificates are additional and vary by jurisdiction.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining under 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if a habitual home exists. Portuguese-source income, payroll, permanent-establishment, VAT, and treaty issues may still arise.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Assume worldwide income reporting and progressive IRS unless a treaty or independently qualified IFICI treatment applies. Foreign taxes should be documented for potential credit relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect Portuguese activity registration, invoicing and filing duties, possible VAT obligations, and generally 21.4% social security on the applicable base, with quarterly reporting and a EUR 20 minimum in low/no-income cases.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The statutory framework and published fee components are well sourced, but the treatment of a particular foreign employment or service contract and the exact D8 fee total require individualized confirmation with the responsible consular post, AIMA, and Portuguese tax and social-security advisers.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The route is designed to lead directly from the residence visa to temporary residence; processing time is not represented as an eligibility waiting period.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The applicant may apply after at least five years as a temporary-residence holder, subject to current statutory conditions.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Citizenship eligibility is based on total legal residence, not a fixed period after obtaining permanent residence. For most third-country nationals, reaching permanent residence at year five leaves approximately five further years before the ten-year naturalization threshold.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Standard threshold for nationals outside the EU and CPLP under applications filed after 19 May 2026. EU/CPLP nationals generally require seven years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current official filing services explain submission channels and status tracking but publish no representative or guaranteed completion time. Processing is additional to the residence-eligibility period and varies by case.

key_conditions.value: Maintain qualifying legal residence and lawful income; demonstrate sufficient Portuguese, knowledge of Portuguese culture, history, national symbols, fundamental rights and duties, and state organization; make the required democratic-rule-of-law declaration; show capacity for self-support; and satisfy criminal-record, security, and sanctions checks. Permanent residence is not a prerequisite for naturalization. Portuguese law does not generally require renunciation, but the other country may restrict multiple nationality.
key_conditions.notes: Detailed implementing rules were undergoing adaptation after the May 2026 nationality reform; filing requirements should be rechecked when eligibility approaches.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse married to, or in a court-recognized de facto union with, a Portuguese citizen for more than three years may apply by declaration. This is a citizenship route, not automatic citizenship at marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Time already spent married to a Portuguese citizen can count toward the more-than-three-year condition if the marriage remains in force when the declaration is made. An existing marriage to a non-Portuguese person creates no Portuguese citizenship shortcut.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage or recognized union must be genuine and continuing. Depending on duration and circumstances, evidence of an effective connection to the Portuguese community may be required; opposition remains possible on statutory integrity, security, and related grounds. False documents or a sham relationship can lead to refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: After six years of marriage or union, or where the couple has Portuguese children, the amended law limits certain opposition grounds, but acquisition is still not automatic.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A Portugal-born child of foreign parents can be Portuguese by origin upon declaration if, at birth, one parent had legally resided in Portugal for at least five years and neither parent was serving their foreign state. Separate rules cover a parent also born and resident in Portugal, stateless children, and foundlings.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Citizenship is not automatic in every migrant-parent case. Under the principal residence condition, the child must be born in Portugal, at least one parent must have five years of legal residence at the birth, the foreign-state-service exclusion must not apply, and the required declaration must be made. A minor may also seek naturalization later under separate cumulative rules.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Because the parents' residence history is unspecified, a universal true-or-false result cannot be assigned.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Portuguese mother or father is Portuguese by origin. For births abroad, Portuguese civil registration or a declaration may be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Portuguese or Portugal-resident minor may apply for temporary residence without a residence visa under Article 122(1)(k) if the parent actually exercises parental responsibilities and supports and educates the child. The child's citizenship does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must independently document identity, address, means, criminal record, tax/social-security registration, parentage, actual parental responsibility, and support.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father can use the Article 122(1)(k) residence route on the same basis as the mother if he effectively exercises parental responsibilities and provides support and education. There is no automatic citizenship for the father merely because the child is Portuguese.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Legal parentage and effective involvement must be documented; biological parentage alone is insufficient.

rank.notes: Portugal was tied in the fifth-ranked group in the current 2026 table inspected on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score combines destinations accessible without an advance visa, including categories such as visa on arrival; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The current Henley ranking page does not publish a separate count of destinations requiring an advance visa.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Henley publishes a combined access score but does not expose a separate visa-on-arrival/eTA total on the inspected ranking page.

passport.notes: Portugal has a very strong EU passport, but the access score can change during the year and should be rechecked near naturalization or travel.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High in international and remote-work settings. The 2025 EF English Proficiency Index placed Portugal sixth globally with very high proficiency, although Portuguese remains important for government procedures and long-term integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF is a reputable private index based on a self-selected testing population, not a government census; proficiency varies by age and region.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No nationwide source reviewed established Russian or Ukrainian as broadly usable for Portuguese administration or daily services. Applicants should plan to use Portuguese and, in international settings, English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages. Availability of community interpreters or services is local and was not quantified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 nationwide average gross monthly remuneration of EUR 1,694 using EUR 1 = USD 1.1567 on 14 August 2026.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official October 2024 mainland median monthly earnings of EUR 1,191. The series covers full-time employees who received complete earnings and therefore is narrower than the nationwide average series.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory 2026 minimum monthly remuneration of EUR 920.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the 2025 average total gross monthly remuneration per worker.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of EUR 1,191 using EUR 1 = USD 1.1567. The underlying official statistic is the October 2024 median monthly earnings of mainland full-time employees who received complete earnings; it is not a whole-population, net-pay, or all-territory median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official personnel series reports decile cut-points and mean earnings within each decile but does not publish the highest observed salary. A top-decile average or boundary is not a national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum remuneration for 2026; Portuguese employment commonly provides 14 salary payments annually.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average total gross monthly remuneration per worker for 2025.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official October 2024 median for mainland full-time employees who received complete earnings. The narrower population and reference month mean it should not be treated as directly identical in scope to the 2025 nationwide average.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The current official personnel series publishes the median, decile thresholds, and mean earnings by decile but no maximum observed salary; no defensible national maximum amount can therefore be stated.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory national minimum; nationwide average total gross remuneration per worker; and mainland full-time-employee median monthly earnings
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum: 2026; average: 2025; median: October 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are citizen/resident labor-market indicators, not the immigration income threshold. The minimum is statutory, the average is an economy-wide gross worker measure, and the median is a narrower mainland full-time-employee statistic. USD conversions use the ECB rate for 14 August 2026.

cost_of_living_note.value: No single current official national cost-of-living basket suitable for an individual remote worker was established. Official housing material indicates continuing housing-access and affordability pressures, so accommodation should be budgeted separately by city rather than inferred from the national salary average.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No numerical cost-of-living estimate is supplied because national averages would obscure substantial Lisbon, Porto, island, and interior differences.

settlement_track.summary: The D8 residence version produces ordinary renewable temporary residence rather than a visitor-like nomad stay. It can lead to permanent residence after five years and naturalization after ten years for most non-EU/non-CPLP nationals, without switching to employer-sponsored status.
settlement_track.notes: This classification applies to the D8 residence visa and resulting residence permit, not the separate temporary-stay visa. Citizenship remains conditional and is not automatic when the residence threshold is reached.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The law expressly covers employees and independent professionals providing remote activity to persons or entities domiciled or headquartered outside Portugal. No Portuguese employer, local client, investment, startup, or exceptional-achievement requirement is inherent in the route.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Portugal record using 36 distinct relevant URLs, including nine focused additions outside the previous source set. The positive D8 conclusion remains supported. This pass resolved the temporary-stay visa's permanent-residence and nationality treatment, quantified current consular and AIMA fee components, calculated the Tech Visa threshold from the 2026 IAS, and added an official EUR 1,191 mainland median-earnings statistic. No official national maximum salary or representative citizenship processing duration is published in the current sources, so those numeric values remain null with precise scope explanations.

reviewed_route_names: D8 residence visa and residence permit for remote work outside Portugal
digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Autorização de residência permanente under Article 80
requirements: Maintain the qualifying residence permit and comply with residence/absence rules.
Show subsistence, accommodation and compliance with tax and social-security obligations.
Prove basic Portuguese and satisfy criminal-record requirements.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The D8 residence permit is renewable and can lead to permanent residence after five years holding temporary residence. Foreign employment or foreign-client services can continue; no local employer or investment route is required.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The five-year period refers to temporary residence permits, not merely a D8 temporary-stay visa. Someone entering on the temporary-stay variant must separately obtain the residence visa/permit; that visa period is not certified here as qualifying. The AIMA pages were verified through their current indexed official text; direct page retrieval returned an error.

data.selection_summary: Qatar has no confirmed digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or independent-professional residence route. Its current entrepreneur permit requires endorsement by a recognized Qatari incubator and a Qatar-oriented venture; its executive permit requires existing Qatari residence, employer nomination, a qualifying local employment contract, senior experience, and a very high local salary. Visitor status is expressly for tourism and prohibits commercial activities. None fits ordinary work for a foreign client. General permanent residence normally requires 20 years of legal residence for a foreign-born person, while naturalization requires 25 consecutive years and remains highly discretionary.

visa_application.title: Residency Program — Entrepreneurs & Executives
visa_application.notes: This is the official route-information and application-entry page for Qatar's closest independent residence option, but it is not a digital-nomad application. Overseas entrepreneurs must first obtain local-incubator endorsement; executives use an employer-led process. Qatar's separate Hayya portal only handles visitor entry permits.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is published. The financial test is an attested three-month bank statement showing at least USD 10,000 for an overseas applicant.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: QAR 36,500 minimum bank balance maintained/evidenced over the preceding three months
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is a balance requirement, not monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income threshold; USD 10,000 (approximately QAR 36,400–36,500) bank balance evidenced for three months
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: USD threshold with official QAR equivalent
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: QAR 36,500 bank balance / USD 10,000 for overseas applicants
income_requirement_display.notes: The official program page uses QAR 36,500 for its general criterion and USD 10,000 for overseas applicants. QAR is officially pegged at 3.64 per USD.

income_proof_months.notes: Three months of attested bank statements are required; this demonstrates a balance rather than recurring income.

key_requirements.requirement: Be at least 18 and hold a passport valid for at least six months.
Obtain an endorsement certificate from a recognized business incubator in Qatar; incubator nomination precedes access to the application platform.
Overseas applicants provide a CV, photograph, attested police-clearance certificate, and attested three-month bank statement with at least USD 10,000.
After approval and arrival, complete medical examination, fingerprinting and QID issuance, then obtain the special work permit.
The project must be a genuine founder/entrepreneur venture intended to establish, operate, or scale in Qatar; a foreign software-engineering contract alone is insufficient.

initial_validity.value: Five-year self-sponsored residence permit
initial_validity.notes: The official launch and FAQ describe a five-year self-sponsored entrepreneur permit.

extension_rules.value: Renewable subject to continuing eligibility; renewal uses the same documentation requirements as the initial application.
extension_rules.notes: Continued incubator/program compliance must be demonstrated.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Directly grants long-term, self-sponsored temporary residence after incubator nomination and government approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is entrepreneur residence, not ordinary freelance or foreign-remote-worker residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No special permanent-residence conversion is published. The ordinary statutory framework generally requires 20 years of legal residence for a foreign-born applicant, sufficient income, good conduct and Arabic knowledge; whether every year on this new permit will be accepted has not been expressly confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence is discretionary and subject to statutory administration and limits.

path_to_citizenship.value: No accelerated entrepreneur route is published. Ordinary naturalization requires at least 25 consecutive years of residence, lawful income, good character and Arabic knowledge, and remains discretionary.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Meeting the minimum conditions does not create an entitlement to citizenship; dual nationality is generally prohibited absent an Emiri decision.

rejected_routes.notes: The permit is independently held once approved, but entry depends on a Qatar-recognized incubator and a genuine Qatar-oriented founder venture. It therefore fails the ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker profile even though it is residence-oriented.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the lowest QAR 50,000 monthly threshold at the official 3.64 QAR/USD peg. Other executive-director titles require QAR 80,000, approximately USD 21,978.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: QAR 50,000/month for Chairman, COO, CTO, CFO or CEO; QAR 80,000/month for other Executive Director titles
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The salary must arise from a qualifying direct local employment contract.

income_requirement_display.value: QAR 50,000–80,000 per month (approximately USD 13,736–21,978)
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: QAR 50,000 or QAR 80,000 monthly depending on title
income_requirement_display.notes: The displayed USD figure is the lowest threshold, converted at the official 3.64 QAR/USD peg.

income_proof_months.notes: The application requires three months of signed and stamped bank statements, alongside proof of qualifying local salary and employment.

key_requirements.requirement: Already hold Qatari residence and be nominated by the employer.
Have at least five years of senior executive-management experience.
Hold a qualifying senior title and a direct local employment contract with an eligible listed company, regulated financial institution, insurer, consulting firm, or state-owned entity.
Provide attested academic degrees and experience letters, CV, health insurance, QID, company records, appointment decision and employment documents.
A valid work permit remains necessary for employment.

initial_validity.value: Up to ten years, renewable
initial_validity.notes: The current detailed program page states up to ten years for executives; the general 2026 launch announcement also describes the newly launched programs collectively as long-term and renewable.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is available subject to continued compliance and requires the initial application documentation again.
extension_rules.notes: Continued qualifying local employment is therefore material.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Provides premium long-term residence after employer nomination and approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Although the resulting permit is described as self-sponsored, the application itself is employer-led and requires an existing qualifying local job.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No special conversion is published; the ordinary permanent-residence framework normally requires 20 years of legal residence for a foreign-born person.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not cure the route's local-employer requirement.

path_to_citizenship.value: No executive fast track is published; ordinary discretionary naturalization generally requires 25 consecutive years plus the statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is not guaranteed.

rejected_routes.notes: This is plainly a local-employment route, not an independent foreign-contract remote-work route. A software engineer cannot qualify solely through a foreign employer or client.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold exists because this is visitor entry, not residence or work authorization.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No relevant income threshold was confirmed.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; visitor status only
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial or accommodation requirements may vary by nationality and visitor category, but they do not create work or residence rights.

income_proof_months.notes: No standardized income-proof period relevant to remote work was found.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through Hayya when a visitor visa is required, or satisfy the applicable visa-on-arrival conditions.
Maintain required visitor health insurance; the standard mandatory visitor policy costs QAR 50 per month when applicable.
Tourist status is for tourism, requires departure after the visit, and does not permit commercial activities.

initial_validity.value: Varies by nationality and visitor category
initial_validity.notes: This is visitor permission, not temporary residence.

extension_rules.value: Any extension is governed by the applicable visitor category and requires insurance; it does not legalize employment or self-employment.
extension_rules.notes: The Ministry of Interior visitor declaration continues to restrict the visit to tourism and prohibit commercial activity.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor entry does not itself become residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time is not presented as qualifying legal residence for permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: None.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor status is not a naturalization track.

rejected_routes.notes: Even if incidental online activity were practically possible, the official visitor declaration says the visitor comes for tourism only and will not undertake commercial activities. It is therefore not a lawful remote-work solution.

summary.value: No ordinary degree-based or independently applied skilled-worker residence route was found. Academic degrees support the Executive Residency application, but that stream requires existing Qatari residence, employer nomination and a qualifying local contract; special-competency permanent residence is exceptional and discretionary rather than an ordinary qualification route.
summary.notes: A software-engineering degree alone does not create eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: A natural person is resident if they have a permanent home in Qatar, spend more than 183 days in Qatar during any 12 months, or have vital interests in Qatar.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The tests are alternatives under the Income Tax Law.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Zero applies to salary, wages, allowances and similar employment remuneration of citizens and residents. It must not be generalized to independent business activity: taxable Qatar-source activity income is generally taxed at 10%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The reviewed Qatari social-insurance law applies to Qatari employees and optionally to qualifying self-employed Qataris, not an ordinary non-GCC foreign remote worker. GCC-national coordination rules can differ, so nationality-specific verification is required.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No lawful digital-nomad or foreign-freelancer route exists from which a recurring resident fixed payment can be calculated. Visitor health insurance is QAR 50 per month, approximately USD 13.74, when applicable, but this is a visitor cost rather than a remote-worker contribution.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, freelancer, non-dom or inbound-worker tax regime was found. Employment salaries are exempt, while Qatar-source taxable business activity is generally subject to 10%.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The salary exemption and business-income rules are part of the general system, not a nomad concession.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether payments are legally characterized as employment salary or independent business income and where services are performed. Working physically from Qatar may create Qatar-source activity income even where the payer is foreign. Because there is no qualifying remote-work immigration route, a prospective filer should obtain Qatar tax and immigration advice before relying on the salary exemption or undertaking business activity.

taxation_system.value: No personal tax on salaries and similar employment remuneration, but a generally flat 10% tax applies to taxable Qatar-source business income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, more than 183 days in any 12 months, or vital interests in Qatar.
taxation_system.income_scope: Primarily Qatar-source taxable income. Activity practiced in Qatar and contracts executed wholly or partly there can be Qatar-source; salary and similar employment remuneration are exempt.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: No ordinary Qatari pension contribution was identified for non-GCC foreign workers. The social-insurance law reviewed principally covers Qatari citizens; GCC coordination can apply separately.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The system is not progressive. The 10% dashboard screening rate concerns taxable business activity, while qualifying salaries and wages are exempt at 0%.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Salaries, wages, allowances and similar employment remuneration
tax_brackets.notes: Statutory exemption; classification as genuine employment remuneration matters.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable income after permitted deductions; no progressive threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Certain special sectors and withholding situations have different rules.

taxation_system.notes: The numeric 10% is a conservative screening rate for a hypothetical self-employed/activity-income case, not the expected tax on an exempt employee salary.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special nomad taxation exists. A hypothetical foreign employee's qualifying salary may be exempt, but independently earned income from services physically performed as a Qatar business activity may fall within the general 10% regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No qualifying route; hypothetical employment-versus-business classification
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% on qualifying salary/wages; generally 10% on taxable Qatar-source business activity
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, more than 183 days in any 12 months, or vital interests in Qatar.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The law is source-focused, but a foreign payer does not automatically make services foreign-source: activity practiced or contracts performed wholly or partly in Qatar can be Qatar-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No ordinary Qatari pension contribution confirmed for a non-GCC foreign remote worker. Qatari and some GCC citizens have separate social-insurance rules.

fixed_payments.status: No qualifying remote-work-route payment schedule exists.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No mandatory Qatari pension percentage confirmed for an ordinary non-GCC foreign worker.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Digital-nomad/residence fees not applicable. Mandatory visitor insurance is QAR 50 per month when required, but visitor status cannot be used as a remote-work residence route.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax, digital-nomad levy or resident remote-worker payment was found. Business registration and licensing costs would depend on a separate authorized business structure.
fixed_payments.notes: The visitor insurance amount must not be presented as the cost of legal remote-worker residence.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Spending fewer than 184 days does not necessarily prevent tax residence because a permanent home or vital interests can also establish residence. Immigration and source rules still apply regardless of tax residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no lawful ordinary remote-worker status. If remuneration is genuine salary, the general salary exemption may apply; if the activity is independent business performed in Qatar, the 10% regime may be relevant.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A separately licensed Qatar business or endorsed entrepreneur should register and file as required when carrying on taxable activity. Visitor entry cannot be converted into lawful self-employment merely by opening an account or registering informally.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is lower than for conventional employees because no official ruling specifically addresses a foreign-contract remote worker operating without a qualifying immigration status.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary remote-worker route grants temporary residence. Founder residence may be granted directly after endorsement, but it is rejected for this profile and no standard processing time is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: This is the ordinary minimum legal-residence period for a foreign-born applicant, not a guaranteed transition from a remote-work route. A person born in Qatar generally needs 10 years.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: This is only the arithmetic difference between the ordinary 20-year PR residence threshold and 25-year naturalization residence threshold. Permanent residence is not a mandatory or guaranteed stepping stone, and citizenship remains discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Minimum consecutive residence for ordinary naturalization consideration; it is not an entitlement and no qualifying remote-worker entry route was found.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official typical processing time was found. Decisions are discretionary, and the law permits no more than 50 grants annually under the ordinary naturalization provisions.

key_conditions.value: PR generally requires qualifying legal residence, sufficient income, good conduct and enough Arabic. Naturalization generally requires 25 consecutive years, lawful income, good reputation, no disqualifying conviction and Arabic knowledge; continuity rules limit absences, approval is discretionary, and dual nationality is generally prohibited without an Emiri decision.
key_conditions.notes: Neither the entrepreneur nor executive program publishes an accelerated citizenship track.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign woman married to a Qatari man may acquire nationality after maintaining the marriage for at least five years from the formal declaration/request, subject to the law and possible deferral. The rule is not gender-neutral.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A legally recognized existing marriage can support the special PR categories for either a non-Qatari husband of a Qatari woman or a non-Qatari wife of a Qatari man. For citizenship, the five-year spousal provision applies specifically to a foreign woman married to a Qatari man and requires an official written request/declaration; marriage alone does not automatically naturalize her.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The reviewed nationality law provides no parallel five-year citizenship route for a foreign husband of a Qatari woman.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must comply with Qatar's law regulating marriages to foreigners and be genuine and legally documented. Ministerial approval and statutory eligibility can be required; the nationality grant may be deferred for renewable one-year periods in the public interest. False statements or documents in nationality proceedings carry severe criminal penalties.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage should never be treated as guaranteed nationality. A sham marriage or false filing creates immigration, nationality and criminal risk.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Qatar alone does not confer citizenship on a child of known foreign parents. A child born in Qatar to unknown parents/foundling is treated as naturalized on humanitarian grounds.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Qatar to two known migrant parents does not acquire Qatari citizenship merely by birth in Qatar. The narrow foundling/unknown-parent rule is different.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parental permanent residence does not create a general jus-soli entitlement.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If the local citizen is the father, a child born in Qatar or abroad is treated as Qatari under the reviewed law. If the local citizen is the mother and the father is foreign, the child receives priority in discretionary naturalization and falls within a special permanent-residence category but is not automatically Qatari.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because the outcome depends on which parent is Qatari, the aggregate boolean is left null rather than implying a gender-neutral rule.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A non-Qatari spouse of a Qatari citizen and children of a Qatari mother are special categories under the Permanent Residency Law. A citizen child or Qatari-mother child may therefore improve family residence options, but does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Approval remains subject to the applicable authority and proof of the legal family relationship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father married to a Qatari woman is included in a special permanent-residence category, and their children are also specially recognized. Neither the child's birth nor the mother's citizenship automatically grants the father Qatari nationality or the five-year spousal-naturalization benefit available to a foreign wife of a Qatari man.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The benefit is principally a possible PR exemption, not automatic citizenship.

rank.notes: Current Passport Power Rank displayed on the Passport Index Qatar dashboard when checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strict visa-free category; its broader mobility score is 118.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified by Passport Index as requiring a visa in advance.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 40 visa-on-arrival destinations and 10 eTA destinations. Other eVisa categories are not included in this combined figure.

passport.notes: Passport indexes use different methodologies. As a cross-check, the July 2026 Henley ranking reported Qatar at rank 48 with access to 112 destinations, but Henley combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access and does not supply the requested full category breakdown on the cited report.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for daily life and international business: official government information says English is widely spoken as a second language. Arabic remains the sole official language and is required for the ordinary PR and naturalization frameworks.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English practicality does not create remote-work immigration permission.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No reliable official evidence was found that Russian or Ukrainian is widely usable for government procedures or general daily life. Applicants should expect to rely on English for ordinary expatriate life and Arabic or translation for official/legal matters.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This cautious conclusion follows the official identification of Arabic and widely spoken English; no directly relevant official Russian/Ukrainian-language prevalence data was located during the focused search.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: QAR 12,416 converted at the official peg of QAR 3.64 per USD; fourth-quarter 2024 average for all paid employees aged 15 and above.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Qatar National Planning Council sources reviewed publish arithmetic mean wages overall and by gender, occupation, economic activity, sector, or nationality/industry compensation; none publishes a national median of individual monthly wages, so no defensible USD median can be converted.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the statutory QAR 1,000 monthly basic minimum wage; this is not an observed minimum salary. Employers must additionally provide or fund prescribed food and accommodation amounts.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official QAR 12,416 mean for paid employees, including citizens and non-citizen residents.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official wage datasets report arithmetic means, not a national individual-worker median; the numeric value remains null rather than treating a subgroup mean or dataset-chart aggregation as a salary median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official sources publish average wages for population subgroups, not the highest salary received by an individual or a statutory national salary ceiling; the numeric value therefore remains null.

min_salary_local_currency.value: QAR 1,000/month basic statutory minimum, plus QAR 500 accommodation and QAR 300 food unless provided in kind
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory private-sector and domestic-worker floor, not an observed wage-distribution minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly wage of paid employees aged 15 and above in Q4 2024.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Qatar’s current official wage publications do not publish a national median of individual monthly salaries; they publish arithmetic means overall and by gender, occupation, economic activity, sector, or nationality/industry compensation.
median_salary_local_currency.notes: No QAR median can be stated without underlying worker-level wage-distribution data. Chart controls labelled median on the data portal would aggregate the displayed subgroup-average records and are not a median worker salary.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Qatar’s current official wage publications do not define or publish a national maximum individual monthly salary or upper salary ceiling; the largest occupation, sector, or industry mean is only a subgroup average and is not a worker-level maximum.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: A national maximum is conceptually open-ended absent a statutory ceiling and cannot be inferred from subgroup averages, so no QAR amount is supplied.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly wage of all paid employees aged 15 and above; minimum field is the statutory basic minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Q4 2024 average; statutory minimum currently verified through the reviewed official source
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are labor-market figures for paid citizen and resident workers, not an immigration income threshold and not citizen-only earnings. Qatar’s official peg makes the USD conversion approximately QAR 3.64 per USD. A focused review of five additional official Qatar open-data wage/compensation datasets confirmed that they publish means or aggregate compensation, not a national individual-worker median or maximum.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No sufficiently robust current official national household cost-of-living amount suitable for a single-person remote-worker budget was established. The residency program advertises merchant discounts and the visitor-insurance source establishes a QAR 50 visitor premium, but neither supports a general monthly cost-of-living estimate.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Hayya and visa-on-arrival permissions are visitor statuses, not remote-work residence or settlement routes. The entrepreneur and executive permits are purpose-specific alternatives that require a founder venture or qualifying local employment.
settlement_track.summary: No current route admits an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker into a qualifying residence track. Even the rejected entrepreneur/executive alternatives have no special settlement conversion and sit within Qatar's exceptional 20-year PR and 25-year discretionary-naturalization framework.
settlement_track.notes: The years-to-citizenship field is null for this route because no qualifying remote-worker route exists; 25 years is the general naturalization minimum, not a timeline available from the selected profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker or ordinary foreign-client freelancer status was found. Entrepreneur residence requires a locally endorsed venture, Executive Residence requires qualifying local employment and employer nomination, and visitor status prohibits commercial activity.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit retained the prior negative selection result and rechecked the broader record against current official immigration, legal, tax, visitor, language, labor, wage and passport sources. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including five distinct official Qatar open-data wage/compensation datasets absent from the previous source set. Those additional datasets publish arithmetic means or aggregate compensation, not a national individual-worker median or maximum; the two flagged local-currency fields now explain that precise publication limitation without inventing values. Other remaining nulls are explained where no official processing time, lawful remote-worker fee schedule, or applicable statistic exists.

data.selection_summary: Romania remains a valid but documentation-heavy option for an ordinary remote employee of a foreign company. The D/AS digital-nomad route grants renewable temporary residence without a Romanian employer and requires monthly income of at least three times the Romanian average gross salary—RON 27,576 using the statutory 2026 figure—for the preceding six months and the requested period. Official long-term-residence rules count continuous lawful temporary residence except for specifically excluded categories; digital nomads are not listed among those exclusions. Long-term residence is therefore available after five years if continuity and the other conditions are met, and citizenship can be requested after eight years of lawful residence while holding long-term residence. A direct freelance service contract with a foreign client is not expressly covered unless it is an employment contract or the applicant owns and remotely manages the foreign company.

visa_application.title: Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs E-VIZA portal
visa_application.notes: The visa file is initiated through the official E‑VIZA portal and associated with a Romanian diplomatic mission or consular post. The D/AS long-stay visa fee is EUR 300 for applications submitted for validation from 27 April 2026; personal attendance and additional documents may still be required.

best_routes.route_name: D/AS Digital Nomad long-stay visa and temporary residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official rule is denominated by a Romanian salary formula. A reliable filing-date RON/USD conversion was not published by the cited authorities, so no potentially misleading USD threshold is supplied.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: RON 27,576 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Three times the 2026 statutory average gross salary of RON 9,192. The applicable average-salary base should be reconfirmed immediately before filing.

income_requirement_display.value: RON 27,576/month for each of the preceding 6 months and throughout the requested visa period
income_requirement_display.notes: The formula, rather than a permanently fixed threshold, is controlling. The 2026 budget law sets the relevant average gross salary at RON 9,192.

income_proof_months.notes: The threshold must be met in each of the six months preceding the visa application and for the entire period covered by the visa.

key_requirements.requirement: An employment contract with a company registered outside Romania for remote ICT-enabled work, or ownership and remote management of a foreign company owned for at least three years.
Original employment/company documents and authenticated Romanian translations, including current company identification, activity and representative information.
Apostilled or legalised tax-compliance and fiscal-residence documentation showing taxes and compulsory contributions are current and no tax-evasion or fraud record.
Accommodation, criminal-record certificate, travel arrangements, and medical insurance covering at least EUR 30,000 for the requested visa period.
For the residence permit: Romanian accommodation, health coverage, medical certificate, passport and continued income at three times the average gross salary.

initial_validity.value: A 90-day D/AS entry visa, followed by an initial six-month temporary residence permit
initial_validity.notes: The visa enables entry and the residence-permit application; it is the residence permit that documents the continuing right to reside.

extension_rules.value: The first digital-nomad residence extension is six months. Subsequent extensions are expressly available, with continued qualifying foreign employment/company status, income of at least three times the average gross salary, a competent tax-authority income certificate, accommodation, health insurance and medical documentation. Other-purpose temporary residence is generally extended successively for periods of up to one year.
extension_rules.notes: The prior record's conclusion that only one extension was available was incorrect. The current IGI guidance expressly lists documents for subsequent digital-nomad extensions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply independently for the D/AS visa, enter Romania, and apply to IGI for the digital-nomad temporary residence permit before the visa stay expires.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Residence-permit documents may be uploaded through the IGI portal, but personal submission may be required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply for Romanian long-term residence after five years of continuous lawful residence. Absences must be under six consecutive months and no more than ten months in total during the five-year period. Digital-nomad residence is not among the temporary statuses excluded by the official rule.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This conclusion follows the official general rule and its express exclusions; the IGI page does not separately name digital nomads as an included category. Written IGI confirmation remains prudent before committing to a five-year plan.

path_to_citizenship.value: After obtaining long-term residence, ordinary naturalization is available once total lawful residence reaches eight years, subject to presence, lawful means, good conduct, loyalty, Romanian language, culture, Constitution and anthem requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is discretionary rather than automatic. A year in which the applicant spends more than six months outside Romania does not count toward the citizenship residence period.

best_routes.notes: This route fully fits a remote employee of a foreign company and an owner of a qualifying foreign company. A standalone contractor/freelancer agreement with a foreign client is not expressly listed and should not be treated as eligible without consular confirmation or restructuring into a covered relationship. The high income threshold and extensive legalisation/translation requirements are significant practical barriers.

rejected_routes.route_name: D/AP long-stay visa for professional activities

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No USD threshold is supplied because the route does not fit ordinary software-engineering remote work.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least the Romanian average monthly gross salary during the requested residence extension
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The IGI page states a formula rather than a permanently fixed amount.

income_requirement_display.value: At least the Romanian average monthly gross salary for the requested extension period
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least 1 × average monthly gross salary
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not the digital-nomad threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page requires means for the requested extension period but does not express the proof as a fixed number of historical months.

key_requirements.requirement: The activity must be a liberal profession regulated by special legislation, with proof that the applicant lawfully practised a similar profession in the country of origin.
Insurance, criminal record, accommodation, health coverage and proof of effective exercise of the regulated profession are required.

initial_validity.value: 90-day long-stay visa followed by a temporary residence permit

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires continued lawful exercise of the regulated professional activity and means of support at the average-gross-salary level.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence is possible for a person admitted to practise an eligible regulated liberal profession.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General five-year long-term-residence rules may apply to qualifying professional-activity residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not relevant to the applicant because a software-engineering degree alone does not establish admission to a specially regulated liberal profession.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization rules could apply after qualifying residence, but this is not an ordinary remote software-engineer route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route is for specially regulated liberal professions and requires legal authorisation to practise that profession. A software-engineering degree or foreign software-client contract alone does not satisfy this route.

rejected_routes.route_name: D/AM employment and EU Blue Card routes

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Not material because a Romanian employment relationship or qualifying assignment is required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Salary rules vary by employment category.

income_requirement_display.value: Category-specific Romanian employment salary rules; no single screening threshold used
income_requirement_display.notes: The route is rejected for requiring Romanian employment, sponsorship or a qualifying posting.

income_proof_months.notes: Not a historical foreign-income route.

key_requirements.requirement: A Romanian individual employment contract, employment notice/work authorisation, or a qualifying intra-company/posting relationship is generally required.

initial_validity.value: Long-stay employment visa followed by a single permit or EU Blue Card

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on the continuing Romanian employment or qualifying posting relationship.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Temporary residence follows qualifying Romanian employment or posting.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Long-term residence may later be available under general rules.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may eventually apply after qualifying residence and long-term residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the selection expressly excludes routes requiring a local employer, job offer, work authorisation, sponsorship or host-country assignment.

summary.value: Romania does not provide a general independent residence route merely for holding a relevant software-engineering degree. D/AP is limited to professions regulated by special legislation, while standard skilled employment and the EU Blue Card require a Romanian employment relationship. Study residence exists but is education attendance, not degree-based migration for an existing graduate.
summary.notes: The applicant's degree may support employability or professional evidence, but it does not independently create residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: Romanian tax residence may arise through Romanian domicile, a Romanian centre of vital interests, or presence exceeding 183 days in any consecutive 12-month period ending in the relevant calendar year. A person crossing the presence threshold generally becomes taxable as a resident from the first day of arrival, subject to an applicable double-tax treaty and the ANAF residence determination process.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 183-day test is not the only residence test; centre of vital interests and treaty tie-breakers can change the outcome.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: General flat personal-income-tax screening rate, not an effective all-in rate. Qualifying digital-nomad foreign salary/activity income is exempt while the statutory no-more-than-183-days condition is met.

social_contributions_percent.notes: General employee-side combined screening rate: 25% social insurance plus 10% health insurance. Qualifying digital nomads staying no more than 183 days in the statutory rolling period are exempt from the specified Romanian contributions. Treaty, EU coordination, foreign-employer payroll and income classification can alter liability.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax or social-security payment applies to every digital nomad. Resident employee and independent-activity liabilities depend on classification, earnings, treaty/social-security coverage and annual contribution bases.

special_tax_regimes.value: Law 69/2023 exempts qualifying statutory digital nomads from Romanian PIT on covered foreign employment/company income and from the specified social contributions while Romanian presence does not exceed 183 days in any consecutive 12-month period ending in the relevant calendar year.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is a limited-presence exemption, not a multi-year tax holiday. A settlement strategy normally requires enough physical presence to lose the exemption.

taxes.caveats: Long-term settlement and the short-stay nomad tax exemption pull in opposite directions. Once presence exceeds the exemption limit or the centre of vital interests moves to Romania, worldwide-income taxation, Romanian reporting and possibly payroll or social-security obligations become relevant. The exact treatment differs between a foreign employee, owner-director and independent contractor and must be checked under the applicable double-tax and social-security agreements.

taxation_system.value: Romania generally applies a flat 10% PIT to taxable personal income. Tax residents are generally taxable on worldwide income, subject to treaties and specific exemptions. Employee social contributions are generally 25% pension plus 10% health; independent activities use statutory annual bases and thresholds.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile, centre of vital interests, or more than 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period; treaty rules may override domestic residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Romanian-source income for non-residents until residence begins; generally worldwide income for residents, subject to treaties and exemptions.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Covered digital-nomad income and specified contributions are exempt when presence does not exceed 183 days under Law 69/2023.
taxation_system.social_security: General employee rates are 25% social insurance and 10% health insurance. Independent-activity contribution bases and caps differ. The digital-nomad exemption applies only within the statutory presence limit.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: PIT is generally flat, not progressive. Contribution thresholds and bases can nevertheless make the all-in effective burden non-linear.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No general PIT income bracket; flat rate
tax_brackets.applies_to: General taxable personal income, subject to category-specific exceptions
tax_brackets.notes: This is the general statutory rate, not an expected effective tax calculation.

taxation_system.notes: PwC pages were reviewed 30 March 2026 and are used as current professional summaries alongside Romanian legislation and ANAF guidance.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Covered foreign digital-nomad income is exempt from Romanian PIT and specified social contributions while Romanian presence remains at or below 183 days in the statutory rolling period. A nomad who settles for multiple years should budget for the general Romanian regime after the exemption ceases or tax residence otherwise arises.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Foreign remote employee or owner-worker of a foreign company under the statutory digital-nomad definition
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% on covered nomad income while the ≤183-day exemption applies; otherwise 10% general PIT screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domestic residence can arise through domicile, centre of vital interests or more than 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period, subject to treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Covered foreign digital-nomad income is exempt within the presence limit; Romanian residents are otherwise generally taxable on worldwide income, subject to treaties and category-specific rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Law 69/2023 targeted PIT, pension and health-contribution exemption for qualifying digital nomads who do not exceed 183 days in the specified rolling period.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Within the exemption window, the specified Romanian CAS/CASS liabilities are excluded. Outside it, general employee rates are 25% pension and 10% health, but foreign-employer payroll, treaty and social-security coordination must be reviewed.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed payment established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Potentially none during the qualifying exemption period; otherwise income- and classification-dependent.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: D long-stay visa fee: EUR 300 from 27 April 2026. Residence-card and renewal charges were referenced by IGI but a single current all-in amount could not be confirmed from the inspected pages.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No universal freelancer levy established. Standard VAT is 21%; registration and liability depend on taxable activity and structure.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health insurance and document translation/legalisation are practical costs but not fixed taxes.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A qualifying statutory digital nomad at or below 183 days can use the specific PIT/CAS/CASS exemption for covered foreign income, subject to treaty and factual-residence checks.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect Romanian reporting and a 10% PIT screening rate on taxable income, with potentially substantial social contributions. A foreign employer may create Romanian payroll/compliance questions.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A direct foreign-client freelancer is not clearly covered by the immigration route. If locally registered or treated as independent, 10% PIT and separate pension/health contribution bases may apply; specialist advice is required.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The exemption is legally clear for the covered profile, but post-183-day treatment is structure-specific and should not be reduced to a single effective percentage.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is obtained after entry on the D/AS visa; there is no multi-year qualifying wait.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Romania calls this long-term residence. It requires five years of continuous lawful stay, with absences under six consecutive months and no more than ten months total.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the five-year long-term-residence point and the ordinary eight-year total lawful-residence requirement. Citizenship requires holding long-term residence when applying.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary statutory baseline, assuming every year counts and the applicant holds long-term residence at filing.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: This is the statutory period for the Citizenship Commission's report, not a guaranteed typical outcome. It may be extended by up to six months for document-authenticity or factual checks, followed by decision, communication and oath steps.

key_conditions.value: Keep the digital-nomad permit continuously valid; meet the high income threshold at every renewal; limit five-year absences to under six consecutive months and ten months total; obtain long-term residence; and for citizenship maintain lawful means, good conduct and loyalty and pass Romanian language, culture, Constitution and anthem requirements. A year with more than six months outside Romania does not count for naturalization.
key_conditions.notes: Tax compliance and genuine Romanian residence are central to a credible settlement file.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The ordinary naturalization residence period is reduced to five years where the applicant is married to and cohabiting with a Romanian citizen. Long-term or permanent residence must still be held at application.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage matters only if the spouse is Romanian and the couple genuinely cohabits. Marriage itself neither changes the foreign spouse's nationality nor eliminates the lawful Romanian residence and long-term-residence requirements.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to another foreign national provides no citizenship reduction.

requirements_and_risks.value: The relationship must be genuine and continuing. Language, culture, Constitution, anthem, lawful-means, loyalty and good-conduct requirements remain. IGI can refuse family residence where the marital/family relationship is not effective or parentage was acknowledged solely to obtain residence.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sham marriage or artificial recognition of parentage creates refusal and potentially broader legal risks.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Romania alone does not confer citizenship. A narrow foundling presumption applies where neither parent is known.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Romania to two foreign parents is not Romanian merely because of birthplace. A resident minor may be included in the parents' later Article 8 naturalization process under the statutory consent and domicile rules.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The special foundling rule is not a general jus-soli rule.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Romanian from birth if either parent is a Romanian citizen, whether the child is born in Romania or abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a minor Romanian citizen may obtain or renew family-member residence by proving that the child is in the parent's care or that a maintenance obligation is regularly fulfilled. The child does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must independently satisfy the residence documentation and later citizenship requirements.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Romanian minor can use the Romanian-child family residence category if he proves care or regularly fulfilled maintenance obligations. There is no automatic permanent residence or citizenship for the father.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Authorities may refuse residence if parentage was acknowledged solely to obtain immigration status.

rank.notes: Passport Index Power Rank as observed on 15 August 2026; this is not a Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strict visa-free category. Its broader mobility score is 171.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category as observed on the research date.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard figure: 42 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 9 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately lists eVisa and other electronic-permission categories, so this is not the full mobility score.

passport.notes: Passport-index methodologies differ. The earlier record's Henley-style 178 accessibility score should not be compared directly with Passport Index's strict 120 visa-free count or its separate VOA/eTA breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Good in major cities and technology/business settings. EF's 2025 index ranks Romania 11th globally with a score of 605, but the self-selected test methodology is only a practical indicator. Romanian remains necessary for government dealings and is required for naturalization.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The digital-nomad permit is temporary and must be renewed; citizenship cannot be requested while relying only on temporary nomad status because long-term residence must be obtained first.
settlement_track.summary: The renewable digital-nomad permit can plausibly and credibly build the five continuous lawful years required for long-term residence because digital nomads are not among the official exclusions. The applicant must then obtain long-term residence and can seek citizenship at the eight-year total-residence point, subject to strict presence, language, livelihood and conduct requirements.
settlement_track.notes: The counting conclusion is based on the official general long-term-residence rule and its express exclusions rather than an IGI statement naming digital nomads individually. Written confirmation from IGI is advisable before relying on this interpretation for a multi-year plan.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True for an employee with a genuine employment contract at a foreign company and for an owner who has held and remotely manages a foreign company for at least three years. A direct independent-contractor or freelance service agreement with a foreign client is not expressly covered and requires manual confirmation or a qualifying structure.

data.notes: The active route, repeated renewals, five-year long-term-residence rule and eight-year naturalization rule are all supported by current official sources. Remaining cautions concern the absence of an official sentence specifically naming digital-nomad time as countable, the exclusion of ordinary client-only freelance contracts from the route's express wording, and structure-specific tax treatment after 183 days.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Renewed digital-nomad temporary residence followed by long-term residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Digital-nomad temporary residence can be renewed and used toward the general five-year continuous-residence requirement for Romanian long-term residence.
requirements: Maintain the qualifying foreign remote activity, income and temporary-residence renewals.
Satisfy the five-year continuity and absence limits, means of support, accommodation, health insurance and other long-term-residence conditions.
reviewed_route_names: D/AS Digital Nomad long-stay visa and temporary residence permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: IGI’s Romanian other-purposes page specifically covers nomad permits and renewals. Its long-term-residence guidance lists excluded statuses without including nomads; counting is the resulting statutory/general-rule inference, not an individual advance approval. The first nomad residence grant is six months; it should not be confused with a permanent status.

data.selection_summary: Russia has no current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance or self-sponsored foreign-income residence category fitting this profile. The eVisa is a short-visit visa; tax or self-employment registration creates no immigration status; and IT residence requires a contract with an accredited Russian IT organization.

A qualifying Russian higher-education diploma with honors can support direct VNZh and simplified citizenship treatment.

extension_rules.notes: The existing foreign degree does not satisfy the Russian-study condition.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This requires new Russian education.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Conditions vary by education and Russian-employment history.
