summary.value: Qualifying full-time study at a state-accredited Russian institution can support an education-purpose RVP and later VNZh. A qualifying Russian honors degree can support direct VNZh, but an existing foreign degree does not qualify.
summary.notes: Available without a local employer only by undertaking qualifying Russian education; it is not a foreign-contract remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: Generally at least 183 calendar days of physical presence in Russia during the relevant 12-consecutive-month determination period; treaty rules can alter the result.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence must be checked for the applicable tax period and treaty position.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate on the principal progressive resident-income scale, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single worker-paid percentage applies across foreign employment, civil contracts, entrepreneurship and NPD. NPD has no mandatory insurance contribution; other structures require separate analysis.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No valid nomad-route payment exists. Patent advance payments vary by region.

special_tax_regimes.value: Professional income tax (NPD) taxes qualifying receipts from individuals at 4% and from organizations or individual entrepreneurs at 6%, subject to a RUB 2.4 million annual limit and no mandatory insurance contributions. Eligibility is limited to Russian, EAEU and Ukrainian citizens; registration creates no immigration status.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Cross-border income characterization requires individual verification.

taxes.caveats: Russia has no digital-nomad tax category. Treatment depends on presence, income source, nationality, residence status, contract form, NPD eligibility and any treaty. Tax registration does not authorize immigration residence or work.

taxation_system.value: Residents are generally taxed on Russian and foreign-source income under a progressive principal PIT scale; nonresidents are generally taxed on Russian-source income under separate rules.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally at least 183 days in the relevant 12-consecutive-month period, subject to treaty analysis.
taxation_system.income_scope: Tax residents generally report worldwide income; nonresidents generally owe PIT on Russian-source income. Remote-service sourcing requires contract-specific advice.
taxation_system.special_regimes: NPD may be available to Russian, EAEU and Ukrainian citizens at 4%/6%, subject to a RUB 2.4 million annual ceiling; it provides no immigration status.
taxation_system.social_security: No nomad-specific system exists. NPD has no mandatory insurance contribution; employment and other business forms have separate contribution rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value is the 22% top marginal screening rate. Each higher rate applies only to the income slice above its threshold.

tax_brackets.notes: First marginal band.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over RUB 2,400,000 through RUB 5,000,000 per year
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal slice.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over RUB 5,000,000 through RUB 20,000,000 per year
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal slice.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over RUB 20,000,000 through RUB 50,000,000 per year
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal slice.
Top marginal screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: The brackets are current for 2026. NPD and payroll information is contextual because no valid remote-worker immigration route exists.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable: Russia has no confirmed digital-nomad or dedicated foreign-remote-worker residence route.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; general PIT or an independently eligible business regime would apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 13%–22% progressive resident PIT; 22% is the top marginal screening rate. Eligible NPD users may instead pay 4%/6%.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally at least 183 days in the relevant 12-consecutive-month period, subject to treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Tax residents generally report foreign-source income; nonresidents generally pay on Russian-source income, subject to contract-specific sourcing analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None. NPD is a general small self-employment tax regime, not a nomad or inbound regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific contribution rule exists. NPD has no mandatory insurance contribution; other structures differ.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment; other payments depend on the independently chosen legal structure.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: NPD has no mandatory insurance contribution; no single amount applies across foreign employment and entrepreneurship.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The eVisa has a non-refundable processing fee, but no stable amount was exposed in the reviewed page; other state fees are route-specific.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Work-patent advance PIT is regionally adjusted. General VAT or business-tax rules do not create immigration eligibility.
fixed_payments.notes: No universal digital-nomad fixed payment exists.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short-term visitor may remain nonresident, but Russian-source income can still be taxable and the eVisa does not authorize remote-work residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If independently lawfully resident and tax resident, foreign-source contract income is generally within Russian PIT and may reach the 22% top marginal band.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Eligible Russian, EAEU and Ukrainian citizens may use NPD at 4%/6% up to RUB 2.4 million annually. Registration alone does not legalize stay.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence that no nomad-specific tax regime exists; individual cross-border sourcing remains advice-dependent.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying remote-worker route exists, so no profile-specific time to RVP can be stated.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General rule: VNZh may be issued after at least one year living on RVP. Separate exceptions can bypass RVP.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires five years of permanent residence measured from the VNZh decision.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total applies to this profile because no qualifying initial residence ground exists. A separately qualifying applicant generally faces about one year to VNZh plus five years of VNZh residence, excluding processing.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The statutory domestic decision period is up to three months and may be extended by another three; consular applications can take up to six months.

key_conditions.value: Separate qualifying residence ground, VNZh, ordinary five-year residence period, Russian-language ability, knowledge of Russian history and law, constitutional compliance, oath and absence of refusal grounds.
key_conditions.notes: Simplified categories can waive some requirements, but none is an ordinary remote-worker category.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A no-quota marriage-based RVP generally requires at least three years of marriage to a qualifying Russian citizen unless the couple has a common child. Simplified citizenship also requires permanent residence and a common child.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support a no-quota RVP after three years, or sooner where the couple has a common child. Marriage alone does not establish the cited simplified citizenship category.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The Russian spouse must satisfy the statutory Russian-residence condition.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be genuine and documented. Residence, family-life evidence and refusal checks still apply; sham arrangements or false evidence can cause refusal or cancellation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A Russian-citizen child does not automatically make the foreign father a citizen.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship primarily follows a Russian parent. Birth in Russia alone is insufficient except under specified parent and anti-statelessness conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Russia-born child of two foreign or stateless parents permanently residing in Russia acquires citizenship only if the child acquires no other citizenship at birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary case; an anti-statelessness exception exists.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is Russian and the other foreign, citizenship follows automatically for a child born in Russia; for a foreign birth, it follows where no other citizenship is acquired at birth. If the other parent is stateless, it follows regardless of birthplace.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Birthplace and other-nationality conditions matter.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Russian-citizen child can support direct VNZh or simplified citizenship for a parent in defined circumstances, but the parent must apply and meet residence, family-life and documentary conditions.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic parental citizenship follows.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father may qualify for direct VNZh or simplified citizenship where the specific Russian-citizen-child, cohabitation, maintenance, residence and family-configuration conditions are satisfied.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage alone is not always sufficient.

rank.notes: The reviewed official Henley 2026 analysis lists the Russian Federation at rank 47.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's mobility score includes qualifying visa-on-arrival and eTA access; it is not a pure visa-free-only total.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The reviewed Henley source did not expose a stable separate visa-in-advance count, so no residual total is inferred.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Henley aggregates these modes into the mobility score and did not expose a separate current Russia total.

passport.notes: Mode-specific destination totals remain null rather than being guessed.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English may be usable in some international technology teams, but the reviewed official sources do not establish broad English-language administrative practicality. Russian assistance should be expected.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide English-proficiency measure was captured.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is the federal state language and the practical language for immigration, tax administration and ordinary naturalization. Ukrainian is not a federal official language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Republics may establish additional state languages locally.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q1 2026 organizational-employee average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The underlying figure is RUB 73,871 for April 2025. USD 943 is an approximate conversion using RUB 78.3159 per USD on 21 July 2026. The biennial wage survey covers organizations excluding small businesses.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official Q1 2026 average nominal accrued wage of employees of organizations.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite nationwide maximum is published; the April 2025 survey top class is RUB 1,000,000 or more
max_salary_local_currency.notes: RUB 1,000,000 is the lower boundary of an open-ended class, not a maximum. Rosstat publishes distributions and highest-decile averages rather than a national individual maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross nominal accrued monthly wage of employees of organizations; minimum field is the separate federal statutory minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 average; April 2025 median; 2026 statutory minimum
average_citizen_salary.notes: RUB 106,979 is a Q1 2026 organizational-employee average, RUB 73,871 is the April 2025 biennial-survey median, and RUB 27,093 is the statutory minimum. These are labor-market measures, not immigration income thresholds. No finite national maximum is published.

cost_of_living_note.value: Rosstat's latest reviewed national household-budget compendium reports average consumer spending of RUB 25,987.5 per household member per month for 2023. This is an observed national expenditure benchmark, not a minimum budget or an expatriate cost estimate. Rosstat also reported that the June 2026 consumer-price index was 104.19% relative to December 2025; current spending needs therefore cannot be inferred by treating the 2023 amount as a 2026 minimum, and housing and other costs vary substantially by region and household type.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The focused pass found authoritative Rosstat expenditure, consumer-price and living-standard datasets, but no single official 2026 nationwide 'cost of living' amount for a remote-working adult. The stated RUB 25,987.5 figure is the latest directly captured national per-member household-consumption amount, while the CPI supplies current price context rather than a household budget.

data.selection_summary: Rwanda has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. The closest independent permits are Class K assured-income residence, which requires a retirement certificate and prohibits intended employment in Rwanda, and entrepreneur/self-employed permits requiring a registered, genuine Rwandan business or prescribed profession. Visitor visas do not authorize work. These routes therefore do not fit an ordinary software engineer continuing a foreign contract.

visa_application.notes: Irembo is the official application portal for temporary and permanent permits. Applicants normally apply after arriving in Rwanda. No fitting remote-worker permit exists, so the portal should not be interpreted as a digital-nomad application channel.

income_requirement_display.notes: The page describes assured income but expressly requires a retirement certificate, a statement from a Rwandan bank and local medical insurance.

income_proof_months.notes: Six preceding months of Rwandan bank statements are expressly required for renewal; the new-application page does not specify a statement period.

Bank statement from a bank in Rwanda
Local Rwandan medical insurance
Detailed CV, application letter and original police clearance
Applicant must not intend to be employed in Rwanda

extension_rules.notes: No maximum number of renewals is published on the route page.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Class K permit is a temporary residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Rwandan law allows discretionary Class L-1 permanent residence after an aggregate 10 years of legal residence, but the reviewed sources do not expressly confirm how Class K time is assessed in practice.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The rule says the permit may be issued, so eligibility is not automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary nationality by residence requires at least 15 consecutive years of residence and physical presence plus substantive naturalization conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make Class K suitable for a non-retired remote worker.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the published checklist requires retirement evidence. A foreign employment or client contract is not identified as an acceptable substitute, and working outside the authorized purpose risks permit cancellation.

income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of an income threshold does not turn these permits into remote-worker permits.

income_proof_months.notes: DGIE does not state a bank-income lookback period for these permits.

Original police clearance covering the previous country of residence

extension_rules.value: Renewal generally requires a trade licence/patente and application letter. Recurring entrepreneur categories, after holding a similar temporary permit at least twice, may receive up to 5 years and require RRA tax clearance.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: These are temporary residence permits tied to the authorized Rwandan business or profession.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Class L-1 permanent residence may be issued after an aggregate 10 years of legal residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The transition is discretionary and continued genuine business and compliance would be material.

path_to_citizenship.value: A genuine entrepreneur may eventually use the ordinary 15-consecutive-year residence ground, but nationality is discretionary and requires physical residence, integration and other conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for the specified profile because these permits authorize a local registered business or prescribed professional activity, not ordinary employment or freelancing solely for a foreign client. Online, free business registration does not itself legalize residence or prove that a paper-only company is sufficient.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from visitor status itself.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time is not established as qualifying residence for nationality.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general salary threshold is published.

Employer recommendation or sponsorship

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires continued employment documentation and employer recommendation.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved employment permit provides temporary residence tied to employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General Class L-1 permanent residence may be issued after an aggregate 10 years of legal residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not remove the employer requirement for the initial route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary residence-based nationality requires at least 15 consecutive years of lawful physical residence and other conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant must have a qualifying employer, employment contract and employer recommendation or sponsorship.

summary.value: The U1 student permit can be obtained with admission/recommendation from a recognized Rwandan school and sponsorship rather than a local employer. It is valid for one year and renewable with continued admission. It is an education route, not a degree-based independent skilled-migration route; post-study P2 work authorization requires an employment contract and employer recommendation.
summary.notes: No official source reviewed confirms a special student-to-permanent-residence transition. General permanent residence may be discretionary after 10 aggregate years of legal residence, but whether all student time is accepted should be confirmed with DGIE.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual who stays in Rwanda for more than 183 days in any 12-month period, continuously or intermittently, is resident for the tax period in which that 12-month period ends. Residents are generally liable on Rwandan and foreign-source income; nonresidents are liable on Rwandan-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Other statutory residence tests may also apply. Treaty residence and foreign tax credits require individual analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal personal/employment-income screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: In 2026 the mandatory pension contribution is 12% of covered remuneration, split equally between employer and employee. It is scheduled to rise to 14% from 1 January 2027. This value does not include medical-scheme contributions and should not be assumed to apply identically to an independent foreign contractor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer or remote-worker payment was established. Class K requires local insurance but publishes no premium; permit fees are periodic, not monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, non-dom or remittance-basis regime was found. Resident taxpayers are generally taxed on domestic and foreign-source income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business taxpayers may have turnover, corporate, simplified or other classifications depending on legal form and revenue; those are not a special remote-worker regime.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the foreign relationship is employment or independent business, source rules, days and permanent-home facts, the payer’s presence, treaty relief and whether a Rwandan business is registered. The 30% figure is a top marginal rate. RSSB medical coverage publishes a 15% contribution split 7.5%/7.5% for covered employment, while the pension rate is separately 12% in 2026; applicability to a particular foreign contractor requires RRA/RSSB advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax with resident worldwide-income taxation and a top monthly marginal rate of 30%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any 12-month period is one statutory individual-residence test.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: domestic and foreign-source income; nonresidents: Rwandan-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or remittance-basis regime confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: Mandatory pension is 12% of covered remuneration in 2026, generally split 6% employee and 6% employer. The RSSB medical scheme states 15% of basic salary, split 7.5%/7.5%, for persons covered by that scheme. Independent-contractor applicability is not established.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Monthly bands are marginal: 0% through RWF 60,000; 10% from RWF 60,001–100,000; 20% from RWF 100,001–200,000; and 30% above RWF 200,000.

tax_brackets.notes: USD approximation uses roughly RWF 1,469 per USD; exchange rates fluctuate.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of monthly taxable employment income in this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of monthly taxable employment income in this band
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Portion of monthly taxable employment income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not the effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The 2025 RRA handbook confirms that the published brackets are marginal. VAT registration is generally mandatory above RWF 20 million in the preceding fiscal year or RWF 5 million in the preceding quarter, subject to exemptions and current filing rules.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a dedicated route: Rwanda has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker permit. A person who becomes Rwandan tax resident may nevertheless be taxable on foreign-source employment or business income under ordinary rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary resident employment or business taxation would apply according to facts.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–30% progressive; 30% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in any 12-month period is a tax-residence trigger.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Generally taxable for a resident taxpayer; treaty relief and foreign tax credits require case-specific analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No remote-worker-specific exemption or fixed contribution was found. Covered salaried work attracts pension contributions; medical and payroll obligations depend on coverage and structure.

fixed_payments.status: No universal remote-worker fixed payment established.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Pension is percentage-based for covered workers, not a published fixed minimum. RSSB coverage for a foreign contractor needs confirmation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Rejected Class K and entrepreneur permits publish a RWF 150,000 application fee, generally for permits valid up to two years.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: RDB business registration is free. VAT registration generally becomes mandatory above RWF 20 million annually or RWF 5 million quarterly. No remote-worker municipal levy was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Local medical insurance is mandatory for Class K, but no standard premium is published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 183 days does not by itself guarantee no Rwandan tax: Rwandan-source income and other residence/source tests must still be considered.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident working from Rwanda for a foreign payer should expect ordinary worldwide-income rules and progressive tax up to 30%, subject to treaty and credit analysis.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered business must assess business-income reporting, VAT thresholds and possible RSSB obligations; registration does not itself create immigration eligibility.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening summary, not a determination that remote work is authorized under immigration law.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No fitting ordinary remote-worker temporary residence route exists. Qualifying entrepreneur, retirement, study or employment applicants can apply directly for their respective temporary permits.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Class L-1 permanent residence may be issued after an aggregate 10 years of legal residence. This is a total-residence rule, not a guaranteed transition exactly 10 years after a particular permit.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: This is the arithmetic difference between the discretionary 10-year permanent-residence eligibility point and the 15-year ordinary nationality residence requirement, not a separate statutory five-year post-PR rule.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary acquisition on residence grounds requires at least 15 consecutive years of lawful residence and physical presence; approval is not automatic.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable official typical processing time was published in the reviewed sources. The nationality law says an application file remains valid for three years, but that is not a promised processing time.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary residence naturalization requires 15 consecutive years of residence and physical presence, integrity and good conduct, knowledge and respect for Rwandan culture and traditions, civic knowledge, social integration, sufficient means and no security threat. Rwanda recognizes dual nationality, subject to declaration rules, so general renunciation was not identified as mandatory.
key_conditions.notes: Continuous physical residence and the treatment of absences should be verified at filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must have been legally married to a Rwandan national for at least five years and still live in marital union at application.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A pre-existing lawful marriage counts toward the five-year marriage duration; the law does not require the marriage to have begun after arrival in Rwanda. The applicant must still be married and living in marital union when applying.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A foreign marriage may require recognition and appropriate civil documentation.

requirements_and_risks.value: The official checklist requires a marriage record, proof of shared marital life, good conduct/criminal-record evidence and identity or residence documents. Nationality is not automatic. False information or fraudulent acquisition is criminally punishable, so genuine-marriage evidence is essential.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The marriage route accelerates citizenship relative to the ordinary 15-year ground but does not validate a sham or paper marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Rwanda alone does not automatically confer nationality. A Rwanda-born person whose foreign parents were legally resident at birth may apply upon reaching adulthood, subject to integrity, cultural/civic knowledge, integration, sufficient-means and security conditions. Foundlings receive separate protection.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship arises solely from birth in Rwanda to two foreign parents. If the parents were legally resident at birth, the child may apply at the age of majority and must satisfy the statutory conditions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is conditional acquisition on application, not automatic jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born to at least one Rwandan parent by origin qualifies for Rwandan nationality by origin. The law also contains provisions concerning minor children when parents acquire nationality.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Documentary application or registration may still be required to evidence the status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer nationality on a foreign father. A parent may investigate a dependent/family residence permit, but must independently satisfy immigration requirements.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed sources do not establish an automatic parent-of-citizen permanent-residence or citizenship entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence. Any benefit would require a separate family/dependent application or another qualifying permit.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Manual confirmation with DGIE is advisable for a parent financially dependent on a Rwandan child.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 35 visa-on-arrival and 3 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately lists eVisa destinations, so totals should not be compared directly with Henley's methodology.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 71. The dashboard uses Passport Index rather than mixing its category counts with Henley figures.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Generally practical in Kigali, government, education and formal business because English is an official language. Kinyarwanda remains important for everyday life and local integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from official-language status and should not be read as universal English fluency.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official language, and no reliable evidence of broad public-service availability in either language was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Expect to rely mainly on English and, depending on context, Kinyarwanda or French.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 average monthly paid-employment income of RWF 82,996 using roughly RWF 1,469 per USD. This is not an average software-engineer salary.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest clearly verified median in the reviewed material: RWF 35,000 per month for 2024. The 2025 report confirms the average but a 2025 median was not established from the accessible extract.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current, generally applicable statutory monthly minimum or reliable observed minimum was established from the reviewed official labour-force sources.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2025 national paid-employment average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2024 national paid-employment median; the period differs from the 2025 average.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A meaningful national maximum salary is not published; the 2024 survey's open-ended RWF 100,000-and-above band is not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: No current, generally applicable statutory monthly minimum or reliable observed minimum was established in the checked official labour-force reports.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 average monthly salary from paid employment.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 median monthly employment income.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A national maximum salary is not published; the survey's highest open-ended income band cannot be treated as a maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: National monthly income from paid employment, nominal; average is 2025 and median is 2024
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 average; 2024 median
average_citizen_salary.notes: The 2025 average is RWF 82,996, with strong sector differences: agriculture RWF 33,326, industry RWF 104,169 and services RWF 141,653. National wages are therefore not representative of foreign-paid software work. USD conversions are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official EICV7 household-survey consumption provides a cautious benchmark rather than a foreign-expat budget. In 2024, real annual consumption per adult equivalent (January 2024 prices) had a national median of RWF 750,000 (about RWF 62,500/month) and mean of RWF 1,011,000 (about RWF 84,250/month); Kigali City was materially higher, with a median of RWF 1,289,000 (about RWF 107,417/month) and mean of RWF 1,976,000 (about RWF 164,667/month). These figures are observed consumption, not a prescribed minimum or a rent-inclusive remote-worker budget. They are also stale in nominal terms: by July 2026 headline CPI was 14.5% above July 2025, with housing/utilities up 21.0% and transport up 24.2% year on year.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The EICV7 table reports amounts in thousands of RWF per adult equivalent per year at January 2024 prices; monthly figures here are simple annual/12 conversions. Household composition, neighborhood, housing standard and imported consumption can make an expatriate or remote-worker budget much higher. The July 2026 CPI rates show current price pressure but are not used to mechanically inflate the 2024 survey benchmark.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor status is non-working and no digital-nomad permit exists. Do not count visitor stays as a residence-to-citizenship strategy.
settlement_track.summary: Rwanda has a general long-term framework—discretionary permanent residence after 10 aggregate years and ordinary nationality after 15 consecutive years—but no qualifying starting route for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. The applicant would need to become a genuine local entrepreneur, retire into Class K, study, join family or obtain sponsored employment.
settlement_track.notes: The existence of general PR and nationality rules does not cure the absence of a fitting initial remote-work permit.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker permit exists. Class K requires retirement evidence; business permits require genuine Rwandan business or prescribed-profession activity; employment permits require an employer; and visitor status does not authorize work.

data.notes: The previous Rwanda record’s negative selection conclusion is preserved. This focused pass rechecked the core immigration, application, tax, social-security, language, business-registration and labor claims and resolved the cost-of-living gap with NISR’s EICV7 consumption benchmarks plus the July 2026 CPI. Unresolved values remain null only where the authority publishes no threshold, national maximum, fixed payment, route timing or typical processing time, with the checked sources and limitation stated.

data.selection_summary: Not currently selectable. The 2021 Immigration amendment legally created a 12-month Digital Residence and expressly contemplated remote employees, freelancers, independent contractors, consultants, technology workers, retirees, high-net-worth individuals, and dependants. However, the operative eligibility clause is drafted around full-time foreign employment, the prescribed programme website is unavailable, and no current government application channel, fee schedule, or implementing guidance could be confirmed. Even if issued, Digital Residence is temporary, has no confirmed permanent-residence conversion, and temporary immigration permission normally does not count for citizenship without ministerial consent. Visitor entry, local-employer work permits, asset-based permanent residence, and investment citizenship do not fit this ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker selection.

visa_application.notes: This is the current general eTA/e-border portal reached from the former government eVisa address. It is not a Digital Residence application portal. No functioning official Digital Residence application channel was found.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Derived from the statutory form's declaration of expected income of at least US$50,000 over the next 12 months. The alternative wording permits proof of sufficient means.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The statutory form publishes the threshold in US dollars, not XCD.

income_requirement_display.value: US$50,000 expected over the next 12 months (about US$4,166.67/month), or sufficient means to support the applicant and accompanying dependants
income_requirement_display.notes: The Act does not establish a past monthly-income test; it requires supporting proof of projected income or sufficient funds.

income_proof_months.notes: This is a prospective 12-month income/support declaration, not a confirmed requirement for 12 months of historical bank statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply independently online from outside Saint Kitts and Nevis, except for renewals or cases otherwise directed by the Minister.
For the remote-worker category, be employed full-time outside Saint Kitts and Nevis by a company registered and operating outside the Federation.
Provide passport details, photograph, local accommodation, proof of employment, proof of income or funds, travel and criminal-history declarations, and medical-insurance evidence.

The Act expressly identifies freelancers who are self-employed or independent contractors, and remote consultants, among the intended Digital Residence groups. However, the operative section 6(7)(a) states a full-time foreign-employment and foreign-company test, so a foreign-client contractor needs filing-level confirmation that the broader introductory wording is accepted in practice.
The form names digitalresidency.kn as the application website, but no functioning current programme or application channel could be verified on 2026-08-15.

initial_validity.value: Maximum 12 months
initial_validity.notes: The Act permits a digital resident to enter and remain for 12 months.

extension_rules.notes: The statutory form contains a renewal checkbox, but no current renewal eligibility, duration, limit, fee, or functioning submission process was confirmed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Act describes Digital Residence as permission to become a digital resident and remain for up to 12 months, but the prescribed online channel is not currently verifiable.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a temporary immigration permission rather than confirmed annual or permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No statutory conversion from Digital Residence to permanent residence was found. General permanent residence has separate conditions.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Temporary immigration permission is normally excluded from citizenship residence calculations unless the Minister consents. No general consent or Digital Residence exception was found.

rejected_routes.notes: The Act contemplates foreign employees, freelancers, independent contractors, and consultants, so the profile is not excluded solely because it uses a foreign-client contract. Yet the operative eligibility language is internally inconsistent with that broader list, no current application channel or implementing guidance was found, the status is limited to 12 months, and no settlement conversion is confirmed.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published remote-worker threshold.

income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor admission must not be treated as work or residence authorization.

Do not work without the required work authorization.

initial_validity.notes: Duration varies with nationality and the immigration decision.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potentially separate application after meeting the Immigration Act's permanent-residence conditions
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic conversion was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through the separate long-term residence and naturalisation rules
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not an independent remote-work pathway.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the work permit is employer-applied, job-specific, and dependent on local employment.

rejected_routes.route_name: General permanent residence after prior residence and substantial assets

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The Act uses discretionary substantial-assets and means-of-support tests rather than a published monthly threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed statutory amount was found.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed amount published; generally requires at least seven years' prior residence plus substantial assets in the Federation, or sufficient assets and means for the retirement category
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an ordinary income-based remote-worker route.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard proof period was found.

key_requirements.requirement: General permanent residence is available to qualifying persons who have resided in the Federation for at least seven years and own substantial assets, with the sufficiency of assets determined by the Minister on Cabinet advice.
A separate permanent-residence category exists for persons wishing to reside in retirement who have sufficient assets and means to support themselves and dependants.
The Act does not supply an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker with an initial seven-year lawful status merely because the person works remotely.

initial_validity.value: Permanent, subject to statutory loss provisions
initial_validity.notes: Certain permanent residents may lose status after voluntarily residing abroad continuously for five years unless exempted.

extension_rules.value: No periodic extension identified for permanent residence
extension_rules.notes: Status remains subject to loss and deportation provisions.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No initial temporary route supplied by this category
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant must already satisfy the prior-residence or retirement conditions.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct permanent residence once the statutory conditions are met and the discretionary application is approved
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not solve how an ordinary remote worker lawfully accumulates the prerequisite residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through separate registration or naturalisation rules after sufficient qualifying residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: Temporary immigration time may be excluded and approval remains subject to statutory checks.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because it is not an initial ordinary remote-work route. The main category requires seven years of prior residence and substantial local assets, while the alternative is specifically a retirement/means route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: This requires capital contribution or investment, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Investment options are quoted in US dollars.

income_requirement_display.value: From US$250,000 for the Sustainable Island State Contribution or Public Benefit Option; approved-development real estate from US$325,000
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Substantial one-time contribution or investment plus fees
income_requirement_display.notes: Additional application, due-diligence, interview, and dependent fees can apply.

income_proof_months.notes: Not a monthly-income programme.

key_requirements.requirement: Apply through a government-authorised agent; direct submissions are not accepted.
Make a qualifying contribution or investment and pass comprehensive due diligence and an interview.

initial_validity.value: Citizenship for life after approval and completion of the investment
initial_validity.notes: Dual citizenship is permitted.

extension_rules.value: Not applicable to citizenship
extension_rules.notes: Passport renewal remains a separate administrative matter.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Not required
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The programme grants citizenship rather than temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Citizenship directly supplies an unrestricted right of residence
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No prior residence is required.

path_to_citizenship.value: Direct after approval, investment, due diligence, and final formalities
path_to_citizenship.notes: The official April 2026 guidance estimated about four to six months.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant profile expressly excludes substantial-capital and investor routes, and the application is not independent of an authorised agent.

summary.value: No independent points-tested, degree-based, or qualification-based residence route was found. Study can be an immigration purpose, but no official source reviewed showed that admission to education or possession of a software-engineering degree directly grants qualifying temporary or permanent residence.
summary.notes: A student or institution-specific permission should not be treated as a skilled independent settlement route.

tax_residency_rule.value: No simple official 183-day test was confirmed. The tax legislation and treaty material refer to domicile, residence, permanent home, centre of vital interests, and habitual abode; individual residence is fact-sensitive. General personal income tax is currently reported as absent, but residence remains relevant to levies, source rules, reporting, and foreign-country tax obligations.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Do not rely on online claims that tax residence begins automatically after 60 or 183 days. Obtain an Inland Revenue determination for treaty or certificate purposes.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Current official-agency materials state that there is no general personal income tax. This is a PIT screening rate, not a zero-total-tax claim. The consolidated Income Tax Act still displays historical individual rate provisions, so filing advice is prudent.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The numeric 5% is the employee share for a locally covered employee aged 16–62, not a Digital Residence-specific rate. The employer pays another 5% plus 1% for employment injury, making 11% total. Self-employed persons pay 10% of a selected weekly-income category; the consolidated scale runs from XCD 40 or 50 per month at the special category to XCD 540 or 675 per month at category L. The immigration amendment does not say whether a digital resident paid directly by a foreign employer is covered, so that payroll nexus requires a Social Security Board determination.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No single fixed monthly payment applies across the unverified Digital Residence scenarios. Covered employees pay percentage-based amounts; covered self-employed persons use an XCD contribution scale. Medical-insurance premiums are private and variable, while no current Digital Residence government fee was published.

special_tax_regimes.value: No current Digital Residence tax exemption or special inbound regime was found. General materials report no personal income tax, while employment-related social security and the Housing and Social Development Levy can still apply.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business registration, corporate tax, VAT, withholding tax, and payroll treatment depend on whether the worker creates or uses a local business or local payroll.

taxes.caveats: The 0% figure concerns general personal income tax only. Local employment can attract employee social security and a progressive Housing and Social Development Levy, while self-employment or a local company can trigger registrations, business taxes, VAT, licence fees, and contributions. The applicant's home-country residence and treaty position may continue to tax foreign earnings.

taxation_system.value: No general personal income tax, but employment and business-related levies remain
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Fact-sensitive domicile/residence analysis; no reliable universal day-count threshold was confirmed.
taxation_system.income_scope: General individual PIT is reported as absent. Local employment, business activity, withholding, VAT, social-security contributions, and the Housing and Social Development Levy remain separate.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No functioning Digital Residence tax regime or exemption was confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees generally contribute 5%; employers contribute 5% plus 1% employment-injury coverage. Self-employed contributors pay 10% using a selected weekly-income scale. Employee Housing and Social Development Levy rates are 0% through XCD 2,253.33 monthly, 3.5% on earnings through XCD 6,500 once over the exemption threshold, 10% on the XCD 6,500.01–8,000 slice, and 12% above XCD 8,000; the employer levy is 3%.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 0% dashboard figure is the general PIT rate, not an effective total burden. The Housing and Social Development Levy is a separate progressive payroll levy.
taxation_system.notes: Official-agency and statutory sources support no general PIT reporting and the stated payroll contribution structure. The applicability of payroll charges to direct foreign payroll under Digital Residence was not established.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No current route-specific tax rules were found. If Digital Residence were operational, general materials indicate 0% personal income tax, but local payroll, social-security, levy, business-substance, and home-country tax questions would require individual review.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Inactive or unverified statutory Digital Residence; no current special tax regime
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% general personal income tax screening rate; not zero total tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No confirmed route-specific day test; domicile, residence, permanent home, centre of vital interests, and habitual abode may matter.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Current official-agency materials report no general personal income tax, but no operational Digital Residence tax guidance was found. The worker's foreign jurisdiction may continue taxing the income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No route-specific tax exemption or inbound regime is established in the 2021 Immigration amendment: it governs immigration eligibility, insurance, and payment mechanics but contains no tax provisions. The checked current government/agency tax materials report no general personal income tax, but none publishes a separate Digital Residence tax holiday, certificate, or special filing regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For covered local employment, the Social Security Board publishes a 5% employee contribution, 5% employer contribution, and 1% employer employment-injury contribution. Covered employee wages can also bear the Housing and Social Development Levy: 0% through XCD 2,253.33 monthly, then 3.5%, 10%, and 12% marginal slices; the employer levy is 3%. Self-employed persons are compulsory contributors under a 10%-equivalent selected-income scale. Neither the Immigration amendment nor the checked Social Security materials determine whether direct foreign payroll with no local employer is covered.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed amount is published in the statute. The statutory form requires proof of medical insurance and refers to full payment in US dollars, but its fee and payment fields are blank; no current official Digital Residence application or renewal fee schedule was located.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed amount applies to a covered employee because contributions are percentage-based. A locally covered self-employed person uses the statutory scale, with listed monthly contributions from XCD 40 or 50 through XCD 540 or 675 depending on category and four- or five-week month; whether a foreign-contract digital resident must register on that scale is not addressed by the route law.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The application form states that full payment must be enclosed and that prices are in US dollars, but it contains no amount. Because the prescribed programme site is unavailable and no replacement official fee page was found, an application or renewal fee cannot be stated.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Local business licensing, VAT, withholding, banking, or registration charges depend on structure and were not established for ordinary foreign-payroll remote work.
fixed_payments.notes: Medical insurance is mandatory evidence, but its private premium varies and is not a government-set monthly payment. The only exact self-employed amounts found are the general Social Security scale, not Digital Residence fees.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No reliable universal day threshold was found. Short presence does not by itself establish exemption from home-country tax, and visitor entry does not authorize work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: General PIT screening is 0%, but tax residence and foreign-source treatment remain fact-sensitive; payroll levies and foreign-country tax may still apply.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A person registering or operating a local business may face social-security registration, business licensing, corporate or unincorporated-business tax, VAT, and withholding obligations. No simple visitor-to-sole-proprietor residence conversion was found.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is reduced because there is no current Digital Residence application channel or route-specific tax guidance.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The statute contemplates direct Digital Residence, but no current application channel or processing timetable was confirmed.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The numeric value remains null because the Immigration Act does not create a Digital Residence-to-permanent-residence conversion or state that Digital Residence time counts. Its separate general permanent-residence category requires at least seven years of residence plus substantial assets and discretionary approval; seven years is therefore a prerequisite for that separate application, not a confirmed number of years after Digital Residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: No fixed PR-to-citizenship interval was established. General residence-based registration or naturalisation uses lengthy residence rules and remains subject to eligibility and ministerial review.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: There is no confirmed citizenship timeline from Digital Residence. General alien naturalisation requires residence throughout the final 12 months and qualifying residence during the preceding 14-year period; temporary immigration permission is normally excluded without ministerial consent.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No typical processing time for ordinary naturalisation was published. If the Minister conducts the statutory investigation applicable to registration cases, the Act provides a determination period not exceeding two years; this is not a typical naturalisation estimate.

key_conditions.value: A credible residence-based case requires lawful and qualifying residence, good character, intent to reside, and satisfaction of the applicable registration or naturalisation provisions. Temporary immigration time normally does not count unless the Minister consents. No language test or mandatory renunciation requirement was found in the reviewed provisions; dual citizenship is permitted.
key_conditions.notes: The exact residence aggregation for an alien naturalisation filing should be confirmed with the Ministry before relying on a calendar estimate.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution entitles a person married to a citizen to apply for registration and states no minimum duration for a current marriage. Zero means no statutory waiting period was found, not automatic or immediate citizenship.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing, still-subsisting marriage to a citizen can support an application for citizenship by registration. The applicant does not need to marry after arriving.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Registration requires an application and prescribed evidence; marriage itself does not instantly confer citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The application form requires a subsisting marriage, marriage and birth certificates, photographs, a police certificate, the prescribed fee, and an oath where applicable. Security, public-order, character, and truthful-disclosure checks remain relevant. False statements are an offence, so a sham or non-subsisting marriage creates refusal and legal risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Current filing fees and procedures should be reconfirmed before application.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship at birth to every person born in the Federation, subject only to narrow diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Saint Kitts and Nevis generally becomes a citizen at birth even if both parents are foreign temporary or permanent residents, unless the narrow diplomatic or enemy-occupation exception applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parents' ordinary immigration category is not part of the general territorial-birth test.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in the Federation is a citizen by birth. A child born abroad may also qualify through a citizen parent in the descent or government-service circumstances specified by the Constitution.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: For an overseas birth, the citizen parent's own basis of citizenship and circumstances must be checked.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a citizen child does not automatically grant either foreign parent residence, permanent residence, or citizenship. A parent may need a separate family, residence, or discretionary immigration application.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic parent-of-citizen status was found.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically receive citizenship or residence because his child is a citizen. Paternity and the child's citizenship may support a discretionary family-based case, but no guaranteed statutory shortcut was established.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Individual immigration advice is needed before relying on parenthood as a status route.

rank.notes: Current Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15. This is not the Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free-only count; it excludes visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Current Passport Index breakdown.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 39 visa-on-arrival and 7 eTA destinations shown by Passport Index. Its overall mobility score was 146.

passport.notes: Index methodologies differ. Henley combines visa-free, visa-on-arrival, and eTA access in its access score, while Passport Index provides the requested separate categories; therefore the figures should not be mixed.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English is the official language and is used in government and administration, making English-language daily life and remote work practical.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Internet quality and reliability should still be checked for the intended island and accommodation.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low without English. No official or reliable evidence of widespread Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was found; English should be expected for immigration, banking, housing, healthcare, and business administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practical inference from English being the sole listed official language, not a measured survey of Russian or Ukrainian speakers.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of XCD 4,047 at the fixed XCD 2.70 per US$1 rate. This is average gross monthly wages per employee for Social Security-reported employment on Nevis in January–July 2024, not a federation-wide average.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The checked Nevis wage release and current ILO profile publish no federation-wide median. The official 2015 Labour Force Survey file is a questionnaire, not a results report.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the statutory XCD 500 weekly minimum: 500 × 52 ÷ 12 ÷ 2.70.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Nevis-only XCD 4,047 average gross monthly wage per employee.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official 2015 Labour Force Survey PDF is the questionnaire and confirms that gross monthly income was collected, but it publishes no result or median. The current ILO country profile and the 2024 Nevis administrative-wage release likewise do not provide a federation-wide median, so no USD conversion can be made.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly conversion of the highest XCD 137,779 annual salary listed in the 2024 federal public-service scale: 137,779 ÷ 12 ÷ 2.70. This is an official public-service wage-band ceiling, not the maximum wage in the national economy.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage effective 1 July 2025, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average gross monthly wage per employee on Nevis for January–July 2024; it is not a federation-wide statistic.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No XCD median estimate is published in the checked current ILO profile or Nevis administrative-wage release. The official 2015 Labour Force Survey file asks respondents for monthly gross income but is a questionnaire rather than a results report.

max_salary_local_currency.value: XCD 137,779/year (approximately XCD 11,481.58/month), highest listed 2024 federal public-service salary scale
max_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the top amount in the published federal salary schedule, not an economy-wide observed maximum; private-sector maximum pay is unbounded and no national wage-distribution maximum was published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory federation-wide minimum wage, Nevis Social Security-reported average gross wage per employee, and federal public-service salary-scale ceiling
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage from 1 July 2025; average wage January–July 2024; public-service scale effective 1 January 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum is the federation-wide statutory wage. The average is registered gross employment wages on Nevis only. No national median results table was published in the checked official/ILO material. The maximum field uses only the top scheduled 2024 federal public-service salary and is not an economy-wide maximum. Salary data is unrelated to the Digital Residence income threshold.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2026 Budget describes continuing cost-of-living relief and an updated consumer-price basket, reflecting the pressure of imported prices in the small island economy. No reliable current household monthly-cost figure was established.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing, imported goods, utilities, and inter-island location can materially change actual costs.
