settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: A visitor or offshore-paid business visit is not a digital-nomad status: work is prohibited and the stay does not create a settlement clock.
settlement_track.summary: Samoa has no regular foreign-contract remote-work route. Business and locally sponsored employment permits are separate non-fitting routes, and even those have no published automatic path to PR; citizenship requires first obtaining PR through another ground and holding it continuously for five years.
settlement_track.notes: The existence of PR application forms and a 10-working-day processing target does not establish eligibility or a temporary-residence-to-PR conversion rule.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker or freelance residence category is listed. Visitor work is prohibited, employment is employer-tied, and the business route requires genuine local foreign-investment and business establishment.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Samoa record and 21 distinct directly relevant URLs, with current 2026 immigration, employment, investment, tax, citizenship, salary, language, exchange-rate and passport material inspected. The previous negative selection result remains correct, while the salary, minimum wage, passport ranking, social contributions, tax sourcing and business-route details were updated or clarified. Unresolved PR eligibility/conversion timing, citizenship processing time, median/max wages and passport-category subtotals remain null because current authoritative sources did not establish them.

data.selection_summary: San Marino has no visa branded as a digital-nomad visa, but its active “atypical residence subject to a preferential tax regime” is a stronger fit: a foreigner producing foreign income may apply independently and obtain registered residence without a local employer. Official tax guidance expressly covers foreign employment and self-employment income. The residence consolidates after 10 years, and continuous registered and actual residence can support naturalisation after 20 years. Important drawbacks are discretionary approval, a €10,000 annual minimum substitute tax, housing and sufficient-resource evidence, full-cost healthcare arrangements, and the exceptionally long citizenship timeline.

visa_application.title: Permits of stay, residence and citizenship — San Marino Foreign Affairs
visa_application.notes: The official route page and current application guide direct applicants to deposit the original application and supporting documents with the Department of Foreign Affairs. No public direct e-form was confirmed; applicants should contact residenze.permessidisoggiorno@esteri.sm before filing.

best_routes.route_name: Residenza atipica soggetta a regime fiscale agevolato

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numeric monthly admission threshold is published. Applicants must prove sufficient foreign income and resources; the separate €10,000 annual minimum tax should not be misrepresented as an income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed minimum income in euros is stated. The official guide asks for a tax return or equivalent evidence of foreign income sufficient to support the applicant and accompanying family.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; sufficient foreign income/resources required. Separate annual tax floor: €10,000.
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Foreign income sufficient for maintenance; 7% substitute tax with €10,000 annual minimum and €100,000 annual maximum
income_requirement_display.notes: At 7%, €10,000 corresponds mathematically to approximately €142,857 of net-frontier income, but the law does not state that amount as an admission threshold and approval remains discretionary.

income_proof_months.notes: The guide requires a tax return or equivalent income evidence and permits additional bank evidence, but specifies no number of income-history months. Foreign documents must generally be no more than six months old; this is document freshness, not an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must not previously have been tax resident in San Marino, unless covered by the statutory non-consolidated-residence condition.
Produce income abroad. Official tax guidance lists foreign employment, self-employment, business, pension, capital, property and other income categories.
Submit the original application personally through the Department of Foreign Affairs and pay the €1,000 filing right.
Provide passport, birth/citizenship and family-status records, residence certificate, criminal-record and pending-charge certificates, CV, and tax-compliance declarations.
Provide a conditional preliminary purchase or rental agreement for suitable housing in San Marino.
Prove sufficient resources for the applicant and accompanying family through a tax return or equivalent evidence; bank evidence may supplement it.
Foreign documents must be apostilled and accompanied by a certified Italian translation and generally be issued within six months before filing.

Healthcare costs must be borne entirely by the resident under arrangements established by the Social Security Institute; current price or contribution amounts were not published in the sources reviewed.

The Congress of State decides within 60 days after receiving a complete application; the statute describes the decision as non-reviewable and caps principal grants at 100 per year unless changed by delegated decree.

initial_validity.value: Registered atypical residence upon approval; no short fixed validity period is stated
initial_validity.notes: This is registered residence rather than a 12-month nomad or visitor permit. It remains conditional and may be revoked for loss of requirements, nonpayment of substitute tax, healthcare noncompliance or false documentation.

extension_rules.value: Maintain qualifying foreign income, tax compliance, effective residence and full-cost healthcare arrangements; residence consolidates after 10 years
extension_rules.notes: The sources do not describe an annual residence-renewal application. Tax and residence requirements are monitored, and the preferential tax regime ends after 15 tax years even though residence may continue under ordinary rules.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved application directly results in entry in the resident-population register; no preceding employer-sponsored work status is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: San Marino calls this residence, not a digital-nomad visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After 10 years in the resident-population register, atypical residence consolidates and ordinary residence rules apply.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The legislation describes consolidated ordinary registered residence rather than a separately named permanent-residence permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation may be requested after at least 20 continuous years of registered and actual residence, subject to B1 Italian, a history/institutions test, character requirements, filing and oath.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Because atypical residence results in registered residence and the citizenship rule measures registered and actual residence, the route supplies a credible citizenship track. Physical residence must remain genuine and continuous.

best_routes.notes: This route is not branded as a digital-nomad program, but it is an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work fit because foreign employment and foreign self-employment income are expressly within the special tax regime. It is expensive at modest income levels and approval by the Congress of State is discretionary.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly income threshold is stated in the current official elective-residence vademecum or the coordinated immigration text. Both require a tax return or equivalent evidence of resources sufficient for the applicant’s maintenance, but publish no numeric floor for that separate maintenance test. The €500,000 figure is the qualifying property purchase or financial deposit, not income; the coordinated regulation’s €12,000 annual benchmark applies to family-reunification provisions, not elective residence, so it is not imported here.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The route requires a qualifying €500,000 property purchase or financial deposit, but the separate sufficient-resources test has no published euro-denominated income floor.

income_requirement_display.value: €500,000 qualifying property purchase or financial deposit; no published monthly-income floor
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR investment threshold plus qualitative maintenance-resources test
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: €500,000 investment; sufficient maintenance resources without a published numeric floor
income_requirement_display.notes: The investment amount is not monthly income and the route is rejected because the applicant context excludes substantial investment routes.

income_proof_months.notes: The official guide requests a tax return or equivalent proof of sufficient resources but specifies no number of income-history months; documents generally must be no older than six months, which is a freshness rule rather than an income-history requirement.

key_requirements.requirement: Purchase qualifying residential property for at least €500,000 or make and maintain the qualifying financial deposit.
Provide a tax return or equivalent evidence of resources sufficient for maintenance; no numeric maintenance-income floor is published.
Bear healthcare costs and forgo specified public benefits before consolidation.

initial_validity.value: Residence that consolidates after 10 years

extension_rules.value: Maintain the statutory investment and other residence conditions until consolidation

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct residence following discretionary investment-based approval

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Consolidates into ordinary registered residence after 10 years
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official materials do not call this a separate permanent-residence permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially subject to the general 20-year continuous actual and registered residence rule
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not selected because the entry route requires substantial investment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because eligibility is investment-based, even though it may create registered residence. The official sources distinguish the €500,000 investment threshold from the unquantified maintenance-resources test.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residenza per motivi economici / entrepreneurial registered residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No personal monthly-income threshold applies or is published for this entrepreneurial route. The governing law instead tests local corporate ownership, employment commitments and a capital/property guarantee; the official document checklists likewise ask for business, corporate and economic/fiscal evidence rather than a set monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No euro-denominated personal income floor is stated. Financial conditions are business-substance requirements: at least 51% ownership, qualifying local hires, and initially a €75,000 security increased within two years to €150,000 or replaced by qualifying property.

income_requirement_display.value: No personal-income floor; local company, hiring and €75,000→€150,000 security/property requirements
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR business guarantee and local economic substance
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least 51% company ownership; 1 qualifying local hire in an incentivized sector or 3 in a non-incentivized sector; €75,000 security rising to €150,000 within two years or qualifying property
income_requirement_display.notes: These are ownership, employment and security requirements, not remote-work income requirements. The route is rejected because it requires a genuine San Marino company and local hiring.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history look-back period is prescribed. The route is not income-tested: the governing law relies on company ownership, local employment and security/property commitments. For an already operating company, the official checklist asks for corporate standing, tax-liability status, shareholder and employee records and a five-year business plan; for a company to be formed, it asks for economic, tax and corporate documentation from the country of origin, but states no number of months. The six-month rule in the checklists concerns certificate freshness, not proof of income over six months.

key_requirements.requirement: Establish or acquire a San Marino company and hold at least 51% of its share capital.
Hire at least one full-time indefinite worker from the local lists in an incentivized sector, or at least three in a non-incentivized sector; additional workforce ratios also apply.
Before resident registration, constitute a €75,000 security; within two years increase it to €150,000 or replace it with qualifying property of at least €150,000.
Provide corporate/tax/employee evidence and a business plan of at least five years; a proposed company must also provide economic, fiscal and corporate documentation from the country of origin.
Obtain the relevant OPEC economic-operator authorization and keep the filing data and business premises compliant.

initial_validity.value: Registered residence while the qualifying business conditions continue; consolidation after 10 years
initial_validity.notes: The law grants residence rather than a short entrepreneurial stay permit, but it is revocable if the statutory ownership, employment, operating, debt or guarantee conditions cease.

extension_rules.value: Continuously maintain the qualifying company, ownership, local-employment ratios, acceptable public-debt position and security/property guarantee; residence consolidates after 10 years if conditions and habitual residence are verified
extension_rules.notes: The law provides a 90-day cure period for specified failures before revocation. This is maintenance of conditional residence, not a published annual income-evidence renewal cycle.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct registration as a resident for economic reasons after satisfying the corporate, employment and guarantee requirements
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No local employer sponsor is required, but the applicant must be the controlling entrepreneur of a locally substantive company.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Residence consolidates after 10 years once continuing eligibility and habitual residence are verified
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: San Marino describes consolidation of registered residence, not a separately named permanent-residence card.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation rules could apply to qualifying continuous registered and actual residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the route's local-business requirement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this applicant because it is a local-company founder/owner route with mandatory local hiring and financial-security/property commitments. Current authorization materials show that self-employed and digitally delivered business activities can be licensed through OPEC, but an operating authorization alone does not supply immigration residence and does not remove the entrepreneurial-residence conditions.

summary.value: A special temporary permit may be issued for education without a local employer, but the official page distinguishes these permits—maximum 12 months, renewable—from registered residence. No degree-only or qualification-based route to registered or permanent residence was found.
summary.notes: Education is a temporary stay category and is not treated as a citizenship-oriented alternative for this applicant.

tax_residency_rule.value: The selected regime is for a person establishing residence in San Marino who was not previously tax resident there. Special taxation applies to foreign income after the person obtains atypical residence; the precise commencement date should be confirmed with the Tax Office for the filing year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: No reliable official source reviewed stated a simple 183-day test for this route, so none is asserted.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Special substitute-tax rate on eligible foreign income calculated on the “net frontier,” not an expected effective rate. A €10,000 annual minimum and €100,000 annual maximum apply.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No universal payroll or social-contribution percentage for a foreign-employer or foreign-client worker under atypical residence was established. Liability depends on employment/self-employment structure and applicable coordination or treaty rules. Healthcare costs are separately borne in full under ISS arrangements.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is a €10,000 annual minimum substitute tax—equivalent to €833.33 per month before currency conversion—and a €1,000 application fee. No reliable same-date USD conversion or fixed monthly healthcare amount was established.

special_tax_regimes.value: Atypical residents pay 7% on eligible net foreign income, subject to a €10,000 annual floor and €100,000 cap. The regime lasts at most 15 tax years and covers foreign employment, self-employment, business, pension, capital, real-estate and other income categories.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Taxes paid in the source country affect the statutory net-frontier calculation. Treaty and foreign-employer payroll treatment require individual advice.

taxes.caveats: The €10,000 floor can make the effective rate much higher than 7% at moderate income. Classification of income as foreign-source, foreign tax credits/net-frontier calculation, payroll withholding, social insurance and treaty effects must be checked with San Marino and source-country advisers. Moving the activity or business substance into San Marino may trigger ordinary rather than special treatment.

taxation_system.value: Mixed: ordinary residents generally face progressive IGR on worldwide income, while the selected atypical-residence route applies a special 7% substitute tax to eligible foreign income with a €10,000 annual minimum and €100,000 maximum.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; the atypical route is specifically for new/non-consolidated tax residents producing foreign income.
taxation_system.income_scope: Eligible foreign income under the atypical regime; ordinary resident rules apply outside the special regime.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Atypical foreign-income residence: 7% net-frontier substitute tax, €10,000–€100,000 annual bounds, maximum 15 tax years.
taxation_system.social_security: No single percentage was confirmed for a foreign-contract worker. Healthcare is at the resident's full cost under ISS arrangements.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 35% figure is the top ordinary personal IGR rate, not the expected tax rate for the selected route. Official 2025 business guidance reports eight ordinary brackets from 9% through 35%; the 2026 reform reviewed did not supply a replacement progressive table in the passages inspected.

tax_brackets.notes: Not the selected route's special rate.
Top marginal rate, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: High confidence in the selected route's 7%/€10,000/€100,000 rules. Medium confidence in presenting the ordinary bracket detail as current because the accessible official consolidated text was distributed as a ZIP and the clearest complete table was the Chamber of Commerce's 2025 profile.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Although not branded as a digital-nomad regime, an atypical resident receiving qualifying foreign employment or self-employment income pays a 7% substitute tax on net-frontier income, with a €10,000 annual minimum and €100,000 maximum for up to 15 years.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Atypical foreign-income tax residence
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 7% of eligible net foreign income; minimum €10,000 and maximum €100,000 per year
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Special taxation applies after obtaining atypical residence and establishing residence in San Marino; confirm the first taxable period with the Tax Office.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign employment and self-employment income are expressly included. The base is net of qualifying tax paid in the source country under the net-frontier concept.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Inbound atypical-residence regime lasting no more than 15 tax years; it is not a digital-nomad visa.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No general contribution rate for a foreign-employer remote worker was confirmed. Foreign payroll, permanent-establishment and social-security coordination require case-specific review.

fixed_payments.status: Confirmed annual minimum tax and application fee; healthcare amount unresolved
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed payroll or social-security payment confirmed. Healthcare costs must be borne in full under ISS arrangements, but the current amount is not publicly stated in the sources reviewed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: €1,000 filing right, absorbing associated stamp and office duties.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: €10,000 annual minimum substitute income tax; €100,000 annual maximum.
fixed_payments.notes: The annual tax floor is a tax liability, not a visa-income threshold.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: San Marino has no separate visitor remote-work or digital-nomad permission established by the official sources. A short visitor should not assume that remote work is authorised or that visitor time counts toward settlement.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: After atypical residence is granted, qualifying foreign employment or self-employment income falls within the 7% net-frontier regime, subject to the €10,000 annual minimum.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Foreign-source self-employment income is listed within the special regime. Establishing a San Marino economic operator or moving business substance or source into San Marino may instead invoke ordinary local business, licensing, 18% separate-tax and contribution rules.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax fit is strong, but the high annual floor makes the route economically unattractive for many ordinary remote workers.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Residence is obtained directly upon approval and registration; the statute gives the Congress of State 60 days to decide a complete application.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: After 10 years the atypical residence consolidates and ordinary residence rules apply. San Marino does not label this transition as a separate permanent-residence permit.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Total continuous actual and registered residence must reach 20 years, so this is approximately 10 additional years after consolidation.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalisation period; the applicant must maintain continuous registered and actual residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Official sources describe filing, examination and oath but publish no reliable typical end-to-end processing time.

key_conditions.value: Twenty years of continuous registered and actual residence; B1 Italian; passing the written history and institutions test; qualifying criminal-record status; application review; and oath. Since the 2026 reform, renunciation of existing citizenship is no longer required.
key_conditions.notes: Passing the test does not replace the residence requirement.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: This is 10 years of continuous registered and actual residence for the spouse or civil partner of a citizen, not merely 10 years elapsed since marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage or civil union to a Sammarinese citizen can support family residence and the reduced 10-year naturalisation residence period, provided no separation, dissolution or nullity proceeding is pending or completed.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to a non-citizen has no citizenship acceleration.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must still reside continuously and actually in San Marino, satisfy B1 Italian and civic-test requirements, meet character conditions and take the oath. Separation, dissolution or nullity defeats the spouse-based reduction; marriage does not grant citizenship automatically.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Authorities may verify civil status and actual residence. A sham marriage or false documentation creates refusal, revocation and potential legal risk.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship primarily descends from a Sammarinese parent. Birth in San Marino alone does not confer citizenship; the narrow territorial rule covers a child whose parents are both unknown or stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship merely from birth in San Marino when the parents are foreign citizens. A resident-from-birth child may use the special naturalisation rule at adulthood, while a child of two unknown or stateless parents is covered by the narrow territorial rule.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The resident-from-birth mechanism is application-based naturalisation, not broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of one Sammarinese parent acquires citizenship by descent, subject to civil registration and the statutory declaration to maintain citizenship within seven years after reaching majority.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2019 amendment applies the rule without distinction between Sammarinese mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship on a foreign parent. Family residence may be available, but the parent must qualify separately; a spouse or civil partner of a citizen can use the 10-year resident naturalisation rule.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No official source reviewed confirmed an automatic permanent-residence or accelerated citizenship entitlement solely from parenthood.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is Sammarinese, the child can be a citizen by descent. The migrant father may investigate family residence, and if married or civilly partnered to the citizen parent may qualify for the 10-year resident naturalisation period; neither the child's citizenship nor paternity makes the father a citizen automatically.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: An unmarried father's exact family-residence entitlement should be verified with Foreign Affairs.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 15 August 2026. Rankings can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category in the named index; this is not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately lists eVisa destinations, so its visa-required count is not the complement of visa-free/VOA/eTA alone.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 48 visa-on-arrival and 8 eTA destinations reported by the index.

passport.notes: Arton reports a mobility score of 158. For comparison, the January 2026 Henley ranking placed San Marino 17th with a score of 168; methodologies and update dates differ.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate. English-language government tourism and Foreign Affairs interfaces exist, and English-speaking tourism services are available, but residence evidence must be translated into Italian and citizenship ultimately requires B1 Italian. English may suffice for a foreign remote job, but not for full administrative integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No country-level English-proficiency statistic specific to San Marino was found.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low and not reliably established. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, and the residence process and long-term integration requirements operate in Italian; English may provide limited support in tourism-facing settings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current source demonstrating broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official report supplies a euro-denominated private-sector average, but no reliable same-date USD conversion was established.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official statistical sources inspected did not publish a national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No official statutory minimum wage or national observed minimum salary suitable for this field was confirmed.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Local-currency average is available; USD value is left null rather than applying an unverified exchange rate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national median wage was published in the official sources reviewed.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum wage was published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: The €2,183.71 contractual territorial average is an average benchmark, not a minimum wage, so it is not entered as a minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 average monthly remuneration in the private sector.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No national median was published in the official bulletin or economic-statistical report inspected.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Sector totals are published, but no defensible national maximum salary is provided.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly gross remuneration, private sector
average_citizen_salary.notes: This is the official private-sector worker average, not a citizen-only statistic and not the mean for public employees or self-employed workers. The same report gives a 2024 average territorial contractual remuneration of €2,183.71.

cost_of_living_note.value: The Q1 2026 statistical bulletin publishes consumer-price movements but not a representative monthly household cost-of-living budget. A reliable comparable monthly cost estimate was therefore not established.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No crowdsourced cost estimate was substituted for official evidence.

settlement_track.summary: Atypical residence is genuine registered residence, not a visitor or temporary nomad permission. It consolidates after 10 years, and continuous registered and actual residence supports the general 20-year naturalisation path without switching to another immigration category.
settlement_track.notes: The route is credible but unusually slow, expensive at moderate income and subject to discretionary initial approval and continuing effective-residence checks.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The statute requires foreign income, and official tax guidance expressly lists both foreign employment and foreign self-employment income. No local employer, local client, startup, elite-talent or investment condition applies to this route.

data.notes: Focused unexplained-null audit: the entrepreneurial-residence income-proof-months field remains null because current law and the two official filing checklists prescribe no income-history period and do not make personal income the admission test. They instead require a controlling local company, local employment, financial security/property, business-plan and corporate/economic/fiscal evidence; the checklists’ six-month rule is document freshness, not an income look-back. Five new canonical sources were added for this focused check. The selected atypical foreign-income residence and its citizenship track remain otherwise supported.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Atypical registered residence consolidating into ordinary residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Atypical residence consolidates into ordinary registered residence after ten years in the resident-population register, provided the route’s continuing requirements are met.
requirements: Obtain the discretionary atypical-residence approval and demonstrate sufficient foreign income.
Maintain effective residence and comply with the scheme’s financial, healthcare and other continuing conditions.
Budget for the scheme’s EUR 10,000 annual minimum substitute tax; this is an ongoing tax condition, not a required property investment.
reviewed_route_names: Residenza atipica soggetta a regime fiscale agevolato
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Article 69 of Law 223/2020 expressly provides consolidation after ten years. This is the country’s consolidated ordinary-residence mechanism, not a separately named PR card and not a dedicated digital-nomad visa. The current official application guide requires evidence of sufficient foreign income; approval is discretionary.

data.selection_summary: The immigration law provides a self-applied residence route for independent professional activity. A service contract is one permitted basis, and qualifying temporary residence can lead to permanent residence and naturalization after five years. However, the live SMF portal asks for a locally constituted company, registered premises, tax clearance and INSS clearance and does not explain whether an ordinary foreign-client contract alone is accepted. Written filing-level confirmation is therefore required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Apply for the independent-professional residence visa, enter São Tomé and Príncipe and obtain a one-year temporary residence certificate. A waiver of the prior residence visa after lawful entry is legally possible but discretionary.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Permanent residence may be obtained after at least five consecutive years of temporary residence, subject to criminal-record and Portuguese-language conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence has no status-expiry limit, although its card is renewed every five years.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after at least five years of legal residence, with language, subsistence, criminal-record and security conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary; the statute does not require first obtaining permanent residence.

best_routes.notes: This is a settlement-oriented residence category, not a digital-nomad or visitor visa. summary.value: An admitted international student may independently seek a study residence visa and normally one-year renewable residence certificate. This is an education route, not a degree-based skilled residence route for continuing ordinary foreign remote work. Although the general law refers to permanent residence after five consecutive years of temporary residence, treatment of student time should be confirmed with SMF.
summary.notes: Enrollment, progress and sufficient means must be maintained. Employment outside study periods requires prior authorization and a local contract.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is tax-resident for a year if any statutory test applies, including presence for more than 180 days, a permanent-looking home on 31 December, or the main base of professional/business activity or economic interests in São Tomé and Príncipe.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Residence can arise without exceeding 180 days if the home or center-of-activity test applies.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate, not an expected effective rate; the progressive table runs from 0% to 25%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Standard employee payroll totals 12% from 1 January 2025: 5% employee plus 7% employer. A correctly classified independent worker instead uses the separate 10% compulsory or 14% expanded scheme on a conventional remuneration tier.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate compulsory self-employed minimum: STN 120/month, calculated as 10% of the lowest conventional remuneration tier of 1 UCSS. The consolidated regulation establishes the 10% rate and one-UCSS floor; the 2025 contribution alert confirms 1 UCSS = STN 1,200. At approximately STN 21.7172/USD, STN 120 is USD 5.53. The 14% expanded-scheme minimum is STN 168, about USD 7.74.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, non-dom or remittance-basis regime was found. Investment incentives exist for approved local investment projects but are not an ordinary foreign-contract regime.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Registration of a local company alone does not establish entitlement to an investment incentive.

taxes.caveats: The tax authority continues to publish the 2009 IRS Code, but later amendments or administrative updates to monetary thresholds should be checked locally. The statutory table uses pre-2018 old dobras; current-STN equivalents divide the legal amounts by 1,000. Contract classification, income source, deductions, foreign-tax credits, social-security status and treaties can materially change the result.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax on worldwide income for residents and São Toméan-source income for non-residents; professional/business income is Category B.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 days, or a permanent-looking home on 31 December, or the principal professional/business/economic-interest base in the country, plus specified public-service and crew tests.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: worldwide income. Non-residents: São Toméan-source income only.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special remote-worker regime found. A 15% Category B withholding payment-on-account may apply when São Toméan entities pay resident professionals; investment incentives are separate.
taxation_system.social_security: Independent professionals are compulsorily covered at 10% under the mandatory scheme or 14% under the optional expanded scheme, applied to conventional remuneration of 1, 3, 5, 7 or at least 10 UCSS. If no tier is chosen, one UCSS applies. With 1 UCSS confirmed as STN 1,200 in 2025, minimum monthly contributions are STN 120 or STN 168. Separate employee payroll totals 12% from 2025.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 25% dashboard number is the top marginal rate. Article 66 applies progressive rates to aggregated Categories A, B and D. Thresholds are converted from old Dbs to current STN at 1,000:1 and are not inflation-adjusted.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Aggregated Categories A, B and D
tax_brackets.notes: No USD conversion is supplied because administrative currency of the threshold should be confirmed.

taxation_system.notes: The current INSS page and consolidated regulation resolve the previous self-employed rate/base gap. Classification remains important: local-company remuneration or an employment relationship uses payroll rules; genuinely autonomous foreign-client services use the independent-worker scheme.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: There is no dedicated digital-nomad tax category. If the independent-professional route is accepted and the applicant becomes resident, foreign employment or professional income enters the worldwide-income system, generally at progressive rates up to 25%.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Independent professional/business income, normally IRS Category B; employment income is Category A
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–25% progressive; 25% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 days or an alternative home/center-of-activity test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are taxed on total income, including foreign income; statutory foreign-tax-credit relief exists subject to its conditions.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the current tax and immigration sources.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For a genuine independent-professional filing, INSS enrollment is compulsory. The mandatory scheme charges 10%, or the optional expanded scheme 14%, on a conventional remuneration tier chosen by the worker: 1, 3, 5, 7 or at least 10 UCSS. If no tier is declared, the one-UCSS tier applies. With 1 UCSS confirmed as STN 1,200 in 2025, the minimum is STN 120/month under the mandatory scheme or STN 168/month under the expanded scheme. The contribution obligation begins with enrollment, with coverage generally effective from the first day of the month following commencement of activity. If the arrangement is instead classified as employment or paid service as a local-company director or manager, employee payroll totals 12% from 2025, split 5% employee and 7% employer. Article 13's temporary-foreign-worker relief appears in the employee regime and requires proof of comparable foreign public coverage; the checked sources do not establish that an ordinary self-employed foreign contractor may claim it, so an exemption should not be assumed without written INSS confirmation.

fixed_payments.status: Confirmed percentage contribution with a conventional-base minimum
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Self-employed: compulsory 10% or optional expanded 14% on the selected conventional remuneration tier. Minimum one-UCSS base is STN 1,200, producing STN 120/month (about USD 5.53) or STN 168/month (about USD 7.74). Employee/local-company payroll, if applicable instead, is 12% of contributory gross pay from 2025.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The accessible SMF portal does not publish a current schedule of residence-visa or residence-card fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Category B taxpayers have registration, invoicing, recordkeeping and annual-return obligations. A 15% withholding payment-on-account applies to certain locally paid Category B income; the checked sources do not establish withholding by a foreign payer.
fixed_payments.notes: The statutory minimum is based on the one-UCSS conventional floor rather than actual foreign-contract revenue. The 10% scheme covers old age, disability and survivors; the 14% scheme adds sickness, parental and funeral cash benefits. Private health-cover costs are contract-specific.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay of 180 days or fewer does not guarantee non-residence because a permanent home or principal professional/business/economic-interest base can independently trigger residence. Work performed physically in the country may also create source and registration issues.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident is taxed within the worldwide-income system. Ordinary remote income has no nomad exemption and may be taxed progressively up to 25%, subject to classification and foreign-tax-credit rules.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect NIF, commencement-of-activity registration, invoices and records, annual returns and compulsory INSS registration. A genuine independent worker chooses a conventional tier and pays 10% or 14%, with a one-UCSS minimum contribution of STN 120 or STN 168 monthly. SMF's additional local-company and premises checklist still requires filing confirmation for a foreign-only contract.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The current INSS page and consolidated regulation resolve the flagged self-employed contribution-rate and minimum-base gap. Remaining questions concern SMF acceptance of a foreign-only contract, classification of the exact working structure and current immigration/card fees.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is the immediate intended result after entry and completion of the in-country certificate process.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Requires five consecutive years of temporary residence, an acceptable criminal record and Portuguese knowledge.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization eligibility begins after five years of legal residence and does not require an additional period after PR.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum if the independent-professional filing is accepted and residence remains continuous; grant is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: DGRN lists service modalities and the law gives the Public Prosecutor 30 days for an opinion, but neither source publishes a reliable end-to-end naturalization processing period.

key_conditions.value: Five years of legal residence; adulthood; sufficient Portuguese or a national language; qualifying criminal record; no terrorism/security threat; and an activity capable of supporting the applicant. Permanent residence separately requires five consecutive years of temporary residence, Portuguese knowledge and no qualifying conviction.
key_conditions.notes: The effect and final enacted status of the 2024 nationality amendment should be checked before filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: More than five years of qualifying marriage; a judicially recognized de facto union requires more than three years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Time in an existing qualifying marriage or de facto union can count if the relationship continues when the declaration is made.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marriage rule is specific about the matrimonial-property regime; obtain advice for foreign marriages.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship requires an application and supporting civil-status and criminal-record documents. A de facto union requires judicial recognition. Fraud or false documents may cause refusal or cancellation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A locally born child is a citizen of origin if a parent is São Toméan, the parents are stateless or unknown under the statutory procedure, or resident foreign parents are not serving their state. Birth to visitors alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Yes if born in São Tomé and Príncipe and both foreign parents reside there and are not serving a foreign state; not established for temporary visitors or nonresident parents.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The law does not specify a minimum parental residence status or duration.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born inside or outside the country can obtain nationality through a São Toméan mother or father, subject to declaration or registration for birth abroad.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. Family members of citizens may be exempt from the prior residence-visa requirement, but treatment of a nondependent parent requires SMF confirmation.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any residence facilitation is separate from citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father may have a facilitated family-residence argument if the child is São Toméan, but citizenship remains nonautomatic and requires an independent statutory basis.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Family definitions and dependency facts require individual review.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: This is not a digital-nomad visa. It is a locally regulated independent-professional residence route requiring tax/INSS and business or service-contract evidence.
settlement_track.summary: If SMF accepts an ordinary foreign-client service contract, this route provides renewable temporary residence, permanent-residence eligibility after five consecutive years and potential naturalization after five years of legal residence. The settlement framework is credible, but acceptance of a foreign-only contract without all live portal company documents needs written confirmation.
settlement_track.notes: Uncertainty concerns initial eligibility for the foreign-contract structure, not the general five-year settlement framework.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Article 58 permits a service contract and does not expressly require a São Toméan client. The live portal nevertheless requests a local company, premises and tax/INSS clearance. SMF must confirm whether a foreign software-services contract plus individual tax and INSS registration is sufficient.

data.notes: Twenty-nine distinct relevant canonical URLs are included, ten outside the previous source set, and more than fifteen directly relevant URLs were inspected during this focused pass. The flagged social-security/payroll gap is substantially resolved: independent workers are compulsorily enrolled at 10% on a conventional remuneration tier or may choose 14% expanded coverage; the one-UCSS minimum produces STN 120 or STN 168 monthly contributions. Selection remains uncertain because SMF does not clearly confirm foreign-only software-service contracts. National salary median, immigration fees and naturalization processing time remain null because the named current sources do not publish those facts.

data.selection_summary: Saudi Arabia has no current dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route. Self-sponsored Premium Residency exists, but its official work rights cover employment in private-sector establishments or commercial activity conducted under the investment framework; they do not expressly authorize unregistered personal software services for a foreign client. Labor rules otherwise require non-Saudis to follow prescribed work-authorization procedures and restrict own-account work. The country therefore does not fit this foreign-contract remote-work selection.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Saudi Arabia has no dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status. Tourist status is expressly not a work visa, and Premium Residency should not be treated as permission for unregistered own-account foreign-client work.
settlement_track.summary: Premium Residency can provide temporary or unlimited-duration residence, but ordinary personal foreign-client work is not expressly authorized without the investment and business-registration framework. Citizenship remains a separate discretionary process, so there is no qualifying remote-work-to-citizenship track.
settlement_track.notes: Paid unlimited-duration residence does not cure the work-authorization mismatch or guarantee naturalization.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The current Premium Residency catalog and law contain no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker category. They permit employment in private-sector establishments and commercial activity under the investment system. MISA states that a foreign investor must register before investment activity and then obtain commercial and activity-specific licenses, while the Labor Law and its implementing regulations restrict non-Saudi own-account work outside prescribed procedures. The tourist eVisa is expressly not a work visa. Consequently, neither Premium Residency nor visitor status alone establishes that an individual may lawfully perform a regular personal software-services contract for a foreign client; doing so through a properly registered Saudi investment/business structure would be a materially different entrepreneur or business route.

data.notes: Focused audit completed using more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including ten canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. The prior rejection remains supported. The flagged wage fields now use null rather than placeholder text because no universal national minimum amount, national median, or national maximum is published in the reviewed current official materials; occupation-specific Saudization thresholds are explicitly distinguished from a national minimum wage. The duplicate previous source id was also resolved.

data.selection_summary: No current dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or independently accessible freelance residence route was found. The expatriate-contract process is employer-initiated, while sole-proprietor registration requires the foreigner already to reside in Senegal and does not confer immigration status. Although ordinary discretionary naturalization exists after 10 years of qualifying residence, no qualifying entry route for this foreign-contract remote-worker profile was confirmed.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax domicile arises through a permanent home or principal stay in Senegal, non-incidental professional activity there, or the center of economic interests. The cited code does not use a standalone 183-day test.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breakers may override domestic rules.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share of the general IPRES pension scheme for local salaried work. Executives additionally pay 2.4% under the complementary scheme; health contributions vary. Current sources place independent workers outside mandatory coverage except optional arrangements.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly nomad or self-employed social contribution was established. A qualifying individual service business under CGU instead has an annual XOF 30,000 tax floor; that annual amount is not converted into a supposed monthly nomad payment. A June 2026 report describes proposed social-security expansion to independent workers, but no enacted contribution schedule was found.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or special inbound personal-tax regime was found. Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on Senegal-source income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business tax, VAT, and withholding depend on registration and contract structure.

taxes.caveats: Work physically performed in Senegal may be Senegal-source even when paid abroad. Tax domicile can arise without waiting for a numeric day threshold. Senegalese advice is needed on treaties, permanent establishment, VAT, contract classification, and any post-2013 amendments.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax from 0% to 40%; residents are taxed on Senegalese and foreign income and non-residents on Senegal-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home or principal stay, non-incidental professional activity, or center of economic interests in Senegal.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or tax category exists. Anyone working physically from Senegal must analyze ordinary resident/non-resident income and business rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated category; ordinary employment, professional-income, or local-business taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 0%–40%; 40% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: A permanent home/principal stay, non-incidental professional activity, or center of economic interests can create tax domicile.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is taxable for Senegal tax domiciliaries, subject to treaties; non-residents are taxable on Senegal-source income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory digital-nomad payment applies because Senegal has no such route. For a qualifying locally registered individual service business, the cited tax code instead imposes annual turnover-based CGU, with an XOF 30,000 annual minimum for individual service providers; this is neither a monthly charge nor evidence of immigration eligibility.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Under the current sources, independent workers are not mandatorily covered and may obtain voluntary accident or private-mutual health coverage. A June 2026 parliamentary report proposes extending coverage, but no enacted independent-worker contribution schedule was established.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The foreigner identity-card procedure lists an XOF 15,000 stamp plus a variable repatriation deposit. Successful naturalization carries XOF 100,000 in chancery rights.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Sole-proprietor setup costs are XOF 16,000–26,000 through the Chamber of Commerce or XOF 10,000–20,000 through APIX; NINEA is free apart from an XOF 1,000 stamp. Eligible CGU service providers face turnover-based annual tax with an XOF 30,000 annual floor.
fixed_payments.notes: The amounts belong to different procedures and must not be aggregated as a nomad-visa fee. CGU eligibility and the effect of later amendments require DGID confirmation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe day-count exemption is established: professional activity, home, principal stay, or economic interests may create domicile, while Senegal-source income may be taxable for non-residents.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide income is subject to ordinary progressive tax up to 40%, subject to treaty relief and contract classification.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registration can trigger income tax, CGU or real-regime tax, VAT, withholding, and filing obligations depending on turnover, activity, and legal form.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Hypothetical tax treatment is not evidence that immigration law authorizes foreign-contract remote work.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No independently accessible qualifying remote-work residence route was found.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No official permanent-residence transition period was established for the examined statuses.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is residence-based rather than a published permanent-residence-plus-years sequence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General discretionary naturalization period, not a timeline available through a qualifying remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The procedure states one year after the filing receipt; actual discretionary processing may vary.

key_conditions.value: Applicant must be at least 18 and provide evidence of qualifying residence, civil and criminal records, residence certificate, medical examination, good-life-and-morals certificate, and tax status. Naturalization is by decree and, if approved, costs XOF 100,000.
key_conditions.notes: No formal language test, absence limit, or mandatory renunciation rule is stated in the inspected procedure.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Five years of married common life from celebration or legal recognition.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing valid marriage can count from its celebration or legal recognition if five years of common life are completed, the marriage remains undissolved, and the Senegalese spouse retains nationality.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The official procedure is gender-neutral.

requirements_and_risks.value: Civil-status documents, proof of the spouse's citizenship, non-renunciation documentation, and residence evidence are required. Continued marriage and common life are conditions; separation, dissolution, false documents, or a sham arrangement may defeat eligibility and create legal risk.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The stated two-day certificate-processing period does not replace the five-year common-life requirement.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Senegal combines descent with conditional territorial acquisition, including birth in Senegal where a parent was also born there. Birth alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born to two first-generation foreign parents is not Senegalese merely by birth. Conditional acquisition may apply when a parent was also born in Senegal, subject to proof and legal exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean assumes neither parent is Senegalese and both were born abroad.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is Senegalese when either parent is Senegalese, whether born in or outside marriage and in Senegal or abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2013 reform removed the former gender distinction.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Senegalese child does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. A parent married to a Senegalese citizen may use the separate five-year marriage route; no parent-of-citizen permanent-residence shortcut was confirmed.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic parental status follows from the child's citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father is not automatically Senegalese because his child is Senegalese. If married to the Senegalese mother, the separate marriage route may apply after five years of common life; a benefit based solely on fatherhood was not established.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required count; eVisa destinations are excluded from its mobility score.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 28 visa-on-arrival plus 3 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Counts and rank change with entry rules; one index methodology is used consistently.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only living is possible in some international settings in Dakar but is not broadly practical for administration or integration. French is official, and Senegal's 2025 EF EPI score of 442 was in the very-low band.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI reflects test participants, not a population census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither language is official, and no inspected source established widespread Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services. French is strongly advisable.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No quantitative proficiency data was located.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the ANSD Q2 2018 national employee median of XOF 54,000. The statistic is historical and should not be treated as a current median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the January 2026 XOF 64,233 monthly SMIG; this is a statutory floor.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the ANSD XOF 122,123 mean monthly salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate current-currency conversion of the exact official Q2 2018 median; the underlying statistic is historical.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The checked sources publish means, a historical median, brackets, aggregate payroll, or earnings-variable metadata but no finite national maximum or representative upper endpoint. A sample outlier maximum would not be a meaningful national wage statistic.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: January 2026 statutory SMIG. CLEISS also states the underlying XOF 371 gross hourly rate for a 40-hour week.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean monthly salary from the nationally representative EHCVM II 2021/2022 survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: ANSD ENES Q2 2018 national median for salaried workers. It resolves the previous marker but is historical and not directly comparable to the broader 2021/2022 survey mean.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: ANSD and ILO materials checked publish means, a historical median, brackets or microdata metadata, and aggregate payroll, but no finite national maximum salary or defined representative upper endpoint. The value remains null rather than inventing a ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly SMIG for the minimum; national household-survey mean for the average; national salaried-worker median for the historical median
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum: January 2026 guide; average: 2021/2022 survey; median: Q2 2018 ENES
average_citizen_salary.notes: The figures have different periods and populations. USD conversions use the cited BCEAO rate and are approximate. No official national maximum or defined upper wage endpoint was published.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No sufficiently current official national cost-of-living amount was established; no speculative expatriate budget is supplied.
