settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor entry, business registration, and employer-controlled contract approval are not independent citizenship-path routes for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.
settlement_track.summary: Senegal has a general 10-year discretionary naturalization route for qualifying residents, but no independently accessible ordinary remote-worker residence route was confirmed. A materially different basis such as sponsored employment, study, or family status is required first.
settlement_track.notes: No permanent-residence conversion timeline was located, and visitor time must not be assumed to count.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated foreign-remote-worker status was found. Employer approval is not independent, and sole-proprietor registration requires prior residence without granting immigration status.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous Senegal record. Thirty-one distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected, including nine URLs outside the previous source set. The audit resolved the median-salary marker with ANSD's published Q2 2018 median, retained an explained null for the unpublished/non-meaningful national maximum, clarified why visitor presence cannot be credited toward naturalization, and distinguished the annual CGU floor from any nonexistent monthly nomad payment.

data.selection_summary: Serbia is a match through the active self-employment single-permit route, not through a dedicated digital-nomad permit. A foreigner can register a Serbian sole proprietorship using a passport, then independently seek a D visa/single temporary residence-and-work permit without a Serbian employer or local client. Ordinary temporary residence can qualify for permanent residence after three continuous years and subsequently for ordinary naturalisation. The enabling law mentions digital nomads, but the government's 2026 work plan schedules the regulation establishing that category's criteria for December 2026, so it is not currently treated as operational.

visa_application.title: eForeigner — Portal for Foreign Nationals
visa_application.notes: This is the official electronic application portal. For the usable route, select employment and then self-employment after registering a Serbian sole proprietorship or company. Applicants who require a visa normally apply for a D visa on the same basis before the single permit.

best_routes.route_name: Self-employment single permit through a Serbian sole proprietorship

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly income threshold is published for the self-employment subcategory. The decisive immigration document is the Serbian business-registration certificate; the authority may request further evidence.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed RSD income threshold is published in the current official self-employment checklist.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income threshold; prior Serbian sole-proprietor or company registration is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Serbian Business Registers Agency registration certificate
income_requirement_display.notes: Serbia's statutory minimum wage and general tax bases are not immigration-income thresholds. The official self-employment checklist does not publish a minimum revenue, salary or bank-balance amount.

income_proof_months.notes: The official self-employment checklist does not prescribe a fixed number of bank-statement or income-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: Register as a sole proprietor, shareholder, or sole/controlling owner in the Serbian Business Registers Agency before relying on the self-employment immigration basis.
A foreign individual may use a passport or foreign identity document for sole-proprietor registration; registration also produces a business number and Serbian tax identification number.

Submit the visa or single-permit application with a valid passport, photograph, Serbian registration certificate, invitation documentation where applicable, accommodation evidence and prescribed fees.
Maintain genuine registered business activity, tax filings, social-insurance compliance and the residence basis throughout the permit period.

initial_validity.value: Up to three years
initial_validity.notes: The exact period depends on the documented basis and the authority's decision. A D visa, when required, covers 90–180 days before transition to the single permit.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for up to another three years while the self-employment basis continues; file no earlier than three months before expiry and no later than expiry
extension_rules.notes: A timely applicant may remain and work while the administrative procedure is pending.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Register the Serbian business, then independently apply electronically for a D visa if required and/or a self-employment single temporary residence-and-work permit
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visa-exempt nationals may generally submit the single-permit request during lawful stay or from abroad; filing details depend on nationality.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Apply after three continuous years of approved temporary residence or single permits, subject to actual-residence and absence limits
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Across the three-year period, multiple absences may total no more than ten months, or a single absence no more than six months.

path_to_citizenship.value: After obtaining permanent residence and completing the ordinary naturalisation conditions, including three years of continuously registered domicile
path_to_citizenship.notes: A conservative sequential estimate is approximately six years from initial temporary residence. Ordinary applicants generally need release from prior citizenship or proof/statement addressing release, unless a statutory exception applies.

best_routes.notes: This route fits ordinary foreign-client software work because self-employment is based on registration of the applicant's own Serbian business and does not require a Serbian employer or local customer. It requires genuine local business registration, accounting, tax and social-insurance compliance. It is settlement-oriented because it produces an ordinary single temporary residence-and-work permit whose time is not excluded from the three-year permanent-residence rule.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No implemented digital-nomad criteria or income threshold are currently published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The implementing regulation intended to establish detailed criteria is scheduled for December 2026.

income_requirement_display.value: Not currently established—the implementing regulation is pending
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Criteria to be established by government regulation
income_requirement_display.notes: The promotional portal page is insufficient evidence of an operational immigration category when the current government work plan still schedules the underlying regulation for December 2026.

income_proof_months.notes: No number of months can currently be stated. Article 40(4) of the Law on Foreigners delegates category-specific criteria to a Government act; the 2026 Government Work Plan schedules that act for December 2026; the current official digital-nomad page is promotional and contains no application checklist; and the current MUP temporary-residence and single-permit materials publish no digital-nomad income-evidence lookback period. The duration is therefore unpublished because category-specific implementing rules are not yet in force, not because a discretionary or applicant-specific period was identified.

key_requirements.requirement: The Law on Foreigners authorises the government to establish categories and detailed criteria that may include digital nomads.
The 2026 Government Work Plan schedules the regulation covering digital nomads and other special-interest categories for December 2026.

initial_validity.notes: No current category-specific duration is published. The general law's maximum of three years should not be presented as an implemented digital-nomad entitlement.

extension_rules.notes: Category-specific digital-nomad renewal rules have not been published because the implementing regulation remains pending.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Pending implementation; use another active legal basis such as registered self-employment
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The official portal describes Serbia as a destination for digital nomads but does not provide category-specific eligibility criteria or an application checklist.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: If an ordinary digital-nomad temporary permit is implemented later, the general permanent-residence rule may become relevant, but that possibility cannot be treated as a current route.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No operational digital-nomad residence category exists from which a settlement timeline can currently be calculated.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected as a current route. The enabling law permits the government to create a digital-nomad category, but the current work plan schedules the regulation defining its criteria for December 2026.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration-income threshold is material because the route fails the local-client test.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official route information does not specify a fixed RSD income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold published; a direct contract with a Serbian employer or end user is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is distinct from registering one's own Serbian business under self-employment.

income_proof_months.notes: The official checklist does not prescribe an income-history lookback period; eligibility instead depends on the required Serbian employer or end-user contract and professional evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign independent-professional registration, direct contract with a Serbian employer or end user, degree or technical qualification, and professional-experience evidence.

initial_validity.value: Up to three years under the general single-permit rules

extension_rules.value: Renewable while the qualifying local engagement continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Single permit based on the Serbian client engagement

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General three-year continuous-residence rule may apply

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary permanent-residence and naturalisation rules

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because a direct Serbian employer or end-user contract is mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Compensation and labor-law requirements depend on the local employment contract.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The statutory minimum wage is not an independent-application income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Serbian employment contract required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: At least applicable Serbian labor-law minimums

income_proof_months.notes: An income-history lookback period is inapplicable because eligibility is based on a current Serbian employment contract rather than past foreign income.

key_requirements.requirement: Serbian employer, employment contract and any required labor-market procedure.

initial_validity.value: Up to three years

extension_rules.value: Renewable while employment continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Single temporary residence-and-work permit

path_to_permanent_residence.value: General three-year continuous-residence rule may apply

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary permanent-residence and naturalisation rules

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a Serbian employer even though the foreigner may technically submit their own application.

summary.value: Admission to an accredited Serbian education program can support temporary residence without an employer. It is not an ordinary remote-work route, does not grant permanent residence directly, and study time counts only one-half toward the three-year permanent-residence period after changing to another basis. Talent and highly qualified special-interest categories should not be treated as currently operational substitutes because their detailed government regulation is scheduled for December 2026.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing degree alone does not create an independent residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is Serbian tax resident if they have residence or a centre of business and life interests in Serbia, or spend at least 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending in the relevant tax year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence may arise before day 183 through the residence or centre-of-interests test. Treaty tie-breaker rules can change the final result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the base tax rate on taxable self-employment profit or administratively determined flat-rate income. It is not the complete effective burden because social contributions and, at sufficiently high income, annual personal income tax can also apply.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Headline self-employment contribution rates are 24% pension/disability, 10.3% health and 0.75% unemployment. The actual base, minimum base, caps, other-insurance status and flat-rate decision affect the amount paid.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No single universal monthly USD payment exists. Flat-rate entrepreneur liabilities depend on activity, municipality and the Tax Administration decision; book-keeping entrepreneurs depend on their selected salary/profit structure and contribution bases.

special_tax_regimes.value: Registered entrepreneurs may be taxed on actual taxable profit or, if eligible, on administratively determined flat-rate income. A separate quarterly freelancer self-assessment system offers 20% or 10% models for certain income paid without Serbian withholding, but a residence applicant operating a registered Serbian sole proprietorship should not assume that the freelancer regime replaces entrepreneur taxation.
special_tax_regimes.notes: No general digital-nomad tax holiday was confirmed.

taxes.caveats: The practical burden depends on whether the applicant registers as a flat-rate entrepreneur, keeps books, elects a personal salary, satisfies Serbia's entrepreneur-independence test, has other health coverage, crosses the VAT threshold, becomes tax resident, or can claim treaty/foreign-tax relief. Obtain Serbian tax advice before invoicing through the new business.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: 10% self-employment income tax, mandatory social contributions, and an additional progressive annual personal-income tax for high-income individuals.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence or centre of business/life interests, or 183 days in a relevant 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on Serbian and foreign income; nonresidents are taxed on Serbian-source income, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Actual-profit or flat-rate entrepreneur taxation; separate quarterly freelancer models; no confirmed digital-nomad holiday.
taxation_system.social_security: For entrepreneurs, headline rates are 24% pension/disability, 10.3% health and 0.75% unemployment, applied to the legally determined base and subject to minimums/caps and coverage exceptions.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 15% figure is the top marginal rate of the additional annual personal-income tax, not the expected effective rate. Ordinary self-employment profit or flat-rate income is taxed at 10%, with contributions added separately. Annual personal-income tax applies only after a statutory high-income threshold tied to average annual salary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable self-employment profit or administratively determined flat-rate income
tax_brackets.notes: Principal business-income rate before contributions and any annual high-income tax.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual personal-income-tax base up to 6× the average annual salary, after the statutory entry threshold and deductions
tax_brackets.notes: The annual tax threshold is formula-based and changes with official salary data.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual personal-income-tax base above 6× the average annual salary
tax_brackets.applies_to: Top slice of additional annual personal income tax
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate; not a flat rate on all income.

taxation_system.notes: The 10% route-level income-tax rate and 15% top annual marginal rate serve different purposes. Neither includes mandatory social contributions.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No operational dedicated digital-nomad immigration or tax regime was confirmed. For the selected self-employment route, use Serbian entrepreneur taxation: normally 10% on taxable profit or flat-rate income, social contributions, and possible additional annual personal income tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Registered Serbian sole proprietor under the self-employment residence route
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% self-employment income tax; up to 15% additional annual high-income tax; contributions extra
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence/centre of interests or at least 183 days in a qualifying 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Serbian tax residents are taxable on worldwide income. Income invoiced through the Serbian business is Serbian self-employment income; treaty credits may prevent double taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No active digital-nomad tax holiday confirmed. Quarterly freelancer models exist but should not automatically be substituted for registered-entrepreneur taxation.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Headline entrepreneur contribution rates total 35.05% on the applicable base: 24% pension/disability, 10.3% health and 0.75% unemployment. Minimum bases, caps and other-insurance status matter.

fixed_payments.status: variable_not_single_fixed_amount
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Monthly or periodic entrepreneur liabilities depend on the tax method, official contribution base, municipality/activity and Tax Administration decision; no universal amount was established.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: D visa: EUR 50 when required. Portal information lists an RSD 430 submission fee plus RSD 22,770 for a single permit. Sole-proprietor registration is RSD 2,500 under the current Serbian-language APR fee page.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Mandatory VAT registration generally starts once turnover exceeds RSD 8,000,000 in the preceding 12 months. Accounting, bank and local administrative costs are variable.
fixed_payments.notes: An older English APR page showed a lower amount, but the current Serbian page and APR's 2026 fee-change notice support RSD 2,500. Confirm all fees in the portal immediately before filing.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying under 183 days does not guarantee nonresidence because a Serbian residence or centre of business/life interests can independently create tax residence. Work performed in Serbia may also be Serbian-source income.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A Serbian tax resident generally reports worldwide income. Operating through the registered sole proprietorship normally produces Serbian self-employment income taxed at 10% on the applicable base, plus contributions and possible annual high-income tax.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Registering the sole proprietorship triggers tax, social-insurance, bookkeeping or flat-rate obligations regardless of whether customers are foreign. VAT, entrepreneur-independence and foreign-exchange rules require case-specific review.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This block describes the selected self-employment route because the dedicated digital-nomad category remains pending. It is not an effective-tax calculation.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The single permit itself is temporary residence and work authorization once approved; there is no preliminary multi-year qualifying period.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Requires continuous actual residence, a valid permit when applying, sufficient means, insurance and compliance with the absence limits.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation requires permanent residence and at least three years of continuously registered domicile. A conservative reading treats this as sequential to permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Conservative estimate of three years to permanent residence plus three years of registered domicile for ordinary naturalisation. Administrative processing and any time needed to secure release from prior citizenship are additional.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: An official Serbian embassy states a usual range of three to nine months; six months is the midpoint used for display. Serbia's citizenship law does not prescribe a universal decision deadline.

key_conditions.value: Maintain genuine self-employment and lawful actual residence; keep total absences within the permanent-residence limits; obtain permanent residence; maintain registered domicile; remain tax and legal compliant; be an adult with legal capacity; declare Serbia to be one's state; and ordinarily obtain release from prior citizenship or qualify for an exception.
key_conditions.notes: The cited ordinary-naturalisation provisions do not publish a Serbian-language or civics-test requirement.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The spouse must have been in a marital union with a Serbian citizen for at least three years and must already hold Serbian permanent residence.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine marriage that already existed can contribute toward the three-year marital-union period; the statute does not say the entire period must occur in Serbia. Permanent residence is still required before applying.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Documentary recognition of a foreign marriage and proof that the marital union is continuing may be required.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage route removes several ordinary-naturalisation conditions, including the ordinary three-year registered-domicile and release requirements, but it does not remove the need for permanent residence, three years in the marital union, and a written declaration that Serbia is considered the applicant's state. Family residence may be refused where evidence indicates a marriage of convenience, such as no shared life, no prior meeting, false personal information, no common language, payment for marriage or previous sham marriages.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage never guarantees approval, and false evidence can cause refusal or later legal consequences.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Serbia is primarily jus sanguinis. Birth or finding in Serbia gives citizenship only where both parents are unknown, of unknown citizenship or stateless, or where the child would otherwise be stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Serbia to two foreign migrant parents does not ordinarily become Serbian. Citizenship at birth applies only under the narrow anti-statelessness, unknown-parent or foundling rules.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: If either foreign parent's nationality passes to the child, Serbian birth alone is insufficient.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is Serbian and the child is born in Serbia, the child acquires Serbian citizenship by descent. For birth abroad to one Serbian and one foreign parent, timely registration or later application rules apply.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The result does not depend on whether the Serbian parent is the mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Serbian-citizen minor can support a foreign parent's family-reunification residence as a parent or close family member, but parent residence and citizenship remain separate applications. A minor with one permanent-resident parent can qualify for permanent residence in a special case, but that rule benefits the child, not automatically the other parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No automatic parent citizenship follows from the child's status.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is Serbian, the child can be Serbian and the migrant father may seek family-reunification residence based on parenthood and genuine family life. He does not automatically obtain permanent residence or citizenship and must follow the applicable residence or spousal-naturalisation route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage, custody, family life, accommodation and authenticity may need documentation.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15. Rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free-only category. Its broader mobility score is 133 after adding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's advance-visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 42 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 6 eTA destinations. Separately, Henley listed Serbia at rank 34 with access to 135 destinations under Henley's broader prior-visa-free methodology.

passport.notes: Passport Index is used for the category breakdown because Henley does not expose visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA and visa-required counts separately on its ranking page. Different indexes use different destination universes and methodologies.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Practical in Belgrade, Novi Sad and the technology/remote-work community. The government relocation portal says English is widely spoken and that many professional events are held in English, although Serbian remains important for administration, accounting and long-term integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The government page is promotional rather than a population-language proficiency survey.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is more practical than Ukrainian for initial navigation because the official Welcome to Serbia portal offers a Russian interface. No equivalent official Ukrainian interface or reliable nationwide Ukrainian-language service evidence was found; Serbian or English should be expected for filings and professional services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practicality assessment based on official portal language support, not a claim that Russian has official status.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The dedicated digital-nomad category is not the selected route and remains pending detailed regulation. Settlement depends on obtaining and maintaining the active self-employment single permit.
settlement_track.summary: The active self-employment single permit is ordinary temporary residence, so three years of continuous actual residence can lead to permanent residence. Ordinary naturalisation is then available under the permanent-resident rule, conservatively producing an approximately six-year citizenship track before processing.
settlement_track.notes: No switch away from self-employment is required before applying for permanent residence, although permanent residence itself is a required later status for ordinary naturalisation.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The fit comes from registering and operating the applicant's own Serbian sole proprietorship. The self-employment route does not require a Serbian employer or local client, so the business may serve foreign customers, but genuine registration, local compliance and entrepreneur tax rules are mandatory.

data.notes: This focused unresolved-field pass inspected 17 directly relevant URLs, including five new official URLs not in the previous source set. The dedicated digital-nomad category still lacks its category-specific implementing act and therefore has no published income-proof lookback period; the operational self-employment single-permit route remains the valid independent settlement path. Other cautious nulls remain limited to variable or unpublished facts, including the absence of a fixed self-employment immigration-income threshold, variable entrepreneur payments and an unpublished national maximum wage.

data.selection_summary: Seychelles offers a Visitors Workcation Permit for foreign employees, freelancers and business owners, but it is visitor status lasting 30 days to one year. The Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2023 expressly excludes a visitor’s permit from the definition of legal residence, so Workcation time cannot count toward naturalisation. The separate self-employed Gainful Occupation Permit requires a Seychelles business proposal, local approvals and licensing and is not a clean continuation route for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

visa_application.title: Visitors Workcation Permit application
visa_application.notes: The current official Tourism Seychelles page directs applicants to this portal and says to apply at least 60 days before arrival. The portal URL responded but exposed no machine-readable application content during this audit; manually verify that it accepts a new Workcation Permit application before paying or arranging travel.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official route page requires proof of income or wealth but publishes no fixed minimum.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed SCR amount published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official route information does not prescribe a minimum amount in Seychelles rupees.

income_requirement_display.value: Proof of foreign employment or self-employment and proof of income or wealth; no fixed threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: Applicants should obtain filing-level confirmation of the documents and financial evidence currently accepted by the portal.

income_proof_months.notes: Neither the official route page nor the accessible portal content specifies an income-history lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport and evidence of being an employee, company or business owner, or freelancer.
Proof of income or wealth and valid medical and travel insurance.
Apply for the Workcation Permit at least 60 days before arrival and complete the Seychelles e-Border entry process after validation.

initial_validity.value: 30 days to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The applicant chooses a temporary workcation period within this range, subject to approval.

extension_rules.value: No renewal beyond the program's one-year maximum was confirmed
extension_rules.notes: Ordinary visitor permits can reach 12 months through extensions, but those extensions do not authorize employment and are not a settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying temporary-residence conversion is published
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The program is a Visitors Workcation Permit, not a residence permit. Obtaining another permit requires a separate qualifying basis and application.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate investment-based PR route exists after five years of qualifying residence and business association. It requires a substantial investment and does not rely on Workcation visitor time.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is a changed investment/business profile, not a confirmed ordinary remote-worker successor. The old tourism Workcation page returned no readable rules, and the old Workcation application URL now displays the generic border portal. Current programme operation and the in-country transition procedure therefore need confirmation; PR investment rules are clearly published.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path from this permit: the Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2023 defines a legal resident as a person residing under an Immigration Decree permit but expressly excludes a visitor’s permit, so Visitors Workcation Permit time does not count as legal residence for naturalisation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A later switch to a non-visitor permit would begin a separate qualifying-residence analysis; the Workcation Permit itself supplies no residence credit.

rejected_routes.notes: This route fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work for temporary living only. It fails the citizenship-oriented selection because it is visitor status, is limited to one year and has no published bridge to qualifying residence or permanent residence; current law expressly prevents its time from counting as legal residence for citizenship.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No personal-income threshold is published; approval is based on the proposed Seychelles business and regulatory requirements.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed personal-income threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Permit and business costs apply separately.

income_requirement_display.value: No nomad-income threshold; Seychelles business proposal, approvals and licensing required
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Local business approval rather than income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: SCR 1,000 processing fee plus SCR 500 per approved permit month on the current Immigration page
income_requirement_display.notes: Other licensing, medical, bond, registration and business costs may apply.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard foreign-income lookback is published because this is a locally regulated business and work permit.

key_requirements.requirement: A self-employed applicant signs their own GOP application, but a person setting up a business must first submit a Project Memorandum to the Seychelles Investment Board.
Local employment approval is generally employer-led; self-employed people are exceptions only in specific areas.
Local business registration, licensing, qualifications and other activity-specific approvals may be required.

initial_validity.value: Duration approved in the GOP application
initial_validity.notes: The current Immigration page charges SCR 500 for each month or part of a month sought but does not state a universal maximum duration.

extension_rules.value: Extension follows the same approval procedure as a new GOP or variation
extension_rules.notes: Continued business and regulatory approval is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The GOP itself permits gainful occupation for its approved duration
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a work permit tied to the approved Seychelles activity, not an unrestricted remote-work residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate permanent-residence application may exist, but no automatic GOP duration or entitlement is published
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official permanent-residence page lists general conditions and rights but no ordinary years-based GOP entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: GOP residence may potentially constitute legal residence because it is not a visitor’s permit, but general naturalisation requires 15 aggregate years and no route-specific entitlement is published
path_to_citizenship.notes: No official source establishes that a foreign-client-only software consultancy would be approved, that every GOP period necessarily counts, or that GOP holders acquire citizenship automatically after 15 years.

rejected_routes.notes: Independent filing is technically possible for an approved self-employed Seychelles business. It does not match an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker because it requires local business substance, investment-board review and regulatory approval rather than merely retaining a foreign client.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence Permit based on family connection or special contribution

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Financial status and bank confirmation are required, but no minimum income is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No minimum income published; SCR 150,000 permit fee for the main applicant for 5 years
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A bank guarantee of at least SCR 20,000 is also required.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold; documentary financial evidence, SCR 150,000 five-year fee and at least SCR 20,000 bank guarantee
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: SCR 150,000 permit fee plus at least SCR 20,000 bank guarantee
income_requirement_display.notes: Using the permit for business additionally requires a GOP.

income_proof_months.notes: The current official page does not prescribe a bank-statement lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: Family or domestic connection with Seychelles, or a special economic, social or cultural contribution.
Documentary financial evidence and a bank guarantee of at least SCR 20,000.
The permit does not authorize gainful occupation; a separate GOP is required to establish a business.

initial_validity.value: 5 years for the published SCR 150,000 main-applicant fee
initial_validity.notes: Approval remains discretionary.

extension_rules.notes: The current official page states the five-year permit fee but does not publish renewal eligibility, procedure or fees.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct five-year residence permit if the discretionary family or special-contribution criteria are met
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not authorize work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic transition or qualifying period is published
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence must be assessed separately.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential legal-residence relevance under the general naturalisation law, but no route-specific citizenship entitlement or conversion is published
path_to_citizenship.notes: The special-contribution or family basis and separate prohibition on work prevent treating this as an ordinary remote-worker citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: This is not a degree-based or ordinary remote-worker route. Its special-contribution criterion is discretionary, and it expressly prohibits gainful occupation without a GOP.

summary.value: A non-Seychellois accepted by an approved local educational institution may apply for a Student Permit without an employer. It costs SCR 1,000 to process and SCR 1,500 per year or part-year, but it does not authorize work and provides no published direct path to permanent residence.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing university degree creates no independent residence entitlement; this option requires new local study and is not a remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is a Seychelles resident person if they reside there, are domiciled there without a permanent abode abroad, or are present for at least 183 days in any 12-month period commencing or ending in a tax year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 183-day rule is not the only test. Residence and domicile can matter independently.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: 30% is the top marginal rate, not an expected effective rate. It applies to the portion of a non-citizen employed person’s monthly taxable emoluments above SCR 83,333; the published lower bands are 15% through SCR 10,000 and 20% on the portion from SCR 10,000.01 through SCR 83,333. The reviewed SRC pages and Income Tax Act do not create a Workcation-specific tax category or state that foreign-employer remuneration earned while physically in Seychelles is exempt; a freelancer may instead fall under business-tax rules, so the correct route-specific effective rate cannot be reduced to one percentage without SRC classification.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the mandatory self-employed pension contribution rate where local self-employment registration applies, generally calculated on verified salary or profit or turnover with a minimum-wage floor. No official source confirms that a temporary Workcation Permit holder without local registration owes this contribution.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax or social payment applies across the workcation scenario. The GOP has an SCR 500 monthly permit fee; self-employed pension is percentage-based rather than a fixed USD sum.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or Workcation Permit income-tax exemption was found. Seychelles describes its business-tax system as territorial, but services performed physically in Seychelles can be Seychelles-source income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A route marketed for remote work should not be assumed to create a tax holiday.

taxes.caveats: Immigration permission, tax residence and income sourcing are separate questions. A foreign contract does not by itself make services performed from Seychelles foreign-source. Obtain Seychelles Revenue Commission advice on employment-versus-business classification, treaty relief, payroll obligations and whether temporary physical presence creates Seychelles-source income.

taxation_system.value: Mixed territorial and progressive system: employment income uses progressive monthly rates, while local business income can fall under presumptive or progressive business-tax rules.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence, domicile, or at least 183 days in any relevant 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Seychelles-source income is taxable. Under the Business Tax Act, service fees for services performed in Seychelles are Seychelles-source; resident business income is generally Seychelles-source unless attributable to an overseas permanent establishment.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No Workcation Permit exemption was identified. Businesses below SCR 1 million annual turnover may qualify for 1.5% presumptive tax on turnover; otherwise sole traders have progressive business-tax rates.
taxation_system.social_security: Local employees generally have employee and employer pension contributions; registered self-employed people contribute 10% subject to the statutory calculation floor. Applicability to a workcation visitor without local registration is not specified by the reviewed pension or Workcation sources.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For a non-citizen employee, published monthly rates are 15% through SCR 10,000, 20% for the portion from SCR 10,000.01 through SCR 83,333, and 30% above SCR 83,333. The displayed 30% is the top marginal screening rate, not the effective rate.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses the Central Bank's 9 July 2026 draft mid-rate of SCR 14.5513 per USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Non-citizen employed person; rate applies to income within this band
tax_brackets.notes: The USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold, not tax due.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Non-citizen employed person; top marginal band
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: The 30% dashboard figure is only the top marginal non-citizen employment-income rate. Official general tax sources establish the rate schedule, but none reviewed classifies foreign-employer or foreign-client income specifically under the Visitors Workcation Permit.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special Workcation Permit tax exemption is published. Potential liability depends on residence, whether services performed from Seychelles are Seychelles-source, and whether the person is treated as an employee or as carrying on business.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary visitor or workcation remote worker; no dedicated tax category is published
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% top marginal employment-income rate if treated as taxable non-citizen employment income; business-tax treatment may apply to freelancers
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence or domicile tests, or at least 183 days in any relevant 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign payment location is not decisive. The Business Tax Act treats fees for services performed in Seychelles as Seychelles-source, so remote services may be taxable even when the client is abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: The reviewed Workcation, SRC and tax-law sources publish no Workcation-specific exemption, tax holiday or inbound-worker regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The reviewed sources publish no route-specific exemption or mandatory contribution rule. Local self-employed registration can trigger a 10% pension contribution, while local employment generally involves payroll withholding and pension contributions.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly Workcation tax or contribution is prescribed in the reviewed route and tax sources
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed payment for the temporary route is specified; locally registered self-employed members generally pay 10% with a minimum-wage floor.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Official tourism information lists €10 standard or €30 premium Workcation Permit processing. A self-employed GOP separately costs SCR 1,000 to process plus SCR 500 per approved month.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Local businesses must register with SRC; mandatory VAT registration begins at SCR 2 million taxable supplies, while voluntary registration starts at SCR 100,000 subject to conditions.
fixed_payments.notes: Health and travel insurance are mandatory for the Workcation route, but the government does not prescribe a fixed premium.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being under 183 days does not automatically eliminate tax: services physically performed in Seychelles may still be Seychelles-source. Treaty and employment-classification review is needed.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days, or where another residence test is met, expect Seychelles tax analysis and possible registration or filing; no nomad exemption is published.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally approved sole trader may face 1.5% presumptive tax below SCR 1 million turnover or ordinary business-tax bands, plus a generally applicable 10% self-employed pension contribution and possible VAT obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The unresolved point is Workcation-specific classification, not the general statutory schedules. SRC’s current FAQ and income-tax materials publish employee and business rates but no Workcation exemption or dedicated filing rule; obtain written SRC advice for the actual contract structure.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The Workcation Permit is visitor status rather than qualifying legal residence. Switching to a Residence Permit or GOP requires an independent basis and approval.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No Workcation-to-permanent-residence transition or ordinary years-based entitlement is published, and the Citizenship Act excludes visitor-permit time from legal residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Official sources state general naturalisation residence conditions but do not publish a separate automatic waiting period measured from permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: There is no citizenship timeline from the Workcation Permit because the Citizenship Act excludes a visitor’s permit from legal residence. General naturalisation has separate requirements after qualifying non-visitor residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current citizenship pages and Immigration guidelines index do not publish a typical or guaranteed naturalisation processing time.

key_conditions.value: General naturalisation requires 15 aggregate years of legal residence, at least 80% on a citizenship examination in English, French or Kreol, no imprisonment of one year or more, and no continuous absence exceeding one year without ministerial permission. Current law defines legal residence to exclude a visitor’s permit, so Workcation time does not satisfy the residence requirement.
key_conditions.notes: Eligibility remains an application under the Citizenship Act rather than an automatic grant after 15 years.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The enacted Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2023 changed the spouse rule to 15 years of marriage and an aggregate 2 years of legal residence. The Immigration FAQ still displays the superseded 10-year marriage and 5-year residence formulation, so the Act and current acquisition page are preferred.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Seychelles citizen can support a Dependant's Permit and a later naturalisation application once 15 years of marriage and an aggregate 2 years of qualifying legal residence are met. Marriage to another migrant does not accelerate either spouse's citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A Dependant's Permit does not authorize work; a GOP is required for employment.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship is not automatic through marriage. Under the enacted 2023 amendment, the applicant must document 15 years of marriage and an aggregate 2 years of legal residence, pass the citizenship examination with at least 80%, and satisfy criminal-record and absence conditions. False documentation or a sham relationship can result in refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The Immigration FAQ's 10-year and 5-year formulation is inconsistent with the later enacted amendment. No official page reviewed supplied a detailed sham-marriage evidentiary checklist, so that warning is a general legal caution.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For births on or after 5 June 1979, birth in Seychelles confers citizenship when at least one parent is a Seychelles citizen. Birth in the territory alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Seychelles to two non-citizen migrant parents does not automatically acquire Seychelles citizenship solely by birth there.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The reviewed constitutional and Immigration sources do not establish a broader territorial entitlement for children of two migrants; exceptional anti-statelessness or registration provisions would require case-specific legal review.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Seychelles citizen at birth if either parent is a Seychelles citizen at the date of birth, whether the birth occurs inside or outside Seychelles.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence on a migrant parent. A family or domestic connection may support a discretionary Residence Permit application, but that permit does not authorize work.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A separate GOP would be needed for gainful occupation.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is a Seychelles citizen, the child can be a citizen, but the migrant father receives no automatic citizenship. He may pursue family-based residence or, if married to the citizen parent, the separate spouse naturalisation rules.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Marriage and parenthood remain separate from the child's automatic citizenship.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank checked on 2026-08-15. Index methodologies and rankings can differ.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Current Passport Index breakdown.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from Passport Index's 41 visa-on-arrival and 6 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: The index's mobility score is 147. Counts are index-specific and can change with entry-policy updates.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for day-to-day remote work: English is one of the three constitutionally recognized national languages and is used across official immigration, tax and tourism services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Internet quality and reliability remain accommodation- and island-specific and were not quantified in this audit.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited compared with English; neither Russian nor Ukrainian is a national language, and the reviewed official sources do not indicate broad public-service availability in either language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian or Ukrainian speakers should expect to use English, French or Seychellois Creole for official matters.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest explicitly published NBS all-sector gross monthly average of SCR 16,710 for Q4 2023 using SCR 14.5513 per USD. NBS reports that later wage releases were delayed because of private-sector data problems.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: NBS publishes an all-sector average and industry or sector averages, not a current national median; the reviewed catalog, summary and release-calendar pages provide no median amount to convert to USD.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate full-time statutory minimum: SCR 40.95 per hour multiplied by 45 hours and 52/12, converted at SCR 14.5513 per USD. This is a statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of official Q4 2023 all-sector gross average earnings.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD conversion is possible because the named current NBS sources do not publish a national median salary in SCR.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD conversion is possible because the named current NBS sources do not publish a national maximum salary in SCR.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Calculated from the statutory SCR 40.95 hourly continuous-worker minimum at 45 hours weekly.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official all-sector average for Q4 2023; later publication was delayed.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: NBS describes its formal-employment series as quarterly average monthly gross earnings by industry and sector, and the National Summary Data Page reports only the all-sector average. The current Employment & Earnings catalog contains no releases after Q4 2023, while the separate Labour Force Survey catalog through Q4 2025 does not publish a national median on its accessible release pages. Accordingly, no official national median salary amount in SCR can be entered from the named current sources.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed NBS employment series publishes averages by sector or industry, not the highest individual salary or an upper national wage bound. A national maximum is not a statutory cap and would change with individual payroll records; none of the current NBS catalog, summary or release-calendar sources publishes a defensible maximum salary in SCR.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory full-time minimum and formal all-sector gross average earnings
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 1 April 2025; average Q4 2023
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are citizen or resident labor-market benchmarks, not immigration income thresholds. The latest explicit official all-sector wage remains Q4 2023 because the NBS Employment & Earnings catalog shows no 2024 documents and the NSDP reports private-sector source-data delays. The NBS series is designed around average monthly gross earnings; it does not publish a national median or maximum in the reviewed current sources.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official employment and summary-statistics sources do not publish a current household monthly living-cost budget. Consumer-price indexes measure change over time and do not supply a defensible monthly household amount.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Visitors Workcation Permit is temporary visitor status capped at one year, and the Citizenship Act expressly excludes a visitor’s permit from legal residence; its time therefore cannot count toward naturalisation.
settlement_track.summary: The route works for a temporary foreign-contract remote-work stay but is not a settlement route. Current citizenship law expressly excludes visitor-permit time from legal residence, and any long-term path requires obtaining a separate non-visitor status on an independent legal basis.
settlement_track.notes: The statutory visitor-permit exclusion resolves the earlier uncertainty about citizenship counting. No automatic Workcation-to-GOP, residence-permit, permanent-residence or citizenship conversion is published.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The permit fits ordinary foreign employment or freelancing for temporary living, but it does not fit the required residence-to-citizenship objective because visitor-permit time is excluded from legal residence. A locally approved self-employed GOP is materially different from simply continuing foreign-client work.

data.notes: Thirty-one distinct directly relevant URLs were reviewed, including nine not present in the previous source set. The focused pass resolved the Workcation citizenship question through the 2023 Citizenship Amendment Act, clarified the 30% tax figure as a top marginal employee rate rather than a route-specific effective rate, and retained null salary median and maximum values with precise NBS publication-scope explanations. Filing-level checks remain advisable for current portal availability and SRC classification of the actual foreign contract.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Qualifying Gainful Occupation Permit / dependent residence and investment-based permanent residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A separate investment-based PR route exists after five years of qualifying residence and business association. It requires a substantial investment and does not rely on Workcation visitor time.
requirements: Invest at least USD 1 million in a Seychelles business and maintain at least five years of business association.
Reside at least five years on a GOP or dependent permit, show maintenance funds and meet absence/character conditions.
Secure the required business and GOP approvals before undertaking local work.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: This is a changed investment/business profile, not a confirmed ordinary remote-worker successor. The old tourism Workcation page returned no readable rules, and the old Workcation application URL now displays the generic border portal. Current programme operation and the in-country transition procedure therefore need confirmation; PR investment rules are clearly published.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was found. Sierra Leone offers annual residence permits for employment, study, dependants, and locally established business/self-employment, but anyone intending to work, provide services, or engage in gainful business also needs a work permit. The business category is restricted to an approved Sierra Leone venture and does not cleanly accommodate a software engineer merely continuing an existing foreign contract.

visa_application.title: Unified Permit
visa_application.notes: Official online portal for Sierra Leone residence and work permits. It does not list a digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category; applicants choose a residence permit, work permit, or both.

rejected_routes.route_name: Business/self-employed residence permit plus work permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly foreign-income threshold is published; eligibility is based on an approved locally established business venture.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official requirements include business-registration evidence and financial-position evidence such as a bank statement, but specify no minimum amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly threshold; local business registration, financial evidence, residence permit and work permit required
income_requirement_display.notes: The portal calculates fees according to nationality, service, process, and role; no single stable fee applies to every applicant.

income_proof_months.notes: A bank statement is required, but the official checklist does not specify a look-back period.

key_requirements.requirement: Establish and document an approved business venture in Sierra Leone and provide current company-registration certificates.
Provide a valid passport, photographs, and evidence of financial position such as a bank statement.
Obtain a non-national identity card and National Identification Number.
Obtain a work permit because a non-citizen who works, provides services, or conducts gainful business requires one.
Operate only within the business area approved for the residence permit.

initial_validity.notes: Both the immigration guidance and Work Permit Act describe annual authorization.

extension_rules.value: Residence and work permits are renewable while the approved venture and compliance conditions continue.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic conversion to permanent residence was identified.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying local entrepreneur or self-employed operator may obtain an annual business residence permit plus the work authorization required to provide services.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is local-business residence, not a foreign-income remote-worker category.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic permanent-residence transition or statutory conversion clock was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed sources describe annual renewal and discretionary naturalisation, not a general permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Long lawful residence may eventually support discretionary naturalisation, generally after 15 years for an applicant whose parents are not persons of African descent.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make the permit an ordinary remote-work route; character, language, contribution, continued-residence, and other statutory conditions also apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for the stated profile. A genuine entrepreneur may apply through a locally registered venture without an unrelated local employer, but the category is purpose-restricted local-business residence. The sources do not establish that an existing foreign software-services contract alone qualifies.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed permit pages do not publish an immigration salary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed permit pages do not publish an immigration salary threshold in local currency.

income_requirement_display.value: Local appointment and employer-supported permits required; no published immigration salary threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: The authorization is tied to the approved employer, occupation, and purpose.

income_proof_months.notes: A historic personal-income look-back is inapplicable. The route instead requires an appointment letter and employer-supported permit application.

key_requirements.requirement: Appointment by a Sierra Leone employer or organization and employer-supported residence documentation.
A purpose-specific work permit and NIN/non-national identity card.

initial_validity.value: Normally one year
initial_validity.notes: Renewal depends on continued approved employment.

extension_rules.value: Renewable while the specific employment and permit conditions remain satisfied.
extension_rules.notes: The permit is not a freely transferable independent-work authorization.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct annual employment residence permit together with a work permit after employer-supported approval.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is temporary employer-specific residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic permanent-residence transition was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official permit page describes annual status, not a permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Long lawful residence may eventually support discretionary naturalisation, but no employer-permit-specific entitlement exists in the reviewed sources.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The general naturalisation rules and conditions apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local appointment and employer-supported permits are required.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed maintenance threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Proof of sponsorship or financial means is required, but the official materials state no minimum amount.

income_requirement_display.notes: This is an education route rather than an income-based route.

income_proof_months.notes: The official checklist does not specify how many months of financial evidence must be supplied.
