Ability to maintain and accommodate the student and dependants without work or other economic activity.

initial_validity.value: Normally one year within the approved study purpose
initial_validity.notes: Continued status depends on qualifying study.

extension_rules.value: Extension may be granted on evidence of regular attendance; an in-country change may be refused where the person did not enter as a student or prospective student.
extension_rules.notes: No post-study conversion entitlement was identified.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct student residence permit after qualifying admission.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The status is study-specific.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent-residence path was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The immigration guidance provides no permanent-residence conversion rule for students.

path_to_citizenship.value: No student-specific citizenship path or confirmation that study time qualifies was found.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The general naturalisation law does not establish a student-specific entitlement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the status does not authorize the applicant to continue working under a foreign software contract.

summary.value: A full-time student accepted by a Sierra Leone institution may obtain an annual student residence permit without an employer, but must maintain themselves without working or engaging in other economic activity. A university degree by itself does not create an independent skilled-residence route.
summary.notes: No independent degree- or qualification-based skilled-migration program was found.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally resident when present in Sierra Leone for more than 182 days in a 12-month period beginning or ending in the tax year. Residents generally face worldwide taxation; non-residents are taxed on Sierra Leone-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A non-citizen who is not domiciled in Sierra Leone and does not intend to remain more than four years may qualify as temporarily resident.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for resident PIT/PAYE, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Total NASSIT contribution is 15% of basic salary: 5% employee and 10% employer. Participation is compulsory for employees but described as voluntary for self-employed persons, who pay 15% of declared income if participating.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly social-security minimum or remote-worker payment was found. Permit and non-national-ID costs are transactional rather than a single monthly payment and vary by applicant and service.

special_tax_regimes.value: A qualifying temporarily resident individual is taxed on Sierra Leone-source income plus foreign income remitted to Sierra Leone rather than automatically on all unremitted foreign income. This is not a digital-nomad exemption.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Services physically performed in Sierra Leone may be Sierra Leone-source even when the client and contract are foreign.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical work location, income source, residence, domicile, intended duration, remittances, business form, NASSIT participation, withholding rules, and any applicable treaty. Professional advice is needed before relying on temporary-resident remittance treatment.

taxation_system.value: Residents are taxed progressively at up to 30%; non-resident individual employment or business income is generally taxed at 25%. Qualifying temporary residents receive modified remittance treatment for genuinely foreign-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 182 aggregate days in a relevant 12-month period, subject to the normal-place-of-abode and other statutory rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide for ordinary residents; Sierra Leone-source income for non-residents; Sierra Leone-source plus remitted foreign-source income for qualifying temporary residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Temporary-resident remittance treatment; no digital-nomad tax holiday found.
taxation_system.social_security: NASSIT totals 15% of basic salary for employees: 5% employee and 10% employer. Self-employed participation is voluntary, with participants paying 15% of declared income.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard number is the top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. The bracket amounts use redenominated new leones and should be checked against the live NRA calculator before filing.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly chargeable income up to NLe 600
tax_brackets.notes: Current NRA reporting confirms the NLe 600 tax-free threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next NLe 600, from NLe 600 to NLe 1,200 monthly
tax_brackets.notes: Schedule expressed in redenominated new leones.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next NLe 600, from NLe 1,200 to NLe 1,800 monthly
tax_brackets.notes: Schedule expressed in redenominated new leones.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Next NLe 600, from NLe 1,800 to NLe 2,400 monthly
tax_brackets.notes: Non-resident individual employment or business income is separately shown at 25% in the NRA guide.
Top marginal rate; the NRA portal reports a 30% maximum.

taxation_system.notes: The 2026 Finance Act was checked for amendments. The reviewed provisions did not establish a digital-nomad regime or replace the resident 30% maximum.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No special digital-nomad category exists. A person working from Sierra Leone is screened under ordinary source, residence, PIT/PAYE, business-registration, withholding, and NASSIT rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary non-resident, temporary-resident, resident-employee, or self-employed/business taxation applies.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% resident PIT; generally 25% for non-resident individual employment or business income
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 182 aggregate days in a relevant 12-month period, subject to additional statutory tests.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Ordinary residents generally face worldwide taxation. Qualifying temporary residents are taxed on Sierra Leone-source income plus remitted foreign-source income. Services performed in Sierra Leone may be locally sourced despite a foreign client.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No nomad exemption; only the generally applicable temporary-resident remittance treatment was found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee NASSIT totals 15% of basic salary. Self-employed participation is voluntary, but participants pay 15% of declared income.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly amount confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No minimum contribution base was found. NASSIT is percentage-based and self-employed participation is described as voluntary.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Residence/work-permit and non-national-ID fees apply, but the portal calculates them according to nationality and service details.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business registration, licensing, GST, withholding, and other charges may apply depending on structure and turnover. No dedicated freelancer flat payment was found.
fixed_payments.notes: The 2026 Finance Act changes some withholding rates, including rules relevant to non-resident contractors. Filing advice is required to distinguish withholding from final tax.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below the day threshold does not automatically eliminate tax. Non-residents remain taxable on Sierra Leone-source income, which may include services performed there.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: An ordinary resident is generally taxable on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 30%. Temporary-resident remittance treatment applies only if its conditions and foreign-source characterization are satisfied.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered sole proprietor or business faces ordinary PIT or applicable business rules, possible registration/GST obligations, permit costs, and voluntary NASSIT at 15% of declared income if participating.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is hypothetical tax analysis because no qualifying remote-worker route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying foreign-contract remote-work route exists. A genuine local-business, employment, or study applicant can obtain annual temporary residence directly, but those are different profiles.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No general permanent-residence status or conversion clock was established in the reviewed immigration and nationality sources.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on residence and statutory qualifications, not on a confirmed period after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General rule for a full-age applicant neither of whose parents is a person of African descent, subject to discretion and additional conditions. This is not a timeline from a qualifying remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No official processing-time standard is published in the reviewed nationality materials. Immigration policy guidance describes naturalisation as lengthy and highly discretionary.

key_conditions.value: For the general 15-year category: qualifying residence, adequate knowledge of an indigenous language used in Sierra Leone, good character, useful or substantial contribution, intention to reside permanently, prescribed fees, oath or declarations, and applicable nationality requirements.
key_conditions.notes: The legislation contains ancestry-based distinctions; current filing requirements should be verified with Immigration.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Section 7 states no minimum marriage or residence period, but expressly concerns a non-Sierra Leonean woman who is or has been married to a Sierra Leonean citizen and makes naturalisation discretionary.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can support an application by a foreign woman married to a Sierra Leonean citizen; the wording also says 'is or has been married.' No equivalent expedited provision for a foreign husband was confirmed.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not confer citizenship automatically.

requirements_and_risks.value: The eligible woman must apply for a naturalisation certificate, take the oath, make the required declaration, pay prescribed fees, and satisfy the authorities. Relationship documentation is required for spouse residence registration, and fraudulent documentation may cause refusal or legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The gender-specific wording materially limits the benefit for a migrant husband; current administrative practice and genuine-relationship checks should be verified.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Sierra Leone alone is insufficient. Citizenship by birth depends on the statutory ancestry and birth links, including a qualifying parent or grandparent born in Sierra Leone and the Act's ancestry conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Sierra Leone to two first-generation migrant parents does not automatically become a citizen solely by birthplace when the required parental or grandparental Sierra Leone birth and ancestry conditions are absent.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Exceptional registration or anti-statelessness facts could affect an individual case, but no broad unconditional jus soli exists.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child with a Sierra Leonean mother or father can generally acquire citizenship through that parent, subject to the precise birthplace and registration facts.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2006 amendment extended transmission through the mother.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Sierra Leonean child does not automatically naturalise either migrant parent. A dependent residence application may be possible, but no citizen-child-specific permanent-residence or citizenship entitlement was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The applicable dependent category should be verified with Immigration.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically receive citizenship or permanent residence because his child is Sierra Leonean. The expedited marriage-naturalisation provision located is written for a foreign woman, not a foreign husband.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A relationship-based permit may be considered administratively, but a special entitlement for the father of a citizen child is not established by the current sources.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank observed on 2026-08-15; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count shown by Passport Index, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index count observed on the research date.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 25 visa-on-arrival and 3 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately reports eVisa destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported mobility score 66 and world reach 33%. Its category definitions differ from Henley's combined methodology.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the official language used in schools and government administration, while Krio is widely spoken. English is usable for administration and professional communication, although infrastructure reliability requires location-specific due diligence.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The source supports language use, not a quantitative claim about internet or electricity quality.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No official or widely established Russian- or Ukrainian-language service environment was found. Applicants should expect to use English and, socially, Krio or other local languages.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the documented official and commonly spoken languages.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national mean monthly employee-earnings amount with a corresponding same-period USD value is published on the inspected official or international statistical pages. Household income and selected occupation statistics were not substituted for a national employee mean.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median monthly employee-earnings amount or corresponding USD value is displayed in the inspected official publications. Available percentiles concern household income or selected subgroups.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The statutory minimum wage is confirmed in local currency, but the reviewed central-bank page did not expose a sufficiently clear same-date exchange-rate observation for a defensible USD conversion.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national average employee-earnings amount and corresponding USD conversion could be established from the inspected official and international statistical sources.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median employee-earnings amount and corresponding USD conversion is published in the inspected sources.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Sierra Leone has no statutory maximum salary, and the inspected national surveys do not publish a meaningful national observed maximum employee wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage effective 1 April 2026, not an observed minimum in a wage distribution.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The official household survey publishes household income rather than a current national mean salary per employee. The ILO catalogue confirms an earnings variable but does not display a national aggregate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Published percentiles concern household income or selected education and training subgroups. The reviewed sources provide no current national employee-salary median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: There is no statutory national maximum salary, and the inspected official surveys do not publish an observed national maximum employee wage. Household upper percentiles were not misclassified as salary maxima.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Current statutory national minimum wage; national average, median, and maximum employee salaries remain unpublished in the inspected current sources.
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage monthly and effective 2026-04-01; unresolved employee-salary evidence principally comes from 2018 survey microdata and older publications.
average_citizen_salary.notes: The only current defensible national wage amount found is the statutory minimum wage of NLe 1,200 monthly. It is labor-market context, not an immigration threshold or average salary. Household income, subgroup earnings, and unverified salary websites were not substituted for national wage statistics.

cost_of_living_note.value: Consumer prices were still rising rapidly at the research date: Statistics Sierra Leone reported annual national CPI inflation of 14.77% in June 2026, up from 12.69% in May. The World Bank links the 2026 rebound to fuel-price increases and higher freight, fertilizer, oil, and energy costs. This measures the change in consumer prices, not the absolute monthly budget for an expatriate or a Freetown-specific cost basket; no authoritative current expatriate budget was found.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This resolves the flagged null with reliable official and multilateral evidence. It deliberately reports cost pressure rather than claiming that CPI is an absolute cost-of-living level. WFP and World Bank materials were also checked for food-market and household-purchasing-power context.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor or eVisa status and an existing foreign contract do not substitute for locally purpose-specific residence and work permits.
settlement_track.summary: Sierra Leone has annual local-employment and local-business permits but no regular foreign-contract remote-work route. A genuine entrepreneur may pursue long lawful residence and later discretionary naturalisation, but that requires an approved Sierra Leone business and is not a match for the stated profile.
settlement_track.notes: No automatic permanent-residence transition was confirmed. The general 15-year naturalisation rule cannot be attached to a nonexistent qualifying remote-worker route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Official categories cover employment, locally established business or self-employment, study, and dependants. Providing services or engaging in gainful business requires a work permit, and business residence is restricted to the approved Sierra Leone venture. No category accepting an ordinary existing foreign software contract as its basis was found.

data.notes: The negative route conclusion remains well supported. The flagged cost-of-living null was resolved with current official CPI evidence and multilateral analysis while clearly distinguishing price inflation from an absolute household budget. Six directly relevant canonical URLs absent from the previous source set were added, and more than 15 relevant URLs were inspected. All remaining sourced null values have specific notes and at least one supporting source ID.

data.selection_summary: Singapore has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract residence route. Work for an overseas organisation is permitted without an additional work pass only when the person already holds another valid stay pass; that permission does not independently grant residence. ONE Pass, PEP, EntrePass and Employment Pass require elite earnings or achievements, Singapore employment, or a qualifying innovative Singapore business, so none fits the stated ordinary foreign-contract software-engineer profile.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct PR; any PR application is separate and discretionary

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through separately obtaining PR and later satisfying citizenship eligibility

rejected_routes.notes: This is a founder/startup route requiring Singapore business substance, innovation or venture backing and later local spending and hiring. It is incompatible with simply continuing an ordinary foreign software contract.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the S$5,600 base threshold using about S$1.28 per US$1; the required salary rises with age and is higher in financial services.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: From S$5,600 per month, increasing with age
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: COMPASS and other employer requirements also apply unless exempt.

income_requirement_display.value: From S$5,600/month (about US$4,375), plus a Singapore job offer and employer application
income_requirement_display.notes: This is unavailable to a foreign-contract remote worker without Singapore hiring.

income_proof_months.notes: No single past-income period creates eligibility; the Singapore employer files the application.

key_requirements.requirement: Job offer from a Singapore-based employer.
Employer or appointed employment agent applies; salary and COMPASS requirements apply.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years for first-time candidates

extension_rules.value: Generally renewable for up to 3 years per renewal

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct employer-linked work pass

path_to_permanent_residence.value: EP holders may apply separately for discretionary PR
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No fixed minimum EP period or guaranteed approval is published.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship eligibility normally follows discretionary PR and at least 2 years as PR

rejected_routes.notes: This is the conventional software-engineer route but requires a Singapore employer and employer filing, so it is rejected under the selection rules.

summary.value: An eligible student already studying in Singapore who has passed a specified national examination or is in the Integrated Programme may independently apply for PR. A foreign university degree alone creates no equivalent residence route, so this does not help the stated applicant unless they first undertake qualifying Singapore education.
summary.notes: The PR application grants PR directly if approved, but qualifying Singapore student status and examination history are prerequisites.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreigner is generally tax-resident for a Year of Assessment after staying or working in Singapore for at least 183 days in the preceding calendar year. IRAS also recognises continuous three-year residence and a qualifying two-calendar-year employment concession.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The two-year concession applies to employees and excludes specified categories.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal resident rate from YA 2024 onward; this is a screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: CPF is not payable for a foreigner who is neither a Singapore citizen nor PR. Different obligations arise after obtaining PR.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly CPF payment applies to a non-PR foreign remote worker. Private insurance, accommodation, tax and route-specific pass fees are excluded.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax regime was found. Limited Area Representative time apportionment can apply to qualifying foreign-employer employees who primarily perform services outside Singapore.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Foreign payer status alone does not make work performed in Singapore foreign-sourced.

taxes.caveats: Singapore-source classification depends on where services and supporting business operations are performed, not merely where the payer is located. Treaty relief, worker classification, short-term exemptions and Area Representative treatment require case-specific review. Immigration permission and tax liability are separate.

taxation_system.value: Resident individuals pay progressive personal income tax from 0% to 24%. Services physically performed or business operations based in Singapore can generate Singapore-source income even when the employer or client is overseas.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally at least 183 days in the preceding calendar year, with specified three-year and two-calendar-year rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Primarily source-based. Income earned from services rendered in Singapore is taxable; genuinely foreign-sourced individual income received in Singapore is generally exempt, subject to exceptions.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Narrow Area Representative time apportionment may apply when qualifying conditions are met.
taxation_system.social_security: Non-citizen, non-PR foreigners are exempt from CPF. Citizens and PRs have different CPF or MediSave obligations.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 24% dashboard value is the top marginal screening rate, not an estimated effective rate. Non-resident employment and professional income can be taxed under different rules.

tax_brackets.notes: Applies only to the excess over S$1 million.

taxation_system.notes: Official IRAS and CPF sources were used. The system is labelled mixed because progressive resident rates coexist with source-based and non-resident rules.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Singapore has no digital-nomad immigration or tax category. If a person independently holds another stay pass and performs foreign-employer or foreign-client work from Singapore, income attributable to services in Singapore can be taxable under ordinary rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated route; ordinary employment or self-employment taxation while holding another stay status
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%-24% progressive resident rates; 24% is the top screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Usually at least 183 days in the preceding calendar year, subject to IRAS's other residence rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign payment for services performed in Singapore is not automatically foreign-sourced. Services rendered in Singapore for a foreign employer can be taxable there.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None; Area Representative time apportionment is narrow and conditional.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A non-PR foreigner is exempt from CPF. Foreign-employer reporting obligations may still arise.

fixed_payments.status: No universal digital-nomad fixed payment because no such route exists
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: S$0 mandatory CPF for a foreigner who is neither a citizen nor PR.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Not applicable to a digital-nomad route; alternative pass fees are route-specific.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business tax and GST obligations depend on facts, structure and registration thresholds.
fixed_payments.notes: No universal monthly freelancer licence fee or foreign-worker social contribution applies to this scenario.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident performing work in Singapore can remain taxable under non-resident rules. Short-term exemptions are conditional and should not be assumed for a software consultant.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days or under another qualifying residence rule, Singapore-source income is assessed at progressive rates up to 24%.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Organised foreign-client activity carried out from Singapore can produce taxable trade income. Business or tax registration does not itself legalise residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This describes taxation if the person already has lawful stay; it does not imply an independent remote-worker visa exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary foreign-contract route exists, so there is no route-specific temporary-residence clock.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: ICA publishes eligible categories and holistic assessment factors but no guaranteed years-to-PR threshold for professional applicants.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: This is the minimum PR-holding period for adult eligibility to apply, not guaranteed approval.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No qualifying starting route and no fixed time to discretionary PR make a defensible total unavailable.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: ICA states applications are generally processed within 12 months, although some take longer.

key_conditions.value: First qualify under a separate immigration category, obtain discretionary PR, maintain PR for at least two years and obtain discretionary citizenship approval. Renunciation and National Service consequences can apply.
key_conditions.notes: ICA publishes no guaranteed ordinary remote-worker conversion path.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The spouse citizenship category requires at least two years as PR and at least two years married to a Singapore citizen. Marriage creates a PR category but no guaranteed approval.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine marriage to a Singapore citizen or PR can support a spouse-sponsored PR application. Citizenship through a citizen spouse requires both the published marriage and PR periods. Marriage to another foreigner creates no equivalent benefit.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The citizen or PR spouse sponsors the PR application.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage does not automatically grant entry, long-term stay, PR or citizenship. Applications remain discretionary and subject to relationship and documentary scrutiny.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A marriage must be genuine; it should not be treated as guaranteed immigration approval.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution's citizenship-by-birth rule does not confer citizenship merely from Singapore birth when neither parent is a citizen, subject to limited discretion and foundling provisions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Singapore-born child of two foreign parents is not automatically a citizen merely because of birth in Singapore.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Temporary or permanent residence of the parents alone does not replace the citizen-parent condition.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Singapore generally acquires citizenship when at least one parent is a Singapore citizen, subject to constitutional exceptions. Overseas births are governed by descent and registration conditions.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage, birthplace and registration affect the exact procedure.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer residence, PR or citizenship on a foreign parent. An adult citizen aged at least 21 may sponsor an aged parent's discretionary PR application.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The relevant benefit depends on the parent's own category and the child's age.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status follows from fathering a Singapore citizen child. A foreign father needs a qualifying family or independent immigration category; an adult citizen child may later sponsor an aged parent for discretionary PR.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Child citizenship must not be presented as automatic father citizenship or PR.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank observed on 2026-08-15; its methodology differs from Henley.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free category; the broader mobility score was 175.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 35 visa-on-arrival and 11 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 175. Rankings and counts change as entry policies are updated.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. English is constitutionally official and widely usable for government, professional, technical and day-to-day activity.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Malay is the national language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited compared with English. Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and the reviewed government sources do not establish broad public-service availability in either language.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: English should be expected for administration and professional work.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of S$6,442 mean gross monthly employment income in Q4 2025 using about S$1.28 per US$1.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 median gross monthly income of S$5,775 for full-time employed residents.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No universal national minimum can be converted: MOM expressly states that Singapore has no general minimum wage or salary. PWM floors apply only to covered jobs, while LQS applies to local employees of firms hiring foreign workers.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion; this is resident-worker income, not an immigration threshold.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion; this is resident-worker income, not an immigration threshold.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official sources publish medians, deciles and occupational 25th/75th percentiles, not a national maximum salary. The highest published percentile is not a maximum and is therefore not used as one.

min_salary_local_currency.value: No universal national minimum wage or salary; pay is negotiated, except where an applicable Progressive Wage Model or Local Qualifying Salary floor applies
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The current LQS is S$1,800 monthly for qualifying full-time local employees in firms hiring foreign workers, but it is not a universal national minimum and must not be presented as one. PWM floors vary by covered sector, occupation and job level.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Mean gross monthly income from employment, including employer CPF and excluding bonuses, for employed residents in Q4 2025.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median gross monthly income from employment, including employer or platform-operator CPF contributions, for full-time employed residents in 2025.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No national maximum salary is defined or published; current official releases provide percentile and occupational distributions rather than a maximum
max_salary_local_currency.notes: MOM's national decile release stops at the 90th percentile, while the occupational survey reports medians and 25th/75th percentiles. Neither statistic is an observed or legal maximum, so no amount is inserted.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official resident-worker statistics: national mean gross monthly employment income, full-time resident median income, national deciles and occupational wage percentiles. CPF and bonus treatment varies by series.
average_citizen_salary.period: Q4 2025 mean; 2025 annual median and labour-force distribution; June 2025 occupational wages released 30 June 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are resident-worker earnings and wage-policy facts, not software-engineer salaries or immigration thresholds. The focused audit confirms that a universal minimum and national maximum are inapplicable, while conditional wage floors and percentile statistics must not be relabelled as national endpoints.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2023 Household Expenditure Survey reported average resident-household spending of S$5,931 per month. This is household spending, not a single remote worker's budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The survey is not an August 2026 price quote.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Foreign-client work can be performed without an additional work pass only after another stay pass has been obtained. That permission is not an immigration status and cannot start a PR or citizenship clock.
settlement_track.summary: Singapore has no ordinary remote-worker residence route. Elite, startup, family, eligible local-student or Singapore-employment statuses can separately lead to discretionary PR and later citizenship eligibility, but a normal foreign software contract cannot initiate that chain.
settlement_track.notes: ONE Pass is independently filed but its top-talent and very-high-income conditions place it outside the ordinary profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Remote work is permitted only for someone who already possesses another valid stay pass. No independently accessible residence status for an ordinary foreign contract was found, and MOM rejects EOR work-pass sponsorship where the foreigner would remain based in Singapore while working for an overseas company.

data.notes: Focused audit completed against the previous Singapore record. Six new official wage sources were inspected in addition to the prior source set. The two flagged local-currency fields now state the precise result: Singapore has no universal national minimum wage, and current official wage releases do not define or publish a national maximum. Conditional PWM/LQS floors and published percentiles were not misrepresented as national endpoints.

data.selection_summary: Slovakia has no dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence category. Its independently filed business residence can lead to long-term residence, but it requires a Slovak trade licence, a credible business plan, and evidence that the proposed activity is feasible, sustainable, and beneficial to Slovakia’s economic interests. An unchanged foreign employment or client contract is therefore not, by itself, a qualifying residence basis for the requested ordinary remote-work profile.

visa_application.title: Residence of Foreigners in Territory of Slovakia
visa_application.notes: Official Ministry of Foreign Affairs residence overview, not an online application portal. A business-residence application is generally filed in person at the competent Slovak diplomatic mission; embassy-specific appointment procedures must be checked separately.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for business — trade licence (živnosť)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the EUR 295.22 monthly subsistence-funds requirement using 1 EUR = USD 1.1392. This is a bank-balance coverage requirement, not a minimum earned salary.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 295.22 for each month of proposed residence, capped at EUR 3,542.64 when the stay exceeds one year, plus EUR 5,904.40 in business funds for a sole trader
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: July 2026 amounts derived from the statutory subsistence minimum. The business-funds amount is separate from personal living funds and thresholds can change.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 295.22/month living funds (maximum EUR 3,542.64 for a stay over one year) plus EUR 5,904.40 sole-trader business funds
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 1× subsistence minimum per month, capped at 12×, plus 20× subsistence minimum for sole-trader business funds
income_requirement_display.notes: Approximately USD 336/month, USD 4,036 capped living funds, and USD 6,726 business funds at the cited ECB rate. These are proof-of-funds balances rather than recurring-income thresholds.

income_proof_months.notes: The published rule requires bank-account balances rather than a specified number of historical monthly income statements.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain a Slovak trade licence before applying for business residence.
Submit a business plan and supporting contracts or other evidence showing feasibility, sustainability, credibility, and benefit to Slovakia’s economic interests.
Apply in person in Slovak, generally through the Slovak diplomatic mission accredited to the applicant’s citizenship or country of residence.

Provide a passport, criminal-record certificates, accommodation for at least six months, sufficient personal and business funds, and subsequently satisfy health-insurance and medical-report obligations.

initial_validity.value: Up to 3 years
initial_validity.notes: The residence card can have a shorter validity if accommodation is documented for a shorter period.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is filed at the Foreign Police or electronically no later than the final day of validity. The applicant must continue satisfying the business purpose, insurance, accommodation, funds, taxable-business-income, and no-arrears requirements.
extension_rules.notes: The published route page lists a EUR 200 paper renewal fee or EUR 150 electronic fee, plus residence-card issuance charges. Renewal is not automatic.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved application directly grants temporary residence for business; no visitor-to-residence conversion is inherent in the route.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Business applicants normally apply through a Slovak mission abroad. The general ability of some visa-free applicants to file other residence applications inside Slovakia does not override the specific restriction applicable to initial business-residence filings.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Long-term residence is generally available after at least 5 years of uninterrupted lawful residence in Slovakia, subject to absence limits, A2 Slovak, regular income, health insurance, and accommodation.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Business residence is not listed among the categories excluded or counted only at half duration, but an applicant should confirm the counting of their exact residence history before relying on it.

path_to_citizenship.value: A conservative ordinary path is approximately 13 years: about 5 years to long-term residence followed by 8 years of continuous permanent residence before naturalisation eligibility.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is discretionary, requires Slovak language and general knowledge, integrity, compliance with tax/social/residence obligations, and actual residence. Meeting the statutory conditions does not create an entitlement to citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a genuine settlement-oriented Slovak sole-trader route, but it is rejected for the requested profile because residence depends on establishing and operating the proposed Slovak business. A foreign contract may support the business plan, but merely continuing ordinary foreign employment or freelancing unchanged is not a dedicated qualifying basis.

rejected_routes.route_name: Temporary residence for employment / EU Blue Card

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No relevant independent remote-worker income threshold; eligibility is tied to qualifying employment and the applicable permit procedure.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not applicable to the requested independent foreign-contract scenario.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable — qualifying employment and employer-side documentation are required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an independent foreign-contract remote-work route.

income_proof_months.notes: No independent income-history rule applies to the requested scenario.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment residence requires an employment permit, employer confirmation, confirmation of the possibility of filling a vacancy, or another specified employment basis.

initial_validity.value: Employment residence may be granted for up to 5 years, depending on its precise basis
initial_validity.notes: Validity does not remove the employer/job basis.

extension_rules.value: Continuation depends on the qualifying employment basis and residence-law requirements.
extension_rules.notes: Not suitable for independent foreign-client work.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence is possible only through the qualifying employment process.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Lawful qualifying residence may eventually count toward long-term residence, but this does not make the route independent.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through long-term/permanent residence and later naturalisation, subject to the general conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Rejected because the initial route requires qualifying employment rather than ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: A software engineer may qualify through Slovak employment or a Blue Card, but these routes do not meet the project’s independent-application requirement.

summary.value: No independent residence route based solely on the applicant’s existing software-engineering degree was confirmed. Slovakia offers study, research, employment, and Blue Card residence categories, but study requires new enrolment, research requires the qualifying research basis, and employment/Blue Card routes are not ordinary foreign-contract remote-work routes.
summary.notes: The applicant’s degree can support employment or business credibility, but it does not independently grant residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally a Slovak tax resident if they have permanent residence or a home indicating an intention to reside permanently in Slovakia, or are present for at least 183 days in the calendar year. Treaty residence rules can override domestic dual-residence results.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Every commenced day can count toward the domestic 183-day test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top 2026 marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Qualifying business/self-employment income with annual taxable revenue no greater than EUR 100,000 is instead subject to a 15% rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Combined headline rate for a normally insured self-employed person: 33.15% social insurance plus 16% public health insurance, each applied to its own assessment base. It is not a simple percentage of gross revenue, and compulsory social-insurance timing/status must be checked individually.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate combined 2026 minimum of EUR 303.11 compulsory self-employed social insurance plus EUR 121.92 health-insurance advance, where both minima apply. New or differently insured sole traders may have different social-insurance timing.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax regime was found. Qualifying business or other self-employment income with annual taxable revenue up to EUR 100,000 receives a 15% income-tax rate; 60% deemed expenses capped at EUR 20,000 may be available to an eligible non-VAT payer or partial-year VAT payer.
special_tax_regimes.notes: These are general small-business rules, not immigration incentives.

taxes.caveats: Tax outcome depends on whether the relationship is employment or genuine self-employment, where work is physically performed, permanent-establishment/payroll exposure for the foreign engager, treaty residence, deductible expenses, VAT place-of-supply rules, and social-security coordination. The rejected business route should be modelled with Slovak professional advice before filing.

taxation_system.value: Progressive general personal-income taxation with a separate 15% qualifying small-business/self-employment rate.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence, a qualifying home, or at least 183 days in the calendar year, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
taxation_system.income_scope: Slovak residents generally have unlimited tax liability; non-residents are taxed on Slovak-source income. Treaty provisions can change the result.
taxation_system.special_regimes: 15% on qualifying business/self-employment taxable income where annual taxable revenue does not exceed EUR 100,000; no special digital-nomad regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: For 2026, the standard compulsorily insured self-employed social rate totals 33.15%, with a EUR 914.40 minimum assessment base and EUR 303.11 minimum contribution. Public health insurance is generally 16%, with a EUR 762 minimum base and EUR 121.92 minimum advance for a self-employed person without disability.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard’s 35% figure is the top marginal screening rate. General 2026 brackets are 19%, 25%, 30%, and 35%. The separate 15% qualifying-business rate may be more relevant to a genuine Slovak sole trader.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable base up to and including EUR 43,983.32
tax_brackets.applies_to: General employment, rental, and specified other taxable bases; also business/self-employment where annual business revenue exceeds EUR 100,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold at 1 EUR = USD 1.1392.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over EUR 43,983.32 up to and including EUR 60,349.21
tax_brackets.applies_to: General progressive base and business/self-employment where annual business revenue exceeds EUR 100,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the upper threshold approximately.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Portion over EUR 60,349.21 up to and including EUR 75,010.32
tax_brackets.applies_to: General progressive base and business/self-employment where annual business revenue exceeds EUR 100,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD value represents the upper threshold approximately.

tax_brackets.applies_to: General progressive base and business/self-employment where annual business revenue exceeds EUR 100,000
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate; USD value is the approximate lower threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Qualifying business/self-employment taxable base where annual taxable business revenue does not exceed EUR 100,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Qualifying business and other self-employment income
tax_brackets.notes: Separate small-business rate rather than a progressive bracket.

taxation_system.notes: Rates and thresholds are current for 2026. Effective tax depends on classification, deductions, tax residence, treaty relief, and contribution assessment bases.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Slovakia has no dedicated digital-nomad immigration or tax category. A short-stay foreign employee may be exempt from Slovak tax only where the foreign-employer, no-permanent-establishment, treaty, and 183-day conditions are all satisfied; this tax result does not supply residence permission. A Slovak sole trader falls under ordinary Slovak business tax and contribution rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad regime; alternative Slovak sole-trader taxation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 15% for qualifying business/self-employment revenue up to EUR 100,000; otherwise progressive rates up to 35%
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent residence, a qualifying home, or at least 183 days in the calendar year, treaty-adjusted.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident worldwide-income treatment and treaty relief generally apply. Work physically performed in Slovakia can create Slovak tax consequences even when the payer is foreign.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: A genuine Slovak sole trader can face 16% health insurance and, when compulsorily insured, 33.15% social insurance on statutory assessment bases. A foreign employee requires separate payroll, permanent-establishment, and social-security analysis.

fixed_payments.status: Confirmed for the alternative self-employed scenario where the statutory minima apply.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: 2026 minimum compulsory self-employed social insurance: EUR 303.11/month; minimum health-insurance advance: EUR 121.92/month for a self-employed person without disability. Compulsory social-insurance commencement can depend on status and prior income.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Business residence filing is generally EUR 330 at Foreign Police or EUR 350 at an embassy under the general application guidance; route renewal is EUR 200 on paper or EUR 150 electronically, plus residence-card issuance/delivery charges.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration application is generally triggered after calendar-year turnover exceeds EUR 50,000, with separate EUR 62,500 immediate-registration rules. From 1 January 2026 an individual entrepreneur is no longer a taxpayer under the Slovak financial-transaction tax.
fixed_payments.notes: Contribution minima and filing fees can change annually. VAT obligations for cross-border B2B services can arise under rules other than the domestic turnover threshold.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident employee paid by a foreign employer without a Slovak permanent establishment may obtain treaty/domestic relief where work in Slovakia does not exceed the applicable 183-day period, but this does not create a lawful long-stay immigration basis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A person becoming Slovak tax resident should expect worldwide-income reporting, treaty analysis, and possible foreign-employer payroll or permanent-establishment issues. There is no nomad exemption.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A genuine Slovak sole trader may use the 15% qualifying-business rate if annual taxable business revenue is no more than EUR 100,000, while separately accounting for health/social contributions, VAT, and business-residence compliance.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section describes tax consequences, not an endorsement of immigration eligibility.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The rejected Slovak-business alternative directly grants temporary residence once approved; zero means no preliminary residence stage, not instant processing.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General long-term-residence threshold after uninterrupted lawful residence. Absence, language, income, insurance, and accommodation requirements apply.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation generally requires eight continuous years of permanent residence immediately before application.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Conservative combination of five years to long-term residence plus eight years of permanent residence. It applies to the rejected genuine Slovak-business alternative, not to ordinary foreign-contract remote work without conversion.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: This is the statutory maximum decision period after the Ministry receives the application, not a published average. The clock can be suspended while opinions or additional documents are obtained.

key_conditions.value: Maintain uninterrupted lawful residence and actual presence; respect absence limits; obtain A2 Slovak for long-term residence; maintain regular income, insurance, accommodation, business and tax compliance; then satisfy the naturalisation integrity, Slovak-language/general-knowledge, and other statutory requirements. Citizenship remains discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: No general renunciation requirement was established in the reviewed current sources; treatment of the applicant’s existing nationality should be checked under both countries’ laws.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For the citizenship residence exception, the marriage must be ongoing and the couple must have lived in a common household in Slovakia for at least five years immediately before applying. Marriage to a Slovak citizen with permanent residence can separately support an application for five-year permanent residence without this five-year wait.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Slovak citizen can qualify, including a foreign marriage, but a marriage concluded abroad must be registered with Slovakia’s Special Registry and evidenced by a Slovak marriage certificate before the spouse applies for marriage-based permanent residence.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to another foreign national does not create the Slovak-citizen spouse benefits.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be genuine and family life must continue. Police must reject a marriage-based permanent-residence application for a marriage of convenience and can cancel status if spouses do not maintain joint family life or if the marriage ends within the specified five-year period. Citizenship also remains discretionary and the language, integrity, and compliance requirements generally continue.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically confer citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Slovakia primarily follows descent. Birth in Slovakia confers citizenship in narrow anti-statelessness cases, including where both parents are stateless or where foreign parents’ child acquires neither parent’s citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A Slovakia-born child of two foreign parents does not ordinarily become Slovak automatically. Citizenship arises at birth if the child acquires neither parent’s citizenship, or if both parents are stateless; foundling and unproved-foreign-citizenship safeguards also exist.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary case of migrant parents whose nationality passes to the child.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child acquires Slovak citizenship if at least one parent is a Slovak citizen, regardless of birthplace.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: A parent’s permanent residence without Slovak citizenship is insufficient by itself.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Slovak-citizen child may support a qualifying dependent direct-line family-residence case, but the relevant dependency and family conditions must be proved. The parent does not automatically receive permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed sources do not establish an unconditional residence entitlement for every foreign parent of a citizen child.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not acquire Slovak citizenship automatically through the child. He may investigate family residence as a dependent direct-line relative of a Slovak citizen, but must independently meet that route’s conditions and later naturalisation requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage, dependency, custody, and genuine family-life evidence can be material.

rank.notes: Current 2026 ranking reviewed on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley access score combines destinations accessible without a prior visa under its methodology, including visa-on-arrival categories; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Henley’s reviewed ranking page did not provide a separate current visa-required count for Slovakia, so no number was inferred.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The reviewed Henley source aggregates its access score and did not provide a reliable separate Slovakia VOA/eTA count.

passport.notes: Strong EU passport. Rank and access score can change during the year.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is reasonably practical for remote work and international technology activity, particularly in larger cities: the 2025 EF English Proficiency Index places Slovakia 10th globally with a score of 606. Slovak remains necessary for residence filings, business administration, the A2 long-term-residence test, and naturalisation.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a reputable secondary proficiency index based on participating test takers, not a guarantee that every public office or service provider operates in English.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian can be useful for limited community or migrant-support communication—Slovakia’s IOM Migration Information Centre advertises consultations in both languages—but neither is an official language or a substitute for Slovak in filings, the long-term-residence language examination, or naturalisation.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide measure of everyday Russian or Ukrainian proficiency was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official EUR 1,611 gross nominal monthly employee wage in Q1 2026. The independently measured ISCP Q1 2026 mean was EUR 1,870; differences reflect methodology and coverage.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the Q1 2026 ISCP median gross monthly wage of EUR 1,571. This structural wage survey uses a different calculation and sample basis from the Statistical Office headline average, so the two figures should not be treated as one internally identical series.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2026 statutory monthly minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of EUR 1,611.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the Q1 2026 ISCP median gross monthly wage of EUR 1,571.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No finite national maximum wage is published. The latest directly accessible national upper-distribution benchmark checked is the Q4 2025 ISCP 9th decile of EUR 3,213 (approximately USD 3,660 at the cited ECB rate), but it is deliberately not entered as a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: 2026 statutory monthly minimum for a monthly paid full-time employee.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average nominal monthly employee wage in the Slovak economy in Q1 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median gross monthly wage in the Q1 2026 ISCP employer survey: half of covered employees earned less and half earned more. The survey reported a Q1 2026 mean of EUR 1,870 and covered a structurally sampled employer dataset; this median is not from the separate headline quarterly average-wage series.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite national maximum is published; EUR 3,213 per month was the Q4 2025 9th-decile gross-wage benchmark
max_salary_local_currency.notes: The 9th decile means 10% of employees were above EUR 3,213; it is an upper-distribution benchmark, not a maximum. The current official structure-of-earnings publication and STATdat dataset publish distributions and descriptive statistics rather than a meaningful national salary ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross nominal monthly employee wages; headline average from Statistical Office business statistics, median and 9th decile from the weighted ISCP employer survey, and minimum from the statutory full-time monthly minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 headline average and ISCP median; Q4 2025 ISCP upper-distribution benchmark; statutory minimum effective in 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are employee-wage statistics for workers in Slovakia, not immigration income thresholds or sole-trader business income. The EUR 1,611 Q1 2026 headline average and EUR 1,571 ISCP median come from different official/statistical methodologies; the median is retained because it directly answers the distribution question. No actual national maximum is meaningful or published, so the EUR 3,213 9th decile is disclosed only as an upper benchmark and the numeric maximum remains null. USD conversions use approximately 1 EUR = USD 1.1392.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The wage-distribution sources reviewed do not publish a directly comparable current national cost-of-living budget, so no amount was inferred from salary data.
