settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence status was confirmed. Visitor presence or short-stay tax treatment must not be treated as a settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: Slovakia has a credible settlement path for a genuine Slovak sole trader, but not for the unchanged ordinary foreign-contract remote-work profile. To pursue settlement, the applicant would need to switch the economic relationship into a substantiated Slovak business that satisfies the business-plan and economic-benefit assessment.
settlement_track.notes: The alternative business path is approximately 13 years under the conservative ordinary naturalisation sequence, but it is not the selected profile’s current route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated foreign-contract remote-work residence category was found. The independent alternative requires a Slovak trade licence and substantive Slovak business case; employment residence requires a qualifying employment basis.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the prior Slovakia result. At least 15 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected, including seven canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. The national wage median is now supported by the Q1 2026 ISCP result; no true national maximum exists in the reviewed releases, so the latest 9th-decile benchmark is stated explicitly without mislabelling it as a maximum. Other cautious nulls remain only where the named current sources do not publish a defensible value or the concept is not applicable.

data.selection_summary: Slovenia has an active temporary residence permit for digital nomads that directly covers non-EU/EEA employees, civil-law contractors and foreign-registered self-employed people working remotely for entities outside Slovenia. It lasts up to one year and is not renewable, but the holder may apply for another temporary-residence purpose before expiry. The Foreigners Act's general five-year permanent-residence rule counts temporary-residence time and does not exclude the digital-nomad permit; nevertheless, a timely follow-on basis is essential. Local self-employment is a plausible independent conversion after one year of continuous legal residence, but applicants should confirm filing timing with the administrative unit before relying on it.

visa_application.title: Temporary residence permit for digital nomads
visa_application.notes: No national online application portal was identified. Apply personally through a Slovenian diplomatic mission or consulate abroad, or at any administrative unit while legally present in Slovenia. The linked Ministry page is the clearest official starting point.

best_routes.route_name: Temporary residence permit for digital nomads

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Indicative conversion only: twice the latest captured official monthly net earnings for May 2026 (€1,680.80 × 2 = €3,361.60), converted at approximately USD 1.1392 per euro. The legally controlling amount is twice the average monthly net salary most recently published for permit purposes, so verify the current amount when filing.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 3,361.60 per month, indicative as of the latest captured May 2026 earnings release
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The statutory requirement is a formula, not a permanently fixed amount: at least twice the most recently published average monthly net salary in Slovenia.

income_requirement_display.value: At least 2× Slovenia's latest officially published average monthly net salary; approximately €3,361.60 (about US$3,830) using the latest captured data
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: EUR formula, with indicative USD conversion
income_requirement_display.notes: Recalculate from the amount applicable on the filing date. Proof may come from any lawful source of funds.

income_proof_months.notes: The official route page and statutory provision establish a monthly threshold but do not prescribe a fixed number of historical bank-statement or payslip months. Confirm the mission or administrative unit's documentary practice.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be a non-EU/EEA national employed by, contracted under civil law to, or registered as self-employed for an entity outside Slovenia, with the work performed remotely using communications technology.
The applicant must not enter the Slovenian labour market; no Employment Service labour-market consent is required.
Valid passport extending at least three months beyond the intended residence period.
Health insurance covering at least emergency healthcare in Slovenia.
Monthly means of subsistence of at least twice Slovenia's latest average monthly net salary, provable from lawful sources.

General first-residence screening includes public-order/security grounds; the general official entry guidance also calls for health insurance, sufficient resources and home-country criminal-record evidence.
Register the Slovenian temporary address within eight days after entry, permit service or taking up residence, and provide evidence of the right to occupy the address.
Family reunification is available immediately under a favourable rule.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: For employees and contractors, validity follows the contract but cannot exceed one year; foreign self-employed applicants receive one year or the shorter intended stay.

extension_rules.value: Not extendable. A new digital-nomad application is permitted six months after expiry. During validity, the holder may apply for a subsequent temporary residence permit based on another purpose.
extension_rules.notes: A gap is avoided only through a successful switch to another qualifying purpose before the digital-nomad status ends.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The route directly grants a Slovenian temporary residence permit. It is not merely a visitor visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The government expressly allows changing from digital-nomad residence to another purpose. After one continuous legal year, self-employment can provide the successor status for a remote professional and the five-year PR residence sequence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official nomad guidance allows a different-purpose application during permit validity; the Employment Service permits self-employment after one continuous legal year without its separate consent. Coordinate the application date around completion of that year, since a nomad permit cannot be renewed. Article 52 includes qualifying pending-application certificates and does not exclude digital nomads; counting nomad time is an inference from that provision.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation generally requires ten years of actual residence, including the final five years continuously, plus the statutory integration, livelihood, criminal-record, tax, public-order, language and usually prior-citizenship-release conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The digital-nomad permit is only the first year of a possible ten-year residence history; a durable follow-on status is mandatory.

best_routes.notes: This is an active ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route and therefore fits the applicant initially. Settlement is conversion-dependent rather than automatic. A particularly relevant follow-on is local self-employment: official employment guidance says third-country nationals may become self-employed after one year of continuous legal residence and no Employment Service consent is required, but the administrative unit should confirm whether the application can be lodged just before the one-year digital-nomad permit expires.

rejected_routes.route_name: Single residence and work permit for employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No route-specific minimum income researched because this route fails the local-employer criterion.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Employment terms and statutory wage rules apply rather than a digital-nomad income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable to selection; requires an employment/work basis and generally labour-market consent
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because it is not ordinary independent foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: Not established because the route is rejected for profile mismatch.

key_requirements.requirement: A willing employer and employment/work contract are normally required; the Employment Service gives consent in the single-permit procedure.

initial_validity.value: Up to 2 years for the first single permit, limited by the employment or work contract

extension_rules.value: Renewable if a timely application is filed and the statutory employment/work conditions continue to be met.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct single residence and work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Can contribute to the general five-year permanent-residence period, subject to continuity and other conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Not selected because it depends on employment/work rather than ordinary independent foreign remote work.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential general ten-year naturalisation route after qualifying actual residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile because ordinary employment requires a job/employment basis and labour-market procedure.

rejected_routes.route_name: Local sole trader/self-employment as a first-entry route

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general monthly income threshold was confirmed for initial access.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: An older SPOT guidance page mentions €10,000 in own resources and business premises for the historical personal-work-permit procedure, but current filing requirements should be verified.

income_requirement_display.value: No current monthly threshold confirmed; local self-employment normally requires one year of prior continuous legal residence
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Current official employment guidance states a one-year prior-residence requirement
income_requirement_display.notes: Useful as a conversion route, not established as an independent first-entry route for an ordinary foreign-client contractor.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed history was established.

key_requirements.requirement: Third-country nationals may generally self-employ only after one year of continuous legal residence; regulated independent professions are excepted.
Sole-trader registration itself is quick, free at SPOT and requires entry in the Slovenian Business Register; this registration does not by itself create immigration status.

initial_validity.notes: The current official page confirms the self-employment residence condition but does not give a standalone first-entry permit validity fitting this profile.

extension_rules.notes: Must be confirmed for the specific single-permit/self-employment filing.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Potential follow-on single permit after satisfying prior lawful residence and self-employment conditions; not a confirmed first-entry route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Qualifying temporary residence may lead to permanent residence under the general five-year rule.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential general ten-year naturalisation route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected only as a stand-alone entry route. It remains the most relevant independent conversion candidate after the digital-nomad year, provided the administrative unit confirms the filing timing and current business requirements.

summary.value: Admission to a recognised Slovenian study programme supports a temporary residence permit without a local employer. It normally lasts up to one year at a time and may be renewed for the study period. Study residence counts only half toward the permanent-residence period, and permanent residence cannot be issued while the applicant remains solely on study status. Graduates of Slovenian higher education may obtain a nine-month job-search/self-employment temporary permit. This is an education route, not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.
summary.notes: A pre-existing foreign university degree alone does not create this residence right; admission to study in Slovenia is required.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence can arise when a person establishes residential links with Slovenia, including a permanent home, family or centre of interests, habitual residence, or presence exceeding 183 days in a calendar year. Slovenian residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are generally taxed only on Slovenian-source income, subject to tax treaties.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax residence are separate. The permit's one-year validity can cross the 183-day threshold, but the threshold is not the only residence test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate for 2026, not the expected effective rate. Five progressive rates apply: 16%, 26%, 33%, 39% and 50%, before considering allowances, deductions, income classification or treaty relief.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single defensible percentage applies to all digital nomads. The published ordinary employment baseline is 22.10% employee and 16.10% employer contributions, but a person employed by a foreign employer may have to handle both sides, and treaty/EU coordination, foreign coverage and newer compulsory contributions can change the result.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly fixed payment was established for digital-nomad holders. Health-insurance cost depends on the policy or compulsory-insurance position. Residence processing/card charges are one-time rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad income-tax holiday or fixed nomad rate was confirmed. Slovenian-registered self-employed persons may, if eligible and properly elected, use actual expenses or a flat-rate-expense method under which self-employment tax is assessed at 20% on the resulting tax base and is final; this is a general business regime, not an automatic benefit of the digital-nomad permit.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The eligibility limits and deemed-expense rules have changed over time; verify the rules in force before registering a Slovenian activity.

taxes.caveats: Tax results depend on days present, permanent-home and centre-of-interests facts, whether the income is employment or business income, where work is legally sourced, the foreign employer's payroll obligations, social-security coordination and the applicable double-tax treaty. Obtain an individual FURS determination or cross-border tax advice before assuming foreign remote income is exempt.

taxation_system.value: Progressive worldwide personal-income taxation for Slovenian tax residents; source-based taxation for non-residents, with treaties potentially reallocating taxing rights or providing double-tax relief.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residential links or more than 183 days can create Slovenian tax residence; treaty residence may differ.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Slovenian-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated nomad regime confirmed. A separate general flat-rate-expense system may be available to qualifying Slovenian self-employed taxpayers.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary published payroll rates are 22.10% employee and 16.10% employer. Digital-nomad exposure is case-specific and may depend on foreign coverage, bilateral or EU coordination and whether the applicant later registers locally.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 50% is the top marginal rate. It applies only to taxable base above the highest threshold; it is not a flat rate on all earnings.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at €1 = US$1.1392.
Upper threshold shown in approximate USD.
Upper threshold shown in approximate USD.
Upper threshold shown in approximate USD.
Top marginal rate, not effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: 2026 brackets come from a current reputable professional tax summary; residence scope and the existence of dedicated nomad guidance are supported by FURS.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The digital-nomad permit does not itself determine tax residence or grant a tax exemption. FURS applies ordinary residence/source rules and international agreements. A tax resident faces progressive tax up to 50% on worldwide taxable income; a non-resident is generally taxed only on Slovenian-source income, but the source and treaty treatment of work physically performed from Slovenia require case-specific analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary residence permit; ordinary personal-income-tax and treaty rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% cannot safely be assumed; resident screening rate is progressive up to 50%
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residential links or presence over 183 days can establish Slovenian tax residence; treaty tie-breaker rules may alter the result.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is taxable for Slovenian residents. For non-residents, only Slovenian-source income is taxable domestically, but the work-location/source and treaty articles must be analysed.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated nomad tax holiday or reduced rate confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Case-specific. Ordinary employee/employer contribution rates are published, but foreign-employer payroll, home-country coverage, bilateral agreements and local self-employment can materially change liability.

fixed_payments.status: No universal monthly fixed nomad tax or contribution established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Ordinary payroll baseline: 22.10% employee and 16.10% employer, subject to coordination and additional-current-law checks.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: A reputable international mobility tracker reports €50 processing, €4.50 application and €15.47 residence-card issuance charges; verify with the receiving mission or administrative unit.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No route-specific fixed freelancer tax or transaction tax confirmed. Local business registration and VAT obligations arise only if a Slovenian activity is established.
fixed_payments.notes: Private health insurance is mandatory for the permit unless adequate qualifying coverage exists, but no universal monthly premium is published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 183 days does not automatically guarantee non-residence because permanent-home and centre-of-interests tests still matter. Even if non-resident, confirm whether work performed from Slovenia is Slovenian-source and whether a treaty exemption applies.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A Slovenian tax resident generally reports worldwide employment or contract income and is screened under the 16%–50% progressive schedule, with foreign-tax-credit or treaty relief where applicable.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Slovenian-registered sole trader enters local tax, contribution, bookkeeping and potentially VAT rules. A qualifying flat-rate-expense method may be available, but it is separate from digital-nomad status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: FURS published dedicated digital-nomad taxation guidance in February 2026, but its downloadable Word document could not be text-inspected through the web interface. Conclusions are therefore limited to the accessible official FURS residence/scope rules and corroborating current sources.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is granted directly upon approval; no prior Slovenian residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General total qualifying-residence period. Because the digital-nomad year appears to count, approximately four further qualifying years could remain after a seamless conversion. This is not guaranteed if a residence gap occurs.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation is based on ten years of actual residence, including the final five continuously; PR at year five does not itself start a separate rigid five-year clock, but five more years is the typical arithmetic.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Minimum ordinary-naturalisation residence screen, assuming continuous qualifying residence and all other conditions.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable current official typical processing duration was found. Administrative-unit workload and the need to document release from prior citizenship can materially affect timing.

key_conditions.value: Maintain continuous lawful and actual residence; avoid excessive absences; convert before the one-year digital-nomad permit ends; obtain A2 Slovenian for permanent residence and basic Slovenian for naturalisation; maintain livelihood, insurance and tax compliance; meet criminal-record/public-order requirements; take the citizenship oath; and normally obtain release from prior citizenship unless an exception applies.
key_conditions.notes: PR permits absences below six consecutive months and no more than ten months in total over the five-year period. Naturalisation requires the last five residence years to be continuous.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Facilitated naturalisation requires at least three years of marriage to a Slovenian citizen plus at least one year of continuous actual residence in Slovenia immediately before applying.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can count toward the three-year marriage period; it does not by itself confer citizenship. The applicant must still complete at least one continuous year of actual residence before applying and satisfy the remaining statutory conditions or applicable exceptions.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage-based naturalisation remains discretionary and requires a genuine relationship, lawful status, livelihood, language, tax and public-order compliance. Release from prior citizenship is generally required, although the government may consent to an exception for a spouse where release would endanger life or livelihood or cause specified property-right loss. False documents or a sham relationship risk refusal and immigration/criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage also supports family residence under the official family-member rules, but it is not automatic PR or citizenship.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Slovenia expressly follows blood ties rather than general place-of-birth citizenship. Territorial acquisition is limited principally to a child born or found in Slovenia whose parents are unknown, of unknown citizenship or stateless.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Slovenia to two foreign nationals does not ordinarily become Slovenian. A narrow safeguard applies when a child is born or found in Slovenia and both parents are unknown, of unknown citizenship or stateless.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: If no citizenship is acquired, the child receives residence linked to a parent's status under the Foreigners Act.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If the child is born in Slovenia and one parent is Slovenian, citizenship is acquired automatically. If born abroad to one Slovenian and one foreign parent, the parents generally must register the child before age 18; the individual can make a declaration independently up to age 36 if not registered as a minor.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child can support a family-residence argument under the rules for family members of Slovenian nationals, but the official guidance does not establish automatic residence for every non-EU parent solely from the child's birth. Dependency, custody and the exact family-member category should be verified. The parent receives no automatic citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Where a child is not Slovenian but is born in Slovenia, its residence generally follows a parent; if a parent has permanent residence, the law provides for permanent residence for the child, not citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship arises merely because the father has a Slovenian citizen child. A genuine caregiving/dependency relationship may support family residence, but the administrative unit must confirm eligibility. The father must naturalise separately under the applicable residence rules.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Do not confuse the child's descent-based citizenship with citizenship for the migrant father.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026 for rank/access score; Passport Index 2026 for separate entry-mode breakdown

rank.notes: Henley global ranking dated 17 June 2026; Slovenia was tied at rank 7.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score counts destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance and therefore includes some visa-on-arrival arrangements; it is not the same as Passport Index's strict visa-free count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index lists 43 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations. eVisa and other online-authorisation categories are not included in this sum.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Generally workable for international remote work, particularly in Ljubljana, tourism and technology settings, and the government provides essential information in English. Slovenian remains the language of public and official life, so local-language help is advisable for administrative, tax, medical and business-registration procedures.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The 2025 EF English Proficiency Index did not publish a Slovenia result, so no unsupported national proficiency rank is claimed.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited as a general working or administrative language. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, and no current nationwide evidence was found showing broad service availability in either language. Diaspora or private interpretation may help, but Slovenian or English should be expected for daily administration and professional services.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No numerical proficiency estimate was found; this is a cautious practical assessment based on official-language and government-service information.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The digital-nomad permit cannot be extended beyond one year. Settlement fails if the applicant does not secure a qualifying follow-on temporary residence basis before it expires.
settlement_track.summary: The permit is genuine temporary residence and its time appears to count under the general five-year permanent-residence rule, because Article 52 counts temporary permits and does not exclude digital nomads. However, the permit ends after one year, so a timely conversion—potentially to local self-employment after the one-year prior-residence condition—is mandatory for a credible citizenship path.
settlement_track.notes: The statutory components are well supported. The practical sequencing of a self-employment application at the end of the one-year nomad permit should be confirmed in writing with the competent administrative unit before relocation.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The statutory definition expressly covers employment and civil-law contracting for a foreign business entity and self-employment abroad, provided the work is remote and the applicant does not enter Slovenia's labour market.

data.notes: The previous record correctly identified the active digital-nomad permit but understated the now-published income formula and did not fully use the consolidated Foreigners Act. This audit confirms that digital-nomad time is not excluded from the five-year PR calculation and identifies local self-employment after one year as the most relevant independent conversion. Confidence is medium rather than high because the non-renewable permit creates a filing-timing risk, no fixed income-proof history or typical citizenship-processing time is officially published, and route-specific tax/social-security outcomes require individual determination.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Single residence/work permit for self-employment after one continuous legal year
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: The government expressly allows changing from digital-nomad residence to another purpose. After one continuous legal year, self-employment can provide the successor status for a remote professional and the five-year PR residence sequence.
requirements: Arrange a timely successor application while nomad residence remains valid.
Register eligible self-employment and meet the single-permit conditions; the ordinary one-year prior legal-residence requirement must be satisfied.
Maintain continuous qualifying residence and meet PR means, insurance and Slovenian A2 requirements.
reviewed_route_names: Temporary residence permit for digital nomads
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The official nomad guidance allows a different-purpose application during permit validity; the Employment Service permits self-employment after one continuous legal year without its separate consent. Coordinate the application date around completion of that year, since a nomad permit cannot be renewed. Article 52 includes qualifying pending-application certificates and does not exclude digital nomads; counting nomad time is an inference from that provision.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or independent-professional residence route was identified. The official visa catalogue offers locally sponsored employment, study, family, special-purpose, and genuine foreign-investment routes; foreign nationals generally require a work permit to work. An investor can convert from visitor or business status only after registering and operating a monitored local investment, which does not legalize an unchanged foreign software contract. A separate permanent-resident visa becomes available after five consecutive years on qualifying visas, but this applicant has no fitting initial route.

visa_application.title: Visas — Solomon Islands Immigration Division
visa_application.notes: The official visa catalogue currently states that online payment is still being tested and that visa applications are being received in person at Immigration Services in Honiara. Other current route pages continue to link to the eVisa portal and describe online filing, so the public instructions are inconsistent. The visa catalogue is therefore the safest current starting point, and the filing method should be confirmed directly with Immigration before submission.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The form publishes application and grant fees but no minimum investment or monthly-income amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-income threshold; Foreign Investment Act registration and a genuine local investment activity are required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No statutory minimum investment amount is stated in the reviewed investor form
income_requirement_display.notes: The applicant must describe the Solomon Islands investment activity, provide relevant skills and experience, and report annual progress.

income_proof_months.notes: No number of income-proof months is specified because this is an investment route.

key_requirements.requirement: Evidence that the activity is registered under the Foreign Investment Act 2005.
Describe the local investment activity, provide a local address and relevant experience, and submit annual progress reports.
Foreign-investment screening may require a passport, overseas incorporation certificate, résumé, business plan, and confirmation that the activity is not reserved or restricted.
The approved investment must actually operate in Solomon Islands and remains subject to government monitoring and compliance action.

initial_validity.notes: The application form identifies two years as the permitted stay for this category.

extension_rules.notes: No automatic renewal or settlement entitlement was identified.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved investor may obtain an investor visa to reside while carrying on the registered local investment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a substantive local-business route, not a foreign-remote-work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least five consecutive years of lawful residence on qualifying visas, a separate resident visa may be requested.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The permanent-resident page also lists sponsorship, work-permit, and company-director or investor-related requirements; approval is not automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation ordinarily requires ten years of ordinary residence immediately before application and the other statutory eligibility conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Investment does not itself confer citizenship, and the Citizenship Commission retains public-policy and national-interest discretion.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires a registered, operating, monitored local investment rather than ordinary remote software work for a foreign client. The form lists SBD 400 to apply, SBD 1,900 upon grant, and an additional SBD 7,000 for conversion from visitor status or SBD 2,000 from business status.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-income threshold is relevant; a Solomon Islands work permit and local employment are required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The visa page does not state a visa-specific minimum salary.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-income threshold; valid work permit and secured employment with a Solomon Islands organization required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No visa-specific minimum salary is published on the route page
income_requirement_display.notes: The visa is tied to the approved job and work-permit terms.

income_proof_months.notes: The route page does not prescribe a fixed income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Secure long-term employment with an organization or company operating in Solomon Islands.
Obtain a work permit and Labour Division support, then provide the employment visa form, passport, police report, medical report, and sponsor indemnity letter.
Apply from outside Solomon Islands.

initial_validity.value: 2 years, with stay and work rights limited by the work permit
initial_validity.notes: The route page states a USD 450 visa fee plus USD 50 online fee, but the general visa catalogue currently says in-person filing is being used while online payment is tested.

extension_rules.value: Extendable in accordance with work-permit terms; the published extension fee is USD 500
extension_rules.notes: Employment changes must be reported and remain subject to approval.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The visa permits residence and work for the approved local employer.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A separate resident visa may be sought after five consecutive years of lawful residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent-resident work rights are not automatic.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ten years of ordinary residence is the ordinary statutory residence requirement for naturalisation.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary and subject to additional character, language, cultural, continuity, and financial-connection requirements.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires secured local employment, sponsorship, and a Solomon Islands work permit.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No qualifying remote-worker income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying residence-income threshold exists.

income_requirement_display.value: No qualifying remote-work residence threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor and short-term business categories are not remote-work residence permits.

income_proof_months.notes: Income-history evidence is not specified for a qualifying residence route because this is not such a route.

key_requirements.requirement: Use visitor status only for permitted visitor purposes and business status only for short-term business activities.
A non-citizen who works generally requires a work permit.

initial_validity.value: Category-dependent; the official catalogue includes short visitor and business stays
initial_validity.notes: Exact duration depends on nationality and visa subtype.

extension_rules.value: Category-dependent; visitor extensions do not create remote-work residence or work authorization

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct qualifying residence path exists for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The investor form allows visitor-to-investor conversion only after substantive investment registration and additional fees.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Visitor status does not itself lead to permanent residence; a person would first have to qualify for and obtain a separate substantive visa, then meet the five-consecutive-year resident-visa conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Conversion to a genuine investor, employment, family, or other accepted status would be a materially different route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor or short-term business status has no direct citizenship path. Ordinary naturalisation requires the applicant to be ordinarily resident when applying and to have accumulated ten years of ordinary residence immediately before applying, without unlawful presence; a visitor would therefore need a separate lawful status that genuinely establishes Solomon Islands as the person's home.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act defines ordinary residence through making Solomon Islands one's home with continuity apart from temporary absences. It does not state that short visitor stays, by themselves, satisfy that test.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor or business status is not residence or general work permission. The only documented visitor conversion relevant here is to a substantive investor visa, not to freelance or remote-worker status.

summary.value: A student visa is available for an admitted course and normally lasts until shortly after the course, but no independent degree-based skilled-migration route was identified. Study is a separate educational purpose, not permission to continue ordinary foreign-contract software work, and any later permanent-resident application would require five consecutive years on accepted lawful statuses and separate approval.
summary.notes: The official pages do not confirm unrestricted work rights for students or an automatic post-study residence route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident for tax purposes when residing, or intending to reside, in Solomon Islands for longer than six months.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The official wording is intention and residence based rather than a precise day-count formula.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the covered employee's share of gross salary, not a universal freelancer contribution. The employer must remit 12.5% in total: 5% deducted from the employee and 7.5% paid by the employer. The Act's employee definition includes a person employed in Solomon Islands under a contract of service. An employee with a foreign employer and foreign contract can obtain an exemption only if the Board is satisfied that the employer's principal office and contract are abroad, comparable foreign social-security coverage exists, and the employee is not resident in Solomon Islands. Consequently, a resident foreign remote employee cannot assume exemption. The reviewed rules do not expressly impose this percentage on a genuinely self-employed independent contractor; filing-specific classification should be confirmed with SINPF.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed SINPF rules prescribe percentage-based contributions for covered employment, not a universal fixed monthly amount. The self-employed or informal-sector schemes described in the current SINPF materials are voluntary, and no digital-nomad immigration category exists.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, or inbound-expatriate personal tax regime was identified. Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Business incentives or corporate rules should not be treated as a personal remote-worker regime.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical presence and intention, income source, whether the activity constitutes a Solomon Islands business, employment versus independent-contractor classification, SINPF employee status, and any applicable treaty. IRD, SINPF, and Immigration should confirm the treatment of a foreign contract before relocation.

taxation_system.value: Progressive individual income tax with a SBD 30,080 personal exemption and marginal rates of 11%, 23%, 35%, and 40%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Resident when residing or intending to reside for longer than six months.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Solomon Islands-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered employment, SINPF requires 5% from the employee and 7.5% from the employer. A foreign-contract employee's exemption is conditional and unavailable if the statutory non-residence condition is not met. The reviewed rules do not publish a compulsory fixed contribution for genuinely self-employed foreign contractors.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard number is the 40% top marginal rate, not an effective rate. The tax authority's current summary states that the first SBD 30,080 is tax-free; its rate table then applies 11%, 23%, 35%, and 40% bands to taxable income.

tax_brackets.notes: The official page states that the first SBD 30,080 is tax-free.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: SBD 1–15,000 of taxable income after the exemption
SBD 15,001–30,000 of taxable income after the exemption
SBD 30,001–60,000 of taxable income after the exemption
SBD 60,001 and over of taxable income after the exemption
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The general official tax and employment-contribution rules are reasonably clear, but the precise classification and collection mechanics for foreign remote-service income require an individual ruling.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special tax category exists; ordinary residence, income-tax, and potentially employment-contribution rules would apply if a person established lawful residence through another route.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Not applicable—no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker immigration category exists.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive, up to a 40% top marginal rate; the first SBD 30,080 is exempt under the current IRD summary.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Resident when residing or intending to reside for longer than six months.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is reportable once resident for tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified in the reviewed immigration and tax materials.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For covered employment, SINPF requires a total of 12.5% of gross salary: 5% deducted from the employee and 7.5% paid by the employer. The Act can encompass a person employed in Solomon Islands under a contract of service. A foreign-contract employee's exemption requires a foreign employer and foreign contract, comparable foreign social-security coverage, and non-residence in Solomon Islands, so a tax-resident remote employee cannot assume exemption. A genuinely self-employed contractor is not expressly assigned a compulsory percentage or minimum payment in the reviewed provisions; SINPF describes voluntary contribution schemes for people outside ordinary employment.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory route-specific or universal fixed monthly payment is published: there is no digital-nomad visa, covered employment uses percentage-based SINPF contributions, and the reviewed self-employed schemes are voluntary.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Covered employment uses 5% employee plus 7.5% employer contributions rather than a fixed amount. No compulsory minimum monthly SINPF amount for a genuinely self-employed foreign contractor is stated in the reviewed Act, contribution page, or voluntary-scheme materials.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad-visa fee applies because no such visa category exists. Fees instead depend on the separate non-fitting immigration category used.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Local business registration, licensing, goods or services taxes, withholding, or stamp duties may arise if a local enterprise is established, but the reviewed current sources do not impose a single universal fixed remote-worker charge.
fixed_payments.notes: This resolves the earlier dataset marker: the applicable published obligations are either percentage-based employment contributions or voluntary savings, not a confirmed mandatory fixed monthly remote-worker payment. SINPF should still determine whether a particular foreign contract is employment or independent contracting.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident is taxed on Solomon Islands-source income, but performing services physically in the country may create local-source, SINPF, or immigration issues before tax residence; an official determination is advisable.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide foreign-contract income would be reportable and taxed under progressive rates up to 40%. If the contract is classified as employment, SINPF coverage may also apply because the foreign-worker exemption requires non-residence.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A sole trader files an IR21 return and may owe provisional tax. Immigration authorization, business registration, licensing, and contractor-versus-employee classification must be checked separately; the reviewed SINPF materials do not state a mandatory fixed contribution for genuine self-employment.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This remains a hypothetical tax analysis because Solomon Islands has no qualifying digital-nomad route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route exists for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Employment, study, investment, and family visas are separate-purpose routes.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: For applicants lawfully resident on other accepted visas, the official resident-visa page requires at least five consecutive years. This does not make the current profile eligible to start the chain.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Illustrative only: permanent residence can be requested after five years, while ordinary naturalisation requires ten years of ordinary residence immediately before application. The statutes do not define a separate mandatory five-year period after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: This is the ordinary statutory residence requirement on a separate qualifying route; no qualifying initial remote-work route exists for this applicant.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Act requires the Commission to decide within 120 days after receiving the application or requested additional information. This is a statutory decision period, not a guarantee of approval or total certificate-processing time.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary residence for ten years immediately before application, no unlawful presence in that period, ordinary residence at filing, good character, sufficient conversational English, Pijin or a Solomon Islands vernacular, respect for local culture and way of life, understanding of citizenship duties, economic sustainability or other evidence of a continuing relationship, and oath or pledge after approval.
key_conditions.notes: The Commission may refuse an otherwise eligible application on public-policy or national-interest grounds.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A spouse must have been continuously married to a birth citizen for at least five years. Section 14(6) does not impose the ordinary ten-year residence test on this category.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A marriage already valid under Solomon Islands law or another country's law can count toward the five continuous years; the statute defines marriage as between a man and a woman.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The applicant must be married to a birth citizen, not merely any naturalised citizen, on the application date.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must be at least 18, be of good character, and be likely to reside in Solomon Islands or maintain a close and continuing relationship. Citizenship is not automatic through marriage, and the Commission retains discretion. Genuine documentation and relationship evidence should be expected; false or misleading information can support refusal, prosecution, or later revocation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The family-relationship visa is a separate immigration status, requires sponsorship and relationship evidence, and does not itself confer citizenship or unrestricted work rights.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Solomon Islands alone does not grant automatic citizenship under the reviewed Act. The amended Act exempts a person born in Solomon Islands from the ordinary ten-year residence requirement, creating a restricted, application-based territorial benefit rather than unconditional jus soli. Children of birth-citizen parents are treated separately as birth citizens.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born to two foreign temporary or permanent residents does not automatically acquire citizenship solely by birth in Solomon Islands. Birth removes the ordinary ten-year residence requirement for a later citizenship application, but the current Act does not establish unconditional automatic citizenship.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No rule granting automatic citizenship based only on a parent's permanent residence appears in the reviewed current Act.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child under 18 of a parent or parents who are birth citizens is treated outside the ordinary application eligibility rules and is entitled as a birth citizen under the amended framework.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Documentary registration or proof procedures may still be necessary even where citizenship exists by law.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence on a foreign parent. The statutory family-relationship visa categories are spouse and child of the citizen sponsor, not parent of a citizen.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A foreign parent must independently qualify through marriage, employment, investment, or another immigration category. The current family-visa form expressly limits eligibility to the sponsor's spouse or child.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship, permanent residence, or parent-of-citizen family visa arises for a migrant father from the child's citizenship. If he is married to the child's birth-citizen mother for five continuous years, he may separately apply under the marriage-based citizenship category, subject to character, connection, and Commission approval requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The current Immigration Regulations and Form 8 define family-relationship visa applicants as the citizen sponsor's spouse or child; they do not publish a category for the citizen child's foreign father. The citizenship law separately recognizes marriage to a birth citizen, but parentage alone is not an accelerated category.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 44 visa-on-arrival and 9 eTA destinations. The index also lists eVisa destinations separately, so these figures should not be interpreted as summing to every destination.

passport.notes: Passport Index reported a mobility score of 136. This differs from Henley-style scores that combine visa-free and visa-on-arrival access under another methodology.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the official language and is used for formal government and private-sector communication. The 2019 census reported English literacy for 72.9% of people aged five and over, rising to 87.4% in Honiara, so English is practical in professional and urban settings; Pijin remains an important lingua franca.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Language practicality does not resolve infrastructure or immigration restrictions.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or widely documented working languages. Daily life and administration should be expected to require English and often Pijin.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The reviewed census materials do not quantify Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking support, so such support should not be assumed.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The completed 2024–2025 HIES page states that data cleaning, analysis, and official reports are the next stage; it does not yet publish a current national wage average. The captured national wage estimate is therefore the much older 2012–2013 HIES in SBD, which is not converted into a purported current USD average.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The 2024–2025 HIES update does not publish a current national median wage. The older 2012–2013 median is retained only in local currency below.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Invest Solomons describes this as a monthly average minimum wage based on a 45-hour week. It is a reference comparison assembled from secondary wage sources, not an observed national minimum salary distribution.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current HIES wage tables have not yet been published. The latest analyzed national figure captured is from 2012–2013 and is too old to present as a current 2026 USD average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current HIES update reports completion of fieldwork but not a national median wage result.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the minimum-wage source nor the available HIES materials define a national maximum salary or current upper wage-distribution ceiling.

min_salary_local_currency.value: SBD 1,560 per month equivalent at SBD 8.00/hour for sectors other than agriculture, plantations and fishing; SBD 1,404 per month equivalent at SBD 7.20/hour for agriculture, plantations and fishing
min_salary_local_currency.notes: These are statutory minimum-wage equivalents, not observed minimum salaries. The hourly rates took effect on 1 August 2019 and WageIndicator lists them as current in June 2026. Monthly equivalents use the 45-hour workweek stated by Invest Solomons and 52 weeks divided by 12 months: 8 × 45 × 52 ÷ 12 = SBD 1,560; 7.20 × 45 × 52 ÷ 12 = SBD 1,404. Actual monthly pay varies with paid hours and employment terms.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2012–2013 HIES average among people in wage or salary jobs; historical, not a current 2026 wage estimate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2012–2013 HIES median among people in wage or salary jobs; historical.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: A statutory maximum wage does not exist in the reviewed minimum-wage material. The historical HIES reports means, medians, and grouped or quintile results rather than a national maximum, while the 2024–2025 HIES wage analysis has not yet been published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory hourly minimum converted to a 45-hour monthly equivalent; historical annual wage or salary income per wage-job worker converted to monthly amounts for average and median

average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum fields now reflect the published statutory sector rates in local currency. settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route can start a settlement chain. Local employment or genuine monitored investment may lead to a separate resident visa after five consecutive years and potentially naturalisation after ten years of ordinary residence, but both require switching to a materially different, non-fitting status.
settlement_track.notes: The ineligible conclusion is preserved. Focused review confirmed that visitor status has no direct settlement path and that the current citizenship reprint requires ten years of ordinary residence immediately before an ordinary application.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official catalogue contains no dedicated digital-nomad, remote-worker, ordinary freelance, or independent-professional visa. Local work requires a work permit, while the independent investor route requires a registered and monitored local investment.

data.notes: Thirty-one distinct directly relevant URLs were retained, including nine focused sources not present in the previous source set. The pass resolved the visitor-to-citizenship wording, employment versus self-employed SINPF treatment, fixed-payment status, parent-of-citizen limitation, and statutory minimum wage. Current official average, median, and maximum wage statistics remain unpublished because the 2024–2025 HIES is still at the analysis and report-preparation stage; those numeric values remain cautiously null.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, independent freelancer, or ordinary self-employed residence route was found. Somalia's published stay-permit rules cover locally sponsored foreign employees, foreign investors with a Somali business permit, government workers, and family cases. The eTAS is a visitor-entry authorization and does not confer qualifying residence or ordinary remote-work permission.

visa_application.title: Somalia Electronic Travel Authorization (eTAS)
visa_application.notes: This is the official visitor eTAS application channel confirmed by the Somali embassy. It is not a digital-nomad, work, or settlement application. The portal currently serves its application interface through an ICA-branded somvisa.com frontend.

income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No numerical income formula applies; eligibility is based on a locally sponsored job, an approved employment contract, and a work permit
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility depends on local employment sponsorship rather than foreign remote income.

income_proof_months.notes: The published requirements prescribe no income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: A Somali company or organization must apply for the foreign employee and provide security, livelihood, residence, and employment guarantees.
An employment contract approved by the Ministry of Labour and a work permit are required.
Passport, photographs, CV, academic or skills evidence, and medical documentation are required or may be requested.
Published work-permit fees are US$780 for 12 months, US$490 for six months, and US$320 for three months; applications are in person.

initial_validity.value: One year, six months, three months, or exceptionally one month
initial_validity.notes: The Foreign Employment Act sets a one-year maximum for a work permit; ICA publishes shorter general stay-permit periods.

extension_rules.value: A renewal application must be filed with the Registrar before the work permit expires. Work may continue while the timely application is pending, and each renewal may not exceed one year.
extension_rules.notes: The Foreign Employment Act states no numerical lead time; filing must occur before expiry. Refusal may be appealed to the Minister within 30 days.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A purpose-specific stay permit is available after local employment and work authorization are established.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is temporary stay tied to local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The reviewed current immigration pages and laws do not publish a fixed transition from this work permit to permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent-residence eligibility and whether work-permit time counts require direct ICA confirmation.

path_to_citizenship.value: The legacy citizenship law provides discretionary naturalization after at least seven years of residence, good conduct, and willingness to renounce foreign citizenship, but no official source confirms that this work-permit category creates an automatic or reliable settlement transition.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The 2012 Constitution called for a new citizenship law, creating uncertainty about the continuing operation of conflicting 1962 provisions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer and locally approved employment contract are mandatory. An unchanged foreign software contract does not satisfy the published route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed current pages prescribe no remote-income threshold or generally applicable minimum-investment figure.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed current pages prescribe no local-currency threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-income threshold; a Somali business permit and substantive local business profile are required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Business permit and genuine local business activity rather than a salary formula
income_requirement_display.notes: The absence of a published general capital threshold does not make this an ordinary freelancer route.

income_proof_months.notes: The published investor stay-permit requirements state no income-history period.

Valid business permit from the Ministry of Commerce and a detailed business profile.
Passport valid for at least one year, photographs, CV, and potentially academic or skills certificates and medical documentation.

initial_validity.value: One year, six months, three months, or exceptionally one month
initial_validity.notes: ICA publishes these general stay-permit periods but does not map a guaranteed period to every investor filing.

extension_rules.notes: The investor must verify both business-licence renewal and a separate stay-permit renewal with the responsible agencies.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A foreign investor with a Somali business permit may apply for a temporary stay permit.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The general legacy rule should not be treated as a guaranteed investor settlement program.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this is a genuine Somali business or investor route, not residence for ordinary work performed solely under a foreign client or employer contract.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No direct eTAS-to-residence transition is published.

summary.notes: Academic qualifications support an employer-sponsored work-permit application but do not independently confer residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident for a tax year if the individual has a permanent home in Somalia; is a Somali citizen unless a permanent home abroad is available throughout the year; is present in Somalia for an aggregate 183 days or more in any 12-month period beginning or ending in the year; or is a Federal Government or Federal Member State employee posted abroad during the year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The permanent-home test is independent of the 183-day test, so fewer than 183 days does not by itself establish nonresidence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal/screening rate under the operative 2025 federal individual schedule. Resident-adult annual bands are 0%, 6%, 12%, and 18%; nonresident individuals are stated to be taxed at 18%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: The 2025 income-tax manual and regulations address retirement contributions but do not publish a generally applicable mandatory social-security percentage for an ordinary foreign remote worker or sole proprietor; the labour programme likewise supplies no such rate.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No qualifying remote-worker route or universal monthly payment exists. Work-permit charges are duration-based; the 12-month fee of US$780 is equivalent to US$65 per permit month but is paid as a permit fee. A separate presumptive-business minimum applies only to qualifying domestic businesses.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime was found. The 2025 manual describes a presumptive regime for resident natural persons carrying on business solely in Somalia with annual turnover not exceeding US$50,000, but listed professionals including engineers are excluded and the regime does not create immigration status.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The presumptive regime requires quarterly payments equal to the greater of US$37.50 or 1.5% of quarterly turnover; it is not a foreign-contract remote-work concession.

taxes.caveats: The 2025 federal rules now establish residence and worldwide-income principles, but the classification and source of services performed in Somalia for a foreign client, federal-member-state overlap, social contributions, treaty relief, and the interaction with immigration permission still require Somali filing advice.

taxation_system.value: The 2025 federal system taxes resident adults progressively at 0%–18%; nonresident individuals are stated to be taxed at 18%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, specified citizenship status, or at least 183 aggregate days in a relevant 12-month period can establish individual residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are assessed on worldwide employment, business, and investment income. Nonresidents are assessed on Somali permanent-establishment income and other Somalia-source employment, business, and investment income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime. A limited presumptive business regime applies only to qualifying resident natural persons with domestic-only business and turnover not exceeding US$50,000; listed professionals including engineers are excluded.
taxation_system.social_security: No generally applicable mandatory percentage for this profile is published in the checked current federal tax and labour materials.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 18% dashboard figure is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. The 2025 annual adult-resident bands are US$0–1,200 at 0%, over US$1,200–6,000 at 6%, over US$6,000–18,000 at 12%, and over US$18,000 at 18%.

tax_brackets.notes: Annual exempt band under the 2025 manual.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Income within this resident-adult annual band
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket.

tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket.
Top marginal rate; nonresident individuals are separately stated to be taxed at 18%.

taxation_system.notes: The Ministry states that the Income Tax Act took effect on 11 May 2025 and the regulations on 15 May 2025. The manual is official practical guidance but says the Act and regulations prevail.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax regime applies because no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route was found. General 2025 individual rules would still need to be considered if a person is lawfully present and working.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No qualifying digital-nomad route; general individual tax rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–18% progressive resident-adult PIT; 18% stated rate for nonresident individuals
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence can arise from a permanent home in Somalia or aggregate presence of at least 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending in the tax year; specified citizenship and government-posting rules also apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident individual is assessed on worldwide employment, business, and investment income and may claim credit for qualifying foreign income tax. A nonresident is assessed on Somali permanent-establishment income and other Somalia-source employment, business, and investment income; the source classification of remote services performed in Somalia for a foreign payer requires Inland Revenue Department advice.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found. The domestic-business presumptive regime is not a nomad concession and excludes listed professionals including engineers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Locally employed persons are subject to employer withholding. No generally applicable mandatory social-security or health-contribution rate for a foreign remote worker or sole proprietor is published in the checked current sources.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad-specific recurring payment exists; no generally applicable fixed social-security or health payment for this profile is published. Separate immigration and business charges apply only if the person qualifies for those different statuses.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed social-security payment is established in the 2025 federal income-tax materials or the reviewed labour programme.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee exists. A locally sponsored work permit costs US$780 for 12 months, US$490 for six months, or US$320 for three months; the stay-permit service page lists a separate US$5 fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: For a qualifying resident natural person in the domestic-only presumptive regime, quarterly tax is the greater of US$37.50 or 1.5% of quarterly turnover, but listed professionals including engineers are excluded. The manual also lists 10% withholding on service-fee payments; filing applicability to a foreign remote contract requires IRD confirmation.
fixed_payments.notes: Business-licence fees vary by activity and are not universal remote-worker payments. No dedicated remote-work status exists.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying fewer than 183 days does not automatically make a person nonresident because a permanent home in Somalia is an independent residence test. If nonresident, Somalia-source employment, business, or investment income and Somali permanent-establishment income remain taxable; the 2025 manual states an 18% rate for nonresident individuals, so there is no supported blanket tax-free short-stay scenario.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident is assessed on worldwide employment, business, and investment income, with foreign-tax-credit relief potentially available. Resident-adult PIT is progressive from 0% to 18%, but the foreign contract must be classified and the work must separately be immigration-authorized.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A sole proprietor is subject to individual tax rules and filing. The presumptive regime is limited to a resident natural person carrying on business only in Somalia with annual turnover not exceeding US$50,000; listed professionals including engineers are excluded, and none of these tax registrations grants residence permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax rules are materially clearer than in the previous record, but they do not create a lawful remote-work immigration route. Source and classification of foreign-paid services should be confirmed with the Inland Revenue Department.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent foreign-contract route exists. Employer and investor stay permits are separate rejected routes.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The reviewed current sources publish no permanent-residence category, clock, or conversion rule applicable to these permits.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The legacy law speaks in terms of residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence stage, so this interval cannot be calculated.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be stated for this profile because there is no qualifying entry route. Separately, the legacy 1962 law provides discretionary naturalization after at least seven years of residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: ICA says citizenship requires rigorous procedures but publishes no typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: Under the legacy law, general naturalization requires at least seven years of residence, good civil and moral conduct, an application, and willingness to renounce foreign citizenship. The 2012 Constitution called for a special citizenship law, so current procedure and conflicting legacy provisions require ICA or legal confirmation.
key_conditions.notes: The reviewed sources publish no language-test requirement, absence allowance, permanent-residence prerequisite, or reliable processing standard.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The 1962 law states that a foreign woman marrying a Somali male citizen acquires Somali citizenship upon marriage; it does not provide an equivalent automatic benefit to a foreign husband of a Somali woman. Current implementation should be verified.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing valid marriage may support the legacy automatic rule only for a foreign wife of a Somali male citizen. A foreign husband of a Somali woman should not assume accelerated citizenship. ICA material recognizes a family-visa basis for spouses and children but publishes no permanent-residence clock.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The sex-discriminatory legacy provisions conflict with modern constitutional equality principles and have been subject to proposed reform.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally valid and genuine. Current documentation, recognition of foreign marriages, citizenship registration, dual-nationality consequences, and the effect of constitutional reforms require direct confirmation. Sham marriage or false documents can create immigration, criminal, and citizenship risks.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The reviewed current official materials publish no marriage-citizenship filing checklist.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The operative legacy framework primarily transmits citizenship through a Somali father. Birth in Somalia alone does not confer broad citizenship; limited protection exists for children of unknown parents born or found in Somalia.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Somalia to two identified foreign parents does not automatically acquire Somali citizenship merely by birthplace.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Anti-statelessness protection is limited, and current reforms should be checked.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Under the 1962 law and 1963 regulations, a child of a Somali father automatically acquires citizenship. Transmission by a Somali mother is restricted and historically required a separate grant after residence unless the father was stateless. Because the Constitution guarantees equality and called for a new law, a claim through either parent requires current verification.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The generic one-citizen-parent flag remains null because the published legacy rule is sex-dependent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Somali citizen child does not automatically naturalize a foreign parent. A spouse or parent may have a family-stay basis, but no automatic permanent-residence or citizenship benefit for the foreign father was confirmed.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Family applications require direct ICA confirmation.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically acquire Somali citizenship because his child is Somali. If the mother is Somali, the child's own claim is also affected by unresolved sex-discriminatory legacy provisions.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The reviewed citizenship law publishes no accelerated parent-of-citizen naturalization rule.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is not an official federal language. Official institutions publish some English-language material, and English can be workable in international organizations and parts of business, but Somali is important for administration, local hiring, and daily integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This is a cautious practical inference from the constitutional language rule and availability of official English services; no national English-proficiency statistic was published.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official status, and the reviewed materials provide no evidence of broad public or administrative use.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Somali, Arabic, and often English are more relevant.
