settlement_track.summary: Somalia has visitor, locally sponsored employment, and genuine investor or business routes, but no published residence route for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker. The legacy seven-year naturalization provision does not cure the absence of a qualifying entry route or establish a confirmed permit-to-settlement transition.
settlement_track.notes: Employer and investor permits may create temporary lawful stay for their stated purposes, but neither fits this profile and no official permanent-residence clock is published.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker visa or ordinary foreign-client freelancer residence route was found. Visitor status is insufficient, employment requires local sponsorship, and the investor category requires a Somali business permit and local business substance.

data.notes: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence route was found. This focused pass reviewed 36 distinct directly relevant URLs in total, including 11 URLs absent from the previous source set. The 2025 federal income-tax manual resolved the individual residence test and worldwide-income treatment; the Foreign Employment Act resolved work-permit renewal. National SOS salary values remain null because current official and ILO materials publish neither a legal minimum-wage amount nor validated national mean, median, or maximum monthly employee wages.

data.selection_summary: South Africa has an active Remote Work Visitor Visa for employees of foreign employers, with a gross-salary threshold of ZAR 650,796 per year and stays exceeding three months up to three years. It is nevertheless a visitor-class visa: it prohibits South African employment and ordinarily cannot be changed to another status from inside South Africa. No official source confirms that time on this visa counts toward permanent residence or citizenship. The separate points-based work routes require a South African employment offer, so South Africa does not satisfy this citizenship-oriented selection for an ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

visa_application.title: Remote Work Visitor Visa requirements
visa_application.notes: This is the official DHA requirements checklist, not a universal online application form. Applications are filed through the responsible South African mission or authorised service provider abroad; the filing route and fees depend on the applicant's country of residence.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of ZAR 54,233 per month using about ZAR 16.5 per USD. The binding threshold is the annual ZAR amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: ZAR 650,796 gross per year, equivalent to approximately ZAR 54,233 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official requirement is expressed as annual gross salary.

income_requirement_display.currency_basis: Official threshold in ZAR; USD is approximate

Gross salary of at least ZAR 650,796 per year, supported by three months of bank statements.
Statement explaining the visit's purpose and duration, return ticket or reservation, qualifying passport, applicable fee, and yellow-fever certificate where relevant.
No employment may be taken up in South Africa.

initial_validity.notes: The official DHA checklist controls over inconsistent country-specific service-provider pages.

extension_rules.value: No route-specific renewal entitlement was confirmed in the official checklist.
extension_rules.notes: The visa can initially be granted for up to three years. Extension eligibility should be confirmed with the responsible mission.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The visa directly authorises temporary residence for prescribed foreign remote work but remains legally classified as a visitor's visa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary legal residence is not equivalent to a settlement-qualifying work visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After the Remote Work Visitor Visa, PR can be pursued through an independently qualifying work or other PR route. The ordinary work route requires five continuous years on qualifying work visas and a permanent South African employment offer.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The remote visa is section 11 visitor status, not section 19 work status, so it does not meet the work-based PR clock. Five years refers to the standard work successor; exceptional-skills and financial-independence PR grounds are separate and may have different requirements. Exit=true refers to the ordinary visitor-to-work successor, not every possible direct PR ground.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship clock is confirmed from the remote-work visitor visa; the applicant would first need a separate route to permanent residence and then satisfy naturalisation rules.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Temporary or conditional sojourns do not establish the required naturalisation residence.

rejected_routes.notes: This route fits foreign-employer remote work for temporary living but has no confirmed PR or citizenship conversion. It therefore fails the citizenship-oriented selection.

rejected_routes.route_name: Points-Based Critical Skills or General Work Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No universal minimum applies to every critical-skills case. The points schedule awards salary points at ZAR 650,976 and ZAR 976,194 annually but separately makes a South African employment offer mandatory.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No universal route-wide minimum; a South African employment offer is mandatory and offered salary affects points
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The points notice awards 20 points from ZAR 650,976 and 50 points above ZAR 976,194 gross annually.

income_requirement_display.value: Mandatory South African employment offer; salary influences points
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: 20 points at ZAR 650,976–976,194/year; 50 points above ZAR 976,194/year
income_requirement_display.notes: An occupation on the critical-skills list scores 100 points, but an employment offer remains mandatory.

income_proof_months.notes: A months-of-income-history measure is inapplicable; the route instead requires an employment offer and qualification evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Mandatory offer of employment in South Africa under the current points notice.
Critical-skills occupation or sufficient points, relevant qualifications, SAQA evaluation, professional-body documentation where applicable, and employment contract.

initial_validity.value: A work visa may be issued for a route-specific period, generally not exceeding five years.
initial_validity.notes: A one-year visa can apply where proof of a pending SAQA evaluation is submitted.

extension_rules.value: Extensions remain conditional on compliance with the work-visa, points, employment, and qualification rules.
extension_rules.notes: This is separate from the Remote Work Visitor Visa.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Qualifying applicants receive a South African work visa tied to local employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not fit continued work solely for a foreign employer.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Under Immigration Act section 26(a), PR may be sought after five continuous years holding section 19 work visas and with a permanent South African employment offer. Separately, section 27(b) permits a discretionary direct PR application for a listed critical skill, with proof of the skill, at least five years of post-qualification experience, testimonials or CV, and a motivation showing benefit to South Africa.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Section 27(b) is discretionary and qualification-based, not a conversion entitlement from the Remote Work Visitor Visa. Current filing practice and the applicant's exact critical-skills entry require confirmation.

path_to_citizenship.value: After permanent residence, naturalisation generally requires five continuous years of ordinary residence as a permanent resident, presence compliance, language ability, good character, and other statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The work-visa branch requires changing to South African employment; critical-skills PR remains discretionary.

rejected_routes.notes: Although an applicant can submit the application personally, the ordinary work-visa profile requires a South African job offer. The separate critical-skills PR ground is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

summary.value: Qualifications, experience, and critical-skills occupations contribute to the points-based work route, but the current points schedule makes a South African employment offer mandatory. Section 27(b) separately provides a discretionary critical-skills PR ground requiring a listed skill and at least five years of post-qualification experience.
summary.notes: The work-visa branch grants temporary residence only with local employment. Critical-skills PR is not a general degree-only entitlement or ordinary remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is tax resident if ordinarily resident in South Africa or, if not ordinarily resident, after satisfying all parts of the physical-presence test: more than 91 days in the current tax year, more than 91 days in each of the preceding five tax years, and more than 915 days total in those five preceding years. Treaty residence can override domestic residence. Services physically rendered in South Africa are generally South African-source even before tax residence begins.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The visa's separate 183-day SARS-registration wording is not the domestic tax-residence test or a blanket exemption.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top 2026/27 marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee UIF is normally 1% of covered remuneration, matched by 1% from the employer and subject to a ceiling. Applicability to foreign-employer remote work requires case-specific review.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the published maximum employee UIF deduction of ZAR 177.12 monthly. This is conditional on UIF coverage, not a universal nomad payment.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special reduced digital-nomad personal-income-tax rate was found. The visa checklist instead contains SARS-registration rules linked to treaty-country status and aggregate 183-day presence.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty relief may apply only when all relevant short-term employment conditions are met.

taxes.caveats: Foreign payment does not make work performed in South Africa tax-free. Non-residents are generally taxed on South African-source services unless treaty relief applies. Payroll, permanent-establishment, UIF, VAT, foreign-tax-credit, and provisional-tax outcomes depend on the contract and structure.

taxation_system.value: Progressive residence- and source-based personal income tax, with 2026/27 marginal rates from 18% to 45%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Ordinary-residence or multi-year physical-presence test; treaty residence may override. South African-source income can be taxable before domestic residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents on South African-source income. Services physically performed in South Africa are normally locally sourced, subject to treaty relief.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad rate or holiday was confirmed.
taxation_system.social_security: UIF is generally 1% employee plus 1% employer on covered remuneration, capped at the published earnings ceiling. Foreign-payroll coverage is contract-specific.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard number is the 45% top marginal screening rate, not an effective-rate estimate. The 2026/27 bands are 18%, 26%, 31%, 36%, 39%, 41%, and 45%.

tax_brackets.notes: USD conversion uses approximately ZAR 16.5/USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Amount above ZAR 245,100, plus base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Amount above ZAR 383,100, plus base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Amount above ZAR 530,200, plus base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Amount above ZAR 695,800, plus base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Amount above ZAR 887,000, plus base tax
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure approximates the upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Amount above ZAR 1,878,600, plus base tax
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal band; USD figure approximates its lower threshold.

taxation_system.notes: Current brackets and remote-visa registration wording were captured. Effective liability still requires treaty and contract analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The remote-work visa has no special concessional income-tax rate. South African-source rules, domestic residence rules, and treaty relief govern the result.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Foreign-employer remote worker on a visitor-class remote-work visa
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 18%–45% progressive PIT; 45% is the top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domestic residence follows ordinary residence or the multi-year physical-presence test. The visa separately requires SARS registration after aggregate presence over 183 days in 12 months for treaty-country residents, or registration without that deferral outside the stated treaty treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally report worldwide income. For non-residents, remuneration for services physically performed in South Africa is generally South African-source unless treaty relief applies.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No reduced-rate or tax-holiday regime confirmed. The visa checklist's 183-day language concerns registration and treaty treatment, not an automatic exemption.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: UIF is normally 1% employee plus 1% employer for covered employment, subject to a ceiling. Foreign-employer payroll, permanent-establishment, and UIF obligations require individual review.

fixed_payments.status: No universal digital-nomad fixed tax or social-security payment confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Conditional maximum employee UIF deduction shown by SARS is ZAR 177.12/month; applicability to foreign payroll is not established by the visa checklist.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The checklist requires the applicable fee, but no universal amount was established because mission and VFS charges vary by filing country.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT applies to local consumption. A locally registered business may face VAT registration once taxable supplies exceed ZAR 2.3 million in a rolling 12-month period from 1 April 2026; this is not automatically imposed on a foreign employee holding the visa.
fixed_payments.notes: Private medical cover is prudent but was not listed as a universal mandatory fixed payment in the reviewed remote-work checklist.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident working physically from South Africa may still earn South African-source remuneration. Treaty relief may apply when presence, foreign-employer, and no-local-PE conditions are satisfied.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A person who becomes ordinarily resident or meets the physical-presence test is generally taxable on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 45%, subject to treaty residence and credits.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The visa is framed around employment with a foreign employer, not an ordinary freelancer or local sole proprietor. Local registration may introduce provisional tax, VAT, payroll, and business-visa issues without creating an immigration conversion path.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Immigration permission and tax liability are separate. Advice should address the treaty, employer location, permanent-establishment exposure, days present, and employment status.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The visa directly authorises a temporary stay; no preliminary residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No number applies because remote-work visitor time has no confirmed conversion or counting rule. Section 26(a) separately requires five years on section 19 work visas and a permanent South African offer; section 27(b) critical-skills PR is a separate discretionary application.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalisation requires five continuous years of ordinary residence after PR, subject to presence, language, character, and approval requirements.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: There is no citizenship timeline from the Remote Work Visitor Visa. A hypothetical move to local employment is a separate profile and approval chain.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official naturalisation form says consideration and finalisation may take 12 months; actual delays can vary.

key_conditions.value: The remote-work route does not start a confirmed settlement clock and ordinarily cannot be changed in-country. Naturalisation after obtaining PR requires continuous ordinary residence, presence compliance, good character, ability to communicate in an official language, citizenship knowledge, intent to remain, and potentially renunciation where the prior country does not permit dual citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: Proposed reforms in the 2026 White Paper were not treated as enacted law.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Five years in a genuine spousal relationship with a South African citizen or permanent resident can support direct PR. Citizenship is not automatic.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage matters only if the spouse is a South African citizen or permanent resident, or as a dependent relationship under another qualifying status. Marriage to another foreign remote worker creates no faster settlement route.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The relationship period and lawful status must be documented.

requirements_and_risks.value: Spousal residence and PR require a legally recognised, good-faith relationship and supporting identity, civil-status, cohabitation, and financial evidence. Spousal naturalisation still requires permanent residence and prescribed residence conditions. Fraud can cause refusal, withdrawal, and criminal or immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A previous two-year citizenship figure reflected superseded statutory wording and was not preserved.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is principally by a citizen parent. South-Africa-born children of permanent residents may qualify at majority after continuous residence and birth registration; other foreign-parent children may apply at majority after continuous residence from birth. Stateless children have a protective rule.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: The child is not ordinarily a citizen automatically at birth. A child born to permanent-resident parents can qualify at majority after continuous residence and registration; a child of other foreign parents may apply at majority after continuous residence from birth.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A protective exception applies to a registered South-Africa-born child who has no other citizenship or right to another nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is a South African citizen at birth, the child is a citizen by birth whether born inside or outside South Africa, subject to registration. One permanent-resident parent alone does not confer automatic citizenship at birth under the amended Act.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The detailed statutory rule controls over a conflicting general government summary.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child can support a separate family immigration application for a foreign parent but does not automatically grant the parent permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Eligibility, financial assurance, dependency, custody, and genuine-parental-relationship evidence still require assessment.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not become a citizen through the child's citizenship. A citizen child may provide a family-based basis for a relatives visa or potentially PR, but the father must apply separately.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage and an ongoing genuine parental relationship should be documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank on the research date; rankings change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free destinations, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 43 visa-on-arrival plus 7 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index was used because it publishes the requested breakdown. Its methodology is not directly interchangeable with Henley.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. English is an official language and is widely used in government, legal, tax, and business documentation. Major urban areas are generally practical for English-speaking remote workers.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Connectivity, electricity resilience, infrastructure, and security should be checked for the specific neighbourhood.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low outside private migrant communities. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official, so English is substantially more practical for government, banking, housing, and business.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No official nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was established.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of ZAR 29,997 average monthly earnings in February 2026; formal non-agricultural payroll data.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the latest captured official median, ZAR 6,000/month for employees in 2024. It is not directly comparable to the formal-sector average.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Illustrative monthly equivalent of the ZAR 30.23 hourly minimum at 40 hours/week. Actual monthly pay depends on hours.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate February 2026 formal non-agricultural sector average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2024 employee median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No USD value is calculated because current official publications provide no finite national maximum salary. A top-5% threshold is a quantile, not a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum effective 1 March 2026, not an observed minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly earnings of formal non-agricultural employees in February 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly employee earnings in the 2024 Labour Market Dynamics report.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Statistics South Africa does not publish a finite national maximum in the reviewed QES or Labour Market Dynamics products. The top-5% threshold of ZAR 38,000/month is a percentile threshold, not a salary ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Mixed official measures: statutory hourly minimum, formal non-agricultural payroll average, and household-survey employee median
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective March 2026; average February 2026; median calendar year 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average and median cover different survey populations. USD conversions use approximately ZAR 16.5/USD.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official urban CPI provides current price-pressure context: consumer prices rose 5.0% year-on-year and 0.7% month-on-month in June 2026. Transport was the main pressure point at 12.7% year-on-year, driven by fuel prices up 34.3%; actual rents rose 4.1%, while food and non-alcoholic beverages rose 1.6%. These are inflation rates, not a monthly living-cost budget; actual costs vary materially by city, housing, transport use, and household profile.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Statistics South Africa publishes authoritative inflation and category movements but not one national monthly budget suitable for a remote worker. SARB corroborates the 2026 pressure from fuel, housing, transport, and services. City-specific housing and consumption estimates are still needed for budgeting.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The Remote Work Visitor Visa is a temporary visitor-class route. It ordinarily cannot be changed in-country, and no official source confirms that its time counts toward PR or citizenship.
settlement_track.summary: The remote-work visa fits foreign-employer remote work but only for a temporary visitor stay of up to three years. Settlement requires a separate work, critical-skills, business, or family status; no official source confirms conversion or counting of remote-work visitor time.
settlement_track.notes: The result is ineligible because selection requires a confirmed residence-to-citizenship path, not merely an active digital-nomad visa.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only as a temporary-living fit: the visa supports a contract with a foreign employer and forbids South African employment. It is not a settlement-path fit.

data.notes: Focused unexplained-null audit completed against 35 distinct canonical sources. At least 16 directly relevant URLs were inspected during this pass, including five URLs absent from the previous source set. The flagged cost-of-living field is now filled with current official CPI evidence and explicitly distinguished from a household budget. Other nulls remain only where a universal threshold, finite national maximum, or route-specific settlement timeline is unpublished or inapplicable.

data.selection_summary: South Korea’s permanent F-1-D Workation visa is a strong temporary fit for an ordinary foreign-employed remote worker: it permits independent application, requires foreign employment or ownership of a foreign company, and allows up to three years of stay. It is not valid for this citizenship-oriented selection because F-1-D prohibits Korean employment or profit-making activity and no current official source confirms that it qualifies for F-5 permanent residence, counts toward an F-5 route, or has an ordinary conversion bridge to settlement.

F-1-D is not shown as a generally available end-to-end electronic visa; mission-specific submission, document authentication, fees and appointments must be checked.

summary.value: D-2 study visas can be obtained without a local employer and directly authorize temporary study residence, but require admission and genuine study. A degree alone does not create an independent ordinary remote-work residence route; post-study D-10 and employment pathways are oriented toward job seeking, startup activity or Korean employment rather than continuing an ordinary foreign-client contract.
summary.notes: Useful only if the applicant genuinely intends to study or later changes career/status. It is not a matched residence route for the stated remote-work profile.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence is based on domicile or a place of residence in Korea; the 183-day test and facts such as occupation and family ties are relevant. A resident generally reports worldwide income, subject to the special limited-remittance rule for qualifying short-term foreign residents and treaty relief.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Visa status and tax residence are separate. Residence may arise through facts and circumstances and should not be modeled solely from day 183.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top national marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Local income tax generally adds 10% of national income-tax liability, making the combined top marginal burden approximately 49.5% before deductions and credits.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single defensible percentage applies to every F-1-D remote worker. National Health Insurance, National Pension, nationality/visa exclusions and social-security agreements must be analyzed separately. Individually insured pension contributions can be 9%, but exact F-1-D applicability depends on nationality, status and treaty coverage.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the published 2026 average foreign local-subscriber health and long-term-care insurance charge of KRW 158,630. This is not a guaranteed invoice or universal minimum.

special_tax_regimes.value: A qualifying foreign resident present in Korea for five years or less during the preceding ten-year period is generally taxed on foreign-source income only when paid in or remitted to Korea. A 19% foreign-employee flat-tax election exists under statutory conditions, but its applicability to an F-1-D worker on foreign payroll is not established and should not be assumed.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The foreign-employee election concerns qualifying wage and salary income and may be unavailable or unattractive depending on classification. It is not a special digital-nomad exemption.

taxes.caveats: Remote work physically performed in Korea can create Korean-source or Korean filing issues even when the payer is foreign. Contract classification, remittances, permanent-establishment risk, deductions, foreign tax credits, double-tax treaties, nationality-based social-insurance rules and social-security agreements can materially change the result. Obtain Korean tax advice before relying on the limited-remittance rule or foreign-employee flat rate.

taxation_system.value: Progressive national personal income tax at 6%–45%, plus local income tax generally equal to 10% of national liability. Residents generally face worldwide taxation, subject to the limited-remittance rule for qualifying short-term foreign residents.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile/place-of-residence facts and a 183-day test; immigration status alone is not determinative.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents generally: worldwide income. Qualifying foreign residents with five years or less in Korea during the previous ten years: foreign-source income generally within scope only when paid in or remitted to Korea. Non-residents: Korean-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Limited-remittance treatment for qualifying short-term foreign residents; possible 19% foreign-employee flat-tax election if its separate statutory conditions are met.
taxation_system.social_security: NHIS generally becomes compulsory for covered foreign residents after more than six months. The 2026 published average foreign local-subscriber health and long-term-care charge is KRW 158,630 monthly. Pension coverage depends on age, nationality, stay status, reciprocity and any social-security agreement.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 45% dashboard number is the top national marginal screening rate. Brackets apply to annual taxable income, and effective tax will normally be lower. Local income tax can raise each national marginal rate by approximately 10% of the national amount.

tax_brackets.notes: National rate; local income tax is additional.

taxation_system.notes: The core tax system is well supported, but the treatment of a particular F-1-D foreign contract requires individualized source-of-income, treaty and worker-classification analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: F-1-D creates no published digital-nomad income-tax holiday. Apply ordinary Korean residence, source, remittance, treaty and social-insurance rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Foreign remote employee or foreign-business owner residing in Korea; classification depends on the contract and actual activities.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 6%–45% progressive national PIT, plus local income tax generally equal to 10% of national liability; 45% is the top marginal screening rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Facts-based domicile/place-of-residence analysis, commonly including the 183-day test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally report worldwide income. A qualifying foreign resident present for five years or less during the previous ten years generally brings foreign-source income into Korean tax only when paid in or remitted to Korea, but work performed physically in Korea requires source analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No F-1-D-specific tax exemption found. Limited-remittance treatment and the possible 19% foreign-employee election are general foreign-taxpayer provisions, not guaranteed F-1-D benefits.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: NHIS generally becomes compulsory after more than six months for covered foreign residents. Pension can also apply, subject to nationality, visa-status exclusions, reciprocity and social-security agreements. Foreign payroll does not by itself settle these questions.

fixed_payments.status: Partially established
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Published 2026 average foreign local-subscriber health plus long-term-care contribution: KRW 158,630 monthly. Pension can be 9% for an individually insured person when applicable, but F-1-D eligibility/exemption is case-specific.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Mission-specific visa fee plus foreign-residence-card and extension charges; no universal F-1-D fee in USD was established because nationality and filing mission affect visa fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No F-1-D-specific fixed freelancer tax was found. Local income tax generally equals 10% of national income-tax liability. Business registration, VAT and local-business obligations would require a different lawful activity/status analysis because Korean profit-making is restricted on F-1-D.
fixed_payments.notes: The NHIS figure is an average assessment, not a guaranteed fixed minimum or quotation.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A short stay does not automatically guarantee non-residence; domicile and occupational/family facts matter. A non-resident is generally taxed only on Korean-source income, but work physically performed in Korea still requires source and treaty analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Potential Korean reporting on employment or business income; worldwide-income or limited-remittance treatment depends on residence history, source and remittance. Progressive rates reach 45% nationally.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: F-1-D permits ownership of a foreign company but restricts Korean employment and profit-making activity. Do not assume that registering a Korean sole proprietorship is compatible with the visa; a different immigration and tax status may be necessary.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: High confidence that there is no published F-1-D tax holiday; medium confidence in any applicant-specific outcome because the foreign contract, place of performance, remittances, nationality and treaty position are unknown.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: F-1-D directly grants temporary long-stay status upon approval; no preliminary residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No official F-1-D-to-F-5 period or conversion path was found. A separately qualifying status is required, and its clock cannot be inferred from F-1-D.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalization requires permanent-residence qualification and at least five consecutive years of domicile, but the Act does not express this as a fixed number of additional years after F-5.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No credible total can be calculated from F-1-D because the route does not provide or confirm progression to permanent residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Ministry publishes category-specific processing notices, but a current August 2026 nationwide general-naturalization duration was not published on the checked notice. Older notices vary materially and were not reused as a current estimate.

key_conditions.value: For general naturalization: at least five consecutive years of domicile, qualification for permanent residence, adulthood, good conduct, self-support, Korean-language and Korean-custom knowledge, and no national-security/public-welfare concern. Naturalized persons generally must renounce their former nationality within one year unless a statutory exception permits a non-exercise pledge.
key_conditions.notes: KIIP can satisfy or support language and integration requirements, but it does not turn F-1-D into an F-5 route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Facilitated naturalization is possible after two consecutive years of domicile in Korea while married to a Korean citizen, or after three years have elapsed since marriage with at least one year of domicile in Korea.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage accelerates naturalization only when the spouse is a Korean citizen and the statutory marriage/domicile conditions are met. Marriage to another foreign national can support dependent-family treatment under F-1-D but does not shorten citizenship timing.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Citizenship is never automatic through marriage.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be genuine and continuing, subject to statutory exceptions for a Korean spouse’s death/disappearance, other causes not attributable to the applicant, or care of a minor child of the marriage. Good conduct, self-support, basic Korean knowledge and discretionary review still apply. False documents or a sham marriage can cause refusal, status cancellation and enforcement consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage-based immigration and facilitated naturalization are separate approvals.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in South Korea alone does not confer citizenship. A Korea-born child is Korean at birth only through a Korean parent or the narrow rule for unknown or stateless parents; foundlings are deemed born in Korea.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Korea to two foreign parents is not automatically Korean unless both parents are unknown or have no nationality. The child ordinarily derives nationality under the parents’ national laws.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is not broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Korean national at birth if either the father or mother is a Korean national at the time of birth.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Parentage, birth registration and any dual-nationality obligations still require proper documentation.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Korean-citizen child can support a foreign parent’s family/child-rearing immigration case in qualifying circumstances, but does not automatically give the parent permanent residence or citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The Visa Portal lists child-rearing and family categories, but exact eligibility depends on parentage, custody and family circumstances.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father does not automatically acquire Korean citizenship through the child. If the other parent is Korean, the child is Korean at birth and the father may be able to seek an appropriate spouse/child-rearing family status, followed by a separate residence or naturalization process.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Marriage, legal parentage, custody, support and genuine family life may be examined.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026 for headline rank/access; Passport Index 2026 for separated visa categories

rank.notes: July 2026 Henley result; tied with Japan and the United Arab Emirates.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley’s access score combines destinations accessible without a prior visa, including visa-on-arrival access; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index methodology, which differs from Henley. It also reports 114 strictly visa-free destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index separates 47 visa-on-arrival and 12 eTA destinations; combined here to match this field.

passport.notes: Do not combine the Henley score of 188 with Passport Index’s separated categories as if they used the same destination universe or methodology.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderate for a foreign-client remote worker in Seoul and other international centers because the work itself remains foreign-facing and major immigration information is available in English. Korean is still important for housing, healthcare, banking, taxes and any integration or settlement pathway.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current official quantitative English-proficiency measure was found; this is a cautious practical assessment, not a claim that daily administration is broadly English-language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited. Some official immigrant-orientation material is available in Russian, but Korean remains the official and operational language. No comparable official Ukrainian-language service coverage was confirmed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Russian or Ukrainian alone should not be considered sufficient for routine administration or long-term integration.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of KRW 3.75 million using roughly KRW 1,485 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2024 median monthly wage-worker income of KRW 2.88 million.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the statutory 2026 monthly minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of official December 2024 wage-worker average income.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of official December 2024 wage-worker median income.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary was published. The source provides subgroup averages, not an upper bound.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory 2026 minimum based on 209 monthly hours, including paid weekly-rest hours.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly income of wage workers as of December 2024.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly income of wage workers as of December 2024.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum was established.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross/administrative wage-worker income for average and median; statutory full-time-equivalent minimum wage for minimum
average_citizen_salary.period: December 2024 for average/median; calendar year 2026 for minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average/median population and minimum-wage population are not identical. USD values are approximate planning conversions and should not replace KRW figures.

cost_of_living_note.value: Statistics Korea reports average monthly consumption expenditure of KRW 1.63 million for one-person households in 2023 (58.4% of the KRW 2.792 million all-household average); housing, water, electricity and fuels were the largest category at 18.2%. The later all-household average was KRW 2.89 million in 2024. These are survey averages, not a quoted budget for a foreign remote worker.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The official one-person figure is the closest published national benchmark located, but it is a 2023 resident-household average and does not isolate F-1-D holders, Seoul, furnished short-term accommodation, deposits, visa costs, private insurance or international travel. Statistics Korea reports July 2026 CPI 2.8% above July 2025 (housing/water/electricity/fuels +1.8%), but its own CPI guidance cautions that CPI is not itself a cost-of-living measure, so the 2023 amount is not mechanically inflation-adjusted here. Seoul uses both jeonse (large refundable deposit) and weolse (deposit plus monthly rent), and the city publishes transaction-level rent data rather than one representative foreign-renter price; actual housing cost therefore depends heavily on district, property, deposit and lease type.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: F-1-D is now a permanent visa program administratively, but each holder receives temporary status for no more than three years. No official F-5 credit or ordinary settlement conversion is confirmed.
settlement_track.summary: F-1-D directly supports up to three years of lawful foreign remote work but is not identified as an ordinary F-5 qualifying status. Citizenship would require leaving this route, qualifying independently for another residence/permanent-residence category, and then satisfying nationality law.
settlement_track.notes: The Ministry’s policy language about encouraging talent to experience Korea is not a legal settlement bridge.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: True only for temporary living and remote work. The route fits a foreign employer or foreign-company owner without a Korean employer, but that does not make it a citizenship-path match.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against 32 distinct directly relevant canonical URLs, including seven official statistics, CPI and Seoul housing/rent pages not present in the previous source set. The decisive immigration result remains unchanged: F-1-D became a permanent program in June 2026 and now allows up to three years, but remains temporary for the holder and has no officially confirmed ordinary F-5/citizenship bridge. The cost-of-living note now uses the closest official one-person-household benchmark and explains why it is not a foreign remote-worker or Seoul rent quote. Current exact naturalization processing time and a universal F-1-D pension charge remain cautious nulls because the checked official sources do not establish them.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Qualifying professional E-7 or other D/E/F-2 status, followed by F-5
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: F-1-D is not among the statuses counted for general F-5 PR. A holder can pursue a separate qualifying professional/resident status and later meet that route’s PR conditions.
requirements: Independently qualify for an eligible successor, such as E-7 professional employment with the relevant Korean work activity.
For general F-5, complete more than five years in qualifying D-7–D-10, E-1–E-7 or F-2 status and satisfy conduct, livelihood and integration criteria.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: An ordinary foreign-employer F-1-D profile does not establish successor eligibility. F-1-D time is outside the published general F-5 qualifying-status list; the successor clock is separate. In-country change acceptance was not verified. The original MOJ download looped, but its official mirrored/indexed guide text was accessible.

data.selection_summary: The Ministry of Labour portal expressly permits an “Individual” account for a freelancer. However, public instructions do not confirm that someone serving only foreign clients qualifies without a South Sudanese institution, registered local business, trade licence or sponsor, or that the permit produces qualifying residence. Filing-level confirmation is required.

visa_application.title: Ministry of Labour Work Permit Portal
visa_application.notes: This is the direct work-permit portal, not a digital-nomad or residence application. It tells freelancers to select Individual. The separate Ministry instructions list contract, institution/business, registration, tax and licensing documents depending on category, so foreign-client-only eligibility requires written confirmation.

best_routes.route_name: Individual/freelancer work permit followed by a separately approved residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum remote-income or salary threshold is published for an individual freelancer.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum income in South Sudanese pounds is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; freelancer eligibility and local-business documentation require manual confirmation
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No statutory minimum-income amount or formula is published for the Individual/freelancer account type
income_requirement_display.notes: The portal accepts an Individual user type for freelancers, but the Ministry document list asks for a contract and may require institution/business registration, TIN and licence documents depending on category. Neither source says that an overseas-client contract alone is accepted.

income_proof_months.notes: No bank-statement or income-history period is published for the freelancer user type.

key_requirements.requirement: Create an individual account and apply through the Ministry of Labour portal; the portal specifically says freelancers should select Individual.

Valid passport, entry visa, photographs, CV and academic certificates; occupation-dependent documents may include a contract, criminal-clearance documents, business registration, TIN, trade licence and operating licence.
A separate residence permit is required for extended residence; sectoral and NGO rules show residence applications normally following an approved work permit.
A foreign taxpayer seeking a TIN is asked for valid alien registration and a valid work permit.

initial_validity.value: One year for the work-permit smart card
initial_validity.notes: The work-permit smart card is valid for one year. Residence is a separate immigration decision: temporary permits are capped at 12 months, ordinary permits are renewable for two-year periods and special permits for five-year periods. The Act does not identify which residence class, if any, an overseas-client-only freelancer can obtain.

extension_rules.value: Annual work-permit renewal appears possible subject to continuing eligibility, updated documents and fees
extension_rules.notes: The FY2023/24 schedule says work-permit classes are valid for one year and renewable, but no freelancer-specific renewal standard is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate residence permit may potentially follow the work permit, but approval for an overseas-client-only freelancer is not established
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The cited sectoral examples involve a company or NGO sponsor. The general Immigration Act has no dedicated remote-worker or freelancer residence class.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The Act provides ordinary and special residence permits but no automatic freelancer conversion or guaranteed fixed clock
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Ordinary residence may be granted after five years of continuous residence, or after more than two years for valuable scientific, technical or commercial activity. Special residence may be granted after three years, or after more than five years for qualifying valuable activity. Both are discretionary and are not labelled permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: If qualifying legal residence is obtained and maintained, ordinary naturalisation may be requested after at least ten continuous and uninterrupted years; whether freelancer-connected residence qualifies is unconfirmed
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary and is not a direct benefit of the work permit.

best_routes.notes: The active portal supports independent filing by an Individual freelancer. The route is not a confirmed ordinary foreign-contract remote-work or settlement path because accepted contract type, local-business substance, residence eligibility and naturalisation counting remain unpublished.

rejected_routes.route_name: Locally sponsored foreign-employee work permit and residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general salary threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general salary threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published salary threshold; South Sudanese employer or institution documentation is required
income_requirement_display.notes: The route is based on authorized local work and sponsorship rather than foreign remote income.

income_proof_months.notes: No general income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Institution or business application, employment contract, passport, entry visa, qualifications and occupation-specific approvals.
The sponsoring company processes the work permit and related residence permit in the reviewed petroleum-sector rules.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: Work and related residence permits are generally aligned in the cited sectoral rules.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually while sponsored employment and regulatory requirements continue
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains dependent on the sponsoring work relationship.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Residence permit after the employer-arranged work permit
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This does not remove the local-employer requirement.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic permanent-residence conversion is established
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Longer ordinary or special residence permits are discretionary.

path_to_citizenship.value: Separate discretionary naturalisation after at least ten years of continuous legal residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not cure the route’s local-employer requirement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires employment or an assignment connected to a South Sudanese institution or locally operating business.

rejected_routes.route_name: eVisa, entry visa or visitor stay

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-income threshold exists because this is entry authorization, not a remote-work route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: An immigration income threshold is inapplicable to this visitor route.

income_requirement_display.value: Not a work or residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor entry does not establish a remote-worker immigration category.

income_proof_months.notes: No general income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport and purpose-specific entry documents; official visa guidance may require an invitation and locally based organization or contract documentation.

initial_validity.value: Visa-category dependent
initial_validity.notes: The public page does not establish a remote-worker category.

extension_rules.value: Any extension must be handled by immigration before expiry
extension_rules.notes: Extension does not change the stay into a work or settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic transition
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate qualifying work, business, family or other residence basis is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No visitor-to-permanent-residence transition is established
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Act’s residence permits require separate approval.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct citizenship path. Ordinary naturalisation requires at least ten years of continuous and uninterrupted legal residence supported by address history, immigration arrival records and a Resident ID; an eVisa or visitor entry alone does not establish that qualifying residence record.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The nationality rules do not expressly exclude every day admitted as a visitor, but they require legal-residence evidence and a Resident ID. Treat visitor time as non-qualifying unless both authorities confirm otherwise in writing.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because an eVisa or visitor entry neither authorizes ordinary remote-work residence nor establishes a settlement track.

summary.value: No independent points-tested, skilled-migration or university-degree residence route was found. Academic certificates may support a work-permit application, but a degree does not itself confer residence.
summary.notes: The software-engineering degree is relevant evidence of qualification only.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident when domiciled in South Sudan or physically present for 183 days or more in a tax period. Residents are taxable on South Sudan-source and foreign-source income; non-residents on South Sudan-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Services physically performed in South Sudan can be South Sudan-source even when the payer is abroad, so staying below 183 days does not necessarily eliminate tax.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top screening rate, not an expected effective rate. FY2023/24 was the latest clearly verified enacted schedule; the FY2025/26 document inspected was still labelled a draft.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Public NSIF material states 8% employee and 17% employer contributions, totaling 25% of gross salary. The Ministry says the fund also registers self-insured persons, but no current freelancer rate or contribution base is published.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly freelancer payment can be calculated. Work-permit, digital-system, residence and registration charges are periodic or transaction-based, and classification-dependent.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate or remittance-basis tax regime was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary wage or entrepreneurial-income rules appear applicable.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on domicile, days present, where services are performed, wage-versus-entrepreneur classification, foreign-tax credits and the applicable Finance Act. Obtain current NRA confirmation because the newer FY2025/26 source was a draft.

taxation_system.value: Progressive/tiered personal income tax for wages and entrepreneurial activity, with a top screening rate of 20%. Residents are taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on South Sudan-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile in South Sudan or physical presence for at least 183 days in a tax period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; South Sudan-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special remote-worker or digital-nomad regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: Public NSIF material states compulsory employee/employer contributions of 8% and 17% of gross salary (25% total). The Ministry says the fund registers self-insured persons, but neither its page nor the accessible 2023 Act records publish a contribution rate, minimum base or payment frequency for an independent foreign freelancer.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 20% figure is a top screening rate, not expected effective tax. The FY2023/24 wording applies a rate to the relevant whole-income band rather than clearly describing conventional marginal slices. The official FY2025/26 draft proposed higher nominal thresholds, but enactment is not established by the current sources.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Monthly taxable income up to SSP 20,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: FY2023/24 enacted PIT schedule for wages and entrepreneurial activity
tax_brackets.notes: Latest clearly verified enacted schedule; USD conversion omitted because the SSP exchange rate is highly unstable.
The source describes a band rate rather than a conventional marginal slice.
Current filing-year thresholds require NRA confirmation.
Current filing-year thresholds require NRA confirmation.
Top screening rate. The FY2025/26 draft instead proposed a top band beginning at SSP 160,001.

taxation_system.notes: Residence and income-scope rules are well supported. Current bands and self-employed social-insurance treatment have lower confidence because a newer enacted Finance Act and authoritative freelancer contribution schedule were not retrievable.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad regime exists. If the freelancer work-permit option is accepted, ordinary personal or entrepreneurial-income rules would apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Potential foreign freelancer under ordinary work-permit and entrepreneurial-income rules; not a digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 20% screening rate under the latest clearly verified enacted schedule; confirm the current Finance Act
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or physical presence for at least 183 days in the tax period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign-source income is taxable for residents. Work physically performed in South Sudan may also be South Sudan-source despite a foreign payer.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For employment, public NSIF material states 8% employee plus 17% employer contributions on gross salary. The Ministry lists self-insured persons within the fund’s mandate, but no current public schedule establishes whether a foreign freelancer must register, the applicable rate or base, or who remits it.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed amount can be calculated: employee rates are percentage-based and self-insured freelancer rates are unpublished.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The Ministry lists a USD 100 application-form cost. The FY2023/24 Act listed USD 1,500 for a professional/service-provider Class C permit plus USD 100 for the digital system; the FY2025/26 draft reproduced FY2024/25 current rates of USD 3,500 for professionals plus USD 200 for the digital system. Freelancer classification and the currently collectible total require Ministry confirmation.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No freelancer-specific fixed tax, municipal levy or transaction tax was identified in the current official pages inspected. An accepted sole proprietor would still face ordinary recordkeeping, quarterly estimated-tax payments and an annual return; foreign TIN registration requires alien registration and a valid work permit. Business-registration and payment portals exist but do not publish a complete freelancer fee schedule before classification.
fixed_payments.notes: Obtain written assessments from the Ministry of Labour, immigration, NRA, business registry and SSIF. Public materials do not support a reliable all-in monthly fixed-payment figure.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Below 183 days a person may remain non-resident, but services performed while physically in South Sudan can still generate taxable South Sudan-source income.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days or when domiciled in South Sudan, worldwide income falls within the resident tax base, subject to allowable credits and current rates.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: If treated as entrepreneurial activity, registration, TIN, records, quarterly estimated payments and ordinary PIT rules may apply. Foreign TIN registration requires alien registration and a valid work permit.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening analysis for an unconfirmed immigration route, not a filing determination.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A work permit is not residence. No guaranteed freelancer-to-residence sequence or processing time is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The Act provides discretionary ordinary and special residence categories but no guaranteed permanent-residence clock for this profile.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Nationality rules use continuous legal residence rather than a separately confirmed PR holding period.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum for ordinary naturalisation. This is not a reliable route forecast because freelancer-linked qualifying residence is unconfirmed and approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The regulations require a response within 12 months after complete evidence is presented; actual practice was not independently established.

key_conditions.value: At least ten years of continuous and uninterrupted legal residence, adulthood, sound mind, intention to reside permanently, no disqualifying conviction, complete evidence, immigration and security checks, discretionary approval and an oath of allegiance.
key_conditions.notes: No current official source confirms that freelancer-linked residence satisfies this clock.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must be lawfully married to a South Sudanese citizen and prove at least five continuous years of legal residence in South Sudan from the marriage date. A presidential waiver is legally possible.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage helps only after the required continuous residence period is met; marriage alone does not immediately grant nationality.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The regulations request a marriage certificate, sworn witness statement and detailed residence evidence.

requirements_and_risks.value: Naturalisation remains subject to approval, complete identity and residence evidence, fingerprints, criminal and security checks, and proof of a genuine lawful marriage. False evidence or a sham marriage risks refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: A spouse naturalised under the marriage provision is not required to renounce the previous nationality.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child is South Sudanese if either parent was South Sudanese at birth. Territorial birth alone is insufficient; a deserted infant found in South Sudan with unknown parents is presumed South Sudanese.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in South Sudan to two foreign parents does not ordinarily acquire nationality solely by territorial birth. The law has a foundling rule but no general domestic safeguard for every otherwise-stateless child.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Parent residence or permanent residence alone does not transmit citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is South Sudanese by birth if either the mother or father was a South Sudanese citizen by birth or naturalisation when the child was born.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Transmission is equal through either parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalise a foreign parent. A foreign spouse of a citizen may use the separate marriage-based naturalisation provision after the required residence period; no parent-of-citizen fast track was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Residence and nationality require separate applications.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically acquire citizenship or residence through the child. If the child’s mother is South Sudanese and the parents are lawfully married, the father may potentially use the five-year marriage-based naturalisation route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The marriage route remains application-based and discretionary.

rank.notes: Current 2026 table inspected on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley’s access score combines destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance, including qualifying visa-on-arrival access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Henley’s public ranking does not provide a separate visa-required total.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The inspected ranking does not separate visa on arrival or eTA from the overall access score.

passport.notes: The previous rank 91 and score 41 were outdated; the inspected 2026 Henley table shows rank 92 and access score 42.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the constitutional official working language and language of instruction, but remote work is operationally difficult because connectivity is limited and current official travel advice warns against all travel.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Legal language accessibility does not overcome infrastructure and security risks.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no reliable evidence of broad day-to-day availability was found; English or local-language assistance would normally be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No practical Russian- or Ukrainian-language service network was established.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current nationally representative mean monthly wage is published. The NBS labor-market page says wages and earnings data are being updated and supplies no amount; its household portal exposes only the 2009 baseline, while the ILO described pre-testing rather than released results.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median wage is published. The NBS labor-market page contains only an update-in-progress notice, its household portal provides no recent wage distribution, and the ILO item describes survey pre-testing.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The only statutory statement found is SSP 2,000 per month in the 2021 consolidated tax schedule. It is not verified as a current 2026 floor, and no defensible current USD conversion is supplied.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The NBS labor-market page publishes no national mean wage and says the data are being updated; its household portal offers only the 2009 baseline. The 2024 NGO study covers participating organizations/local staff and cannot supply an average-citizen USD wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected NBS and ILO pages publish no current national wage distribution from which a median can be stated. The NGO study is not nationally representative, and its household-expenditure median is a cost measure rather than salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No official national wage-distribution upper bound or statutory maximum salary is published.

min_salary_local_currency.value: SSP 2,000/month in the 2021 consolidated Taxation Act schedule; no current 2026 national minimum-wage amount was published in the sources inspected
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is historical legal context, not a verified current wage floor. The FY2023/24 Act raised the PIT zero-rate threshold to SSP 20,000 but did not label that threshold a minimum wage, so it is not substituted as one.

average_salary_local_currency.value: Unpublished: the current NBS labor-market page provides no national mean wage amount
average_salary_local_currency.notes: The official page says wage data are being updated; the accessible household resource is the 2009 baseline and the ILO item reports pre-testing rather than results.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Unpublished: the current NBS labor-market page provides no national median wage amount
median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current nationally representative wage distribution is available on the inspected NBS or ILO pages.

max_salary_local_currency.value: Inapplicable as a stable national statistic: no official wage-distribution upper bound or statutory maximum salary is published
max_salary_local_currency.notes: An individual highest salary is not a meaningful national wage indicator; no official percentile ceiling or maximum wage is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average citizen/resident worker wage; no current nationally representative result published
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly
average_citizen_salary.notes: Current average-citizen/resident worker salary remains unpublished. The SSP 2,000 minimum-wage statement is retained only as historical legal context, and the 2024 NGO salary study is not treated as nationally representative.

cost_of_living_note.value: A 2024 MSF-supported study estimated median monthly living costs for a South Sudanese family at about SSP 748,600, or USD 604 using its February 2024 exchange rate. It is an NGO/local-staff household budget, not a 2026 single-person estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Inflation and currency depreciation make this unsuitable as a current fixed budget.
