settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The possible freelancer work permit is not a residence permit. Separate residence approval is required, and no official source confirms that a foreign-client-only freelancer can obtain it or that connected time counts toward naturalisation.
settlement_track.summary: The active portal recognizes Individual freelancer applications, but the accepted client/business structure and subsequent residence basis are unpublished. Although nationality law permits naturalisation after ten years of legal residence, the link from this exact route to qualifying residence remains unverified.
settlement_track.notes: Written confirmation from both the Ministry of Labour and the Directorate of Immigration is required before treating this as a settlement route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The freelancer user type may permit independent application, but no public official rule confirms that an ordinary software engineer with only a foreign client and no local business, customer or sponsor is eligible for both work and residence permits.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed using more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including more than five outside the previous source set. Overseas-client-only eligibility, local-substance requirements, residence approval and settlement counting remain unresolved. Residence durations, social-insurance uncertainty and wage-data gaps are now stated precisely. Current official advice warns against all travel because of severe security risks.

data.selection_summary: Spain’s International Teleworker authorization directly fits a non-EU software engineer working remotely for a foreign employer or foreign clients. A person legally present in Spain can self-file for a residence-and-work authorization of up to three years; applicants abroad use the one-year telework visa and can subsequently obtain the residence authorization. The status is renewable, is expressly classified as residence, and can build toward long-term residence after five years and ordinary citizenship eligibility after ten years.

visa_application.title: Presentation of international-mobility residence applications under Law 14/2013
visa_application.notes: This is the direct electronic filing route for applicants legally present in Spain; the teleworker personally submits the application. A person applying from abroad must instead apply for the telework visa through the Spanish consulate responsible for their residence.

best_routes.route_name: International Teleworker Residence and Work Authorization

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of EUR 2,442 at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. The legally controlling amount is in euros.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 2,442 per month
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The principal applicant must show 200% of the monthly SMI. The 2026 SMI is EUR 1,221 per month.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 2,442/month (approximately USD 2,782) for the principal applicant
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 2,442; add 75% of SMI for the first accompanying family member and 25% for each additional member
income_requirement_display.notes: The threshold changes when the annual SMI changes. USD conversion uses the latest ECB rate captured in this review and is only approximate.

income_proof_months.notes: The official minimum is a three-month pre-existing employment or commercial relationship. This is not a guarantee that only three bank statements will be requested; authorities may request additional evidence of continuing resources.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be a non-EU/EEA/Swiss adult performing genuinely remote work through computer and telecommunications systems for an entity outside Spain.
The foreign company or group must have conducted real and continuous activity for at least one year, and the employment or commercial relationship must have existed for at least three months.

A foreign employer must authorize remote work from Spain. An independent professional must document the foreign commercial contract and may obtain no more than 20% of professional activity from Spanish companies.
Applicant must have a qualifying university/postgraduate or recognized professional qualification, or at least three years of relevant professional experience.
Required evidence includes passport, criminal-record documentation, sufficient work-derived resources, and Spanish public-health/social-security coverage or qualifying private health insurance.

Spanish Social Security registration is normally mandatory. Employees may rely on imported coverage only under an applicable international agreement and appropriate certificate; self-employed teleworkers must register in RETA.

initial_validity.value: Up to three years for an in-country residence authorization; up to one year for a consular telework visa
initial_validity.notes: If the underlying work period is shorter, validity can be limited accordingly.

extension_rules.value: Residence authorization may be renewed in successive two-year periods while the qualifying conditions continue. A visa holder may apply for the residence authorization during the final 60 calendar days of the visa.
extension_rules.notes: Income, foreign work, social-security and other continuing requirements are rechecked.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A person legally present in Spain can directly self-file for the Law 14/2013 residence-and-work authorization. A person abroad first obtains the one-year telework visa and then applies for the residence authorization.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Ordinary tourist status does not itself authorize work; the applicant must remain in regular status and obtain the teleworker authorization.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: International teleworker residence is a renewable residence authorization. Five years of qualifying continuous legal residence can support an application for EU long-term residence while retaining foreign remote employment or professional activity.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The initial teleworker visa and subsequent residence authorization are stages of the same remote-work route; the latter can be granted for up to three years and renewed for two. Long-term residence is a separate application, not an automatic grant. Years refer to qualifying legal residence, not citizenship.

path_to_citizenship.value: The general rule is ten years of legal, continuous residence immediately before applying. Shorter periods apply to specified nationalities and circumstances but are not assumed for the ordinary applicant profile.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship remains discretionary upon proof of good civic conduct and sufficient integration; residence eligibility is not automatic approval.

best_routes.notes: This is an exact ordinary foreign-contract remote-work match and a settlement-oriented residence route, not merely a visitor or workcation permission. The employee version permits work only for foreign entities. The professional/freelance version allows Spanish professional clients only up to 20% of total activity. Tax and social-security treatment differs materially between employees and freelancers.

rejected_routes.route_name: EU Blue Card / Highly Qualified Professional authorization

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The route has a separate salary threshold, but it is irrelevant to the selected foreign-contract profile.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The threshold was not extracted because this route fails the local-employment criterion.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable to this selection; a qualifying Spanish job contract or firm offer is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer/job-offer route, not ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: Historical foreign-income proof is inapplicable because eligibility is based on a qualifying Spanish employment contract or firm offer.

key_requirements.requirement: Requires a valid high-skilled employment contract or firm offer and qualifying education or experience.

initial_validity.value: Up to three years, depending on the employment contract

extension_rules.value: Renewal is possible while route-specific employment requirements continue.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Employer/job-offer-based residence
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Does not fit continued ordinary work for an unrelated foreign client or employer.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Potential long-term residence after qualifying legal residence
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Rejected only because it does not fit the applicant’s foreign-contract scenario.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potential ordinary residence-naturalization track
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not the selected route.

rejected_routes.notes: Attractive to software engineers who obtain Spanish employment, but invalid for this selection because it requires a qualifying employment contract or offer. Spain’s separate international-teleworker route is the correct match.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the controlling 2026 threshold of EUR 2,400 per month (400% of the EUR 600 monthly IPREM) at EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. The route requires resources for the full requested residence period; the consular initial authorization is one year, so the principal applicant normally demonstrates EUR 28,800 in annual resources or an equivalent guaranteed periodic source. This threshold is documented for completeness even though the route is rejected because it prohibits work.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: EUR 2,400 per month; EUR 28,800 for the initial one-year authorization
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The principal-applicant minimum is 400% of IPREM; add 100% of IPREM (EUR 600/month in 2026) for each accompanying family member. Resources must be available without undertaking employment or professional activity.

income_requirement_display.value: EUR 2,400/month (approximately USD 2,734), demonstrated for the full authorization period
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 2,400/month for the principal applicant plus EUR 600/month per accompanying family member
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a passive-means threshold, not permission to earn the amount through remote work while holding the status.

income_proof_months.notes: The reviewed rules require resources covering the full authorization period and allow multiple forms of proof, but do not prescribe a fixed number of historical bank-statement or income-proof months. For the one-year initial authorization, the required resource horizon is 12 months.

key_requirements.requirement: Must qualify without performing work; remote work under this status is not authorized.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: The initial non-lucrative residence authorization is expressly valid for one year.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is granted for two years unless long-term residence is due. Apply during the two months before expiry; a filing within three months after expiry is still accepted but may trigger sanction proceedings.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal requires sufficient non-work resources for the renewal period, continued health insurance, payment of the fee, schooling of dependent children where applicable, and more than 183 days of real and effective residence in Spain during the calendar year. A timely filing extends the prior authorization while the case is decided; the statutory decision period is three months and silence is positive.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct non-working residence only

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Legal residence may eventually qualify under general long-term-residence rules, but work remains outside this route’s purpose.

path_to_citizenship.value: General residence rules may apply, but this route does not authorize the intended work.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant intends to keep working. Using a non-lucrative permit for ordinary remote work creates compliance risk when a purpose-built international-teleworker route exists.

summary.value: A university degree helps satisfy the international-teleworker qualification requirement, but a degree alone does not create a separate independent residence route. Spain’s EU Blue Card and highly qualified professional routes require qualifying employment or an offer.
summary.notes: The degree is useful within the selected teleworker route; it is not an independent basis for residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally Spanish tax resident when present in Spain for more than 183 days during the calendar year or when Spain is the principal centre or base of economic activities or interests. A rebuttable family presumption and treaty tie-breakers can also matter.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax residence are separate tests.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the Article 93 special-regime rate on qualifying employment income through EUR 600,000, not an estimated effective rate and not automatically available to every freelancer.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening total for a standard self-employed person in 2026: 28.30% common contingencies, 1.30% professional contingencies, 0.90% cessation, 0.10% training and 0.90% intergenerational-equity mechanism, applied to the applicable contribution base rather than directly to gross revenue. Employee payroll rates and treaty-covered employees differ.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate derived minimum RETA contribution for a self-employed person with net monthly returns around the EUR 2,442 immigration threshold: minimum 2026 contribution base EUR 1,356.21 × 31.5% ≈ EUR 427.21, or about USD 487. Actual assessment depends on final net-return bracket, adjustments and any relief.

special_tax_regimes.value: Eligible inbound employees, including qualifying international teleworkers, may elect Article 93 treatment for the year tax residence begins and the following five tax years, provided they were not Spanish tax resident during the preceding five tax years and meet the other conditions. Ordinary foreign-client freelancers do not qualify merely because they hold the immigration authorization; self-employed eligibility is limited to specified entrepreneurial or highly qualified startup/R&D activities.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Election eligibility and filing deadlines require individualized verification.

taxes.caveats: Tax results depend on employee versus independent-contractor classification, days present, the location where work is physically performed, permanent-establishment risk, autonomous-community rules, social-security agreements and the applicable double-tax treaty. The 24% figure is not a blanket digital-nomad tax rate.

taxation_system.value: Ordinary Spanish residents are subject to progressive IRPF on worldwide income. Qualifying inbound workers may elect the Article 93 special regime, which applies modified non-resident rules while they remain IRPF taxpayers.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in the calendar year or Spain as the main centre of economic interests; treaty tie-breakers may override dual residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income under ordinary IRPF. Article 93 applies modified source and non-resident rules; qualifying employment income is generally taxed at the special employment-income scale.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Article 93: qualifying employment income through EUR 600,000 is taxed at 24%, with 47% on the excess, for the arrival tax year plus five following tax years. The regime expressly covers qualifying employed international teleworkers, but ordinary freelancers require a separate statutory qualifying category.
taxation_system.social_security: Spanish registration is normally mandatory. Employees may sometimes import coverage under an applicable international agreement and certificate. Independent professionals must register in RETA according to the official teleworker FAQ.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard screening rate is 47%, the top special-regime marginal rate on employment income above EUR 600,000. It is not the expected effective rate. The ordinary combined state and autonomous-community IRPF schedule varies by region and is not represented by these two special-regime rows.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable qualifying employment income up to EUR 600,000
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold using EUR 1 = USD 1.1392.
Top marginal screening rate, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The special regime is well supported for an employed international teleworker. A foreign-client freelancer should assume ordinary IRPF unless a tax adviser confirms that the particular activity meets an Article 93 self-employed category.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: An employed international teleworker may be eligible for the elective Article 93 inbound regime. A self-employed foreign-client teleworker normally faces ordinary IRPF and RETA unless separately qualifying for Article 93 as an entrepreneur or specified highly qualified professional.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: International remote employee or independent professional; tax outcome depends on contract classification
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 24% special-regime rate through EUR 600,000 and 47% above for qualifying employment income; otherwise ordinary progressive IRPF
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in a calendar year or Spain as the principal centre of economic interests, subject to treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Ordinary Spanish tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income. Article 93 applies modified non-resident rules, but employment income earned while working physically from Spain is not simply exempt foreign income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: Article 93 is available to qualifying employed international teleworkers who meet prior-non-residence and other statutory conditions. The immigration permit alone does not guarantee the election, particularly for freelancers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Spanish social-security registration is normally mandatory. A foreign employer may need Spanish non-resident employer registration unless an applicable social-security agreement and certificate preserve home-country coverage. Independent professionals must enter RETA.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: For self-employed persons, 2026 RETA contribution bases depend on net-return brackets. At net returns around EUR 2,442/month, the minimum base is EUR 1,356.21 and the listed standard rates total 31.5%, producing an indicative minimum contribution near EUR 427.21/month. Employee payroll contributions require employer-specific calculation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The electronic residence application requires Modelo 790 code 038, point 7, for initial or renewed Law 14/2013 mobility authorization. The filing page does not display a stable amount. Consular visa fees vary by nationality, consulate and reciprocity; the Washington consulate’s 2026 schedule, for example, ranges from USD 106 for many nationalities to much higher reciprocal fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No universal route-specific monthly tax was found. Independent professionals may have VAT, income-tax prepayment and business-registration obligations depending on activity; exact liabilities were not established as a single fixed amount.
fixed_payments.notes: The RETA estimate is derived from official 2026 bases and rates and is not a guaranteed invoice. Residence-card, translation, apostille, insurance and professional-advice costs are also applicant-specific.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay of 183 days or less does not automatically eliminate Spanish taxation: economic-interest, source, physical-work-location and treaty rules must still be checked. Immigration residence does not decide tax residence by itself.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A qualifying employee may elect Article 93 if all conditions and deadlines are met; otherwise Spanish tax residents generally report worldwide income under ordinary IRPF.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The official teleworker FAQ requires an independent professional to register in Spanish RETA. Ordinary foreign-client freelance activity is not automatically eligible for Article 93, and VAT, invoicing and income-tax prepayment rules require local review.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Official sources establish the principal rules, but no single tax percentage accurately represents every teleworker because employment status and Article 93 eligibility change the result.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The qualifying status is itself temporary residence. A legally present applicant can apply directly; an overseas applicant first obtains a residence visa.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Five years of legal and continuous residence, subject to absence limits and the long-term-residence requirements.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: For a general applicant, long-term residence at year five does not shorten the ten-year citizenship residence requirement, leaving approximately five additional years. Reduced citizenship periods may apply to specified nationalities or circumstances.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General residence-naturalization period. This is eligibility timing, not guaranteed approval timing.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Twelve months is the statutory maximum resolution-and-notification period, not a reliable empirical average. Actual files can exceed it; silence after the statutory period is treated as rejection for procedural purposes.

key_conditions.value: Maintain legal and continuous residence, observe long-term-residence absence limits, preserve the qualifying teleworker relationship and income while on that permit, comply with tax and social-security duties, demonstrate good civic conduct and sufficient integration, and normally pass CCSE and DELE A2 unless exempt. A successful citizenship applicant must complete the oath/registration formalities and renounce the prior nationality when Spanish law requires it.
key_conditions.notes: Applicants from Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea or Portugal, and persons of Sephardic origin, have special nationality and renunciation rules; these are not assumed for the generic applicant.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship may use the one-year legal-residence period where the applicant has been married to a Spanish citizen for at least one year at application and is not legally or de facto separated. Both the qualifying residence and marriage conditions matter.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Spanish citizen can qualify even if created before immigration, provided it remains valid and the one-year marriage and residence requirements are met. A marriage between two non-Spanish migrants does not shorten nationality residence.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage can also create a separate family residence basis.

requirements_and_risks.value: The relationship must be genuine and continuing. Spain’s family-residence rules expressly exclude marriages or registered partnerships celebrated fraudulently. Citizenship still requires legal residence, good civic conduct, integration and applicable language/civics evidence; sham marriage or false documents can cause refusal, loss of status and other sanctions.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Spain combines descent with limited birth-based rules: a Spain-born child is Spanish by origin if a parent is Spanish, if at least one foreign parent was also born in Spain other than a diplomat, if neither parent’s law transmits nationality, or if parentage is undetermined. Birth in Spain alone is not enough in the ordinary two-migrant case.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Usually no automatic Spanish citizenship when both foreign parents transmit a nationality and neither foreign parent was born in Spain. Citizenship can arise under the anti-statelessness rule or double-jus-soli condition, and a person born in Spain can later use a shortened one-year residence-naturalization period.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The answer depends on both parents’ nationality laws because failure of either law to transmit nationality can activate Spain’s anti-statelessness rule.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born to a Spanish mother or father is Spanish by origin, irrespective of whether the other parent is a migrant.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent, guardian or custodian of a Spanish minor can qualify for a separate temporary family residence authorization if responsible for and living with the child or current on parental obligations. The child’s citizenship does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The current family authorization can be valid for up to five years, but eligibility and custody/maintenance evidence must be established.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Spanish minor may seek the family residence authorization when he has the child in his care and cohabits with the child or is current on parental obligations. Fatherhood alone does not grant Spanish citizenship; the father must independently satisfy a nationality route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Recognition of parentage and the child’s Spanish citizenship must be legally documented.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank captured on 2026-08-15. This differs from Henley’s methodology and earlier Spain rank data.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified specifically as visa-free by Passport Index; this does not include visa on arrival or eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category as displayed on the research date.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 42 visa-on-arrival destinations and 11 eTA destinations. The source lists these separately.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 174, consisting of 121 visa-free, 42 visa-on-arrival and 11 eTA destinations. Index methodologies and destination rules can change frequently.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is practical inside many international remote-work and technology environments, especially in larger cities, but it is not sufficient for reliably handling government, tax, healthcare, housing and long-term integration. EF EPI 2025 placed Spain 36th of 123 with 'medium' proficiency and 26th of 37 in Europe.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected test dataset rather than an official population census, so it supports only a cautious practicality assessment.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian communities exist, but neither language is official or broadly usable for Spanish administration. INE’s 2025 census listed approximately 202,105 Ukrainian and 109,604 Russian foreign nationals, suggesting community support may be found in larger cities; Spanish remains necessary for most official and everyday matters.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Population by nationality does not measure language ability or guarantee local-language services.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official 2024 median gross monthly wage of EUR 2,001.40.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the EUR 1,221 statutory monthly SMI in the 14-payment convention. It is not an observed minimum salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of official median gross monthly employee earnings.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: INE does not publish a finite national maximum salary in the reviewed monthly-wage release or its current salary-distribution index. The 2024 release reports only an open-ended upper group of EUR 2,659.80 or more, so no defensible USD maximum can be derived.

min_salary_local_currency.value: EUR 1,221 per monthly payment; EUR 17,094 annually
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory 2026 full-time minimum in Spain’s 14-payment convention, not an observed wage-distribution minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 Labour Force Survey wage estimate for employees’ main jobs.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024 median for employees’ main jobs.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: INE’s current national wage outputs publish averages, medians, decile thresholds, decile means and percentiles, but not a finite maximum observed salary. The highest published monthly category for 2024 is open-ended at EUR 2,659.80 or more; that threshold is not a maximum and therefore is not placed in this field.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly wage from the employee’s main job; statutory SMI shown separately
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 wage distribution; 2026 statutory minimum
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe ordinary employees/resident workers, not software-engineer pay and not the immigration income threshold. USD figures are approximate and use EUR 1 = USD 1.1392. INE’s salary-distribution products do not publish a finite national maximum, so both maximum fields remain null rather than treating an open-ended top-decile threshold as a cap.

cost_of_living_note.value: A reliable Spain-specific national cost-of-living index value was not established from the official sources inspected. Eurostat confirms large 2025 consumer-price-level differences across the EU, but the reviewed summary did not display Spain’s exact figure; housing costs also vary substantially by Spanish city.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Kept cautious rather than substituting a commercial crowd-sourced city estimate.

settlement_track.summary: The international-teleworker authorization is a renewable residence-and-work status, not a visitor-like nomad permission. Its lawful residence can build directly toward five-year long-term residence and the ordinary ten-year citizenship residence period without a mandatory status conversion.
settlement_track.notes: The route’s settlement strength depends on maintaining continuous legal residence and satisfying absence, conduct, integration, tax and social-security requirements. Citizenship approval is never automatic.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The route expressly covers employees working remotely only for foreign companies and independent professionals with foreign commercial contracts; professionals may additionally perform up to 20% of activity for Spanish companies. No local employer, startup, investment or elite-achievement condition applies.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous Spain record using more than 15 directly relevant current URLs, including six canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. The non-lucrative residence threshold and renewal rules were resolved from the current Immigration Regulation, Ministry information sheets and 2026 consular guidance. The salary maximum remains null because INE publishes an open-ended top wage group and distribution statistics, not a finite national maximum. The prior positive selection through the International Teleworker authorization remains supported.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: EU long-term residence authorization
requirements: Maintain legal residence for five years, respecting the applicable absence limits.
Meet the long-term residence income, health-insurance and criminal-record requirements.
Keep the teleworker authorization valid until eligible for the successor status.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: International teleworker residence is a renewable residence authorization. Five years of qualifying continuous legal residence can support an application for EU long-term residence while retaining foreign remote employment or professional activity.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The initial teleworker visa and subsequent residence authorization are stages of the same remote-work route; the latter can be granted for up to three years and renewed for two. Long-term residence is a separate application, not an automatic grant. Years refer to qualifying legal residence, not citizenship.

data.selection_summary: Sri Lanka's active Digital Nomad Visa independently accommodates employees, freelancers, and owners of foreign businesses serving clients outside Sri Lanka. It requires at least USD 2,000 in monthly remittances and provides renewable one-year residence, but no official source establishes a conversion to permanent residence or an ordinary residence-years naturalization route for an unrelated foreign national. It is therefore suitable for temporary remote living, not the requested citizenship-oriented selection.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad Visa Category — official requirements and submission instructions
visa_application.notes: The official PDF directs applicants to submit documents to the Department of Immigration and Emigration's Residence Visa Division. No dedicated online DNV application portal was identified; the general applications page provides residence-visa forms.

best_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Minimum monthly remittance for the principal applicant.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official threshold is denominated in USD, not LKR.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 2,000 per month; an additional USD 500 per month for each dependent when the dependent count exceeds two
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 500/month for each dependent beyond two
income_requirement_display.notes: The wording in the official PDF does not clearly state whether the first two dependents require any additional remittance, so applicants should confirm dependent calculations with the Residence Visa Division.

income_proof_months.notes: Proof of the minimum monthly remittance is required, but the official rules do not specify a fixed bank-statement look-back period.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be at least 18 and remotely employed, freelancing, or own a business not registered in Sri Lanka that serves clients outside Sri Lanka.
Passport valid for at least six months, application form, request letter, photographs, security-clearance form, medical clearance, and a police certificate issued within the preceding three months.
International health insurance covering treatment in Sri Lanka and a recommendation from the Ministry of Digital Economy.
Proof of the required foreign-currency monthly remittance; local employment is prohibited and all income must come from foreign sources.
Annual visa fee of USD 500 for the principal applicant and USD 500 for each spouse or dependent.
Renewal requires the initial documents plus proof of registration with the Inland Revenue Department.

initial_validity.value: One year
initial_validity.notes: The visa provides lawful residence for up to 12 months.

extension_rules.value: Renewable annually while eligibility continues; renewal requires the initial supporting documents and proof of Inland Revenue tax registration.
extension_rules.notes: The official document does not state a maximum number of renewals.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The DNV itself authorizes legal residence for 12 months at a time and permits personal bank accounts, residential leases, private or international schooling for dependents, and access to local utilities and coworking facilities.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a residence-visa category, not visitor status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Sri Lanka publishes a separate Permanent Residence Visa for specified descent, former-citizenship and family categories. An ordinary remote worker does not qualify merely by renewing the Digital Nomad Visa.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The DNV is renewable annually but supplies no general PR clock. The separate family/descent PRV grants permanent residence with a renewable card up to ten years; this corrects the overly broad implication that Sri Lanka has no permanent-residence category. The five-year marriage condition is not five years of nomad residence.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship law provides descent, specified family-registration, and highly discretionary eminence/public-service categories, but no ordinary naturalization entitlement based solely on years spent on the DNV.

best_routes.notes: This route is an excellent profile match for temporary foreign-contract remote work. It fails the final selection because official sources do not connect it to permanent residence or ordinary citizenship.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Not applicable to visitor status.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold; visitor status is not the DNV
income_requirement_display.notes: A visit visa does not establish residence for this selection.

income_proof_months.notes: A remote-work income-proof period is inapplicable to this visitor category.

key_requirements.requirement: Activities must remain within the purpose and conditions endorsed on the visa; unauthorized paid or unpaid employment, trade, or business is prohibited.

initial_validity.value: Depends on the visitor visa or ETA issued
initial_validity.notes: Visitor validity is irrelevant to a qualifying residence track.

extension_rules.value: Visitor extensions do not convert the stay into the Digital Nomad Visa or a settlement status.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A visit visa is not qualifying temporary residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official visitor-visa material provides no visitor-to-permanent-residence transition.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time does not create an ordinary naturalization entitlement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor permission is not a remote-work residence or citizenship route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official employment-category page does not publish a uniform income threshold relevant to this foreign-contract profile.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official page makes eligibility category- and sponsor-dependent rather than specifying a general LKR threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No general published income threshold; local institutional sponsorship is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Requirements vary by employment subcategory.

income_proof_months.notes: The official page does not impose a uniform income look-back period across employment subcategories.

key_requirements.requirement: Private-sector cases require documents from a Sri Lankan company and a recommendation from the relevant line ministry.

initial_validity.value: Generally one year or the period recommended by the relevant authority
initial_validity.notes: Renewable annually with the necessary recommendation.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires continued support or recommendation from the relevant Sri Lankan authority or employer.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct employer-linked residence visa

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official employment-category page publishes annual renewal rules but no general automatic permanent-residence transition.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act does not create an ordinary years-based naturalization entitlement for this employment status.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it depends on a Sri Lankan employer or host institution and line-ministry recommendation.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: These routes are investment-based rather than income-threshold remote-worker routes.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A monthly LKR income test is inapplicable because eligibility turns on investment or legacy status.

income_requirement_display.value: Substantial investment or legacy-scheme eligibility required
income_requirement_display.notes: Not suitable for an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer.

income_proof_months.notes: A monthly income-proof period is inapplicable to these investment or legacy categories.

key_requirements.requirement: Investor categories require investment and government recommendations; the Resident Guest Scheme is extension-only for existing holders.

initial_validity.value: Category-specific residence permission
initial_validity.notes: Not an ordinary remote-work route.

extension_rules.value: Category-specific; the Resident Guest Scheme page addresses existing holders and investment progress.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Possible only through the relevant investment category or existing legacy status

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The named official residence and Resident Guest pages do not publish a direct general permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Investment residence does not establish an ordinary naturalization entitlement in the reviewed law.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant context excludes substantial investment and legacy-only programs.

summary.value: Foreign university students and students at approved institutions can obtain a renewable educational residence visa without an employer, but admission and recommendations from the university, Ministry of Higher Education, academic institution, or relevant mission are required. The status is temporary, and the official residence and citizenship materials provide no student-to-PR or ordinary naturalization track.
summary.notes: A software-engineering degree alone does not qualify the applicant; enrollment in an eligible Sri Lankan program is necessary.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they reside in Sri Lanka or are present for at least 183 days in any 12-month period beginning or ending during the year of assessment. When residence arises only through the 183-day rule, residence starts at the beginning of that 183-day period; otherwise the person is treated as resident for the whole assessment year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The year of assessment runs from April 1 to March 31. Treaty residence and the separate 'resides in Sri Lanka' test require fact-specific analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Route-specific screening rate: qualifying foreign-source income or services used outside Sri Lanka, paid in foreign currency and remitted through a Sri Lankan bank, are capped at 15%. This is not the general top marginal rate, which is 36%, and eligibility for the 15% treatment depends on the income's legal classification and remittance conditions.

social_contributions_percent.notes: There is no single compulsory employee-side percentage established for both DNV contract structures. For a covered employee, EPF is 8% from the employee and 12% from the employer, while ETF is a further 3% paid only by the employer; official guidance includes foreign or expatriate employees working in Sri Lanka. The DNV bars local employment, and the reviewed legislation and agency guidance do not expressly say whether an offshore employer with no Sri Lankan establishment must register and remit EPF or ETF for a DNV remote employee. For a freelancer, the reviewed sources impose no compulsory EPF percentage: the ETF Act lets a self-employed person apply voluntarily and, if accepted, choose a monthly contribution in LKR 25 multiples; the current Surekuma pension is likewise opt-in with contributions selected according to the desired pension.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Annualized equivalent of the mandatory USD 500 yearly DNV fee for the principal applicant. The actual payment is USD 500 annually, not USD 41.67 monthly; health-insurance cost is variable and excluded.

special_tax_regimes.value: For 2025/26, gains from services rendered in or outside Sri Lanka for use outside Sri Lanka, and qualifying foreign-source gains, are capped at 15% when earned in foreign currency and remitted through a Sri Lankan bank. Resident foreign-employer employees have a dedicated APIT table; independent service providers and freelancers are treated as earning business income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This is a general foreign-currency income rule, not a DNV tax exemption.

taxes.caveats: Tax depends on whether the person is an employee, independent contractor, or business owner; whether services are utilized outside Sri Lanka; the payment currency and banking route; residence and source rules; and any applicable treaty. DNV renewal requires tax registration, but the visa document does not promise tax exemption or guarantee the 15% cap. Social-security treatment also depends on contract structure: covered employment normally triggers EPF or ETF, self-employed schemes are opt-in, and the current official sources do not expressly address EPF or ETF registration by an offshore employer with no Sri Lankan establishment.

taxation_system.value: Sri Lanka generally taxes individuals progressively, with a 36% top marginal rate after personal relief. A maximum 15% rate applies to qualifying foreign-currency service-export and foreign-source income remitted through a Sri Lankan bank.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Residence can arise through residing in Sri Lanka or presence of at least 183 days in a qualifying 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Sri Lanka-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Maximum 15% for qualifying foreign-currency service-export or foreign-source income remitted through a Sri Lankan bank.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employment generally carries EPF contributions of 8% employee plus 12% employer and an additional ETF contribution of 3% paid by the employer. Labour Department and ETF guidance expressly include foreign or expatriate employees working in Sri Lanka. However, the DNV prohibits local employment, and neither the EPF or ETF statutes nor current agency guidance expressly determines whether an offshore employer with no Sri Lankan establishment must register and remit for a DNV holder working remotely from Sri Lanka. For freelancers, no compulsory EPF rate is published: self-employed ETF membership is elective under section 18 of the ETF Act, with an accepted member choosing a monthly amount in multiples of LKR 25, and the current Surekuma pension is also opt-in. A DNV applicant should obtain written coverage guidance from the Department of Labour or ETF Board for the exact contract.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For 2025/26, residents receive LKR 1.8 million personal relief. Taxable income after relief is charged at 6%, 18%, 24%, 30%, and 36%. The 36% figure is the general top marginal rate, not an expected effective rate and not necessarily the rate on qualifying remitted foreign income.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: First LKR 1,000,000 of taxable income after applicable relief
tax_brackets.notes: Personal relief is applied separately.
Top marginal screening rate.

taxation_system.notes: Income-tax rules are well supported by official sources. The social-security audit establishes the ordinary EPF and ETF rates, coverage of foreign employees working in Sri Lanka, and voluntary self-employed options, but the named current sources do not publish a DNV-specific rule for an offshore employer without a Sri Lankan establishment; the route therefore has no defensible single mandatory social-contribution percentage.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: A DNV holder receives no stated visa-based tax holiday. Once resident, worldwide-income rules apply, subject to source, treaty, and special-rate provisions. Qualifying foreign-currency remote employment or service income remitted through a Sri Lankan bank may be capped at 15%; a resident employee of a foreign employer generally self-pays APIT monthly because the offshore employer does not withhold.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Resident foreign-employer employment income or freelancer/business income, depending on contract structure
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 15% on qualifying foreign-currency remote income; otherwise ordinary progressive rates can reach 36%
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence generally arises through residing in Sri Lanka or at least 183 days in a qualifying 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are taxable on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxable on Sri Lanka-source income, while qualifying foreign-source or exported-service income remitted through a Sri Lankan bank may receive the 15% maximum rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: The DNV rules publish no visa-specific exemption. The relevant concession is the general 15% maximum for qualifying remitted foreign-currency income.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: For a covered employee in Sri Lanka, EPF is 8% employee plus 12% employer and ETF is 3% employer-only; foreign or expatriate employees working in Sri Lanka are expressly included in agency guidance. A DNV holder cannot take local employment. Although the statutes define employee and employer broadly, the reviewed sources do not expressly explain registration or remittance where the employer is wholly offshore with no Sri Lankan establishment, so applicability requires a written coverage determination. Freelancers are outside the foreign-employer APIT table and no mandatory EPF percentage was established for them; self-employed ETF and Surekuma participation are opt-in.

fixed_payments.status: USD 500 annual DNV fee per applicant; international health insurance required
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No DNV-wide compulsory fixed social-security payment can be stated. Covered employment uses earnings percentages—8% employee EPF, 12% employer EPF, and 3% employer ETF—not a fixed amount. A self-employed person may elect ETF membership and choose a constant monthly contribution in multiples of LKR 25 for the calendar year; Surekuma contributions are selected according to the desired pension.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: USD 500 per year for the principal applicant, USD 500 for the spouse, and USD 500 for each dependent.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The reviewed DNV, tax, EPF, ETF, and self-employed pension materials publish no DNV-specific municipal fee, stamp duty, freelancer levy, or fixed monthly tax.
fixed_payments.notes: Insurance cost varies by provider, and tax registration is required for visa renewal. Offshore-employer EPF or ETF coverage should be confirmed in writing; voluntary ETF or Surekuma payments are choices, not DNV fees.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A stay below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence because the separate 'resides in Sri Lanka' test can apply. A non-resident remains taxable on Sri Lanka-source income, so remote-work source analysis is still necessary.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A qualifying resident foreign employee may use the dedicated APIT table: LKR 1.8 million relief, 6% over LKR 1.8 million up to LKR 2.8 million of cumulative employment income, and a 15% formula above LKR 2.8 million, with monthly self-payment.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Freelancers are excluded from the foreign-employer APIT table and are treated as earning business income. The 15% foreign-currency service rule may apply if all statutory conditions are met; business registration, VAT, and source consequences require individual advice.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Official sources establish the residence tests, income-tax framework, APIT mechanics, visa fee, ordinary EPF and ETF rates, and voluntary self-employed pension options. They do not publish a DNV-specific coverage rule for a wholly offshore employer, so a single mandatory contribution rate remains inapplicable across all DNV contract structures and filing-level confirmation is necessary for foreign employees.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The approved DNV itself grants one-year lawful residence; no prior residence period is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The current DNV, residence-visa, and Resident Guest materials publish no conversion or qualifying residence-accumulation rule from the DNV to permanent residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The reviewed citizenship law provides no ordinary residence-years naturalization route for an unrelated foreign national, with or without prior permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total DNV-to-citizenship period is applicable because the DNV has no statutory settlement or ordinary naturalization transition.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official citizenship information page publishes office procedures but not a standard processing-time statistic for the relevant statutory registration categories.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary DNV residence does not create citizenship eligibility. Statutory citizenship routes principally concern descent and specified family cases; registration for distinguished public service or eminence is ministerial, limited to 25 persons annually, and not an ordinary software-engineer route. Registration normally requires renunciation of other citizenship unless the Minister grants an exemption.
key_conditions.notes: No language-test or integration-test timeline is stated because no general naturalization track applies to this route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship Act section 12 requires residence in Sri Lanka throughout the one year immediately preceding application by the spouse, widow, or widower of a Sri Lankan citizen. Citizenship registration remains discretionary. Separately, the current spouse-visa page requires a subsisting marriage of more than six months for first issuance.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage matters only when the other spouse is a Sri Lankan citizen. A marriage between two foreign migrants does not shorten a citizenship or PR timeline.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marriage must still satisfy the current spouse-visa and citizenship-registration requirements.

requirements_and_risks.value: The foreign spouse may obtain a family residence visa after the marriage has subsisted for more than six months; first issuance is one year, followed by two-year extensions until five years of spouse-visa residence and five-year extensions thereafter. Citizenship registration additionally requires one year of immediately preceding residence, ordinary-residence intent, and ministerial approval. Marriage is not automatic citizenship, refusal may occur on public-interest grounds, and false documents or a non-genuine marriage can cause refusal or cancellation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The reviewed official materials do not publish a separate quantified cohabitation test beyond the subsisting-marriage and residence requirements.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Sri Lanka alone does not confer citizenship. A child born in Sri Lanka is a citizen by descent when either parent is or was a Sri Lankan citizen; foundlings of unknown parentage are protected by a presumption of citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Sri Lanka to two foreign parents does not ordinarily become a citizen merely by birthplace. The statutory exception for a newly born deserted infant of unknown and unascertainable parentage does not establish broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If either parent is a Sri Lankan citizen at the child's birth, a child born in Sri Lanka acquires citizenship by descent. A child born abroad must be registered through the prescribed process, normally within one year, with late registration possible subject to additional requirements and fees.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The 2003 amendment replaced the earlier father-only wording with either-parent rules.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Sri Lankan citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. Any benefit must arise through a separate family residence or citizenship-registration category; the reviewed materials do not establish an automatic parent-of-citizen PR route.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A foreign spouse may qualify through marriage to the Sri Lankan parent, but that is a spouse route rather than an automatic benefit from the child.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is a Sri Lankan citizen, the child can be Sri Lankan, but the foreign father does not automatically receive citizenship or permanent residence. He may use the spouse route if married to the Sri Lankan citizen and must independently satisfy its visa and citizenship requirements.

rank.notes: Passport Index power rank observed on 2026-08-15. A separate July 2026 report citing Henley placed Sri Lanka 94th with access to 39 destinations; the indexes use different methodologies.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category; eVisa destinations are treated separately by that index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reports 34 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations, combined here. Its total mobility score is 54.

passport.notes: Passport figures are index- and methodology-dependent. Henley combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access and was reported as rank 94 with 39 accessible destinations in July 2026, while Passport Index supplies the breakdown required by this schema.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is constitutionally the link language and is widely usable for technology, tourism, private services, and many official materials. Sinhala or Tamil remains important for deeper local administration and integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The official sources establish legal language status; the practical remote-work assessment is an inference from English's link-language role and the availability of English government services.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official or link languages, and the official language framework provides no government-backed general service entitlement in either language. They should not be relied upon for administration or long-term integration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official language framework; the cited sources do not publish nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-usage statistics.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey reports LKR values. No USD amount is supplied because selecting a volatile exchange rate would add a non-survey assumption.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey publishes the median in LKR, not USD; the local-currency value is retained without a potentially misleading FX conversion.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The statutory instrument establishes an LKR minimum but does not publish a USD equivalent.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey publishes the national average in LKR rather than USD.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official survey publishes the national median in LKR rather than USD.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The Labour Force Survey publishes means and medians but no meaningful national maximum salary in LKR or USD.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: National statutory minimum effective January 1, 2026; this is not an observed minimum in the wage distribution.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 mean monthly gross salary for all monthly wage or salary earners. Sector means were LKR 76,480 urban, LKR 54,187 rural, and LKR 31,576 estate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: 2024 median monthly gross salary for all monthly wage or salary earners. Sector medians were LKR 54,600 urban, LKR 47,200 rural, and LKR 28,000 estate.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The Labour Force Survey publishes national means and medians, not a maximum wage statistic.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly salary of monthly wage or salary earners; statutory national minimum shown separately
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 wage survey; minimum wage effective 2026-01-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: The prior record's sector figures were retained as context and improved with the survey's national total mean and median. These labor-market figures are far below the DNV's USD 2,000 monthly remittance threshold and do not affect DNV eligibility.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official benchmarks: the 2019 Household Income and Expenditure Survey reported average monthly household expenditure of LKR 63,130 nationally, LKR 95,392 in urban areas, and LKR 108,893 in Colombo District. These are household—not single-person or expatriate—figures and are not current-price budgets. By June 2026, the official NCPI was 222.3 with 6.5% year-on-year inflation, and the national official poverty line was LKR 17,592 per person per month. Actual remote-worker costs therefore vary substantially by city, household size, housing standard, and imported consumption.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Resolved with official statistics. The latest comprehensive HIES expenditure benchmark is from 2019, so it is presented alongside June 2026 price-level and poverty-line context rather than mechanically inflated into a speculative current budget.
