settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: General residence is not a digital-nomad or remote-work authorization. Foreign means supporting a residence application do not by themselves authorize foreign-client work.
settlement_track.summary: General residence can eventually support a five-year naturalization application, but the reviewed official rules do not authorize ordinary foreign-contract remote work as the basis for that residence. The documented work channel requires a local employer, so this profile has no qualifying citizenship track.
settlement_track.notes: The general settlement framework and the applicant's right to work must not be conflated. A switch to authorized local employment, genuine family status, ancestry status, or another qualifying basis would be required.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker visa or independently authorized foreign-contract freelance/self-employed route was found. Proof of foreign means in a residence application is not equivalent to work authorization.

data.notes: At least 19 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected in this focused pass, including eight canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. The PSA renewal and stay-extension rules, AOV liability, pension participation, compulsory health premium, and reason for the unavailable maximum-salary figure are now stated precisely. Remaining nulls reflect rules or statistics that the named current sources do not publish, rather than unexamined gaps.

data.selection_summary: Sweden has no dedicated digital-nomad visa, but it has an independently filed residence permit for self-employed people that can reach permanent residence after two years. A foreign-client software consultant may be able to use it only by establishing and genuinely operating a Swedish business, owning at least 51%, presenting a credible budget and customer network, and committing personal and operating capital. The official rules do not expressly confirm that an ordinary consultant relying principally on one foreign contract will qualify, so filing-level confirmation is needed before treating this as a match.

visa_application.title: Apply for a residence permit to run your own business in Sweden
visa_application.notes: The official route page contains the e-service and paper-form application paths. A first application normally must be made and decided from outside Sweden. The page is route information rather than a stable, separately addressable direct e-service URL.

best_routes.route_name: Residence permit for self-employed people

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no published monthly-income threshold for the initial permit. The route instead uses maintenance capital and separate business-capital requirements.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: SEK 200,000 personal maintenance funds, plus SEK 100,000 for a spouse and SEK 50,000 per accompanying child; separate business funds also required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is capital intended to cover two years, not monthly income. Loans are not normally accepted for business funding.

income_requirement_display.value: SEK 200,000 maintenance capital for the principal applicant, plus separate operating/investment capital
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: SEK capital requirement, not monthly earnings
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: SEK 200,000 applicant + SEK 100,000 spouse + SEK 50,000 per child, plus enough own funds to operate or acquire the business
income_requirement_display.notes: SEK 200,000 is approximately USD 20,474 using about SEK 9.7685 per USD on 14 August 2026, but displaying it as monthly income would be misleading.

income_proof_months.notes: The initial application requires bank statements for the preceding three months, together with evidence that the available amount can support the applicant for two years.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport and first application normally made from outside Sweden.
Relevant industry and business-management experience, with relevant Swedish or English knowledge.
Personally run the business, have decisive responsibility, and own at least 51%.
Credible budget, established customer contacts or networks, and sufficient own operating or acquisition capital.
Swedish company documentation, three months of bank statements, business plan and supporting commercial evidence.
Application fee SEK 2,000 for the principal self-employed applicant.

initial_validity.value: Up to two years
initial_validity.notes: Never longer than passport validity.

extension_rules.value: Extendable while the applicant continues to control and genuinely operate a compliant, profitable and durable business, maintains proper accounting and permits, pays taxes and fees, and supports the family from the business.
extension_rules.notes: An extension application may include a permanent-residence request after at least two years on this permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved application directly grants a Swedish residence and work permit for running the applicant's own business.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is a business-owner residence permit, not a digital-nomad or foreign-employment permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Permanent residence may be requested with an extension after at least two years of holding and complying with the self-employed permit, provided the applicant sustainably supports themselves through the business.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The business must be professional, independent, profitable and durable; only actual taxed business income counts.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially counts as settlement-based residence toward the general eight-year citizenship period, followed by citizenship if permanent-status or applicable statutory-status, identity, maintenance, language, society-knowledge and conduct requirements are met.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is an inference from the permit's direct permanent-residence path and the citizenship rules for settlement-based permits. The Migration Agency should confirm how the applicant's precise permit history will be counted.

best_routes.notes: Potentially suitable only after converting the foreign-contract profile into a genuine Swedish self-employed business. The rules do not mandate a Swedish employer or expressly require Swedish customers, but they also do not expressly confirm that a one-client foreign consulting arrangement is sufficient. Customer diversification, independence, Swedish-business substance and commercial viability are likely to be scrutinised.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence permit for highly qualified people to look for work or explore starting a business

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of SEK 13,000 using SEK 9.7685 per USD.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: SEK 13,000 in bank assets for each requested month, plus return-travel funds
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is a savings requirement, not required recurring income.

income_requirement_display.value: SEK 13,000 of available funds per requested month
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: SEK 13,000 × requested months, plus return travel
income_requirement_display.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses the cited 14 August 2026 rate.

income_proof_months.notes: The authority requires documentary proof of sufficient assets for every requested month but does not specify a trailing bank-statement history on the cited page.

key_requirements.requirement: Second-cycle qualification equivalent to a qualifying Master's, professional or postgraduate degree.
Must intend to seek Swedish employment or investigate establishing a Swedish business.
Comprehensive health insurance, sufficient assets, valid passport, verified academic documents and presence outside Sweden when applying.

initial_validity.value: Up to nine months
initial_validity.notes: Never longer than passport validity.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary extension path is stated; the holder must obtain Swedish employment or start a qualifying business and apply for the corresponding status.
extension_rules.notes: A successful holder may apply in Sweden for a work permit or self-employed permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary job-seeker/business-exploration residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not authorize ordinary ongoing foreign-contract remote work as the purpose of stay.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path; conversion to an employer-based work permit or qualifying self-employed permit is required.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The exploratory permit is temporary and is not itself a permanent-residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only after conversion to a qualifying settlement-based permit and completion of the applicable residence period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This route is rejected because it is for prospective Swedish employment or starting a Swedish business, not ordinary foreign-client remote work.

rejected_routes.notes: Independent and degree-based, but expressly aimed at seeking Swedish employment or exploring a Swedish business. It is not a remote-worker permit and therefore does not qualify even though a software engineer with an eligible advanced degree may satisfy its academic criteria.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximate conversion of the current SEK 34,470 salary floor using SEK 9.7685 per USD.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: At least SEK 34,470 per month under the 90%-of-median rule current from 16 June 2026, subject to any higher occupation/collective-agreement standard
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Employer-sponsored threshold included only for context.

income_requirement_display.value: At least SEK 34,470/month for an employer-sponsored permit
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because a Swedish employment offer and employer process are required.

income_proof_months.notes: The route is based on a qualifying employment offer and conditions rather than a stated trailing-income period.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualifying employment and employer participation in the permit process.
Salary and employment conditions must meet statutory and applicable occupational standards.

initial_validity.value: Temporary work and residence permit tied to qualifying employment
initial_validity.notes: Exact validity depends on employment and passport duration.

extension_rules.value: May be extended if employment-permit conditions remain satisfied.
extension_rules.notes: Employer-sponsored route outside the applicant selection criteria.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary work-based residence after employer-supported approval.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A permanent residence permit may be requested together with an extension after the employee has held and complied with a work permit and worked in Sweden for at least four of the preceding seven years; sustainable self-support and good conduct are also required.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Although this employer-sponsored route is rejected for the selected profile, its permanent-residence rule is published. The employee applies only in connection with an extension, after at least four qualifying work-permit/work years in the past seven, and must show sustainable self-support and a well-behaved life. If permanent residence is refused but extension conditions are met, the temporary work permit may still be extended; none of this creates an independent path based on the applicant’s foreign remote contract.

path_to_citizenship.value: Possible through the general settlement framework after qualifying residence, but irrelevant to the independent foreign-contract selection.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route requires qualifying employment and employer participation.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor residence permit for stays over 90 days

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold establishes eligibility.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Visitor financial rules are not a qualifying remote-worker income route.

income_requirement_display.value: No qualifying remote-worker threshold; visitor status only
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status cannot substitute for permission to reside and work through a foreign contract.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable to the selection.

key_requirements.requirement: Temporary visit purpose and intention to leave after the visit.

initial_validity.value: Temporary visit over 90 days for the approved visitor period

extension_rules.value: Visitor rules only; not a business or settlement extension path.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying work/self-employment residence status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None through visitor status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Temporary visitor time is excluded from the five-year long-term-resident calculation.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time does not establish the selected settlement path.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The citizenship authority expressly excludes visitor permits from habitual-residence counting.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor status is temporary, does not create a regular remote-work right and does not count as a settlement route.

summary.value: A person with a second-cycle qualification may independently obtain up to nine months of temporary residence to seek Swedish work or explore starting a Swedish business. It requires SEK 13,000 in assets per requested month and comprehensive insurance, but it is not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route and requires conversion to employment or self-employment for continued residence.
summary.notes: A generic university degree is insufficient unless it corresponds to the specified second-cycle or professional-degree level.

tax_residency_rule.value: Unlimited Swedish tax liability applies if the person is domiciled in Sweden, stays there regularly for six consecutive months or more, or has significant connections to Sweden. Unlimited liability covers worldwide income; treaties may limit Sweden's taxing right.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A residence-permit holder who actually relocates to Sweden may become fully taxable earlier through domicile even before six months; the six-month rule is not the sole test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening top marginal approximation, not an expected effective rate: approximately 30% variable municipal tax plus 20% state tax on taxable earned/business income above SEK 643,000 in 2026.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Full self-employed contributions for active sole-trader business are 28.97% of the contribution base/business surplus. Age, social-security coverage, deductions and business form can change the result.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly equivalent of the maximum 2026 public-service fee of SEK 1,184 annually. This is collected through tax and is not a freelancer licence fee. Variable income tax and social contributions are not included.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax regime was found. Limited-tax-liability employment income may instead fall under SINK at 22.5% in 2026, but that is not a general exemption for a resident foreign-client business owner. Sweden also has application-based relief for certain foreign experts, researchers and key employees, which should not be assumed to cover an ordinary self-employed consultant.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty, employer, permanent-establishment and social-security coordination can materially change the result.

taxes.caveats: The displayed 50% is an approximate top marginal screening rate, not total effective burden and not automatically additive to 28.97% self-employed contributions. Municipal rates, deductions, entity form, foreign-employer compliance, permanent establishment, social-security coordination and an applicable double-tax treaty require professional analysis.

taxation_system.value: Progressive municipal and state taxation of earned and active business income, with worldwide income generally reportable by persons with unlimited Swedish tax liability.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile, a regular stay of at least six consecutive months, or significant connections can create unlimited liability.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for unlimited-liability residents; limited-liability taxpayers are taxed only on specified Swedish-source income, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. SINK is 22.5% in 2026 for qualifying nonresident employment income; specialist relief is separately application-based and not assumed available here.
taxation_system.social_security: Full self-employed contributions are normally 28.97% of active business surplus, subject to age, coverage and deduction rules.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Municipal tax is approximately 30% and varies by municipality. An additional 20% state tax applies to taxable earned income above SEK 643,000 in 2026. The approximately 50% dashboard number is a marginal screening rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: From taxable earned/business income after applicable allowances
tax_brackets.notes: The actual municipal rate varies; 30% is an official approximation, not a uniform national bracket.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Additional state tax on taxable earned income exceeding SEK 643,000 in 2026
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD threshold uses SEK 9.7685 per USD. This 20% is added to applicable municipal tax on the excess.

taxation_system.notes: High confidence in the general rules; the applicant's actual effective rate remains fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special visa regime. If the applicant qualifies through the Swedish self-employed permit and relocates, ordinary Swedish resident business taxation normally applies.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Potential Swedish self-employed business owner; no digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Approximately 30% municipal tax, plus 20% state tax above SEK 643,000; 50% is a top marginal screening approximation.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Unlimited liability can arise through Swedish domicile, six consecutive months of regular presence, or significant connections.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is generally reportable under unlimited tax liability, subject to domestic exemptions and double-tax treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad regime found. Do not assume SINK or expert relief applies to a resident self-employed foreign-client consultant.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: An active sole trader normally pays 28.97% self-employed contributions on the contribution base/business surplus; a foreign employer arrangement may create separate payroll-registration issues.

fixed_payments.status: No fixed monthly freelancer tax was found.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Social-security contributions are percentage-based rather than a confirmed fixed minimum monthly payment.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Initial self-employed permit fee SEK 2,000; accompanying adult SEK 1,500 and child SEK 750. Highly qualified job-seeker route fee SEK 2,200.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Maximum public-service fee SEK 1,184 annually for 2026. Businesses based in Sweden with annual turnover no more than SEK 120,000 may generally qualify for VAT exemption; standard VAT is otherwise commonly 25%, subject to place-of-supply and reverse-charge rules.
fixed_payments.notes: Residence-card, accounting, insurance, company-registration or professional-service costs are not represented as fixed taxes because no universal amount was established.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person who is neither domiciled nor regularly resident may have limited liability. SINK at 22.5% can apply to qualifying nonresident employment income, but foreign-client self-employment, Swedish work location and permanent-establishment rules require separate analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A person relocating and becoming unlimited-liability resident generally reports worldwide employment and business income and faces progressive municipal/state tax, subject to treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Swedish active sole trader generally pays ordinary progressive income tax and 28.97% self-employed contributions on business surplus, registers for relevant taxes, and may need VAT registration once applicable rules or thresholds are met.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is lower than for the general tax system because no dedicated nomad status exists and treatment depends on whether the applicant remains an employee, becomes a sole trader, or uses a company.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The self-employed alternative directly grants temporary residence upon approval; it does not require a prior Swedish employer permit.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Earliest route-specific eligibility after at least two years on a compliant self-employed permit and sustainable support from the business.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Derived from the earliest two-year permanent-residence point and the general eight-year habitual-residence rule. Citizenship is based on total qualifying habitual residence, not a separate mandatory six-year wait after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General rule effective in 2026, assuming all relevant residence is countable and the other citizenship conditions are met.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Migration Agency reports that 75% of recently decided adult-citizenship cases were decided within 55 months. This is a current service statistic, not a guaranteed individual processing time.

key_conditions.value: Genuine and durable Swedish business activity, tax/accounting compliance and sustainable self-support are required for route-specific permanent residence. Citizenship generally requires eight years of qualifying habitual residence, verified identity and personal appearance, qualifying permanent or statutory residence status, maintenance, orderly and honourable conduct, Swedish reading/listening at B1 and speaking/writing at A2, and knowledge of Swedish society. Time abroad exceeding six weeks in a year is deducted in full.
key_conditions.notes: The citizenship test in Swedish was not yet generally available on the research date; the official page lists interim accepted evidence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A spouse, registered partner or cohabiting partner of a Swedish citizen may qualify after seven years of Swedish residence instead of the general eight, provided the couple has lived together for the preceding five years and the citizen-status conditions are met.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage alone does not grant citizenship or shorten the period immediately. The applicant still needs qualifying Swedish residence, five years of actual cohabitation, and generally a partner who has held Swedish citizenship for at least five years if the partner was formerly foreign or stateless.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to another migrant does not accelerate the principal applicant's citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The relationship must be genuine and documented. Citizenship remains subject to identity, residence, maintenance, language, society-knowledge and conduct requirements. False information or a sham relationship can cause refusal, revocation or immigration and criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official citizenship page describes spouse/cohabitant residence conditions; the consequences statement is a general legal-risk warning and should be confirmed for any individual case.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Sweden alone does not confer citizenship. Citizenship is normally acquired through a Swedish parent, with special rules for stateless children.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Sweden to two non-Swedish parents does not automatically become Swedish merely by birth; non-EU/EEA parents generally must apply for the child's residence permit.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Special anti-statelessness and later child-naturalisation rules may apply, but they are not broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born after 1 April 2015 automatically acquires Swedish citizenship if either parent is Swedish at the time of birth, regardless of birthplace.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule is gender-neutral, so it applies whether the Swedish citizen is the mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Swedish-citizen minor child may be a basis for a parent's family-residence application in limited circumstances, but parent-of-child immigration is restrictive and citizenship of the parent is never automatic.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Where the parent also has a partner in Sweden, the Migration Agency normally first examines residence through the partner relationship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father receives no automatic residence, permanent residence or citizenship merely because his child is Swedish. He may seek family residence if he satisfies the parent/guardian, cohabitation, dependency or visitation requirements applicable to his circumstances.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The same rules apply without a special male-parent advantage.

rank.notes: Passport Index's Passport Power Rank, not Henley's differently calculated rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category as displayed on 15 August 2026.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 42 visa-on-arrival and 11 eTA destinations. Passport Index also lists eVisa and other authorization categories separately, so the mobility score is not the sum of only these three dashboard fields.

passport.notes: The previous record used a Henley access score that combined visa-free and visa-on-arrival access. Passport Index is used here because it publishes the requested visa-free, visa-on-arrival/eTA and visa-required breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for day-to-day life, international technology work and preparing the self-employed application: the Migration Agency accepts relevant Swedish or English knowledge, and English is widely used in Swedish academia and international workplaces. Swedish remains the principal public-sector language and is now required at specified levels for citizenship.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English practicality does not remove Swedish-language integration and citizenship requirements.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited as a primary working or administrative language. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is Sweden's principal language or one of the five protected national minority languages listed by the Swedish Institute; English or Swedish should be expected for business and public administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current nationwide measure of Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found, so availability should be checked locally.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 national gross monthly mean of SEK 42,900 using SEK 9.7685 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the 2025 national gross monthly median of SEK 38,300.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Sweden has no universal statutory national minimum wage; wage floors are commonly set through collective agreements, so no single defensible national minimum USD amount is reported.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion; exchange rates fluctuate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion; exchange rates fluctuate.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statistics Sweden does not publish a meaningful national maximum salary on the cited national summary page.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: No universal statutory national minimum wage was established.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 mean for all sectors and occupations, both sexes.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: 2025 median for all sectors and occupations, both sexes.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly salary across all sectors and occupations
average_citizen_salary.period: 2025 wage data, published 16 June 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: Official SEK figures are high-confidence. USD values are approximate conversions using a 14 August 2026 market rate.

cost_of_living_note.value: EURES reports an estimated 2026 basic living cost of about SEK 9,000 per month for one person excluding housing. It also reports average 2025 rent of about SEK 9,100 per month for a 70 m² apartment including heating and water but excluding electricity and parking; major-city costs can be materially higher.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The basic-consumption estimate is attributed by EURES to Swedbank and is not an official minimum-maintenance amount.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Sweden has no dedicated digital-nomad permit. The usable possibility is a genuine Swedish self-employed business permit, not residence based merely on continuing foreign employment.
settlement_track.summary: The self-employed permit itself is settlement-capable and may reach permanent residence after two compliant years, with qualifying residence potentially leading to citizenship after the general eight-year period. The unresolved issue is entry eligibility for an ordinary foreign-client consultant: the applicant must first present a credible, independent Swedish business rather than rely on remote-worker status.
settlement_track.notes: Classified as possible with conversion because the applicant must convert the foreign-contract activity into a genuine Swedish business before approval. No later status switch is required once the self-employed permit is granted.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official rules do not require a local employer or expressly require Swedish customers, but they require a Swedish business controlled and actively operated by the applicant, credible commercial plans, customer contacts or networks and adequate capital. Official sources do not expressly confirm whether a software consultant principally serving one foreign client is sufficiently independent and commercially established.

data.notes: This focused pass inspected 16 distinct directly relevant URLs, including six not present in the previous source set; the full source list retains 33 distinct URLs, predominantly official primary sources. The flagged employee-route permanent-residence note is now resolved with the published four-of-seven-year rule, extension-only filing procedure, maintenance and good-conduct conditions. The main selection uncertainty remains whether the Migration Agency would accept this applicant’s specific foreign-client arrangement as a genuine independent Swedish business.

data.selection_summary: Switzerland has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence route for a non-EU/EFTA applicant. Third-country self-employment can produce residence only where a quota-controlled, cantonally reviewed business demonstrates a lasting positive effect on the Swiss labour market and overall Swiss economic interest; an ordinary software-engineering contract with a foreign client is insufficient. EU/EFTA nationals have materially easier self-employment access, so nationality must be assessed separately.

visa_application.title: SEM — Basis for admission to the Swiss employment market
visa_application.notes: This is official route information, not a direct application portal. Work and residence applications are handled by the competent cantonal immigration or labour-market authority; any required entry visa is normally obtained from a Swiss representation after permit approval.

rejected_routes.route_name: Third-country self-employed admission under Article 19 FNIA

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Federal guidance publishes no fixed monthly-income threshold. Authorities instead assess financing, operating requirements, investment, projected turnover and profit.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed CHF income threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Financial viability is assessed through the complete business case rather than a stated salary threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold; viable Swiss-impact business required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No fixed CHF amount; assessment uses the business plan, investment, staffing, turnover and profit forecasts
income_requirement_display.notes: The decisive test is lasting positive impact on the Swiss labour market and overall economic interest. The current SEM guidance does not convert that test into a monthly-income formula.

income_proof_months.notes: The current federal guidance requires financial and business-plan evidence but prescribes no fixed lookback period for bank statements or prior income.

key_requirements.requirement: Demonstrate a lasting positive impact on the Swiss labour market and overall Swiss economic interest.
Submit a business plan covering activities, market opportunity, staffing and recruitment, planned investment, turnover and profit.
Provide organisational links, formation documents and a commercial-register extract where applicable.
Meet personal, accommodation, quota and other labour-market admission conditions.

initial_validity.value: Permit L or B may be granted according to the approved purpose and cantonal decision; no uniform initial term was confirmed on the reviewed federal route pages.
initial_validity.notes: Permit type and duration require confirmation with the competent canton.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is handled by the canton and depends on continuing satisfaction of the permit and business conditions.
extension_rules.notes: The reviewed national guidance does not publish a single renewal entitlement or term for this entrepreneurial admission.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A successful Article 19 self-employment application can support a Swiss residence/work permit through the competent canton.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Approval is discretionary and subject to the substantive economic-interest test.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying residence permit can eventually support a C settlement permit, commonly after five or ten years depending on nationality and circumstances; this is not direct permanent residence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The precise earliest C-permit date depends on nationality, treaties, integration and canton.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation generally requires ten years of qualifying residence and a C permit; time on B and C permits counts, while L-permit time does not.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This pathway matters only if the applicant first qualifies for and continuously maintains a genuine residence status.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a locally significant entrepreneur/business route, not an ordinary freelance or remote-worker route. A foreign software contract alone does not demonstrate the required Swiss labour-market impact, so the route is rejected for the supplied profile even though a materially different Swiss-impact business could qualify.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed national income threshold is stated; applicants must prove genuine self-employment and ability to support themselves and their family.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed CHF threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Evidence such as accounting records is assessed.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; prove genuine self-employment and self-support
income_requirement_display.notes: This route is nationality-dependent and applies to EU/EFTA citizens, not ordinary third-country applicants.

income_proof_months.notes: The federal guidance requires evidence of genuine self-employment and sufficient means but does not prescribe a standard number of prior-income months.

key_requirements.requirement: EU/EFTA nationality.
Register arrival within 14 days and apply for a residence permit before beginning the relevant activity.
Prove actual or planned self-employment and sufficient resources, for example through accounting records.

initial_validity.value: Depends on the activity and permit issued; a single term was not established on the reviewed page.
initial_validity.notes: Confirm with the commune or canton.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is handled by the canton and depends on continuing eligibility and activity.
extension_rules.notes: No single national renewal term was captured.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: EU/EFTA citizens may apply locally for a residence permit based on self-employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A C permit may be available after five or ten years; specified EU/EFTA nationalities benefit from five-year settlement arrangements.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Nationality-specific treaty and integration rules apply.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation generally becomes possible after ten years of qualifying residence while holding a C permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Potentially compatible with genuine foreign-client freelancing, but only for EU/EFTA nationals. It is rejected for the generic/non-EU/EFTA profile because applicant nationality was not supplied and ordinary third-country rules are materially stricter.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employer-sponsored admission for qualified third-country nationals

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration-wide salary amount applies; customary regional and sector conditions are assessed.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No single national CHF threshold
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Salary must satisfy customary regional and sector conditions.

income_requirement_display.value: No single threshold; Swiss customary salary rules apply
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sector-, occupation- and region-specific customary wage
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer-driven route and does not fit independent foreign-contract work.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not a prior-income-history route; the authorities examine the proposed Swiss employment contract and customary salary conditions.

key_requirements.requirement: Firm job offer from a Swiss employer.
Employer submits the work-permit application.
Generally limited to highly qualified managers, specialists or graduates with experience and subject to quotas and precedence rules.

initial_validity.value: Permit term depends on the approved employment and permit type.
initial_validity.notes: No uniform term applies.

extension_rules.value: Depends on continued approved employment and cantonal renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved Swiss-employer application may produce an L or B work/residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Possible later through qualifying residence, but not granted directly.

path_to_citizenship.value: Possible under the general ten-year naturalisation framework after obtaining a C permit.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Swiss employer, firm local job offer and employer-filed permit application are mandatory.

rejected_routes.route_name: Post-study admission following a recognised Swiss higher-education degree

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No special fixed salary or monthly-income threshold is published for the post-study employment exception. The proposed local employment remains subject to the other admission conditions, including customary salary and working conditions.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed CHF threshold; customary salary conditions apply to the proposed Swiss job
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The six-month post-study job-search period is not itself a published income formula.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold; local job must satisfy customary salary conditions
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No federal fixed CHF amount or formula; assess the proposed Swiss salary against customary local, occupational and sector conditions
income_requirement_display.notes: Current SEM materials confirm a six-month job-search window for graduates of Swiss higher-education institutions and require any resulting employment to be of overriding scientific or economic interest. They do not publish a special graduate salary floor or a monthly means formula.

income_proof_months.notes: No prior-income or bank-statement lookback period is prescribed in the current federal post-study employment guidance. The stated six months is the maximum job-search window after graduation, not an income-proof period; document requirements are determined by the canton and the eventual employer-filed application.

key_requirements.requirement: Degree from a recognised or accredited Swiss higher-education institution.
Employment must be of overriding scientific or economic interest and correspond to the completed studies.
A Swiss employer and local employment-admission process remain necessary.

initial_validity.value: A Swiss graduate may remain for up to six months after completing studies to seek a qualification-matched job; any later work-permit term depends on the approved Swiss employment.
initial_validity.notes: The six-month period is a job-search allowance, not a standalone remote-work permit.

extension_rules.value: The federal materials do not establish an extension of the six-month graduate job-search window. Continued residence afterward depends on approval under another qualifying status, normally local employment.
extension_rules.notes: Any resulting employment permit is renewed under its own permit conditions through the canton.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: May support a work/residence permit after Swiss study and qualifying local employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant's existing foreign degree does not satisfy the Swiss-degree condition.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Only later through the general residence system after obtaining and maintaining a qualifying permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through ten years of qualifying residence and a C permit; time on an L permit does not count toward ordinary naturalisation.

rejected_routes.notes: The applicant's foreign university degree does not activate this exception. The route is limited to graduates of recognised Swiss institutions and requires prospective Swiss employment rather than continuation of an ordinary foreign contract.

summary.value: Admission for study at a Swiss institution can independently provide temporary student residence, but a foreign degree alone creates no independent skilled-residence entitlement. The post-study labour-market exception applies only to graduates of recognised Swiss institutions and still concerns qualifying Swiss employment.
summary.notes: Student residence is education-purpose temporary residence, not direct permanent residence or an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: Unlimited Swiss tax liability arises through domicile or qualifying residence. A stay is tax-resident from at least 30 days when gainfully employed or at least 90 days when not gainfully employed, disregarding temporary interruptions.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breakers and economic connections can alter or create limited liability.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the statutory maximum average direct federal income-tax rate, not the total Swiss rate or expected effective rate. Additional progressive cantonal and communal taxes vary substantially by residence and personal circumstances.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Full 2026 OASI/DI/IC rate for self-employed income of at least CHF 60,500. Lower rates apply below that amount, and the self-employed person pays the full contribution.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal minimum monthly total can be stated. Self-employed OASI/DI/IC has a CHF 530 annual minimum below CHF 10,100 income, while compulsory health-insurance premiums vary by age, canton, insurer, model and deductible. The 2026 all-insured average health premium is CHF 393.30 monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad tax regime was found. Ordinary federal, cantonal and communal rules apply. Separate lump-sum arrangements may exist for qualifying non-working wealthy residents but do not fit gainful remote work.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Canton-specific advice is essential.

taxes.caveats: Swiss tax is highly location- and fact-dependent. Federal, cantonal and communal income taxes, possible wealth tax, social-insurance classification, compulsory private health insurance, foreign-employer payroll obligations and treaty relief must be reviewed together.

taxation_system.value: Progressive federal, cantonal and communal taxation. Federal direct tax has a statutory maximum average rate of 11.5%; total liability cannot be represented by one nationwide percentage because cantonal and communal scales differ.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or at least 30 days with gainful activity / 90 days without gainful activity.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents have unlimited liability; employment and self-employment income are included in taxable total income. Foreign business establishments and foreign real estate may require allocation, and treaties can limit Swiss taxation.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Ordinary canton-dependent taxation applies.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed OASI/DI/IC is 10% from CHF 60,500 annual income, with a degressive 5.371%–9.321% scale below that and a CHF 530 annual minimum below CHF 10,100.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 11.5% dashboard number is only the maximum average direct federal rate, reached under 2025 scales at CHF 793,400 taxable income for single taxpayers or CHF 940,900 for married/single-parent taxpayers. Cantonal and communal taxes are additional, so 11.5% must not be read as the total or expected effective burden.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: From CHF 793,400 taxable income (single/basic scale); CHF 940,900 (married or single-parent scale), 2025 scale
tax_brackets.applies_to: Maximum average direct federal tax rate
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate single-person USD threshold uses CHF 1 = USD 1.2292 on 2026-08-14. Annual scales are inflation-adjusted; this is not a full bracket table or combined canton/commune rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official sources establish the federal structure and self-employed contributions. A combined top rate is intentionally not invented because it depends on canton, commune, marital status, deductions and church-tax position.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Switzerland has no dedicated digital-nomad status. A person who nevertheless obtains valid Swiss residence and works remotely is taxed under ordinary rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad route; ordinary employee or self-employed taxation if lawfully resident
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 11.5% maximum average federal rate, plus variable cantonal and communal taxes
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Tax residence can arise after 30 days with gainful activity or 90 days without gainful activity, or through domicile.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign salary or self-employment income is included in ordinary total income for a resident, subject to source allocation and treaty relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found for ordinary remote workers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Classification depends on whether the person is an employee or genuinely self-employed and on applicable international coordination. Swiss self-employed OASI/DI/IC reaches 10%; a foreign employer may face Swiss payroll obligations.

fixed_payments.status: Partly confirmed; no single universal monthly total
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Self-employed OASI/DI/IC minimum CHF 530 annually below CHF 10,100 income; percentage rates apply above that.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Cantonal permit and visa fees vary and no single national route fee applies.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Compulsory health insurance varies; the official 2026 average across all insured persons is CHF 393.30 per month. VAT registration generally becomes relevant from CHF 100,000 qualifying worldwide turnover for a Swiss business, subject to the detailed supply rules.
fixed_payments.notes: Health insurance is not a tax but is a material mandatory recurring cost. Exact premiums depend on canton, age, insurer, model and deductible.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Short presence does not create unlimited liability solely under the 30/90-day presence test, but domicile, a Swiss permanent establishment, Swiss-source income or treaty rules may still create liability.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary federal, cantonal and communal income taxation applies; there is no nomad exemption.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A genuinely self-employed resident generally pays OASI/DI/IC directly and may need VAT registration from the applicable CHF 100,000 turnover threshold. Immigration approval is separate and must come first.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax treatment is described for a hypothetical lawful resident because no qualifying digital-nomad route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A successful qualifying self-employment or employment application grants residence at approval; there is no preliminary residence accumulation period. This does not make the ordinary foreign-contract profile eligible.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Conservative generic planning value. Some nationalities can receive a C permit after five years, while others generally face a ten-year framework; canton and integration conditions apply.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation requires ten total qualifying residence years and a C permit. If the C permit is obtained at year ten, no additional statutory federal residence period necessarily follows, but processing and local requirements remain.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Earliest ordinary federal residence threshold for an adult on qualifying counted permits; approval is not automatic.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable nationwide total processing time was established. The official page states that the canton must decide within one year after the federal naturalisation licence, but that is only one stage of the process.

key_conditions.value: Ten years of qualifying residence, C permit, three years in the five years before applying, successful integration, familiarity with Swiss life, no security threat, national-language ability at B1 oral/A2 written, compliance with public order and taxes, and canton/commune residence requirements of two to five years. B/C time counts; L time does not.
key_conditions.notes: Switzerland permits dual nationality, but the applicant should also check the law of their present nationality.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For a spouse living in Switzerland: three years married and living together, five total years of Swiss residence, and residence in Switzerland during the year immediately before application. A spouse living abroad generally needs six years of marriage and close ties to Switzerland.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a person who was already Swiss can count toward the required marriage period. Simplified naturalisation is unavailable where both spouses were foreign when they married and the spouse became Swiss later through ordinary naturalisation.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Residence through family reunification is separate from citizenship and depends on the sponsor and permit conditions.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must remain genuinely married and living together, satisfy integration, language, public-order, tax and security requirements, and document the relationship. False statements or a sham marriage can lead to refusal, annulment and immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates eligibility but does not create automatic citizenship or permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Switzerland alone does not confer Swiss nationality. The ordinary rule is descent from a Swiss parent, with limited simplified-naturalisation provisions such as the third-generation procedure.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Switzerland to two non-Swiss migrant parents does not automatically become Swiss merely by birth. A qualifying third-generation child may later use simplified naturalisation, but that is conditional and application-based.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child generally acquires Swiss citizenship by descent when a parent is Swiss. Where the Swiss father is unmarried to the foreign mother, legal recognition of paternity is important; recognised children obtain citizenship through the Swiss father.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Historic cases, adoption, loss for unregistered births abroad and parentage disputes have special rules.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Swiss child may support a fact-specific family-residence claim, but the child's citizenship does not automatically grant the foreign parent permanent residence or Swiss citizenship.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: No general automatic parent-naturalisation benefit was found.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Swiss, the child is generally Swiss by descent, but the migrant father must rely on family-reunification/residence rules and later naturalisation rules. Fatherhood alone does not automatically confer residence, a C permit or citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Custody, actual family life, support and immigration status can affect an individual residence case.

rank.notes: Current ranking page checked 2026-08-15; Henley rankings can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score includes destinations accessible without a prior traditional visa, including visa-on-arrival arrangements; it is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Inferred as 227 Henley destinations minus the access score of 185. Henley does not provide this as a separately displayed Swiss value on the captured ranking page.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The current Henley ranking page did not provide a separate combined visa-on-arrival/eTA count, so no split was invented.

passport.notes: The current live Henley table differs from its January 2026 press release; the live ranking was preferred.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is useful in international business and has become important across Switzerland's language regions, but it is not a general federal official language. Long-term administration, integration and naturalisation are more practical with the local national language.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Practicality varies substantially by canton, city and employer.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and cannot be relied on for immigration, tax or naturalisation procedures. Availability of community services was not established from authoritative national sources.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Use of a local national language, or English where accepted, remains necessary.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official ESS releases and tables publish medians and percentiles, not a directly comparable national arithmetic-average monthly wage; no mean was derived from quantiles.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of CHF 7,024 using CHF 1 = USD 1.2292 on 2026-08-14.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Switzerland has no nationwide statutory minimum wage. Binding minimums can instead arise under cantonal rules, collective agreements or standard employment contracts, so no single national USD amount applies.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed 2024 ESS outputs do not publish a citizenship-specific arithmetic mean comparable with the Swiss-employee median; no average was inferred from the median or percentiles.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official CHF 7,480 median monthly wage for Swiss employees in 2024.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official wage sources publish medians, percentiles and selected occupational or responsibility subgroups, not a finite national maximum salary. A subgroup or upper percentile was not mislabeled as the national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: No single nationwide CHF minimum wage; applicable floors depend on canton, collective agreement, sector or binding standard employment contract
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is a legal inapplicability, not missing numerical data. Switzerland has no national statutory minimum wage from which one countrywide monthly amount could be reported.

average_salary_local_currency.value: No citizenship-specific arithmetic mean is published in the reviewed 2024 ESS releases or current percentile tables; the official Swiss-employee benchmark is the CHF 7,480 monthly median
average_salary_local_currency.notes: The FSO tables explicitly organize the monthly wage results around the median and other quantiles. A mean cannot be reconstructed reliably from those statistics.

median_salary_local_currency.value: CHF 7,480 monthly for Swiss employees; CHF 7,024 for the whole economy
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Both are gross full-time-equivalent 2024 medians.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No finite nationwide maximum salary is defined or published; official 2024 ESS outputs provide percentiles and subgroup wages instead
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Senior-manager figures and upper percentiles describe particular groups or distribution points and are not a national maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross monthly full-time-equivalent employee wage; citizen-specific median supplemented by the whole-economy median
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are worker salary statistics, not immigration income thresholds. The citizen-specific median was CHF 7,480; foreign employees' median was CHF 6,235 and the whole-economy median was CHF 7,024. Switzerland has no nationwide statutory minimum wage, and the official current sources do not publish a citizenship-specific arithmetic mean or finite nationwide maximum. USD conversions use the latest available 2026-08-14 rate of CHF 1 = USD 1.2292.

cost_of_living_note.value: Compulsory health insurance is a major recurring cost: the official average premium across all insured persons is CHF 393.30 per month in 2026, with actual adult premiums varying by canton, insurer, model and deductible.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This is a documented mandatory-cost indicator, not a complete national cost-of-living estimate.
