settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad status exists. Visitor or visa-free presence does not legalise ordinary gainful remote work or create a settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route was confirmed. Citizenship is possible only after first qualifying under a materially different status, such as an approved Swiss-impact business, Swiss-sponsored employment, qualifying family residence or EU/EFTA free movement, and then satisfying the general ten-year naturalisation framework.
settlement_track.notes: The entrepreneurial route can lead to settlement for a genuinely qualifying Swiss-impact business, but the supplied foreign-contract profile does not meet that route merely by registering as a freelancer.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker permit was found. Third-country self-employment requires demonstrated lasting Swiss labour-market impact, while ordinary employment requires a firm Swiss job offer. EU/EFTA nationality would materially change the analysis.

data.notes: The focused audit confirms the previous negative selection result. Twenty-nine distinct directly relevant sources are retained, including eight official/statistical URLs not present in the previous source set. The post-study income fields now distinguish the six-month job-search window from income-proof requirements, and the salary fields precisely explain why nationwide minimum, citizenship-specific arithmetic-mean and finite maximum figures are inapplicable or unpublished rather than labeling them merely unconfirmed.

data.selection_summary: No current Syrian digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, independent freelance, or ordinary self-employed residence route was found. Syrian labour legislation requires non-nationals to obtain a ministerial work permit tied to an approved employer and activity. Residence law provides temporary, work, regular, and special permits but no foreign-contract remote-work channel; current visa material covers tourist, business, and student entry. Syria therefore does not fit the requested independent, citizenship-oriented remote-work selection. Current official foreign travel advice also warns against all travel.

visa_application.title: Embassy of the Syrian Arab Republic — Visa Requirements
visa_application.notes: Official information for tourist, business, student, diplomatic, and official visas, not a digital-nomad, independent-work, or residence application portal. Applications use a form and diplomatic-mission submission. The page states indicative processing of 7–10 business days but publishes no remote-work category.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employer-specific foreign work permit and work residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed laws publish no universally applicable numeric minimum-income threshold for foreign workers.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Residence law requires sufficient means but states no numeric threshold for work residence.

income_requirement_display.value: No published numeric threshold; sufficient means and an approved employer/work permit are required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Not numerically specified in the governing laws
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a foreign-income route. Employer approval and Ministry of Labour authorization are the controlling requirements.

income_proof_months.notes: The governing laws do not prescribe a standardized number of months of income evidence.

key_requirements.requirement: Ministry-issued work permit for any non-national working in Syria.
Employer financial guarantee and permit fee may be required under ministerial rules.
Work is restricted to the employer and activity shown on the permit.
Work residence requires Ministry of Labour approval and sufficient means.

initial_validity.value: Work residence permit: up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: This is the statutory maximum; an individual visa or permit may be shorter.

extension_rules.value: Renewal may be requested, but approval and current work authorization remain necessary
extension_rules.notes: Law No. 2/2014 requires departure when an authorized stay ends unless the residence permit is renewed and delegates renewal forms, authorities, exemptions, and procedures to a ministerial decision. The reviewed law and current official entry materials do not publish that implementing decision, a filing deadline, fee schedule, or online renewal channel; continued Ministry of Labour approval remains necessary for work residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A work residence permit can be issued after Ministry of Labour approval
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is employer- and work-approval-dependent and therefore fails the selection criteria.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No permanent-residence category was confirmed. The law instead provides three-year regular residence after at least five years of legal residence and five-year special residence after 15 years, or after five years plus qualifying useful work or service.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: These are renewable fixed-term classifications, not permanent residence. The law does not make progression from employer-specific work residence automatic, and useful work or service for special residence requires official assessment.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalization may be requested after at least 5 consecutive years of residence but remains discretionary and is not a confirmed consequence of this work-permit route.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No current official source states that work-residence time guarantees naturalization beyond potentially satisfying the residence element.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest conventional work route, but it requires an approved employer, Ministry authorization, an employer guarantee, and adherence to the named employer and activity. It cannot support ordinary independent work for a foreign client and is not a confirmed permanent-settlement route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist or business visa used for remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold applies because these are visitor or business-entry categories, not remote-worker statuses.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current entry sources publish no numeric remote-income requirement.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable — no remote-worker category
income_requirement_display.notes: A tourist or business visa does not establish permission for ongoing remote work or a residence-to-citizenship track.

income_proof_months.notes: No standardized remote-income history applies to the published tourist and business categories.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport valid for at least 6 months and an advance entry visa unless exempt.
Tourists provide itinerary and accommodation evidence; business applicants require a Syrian host invitation and an employer letter.

initial_validity.value: Visa-specific; tourist residence is statutorily limited to 3 months
initial_validity.notes: The embassy page does not publish one universal stay duration for all visas.

extension_rules.value: Any extension is discretionary and does not convert visitor status into remote-work authorization
extension_rules.notes: Law No. 2/2014 contemplates residence renewal under Interior Ministry procedures but establishes no tourist-to-remote-worker conversion category.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct qualifying residence
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate statutory residence basis and residence-permit application would be required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No permanent-residence progression from tourist or business entry is established
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Tourist residence is capped at three months. Although the general law permits three-year regular residence after at least five years of legal residence, neither the law nor current official visa guidance states that visitor or tourist time supplies a qualifying settlement route, and visitor status does not authorize ongoing remote work.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path arises from the visitor or business visa itself
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization law does not convert visitor entry into a qualifying immigration route.

rejected_routes.notes: Tourist and business entry cannot substitute for a digital-nomad or independent residence permit. The labour law's broad definition of work creates material compliance risk for remote work performed while physically in Syria.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official visa page requires tuition payment or financial sponsorship but publishes no numeric threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official visa page does not state a numeric financial amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No published numeric threshold; tuition payment or financial sponsorship required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an education route, not an ordinary remote-work or qualification-based migration route.

income_proof_months.notes: The official student-visa page requires financial sponsorship or tuition evidence but specifies no standardized evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: Acceptance from a Syrian educational institution.
Proof of tuition payment or financial sponsorship, enrollment, and accommodation.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence for the period of study, subject to approved enrollment and issuance of the separate residence permit
initial_validity.notes: The law ties student temporary residence to the study period but the reviewed current sources do not publish a universal residence-card term or filing-level validity rule.

extension_rules.value: Student temporary residence may continue for the approved period of study; renewal requires a residence-permit renewal under Interior Ministry procedures
extension_rules.notes: Article 20 ties student temporary residence to the period of study, while Articles 16 and 25 contemplate renewal and delegate the detailed process to the Interior Ministry. The reviewed current visa page and residence law do not publish the implementing form, filing window, fee, or online channel.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Registered students at Syrian-government-approved universities, colleges, or schools are statutorily eligible for temporary residence for the period of study
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The student visa is the entry document; the residence permit is a separate application to Immigration and Passports. The law establishes eligibility and the duration basis, but current filing procedures and residence-card validity were not published in the reviewed sources.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No education-specific permanent-residence progression is established
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The residence laws contain general fixed-term residence classifications but no graduate settlement or education-to-permanent-residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: No study-specific citizenship route is established
path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary discretionary naturalization rules are separate, and the reviewed law does not promise that study leads to naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Admission can be obtained without a local employer, but this requires actual study and does not fit an established software engineer continuing ordinary work under a foreign contract. No graduate-to-settlement route was confirmed.

summary.value: With admission and enrollment at a Syrian-government-approved institution, a foreign student may obtain temporary residence for the period of study. No independent degree-based skilled-migration route or confirmed study-to-permanent-residence track exists.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing software-engineering degree alone creates no residence entitlement. Study requires actual enrollment; a student visa and residence-permit filing are separate steps.

tax_residency_rule.value: No current official day-count tax-residency test was located. Legacy material describes Syrian taxation principally by source or activity in Syria rather than a general 183-day worldwide-income rule.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The 2019 secondary tax summary is old. Current professional advice is essential before performing services from Syria.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Legacy statutory top marginal wage and salary rate under the 2020 amendment. This is a screening rate, not an expected effective rate or digital-nomad rate. The government was still discussing unified-income-tax reform in 2026, so the operative post-redenomination schedule must be verified.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Legacy combined ordinary social-insurance contribution: 14% employer, 7% employee, and 0.1% employer administration. The guide states that a voluntarily subscribing self-employed person pays the full 21.1%. A further 3% employer work-injury contribution may apply. Current 2026 official reporting confirms new contribution bases but not all rates.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable USD fixed payment can be calculated for an ineligible remote worker. Social insurance is percentage-based, the 2026 contribution bases are denominated in new Syrian pounds, and current voluntary coverage of a foreign self-employed worker was not established.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, expatriate, or remittance-basis regime was found. Government statements in 2026 described proposed unified-income-tax reforms and higher exemptions, not a nomad regime.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The proposals should not be treated as enacted rules without final legislation and implementation guidance.

taxes.caveats: Syria has no qualifying remote-worker route. Tax law is undergoing reform, currency values have been redenominated, and no clear 2026 official guide establishes the treatment of services performed in Syria for a foreign payer. Social-insurance liability depends on whether the person is lawfully treated as an employee, licensed worker, or locally registered self-employed person. Current Syrian tax and immigration advice is essential before working or registering.

taxation_system.value: Legacy law uses schedular and source-based taxation, including progressive wage and salary bands reaching 18%; unified-income-tax reforms remained upcoming or proposed in the reviewed 2026 government material.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No current official day-count rule was established; legacy treatment focuses on Syrian-source income and services or activities performed in Syria.
taxation_system.income_scope: Legacy secondary guidance states that Syrian-source income or activities are taxable regardless of residence and that non-Syrian-source income is outside scope. Remote services physically performed in Syria require professional source analysis.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Legacy ordinary total is 21.1%: 14% employer, 7% employee, and 0.1% employer administration; voluntarily subscribing self-employed persons were reported to bear the full 21.1%. Official 2026 minimum and maximum contribution bases are SYP 12,560 and SYP 211,400 in new currency from 1 June 2026.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 18% is the top marginal rate in the last clearly captured statutory wage schedule, not an effective rate. Its old-currency thresholds should not be used after the 2026 currency and tax changes without official confirmation. Government reporting described proposed exemptions and upcoming unified-tax legislation, but a final enacted schedule was not located.
taxation_system.notes: Exact current brackets are omitted because the captured statutory thresholds predate the 2026 redenomination and government sources describe continuing reforms. The legacy top rate is retained only as a cautious screening figure.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable: Syria has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad route; potential Syrian-source services or unlicensed work require individual legal analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: No digital-nomad tax rate applies because Syria has no such status; 18% is only the legacy top marginal wage/salary screening rate, and its operative 2026 applicability must be verified amid pending tax reform.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No current official day-count test was established; legacy law and secondary guidance focus on Syrian-source activities.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Legacy secondary guidance describes foreign-source income as outside Syrian tax, but services physically performed in Syria may be Syrian-source even when paid abroad.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad, inbound remote-worker, or remittance-basis regime was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad rule exists. Legacy employee contributions and voluntary self-employed insurance can be relevant only where lawful local work status and registration exist.

fixed_payments.status: No route-specific fixed-payment schedule is applicable because Syria has no digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker status.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No nomad-specific fixed contribution exists. General social insurance is percentage-based; official 2026 reporting sets contribution bases of SYP 12,560 to SYP 211,400 in new currency, while neither that source nor the employment guide establishes mandatory coverage for a foreign remote worker lacking lawful local work registration.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Visa fees vary by nationality and visa type; the embassy instructs applicants to confirm the amount before submission.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No nomad-specific municipal fee, freelancer levy, VAT threshold, stamp duty, or transaction tax applies as a published route charge because the route does not exist. General business taxes and fees would require separate classification and lawful registration.
fixed_payments.notes: A fixed monthly total cannot be calculated: the immigration category does not exist, visa fees vary by nationality and type, contribution liability depends on lawful employee or voluntary self-employed registration, and current sources publish contribution bases rather than a nomad-specific flat amount.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No safe tax-free remote-work scenario can be stated because no official day-count test or visitor remote-work permission was established.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Requires individual legal analysis of income source, work authorization, the changing income-tax law, and treaty position; no special regime applies.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: General social-insurance material describes voluntary self-employed participation, but this creates neither immigration nor work authorization, and no foreigner-friendly sole-proprietor residence path was confirmed.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The numeric figure is a legacy top marginal screening rate, not a nomad tax rate. Current filing treatment remains unresolved because the immigration route does not exist and tax reform remains in progress.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent route exists. Employer-approved work residence can be issued directly for up to one year, but it fails the applicant criteria.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No permanent-residence category or guaranteed transition from temporary work residence was established. Regular and special residence are renewable fixed-term statuses.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on qualifying residence rather than a separately established permanent-residence starting point.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five consecutive years is the statutory ordinary-naturalization residence minimum, not a guaranteed timeline and not available through a confirmed independent remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The reviewed nationality texts publish no current service standard or typical processing period.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalization is discretionary and generally requires at least five consecutive years of residence, full legal capacity, good conduct, lawful means of support, and Arabic reading and writing. Approval is by decree or ministerial process; satisfying the conditions does not guarantee nationality. No qualifying remote-work residence route was found.
key_conditions.notes: The 2026 Kurdish nationality program concerns a specific historically stateless population and is not an ordinary migrant route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign woman married to a Syrian man may acquire nationality after applying, maintaining the marriage for two years from the application, residing lawfully during that period, and receiving ministerial approval. The rule does not equivalently benefit a foreign husband of a Syrian woman.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can supply the family relationship, but the statutory two-year period runs from the nationality application and requires the marriage to continue. Marriage to a Syrian woman does not create the same accelerated nationality right for a foreign husband.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage registration and recognition must be verified before relying on the provision.

requirements_and_risks.value: The accelerated rule is gender-asymmetric and discretionary and requires a valid continuing marriage, lawful residence, an application, and ministerial approval. Documentary and security review should be expected; sham marriage or false documents can result in refusal, loss of status, or other penalties.
requirements_and_risks.notes: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence arises merely from marriage.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Nationality is principally transmitted through a Syrian father. Syrian birth alone is insufficient, subject to narrow provisions for unknown or stateless parents, foundlings, children unable to acquire another nationality at birth, and a child born in Syria to a Syrian mother where legal paternity is not established.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: An ordinary child born in Syria to two foreign migrant parents does not automatically become Syrian. Narrow anti-statelessness, unknown-parent, or foundling provisions may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for ordinary foreign parents able to transmit another nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A Syrian father generally transmits Syrian nationality whether the child is born inside or outside Syria. A Syrian mother does not generally transmit nationality on equal terms; a child born in Syria may qualify through her where legal paternity is not established.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because the outcome depends on whether the Syrian parent is the father or mother, the single boolean field is null rather than masking the gender distinction.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having a Syrian citizen child does not automatically naturalize or grant permanent residence to a foreign parent. Any family residence or naturalization request remains a separate, discretionary legal process.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The residence law expressly favors a foreign wife of a Syrian man for special residence after two years but establishes no equivalent automatic parent-of-citizen benefit.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father receives no automatic citizenship from a Syrian child. If the child's mother is Syrian, the child generally does not acquire Syrian nationality through her unless a narrow statutory exception applies; any residence benefit for the father requires a separate legal basis.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parental status must not be inferred automatically from the child's nationality.

rank.notes: Live Passport Power Rank observed on 2026-08-15; live rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-free category, not its broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 live breakdown.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 27 visa-on-arrival plus 3 eTA destinations. eVisas are not included in this combined field.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 36. Different passport indexes use different methodologies, so their ranks and category totals should not be combined.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English may be usable within some professional or educated circles, but official administration is Arabic and remote work is operationally difficult. Internet Society reports low network resilience, approximately 36% internet use, about 4.36 Mbps average broadband download speed, and very poor ISP choice; a 2026 urban survey found only 39% always had internet or Wi-Fi access.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: These are national or limited urban-sample indicators, not a guarantee for a particular address. Arabic literacy is also relevant to ordinary naturalization.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian cannot be relied upon for government procedures or everyday administration; Arabic remains the official language. The reviewed current sources do not quantify Ukrainian-language availability or dependable Russian-language service coverage.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This cautious qualitative assessment reflects the absence of current proficiency or service-coverage statistics in the inspected sources.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current unified national all-worker mean in USD was established. SCPR publishes selected occupational and sector averages in SYP, while currency redenomination and exchange-rate differences prevent a dependable single USD conversion.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed sources publish no national all-worker median, and WorkLink's salary-disclosing vacancy sample is too sparse to calculate one.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent reported by official state media for the 2026 statutory minimum wage; highly exchange-rate-sensitive.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: SCPR supplies selected category means in SYP, not one all-worker mean. A single USD value would also be unstable because of redenomination and exchange-rate fragmentation.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither source publishes a national all-worker median, and only 19 of 2,573 WorkLink vacancies disclosed salary in H1 2026.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither source defines a national maximum wage; converting an unrepresentative observed maximum would not produce a meaningful national statistic.

min_salary_local_currency.value: SYP 12,560 new pounds monthly, equivalent to SYP 1,256,000 old pounds
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory general minimum wage under the 2026 wage changes, not an observed minimum or average salary.

average_salary_local_currency.value: November 2025 national category averages: SYP 1,151,013 for a public-sector university graduate, SYP 1,303,698 for a private-sector shop worker, and SYP 2,967,658 for a civil-sector university graduate.
average_salary_local_currency.notes: SCPR publishes nationally aggregated averages for selected worker categories, not one all-worker national mean. The category values are presented without collapsing them into an invented single figure.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither source publishes a national all-worker median. SCPR reports selected occupation and sector means, while WorkLink reports that only 19 of 2,573 verified vacancies disclosed salary in H1 2026, which is insufficient to calculate a representative median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither source defines or estimates a national maximum monthly wage. SCPR gives selected occupation averages and WorkLink salary disclosure is too sparse; a maximum would be sample-dependent rather than a meaningful national statistic.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum wage for the minimum field; November 2025 nationally aggregated mean wages for selected occupations and sectors for the local average field; no all-worker national mean, median, or maximum.
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage effective May 2026; selected wage-category averages for November 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The USD 105 figure is the reported statutory minimum wage, not an average citizen salary. Redenomination, inflation, fragmented labour markets, and exchange-rate differences make USD comparisons unstable.

cost_of_living_note.value: No single reliable nationwide monthly cost-of-living total was established. A 2026 survey of 600 people aged 16–35 in Damascus, Aleppo, and Homs found widespread difficulty affording housing, food, basic goods, and services, so a low nominal wage should not be read as evidence of easy affordability.
cost_of_living_note.notes: The survey is urban and age-limited; it provides context rather than a national cost basket.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tourist and business visas do not create remote-work permission or a settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: Only an employer-approved, activity-specific foreign work permit and work residence were confirmed. Syria has no independent ordinary remote-work route, and its discretionary five-year naturalization law does not cure that missing entry or residence basis.
settlement_track.notes: The statutory five-year naturalization residence minimum should not be displayed as a usable route timeline because no qualifying independent route exists and naturalization remains discretionary.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor entry does not establish work rights, while lawful foreign work requires Ministry authorization tied to an approved employer and activity.

data.notes: Thirty distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected, including six canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. Targeted checks covered residence renewal and fixed-term regular and special residence, student temporary residence, current entry rules, wage statistics and salary disclosure, 2026 wage and social-insurance changes, and current tax reform. The no-route conclusion remains high confidence. Remote-worker taxation and filing-level renewal procedures remain low confidence because no such immigration category exists and consolidated 2026 official implementation guidance was not published. FCDO advice reviewed for 2026-08-15 advises against all travel because of unpredictable security conditions and terrorism risk.

data.selection_summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was confirmed. The eVisa is short and non-extendable; work permission requires a Tajik inviter and contract; and the commercial-activity/individual-entrepreneur route requires prior immigration permission, local business formalities, and ultimately a work permit without a confirmed settlement conversion.

visa_application.title: Tajikistan Visa Electronic Application Center
visa_application.notes: Official general visa application portal. It processes standard visas but does not show a dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence category.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold is published because this is visitor/business entry permission.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; visitor/business eVisa only
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not a residence or remote-work category.

income_proof_months.notes: No recurring-income proof period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Online application, valid travel document, and USD 50 electronic processing fee.
Travel purpose must be tourism or business rather than residence or local employment.

initial_validity.value: Valid for 90 days, with a maximum stay of 45 calendar days.
initial_validity.notes: Visa validity and permitted stay are different.

extension_rules.value: Not extendable; the holder must leave by the permitted date.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed from this eVisa.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The eVisa is not a residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed from this eVisa.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence requires a separate permission and residence permit.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from the eVisa itself.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires five years from obtaining a permanent residence permit.

rejected_routes.notes: The eVisa is independently obtainable but is visitor-like, non-extendable, and not a settlement route. It therefore fails the citizenship-oriented selection criteria.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying salary threshold was established.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker threshold; Tajik inviter and contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility depends on sponsorship documents rather than a foreign-income floor.

income_proof_months.notes: No foreign-income history requirement applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Petition from an inviting organization or Tajik citizen.
Signed labor or civil contract and applicable work authorization.

initial_validity.notes: The exact general maximum was not established from the current official material reviewed; validity depends on the approved work basis.

extension_rules.value: Continued validity depends on the contract, inviter, and work authorization.
extension_rules.notes: Filing-level confirmation is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence permit is granted by the work visa itself.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The visa authorizes a purpose of stay; residence documentation is separate.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence requires a separate permission.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only through a separate permanent-residence basis followed by the nationality-law residence period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This is not available independently for the stated foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.notes: This route requires a Tajik inviter and labor or civil contract. It does not fit ordinary remote work for an overseas employer or client.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No minimum foreign income is specified because eligibility depends on local commercial authorization and registration rather than an income floor.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current registration and visa materials do not prescribe an immigration income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; local commercial authorization and business formalities apply
income_requirement_display.notes: The unresolved issue is independent eligibility and settlement, not income.

income_proof_months.notes: The current materials do not prescribe a foreign-income history period.

key_requirements.requirement: A foreign individual must already hold a visa, registration card, or residence permit authorizing stay and entrepreneurial activity for at least three months.
Individual-entrepreneur registration requires a Tajik address, taxpayer number, identity documents, and proof of the business location.

Official visa guidance describes an initial commercial visa of up to three months; extension requires commercial-organization documentation, tax clearance, entrepreneur patent where applicable, and a work permit.

initial_validity.value: Initial commercial visa up to three months.
initial_validity.notes: This is a visa, not qualifying residence.

extension_rules.value: Extension is tied to local commercial documentation and a Migration Service work permit.
extension_rules.notes: The official material does not establish a simple self-sponsored foreign-client renewal route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct temporary residence status was confirmed.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Business registration does not itself create immigration status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic or confirmed conversion from this commercial visa was found.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence is separately approved by the internal-affairs authorities.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path; a separately approved permanent residence permit would be needed before the ordinary five-year naturalization clock.

rejected_routes.notes: This is not a clean visitor-to-self-employed route. Registration depends on prior permission to conduct business, while extension requires local commercial substance and a work permit. No official source confirmed that an ordinary foreign-client software contractor can apply independently or convert this status into settlement.

summary.value: An educational visa can be requested without an employer, but it requires a petition from an educational or scientific institution. It is a study visa, not an independent degree-based residence or permanent-residence route for an already-qualified software engineer.
summary.notes: No independent points-tested, degree-recognition, or skilled-migration residence route was found.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual generally becomes resident after being physically present in Tajikistan for more than 182 consecutive days in any 12-month period ending in the calendar year, beginning on day 183. Special rules can also treat permanent-residence applicants and certain citizens as residents.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and the current Tajik-language code should be checked before filing.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for individual taxable income outside the resident main-place-of-employment and specified nonresident-employment categories. Resident main-place employment is generally 12%; Tajik-source nonresident employment is 20%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Typical insured-person rate for non-budget organizations. The corresponding organization rate is 20%; budget institutions use 1% employee and 25% organization rates. Individual entrepreneurs have separate rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no universal monthly amount. Patent tax depends on activity and locality; certificate-based entrepreneur social tax uses statutory formulas and minimums, so a reliable USD figure cannot be calculated without a confirmed activity, regime, patent amount, calculation indicator, and regional coefficient.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, inbound-worker, remittance-basis, or foreign-remote-worker tax concession was identified. Individual entrepreneurs may use certificate or patent systems depending on activity.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Entrepreneur tax treatment does not establish immigration eligibility.

taxes.caveats: Remote income can be characterized as employment, services, or entrepreneurial income. Tax residence, Tajik-source rules, treaty residence, deductions, payroll obligations, and business registration should be reviewed professionally before working from Tajikistan.

taxation_system.value: Category-based personal income tax system: generally 12% for resident main-place employment, 20% for Tajik-source employment of a nonresident, and 15% for other taxable individual income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 182 consecutive days in a 12-month period, with additional statutory residence rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally exposed on worldwide taxable income; nonresidents are taxed on Tajik-source income. Source and contract characterization remain important.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-remote-worker regime identified; entrepreneur certificate and patent systems are activity-specific.
taxation_system.social_security: For non-budget organizations, the official Social Insurance and Pension Agency states 20% for the policyholder and 2% for the insured person. Certificate-based individual entrepreneurs generally face 1% subject to statutory minimums.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The system is not progressive by income threshold; rates differ by taxpayer and income category. The 20% figure is a top screening rate, not the expected effective rate for a resident foreign contractor.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No monetary threshold; resident main-place-of-employment category
tax_brackets.applies_to: Taxable income of a resident individual at the main place of employment after applicable deductions.
tax_brackets.notes: Category rate, not a progressive bracket.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Taxable income of individuals not covered by the resident main-employment or specified nonresident-employment categories.
tax_brackets.notes: Likely screening category for many non-payroll contractor situations; professional classification is required.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No monetary threshold; nonresident Tajik-source employment category
tax_brackets.applies_to: Taxable Tajik-source employment income of a nonresident individual.
tax_brackets.notes: Top category rate, not a progressive bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The 2025 English Tax Code is an unofficial translation hosted by the Tax Committee. Current Tajik text and any treaty must control.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Tajikistan has no identified digital-nomad immigration or tax category. Ordinary income-tax, source, payroll, and entrepreneur rules would need to be applied to the actual arrangement.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; employment, services, or entrepreneurial income
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 15% contractor/other-individual screening rate; 12% resident main employment and 20% nonresident Tajik-source employment may apply instead
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 182 consecutive days in a 12-month period, subject to additional statutory and treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident may be taxable on worldwide income; a nonresident is generally taxable on Tajik-source income. Remote-work source characterization was not conclusively established.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated regime is provided in the current tax and visa material reviewed.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No special foreign-employer exemption was identified. Ordinary employee rates or certificate/patent entrepreneur rules may apply after local registration.

fixed_payments.status: No dedicated digital-nomad fixed payment applies because Tajikistan has no digital-nomad immigration or tax category. If a foreigner separately qualifies and registers as an individual entrepreneur, patent holders prepay an activity- and location-specific fixed tax, while certificate-based entrepreneurs and social-tax rules use separate formulas; the current official material does not support one universal monthly amount for a foreign software contractor.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed monthly amount. Certificate-based entrepreneurs face 1% subject to statutory minimums linked to patent amounts, calculation indicators, and regional coefficients.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The visitor/business eVisa processing fee is USD 50. No digital-nomad visa or renewal fee exists because no such route was identified.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Registration, patent, VAT, banking, and transaction obligations depend on the activity and legal form; the current sources do not establish a universal remote-worker package.
fixed_payments.notes: The Tax Code distinguishes patent fixed amounts from certificate taxation and restricts use of the special entrepreneur regime where services mainly go to one person or resemble employment. The 2026 Tax Committee rate page and calculator require activity and locality inputs, so a single fixed amount would be misleading.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: The person may remain nonresident, but Tajik tax can still arise if the income is treated as Tajik-source. Visitor immigration status does not itself authorize work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide taxable income may fall within Tajik residence rules; 15% is a practical contractor screening rate, but 12% employment or other rules can apply.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Individual-entrepreneur registration triggers certificate or patent tax and social-tax rules. It requires prior immigration permission to conduct business and does not itself provide residence.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a tax screen for a hypothetical arrangement, not confirmation that the immigration route is available.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent temporary-residence route was identified.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The law provides a separately approved permanent residence permit, but no minimum conversion period from the rejected visitor, work, or commercial visas was established.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The five-year continuous-residence period runs from the date the permanent residence permit is obtained, not from an eVisa or ordinary temporary visa.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: A total cannot be calculated for this profile because no qualifying route to the permanent residence permit was confirmed.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The statutory maximum is one year after a properly completed application and all required documents are submitted; actual processing may vary.

key_conditions.value: Five years of continuous permanent residence from receipt of the residence permit; any single annual absence generally no longer than three months except for study, treatment, or business travel; conversational Tajik; no criminal prosecution; and compliance with restrictions on holding another citizenship where no applicable interstate treaty exists.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and does not cure the absence of a qualifying immigration route.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The current citizenship law does not list a citizen spouse among its simplified-naturalization categories, and the reviewed current laws do not state a marriage-duration shortcut.

existing_marriage_effect.value: The migration law recognizes a person married to a Tajik citizen as a settler and may support family or permanent-residence processing. However, the current 2015 citizenship law, recorded as amended in 2025, does not provide the spouse-based registration shortcut shown on older MFA material.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The precise residence-permit basis, documents, and timing require confirmation with the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be legally valid and genuine. It does not automatically confer residence or citizenship; false information or documents can cause refusal, and citizenship decisions can be revoked when obtained unlawfully.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Older official English pages describe a superseded spouse shortcut and should not be relied upon over the current law.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Tajikistan alone is insufficient for a child of two foreign citizens. Territorial rules mainly protect children who would otherwise be stateless, children of qualifying stateless permanent residents, and foundlings.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child of two foreign-citizen parents is not automatically Tajik merely because of birth in Tajikistan, unless the parents' national laws do not grant the child citizenship. A child born to stateless parents qualifies when both or one parent permanently resides in Tajikistan.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for the ordinary case of two foreign parents whose citizenship passes to the child.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: When one parent is Tajik and the other is foreign, the child acquires Tajik citizenship if born in Tajikistan. For birth abroad, parental permanent residence and written agreement rules apply. If the other parent is stateless or unknown, citizenship applies regardless of birthplace.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically give a foreign parent citizenship. Family immigration or permanent-residence processing may be relevant, but the current law does not establish an automatic parental status.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A separate application and qualifying basis are required.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence. If the other parent is Tajik, the child can be Tajik under the birth rules; the foreign father must separately establish a family or residence basis.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parenthood may support a family case but is not itself a grant of status.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the live Tajikistan passport dashboard on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free category; it excludes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately classifies many additional destinations as eVisa rather than visa required.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 41 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 67. Its strict category breakdown differs from Henley's combined visa-free/visa-on-arrival access score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be sufficient within an overseas remote team, but it is neither the state language nor the constitutionally recognized interethnic language. Tajik or Russian is more practical for government, banking, registration, and everyday administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This practicality assessment is an inference from the constitutional language framework; no current national English-proficiency dataset was identified.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is constitutionally designated as the language of interethnic communication and is practically useful. Ukrainian has no official status and should not be expected to substitute for Tajik or Russian in administration.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official May 2026 arithmetic mean of TJS 3,304.05 using TJS 9.2448 per USD, the closest pre-research-date official exchange rate captured.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official wage catalogue and January–June 2026 report publish arithmetic means and sectoral averages but no national median or percentile distribution from which a USD median could be calculated.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the TJS 1,000 statutory minimum wage; this is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official May 2026 average monthly gross accrued wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official analytical tables and January–June 2026 report publish monthly arithmetic means and sectoral averages, but no national median wage or percentile distribution from which a median could be calculated; the USD value therefore remains null.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official January–June 2026 report gives sectoral mean wages, not a maximum individual wage or upper bound, so no numeric USD maximum is inferred.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory monthly minimum effective from 1 September 2025.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official average monthly gross accrued wage for May 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.value: The current official 2026 wage tables publish arithmetic means, not a national median wage.
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither the official analytical-table catalogue nor the January–June 2026 wage report includes a median or percentile distribution.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No national maximum wage is published; the May 2026 report's highest listed mean was TJS 14,712.74 for extraterritorial organizations and TJS 8,186.51 for financial intermediation and insurance among ordinary service sectors.
max_salary_local_currency.notes: These are sectoral averages, not maximum salaries earned by individual workers; the field therefore preserves the distinction instead of treating a sectoral mean as a national ceiling.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official average monthly gross accrued wage and statutory monthly minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: May 2026 average; minimum effective from September 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe domestic employees and are unrelated to immigration eligibility. The official series reports arithmetic mean gross accrued wages and the statutory minimum; it does not publish a national median or individual maximum. USD conversions use the National Bank's 29 July 2026 rate of TJS 9.2448 per USD because an exact 15 August archived USD rate was not surfaced.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official statistics publish prices and price indices but not a current national monthly cost-of-living budget suitable for this field; a private crowd-sourced estimate was not substituted.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The independent eVisa is limited to a 45-day stay and is non-extendable. It is not residence and does not start the five-year permanent-residence citizenship clock.
settlement_track.summary: No regular remote-worker settlement route was confirmed. Work requires a Tajik inviter and contract, while commercial self-employment requires prior business permission, local formalities, and a work permit without a confirmed path to permanent residence.
settlement_track.notes: Although permanent residence exists in Tajik law, no official source established an independently accessible foreign-contract remote-work basis or conversion from the rejected visas.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-employer remote-work visa appears in the official visa categories. A work visa requires a Tajik inviter and labor or civil contract. The commercial/individual-entrepreneur alternative requires prior authorization to conduct business in Tajikistan, local registration documents and, for visa extension, work-permit formalities; neither the current registration law nor visa rules confirms that an ordinary foreign-client software contractor can self-sponsor or convert this status into qualifying residence.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit preserved the ineligible conclusion. Current official tax material clarifies that entrepreneur fixed payments depend on activity, locality and regime rather than a universal digital-nomad amount; current official wage tables publish arithmetic means and sectoral averages but no national median or individual maximum; and current visa and entrepreneur-registration materials still do not establish an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work or settlement route.

data.selection_summary: Tanzania has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. Class A is a self-employed foreign-investor route requiring a registered Tanzanian business, work authorization, licences, tax registration, assets and investment substance; Class B requires specific Tanzanian employment. Visitor and business visas are temporary and cannot substitute for residence authorization.

visa_application.title: Tanzania Online Residence Permit Portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct residence-permit portal. It does not offer a fitting remote-worker category; most applications are submitted through a Tanzanian institution, company or employer, while Class A requires an investor business.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence and Work Permit Class A — self-employed foreign investor

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No salary or foreign-remote-income threshold is published. Eligibility instead depends on a Tanzanian investment business and applicable capital rules.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly-income threshold is published in TZS.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income threshold; a registered Tanzanian investment business and applicable capital requirements apply
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an investor/entrepreneur permit, not an ordinary freelancer permit.

income_proof_months.notes: The official matrix does not express eligibility as a specified number of income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Class A work permit for a foreign investor who is self-employed.
Registered Tanzanian company or institution, application letter, work permit, passport and applicable professional or business licences.
Company assets, bank information where requested, TIN, tax clearance, business premises and physical verification may be required.
The immigration Class A investor matrix lists a USD 3,000 residence-permit fee for the general other-sector investor category; category and EAC fees differ.

initial_validity.value: Work permit normally 24 months
initial_validity.notes: The employment statute fixes the work-permit period at 24 months unless cancelled earlier; the exact residence-permit expiry must be checked on the grant.

extension_rules.value: Work permits may be renewed, normally up to eight total years; a high-value investor's total period may exceed ten years
extension_rules.notes: Renewal is discretionary and remains tied to the approved investment activity.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Class A can support a temporary residence permit after approval of the self-employed investment and work authorization
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This requires genuine Tanzanian investment/business substance.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic, time-based permanent-residence conversion for Class A was found in the inspected official materials.

path_to_citizenship.value: Lawful residence may eventually support discretionary naturalisation after the statutory residence periods, but the sources do not establish an automatic Class A-to-permanent-residence or Class A-to-citizenship conversion
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make Class A suitable for the specified ordinary foreign-contract remote worker.

rejected_routes.notes: Although information technology and consultancy can fall within Class A investment activities, the applicant must operate an eligible Tanzanian investment business. A foreign client contract by itself is insufficient, so the route is excluded under the selection rules.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence Permit Class B — specific Tanzanian employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-income threshold; a specific Tanzanian job and employer are required
income_requirement_display.notes: The route is employer-sponsored.

income_proof_months.notes: Eligibility is based on employment and qualifications rather than a published income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Specific employment by a specific Tanzanian employer.
Work permit, employer covering letter, academic certificates, CV, TIN and tax clearance.
Authorities must be satisfied that efforts were made to obtain a local expert.

initial_validity.value: Work permit normally 24 months

extension_rules.value: Renewable subject to approval, normally up to eight total years
extension_rules.notes: The permit remains tied to its authorized employer and occupation.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approved employment can support a temporary Class B residence permit

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic Class B permanent-residence transition was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Long lawful residence may contribute to a later discretionary naturalisation application, but no automatic employment-permit conversion is established

rejected_routes.notes: This route is rejected because a local employer and prior work authorization are mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-income threshold exists.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; evidence of a qualifying short assignment is required
income_requirement_display.notes: The business-visa fee is USD 250.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period is prescribed.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport, return ticket, USD 250 fee and a contract or proof of a qualifying assignment lasting no more than three months.
Permitted purposes are limited to recognized short-term professional or business tasks.

initial_validity.value: Single entry, maximum 90 days

extension_rules.value: It cannot be used instead of a residence permit; activity exceeding three months requires work and residence authorization

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence is granted
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate qualifying work/residence application is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This is visitor-like temporary permission.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from the business visa itself
path_to_citizenship.notes: The visa is not a qualifying settlement route.

rejected_routes.notes: A business visa is limited to short assignments and expressly cannot replace a residence permit. It is not permission to relocate indefinitely while performing ordinary remote work.

summary.value: A foreign national admitted to a registered Tanzanian institution may obtain a student visa or Student Pass without a local employer. This is temporary study status, requires institutional documentation, and no direct permanent-residence or independent degree-based skilled-migration route was found.
summary.notes: An existing software-engineering degree alone does not qualify the applicant for residence.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they have a permanent home in Tanzania and are present during the year, are present for at least 183 days in the year, or are present in the current and two preceding years for an average exceeding 122 days per year.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and the precise character of foreign-client income require individual analysis.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for resident individuals, not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: NSSF states a joint contribution of 20% of wages, normally 10% employee and 10% employer; the employee share must not exceed 10%. Applicability to a foreign-payroll worker without Tanzanian registration is not established, and no matching remote-work route exists.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer payment was confirmed. NSSF is wage-percentage based, and permit fees are transactional rather than monthly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remittance-basis or special foreign-remote-worker tax regime was found. A resident individual who has been resident for two years or less in their lifetime is subject to a special short-term-resident source limitation under the Income Tax Act.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The short-term-resident rule is not a digital-nomad incentive and does not create immigration eligibility.

taxes.caveats: Tax results depend on physical work location, whether receipts are employment or business income, residence duration, Tanzanian-source rules, business registration, available foreign-tax credits and any applicable treaty. Mainland and Zanzibar administration or rates can also differ.

taxation_system.value: Progressive resident-individual income tax with a 30% top marginal rate; non-resident and short-term-resident source rules differ.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home plus any presence, 183 days in a year, or an average exceeding 122 days in each of the current and preceding two years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Long-term residents are generally taxed on worldwide employment, business and investment income. Non-residents and qualifying short-term residents are generally limited to Tanzania-source income; services physically performed in Tanzania can be Tanzania-source.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad regime. Statutory presumptive business taxation may apply to eligible small businesses, but independent professional and technical-service classifications require careful verification.
taxation_system.social_security: NSSF covers private-sector employees, foreigners employed in Mainland Tanzania and self-employed persons. The standard joint contribution is 20% of wages, usually split 10%/10%.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate. The monthly brackets below are confirmed by a current professional tax summary and correspond to the annual thresholds in the official Income Tax Act.

tax_brackets.notes: Upper threshold converted at the Bank of Tanzania mean rate of TZS 2,645.2396 per USD on 15 August 2026.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over TZS 270,000 up to 520,000 per month
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over TZS 520,000 up to 760,000 per month
tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over TZS 520,000, after the fixed amount from lower bands
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over TZS 760,000 up to 1,000,000 per month
tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over TZS 760,000, after the fixed amount from lower bands
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess over TZS 1,000,000, after the fixed amount from lower bands
tax_brackets.notes: USD value is the approximate starting threshold.

taxation_system.notes: Current 2026 professional guidance confirms the statutory resident brackets. The official 2026 Finance Act was not available through a stable primary page in the inspected results, so filing advice should confirm that no later commencement provision changes the treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Tanzania has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker immigration route.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 30% progressive resident PIT; this is a screening rate, not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Residence can begin through a permanent-home test, 183 days, or the three-year average-presence test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Long-term residents generally have worldwide scope. Non-residents and qualifying short-term residents have source-limited scope, but work physically performed in Tanzania can be Tanzania-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: NSSF's standard joint contribution is 20% of wages where the Tanzanian system applies; no pure foreign-payroll exemption or fixed nomad contribution was confirmed.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment exists; structure-specific obligations remain
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based NSSF may apply to Tanzanian employment or self-employment; no universal monthly minimum was confirmed.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Business visa USD 250; Class A residence-permit fees vary by category and the general other-sector investor matrix lists USD 3,000. Work-permit and other registration fees may also apply.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business licensing, registration, tax-clearance and sector charges depend on the entity and activity; no ordinary remote-freelancer package was found.
fixed_payments.notes: These are not digital-nomad fees because the immigration category does not exist.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining under 183 days does not by itself guarantee no Tanzanian tax: permanent-home and average-presence tests may apply, and services performed in Tanzania can be Tanzania-source.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A long-term resident may face progressive tax up to 30% on worldwide income, subject to short-term-resident rules, credits and treaties. Immigration authorization remains a separate problem.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered investor business may face individual/business tax, NSSF, licensing and permit obligations. Independent professional or technical services should not be assumed to qualify for simplified presumptive treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This section is hypothetical tax screening because no qualifying digital-nomad route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No fitting ordinary remote-worker route reaches temporary residence. Investor and employer routes can obtain temporary permits but are rejected for this profile.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No general automatic permanent-residence transition for the rejected permit routes was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Citizenship Act bases ordinary naturalisation on residence rather than a captured permanent-residence holding period.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The statutory pattern requires residence throughout the final 12 months plus at least seven aggregate years during the preceding ten years. This is an eligibility minimum for discretionary naturalisation, not a timeline available through a fitting remote-worker route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Neither the current Citizenship Act nor the official application form publishes a typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Final 12 months of continuous residence; at least seven aggregate years in the preceding ten; adequate Kiswahili or English; good character; suitable past and potential national contribution; intention to reside permanently; oath of allegiance; and generally renunciation of other nationality.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalisation is ministerial and not automatic when the minimum conditions are met.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Act says a foreign woman married to a Tanzanian male citizen may apply at any time during the husband's lifetime; it sets no minimum marriage duration. This gender-specific provision does not accelerate the route for a foreign husband.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support the special naturalisation application only for a foreign woman married to a Tanzanian citizen man. A foreign male applicant married to a Tanzanian woman is not given the same statutory shortcut and would generally rely on ordinary naturalisation rules.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The rule is expressly gender-specific.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship is not automatic through marriage. The applicant must file the prescribed application and comply with nationality-renunciation and allegiance requirements. Fraud, false representation or concealment can lead to deprivation of naturalised citizenship.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage documents and relationship authenticity should be expected to receive scrutiny; sham arrangements create refusal, cancellation and possible criminal risks.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Section 5 of the current revised Citizenship Act grants citizenship to a person born in Tanzania on or after Union Day, subject only to narrow diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions. This primary law is broader than the Immigration Department's short administrative webpage, which says one parent must be Tanzanian; the current statute is used here.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Tanzania is ordinarily a citizen even when both parents are foreign migrants, unless the narrow diplomatic-immunity or enemy-occupation exception applies.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This conclusion follows the current revised Act rather than the conflicting abbreviated administrative webpage.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Tanzania is a citizen by birth; a child born abroad also acquires citizenship by descent where a parent is Tanzanian otherwise than solely by descent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Citizenship by descent can be limited where the Tanzanian parent is themselves a citizen only by descent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Tanzanian citizen child does not automatically naturalise either foreign parent or create a confirmed permanent-residence entitlement. Any family status must be applied for separately.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The inspected dependent-pass material does not establish an automatic parent-of-citizen settlement route.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically acquire residence, permanent residence or citizenship because his Tanzania-born child is a citizen. He needs an independent immigration basis and ordinarily remains subject to the general naturalisation rules.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No special accelerated citizenship provision for a foreign father was found.

rank.notes: Live Passport Index power rank checked on 15 August 2026.

visa_free_destinations.notes: The index separately reports visa-free destinations.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Live index value; eVisa-only destinations are treated separately by the index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Sum of 27 visa-on-arrival and 4 eTA destinations reported by the live index.

passport.notes: The live Passport Index mobility score was 73. Rankings and destination classifications can change frequently.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is used in business, higher education, secondary education and official correspondence, so English-only remote work is practical in major commercial centres. Swahili remains the dominant national and everyday language and is important for administration and integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Government sources describe Swahili as the national/official language and English as an official or recognized working language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official or general working-language role. Daily life and administration should be expected to require Swahili or English.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable evidence of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of TZS 689,730 at the Bank of Tanzania mean rate of TZS 2,645.2396 per USD on 15 August 2026.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No exact national median can be converted to USD. The June 2026 formal-sector report publishes averages and wage bands but contains no median table. The 2024 Mainland household-based income distribution places the median paid employee in the TZS 150,001–300,000 monthly band, but grouped data do not identify an exact median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the lowest captured sectoral monthly minimum, TZS 80,000 for one domestic-work category. This is a statutory minimum, not an observed national minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official formal-sector monthly average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No exact national median is published, so no USD conversion is supplied. The latest exact evidence is only a TZS 150,001–300,000 median band for Mainland paid employees in the 2024 household-based distribution.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national individual maximum salary is published, so no USD value is supplied. NBS formal-sector reports publish averages, while the household table has an open-ended top band; catalog maxima for older EES variables are establishment aggregates and explicitly are not population salary statistics.

min_salary_local_currency.value: TZS 80,000 per month in the lowest captured domestic-work category; TZS 175,000 for agriculture and unspecified private-sector activities
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Tanzania has sector- and activity-specific minimum wages effective 1 January 2026, not one uniform private-sector minimum.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2024/25 average monthly cash earnings across formal-sector employees.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The June 2026 EES analytical report publishes national averages and wage-rate bands but no national median, even though the NBS catalog metadata lists median monthly earnings among the survey topics. The 2024 Statistical Abstract gives grouped Mainland paid-employee counts: the cumulative distribution places the median in TZS 150,001–300,000 per month, but the exact median cannot be recovered from those grouped counts. Earlier ILFS, EES and abstract sources checked also do not publish a current exact national median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No current official source checked publishes a national maximum individual salary. The 2024 household table ends with an open-ended TZS 1,500,001-and-above band, and the 2024/25 EES reports national, sector and industry averages rather than the highest individual pay. The large maxima exposed for 2022/23 EES variables are establishment-level gross or annual cash-earnings aggregates; the catalog warns that case values cannot be treated as population summary statistics, so they are not a worker salary maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official formal-sector average monthly cash earnings; minimum field uses statutory sectoral minimum wages
average_citizen_salary.period: Formal-sector earnings as at 30 June 2025; minimum wages effective 1 January 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average remains the latest official formal-sector employee average, not an all-citizen salary. The focused median/max audit found that NBS publishes an exact average but only grouped employee-income distributions: the 2024 Mainland median lies in TZS 150,001–300,000, and the top band is open-ended at TZS 1,500,001 and above. Exact median and maximum values therefore remain null rather than being guessed.

cost_of_living_note.value: Tanzania's NBS reported annual headline CPI inflation of 4.0% for June 2026. This measures price change, not the absolute monthly cost of living, so it should not be treated as a household budget estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: No reliable official national monthly household-cost figure suitable for the dashboard was found.
