settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor and business visas are short-stay permissions and cannot substitute for a residence permit. Tanzania has no confirmed digital-nomad status.
settlement_track.summary: Only investor/business-substance, employer-sponsored, study and temporary visitor routes were confirmed. Ordinary naturalisation exists after lengthy qualifying residence, but the specified foreign-contract remote worker has no fitting independent route into that settlement track.
settlement_track.notes: Class A could lead to lawful residence for a genuine investor, but using it requires materially changing the applicant profile into a Tanzanian business investor.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign contract alone does not qualify. Rewarded work requires appropriate work authorization, Class A requires investor business substance, and Class B requires a Tanzanian employer.

data.notes: Thirty-seven distinct directly relevant URLs are retained, including thirteen new official NBS/OCGS labor-statistics URLs inspected in this focused unresolved-field pass. The current official sources establish only a median income band for Mainland paid employees and no national individual maximum; the two flagged local-currency values are therefore precise explained nulls. The negative remote-work selection conclusion remains unchanged and well supported.

data.selection_summary: Thailand supports ordinary foreign-contract remote work through the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), while qualifying high-income employees of substantial overseas companies may use the LTR Work-from-Thailand Professional visa. Neither is a confirmed citizenship route: DTV is temporary workcation status, and no official source reviewed confirms that DTV or LTR remote-worker time satisfies Thailand's permanent-residence prerequisites. Thailand therefore fits temporary remote living but not this citizenship-oriented selection.

visa_application.title: Thai e-Visa official application portal
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct application portal for DTV. Applicants must file through the embassy or consulate responsible for their place of residence, whose documentary and local-fee requirements may vary.

best_routes.route_name: LTR Visa — Work-from-Thailand Professional

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Standard threshold is USD 80,000 annually in each of the preceding two years. A USD 40,000 alternative requires a master's degree, qualifying intellectual property, or at least USD 1 million Series A funding.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 80,000/year, or USD 40,000/year with an additional qualifying credential
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official threshold is denominated in USD rather than THB.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 80,000/year (about USD 6,667/month); conditional alternative USD 40,000/year plus an additional qualifying credential
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 80,000/year for each of the previous two years
income_requirement_display.notes: The lower threshold is not generally available.

income_proof_months.notes: Income must be demonstrated for the preceding two years.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment or service relationship with an overseas listed company, or an overseas private company operating for at least three years with at least USD 50 million combined revenue over the previous three years.
Health insurance covering at least USD 50,000 in Thailand for at least ten months, qualifying Thai social security, or a USD 100,000 deposit held for twelve months.
Online BOI qualification endorsement; visa issuance must be completed within 60 days after endorsement.
Work-from-Thailand holders work remotely for an overseas employer and do not receive the ordinary Thai digital work permit for that foreign employment.

initial_validity.value: Five-year stay, extendable once for another five years, or limited by passport validity
initial_validity.notes: The advertised ten years comprises an initial five-year permission and a reassessed second five-year period.

extension_rules.value: A further five years is available after continued qualification is reassessed.
extension_rules.notes: Extension is not unconditional.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: LTR directly authorizes a long-term temporary stay for remote work for a qualifying overseas employer.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: PR is possible through a separately qualifying non-immigrant and PR category. Neither LTR Work-from-Thailand nor DTV alone is confirmed to satisfy the PR requirements while retaining ordinary foreign-only remote work.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The selected route is LTR Work-from-Thailand: it grants five-year stay blocks and no Thai work permit for foreign remote work. DTV separately grants 180-day stays plus one extension per entry; those are not the standard annual PR extensions. A qualifying successor may require local employment, investment or family eligibility. Nomad-time credit and exact change/exit procedure remain unconfirmed; three years refers to the qualifying successor.

path_to_citizenship.notes: General naturalization is possible after separately qualifying residence and domicile, but no official LTR-to-PR or LTR-to-citizenship bridge was established.

best_routes.notes: This independently applied route permits foreign-employer remote work but is restricted by high personal-income and overseas-employer tests. It is not valid for this selection because it is not an ordinary remote-worker route and its settlement bridge is unconfirmed.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: DTV uses financial-means evidence rather than a universal monthly-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: THB 500,000 financial means
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is a balance requirement, not monthly income.

income_requirement_display.value: THB 500,000 financial evidence; no universal monthly-income threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: The form of evidence, acceptable accounts, currency conversion and fee depend on the responsible mission.

income_proof_months.notes: Cairo expressly requires the qualifying balance for three consecutive months, while Fukuoka requests transaction statements for the last three months. Other missions may accept different evidence, including sponsorship.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign employment contract or certificate, or a professional portfolio/business registration demonstrating digital-nomad, remote-worker or freelancer status.
Financial evidence of at least THB 500,000 or the mission's local-currency equivalent.
Application through Thai e-Visa under the embassy or consulate responsible for the applicant's residence.

initial_validity.value: Five-year multiple-entry visa with up to 180 days per entry
initial_validity.notes: Five-year visa validity does not mean five years of continuous residence.

extension_rules.value: Each entry may be extended once for up to another 180 days; after 180 plus 180 days, the holder must leave and may re-enter while the visa remains valid.
extension_rules.notes: Extension and any change of visa category remain subject to Immigration Bureau discretion.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: DTV grants temporary workcation stays but not a permanent or settlement-oriented residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is visitor/workcation-like for settlement analysis.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No official rule confirms that DTV time meets the three-year PR prerequisite or converts to an eligible PR category.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No official source confirms a DTV-to-citizenship path.

rejected_routes.notes: DTV is the best ordinary foreign-contract remote-work fit but is temporary-only and fails the citizenship-oriented selection rule.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor entry followed by sole-proprietor or freelance registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold can be stated because no ordinary visitor-to-sole-proprietor or visitor-to-freelancer immigration route was established. The closest official in-country Non-B procedure is for working in a Thai company or limited partnership, not foreign-client freelancing.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Foreign-business licensing, company capital and immigration eligibility are separate matters; none of the checked official sources publishes a freelance-residence income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No ordinary visitor-to-self-employed residence threshold or route confirmed
income_requirement_display.notes: The official alternatives found concern licensed foreign business entities or work in a Thai company/limited partnership and do not create an independent foreign-client freelancer status.

income_proof_months.notes: Inapplicable: no qualifying visitor-to-freelancer immigration route exists for which an income-evidence period could be measured. The Foreign Business Act and DBD report address business permission, while the immigration materials address company/partnership employment and publish no income-proof-month rule for independent foreign-client freelancing.

key_requirements.requirement: Foreign-controlled service businesses may require permission under the Foreign Business Act; obtaining business permission does not itself grant immigration status or work authorization.
The official visitor/tourist-to-Non-B procedure reviewed is for working in a company or limited partnership and requires extensive Thai company documentation.

A subsequent business-necessity extension ordinarily requires non-immigrant status, qualifying salary, at least THB 2 million paid-up company capital, audited operations and four permanent Thai employees per foreign employee, subject to listed exceptions.

initial_validity.value: No immigration status is issued by freelance or foreign-business registration alone; the closest official in-country Non-B change for work in a company or limited partnership is granted for no more than 90 days.
initial_validity.notes: The 90-day Non-B company/partnership permission is a different, locally structured route and does not validate the rejected sole-proprietor or foreign-client freelancer scenario.

extension_rules.value: No extension exists for the rejected visitor-to-freelancer scenario. A business-necessity extension is a separate Thai-company route requiring non-immigrant status, qualifying salary, company capital, operating history and local employees.
extension_rules.notes: Registration or a foreign-business licence alone does not create an extendable residence status. Any company-based extension must be assessed under its own immigration and work-permit requirements.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Opening an account, registering or licensing a business, or holding a foreign contract does not by itself legalize residence or work. The identified Non-B alternative is tied to work in a Thai company or partnership.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate qualifying non-immigrant working/business status and three consecutive one-year extensions would be required before PR filing eligibility; visitor or registration time does not establish that status.

path_to_citizenship.notes: No direct path exists from visitor status, sole-proprietor registration or a foreign-business licence to citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: Thailand has no simple enter-as-visitor, register-as-freelancer and legalize-residence route for an ordinary foreign-client software engineer. Although visa-exempt visitors may apply for a different visa type while present, the official business conversion found is for work in a Thai company or limited partnership and therefore requires local business/employer substance.

summary.value: A Non-Immigrant ED visa is available for genuine study and requires an eligible educational purpose and supporting institution. It provides temporary study-related stay, not permanent residence, and is not a degree-based independent migration route for continued ordinary foreign remote work.
summary.notes: No direct PR or citizenship benefit was confirmed.

tax_residency_rule.value: A person staying in Thailand for periods aggregating more than 180 days in a calendar year is treated as tax resident.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and tie-breaker rules may change the final cross-border position.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not expected effective tax. Qualifying LTR Work-from-Thailand foreign income may be exempt.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No mandatory Thai social-security percentage was established for DTV or LTR Work-from-Thailand holders working solely for a foreign employer; local employment is a different payroll scenario.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory monthly state payment was established. Visa fees, insurance and extension charges are periodic or one-off.

special_tax_regimes.value: Royal Decree No. 743 exempts qualifying LTR Work-from-Thailand Professionals from Thai PIT on specified foreign-source income brought into Thailand. No comparable DTV exemption was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The 17% LTR rate concerns qualifying Thai employment income of Highly Skilled Professionals, not ordinary Work-from-Thailand foreign income.

taxes.caveats: Days present, income sourcing, remittance timing, contract form, permanent-establishment exposure, foreign tax credits, treaties and continued LTR qualification require individualized analysis.

taxation_system.value: Ordinary PIT is progressive from 0% through 35%. Residents are generally taxed on Thai-source income and foreign-source income brought into Thailand, subject to exemptions and treaties.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 aggregate days in a calendar year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Non-residents are taxed on Thai-source income; residents are taxed on Thai-source income and foreign-source income brought into Thailand, subject to exemptions and treaties.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Qualifying LTR Work-from-Thailand Professionals receive a statutory exemption for specified foreign-source income; DTV holders remain under ordinary rules.
taxation_system.social_security: No Thai payroll contribution was confirmed for the foreign-employer-only DTV or LTR scenario.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 35% is the top marginal rate; deductions and allowances can make effective tax materially lower.

tax_brackets.notes: Exempt band.
Top marginal band.

taxation_system.notes: Official tax materials support the residence rule, brackets, TIN and treaty principles, and LTR exemption.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: DTV holders have no identified nomad tax holiday and fall under ordinary Thai tax rules when applicable. Qualifying LTR Work-from-Thailand Professionals have a specific exemption for covered foreign-source income.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: DTV: ordinary progressive PIT; LTR Work-from-Thailand: special foreign-income exemption
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% on qualifying exempt foreign-source income for an eligible LTR Work-from-Thailand holder; otherwise progressive PIT up to 35%
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 180 aggregate days in a calendar year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are ordinarily liable on foreign-source income brought into Thailand; Royal Decree No. 743 exempts covered foreign income of qualifying LTR Work-from-Thailand Professionals.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: LTR Work-from-Thailand foreign-income exemption; no DTV-specific exemption identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No mandatory Thai payroll contribution was confirmed for foreign-employer-only remote work.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory monthly state payment confirmed.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Not established for foreign-employer-only DTV/LTR work; analyze local employment separately.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: LTR issuance in Thailand costs THB 50,000 per person. DTV fees are mission-specific; the reviewed missions publish £300, EUR 350 or EGP 18,000.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Local business activity may trigger licensing, TIN, withholding, VAT, work-permit and other compliance duties; amounts depend on the structure and were not treated as DTV monthly charges.
fixed_payments.notes: LTR insurance or deposit evidence is an immigration condition, not a monthly tax.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying 180 days or fewer avoids domestic tax residence, but Thai-source income and physically performed work still require analysis.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A DTV holder exceeding 180 days should screen remitted foreign income under progressive PIT up to 35%; a qualifying LTR holder may claim the statutory exemption.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A Thai business can trigger licensing, TIN, withholding, VAT and work-authorization duties. DTV does not create a local freelancer regime.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Broad rules and the LTR exemption are officially supported; sourcing and treaty outcomes remain fact-specific.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: DTV and LTR authorize temporary stay upon issuance or entry; neither is permanent residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Three years is only the earliest filing-eligibility interval after obtaining qualifying non-immigrant status and maintaining consecutive one-year extensions. It is not guaranteed time to PR: the applicant must fit an eligible category and quota, and approval is discretionary. No reviewed source confirms that DTV or LTR Work-from-Thailand time counts.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires at least five consecutive years of qualifying domicile, generally evidenced through residence and civil registration.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Eight years is an eligibility-floor model—three years of qualifying annual extensions before PR filing plus five years of qualifying domicile—not a typical completion time. It excludes discretionary PR consideration and naturalization processing and does not apply directly to DTV or LTR remote-worker status.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The DOPA service manual states 730 days for an ordinary foreigner's naturalization service, approximately 24 months. This is an administrative target, not guaranteed approval.

key_conditions.value: PR requires qualifying annual non-immigrant extensions, an eligible investment, working/business or humanitarian category, quota availability, income/assets, character, health and Thai-language assessment. Ordinary naturalization requires majority, good conduct, stable occupation, five years' qualifying domicile, Thai knowledge, residence/civil-registration evidence, income and tax evidence, a qualifying score and discretionary approval.
key_conditions.notes: The administrative manual also requests evidence concerning relinquishment of prior nationality; applicants should obtain nationality-specific advice about dual-nationality consequences.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: For a foreign husband of a Thai citizen, the current DOPA manual states three years of registered marriage, reduced to one year if the couple has a child. Other spouse categories have different periods.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Marriage to a Thai citizen can create a humanitarian PR basis. The Nationality Act provides sex-specific naturalization exceptions; a foreign husband of a Thai citizen is exempt from the ordinary five-year domicile and Thai-language conditions, subject to administrative requirements.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to another foreigner does not accelerate Thai citizenship. Citizenship remains discretionary, not automatic.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants need a legally valid and genuine marriage, civil-status proof, income and tax evidence where required, good conduct and interviews. Concealment, false statements or sham documentation can cause refusal, criminal consequences or later revocation.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Sex-specific eligibility and the current filing checklist should be confirmed before applying.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Thai law combines descent with conditional birthright citizenship. A Thailand-born child of alien parents is excluded where a relevant parent has only temporary permission or leniency, or lacks lawful status; diplomatic-type exceptions also apply.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Status-dependent. A child born to parents holding only temporary immigration permission normally does not acquire Thai nationality automatically. Other parental statuses and separate discretionary or anti-statelessness mechanisms require case-specific analysis.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A single boolean would be misleading because the parents' exact immigration status controls the result.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Thai mother or father acquires Thai nationality by descent whether born in or outside Thailand, subject to proof of parentage.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Prescribed parentage proof may be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Thai-citizen child can support a foreign parent's humanitarian PR category and reduce some naturalization income screening, but gives the parent neither PR nor citizenship automatically.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Residence, documentation, income, conduct and discretionary requirements remain.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Thai, the child is Thai by descent. The foreign father may use the documented parent-child relationship in a humanitarian PR or later naturalization application but receives no automatic status.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parentage and the genuine family relationship must be documented.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026; Passport Index 2026 for category breakdown

rank.notes: Live Henley ranking observed on the research date; rankings change periodically.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score includes destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance and is broader than strict visa-free access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index uses a different destination universe and methodology from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reports 48 visa-on-arrival and five eTA destinations; it separately reports 40 strictly visa-free destinations.

passport.notes: Do not treat the Henley access score and Passport Index category counts as methodologically identical.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable in international companies and major tourist or business centres but unreliable for all government, healthcare, banking, landlord and local-service interactions. Thailand ranked 116th of 123 jurisdictions with very low proficiency in EF EPI 2025.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI uses self-selected adult test takers and is a practical indicator rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian may be encountered in some tourism areas, but neither Russian nor Ukrainian is official or dependable for nationwide administration and daily life. Thai is primary, with English the more useful international fallback.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No authoritative nationwide measure of Russian or Ukrainian service availability was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of THB 15,565 at roughly THB 33.2/USD; exchange rates fluctuate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Current NSO releases checked publish arithmetic means and employee counts within broad wage bands, not an exact national median monthly employee wage. A grouped-band interpolation would be researcher-generated, so no USD median is supplied.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 26-day equivalent of the lowest THB 337 daily minimum; this is a statutory floor, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of THB 15,565 per month.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current NSO publications report means, subgroup averages and broad wage-band counts, but no exact current national all-employee median. No unsupported interpolation is used.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A meaningful national maximum salary is not published; the highest minimum-wage region is not a maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.value: THB 337–400 per day, depending on province, district and covered sector
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Rates effective 1 July 2025.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official 2025 employee average; the table reports THB 14,273 for private employees and THB 21,071 for government employees.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed current NSO sources do not publish a named national median monthly wage for all employees. Broad bands identify only a median band, not an exact THB value.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Official average monthly employee wage and statutory daily minimum; gross/net treatment is not explicitly established in the cited summary table.
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average citizen or resident employee and statutory-minimum benchmarks, not remote-visa thresholds. USD amounts are approximate and rounded.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2025 Statistical Yearbook reports average household expenditure of approximately THB 23,695 per month, with substantial regional and household-size differences.
cost_of_living_note.notes: This household statistic is not a single-person digital-nomad budget.

settlement_track.summary: Thailand has genuine remote-work visas but no confirmed remote-worker-to-PR bridge. DTV is temporary workcation status and LTR is high-threshold; neither can be ranked as a citizenship path.
settlement_track.notes: General PR and naturalization may become possible after switching to and maintaining separately qualifying status, but that is not citizenship from the remote-work route itself.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: DTV expressly covers digital nomads, remote workers and freelancers with foreign-employer evidence, business registration or a professional portfolio. This is a temporary-living fit, not a settlement match.

data.notes: This focused unexplained-null audit inspected more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including over five official URLs absent from the previous source set. For the rejected visitor-to-freelancer scenario, no income-proof period exists because no such immigration route was established; the closest official in-country Non-B procedure is limited to company or partnership work for up to 90 days, and its business extension requires substantial local-company substance.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Qualifying non-immigrant working/business or other eligible PR category
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: PR is possible through a separately qualifying non-immigrant and PR category. Neither LTR Work-from-Thailand nor DTV alone is confirmed to satisfy the PR requirements while retaining ordinary foreign-only remote work.
requirements: Meet an eligible PR category, such as working/business, investment or qualifying family grounds.
Standard guidance requires at least three consecutive years of one-year extensions on non-immigrant status before applying.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The selected route is LTR Work-from-Thailand: it grants five-year stay blocks and no Thai work permit for foreign remote work. DTV separately grants 180-day stays plus one extension per entry; those are not the standard annual PR extensions. A qualifying successor may require local employment, investment or family eligibility. Nomad-time credit and exact change/exit procedure remain unconfirmed; three years refers to the qualifying successor.

Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) — Workcation

data.selection_summary: No dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker route was found. The closest option is the Visa to Establish Residence for professional activity, which leads to a two-year temporary residence permit and can eventually lead to permanent residence and citizenship. However, approval is tied to Timor-Leste's skilled-labour, technology-transfer, local job-creation and training objectives, and current official sources do not confirm that ordinary software work performed only for a foreign client qualifies. Tourist status expressly prohibits professional activity, and the work and business visas are not qualifying remote-work settlement routes.

visa_application.title: Visa Application Form and Required Documents
visa_application.notes: This is the official downloadable form covering work, business and residence-establishment visas, not an online filing portal. Applications are lodged through the competent Timorese diplomatic or consular post or migration authority; the law states a 30-working-day decision period for a residence-establishment visa.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visa to Establish Residence — Professional Activity (VFR1)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The law requires adequate means of subsistence but publishes no universal monetary threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed amount published; Timor-Leste uses the US dollar
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Applicants must document adequate subsistence and accommodation.

income_requirement_display.value: Adequate means of subsistence; no fixed threshold published
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: USD is Timor-Leste's official currency, but no amount is specified
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No statutory monthly amount is published for VFR1
income_requirement_display.notes: The application form requests documentary proof of subsistence without defining an amount or income-history period.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard number of bank-statement or income-proof months is stated in the official form.

key_requirements.requirement: Intention to stay permanently, adequate subsistence and accommodation, valid travel document and clean criminal record.
Professional qualifications and documents supporting the purpose and conditions of stay.
Professional activity must support skilled-labour needs, productivity and technology transfer; local job creation and training are also approval criteria.
Periodic government resolutions may limit the number admitted and economic sectors in which applicants may work.

initial_validity.value: 90-day multiple-entry visa, followed by a two-year temporary residence permit if approved
initial_validity.notes: The visa permits entry to apply for temporary—not permanent—residence.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence is renewable for successive two-year periods; renewal must be requested at least 30 days before expiry
extension_rules.notes: Renewal considers continued eligibility, subsistence, housing, criminal history and compliance with immigration, labour, tax and corporate law.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The VFR1 permits entry for 90 days to apply for a two-year temporary residence permit for professional activity.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Residence approval remains discretionary and depends on the professional-activity criteria.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Permanent residence may be requested after at least six years holding temporary residence, or after ten consecutive years as a legal resident, subject to subsistence, accommodation, criminal-record and positive-contribution conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Permanent residence is not granted directly by the entry visa.

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinary naturalisation may be requested after at least ten years of usual and regular residence, with official-language, integration, subsistence, history and culture requirements.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary and residence under a qualifying permit must remain usual and regular.

rejected_routes.notes: This is settlement-oriented and can be applied for personally without an express statutory requirement for a local employer. It nevertheless does not fit ordinary foreign-contract remote work: current law evaluates professional applications against domestic skilled-labour, productivity, technology-transfer, local-job and training objectives. Focused searches of current immigration pages, legislation and the official gazette did not locate a digital-nomad rule or a current resolution expressly admitting foreign-client-only software work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker or general Work Visa income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed amount published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Means of support and evidence of the authorized professional activity are required.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No fixed amount: Article 15's USD 100 per entry plus USD 50 per day formula applies only to transit, tourist and Business Class I visas, not to the Work Visa
income_requirement_display.notes: The current Immigration and Asylum Act requires sufficient means of subsistence but publishes no monetary formula for a Work Visa. The official visa form requests supporting evidence without specifying an amount or number of months.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Employment contract or service-provision arrangement supporting the specific authorized activity.
Passport, accommodation, means of support, qualifications and documentation supporting the proposed work.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year, with multiple entries

extension_rules.value: Renewable for equal periods
extension_rules.notes: The holder may perform only the professional activity on which approval was based.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence permit is granted; this is a renewable work visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No confirmed conversion from an ordinary work visa to permanent residence was found; the residence-establishment visa is the statutory residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path was confirmed from work-visa status alone.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship requires usual and regular residence; the sources do not establish that work-visa time alone qualifies.

rejected_routes.notes: The visa covers employment contracts and provision of services, but it is activity-specific, temporary and not presented as a digital-nomad or foreign-employer remote-work settlement route. Whether a foreign-client service contract can support it requires case-specific confirmation, and no conversion to qualifying residence was established.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No salary or monthly income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed salary threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Business registration, economic-activity authorization and means of support are required.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold; local commercial registration is required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: No fixed amount: Article 15's USD 100 per entry plus USD 50 per day formula applies to Business Class I, not Business Class II; Class II requires means of support without a published amount
income_requirement_display.notes: The current Act limits the stated visitor-funds formula to Business Class I. The official Class II page instead requires means of subsistence, company registration and economic-activity authorization but gives no minimum amount or income-history period.

income_proof_months.notes: No standard income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Membership or management role in a commercial company registered or to be registered in Timor-Leste.
Commercial registration, authorization for economic activity, tax-compliance certificate, accommodation, medical certificate and criminal record.
For extension, effective company registration, continuing legal compliance and presence for at least 183 days per year.

initial_validity.value: Six months, multiple entry
initial_validity.notes: Official issuance fee is USD 150.

extension_rules.value: Extendable for periods of two years
extension_rules.notes: Official extension fee is USD 150 and continued local business compliance is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence permit is stated; the status remains a business visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A separate qualifying residence permit would be required.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct citizenship path is confirmed from the business visa itself.

rejected_routes.notes: This route requires a locally registered commercial company and active business role. It does not fit an ordinary software engineer continuing only a foreign employment or client contract.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Visitor funds are an entry requirement, not a remote-work income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 100 per entry plus USD 50 per intended day of stay
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is proof of visitor funds.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 100 per entry plus USD 50 per intended day
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 100 + USD 50 for each day of intended stay
income_requirement_display.notes: This is not an immigration income threshold and does not authorize work.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-history period applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Passport, accommodation, onward or return travel and sufficient visitor funds.

initial_validity.value: Up to 90 days in total

extension_rules.value: Extensions are limited to the statutory maximum total tourist stay
extension_rules.notes: Published extension fees are USD 35 for up to 30 days and USD 75 for 30–60 days on the official visitor information page.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed; tourist status is not residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from tourist status.

rejected_routes.notes: The 2017 migration law expressly prohibits tourist-visa holders from carrying on professional activity. It cannot be used for remote work or a citizenship-oriented residence path.

summary.value: No separate degree-based or independently points-tested residence route was found. Professional qualifications support VFR1, but approval remains tied to domestic skilled-labour, technology-transfer, local-job and training objectives and does not follow automatically from holding a software degree.
summary.notes: The applicant's degree is useful evidence but does not independently establish eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident when present in Timor-Leste for 183 days or more in any 12-month period beginning or ending during the tax year, unless the person's permanent place of abode is outside Timor-Leste.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Government employees posted abroad are also treated as residents under the statutory rule.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal/screening rate. Resident annual taxable income is taxed at 0% through USD 6,000 and 10% above it; resident monthly wages are taxed at 0% through USD 500 and 10% on the excess. Non-resident wages and non-resident natural-person taxable income are generally taxed at 10%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For employees, the total is 10% of the contribution base: 4% employee and 6% employer. Foreign self-employed persons may voluntarily enroll and pay 10% of a selected contribution band. A temporary foreign employee may seek exemption with evidence of active mandatory foreign coverage.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment is published. Employee contributions are percentage-based, while optional self-employed contributions are 10% of a selected contribution band.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad, remote-worker or inbound-expatriate personal tax regime was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary wage or business-income rules apply according to the legal characterization of the arrangement.

taxes.caveats: A foreign employee physically performing services in Timor-Leste may have Timor-Leste employment income even when the payer is abroad. A resident person's non-wage gross income includes worldwide sources, with a foreign-tax credit subject to statutory limits. Classification as wages, independent business income or foreign-source income, the foreign employer's withholding obligations, social-security coverage and treaty relief require professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Resident natural persons are generally subject to 0% on the first USD 6,000 of annual taxable income and 10% above that amount. The corresponding resident wage bands are USD 0–500 monthly at 0% and the excess at 10%. Residents' non-wage gross income includes domestic and foreign sources, while non-residents generally include only Timor-Leste-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183 days in any relevant 12-month period, subject to the permanent-place-of-abode exception.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident non-wage gross income includes worldwide sources; non-residents include Timor-Leste-source income. Wage tax covers services performed in Timor-Leste. Foreign tax credits may be available to residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or remote-worker concession was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Employees, including foreign nationals under covered employment contracts: 4% employee plus 6% employer. Foreign self-employed persons may voluntarily pay 10% of a selected contribution band. Temporary foreign employees may request exemption with proof of active mandatory foreign coverage.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 10% is the top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Income within the USD 6,000 annual or USD 500 monthly resident allowance is taxed at 0%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: USD 0–6,000 annual taxable income for a resident natural person
tax_brackets.notes: Equivalent resident wage allowance is USD 0–500 per month.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident natural person, marginal rate on the excess
tax_brackets.notes: Resident wages use 10% on the monthly amount above USD 500.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Non-resident natural-person taxable income and non-resident wages
tax_brackets.notes: The exact source and withholding treatment depends on income classification.

taxation_system.notes: The rates are supported by current Tax Authority and Social Security pages and the Taxes and Duties Act. The applicant's precise category remains fact-dependent because no dedicated remote-worker immigration or tax status exists.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Timor-Leste has no confirmed digital-nomad route or special nomad tax regime. If a person independently obtains qualifying residence, ordinary resident wage or business-income rules apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; hypothetical foreign employee or resident individual business operator
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Top marginal rate 10%; resident allowance USD 6,000 annually or USD 500 monthly for wages
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally 183 days in a relevant 12-month period, subject to the permanent-place-of-abode exception.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A resident person's non-wage gross income includes worldwide sources. Wage income is taxed where employment services are performed in Timor-Leste. A foreign-tax credit may apply to foreign-source income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Foreign nationals who are employees under Timor-Leste labour contracts are included in mandatory employee registration: 4% is withheld from gross contributory remuneration and the employer pays another 6%, registers the employee and files monthly remuneration statements. A temporarily assigned foreign employee may request exemption by documenting active mandatory foreign social-security coverage and renewing that evidence annually. Foreign self-employed persons may instead join voluntarily and pay 10% of a selected contribution band. The official materials do not state how an ordinary remote employee of an overseas employer with no registered Timor-Leste payroll must register, so that scenario requires an INSS ruling.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly tax or contribution applies
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Local employee treatment: 4% employee plus 6% employer on the contribution base, paid monthly by the employer. Foreign self-employed optional coverage: 10% of a selected contribution band. Temporarily assigned foreign employees may seek exemption with annual proof of active foreign mandatory coverage.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Residence-establishment visa USD 50; temporary residence permit USD 100; permanent residence permit USD 150 under the 2017 law. These are one-time issuance fees, not monthly payments.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business registration, sales/service taxes or other transaction charges depend on local activity; no nomad-specific fixed charge was found.
fixed_payments.notes: The unresolved point is not the published rates but which registration workflow INSS will apply to a foreign-company remote employee with no Timor-Leste payroll. Current employee, temporary-assignment and voluntary-self-employment materials do not expressly address that structure. No mandatory private health-insurance premium or fixed freelancer tax for this scenario was published.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Non-residence does not automatically eliminate Timor-Leste tax: wages for services physically performed in Timor-Leste and other Timor-Leste-source income may remain taxable, commonly at 10%.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Resident wage income is generally 0% through USD 500 per month and 10% on the excess; a foreign employer's local withholding, payroll and social-security registration position requires advice or a ruling.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A resident individual operating a business must register to operate and file under ordinary income-tax rules; annual taxable income is 0% through USD 6,000 and 10% above it, subject to deductions and income classification. Social-security enrollment is optional for foreign self-employed persons and costs 10% of a selected contribution band if elected.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Income-tax rates and the main employee/self-employed contribution rules are well supported. Confidence is lower for the precise foreign-company remote-worker treatment because no immigration route defines a digital nomad and the published payroll workflows do not expressly address an overseas employer with no Timor-Leste registration.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The residence-establishment visa is valid for 90 days and the law gives a 30-working-day visa decision target, but no reliable end-to-end residence-permit processing time is published.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Permanent residence may be granted after at least six years holding temporary residence, alternatively after ten consecutive years as a legal resident, subject to all other conditions.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: This is an illustrative minimum based on permanent residence after six years and ordinary naturalisation after ten total years. Citizenship law does not require four years of permanent residence as a separate rule.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: At least ten years of usual and regular residence is required for ordinary naturalisation; approval is discretionary.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The citizenship law, government guidance and implementation material reviewed do not publish a typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Adult status; at least ten years of usual and regular residence; ability to speak Tetum or Portuguese; moral and civic integration; ability to support oneself; knowledge of Timor-Leste's history and culture. Residence permits require continued lawful status, accommodation, subsistence, compliance and restricted absences.
key_conditions.notes: Temporary residence may be cancelled after six consecutive months abroad or ten non-consecutive months within two years. The citizenship law does not impose automatic renunciation of another citizenship, although conflicts of nationality require individual legal review.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship by marriage requires more than five years of marriage, at least two years of residence in Timor-Leste and ability to speak an official language. Permanent-residence law separately includes foreign spouses married to a citizen for more than five years.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A marriage entered before migration can count toward the more-than-five-year duration because the law tests the duration on the application date; at least two years of Timor-Leste residence is still required for citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The sources do not require all five marriage years to have occurred in Timor-Leste.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must request citizenship, prove the marriage and residence periods, and speak Tetum or Portuguese. A marriage entered solely to obtain residence is grounds for residence cancellation and marriage of convenience is criminalized under migration law.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Authorities may investigate whether the relationship is genuine; sham arrangements carry immigration and criminal risk.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Timor-Leste is an original citizen if a parent was born in Timor-Leste, or if the parents are unknown, stateless or of unknown citizenship. A locally born child of other foreign parents may declare a wish to become Timorese after age 17; citizenship is not automatic at birth in that case.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: If neither migrant parent is Timorese or was born in Timor-Leste, their child does not automatically acquire citizenship merely by birth in the country. The locally born child may declare a wish to become Timorese after turning 17; anti-statelessness rules apply where relevant.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A different result applies if one foreign parent was itself born in Timor-Leste.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of a Timorese mother or father is an original citizen, including when born abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Birth registration and proof of parentage remain practically necessary.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a minor Timorese citizen can benefit from a waiver of the residence-establishment visa under the amended migration law, but must still secure the appropriate residence authorization. The citizen child's status does not automatically naturalise the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Family-residence eligibility and documentary requirements must be handled separately.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father whose child is Timorese may use the family-residence provisions and residence-visa waiver applicable to parents of minor Timorese citizens. He does not automatically receive permanent residence or citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: He must prove legal parentage and satisfy the applicable residence process.

rank.notes: Live Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15; index values can change during the year.

visa_free_destinations.notes: This is the index's strictly visa-free category, not its broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The live index separately classifies eVisa destinations; its displayed visa-required count is reproduced here.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Calculated from 43 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations shown by the same index.

passport.notes: The index displayed a mobility score of 102. This breakdown is used instead of combining visa-free and visa-on-arrival access into a Henley-style access score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is constitutionally recognized as a working language in the civil service alongside Indonesian for as long as necessary, so it has practical institutional use. It is not an official language, and Tetum or Portuguese remains important for government procedures, integration and citizenship.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English-only remote work may be workable in parts of Dili and international organizations, but nationwide fluency and service availability were not established by a reliable current source.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official or recognized working-language status, and no reliable evidence of broad practical use was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Applicants should plan to use Tetum, Portuguese, English or Indonesian rather than rely on Russian or Ukrainian.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Average monthly wage of salaried employees in their main job in the 2021 Labour Force Survey.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The full survey's national earnings tables publish arithmetic averages but no national median; the official summary also reports an average only, and the ILO metadata publishes source variables rather than a weighted median estimate.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statutory national minimum wage used in the Social Security authority's current examples; it is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Official-survey average monthly wage of salaried employees in the main job.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The 2021 Labour Force Survey's national earnings tables publish arithmetic averages by sex, activity, occupation and region, but not a national median monthly wage. The official summary likewise reports an average only, and the ILO survey metadata identifies underlying wage variables without publishing a weighted national median. No median was calculated from microdata because an official estimate would require survey weights and documented treatment of missing values and outliers.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Neither the official full report nor its summary publishes a national maximum individual monthly salary. High subgroup averages are not individual maxima, and no raw-survey extreme was substituted for a nationally meaningful maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Timor-Leste uses the US dollar, so no currency conversion is required.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Timor-Leste uses USD, but the reviewed official full report and summary do not publish a national median monthly wage in USD or any other currency. The ILO survey metadata exposes source wage questions, not an official median aggregate.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Neither the official full report nor its summary publishes a national maximum individual monthly salary. The reports contain subgroup averages, which are not maxima; an observed top-coded or outlier survey response would not be a meaningful national salary maximum.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly gross wages in the main job of salaried employees; minimum field is the statutory national minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.period: 2021 Labour Force Survey; minimum-wage amount confirmed on the current Social Security page accessed 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe resident workers, not an immigration income threshold. The 2021 full Labour Force Survey reports USD 248 average monthly wages for salaried employees in their main job and USD 142 average monthly main-job income for self-employed workers; its separate summary gives USD 252.2 under a slightly different summary presentation. The full-report figure is retained for internal consistency with its detailed table. No official national median or maximum is published in the full report, summary or ILO survey metadata.

cost_of_living_note.value: Official sources show that aggregate consumer-price pressure was low recently: World Bank data report 0.4% annual consumer-price inflation for 2025, while the Central Bank displayed -0.1% inflation for April 2026. The official CPI basket assigns 54.1% to food and non-alcoholic beverages and 6.3% to housing, indicating that food-price changes have an unusually large household-budget effect. These indicators measure price movements, not the absolute monthly cost of living, and no current official national or Dili monthly household budget was found.
cost_of_living_note.notes: INETL's February 2025 bulletin reported the all-groups CPI down 0.2% year on year and explicitly defines CPI as the change in the cost of a representative household basket. The Central Bank confirms that the current basket weights still derive from the 2014–2015 Living Standards Survey. A 2024 TLSLS-4 survey was intended to update household consumption and the CPI weights, but focused searches did not locate an official published TLSLS-4 expenditure table or authoritative monthly cost benchmark as of 2026-08-15. Therefore no crowd-sourced expatriate budget or inferred monthly amount is supplied.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: No digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker status exists. Visitor status expressly prohibits professional activity, and citizenship would require separately qualifying under the professional residence system.
settlement_track.summary: Timor-Leste has a genuine residence-to-permanent-residence-to-citizenship framework, but the professional route is designed around domestic skilled-labour, technology-transfer, job-creation and training objectives. Current official sources do not confirm eligibility for a software engineer who only continues ordinary work for a foreign employer or client, so the country is not a valid remote-work citizenship track.
settlement_track.notes: VFR1 is a 90-day entry visa leading first to a two-year temporary residence permit; permanent residence generally follows six years of temporary residence or ten years of legal residence. That settlement framework does not establish that ordinary foreign-client-only remote work qualifies for VFR1.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker route was found. VFR1 does not expressly require a local employer but applies domestic economic-benefit criteria incompatible with assuming that ordinary foreign-client-only software work qualifies. Tourist work is prohibited, while the business route requires a local commercial company.

data.notes: Thirty-eight distinct directly relevant canonical URLs were retained, including six focused cost-of-living and price-statistics sources not in the previous source set. Current primary government, official-gazette, tax-authority, social-security and statistics materials were prioritized. The flagged cost-of-living gap is resolved with official CPI and basket evidence while explicitly distinguishing price inflation from an absolute monthly budget. No authoritative current monthly national or Dili household-cost benchmark was found. Confidence remains medium because no current official rule confirms ordinary foreign-client-only software work under VFR1, and INSS materials do not expressly classify a remote employee of an overseas employer with no Timor-Leste payroll.

data.selection_summary: Togo publishes a self-employed-foreigner residence-card category and permits naturalisation after five years of habitual residence. However, first-time eligibility is procedurally circular: residence requires an enterprise card and tax/social clearances, while individual-enterprise registration requires a non-ECOWAS foreigner to hold a Togolese residence title. Written DGDN/CFE confirmation that initial registration and exclusively foreign-client revenue are accepted is needed.

visa_application.title: Demande de carte de séjour
visa_application.notes: Official online residence-card application. The applicant completes and pays online, then submits the printed form and evidence to DGDN. Self-employed first-filing eligibility still requires DGDN/CFE confirmation.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The procedure requires sufficient financial resources but publishes no numerical minimum.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Sufficient resources; no fixed XOF threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A bank or comparable financial-resource record is required.

income_requirement_display.value: Proof of sufficient resources; no published minimum
income_requirement_display.notes: Neither a monthly minimum nor a required bank balance is published.

income_proof_months.notes: The procedure does not specify a required number of months of financial history.

key_requirements.requirement: Online form, qualifying passport, photograph, recent criminal-record evidence, medical certificate and proof of sufficient resources.
Self-employed applicants additionally need an enterprise-creation card and enterprise, personal-tax and social-security clearances.
Non-ECOWAS individual-enterprise registration costs XOF 30,400 and lists a residence title among its requirements.
Obtain written confirmation that a first-time non-ECOWAS applicant can overcome the residence-title/enterprise-card circularity and serve exclusively foreign clients.

initial_validity.value: One-year temporary residence card
initial_validity.notes: The current page lists a XOF 200,000 non-student fee and 30–45 day indicated processing time.

extension_rules.value: Renewable temporary residence; after at least three years, an ordinary three-year residence card may be requested. A privileged category is available after more than 12 years, although current pages conflict on whether that card lasts five or ten years.
extension_rules.notes: The ordinary category is residence without intended time limitation, but its physical card remains renewable rather than being a separately named permanent-residence permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Approval directly grants temporary residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The self-employed prerequisites must already be satisfied.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least three years, an immigrant intending residence without time limitation may request the renewable three-year ordinary residence card.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No separately named permanent-residence permit was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation may be requested after five years of habitual residence immediately preceding the application.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalisation is discretionary and requires principal interests in Togo and renunciation of the former nationality.

best_routes.notes: Potentially residence-oriented self-employment, not a digital-nomad visa. No local employer or stated capital minimum is published, but first-time registration sequencing and acceptance of foreign-client-only software revenue remain unresolved.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker threshold applies to ordinary entry permission.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.notes: The visa page creates neither residence nor remote-work rights.

income_proof_months.notes: Not stated.

initial_validity.value: One to 90 days
initial_validity.notes: Maximum validity stated by the general visa procedure.

extension_rules.notes: No settlement-oriented extension is published.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A visa is entry/stay permission, not a residence card.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No direct path.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time alone is not established as qualifying residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because ordinary visitor permission is not a remote-worker residence or citizenship route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No route-specific minimum salary is stated.

income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility rests on local invitation/employment documents.

key_requirements.requirement: A Togo-based company, NGO or person initiates work-entry authorization; salaried residence applicants need hiring authorization, a contract and employer documentation.

initial_validity.notes: The work-entry page does not state validity.

extension_rules.notes: No extension rule was established.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A qualifying employee may subsequently apply for a residence card.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Local employment documents are required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Ordinary residence may become available after three years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not remove the local-employer requirement.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may be requested after five years of habitual residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Not valid for the requested independent profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires local invitation or employment and cannot be used independently.

summary.value: An enrolled foreign student may independently request a one-year student residence card; a foreign university degree alone does not create an independent skilled-residence route.
summary.notes: Education residence does not fit an already-qualified engineer continuing ordinary foreign-contract work.

tax_residency_rule.value: Fiscal domicile arises if Togo is the home or principal stay, place of non-accessory employment or self-employment, or centre of economic interests. The statute does not use a simple 183-day threshold.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breaker rules may override domestic domicile.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Self-employed business-income screening rate, not expected effective tax. TPU or another classification may apply.

social_contributions_percent.notes: CNSS currently states 21.5% of declared self-employed income; the 2026 ISSA profile reports 16.5%, requiring written CNSS confirmation.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly payment was established; contributions are income-based and tax depends on classification and turnover.

special_tax_regimes.value: The TPU synthetic regime covers qualifying individual enterprises with turnover up to XOF 60 million and can replace several ordinary taxes. Covered registered enterprises receive a 24-month TPU exemption; BNC/professional and import/export activities are excluded.
special_tax_regimes.notes: OTR must confirm whether software services are ordinary services or excluded BNC.

taxes.caveats: Working from or establishing a home in Togo may create fiscal domicile without 183 days. Residents are potentially taxable on worldwide income, subject to treaties. IRPP, TPU/BNC classification, VAT, withholding, CNSS and foreign credits require professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Mixed: residents generally face worldwide taxation. Relevant Article 74 income is progressive to 35%; self-employed business income generally uses 30%; eligible small individual enterprises may use TPU.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Home/principal stay, non-accessory professional activity or centre of economic interests; no standalone 183-day rule.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: Togolese and foreign-source income, subject to treaties. Non-residents: Togolese-source income and applicable statutory minimum rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: TPU turnover ceiling XOF 60 million; declarative service rate 8% for the XOF 30–60 million band, XOF 20,000 annual minimum, and 24-month exemption for covered newly registered enterprises. BNC and import/export are excluded.
taxation_system.social_security: CNSS states 21.5% of declared income for formal self-employed workers.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The progressive schedule is not the ordinary freelancer schedule; 35% is a top marginal screening rate.

tax_brackets.notes: Exempt band.
Top marginal rate, not effective tax or the separate business-income rate.

taxation_system.notes: Official tax code is authoritative; software classification and the CNSS/ISSA conflict require confirmation.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax regime exists; a possible self-employed resident uses ordinary individual-enterprise, income-tax and social-security rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Potential self-employed individual enterprise; OTR must confirm business-income, BNC or TPU classification.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 30% business-income screening rate; eligible TPU services may instead face turnover tax. The 35% rate is the Article 74 top marginal rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile can arise through home/principal stay, work or centre of economic interests; no general 183-day safe harbor.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Fiscal residents are potentially taxable on Togolese and foreign-source income, subject to treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: CNSS states 21.5% of declared self-employed income; ISSA reports 16.5%, so written assessment is needed.

fixed_payments.status: Variable rather than universally fixed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Income-based; no universal monthly minimum was identified.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Temporary card XOF 200,000; ordinary three-year card XOF 500,000; privileged card XOF 800,000; non-ECOWAS enterprise creation XOF 30,400.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Potential TPU annual minimum XOF 20,000; covered new enterprises receive a 24-month exemption.
fixed_payments.notes: Residence fees are subject to regulatory change; TPU applicability is unresolved.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No published day count safely prevents residence; home or regular work may independently create domicile.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide income may be taxable; revenue may face 30% business IRPP or qualifying TPU plus CNSS.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Register through CFE, obtain tax/CNSS identifiers and confirm OTR classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: No remote-worker exemption was identified.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Direct upon approval; portal estimate is 30–45 days.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Ordinary residence becomes available after three years, but remains a renewable card.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Difference between the three-year ordinary-card point and five-year naturalisation minimum; the law does not require holding that card for two years.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Minimum habitual residence before discretionary naturalisation.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The naturalisation procedure publishes no processing time; the certificate procedure's two months concerns proof of existing nationality.

key_conditions.value: Age 21; five immediately preceding years of habitual residence; principal interests in Togo; good character, qualifying criminal record, medical fitness, assimilation including sufficient knowledge of a Togolese language, and renunciation of former nationality.
key_conditions.notes: No standardized language level or precise absence allowance is published.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No minimum marriage duration is stated for privileged residence. Automatic marriage nationality applies to a foreign wife of a Togolese man, not a migrant husband.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage to a Togolese woman may support a foreign husband's privileged residence card without stated prior residence, but not automatic nationality. A foreign wife married to a Togolese man has a published marriage-nationality procedure.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The published nationality rules are gender-asymmetric.

requirements_and_risks.value: Marriage must be valid and documented. Applications can be investigated; fraud can cause refusal and legal consequences. No standardized cohabitation period is published.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage is not an automatic citizenship route for a foreign husband.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Restricted rules include double jus soli, anti-statelessness/foundling provisions and a declaration route at majority after qualifying residence; birth alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Birth alone generally does not confer citizenship. Exceptions include double-jus-soli and unknown/stateless-parent rules, with a later declaration route after qualifying residence.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: False for the ordinary case where two foreign parents transmit their nationalities and were not born in Togo.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The current certificate procedure states that a child born to a Togolese parent may document nationality whether born in Togo or abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This wording is broader than some gendered provisions of the 1978 text.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically naturalise a foreign parent. No automatic residence-card procedure based solely on a Togolese child was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Confirm any family-based benefit with DGDN.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father does not automatically receive citizenship through a Togolese child. Marriage to a Togolese woman provides a clearer published privileged-residence basis than parenthood.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No separate citizen-child sponsorship procedure was confirmed.

english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Practical inference; no national English-proficiency statistic was identified.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Neither language has official status or published support on the reviewed government portals; French assistance would likely be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable community-size statistic was identified.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ILOSTAT carries a national employee-earnings series through 2022, but the inspected stable official pages did not expose the exact national mean. The World Bank report publishes only 2019 sector means.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the XOF 52,000 ECVM 2022 employee median using roughly XOF 576/USD from late-July 2026. Current rather than 2022 FX is used.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the statutory XOF 52,500 private-sector monthly minimum; not an observed minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The exact national-total mean was not exposed by the inspected stable official pages. The World Bank reports only sector means; a rounded secondary USD ranking was not used to manufacture a value.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate current-FX conversion of the 2022 employee median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum is published in the aggregate sources.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory SMIG/SMAG effective 1 January 2023; SMIG applies to the private sector.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The exact all-employee national mean in XOF is not displayed on the inspected stable official pages. ECVM confirms the earnings variable and ILOSTAT confirms series coverage through 2022; the World Bank instead reports 2019 sector means of XOF 37,575 for agriculture, XOF 49,735 for manufacturing and XOF 91,659 for combined market services. Anker's 2025 XOF 99,708 rural and XOF 133,597 urban figures are living-wage benchmarks, not national average salaries. The value remains null rather than mislabelling a sector, normative or rounded estimate.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: ILOSTAT-harmonized national total from ECVM 2022: median monthly earnings of employees in the main job, not all-citizen income.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No statutory or representative national maximum is published; a microdata extreme would not be meaningful.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory private-sector minimum; 2022 national median monthly employee earnings; national mean unresolved
average_citizen_salary.period: Employee median: 2022; SMIG effective since 2023; living-wage comparison updated for 2025
average_citizen_salary.notes: The focused pass resolves the employee median at XOF 52,000/month and retains the official XOF 52,500 statutory minimum. The mean remains null because reviewed stable official pages identify the series but do not display the exact Togo total.

cost_of_living_note.notes: Anker's 2025 rural and urban living-wage values are normative decent-living benchmarks, not a general official remote-worker cost-of-living budget.

settlement_track.summary: If obtainable, the self-employed card is qualifying residence and supports ordinary residence after three years and discretionary naturalisation after five. The track remains weak until DGDN/CFE confirms first-enterprise sequencing and foreign-client-only revenue.
settlement_track.notes: Switch from temporary to ordinary residence is required; initial self-employed filing remains unresolved.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad status exists. Self-employment may be possible without a local employer, but foreign-client-only acceptance and first registration are not expressly resolved.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including more than five absent from the prior source set. The pass resolves the 2022 employee median and precisely explains why the exact national mean remains null; the immigration conclusion is unchanged.

data.selection_summary: Tonga has no dedicated digital-nomad visa. Its Immigration Regulations allow an independent application for a permit to reside while conducting business on the applicant's own behalf, so a locally registered foreign-client software-services business may be possible without a local employer. However, official material does not expressly confirm that a business serving only overseas clients is accepted, that ordinary remote employment can use this permit, or that time on this exact permit counts toward the five-year discretionary naturalisation rule. Written pre-application confirmation is required.

visa_application.title: Obtain a Business Visa
visa_application.notes: This government trade portal provides official procedure information, not direct online filing. The regulations direct residence-permit applications to the Principal Immigration Officer. Confirm the current form, filing location, and eligibility of a foreign-client software-services business before applying.
