Provide two referees who have known or been closely associated with the applicant during the preceding five years.
Provide a banker's reference or other acceptable evidence of financial background and status.
Obtain Foreign Investment Certification; the filing requests the business activity, proposed location, estimated investment, and expected employment.
Complete local business setup and TIN registration; consumption-tax registration generally becomes compulsory at TOP 100,000 of taxable supplies.
Obtain written confirmation that software services provided solely to overseas clients constitute an accepted business and immigration basis.

best_routes.notes: This is an independent-business possibility, not a dedicated remote-worker visa. The unresolved issues are whether a one-person software business with only foreign clients has sufficient local substance and whether its permit history counts for naturalisation. Visitor-to-business transfer is contemplated but costs TOP 7,500; advance approval is safer.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Evidence of sufficient visitor funds may be requested.

income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor or short-term business access does not create an ordinary remote-work residence track.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed evidence period is published.

Transfer from visitor status to a business permit costs TOP 7,500 under the published fee schedule.

initial_validity.notes: Nationality-specific pre-approval rules apply.

extension_rules.value: Extensions may be requested before expiry and are charged by period.
extension_rules.notes: An extension remains visitor status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct qualifying residence; a separate business-permit application is required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Changing status is costly and discretionary.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No permanent-residence right arises from visitor status itself.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The Nationality Act section 8 and Naturalization Regulations regulation 7 require at least five years of residence in Tonga, but neither defines which immigration statuses count or says visitor-permit days qualify. The Immigration Act treats a visitor permit as temporary, normally no more than six months, and prohibits employment without written permission. No current published rule therefore establishes visitor status itself as citizenship-counting residence.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general minimum salary is published.

income_requirement_display.notes: The route depends on approved local employment and labour-market support.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not an income-history route.

initial_validity.notes: The official embassy page describes the visa as renewable.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The visa allows residence in Tonga.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a non-working assured-income category.

path_to_citizenship.value: General law requires at least five years' residence, but counting of this visa was not expressly confirmed.
path_to_citizenship.notes: It does not fit an applicant who intends to continue working remotely.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because eligibility is limited to overseas pension or fund income and the holder is expressly prohibited from working or starting a business.

summary.value: A study permit can independently authorise entry and residence for an approved course. Applicants must provide course, grant or fellowship details and financial status; the published adult annual fee is TOP 200. No degree-based skilled residence route, post-study PR route, or direct PR based solely on qualifications was confirmed.
summary.notes: This is education-based temporary residence, not an independent skilled-worker route or a fit for ongoing foreign-contract work unless separately authorised.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they have a home in Tonga at any time during the fiscal year, are present for at least 183 days in a relevant 12-month period commencing or ending during that year, or are a Tongan government employee posted abroad. Part-year rules apply.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The home test can create residence before 183 days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for personal employment income, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share of the National Retirement Benefits Fund contribution. The employer pays at least 7.5%. This is not a confirmed mandatory sole-trader rate: persons outside the workforce may enroll voluntarily and choose an amount.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Monthly equivalent of the TOP 300 annual business-permit fee using TOP 1 = USD 0.42. This excludes one-time certification, licensing, tax, and setup costs.

special_tax_regimes.value: Individuals in business with annual turnover below TOP 100,000 may use Small Business Tax. Official material describes fixed annual amounts for lower bands and 2% of turnover from TOP 50,001 to TOP 100,000. Consumption-tax registration generally becomes compulsory at TOP 100,000.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Confirm eligibility and classification of a foreign-client software business with Revenue.

taxes.caveats: There is no special digital-nomad tax regime. Working physically from Tonga for a foreign payer is not automatically tax-free below 183 days: the home test can create residence earlier, and services performed in Tonga may be Tonga-source income. Classification as employment income, ordinary business profit, or Small Business Tax turnover materially changes the result.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax, with a separate turnover-based Small Business Tax option for qualifying individuals in business.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Home in Tonga or at least 183 days in a relevant 12-month period, subject to part-year rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident status and Tonga-source income are distinguished. The reviewed official material does not provide a sufficiently clear current plain-language statement of every foreign-income rule; services physically performed in Tonga may be taxable even when paid by a foreign client.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Small Business Tax below TOP 100,000 annual turnover; no digital-nomad or inbound-worker holiday was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: The National Retirement Benefits Fund regime is employment-based: every non-exempt employer and employee must contribute monthly, currently 5% from the employee and at least 7.5% from the employer. A non-Tongan employee may obtain an exemption by proving coverage under an equivalent-or-better statutory overseas superannuation scheme. A person outside the workforce may instead register as a voluntary contributor and select a contribution amount and weekly, fortnightly, or monthly frequency; the reviewed Act, regulations, Fund pages, and form publish no compulsory sole-trader rate or minimum amount.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Annual employment-income brackets run from 0% to 25%. The displayed 25% is the top marginal rate, not an effective rate. Business income may instead fall under ordinary net-income rules or Small Business Tax.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at TOP 1 = USD 0.42.
USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.
USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.
The top marginal rate begins above approximately USD 29,400.

taxation_system.notes: Employee tax brackets are current on the official Revenue page. Retirement rules are supported by the governing Act, regulations, current Fund pages, and voluntary-contributor form. For a foreign-client sole trader with no employees, official material confirms voluntary enrollment but does not publish a mandatory rate or minimum; Revenue and NRBF should confirm classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated digital-nomad tax treatment exists. A person approved for an own-account business permit generally needs a TIN and must determine whether ordinary income tax or Small Business Tax applies.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Potential resident sole trader or foreign-owned local business; filing classification requires Revenue confirmation
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–25% progressive personal rate; qualifying small businesses may instead face fixed or turnover tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Home in Tonga or at least 183 days in a relevant 12-month period, with part-year rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Payment from abroad alone does not establish exemption. Services performed from Tonga can raise Tonga-source taxation, and residents may have broader reporting exposure; official guidance does not resolve every foreign-income classification issue.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker special regime was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific payroll regime exists. If treated as an employee in Tonga, the National Retirement Benefits Fund requires 5% employee and at least 7.5% employer contributions unless an exemption applies, including approved proof for a non-Tongan of equivalent-or-better statutory overseas superannuation coverage. If operating alone and outside the workforce, NRBF permits voluntary membership with a self-selected amount and payment frequency; it publishes no compulsory sole-trader rate or minimum.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed mandatory sole-trader retirement payment is published. Voluntary contributors choose the amount and payment frequency. If classified as an employee, contributions are percentage-based at 5% employee and at least 7.5% employer unless exempt.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Business permit or extension: TOP 300 per person per year; visitor-to-business transfer: TOP 7,500; Foreign Investment Certification: TOP 500 one time.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Small Business Tax material describes annual TOP 100, TOP 250, or TOP 500 amounts for lower turnover bands and 2% of turnover from TOP 50,001–100,000. Consumption tax is 15% where registration applies.
fixed_payments.notes: The voluntary-contributor form leaves the contribution amount for the applicant and offers weekly, fortnightly, or monthly frequencies, so no universal fixed amount can be reported. Business licensing and sector-specific fees remain filing-dependent.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 183 days does not guarantee no Tonga tax: the home test may apply, and personal services performed in Tonga may be Tonga-source income.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: The 25% top marginal rate is a screening figure. Determine whether receipts are employment income, ordinary business income, or Small Business Tax turnover, and examine foreign-tax-credit or treaty exposure.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect Foreign Investment Certification, business setup, TIN registration, possible Small Business Tax, and consumption-tax registration once applicable TOP 100,000 tests are met.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Because Tonga has no nomad-specific regime and immigration eligibility remains uncertain, this is a conservative business-permit tax screening rather than a personalised liability calculation.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: An approved business permit itself authorises entry and residence; no prior local-employer stage is required.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No statutory automatic permanent-residence milestone for business-permit holders is published.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Permanent residence is not stated as a prerequisite; naturalisation uses a direct minimum five-year residence test.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum before discretionary naturalisation. The law does not expressly establish that every year on an own-account business permit counts.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The regulations prescribe documents and an interview but publish no standard processing period.

key_conditions.value: At least five years' residence, good character, adequate Tongan, intent to reside in Tonga, supporting documents, interview, discretionary royal approval, and oath of allegiance. No general renunciation requirement was found; Tonga has allowed dual nationality since the 2007 amendments.
key_conditions.notes: The law publishes no detailed physical-presence or absence formula beyond residence in Tonga.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No waiting period is stated: a non-Tongan marrying a Tongan may assume nationality by lodging the prescribed declaration and taking the oath.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A valid existing marriage to a Tongan appears sufficient for the declaration-and-oath nationality provision. A temporary-residency checklist separately recognises applicants married to Tongans.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Confirm the current form, authentication requirements, and filing office under the 2025 institutional amendments.

requirements_and_risks.value: Provide proof of the Tongan spouse and marriage, lodge the written declaration with the responsible minister, and take the oath. The residence checklist requests financial support or maintenance evidence. The marriage must be legally valid and genuine; false representations can lead to refusal, revocation, and other consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The 2025 amendment replaces references to the Minister for Foreign Affairs with the Minister of His Majesty's Diplomatic Services when the relevant Act commences.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Tonga confers nationality when a parent is Tongan; there is no general territorial citizenship for a child of two foreign parents. Descent is available through a Tongan father or mother for a child born abroad.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No. Birth in Tonga alone is insufficient when neither parent is Tongan.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No general jus soli or parent-permanent-resident alternative was identified.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Tonga to a Tongan parent is Tongan; a child born abroad may also derive nationality through either Tongan parent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The provision applies through the father or mother.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's foreign parent does not automatically become a citizen or permanent resident solely through parenthood. If married to the Tongan parent, the separate marriage nationality provision may apply.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: A discretionary dependent-family permit may be relevant, but no automatic parent-of-citizen settlement right was confirmed.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Tongan, the child can be Tongan, but an unmarried foreign father receives no confirmed automatic residence, PR, or citizenship merely because of the child. Marriage creates a separate statutory nationality route.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Confirm family-permit options with Immigration for an unmarried parent.

rank.notes: Live Passport Power Rank checked 2026-08-15; rankings can change.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 39 visa-on-arrival and 5 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index is used because its country page provides the requested category breakdown. It is not directly comparable with Henley's broader mobility score.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is official and widely usable in government and business material, making English-only remote work reasonably practical. Tongan is important for integration and required at an adequate level for ordinary naturalisation.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Local business and small-community dealings may still benefit substantially from Tongan-language assistance.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official, and no government or business-service support in either language was identified. Applicants should expect to operate in English or Tongan.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a practicality assessment based on the official-language environment, not a population-proficiency statistic.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Current official labour-market pages report employment data but no national mean wage. Invest Tonga publishes only a lowest-average-salary proxy.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current national median individual wage is published on the reviewed official pages.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Invest Tonga calls this a lowest-average-salary proxy. Tonga has no statutory minimum wage, so it is not a legal wage floor or observed national minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No comparable national average employee salary was established.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official median wage was located.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum or published wage-distribution ceiling was located.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Approximate conversion of the USD 195 proxy at TOP 1 = USD 0.42; it is not a statutory minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national mean employee wage in TOP was established.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current national median employee wage in TOP was established.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No reliable national maximum salary was published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Lowest-average-salary proxy for 195 hours monthly; not statutory minimum, national mean, or median
average_citizen_salary.period: Investor-cost page checked 2026-08-15; exchange-rate reference February 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: Official statistics, labour-market, household-income, government, and investor sources did not yield a current nationally representative mean or median individual wage. Nulls are retained instead of substituting household income or an unsourced salary-site estimate.

cost_of_living_note.value: No comprehensive comparable monthly cost-of-living estimate was established. Official statistics reported 7.1% annual inflation in June 2026, indicating recent price growth but not a household budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Housing, island, household size, and imported-goods consumption materially affect costs.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Tonga has no dedicated digital-nomad status. The only potentially fitting route requires operation of an approved local business, not merely continuation of ordinary foreign employment.
settlement_track.summary: An own-account business permit grants residence and general naturalisation is legally possible after at least five years, but official sources do not expressly confirm foreign-client-only remote services or that time on this permit counts. Written Immigration confirmation and local legal review are required.
settlement_track.notes: The independent-business possibility is preserved, but the citizenship track remains weak or uncertain because the remote-work eligibility and qualifying-residence links are not officially established.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The law permits business on one's own behalf but does not say whether an employee remotely serving one foreign employer qualifies. A genuine locally registered software-services business with foreign clients may fit, subject to certification, business substance, licensing, tax registration, and advance Immigration approval.

data.notes: Thirty-four distinct directly relevant URLs were reviewed, including six focused official URLs absent from the previous source set. The focused pass established the employee-versus-voluntary retirement contribution rules and precisely documented why visitor residence cannot be treated as citizenship-counting. Remaining nulls concern facts current sources do not publish: direct online business-permit filing, confirmation that business-permit time counts for naturalisation, an automatic PR milestone, citizenship processing time, a compulsory sole-trader retirement minimum, and nationally representative current mean or median wages.

data.selection_summary: No current digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was found. The Immigration Act contains a discretionary resident-status class for a permitted entrant who establishes a profession, trade, or self-operating business after substantial continuous residence, but official sources do not identify an initial status that lets this applicant legally reside and work remotely until eligible. Work permits are company/employer-based, while visitor, eVisa, and student permits are not settlement routes.

visa_application.title: Work Permits — Ministry of Homeland Security
visa_application.notes: This is official route information for the available work-permit process, not a digital-nomad application. Online filing uses TTBizLink and requires a corporate organization plus a form signed by the employee and employer. The separately checked Immigration Division, eVisa, and student-permit portals reveal no ordinary remote-worker application channel.

rejected_routes.route_name: Resident status for qualified professional, trade, or self-operating business — Immigration Act section 6(1)(a)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No numeric income threshold is prescribed; the Act instead requires sufficient means to support the applicant and immediate family.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No published numeric threshold; sufficient means of support required

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold published
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sufficient means to maintain the applicant and immediate family
income_requirement_display.notes: The amount is discretionary and should be verified with the Citizenship and Immigration Unit before relying on this route.

income_proof_months.notes: The statute does not specify a fixed bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Be a permitted entrant who entered legally and is not in a prohibited class.

Through education, occupational qualifications, employment record, training, skills, or other qualifications, have established or be likely to establish successfully in Trinidad and Tobago in a profession, trade, self-operating business, or agricultural enterprise.
Have sufficient means to support the applicant and immediate family.
Normally have five years of continuous residence; the Minister may accept a shorter period of at least 12 months in special circumstances.
Provide proof of tax compliance and a police certificate of good character with the resident-status application.

initial_validity.value: Resident status, if granted
initial_validity.notes: This is permanent resident status rather than a temporary remote-work permit, but approval is discretionary.

extension_rules.value: Not a renewable temporary permit; resident status may be lost after one continuous year abroad unless an exemption certificate is obtained

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: No official source identified an independent temporary status that permits ordinary foreign-client remote work while accumulating the required residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying permitted entrant may apply for resident status after five years of continuous residence, or exceptionally after at least 12 months, subject to ministerial discretion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Time spent in Trinidad and Tobago under a statutory permit is expressly excluded from acquisition of resident status under section 5(2)(c), making the required precursor status a material unresolved issue.

path_to_citizenship.value: For a non-Commonwealth alien, naturalisation generally requires residence throughout the final 12 months plus at least five aggregate years of residence or government service during the preceding seven years, good character, adequate English and citizenship knowledge, and the oath of allegiance.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The resident-status route is not an automatic citizenship grant; naturalisation remains discretionary.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected for this profile. It requires successful establishment in Trinidad and Tobago and prior qualifying continuous residence; official sources do not confirm that ordinary work solely for a foreign client supplies either the required local establishment or a lawful precursor status.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general minimum salary was published on the inspected official pages.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general minimum salary was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No general minimum salary published
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility is based on the employment and work-permit case rather than a digital-nomad income test.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed income-history period was identified.

key_requirements.requirement: A work permit is required for a non-national engaging in gainful occupation for more than 30 days in any 12 consecutive months.
Access and filing through TTBizLink require a registered corporate organization.
The individual application must be signed by both employee and employer.
The work-permit review protects employment opportunities for Trinidad and Tobago nationals and assesses the need for foreign skills.

initial_validity.notes: The inspected official pages did not publish one standard permit duration.

extension_rules.value: Extensions can be filed through the same work-permit process
extension_rules.notes: Approval and duration remain case-specific.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Work authorization only; no direct qualifying temporary-residence grant was confirmed

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion; a separate discretionary resident-status application would be required
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The Immigration Act states that time in Trinidad and Tobago under a permit does not count toward acquisition of resident status under section 5(1)(b) or 5(1)(d).

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path from the work permit was confirmed; separate qualifying residence and naturalisation rules apply

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the process is corporate/employer-based and therefore does not satisfy independent foreign-contract remote work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The eVisa is short-visit permission, not a remote-worker route.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: The current central eVisa page publishes an application fee of TTD 800; this is a fee, not an income requirement. Mission-specific financial-document rules vary.

income_proof_months.notes: No single nationally uniform income-history period can be stated for the eVisa or visitor route. The central eVisa checklist requires supporting documents but does not specify a period; official mission instructions differ: the New York Consulate and Abuja High Commission require at least three months of bank or financial statements, while the London High Commission requires six months. The applicable checklist must therefore be verified for the applicant's nationality and processing post.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport with at least six months' validity, digital photograph, supporting documents, email, and payment card.
The eVisa is for short-term visits by eligible visa-required nationals.
Gainful occupation beyond 30 days in a 12-month period requires a work permit.

initial_validity.value: Duration of the approved short stay
initial_validity.notes: No universal stay length was stated on the inspected central service pages.

extension_rules.value: A visitor may separately request an extension of stay
extension_rules.notes: An extension remains visitor permission and does not create a remote-work or settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor permission is not a qualifying independent remote-work residence route.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from visitor or eVisa status

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is short-term visitor permission. The 30-day work-permit exemption does not turn visitor status into a residence or citizenship path.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No standardized monthly income threshold was published in the inspected central student-permit materials.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No standardized monetary threshold was published.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: The permit form asks about available funds and support, but the route primarily requires admission to full-time study and publishes no uniform minimum amount.

income_proof_months.notes: The central student-permit page and official student-permit form require supporting or funds information but publish no fixed statement-history period. The Abuja student-entry-visa checklist asks for the sponsor's last three months of financial statements, whereas the New Delhi checklist asks for a bank balance letter without a month count. Those are mission-specific entry-visa requirements, not a universal student-permit rule, so no national month value is established.

key_requirements.requirement: Acceptance into a full-time programme at a designated learning institution.
Passport valid for at least 12 months, digital photograph, supporting documents, and online payment.
Current central application fees: TTD 200 for a CARICOM national and TTD 400 for a non-CARICOM national.

initial_validity.notes: The permit is intended for the full duration of study, but no uniform numeric validity period was published because programme lengths vary.

extension_rules.value: Renewal applications require an assessment form

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Student permission only; no qualifying residence was confirmed
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Time under a permit is excluded by the Immigration Act from the specified acquisition of resident status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path confirmed

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path confirmed

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires full-time education and is neither an ordinary remote-worker route nor confirmed qualifying residence for settlement.

summary.value: A student permit can be applied for after acceptance into full-time study without a local employer, but it is permit-based study authorization. Education and professional qualifications can also support a discretionary resident-status application under Immigration Act section 6(1)(a), normally only after substantial prior continuous residence; qualifications alone do not provide a direct independent entry residence route.
summary.notes: The Act excludes time spent under a permit from the specified acquisition of resident status, so the student permit should not be treated as a direct settlement bridge.

tax_residency_rule.value: The Inland Revenue Division describes an individual present for fewer than 183 days in a calendar or tax year as non-resident; 183 days is therefore the practical residence threshold, subject to treaty and fact-specific evaluation.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Non-residents are instructed to obtain an individual evaluation from the International Tax Unit.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate. Chargeable profit is taxed at 25% through TTD 1,000,000 and 30% above that amount.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share inferred from the official 2026 contribution table; the combined NIS rate is 16.2%, generally split approximately 5.4% employee and 10.8% employer. This employment-based NIS treatment should not be assumed to apply identically to a foreign self-employed contractor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: A self-employed person above the low-income threshold pays a fixed health surcharge of TTD 8.25 per week, approximately TTD 35.75 monthly. No reliable same-date USD conversion was established, so a USD figure is intentionally omitted.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate remittance-basis, or tax-holiday regime was identified. Treaty relief may alter a non-resident's position.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Sole-trader registration is a tax and business compliance mechanism, not immigration permission.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical presence, whether services performed while in Trinidad and Tobago are locally sourced, employment versus self-employment characterization, permanent-establishment issues, allowable expenses, and any applicable tax treaty. Residents are taxed on worldwide income and non-residents on Trinidad and Tobago-source income, while non-residents must obtain an IRD evaluation. Tax registration does not legalize immigration status.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax on chargeable income or profit, with worldwide taxation for residents and source-based taxation for non-residents.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Fewer than 183 days is described as non-resident; treaty provisions and individual evaluation may modify the result.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents: worldwide income. Non-residents: income derived from or accrued within Trinidad and Tobago, subject to exemptions or treaty relief.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad regime found; double-tax treaty relief may apply.
taxation_system.social_security: The official 2026 NIS contribution rate is 16.2% of insurable earnings, with class-based weekly amounts and an approximate one-third employee/two-thirds employer split. Applicability to a foreign contractor requires classification review. A separate health surcharge applies.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 30% dashboard figure is the top marginal rate. The first TTD 1,000,000 of chargeable income or profit is taxed at 25%, and only the excess is taxed at 30%. Personal allowances and deductions affect taxable income; official pages displayed inconsistent historical allowance amounts, so no current allowance is used in the bracket calculation.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Chargeable personal income or sole-trader profit
tax_brackets.notes: This is a marginal bracket; allowances and allowable business expenses may reduce chargeable income.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Excess chargeable personal income or sole-trader profit
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate, not an effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The core residence, income-scope, and rate rules come from IRD and NIBTT. A filing-level review is still necessary for foreign-contract services.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special tax category exists. A person nevertheless carrying on self-employed activity in Trinidad and Tobago may need BIR registration, quarterly income-tax and health-surcharge payments, business levy, and possibly VAT registration.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated route; hypothetical resident or non-resident employee/self-employed treatment
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 25% through TTD 1,000,000 of chargeable income or profit; 30% on the excess. The displayed 30% is the top marginal screening rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Fewer than 183 days is treated by IRD as non-resident, subject to treaty and individual evaluation.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are generally taxed on Trinidad and Tobago-source income; services physically performed in the country require an IRD source and treaty analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Formal employment uses earnings-class NIS contributions at a 16.2% combined 2026 rate. Self-employed persons also face the health surcharge; NIS treatment depends on classification and cannot be assumed from employee tables alone.

fixed_payments.status: No visa-specific fixed tax. General self-employed charges may apply.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Health surcharge: TTD 8.25 weekly where average monthly income exceeds TTD 469.99, otherwise TTD 4.80 weekly. NIS, if applicable, uses contribution classes rather than one universal monthly amount.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Current central Ministry pages publish a multiple-entry eVisa fee of TTD 800 and student-permit fees of TTD 200 for CARICOM nationals or TTD 400 for non-CARICOM nationals. No digital-nomad fee exists.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Self-employed income tax is paid quarterly. Business levy is 0.6% of gross sales or receipts, with a stated first-three-years exemption. VAT registration is required above TTD 500,000 of annual commercial supplies.
fixed_payments.notes: These are general tax or visitor/student charges, not proof of a right to work remotely.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being present fewer than 183 days generally leaves the person non-resident, but it does not automatically exempt income from services performed while physically in Trinidad and Tobago. IRD evaluation and treaty analysis are needed.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days or otherwise resident, worldwide income may be taxable at progressive rates up to 30%, with registration and filing or payment obligations depending on classification.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A sole trader must obtain a BIR file number, keep records, file an annual return, and pay quarterly income tax and health surcharge; business levy and VAT may also apply. This registration does not create immigration permission.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Because there is no digital-nomad status, this section describes hypothetical tax consequences and must not be interpreted as immigration eligibility.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent temporary remote-work residence route was found.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: This is the normal continuous-residence benchmark for the discretionary section 6(1)(a) resident-status class, not a confirmed timeline from a remote-worker visa. The Minister may accept a special-case period of at least 12 months.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: For a non-Commonwealth alien, this is a best-case statutory sequence inferred from resident status after five continuous years followed by satisfaction of the naturalisation rule requiring the final 12 months plus five aggregate years in the preceding seven. It is not guaranteed, and naturalisation remains discretionary.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Minimum residence pattern for alien naturalisation: the 12 months immediately before application plus at least five aggregate years during the preceding seven. No qualifying remote-work route was found to start this timeline.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable official typical processing duration was published on the inspected current service page or statutory material.

key_conditions.value: For alien naturalisation: full age and capacity, good character, adequate knowledge of English and citizen duties, required residence, and oath of allegiance. Residence and resident-status grants are discretionary; legal entry, good character, tax compliance, and sufficient support are relevant. Resident status may be lost after one continuous year abroad unless exempted.
key_conditions.notes: No general statutory renunciation requirement was identified in the provisions inspected; case-specific nationality advice remains appropriate.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Immigration Act section 6(1)(c) lists the spouse of a citizen or resident as a class that may apply for resident status without stating a minimum marriage duration. Approval is discretionary; zero means no statutory duration was identified, not immediate guaranteed approval.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Trinidad and Tobago citizen or resident can place the foreign spouse in the statutory class eligible to apply for resident status. It does not itself confer residence or citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The ordinary naturalisation or Commonwealth-registration rules still apply after residence; no separate automatic spousal citizenship rule was identified.

requirements_and_risks.value: The Minister must approve resident status. The applicant must have entered legally, not be in a prohibited class, and demonstrate good character; the prescribed application requires supporting civil-status evidence, tax compliance, and a police certificate. A marriage certificate and evidence of the citizen or resident spouse should be expected. False or sham-marriage representations can lead to refusal and immigration or criminal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Official sources did not publish a standard processing time for spouse-based resident status.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship automatically to a person born in Trinidad and Tobago, with narrow exceptions for a child whose non-citizen parent has diplomatic immunity or an enemy-alien birth in occupied territory.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Trinidad and Tobago normally becomes a citizen at birth even when both parents are migrants, subject to the narrow diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Trinidad and Tobago is a citizen by birth. A child born abroad also acquires citizenship at birth where either parent is a Trinidad and Tobago citizen otherwise than by descent, subject to the constitutional descent limitation.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Citizenship through a citizen parent born abroad may be restricted where that parent is only a citizen by descent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: The parent of a citizen is a statutory class that may apply for resident status, but the Minister retains discretion. The citizen child's birth does not automatically legalize, permanently reside, or naturalise either parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The parent must still file the prescribed resident-status application and satisfy legal-entry, character, and other requirements.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a citizen child may apply for resident status as the parent of a citizen under Immigration Act section 6(1)(b). Residence and later citizenship are not automatic, and naturalisation requires a separate application and residence history.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and the genuine parental relationship must be documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank shown on the live Passport Index page on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category; this excludes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 39 visa-on-arrival destinations and 7 eTA destinations. Passport Index also lists eVisas separately in destination details.

passport.notes: Index methodologies differ. A January 2026 secondary report citing Henley reported rank 28 with access to 146 destinations, while the live Passport Index provides the category breakdown used here.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for communication: English is the official language and is spoken throughout the islands. This language practicality does not overcome the absence of a qualifying remote-worker immigration route.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Local English-based Creole varieties are common.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low outside expatriate or private networks; no official source reviewed identified broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language public-service availability.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: English should be expected for immigration, tax, business, and daily administrative matters.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official CSO page provides labour-force and monthly-income-group workbooks but does not publish a current national mean worker salary directly on the inspected page. A value was not inferred from grouped files.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national median salary was directly established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The statutory national minimum wage is published in TTD; no same-date authoritative USD conversion was established.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national mean salary amount was directly established.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national median salary amount was directly established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A meaningful national maximum salary is not published and should not be invented.

min_salary_local_currency.value: TTD 20.50 per hour; approximately TTD 3,553.33 per month at 40 hours/week and 52 weeks/year
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the statutory national minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary. The monthly amount is a transparent arithmetic conversion and excludes overtime.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The current CSO landing page did not state a national average monthly worker income.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The current CSO landing page did not state a national median monthly worker income.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful official national maximum salary was found.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory hourly minimum wage converted to a 40-hour week; average and median unresolved
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage confirmed in the FY2025 Budget Statement; CSO labour-force page reviewed through 2026 Q1 and income-group resources through 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: This is statutory-minimum-wage information, not average citizen salary. Focused searches and the current official CSO labour-force page exposed income-group spreadsheets but not a directly stated current national mean or median, so those fields remain cautiously null.

cost_of_living_note.value: No current official national single-person cost-of-living estimate was established. The CSO household-budget page contains household income and expenditure material, but prominent figures are historical or household-level and are not a defensible current individual living-cost estimate.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A household statistic was not substituted for an individual remote-worker budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor or eVisa permission and the 30-day work-permit exemption are not residence or citizenship paths.
settlement_track.summary: Naturalisation and discretionary resident status exist, but no current official route connects ordinary work for a foreign client to lawful qualifying residence. A different employer, family, or locally established professional or business basis would be required before the statutory residence-to-citizenship rules could become relevant.
settlement_track.notes: The section 6(1)(a) professional or self-operating-business resident class is not treated as a match because it requires prior continuous residence and successful establishment in Trinidad and Tobago, while no compatible independent precursor status was confirmed.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated foreign-remote-worker status exists in the current official service catalogue. Sole-trader tax registration does not grant immigration permission, work permits are corporate or employer-based, and visitor or student permits do not supply a qualifying settlement route.

data.notes: Audit completed against the previous country record and 31 distinct directly relevant URLs, including eight newly inspected official URLs. The false verdict remains: no current ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route was found. The focused null pass resolved the two unexplained income-proof-period gaps: both remain null because central eVisa and student-permit materials publish no universal period and official mission checklists vary by route and post. Other remaining null values have source-backed explanations for unpublished, inapplicable, discretionary, or unavailable measures.

data.selection_summary: No current Tunisian digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary freelance residence category was found. Official procedures cover approved Tunisian employment, study, marriage, non-working retirees, and investors or company managers. Establishing a Tunisian enterprise can support investor residence, but that requires genuine local business substance and does not fit an ordinary software engineer working solely under a foreign contract.

visa_application.title: Octroi de la carte de séjour pour étrangers
visa_application.notes: This is the official residence-card procedure, not an online application portal. Applications are filed with the competent security service or designated investment office. No dedicated remote-worker application channel was identified.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No dedicated remote-worker threshold is published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Foreign-client work is not listed as an independent residence basis.

income_requirement_display.value: No dedicated remote-worker route or income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Not applicable because the category does not exist
income_requirement_display.notes: This is the absence of a qualifying category, not a zero-income route.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker program exists, so no income-proof period applies.

key_requirements.requirement: A foreign contract alone is not a listed residence basis; remunerated activity instead requires approved Tunisian employment or an exemption tied to an eligible local activity.

initial_validity.notes: No status is available under this description.

extension_rules.notes: No corresponding status exists to renew.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct route was confirmed for ordinary work performed remotely for a foreign employer or client.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor presence and a foreign contract do not substitute for a listed residence basis.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: There is no remote-worker status from which a permanent-residence transition could be assessed.

path_to_citizenship.notes: The general naturalisation framework does not cure the absence of a qualifying initial residence route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because current official procedures do not contain a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract freelancer category. This conclusion is based on the affirmative residence categories and the separate foreign-employment system; authorities generally do not publish a page expressly stating that a nonexistent visa does not exist.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The residence procedure publishes no fixed personal-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Eligibility depends on investor and company documentation instead.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold; a genuine Tunisian investment or company basis is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Formation, operation, sector authorization, and capital requirements depend on the business.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed bank-statement period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Company-manager or investor documentation, applicable employment-contract exemption, accommodation evidence, passport, photographs, and residence-card form.
A genuine Tunisian investment or enterprise and compliance with activity-specific authorization requirements.

initial_validity.value: Normally tied to supporting documents and no more than one year; qualifying foreign business investors resident for at least one year may exceptionally receive a renewable five-year temporary stay visa.
initial_validity.notes: The five-year document remains temporary residence rather than permanent residence.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continuation of the qualifying investor basis; the exceptional five-year investor authorization is renewable.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic permanent status follows.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available after satisfying the investor or company-manager documentation requirements.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed legislation establishes renewable residence documents but no automatic permanent-residence milestone for this route.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalisation may be requested after the applicable residence requirement, ordinarily five years, but it is not an automatic consequence of investor residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Continuous lawful residence and current administrative practice should be verified before relying on investor-residence years.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because this is a founder or investor route requiring a real Tunisian enterprise and local compliance. Registering a business does not turn ordinary overseas-client remote work into a qualifying freelance residence route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The procedure requires regular transfers but publishes no minimum amount.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Regular periodic pension or other transferred income; no fixed amount published

income_requirement_display.value: Regular transferred pension or other means; amount not published
income_requirement_display.notes: The category is framed for retirees not exercising salaried professional activity.

income_proof_months.notes: The procedure does not specify a bank-statement period.

key_requirements.requirement: Periodic and regular transfer of pension or other income, accommodation evidence, passport, photographs, and residence-card form.
The applicant must be a retiree not exercising salaried professional activity.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence is generally limited by the supporting documents and normally does not exceed one year.
initial_validity.notes: Special authorization can alter the duration, but none is promised for this category.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continuation of the qualifying basis and must be obtained before expiry.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available to a qualifying non-working retiree with regularly transferred means.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic permanent-residence transition for this category was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: Only the separate discretionary naturalisation process could apply after qualifying residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: No retiree-specific citizenship entitlement was found.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the official category concerns retirees who do not exercise salaried professional activity; active software work under a foreign contract does not match it.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration salary threshold was established; ordinary employment and labor-approval rules apply.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No immigration-specific threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The employment must comply with Tunisian wage law.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration-specific salary threshold; approved Tunisian employment required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a local-employment route, not foreign-contract remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: An employment contract approved by the employment ministry or an applicable exemption from contract approval.
Employer documentation, accommodation, passport, photographs, and residence-card application.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence is tied to the employment documentation and normally cannot exceed one year without special authorization.

extension_rules.value: Renewal depends on continued approved employment and residence compliance.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Available after obtaining the required Tunisian employment authorization or exemption.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No automatic permanent-residence milestone was established.

path_to_citizenship.value: General discretionary naturalisation may eventually be requested after qualifying residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Tunisian employer and labor authorization are required.

summary.value: A foreign student may independently request temporary residence using current enrollment, proof of income, accommodation, passport, photographs, and the application form. This is an education route, not degree-based skilled migration, and no direct permanent residence or post-study settlement bridge was confirmed.
summary.notes: An existing software-engineering degree does not itself create a Tunisian residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident when their principal residence or domicile is in Tunisia or, if their principal dwelling is abroad, they spend at least 183 days in Tunisia during the calendar year. Treaty tie-breakers can override dual residence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The principal-residence test can apply without reaching 183 days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal PIT screening rate from 2025, not an expected effective rate. A 0.5% social-solidarity contribution can also apply during FY2026.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee-side ordinary non-agricultural payroll rate, including the additional 0.5% contribution from 2025. It does not determine the treatment of every foreign-paid or self-employed worker.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly payment applies to a nonexistent digital-nomad category. A registered non-agricultural self-employed person is instead subject to class-based CNSS contributions: the ordinary schedule inspected states a minimum TND 224.180 per quarter from Q2 2025, approximately TND 74.727 per month, but coverage, class, and continuing 2026 applicability must be confirmed for the individual's legal status.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary inbound remote-worker regime was found. Narrow flat-rate treatment exists for certain non-resident employees and specified foreign staff, but it does not create immigration eligibility.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The non-resident employee rule should not be assumed to cover an independent foreign-contract worker.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on where services are physically performed, residence, salary versus professional-income classification, Tunisian registration, social-security coverage, foreign tax, and any applicable treaty. Immigration eligibility and tax liability are separate.

taxation_system.value: Progressive resident taxation of worldwide income, with statutory treatment for foreign income already taxed abroad and treaty relief where applicable.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Principal residence or domicile in Tunisia, or at least 183 days in a calendar year when the principal dwelling is abroad; treaty tie-breakers can apply.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income, including foreign-source income except income already subjected to foreign tax under the stated domestic rule; non-residents are generally taxed on Tunisian-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad regime. Certain non-resident employees present no more than six months and specified foreign employees may use a 20% gross-income rule.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary payroll generally has 9.68% employee and 17.07% employer contributions from 2025. Registered non-agricultural self-employed workers use a separate 14.71% class-based system. Classification and treaty coverage require individual review.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard value is the 40% top marginal PIT rate. The FY2026 0.5% social-solidarity contribution can make the top combined marginal screening rate 40.5%. Effective tax is lower because the brackets are progressive.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD ceiling uses about USD 0.338 per TND.
Excludes the separate FY2026 solidarity contribution.
This is the top marginal rate, not the effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: The consolidated 2026 tax code confirms the revised 0%–40% scale and an annual minimum tax for commercial and non-commercial activities. The 2026 Finance Law extended the temporary 0.5% solidarity contribution through FY2026.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Tunisia has no confirmed digital-nomad immigration or tax category. A person nevertheless living and working from Tunisia may become taxable under ordinary residence, source, professional-income, registration, social-security, and treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated route; ordinary salary, non-commercial professional income, or business classification must be determined
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive PIT up to 40%, potentially 40.5% with the FY2026 solidarity contribution; this is a top marginal screening figure
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Principal residence or domicile in Tunisia, or the applicable 183-day test, subject to treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally fall within worldwide-income taxation; the treatment of foreign income already taxed abroad and treaty relief must be assessed.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker regime was identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No digital-nomad exemption exists. Employee payroll and registered self-employed contributions use different regimes, and neither automatically establishes the treatment of an unregistered foreign-paid worker.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad-specific fixed payment exists; conditional fixed or minimum obligations are published for registered self-employed and business taxpayers.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Registered non-agricultural self-employed workers are subject to a 14.71% CNSS contribution on a class-based deemed-income base. The ordinary schedule inspected states a minimum TND 224.180 per quarter from Q2 2025, about TND 74.727 per month. A separate 2026 artist schedule confirms current SMIG-linked class mechanics but is not applicable to an ordinary software engineer. Eligibility, classification, and any treaty exemption require confirmation.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: There is no digital-nomad fee. The official stamp-duty compilation lists TND 150 for an ordinary foreign residence card and TND 300 for late, lost, or destroyed-card renewal, but that compilation is dated 2017; the amount should be rechecked with the issuing office before payment.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: The consolidated March 2026 income-tax code imposes an annual minimum for commercial and non-commercial activities of 0.2% of turnover or gross receipts, with a TND 300 minimum, subject to statutory exceptions including a limited new-business period. A TND 200 minimum applies only to the narrower 0.1% category described by the code. Local establishment tax and VAT can also apply according to activity, place, and classification; these are not universal remote-worker fees.
fixed_payments.notes: The unresolved marker was replaced with the applicable factual distinction: no route-specific payment exists, but locally registered professional activity can trigger published minimum tax and class-based social-security liabilities. These obligations do not create residence eligibility.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Fewer than 183 days does not guarantee non-residence when the principal residence or domicile is in Tunisia. A non-resident can still have Tunisian-source liability depending on where services are performed and treaty rules.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident may face progressive taxation of worldwide income up to 40%, plus the FY2026 solidarity contribution where applicable, subject to foreign-tax and treaty relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A locally registered professional must file a declaration of existence and determine PIT, annual minimum tax, CNSS class, VAT, local establishment tax, invoicing, and foreign-exchange obligations. Registration does not independently create immigration eligibility.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Ordinary tax and registered-self-employed rules are documented, but confidence remains below high for this scenario because Tunisia has no digital-nomad route and the applicant's exact contract, registration, residence, and social-security classification are unknown.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary remote-worker route exists, so there is no route-specific time to temporary residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No automatic permanent-residence milestone was established for the rejected routes.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalisation is based on residence and discretionary approval rather than a confirmed number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the ordinary residence prerequisite for requesting discretionary naturalisation, not a guaranteed route-specific outcome. Because no qualifying remote-work residence route exists, it is not a usable five-year pathway for this profile.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Ministry of Justice describes submission requirements but does not publish a reliable typical processing time.

key_conditions.value: Ordinarily at least five years' residence, a formal application with supporting documents, and discretionary state approval. Statutory spousal and other exemptions can remove the five-year prerequisite but do not make approval automatic.
key_conditions.notes: Continuity of residence, language or integration practice, criminal-record documents, dual-nationality consequences, and decree-stage processing should be verified before filing.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The rules are sex-specific. The official summary describes at least two years' residence together in Tunisia for a foreign wife in the stated acquisition case. A foreign husband married to a Tunisian can be exempted from the ordinary five-year naturalisation prerequisite, but no fixed marriage duration for him is stated.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Tunisian can support family residence. Nationality consequences differ by sex: the official summary describes a two-year joint-residence condition for a foreign wife in the relevant category and an exemption from the ordinary five-year naturalisation prerequisite for a foreign husband.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not automatically naturalise a foreign husband.

requirements_and_risks.value: Residence filing requires an authenticated or Tunisian marriage certificate plus identity, accommodation, and application documents. Nationality remains subject to the applicable procedure and, for naturalisation, discretion. Authorities can verify civil-status documents and the relationship; fraudulent marriage can cause refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Case-specific advice is important because the nationality provisions distinguish foreign wives and husbands.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Tunisia alone is insufficient. Double jus soli applies in the described case when the child, father, and paternal grandfather were born in Tunisia; separate protections cover specified stateless-parent, unknown-parent, and foundling cases.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Two ordinary foreign parents do not transmit Tunisian citizenship, and birth in Tunisia alone does not confer it. Limited double-jus-soli, statelessness, unknown-parent, or foundling rules may apply.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent residence of a parent is not equivalent to Tunisian citizenship for automatic descent citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child of either a Tunisian father or Tunisian mother is Tunisian by descent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: This applies regardless of which parent is the migrant.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child's birth does not automatically naturalise either foreign parent. No general residence entitlement based solely on parenthood of a Tunisian child was confirmed in the reviewed residence procedure.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Parents should not rely on the child's citizenship as an automatic residence or citizenship route.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the mother is Tunisian, the child is Tunisian, but the foreign father does not automatically become a citizen. Marriage to the mother may support family residence and exemption from the ordinary five-year naturalisation prerequisite, subject to the separate marriage and naturalisation rules.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: No automatic permanent residence or citizenship follows merely from paternity.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026; Passport Index for category breakdown

rank.notes: The dynamic Henley 2026 table inspected on the research date showed Tunisia tied at rank 71.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score includes destinations accessible without obtaining a visa in advance and is not identical to Passport Index's strict visa-free count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 category count; its methodology differs from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index listed 35 visa-on-arrival and four eTA destinations. Its separate strict visa-free count was 36.

passport.notes: Passport rankings and entry categories change frequently. Henley and Passport Index use different methodologies, so their category totals should not be combined into one calculation.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English-only remote work is reasonably practical in Tunis and the technology sector but less reliable for government, legal, banking, and everyday administrative matters, where Arabic and often French are more useful. EF's 2025 index scored Tunisia 498 and its IT-function score was 538.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF uses a self-selected testing sample and is a practical indicator rather than a census.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian have no official status, and no reliable evidence of broad administrative or workplace usability was found. They should not be relied on for immigration, tax, banking, or business procedures.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Support is likely limited to particular individuals and tourism businesses.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official survey's TND 924 average monthly base salary for permanent employees in surveyed enterprises in 2022, using about USD 0.338 per TND. This is historical formal-enterprise salary data.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: A TND 422 private-sector median is published for April 2011, but converting that historical amount using a 2026 exchange rate would be misleading. No current national median suitable for a 2026 USD figure was established.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD value of the 2026 statutory non-agricultural minimum of TND 554.736 per month for a 48-hour week; it is not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2026-rate conversion of the TND 924 average monthly base salary reported by the 2022 INS enterprise survey.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The only directly published broad median located was TND 422 for formal private-sector employees in April 2011. It is too old to convert into a meaningful current USD salary, and the 2022 enterprise survey reports averages rather than a national employee median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed sources publish averages, percentiles, deciles, or wage-growth indices, not a national maximum salary. A percentile boundary is not a maximum and was not substituted for one.

min_salary_local_currency.value: TND 554.736/month for a 48-hour week; TND 470.251/month for a 40-hour week
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory non-agricultural minimum effective from 1 January 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly base salary of permanent employees in surveyed enterprises in 2022.

median_salary_local_currency.value: TND 422/month for formal private-sector employees in April 2011
median_salary_local_currency.notes: This resolves the prior vague marker with the exact published median, but it is historical and sector-limited, not a 2026 national median. The same 2011 distribution reported a first quartile of TND 332, third quartile of TND 576, and 90th percentile of TND 915. The newer 2022 enterprise survey publishes average base salaries but no national employee median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum salary is published in the current INS enterprise survey, the INS wage-growth series, the ILO earnings catalogue, the 2011 private-sector distribution, or the 2017 public-sector distribution. Those sources provide averages, quantiles, deciles, or index growth; none establishes the highest salary received nationally, so a maximum cannot be stated defensibly.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2026 statutory minimum; 2022 formal-enterprise average base salary; 2011 formal private-sector median
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum: 2026 monthly; average: 2022 monthly base salary; median: April 2011 monthly remuneration
average_citizen_salary.notes: The minimum is a current statutory floor, the average is a 2022 formal-enterprise employee average, and the median is an older formal private-sector statistic retained only because it is the exact published median located. No national maximum was published. These are labor-market figures, not immigration income requirements.

cost_of_living_note.value: The latest detailed official household-budget survey located reports 2021 annual expenditure of TND 5,468 per person and TND 20,328 per household, equivalent at that time to about TND 456 per person or TND 1,694 per household per month. These historical figures should not be treated as a 2026 budget because prices have changed.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Current city-specific housing and lifestyle costs can differ substantially.
