settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: There is no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-work status. Visitor presence, business or tax registration alone, and receipt of overseas income should not be treated as a settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: Tunisia has temporary residence and a general discretionary naturalisation framework, but the independently accessible residence bases confirmed are investor or company-manager, non-working retiree, study, and family categories. None fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work.
settlement_track.notes: The applicant would need to switch to approved Tunisian employment, a genuine local investor or company-manager basis, family residence, or another independently qualifying status. Tax or sole-proprietor registration does not itself legalize residence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign employment or client contract is not an independent residence basis. Local tax registration may be required for activity but does not create immigration status.

data.notes: The previous rejection remains supported. This focused pass resolved the fixed-payment status by distinguishing the nonexistent digital-nomad fee from conditional self-employed CNSS, minimum-tax, stamp-duty, VAT, and local-tax rules. It replaced the vague median marker with the exact historical TND 422 formal-private-sector median while clearly identifying its April 2011 scope, and retained a precisely explained null for maximum salary because reviewed current and historical wage sources publish no national maximum. More than 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including more than five canonical URLs absent from the previous source set.

data.selection_summary: Türkiye has an active Digital Nomad Visa that fits a Ukrainian software engineer working for a foreign employer or client. However, the officially described follow-on status is a six-month tourism-purpose short-term residence permit, and no official digital-nomad-specific renewal or conversion chain was established. The route is useful for temporary remote living but is not a confirmed permanent-residence or citizenship path.

visa_application.title: Digital Nomad Identification Certificate application
visa_application.notes: This is the direct application for the prerequisite Digital Nomad Identification Certificate, not the final visa. After obtaining the certificate, the applicant applies for the visa through a Turkish consulate or visa centre and, after arrival, applies separately through e-Residence for the six-month residence permit.

rejected_routes.route_name: Digital Nomad Visa and six-month short-term residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The alternative annual threshold is USD 36,000.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: USD 3,000 per month or USD 36,000 per year
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official eligibility threshold is denominated in US dollars rather than Turkish lira.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 3,000/month or USD 36,000/year
income_requirement_display.notes: Official threshold; no TRY conversion is required for eligibility.

income_proof_months.notes: The official route and consular materials require proof of income but do not specify a fixed number of historical bank-statement months.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be aged 21–55 and hold citizenship from an eligible country; Ukraine, Russia and Belarus are included.
University degree or equivalent graduation certificate.
Foreign-company employment contract or, for a freelancer, a business contract with a company not established in Türkiye.
Passport valid for at least six months from arrival and a biometric photograph.
Consular guidance additionally requests travel insurance, proof of accommodation and a certificate of good conduct; the exact mission-specific checklist should be reconfirmed before filing.
Obtain the Digital Nomad Identification Certificate online, then submit the visa application through a Turkish visa centre or consulate.

initial_validity.value: Digital Nomad Visa followed, after arrival and separate approval, by a six-month tourism-purpose short-term residence permit
initial_validity.notes: YİMER’s current digital-nomad answer specifies a six-month residence permit issued for tourism purposes. The reviewed official materials do not state a longer initial digital-nomad residence period.

extension_rules.value: The general e-Residence system accepts extension applications filed before an existing permit expires, but the reviewed official digital-nomad materials do not grant renewal on the digital-nomad basis or specify how many successive six-month permits may be issued. Any extension is a new discretionary assessment under the applicable short-term-residence basis.
extension_rules.notes: General rules allowing short-term permits of up to two years in some categories do not replace YİMER’s route-specific six-month statement and do not establish a renewable digital-nomad chain.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: After entering with an approved Digital Nomad Visa, apply independently through the e-Residence system for a six-month tourism-purpose short-term residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The residence permit requires a separate application and approval; the visa or identification certificate alone is not the residence card.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A subsequent qualifying work/residence status can lead to indefinite long-term residence after eight qualifying years, but the initial nomad permission does not itself establish a renewable eight-year route.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Migration Management counts non-student residence-permit periods in full toward long-term residence. The Labour Ministry publishes both domestic and abroad work-permit applications, and discretionary independent work assessed on professional/economic contribution. These successor paths require additional eligibility; keeping a foreign remote job alone was not verified as sufficient. Exit depends on the actual permit and application situation.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalisation may be requested after five uninterrupted years of lawful residence, subject to settlement intent, Turkish-language ability, income, character, public-health and security requirements. The six-month digital-nomad residence has no confirmed renewal chain capable of sustaining that period.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Satisfying the statutory naturalisation conditions does not create an absolute right to citizenship.

rejected_routes.notes: This is a strong temporary fit for ordinary foreign-contract remote work, but it fails the citizenship-oriented selection because official sources confirm only a six-month tourism-purpose residence permit and do not confirm durable renewal or conversion.

rejected_routes.route_name: Ordinary Turkish work permit through local employment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no independent remote-worker income threshold for this route; salary criteria depend on the sponsored position and permit assessment.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A standalone income threshold is inapplicable because this is a Turkish-employer-specific work-permit route.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable—Turkish-employer sponsorship route
income_requirement_display.notes: Rejected because the ordinary foreign-contract applicant cannot substitute a foreign contract for the required Turkish employer filing.

income_proof_months.notes: The route is assessed through the employment contract and employer filing rather than a published number of personal income-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: For an overseas application, the foreigner first applies at a Turkish mission and receives a reference number; the employer in Türkiye must then file through the e-İzin system.
The standard dependent work permit is tied to a specific employer, workplace and job.

initial_validity.value: Up to one year on the first approved employer-specific work permit, and never longer than the employment or service contract
initial_validity.notes: The Ministry’s current work-permit FAQ states that the first dependent permit may be issued for up to one year for work at the specified employer, workplace and job. The approved period can be shorter when the employment or service contract ends earlier.

extension_rules.value: Apply electronically from 60 days before expiry and before the permit expires. If approved for the same employer, the first extension may be issued for up to two years and subsequent extensions for up to three years; changing employer is assessed as a first application.
extension_rules.notes: Extensions remain conditional on approval and continued employer-specific sponsorship. A pending timely extension permits continued work for no more than 90 days after expiry if the job and workplace do not change.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved work permit confers the right to work and reside during its validity, but only through the sponsored employment basis.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not independently usable by the specified foreign-contract applicant.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A foreigner with at least eight years of legal work permits may apply for a permanent work permit, subject to assessment; long-term residence also has separate general conditions.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This potential settlement path does not cure the initial requirement for Turkish-employer sponsorship.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through general naturalisation after five uninterrupted years of qualifying lawful residence if all statutory conditions are met, but the starting route requires local sponsorship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Rejected for the applicant context even though sponsored residence can potentially support a later general naturalisation application.

rejected_routes.notes: The ordinary permit requires a Turkish employer and is tied to the approved employer, workplace and job. It therefore does not fit independent foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: Admission to a Turkish higher-education programme can support a student residence permit without a local employer. A foreign university degree alone does not create residence. Student-permit time counts at half value toward the eight-year long-term-residence calculation, and this is an education route rather than a remote-work route.
summary.notes: The applicant’s existing software-engineering degree does not independently qualify them; actual enrolment in Türkiye is required.

tax_residency_rule.value: Individuals domiciled in Türkiye, or generally present continuously for more than six months in a calendar year, are treated as residents, subject to statutory temporary-purpose exceptions and treaty tie-breakers.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax residence are separate determinations.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the indicative standard 4/1-b self-employed contribution rate reflected by the official 2026 minimum calculation. Eligible compliant contributors may receive a five-point reduction. Whether a digital nomad must register under 4/1-b depends on the actual employment or business structure and treaty coverage.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the standard 2026 minimum 4/1-b self-employed premium of TRY 11,808.23, using the 14 August 2026 official indicative exchange rate. It is not automatically payable merely because someone holds the Digital Nomad Visa.

special_tax_regimes.value: From 2026, new residents meeting the preceding-three-calendar-year domicile and tax-liability conditions may obtain a certificate for a 20-year exemption on qualifying income and gains sourced outside Türkiye. It is not digital-nomad-specific, and services physically performed in Türkiye may not qualify as foreign-source merely because the payer is abroad.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A Turkish tax ruling or professional analysis is necessary before applying the exemption to remote employment or software-contract income.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the relationship is employment or independent professional activity, where services are performed and used, whether the payer has Turkish activity, eligibility for the new-resident certificate, VAT and invoicing rules, social-security registration and the applicable double-tax treaty. The Digital Nomad Visa itself does not grant a tax holiday.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax from 15% to 40%, combined with a certificate-based 20-year exemption for qualifying foreign-source income of eligible new residents.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Domicile in Türkiye or generally continuous presence exceeding six months in a calendar year, subject to statutory exceptions and treaties.
taxation_system.income_scope: Ordinary residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Turkish-source income. Eligible new residents may exempt qualifying income and gains sourced outside Türkiye for 20 years.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Article 20/D new-resident foreign-source-income exemption; eligibility requires no Turkish domicile and no Turkish tax liability during the preceding three calendar years, a timely application and an exemption certificate.
taxation_system.social_security: Self-employed 4/1-b contributions range from a 2026 minimum of TRY 11,808.23 per month to TRY 106,274.03 before the five-point compliance incentive. A separate 2026 general-health-insurance reference amount is TRY 1,981.80 monthly for people within that category. Applicability to a foreign remote worker requires individual review.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard rate is the 40% top marginal rate, not an effective rate. For ordinary non-wage income, the 2026 bands are 15% through TRY 190,000; 20% to TRY 400,000; 27% to TRY 1,000,000; 35% to TRY 5,300,000; and 40% above that. Wage income has a higher third-band endpoint of TRY 1,500,000.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion at about TRY 47.76 per USD.

tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 annual taxable income; USD figure is the upper endpoint
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 annual taxable income; USD figure represents the ordinary upper endpoint
tax_brackets.notes: Wage income uses the higher TRY 1,500,000 endpoint.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: TRY 1,000,000–5,300,000; wage band begins after TRY 1,500,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 annual taxable income; USD figure is the upper endpoint
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.
Top marginal rate.

taxation_system.notes: The rates, contribution figures and inbound exemption are current official rules. Confidence is lower for their application to this individual because the source and classification of remote-service income and social-security liability are fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The visa has no separate tax status. Ordinary rules apply unless the applicant qualifies for a general exemption such as Article 20/D; compensation earned while physically working in Türkiye requires source and treaty analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Temporary digital-nomad visa plus tourism-purpose short-term residence; no visa-specific tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 15%–40% progressive ordinary rates; potentially 0% only for income conclusively qualifying under the new-resident foreign-source exemption
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domicile or generally more than six months’ continuous presence in a calendar year, subject to exceptions and treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Ordinary tax residents generally face worldwide taxation. Article 20/D exempts qualifying foreign-source income of eligible new residents, but foreign payment alone does not establish that software or employment income generated by work in Türkiye is foreign-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad-specific tax regime was identified. The 2026 Article 20/D inbound regime may exempt qualifying foreign-source income for 20 years after a timely certificate application.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Possible employee, self-employed 4/1-b or treaty treatment. The official 2026 minimum 4/1-b contribution is TRY 11,808.23 monthly before the five-point incentive; applicability is not automatic for every visa holder.

fixed_payments.status: Partially confirmed; nationality and business structure determine the final amount
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: If mandatory 4/1-b registration applies, the 2026 minimum is TRY 11,808.23 monthly, or TRY 10,156.73 with the five-point compliance incentive. The separate GSS reference premium is TRY 1,981.80 monthly for people falling within that category.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The 2026 general tariff lists TRY 9,376.40 for a single-entry visa, but the Ministry of Foreign Affairs may determine whether and what a nationality is charged under reciprocity. Every residence card costs TRY 964. The separate residence-permit fee is nationality- and duration-dependent and is calculated in e-Residence; the general published tariff for otherwise ungrouped nationalities is TRY 348.10 per day for the first month, subject to a TRY 653.70 minimum and TRY 3,359.90 maximum, plus TRY 2,232.30 for each later month.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No digital-nomad-specific recurring transaction tax was identified. Confirmed application charges are the TRY 964 residence-card fee, a nationality- and duration-dependent residence-permit fee, and any reciprocity-based visa charge. A person who registers Turkish self-employed activity may additionally incur VAT, electronic-receipt, bookkeeping, municipal/workplace and stamp-tax obligations according to the transactions and registration chosen; the reviewed official sources do not establish one fixed amount payable by every digital-nomad holder.
fixed_payments.notes: Health insurance is required in the application process. Do not add the GSS and 4/1-b amounts without establishing which social-security category applies. The published general visa and residence tariffs do not by themselves establish the exact amount charged to a Ukrainian applicant.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person without Turkish domicile and not exceeding the general continuous six-month threshold may remain a non-resident, but Turkish-source income and treaty rules still require review.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary marginal rates can reach 40%. Article 20/D may reduce tax on qualifying foreign-source income to zero, but work physically performed in Türkiye needs a source-of-income determination and an exemption certificate.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A registered independent professional may face progressive income tax, invoicing or e-receipt duties, VAT obligations and 4/1-b social security. Official guidance treats genuinely independent professional work as professional income, but the result remains fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Ordinary rates, application fees and contribution figures are official. The unresolved filing-level issue is whether this applicant’s foreign-contract income qualifies as foreign-source under the inbound exemption and which registration, VAT and social-security obligations apply.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The six-month short-term permit can be requested after entry during the digital-nomad visa period; no multi-year waiting period applies.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General long-term residence requires eight continuous qualifying years, but no official digital-nomad renewal chain sustains this applicant for eight years. A dependable route-specific number therefore cannot be stated.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalisation may be requested after five uninterrupted lawful-residence years and does not require first obtaining the eight-year long-term permit. It is therefore not meaningfully measured as years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The general statutory benchmark is five uninterrupted lawful-residence years, but the digital-nomad route supplies only a six-month tourism-purpose permit with no confirmed continuation. Returning five years would incorrectly imply a complete route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The inspected current official citizenship sources do not publish a nationwide typical processing-time statistic; naturalisation remains discretionary after eligibility, document and security review.

key_conditions.value: For general naturalisation: five uninterrupted years of lawful residence before filing, demonstrated intent to settle, sufficient Turkish, income or a profession supporting the household, good character, no public-health obstacle and no national-security or public-order obstacle. The applicant may spend no more than 12 months abroad during the statutory residence period, and satisfying the conditions creates no absolute right to citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: The decisive missing condition for this profile is a renewable qualifying residence basis after the initial six-month permit.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: At least three years of continuing marriage to a Turkish citizen before applying for citizenship; citizenship is not automatic.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Time already spent in a genuine, continuing marriage to a Turkish citizen can count toward the three-year marriage condition. Marriage to another foreign national does not accelerate Turkish citizenship.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The marriage-based route is separate from the digital-nomad route.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must live within the unity of marriage, avoid conduct incompatible with that unity and have no national-security or public-order obstacle. Authorities examine whether the marriage is genuine; misrepresentation can lead to refusal or later cancellation. Marriage does not itself confer citizenship.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Article 16 does not state a separate Turkish-language or residence-duration condition, but documentary checks, interviews and administrative or security review still apply.

birthright_citizenship.notes: A child born in Türkiye does not ordinarily become Turkish solely through birthplace. Citizenship by place of birth applies where the child acquires no citizenship from either foreign parent; foundlings are presumed born in Türkiye.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Normally no. A Türkiye-born child of two foreign parents becomes Turkish at birth only if the child would otherwise acquire no nationality; the parents’ migrant or residence status alone is insufficient.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is an anti-statelessness provision rather than broad jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born to a Turkish mother, or to a Turkish father within marriage, is Turkish from birth. For a Turkish father and foreign mother outside marriage, citizenship follows once legal descent is established.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The other parent’s migrant status does not prevent transmission.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a Turkish citizen child does not automatically naturalise either foreign parent. Family circumstances may support a separate residence or naturalisation case, but an independent legal basis must be established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The standard family residence rules do not establish automatic parental permanent residence or citizenship merely because a child is Turkish.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence. If the mother is Turkish and the parents are married, the father may qualify as the foreign spouse for family residence and, after three years of genuine continuing marriage, may apply for citizenship. If they are not married, no automatic parent-based citizenship route was established.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Any child-welfare, family-life or humanitarian residence argument would require individual assessment.

rank.notes: Ranking displayed on the inspected 2026 Henley page when checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley access score, which combines destinations accessible without a prior visa, including qualifying visa-on-arrival and electronic-travel-authorisation access under Henley’s methodology.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The inspected Henley ranking page publishes an aggregate access score but not a separate count of destinations requiring an advance visa.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The inspected Henley page does not separate visa-on-arrival and eTA destinations from the aggregate access score.

passport.notes: The live 2026 Henley page supported rank 48 and an access score of 113; its score should not be described as a strict visa-free-only count.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English can be workable in international technology, tourism and major-city settings, but nationwide proficiency is limited and Turkish is important for immigration, tax, banking and routine administration. EF EPI 2025 ranks Türkiye 71st of 123 with low proficiency; Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir and Antalya perform better than the national result.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a self-selected test-taker index rather than a census and is used only as a practical indicator.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian may help within expatriate and tourism communities, but neither is official and the reviewed sources do not provide a reliable nationwide proficiency measure.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Turkish, or English in internationally oriented environments, will generally be needed for official and professional matters.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate 2026-USD conversion of derived 2024 monthly gross earnings of about TRY 39,231. The TRY estimate applies the official 85.7% gross-earnings share to average labour cost of TRY 45,777.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current inspected TÜİK labour-cost and Structure of Earnings releases publish arithmetic means, sector and occupational averages, but not a national median monthly employee wage. TÜİK’s income-distribution release concerns equivalised household disposable income and cannot substitute for employee salary.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the 2026 statutory gross minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary. The official net minimum is approximately USD 588 using the same exchange rate.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of derived 2024 monthly average gross earnings; it is not a 2026 nominal salary observation.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: TÜİK’s current Structure of Earnings release reports arithmetic monthly averages and subgroup averages but no national median monthly wage or earnings amount. Its Income Distribution release defines median income using equivalised household disposable income, a different population, unit and income concept that cannot be converted into a median employee salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official releases provide sector and occupational-group averages but no finite national maximum individual salary. The highest occupational-group average is not a salary ceiling and was not inserted as a maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: TRY 33,030 gross per month; TRY 28,075.50 net
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum wage effective from 1 January through 31 December 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Derived from the official 2024 average labour cost of TRY 45,777 and its reported 85.7% gross-earnings component. The separate 2023 Structure of Earnings release reported TRY 26,402 in monthly average gross earnings.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No national median monthly employee salary is published in the inspected current TÜİK earnings releases. The separate TÜİK household-income statistics measure equivalised disposable household income and are not a valid local-currency median salary substitute.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected TÜİK releases do not publish a national maximum individual monthly salary or a statutory salary ceiling. Their highest sectoral or occupational average measures a group mean, not the maximum salary earned by an individual.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: 2026 statutory monthly minimum wage; derived 2024 monthly average gross earnings for registered employees
average_citizen_salary.period: 2024 average and 2026 statutory minimum
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are resident labour-market measures rather than immigration income thresholds. USD conversions use approximately TRY 47.76 per USD from the 14 August 2026 official indicative rate. Inflation and the different reference years make USD comparisons time-sensitive. Median and maximum values remain null because the inspected official wage releases do not publish those national employee-salary statistics.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official income-distribution source reports household income distribution rather than a standardized national household budget. A defensible current cost-of-living amount would require assumptions about city, household size, rent and consumption and is therefore not supplied.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The official follow-on residence is only six months and is issued for tourism purposes. A separate, independently qualifying and renewable residence basis is needed for a dependable settlement path.
settlement_track.summary: Türkiye’s Digital Nomad Visa fits foreign-employer and foreign-client remote work, but the officially confirmed residence period is only six months under a tourism purpose. With no official DNV-specific renewal or conversion chain, it is temporary-nomad-only rather than a citizenship route.
settlement_track.notes: The general five-year naturalisation and eight-year long-term-residence rules do not cure the missing ability to remain continuously on this exact route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The program expressly accepts foreign-company employment and foreign-client contracts without a Turkish employer. This is a temporary-living fit only and does not make the route a citizenship-path match.

data.notes: The active remote-worker route and its six-month follow-on residence are confirmed by current official sources. The focused audit also established ordinary sponsored-work-permit durations and current 2026 visa and residence application charges. Median and national maximum salary values remain null because current TÜİK earnings releases publish averages but not those employee-salary statistics.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: A qualifying work permit or other independently justified continuing residence, followed by long-term residence
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A subsequent qualifying work/residence status can lead to indefinite long-term residence after eight qualifying years, but the initial nomad permission does not itself establish a renewable eight-year route.
requirements: Obtain a qualifying Turkish employment/work permit or meet the separate independent-work-permit criteria.
A domestic employer application normally requires a still-valid residence permit issued for at least six months; otherwise use the consular procedure.
Meet continuity, stable income, insurance and other long-term-residence conditions.
reviewed_route_names: Digital Nomad Visa and six-month short-term residence permit
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Migration Management counts non-student residence-permit periods in full toward long-term residence. The Labour Ministry publishes both domestic and abroad work-permit applications, and discretionary independent work assessed on professional/economic contribution. These successor paths require additional eligibility; keeping a foreign remote job alone was not verified as sufficient. Exit depends on the actual permit and application situation.

data.selection_summary: Turkmenistan does not publish a digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract freelance residence route. Work and entrepreneurship visas require an invitation approved by the State Migration Service, and the work-visa instructions direct applicants to a Turkmen employer or partner. A residence permit may be sought on narrow grounds such as marriage, a USD 500,000 investment, or exceptional qualifications useful to Turkmenistan, but none fits an ordinary foreign-client software engineer.

visa_application.title: State Migration Service of Turkmenistan
visa_application.notes: No independent remote-worker application portal was found. The official immigration authority should be consulted, but ordinary visas generally require an invitation issued by the State Migration Service on behalf of a Turkmen legal or natural person.

rejected_routes.route_name: Work visa (WP) or entrepreneurship visa (BS1/BS2) with approved local invitation

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-income threshold is published because this is an invitation-based visa, not a digital-nomad route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum-income requirement was found in the published visa instructions.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; an approved Turkmen invitation is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial eligibility is not framed as a foreign monthly-income test.

income_proof_months.notes: The official instructions do not specify a remote-income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Invitation issued by the State Migration Service on behalf of a Turkmen legal or natural person.
For a WP work-visa invitation, contact an employer or partner in Turkmenistan.
Passport, visa application and photographs; visa fees depend on validity and number of entries.
Registration at the place of stay is generally required within three working days.

initial_validity.value: From up to 10 days or one month, with longer periods priced by each additional month
initial_validity.notes: The embassy publishes single- and multiple-entry fee schedules tied to intended duration; it does not describe one standard WP validity.

extension_rules.value: Extension requires migration approval and continued underlying visa/invitation basis
extension_rules.notes: No independent conversion or renewal rule for foreign-client remote work was found.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path. A separate residence-permit petition must satisfy one of the statutory grounds and is decided by presidential act.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Holding a WP or BS visa does not itself establish eligibility for the separate residence permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic visa-to-permanent-residence transition was confirmed
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The law provides a renewable residence permit on specified grounds, but not a settlement entitlement arising merely from a work or entrepreneurship visa.

path_to_citizenship.value: No path from this visa alone. Naturalization generally requires five years of permanent residence, Turkmen-language ability, lawful means and presidential approval.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Temporary stays do not count as permanent residence under the citizenship law.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant cannot self-sponsor ordinary work for a foreign client. The visa instructions explicitly require an approved invitation and direct WP applicants to a Turkmen employer or partner.

rejected_routes.route_name: Residence permit based on high qualification or achievements useful to Turkmenistan

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monetary income threshold is published for this ground.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No local-currency income threshold is specified.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; exceptional qualification and national-interest assessment required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a discretionary talent/national-interest ground, not an ordinary remote-work income route.

income_proof_months.notes: No defined income-history period was found.

key_requirements.requirement: High qualification in a field or major achievements in science, culture, art or sport that can be used in Turkmenistan's interests.
Normally at least two years of prior residence in Turkmenistan before applying.
Petition addressed to the President through the State Migration Service or, from abroad, through a Turkmen diplomatic mission or consulate.
Approval is discretionary and made by presidential act; statutory review may take up to six months.

initial_validity.value: Up to 5 years, limited by the applicant's travel-document validity
initial_validity.notes: The residence permit is time-limited.

extension_rules.value: May be extended by the State Migration Service after checks
extension_rules.notes: Extension can be refused on statutory grounds.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct application for a time-limited residence permit is legally possible only if the exceptional qualification/national-interest ground is accepted.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This is not a degree-only or ordinary software-engineer route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The law uses a renewable residence permit and permanent-residence concepts, but does not publish an automatic permanent-status transition for this ground.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Filing-level confirmation would be required regarding how the permit is recorded for citizenship residence counting.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalization may be requested after five years of permanent residence, subject to language, lawful-means, absence and other conditions and presidential decision.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A profession or qualification representing state interest may allow the five-year period to be reduced or waived, but that is exceptional and discretionary.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected under the applicant criteria because it requires exceptional qualifications or achievements usable in Turkmenistan's national interest. A relevant software-engineering degree and ordinary foreign contract do not establish eligibility.

rejected_routes.route_name: Tourist, private or other visitor visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No digital-nomad income test applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No qualifying remote-income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Not applicable; visitor visas are not remote-work residence routes
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor status cannot be treated as an independent work or settlement route.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-worker income history applies.

key_requirements.requirement: An approved invitation is generally required for visa issuance.
Foreign visitors must comply with visa purpose and migration registration rules.

initial_validity.value: Visa- and invitation-specific
initial_validity.notes: No dedicated remote-work validity period exists.

extension_rules.value: Migration approval and continuing visitor basis required
extension_rules.notes: Extension does not legalize ordinary remote work.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic path
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate statutory residence-permit ground is required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Visitor time is not established as permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor or other temporary presence does not count as the five years of permanent residence required for ordinary naturalization.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because tourist, private and other visitor visas neither authorize a dedicated foreign-remote-work arrangement nor create a qualifying settlement track.

summary.value: A university degree by itself does not create an independent residence route. The only remotely related ground requires high qualification or major achievements that can be used in Turkmenistan's interests, making it a discretionary talent/national-interest route rather than education-based migration.
summary.notes: The software-engineering degree alone is insufficient.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is a Turkmenistan tax resident when present for an aggregate of at least 183 calendar days during the tax year. Resident status is determined for each tax period.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Diplomatic and consular personnel and their families are excluded under the cited rule.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: The Tax Code's general individual income-tax rate is a flat 10%, unless another provision applies.

social_contributions_percent.notes: A reputable local professional guide reports that mandatory pension contributions for individual entrepreneurs are at least 10%, depending on the calculation base. Employers generally pay 20% of employee wages. No lawful digital-nomad/self-employed immigration scenario was found, so applicability to a foreign remote worker cannot be assumed.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer payment was established. The contribution base and foreigner's registration status would need professional confirmation.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, inbound-worker or remittance-basis regime was found. Residents are generally taxed on income regardless of source; non-residents on Turkmenistan-source income.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty relief may be available when the prescribed foreign-residence documentation is submitted.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on physical work location, residence, whether activities create a Turkmen permanent workplace, entrepreneur registration, treaty status and whether the foreign payer's income is classified as Turkmenistan-source. The immigration research did not identify a legal ordinary remote-worker status, so professional immigration and tax advice is essential before working from Turkmenistan.

taxation_system.value: Flat personal income tax system: generally 10%. Tax residents are taxable on income regardless of source, while non-residents are taxable on Turkmenistan-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 calendar days in Turkmenistan during the tax year.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Turkmenistan-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound remote-worker regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: A local professional guide reports employer mandatory pension contributions of 20% of wages and individual-entrepreneur contributions of at least 10%, depending on the calculation base. Voluntary funded contributions are at least 2% of wages.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable; the general PIT rate is flat rather than progressive.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No general threshold; applies unless the Tax Code provides otherwise
tax_brackets.notes: This is the statutory general rate, not an expected effective rate after deductions or exemptions.

taxation_system.notes: The rate and residence/scope rules come from the current official Tax Code. Social-contribution detail comes from a reputable local professional guide because a sufficiently clear current official contribution schedule was not located.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route exists. If a person nevertheless became tax resident under another lawful status, the general 10% PIT and worldwide-income rules would be the starting point, subject to classification, deductions and treaty relief.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad tax category; general individual taxation only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 10% flat general PIT screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 days in the tax year.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Resident individuals are taxed on income regardless of source; non-residents are taxed on Turkmenistan-source income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No route-specific rule exists. Individual entrepreneurs reportedly contribute at least 10% to mandatory pensions depending on the base; employers generally contribute 20% of wages.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed-payment regime found
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed amount confirmed; contributions are percentage-based and status-dependent.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: WP visa fees begin at USD 35 for a single-entry stay up to 10 days and vary by duration, entries and expedited processing; these are not digital-nomad fees.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No dedicated remote-worker fixed tax or fee confirmed.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa fees are included only as context for the rejected WP route.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person below 183 days is generally non-resident, but Turkmenistan-source income may still be taxable and working must still be authorized under immigration law.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: At 183 days, worldwide income generally enters the 10% PIT base; however, no ordinary foreign-remote-worker immigration route was found.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Entrepreneur registration and activity legality require separate confirmation. A local guide reports pension contributions of at least 10% for individual entrepreneurs.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening analysis, not confirmation that foreign remote work is lawful under a visitor or invitation-based visa.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying remote-work route exists. For narrow residence-permit grounds, the law normally requires at least two years of prior residence, but that is not a guaranteed route for this applicant.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The statutes reviewed do not publish an automatic temporary-to-permanent conversion timeline for the rejected routes.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalization requires permanent residence during the previous five years; annual absences generally must not exceed three months.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated for this applicant because there is no qualifying entry/residence route and no guaranteed time to obtain permanent residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The statutory maximum for consideration of a citizenship application is six months; actual grant remains a presidential decision.

key_conditions.value: Five years of permanent residence, conversational knowledge of the Turkmen state language, lawful means of subsistence, respect for the Constitution and laws, normally no more than three months abroad per year, no disqualifying serious criminal/security grounds, and resolution of existing foreign citizenship because an applicant who remains a citizen of another state may be refused.
key_conditions.notes: Exceptional categories, including qualifications of state interest, may receive a reduced or waived residence period at discretion.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage to a Turkmen citizen is a residence-permit ground, but the migration law normally requires at least two years of residence in Turkmenistan before applying. It does not specify a two-year marriage duration.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Turkmen citizen supplies a statutory ground for a residence-permit petition, including submission through a Turkmen mission from abroad. Marriage does not automatically change either spouse's citizenship and does not expressly waive the ordinary five-year permanent-residence naturalization rule.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Family-visa entry and residence permission remain separate procedures.

requirements_and_risks.value: Residence approval is discretionary by presidential act. A sham marriage can cause permit cancellation. A marriage-based permit may also be cancelled if the marriage ends within five years and there are no children of the marriage. Citizenship still requires an application and the statutory naturalization conditions unless a discretionary exception applies.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage must be legally registered and genuine.

birthright_citizenship.notes: There is no general jus soli. Citizenship at birth is primarily by descent, with limited territorial rules for children who would otherwise be stateless, children of resident stateless parents and foundlings.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Turkmenistan to two foreign parents does not ordinarily acquire Turkmen citizenship. The child does acquire it if the parents' country does not transmit its citizenship; children born there to permanently resident stateless parents and foundlings are also covered.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is restricted anti-statelessness jus soli, not unconditional birthright citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is a Turkmen citizen and the other is foreign, a child born in Turkmenistan is a citizen. Citizenship also follows regardless of birthplace where either parent permanently resided in Turkmenistan; if both lived abroad and the child was born abroad, a joint parental application is generally required unless the child would otherwise be stateless.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The rule applies regardless of whether the Turkmen parent is the mother or father.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Turkmen citizen child is a close relative and may have a statutory ground to petition for a residence permit, but approval remains discretionary and normally follows two years of residence. The child's citizenship does not automatically naturalize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The close-relative provision includes children.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is a Turkmen citizen and the child meets the birth rules, the child can be Turkmen. The migrant father may then rely on the citizen child as a close-relative residence-permit ground, but receives neither automatic residence nor citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Residence and citizenship require separate applications and decisions.

rank.notes: Passport Index displayed Passport Power Rank 81 when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change dynamically.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations in the named index, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately displayed 139 destinations as visa required.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined dashboard value: 42 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 4 eTA destinations. The index also lists eVisas separately and reports an overall mobility score of 59.

passport.notes: This uses Passport Index rather than mixing Henley's combined visa-free/visa-on-arrival score with another provider's category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Low. English is taught in schools and used in some higher education, but it is not an official language. More importantly for remote work, independent reporting documents extensive internet and social-media restrictions, making dependable access to common online services a serious practical risk.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The UN record reports statements by Turkmenistan's representatives about language education and remote-work tools; Freedom House provides independent evidence of online restrictions.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is described in the official Language Act discussion as a lingua franca and is likely the most useful non-Turkmen language for daily communication. Ukrainian is not official and no evidence of broad practical use was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Turkmen remains the sole official language.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current UN country analysis publishes sex-disaggregated average wages rather than a single all-worker mean, so an overall USD average was not invented. At the official TMT 3.5/USD reference rate, the reported 2024 male and female averages are approximately USD 679 and USD 597 per month respectively.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable current national median wage was located after checking UN and official statistics sources.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Statutory monthly minimum wage of TMT 1,410, converted at the UN operational/reference rate of TMT 3.5 per USD. This official-rate conversion may not reflect practical purchasing power or parallel-market exchange conditions.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No single combined national average was published in the source. The reported 2024 averages were TMT 2,376 for men and TMT 2,088 for women, approximately USD 679 and USD 597 at TMT 3.5/USD.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A current national median was not established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful statutory or observed national maximum salary is published; employers determine pay structures subject to labor law.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory minimum effective from 1 January 2025 and still reported by an official state service in 2026.

average_salary_local_currency.value: 2024 average wage: men TMT 2,376/month; women TMT 2,088/month
average_salary_local_currency.notes: Sex-disaggregated figures from the UN Country Analysis 2025; a combined weighted average was not supplied.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current median wage was found.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum wage is established or statistically meaningful.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum wage; sex-disaggregated average monthly wages for 2024
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 2025 and re-confirmed by an official source in 2026; averages refer to 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: Official wage transparency is limited. USD conversions use the official/reference TMT 3.5 per USD rate and should not be treated as an estimate of freely convertible take-home pay.

cost_of_living_note.notes: No sufficiently reliable, current and comparable household cost-of-living basket was located. Salary conversions are particularly sensitive to Turkmenistan's exchange-rate and data-transparency constraints.
