settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor, work and entrepreneurship visas are not independent digital-nomad statuses and do not themselves establish qualifying permanent residence.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route exists. The applicant would need an entirely different qualifying basis—such as genuine marriage, a USD 500,000 investment, or exceptional qualifications accepted as serving Turkmenistan's interests—before the separate residence and five-year naturalization framework could become relevant.
settlement_track.notes: The prior record's ineligibility conclusion is retained, but the classification is broadened from employer-required because official law also shows non-fitting investor, marriage and exceptional-talent residence grounds.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker or ordinary foreign-client freelance residence status was found. Published work-visa rules require a locally connected invitation, while residence grounds exclude ordinary remote work.

data.notes: More than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected, with official statutes and government sources prioritized. The earlier false selection result remains correct. Material improvements include the statutory residence-permit grounds and two-year prerequisite, five-year rather than seven-year ordinary naturalization period, six-month citizenship processing ceiling, exact 10% PIT and 183-day/worldwide-income rules, marriage-permit cancellation risks, detailed child-citizenship rules, current passport-category breakdown, and current wage evidence. Nulls remain where no reliable median wage, combined national average, maximum wage, fixed freelancer payment or automatic residence-conversion timeline could be established.

data.selection_summary: Tuvalu has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route. An applicant may independently request a permit to enter and reside for conducting a business, but approval is discretionary, the business must operate in Tuvalu, current foreign-investment requirements require filing-level verification, and ordinary extensions are limited to three within five years. This does not provide a reliable seven-year path to naturalisation.

visa_application.title: Immigration Regulations 2014 — Permit to Enter and Reside forms and requirements
visa_application.notes: This official regulations PDF contains Form 3 and the filing requirements, but it is not an online application portal. No current Immigration Department application website or dedicated remote-worker application channel was found.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permit to Enter and Reside — conduct of business

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No fixed monthly-income threshold is published. Applicants must instead provide proof of financial resources and evidence supporting the proposed business.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed threshold; proof of financial resources required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The regulations use Australian dollars for fees but do not prescribe a minimum income or capital amount for this permit.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum income; financial resources and a business description are required
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: AUD requirements without a fixed income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: The immigration officer may request additional evidence. This should not be interpreted as a predictable income-based remote-worker route.

income_proof_months.notes: The regulations do not prescribe a fixed number of bank-statement or income-proof months.

key_requirements.requirement: Submit the prescribed Form 3 in English or Tuvaluan with a passport or identity certificate, two photographs and the filing fee.
Provide a description of the business, proof of financial resources and any additional evidence requested by the Principal Immigration Officer.
Show good health and character and possess an outward ticket or provide a repatriation bond.

For intended residence beyond one year, provide medical and radiological examinations and police reports from every jurisdiction where the applicant lived for more than one year during the preceding five years.

Confirm compliance with current business-registration, licensing and foreign-investment rules; the official legislation index identifies a Foreign Direct Investment Act 2025, but its detailed effect on a one-person foreign remote business could not be established from an accessible consolidated filing guide.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The permit directly authorizes entry and residence, subject to its stated conditions.

extension_rules.value: Extensions are available, but ordinarily no more than three extensions may be granted in any five-year period
extension_rules.notes: Further extensions require the Minister, acting on Citizenship Committee advice, to certify that they are in the national interest. This prevents treating the permit as a routine seven-year settlement route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes. The permit itself authorizes entry and residence for up to one year.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Grant remains discretionary and conditioned on the approved activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent-residence category or automatic conversion is provided by the cited immigration legislation.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The legislation contains no general permanent-residence status, and ordinary extensions are restricted.

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation generally requires seven immediately preceding years of ordinary residence, at least AUD 250,000 in personal assets, familiarity with Tuvaluan laws and customs, good character, health and an intention to make Tuvalu the permanent home. The business permit's ordinary extension limit does not provide a predictable way to complete those seven years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Citizenship Act says immigration noncompliance alone does not automatically disregard residence, but this is not permission to remain, and naturalisation is not an automatic permit conversion.

rejected_routes.notes: Although this is an independently filed residence permit, it is for conducting a business in Tuvalu—not a published foreign-client remote-work category. Business substance, current foreign-investment approval and long-term extension eligibility require manual confirmation, and the route cannot credibly be ranked as a citizenship track for an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer.

rejected_routes.route_name: Permit to Enter and Reside — employment in Tuvalu

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No immigration income threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Employment applications instead require employer sponsorship.

income_requirement_display.value: No published threshold; Tuvalu employer sponsorship is mandatory
income_requirement_display.notes: This route fails the applicant's no-local-employer requirement.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed period is specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Provide an employer sponsorship using the prescribed Form 5.
Comply with Tuvalu employment law and any permit conditions limiting the employer, profession or occupation.

initial_validity.value: Up to 1 year
initial_validity.notes: The permit is conditional on the approved employment.

extension_rules.value: Normally no more than three extensions within five years; continued employment is required
extension_rules.notes: The permit may be cancelled if employment ends or changes.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, through the employer-sponsored permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent-residence category was identified.

path_to_citizenship.value: No confirmed employer-permit conversion path; naturalisation is separately available after seven years of ordinary residence and other demanding conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Ordinary permit-extension limits make continuity uncertain.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Tuvalu employer must sponsor the application.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor permit with business or employment endorsement

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No income threshold is specified.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No threshold published

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Visitor endorsement fee: AUD 100 in addition to any visitor fee
income_requirement_display.notes: The endorsement is short-term visitor permission, not qualifying residence.

income_proof_months.notes: Not specified.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain a special endorsement before undertaking business or employment; an ordinary visitor permit prohibits work and business.
Business activities expressly include professional services performed in Tuvalu, conferences, training and exploratory negotiations.

initial_validity.value: Maximum 30 days for a business or employment endorsement
initial_validity.notes: Ordinary visitor extensions may also be granted for up to 30 days under the regulations.

extension_rules.value: Short visitor extensions are discretionary and fee-based
extension_rules.notes: Visitor presence is limited and is not a settlement program.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No. This remains a visitor permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No

path_to_citizenship.value: No confirmed path from this visitor endorsement

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is visitor-like, lasts no more than 30 days and has no confirmed conversion or settlement track.

summary.value: A person may independently apply for a permit to enter and reside for study, normally for up to one year. It requires evidence supporting the study purpose and financial capacity, but the applicant's existing university degree creates no separate skilled or qualification-based immigration entitlement, and no study-to-permanent-residence conversion was found.
summary.notes: The study permit fee is AUD 300 for the principal applicant and AUD 150 per dependent. Ordinary extensions remain subject to the three-in-five-years limit.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if their permanent place of abode is in Tuvalu or if they are present for more than 183 days in any 12-month period; the presence test applies from the first day of presence. Residence generally ends only after both the Tuvalu permanent abode has ceased and the person has been absent for more than 183 days, as applicable.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The statutory definition contains special rules, including a possible ministerial exception for certain short-term Crown or statutory-corporation service.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for a resident individual. The Act states a 30% rate, while the regulations recognize an annual AUD 10,000 tax-free threshold for employment withholding; this is not an estimated effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For an employed person, the member contributes 13% of gross earnings and the employer contributes an additional 10%, for 23% total. The compulsory percentage does not automatically establish coverage for a genuinely independent foreign contractor; TNPF classification is required.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable USD monthly equivalent is supplied because there is no digital-nomad route. A registered or registrable business with a Tuvalu place of business or Tuvalu enterprise profits is generally subject to presumptive tax of AUD 100 quarterly; other Tuvalu businesses pay AUD 20 quarterly.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax concession was found. Income Tax Regulations impose quarterly presumptive tax on businesses, and the Income Tax Act applies a territorial source rule.
special_tax_regimes.notes: A business may still have normal annual income-tax obligations; presumptive tax should not be assumed to replace every liability without Revenue confirmation.

taxes.caveats: Tuvalu uses a territorial source rule, but services physically performed from Tuvalu may be treated as Tuvalu-source because the work is performed wholly or partly there. Residence, business characterization, deductions, foreign tax credits, treaty position and TNPF coverage require advice from Tuvalu Revenue and TNPF.

taxation_system.value: Territorial personal income tax: both residents and non-residents include only Tuvalu-source gross income. Resident individuals face a 30% statutory rate, with an AUD 10,000 annual tax-free threshold reflected in employment withholding rules.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of abode in Tuvalu, or more than 183 days' presence in any 12-month period from the first day of presence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Tuvalu-source income only. Income from arrangements entered into or work wholly or partly performed in Tuvalu can be allocated to a Tuvalu source, so foreign-paid remote work performed from Tuvalu is not safely treated as foreign-source.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad concession found. Registered or registrable Tuvalu businesses generally pay AUD 100 quarterly presumptive tax; other businesses pay AUD 20 quarterly.
taxation_system.social_security: TNPF requires a 13% employee contribution and a 10% employer contribution on gross earnings for an employed person. A person who is not an employed person may apply for voluntary membership, subject to the regulatory exclusions, and Schedule 1 sets voluntary contributions at not less than AUD 2 payable at any time. The rules do not prescribe a mandatory monthly amount for an ordinary independent contractor. Whether a foreign-client contractor is genuinely independent, an employed person, or eligible for voluntary membership requires TNPF classification.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The system is not conventionally progressive. The dashboard number is the 30% statutory screening rate, with an AUD 10,000 tax-free threshold/rebate mechanism rather than multiple confirmed marginal bands.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Taxable employment income up to AUD 10,000 annually
tax_brackets.notes: The regulations describe an annual tax-free threshold of AUD 10,000; a current USD approximation was intentionally omitted rather than using an unverified exchange rate.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Resident-individual taxable income above the effective tax-free threshold
tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident individual in a personal capacity
tax_brackets.notes: The Act specifies 30% and a weekly rebate designed to create a zero-rate threshold.

taxation_system.notes: The accessible official Income Tax Act is hosted by the Ministry of Finance, and the legislation portal supplies the current revised TNPF regulations. The employee rates are current and explicit; filing treatment of a foreign-client software contract and the worker’s TNPF status should still be confirmed with Tuvalu Revenue and TNPF.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Tuvalu has no confirmed digital-nomad route. A person admitted under another permit would be subject to ordinary source, residence, business and TNPF rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary resident/non-resident individual or business treatment
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 30% statutory resident-individual screening rate, subject to territorial sourcing and an AUD 10,000 employment tax-free threshold
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of abode or more than 183 days in a 12-month period, with residence under the presence test beginning from the first day.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Only Tuvalu-source income is included, but remote services physically performed in Tuvalu may be Tuvalu-source even when the client and payer are foreign.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: There is no nomad-specific payroll regime. If classified as an employed person, TNPF is 13% employee plus 10% employer on gross earnings. An eligible person who is not an employed person and is aged 6–60 may apply for voluntary membership; the minimum voluntary contribution is AUD 2 payable at any time, not a prescribed monthly minimum. The regulations exclude certain non-citizens domiciled outside Tuvalu who reside in Tuvalu solely or principally for their own or a spouse’s employment, so a foreign remote worker needs a filing-level TNPF classification.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payment; ordinary permit and business charges may apply
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No nomad-specific or mandatory self-employed monthly amount is prescribed. Compulsory employed-person rates are 13% employee plus 10% employer of gross earnings; eligible voluntary members may contribute at least AUD 2 at any time.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Business residence permit: AUD 600 for the principal applicant if lodged outside Tuvalu or AUD 1,200 if lodged inside, plus dependent fees. Visitor business endorsement: AUD 100 in addition to any visitor fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: A registered or registrable business with a Tuvalu place of business or Tuvalu enterprise profits generally pays AUD 100 quarterly presumptive tax; other businesses pay AUD 20 quarterly.
fixed_payments.notes: The AUD 2 amount is a per-payment floor for eligible voluntary members, not a monthly charge and not proof that every foreign contractor can enroll. Employee/contractor status, voluntary-member eligibility, business fees and tax filing should be confirmed with TNPF and Tuvalu Revenue.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Staying 183 days or fewer does not by itself eliminate Tuvalu tax: services physically performed in Tuvalu may already be Tuvalu-source. Visitor permission also normally prohibits work or business unless specially endorsed.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident remote worker should screen Tuvalu-source service income at the 30% statutory individual rate and obtain advice on the AUD 10,000 threshold, deductions and foreign tax credits.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A person operating a Tuvalu business may face registration/licensing, foreign-investment compliance, quarterly presumptive tax and ordinary income tax. TNPF compulsory employed-person rates do not automatically apply to a genuinely independent contractor; eligible non-employees may apply for voluntary membership with contributions of at least AUD 2 at any time, subject to the non-citizen exclusion and TNPF classification.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a hypothetical tax analysis because no ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker immigration route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A granted permit directly authorizes temporary residence; there is no preliminary residence waiting period.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No general permanent-residence status, qualifying period or automatic temporary-to-permanent conversion was identified in the official immigration legislation.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Citizenship Act uses seven years of ordinary residence rather than a separately identified permanent-residence stage.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum of seven immediately preceding years of ordinary residence, but no fitting remote-worker route reliably supports that period.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Act and fee regulations contain no standard processing-time commitment, and no current official service standard was found after focused searches.

key_conditions.value: Seven immediately preceding years of ordinary residence; intention to make Tuvalu the permanent home; at least AUD 250,000 in personal assets; familiarity with Tuvaluan laws and customs; good character; no permanent communicable disease; any other matters considered material by the Citizenship Committee; and the Oath of Allegiance.
key_conditions.notes: Dual citizenship is permitted, so general renunciation is not stated as an ordinary naturalisation requirement.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No minimum marriage duration or residence period is specified. Eligibility exists when the applicant is lawfully married at the application date to a qualifying Tuvalu citizen.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing lawful marriage can qualify immediately for citizenship registration if the Tuvalu citizen spouse falls within the statutory qualifying categories.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Registration requires an application; citizenship is not automatic on marriage.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must be at least 18, apply to the Registrar, pay the prescribed fees and prove the marriage and spouse's qualifying citizenship through documentary or oral evidence requested by the Registrar. Constitutional national-security or public-policy qualifications may apply. False evidence or a sham marriage can lead to refusal, loss of status and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The current statutory fees are AUD 100 for the registration application and AUD 500 for the registration certificate.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants citizenship to a person born in Tuvalu, subject only to narrow diplomatic-envoy and enemy-occupation exceptions. It also grants citizenship by descent to a child born abroad when either parent is a Tuvalu citizen.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Tuvalu is generally a citizen even when neither parent is a citizen or permanent resident, except for the narrow diplomatic-envoy or enemy-occupation cases.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is broad territorial birthright citizenship.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a Tuvalu citizen if born in Tuvalu and also qualifies by descent if born abroad when either parent is a Tuvalu citizen.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The constitutional wording is parent-neutral for citizenship by descent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence on a migrant parent. A discretionary permit to enter and reside exists for family reunion or family support, but no automatic parent settlement entitlement was found.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The family permit is temporary and subject to the same general extension framework.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: The migrant father may seek a family-reunion or family-support residence permit, but the child's citizenship does not automatically make the father a citizen or permanent resident.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: If the father is lawfully married to a qualifying Tuvalu citizen, the separate citizenship-by-marriage registration route may apply.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on 2026-08-15; passport indexes use different methodologies and may produce different ranks.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index's strictly visa-free category, not its broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category as displayed; electronic visas are not included in the visa-free/VOA/eTA total and may fall within the broader prior-authorization side of its methodology.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 40 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 5 eTA destinations. The index's broader mobility score is 126 when these are added to 81 visa-free destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index was used because it publishes a current route-category breakdown. This should not be mixed with Henley's broader visa-free-access count.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is an official language and the 2022 census reports English literacy among 91.2% of residents aged 15 and over, so routine communication is generally practical. Immigration forms may be completed in English or Tuvaluan.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Language practicality does not cure the absence of a suitable immigration route.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages, and no government or census evidence of meaningful local-language support was found. An applicant should expect to operate in English or Tuvaluan.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This is a cautious inference from the official-language and census evidence, not a measured count of Russian- or Ukrainian-speaking residents.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current official average monthly wage for an individual worker was found. Official HIES figures measure household or per-capita income and should not be relabeled as wages.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No official median individual wage was found after focused searches of the statistics office, census, HIES and international statistics sources.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current statutory minimum wage amount was published in the inspected Act, ILO review or EPIC country record, so there is no valid AUD amount to convert to USD.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national individual-worker mean wage was published; household income and aggregate government staffing expenditure are not converted into an average salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national individual-worker median wage was published; the household median is not converted into a worker salary.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary or worker-wage distribution ceiling was published, so no USD value is inferred.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: The Labour and Employment Relations Act establishes a Minimum Wage Board but does not set an amount. EPIC reports that no minimum wage had been set, and the ILO’s November 2025 review describes Tuvalu’s wage-setting framework as emerging; none of these current sources publishes a statutory minimum wage in AUD.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The HIES publishes household and per-capita income, while the 2025–26 Nominal Roll and 2025 IMF report publish aggregate government staffing or wage expenditure. None publishes a national mean salary per individual worker in AUD, so no household or public-budget proxy is inserted.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The HIES median of AUD 22,176 annually is household income, not an individual worker wage. The inspected 2025 ILO wage-system review and 2025–26 government Nominal Roll do not publish a national median individual salary in AUD.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No inspected current official or ILO source defines a national maximum wage or a representative upper endpoint of the worker salary distribution. Public-service staffing allocations and office-holder salary statutes are not a national maximum salary.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Individual worker wage requested; current sources publish household/per-capita income, labour-force counts, and aggregate public-sector staffing expenditure, but not national minimum, mean, median or maximum individual-worker wages
average_citizen_salary.period: Monthly requested; no valid monthly individual-worker wage statistic is published
average_citizen_salary.notes: All four local-currency salary values remain null because a current national individual-worker wage series was not published in the inspected sources. The HIES figures are household income; the Nominal Roll and IMF figures are aggregate public expenditure. Neither is relabeled as average-citizen salary.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2022–23 HIES reports average annual household expenditure of AUD 29,383 (about AUD 2,448.58 monthly) and median annual household expenditure of AUD 24,428 (about AUD 2,035.67 monthly). Food and non-alcoholic beverages represented 34% of consumption expenditure and housing 26%. These are household, not single-person, costs.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Monthly amounts are simple annual-to-monthly conversions, not inflation-adjusted 2026 budgets.

settlement_track.summary: Tuvalu has discretionary business, employment, study and family residence permits but no defined ordinary foreign-contract remote-work category. The business permit's normal extension limit does not support the seven continuous years required for naturalisation, so it is not a credible citizenship path for this profile.
settlement_track.notes: A ministerial national-interest exception exists for additional extensions, but that exceptional discretion is not a regular conversion or settlement route.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad route exists. A foreign contract does not by itself satisfy the business-permit purpose, and current rules do not confirm that a one-person foreign-client software business without Tuvalu customers or local economic substance will be approved.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed on 2026-08-15. The negative immigration-route conclusion remains supported by official legislation. TNPF rules now resolve the employed-person rates (13% employee plus 10% employer) and show that eligible voluntary members may pay at least AUD 2 at any time, but they do not prescribe a mandatory monthly amount for an ordinary independent foreign contractor; TNPF must classify the actual arrangement. Current official statistics, the November 2025 ILO wage-system review, the 2025–26 Tuvalu Nominal Roll and the 2025 IMF report do not publish national individual-worker minimum, mean, median or maximum salaries, so those local-currency values remain null rather than using household-income or aggregate-public-budget proxies. Remaining limitations are the absence of a modern immigration application portal, filing-level uncertainty under the 2025 foreign-investment framework, and no published citizenship processing standard.

data.selection_summary: Uganda has no current dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. The closest independent category, Class H, requires at least USD 36,000 per year in assured foreign-source income but also an undertaking not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activity, making it incompatible with an active foreign software contract. Class D requires a Ugandan general-trade company and substantial capital; Class F is limited to listed regulated professions; Class G2 requires a Ugandan employer. Although qualifying legal migrants can seek permanent residence or citizenship registration after 10 years, no compatible initial route was confirmed for this applicant.

visa_application.title: Uganda e-Immigration Portal
visa_application.notes: Official portal for visa, entry-permit, certificate-of-residence, and citizenship applications. It is a general portal rather than evidence of a dedicated remote-worker category.

rejected_routes.route_name: Class H Entry Permit — Ordinary Resident with Foreign-Source Assured Income

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official Class H page requires documentary proof of assured foreign-source income of at least USD 36,000 per year, equivalent to USD 3,000 per month.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official requirement is denominated in USD; no UGX equivalent or separate local-currency threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 36,000 per year (USD 3,000/month equivalent) in assured foreign-source income
income_requirement_display.notes: Class H also requires an undertaking not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activity, so active foreign employment or client earnings do not fit.

income_proof_months.notes: The official Class H page requires documentary proof of assured income but does not prescribe a fixed bank-statement or income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Documentary proof of assured income of at least USD 36,000 per year from outside Uganda.
Letter undertaking not to accept employment or engage in any income-generating activity.
Passport, photograph, applicant cover letter, current immigration status, and home-country or Interpol police clearance issued within the preceding six months.

initial_validity.value: 6, 12, 24, or 36 months
initial_validity.notes: Published Class H fees are USD 750, USD 1,500, USD 3,000, and USD 4,500 respectively; the 24- and 36-month listings state that the fee includes a USD 1,500 non-refundable component.

extension_rules.value: A still-valid Class H permit can be submitted for extension through the e-Immigration portal using the original application ID, passport number, and date of birth; the Act states that entry permits may be renewed.
extension_rules.notes: The Class H page and current extension FAQ do not publish a separate renewal duration, renewal-document checklist, filing window, or guaranteed approval rule. Renewal remains an application to the Board, and continued Class H compliance—including assured foreign income and no employment or income-generating activity—must be maintained.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved Class H entry permit provides time-limited lawful residence to an ordinary resident supported by assured foreign-source income.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not a remote-work permit because the applicant must undertake not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A Class H holder may later apply under the general certificate-of-permanent-residence rule after 10 years of continuous legal residence, but must also prove socioeconomic or intellectual contribution, good character and integrity, tax compliance, no criminal antecedents, and financial solvency; approval is discretionary.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The law does not exclude Class H time from the 10-year continuous-legal-residence test, but neither the Class H page nor the residence sources say that passive residence alone satisfies the separate contribution requirement. Because Class H forbids employment and income-generating activity, how such a holder would prove qualifying socioeconomic or intellectual contribution is fact-specific and must be accepted by the Board; this is not direct or automatic permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship registration for a person who legally migrated to and lived in Uganda is available after at least 10 years, while naturalisation requires an aggregate 20 years and 24 continuous months immediately before applying.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Eligibility is not automatic approval, and the citizenship rules do not make Class H suitable for remote employment.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because Class H expressly requires an undertaking not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activity. An active foreign employment or client contract therefore cannot be used as ordinary remote-work permission even though the income is foreign-source.

rejected_routes.route_name: Class D Entry Permit — General Trade Shareholder

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no monthly-income test. Foreign persons engaging in trade must instead demonstrate access to USD 100,000 in operating capital.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No monthly-income threshold; USD 100,000 operating capital
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official requirement is capital, not recurring income.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 100,000 operating capital; not a monthly-income route
income_requirement_display.notes: This substantial-capital trading route is excluded by the applicant profile.

income_proof_months.notes: The Class D page requests a certified company bank statement for the preceding three months.

key_requirements.requirement: Applicant must be a shareholder of a company engaged in general trade.
Certified company bank statements covering the preceding three months.
Valid trading licence, tax clearance, police clearance, passport, photograph, current immigration status, and agency covering letter.
A foreign trader must demonstrate access to USD 100,000 operating capital before trading-licence and work-permit recommendations can issue.

initial_validity.value: 6, 12, 24, or 36 months
initial_validity.notes: Published fees are USD 1,250, USD 2,500, USD 5,000, and USD 7,500 respectively.

extension_rules.value: Renewal is legally possible if the permit conditions continue to be met; the official page offers durations up to 36 months per application.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains discretionary and requires continued company, licence, tax, capital, and immigration compliance.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved Class D entry permit authorizes residence for the permit period while conducting the approved Ugandan general-trade business.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is a local-company trading route, not permission to remain solely as a foreign-contract software engineer.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After 10 years of continuous legal residence, an applicant may seek a certificate of residence if the contribution, character, tax, criminal-record, and solvency conditions are met.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official long-stay certificate page also requests evidence of employees, NSSF or PAYE contributions, and socioeconomic contribution.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship registration due to long stay is described after 10 years of legal residence and socioeconomic contribution; naturalisation is an alternative after 20 aggregate years.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Neither outcome is automatic.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the route requires a Ugandan general-trade company and substantial operating capital. It is not an ordinary low-substance foreign-client remote-work or freelance route.

rejected_routes.route_name: Class F Entry Permit — Regulated Professional Shareholder

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No UGX income threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published income threshold; company shareholding and regulated-profession registration required
income_requirement_display.notes: Software engineering is not included in the official list of eligible professions.

income_proof_months.notes: The official Class F page does not prescribe an income-proof period.

key_requirements.requirement: Shareholding in a company engaged in one of the specifically listed professions.
Registration with the relevant Ugandan professional body.
Passport, photograph, agency letter, police clearance, tax clearance, and proof of current immigration status.

initial_validity.value: 6, 12, 24, or 36 months
initial_validity.notes: Published fees are USD 1,500, USD 3,000, USD 6,000, and USD 9,000 respectively.

extension_rules.value: Renewable under the general entry-permit law while eligibility continues.
extension_rules.notes: Continuing company and professional-registration requirements apply.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: An approved Class F entry permit provides time-limited residence to practise the approved regulated profession.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The prescribed categories include specified medical, legal, engineering, accounting, architecture, surveying, veterinary, valuation, nursing, and related professions.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The general long-stay certificate-of-residence route may become available after 10 years of continuous legal residence and documented contribution.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No shorter Class F-specific permanent-residence pathway was found.

path_to_citizenship.value: General citizenship registration after 10 years of legal migration or naturalisation after 20 aggregate years may be relevant to a qualifying long-term resident.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Software engineering does not establish Class F eligibility.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because software engineering is not one of the professions listed on the current official Class F page, and the route requires company shareholding and Ugandan professional-body registration. A software degree alone does not create an independent qualification-based residence right.

rejected_routes.route_name: Class G2 Entry Permit — Locally Employed Expatriate

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No salary floor is published on the official route page.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No UGX salary floor is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published salary threshold; Ugandan appointment and labour-market evidence required
income_requirement_display.notes: The route cannot be based solely on the applicant's foreign contract.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Appointment letter and covering letter from the Ugandan employing organization.
Proof that the employer failed to find a qualified Ugandan.
Qualifications, police clearance, tax clearance, passport, photograph, current status, and employee-nationality list.

initial_validity.value: 6, 12, 24, or 36 months
initial_validity.notes: Published fees range from USD 1,250 to USD 7,500.

extension_rules.value: Renewable under the general entry-permit law while sponsored employment and all route conditions continue.
extension_rules.notes: A continuing Ugandan employer relationship is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The approved employer-sponsored entry permit authorizes time-limited residence and local employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not authorize residence based solely on a foreign employer or client.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The general certificate-of-residence route requires at least 10 years of continuous legal stay and separate contribution and compliance evidence.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: There is no direct permanent-residence grant through G2.

path_to_citizenship.value: Long-stay citizenship registration may be sought after 10 years of legal migration, or naturalisation after 20 aggregate years, subject to statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not remove the initial local-employer requirement.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Ugandan employer, appointment letter, and proof of failure to employ a qualified Ugandan are mandatory. Foreign-employer remote work is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-work income threshold exists because this is visitor permission.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: A monthly-income threshold is inapplicable to visitor status.

income_requirement_display.value: No income threshold; visitor status does not authorize employment or private business
income_requirement_display.notes: A tourist or visitor application is not a residence or self-employment legalization route.

income_proof_months.notes: The visitor page does not prescribe a route-wide income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Online visa application and approval before travel for visa-prone travellers.
Visitor status does not replace the entry permit or certificate required for employment, a profession, or private business.

initial_validity.value: Depends on the visa or visitor authorization issued
initial_validity.notes: The official page lists single- and multiple-entry visa categories but does not create remote-worker status.

extension_rules.value: Visitor extensions, where allowed, remain visitor permission and do not themselves legalize remote employment or private business.
extension_rules.notes: An extension changes the authorized visitor period, not the immigration category or work rights.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence status.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separate qualifying permit would be required.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No tourist-to-permanent-residence conversion path is established.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Long-stay permanent residence requires continuous lawful residence and separate contribution and compliance evidence; visitor extensions do not create a dedicated conversion route.

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor status alone is not an established citizenship pathway.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A qualifying long-term lawful status and all citizenship conditions would have to be established separately.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor or tourist permission is not a work or residence route and cannot be used as the basis for ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: No independent degree-only, points-tested, or qualification-based residence route was found. Class F requires company shareholding and registration in one of the prescribed regulated professions, and software engineering is not listed. Class G2 accepts graduate qualifications but requires a Ugandan employer and labour-market evidence.
summary.notes: A relevant software-engineering degree does not independently establish immigration eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they have a permanent home in Uganda, are present for at least 183 days in a financial year, or are present for more than 122 days in that year and each of the two preceding years.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breakers and the applicant's exact facts can change the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Dashboard screening value: the highest marginal burden on income above UGX 10,000,000 per month is the normal 30% rate plus an additional 10% on the excess. It is not the expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For covered employees, 5% is deducted from gross wages and the employer adds 10%. Self-employed persons can participate voluntarily; this is not a mandatory 15% charge on an independent freelancer.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly freelancer tax, compulsory self-employed NSSF minimum, or mandatory health contribution was identified. Business registration and licensing costs depend on structure and locality.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, non-dom, or general inbound-worker tax regime was identified. Limited sectoral investment and export incentives do not fit an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Investment incentives have separate capital, activity, employment, export, or licensing conditions.

taxes.caveats: Ugandan tax depends on residence, whether the contract is employment or independent business income, where services are physically performed, deductible expenses, VAT status, withholding, and any applicable double-tax treaty. A resident taxpayer's foreign-source income can be included in Ugandan gross income with foreign-tax-credit relief; professional advice is appropriate before working from Uganda.

taxation_system.value: Progressive individual income tax. Residents have a monthly tax-free band followed by 10%, 20%, and 30% bands, with an additional 10% charge on income above UGX 10,000,000 per month. Non-residents have no tax-free band and use different base amounts.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, 183-day test, or presence exceeding 122 days in the current and each of the two preceding financial years.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents may be taxed on foreign-source income included in gross income, with a foreign-tax credit subject to limits. Non-residents are generally taxed on Ugandan-source income; services physically performed in Uganda require specific source analysis.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or ordinary inbound-remote-worker regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Covered employees: 15% of gross monthly wages in total, comprising 5% employee and 10% employer. Self-employed participation is available voluntarily.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 40% dashboard number is the top marginal screening rate: income over UGX 10,000,000 per month bears the ordinary 30% computation plus an additional 10% on the excess. Lower portions are taxed at lower rates, so 40% is not an effective-rate estimate.

tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses roughly UGX 3,750 per USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: UGX 235,000–335,000 per month; 10% of excess over UGX 235,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: UGX 335,000–410,000 per month; UGX 10,000 plus 20% of excess over UGX 335,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: UGX 410,000–10,000,000 per month; UGX 25,000 plus 30% of excess over UGX 410,000
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure is the approximate upper boundary.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Above UGX 10,000,000 per month; normal 30% computation plus 10% of excess over UGX 10,000,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Top marginal portion of resident individual income
tax_brackets.notes: The combined marginal rate on the excess is 40%; this is not a flat rate on all income.

taxation_system.notes: Official URA pages provide the residence tests, individual brackets, and foreign-tax-credit treatment. Classification of a particular foreign contract remains fact-specific.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Uganda has no identified digital-nomad immigration or tax category. A person who became tax resident and lawfully performed services from Uganda would ordinarily fall within general individual tax rules rather than a nomad concession.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad route or tax category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive general PIT; top marginal screening rate 40%, not an expected effective rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home, 183 days, or the more-than-122-day multi-year presence test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: URA states that foreign-source income included in a resident taxpayer's gross income may receive a foreign-tax credit. The source and characterization of remote-service income require specific review.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The mandatory 15% NSSF contribution applies through covered employment, split 5% employee and 10% employer. Self-employed participation is voluntary on the reviewed NSSF page.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly remote-worker payment identified
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No mandatory fixed self-employed NSSF minimum identified; employee contributions are percentage-based.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad-visa fee exists. Alternative permits have category-specific fees; Class H ranges from USD 750 for six months to USD 4,500 for 36 months.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Business-name reservation is UGX 35,000 and registration is UGX 55,000. Company registration and local trading-licence costs vary. VAT registration is compulsory when taxable sales exceed UGX 37.5 million in three months or UGX 150 million in 12 months.
fixed_payments.notes: Business registration does not confer immigration permission. Local trading licences and other sector or municipal charges cannot be reduced to one universal monthly amount.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence because a permanent home or the multi-year 122-day test can apply. Non-resident Ugandan-source income may still be taxable.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: If lawful immigration permission existed and the worker became resident, general progressive PIT could apply to foreign-source income, with possible foreign-tax-credit relief.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A local business requires URSB registration, a TIN, and normally a local trading licence; non-East Africans require trade-ministry clearance. These steps do not replace an entry permit and may trigger income-tax, VAT, invoicing, and local-licence obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Confidence is below high for the hypothetical remote-worker scenario because no lawful digital-nomad route exists and contract characterization would be fact-specific.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No compatible temporary-residence route exists for ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Alternative entry permits grant status upon approval but impose incompatible no-work, business, professional, or sponsorship conditions.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: General long-stay permanent-residence eligibility requires 10 years of continuous legal stay plus contribution, integrity, tax, criminal-record, and solvency conditions. This is contextual, not a timeline from a qualifying remote-worker route.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Permanent residence is not stated as a prerequisite for long-stay citizenship registration. Both provisions use a 10-year legal-residence threshold, so eligibility may overlap; approval is not automatic.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Contextual earliest statutory long-stay registration threshold for a qualifying legal migrant, not a confirmed timeline for this applicant. Naturalisation separately requires 20 aggregate years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current citizenship route pages and service-delivery-standards material checked do not publish a reliable typical end-to-end processing time in months.

key_conditions.value: Long-stay citizenship registration requires legal migration and at least 10 years' residence; the official route also requests evidence of occupation, achievements or innovations, tax compliance, referees, local recommendations, and valid current status. Naturalisation requires 20 aggregate years, 24 continuous months immediately before filing, adequate English or a prescribed vernacular language, good character, and intent to reside permanently.
key_conditions.notes: The immigration authority's documentary assessment and decision remain decisive.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Citizenship registration requires a legal and subsisting marriage of at least five years; the current filing page additionally asks for evidence of five years' continuous legal stay in Uganda. Permanent residence may be available after three years of subsisting marriage.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Ugandan can count toward the five-year marriage period, but the citizenship checklist separately requires five years of continuous legal stay in Uganda. A person married to a Ugandan may seek permanent residence after a three-year subsisting marriage under the Act.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A marriage conducted outside Uganda must be appropriately certified for filing.

requirements_and_risks.value: The citizenship checklist includes a marriage certificate, spouse support, proof of the spouse's Ugandan citizenship, five years of continuous legal stay, police clearance, medical report, referees, local-security recommendations, occupation evidence, oath, and fees. The Act permits cancellation of marriage-based permanent residence obtained through a marriage of convenience, and dissolution can end that certificate.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage must be genuine and legally subsisting; sham-marriage filings create cancellation and enforcement risk.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Uganda alone does not generally confer citizenship. Citizenship by birth depends primarily on qualifying indigenous-community ancestry or a parent or grandparent who was a Ugandan citizen by birth; a foundling aged no more than five with unknown parents is presumed a citizen.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Uganda to two ordinary migrant parents does not acquire citizenship merely by local birth. Qualifying Ugandan-by-birth ancestry or the narrow foundling rule could change the result.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This assumes neither parent nor grandparent satisfies the statutory citizenship-by-birth ancestry rules.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child is a citizen by birth when a parent or grandparent was, at the child's birth, a Ugandan citizen by birth. The reviewed provision does not support an unconditional statement for every registered or naturalised Ugandan parent, so the citizen parent's citizenship category must be checked.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The generic boolean remains null to avoid overstating citizenship for every category of Ugandan parent.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a citizen child does not automatically grant either migrant parent permanent residence or citizenship. Any family-based residence or citizenship filing remains separate and must meet its own statutory category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed law does not establish an automatic parent-regularisation right solely from the child's citizenship.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence arises for the migrant father. A citizen child's status may be relevant evidence in a discretionary family or dependency matter, but no direct father-to-residence entitlement is established in the reviewed law.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The father must qualify independently for immigration status or citizenship.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the research date; rankings are dynamic.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count, not the broader mobility score.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required category.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined value: 31 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 5 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately reports a mobility score of 70.

passport.notes: Passport Index was used because it exposes the required category breakdown. Passport access figures can change at any time.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is Uganda's primary official language, so administration, contracts, and ordinary professional communication in English are practical. Connectivity and service quality still vary by location.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The practical conclusion is an inference from English's constitutional official status; no nationwide remote-work infrastructure score was used.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low outside personal or expatriate networks. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official status, while the Constitution identifies English and Swahili as official languages.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The current sources checked do not establish widespread Russian- or Ukrainian-language public services.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of UGX 539,379 average monthly earnings per employee using roughly UGX 3,750 per USD. The source is the Uganda Business Inquiry 2019/20.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official UGX 200,000 median monthly cash earnings for paid employment in 2023/24.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the nominal UGX 6,000 statutory minimum. The ILO notes that it has not been adjusted since 1984 and is not a meaningful living-wage measure.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion; the underlying average is UGX 539,379 per employee per month from the Uganda Business Inquiry 2019/20.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD conversion of the 2023/24 national median monthly cash earnings for paid employment.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national maximum local-currency salary is published in the official wage sources checked, so there is no defensible maximum to convert to USD. Sector averages, subgroup medians, and public-service salary scales are not an observed national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Nominal national statutory minimum unchanged since 1984; it is not a realistic observed wage floor or living-wage estimate.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average monthly earnings per employee across sectors covered by the Uganda Business Inquiry 2019/20.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median monthly cash earnings for persons in paid employment in 2023/24.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful national maximum monthly salary is published in the current official sources checked. The 2023/24 household survey reports national and subgroup medians; the business inquiry reports averages; the 2025 labour-market and 2023/24 human-resource publications describe labour-market or salary-scale distributions; and the public-service report covers government salary scales. None establishes the highest observed monthly salary across all Ugandan workers, so a numeric maximum would be misleading.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly earnings per employee from the 2019/20 Uganda Business Inquiry; median monthly cash earnings of paid employees from the 2023/24 household survey; nominal statutory minimum from ILO supervisory reporting
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: 2019/20; median: 2023/24; minimum: unchanged since 1984 and reviewed by ILO in 2024
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are citizen or resident labour-market indicators, not immigration income requirements. The average is older than the median and may overrepresent establishments covered by the business inquiry; the statutory minimum is obsolete in practical purchasing-power terms. Focused checks of newer UBOS labour-market and human-resource publications did not identify a national maximum salary.

cost_of_living_note.value: The 2023/24 household survey reported average monthly household expenditure per person of approximately UGX 130,950, with large regional and household-size differences. This is a national household-survey measure, not an expatriate or Kampala remote-worker budget.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Approximately USD 35 per person at UGX 3,750/USD. Housing, imported goods, private healthcare, coworking, and reliable connectivity can make an individual remote worker's actual budget substantially higher.
