settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Uganda has no identified digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker permit. Class H is residence-oriented but requires an undertaking not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activity, so it cannot accommodate this active foreign contract.
settlement_track.summary: Uganda is not valid for this profile because every identified initial status is incompatible: Class H forbids employment and income-generating activity, Class D requires substantial trading capital and a local company, Class F is limited to prescribed professions, and G2 requires a Ugandan employer. Ten-year permanent-residence and citizenship rules exist, but there is no compatible route from which this ordinary remote worker can begin that track.
settlement_track.notes: The previous false verdict is preserved. The audit adds the current Class H threshold and duration, extension mechanics, a more precise explanation of the discretionary permanent-residence contribution condition, and focused official wage-source checks.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No ordinary route permits a software engineer to reside independently while working under a foreign employer or client contract. Class H's foreign-income feature is not a match because the holder must undertake not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activity.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed using more than 15 directly relevant URLs, including more than five URLs absent from the previous source set. Class H's USD 36,000 annual threshold and 6–36 month durations are now established. Its renewal details beyond portal mechanics and the Board's assessment of permanent-residence contribution remain discretionary as precisely explained. A national maximum salary remains null because the named official sources publish medians, averages, subgroup results, or salary-scale distributions rather than an all-worker maximum.

data.selection_summary: Ukraine does not offer a current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary foreign-client freelance residence route. The employment-based temporary residence permit requires a Ukrainian employer or qualifying local entity, while registering as an entrepreneur does not itself provide a residence basis. Investor/founder and discretionary high-skilled immigration categories do not fit an ordinary foreign-contract software engineer.

visa_application.title: Issuance of temporary residence permit
visa_application.notes: This is the official information page for Ukraine's temporary residence categories. No dedicated remote-worker application channel was found; the page instead confirms employment, study, family, investment and other specific bases.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employment or Diia City gig-contract temporary residence permit

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No foreign-remote income threshold applies; this is a Ukrainian-employment route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No generally applicable minimum salary threshold was established on the official route pages reviewed.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-income threshold; qualifying Ukrainian employment or gig contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial evidence does not replace the required Ukrainian employment basis.

income_proof_months.notes: The official residence page does not prescribe a remote-income evidence period.

key_requirements.requirement: A Ukrainian employer, or the relevant Ukrainian resident entity for a qualifying gig arrangement, must obtain or support the required employment authorization.
Passport, lawful stay or appropriate long-stay visa where required, health-insurance policy, employment authorization and the employer/entity undertaking or contract documents.

initial_validity.value: Duration of the employment contract or authorized work period
initial_validity.notes: The official page states that an employment-based permit is issued for the contract term.

extension_rules.value: Exchange/renewal requires the qualifying Ukrainian employment basis to continue
extension_rules.notes: Loss of the supporting employment basis can require cancellation or non-renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence after the qualifying Ukrainian employment documentation is obtained

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least five years of continuous residence on qualifying employment or gig-contract temporary-residence permits, the person may apply for an immigration permit under Article 4(2)(11) of the Law on Immigration; after that permit is granted, the person may apply for a permanent-residence permit. This is not an automatic conversion.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The earlier uncertainty is resolved by current primary sources. Employment and gig-contract residence falls under Article 4(4) of the Law on the Legal Status of Foreigners and Stateless Persons. Effective 5 August 2025, Article 4(2)(11) of the Law on Immigration covers persons in parts 4–6, 8–12 and 15 of that law after five years of continuous residence on temporary-residence permits. The applicant must document the five-year period, satisfy the statutory continuity limits, obtain an immigration-permit decision, and then apply for the permanent-residence card; elapsed time alone does not grant PR. The DMS explains that immigration quotas are imposed only if the migration situation triggers them, but ordinary eligibility remains subject to adjudication and refusal grounds.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization can be available after five years of continuous lawful residence and satisfaction of the citizenship conditions, but the employment TRP does not itself guarantee immigration permission or permanent residence
path_to_citizenship.notes: This does not make the route valid for the target foreign contract because Ukrainian employment is required.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the applicant's unchanged foreign-client or foreign-employer contract cannot substitute for a Ukrainian employer or resident entity.

rejected_routes.route_name: Founder or participant temporary residence based on a substantial Ukrainian investment

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The requirement is capital investment, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official threshold is denominated in euros rather than UAH income.

income_requirement_display.value: At least EUR 100,000 ownership contribution/investment in a Ukrainian legal entity
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: EUR 100,000 investment; not a monthly-income test
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a substantial-capital founder/investor route and is excluded for the ordinary remote-worker profile.

income_proof_months.notes: Not an income-history route.

key_requirements.requirement: Founder, participant or beneficial-owner status in a Ukrainian legal entity and a qualifying ownership contribution of at least EUR 100,000.
Constituent and investment evidence plus the Ukrainian entity's undertaking to notify the migration service if the qualifying status ends.

initial_validity.value: 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Official duration for the qualifying founder/participant category.

extension_rules.value: Exchange is possible while the qualifying investment and ownership basis continues

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct temporary residence on the qualifying investment basis

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion; a separate immigration-permit category is required

path_to_citizenship.value: No special investor citizenship track was confirmed; general naturalization conditions would apply through a separately qualifying residence history

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it requires substantial investment and local corporate substance, which the applicant profile does not assume.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No digital-nomad income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-work income threshold; visitor status only
income_requirement_display.notes: Visitor or e-Visa permission is not a residence or settlement route.

income_proof_months.notes: No remote-income evidence period applies.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligible nationality, passport, permitted visit purpose and ordinary visa supporting documents.

initial_validity.value: E-Visas are generally single- or double-entry visas allowing visits of up to 30 days
initial_validity.notes: Eligibility and permitted purposes must be checked on the current MFA portal.

extension_rules.value: No remote-worker renewal or settlement conversion was found

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None merely from visitor or e-Visa status; a separate statutory residence basis is required

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None

path_to_citizenship.value: Visitor time is not established as a qualifying independent citizenship route

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor and e-Visa permission is not a digital-nomad residence status and does not create a citizenship-oriented residence chain.

summary.value: Enrollment and actual study at a Ukrainian educational institution can support a study temporary residence permit without a local employer. An already-held software-engineering degree does not independently qualify the applicant, and study residence does not directly grant permanent residence.
summary.notes: The institution must document actual study and undertake to notify the migration service if enrollment ends. This is a study route, not an independent degree-recognition or foreign-remote-work route.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence is determined through permanent home, centre of vital interests and related statutory tests, with presence of at least 183 days in a tax year serving as an important fallback indicator.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Citizenship and treaty tie-breaker rules can also affect the result; 183 days should not be treated as the only test.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Flat personal income-tax screening rate for ordinary employment, civil-contract and foreign income. A separate 5% military levy generally applies to foreign income accrued or paid from 1 January 2025.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Single social contribution rate for relevant employers, entrepreneurs and self-employed persons. The contribution base and exemptions depend on status.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate USD equivalent of the 2026 minimum single social contribution of UAH 1,902.34, using roughly UAH 41.8/USD. It applies where the person is registered in a covered entrepreneurial/self-employed category; it is not a digital-nomad fee.

special_tax_regimes.value: Ukraine has simplified taxation regimes for registered individual entrepreneurs, including fixed or turnover-based taxes depending on group. These regimes do not create immigration status and eligibility depends on registration, activity, clients, turnover and other tax rules.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The sources reviewed did not establish that a foreigner may use entrepreneur registration as a substitute for a lawful residence basis.

taxes.caveats: There is no digital-nomad tax regime. A Ukrainian tax resident receiving foreign income generally faces 18% PIT plus the applicable military levy, subject to treaty relief and documented foreign-tax credits. Entrepreneur treatment, social contributions, VAT and source rules depend on registration and contract structure; professional advice is appropriate.

taxation_system.value: Mixed system: ordinary foreign or civil-contract income is generally subject to flat 18% PIT plus a separate 5% military levy, while registered entrepreneurs may qualify for simplified regimes. Social contribution can apply separately.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home and centre-of-vital-interests tests apply, with 183 days as a fallback indicator and treaty tie-breakers potentially relevant.
taxation_system.income_scope: Ukrainian tax residents generally declare Ukrainian and foreign income; documented foreign taxes may be creditable within statutory and treaty limits.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Simplified individual-entrepreneur regimes exist but do not confer immigration status and were not treated as a remote-worker visa.
taxation_system.social_security: Relevant entrepreneurs and self-employed persons generally face a 22% single social contribution. The 2026 minimum contribution is UAH 1,902.34 per month, subject to statutory exemptions.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Ordinary personal income is not taxed through progressive brackets for this screening scenario; the 5% military levy is separate from the 18% PIT figure.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Ordinary taxable employment, civil-contract and foreign income; no general progressive threshold
tax_brackets.notes: The separate military levy is not included in this bracket.

taxation_system.notes: The displayed 18% is a flat PIT screening rate, not the complete burden. For foreign income from 2025 onward, the official tax authority states a separate 5% military levy generally applies.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Ukraine has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence program. If the person independently becomes a Ukrainian tax resident, foreign income is generally taxable under the ordinary rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; ordinary individual or registered entrepreneur rules only
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 18% PIT plus generally 5% military levy on foreign income; entrepreneur regimes require separate lawful registration
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home and centre-of-vital-interests tests, with 183 days as a fallback indicator and possible treaty tie-breakers.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents generally declare foreign income; foreign-tax credits require appropriate evidence and are limited by domestic and treaty rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific contribution. Registered entrepreneurs or self-employed persons may owe the 22% single social contribution, with a 2026 minimum of UAH 1,902.34 per month where applicable.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed payment; entrepreneur payments may apply after valid registration
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Minimum single social contribution: UAH 1,902.34/month in 2026 where applicable.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad visa fee exists. Fees depend on the separate visa or residence category.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: For 2026, first- and second-group entrepreneurs have locally set single-tax limits and a UAH 864.70 monthly military levy; these groups are not assumed suitable for the applicant's foreign-client activity.
fixed_payments.notes: Entrepreneur tax registration must not be confused with immigration authorization.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being present for fewer than 183 days does not automatically guarantee non-residence because permanent-home and centre-of-vital-interests tests can control. Visitor status also does not establish permission for a long-term remote-work stay.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Ordinary foreign income is generally subject to 18% PIT plus the applicable 5% military levy, with treaty and foreign-tax-credit analysis required.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Simplified or general entrepreneur taxation and social contributions may apply, but FOP registration alone does not create a temporary-residence basis.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax information is current, but it does not cure the absence of a qualifying immigration route.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent foreign-contract route exists. Other bases can grant temporary residence immediately after approval, but require employment, study, family, investment or another statutory ground.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No qualifying independent foreign-contract route exists. For the rejected Ukrainian employment/gig-contract route, current law creates eligibility to apply for an immigration permit after five years of continuous residence on qualifying temporary-residence permits; approval and the later PR-card application are not automatic.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization uses a five-year continuous-residence condition rather than a simple fixed number of years after PR; the applicant must also hold an immigration permit where required and satisfy all other conditions.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory continuous-residence threshold, not a timeline available through the rejected foreign-contract scenario.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official page states that total handling is generally no more than one year where no additional examination is needed; internal migration-service review for presidential cases should not exceed eight months.

key_conditions.value: Generally five years of continuous lawful residence, an immigration permit, command of Ukrainian, knowledge of Ukraine's Constitution and history under current rules, lawful sources of subsistence, compliance with the Constitution and laws, and satisfaction of current multiple-citizenship or termination/declaration requirements. Absence limits and exceptions must be checked for the applicant's category.
key_conditions.notes: Citizenship law and procedures changed in 2026; filing-level verification is essential.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Marriage to a Ukrainian citizen for longer than two years is an immigration-permit/PR category. For naturalization, the ordinary five-year continuous-residence condition does not apply where the marriage has lasted more than three years, although other citizenship requirements remain.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A genuine existing marriage can support family-reunification temporary residence; after more than two years of marriage to a Ukrainian citizen it can support an immigration permit. A marriage validly concluded abroad may be recognized under Ukrainian private-international-law rules.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not itself grant citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants must document a legally valid, subsisting marriage and the Ukrainian spouse's identity/status. Migration and citizenship authorities may verify the factual and legal basis; fictitious marriage, false documents or misrepresentation can lead to refusal, cancellation and other liability. Language, exams, lawful income and other naturalization requirements can still apply.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The shortened rules depend on marriage duration and the precise immigration or citizenship application.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Ukraine primarily transmits citizenship through a Ukrainian parent. Birth-based citizenship also covers specified anti-statelessness, refugee-parent and foundling cases, but birth in Ukraine alone is not sufficient in the ordinary case.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not ordinarily from birth in Ukraine alone. Citizenship can arise where the statutory conditions are met, notably when qualifying resident foreign parents do not transmit another citizenship, where parents have protected or stateless status, or for a foundling.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: The boolean is false for ordinary foreign parents because the outcome is conditional on their status and the child's acquisition of another nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If either parent was a Ukrainian citizen when the child was born, the child is a Ukrainian citizen from birth regardless of the place of birth.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A Ukrainian-citizen child can place a foreign parent within the immigration-permit category for parents of Ukrainian citizens, but the parent must apply and satisfy the immigration procedure. Citizenship is not automatic.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Ukrainian-citizen child may apply under the family immigration category as a parent of a Ukrainian citizen. The child does not automatically transmit Ukrainian citizenship to the father, and documentary parentage plus all immigration requirements must be established.

rank.notes: Henley's January 2026 report states that Ukraine had risen to 30th place. A frequently updated secondary table displayed 31st when checked, so the dated primary Henley report is used for rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: The secondary country table reports visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 142 destinations. Henley's accessible primary press page confirmed rank but did not expose Ukraine's score in static page text.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The reviewed Henley interface and secondary table did not publish a stable aggregate count limited to destinations requiring a visa in advance; it was not inferred from the 227-destination universe because restricted and other categories complicate subtraction.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Practical Russian use varies considerably by region and individual circumstances.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Ukraine has no confirmed digital-nomad status. Visitor permission and entrepreneur registration cannot be treated as a qualifying settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route starts a qualifying residence chain. Ukraine has general naturalization and separate immigration-permit categories, but the applicant would need a materially different basis such as Ukrainian employment, qualifying family ties, study followed by another basis, or substantial investment.
settlement_track.notes: The five-year general citizenship rule does not cure the absence of an eligible entry/residence route for this profile.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The official residence categories reviewed contain no dedicated foreign-employer or foreign-client remote-work basis. Employment requires a Ukrainian employer or qualifying resident entity, while visitor status and FOP registration do not independently legalize long-term residence.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous Ukraine record. At least 15 directly relevant URLs were inspected, including eight canonical URLs absent from the previous source set. Current primary law resolves the flagged PR-transition note: qualifying Ukrainian employment/gig-contract TRP holders may apply for an immigration permit after five years of continuous TRP residence, and may obtain PR only after that permit is granted; this is neither automatic nor available on the applicant’s unchanged foreign contract. The country therefore remains invalid for selection. Other cautious nulls are preserved with their existing factual explanations.

data.selection_summary: The five-year renewable Green Residency for freelancers/self-employed people is self-sponsored and could fit a degree-qualified foreign-client software engineer who obtains the required MoHRE permit and documents AED 360,000 annual freelance income in each of the previous two years. Official sources do not clearly confirm that a contractor serving only foreign clients can obtain the permit without additional UAE licensing, or that Green Residency time counts toward the discretionary 30-year naturalisation provision. The separate Virtual Work Residence fits foreign employment but is a one-year renewable temporary status with no confirmed settlement conversion. Filing-level verification is required; the UAE is not fully matched.

visa_application.title: ICP Green Residency
visa_application.notes: Official federal information for the potentially settlement-relevant freelance/self-employed Green Residency. The page describes eligibility but does not expose a clearly route-specific public application form. Verify the required MoHRE freelance/self-employment permit and filing sequence with ICP before applying.

The eligibility test is annual freelance income in each of the previous two years, not current monthly salary; official rules alternatively mention financial solvency.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Equivalent screening amount is AED 30,000 monthly, but eligibility is expressed as a two-year annual-income test.

Hold at least a bachelor's degree, specialised diploma or equivalent.
Show stable income or financial solvency and normally at least AED 360,000 annual freelance income in each of the previous two years.
Meet residence formalities including a passport valid for at least six months, medical fitness, health insurance, competent-authority approval and applicable guarantee/residence documents.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed official sources identify no ordinary permanent-residence status or conversion from Green Residency. Renewable five-year residence is not legally permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: The nationality law allows discretionary naturalisation of a qualifying non-Arab applicant after at least 30 years of continuous legal residence, with lawful income, good conduct and Arabic proficiency, plus general qualification, security-approval, allegiance and ordinarily renunciation requirements. Official sources do not specifically confirm how Green Residency time is assessed or create an entitlement to citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The statute uses discretionary language. This is an exceptionally long and weak citizenship track, not a guaranteed residence-to-citizenship program.

best_routes.notes: This is the most relevant independent residence-oriented route. It potentially fits foreign-client self-employment, but official material does not clearly explain whether an applicant serving only foreign clients can obtain the MoHRE permit without additional UAE licensing, establishment, activity or nomination steps. That issue and citizenship residence counting require manual confirmation.

Passport valid for at least six months, personal photo, valid health insurance and medical-fitness formalities.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct one-year virtual-work residence after completing entry and residence formalities
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The GDRFA entry visa permits 60 days to complete residence issuance.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: A uniform monthly-income value is inapplicable. Categories use different capital, project revenue/value, salary, nomination, achievement, education or service tests.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No single local-currency income threshold governs the combined route. Examples include AED 2 million investment/property/deposit, AED 250,000 annual tax, entrepreneur project tests and AED 30,000 monthly salary for Dubai specialised professionals.

income_requirement_display.value: No uniform remote-worker threshold; category-specific capital, project, salary, nomination or achievement tests apply
income_requirement_display.notes: Official sources publish no single monthly-income test across Golden Residency. Investor categories use AED 2 million capital/property/deposit or AED 250,000 annual tax; entrepreneur categories use project value, revenue, incubator or authority approval, or prior-sale tests; Dubai's specialised-professional category requires UAE employment and AED 30,000 monthly salary, while ICP lists AED 50,000 for executive directors. Many talent, student and humanitarian categories instead use nomination, achievement, education or service criteria. The numeric income fields therefore remain null for this combined rejected route because a uniform remote-worker threshold is inapplicable, not unpublished.

income_proof_months.notes: No uniform period applies. Dubai specialised professionals must show six months of salary transfers, while investment and other categories use different documentary tests.

key_requirements.requirement: Eligibility depends on an exceptional-talent, advanced-specialist, investor, entrepreneur, high-achieving student or comparable designated category rather than ordinary foreign-contract software work.

initial_validity.value: 5 or 10 years depending on category and applicable authority rules
initial_validity.notes: Renewable long-term residence for most qualifying categories, not permanent residence. Official federal and Dubai materials differ on the stated entrepreneur duration, so the filing authority's current service card must be checked.

extension_rules.value: Generally renewable subject to continued category eligibility; some student categories are not renewable
extension_rules.notes: Renewal rules are category-specific.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct long-term renewable residence for designated qualifying categories
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It remains a time-limited residence permit despite the 'Golden' label.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Official descriptions provide five- or ten-year residence, not an ordinary permanent-residence entitlement.

path_to_citizenship.value: Certain investors and exceptional specialists or talents may be nominated for citizenship, but ordinary residence does not create nomination eligibility or an entitlement
path_to_citizenship.notes: Outside the applicant's ordinary remote-worker profile.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it depends on investment, entrepreneurship, exceptional achievement, high-level local employment, academic excellence or nomination rather than ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: A degree helps qualify a freelancer/self-employed applicant for Green Residency, but the route also requires a MoHRE freelance/self-employment permit and substantial prior freelance income or solvency. The separate skilled-worker category requires a valid UAE employment contract, so education alone does not provide independent residence.
summary.notes: The employer-free answer refers only to the freelancer/self-employed category; there is no degree-only permanent-residence route.

tax_residency_rule.value: For UAE domestic purposes, a natural person may be resident by being physically present for at least 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period; by spending 90–182 days while also being a UAE citizen or resident with UAE employment, business or a permanent home; or by having both a usual or primary residence and centre of financial and personal interests in the UAE. Treaty residence can apply different tie-breakers.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Tax residence is separate from immigration residence and does not settle residence under another country's law or a tax treaty.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: General personal-income-tax screening rate, not a corporate or self-employment business rate. The UAE does not levy personal income tax on individuals.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No UAE pension scheme was identified for ordinary non-GCC expatriate workers. Private health insurance, home-country social security, contractual payroll obligations and special GCC-national rules may still apply.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly tax or social-security payment applies to this foreign remote-worker scenario. Insurance premiums vary, while visa and ID charges are transactional or annual rather than fixed monthly taxes.

special_tax_regimes.value: No special digital-nomad personal-income-tax regime was identified; the general 0% individual PIT position applies. A natural person conducting business in the UAE enters corporate-tax scope only when annual business turnover exceeds AED 1 million; wages, personal investment income and real-estate investment income are excluded from that business test.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Whether foreign-client contracting constitutes a UAE business activity is fact-sensitive and should be reviewed professionally.

taxes.caveats: The 0% PIT headline does not make every structure tax-free. A freelancer carrying on business in the UAE may face corporate-tax registration and 9% tax on taxable business income above the applicable threshold; VAT registration can arise when UAE taxable supplies or imports exceed AED 375,000. Home-country residence, treaty rules, permanent-establishment exposure, foreign payroll/social-security law, licensing, insurance and emirate-level fees require separate review.

taxation_system.value: The UAE has no general personal income tax. A natural person's UAE business activity with calendar-year turnover above AED 1 million can fall under corporate tax; wages and specified personal investment and real-estate investment income are excluded. General corporate-tax rates are 0% on the first AED 375,000 of taxable income and 9% above it.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: 183-day test; alternative 90-day test with specified UAE connections; or primary-residence and centre-of-interests test, subject to treaty rules.
taxation_system.income_scope: No general individual PIT. Separate corporate-tax rules can apply to UAE business activity by a natural person; foreign-client contracting requires fact-specific classification.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated nomad PIT holiday was identified because general individual PIT is 0%.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary non-GCC expatriates are not covered by a UAE pension scheme; variable health-insurance and possible home-country obligations remain.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Personal income tax is not progressive because general PIT is 0%. The separate 0% and 9% corporate-tax bands concern taxable business income, not personal salary, and are not PIT brackets.
taxation_system.notes: High confidence in the general statutory framework; contract-specific classification requires the actual agreement and operating facts.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: A virtual-work employee generally faces 0% UAE personal income tax. A Green Residency freelancer may also have no PIT, but corporate tax can apply if the person conducts business in the UAE and annual business turnover exceeds AED 1 million. The first AED 375,000 of taxable business income is generally taxed at 0% and the excess at 9%.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: remote employee or self-employed natural person, depending on route and contract
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% general personal income tax; possible separate 9% corporate tax on qualifying taxable business income above AED 375,000 once the natural-person business-turnover test is met
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Domestic residence can arise at 183 days, under a qualifying 90-day test, or through primary residence plus centre of interests; treaties may modify the result.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: There is no general individual PIT on foreign salary. Foreign-client business receipts may require corporate-tax analysis if the activity is conducted as a business in the UAE.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No separate nomad tax regime identified; the ordinary no-PIT framework applies.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No UAE pension scheme for ordinary non-GCC expatriates was identified. Mandatory health insurance varies in cost; foreign payroll or home-country social-security rules may still apply.

fixed_payments.status: route-dependent fees; no universal fixed monthly tax
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No fixed UAE pension contribution identified for an ordinary non-GCC remote worker; health-insurance premiums vary.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Federal Virtual Work information lists AED 300 in core application, issuance and smart-service fees. Dubai lists AED 200 plus 5% VAT, AED 10 knowledge, AED 10 innovation and AED 500 inside-country fee when applicable. Resident Emirates ID renewal is AED 100 per year plus AED 100 smart-service fee.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration is mandatory for a UAE-resident business when taxable supplies/imports exceed AED 375,000 over the previous 12 months or are expected to exceed it in the next 30 days. A tax-residency certificate for a natural person without a corporate-tax TRN carries AED 50 submission plus AED 1,000 electronic-certificate review/issuance fee.
fixed_payments.notes: Insurance, medical testing, typing, delivery, guarantee, status-change and emirate-specific charges can add to headline fees.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: UAE PIT remains 0%, but the person may continue to be tax resident elsewhere and can still create UAE business, VAT, licensing or permanent-establishment issues.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A foreign employee normally has no UAE PIT on salary, but should document treaty residence and examine foreign payroll and social-security obligations.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Assess the AED 1 million natural-person corporate-tax turnover threshold, 0%/9% taxable-income bands, AED 375,000 VAT threshold, licensing and bookkeeping requirements.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: General rules are well supported by official sources. Contract-specific treatment remains uncertain because the distinction between foreign-employment wages and UAE-conducted freelance business is factual.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: A qualifying applicant applies directly for temporary Green Residency; no prior residence period is prescribed.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No ordinary permanent-residence stage or conversion timeline is published. Renewable five- or ten-year residence is not permanent residence.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Nationality law uses continuous legal residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence stage, so no after-PR interval applies.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Statutory minimum continuous legal residence for a non-Arab applicant under the general provision. Grant remains discretionary, and official sources do not expressly confirm Green Residency counting or create an entitlement after 30 years.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: Official law and government guidance publish no routine processing standard for ordinary naturalisation; the decision is discretionary.

key_conditions.value: For the general 30-year provision: continuous legal residence, lawful income, good conduct, no disqualifying convictions and Arabic proficiency. General grant conditions also include educational qualification, security approval, allegiance and ordinarily renunciation of other nationality. Exceptional nominated categories may follow different rules.
key_conditions.notes: The government page states that nominated exceptional categories may retain their original nationality; that exception should not be assumed for ordinary naturalisation.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign woman married to a UAE national may be granted citizenship seven years after submitting the application if the couple has at least one child, or after ten years without children, while the marriage continues. This is gender-specific and discretionary.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a UAE-national man can support the statutory route for a foreign wife, but the seven- or ten-year period runs from submission of the nationality application, not automatically from the wedding. No equivalent simplified citizenship route was identified for a foreign husband of an Emirati woman.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: For the presumed male applicant, marriage to an Emirati woman should not be treated as a citizenship shortcut.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must continue. A qualifying widow or divorcee with children of the Emirati husband may retain eligibility under specified residence and remarriage conditions. Citizenship is discretionary, and false documents or sham relationships can cause refusal, cancellation and other legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The law establishes gendered timelines but publishes no routine approval probability or processing time.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is primarily by descent through an Emirati father. Limited rules cover an Emirati mother where the father is unknown or stateless or filiation is unproved, foundlings, and a discretionary post-birth route for children of an Emirati mother and foreign father. UAE birth alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in the UAE to two known foreign parents does not become Emirati merely by birth. Narrow foundling, unknown-parent and anti-statelessness provisions do not create general jus soli.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: A UAE birth certificate is not proof of Emirati nationality.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If the local parent is an Emirati father, the child is a citizen by operation of law whether born in the UAE or abroad. If the local parent is an Emirati mother and the father is foreign, citizenship is not equivalently automatic; the law permits a grant after at least six years from birth subject to implementing rules. If the father is unknown or stateless, stronger maternal-descent rules apply.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Because the result depends on which parent is Emirati and the father's status, the normalized one-parent boolean remains null.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalise a foreign father. Any family-residence benefit requires a separate family sponsorship or residence basis, and the foreign husband of an Emirati woman has no equivalent seven-year spousal citizenship shortcut.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The reviewed official sources establish no automatic permanent-residence or citizenship benefit for a migrant father solely because his child is Emirati.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the child's mother is Emirati, the child may be Emirati automatically only in specified paternal-status cases or may later receive a discretionary grant where the father is foreign. The migrant father does not receive citizenship automatically and must maintain a separate lawful residence basis.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Potential family sponsorship is not permanent residence or citizenship.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index (rank/access); Passport Index 2026 (category breakdown)

rank.notes: July 2026 Henley update; the UAE shares second place with Japan and South Korea.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's access score combines destinations accessible without a prior visa, including visa-on-arrival access; it is not a strict visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index 2026 category count; methodology differs from Henley.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index lists 44 visa-on-arrival and 10 eTA destinations; combined here. Fast-track eVisa destinations are excluded.

passport.notes: The UAE passport is exceptionally strong, but passport strength should not be confused with accessibility of citizenship through Green or Virtual Work residence.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High. Arabic is the national official language, but official UAE information states that road, traffic and commercial signs use Arabic and English, and Dubai's tourism authority identifies English as commonly spoken. English-only remote work and daily life are generally practical in major expatriate centres, although Arabic controls many legal and official contexts.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English is authorised in specified court contexts but is not the national official language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian has some expatriate-community and institutional usefulness—the government fact sheet lists it among additional court languages—but neither Russian nor Ukrainian is a national official language. English remains the safer default for government, banking, housing and remote-work logistics.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable nationwide measurement of Russian- or Ukrainian-language service availability was identified; availability varies by emirate and provider.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of Numbeo's June 2026 crowdsourced UAE average monthly net salary of AED 11,639.48 at AED 3.6725/USD. This is not an official wage statistic.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official UAE.Stat portal and ILOSTAT catalogue were checked, but they did not provide an extractable current nationwide median employee wage. It remains null rather than being inferred from the average.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate equivalent of the AED 6,000 minimum monthly wage applying specifically to Emiratis in the private sector from 1 January 2026. It is not a general expatriate minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Crowdsourced average net salary for UAE residents and workers, not a citizen-only average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official/statistical sources did not provide an extractable current national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful statutory or observed nationwide maximum salary is published.

min_salary_local_currency.value: AED 6,000/month for Emiratis in the private sector; no general Labour Law minimum for expatriate private-sector workers
min_salary_local_currency.notes: The AED 6,000 floor is citizenship- and sector-specific.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Numbeo country average updated June 2026; not official and not citizen-only.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected statistics sources do not publish an extractable current nationwide median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No meaningful nationwide maximum is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Minimum: citizenship- and sector-specific wage floor for Emirati private-sector employees. Average: crowdsourced monthly net salary for residents/workers. Median and maximum remain null after official and international statistical checks.
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum effective 2026; average updated June 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is suitable only for rough comparison because it is crowdsourced; a sufficiently clear current official nationwide mean or median was not accessible.

cost_of_living_note.value: Numbeo's June 2026 crowdsourced UAE data reports a one-bedroom apartment averaging about AED 5,908 monthly in a city centre and AED 4,100 outside, with substantial emirate variation. The USD 3,500 Virtual Work threshold may be tight for central Dubai after housing and mandatory insurance.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Crowdsourced secondary data, not an official household-budget measure.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Virtual Work Residence is temporary-only for settlement purposes. Freelancer Green Residency is renewable long-term residence, but no permanent-residence entitlement exists and its treatment under the 30-year discretionary naturalisation rule requires legal confirmation.
settlement_track.summary: Freelancer Green Residency may provide continuous self-sponsored legal residence, and nationality law contains a discretionary 30-year naturalisation provision. Official sources do not specifically confirm Green Residency counting or the permit path for a contractor serving only foreign clients; the one-year Virtual Work route has no confirmed settlement conversion.
settlement_track.notes: Filing-level confirmation should cover MoHRE permit accessibility, local licensing or substance requirements, continuity and absence rules, and whether every Green Residency year is accepted as continuous legal residence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: Foreign employment clearly fits temporary Virtual Work Residence. Foreign-client freelance work may fit Green Residency, but official sources do not clearly confirm permit issuance for applicants serving only foreign clients or rule out additional UAE licensing and activity requirements.

data.notes: Current official research confirms temporary Virtual Work Residence, five-year freelance/self-employed Green Residency and category-specific Golden Residency rules. Confidence is high on published visa, tax and nationality rules, but medium overall because decisive Green Residency foreign-client fit and residence-to-citizenship counting remain unresolved. The focused Golden Residency income-note audit used five additional current official URLs; all 36 source URLs are distinct.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: Virtual Work Residence is renewable annual residence. Green and Golden Residence are renewable five- and ten-year permissions, respectively; these are not an ordinary permanent-residence status.
requirements: Maintain and renew the chosen residence permission, or independently meet Green/Golden Residence conditions.
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: The reviewed general framework defines residence for a specified term and publishes no ordinary PR conversion for this profile. Longer renewable residence remains possible. Switch and exit fields are false because there is no PR transition being asserted, not because every change to another temporary category is automatic. The old Green URL returned 404; its current official service guide was reviewed.
reviewed_route_names: Virtual Work Residence

data.selection_summary: The United Kingdom has no dedicated digital-nomad visa or ordinary independent residence route for a software engineer working for a foreign client. Visitors may perform limited remote duties for overseas employment only when remote work is not the primary purpose of the visit; this is not residence and cannot be used to live in the UK through successive visits. HPI is independently accessible only to graduates of listed universities but is expressly non-settlement. Global Talent is unsponsored and settlement-capable but requires leader or potential-leader recognition, while Skilled Worker requires a sponsored UK job. None fits the ordinary foreign-contract profile.

visa_application.title: Work in the UK
visa_application.notes: This is the official UK work-visa directory, not a dedicated remote-worker application. No current ordinary digital-nomad or foreign-client freelance route was identified.

rejected_routes.route_name: Standard Visitor — incidental overseas remote work

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No prescribed monthly income threshold exists; the visitor must fund the visit without making remote work its primary purpose.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed income threshold; sufficient funds for the visit are required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: This is a visitor-funds test, not a digital-nomad income requirement.

income_requirement_display.value: No published remote-worker income threshold; remote work must be incidental to a genuine visit
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Sufficient funds for visit costs; no fixed amount
income_requirement_display.notes: The route cannot be used principally to work remotely or to make the UK a main home.

income_proof_months.notes: The official overview does not prescribe a fixed number of months of income history.

key_requirements.requirement: The primary purpose must be a permitted visit rather than remote work; the applicant must leave after the visit and must not make the UK a main home through frequent or successive visits.
Remote activities may relate to overseas employment, but visitors cannot establish or run a UK business as a self-employed person.

initial_validity.value: Usually up to 6 months per visit
initial_validity.notes: Long-validity visitor visas do not permit continuous residence; each stay remains subject to visitor conditions.

extension_rules.value: No general extension or residence conversion for remote work
extension_rules.notes: Remote work does not create an extension or settlement entitlement.

path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor permission is not temporary residence for settlement purposes.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: There is no visitor-to-settlement path based on foreign remote work.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time does not provide the requested residence-to-citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the permission is visitor-like and remote work must remain secondary. It is not a digital-nomad residence status and cannot support long-term settlement.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no monthly earnings threshold. The £1,270 requirement is one-time maintenance funding, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: £1,270 maintenance funds held for 28 consecutive days
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The final day of the holding period must be within 31 days of applying; an exemption can apply after 12 months with valid UK permission.

income_requirement_display.value: £1,270 savings for 28 days; no monthly income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Approximately USD 1,690 at the research conversion assumption, but this is not monthly income. Separate application, Ecctis and annual healthcare-surcharge costs apply.

income_proof_months.notes: Normalized from the official 28-day funds requirement; this concerns savings rather than income history.

key_requirements.requirement: A qualifying degree must have been awarded within the previous five years by a university appearing on the applicable Global Universities List.
English-language ability and maintenance funds are required; no job offer is required.
Current published costs are £252 for Ecctis, an £880 visa fee and normally a £1,035 healthcare surcharge for each visa year.

initial_validity.value: 2 years, or 3 years for a PhD or other doctoral qualification

extension_rules.value: Cannot be extended as HPI; switching to another eligible visa may be possible
extension_rules.notes: Time on HPI does not count toward settlement under this route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct time-limited immigration permission allowing most work and self-employment

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official page expressly says HPI cannot be used to settle permanently and HPI time does not count toward settlement.

path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship would require switching to and qualifying through a separate settlement route.

rejected_routes.notes: Independent and potentially usable for temporary self-employment, but eligibility is restricted to recent graduates of listed universities and the visa is expressly non-settlement. It is therefore neither an ordinary foreign-contract route nor a confirmed citizenship track.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official route has no minimum salary requirement.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No minimum salary requirement

income_requirement_display.value: No minimum salary
income_requirement_display.notes: Applicants qualify through exceptional-talent or exceptional-promise criteria, not ordinary income.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed pre-application income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: Endorsement as a leader or potential leader in digital technology, or an eligible prestigious prize, is normally required.
The applicant must provide substantial evidence of recognition and achievements beyond merely holding a software-engineering degree and foreign contract.

initial_validity.value: Applicant chooses a period of up to 5 years

extension_rules.value: Renewable repeatedly while the eligibility conditions continue to be met
extension_rules.notes: Extensions require qualifying earnings in the expert field.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct permission allowing employment, self-employment and company directorship

path_to_permanent_residence.value: ILR after 3 years as a leader or 5 years as a potential leader, subject to all settlement conditions

path_to_citizenship.value: Naturalisation can normally follow once the five-year lawful-residence requirement and 12 months free from immigration time restrictions are satisfied; the 12-month wait is waived for spouses of British citizens.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A three-year Global Talent ILR route does not necessarily reduce the ordinary naturalisation residence requirement below five years.

rejected_routes.notes: This is independently accessible, permits self-employment and has a settlement path, but it is rejected under the specified profile because it requires exceptional leader or potential-leader credentials. An ordinary foreign contract alone is insufficient.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Salary requirements depend on the sponsored occupation and circumstances; they are not applicable to this profile because an approved UK sponsor is mandatory.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Occupation-specific sponsored salary requirement
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No single route-wide figure is reported because occupation and transitional rules vary.

income_requirement_display.value: Sponsored UK job and applicable salary threshold required
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Higher of the applicable general threshold and occupation going rate, subject to exceptions
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a local-employer route, not foreign-client remote work.

income_proof_months.notes: Eligibility is based on a qualifying sponsored job and certificate of sponsorship, not past foreign income.

key_requirements.requirement: A job offer from an approved UK employer and a certificate of sponsorship are mandatory.
The job must be eligible and satisfy the applicable salary and other immigration requirements.

initial_validity.value: Time-limited work permission based on the certificate of sponsorship
initial_validity.notes: Exact grant length depends on the sponsored employment.

extension_rules.value: Extendable while sponsored-route requirements continue to be met

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct sponsored work permission

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Settlement may normally become possible after 5 qualifying years, subject to route conditions

path_to_citizenship.value: Ordinarily after qualifying settlement, five-year lawful residence and normally 12 months holding ILR

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a job offer and sponsorship from an approved UK employer are mandatory.

summary.value: HPI can be obtained without a job offer by a recent graduate of an institution on the applicable Global Universities List. It grants two or three years of temporary permission and allows self-employment, but it cannot be extended, HPI time does not count toward settlement, and permanent residence requires switching to another qualifying route.
summary.notes: A relevant university degree alone is insufficient: the awarding institution and award date must satisfy the restricted HPI rules.

tax_residency_rule.value: The Statutory Residence Test applies for each 6 April–5 April tax year. Residence can arise at 183 UK days, through an automatic home or full-time-work test, or through the sufficient-ties test; automatic overseas tests can produce non-residence at lower day counts.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The rule is not simply 183 days. Homes, workdays, prior residence and family ties can change the result, and split-year treatment may apply on arrival or departure.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the highest 2026–27 Scottish marginal rate used as a conservative screening number. The top rate is 45% in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. It is not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For a UK self-employed person in 2026–27, Class 4 National Insurance is 6% on profits from £12,570 through £50,270 and 2% above £50,270. Cross-border employees may instead fall under employee/payroll or social-security coordination rules.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No generally mandatory fixed monthly Class 2 payment applies at qualifying self-employed profit levels: Class 2 is treated as paid from £7,105 profits. A person below that level may voluntarily pay £3.65 weekly. This excludes visa fees and the immigration health surcharge.

special_tax_regimes.value: A qualifying new resident may claim the four-year foreign income and gains regime during the first four UK-resident tax years after at least ten consecutive non-UK-resident tax years. Eligible foreign income and gains can be relieved, but claiming can forfeit specified allowances. The regime replaced the remittance basis from 6 April 2025.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Whether compensation for duties physically performed in the UK is eligible foreign income requires professional analysis; the foreign payer or foreign bank account alone does not determine source.

taxes.caveats: There is no UK digital-nomad tax regime. Immigration permission and tax residence are separate: even permitted incidental visitor work can require residence and source analysis. Contract structure, where duties are physically performed, employee versus self-employed classification, Scotland versus the rest of the UK, social-security coordination and double-tax treaties can materially change the result.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax applies. For 2026–27 the highest marginal rate is 45% in England, Wales and Northern Ireland and 48% in Scotland. UK residents normally pay UK tax on worldwide income unless a specific relief such as the qualifying four-year FIG regime applies.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Statutory Residence Test, including automatic overseas tests, automatic UK tests and the sufficient-ties test; 183 UK days is one automatic UK test but not the only way to become resident.
taxation_system.income_scope: Non-residents generally pay UK tax on UK income. Residents normally pay tax on UK and foreign income, subject to source rules, treaties, split-year treatment and available reliefs.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Four-year foreign income and gains regime for qualifying new residents after at least ten consecutive non-resident tax years; claim-based and subject to loss of certain allowances.
taxation_system.social_security: For self-employed profits in 2026–27, Class 4 National Insurance is 6% from £12,570 to £50,270 and 2% above £50,270. Class 2 is generally treated as paid from £7,105 profits; voluntary Class 2 below that level is £3.65 weekly.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 48% dashboard figure is the top Scottish marginal screening rate, not an estimate of effective tax. England, Wales and Northern Ireland top out at 45%. Scottish earned-income bands differ, and savings and dividend rules require separate treatment.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Personal Allowance generally up to £12,570 of gross income
tax_brackets.applies_to: England, Wales and Northern Ireland; allowance can taper at high income
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses £1 ≈ USD 1.33 for screening.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: £12,571–£50,270 gross income with the standard allowance
tax_brackets.applies_to: England, Wales and Northern Ireland non-savings earned income
tax_brackets.notes: Upper boundary shown in approximate USD.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: £50,271–£125,140 gross income with the standard allowance
tax_brackets.applies_to: England, Wales and Northern Ireland non-savings earned income
tax_brackets.notes: Personal Allowance tapering can create a higher effective marginal rate within part of this range.

tax_brackets.applies_to: England, Wales and Northern Ireland additional rate
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate outside Scotland.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over £125,140; Scotland has additional starter, basic, intermediate, higher and advanced bands below this
tax_brackets.applies_to: Scottish top rate on relevant non-savings income
tax_brackets.notes: Conservative national screening rate; not applicable throughout the UK.

taxation_system.notes: Current official 2026–27 rates were captured. Individual liability still requires residence, source, employment-status, treaty and devolved-rate analysis.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special visa category because the UK has no dedicated digital-nomad route. A person who nonetheless becomes UK tax resident is generally taxed under ordinary UK rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad route; visitor remote work is permitted only as an incidental activity
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Ordinary progressive UK tax: up to 45% outside Scotland or 48% in Scotland; displayed rate is top marginal, not effective
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Statutory Residence Test; 183 days is one automatic test, but residence may arise earlier through home, work or sufficient ties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: UK residents normally face tax on worldwide income. Qualifying new residents may claim four-year FIG relief for eligible foreign income and gains, but work performed physically in the UK may require different source treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad regime. The general four-year FIG regime may be available to qualifying new residents after ten non-resident tax years.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary employment or self-employment rules apply. Self-employed Class 4 National Insurance is 6% and then 2% across the official 2026–27 profit bands; cross-border social-security rules may alter liability.

fixed_payments.status: No dedicated nomad fixed-tax package; ordinary tax, National Insurance and immigration charges apply according to status
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No compulsory fixed monthly Class 2 amount at qualifying profits; voluntary Class 2 below the small-profits threshold is £3.65 weekly. Class 4 is percentage-based.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: There is no nomad-visa fee. A six-month Standard Visitor visa currently costs £135 where a visa is required; HPI instead has an £880 application fee, £252 Ecctis assessment and normally £1,035 healthcare surcharge per year.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No special fixed freelancer tax or digital-nomad levy was identified. VAT, business-registration and other obligations depend on actual UK business activity and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: Visitor permission does not authorize establishing or running a UK self-employed business. Immigration-health-surcharge costs belong to qualifying residence visas, not incidental visitor remote-work permission.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A non-resident normally pays no UK tax on foreign income, but UK-source income, duties performed in the UK, treaty rules and the full Statutory Residence Test must still be checked.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A UK tax resident generally reports worldwide income and faces progressive rates up to 45%, or 48% in Scotland, unless treaty relief or the qualifying four-year FIG regime applies.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A genuinely UK self-employed person must notify HMRC and use Self Assessment; Class 4 National Insurance generally applies above the profit threshold. Visitor status cannot be used to establish or run that business.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax description is contextual only because no qualifying digital-nomad immigration route exists.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying ordinary foreign-contract route grants UK temporary residence. Visitor permission is not residence; HPI is non-settlement; Global Talent is elite; Skilled Worker is sponsored.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No permanent-residence timeline exists for the requested profile. Excluded alternatives include Global Talent ILR after 3 or 5 years and sponsored-worker settlement commonly after 5 years.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Ordinary naturalisation normally requires 12 months free from immigration time restrictions. A spouse or civil partner of a British citizen can apply once holding ILR without that 12-month wait, provided the three-year residence and other requirements are met.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total is stated for the requested profile because no qualifying entry route exists. Under an otherwise eligible route, ordinary naturalisation requires at least five years of lawful residence and normally 12 months holding ILR.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: GOV.UK says a decision is usually made within six months, although some cases take longer.

key_conditions.value: Naturalisation normally requires lawful residence, ILR or equivalent freedom from immigration time restrictions, permitted absences, physical presence at the start of the qualifying period, English, Welsh or Scottish Gaelic, the Life in the UK Test, good character and—on the ordinary route—an intention to continue living in the UK. The UK permits dual citizenship.
key_conditions.notes: The ordinary five-year naturalisation residence period is distinct from an immigration route’s ILR qualifying period.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must have lived in the UK for at least three years and already hold ILR, settled status or indefinite leave to enter. Marriage itself does not automatically grant citizenship or ILR.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legally recognized marriage or civil partnership to a British citizen allows use of the spouse naturalisation provisions once the applicant has the required three-year UK residence and is free from immigration time restrictions. It does not itself provide citizenship or excuse the need to obtain qualifying immigration status.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Unlike the ordinary route, a qualifying spouse need not wait 12 months after obtaining ILR.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must meet residence and absence rules, have English, Welsh or Scottish Gaelic knowledge, pass the Life in the UK Test, be of good character and hold ILR or equivalent status. Immigration partner routes require a genuine and subsisting relationship; false evidence or a sham marriage can lead to refusal and serious immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates naturalisation timing but does not automatically accelerate every route to permanent residence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: For births on or after 1 January 1983, UK birth normally gives automatic British citizenship only if at least one parent is British or settled at birth. Later registration rights can arise if a parent subsequently becomes British or settled, or after the child lives in the UK for the first ten years subject to statutory conditions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: Not automatically if neither parent is British or settled when the child is born. The child may later register if a parent becomes British or settled while the child is a minor, or through the ten-year UK-birth residence provision.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: If either migrant parent already holds ILR or another qualifying settled status at birth, the child is normally British automatically.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A UK-born child is normally automatically British when the other parent is a British citizen at birth. The same automatic result normally applies where that parent is settled, including holding ILR.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Specific parentage and historical rules should be checked for unusual cases.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A British or settled child can support a separate family-visa application by a parent who has sole or qualifying shared parental responsibility and takes an active role in the child’s upbringing. The earliest settlement point on the five-year parent route is after five continuous years on that family visa; the child’s birth does not automatically regularize the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: If the parents remain partners, the applicant may be required to use the partner route instead of the parent route.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic residence, ILR or citizenship is granted to a migrant father merely because his child is British. A qualifying father may apply through the family parent or partner rules, proving the genuine parental or partner relationship, immigration conditions, English and financial support.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Time on other visas does not count toward the five continuous years required for ILR on the five-year parent route.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed by Passport Index when checked on 2026-08-15.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Passport Index’s strict visa-free category, excluding visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index category requiring a visa in advance; eVisa categories may be classified separately by the index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 45 visa-on-arrival destinations and 11 eTA destinations shown by Passport Index.

passport.notes: Passport-index figures change frequently and classification methods differ. This uses a single named index consistently because it publishes the requested category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. English is the dominant language of government, commerce and daily life throughout the UK, so an English-speaking software engineer can work and live without a language barrier. Welsh has official status in Wales and is used alongside English in Welsh public services.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The UK has no single codified nationwide official-language provision making English de jure official everywhere; English is therefore described as de facto UK-wide.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are community languages rather than official or generally sufficient working languages. Community and interpretation services exist in major cities, but English is ordinarily necessary for work, government services, housing and long-term integration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: No reliable current national measure supports a claim of broad Russian- or Ukrainian-language practicality.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of £749 average weekly total earnings multiplied by 52/12, using £1 ≈ USD 1.33. This is gross average employee pay in Great Britain, including bonuses, not software-engineer pay.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official ASHE median gross annual earnings of £39,039 for full-time employees in April 2025, divided by 12. The median and average measures cover different populations and periods.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official minimum is hourly and varies by age and apprenticeship status. A monthly USD amount is not supplied because conversion would require an assumed number of paid hours.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate May 2026 gross average employee total pay converted from £749 weekly.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate monthly conversion of £39,039 annual median gross earnings for full-time employees in April 2025.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The UK has no statutory national maximum salary, and the current official earnings sources reviewed publish means, medians and percentiles rather than the largest salary earned. The £16,461 PAYE figure for April 2026 is the 99th-percentile monthly-pay benchmark, not a maximum, so it was not converted into a maximum-salary value.

min_salary_local_currency.value: £12.71 per hour for workers aged 21 and over from April 2026
min_salary_local_currency.notes: This is the statutory National Living Wage, not an observed minimum monthly salary. Lower statutory rates apply to younger workers and some apprentices.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Seasonally adjusted average total earnings, including bonuses, for employees in Great Britain in May 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Median gross annual earnings for full-time employees who had been in their jobs at least one year, April 2025.

max_salary_local_currency.value: No statutory or statistically published national maximum salary; official distributions stop at percentile benchmarks
max_salary_local_currency.notes: Focused review found official ONS ASHE tables for the 90th through 99th percentiles and PAYE RTI monthly distributions through the 99th percentile, but neither series publishes the single highest salary or a national ceiling. PAYE RTI reported £16,461 per month at the 99th percentile for April 2026; that means about 1% of covered employees were above that level and therefore cannot be represented as a maximum. PAYE RTI also excludes self-employment income, while ASHE samples employee jobs.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Gross employee earnings: May 2026 average weekly total pay for Great Britain; April 2025 median annual full-time pay for the UK; statutory hourly minimum from April 2026. High-end checks used ASHE employee-job percentiles and PAYE RTI payrolled-employee percentiles, neither of which is a maximum.
average_citizen_salary.period: Average: May 2026; median: April 2025; minimum wage: effective April 2026; high-end verification: ASHE April 2025 and PAYE RTI April 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: These are average citizen/resident employee wage indicators, statutory minimum wage and distribution benchmarks—not immigration income thresholds and not software-engineer-specific. No maximum salary is reported because an actual nationwide maximum is neither a meaningful statutory amount nor published in the checked official datasets. USD conversions use an approximate £1 = USD 1.33 screening rate because the research date fell on a weekend and the Bank of England describes its daily spot series as indicative rather than an official transaction rate.

cost_of_living_note.value: No single reliable official nationwide monthly cost-of-living budget was established. Costs vary substantially by region and household, especially housing, so wage figures should not be treated as proof of affordability.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A cautious qualitative note is retained instead of inserting a commercial crowd-sourced estimate.
