settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Incidental remote work as a Standard Visitor is temporary and cannot be the primary purpose of the visit. It is not a residence or settlement route.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-work route leads from UK residence to settlement. The unsponsored HPI route is expressly non-settlement, while settlement-capable alternatives require elite Global Talent credentials, a sponsored UK job or another excluded basis.
settlement_track.notes: Switching to an independently qualifying settlement route would be necessary, but no routine conversion based solely on the existing foreign software contract is available.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The only ordinary foreign-employment remote-work permission identified is incidental activity during a genuine visit. It cannot be the visit’s primary purpose and provides no qualifying residence. Other routes impose listed-university, exceptional-talent or UK-sponsorship requirements.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit completed against the previous UK record. Thirty-one distinct canonical URLs are retained, including five new official ONS URLs specifically examining high-end earnings, percentiles and dataset coverage. Those sources establish that current official statistics publish high-percentile benchmarks but not a national maximum salary; the flagged local-currency field therefore contains a precise explanation instead of a vague unresolved marker, while the numeric maximum remains null rather than treating the 99th percentile as a ceiling. Official UK sources continue to support the ineligible immigration result.

data.selection_summary: The United States has no dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. EB-2 National Interest Waiver (NIW) is a self-petitioned, settlement-oriented alternative that can lead directly to lawful permanent residence without a U.S. employer, but a degree, software-engineering occupation, and foreign contract are not sufficient by themselves: the proposed endeavor must have substantial merit and national importance, the applicant must be well positioned to advance it, and USCIS must find that waiving the job-offer and labor-certification requirements benefits the United States. Under the supplied criteria this is a partial independent skilled/qualification route, not a regular remote-work match.

visa_application.title: Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers
visa_application.notes: This is the official USCIS form and filing-information page used for an EB-2 NIW self-petition. Confirm the current form edition, filing address or online-filing availability, fees, and whether an immigrant visa or adjustment-of-status process is appropriate before filing.

best_routes.route_name: EB-2 National Interest Waiver (NIW)

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: USCIS publishes no fixed monthly-income threshold for EB-2 NIW.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed income threshold exists; the currency is USD.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly-income threshold; EB-2 qualification and the discretionary NIW merits test apply
income_requirement_display.notes: Financial resources, contracts, revenue, or funding may help demonstrate that the applicant is well positioned, but they do not replace the EB-2 and NIW legal tests.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed number of prior income months is prescribed.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualify for underlying EB-2 classification as an advanced-degree professional or person of exceptional ability.
Show that the specific proposed endeavor has substantial merit and national importance.
Show that the applicant is well positioned to advance the proposed endeavor.
Show that, on balance, waiving the job-offer and permanent labor-certification requirements would benefit the United States.
File Form I-140 with supporting evidence; after approval, complete consular immigrant-visa processing or adjustment of status when a visa number is available and satisfy admissibility requirements.
A foreign software contract, university degree, or ordinary remote job alone does not establish national importance or the other NIW elements.

initial_validity.value: Immigrant classification leading to lawful permanent residence after immigrant-visa issuance and admission, or approval of adjustment of status
initial_validity.notes: An approved I-140 petition alone is not a green card, work authorization, or permission to enter or remain in the United States. Visa availability and admissibility still apply.

extension_rules.value: Not a temporary residence route; lawful permanent-resident status has no fixed expiration, although the physical card normally must be renewed
extension_rules.notes: Maintaining LPR status requires treating the United States as the permanent home and avoiding abandonment; the NIW petition itself is not periodically renewed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No temporary-residence stage is granted by NIW itself
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: A separately valid nonimmigrant status may be needed while a case is pending, but that is not supplied automatically by filing or approval of Form I-140.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Direct immigrant route: approved NIW-based I-140 followed by immigrant-visa issuance and U.S. admission, or adjustment of status, subject to visa availability and admissibility
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: In the August 2026 Visa Bulletin, EB-2 was current for most chargeability areas but not for China-mainland-born or India; availability can retrogress and must be checked monthly.

path_to_citizenship.value: Generally eligible to apply for naturalization after at least five years as an LPR, with continuous residence, at least 30 months of physical presence, good moral character, English and civics requirements, and other statutory conditions
path_to_citizenship.notes: Time spent preparing or awaiting the NIW petition before LPR admission does not start the five-year naturalization period.

best_routes.notes: NIW is independently petitionable and settlement-oriented, so it is a useful partial option for a highly developed software or technology endeavor. It is not an ordinary remote-worker visa: the applicant must build a fact-specific national-interest case going materially beyond having a foreign client, degree, and marketable profession.

rejected_routes.route_name: B-1/B-2 visitor status or Visa Waiver Program business/tourist admission

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: There is no remote-worker income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No applicable threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker threshold; visitor status does not authorize ordinary work in the United States
income_requirement_display.notes: Ability to pay travel expenses may be requested, but that is not a remote-work eligibility test.

income_proof_months.notes: No standardized remote-income history because this is not a remote-worker route.

key_requirements.requirement: B-1 permits limited business activities such as meetings, negotiations, consultations, conferences, and certain commercial transactions that do not involve gainful employment in the United States.
The State Department states that a B-1/B-2 visitor is not permitted to accept employment or work in the United States.

initial_validity.value: Visa validity and the period of authorized admission are separate; the admission period is determined at entry
initial_validity.notes: Neither visa validity nor a visitor extension creates residence rights.

extension_rules.value: A visitor may qualify to request an extension or change of status in limited circumstances, but approval does not create a general foreign-remote-worker category
extension_rules.notes: A change of status requires eligibility for a separate classification.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying temporary residence for ordinary remote employment

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct path from visitor status
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A later independent immigrant basis would be a separate route, with intent, status, and admissibility issues requiring legal review.

path_to_citizenship.value: No; visitor time does not count as LPR residence for naturalization

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because visitor or visa-waiver admission is not a lawful ordinary remote-employment residence solution and is not a citizenship-path status.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general monthly threshold; category-specific prevailing-wage and labor rules can apply.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No single threshold across temporary-worker categories.

income_requirement_display.value: Category-specific wage requirements; no ordinary foreign-remote-worker threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: H-1B normally requires a U.S. petitioner and specialty-occupation employment.

income_proof_months.notes: Not a foreign-income-history route.

key_requirements.requirement: A prospective U.S. employer or qualifying agent generally files the worker petition; H-1B also involves Department of Labor requirements.

initial_validity.value: Varies by nonimmigrant worker category
initial_validity.notes: These are temporary, purpose-specific classifications.

extension_rules.value: Varies by category and statutory maximums

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, as a category-specific nonimmigrant stay
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This does not satisfy the independent-application requirement.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion; any employment-based immigrant petition is a separate process

path_to_citizenship.value: Only after separately obtaining lawful permanent residence and satisfying naturalization rules

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because the ordinary H-1B-style route requires a U.S. employer or petitioner and is incompatible with the specified independent foreign-contract profile.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor entry followed by sole-proprietor or freelancer registration

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No such immigration route or threshold was found.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No such threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration program found; business or tax registration does not itself authorize work or residence
income_requirement_display.notes: The official visa directory contains no general freelancer or digital-nomad classification.

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable.

key_requirements.requirement: A person must independently qualify for an immigration classification that authorizes the intended activity; forming or registering a business does not create immigration status.

initial_validity.value: No qualifying status

extension_rules.value: Not applicable

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No confirmed path

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No confirmed path merely from freelancer or sole-proprietor registration

path_to_citizenship.value: No
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires prior lawful permanent residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Focused review found no visitor-to-freelancer legalization mechanism. Corporate, banking, or tax formalities are separate from immigration authorization.

summary.value: EB-2 NIW permits self-petitioning without a U.S. employer or permanent labor certification and can lead directly to an immigrant visa or adjustment to lawful permanent residence. It requires underlying EB-2 qualification plus a discretionary national-interest showing; a relevant degree alone is insufficient.
summary.notes: This is the reason the United States is classified as partial rather than fully ineligible. It remains a demanding skilled/qualification route, not an ordinary foreign-contract remote-work program.

tax_residency_rule.value: A foreign national is generally a U.S. tax resident if the green-card test or substantial-presence test is met. The substantial-presence test normally requires at least 31 days in the current year and a weighted total of 183 days across the current and preceding two years, counting all current-year days, one-third of prior-year days, and one-sixth of second-prior-year days, subject to exclusions, closer-connection rules, and treaties.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration status and federal tax residency are separate analyses.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top 2026 federal marginal rate for a single filer, not the expected effective rate. State and sometimes local income taxes may apply separately.

social_contributions_percent.notes: 2026 self-employment tax screening rate: 12.4% Social Security up to the applicable wage base plus 2.9% Medicare, with an additional 0.9% Medicare tax above specified income thresholds. Classification, foreign social coverage, totalization agreements, and deductions can change the result.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal fixed monthly federal freelancer or digital-nomad payment exists. Federal income and self-employment taxes are percentage-based; health insurance, state taxes, licenses, and business fees vary.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated federal digital-nomad tax regime was found. Closer-connection and treaty residence rules, foreign tax credits, and other ordinary international-tax provisions may affect a particular case.
special_tax_regimes.notes: These are general tax rules, not immigration benefits or nomad incentives.

taxes.caveats: Working physically in the United States can create U.S.-source compensation or effectively connected income even before tax residency, while tax compliance does not cure a lack of immigration work authorization. State residence, entity structure, employee-versus-contractor classification, treaty residence, foreign tax credits, and totalization agreements require case-specific advice.

taxation_system.value: Progressive federal personal income tax, plus potentially state and local income taxes and payroll or self-employment taxes
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Green-card test or substantial-presence test, subject to statutory exceptions and treaty positions
taxation_system.income_scope: Resident aliens are generally taxed on worldwide income; nonresident aliens are generally taxed under source and effectively-connected-income rules.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No dedicated digital-nomad regime; ordinary treaty, closer-connection, foreign-tax-credit, and international reporting rules may apply.
taxation_system.social_security: For 2026, the combined employee payroll rate is generally 7.65%, with an employer match; the headline self-employed rate is 15.3%, subject to the Social Security wage base, additional Medicare tax, deductions, classification rules, and totalization agreements.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The displayed 37% is a top federal marginal screening rate, not an effective rate. The brackets below use 2026 taxable-income thresholds for single filers; deductions and filing status materially affect liability.

tax_brackets.notes: Lowest marginal bracket.
Threshold shown is the lower bound.
Threshold shown is the lower bound.
Threshold shown is the lower bound.
Threshold shown is the lower bound.
Threshold shown is the lower bound.
Top marginal federal bracket.

taxation_system.notes: Federal rules are well supported by current IRS and SSA sources. State and local taxation is intentionally not reduced to one national percentage.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because the United States has no dedicated digital-nomad visa or tax regime. A person physically performing services in the United States must separately analyze immigration authorization, U.S. source rules, federal tax residency, state residency, and payroll or self-employment tax.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; ordinary resident/nonresident and employee/self-employed rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 37% federal marginal income tax for 2026, plus possible state/local tax and up to a 15.3% headline self-employment tax; this is not an expected effective rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Green-card test or weighted substantial-presence test, subject to exceptions and treaties.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is generally taxable for resident aliens. Nonresident treatment is source- and effectively-connected-income dependent; services physically performed in the United States require particular care.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Employee payroll tax is generally 7.65% with employer matching; self-employed persons face a headline 15.3% combined Social Security and Medicare rate, subject to caps, additional Medicare tax, deductions, classification, and totalization agreements.

fixed_payments.status: No universal fixed monthly nomad or freelancer payment
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based rather than a fixed monthly amount; 15.3% headline self-employment rate for 2026.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad visa fee exists. NIW applicants must check current Form I-140, immigrant-visa or adjustment, medical, biometrics, and related fees through official filing channels.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: State business registration, franchise, sales-tax, local licensing, and health-insurance costs vary by location and structure; no reliable national fixed amount exists.
fixed_payments.notes: A zero fixed-payment value should not be inferred; the applicable costs are variable rather than absent.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Remaining below the substantial-presence threshold does not automatically make work performed physically in the United States tax-free or immigration-authorized. Nonresident source and effectively-connected-income rules may apply.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident alien generally reports worldwide income and applies the ordinary progressive federal system, plus applicable state/local and payroll or self-employment rules.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Business or tax registration does not create immigration work authorization. If lawfully self-employed, federal income tax, estimated payments, self-employment tax, state rules, licensing, and information-reporting obligations may apply.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax rules are current, but there is no lawful nomad route to which a special tax treatment can be attached.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: NIW is not a temporary-residence route. Zero means there is no required temporary-residence stage, not that filing creates immediate status.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The route is directly immigrant-oriented. Actual time to LPR status depends on petition adjudication, visa availability, consular or adjustment processing, admissibility, and chargeability.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General minimum statutory residence period for an LPR; qualifying spouses of U.S. citizens may use a three-year rule.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Five years is the minimum counted from LPR admission, not from filing the NIW petition. Pre-LPR processing adds an indeterminate period, so the real end-to-end timeline is longer.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: USCIS historical national median for ordinary N-400 applications in FY2026 through February 28, 2026. Current field-office times can differ and should be rechecked at filing.

key_conditions.value: Obtain LPR status; maintain continuous residence for the statutory period; meet physical-presence requirements (normally 30 months in five years); reside in the relevant state or USCIS district; demonstrate good moral character, tax compliance, basic English, civics knowledge, constitutional attachment, and eligibility for the oath. Extended absences can disrupt continuous residence, and abandonment can jeopardize LPR status. U.S. law does not require choosing only one nationality, although the other country's law must also be checked.
key_conditions.notes: Naturalization is not automatic after five years; the applicant must file and qualify.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The common accelerated naturalization rule requires three years as an LPR while married to and living in marital union with a U.S. citizen; it is not merely three years since the wedding.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a U.S. citizen can support family-based permanent residence and, after LPR admission, may permit the three-year naturalization rule if the citizen spouse and marital-union requirements are continuously met. Marriage to a noncitizen does not accelerate naturalization.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Time married before becoming an LPR does not replace the required period as an LPR.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid and bona fide. For the three-year naturalization provision, the applicant generally must remain married to and living in marital union with the U.S.-citizen spouse through the relevant period and remain married through the oath. Residence, physical presence, good moral character, English, civics, and other naturalization requirements still apply. Fraudulent or sham marriages can cause denial, removal consequences, criminal exposure, and future immigration bars.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Special rules exist for certain military spouses, surviving spouses, and abuse survivors and require separate analysis.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Fourteenth Amendment and controlling doctrine grant citizenship to persons born in the United States and subject to its jurisdiction, with narrow exceptions such as children of accredited foreign diplomats and hostile occupying forces. This is classified as unconditional jus soli under the supplied methodology despite those narrow exceptions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in the United States is generally a U.S. citizen at birth even when both parents are foreign nationals and regardless of whether they are temporary visitors, residents, or lack lawful status, subject to the narrow jurisdictional exceptions.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth in certain U.S. territories can involve different statutory rules; this statement concerns birth in the 50 states and District of Columbia.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in the United States generally acquires citizenship by place of birth. A child born abroad to a U.S.-citizen parent may acquire citizenship at birth only if the applicable statutory parentage, residence or physical-presence, and relationship requirements are met.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The exact transmission rule depends on the child's birth date, the parents' marital status, and the citizen parent's prior U.S. presence.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Birth of a U.S.-citizen child does not immediately legalize either migrant parent or grant work authorization, permanent residence, or citizenship. A U.S.-citizen child generally cannot petition for a parent until age 21, and the parent must still qualify and be admissible.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Unlawful presence, entry history, removal orders, misrepresentation, and other inadmissibility grounds can remain decisive.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status or citizenship. If the child is a U.S. citizen, the child may generally file a parent petition after reaching age 21; the father must establish the qualifying parent-child relationship and satisfy all other immigration requirements.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: A permanent-resident child cannot petition for a parent. Humanitarian or discretionary considerations are case-specific and are not an automatic birth benefit.

rank.notes: Henley's live country page showed the United States in 10th place on the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley's live score on 2026-08-15 was 180 destinations accessible without obtaining a prior visa under Henley's methodology, which includes qualifying visa-on-arrival and electronic travel-authority access.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's separately reported 'visa required' count. Its methodology and destination universe differ from Henley's; it also separately listed eVisa destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Passport Index reported 46 visa-on-arrival destinations and 10 eTA destinations, combined here. This breakdown should not be arithmetically reconciled with the Henley score because the indexes use different category and destination methodologies.

passport.notes: Henley's January 2026 release initially reported 179 destinations, while its live monthly index showed 180 on 2026-08-15; the fresher live value is used. Passport Index separately reported 111 strictly visa-free, 46 visa-on-arrival, 10 eTA, 31 visa-required, and additional eVisa destinations.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Very high. English is the federally designated official language and the dominant language of government, business, contracts, technology work, and daily administration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: Executive Order 14224 designated English as the official language in 2025. Federal and local agencies may still provide multilingual services.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Limited as a nationwide working language. Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking communities and services exist in some metropolitan areas, but an applicant should expect English to be necessary for immigration filings, most professional work, housing, healthcare, banking, and daily administration.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The cited Census language tables confirm extensive linguistic diversity but do not establish Russian or Ukrainian as broadly sufficient substitutes for English; the practicality assessment is therefore a cautious inference.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The selected current nationwide CPS earnings release publishes medians and distribution points, not an arithmetic mean. No incompatible average series was substituted merely to fill the field.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Converted from USD 1,251 median usual weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers in Q2 2026: 1,251 × 52 ÷ 12, rounded to the nearest dollar.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Illustrative monthly equivalent of the federal statutory minimum wage: USD 7.25 × 40 hours × 52 ÷ 12. This is not an observed minimum salary, does not apply to every worker, and many states require higher rates.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A comparable arithmetic average was not published in the cited current CPS release; retained as a cautious null.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Converted from the Q2 2026 non-seasonally-adjusted weekly median of USD 1,251 for full-time wage and salary workers.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: There is no meaningful national maximum salary. BLS publishes distribution points, not a statutory or observed maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.value: USD 7.25 per hour federally; approximately USD 1,256.67 per month at 40 hours per week
min_salary_local_currency.notes: State and local minimum wages may be higher; exemptions also exist.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No arithmetic average in the selected release.

median_salary_local_currency.value: USD 1,251 per week; approximately USD 5,421 per month
median_salary_local_currency.notes: Gross usual earnings before taxes and deductions.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Median usual gross weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers; minimum field is a statutory federal hourly wage converted at 40 hours per week
average_citizen_salary.period: Q2 2026 for median; current federal minimum wage checked 2026-08-15
average_citizen_salary.notes: The median excludes self-employed workers and is not an immigration income threshold. National pay and minimum-wage comparisons conceal large differences by occupation, state, city, hours, and worker coverage.

cost_of_living_note.value: Costs vary sharply by location. BEA's latest regional price parities showed 2024 all-item price levels from 86.9 in Arkansas to 110.7 in California relative to the national level of 100; housing-rent differences were wider, from 54.2 in West Virginia to 154.3 in California.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Regional price parities compare geographic price levels and are not a personal monthly budget. Housing, health insurance, transportation, and taxes require city-specific estimates.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The settlement strength applies only to a successful EB-2 NIW immigrant case. The United States has no dedicated digital-nomad status, and ordinary foreign-contract remote work does not itself qualify for NIW.
settlement_track.summary: EB-2 NIW is a direct immigrant route: after petition approval and immigrant-visa admission or adjustment, the applicant becomes an LPR and can normally use the five-year naturalization track. The settlement link is strong, but eligibility is only partial for this profile because NIW requires a demanding national-interest case and is not a regular remote-worker program.
settlement_track.notes: The previous record correctly identified NIW but inconsistently marked the overall result and NIW route false despite the prompt's explicit partial classification for independent qualification-based routes. This audit changes both to partial while retaining fully_matched=false and remote-work fit=false.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence classification was found. NIW can be self-petitioned, but a foreign contract and remote software work alone do not meet its national-interest requirements.

data.notes: Twenty-seven distinct directly relevant URLs were reviewed, predominantly primary U.S. government sources. The principal unresolved values are those for which no meaningful national figure exists: a fixed NIW income threshold, fixed income-proof period, arithmetic average or maximum national salary, and universal monthly freelancer payment. These remain cautious nulls with explanations rather than estimates. Immigration eligibility, work authorization, visa availability, tax residence, and nationality-specific entry restrictions must be rechecked at filing.

data.selection_summary: Uruguay is a strong match through ordinary permanent legal residence, not through the short digital-nomad document. The current procedure expressly accommodates independently applying workers employed by a foreign company without a Uruguayan branch and self-employed sole proprietors. Legal citizenship may follow five years of habitual residence, or three years with family constituted in Uruguay.

visa_application.title: Residencia legal
visa_application.notes: The Ministry of Interior portal permits online initiation after authentication. Original documents and personal attendance before DNM are still required, so the process cannot be completed wholly from abroad.

best_routes.route_name: Residencia Legal Permanente — foreign-company employee or independent sole proprietor

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: DNM publishes no fixed USD threshold; documented monthly nominal income must be sufficient for the applicant's maintenance.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No fixed amount; sufficient monthly nominal income required
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The permanent-residence checklist does not quantify what DNM considers sufficient.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed threshold published — prove sufficient monthly nominal income
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Monthly nominal income sufficient for maintenance
income_requirement_display.notes: The national minimum wage should not be treated as a guaranteed permanent-residence threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: The checklist requires notarized or accounting certification of monthly income but specifies no fixed lookback period.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid identity document and a valid entry visa if required for the applicant's nationality.

National criminal-record certificates from the country of origin and countries where the applicant lived for at least six months during the relevant preceding five years; apostille/legalization and Spanish translation normally apply.
Uruguayan health card and vaccination certificate.

For a foreign-company employee, a Uruguayan notary must certify the employment relationship, company details, absence of a Uruguayan branch, income and payment method, how the work is performed from Uruguay, and whether Uruguayan labor or social-security registration applies.
A sole proprietor must provide notarized business and income evidence and an accounting certificate covering monthly income, fiscal address, and DGI/BPS registration.
Online initiation followed by personal attendance with original documents; an interpreter is required if the applicant cannot communicate in Spanish.

initial_validity.value: Permanent residence if granted
initial_validity.notes: No prior temporary-residence holding period is published. Renewal of an identity document is distinct from the permanence of the underlying status.

extension_rules.value: No ordinary temporary-status extension is required after permanent residence is granted; identity-document renewal and continuing compliance are separate matters.
extension_rules.notes: The cited route page does not publish an expiration period for the underlying permanent residence.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: A separate non-Mercosur temporary-residence route is available for qualifying work, study or other statutory activities for six months to two years.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is optional rather than a prerequisite for the selected direct permanent route.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A qualifying non-Mercosur foreigner intending permanent settlement can apply directly. The current checklist expressly contains evidentiary categories for foreign-company employees and independent sole proprietors.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Approval remains evidence-based and discretionary; direct eligibility does not guarantee approval.

path_to_citizenship.value: Legal citizenship is available after five years of habitual residence without family constituted in Uruguay, or three years with family constituted there, subject to good conduct, livelihood or qualifying occupation, Spanish ability and residence evidence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: A continuous absence exceeding six months restarts the relevant factual-residence period under current Electoral Court guidance.

best_routes.notes: This route directly fits an ordinary software engineer working remotely for a foreign company without a Uruguayan branch. Self-employment can also fit but normally entails local DGI, BPS or professional-fund structuring. Opening a bank account before residence is not an immigration requirement established by the reviewed official sources.

rejected_routes.route_name: Hoja de Identidad Provisoria — Nómada Digital as the sole settlement route

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official procedure publishes no numerical income threshold and instead requires the prescribed declaration.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: No numerical threshold published
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The current checklist specifies no minimum UYU amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed income threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: The applicant must still make the required declaration and satisfy DNM.

income_proof_months.notes: The current official procedure specifies no fixed income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Identity document and prescribed sworn declaration for the initial digital-nomad application.
Renewal requires a valid Uruguayan identity document, sworn declaration, qualifying national criminal records and a Uruguayan vaccination certificate.
A separate entry visa is required when applicable to the applicant's nationality.

initial_validity.value: Up to 180 days
initial_validity.notes: The current procedure describes activity lasting under 180 days; Ministry guidance describes a maximum 180-day authorization.

extension_rules.value: Renewable once for another 180 days under Ministry guidance.
extension_rules.notes: The current route page lists renewal documents; the Ministry's residency overview supplies the one-additional-180-day limit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Hoja is itself a limited provisional authorization for activity lasting up to 180 days; it is distinct from ordinary six-month-to-two-year temporary legal residence.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Possession can support a Uruguayan identity-document application but does not make the holder a permanent resident.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: Yes, through a separate ordinary permanent-residence application available to qualifying foreign-company remote employees or independent sole proprietors; no prior residence clock is required.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Zero means no statutory residence waiting period before the direct PR application, not instant approval. Nomad-time credit is unnecessary for this pathway. The permanent-page direct open timed out, but its complete official indexed checklist was accessible; the current July 2026 residence landing page and Hoja checklist opened successfully.

path_to_citizenship.value: The digital-nomad Hoja does not by itself provide the status required for a citizenship filing. The current Electoral Court manual requires a Migration certificate stating that the applicant entered legally and is authorized to reside permanently, plus proof of three or five years of habitual residence. A Hoja holder must therefore obtain permanent residence separately before applying for legal citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The Hoja can document lawful physical presence, but no current official rule automatically credits Hoja-only time. The Electoral Court separately evaluates dated evidence of habitual residence and absences while requiring permanent-residence authorization at filing. Acceptance of any pre-permanent Hoja period toward the factual three- or five-year period is therefore case-specific and should be verified with the Court.

rejected_routes.notes: The Hoja is useful for an initial remote-working stay but is rejected as the selected citizenship-track route. A holder must qualify separately for permanent residence before filing for legal citizenship.

summary.value: A regular student at a recognized educational institution may independently request temporary residence and prove sufficient means. A university or software-engineering degree does not itself confer permanent residence.
summary.notes: This is a study route, not an independent degree-based skilled-migration program.

tax_residency_rule.value: Tax residence can arise through more than 183 days in the calendar year or alternative vital-interest, principal-economic-activity or qualifying-investment tests. Certain absences of no more than 30 consecutive days count unless foreign tax residence is proved.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Immigration residence and tax residence are separate.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the top marginal screening rate for resident Category II work income, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: No single percentage applies across foreign employment, sole proprietorships, monotributo, BPS and professional-fund treatment.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal monthly USD payment applies; official contribution amounts depend on registration category and health/family options.

special_tax_regimes.value: New tax residents can elect an IRNR-style holiday for qualifying foreign movable-capital returns for the arrival year plus ten following fiscal years, or 7% IRPF on those returns indefinitely. This does not exempt employment or professional-service income. Qualifying software or technical services used exclusively abroad may receive export-of-services VAT treatment.
special_tax_regimes.notes: The inbound election concerns specified passive foreign capital income, not salary or professional fees.

taxes.caveats: Services physically performed from Uruguay for a foreign company are Uruguayan-source work income according to DGI. Employee-versus-contractor characterization, treaties, social-security affiliation, professional-fund rules, VAT export conditions and permanent-establishment exposure require individual advice.

taxation_system.value: Resident Category II work income is taxed progressively from 0% to 36%. Independent workers generally apply a 30% deemed expense deduction before the progressive calculation and permitted personal deductions. Although Uruguay has territorial features, services physically performed in Uruguay for a foreign customer are taxable Uruguayan-source income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days in the calendar year or an alternative vital-interest, principal-activity or qualifying-investment test.
taxation_system.income_scope: Primarily source-based with specified extensions; remote services physically performed in Uruguay are Uruguayan-source even when delivered online to a foreign company.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Inbound holiday or perpetual 7% election for specified foreign movable-capital returns; conditional VAT export treatment for qualifying software and technical services used exclusively abroad.
taxation_system.social_security: Structure-dependent. Local self-employment can trigger BPS or professional-fund obligations; no universal percentage or minimum applies to every software-engineer structure.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 2026 individual monthly scale uses BPC multiples. The displayed 36% is the top marginal rate, not an estimate of effective tax. The 2026 BPC is UYU 6,864.

tax_brackets.applies_to: 2026 IRPF Category II individual monthly scale
tax_brackets.notes: Exempt band.
Dashboard screening rate, not the effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Current DGI material expressly addresses foreign-client services performed from Uruguay.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: The immigration document creates no general tax holiday. Resident remote-work income performed in Uruguay enters progressive IRPF up to 36%; qualifying independent software exports may receive conditional VAT treatment.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: Digital-nomad Hoja for short stay; ordinary permanent residence for settlement
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0%–36% progressive IRPF; 36% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 days or an alternative statutory test; immigration status does not determine tax residence.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: A foreign payer does not determine labor-income source. Services physically performed in Uruguay are taxable work income; specified passive foreign-capital income has separate inbound elections.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: No digital-nomad labor-income exemption was established. The inbound 10+1-year IRNR election or perpetual 7% option is limited to specified foreign movable-capital returns.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: The Hoja does not publish a general contribution exemption. Foreign-employment or local self-employment registration must be assessed; sole-proprietor structures can trigger BPS or professional-fund payments.

fixed_payments.status: Immigration fees are published; recurring tax and social-security amounts vary by structure.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal figure. BPS publishes category-specific monotributo amounts, but eligibility and professional-fund treatment require individual verification.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Digital-nomad Hoja: 55.71 UI. Permanent or temporary legal residence: 557.30 UI, plus 55.70 UI for the migration certificate used for the identity document. A re-entry permit while residence is pending costs 225.60 UI.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Independent personal services normally require IRPF and VAT analysis. Qualifying exported software or technical services may be outside output VAT; otherwise the basic VAT rate is 22%.
fixed_payments.notes: UI amounts fluctuate with the indexed-unit value; no unreliable USD conversion is supplied.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 183 days does not itself guarantee zero Uruguayan tax because work performed locally can still be Uruguayan-source and other residence tests may apply.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Expect IRPF on work performed from Uruguay at progressive rates up to 36%; a foreign payer does not make that labor income foreign-source.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Expect DGI registration, IRPF computation, VAT/export analysis and possible BPS or professional-fund contributions.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Payroll and social-security affiliation remain dependent on profession and contract structure.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Temporary residence is not a prerequisite for the direct permanent route; zero does not mean immediate adjudication.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Direct permanent residence is available without a published temporary-residence holding period.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Conservative no-family case. The legal test is factual habitual residence, not strictly five years counted from the permanent-residence grant; three years applies with qualifying family constituted in Uruguay.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: Conservative ordinary case without family constituted in Uruguay.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The current route page publishes no typical duration. Although Law 8.196 contains a decision provision, the reviewed current administrative material does not establish a reliable end-to-end processing time.

key_conditions.value: Permanent-residence authorization at citizenship filing; three or five years of habitual factual residence; no continuous absence exceeding six months; age 18; good conduct; qualifying capital, property, science, art or industry; documented livelihood; and ability to understand and express oneself in Spanish.
key_conditions.notes: The Electoral Court decides legal-citizenship eligibility.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Three years refers to habitual residence with family constituted in Uruguay, not a standalone marriage-duration requirement.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage can support the family-constituted classification when the family resides in Uruguay. Marriage to a Uruguayan also creates a direct permanent-residence family link; marriage to another foreigner does not create that link by itself.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The relationship and residence of qualifying family members must be documented.

requirements_and_risks.value: Citizenship is not automatic through marriage. Habitual residence, livelihood or qualifying occupation, good conduct, Spanish ability and permanent-residence authorization remain necessary. False documents or a sham relationship can cause refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: DNM and the Electoral Court may require additional evidence.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 74 broadly makes people born anywhere in Uruguay natural citizens without a parent-residence condition.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Uruguay is a natural citizen even when both parents are foreign migrants.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Civil registration is required to document the birth and status.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Uruguay is a natural citizen by birthplace. A child born abroad to a Uruguayan parent falls within the descent rule after taking residence in Uruguay and registering in the Civic Registry.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The nationality system is mixed despite broad domestic jus soli.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Uruguayan child may apply directly for permanent residence through the Uruguayan-family-link category. The child does not automatically confer citizenship on the parent.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The relationship and ordinary residence requirements must be documented.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Uruguayan child has a direct permanent-residence basis as the child's parent but still follows the ordinary three- or five-year habitual-residence citizenship rules.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Paternity and the child's Uruguayan status must be legally documented.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank rather than Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Advance-visa-required count shown by Passport Index.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 45 visa-on-arrival and 9 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 150. Its strict visa-free count should not be compared directly with indexes that combine access categories.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable within an international remote team, but Spanish is practically necessary for immigration, tax, notarial and citizenship procedures. An interpreter is required for immigration if the applicant cannot speak Spanish, while citizenship applicants must understand and express themselves in Spanish.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: The Constitution does not expressly designate an official language; Spanish is the accepted institutional language.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian or Ukrainian alone is not practical for official procedures; a Spanish interpreter or translator should be expected.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: This does not exclude the existence of private community services.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current INE material reviewed reports household and per-capita household income rather than an average individual worker wage.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national median individual wage amount was established; household-income medians and wage indexes are not equivalent.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The statutory minimum is confirmed in UYU, but no same-date authoritative exchange rate was captured.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official average individual monthly salary amount was established.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official median individual monthly salary amount was established.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Uruguay publishes no meaningful statutory national maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory national minimum wage effective 1 July 2026, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: INE reported Q1 2026 mean household income of UYU 97,541 and per-capita household income of UYU 34,606; neither is an individual wage.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No current official median worker salary was established.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No reliable national maximum wage is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly national minimum wage; current average and median individual worker wages were not established from the reviewed official sources
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage effective 2026-07-01; comparison income source Q1 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: Only the statutory minimum is populated because household income was not misrepresented as individual salary.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The reviewed official sources publish no directly comparable current cost-of-living budget for a single remote worker.
