settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The digital-nomad Hoja is limited to up to 180 days and one further 180-day renewal; it is not permanent residence. The current Electoral Court manual requires permanent-residence authorization at citizenship filing, and no official source automatically credits Hoja-only time.
settlement_track.summary: The selected route is direct ordinary permanent residence expressly open to qualifying foreign-company remote employees and independent sole proprietors. Genuine habitual residence can support legal citizenship after five years, or three years with family constituted in Uruguay.
settlement_track.notes: The strong classification relies on the direct permanent-residence route, not on an assumed citizenship conversion from the digital-nomad Hoja.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The permanent-residence checklist expressly addresses employees of foreign legal entities without a Uruguayan branch and separately recognizes independent sole proprietors. Neither category requires a local employer.

data.notes: This focused audit preserves Uruguay's positive selection through direct ordinary permanent residence. It resolves the flagged Hoja-to-citizenship field: current Electoral Court rules require permanent-residence authorization at citizenship filing, while habitual residence is proved factually for three or five years. No current official rule automatically credits Hoja-only time; acceptance of any pre-permanent period remains filing-specific.

digital_nomad_pr_transition.qualifying_status: Ordinary legal permanent residence as a foreign-company employee or independent sole proprietor
digital_nomad_pr_transition.summary: A Hoja digital-nomad holder can separately apply for ordinary permanent residence. The official checklist expressly accepts foreign-company remote employees and independent sole proprietors; no minimum prior residence period is required for that direct PR application.
requirements: Intend genuine permanent residence in Uruguay and submit the ordinary PR application with identity, background and vaccination documents.
Document sufficient livelihood through the appropriate notarial/accounting certification; foreign-company employees must document their employer, income, payment method and remote activity.
reviewed_route_names: Hoja de Identidad Provisoria — Nómada Digital as the sole settlement route
digital_nomad_pr_transition.notes: Zero means no statutory residence waiting period before the direct PR application, not instant approval. Nomad-time credit is unnecessary for this pathway. The permanent-page direct open timed out, but its complete official indexed checklist was accessible; the current July 2026 residence landing page and Hoja checklist opened successfully.

data.selection_summary: Uzbekistan has no confirmed dedicated digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. The three-year IT Visa is available to IT Park-linked employees, founders and investors, but the specialist category requires employment by an Uzbek resident legal entity; registering as self-employed does not itself grant or legalize residence. Uzbekistan therefore does not fit the applicant's independent, citizenship-oriented remote-work profile.

visa_application.title: Application for an IT Visa
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct IT Visa application service. It is provided as the closest relevant application channel, but the IT-specialist category requires an employer letter from an Uzbek resident legal entity and is not an ordinary foreign-client remote-work route.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The official threshold is USD 30,000 of IT-activity income during the preceding 12 months, expressed here as a USD 2,500 monthly average. Meeting the income threshold does not remove the Uzbek-employer requirement.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: Approximately UZS 30.09 million per month, based on USD 2,500 and the CBU rate displayed near the research date
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The legal threshold is denominated in USD, not UZS. The conversion uses approximately UZS 12,035.26 per USD and is only a dashboard estimate.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 30,000 during the preceding 12 months (USD 2,500 monthly average)
income_requirement_display.notes: Income must be confirmed by a bank or competent authority. The applicant also needs an Uzbek resident-company employer letter.

income_proof_months.notes: The application service requests evidence of income for the preceding 12 months.

key_requirements.requirement: Qualification or specialization in information technology, supported by a diploma, certificate or CV.
Employment in an Uzbek resident legal entity in an IT specialty and a letter confirming that entity's intention to employ the applicant.
At least USD 30,000 of IT-activity income during the preceding 12 months.
Passport copy and information about accompanying spouse, parents or children, where applicable.

initial_validity.value: 3 years
initial_validity.notes: IT Park's official program page states that the IT Visa is valid for three years and permits work without a separate work permit.

extension_rules.notes: The current pages confirm three-year validity but do not clearly state a route-specific renewal limit or renewal procedure. General visa-extension fees should not be assumed to establish IT Visa eligibility for renewal.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The IT Visa provides a three-year lawful-stay and work status for qualifying IT Park-linked applicants.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is treated here as temporary immigration status, not as permanent residence.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic conversion from the IT Visa to permanent residence was confirmed. Permanent residence is a separately processed status.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official permanent-residence pages do not state that IT Visa time creates entitlement to permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct citizenship path from the IT Visa was confirmed. Ordinary naturalization requires a residence permit followed by five years of continuous permanent residence, lawful income, Uzbek-language ability and renunciation of foreign citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Because acquisition of permanent residence is separate and not assured, the IT Visa is not a confirmed citizenship-track route.

rejected_routes.notes: This category is attractive for software engineers but fails the applicant profile because a resident Uzbek legal-entity employer is mandatory. The 2025 expansion added startup participants, academics and IT Park company executives, but those are specialized founder, startup, academic or local-company categories rather than ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

rejected_routes.route_name: IT Visa — founder or investor categories

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly-income threshold is stated for founders. Investors instead must finance an IT-sector legal entity by at least USD 10,000.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The program publishes an investment amount in USD rather than a monthly local-currency income threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly income threshold; investor category requires at least USD 10,000 investment
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: Approximately UZS 120.35 million one-time investment equivalent at the displayed CBU rate
income_requirement_display.notes: The founder category requires founding an IT Park resident legal entity. These categories materially change the applicant profile.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is published for these categories.

key_requirements.requirement: Founder category: be a founder of a duly registered legal entity included in the IT Park resident register.
Investor category: finance an IT-sector legal entity under an agreement by at least USD 10,000.
Expanded categories include qualifying foreign startup participants and executives of IT Park resident companies.

initial_validity.value: 3 years

extension_rules.notes: Route-specific renewal rules were not clearly published on the pages inspected.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Qualifying founders and investors may receive the three-year IT Visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No automatic IT Visa-to-permanent-residence entitlement was confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: Citizenship would require separately obtaining permanent residence and satisfying the general naturalization rules.

rejected_routes.notes: Independent filing may be possible, but only after adopting a founder or investor profile with local corporate or investment substance. It is excluded for an ordinary software engineer continuing a foreign employment or client contract.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The registration pages publish no minimum income requirement.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No minimum income threshold is stated.

income_requirement_display.value: No immigration income threshold; this is business/tax registration, not a residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: Registration does not supply an immigration basis to remain in Uzbekistan.

income_proof_months.notes: No income-proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Obtain a PINFL/JShShIR and OneID access; foreigners can obtain the identification number through public-service centers or migration offices.
Register through the Soliq application or government portal and select an allowed activity and place of activity.
From 2026, self-employed persons with turnover within the applicable ceiling are generally subject to 1% turnover tax; the permitted-activity list was narrowed.

initial_validity.value: Economic registration; no immigration validity period published

extension_rules.value: Not applicable as an immigration status

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None confirmed. A PINFL, bank account or self-employed registration does not itself extend a visa, temporary registration or authorized stay.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed from self-employed registration.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from this registration alone.

rejected_routes.notes: This can facilitate legal economic and tax registration after entry, but the official materials do not establish it as a route to temporary or permanent residence. Entering as a visitor, obtaining a PINFL and registering as self-employed therefore does not legalize long-term residence.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visitor, visa-free stay or electronic visa

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker threshold applies.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-work income threshold; visitor entry is not a residence route

income_proof_months.notes: Not applicable.

key_requirements.requirement: Entry eligibility depends on nationality, the visa-free list or successful eVisa issuance.
Foreign visitors generally must register their place of stay within three working days unless an exception applies.

initial_validity.value: Depends on nationality and visa type

extension_rules.value: General visa extension rules and fees apply where an extension is legally available.
extension_rules.notes: An extension does not convert visitor status into a remote-worker residence route.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None directly

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None directly

path_to_citizenship.value: None directly

rejected_routes.notes: Visitor, visa-free and eVisa entry is unsuitable for the citizenship-oriented selection. No official source inspected grants ordinary foreign-contract remote-work residence rights through visitor status.

summary.value: Foreign students can receive an A-1 or STD student visa for up to one year upon a request from an Uzbek educational institution. This is institution-supported study permission and temporary registration, not direct qualifying temporary or permanent residence, and no independent degree-only skilled-migration route was found.
summary.notes: A university degree helps demonstrate IT qualification for the employer-linked IT Visa but does not independently create residence eligibility.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally tax resident when present in Uzbekistan for 183 days or more during any consecutive 12-month period beginning or ending in the relevant tax period. PwC also reports a secondary test where the individual spends fewer than 183 days in Uzbekistan but more time there than in any other country.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and the facts of each stay can alter the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the flat general PIT screening rate for employment, rent, capital gains and similar taxable income, not an estimated effective rate. A self-employed person under the 2026 turnover regime may instead face 1% of turnover.

social_contributions_percent.notes: This is the ordinary employer-paid social tax on gross payroll, not a confirmed employee deduction. Self-employed persons may make a voluntary annual social-tax payment for pension/employment-history credit.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No universal mandatory monthly social contribution or digital-nomad fixed payment exists. Self-employed social tax for work-history credit is described as an annual voluntary payment, while visa and registration charges depend on status and duration.

special_tax_regimes.value: From 1 January 2026, qualifying individual entrepreneurs and self-employed persons are generally subject to 1% turnover tax within the applicable turnover ceiling. No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker tax holiday was found.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Activity eligibility, turnover ceiling, VAT exposure and whether a foreigner's services qualify require filing-level confirmation.

taxes.caveats: Tax outcome depends on physical presence, whether the contract is employment or independent services, source-of-income rules, self-employed registration, applicable turnover thresholds, VAT rules and any tax treaty. Economic registration does not cure an immigration-status problem.

taxation_system.value: Uzbekistan generally applies flat 12% PIT to residents' worldwide taxable income and to most Uzbek-source income of non-residents. A separate 1% turnover-tax regime can apply to qualifying self-employed persons and individual entrepreneurs.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Generally 183 days or more in any consecutive 12-month period; a secondary comparative-presence test may also apply.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Uzbekistan-source income.
taxation_system.special_regimes: Qualifying self-employed persons and individual entrepreneurs face 1% turnover tax from 2026 within the applicable ceiling. No nomad-specific regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Ordinary employer social tax is 12% of gross payroll. The Tax Committee states that a self-employed person may voluntarily pay at least one BCU annually for work-history credit; this was UZS 412,000 in the cited 2026 notice.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: PIT is not progressive. The 12% value is a flat general rate. The 1% self-employed turnover tax is imposed on turnover rather than net income and should not be compared directly with PIT.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: No income threshold; general flat rate
tax_brackets.applies_to: Employment income, rent, capital gains and similar taxable income
tax_brackets.notes: Dividends and interest have separate rates and exemptions.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Qualifying self-employed or individual-entrepreneur turnover within the applicable 2026 ceiling
tax_brackets.notes: The Tax Committee notice cites annual turnover up to UZS 1 billion; later 2026 amendments may affect thresholds, so current filing treatment should be confirmed.

taxation_system.notes: Official government material supports the 183-day rule and 2026 self-employed changes; PwC supplies the clearest consolidated worldwide-income and social-tax treatment.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad route or special nomad tax regime exists. A person who independently establishes lawful residence and becomes tax resident would generally face 12% PIT on worldwide taxable income unless properly registered under an applicable self-employed turnover-tax regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No DNV; hypothetical foreign remote worker or locally registered self-employed person
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 12% flat general PIT; potentially 1% of turnover under the qualifying 2026 self-employed regime
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally 183 days in a consecutive 12-month period, with a possible comparative-presence test.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income; non-residents are taxed on Uzbekistan-source income.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary employer social tax is 12%. No mandatory employee-side contribution was confirmed for a foreign remote worker. Self-employed persons may voluntarily pay annual social tax for work-history credit.

fixed_payments.status: partially_confirmed
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Voluntary self-employed social-tax payment of at least one BCU annually for work-history credit; the cited 2026 notice states UZS 412,000 per year.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Uzbekistan has no digital-nomad visa. For the closest relevant status, the IT Visa, the direct application page publishes no service price. Separate official general schedules list a USD 350 consular fee for a multiple-entry visa valid up to three years (plus location-dependent actual processing costs), while the state-duty schedule lists 14 BCV for a multiple-entry exit-entry visa up to three years and 12 BCV for temporary registration up to three years. Neither general schedule expressly labels those amounts as the IT Visa charge, so the payable IT Visa amount remains filing-specific and must be confirmed in the application portal.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: Qualifying self-employed activity is generally subject to 1% turnover tax from 2026. VAT and other business taxes depend on registration and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: The fixed-payment review is partly conclusive: there is no dedicated nomad status or nomad fee; the IT Visa service page omits a price; and the two official general visa schedules publish different categories of charges rather than an IT-Visa-specific total. Confirm all portal, consular, registration and processing charges before filing.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person below the residence threshold is generally taxed only on Uzbekistan-source income, but source characterization and treaty rules must be checked. Visitor status still does not authorize long-term remote-worker residence.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident is generally exposed to 12% PIT on worldwide taxable income unless a valid business regime applies.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A qualifying registered self-employed person may face 1% turnover tax and may voluntarily pay annual social tax, but registration does not grant immigration status.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening analysis, not a filing determination. There is no dedicated nomad status whose tax treatment can be evaluated separately.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: The IT Visa grants a three-year stay to qualifying linked applicants, but there is no confirmed ordinary remote-worker route and no published self-employment-to-residence waiting period.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No automatic conversion period from IT Visa, visitor status, student status or self-employment registration to permanent residence was confirmed.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: General naturalization requires five years of continuous permanent residence from obtaining the residence permit to applying.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The total cannot be calculated because no fitting route or fixed timeline to permanent residence was established.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The official guidance states that total review and processing must not exceed one year.

key_conditions.value: Renunciation of foreign citizenship, five years of continuous permanent residence, lawful income, respect for the Constitution and sufficient Uzbek for everyday communication. The official guidance treats absences and continuity as legally significant.
key_conditions.notes: The five-year period begins from permanent residence, not from ordinary visitor entry or self-employed registration.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No reduced citizenship period was confirmed for an ordinary foreign citizen married to an Uzbek citizen. The law's three-year marriage/cohabitation exception is expressly framed for a stateless person.

existing_marriage_effect.value: A foreign marriage validly concluded under the law of the place of celebration can be recognized in Uzbekistan, and a marriage certificate is relevant to residence or citizenship documentation. Marriage alone does not automatically confer permanent residence or citizenship.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage must be legally valid and documented. Uzbekistan identifies a fictitious marriage—registered without intent to create a family—as a ground for judicial invalidation. Foreign citizens should not rely on marriage as an automatic status or citizenship shortcut.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The special three-year naturalization exception should not be generalized beyond stateless spouses without case-specific legal advice.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is mainly by descent. Birth in Uzbekistan grants citizenship where the parents are stateless, and foundlings are protected, but birth to two foreign-citizen parents does not by itself grant citizenship.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Uzbekistan to two foreign-citizen migrant parents does not obtain Uzbek citizenship merely by birth. A child born there to stateless parents does acquire citizenship, and a foundling is treated as a citizen.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If either parent is an Uzbek citizen, the child acquires Uzbek citizenship by birth regardless of place of birth, including where the other parent is a foreign citizen.

parent_benefit_summary.value: Having an Uzbek-citizen child does not automatically make a foreign father a citizen. Any residence benefit must be pursued under separate immigration rules, and no automatic parent route was confirmed in the official pages inspected.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Family evidence may be relevant to an application but is not equivalent to approval.

benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The sources confirm the child's citizenship rules but do not establish an automatic or accelerated permanent-residence or citizenship entitlement for the foreign father solely because the child is Uzbek.

rank.notes: Passport Index's current Passport Power Rank, not the Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Passport Index's visa-required count.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Combined from 39 visa-on-arrival destinations and 3 eTA destinations. Passport Index separately reports these categories.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 70, consisting of 28 visa-free, 39 visa-on-arrival and 3 eTA destinations. Electronic visas are not included in the visa-on-arrival/eTA total.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is usable in parts of the technology and outsourcing ecosystem, and major IT Visa information is published in English, but government procedures and long-term integration should not be assumed to work entirely in English.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current nationwide English-proficiency measure was found in the official sources inspected.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian is practically useful because substantial government guidance and services are published in Russian, but it is not the state language. Ukrainian has no confirmed official or broadly supported administrative role.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Uzbek remains necessary for naturalization and is the constitutionally designated state language.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official UZS 7,091,104.5 national average monthly nominal accrued wage for April–June 2026 using the latest displayed CBU rate of UZS 12,035.26 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The current official labor-market catalog and the annual and quarterly wage tables publish arithmetic averages by country, region and activity, but no employee-level 50th-percentile wage. The living-standards tables publish household total-income shares and an income-differentiation coefficient, which are not a median employee salary and cannot be converted into one.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the UZS 1,271,000 national minimum wage. This is a statutory minimum, not an observed lower bound of salaries.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the official April–June 2026 national average monthly nominal accrued wage.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No national employee-wage median is published in the current official tables inspected. They report arithmetic average wages by geography/activity, while the separate household-income distribution series reports shares and a differentiation coefficient rather than a median salary; therefore no defensible USD median can be calculated.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The current official wage tables do not publish an individual national maximum or an upper employee-wage percentile. The UZS 18,595,800 figure published for banking, insurance, leasing and credit is the highest sectoral average in the January–March comparison, not a maximum salary, so it is not used as a national maximum.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: National statutory minimum wage cited in a 2026 government-hosted project document.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Official national average monthly nominal accrued wage for April–June 2026; this is an arithmetic mean, not a median.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The named current official sources do not publish a national 50th-percentile employee wage in UZS. Household total-income deciles are a different population-level measure and do not supply or permit derivation of a median salary.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No individual national maximum salary or upper wage-distribution bound is published in the named current official sources. Their highest reported category is a sectoral arithmetic average, which is not a worker-level maximum and is therefore not substituted here.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory minimum wage plus official average monthly nominal accrued wage
average_citizen_salary.period: April–June 2026 for average wage; current cited national minimum wage
average_citizen_salary.notes: These figures describe citizen/resident worker wages, not immigration income thresholds. The average is the current official preliminary nominal accrued arithmetic mean for April–June 2026; the minimum is statutory. Official wage tables do not publish a median or worker-level maximum, and household-income distribution measures are not substitutes. USD conversions use the latest displayed CBU rate and are approximate.

cost_of_living_note.notes: Official household-consumption totals were checked, but they do not provide a defensible individual monthly cost-of-living budget. No estimate is supplied rather than converting a national aggregate into a misleading personal figure.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor entry, a PINFL, bank account or self-employed registration does not create residence rights. The IT Visa requires local IT Park-linked employment, founder status or investment.
settlement_track.summary: No ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker route was confirmed. The IT Visa is a three-year local-company, founder or investor program, while self-employed registration has no confirmed residence conversion; citizenship would require separately obtaining permanent residence and then completing five years of continuous residence.
settlement_track.notes: The prior result's ineligible conclusion is retained and strengthened. Current official sources confirm that the attractive IT-specialist category requires an Uzbek resident-company employer letter.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker residence status was found. The relevant IT Visa specialist category requires local employment, and economic self-registration does not legalize residence.

data.notes: Audited against the previous Uzbekistan record and 33 distinct directly relevant URLs, including six focused new official URLs outside the previous source set. The IT Visa fee is now precisely bounded by the published general schedules but remains filing-specific because the IT Visa application page omits a price. Current official wage sources publish an April–June 2026 arithmetic average but no national employee-wage median or worker-level maximum; household-income distribution data are not substituted for salary percentiles. Other remaining nulls are facts not defensibly established: IT Visa renewal rules, the timing or entitlement for conversion to permanent residence, an individual cost-of-living budget, and any automatic immigration benefit to the foreign father of an Uzbek child.

data.selection_summary: Vanuatu has no current digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker route. Its independently accessible self-funded residence visa requires certified monthly income of VT250,000 and can support lawful residence, but residence holders remain subject to work-permit and business-licensing laws; official work guidance and Vanuatu case law do not establish a way for an ordinary foreign-client software contractor to work independently without local sponsorship or separate authorization. Visitor consultancy authority is limited to 12 weeks and requires an employer or organization undertaking. The previous false verdict is therefore retained and strengthened.

visa_application.title: Vanuatu eVisa Portal — Explore your visa options
visa_application.notes: This is the official general online visa portal. No dedicated digital-nomad application was found. The self-funded residence route is described on the Immigration Department’s residence page and uses its residence form/checklist; the official sources do not establish that self-funded residence itself authorizes the proposed foreign-client work.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: Approximation: VT250,000 divided by the Reserve Bank’s 27 July 2026 indicative rate of VT117.44 per USD. Exchange rates fluctuate.

minimum_income_local_currency.value: VT250,000 per month for one applicant; VT500,000 if including a spouse or de-facto partner
minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The income must be certified by a Vanuatu bank.

income_requirement_display.value: VT250,000/month (about US$2,129); VT500,000 with spouse/partner
income_requirement_display.currency_basis: VUV threshold converted using an indicative July 2026 RBV rate
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: VT250,000/month individual; VT500,000/month with spouse or de-facto partner
income_requirement_display.notes: The local-currency requirement controls. The USD figure is only an approximation.

income_proof_months.notes: The checklist requires evidence of monthly income certified by a local bank but does not state a required bank-statement history in months.

key_requirements.requirement: Completed residence application form, passport valid for more than six months and two recent photographs.
Recent police clearance and medical certificate.
Immigration bond held at the National Bank of Vanuatu.
Evidence of VT250,000 monthly income certified by a Vanuatu bank.
VT57,600 application fee; an applicant changing status from inside Vanuatu is listed as paying an additional VT100,000.
Any employment remains subject to the Labour (Work Permits) Act, and commercial or business activity remains subject to business-licensing, foreign-investment and other applicable laws.

initial_validity.value: At least 1 year and no more than 10 years, as determined on grant
initial_validity.notes: This is the statutory range for a residence visa, not a guaranteed ten-year grant.

extension_rules.value: Continued residence requires another filing under the published self-funded renewal process; the Immigration Act states that a visa cannot be extended or renewed, so the checklist appears to operate as a replacement/re-grant process rather than a statutory extension.
extension_rules.notes: Applicants should confirm the filing mechanism and timing directly with Immigration because the website terminology and the Act are not perfectly aligned.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Direct residence visa upon approval
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is genuine residence, but residence status alone does not remove separate work-permit and business-authorization requirements.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No separate direct permanent-residence status or automatic conversion was confirmed in the current Immigration Act and official route materials.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The residence visa may be granted for up to ten years, but it is not described as permanent residence.

path_to_citizenship.value: General naturalization may be requested after 10 years of continuous ordinary and legal residence, subject to character, financial self-sufficiency, cultural knowledge, Bislama testing and other citizenship requirements. This does not cure the absence of authorization for the proposed remote work.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The residence-to-naturalization rule is real, but this route is rejected for this applicant because lawful continuation of the active foreign-client contract is not established.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest independent residence option, but it is an income-supported residence category rather than a remote-worker authorization. Section 45 of the Immigration Act makes residence-holder work and business activity subject to other laws; the official work page is employer-oriented, and the cited Court of Appeal authority applies the work-permit framework to non-citizen work, including contract-for-service arrangements. Filing-level legal advice is necessary before performing any foreign-client services from Vanuatu.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The page requires sufficient upkeep funds but publishes no amount.

income_requirement_display.notes: This authority is unsuitable regardless of income because it is visitor-based, limited to 12 weeks and requires an employer or organization undertaking for workers.

income_proof_months.notes: No number of proof months is stated.

Return ticket, passport copies, sufficient upkeep funds, passport submission after approval and the applicable fee.

extension_rules.value: No continuation beyond the stated 12-week maximum was confirmed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: None; this remains authority attached to visitor status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None confirmed.

path_to_citizenship.value: None from this visitor authority.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor-like temporary authorization is not treated as a citizenship path.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is temporary visitor authority, not residence, and workers need an employer or organization undertaking. The page also appears to retain references to the superseded 2003 Act, so current applicability should be confirmed before relying on it.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No employee salary threshold is published on the cited visa pages.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No employee salary threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published minimum salary on the cited route page
income_requirement_display.notes: Eligibility instead depends on employer sponsorship, a Vanuatu employment contract and work permission.

income_proof_months.notes: This is not an income-proof route.

key_requirements.requirement: Acceptable sponsorship from an employer and skilled work for a business operating in Vanuatu.
Permission to work under the Labour (Work Permits) Act.
The visa holder must remain employed by the business on which the visa was granted.

initial_validity.notes: The official page lists a VT257,500 employment-visa charge.

extension_rules.value: No independent renewal path was established; continued eligibility remains tied to the sponsoring employment and work permit.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct residence status; this is an employment visa.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct permanent residence; the page says change of status is allowed only to an investor visa.

path_to_citizenship.value: No employer-visa-specific citizenship conversion was confirmed.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a local employer, sponsorship, Vanuatu work and a work permit are required.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: Support-funds requirement, not employment income.

income_requirement_display.notes: The local amount controls.

income_proof_months.notes: Funds must cover the visa duration, but no retrospective statement period is specified.

Passport, photographs, security deposit equivalent to return airfare, support funds and medical examination for adults.
Employment or business activity is prohibited unless it forms a required part of the study program.

initial_validity.notes: The sources contain differing fee amounts and should be checked at filing.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None; the official study page says the student may not change status.

path_to_citizenship.value: No student-visa settlement or citizenship path was confirmed.

summary.value: A self-sponsored student may apply without a local employer after acceptance by a Vanuatu institution, but receives temporary student status rather than residence. Work is restricted to activity required by the course, and the official study page says the status cannot be changed.
summary.notes: This is not a degree-based skilled migration route and does not fit an applicant wishing to continue ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: Vanuatu currently imposes no general personal income tax, so no domestic PIT-residency day threshold was identified for individuals. Immigration residence, VAT/business registration and another country’s tax-residence rules remain separate questions.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Official Vanuatu revenue materials describe VAT and previously consulted on introducing personal and corporate income taxes; no enacted general PIT regime was found in the current additional search.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening rate for general personal income tax, not a special digital-nomad exemption. The absence of Vanuatu PIT does not validate the proposed work under immigration or labour law.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share from 1 January 2026; the total mandatory VNPF contribution is 12%, split 6% employee and 6% employer. VNPF states self-employed workers are not obliged to join and may contribute voluntarily.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly VNPF payment for an independently self-employed person is published in the cited guidance. Employee contributions are percentage-based.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax regime was found. Vanuatu’s general absence of personal income tax applies independently of visa eligibility. VAT is 15%, with compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed VT4 million in a 12-month period; services to non-residents outside Vanuatu may be zero-rated under the published VAT guidance.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Whether foreign software services constitute a Vanuatu taxable activity and qualify for zero rating requires professional advice.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on whether the person is legally carrying on employment or business in Vanuatu, the client’s location, VAT registration and place-of-supply rules, and continuing tax residence or treaty obligations elsewhere. Vanuatu’s zero PIT rate should not be confused with permission to work.

taxation_system.value: No general personal income tax; separate consumption, business, licensing and social-security rules apply.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No operative PIT-residence threshold was identified because Vanuatu does not currently levy general personal income tax.
taxation_system.income_scope: No general individual income-tax base; VAT and other transaction or business taxes can still apply.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker PIT regime found.
taxation_system.social_security: From January 2026, mandatory VNPF contributions for covered employees total 12% of remuneration, split 6% employee and 6% employer. Self-employed workers are not compulsory members according to VNPF guidance.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Not applicable: the displayed 0% is the absence of general PIT, not a progressive top rate.
taxation_system.notes: The official tax sources do not publish a conventional individual tax-residence guide because there is no general PIT. Advice is still needed for VAT, licensing, foreign tax residence and contract structure.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Vanuatu has no confirmed digital-nomad route. General PIT is 0%, but this does not authorize foreign-contract work. A self-funded resident performing services may face immigration, work-permit, business-licence and VAT questions.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; hypothetical self-funded resident or locally authorized worker
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 0% general personal income tax; not a nomad-specific concession
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: No domestic PIT day-count threshold was found because no general PIT is imposed.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: No general Vanuatu PIT was identified for foreign employment or service income; home-country taxation and business/VAT rules may still apply.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Covered employees pay 6% VNPF and employers pay 6% from January 2026. Self-employed workers are not obliged to join, according to the VNPF employer guidance.

fixed_payments.status: No mandatory fixed monthly tax or social-security payment confirmed for an independently self-employed person.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage-based VNPF contributions apply to covered employment; voluntary membership is available for self-employed workers.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Self-funded residence checklist: VT57,600 application fee, plus VT100,000 for an in-country change of status where applicable. An immigration bond is also required, but its amount is not published in the checklist.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT is 15%. Compulsory VAT registration begins when taxable supplies exceed VT4 million over 12 months. Business-licensing or foreign-investment charges were not quantified for this incompatible scenario.
fixed_payments.notes: The residence fees are filing costs rather than monthly taxes.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: No PIT threshold applies, but visitor status prohibits paid employment or commercial activity unless separate limited authority is obtained.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no confirmed remote-worker status. Even with self-funded residence and 0% PIT, work and business remain subject to labour, licensing and investment laws.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: Self-employed persons are not compulsory VNPF members, but VAT registration may be required above VT4 million taxable supplies. Registration does not itself create immigration or work authorization.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: Tax facts are clearer than immigration fit: PIT is absent, but no official source converts that tax position into permission for ordinary foreign-client remote work.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: Self-funded residence is granted directly after approval, but it is not selected as a qualifying remote-work route. No official processing duration specific to residence was published; Immigration only asks applicants to wait 21 working days before making visa enquiries.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No distinct permanent-residence stage or conversion timeline is established in the reviewed official framework.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Naturalization is based on 10 years of continuous ordinary/legal residence, not on a published number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: The general rule is 10 years of continuous ordinary and legal residence, but no matching foreign-remote-work route was found, so a route-specific total is not reported.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Department says it responds to citizenship enquiries only after 60 days, but this is not a promised or typical completion time.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires 10 years’ continuous ordinary/legal residence, intention to continue residing, good character, financial self-sufficiency, respect for Vanuatu culture, citizenship knowledge, allegiance requirements and a Bislama citizenship test under later amendments. Dual citizenship is now recognized, but applicants should verify current documentary requirements and absence rules with the Citizenship Office.
key_conditions.notes: These are general citizenship rules, not proof that the rejected self-funded status authorizes remote work.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The applicant must be legally married and have lived with the citizen spouse in Vanuatu for at least two years before applying.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing legal marriage can support a partner residence application and later citizenship, but it does not create immediate citizenship. The couple must live together in Vanuatu for the required two-year period.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: A genuine de-facto relationship can support residence, while the citizenship route is described in terms of legal marriage.

requirements_and_risks.value: Provide the marriage certificate and proof of the spouse’s Vanuatu citizenship; pass the Bislama citizenship test and satisfy citizenship screening. Residence applications require a genuine relationship. False statements or sham arrangements can result in refusal and legal consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Marriage accelerates citizenship eligibility but does not waive genuine-relationship, residence or testing requirements.

birthright_citizenship.notes: The Constitution grants post-independence citizenship to a person born in Vanuatu or abroad only if at least one parent is a Vanuatu citizen. Birth in the territory alone is insufficient.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Vanuatu to two non-citizen migrant parents does not obtain citizenship merely by birth. Separate anti-statelessness, adoption, entitlement or later naturalization provisions may need case-specific review.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No broad jus soli rule exists.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: The child becomes a Vanuatu citizen if at least one parent is a Vanuatu citizen, whether the child is born in Vanuatu or abroad.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Birth registration and proof of parentage remain practical requirements.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence on a migrant father. A parent may have a family-based residence or citizenship claim only through a separate qualifying relationship or statutory category.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The residence page expressly lists partner and dependent-child grounds, but does not publish an automatic parent-of-citizen-child residence entitlement.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic status. If the father is married to or in a genuine de-facto relationship with the child’s Vanuatu-citizen parent, he may pursue partner residence; citizenship through marriage still requires legal marriage and two years living together in Vanuatu.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Parenthood alone should not be treated as a shortcut.

passport.index_name: Henley Passport Index 2026, as reproduced by a current specialist secondary source

rank.notes: The current specialist source reports approximately 57th place using the 26 June 2026 Henley data. Henley’s live page was inspected, but its accessible text did not expose Vanuatu’s row; treat the exact rank as medium-confidence and recheck the live index before relying on it.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Henley-style access score combining destinations available without a prior visa, including visa on arrival. It is not a pure visa-free-only count.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Neither the accessible official Henley page nor the inspected current secondary source supplied a complete separate count of advance-visa destinations.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: The current source combines visa-free and visa-on-arrival access into 87 and does not provide a reliable separate VOA/eTA subtotal.

passport.notes: Vanuatu lost UK visa-free access in 2023 and Schengen visa exemption was permanently revoked by the EU in December 2024. The current combined access score is therefore materially below older records.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is an official language and one of the two principal languages of education, so administration and professional interaction in English are broadly practical, especially in Port Vila. Bislama remains the national lingua franca and is important for local integration.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This addresses language practicality only; infrastructure quality and work authorization are separate issues.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No official or reliable source reviewed identified Russian or Ukrainian as commonly supported languages. A Russian- or Ukrainian-only resident should expect to rely on English, French or Bislama and on translation where necessary.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Cautious assessment based on the official language framework; no quantitative proficiency data for Russian or Ukrainian was found.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The official 2019–2020 labour-market monograph reports wage bands rather than an arithmetic mean, so an average USD salary cannot be calculated reliably without microdata.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The published distribution places the median employee in the VT40,000–VT60,000 monthly band, but it does not publish an exact median amount; no midpoint is invented.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the VT52,800 statutory monthly equivalent using the Reserve Bank rate of VT117.44 per US dollar retained from the previous record; the rounded figure is about US$450 and varies with exchange rates.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official labour-market report publishes wage bands rather than an arithmetic mean.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The exact median is unpublished; the median falls within the reported VT40,000–VT60,000 monthly band.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The official distribution has an open-ended 'more than VT200,000' category, not a national maximum salary.

min_salary_local_currency.value: VT300 per hour; VT52,800 per month statutory equivalent on a 22-day, 8-hour basis
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Focused audit result: Minimum Wage and Minimum Wages Board (Amendment) Order No. 127 of 2023 raised the national floor to VT300 per hour. The Minimum Wage Act uses 22 working days per month and 8 hours per day as its calculation basis, and the Supreme Court applied that formula in December 2025 to state a current equivalent of VT52,800 per month. This reconciles the employers’ guide: VT52,800 is a statutory equivalent, not a separately prescribed flat monthly rate, so actual lawful monthly pay depends on hours worked; specified seasonal, student and young-worker exceptions may apply.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The official report provides band shares, not an arithmetic mean.

median_salary_local_currency.value: Exact value unpublished; median lies in the VT40,000–VT60,000 monthly band
median_salary_local_currency.notes: About 56.3% of employees with declared wages earned VT20,000–VT60,000; the cumulative distribution places the median in the VT40,000–VT60,000 band.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: Only an open-ended 'more than VT200,000 per month' band is published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory minimum wage (hourly legal floor and Act-based monthly equivalent); separate 2019 employee main-job wage-band distribution for median and other salary fields
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum wage current through sources checked to 2026-08-15; wage distribution from the 2019 HIES
average_citizen_salary.notes: The statutory minimum is VT300 per hour. The Act’s 22-day, 8-hour monthly basis produces VT52,800, expressly confirmed as the current monthly equivalent by the Supreme Court in December 2025; this is a legal minimum-wage calculation, not an observed average citizen salary. The HIES still supports only wage bands, not exact national mean or median pay. The Department of Labour, Ministry materials, Government Remuneration Tribunal review, current court judgment, employers’ guide and current WageIndicator record were checked for a later rate; none identified a post-Order-127 increase by 2026-08-15.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official labour-market source does not publish a current nationwide cost-of-living estimate. A speculative crowdsourced amount is therefore not supplied.
