settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor consultancy authority lasts no more than 12 weeks and is not residence. Self-funded residence is longer-term but does not independently authorize the proposed foreign-client work.
settlement_track.summary: No current route combines independent foreign-contract work authorization with a qualifying settlement path. Although self-funded residence can potentially accumulate ordinary residence toward the general ten-year naturalization rule, the applicant would need separate lawful work or business authorization incompatible with the ordinary unsponsored remote-worker profile.
settlement_track.notes: The previous result correctly rejected Vanuatu. Current official pages still show self-funded residence, employer-sponsored work, temporary visitor consultancy and student routes, but no digital-nomad or ordinary independent foreign-remote-worker category.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No dedicated remote-worker status exists. Residence-holder work remains subject to labour and business laws; ordinary work visas require a Vanuatu employer, while visitor consultancy requires an employer or organization undertaking and lasts only 12 weeks.

data.notes: Focused unresolved-field audit retained the previous false selection verdict and all still-supported immigration, tax, citizenship, family, passport, language and wage-distribution findings. Thirty-three distinct relevant URLs are listed, including six focused wage sources not present in the previous source set. The flagged minimum-wage note is now resolved: VT300 per hour remains the published floor, while VT52,800 is the Act-based monthly equivalent expressly applied by the Supreme Court in December 2025, not a separately prescribed flat monthly salary. Other remaining nulls are explained where the named current sources do not publish an exact figure.

data.selection_summary: Venezuela has no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker residence route. The closest independent option is the one-year renewable Transeúnte Rentista visa, limited to foreign rent or pension income rather than active remote-work earnings. A visa resolution says a TR-RE holder who remains continuously for at least one year may request discretionary Resident status renewable every five years, but this does not make an ordinary foreign software contract eligible for TR-RE; current filing practice should be confirmed.

visa_application.title: Visa de Transeúnte Rentista (TR-RE)
visa_application.notes: Official Ministry of Foreign Affairs route-information page for the closest independent visa. It is not a direct online application portal; applicants must consult the responsible Venezuelan diplomatic or consular mission. No dedicated digital-nomad application channel was found.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The applicant must document at least USD 1,200 per month from foreign rents or a pension, plus USD 500 for each accompanying family member.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The official threshold is denominated in US dollars, not bolívares.

income_requirement_display.value: USD 1,200 per month from foreign rents or pension; USD 500 extra per accompanying family member
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: USD 1,200 + USD 500 per accompanying family member
income_requirement_display.notes: Active salary or foreign-client contract income is not expressly accepted. Official pages refer to rent, retirement, or pension income.

income_proof_months.notes: The official pages require proof of continuing qualifying income but do not state a fixed bank-statement history.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport with at least six months remaining and photographs.
Documents proving foreign rent or pension income of at least USD 1,200 monthly.
Return or onward ticket, medical certificate, and payment of the mission-specific consular fee.
Some consular missions additionally request a recent apostilled criminal-record certificate and Spanish translations.

initial_validity.value: 1 year, multiple entries, with permission to remain for the same period
initial_validity.notes: The Ministry expressly describes the holder as a non-migrant.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for equal one-year periods by the ministry responsible for interior affairs, subject to proof that the foreign income source continues
extension_rules.notes: No maximum number of renewals is stated.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No conversion to an intermediate temporary-migrant status was established; the captured rule instead permits a direct request for Resident status after the qualifying period.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: TR-RE is described as non-migrant notwithstanding the separate discretionary Resident application provision.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least one uninterrupted year in Venezuela on TR-RE, Article 40 of the visa-procedure resolution permits the holder to request Resident status; the Interior Ministry may grant it, and the resulting status is renewable every five years. The wording is discretionary, not automatic.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Resolution No. 364 dates from 2000, while the 2004 migration law later reorganized migration categories without reproducing a route-specific procedure. Applicants should confirm with SAIME that Article 40 remains applied before relying on it.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially, but not directly: obtain discretionary Resident status after at least one uninterrupted TR-RE year, then satisfy the Constitution's domicile and uninterrupted-residence requirement—normally 10 years immediately before applying, reduced to 5 years for nationals by birth of Spain, Portugal, Italy, Latin American countries, and Caribbean countries. Naturalization remains discretionary and requires the Carta de Naturaleza process.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The reviewed sources do not state whether every day on pre-Resident TR-RE status is credited toward the constitutional residence period. The Naturalization Law also contemplates Spanish-language knowledge.

rejected_routes.notes: This is the closest independent route and has a plausible discretionary settlement conversion, but it does not match ordinary foreign-contract software work because eligibility is framed around passive rent or pension income.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general monthly-income threshold is published; the routes instead require qualifying business activity, company ownership, or an accepted Venezuelan investment.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general local-currency threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published monthly-income threshold; qualifying business activity or Venezuelan investment is required
income_requirement_display.notes: These are commercial or investment categories, not foreign-remote-work residence routes.

income_proof_months.notes: No standardized income-history period is published.

key_requirements.requirement: The business visa requires a commercial purpose, bank letter, business registration, and a contact or company address in Venezuela.
The empresario-industrial category requires ownership of a company or industry abroad or a Venezuelan affiliate and travel connected with that enterprise.
The investor category requires a realized Venezuelan investment accepted by the appropriate official bodies.

initial_validity.notes: The official mission pages reviewed did not consistently expose the duration for every grouped category.

extension_rules.notes: No common renewal rule applies across the three grouped categories.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying route for ordinary foreign-client remote work was established.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Status depends on maintaining the approved business or investment activity.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: The grouped categories do not share one rule. Article 40 expressly allows a TR-I investor who has remained continuously for at least one year to request discretionary Resident status renewable every five years; it does not list TR-N business or TR-E-I entrepreneur/industrial visas, so no equivalent route was established for those two categories.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Only the investor subcategory has the captured one-year Resident application provision. All three remain rejected because they require Venezuelan business, enterprise, or investment activity.

path_to_citizenship.value: A TR-I holder who obtains Resident status could subsequently use the general constitutional naturalization framework. No route-specific citizenship transition was established for TR-N or TR-E-I.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization remains discretionary and subject to domicile and qualifying uninterrupted residence.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because these categories require Venezuelan commercial activity, company ownership, or investment. A foreign software contract alone does not satisfy their purposes.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No immigration salary threshold is published on the official page.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No immigration salary threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: No published visa salary threshold; Venezuelan labor authorization is required
income_requirement_display.notes: This route depends on authorized employment and fails the independent-application criterion.

income_proof_months.notes: No standardized income-history period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Prior authorization involving the Venezuelan interior and labor authorities.
A Venezuelan Ministry of Labor work permit and supporting employment documentation.
Valid passport, photographs, criminal-record certificate, and consular fee.

initial_validity.value: 1 year, multiple entries, with one year of permitted stay
initial_validity.notes: The captured resolution supplies the duration omitted from the reviewed consular page.

extension_rules.value: Renewable for one-year periods after ratification of the labor authorization
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains employer and work-authorization dependent.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The category authorizes temporary labor residence, but only through approved employment.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not available for independent foreign-contract remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: After at least one uninterrupted year on TR-L, Article 40 permits the worker to request discretionary Resident status renewable every five years, but initial eligibility requires Venezuelan labor authorization and therefore remains employer-dependent.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This transition does not cure the route's failure of the independent-application criterion.

path_to_citizenship.value: A worker who obtains Resident status may later use the general constitutional naturalization framework, but this does not make the employer-dependent visa suitable for selection.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization ordinarily requires 10 years of qualifying uninterrupted residence, subject to specified five-year nationality reductions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because Venezuelan labor authorization and an employment basis are required.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The institution must indicate the student's means of support, but no numerical minimum is published.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No numerical local-currency threshold is published.

income_requirement_display.value: Sufficient means must be documented; no official numerical minimum is published
income_requirement_display.notes: Admission to a Venezuelan educational institution or qualifying internship is required.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed proof period is stated.

key_requirements.requirement: Acceptance by a Venezuelan technical, university, specialization, or internship institution.
Institutional support letter stating the means available to the student.
Educational records, medical certificate, passport, photographs, and consular fee.

initial_validity.value: 1 year, multiple entries, with one year of permitted stay
initial_validity.notes: The Ministry describes this as a non-migrant student visa.

extension_rules.value: Extension must be requested at least two months before expiry
extension_rules.notes: The official page does not establish conversion to settlement status.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct qualifying migrant residence or post-study conversion was established.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: TR-E is classified as non-migrant.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct student-to-Resident rule was established. Article 40's list of visas eligible to request Resident status after one uninterrupted year omits TR-E, while the current official TR-E page only provides one-year stay and extension rules.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A student would need a separately qualifying status change; no current official post-study conversion procedure was found.

path_to_citizenship.value: No citizenship path was established from TR-E itself. The student visa is non-migrant and omitted from the captured one-year Resident conversion list; naturalization separately requires domicile and qualifying uninterrupted residence, so a student would first need another accepted status.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Do not assume TR-E time counts toward naturalization. No official interpretation confirming such credit was located.

rejected_routes.notes: Educational admission, not the applicant's existing degree, creates eligibility. It is not an independent skilled-graduate route or an ordinary remote-work match.

summary.value: A one-year renewable student visa is available without a local employer, but it requires admission or an approved internship and is described as non-migrant. It is omitted from the captured one-year Resident conversion list. No independent degree-recognition, skilled-graduate, or confirmed post-study permanent-residence route was established.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing software-engineering degree alone creates no residence entitlement.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally tax resident after more than 183 aggregate days in Venezuela during the calendar year or the immediately preceding year. Establishing a residence or home can also create residence unless tax residence in another country is proven.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty residence and the facts of an established home may change the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not an expected effective rate. Resident individuals are taxed progressively from 6% to 34%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: For a dependent employee, the principal employee-side charges are 4% mandatory social security, 0.5% employment-benefit regime, and 1% housing, totaling 5.5% on different bases and caps. This figure should not be applied mechanically to an independent foreign contractor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: There is no dedicated digital-nomad or universal freelancer fixed payment. Employee contributions are percentage-based, and the reviewed statutes do not publish a single current monthly tariff for a newly arriving independent contractor.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or inbound-worker tax holiday was found. Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income and may claim a limited credit for qualifying foreign income tax.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Treaty relief depends on the other country and contract structure.

taxes.caveats: Tax treatment depends on days present, whether a Venezuelan home or fixed base is established, employment versus self-employment classification, income source, foreign-employer registration, treaty residence, and foreign tax credits. Tax-unit and exchange-rate volatility make bolívar comparisons unstable.

taxation_system.value: Progressive worldwide-income taxation for residents; Venezuela-source taxation for non-residents, with special rules for certain non-resident service income.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: More than 183 aggregate days in the calendar year or immediately preceding year; establishing a home can also trigger residence unless foreign tax residence is demonstrated.
taxation_system.income_scope: Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxed on Venezuela-source income; foreign residents with a Venezuelan fixed base are taxed on income attributable to it.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad regime found. Foreign tax credits may be available for tax paid on foreign-source income, capped at the corresponding Venezuelan tax.
taxation_system.social_security: Dependent employees are within mandatory social insurance: the employee rates summarized for 2026 are 4% mandatory social security, 0.5% employment-benefit regime, and 1% housing, on different bases and caps. The Social Security Law says an optional scheme is to be established for non-dependent workers, but the reviewed law and current tax summary do not publish a generally applicable independent-worker rate or fixed monthly base. A previously insured person with at least 250 weekly contributions in the prior 10 years may elect continuation within six months and pay both employee and employer shares monthly, calculated from the last 100 weeks' contributory salary.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The 34% dashboard figure is the top marginal screening rate. Liability is calculated progressively in tax units; the 2025 tax-unit value captured by the 2026 source was VES 43.

tax_brackets.notes: Deduction: 0 tax units.
Deduction: 30 tax units.
Deduction: 75 tax units.
Deduction: 155 tax units.
Deduction: 255 tax units.
Deduction: 375 tax units.
Deduction: 575 tax units.
Top marginal bracket; deduction: 875 tax units. No USD conversion is supplied because tax-unit and exchange-rate volatility would make it misleading.

taxation_system.notes: Employee percentages are supported but should not be applied mechanically to a foreign-client contractor. The law distinguishes mandatory dependent employment, a contemplated facultative regime for non-dependent workers, and voluntary continuation for previously insured people; no current official IVSS schedule for a newly arriving independent contractor was located.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No dedicated regime exists. A person who nevertheless works remotely while present may fall under ordinary Venezuelan residence, source, income-tax, and registration rules.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad tax category; ordinary individual taxation would apply if the activity is legally performed.
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Progressive 6%–34%; 34% is the top marginal screening rate
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally more than 183 days in the calendar year or preceding year, or an established Venezuelan home subject to the foreign-residence exception.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Worldwide income is taxable for residents, with a limited foreign tax credit potentially available.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: Ordinary employee contributions may apply if the relationship falls within Venezuelan payroll rules. The reviewed statutes do not provide a single current contribution tariff for a new independent foreign contractor.

fixed_payments.status: No dedicated digital-nomad or universal freelancer fixed payment applies because Venezuela has no such immigration or tax category. Employee contributions are percentage-based. For non-dependent workers, the law contemplates facultative insurance but the reviewed current sources do not publish a generally applicable fixed monthly amount; prior contributors who qualify for continuation pay a variable amount based on earlier contributory salary.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed monthly amount. Dependent-employee charges are percentage-based; newly arriving independent-worker coverage lacks a published current rate/base. Optional continuation is limited to persons with at least 250 contribution weeks in the preceding 10 years and requires payment of both shares based on the last 100 weeks' contributory salary.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: The consular pages require a fee but direct applicants to the diplomatic mission for the current amount.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No dedicated freelancer flat tax or digital-nomad levy was established. Ordinary VAT, municipal, and transaction-tax rules may apply depending on activity and registration.
fixed_payments.notes: The absence of an exact fixed amount is factual: no digital-nomad regime exists, employee charges vary with wages, and the statutes reviewed do not set a single current monthly tariff for an ordinary new foreign contractor. Municipal registration, residence-card, and consular fees remain filing-specific.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Non-residence does not legalize remote work. A non-resident is generally taxed only on Venezuela-source income, but services physically performed in Venezuela may create source or fixed-base issues.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: Worldwide foreign-contract income would generally enter the progressive 6%–34% system, subject to deductions, treaty residence, and foreign tax credits.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: No immigration route expressly enabling ordinary foreign-client freelancing was established. Tax, municipal, VAT, social-security, and exchange-rate obligations require local professional review before registration.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a hypothetical ordinary-tax analysis, not confirmation that remote work is permitted under visitor or rentista status.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker transition to temporary migrant residence exists.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No qualifying remote-work route exists. For the rejected TR-RE, TR-I, TR-FV, TR-ED, TR-REL, and TR-L categories, a resolution permits a discretionary Resident application after at least one uninterrupted year.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Constitution measures domicile and uninterrupted residence rather than a clearly stated number of years after Resident status.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General constitutional minimum immediately before application; reduced to five years for nationals by birth of Spain, Portugal, Italy, Latin American countries, and Caribbean countries. This is not a confirmed timeline from an eligible remote-work route.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The Naturalization Law states that the Carta de Naturaleza decision is due within no more than five months after all required documents are delivered. This is a statutory decision deadline, not verified current real-world processing performance.

key_conditions.value: General naturalization requires Venezuelan domicile and uninterrupted qualifying residence. The Naturalization Law contemplates Spanish-language knowledge and leaves issuance of the Carta de Naturaleza discretionary. Dual nationality is constitutionally permitted.
key_conditions.notes: Status-counting and current documentary practice should be verified with SAIME or Venezuelan nationality counsel.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign spouse may declare the wish to become Venezuelan after at least five years from the marriage date.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can count because the constitutional period runs from the date of marriage, but a foreign marriage must be recognized and, for the family visa, registered through a Venezuelan consular office.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: The sources do not state that the five-year clock restarts upon arrival.

requirements_and_risks.value: The marriage and civil-status documents must establish a genuine legal relationship. Citizenship is not automatic at marriage or at the five-year anniversary; a declaration and administrative process remain necessary. Fraudulent documentation can lead to refusal and immigration consequences.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The five-month Naturalization Law deadline applies after delivery of the complete required file, not from the marriage anniversary.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Article 32 grants Venezuelan nationality by birth to every person born in Venezuelan territory without a parental nationality or residence condition.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Venezuela is Venezuelan by birth even when both parents are foreign migrants.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Birth registration is still necessary to document the status.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born in Venezuela is Venezuelan by birth. A child born abroad to a Venezuelan parent may also qualify by descent, subject to the constitutional residence or declaration rules.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: The migrant father's nationality is not automatically changed by the child's status.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A foreign parent of a Venezuelan child may apply for the Transeúnte Familiar Venezolano family visa upon proving the relationship. Article 40 also lists TR-FV among statuses that may request Resident status after one uninterrupted year, but citizenship is not automatic.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The Resident application is discretionary.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A migrant father of a Venezuelan child can seek the family visa and, after at least one uninterrupted TR-FV year, may request discretionary Resident status. Citizenship remains separate and non-automatic.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The father's immigration and nationality applications require their own filings and evidence.

rank.notes: Passport Index Passport Power Rank, not Henley rank.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as visa-free by Passport Index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring an advance visa.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: Moderately practical within international, professional, and IT circles, but Spanish is needed for government, immigration, housing, healthcare, and most daily interactions. EF EPI 2025 gives Venezuela a score of 520 and reports an IT-function score of 532; median fixed broadband was reported at 92.09 Mbps at the end of 2025.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI reflects test participants rather than universal population fluency. Connectivity and electricity reliability vary sharply by location.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low for ordinary daily life and administration. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian is an official language, and no reliable evidence of broad service availability in either language was found.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Spanish proficiency or local translation support would be necessary.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ENCOVI 2025 private-sector employee average; not a nationwide all-worker average.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ENCOVI publishes category averages and average income by decile but no exact national median wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate April 2026 value of the statutory VES 130 monthly minimum wage, not an observed minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: ENCOVI 2025 private-sector employee average. It is not the average across public employees, self-employed people, and all residents.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed ENCOVI materials do not publish an exact national median wage; decile averages cannot establish it.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: ENCOVI's USD 474.5 figure is the highest decile's average per-capita income, not a maximum wage or upper endpoint.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory wage base in force since March 2022; non-wage bonuses can materially increase actual public-worker income.

average_salary_local_currency.value: Approx. VES 177,346 per month at the 14 Aug 2026 official-rate reference (USD 230 × VES 771.0714/USD)
average_salary_local_currency.notes: A transparent current-currency conversion of ENCOVI 2025's USD-denominated private-sector average, not a salary originally observed or published in bolívares. It is only a 14 August 2026 snapshot.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: ENCOVI 2025 publishes average monthly USD income by decile and selected worker categories, but no national median wage in VES. An exact median cannot be derived without the underlying microdata.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: ENCOVI reports USD 474.5 as the average per-capita monthly income of the highest decile, not a maximum salary. No national maximum wage in VES is published in the reviewed sources.

average_citizen_salary.currency: VES (bolívar); wage evidence is frequently reported in USD because of inflation and de facto dollar pricing
average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Statutory monthly minimum wage plus a separate ENCOVI 2025 private-sector employee average; not a national all-worker mean
average_citizen_salary.period: Minimum checked in 2026; private-sector average relates to 2025; VES conversion uses the 2026-08-14 official-rate reference
average_citizen_salary.notes: Salary evidence is fragmented. VES 130 is the statutory monthly base minimum; USD 230 is ENCOVI 2025's private-sector employee average, converted only as a current VES snapshot. ENCOVI reports other worker categories and income deciles in USD but no national median or maximum wage. These figures are unrelated to immigration income requirements.

cost_of_living_note.value: A 2026 report placed a basic family basket above USD 500 per month, far above the statutory wage base. ENCOVI 2025 also found persistent income poverty and major electricity and water-service gaps, so remote workers should budget for backup power, connectivity, and private services.
cost_of_living_note.notes: Costs differ substantially by city and required service reliability.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: The rentista visa is limited to foreign rent or pension income. Although a discretionary Resident conversion is documented, it is not an ordinary remote-work route.
settlement_track.summary: No current route fits ordinary foreign-contract remote work. A qualifying passive-income TR-RE holder may request discretionary Resident status after one uninterrupted year and could then pursue general naturalization, but active software-contract earnings are not accepted as TR-RE income and current SAIME practice should be confirmed.
settlement_track.notes: The residence-conversion gap is partly resolved. The country still fails selection because the applicant's active foreign contract does not match the official rent-or-pension eligibility test.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The current visa catalogue contains rentista, business, company-owner, investor, student, family, and labor categories but no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-client freelance route. Rentista eligibility is framed around rent or pension income, not active contract earnings.

data.notes: The negative selection result is preserved. The focused pass found a discretionary Resident conversion after one uninterrupted year for TR-RE, TR-I, TR-FV, TR-ED, TR-REL, and TR-L under Resolution No. 364, but not for student, ordinary business, or entrepreneur/industrial visas. It clarified dependent-versus-independent social insurance and supplied a transparent current VES conversion for the published private-sector average while retaining precise nulls for unpublished median and maximum wages. More than 15 relevant URLs were inspected, including seven canonical URLs absent from the prior source set.

data.selection_summary: Vietnam is not a match for the stated profile. No active digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary independent freelance residence category was found. The eVisa permits visitor entry for up to 90 days but is not a remote-work residence status; employment-based status requires a Vietnam-linked employer, while investment, family, education, and exceptional-expert categories change the applicant profile.

visa_application.title: Vietnam National Electronic Visa system
visa_application.notes: This is the official direct application channel for a visitor eVisa, not an application for digital-nomad, freelance, work, or qualifying residence status.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists because the eVisa is an entry visa rather than a remote-work category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published remote-worker income requirement.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold; this is visitor entry only
income_requirement_display.notes: The application requests estimated trip funding but does not establish a qualifying monthly-income threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: No prescribed number of remote-work income months was found.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport and completed electronic application, including intended entry purpose, accommodation, and trip-funding information.
The intended activity must remain consistent with the declared entry purpose; the eVisa does not independently establish work authorization.
Current visa fee is US$25 for single entry or US$50 for multiple entry under 90 days.

initial_validity.value: Maximum 90 days, single or multiple entry
initial_validity.notes: This is authorized temporary stay, not a temporary residence card.

extension_rules.value: No automatic renewal or remote-worker extension. Any extension or change must independently satisfy the immigration law's purpose and sponsorship requirements.
extension_rules.notes: A visitor should not assume that repeated eVisas or temporary-stay extensions create residence rights.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No direct path. A qualifying purpose such as Vietnam-linked employment, study, investment, or eligible family sponsorship would be required.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: The applicant would have to qualify under a materially different status.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None through the eVisa.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Vietnamese permanent residence is confined to specified categories, including certain recognized experts and qualifying citizen-sponsored relatives.

path_to_citizenship.value: None through the eVisa. Naturalization requires qualifying permanent residence and other statutory conditions.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Visitor time is not established as a citizenship route.

rejected_routes.notes: The route is usable for short visits but fails both the residence and citizenship-path requirements of this selection.

rejected_routes.route_name: Vietnam employer-sponsored work permit and LD temporary residence status

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general immigration income threshold was found; eligibility is based on qualifying employment and worker credentials.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No route-specific minimum salary was identified.

income_requirement_display.value: No published route-wide minimum income; Vietnam employer sponsorship is required
income_requirement_display.notes: Regional labor minimum wages are not an immigration eligibility threshold.

income_proof_months.notes: Not expressed as a foreign-income history requirement.

key_requirements.requirement: Employer's written request explaining the need to hire the foreign worker.
Qualification for an eligible foreign-worker category and a work permit or applicable exemption.
Temporary residence documentation must be filed through the inviting or sponsoring organization or person.

initial_validity.value: Work-linked LD temporary residence cards may be valid for up to 2 years
initial_validity.notes: Validity is linked to the qualifying work basis and passport validity.

extension_rules.value: An expired qualifying temporary residence card may be considered for a new card if the underlying basis continues.
extension_rules.notes: This is not an independent renewal right.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Possible after obtaining qualifying Vietnam-linked employment, work authorization, and sponsorship.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not fit an applicant retaining only an ordinary foreign employer or client.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No routine time-based employment-to-PR progression was confirmed. Permanent residence for a scientist or expert requires high-level governmental recommendation and remains discretionary.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Ordinary software-engineering employment is not enough by itself.

path_to_citizenship.value: No reliable route-specific citizenship timeline because ordinary employment does not automatically lead to permanent residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization requires qualifying permanent residence and statutory conditions.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Vietnam-linked employer and employer filing are mandatory, contrary to the independent-application requirement.

summary.value: Admission to a Vietnamese educational institution can support a DH study visa and temporary residence card, potentially valid for up to five years. A foreign degree by itself does not create an independent skilled-migration category, and study status does not directly grant permanent residence.
summary.notes: This requires local institutional admission and sponsorship and is not a route for continuing ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident when present in Vietnam for at least 183 days in a calendar year or in 12 consecutive months from first arrival, or when maintaining a qualifying habitual residence in Vietnam. Residents are taxable on income inside and outside Vietnam; non-residents are taxable on Vietnam-source income.
tax_residency_rule.notes: The habitual-residence limb can matter even below 183 days and must be checked alongside treaty residence.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal screening rate for resident salary and wage income, not the expected effective rate. Non-resident Vietnam work income is generally taxed at 20%.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Potential employee-side social insurance plus health insurance rate for an eligible foreign employee with a qualifying Vietnam labor contract: 8% social insurance and 1.5% health insurance. Unemployment insurance does not apply to foreign employees. This is not established as applicable to an unsupported foreign-contract visitor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No mandatory fixed monthly payment was established for the requested scenario because Vietnam has no digital-nomad or independently registered remote-worker status. Employment contributions are percentage-based; visa and residence-document charges are transaction fees.

special_tax_regimes.value: No dedicated digital-nomad, remote-worker, remittance-basis, or general inbound-worker tax holiday was identified in the current PIT law and implementation material reviewed.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Narrow exemptions may exist for specified official-development or international-organization experts, but these do not fit the ordinary profile.

taxes.caveats: Remote services physically performed in Vietnam may present Vietnamese-source-income and immigration-compliance issues even when the payer is abroad. Residence, income characterization, deductions, treaty tie-breakers, foreign-tax credits, invoicing structure, and social-insurance coverage require professional advice.

taxation_system.value: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Resident salary and wage income uses five progressive brackets from 5% to 35%; non-resident salary or wage income for work performed in Vietnam is taxed at 20%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: At least 183 days in a calendar year or rolling 12-month period, or a qualifying habitual residence in Vietnam.
taxation_system.income_scope: Worldwide income for residents; Vietnam-source income for non-residents.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No generally available digital-nomad or ordinary inbound remote-worker regime was found.
taxation_system.social_security: Eligible foreign employees under qualifying Vietnam fixed-term labor contracts may owe 8% social insurance and 1.5% health insurance; foreign workers are not covered by unemployment insurance under the reviewed source.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: Brackets apply to monthly assessable salary/wage income after applicable deductions. The personal deduction is VND 15.5 million monthly and the dependent deduction is VND 6.2 million monthly under the 2025 PIT law effective for the 2026 tax period.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Up to VND 10 million/month assessable income
tax_brackets.notes: Approximate USD conversion uses VND 25,306 per USD; assessable income is after applicable deductions.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over VND 10 million to VND 30 million/month
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over VND 30 million to VND 60 million/month
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Over VND 60 million to VND 100 million/month
tax_brackets.notes: USD figure represents the approximate upper threshold.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident salary and wage income above the threshold
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal rate; this is not the effective tax rate on total income.

taxation_system.notes: The revised PIT law is effective from July 1, 2026, with resident business, salary, and wage provisions applying from the 2026 tax period.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special category because Vietnam has no confirmed digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-remote-worker residence program. General PIT rules may nevertheless apply based on tax residence and where the services are performed.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No dedicated digital-nomad category; general resident or non-resident PIT rules
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: 5%-35% progressive resident PIT; generally 20% on non-resident wages for work performed in Vietnam
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: 183-day or habitual-residence test; treaty rules may alter the result.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Residents are taxable on income arising inside and outside Vietnam. The treatment of foreign-employer compensation for services physically performed in Vietnam requires source and treaty analysis.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified for ordinary foreign-contract remote workers.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No remote-worker contribution system exists. Eligible locally contracted foreign employees may owe 9.5% employee-side social and health insurance; employer obligations are separate.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad fixed monthly tax or contribution found
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: Percentage contributions may apply only if the person enters an eligible Vietnam labor relationship.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: Single-entry visa US$25; multiple-entry visa under 90 days US$50; temporary-residence-card fees range from US$145 to US$165 depending on validity; permanent-residence card US$100.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No special freelancer municipal fee, fixed remote-worker tax, or digital-nomad levy was established.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa fees do not legalize remote work and should not be treated as recurring tax.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being below 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if a qualifying habitual residence exists. If genuinely non-resident, Vietnam-source salary for work performed in Vietnam may be taxed at 20%.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident is generally taxed on worldwide taxable income at progressive rates up to 35%, subject to deductions, treaty relief, and foreign-tax-credit rules.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: The PIT law taxes business and service income, but no immigration source confirmed that a visitor can register an ordinary foreign-client freelance activity and thereby obtain residence. Tax registration would not cure the immigration problem.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a screening summary, not a determination that remote work on visitor status is lawful.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying temporary-residence route exists for the ordinary foreign-contract profile. Visitor entry is immediate temporary stay but is not counted here as residence.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: Vietnam has no general time-based temporary-residence-to-PR rule for an ordinary remote worker. Citizen-sponsored parents, spouses, or children may apply after at least three consecutive years of temporary residence, but that is a separate family route.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The law requires qualifying permanent residence and five years of residence by the naturalization application, but the reviewed sources do not establish that five additional years must always run after the permanent-residence card is issued.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total can be calculated for this profile because there is no qualifying entry route and no routine path to permanent residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The legislation specifies multiple agency stages and identity checks, including 45 days extendable to 60 for some verification, but no reliable single typical end-to-end processing duration was established after focused review.

key_conditions.value: Ordinary naturalization requires permanent residence, at least five years of qualifying residence by application, sufficient Vietnamese for integration, lawful conduct, and ability to support oneself. Renunciation of prior nationality is generally required, although specified special cases may be permitted to retain it. Approval remains discretionary.
key_conditions.notes: These general naturalization rules do not create a route from the eVisa.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: No minimum duration of marriage was identified for the naturalization exemption itself. For permanent residence through a Vietnamese citizen spouse, parent, or child, the immigration law requires at least three consecutive years of temporary residence; this is a residence condition, not necessarily a marriage-duration rule.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing genuine marriage to a Vietnamese citizen can support family sponsorship and can materially improve access to temporary and permanent residence. Spouses of Vietnamese citizens are also within a statutory naturalization exception that may waive the ordinary language, five-year-residence, and livelihood conditions, but permanent residence and discretionary approval still require filing-level confirmation.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage to a non-citizen does not create the same benefit.

requirements_and_risks.value: The applicant must document the genuine civil relationship, sponsorship, lawful accommodation, and continuous residence where required. Citizenship is not automatic through marriage, and false documents or a sham marriage can cause refusal and other legal consequences. Retaining a prior nationality is discretionary rather than guaranteed.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Current procedural advice should be obtained before relying on the naturalization exemption.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Vietnam primarily follows descent. Territorial rules principally protect specified stateless children and foundlings rather than granting citizenship to every child born in Vietnam.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Vietnam to two foreign-national migrant parents does not ordinarily acquire Vietnamese citizenship by birth. A child of two stateless parents acquires citizenship if both permanently reside in Vietnam; foundlings and certain children of a stateless mother are also protected.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent residence of foreign-national parents alone does not create ordinary jus soli.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: If one parent is Vietnamese and the other is a foreign national, the child acquires Vietnamese nationality when the parents agree in writing at birth registration. If the child is born in Vietnam and the parents cannot agree, Vietnamese nationality applies.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Timely and accurate birth registration remains important.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child can potentially sponsor a foreign parent for family residence and, after at least three consecutive years of temporary residence plus lawful accommodation and stable means, permanent residence. The parent's citizenship is never automatic.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The child's citizenship and the parent-child relationship must be documented.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: A foreign father of a Vietnamese citizen child may potentially use the citizen-child family sponsorship category for temporary residence and later apply for permanent residence after the statutory continuous-residence period. He must apply separately and receives no automatic citizenship from the child's birth.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: This benefit depends on the child actually acquiring Vietnamese citizenship and on genuine parentage, sponsorship, accommodation, and means.

rank.notes: Vietnam Government News reported rank 84 in March 2026, citing the Henley Passport Index.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strictly visa-free destinations in the source's breakdown.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Henley-based government reporting did not publish an advance-visa-required count. Passport Index reports 129 but uses a different destination universe and classification method, so it was not mixed into the Henley figures.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: Derived from the source's total of 48 destinations accessible without a prior conventional visa minus 23 strictly visa-free destinations; the remainder includes VOA, eVisa, or ETA, so this is a combined figure rather than VOA/ETA alone.

passport.notes: Passport figures are time-sensitive. A separate 2026 Passport Index source reports power rank 68, 24 visa-free, 40 VOA, 5 ETA, and 129 visa-required destinations; these are retained only as a methodological cross-check and not combined with Henley rank 84.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is workable in major cities, technology workplaces, and international services, but Vietnamese remains important for government procedures, leases, banking, healthcare, and daily life. EF EPI 2025 placed Vietnam 64th with a score of 500, categorized as moderate proficiency; its IT-function score was also 500.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: EF EPI is a private, self-selected test-based index and should be treated as a practical indicator rather than a census measure.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: No reliable current nationwide evidence established that Russian or Ukrainian is broadly usable for administration or everyday life. Vietnamese is the national language, so Russian- or Ukrainian-only living should not be assumed practical outside limited tourism or expatriate settings.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: Focused searches did not produce a dependable nationwide usage measure; this conclusion is deliberately cautious.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of Q1 2026 average employee income of VND 9.0 million using VND 25,306 per USD.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official releases reported averages, not a national median. Focused searches did not establish a current official median.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate conversion of the lowest 2026 statutory regional minimum wage, VND 3.7 million. This is not an observed minimum or national typical salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Approximate Q1 2026 employee-income average.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No current official national median was found after focused searching.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Vietnam has no meaningful nationwide maximum salary in the sources reviewed. The highest regional minimum wage and average income are not maximum earnings.

min_salary_local_currency.value: VND 3,700,000-5,310,000 per month, depending on region
min_salary_local_currency.notes: Statutory regional minimum wages effective January 1, 2026; Region IV is the lowest and Region I the highest.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: Average employee income in Q1 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: Not published in the official release reviewed.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No reliable national maximum was published.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly employee income; minimum values are statutory regional minimum wages for workers under labor contracts
average_citizen_salary.period: Q1 2026 average; minimum wages effective 2026-01-01
average_citizen_salary.notes: USD figures use the State Bank-derived mid reference of approximately VND 25,306 per USD on July 28, 2026. Actual commercial conversion rates differ.

cost_of_living_note.value: No reliable official household-budget amount suitable for a remote worker was established. Official statistics provide CPI movements rather than a single national monthly cost-of-living budget, and costs vary materially by city and housing choice.
cost_of_living_note.notes: A private crowdsourced budget was not substituted for official data.
