settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Vietnam's eVisa is visitor entry for up to 90 days, not a digital-nomad or qualifying residence status, and it should not be used as a citizenship-path proxy.
settlement_track.summary: No active status fits ordinary foreign-client or foreign-employer remote work while providing a qualifying settlement track. The applicant would need to switch to a materially different employer-sponsored, family, investment, education, or exceptional-expert basis, none of which validates the requested profile.
settlement_track.notes: The previous result's negative conclusion is preserved but strengthened with current immigration, work-permit, tax, nationality, fee, passport, and labor-market evidence.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: A foreign contract or foreign salary does not itself create a Vietnamese visa, work authorization, temporary residence card, permanent residence category, or citizenship path.

data.notes: At least 15 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected. The main unresolved values—national median or maximum wage, a single typical citizenship processing duration, a visa-required count compatible with Henley's methodology, and fixed payments for a nonexistent remote-worker category—remain null with specific explanations rather than estimates.

data.selection_summary: Yemen is not suitable for this selection. No current digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, independent-freelancer, or comparable self-applied residence route was found. Visitor status prohibits work inconsistent with the entry purpose, while employment residence requires a Yemeni employer, work permit, and labor-market approval. Study residence exists but does not authorize ordinary foreign-contract remote work. Conflict, divided administration, and unreliable infrastructure also make filing and remote work exceptionally impractical.

visa_application.title: Yemen eVisa Application Portal
visa_application.notes: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced the Immigration, Passports and Nationality Authority eVisa portal as operational in June 2025. It is a direct application channel for ordinary entry visas, not a digital-nomad or remote-worker route; nationality eligibility, visa type, and approval remain case-specific.

rejected_routes.route_name: Visit, tourism, or business visa and 30-day short residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies to this visitor category.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No remote-worker income threshold applies to this visitor category.

income_requirement_display.value: No remote-worker income threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: This is a visitor category, not a remote-work residence program.

income_proof_months.notes: The consular instructions do not prescribe a number of months of income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Valid passport, prior entry authorization, health certificate, and arrival form under the aliens regulations.
The Washington embassy requires an invitation letter issued through Yemen's immigration department.
A visitor, tourist, or business entrant may not undertake work inconsistent with the purpose of the visa.

initial_validity.value: The aliens regulations grant 30 days of short residence after lawful entry unless reciprocity rules provide otherwise.
initial_validity.notes: The underlying visa's entry validity may differ and must be confirmed with the responsible embassy or eVisa portal.

extension_rules.value: The person must leave when the short residence ends unless the competent authority authorizes an extension or another lawful residence.
extension_rules.notes: No visitor-to-freelancer conversion procedure is provided.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No qualifying remote-worker residence path. A separate residence application needs a recognized purpose such as employment, study, or family relationship.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Visitor residence is not qualifying temporary residence for this selection.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The legislation does not provide a prospective visitor-to-permanent-residence route. Its ordinary and special long-residence categories largely protect people whose qualifying residence predated the 1991 law.

path_to_citizenship.value: No direct path. Separate discretionary naturalization may be available after ten consecutive years of lawful residence to an Arab or foreign Muslim satisfying the statutory conditions, but visitor status is not a credible basis for maintaining that residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Naturalization is discretionary and restricted by the nationality law.

rejected_routes.notes: The current eVisa portal permits direct entry-visa applications, but an entry visa does not authorize foreign-contract remote work or establish a settlement route. Consular requirements and fees vary by jurisdiction, and travel remains subject to extreme security risk.

rejected_routes.route_name: Employer-sponsored foreign-worker entry visa, work permit, and temporary residence

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No statutory foreign-worker salary threshold is stated; the proposed local employment contract must state remuneration.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed official material does not set a minimum foreign-worker salary amount.

income_requirement_display.value: No published salary threshold; local employment contract required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is employer sponsorship, not a foreign-contract remote-worker route.

income_proof_months.notes: Prior income history is not the criterion; employer sponsorship and a proposed employment contract are required.

key_requirements.requirement: The Yemeni employer submits the foreign-worker recruitment or entry-visa request.
Official residence and work permits are mandatory.
The employer must show that qualified Yemeni labor is unavailable for the position.
Qualifications, experience, medical fitness, and a proposed employment contract must be documented.
Foreign workers generally may not exceed 10% of the employer's Yemeni workforce, subject to ministerial adjustment.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence may be granted for up to one year.
initial_validity.notes: The permits issued determine the precise work-card and residence duration.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence may be renewed; the employer must seek work-card renewal at least one month before expiry.
extension_rules.notes: Renewal remains dependent on employment and administrative approval.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, through the employer-sponsored work and residence process.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It does not fit independent foreign-client remote work.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: No current prospective permanent-residence transition was established. Statutory ordinary and special residence provisions are framed around residence completed before the 1991 law took effect.

path_to_citizenship.value: It may provide lawful-residence time relevant to a separate discretionary naturalization application after ten consecutive years for an Arab or foreign Muslim, but the employment route itself does not grant citizenship.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Arabic ability, good conduct, lawful livelihood, needed skills, and presidential approval on the minister's recommendation apply.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because a Yemeni employer, local employment contract, work permit, and labor-market check are mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The reviewed regulations do not prescribe a general student-income threshold.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: The reviewed regulations do not publish a monetary threshold.

income_requirement_display.value: No published general income threshold
income_requirement_display.notes: Admission or confirmation from the educational institution is the relevant basis.

income_proof_months.notes: The regulations do not prescribe a number of income-history months.

key_requirements.requirement: Lawful entry, health certificate, personal declaration, photographs, fee receipt, and confirmation from the university or education authority.

initial_validity.value: Temporary residence is generally limited to a maximum of one year.
initial_validity.notes: The permit issued for the study purpose controls the actual duration.

extension_rules.value: Temporary residence may be renewed while the recognized purpose and approval continue.
extension_rules.notes: No automatic long-term status follows.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: Yes, for genuine study rather than remote work.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: This does not independently authorize ordinary work for a foreign client.

path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The reviewed legislation does not provide a study-to-permanent-residence transition.

path_to_citizenship.value: No education-specific path exists; only the separate, restricted, discretionary naturalization provisions may be relevant after qualifying lawful residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Study status is not a confirmed citizenship track.

rejected_routes.notes: Rejected because it is a study route and no permission for ordinary foreign-contract remote work or confirmed settlement conversion exists.

summary.value: A foreign student may seek residence using confirmation from a university or education authority. Temporary residence is generally limited to one year and renewable, but no independent degree-based skilled migration, study-to-permanent-residence transition, or authorization for ordinary foreign-client remote work was found.
summary.notes: This is education-purpose residence, not qualification-based skilled migration.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is resident if they have a permanent place of residence in Yemen or are present for at least 183 consecutive or intermittent days within the relevant 12-month period.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A permanent home can trigger residence before 183 days.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Screening figure: the top marginal rate for a resident natural person's commercial, service, or professional income. Resident payroll income is capped at 15%; classification of foreign-contract income requires local advice.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening figure for the covered employee share under the 2013-amended private-sector scheme published by the Sana’a-based authority. The employer old-age/disability/survivor share is 11%, with a separate 2% employer work-injury contribution. ISSA states that the amendment is not applied in Aden, where the legacy employee/employer old-age rates remain 6%/9%. These are employment rates, not a confirmed mandatory rate for a foreign independent remote worker.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No single mandatory USD monthly payment applies to the unsupported remote-worker scenario. The Sana’a-administered scheme offers optional self-employed coverage at 18% of a chosen YER income band: YER 7,200–108,000 per month on published bands of YER 40,000–600,000. The forms are listed as free. Foreign eligibility and applicability outside that administration are not established, and ISSA describes self-employed people as excluded from the ordinary employee scheme.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad, remote-worker, expatriate, remittance-basis, or freelancer tax holiday was identified.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Ordinary income-tax rules apply; divided administration can affect enforcement.

taxes.caveats: Yemen has no digital-nomad route. A person physically performing services from Yemen can generate Yemen-source service income even when paid by a foreign client. Whether income is payroll, professional, or commercial affects the rate and compliance mechanism. Fiscal administration and exchange rates differ sharply between areas, so locally competent advice is essential.

taxation_system.value: Territorial/mixed individual income tax: Yemen taxes resident natural-person income within the statutory scope and services performed in Yemen, including externally paid services. Resident professional or business income uses progressive rates up to 20%; resident payroll tax is capped at 15%.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Permanent place of residence or at least 183 days during the relevant 12-month period.
taxation_system.income_scope: Services performed in Yemen are Yemen-source even if paid externally. The English law gives resident legal persons explicit worldwide taxation but does not give resident natural persons the same explicit worldwide wording.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No special digital-nomad or inbound-worker regime identified.
taxation_system.social_security: Yemen has territorially divided private-sector social-insurance practice. Under the 2013-amended scheme published by the Sana’a-based authority, covered employees pay 7% and employers pay 11% for old-age, disability, and survivor insurance, while employers additionally pay 2% for work-injury insurance. ISSA reports that the amendment is not applied in Aden, where the legacy old-age rates are 6% employee and 9% employer. The Sana’a authority also publishes optional self-employed/professional coverage at 18% of a chosen income band, producing monthly contributions of YER 7,200–108,000 on the current table; this does not create immigration permission, and eligibility of a foreign remote worker is not established.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: For resident natural persons subject to commercial, industrial, or professional income tax: YER 120,000 annual exemption; 10% on the next YER 120,000; 15% on the next YER 600,000; and 20% above YER 840,000. Resident payroll tax is separately capped at 15%.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to YER 120,000
tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident natural-person commercial, professional, and comparable income
tax_brackets.notes: Annual exemption. No USD conversion is supplied because Yemen has materially different regional exchange rates.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident natural-person commercial, professional, and comparable income
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident natural-person commercial, professional, and comparable income
tax_brackets.notes: Marginal bracket; resident payroll taxation is separately capped at 15%.

tax_brackets.applies_to: Resident natural-person commercial, professional, and comparable income
tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not the expected effective rate.

taxation_system.notes: Income-tax residence, source, and rate rules are statutory. Social-insurance rates depend on the administering authority: Sana’a publishes the amended 7%/11% scheme and optional self-employed bands, while ISSA records non-application of that amendment in Aden. A foreign remote worker has no matching immigration status, so classification and voluntary coverage require confirmation with the locally competent authorities.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: No digital-nomad tax category exists. A hypothetical independent service provider working physically from Yemen would need classification under ordinary professional or commercial income rules, potentially reaching the 20% top marginal rate.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No route; hypothetical resident independent professional
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 20% progressive PIT for professional/business income; resident payroll PIT is capped at 15%.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Permanent home in Yemen or at least 183 days in the relevant 12-month period.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Foreign payment does not by itself make remote-work income foreign-source: services performed in Yemen fall within Yemen's source rules. The law does not expressly impose worldwide taxation on resident natural persons in the same way it does on resident legal persons.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None identified.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: There is no digital-nomad category. Covered private employment is subject to regionally divergent rates: 7% employee and 11% employer under the Sana’a-published amendment, plus 2% employer work-injury funding, versus legacy 6%/9% old-age rates reported for Aden. Sana’a also publishes optional self-employed coverage at 18% of a selected income band, but foreign eligibility and applicability to an unauthorized remote worker are not established.

fixed_payments.status: No digital-nomad-specific fixed payment; ordinary visa fees vary, and optional self-employed insurance bands exist in Sana’a-administered areas
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No mandatory freelancer payment can be assigned to this nonexistent route. The Sana’a authority publishes optional self-employed contributions at 18% of a chosen YER 40,000–600,000 income band, equal to YER 7,200–108,000 monthly. Covered employment instead uses percentage contributions; ISSA records different legacy rates in Aden.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee exists because Yemen has no such route. For ordinary entry visas, the Washington embassy publishes US$65; the embassy in Rabat publishes US$29 for single entry and US$64 for six-month multiple entry; Ottawa directs applicants to call for the current fee. The national eVisa portal is active, but its publicly accessible pages did not expose a fee schedule during this review. Current residence-card, work-card, and renewal amounts were not published in the reviewed official sources, so there is no defensible single Yemen-wide total.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No fixed freelancer tax was identified. Business registration, professional licensing, withholding, sales-tax, or other obligations may arise depending on structure.
fixed_payments.notes: Visa charges are consular-jurisdiction and category specific, not monthly tax payments. Social-insurance rules differ between administrations, and optional enrollment does not legalize immigration status.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: A person without a permanent home and present fewer than 183 days can remain nonresident, but income from services physically performed in Yemen may still be Yemen-source and taxable. Visitor status does not authorize the work.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A resident performing services from Yemen should expect ordinary Yemen income-tax rules; independent professional/business income can reach 20%. There is no nomad exemption.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: No immigration route allowing a visitor to register as a freelancer and thereby legalize residence was established. Business registration would be separate from immigration permission and could trigger tax, licensing, and optional or mandatory insurance obligations.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This remains a hypothetical tax analysis because no remote-worker immigration route exists. The focused audit established published ordinary visa examples and social-insurance bands but no digital-nomad fee or nationally uniform foreign-freelancer contribution.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: There is no qualifying independent remote-worker route. Employment, study, and family residence require separate recognized grounds.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: The legislation does not establish a prospective permanent-residence transition for an ordinary remote worker.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The nationality law uses lawful residence rather than a confirmed permanent-residence prerequisite.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: General statutory residence period for discretionary naturalization of an Arab or foreign Muslim, not a timeline from a qualifying remote-worker route. Exceptional ministerial settlement permission can reduce it to five years in urgent cases, but that is not a normal application track.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The law does not publish a processing deadline, and no dependable current administrative average is available. A grant remains discretionary and requires presidential decision.

key_conditions.value: For general naturalization: adulthood, ten consecutive years of lawful ordinary residence, good conduct, no disqualifying conviction, lawful livelihood, Arabic ability, and skills needed by the country. The provision applies to an Arab or foreign Muslim and says nationality may be granted by presidential decision on the minister's recommendation; annual quotas may be set.
key_conditions.notes: This restricted discretionary rule is not a confirmed route for every foreign national and does not make Yemen selectable for remote work.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: A foreign woman lawfully married to a Yemeni man may acquire nationality after applying and at least four years of marriage, provided the minister does not issue a reasoned objection. The rule is not gender-neutral.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing valid marriage can support family residence. A foreign wife of a Yemeni may receive residence for up to five years, renewable. A foreign husband of a Yemeni woman may receive residence for up to two years, with renewal subject to regulatory conditions; the nationality law does not give him the foreign-wife four-year citizenship route.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage must be valid and continuing. A Yemeni woman marrying a foreign man also requires ministerial permission under the 2010 amendment.

requirements_and_risks.value: Applicants should expect proof of a valid continuing marriage, lawful entry, registration, and ministerial review. The legislation treats foreign wives and husbands differently. Citizenship is not automatic, and fraud or false documents can cause refusal, penalties, loss of residence, or removal.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The four-year acceleration principally benefits a foreign wife of a Yemeni man, not the male applicant profile.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Citizenship is primarily by descent from either Yemeni parent after the 2010 amendment. Birth in Yemen alone does not automatically confer citizenship, except for foundlings or children of unknown parents; certain locally born children may apply later under conditional provisions.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Yemen to two known foreign parents is not automatically Yemeni. A child born there who remains until adulthood may seek discretionary citizenship within one year after reaching majority if statutory language, health, conduct, and other conditions are met. A child of unknown parentage born in Yemen is treated as Yemeni.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: This is restricted or conditional jus soli, not birthright citizenship for ordinary migrant families.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: A child born inside or outside Yemen to either a Yemeni father or Yemeni mother enjoys Yemeni citizenship under the 2010 amendment.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Civil registration and proof of parentage may still be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically naturalize either foreign parent. Family residence may be available through the Yemeni spouse; the regulations separately grant renewable residence to a foreign mother whose Yemeni child is her sole provider, but no equivalent child-based shortcut for a foreign father was established.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any benefit depends on a separate residence ground and administrative approval.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: No automatic citizenship or permanent residence follows from having a Yemeni child. If the child's mother is Yemeni, the foreign husband may use marriage-based residence provisions, generally granting up to two years and imposing ministerial conditions; this is not a child-based citizenship shortcut.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: The foreign-wife four-year nationality provision does not apply symmetrically to a foreign husband.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed when checked on 2026-08-15; rankings can change frequently.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Destinations classified strictly as visa-free by this index.

visa_required_destinations.notes: Destinations classified as requiring a visa in advance; separate eVisa categories may not be included.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 31 visa-on-arrival destinations plus 3 eTA destinations according to the source.

passport.notes: Passport Index reports a mobility score of 43. Its methodology differs from Henley; this record uses one current source consistently for the requested breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is described by an official Yemeni embassy as widely used and understood, but Arabic is the sole official language. English may work in some business or educated circles; government and legal processes should be expected in Arabic. Security, electricity, and connectivity disruption make practical remote work poor regardless of language.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: No current nationwide English-proficiency statistic is available, so the assessment is qualitative.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Low. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian has official status, and no evidence of broad everyday or administrative availability was identified. Arabic—and sometimes English—would be needed.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The reviewed sources do not publish dependable nationwide Russian- or Ukrainian-usage data.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: Historical survey conversion reported by the ILO for the 2013–2014 Yemen Labour Force Survey; it is not a current 2026 wage estimate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed official and international datasets do not publish a national median wage for Yemen.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed ILO and WageIndicator material does not provide a dependable current statutory minimum wage or observed national minimum salary.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: ILO's contemporaneous USD conversion of 2013–2014 national average monthly earnings; retained as a historical survey figure, not a current salary.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The reviewed national and international datasets do not publish a national median.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum or wage-distribution ceiling is published.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: A current national statutory minimum amount is not published in the reviewed sources.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: National average monthly earnings from the 2013–2014 Labour Force Survey.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The reviewed sources do not publish a national median.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: No national maximum is published, and such a figure is not meaningful without a defined distribution.

average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: Average monthly earnings from the national 2013–2014 Labour Force Survey; historical nominal amount and contemporaneous USD conversion
average_citizen_salary.notes: The average is stale because no newer comparable national wage survey was located. A current USD conversion would be misleading because Yemen has sharply different Aden and Sana’a exchange rates and substantial inflation. Women averaged YER 40,400 and men YER 53,300 in the cited survey.

cost_of_living_note.value: Costs and purchasing power vary sharply by governing area and exchange rate. The World Bank reported that the basic food basket in IRG-controlled areas was 26% more expensive year over year in June 2025; the Aden-market rial reached YER 2,905 per USD in July before recovering to YER 1,676 in early August. More than 60% of households in both major control areas reported inadequate food consumption. Electricity and internet interruptions materially hamper business operations.
cost_of_living_note.notes: These indicators describe economic hardship and infrastructure reliability, not a complete expatriate budget.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor or business entry neither authorizes ordinary foreign-contract remote work nor supplies a settlement track.
settlement_track.summary: No regular independent remote-work route exists. Employment residence needs a Yemeni employer, study residence is purpose-limited, and the separate restricted ten-year naturalization provision does not create an immigration route for a foreign remote worker.
settlement_track.notes: The negative conclusion is supported by the aliens, labor, and nationality legislation and the current employer service. Fragmented administration means filing details should still be verified directly before travel.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: The direct eVisa portal is only an entry-visa channel. Visitor status prohibits work inconsistent with the entry purpose, and the identified work route requires a Yemeni employer, local contract, work permit, and labor-market approval. No digital-nomad or independent foreign-client freelancer residence status was found.

data.notes: Thirty-one distinct directly relevant canonical URLs are retained. This focused pass inspected more than fifteen relevant pages, including nine URLs absent from the previous source set. It resolved the social-insurance field into administration-specific employee, employer, work-injury, and optional self-employed rates and documented current ordinary visa-fee examples. No digital-nomad fee or nationally uniform residence/work-card fee schedule is published in the reviewed current sources. Overall confidence remains medium because Yemen’s administration is divided and the applicant has no matching remote-work immigration route.

data.selection_summary: Zambia does not currently publish a digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, freelance, or ordinary self-employed immigration permit that fits a software engineer working only for a foreign client. The official permit catalogue instead offers employer-controlled employment permits, high-capital investor permits, study permits, spouse permits, and visitor permissions. Visitor entry does not authorize gainful activity or create residence, while the potentially settlement-bearing employment and investor routes require, respectively, a Zambian employer or substantial investment in a Zambian business.

visa_application.title: Zambia Immigration e-Services
visa_application.notes: This is the official online visa and permit portal. It is a genuine application channel, but the current official permit catalogue contains no digital-nomad or ordinary foreign-contract remote-worker category.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No remote-worker income threshold exists because this is a visitor permission, not a remote-work route.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No published minimum monthly income; applicants instead show a return ticket or ability to return.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly income threshold; visitor status is not a work/residence route
income_requirement_display.notes: The Visiting Permit requirements mention a return ticket or bank evidence of ability to return, not qualifying remote income.

income_proof_months.notes: The official requirements do not specify a fixed number of bank-statement months.

key_requirements.requirement: A Visiting Permit is for an ordinary visitor wishing to remain beyond 90 days and requires an applicant letter, host consent/status, passport, photograph, return ticket or evidence of ability to return, and the fee.
It is not an authorization for ordinary foreign-contract remote work and does not confer temporary or permanent residence.

initial_validity.value: 3 months
initial_validity.notes: This concerns the Visiting Permit issued after the ordinary visitor wishes to remain beyond 90 days.

extension_rules.value: May be extended, but total Visiting Permit time cannot exceed 9 months in any 12-month period.
extension_rules.notes: Temporary visitor permission only.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: No automatic or published conversion from visitor status to a qualifying remote-worker residence permit.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: Other permits require their own substantive grounds.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: None from visitor status was confirmed.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: The official permanent Residence Permit eligibility list does not include ordinary visitors.

path_to_citizenship.value: No route-specific citizenship path; visitor presence should not be assumed to constitute qualifying ordinary residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Citizenship law measures qualifying ordinary residence, not tourism.

rejected_routes.notes: Independent visitor applications are possible, but visitor permission fails both the work-authorisation and citizenship-path tests.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No general minimum salary was found; eligibility is based on qualifying Zambian employment and employer filings.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No general minimum salary threshold is published on the official permit page.

income_requirement_display.value: No general salary threshold published; Zambian employment and sponsorship required
income_requirement_display.notes: This is an employer-sponsored route, not a foreign-income route.

income_proof_months.notes: Not expressed as prior income history.

key_requirements.requirement: Only an employer, practising lawyer, or registered immigration consultant may submit the initial application; the expatriate cannot self-apply.
Requires a Zambian employment contract or offer, employer covering letter, police clearance, CV, qualifications, succession/training plan, corporate documents, and recruitment advertisements.
Applicants must remain outside Zambia until approval.

initial_validity.value: For employment exceeding 6 months; exact first grant is permit-specific.
initial_validity.notes: The official page does not state a universal initial term.

extension_rules.value: Renewable up to a maximum aggregate period of 10 years, with employer letter, extended contract, passport, and fee.
extension_rules.notes: Continued local employment is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Employment Permit itself authorizes residence for the approved employment period.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is tied to specified local employment.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A holder may qualify to apply for a permanent Residence Permit after continuously holding an Employment Permit for more than 10 years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: This does not make the route usable for an ordinary foreign-client remote worker.

path_to_citizenship.value: General citizenship by registration may be available after at least 10 continuous years of qualifying ordinary residence, but no official source confirms that every Employment Permit period automatically satisfies that test.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Separate filing-level verification would be required.

rejected_routes.notes: Potentially settlement-bearing, but categorically rejected because local-employer control and a local job are mandatory.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: The requirement is investment capital, not monthly income.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No monthly-income test; capital is stated in US dollars.

income_requirement_display.value: No monthly-income test; US$250,000 investment for a new business or US$150,000 to join an existing business
income_requirement_display.local_or_formula_value: US$250,000 new business / US$150,000 existing business
income_requirement_display.notes: These are capital requirements and must not be displayed as recurring income.

income_proof_months.notes: Proof concerns invested capital rather than an income-history period.

key_requirements.requirement: Must establish or invest in a Zambian business, or join an existing company.
Requires incorporation/share-capital documents, directors list, proof of capital, and Zambian ownership or lease evidence; an investment licence may also be supplied.
Renewal requires tax receipts or tax-clearance certificate, audited accounts, bank statement, lease where applicable, and an immigration inspection.

initial_validity.notes: The current official route page and Act excerpts inspected do not establish a universal initial term; it is specified on the permit.

extension_rules.value: Renewable subject to continued business, tax, audit, financial, premises, fee, and inspection evidence.
extension_rules.notes: No universal renewal length was confirmed.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The Investor's Permit authorizes the holder to remain in Zambia and conduct or supervise the approved business.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is business-specific and not ordinary foreign-contract freelancing.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: A holder may qualify to apply for a permanent Residence Permit after holding an Investor's Permit for more than 3 years.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: Qualification remains application-based.

path_to_citizenship.value: Potentially through the general rule requiring at least 10 continuous years of qualifying ordinary residence, not through a special investor naturalisation rule.
path_to_citizenship.notes: The exact counting of permit time should be confirmed before relying on it.

rejected_routes.notes: This is independently accessible and can lead toward permanent residence, but it is excluded because it requires substantial capital and real Zambian business activity rather than ordinary work for a foreign client.

minimum_monthly_income_usd.notes: No monthly threshold was confirmed; financial support evidence may be required in the individual application.

minimum_income_local_currency.notes: No fixed amount is published on the inspected route page.

income_requirement_display.value: No fixed monthly threshold published
income_requirement_display.notes: Study admission, not remote income, is the substantive basis.

income_proof_months.notes: No fixed period was confirmed.

key_requirements.requirement: Requires full-time or part-time study at a Zambian educational institution and an institutional acceptance/covering letter.
The holder may not engage for gain in an activity, business, trade, employment, or profession not specified in the permit.

initial_validity.value: Tied to approved study; required where study exceeds 3 months.
initial_validity.notes: No universal first-grant duration was published.

extension_rules.value: Renewal requires a school covering letter, latest transcript or progress report, and fee.
extension_rules.notes: Continued study is required.

path_to_temporary_residence.value: The permit authorizes temporary stay for study.
path_to_temporary_residence.notes: It is not a general work permit.

path_to_permanent_residence.value: No direct study-to-permanent-residence transition was found in the official Residence Permit eligibility list.
path_to_permanent_residence.notes: A different qualifying status would be needed.

path_to_citizenship.value: No study-specific path was confirmed, and study time should not be assumed to count as qualifying ordinary residence.
path_to_citizenship.notes: Manual legal verification would be required.

rejected_routes.notes: Available independently through admission, but it prohibits unrelated gainful work and is neither a remote-work nor confirmed settlement route.

summary.value: A foreign national admitted to a Zambian institution may independently seek a Study Permit for study exceeding three months. It authorizes temporary study-related stay, prohibits gainful activity outside the permit conditions, and is not listed as a direct basis for permanent Residence Permit eligibility.
summary.notes: The applicant's existing software-engineering degree alone creates no independent skilled-residence route.

tax_residency_rule.value: An individual is generally treated as resident if present in Zambia for 183 days or more in a charge year. Residence may arise sooner where presence is not temporary and the individual intends to establish residence.
tax_residency_rule.notes: Treaty tie-breakers and personal facts can alter the result.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: This is the 2026 top marginal personal-income-tax rate, not an expected effective rate.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Screening employee share: NAPSA is 5% of pensionable earnings and NHIMA formal-sector employee contribution is 1%. NAPSA has a ceiling, the employer matches both contributions, and applicability to a foreign-contract freelancer without lawful local work status is not established.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: No reliable USD conversion or universal fixed remote-worker payment exists. The 2026 NAPSA schedule states a K1.50 minimum total monthly contribution and K3,723.60 maximum total contribution, while NHIMA assesses informal-sector contributions separately.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad or special inbound remote-worker tax regime was found. Zambia generally uses source-based taxation, with residents additionally taxed on certain foreign interest and dividends.
special_tax_regimes.notes: This does not mean services physically performed from Zambia for a foreign client are automatically foreign-source or exempt.

taxes.caveats: No qualifying remote-worker immigration status exists. If services are nevertheless lawfully performed while physically in Zambia, source characterization, employment versus independent-business classification, turnover/VAT registration, provisional tax, social insurance, and treaty relief require advice from ZRA or a Zambian tax practitioner.

taxation_system.value: Progressive personal income tax under a primarily source-based system.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: Resident at 183 days in a charge year, or potentially earlier where presence is not temporary and there is an intention to establish residence.
taxation_system.income_scope: Zambian-source income is generally taxable. Residents are also taxed on foreign-source interest and dividends; the treatment of foreign-client service income depends on source and factual classification.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad or ordinary remote-worker exemption was identified.
taxation_system.social_security: NAPSA total contribution is 10% of pensionable earnings, split 5% employee and 5% employer, subject to the 2026 K37,236 monthly ceiling. NHIMA formal-sector contributions are stated as 1% employee plus 1% employer; informal-sector premiums are assessed separately.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: 2026 annual bands are 0% through K61,200; 20% from K61,201 to K85,200; 30% from K85,201 to K110,400; and 37% above K110,400.

tax_brackets.threshold_local: Annual taxable income up to ZMW 61,200
tax_brackets.notes: 2026 charge year.

tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.notes: Marginal band.

tax_brackets.notes: Top marginal screening rate, not effective tax.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a dedicated category because Zambia has no confirmed digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker permit or tax regime.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 37% top marginal rate if income is taxable in Zambia; this is not an effective-rate estimate.
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Generally 183 days in a charge year, with a possible earlier residence finding where presence is not temporary and residence is intended.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: The system is principally source-based; residents are additionally taxable on foreign interest and dividends. Foreign payment does not by itself establish that remotely performed services are foreign-source.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: No nomad-specific exemption. Formal employment can trigger 5% employee NAPSA plus 1% employee NHIMA, with matching employer shares; independent/informal treatment requires classification and registration review.

fixed_payments.status: No nomad-specific fixed payments
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: The 2026 NAPSA schedule sets K1.50 minimum total and K3,723.60 maximum total monthly contributions. NHIMA formal-sector premiums are percentage-based; informal premiums use an assessment tool.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No digital-nomad fee exists. Other visa and permit fees depend on the unrelated status selected.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: No universal fixed freelancer tax was established. Business registration, provisional income tax, turnover tax, VAT, or other obligations depend on activity and turnover.
fixed_payments.notes: These amounts do not legalize remote work under visitor status.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Being present fewer than 183 days does not guarantee non-residence if facts show an intention to establish residence, and Zambian-source income can remain taxable even for a non-resident.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: A tax resident performing services from Zambia should obtain a source and classification determination; foreign payment alone does not create an exemption.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: A taxpayer commencing business generally must register with ZRA and obtain a TPIN within 30 days, but tax/business registration does not create immigration permission to reside or work.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: The tax description is screening guidance only because there is no matching immigration route and official sources do not directly address the exact foreign-client remote-work fact pattern.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-work route exists, so there is no route-specific temporary-residence starting point.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: No remote-worker transition exists. Unrelated eligibility includes more than 3 years on an Investor's Permit, more than 10 continuous years on an Employment Permit, or at least 5 years on a Spouse Permit.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: Citizenship law uses qualifying ordinary residence rather than a stated number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: There is no total for this profile because no qualifying entry route exists. The general constitutional registration rule is at least 10 continuous years of ordinary residence immediately before application.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: No reliable current typical processing duration was found. The Act says the Board decides within a prescribed period and registration follows within 21 days after approval, but that is not the total processing time.

key_conditions.value: General registration requires adulthood and at least 10 continuous years of ordinary residence immediately before applying. The Act permits rejection for falsehood, fraud, a qualifying conviction, bankruptcy, prohibited-immigrant status, or public-interest reasons; approved applicants take an oath or affirmation. Dual citizenship is permitted.
key_conditions.notes: No official source confirmed that visitor or study time counts as ordinary residence.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: Five years holding a Spouse Permit is listed for permanent Residence Permit eligibility; citizenship law separately permits application after at least five years of marriage to a Zambian citizen.

existing_marriage_effect.value: An existing marriage can count toward the five-year citizenship rule because a marriage recognized under Zambian law may have been solemnized in Zambia or abroad. For permanent residence, however, the immigration page specifically requires at least five years holding a Spouse Permit.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage duration and permit-holding duration should not be conflated.

requirements_and_risks.value: For citizenship, the marriage must be legally recognized; the applicant must not be a prohibited immigrant or have been convicted and sentenced to imprisonment, and the marriage must not have been entered into to obtain immigration or citizenship status. A Spouse Permit requires the spouse's consent/status, marriage certificate, passport, sustenance evidence, and fees.
requirements_and_risks.notes: Citizenship is by application, not automatic. False documents or a sham marriage create refusal, criminal, and possible deprivation risks.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Zambia alone is insufficient. At least one parent must be or have been a Zambian citizen at the child's birth; a found child aged no more than eight with unknown nationality and parents is presumed a citizen.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: A child born in Zambia to two non-citizen migrant parents does not acquire citizenship merely by birth in Zambia. The narrow foundling presumption does not ordinarily apply when the parents are known.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: No broader automatic statelessness exception was established in the provisions inspected.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Zambia is a citizen by birth if at least one parent is or was a citizen at the time of birth. A child born abroad is a citizen by descent if at least one parent is or was a citizen by birth or descent.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Birth registration and documentary proof remain practically necessary.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer citizenship or permanent residence on a foreign father. Any benefit must arise through a separately qualifying spouse, dependant, or other immigration application.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: The official Residence Permit list includes a foreign dependant under a citizen's care but does not state that parenthood alone automatically qualifies a migrant parent.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is a Zambian citizen and the parents are married, the father may use the separate Spouse Permit and marriage-based citizenship provisions. The child's citizenship itself does not automatically naturalize or regularize the father.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: Unmarried-parent and dependency cases require individual confirmation.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: High for administration and business: English is the constitutional official language, and the Ministry of Tourism states that media and business operate in English and that it is widely spoken. Internet quality, power reliability, and local connectivity still require location-specific checks.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: This evaluates language practicality only, not immigration legality.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: English or a commonly used local language would normally be needed.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: No official national median monthly wage amount was established from the inspected 2024 survey materials or 2026 reference schedule.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No single current nationwide statutory minimum covering all occupations was established. Sectoral minimum wages should not be presented as a universal observed minimum.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Not converted without a date-matched official exchange rate.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The 2024 Labour Force Survey was inspected, but a defensible published national median amount was not located.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: No meaningful national maximum salary is published; an earnings ceiling for pension contributions is not a maximum wage.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: Minimum-wage legislation exists, but a single current universal monthly amount was not established because rates are occupational/sectoral.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: The 2026 National Pension Scheme statutory schedule labels this the national average monthly earnings reference value for 1 January–31 December 2026.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: No official median amount confirmed.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The ZMW 37,236 social-security ceiling is a contribution ceiling, not a maximum wage.

data.notes: At least 22 distinct directly relevant URLs were inspected. Remaining nulls are limited to facts that the current materials did not establish reliably, including a route-specific income threshold, typical citizenship processing time, national median/minimum/maximum wages, date-matched USD wage conversion, and an official current cost-of-living basket.

data.selection_summary: Zimbabwe has no dedicated digital-nomad, foreign-remote-worker, or ordinary foreign-client freelancer residence route. Its visitor rules prohibit engaging in an occupation without authorization; the published employment permit requires an employment contract, local advertising, shortlisted candidates, an understudy, and company documents, while residence routes otherwise depend on family or substantial investment. It therefore does not fit independent ordinary foreign-contract remote work.

summary.value: A foreign student accepted by an approved college or university can independently apply for a student permit lasting up to one year and renewable in one-year periods. It restricts work and has no confirmed direct permanent-residence transition, so a degree alone does not create an independent skilled-residence route.
summary.notes: The inspected immigration categories contain no independent qualification- or degree-based skilled migration route comparable to a points-tested residence program.

tax_residency_rule.value: Zimbabwe's operative Income Tax Act is principally source-based. No reliable current official source reviewed established that an individual becomes taxable on worldwide income solely after a simple 183-day threshold; services physically performed from Zimbabwe may nevertheless be Zimbabwe-source regardless of a foreign payer.
tax_residency_rule.notes: A 183-day residence rule appears in an older Income Tax Bill, but its enactment and current operative status were not established, so it is not treated as law here.

income_tax_rate_percent.notes: Top marginal or screening PAYE rate, not the expected effective rate. The official ZIMRA page still displays 2025 tables; a current 2026 secondary table reports the same 40% top rate but should be confirmed before filing.

social_contributions_percent.notes: Employee share of the mandatory NSSA Pension and Other Benefits Scheme for covered formal employment. The employer contributes another 4.5%, making 9% combined, on monthly insurable earnings capped at US$700; the maximum employee deduction is therefore US$31.50 monthly. This percentage is not established as a mandatory charge on an ordinary self-employed foreign contractor.

fixed_payments_usd_monthly.notes: NSSA is percentage-based rather than a universal fixed payment. For a covered employee earning at least the US$700 insurable-earnings ceiling, the employee share is capped at US$31.50 monthly, but lower earners pay 4.5% of actual covered earnings. Official material describes the schemes as employment-based and does not establish a compulsory fixed contribution for a self-employed foreign-contract remote worker.

special_tax_regimes.value: No digital-nomad tax exemption was found. The 2026 budget proposes special incentives for qualifying Business and Knowledge Process Outsourcing operators and a 15% rate for specified skilled essential expatriate staff, but these are business or employment incentives, not an ordinary foreign-contract nomad regime.
special_tax_regimes.notes: Eligibility and implementing legislation for the 2026 incentives require professional confirmation.

taxes.caveats: Zimbabwe has no digital-nomad route, and the tax characterization of foreign-paid remote work depends on where services are performed, whether the person is an employee or independent trader, business registration, source rules, currency of receipt, and any applicable treaty. The current official ZIMRA PAYE page had not been updated beyond 2025, and the inspected commercial 2026 tax tables were not fully consistent. NSSA's 4.5% employee rate and US$700 ceiling are supported for covered employment, but the official sources inspected do not impose that payroll contribution on an ordinary self-employed foreign contractor. Obtain ZIMRA, NSSA, or professional advice before filing.

taxation_system.value: Mixed source-based system: progressive PAYE for employment income, while ZIMRA lists income of an individual from trade and investments at 25%; a 3% AIDS levy applies to income tax payable.
taxation_system.tax_residency_rule: No operative, current official bright-line day-count rule was confirmed; source of income is central.
taxation_system.income_scope: Income from a Zimbabwe source or deemed Zimbabwe source. Remote services performed while physically in Zimbabwe may be taxable even when paid abroad.
taxation_system.special_regimes: No digital-nomad exemption. Separate 2026 proposals target qualifying BPO/KPO operators and specified essential expatriate staff.
taxation_system.social_security: For covered formal employment, NSSA's Pension and Other Benefits Scheme requires 4.5% of monthly insurable earnings from the employee and 4.5% from the employer, capped on US$700 of earnings, so each side's maximum is US$31.50 monthly. The scheme covers employees aged over 16 and under 65, including expatriate employees; employer remittance is due by the 10th of the following month. The separate Accident Prevention and Workers' Compensation Scheme is funded wholly by employers at an industry-risk-based premium, with government, domestic-worker employers, and the informal sector identified as exempt in the current employer guide. Official NSSA publications characterize these schemes as employment-based and state that self-employed occupational injuries are generally outside workers' compensation coverage; they do not publish a mandatory NSSA percentage or fixed contribution for an ordinary self-employed foreign-contract remote worker.
taxation_system.progressive_tax_notes: The dashboard's 40% figure is the top PAYE marginal rate, not an effective rate. A secondary 2026 table reports USD and ZiG bands, but the official ZIMRA page still shows 2025 data and must be checked for filing.

taxation_system.notes: The focused social-security audit resolved the covered-employee rate and ceiling: 4.5% employee plus 4.5% employer on earnings capped at US$700. APWCS is a separate employer-funded, risk-rated scheme. No inspected official source established a compulsory NSSA contribution for this hypothetical self-employed remote-worker profile. Exact 2026 PAYE bands remain lower-confidence because ZIMRA's current page still displays 2025 tables.

digital_nomad_taxation.value: Not applicable as a special regime because Zimbabwe has no digital-nomad or remote-worker status. If a person were separately authorized to work, employment income could fall under progressive PAYE up to 40%, while ZIMRA lists individual trade and investment income at 25%, with a 3% AIDS levy on tax payable.
digital_nomad_taxation.route_tax_category: No digital-nomad category; hypothetical authorized employment or individual trade
digital_nomad_taxation.income_tax_display: Up to 40% marginal PAYE; individual trade and investment income listed at 25%, plus 3% AIDS levy on tax
digital_nomad_taxation.tax_residency_rule: Source of the income and place where services are performed are more important than a presumed 183-day rule; no operative official bright-line rule was confirmed.
digital_nomad_taxation.foreign_income_treatment: Payment by a foreign client does not necessarily make services performed from Zimbabwe foreign-source. Filing-level advice is required.
digital_nomad_taxation.special_digital_nomad_or_inbound_regime: None found.
digital_nomad_taxation.social_security_and_payroll: If the person is a covered employee, NSSA POBS is 4.5% employee plus 4.5% employer on earnings capped at US$700, with a maximum US$31.50 monthly charge for each side. APWCS is an additional employer-only risk-rated premium. The official sources inspected do not establish a compulsory NSSA contribution for an ordinary self-employed foreign-contract remote worker, and Zimbabwe has no nomad status to define a special contribution treatment.

fixed_payments.status: No universal nomad or freelancer fixed monthly tax was identified.
fixed_payments.social_security_or_payroll: No universal fixed amount applies. Covered employees pay 4.5% of insurable earnings, capped at US$31.50 monthly; a compulsory self-employed remote-worker contribution was not established in the inspected official materials.
fixed_payments.visa_or_state_fees: No nomad fee exists. Temporary Employment Permit and ordinary residence applications are generally US$500; visitor eVisa fees vary by category.
fixed_payments.other_fixed_or_transaction_taxes: VAT registration is compulsory once taxable supplies exceed US$25,000 or ZiG equivalent in 12 months under the current ZIMRA page. The 2026 budget states IMTT of 1.5% for ZiG transactions and 2% for foreign-currency transactions, subject to applicable rules.
fixed_payments.notes: VAT treatment of exported services and transaction-tax exemptions require individual review.

practical_scenarios.under_tax_residency_threshold: Short presence does not itself authorize work or guarantee tax exemption. Visitor rules prohibit engaging in an occupation without an authorizing permit.
practical_scenarios.tax_resident_remote_worker: There is no lawful nomad route. If work were separately authorized, services performed in Zimbabwe could be Zimbabwe-source and taxable under PAYE or trade rules.
practical_scenarios.self_employed_or_local_registration: No immigration source confirms that registering a local business or tax number after visitor entry legalizes residence. Business, tax, and immigration authorization are separate. Official NSSA sources describe compulsory contributions in employment terms and do not establish a mandatory self-employed remote-worker contribution.

digital_nomad_taxation.notes: This is a hypothetical tax screening because the immigration route does not exist. The displayed 40% is a top marginal rate, not an expected effective rate.

years_to_temporary_residence.notes: No qualifying independent remote-worker route exists, so there is no applicable remote-worker temporary-residence timeline.

years_to_permanent_residence_after_tempo.notes: A Temporary Employment Permit can support a residence-permit application after 5 continuous years, but that route requires non-fitting employment conditions and is not the selected profile's route.

years_to_citizenship_after_permanent_res.notes: The Constitution measures citizenship eligibility from at least 10 years of continuous lawful residence, not from a universally stated number of years after permanent residence.

total_years_to_citizenship.notes: No total is assigned to the requested profile because there is no qualifying starting route. The general constitutional threshold is at least 10 years of continuous lawful residence.

typical_citizenship_processing_time_mont.notes: The inspected official legislation publishes no current service standard or typical citizenship processing period.

key_conditions.value: General citizenship by registration requires at least 10 years of continuous lawful residence and satisfaction of statutory conditions. Older Citizenship Act text refers to good character, intention to continue residing, and willingness to renounce another citizenship; constitutional and current filing-level interpretation should be confirmed.
key_conditions.notes: The accessible Citizenship Act is not fully aligned with the Constitution's 10-year wording, so the constitutional rule controls this screening.

years_of_marriage_or_residence_required.notes: The Constitution entitles a person married to a Zimbabwean citizen for at least 5 years to apply for citizenship by registration, subject to statutory conditions.

existing_marriage_effect.value: Time married before or after the Constitution's effective date can count toward the 5-year marriage period. A foreign spouse may also apply for spouse residence with sponsorship or support from the Zimbabwean spouse.
existing_marriage_effect.notes: Marriage does not grant citizenship automatically; an application and satisfaction of prescribed conditions remain necessary.

requirements_and_risks.value: The spouse-residence checklist requires a marriage certificate, close-relative guarantee, accommodation and funds evidence, police clearance, medical or radiological documentation, and support from the local spouse. False documents, concealment or a non-genuine marriage can lead to refusal, cancellation or revocation; genuine-marriage evidence may be examined.
requirements_and_risks.notes: The official checklist does not publish a detailed sham-marriage test, so ordinary fraud and authenticity risks are stated cautiously.

birthright_citizenship.notes: Birth in Zimbabwe alone is insufficient. A Zimbabwe-born child is a citizen by birth when either parent is a Zimbabwean citizen or a grandparent was a citizen by birth or descent; unknown-parent foundlings under 15 are presumed citizens.

if_both_parents_migrants.value: No automatic citizenship arises merely because the child is born in Zimbabwe to two non-citizen migrant parents. Citizenship may still arise through a qualifying Zimbabwean grandparent or the foundling rule.
if_both_parents_migrants.notes: Permanent or temporary residence of the parents alone is not listed as a constitutional birthright condition.

if_second_parent_local_citizen.value: Yes. A child born in Zimbabwe is a citizen by birth if either the mother or father is a Zimbabwean citizen. A child born abroad may qualify by birth or descent depending on the citizen parent's residence or status and birth registration.
if_second_parent_local_citizen.notes: Registration of an overseas birth may be required.

parent_benefit_summary.value: A citizen child does not automatically confer residence, permanent residence or citizenship on a migrant father. The published residence categories include spouses, minor children, and dependent parents of a resident, but no automatic parent-of-citizen-child status was identified.
parent_benefit_summary.notes: Any family or dependency application would be discretionary and must be verified with Immigration.

benefit_to_migrant_father.value: If the other parent is Zimbabwean, the migrant father may have a separate spouse-residence and five-year marriage citizenship route. His status comes from the marriage or family application, not automatically from the child's citizenship.
benefit_to_migrant_father.notes: If there is no qualifying marriage or other permit basis, the child's citizenship alone is not shown to legalize the father's stay.

rank.notes: Passport Power Rank displayed on the source at the research date.

visa_free_destinations.notes: Strict visa-free count; it excludes visa on arrival and eTA.

visa_required_destinations.notes: The index separately lists eVisa destinations; its visa-required total is reproduced as published.

visa_on_arrival_or_eta_destinations.notes: 28 visa-on-arrival plus 5 eTA destinations.

passport.notes: Passport indexes use different methodologies. This record uses one current index consistently for rank and category breakdown.

english_remote_work_practicality.value: English is the principal language of business, education, media and government, so daily professional work in major cities is generally practical in English. Connectivity and power reliability can still constrain remote work, especially outside well-served urban locations.
english_remote_work_practicality.notes: English practicality is linguistic and infrastructural only; it does not imply immigration permission to work remotely.

russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.value: Russian and Ukrainian are not official languages and the inspected official language material supplies no evidence of broad everyday use. A Russian- or Ukrainian-only speaker should expect to rely on English or arrange interpretation.
russian_or_ukrainian_practicality.notes: The official materials inspected publish no quantitative measure of local Russian or Ukrainian usage.

average_wage_usd_monthly.notes: ZIMSTAT publishes income distributions and industry averages, but the inspected reports do not expose a defensible single national mean in extractable text. Currency volatility also makes an unsupported USD conversion inappropriate.

median_wage_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected current official labour reports do not publish an extractable national median monthly wage.

min_salary_usd_monthly.notes: Zimbabwe uses sector-specific wage arrangements; the inspected official labour reports do not establish a single national statutory minimum wage.

average_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The Q2 2025 Labour Force Survey contains industry-average income graphics but no confidently extractable national average suitable for this normalized field.

median_salary_usd_monthly.notes: The inspected official reports do not publish a national median monthly amount suitable for this field.

max_salary_usd_monthly.notes: A meaningful national maximum salary is not published and should not be inferred from an income-band chart.

min_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official reports do not establish a single national ZiG minimum wage.

average_salary_local_currency.notes: No single national mean amount can be established from the inspected official report text.

median_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official reports do not publish a national ZiG median monthly wage.

max_salary_local_currency.notes: The inspected official reports do not publish a national maximum wage.

average_citizen_salary.currency: Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG), with substantial USD use
average_citizen_salary.salary_basis: ZIMSTAT household labour-force income distributions and formal-sector employment and earnings indices
average_citizen_salary.period: Latest inspected reports cover Q2 2025 and Q4 2025, published through July 2026
average_citizen_salary.notes: The wage fields remain null because the official publications do not provide a defensible single national mean or median in accessible text. The Q2 survey reports that 58.5% of employment was informal, while the later earnings index primarily captures covered or formal establishments, so the measures are not interchangeable.

cost_of_living_note.notes: The inspected official labour publications do not provide a current national cost-of-living amount directly comparable with the salary fields; private crowd-sourced city estimates were excluded.

settlement_track.nomad_only_warning: Visitor or eVisa status does not authorize an occupation and is not qualifying remote-worker residence.
settlement_track.summary: Zimbabwe's permit system provides employment, investment, study and family routes but no ordinary independent foreign-contract remote-work route. Although employment-permit holders may reach residence after five years and general lawful residents may become eligible for citizenship after ten years, the applicant cannot start that track through the requested remote-work profile.
settlement_track.notes: A switch would require a materially different basis such as qualifying local employment, substantial investment, study followed by another status, or family sponsorship.

regular_foreign_contract_remote_work_fit.notes: No digital-nomad or foreign-remote-worker category appears in the official permit system. Visitor rules prohibit occupation, and the published employment checklist requires employment, company, and labour-market documentation.

data.notes: High confidence in the negative immigration selection and in the covered-employee NSSA rate and ceiling. Overall confidence remains medium because exact 2026 PAYE bands, the tax-source characterization of a particular foreign contract, and national wage aggregates require further authoritative or filing-level confirmation. The focused pass inspected more than 15 distinct directly relevant URLs, including at least 7 URLs outside the previous source set.
